kusaal: Vɔt kan la ni ka Nana Akufo-Addo onɛ da an Minister for Foreign Affairs Zugraan president John Kufuor gɔmina ni ka an Wabʋg Paati la nid la da di gɔmina zugraan ka lieb Ghana President.
english: Former foreign minister Nana Akufo-Addo of the opposition New Patriotic Party was elected President on his third attempt, defeating incumbent President John Mahama of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Nana Konadu Agyeman Rawlings, onɛ da an National Democratic Party mɛ da paas banɛ ka ba da pʋ tisi ba suor la.
english: The disqualified candidates included former first lady Nana Konadu Agyeman Rawlings, the president of the National Democratic Party.

kusaal: Amaa Progressive People's Party (PPP) na'anya'ad onɛ an Paa Kwesi Nduom la da zaŋ EC la dʋ kooto bam pʋ tis o suor la zug.
english: However, the presidential candidate of the Progressive People's Party (PPP) Paa Kwesi Nduom took the EC to court over his disqualification.

kusaal: Gɔmma zugdaan John Mahama da mɔr suor ka zi'enɛ paasi o nɔɔra ayi' bɔzugɔ o di'el na'am la ka li kpɛm nwadis ayuobʋ ma'aa nɛ ban na vɔt yi o zuraag John Atta Mills ni.
english: Incumbent John Mahama was eligible for a second full term since he had ascended to the presidency with only six months remaining in the term of his predecessor and running mate, John Atta Mills.

kusaal: NDC nɛ NPP wʋsa mɔr 275 na'anya'adib, ka CPP (222 na'anya'dib) nɛ PPP (163) ka paati nam ayi daa an paati banɛ ma'aa paam na'am la pʋʋsʋg -pʋʋsʋg .Ka PNC mɔr 64 na'anya'adib, ka NDP mɔr 33 na'anya'adib, ka APC mɔr 20 na'anya'adib, ka GCPP mɔr 10 na'anya'adib, ka UFP mɔr six na'anya'adib , ka DPP nɛ UPP wʋsa mɔr na'anya'ad yinne- yinne ma'aa.
english: The PNC nominated 64 candidates, the NDP 33, the APC 20, the GCPP 10, the UFP six and the DPP and UPP both had only one candidate.

kusaal: O da nya'a na'am lanɛ nɔɔra atan' yʋ'ʋn di ka bas gɔmina zugdaan John Mahama onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Paati (National Democratic Party) la nid.
english: Former foreign minister Nana Akufo-Addo of the opposition New Patriotic Party was elected President on his third attempt, defeating incumbent President John Mahama of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Lin da yi miti pisnu nɛ yinne gaad kɛrifa ayɔpɔi zaamnɔɔr la, ka Mahama da buol Akufo-Addo pʋ'ʋs o nɛ o zusʋŋ.
english: At 20:45, the Electoral Commission declared that Akufo-Addo had defeated Mahama in a single round.

kusaal: Suokanɛ ka ba dɔlisidi vɔɔtid Gɔmma Zugraan Ghana nwa anɛ linɛ ka ba buon ye two-round system, ka din pa'al ye asɛɛ ka onɛ di la paam banɛ vɔɔt la kal pʋsʋg nɛ bi'ela bɛɛ 50% amaa wadmaanib banɛ an 275 ka zi'e tis constituency yinne-yinne la, ba yinne vɔt kal ya'a gaad bama la bi'ela, on sɔbi di kuk la.
english: The president is elected using the two-round system, whilst the 275 members of Parliament are elected in single-member constituencies using first-past-the-post voting.

kusaal: Amaa Vɔɔtʋg ofis dim bɛɛ Electoral Commission (EC) da ki'is ya ye ban yɛt si'em la ka' sida.
english: The Electoral Commission denied all accusations.

kusaal: Ivor Greenstreet onɛ da an Convention People's Party na'anya'ad la da an yiiga sɔbi nya'a teŋgbauŋ Zugraan ka an pɔn'ɔr.
english: Ivor Greenstreet from the Convention People's Party was the first physically challenged candidate to contest a presidential election.

kusaal: Ghana, nwa ni gɔmma zugdaan nya'adɔl ya'a di'e na'am la , ka gaŋ saŋkanɛ ka ba mɔr na'am la pʋʋsʋg kpɛlim , ba na basi o ka mɔr na'am la saŋa yinne ma'aa.
english: In Ghana, when a vice-president ascends to the presidency with more than half of a presidential term remaining, he is only allowed to run for a single full term in his own right.

kusaal: ka 74 an asu'oe -m-mɛŋ na'anya'adib.
english: The other 74 candidates were independents.

kusaal: Gɔmma zugdaan Ghana nwa, na di ka bɛ na'am la ni nɔɔra ayi,ka 275 wadmaanib wʋsa mɛ na an yinne ayinne bɛ wadaanib yir ka an linɛ ka nidib la vɔɔt gaŋ nid yinne ma'aa.
english: The President of Ghana is elected using the two-round system, whilst the 275 members of Parliament are elected in single-member constituencies using first-past-the-post voting.

kusaal: Akwasi Addae Odike n zi'enɛ tis United Progressive Party, Nana Agyenim Boateng n zi'enɛ tis United Front Party and Kwasi Busumbru n zi'enɛ tis People's Action Party daa mɛ pʋ sʋm ye o zi'eli.
english: Akwasi Addae Odike of the United Progressive Party, Nana Agyenim Boateng of the United Front Party and Kwasi Busumbru of the People's Action Party were also not eligible.

kusaal: Nwadis piinɛ ayi la li daba anii daar, vɔtʋg la dabisir la gat la , ka labaya yina ye malifɔ sa nwɛ'ɛn ka ba gban'a Nii Lante Vanderpuye onɛ an wadmaan tis Odododiodio constituency.
english: On 8 December, a day after the elections there were reports of gunshots leading to the arrest of Nii Lante Vanderpuye the incumbent Member of Parliament (MP) for the Odododiodio constituency.

kusaal: Vɔtʋg lʋgir daa mɔl ye,dɔlisig banɛ na pʋʋdig Guan District bɛ Oti Region n yi Guan District Local Government (Guan District Assembly) (Establishment) Instrument, 2020, ka nidib banɛ bɛ zin'ikaŋa ma'aa nɛ nyaŋ vɔt gɔmma zʋgdaan nam vɔtʋg.
english: The Electoral Commission announced that following the creation of the Guan District in the Oti Region through the Guan District Local Government (Guan District Assembly) (Establishment) Instrument, 2020, people in this area will only be able to take part in the presidential election.

kusaal: Ben Ephson onɛ tʋm Daily Dispatch newspaper daa ti bu'os nididb pʋtɛn'ɛra zaŋi keŋ vɔtʋg ni, n bɛ Greater Accra, Central nɛ Western region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Ben Ephson of the Daily Dispatch newspaper conducted polls in the Greater Accra, Central and Western regions.

kusaal: O daa bugʋ ye ,Akufo-Addo onɛ zi'enɛ tis NPP na di vɔtʋg la nɛ 52.6% vɔɔts ka Mahama na paam 45.7%.
english: He predicted that Akufo-Addo of the NPP will win the election with 52.6% of the votes while Mahama will obtain 45.7%.

kusaal: Political Science Department bɛ University of Ghana daa mɛ bu'os nidib pʋtɛn'ɛra ka paam 11,949 nidib ka banɛ lɛs ba pʋtɛn'ɛra , ka mɛ bugʋ ye rest Akufo-Addo onɛ zi'enɛ tis(NPP) na di vɔtʋg la nɛ 51.7% vɔɔts ka Mahama mɛ paam 40.4%.
english: The Political Science Department of the University of Ghana polled 11,949 respondents and predicted that Akufo-Addo (NPP) will win 51.7% of the vote while Mahama wins 40.4%.

kusaal: Asu'oe-m-mɛŋ ka ti buon ye ,An iPoll daa mɛ vɛɛns ka paam 670 nidib banɛ lɛs ba pʋtɛn'ɛra ka mɛ bugʋ 48.7% vɔɔts tis Mahama nɛ 46.7% tis Akufo-Addo ka li bigis ye asɛ ka ba maligim vɔt ya'as bʋzugɔ ba yinne pʋ paam im 50% vɔɔts.
english: An iPoll survey of 670 respondents predicted 48.7% of the votes for Mahama and 46.7% for Akufo-Addo implying that the election may go a second round as the winner has to have over 50% of the votes.

kusaal: ka Governance Research Bureau mɛ bʋgʋ ye, Akufo-Addo na paam 49.19%vɔɔtska Mahama mɛ paam 48.27% ka li bigis ye ba na maligim vɔt ya'as.
english: The Governance Research Bureau predicted that Akufo-Addo will obtain 49.19% of the votes and Mahama 48.27% also implying a second round of elections may be needed.

kusaal: ka asu'oe-m-mɛŋ dim lugir ka ti buon ye, A research group Research and Grant Institute of Ghana nɛ, lʋgir buon ye, Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO) yɛl ye vɔtʋg tʋʋma dim la ye, ba yina maal yɛlkanɛ bɛ la.
english: A research group Research and Grant Institute of Ghana raised concerns about this and the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO) urged the commission to come out and clarify the errors properly instead of just issuing press releases.

kusaal: On an Ghana gɔmma zugdaa nannnana la, Nana Akufo-Addo n an wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid la, ba daa lɛm vɔt gaan ya'as ka li an o yiiga , ka o paam vɔɔts bɛdigʋ.
english: Incumbent President Nana Akufo-Addo of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) was re-elected in the first round after securing a majority of the votes.

kusaal: Ka gɔmma zugdaan kʋdʋg John Dramani Mahama daa yina ye o pʋ siak tis vɔtʋg la yi si'em na la.
english: Former President John Dramani Mahama announced that he would contest the results.

kusaal: ka daa mɔr tua'am la keŋ Ghana kɔɔtʋ ti'ta'ar la ni, bɛ nwadis piinɛ ayi la , li dab pitan' daar, ka ba wʋsa daa siak ka bas tua'am la bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piisi nɛ yinne la, li nwadis atan' la ni, li daba anaasi.Wabʋg na'adɔɔg wadaanib daa kae bɛdigʋ lɛb wadmaanib yir la na,ka wadmaanib kal zim nɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg wadamaanib, ka ba zu'oe wadmaanib yir la,nɛ asu'oe-m-mɛŋ wadmaan yinne (Andrew Asiamah Amoako) onɛ na nyaŋi di'es na'am.
english: The NPP lost its majority in the parliament, winning the same number of seats as the opposition NDC, resulting in a hung parliament with a single independent (Andrew Asiamah Amoako) in the position of kingmaker, who later chose to support the NPP.

kusaal: nwadig yinne la ni, onɛ an gɔmma zugdaan la, Nana Akufo-Addo daa yɛl ye, on na lɛm zi'el wabʋg na'adɔɔg la n nya'ad gɔmma zugdaan na'am la ya'as.
english: In December, incumbent president Nana Akufo-Addo announced that he intended to run for re-election as the New Patriotic Party (NPP) candidate.

kusaal: Ba nidib yinne onɛ daa nɔki o gbana bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la, li nwadis piiga la, li daba anu daar, an gɔmma zudaan Nana Akufo-Addo.Na'anya'adib la wʋsa sʋm ka ba yɔ GH¢100,000 tis vɔtʋg lʋgir.Akwasi Addai Odike onɛ zi'el tis United Progressive Party daa zɛ'ɛrig wabʋg paati nɛ vɔtʋg lʋgir, ye ba nanɔɔr gu' ka o kʋ nyaŋ nɔki gbana la.wabʋg paati kʋk daan Peter Mac Manudaa ti yina kis ka ma'asim tiig paati daa ti yina bu'os ye bɔ ka vɔtʋg lʋgir la na pʋ naar vɔtʋg gbana la ka na'anya'adib nɔki gbana bɛ.
english: Akwasi Addai Odike of the United Progressive Party claimed that there was a conspiracy by the NPP and the Electoral Commission to prevent him from filing his nomination papers.

kusaal: Ka li anɛ na'asaa sɔ'ʋg la ni ka ba nɔk taasi zin'in kanɛ ti buon ye,Criminal Investigation Department la n bɛ Ghana Police Service.
english: These include IT issues with their forms and some had been forwarded to the Criminal Investigation Department of the Ghana Police Service.

kusaal: Banɛ pʋ sʋm ye ba zi'el la anɛ Kofi Koranteng nɛ Marricke Kofi Gane ba wʋsa zi'el tis asu'oe-m-mɛŋ .
english: Those disqualified include Kofi Koranteng and Marricke Kofi Gane who are both Independent.

kusaal: Ghana gɔmma zugdaan , Nana Akufo-Addo bɛ yiiga ka gɔmma zugdaan kʋdʋg John Mahama dɔl.Ba yʋ'ʋra nɛ si'em la digin nwa.
english: The incumbent president, Nana Akufo-Addo will be the first on the list followed by John Mahama, a former president.

kusaal: Banɛ dɔlis si'em nwa,banɛ ka ba ye ba pʋ ka ba zi'el la yinne, Nana Agyenim Boateng, onɛ an UFP toun gat,daa ti mɔr antu'a keŋ kɔɔtʋ ni ye ba gu'ur ka vɔtʋg la da kena ,Amaa ka Accra kɔɔtʋ tita'ar la pʋ nyɛ si'eli na nyaŋ gu'ur vɔtʋg la.
english: Following this, one of the disqualified candidates, Nana Agyenim Boateng, leader of the UFP, took to court to seek redress and prevent the elections from going ahead but the Accra High Court found no grounds to grant this relief.

kusaal: Ghana Police yɛl ye nidiba anu kpi' ka piinɛ awai paam sampʋat bɛ vɔtʋg la daar nɛ linɛ gat.
english: The Ghana Police reported 5 deaths and 19 injuries during and after the election.

kusaal: bɔzugɔ Guan constituency pʋ paaae ye pʋʋgin li.
english: This is because the Guan constituency had not yet been formally created.

kusaal: Nidib banɛ wʋsa daa sɔbi ba yʋ'ʋra vɔtʋg tʋʋma lugir la, anɛ 17,027,655.
english: The total number of registered voters was 17,027,655.

kusaal: Nwadis piiga la ni, li daba awai daar, ba daa yina yɛl ye, Ghana zugdaan Nana Akufo-Addo di vɔtʋg , onɛ daa paam vɔɔts bɛdigʋ kanɛ na gu'ur ka kʋ lɛm vɔt ya'asɛ.
english: On 9 December, incumbent Ghana President Nana Akufo-Addo was declared the winner after securing a majority of the votes needed to avoid a runoff.

kusaal: Ban daa yine yɛl onɛ di la, Techiman South daa pʋ paasi .
english: The declared results exclude the figures for the Techiman South as the results there are being contested.

kusaal: Ka vɔtʋg lʋgir kpɛɛm la daa yɛl ye, constituency kana vɔɔts kʋ nyaŋ tiak vɔtʋg la pʋn an si'em la.
english: The Electoral Commissioner states that the results of this constituency alone will not change the outcome of the election.

kusaal: Li daa yʋ'unɛ hali ka ba na yina yɛl banɛ di wadmaanib na'anya'ad vɔtʋ la.nwadis piinɛ ayi la, li dabisim piinɛ anaasi daar ka vɔtʋg tʋʋma dim na yina yɛl ye , ban muki ba mɛŋ hali ye ba naar Sene West constituency vɔtʋg la.
english: On 14 December, a week after voting was completed, the Electoral Commission announced that it was working on finalising the results for Sene West constituency.

kusaal: Abantu for Development anɛ an asʋ'ʋm-mɛŋ pʋ'ab la'asʋg dim (non-governmental organisation).
english: ABANTU for Development is an international women's non-governmental organisation.

kusaal: Li la'asʋg dɔɔdi lɛm bɛ tensieba anɛ Kenya, Tanzania, Ghana nɛ Nigeria.
english: Its other offices are in Kenya, Tanzania, Ghana, and Nigeria.

kusaal: Zina nwa' li la'asʋg dɔtitada bɛnɛ tɛɛns bama London, United Kingdom, Nairobi, Kenya nɛ Tanzania.
english: Its present-day main offices are in London, United Kingdom; Nairobi, Kenya; and Tanzania.

kusaal: Li mɛ paas Gender Action on Climate Change for Equality and Sustainability dim pʋʋgin.
english: It is also part of Gender Action on Climate Change for Equality and Sustainability.

kusaal: Abantu mɛ tʋmmi li tʋʋma nɛ United Nations Economic Commission for Africa nɛ Organisation of African Unity dim.
english: ABANTU has also collaborated with the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the Organisation of African Unity.

kusaal: Abantu mɔr pa'annib ka ba gaad kɔbisnu (500) pa'an la'asʋg kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb Africa nɛ United Kingdom.
english: ABANTU has more than 500 trainers from its workshops in Africa and the United Kingdom.

kusaal: Pa'annib bama maan vɛɛnsʋg dap nɛ pʋ'ab nɛ yɛla maalʋg ba tɛɛnsin nwɛnɛ gender stereotypes, social change, climate change nɛ HIV tʋntʋnnib.
english: These trainers conduct gender and policy analysis and host workshops in their countries on themes such as gender stereotypes, social change, climate change and support of HIV-infected workers.

kusaal: Abantu's Gender and Poverty Hearings bɛdegʋ Eastern nɛ Southern Africa sʋŋya ka gɔmena gban'a nie nyain.
english: ABANTU's series of Gender and Poverty Hearings in Eastern and Southern Africa have contributed to transparency of government policies.

kusaal: Abantu paae tɛɛns bɛdigʋ ka ba mi'i di yɛla, ka li yinɛ ban mɔr la'asʋg dɔɔg London la, anina ka pʋ'abanɛ da yit ninsabilis tɛn'ɛsin (Africa) da pin'il la'asʋg nwa' yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991) la ni.
english: ABANTU attracts international attention through its offices in London, where it was founded in 1991 by African women.

kusaal: Abantu mɔr suoya nwɛ'ɛb nɛ United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).
english: ABANTU has a special consultative status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).

kusaal: Ti ya-tuona ninsabilis sʋ'ʋlim (West Africa) la'asʋg dɔtita'ar bɛnɛ Accra, Ghana ka li kpɛɛm an Rose Mensah-Kutin ka li la'asʋg dɔbil mɛ bɛ Nigeria.
english: The regional office for West Africa is located in Accra, Ghana (Regional Programme Manager Rose Mensah-Kutin); and there is a branch office in Nigeria.

kusaal: Abantu mɔr suora nwɛ'ɛb nɛ United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).
english: ABANTU has a special consultative status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).

kusaal: Lin nwɛ'ɛd sʋora nɛ United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) la nɛ ba la'asʋg dɔɔgi bɛ London tɛŋin la kɛ ka li paam sʋŋir bɛdego.
english: ABANTU has a special consultative status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).

kusaal: Ninsabilis tɛɛnsin (Africa), li nyɛ yu'ur hali nɛ ya-tuona ninsabilis sʋ'ʋlim (West Africa).
english: In Africa, it is particularly known in the West African region.

kusaal: Li bɔɔdim anɛ di tis pʋ'ab paŋ ka ba paas na'am nya'ab pʋʋgin nɛ da' diib pʋʋgin wʋsa, ka yis linɛ wʋsa gu'ud pʋ'ab kati wa'ae ba na'am nya'ab pʋʋgin, wada pʋʋgin, malima banɛ gu'udi ka ba paami ba nyadi wada pʋʋgin nɛ ba da' diib pʋʋgin.
english: It seeks to increase women's participation in both politics and the economy, and erase political, legal and cultural barriers to women's equal standing before the law and their economic independence.

kusaal: La'askaŋa nwa nye yɛlkpana anaasi ka li nar ye ba gɔsi li yɛla: pʋ'ab nɛ dap nɛ nɔŋ pʋʋgin bɛllim yɛla, pʋ'ab nɛ dab nɛ zaba pʋʋgin yɛla, pʋ'ab nɛ dab nɛ teŋ sʋ'ʋgʋr yɛla nɛ pʋ'ab nɛ dab labaya tisib pʋʋgin nɛ pian'ad pʋʋgin sʋŋir la'ad yɛla.
english: The organisation has identified four areas of key interest: gender and poverty, gender and conflict, gender and governance, and gender and information and communication technologies.

kusaal: Abdul Salam Mumini anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ maan sini.
english: Abdul Salam Mumini is a Ghanaian film maker.

kusaal: Sini kanɛ ka o maal yiiga anɛ God Loves Prostitutes, anina ka Nollywood sini maan, Genevieve Nnaji da paas.
english: His first film was God Loves Prostitutes, which starred Nollywood star Genevieve Nnaji.

kusaal: Salam's Venus Film Production nyaŋi yis nimbama nwa' baŋir paalʋ: Van Vicker, Jackie Aygemang, Nadia Buari ka bɛdigʋ nan kpɛlim.
english: Salam's Venus Film Production is responsible for the discovery of the likes of Van Vicker, Jackie Aygemang, Nadia Buari and a host of emerging others.

kusaal: Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Mion sυ'υlυm wadmaan.
english: Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah (born 1 January 1986) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of parliament for the Mion constituency in the Northern Region.

kusaal: O yinɛ Sang linɛ bɛ Gaana Northern tuuru sυ'υlυm la.
english: He was born on January 1, 1986, and hails from Sang in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ka yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni, ka o tɔlisi maal o Post graduate kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Public Administration la ka yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ piiga la ni ka o lɛn tɔlisi maal Digiree linɛ an Economics la.
english: In 2017, he had his Post graduate certificate in Public Administration and in 2010, he further had Degree in Economics.

kusaal: O da maali atʋm-pɛsig yυυm yinne tis Gɔmina bɛ National Health Insurance Authority ni ka lin nya'aŋ ka kena tυm n an dministrator tis Local Government Service dim tυυma la.
english: He was a national service personnel at the National Health Insurance Authority and later the administrator for the Local Government Service.

kusaal: Onɛ an kpɛɛm linɛ an General Manager bɛ Alhaj Musah Enterprise tυυma la ni.
english: He is the General Manager for Alhaj Musah Enterprise.

kusaal: Ban da vot ka o paam vot si'em anɛ 21,552 ka Mohammed Abdul Aziz onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig nid la mɛ da paam vot 14,158.
english: He won the seat with 21,552 votes whilst Mohammed Abdul Aziz of the NDC had 14,158 votes.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ piisi nɛ yinne la ni, ka ba da bas nɔɔr n tis Abdul-Aziz, Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin, Johnson Kwaku Adu, Laadi Ayii Ayamba nɛ Emmanuel Kwasi Bedzrah ye ba si'iŋ tυυma la'asυg linɛ da maal Extraordinary Session yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ piisi nɛ yinne la ni n bɛ wadmaanib yin la nɛ ECOWAS dim la'as kanɛ da naam Freetown linɛ bɛ Sierra Leone sυ'υlυm la.
english: In 2021, Abdul-Aziz together with Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin, Johnson Kwaku Adu, Laadi Ayii Ayamba and Emmanuel Kwasi Bedzrah were sworn in during the Extraordinary Session 2021 of the Parliament of the ECOWAS which happened in Freetown in Sierra Leone.

kusaal: O paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Special Budget la ni ka mɛ paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid tυυma nɔ'ɔsυg yɛla la ni, nɛ banɛ gɔsid Social Welfare and State Enterprises la ni.
english: In Parliament, he has served on various committees including the Special Budget and Employment, Social Welfare and State Enterprises Committees.

kusaal: Onɛ an yiiga wadmaan kanɛ an Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid ka di Mion sυ'υlυm wadmaanib kυk la.
english: Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah (born 1 January 1986) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of parliament for the Mion constituency in the Northern Region.

kusaal: O da naae o gbaυŋ zamisυg linɛ an SSSCE yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni.
english: He had his SSSCE in 2005.

kusaal: Abdul Aziz anɛ mɔr.
english: Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah is a Muslim.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ piisi la ni, o da tɔd na'anam mɔtɔnam Jagrido linɛ bɛ ti Gaana Northern tuuru sυ'υlυm la ni.
english: In 2020, he donated a motorcycle to the Chief of Jagrido in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Wa Central constituency bɛ Upper West Region, Ghana la.
english: He is the current Member of Parliament for Wa Central constituency in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o Middle School Leaving Certificate nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (1976).
english: He had his Middle School Leaving Certificate in 1976.

kusaal: O da maali o O level Education nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan la ni (1983) ka maali o A level Education yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1986).
english: He had his O level education in 1983 and his A level education in 1986.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr Diploma in Economics yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi la ni (1994) ka tɔlisi maali o Degree Psychology niyʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi la ni (1994).
english: He earned a diploma in Economics in 1994 and a degree in Psychology in 1994.

kusaal: O da lɛn maali o master's degree nɛ International Affairs ni yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii la ni (1998).
english: He also has a master's degree in International Affairs in 1998.

kusaal: O mɔr PhD in Development Policy dinɛ ka o paam yi University of Ghana, African Studies yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan' la ni (2013).
english: He earned a PhD in Development Policy from the University of Ghana, African Studies in 2013.

kusaal: O da anɛ consultant tis Institute of Policy Alternatives.
english: Pelpuo was a consultant for the Institute of Policy Alternatives.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Deputy Coordinator for Finance tis National Youth Council ka din nya'aŋ ka o lieb Director tis lʋg kan la.
english: For the National Youth Council, he was Deputy Coordinator of Finance, then its director, and then its Agricultural Ag.

kusaal: Abdul-Rashid da lieb Majority Leader nya'adɔl ka Akua Dansua di'e o zin'igi lieb Minister for Youth and Sports.
english: He was replaced by Ghana's first female Minister for Sports, Akua Dansua, and appointed deputy Majority Leader in Parliament instead.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt o ka o paas Ghana nidib anu banɛ da paas Ninsabilis Sʋ'ʋlim Wadmaanib yikanɛ bɛ South Africa la ka o da tʋm nɔɔr ayi' paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan' la ni (2013).
english: He was also nominated as one of Ghana's five Members to the Pan African Parliament in South Africa, where he served for a term until 2013.

kusaal: John Mahama saŋa la (2012 - 2016) o da gaŋ o ye o an Minista of State President ɔfisin gɔsid gɔmena nɛ Asʋ'oe-m-mɛŋ nɔɔr yinne yɛla bɛɛ Private Sector Development and Public Private Partnership (PPP).
english: In the John Mahama administration (2012–2016), Pelpuo was appointed Minister of State at the Office of the President in Charge of Private Sector Development and Public Private Partnership (PPP).

kusaal: O da lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Economic Management Team (EMT) yɛla la ya'as.
english: He was also a member of the Economic Management Team (EMT).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016), o da lɛn dii o kʋk la paas nɔɔr anaasi ye o lɛn keŋ yʋma anaasi ya'as tis Wa Central Constituency dim.
english: In 2016, he won his seat for another four-year term as the Member of Parliament for the Wa Central Constituency.

kusaal: O lɛn anɛ ranking member tis Government Assurance Committee, la'askanɛ gɔsid gɔmena Ministanam ka ba tʋm ban yɛl si'eli zi'el la.
english: He also held the ranking member position on the Government Assurance Committee, an important oversight committee that monitors and holds government ministers to task for promises they make.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt o paas nɔɔr atan' ye o an kʋkdaani tis Population and Development Caucus and Ranking Member of the Lands Committee.
english: He was appointed to serve another term as Chairman of the Population and Development Caucus and Ranking Member of the Lands Committee.

kusaal: O da lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid bugum nɛ kpikpiŋ yɛla bɛɛ Energy and Business Committee.
english: He is also a member of the Energy and Business Committees.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi (21,272) yi vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ yinne (41,501).
english: He was elected with 21,272 votes out of a total 41,501 valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas Mornah Anbataayela Bernard onɛ an People's National Convention nid la, Mohammed Adama Kpegla onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid, Abu Mumuni onɛ an Convention People's Party nid, Osman Mohammed onɛ an Democratic People's Party nid nɛ Osman Imam Sidik onɛ pʋ mɔr Na'adɔɔgɔ, independent candidate.
english: He was elected over Mornah Anbataayela Bernard of the People's National Convention, Mohammed Adama Kpegla of the New Patriotic Party, Abu Mumuni of the Convention People's Party, Osman Mohammed of the Democratic People's Party, and Osman Imam Sidik, an independent candidate.

kusaal: O yinɛ Wa teŋ kanɛ bɛ Upper West Region, Ghana.
english: He is the current Member of Parliament for Wa Central constituency in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Agricultural Ag.
english: For the National Youth Council, he was Deputy Coordinator of Finance, then its director, and then its Agricultural Ag.

kusaal: O da kpɛn' Ghana Wadmaanib yin lanɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anu (2005) la ni.
english: Pelpuo entered the Parliament of Ghana in 2005 after winning the Wa Central seat on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress in the December 2004 election.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg zugʋ nya' Ghana Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ anaasi li Nwadis piinɛ ayi' (Samanpiid Nwadig, 2004) la ni.
english: Pelpuo entered the Parliament of Ghana in 2005 after winning the Wa Central seat on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress in the December 2004 election.

kusaal: Pelpuo da anɛ Minister of State Zugraan ɔfisin.
english: Pelpuo was a Minister of State at the office of the President until September 2009 when President John Atta Mills moved him to the Ministry of Youth and Sports following the resignation of Muntaka Mohammed Mubarak.

kusaal: Zugraan John Atta Mills da gaŋ o ye an minista onɛ gɔsid dasam nɛ pʋ'asada nɛ ninwisigir yɛla yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai la, li Nwadisa awai la ni (September 2009).
english: Pelpuo was a Minister of State at the office of the President until September 2009 when President John Atta Mills moved him to the Ministry of Youth and Sports following the resignation of Muntaka Mohammed Mubarak.

kusaal: Akua da an pu'akanɛ lieb tʋʋma lʋg kaŋa minista yiiga Ghana nwa.
english: He was replaced by Ghana's first female Minister for Sports, Akua Dansua, and appointed deputy Majority Leader in Parliament instead.

kusaal: Girimadaan Pelpuo da lɛn nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Wadmaanib nɛ Pirɛsidɛn nam vɔɔtʋg la ka di paas nɔɔr anu ye o lɛn keŋ yʋma anaasi an Wadmaani tis Wa Central.
english: Pelpuo was elected as the member of parliament of the Wa Central constituency in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt Pelpuo ye an Wadmaani tis Wa Central constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Pelpuo was elected as the member of parliament of the Wa Central constituency in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O da zi'eni tisi o sʋ'ʋlim la Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anaasi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni (4th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana).
english: He thus represented the constituency in the 4th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'al atan' kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.3%).
english: This was equivalent to 51.3% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Mornah da paamnɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayi' nɛ kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnii (12,280) ka Mohammed paam vɔɔt tusa ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (7,249) ka Abu paam kɔbistan' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (376) ka Osman paam kɔbiga nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' (172) ka Osman Imam paam kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi (152).
english: These obtained 12,280 votes, 7,249 votes, 376 votes, 172 votes and 152 votes respectively out of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋgin, ba da paamnɛ pisi nɛ awai du'ali ayuobʋ (29.6%), piinɛ ayɔpɔi du'ali anu (17.5%), nɛɛm du'ali awai (0.9%), nɛɛm du'ali anaasi (0.4%) nɛ nɛɛm du'ali anaas (0.4%).
english: These were equivalent to 29.6%, 17.5%, 0.9%, 0.4% and 0.4% respectively of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress zugʋ nya'.
english: Pelpuo was elected on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da anɛ tuon gat la'askanɛ gɔsid tam nɛ tiis yɛla bɛɛ Lands and Forestry Committee la ni.
english: He was appointed to serve another term as Chairman of the Population and Development Caucus and Ranking Member of the Lands Committee.

kusaal: O da lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid sanlima tuub nɛ bugum bɛɛ Mines and Energy Committee la.
english: He is also a member of the Energy and Business Committees.

kusaal: O lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid kpikpiŋ bɛɛ Business Committee yɛla la.
english: He is also a member of the Energy and Business Committees.

kusaal: O da tʋmnɛ ala nɛ president n ti lɛn ti'asi ba yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la ni, 2010.
english: He served in this capacity until a cabinet reshuffle in January 2010.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Abdul-Rauf Ibrahim nɛ nwadis piiga dabisim piiga, 1968 la ni.
english: Abdul-Rauf Ibrahim was born on 10 October 1968.

kusaal: O yinɛ Yagaba linɛ bɛ Ghana North East Region sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: He comes from Yagaba in the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋ nɛ Navrongo Secondary Sakʋr la naae ka di'e GCE 'A' Kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋma 1989 la ni.
english: He attended Navrongo Secondary School where he acquired his GCE 'A' Level Certificate in the year 1989.

kusaal: Li anɛ Abdul-Rauf Ibrahim n da an Tass Klia Enterprise Limited tʋʋma zugdaan lin da yi 1983 ti paae 2016.
english: Abdul-Rauf Ibrahim was the managing director of Tass Kalia Enterprise Limited from 1983 to 2016.

kusaal: O mɛ da anɛ Hajj kʋkdaan n bɛ gɔmina la tʋʋma dɔɔgin lin da yi 2013 ti paae 2016.
english: He was also the Hajj Chairman at the Office of the President from the year 2013 to 2016.

kusaal: O da lɛn paamɛ o kʋk la ya'as n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anu la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la yʋʋm 2008 la ni.
english: He retained his seat and became a member of the Fifth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana in the year 2008.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2012 la ni ka ba da maal Ghana vɔɔt la ka o lu ka Ussif Mustapha onɛ da nya'ad nɛ o la zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg bɛɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) la nɔba zugu di ka bas o.
english: In the year 2012, he lost his seat as a member of parliament in the 2012 Ghanaian general election to Ussif Mustapha of the opposition Party, New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ka mɛ an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anaasi , anu, nɛ ayɔpɔi Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni onɛ zi'en Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la zugu zi'enɛ tis Yagaba-Kubori bɛ North East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ghana la.
english: Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim is a Ghanaian politician, a Development Planner/Architect, Quantity Surveyor and member of the Fourth, Fifth and Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Yagaba-Kubori Constituency in the North Eastt Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Abdul-Rauf Ibrahim anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg bɛɛ National Democratic Congress (NDC) la nid.
english: Abdul-Rauf Ibrahim is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ban da maal Ghana vɔt yʋʋm 2004 la, o da zi'enɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zugu di n tis Yagaba-Kubori sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: He contested and won in the 2004 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress for the Yagaba-Kubori constituency which was a new constituency with 6,460 votes out of the 12,080 valid votes cast thus 53.5%.

kusaal: O da lɛn zi'enɛ nya'a yʋʋm 2016 vɔɔt linɛ ka Ghana dim da maal la ka di.
english: He again stood for the seat again in the 2016 Ghanaian general election and won.

kusaal: Nɛ' da sʋŋ ka o mɛ paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: As a result, he became a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg bɛɛ National Democratic Congress (NDC) nɔba zug.
english: As a result, he became a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Abdul-Rauf Ibrahim mɔr pu'a nɛ biis ayuobʋ.
english: Abdul-Rauf Ibrahim is married with six children.

kusaal: Abdul-Razak Tahidu anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka wadmaan n tis Chereponi linɛ bɛ Ghana North East region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Abdul-Razak Tahidu is a Ghanaian politician and member of parliament for the Chereponi constituency in the North East region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da pin'ili o sakur zamisυg nɛ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ ayi' ka maal o SSSCE yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ anu la ni.
english: He had his basic education in 1992 and had his SSSCE in 1995.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Budget and Examinations Officer n tis ti Ggana gbaυŋ zamisυg lυgυr dim la ka lin nya'aŋ ka o kena an District Chief Executive n bɛ Ministry of Local Government n tis Chereponi sυ'υlυm la.
english: He was the Budget and Examinations Officer at Ghana Education Service and later the District Chief Executive at the Ministry of Local Government for the Chereponi district.

kusaal: Nannanna o paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Petroleum Commission la ni.
english: Currently, he is a board member for the Petroleum Commission.

kusaal: O paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Subsidiary Legislation la ni ka mɛ paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Trade, Industry nɛTourism la ni.
english: He is a member of the Subsidiary Legislation Committee and also a member of the Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee.

kusaal: Ba da du'anɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la li dabisim piisi nɛ anii yυυm tusri nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni, o yinɛ Chereponi linɛ bɛ Ghana North East region sυ'υlυm la.
english: He was born on 28 January 1977 and hails from Chereponi in the North East region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maal linɛ an pa'alυg kasɛta gbaυŋ yυυma tusa yi' la ni ka tɔlisi maal o Digirɛɛ linɛ an Basic Education yυυma tusa yi' nɛ ayɔpɔi ka lɛn tɔlis maal mastɛs digirɛɛ linɛ an Leadership & Development yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piian tan'.
english: He also had his Teacher certificate in 2000 and his Degree in Basic Education in 2007 and further had his master's degree in Leadership & Development in 2013.

kusaal: Abdul-Razak anɛ Mɔr.
english: Abdul-Razak is a Muslim.

kusaal: O keŋnɛ Ghana Senior High sakur linɛ bɛ Tamale, linɛ ka nidib mi' li ye GHANASCO la.
english: He attended Ghana Senior High School in Tamale, popularly known as GHANASCO.

kusaal: O mɛ da keŋ Tamale Polytechnic sakurin yʋʋma 2000 la zamis gɛligir tʋʋma ka tɔlisi maal o mastɛs digirii linɛ an NGO nɛ Rural Development n bɛ University for Development Studies sakurin la 2010.
english: He studied accounting at Tamale Polytechnic in the year 2000 and proceeded to obtain a master's degree in NGO and Rural Development from the University for Development Studies in the year 2010.

kusaal: Gunu anɛ pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd n zi'e Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug ka mɛ paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la; 4th Republic of Ghana la ni.
english: Gunu was a member of the seventh parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana .

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ nya'a yʋʋm 2016 la ni ka di nɛ vɔt linɛ an 13,334 ka di pa'al ye kubiga pʋʋgin o da paamɛ 34.21% n yi vɔt la wʋsa la ni.
english: In 2016 elections, he became his party's first candidate to win the Savelugu Parliamentary seat with a total of 13,334 votes, representing 34.21% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Savelugu linɛ bɛ Northern Region Sʋ'ʋlʋm la, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid New Patriotic Party (NPP).
english: Abdul-Samed Muhamed Gunu (born 6 April 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Gunu yinɛ Savelugu linɛ bɛ Ghana Northern Region la.
english: He served in the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Savelugu Constituency in the Northern Region.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ tis Savelugu sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Northern Region Gaana la.
english: He served in the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Savelugu Constituency in the Northern Region.

kusaal: Abdulai Abanga (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ 25 May 1970) ka o an Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid.
english: Abdulai Abanga (born 25 May 1970) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Abdulainɛ Akwatia tenkanɛ bɛ Eastern region, Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi Nwadisa anu la dabpisi nɛ anu daar (25 May 1970) o yinɛ Banse bɛ Binduri/Bawku Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Abanga was born in Akwatia a town in the Eastern Region of the Republic of Ghana on 25 May 1970 but he hails from Binduri/Bawku in the Upper East Region of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ Akwatia L/A Primary School ka tɔlisi keŋ Bansi Primary School bɛ Binduri la ka keŋi o High school education Ghana Secondary School (Ghanasco), bɛ Tamale la.
english: He attended Akwatia L/A Primary School and later continued at Bansi Primary School in Binduri and had his High School at Bawku Junior High School, and later had his Senior High School education at the Ghana Secondary School (Ghanasco), in Tamale.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Binduri constituency bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim la dim.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Binduri constituency in the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Abed-nego Bandim dʋ'anɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piayɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadisa ayi la dabpiinɛ ayi (12 February 1977) anɛ p ka paas ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress.
english: Abed-nego Bandim (born 12 February 1977) is a Ghanaian politician, a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Bunkpurugu (Nyankpanduri District) bɛ North East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Honorable Abed- nego Bandim is the member of parliament for the Bunkpurugu (Nyankpanduri District) in the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Abed-Nego yinɛ Nakpanduri bɛ North East Region la.
english: Abed-Nego hails from Nakpanduri in the North East Region.

kusaal: o mɔr Masters of Law, Information Communication and Technology Law.
english: He holds Masters of Law in Information Communication and Technology Law.

kusaal: O da sɔbi o WAEC certificate nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la ni (1995)
english: He obtained his WAEC certificate in 1995.

kusaal: O anɛ Chief Manager tis National Communication Authority (NCA).
english: He is not only a politician, but also Chief Manager at National Communication Authority (NCA).

kusaal: Abed-Nego anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Honorable Abed-Nego Bandim is a Christian.

kusaal: Abedi Ayew Pele, ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi Nwadis piinɛ yinne la daba anu daar (5 November 1964), ka ba mi' o tʋʋma ni ye Abedi Pele, anɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd kʋdʋg onɛ da nwɛ'ɛd bɔɔl pak la tensʋg ka da an kpɛɛm tis Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib la (Ghana national team).
english: Abedi Ayew ( ə-BAY-dee ə-YOO; born 5 November 1964), known professionally as Abedi Pele, is a Ghanaian former professional footballer who played as an attacking midfielder and served as captain of the Ghana national team.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Abedi Ayew nɛ tempʋkanɛ bɛ Kibi ka o nɔbʋg Dome tempʋʋgin bɛ Accra teŋkpɛŋ ya-dagɔbʋg baba.
english: Abedi Ayew was born into a family in the town of Kibi and grew up in the town of Dome at the northern outskirts of the city Accra.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Ghana Senior High School bɛ Tamale la.
english: He attended Ghana Senior High School in Tamale.

kusaal: O yi Ghana nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii na ayi (1982) African Cup la nya'aŋ n keŋ la'as nɛ Al Sadd n bɛ Qatar tis $1,000 Na'asarteŋ ligidi la yɔɔb.
english: He left Ghana after the 1982 African Cup of Nations to join Al Sadd in Qatar for a $1,000 transfer fee.

kusaal: On da nwɛ'ɛ tis Zürich FC nya'aŋ la, o da lɛb Ghana na amaa, Kotoko nɛ Hearts of Oak da zan'as ka pʋ n gʋlisi o yʋ'ʋri ba la'asʋg la ni la, o da la'asnɛ AS Dragons FC de I'Ouémé n bɛ Berlin sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: After a short spell with FC Zürich in which he did not play a single league match, he returned to Ghana but, after both Kotoko and Hearts of Oak failed to sign him, joined AS Dragons FC de l'Ouémé in Benin.

kusaal: O da pin'ili o bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb tʋʋma nɛ Europe teŋin nɛ French zin'ig Chamois Niort, n la'asid nɛ Marsheille ka nya'an tɔlisi keŋ Lille ligid pɛ'ɛŋir ni.
english: He began his career in Europe with French side Chamois Niort, subsequently joining Marseille before transferring to Lille on loan.

kusaal: Abedi anɛ Kwame nɛ Sola Ayew pitʋ (Black Meteor kʋdigi tis Hearts of Oak).
english: Abedi Pele is the brother of Kwame and Sola Ayew (ex-Hearts of Oak and Black Meteors).

kusaal: O mɛ lɛm anɛ André, Jordan, Rahim nɛ Imani saam, ka o pʋ'a an Maha.
english: He is also the father of André, Jordan, Rahim, Imani, and is married to Maha.

kusaal: O biribis, Ibrahim, André nɛ Jordan, anɛ banɛ mɛ kena lieb Teŋgbaʋŋ wusa nwɛ'ɛdibi tis Ghana.
english: His sons, Ibrahim, André and Jordan, have also become internationals for Ghana.

kusaal: André nɛ Rahim da zi'eni tis Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga la ni (2010) FIFA dunia wusa bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb n da naam South Africa teŋin la, ka Jordan nɛ Andre mɛ zi'eni tis Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piina anaasi 2014) FIFA dunia wusa bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛbin la ni Brazil nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piina ayi (2022) FIFA dunia wusa bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb Qatar teŋin la.
english: André and Rahim – represented Ghana in the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa while Jordan and André represented Ghana in the 2014 FIFA World Cup in Brazil and the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.

kusaal: O nwɛ'ɛ tis Europe dim kilabnam bɛdigʋ ka paam yʋ'ʋri yi French Ligue 1, Lille nɛ Marseille, ka da di UEFA Champions League yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan la ni 1993, paas kpɛŋ sieba ni.
english: At the latter, he won the UEFA Champions League in 1993, among other titles.

kusaal: Onɛ da an yiiga di CAF piini yʋʋm tusi kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la ni (1992).
english: He was also the first to win the CAF award in 1992.

kusaal: Onɛ daa an Ninsabilis teŋ nid (African) bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd onɛ mɔ'ɔ hali European bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd la'asʋg la ni.
english: Abedi Pele was one of the first African players to make an impact on European club football.

kusaal: Abedi Pelé bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd giiliŋ la da pin'ili Real Tamale United ni n bɛ Ghana la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi na anii (1978).
english: His nomadic career began with Real Tamale United in Ghana in 1978.

kusaal: Nya'aŋa, o da na lɛb Ghana na nwɛ' tis Real Tamale United tis nwɛ'ɛb saŋa yinne.
english: He would later return to Ghana and play for Real Tamale United for one season.

kusaal: La'asʋg zin'iginɛ, o da anɛ nintenriŋ Marsheille tuon French league la ni, ken league nam anaasi ni gandaaʋgin nɛ European la'asʋg yiib nɔɔra ayi ni.
english: At club level, he was a key figure in Marseille's dominance of the French league, resulting in four league championships and two European Cup finals appearances.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ ka nidib nyɛ o ka o an bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd tita'ari o saŋa.
english: He is considered by several pundits to be one of the greatest African footballers of all time.

kusaal: Abeiku Crentsil anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni an Wadmaani tis Ekumfi Constituency n bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Abeiku Crentsil is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ekumfi Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Abeiku nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan la Nwadisa atan dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 March 1973) o yinɛ Ekumfi Essuehyiam bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Gaana.
english: Abeiku was born on 28 March 1973 and hails from Ekumfi Essuehyiam in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ National Engineering College bɛ Takoradi la, zin'ikanɛ ka o da maal Construction Technician I yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piwai nɛ anu (1995).
english: He attended National Engineering College in Takoradi where he obtained Construction Technician I in 1995.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la, o da kɔ'ɔŋi Ekumfi Constituency parliamentary kʋk la ka Wabug Na'adɔɔg, NPP nid, Francis Kingsley Ato Codjoe di.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, he lost the Ekumfi Constituency parliamentary seat to the NPP parliamentary candidate Francis Kingsley Ato Codjoe.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ yinne, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pistan nɛ ayi (11,632) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (47.6%) ka Francis paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayi, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnaasi (12,240) dinɛ an pisnu du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.1%), PPP nid la, Stephen Quansah da paamnɛ kɔbisnu nɛ anu (505) dinɛ an ayi du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (2.1%) ka CPP nid la, Kweku Essuoun paam vɔɔt pisyɔpɔi (70) dinɛ an nɛɛm du'al atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.3%).
english: He lost with 11,632 votes making 47.6% of the total votes cast whilst Francis had 12,240 votes making 50.1% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Stephen Quansah had 505 votes making 2.1% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Kweku Essuoun had 70 votes making 0.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la, o da di Ekumfi Constituency sʋ'ʋlim Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayuobʋ nɛ pistan nɛ ayɔpɔi (16,037) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ atan du'ali ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (53.6%) ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP nid la, Francis Kingsley Ato Codjoe paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ atan, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (13,468) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (45.0%), GUM nid la, Regina Amoah da paam vɔɔt kɔbistan nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛyinne (371) dinɛ an yinne du'alayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.2%)ka CPP nid la Ibrahim Anderson mɛ paam vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ anii (48) dinɛ an nɛɛm du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.2%).
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he won the Ekumfi Constituency parliamentary seat with 16,037 making 53.6% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Francis Kingsley Ato Codjoe had 13,468 votes making 45.0% of the total votes cast, the GUM parliamentary candidate Regina Amoah had 371 votes making 1.2% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Ibrahim Anderson had 48 votes making 0.2% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ Deputy Ranking member tis Privileges Committee ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid tam nɛ tiis yɛla la (Lands and Forestry Committee).
english: He is the Deputy Ranking member of the Privileges Committee and also a member of the Lands and Forestry Committee.

kusaal: O da anɛ Head of Bio-fuel Solutions bɛ Land Acquisition and Survey din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008).
english: He was the Head of Bio-fuel Solutions at Land Acquisition and Survey from 2007 to 2008.

kusaal: O lɛn anɛ Development Worker/Architect/Quantity Surveyor.
english: He is a Development Worker/Architect/Quantity Surveyor.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig, ka ken Methodist pʋ'ʋsim.
english: He is a Christian (Methodist).

kusaal: O anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress la.
english: He is a member of National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa anaasi.
english: He is married with four children.

kusaal: O da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid gaansʋg lyɛla la.
english: He was a committee member of Selection.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Mensah nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa ayuobʋ dapisi nɛ yinne daar (21 sigir 1977) n bɛ Assin Kushea teŋkanɛ bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Abena Durowaa Mensah was born on 21st June 1977 in Assin Kushea in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr Diploma in Insurance kasɛta gbaʋŋ dinɛ ka o paam yi Ghana Insurance College, ka lɛn mɔr Marketing kasɛta gbaʋŋ Prfessional Certificate in Marketing (CIM - UK ), nɛ Bachelor's Degree in Marketing kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Christian Service University College.
english: She holds a Diploma in Insurance from Ghana Insurance College, a professional Certificate in Marketing (CIM - UK ), and a bachelor's degree in marketing from Christian Service University College.

kusaal: Mensah da anɛ Esich Life Assurance Manager n bɛ Sunyani sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: Abena Durowaa Mensah was the Manager for Esich Life Assurance in Sunyani.

kusaal: O da anɛ Assin North Constituency wadmaan din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) la ken paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021).
english: She was the Member of Parliament for Assin North Constituency from 2017 to 2021.

kusaal: Progressive People Party (PPP) wadmaan na'anyi'adi Isaac Manu da mɔri vɔɔt kal kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (979), ka din mɛ pa'al ye kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da paamnɛ atan' du'ali ayuobʋ (3.6%) yi vɔɔtnam la wʋsa pʋʋgin, ka Convention People Party (CPP) wadmaan na'anyi'ad la, Sanni Mahama da paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ anu (115) ka di pa'al ye kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da paamnɛ nɛɛm du'ali anaasi (0.4%) yi vɔɔtnam la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, she won the Assin North Constituency parliamentary seat with 15,553 votes making 56.8% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Samuel Ambre had 10,751 votes making 39.2% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Isaac Manu had 979 votes making 3.6% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Sanni Mahama had 115 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi 2020 Ghanaian general election la ni la, o da nyi'a Assin North Constituency wadmaan na'am kʋk la ka pʋ dii amaa ka ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la, NDC wadmaan na'anyi'ad James Gyakye Quayson da di.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general election, she lost the Assin North Constituency seat to the NDC parliamentary candidate James Gyakye Quayson.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔtnam kal tusa pii nɛ anaasi nɛ kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ atan' (14,193), ka din pa'al ye kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da mɔri pisnaasi nɛ anaasi du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (44.79%) yi vɔɔtnam la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: She had 14,193 votes making 44.79% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O da anɛ Assin North Constituency.
english: She was the member of parliament for Assin North Constituency.

kusaal: Mensah paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party ni.
english: Abena Durowaa Mensah is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ 2016 Ghanaian general election la ni la, o da dii Assin North Constituency Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ anu nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' (15,553).
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, she won the Assin North Constituency parliamentary seat with 15,553 votes making 56.8% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Samuel Ambre had 10,751 votes making 39.2% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Isaac Manu had 979 votes making 3.6% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Sanni Mahama had 115 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC na'anyi'ad Samuel Ambre mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa piiga nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne (10,751); ka din mɛ pa'al ye kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da paamnɛ pistan' nɛ awai du'ali ayi' (39.2%) yi banɛ vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, she won the Assin North Constituency parliamentary seat with 15,553 votes making 56.8% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Samuel Ambre had 10,751 votes making 39.2% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Isaac Manu had 979 votes making 3.6% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Sanni Mahama had 115 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Mensah mɔr sid nɛ biisa ayi.
english: Abena Durowaa Mensah is married with two children.

kusaal: Abena Osei-Asare anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd, o anɛ tυm ligidi tυυma Chartered Accountant.
english: Abena Osei-Asare (born 16 January 1979) is a Chartered Accountant, Ghanaian politician and currently a Member of Parliament for Atiwa East (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Abena Osei Asare da pin'ili sakur n bɛ Achimota Primary sakur la ni ka yii ni tɔlis Wesley Girls High Sakur la ni linɛ bɛ Cape Coast yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ awai nɛ anu la, ani ka o da zamis General Arts.
english: Abena Osei Asare attended Achimota Primary School and continue her secondary education at Wesley Girls High School-Cape-Coast (1995–97) where she read General Arts with elective subjects as Economics, Geography and Elective Mathematics.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o tɔlisi keŋ University of Ghana naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an B. A Economics Geography, o da lɛn tɔlisi zamis University of Ghana ya'as naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Msc.
english: She holds a B.A. (Hons.) in Economics with Geography from the University of Ghana and an Msc.

kusaal: On da lieb tυυma la nid la ka li dɔlisi ani ka o kena tυm nɛ Institute of Chartered Accountants (ICA) banɛ bɛ Gaana la.
english: Also, her membership extends to the Institute of Chartered Accountants Ghana (ICAG).

kusaal: O mɛ lɛn mɔr kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Ligidi tɔlυŋ yɛla la (Financial Markets Association).
english: She also has a certificate in Dealing from ACI (Financial Markets Association).

kusaal: Abena Osei-Asare da naae o yiiga digirɛɛ la, ka tυm yυυm yinne tis Gɔmina n bɛ Gɔmina tυυma dɔɔgin Gaana, ti Gɔmina kυdυg John Agyekum Kufour win la.
english: Abena Osei-Asare upon completion of her first degree did her national service at the President's Special Initiative on Textiles and Garments under President John Agyekum Kufuor.

kusaal: O da lɛn tυm nɛ Absa Bank dim ka lɛn tυm nɛ Barclays Bank Ghana, o da anɛ wada tυmtυmnib la kpɛɛm lin da yi yυυma tusa yi nɛ ayɔpɔi ti paae yυυma tusa yi nɛ awai la ni.
english: She continued her career at Absa Bank [then Barclays Bank Ghana] and served as a customer team lead in the retail department between 2007-2009.

kusaal: O da lɛn tum nɛ Annual Auditor General's Report dim ka mɛ lɛn paas Prestigious Parliamentary Service Board(PSB) la ni.
english: Again she was also a board member of the Prestigious Parliamentary Service Board(PSB).

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi nɛ piina yɔpɔi ka o da yυma piistan' nɛ anii ka ba gaŋ o yɛ an Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning la kpɛɛm nya'andɔl onɛ da an yiiga daan onɛ ka ba gaŋ ka o an biig bɛɛ o yυυma pɔɔd tυυm kan ni.
english: In 2017, at age 38, Abena was the youngest woman ever to be appointed to the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning as a deputy minister.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn zi'en MInista nam la nɔba zug n bɛ bank nam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb wυυ ADB BANK, SSNIT, NHIA and GIADE.
english: In terms of Corporate Governance, She represented the Ministry of Finance as a Director on the following boards; ADB BANK, SSNIT, NHIA and GIADEC.

kusaal: O el sidi mɔr biis atan', o mɔr ligidi linɛ an sυŋ din linɛ ka o pυd li yυ'υr ye Waterbrook Foundation n sυŋid sakur bibis banɛ mɔr baŋir amaa ka ligidi kae la.
english: She also runs an NGO, The Waterbrook Foundation which supports brilliant but needy students with their Education.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Atiwa East linɛ bɛ Gaana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Abena Osei-Asare (born 16 January 1979) is a Chartered Accountant, Ghanaian politician and currently a Member of Parliament for Atiwa East (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Lin ya'aŋ ka o tυm nɛ Chartered Certified Accountants n bɛ UK yυυma tusa yi nɛ awai la ni, tυυma la nya'aŋ ka ba nɔk o paas ye o an ba nid yinne yυυma tusa yi nɛ piina naasi la ni.
english: She became a member of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) in 2009 and later a fellow in 2014.

kusaal: On da naae ani la ka yυ'υn tυm n an onɛ gɔsid la'adnam nɛ ligidi nam yɛla n bɛ New York University linɛ bɛ Gaana la, lin da yi yυυma tusa yi nɛ anaasi n ti paae yυυma tusa yi nɛ ayɔpɔi.
english: She proceeded to work as the assistant director for Facilities and Finance at the New York University, Accra in Ghana between the period of (2004 and 2007).

kusaal: Abena da zi'en Wabug Na'adɔɔg la zugu nya'a di Atiwa East wadmaanib kυk linɛ bɛ Gaana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la yυυma tusa yi ne piina yi la ni.
english: Abena contested and won the New Patriotic Party parliamentary seat for Atiwa East Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana in 2012.

kusaal: O da anɛ niŋ kpiυŋ hali bɛ wadmaanib yira ni n zi'enɛ tisi Atiwa East sυ'υlυm la.
english: As a Member of Parliament, she actively participated in the business of parliament as a representative of the people of Atiwa East.

kusaal: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo yiiga yυυma anaasi la ni.
english: She was instrumental resolving a lot of the labour union issues under the first four years of H.E. Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: O zi'enɛ ti Gaana minista nam la nɔba zug temis wυυ UN mitin kanɛ da maal SDGs nɛ ILO tυmtυmnib yɛla la.
english: She has also represented the Minister at various international conferences including the UN meetings on SDGs and ILO on labour issues.

kusaal: Abena anɛ Kristo biig, o anɛ Presby karimbiig.
english: Abena is a Christian who fellowships at the Presbyterian church.

kusaal: O paamɛ vɔtnam bam 17,399 n yi vɔt la kanl wυsa linɛ da an 22,486 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 77.81% vɔt.
english: Abena won the election by obtaining 17,399 votes of the 22,486 cast, representing 77.81 percent of total valid votes.

kusaal: On minista banɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla tυυma la nil aa, o da anɛ gɔsid ti ligidi pɛmisυg yɛla ka mɛ gɔsidi ti yυυm pυυgin wυsa ligidi yɛla.
english: As the Deputy Minister in charge of budget, she, acting under the Minister of Finance, supported in the smooth preparation and implementation of the government budget for the last 4 years.

kusaal: Abetifi Constituency bɛnɛ Eastern region sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Ghana la.
english: The Abetifi constituency is in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ an constituency la wadmaan anɛ Bryan Acheampong.
english: The current member of Parliament for the constituency is Bryan Acheampong.

kusaal: O da di'enɛ Peter Wiafe Pepera san'an onɛ da zi'en constituency la nɔba zʋg 5th Republic parliament la ni dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) ni.
english: He succeeded Peter Wiafe Pepera who had represented the constituency in the 5th Republican parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) la ni ka o da paam vɔɔt tusa awai, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi gaad o tiraan la, ka di constituency vɔɔtigin la ka kilim wadmaan.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and won a majority of 9,724 votes more than candidate closest in the race, to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: O anɛ pʋ'akanɛ kuosid diib, sʋ'ʋe diib kuosʋg zin'ig ka lɛn an creative director tis 4Roomed, dinɛ ka ba buon te 4Roomed eKasi Culture bɛɛ eKasi, dinɛ bɛ Khayelitsha tempʋʋgʋn, 30 kilometres (19 mi) yit Cape Town, dinɛ bɛ South Africa la kpikpɛŋ.
english: She is the chef, owner and creative director of 4Roomed, also called 4Roomed eKasi Culture or just eKasi, in Khayelitsha township, 30 kilometres (19 mi) outside Cape Town, South Africa. In 2019 4Roomed was named in a combined project by Food & Wine and Travel + Leisure magazines as one of the 30 best restaurants in the world.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Mbalo-Mokoena bɛnɛ Gugulethu ka o nɔbʋgʋ bɛ Khayelitsha.
english: Mbalo-Mokoena born in Gugulethu and grew up in Khayelitsha.

kusaal: O da tʋmnɛ nyina dʋ'ata tʋʋma yʋma piinɛ ayɔpɔi ka naan yɔ'ɔgi o diib kuosʋg zin'ig la ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014) la ni ka o da tʋm bɛ Cape Peninsula University of Technology lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid nyina la ni.
english: She worked as a dental technologist for 17 years before opening the restaurant and in 2014 was working at Cape Peninsula University of Technology's Dental Sciences department.

kusaal: Saveur buoli dinɛ "yir nya'aŋ diib zin'ig." The Sunday Times labaya gbaʋŋ pa'al ye "sɔ' ya'a daam South African diib zin'ig la nɛ disi'a tempʋʋgʋn la ka mak nɛ dikanɛ ka ba ye dinɛ an disʋŋ la".
english: Saveur called it "backyard fine dining." The Sunday Times said it was "disrupting the South African food scene with its re-imagined township cuisine that challenges notions of what constitutes fine dining." Mbalo-Mokoena also has a casual restaurant and carryout a few blocks from 4Roomed.

kusaal: Di da paasnɛ diib kuosʋg zin'is atan bɛ Africa; banɛ kpɛlim la anɛ Johannesburg's Le Wine Chambre nɛ The Ruined Garden dinɛ bɛ Fez, Morocco.
english: It is one of only three restaurants in Africa to make the list; the others are Johannesburg's Le Wine Chambre and The Ruined Garden in Fez, Morocco.

kusaal: Mbalo-Mokoena nɛ sid, da bɛ Cape Town teŋkanɛ da bɛ Melkbosstrand, da yi lɛb Khayelitsha bɔzugɔ ba da baŋ ye ban zamis gbana lalig ka yi ka bas teŋ la, ba kɛnɛ ka teŋ la kɔ'ɔŋ dinɛ nar ye ba paam.
english: Mbalo-Mokoena and her husband, who were living in the Cape Town suburb Melkbosstrand, moved back to Khayelitsha because they "realized that by moving out of the townships when we got our qualifications and our degrees, we were actually depriving the economy of the townships." They believed that when educated members of the community leave for the suburbs or urban centers, "the kids have no one to look up to."

kusaal: O sid da anɛ Sam Mokoena.
english: She is married to Sam Mokoena.

kusaal: O yinɛ Xhosa tuŋ ni ka sid la yi South Sotho.
english: She is of Xhosa heritage and her husband, South Sotho.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019) la ni, ba da tiak 4Roomed yʋ''ʋri la'as ka di paas nɛ Food & Wine nɛ Travel + Leisure labaya gbana ni ka di paas diib kuosʋg zin'is pistan (30) la ni dunia wʋsa.
english: She is the chef, owner and creative director of 4Roomed, also called 4Roomed eKasi Culture or just eKasi, in Khayelitsha township, 30 kilometres (19 mi) outside Cape Town, South Africa. In 2019 4Roomed was named in a combined project by Food & Wine and Travel + Leisure magazines as one of the 30 best restaurants in the world.

kusaal: Mbalo-Mokoena anɛ onɛ pa'ali o mɛŋ.
english: Mbalo-Mokoena is self-taught.

kusaal: O diib kuosʋg zin'ig la da pin'il tʋʋma bɛnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014) la ni ka di an lɔr kanɛ kuosid diib zi'e pʋ lal nɛ shisa nyama ka yʋma atan nya'aŋ ka o yisi di keŋ yikanɛ mɔr daaɔd anaasi ni.
english: The restaurant opened in 2014 as a food truck parked next to a shisa nyama and three years later moved into a four-roomed house.

kusaal: Ba da buon four-room, multi-family bungalow nwɛnɛ ban maani ba si'em bɛ South Africa's eKasi (tempʋʋdin la).
english: The restaurant is named for the four-room, multi-family bungalow typical in South Africa's eKasi (townships).

kusaal: Mbalo-Mokoena da nɔbʋgnɛ yikaŋa buudi ni.
english: Mbalo-Mokoena was raised in this type of home.

kusaal: O diib kuosʋg zin'ig la da anɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ba kuosid dibanɛ an teŋin diib, di kas-kas anɛ dibanɛ bɛ South African.
english: The restaurant specializes in modern interpretations of traditional African dishes, and especially South African dishes.

kusaal: Mbalo-Mokoena da lɛm mɔr diib kuosʋg zin'ikanɛ da pʋ lal nɛ zin'ikanɛ ka 4Roomed da bɛ la.
english: Saveur called it "backyard fine dining." The Sunday Times said it was "disrupting the South African food scene with its re-imagined township cuisine that challenges notions of what constitutes fine dining." Mbalo-Mokoena also has a casual restaurant and carryout a few blocks from 4Roomed.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014) la ni, Mbalo-Mokoena da nya'a bɛ Master Chef South Africa dinɛ da paasi atan daan la ni, zin'ikanɛ ka o da paas nidib ayuobʋ banɛ bɛ agɔl la ni.
english: In 2014 Mbalo-Mokoena competed on the third season of MasterChef South Africa, where she reached the top six.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019) la ni, ba da tiak 4Roomed yʋ'ʋr ka di yʋ'ʋm paas bʋnsieba ka di an Diib & Daam nɛ nwienr + Vʋ'ʋsʋg labaya gbana da pa'al ye di paas diib kuosʋg zin'is pistan' banɛ gaad tuon dunia wʋsa ni la.
english: In 2019 4Roomed was named in a combined project by Food & Wine and Travel + Leisure magazines as one of the 30 best restaurants in the world.

kusaal: O da gban'e ye o yɔ'ɔg diib kuosʋg zin'ig la bɔzugɔ o da baŋ ye South Africa dim pʋ nɔŋi ba mɛŋ diib la ka nwɛ'ɛd nyɔ'ɔgʋ di yɛlaa.
english: She decided to open a restaurant because she felt that South Africa wasn't celebrating its own food heritage.

kusaal: Ablekuma North bɛnɛ Accra metropolis kanɛ bɛ Accra region tentita'ar sʋ'ʋlʋmin laLi bɛɛn yɛla.
english: Ablekuma North is located in the Accra Metropolis in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Ga East district kanɛ bɛ Greater Accra region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The constituency also doubles as the Ablekuma North Municipal Assembly of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Ga East district kanɛ bɛ Greater Accra region sʋʋlim, Ghana.
english: The constituency also doubles as the Ablekuma North Municipal Assembly of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba ɛɛnti vɔɔdnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaan ka zi'eni tis Constituency la wadmaanib yin, la lin pin'il yiiga vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Ablekuma West bɛnɛ Accra metropolis teŋkanɛ bɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlʋm tita'ar Ghana nwa la.
english: Ablekuma West is located in the Accra Metropolis in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ablekuma West da anɛ constituency nam paala 45 banɛ ka ba da maal ye ba la'am paas yʋʋm 2012 vɔɔt tita'ar ni vɔɔt gaŋi ba wadmaan.
english: Ablekuma West was one of 45 newly created constituencies for the 2012 general election.

kusaal: li mɔr distrik nam banɛ an Dansoman nɛ sahara nɛ Gbegbeyise nɛ Agege nɛ Glefe nɛ opetekwe nɛ shiabu.yiiga ka yʋʋm 2016 vɔɔdʋg la naan kena la,ban da ye ba vɔɔt gaans NPP nidib banɛ na mɔr suor ye ba zi'e nyi'a na'am la, Theophilus Tettey Enyo onɛ an constituency kʋk daan la nɛ Roni Nicole onɛ an kpikpiʋŋ sɔb la da duoe zi'en nɛ Ursula Owusu gaansʋg vɔɔt la ni.
english: Before the 2016 general election, incumbent MP Ursula Owusu was challenged in an NPP primary election by constituency chairman Theophilus Tettey Enyo and businessman Roni Nicole.

kusaal: Owusu da gaŋ Nicole nɛ vɔɔt kal 554 ka o mɔr vɔɔt 317 nɛ nidib 400 banɛ da zi'en nyia la wʋsa.
english: Owusu beat Nicole by 554 votes to 317, with up to 400 members reported to have boycotted the contest in protest.

kusaal: ninkanɛ ka ba da vɔɔt gaŋ o bɛ Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋʋm 2012la ni la da anɛ Ursula Owusu kanɛ an wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Before the 2016 general election, incumbent MP Ursula Owusu was challenged in an NPP primary election by constituency chairman Theophilus Tettey Enyo and businessman Roni Nicole.

kusaal: Gaansʋg vɔɔt kaŋa da mɔr nɔgbannwa'asim nɛ zaba kena wa'ae katnɛ ninbanɛ vɔɔt la gaŋ ninbanɛ yʋdaa bɛ gbaʋŋʋn nar ye ban ma'a vɔɔt la, ka li taas ka ba yiis Enyo bas ka yɛldaamʋg duoe paati nam la sʋʋgin.
english: The primary proved controversial, with disputes over voting registers used resulting in legal challenges by party members and Enyo's withdrawal.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Odoom nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi' li nwadis anii la dabisim pii nɛ yinne daar (11 mɔtul nwadig 1952).
english: Odoom was born on 11 August 1952 and hails from Twifo Ayaase in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr kasɛtta gbaʋŋ dinɛ an Political nɛ Economic Change n yit J. F. Kennedy School of Governance, Harvard University yʋʋm 2007 la ni.
english: He has a certificate in Political and Economic Change from the J. F. Kennedy School of Governance, Harvard University in 2007 and also a Diploma in Accounting from the University of Ghana in 1979.

kusaal: Odoom da an kpɛɛm bɛ Cocoa Redevelopment tʋʋma ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ li nwadis ayuobʋ ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi li nwadig yinne la ni, li daba ayuobʋ daar (sigir nwadig 2016 ti paae 6 yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2017).
english: Odoom was a Lead Consultant in Cocoa Redevelopment from June 2016 to 6 January 2017.

kusaal: O da lɛn tʋmnɛ Nigeria gɔmena lʋgir kanɛ buon ye Ministry of Agriculture nɛ Natural Resources bɛ Akwa Ibom State kanɛ bɛ Nigeria sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: He also worked at the Ministry of Agriculture and Natural Resources in Akwa Ibom State in Nigeria.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn anɛ Policy Advisor at Bill/Melinda Gates/J. A Kufuor Foundation Competitive African Rice Initiative Project linɛ bɛ Nigeria din yi 2014 ti paae sigsaa nwadig 2016 la ni.
english: He was also a Policy Advisor at Bill/Melinda Gates/J. A Kufuor Foundation Competitive African Rice Initiative Project in Nigeria from 2014 to May 2016.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Twifo Atti-Morkwa Constituency kanɛ bɛ Central Region Ghana nwa la, din yi yʋʋm 2017 ti paae 2021 l ni.
english: He was the member of parliament for Twifo Atti-Morkwa Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana from 2017 to 2021.

kusaal: O anɛ Ma'asim Tiig na'adɔɔg na'anyi'ad; ka Samuel Ato Amoah paam vɔɔt kal 14,887, ka li an 40.8% kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ yit nidib banɛ daa vɔɔt la wʋsa ni, ka PPPP na'anyi'ad Abu Ayuba paam 273 ka li an 0.8% kɔbiga yit nidib banɛ da vɔɔt la wʋsa ni, ka CPP na'anyi'ad Ebenezer Appiah da paam vɔɔt kal 115 ka li an 0.3% kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ yit nidib banɛ daa vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: He won with 21,231 votes making 58.2% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Samuel Ato Amoah had 14,887 votes making 40.8% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Abu Ayuba had 273 votes making 0.8% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Ebenezer Appiah had 115 vote making 0.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Odoom daa anɛ Laafi Lʋgir la Minista kʋdʋg Nya'andɔl bɛɛ Deputy Minister tis nimma'asim lʋgir la Kufuor gɔmena saŋa la.
english: Odoom is the former Deputy Minister for Health during the Kufuor administration.

kusaal: O mɛ da anɛ Minista kʋdʋg nya'andɔl bɛ gɔmena lʋgir kanɛ buon ye Local Government la ni.
english: He is the former Deputy Minister for Local Government.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2004 ni la, onɛ da an District Chief Executive kanɛ tʋʋm hali gat o taaba bɛ Twifo Hemang Lower Denkyira District Assembly bɛ Ghana kpɛla.
english: In 2004, he emerged the best District Chief Executive for the then Twifo Hemang Lower Denkyira District Assembly in Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2019 ni la li sapal nwadig la, o da di'e Lifetime Achievement Honorary piini.
english: In November 2019, he was presented with a Lifetime Achievement Honorary Award.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Twifo Atti-Morkwa Constituency n bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, ka an wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Abraham Dwuma Odoom is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Twifo Atti-Morkwa Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba di kasɛta ye onɛ vɛɛnsi sɔb gbaʋŋ kanɛ sʋŋ ka Nigeria mui kuob nɛ di maalʋg keŋ tuon sʋ'ʋŋa.
english: He is credited with developing a concept note behind Nigeria's 'successful' rice production story.

kusaal: O yinɛ Twifo Ayaase teŋkanɛ bɛ Central Region Ghana nwa la.
english: Odoom was born on 11 August 1952 and hails from Twifo Ayaase in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛm mɔr Diploma in Accounting n yit University of Ghana yʋʋm 1979 la ni.
english: He has a certificate in Political and Economic Change from the J. F. Kennedy School of Governance, Harvard University in 2007 and also a Diploma in Accounting from the University of Ghana in 1979.

kusaal: Odoom anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: During the 2016 Ghanaian general election, Odoom won the Twifo Atti Morkwa Constituency parliamentary seat.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm 2016 vɔɔtʋg tita'ar la ni la, Odoom da di lieb wadmaan tis Twifo Atti Morkwa Constituency.
english: During the 2016 Ghanaian general election, Odoom won the Twifo Atti Morkwa Constituency parliamentary seat.

kusaal: Nidib tusa pisi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan' nɛ yinne (21,231) da vɔɔti tis o, ka di pa'al ye kɔbiga pʋʋgin o paamnɛ vaar 58.2% yit nidib banɛ da vɔɔt la, wʋsa ni.
english: He won with 21,231 votes making 58.2% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Samuel Ato Amoah had 14,887 votes making 40.8% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Abu Ayuba had 273 votes making 0.8% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Ebenezer Appiah had 115 vote making 0.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Odoom anɛ kristo biig.
english: Odoom is a Christian.

kusaal: Abuakwa State College anɛ anaae ka tɔlis sakur linɛ paas ayi linɛ bɛ Kibi Ghana Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: Abuakwa State College is a co-ed second cycle institution in Kibi in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da yɔ'ɔg sakur la nɛ yʋʋma 1936 la ni ka kpɛɛmnam atan' banɛ da bɛ Methodist karimdɔɔg linɛ Asafo-Akyem la da sʋŋi yɔ'ɔgi li pin'il biis sakur la ni ye li sʋŋi ti'enb Ghana biis banɛ bɔɔdi sɔb akarim gaad taaba zamisʋŋ la.
english: The school was established in 1936 by three elders of the Methodist Church at Asafo-Akyem as a preparatory institution to prepare Ghanaian students who wanted to sit the then Junior Cambridge Examination.

kusaal: Ba da tiak zig la lɛbis Kyebi sʋ'ʋlʋm yʋʋma 1937 la ni, Nana Sir Ofori Atta onɛ an yiiga I la onɛ da pin'il ɛɛnbir la Sawa'ar nwadig dabisim piinɛ nɛ yinne yʋʋma 1937 la ni linɛ pa'al ye onɛ da da pin'il sakur la nɛ kpɛɛm sakurin la, Abuakwa State College sakur la da yɔ'ɔki ye li sʋŋ sakur bibis banɛ bɛ Akyem Abuakwa ye li sʋŋi ba.
english: It was relocated to Kyebi in 1937 by Nana Sir Ofori Atta I who laid the foundation stone on 11 October 1937 thus becoming the founder and father of the school, Abuakwa State College was born to enable more students especially those from Akyem Abuakwa to enroll in the school.

kusaal: Abu-Bakar Siddique Boniface anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd onɛ an Minister of State nannanna n bɛ Gɔmina nya'andɔl tʋʋma dɔɔgin la ka mɛ da an minista onɛ gɔsid Ghana nidib nɛ Zongo Nɔbigir yɛla, ba da du'a Abu-Bakar Siddique Boniface nɛ nwadis pii nɛ yinne la dabisim pii nɛ anaasi, yʋma 1960 la ni.
english: Abu-Bakar Siddique Boniface (also: Abubakar Saddique Boniface) (born November 14, 1960) is a Ghanaian politician and currently Minister of State at the Office of the Vice President and a former minister for Inner cities and Zongo Development.

kusaal: Onɛ da an minista tis bipula, tʋʋma, nɛ tʋʋma nɔgʋsʋg (Ninsaal paŋ, bipula nɛ tʋʋma nɔgʋsʋg) lin da yi yʋma 2005 nɛ nwadisa ayɔpɔi la yʋma 2007 la ni.
english: He was a Minister of Youth, Labour, and Employment (Manpower, Youth and Employment) between 2005 and July 2007.

kusaal: Abu-Bakar Saddique Boniface anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid, ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anaasi la n paas Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi ba da maal Ghana wʋsa vɔɔt yʋma 2004 la ni ka o di n an wadmaan n tis salaga sʋ'ʋlʋm, o mɛ lɛn paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas atan' la ni Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ka Ghana da maal vɔɔt la nɛ yʋma 2000 la ni ka o di, o da paam vɔɔt kal 1821.
english: Abu-Bakar Saddique Boniface from New Patriotic Party, is a member of the 4th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana elected in 2004 Ghanaian general election for the salaga constituency and also a member of the 3rd parliament of the 4th parliament elected in 2000 Ghanaian general election with a majority of 1821 votes.

kusaal: O pɔlitis tʋʋma nii, Alhaji Abubakar Saddique Boniface da pian'a nɔɔri zi'el ye o na zi'enɛ o tʋʋma linɛ an minista tʋʋma la zugu sʋŋ Zongo dim la tituaa wʋʋ lin nar si'em la, li ba' kae nɛ ba pʋ'ʋsim kanɛ ni ka ba bɛ bɛɛ ba buudi nɛ ba kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔba.
english: During his political duty, Alhaji Abubakar Saddique Boniface has promised to discharge his duty - as a Minister of State with diligence and treat all Zongo dwellers with fairly despite their religious, ethnic and social differences.

kusaal: Abu-Bakar Saddique Boniface da keŋi o sakuri bɛ University of Exeter ani ka maal o master of Arts in Economics ka lin nya'aŋ ka o keŋ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology sakur la ni.
english: Abu-Bakar Saddique Boniface schooled at the University of Exeter where he obtained his master of Arts in Economics and after went to the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology.

kusaal: Abu-Bakar Saddique Boniface da anɛ Economist nɛ Gɔmina tʋmtʋm.
english: Abu-Bakar Saddique Boniface is an Economist and a Civil Servant.

kusaal: Nwadis anii la yʋma 2007 la ni, ka Boniface da nɔki o mɛŋi paas Minista banɛ gɔsid kʋ'om yɛla, Ghana tʋʋma nɛ Ya yɛla la ni n bɛ Gɔmina minista nam la ni.
english: In August 2007, Boniface joined the Ministry of Water Resources, Public Works and Housing as a government minister.

kusaal: O da di'e kʋk la nɛ yi Hamidu Baba Braimah onɛ da an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la ka da yʋ'ʋn yɔɔlim nya'aŋ n zi'enɛ o nyari la.
english: He took the seat from Hamidu Baba Braimah of National Democratic Congress at this time he was an Independent.

kusaal: Abu-Bakar Saddique Boniface tʋʋma anɛ Economist nɛ onɛ an gɔmina tʋmtʋm.
english: Abu-Bakar Saddique Boniface is an Economist and a Civil Servant.

kusaal: Boniface anɛ Mor, o di pu'a mɔr biis anu.
english: Boniface is a Muslim, married with 5 children.

kusaal: Abukari Dawuni (dʋ'anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27 January 1977) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Ma'asm tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: Abukari Dawuni (born 27 January 1977) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Dawuni nɛ Wulensi, o mɔnrɛ BA in Admin (Management Technology)
english: Dawuni was born in Wulensi, He holds a BA in Admin (Management Technology)

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2021 nidib kaanlʋg la nii, Accra Metropolitan District, 20.4 km2 (7.9 sq mi), mɔri nidib kanl wʋʋ 284,124, ka tita'ar Greater Accra Region, 3,245 km2 (1,253 sq mi), mɔr nidib kanl wʋʋ 5,455,692.
english: As of the 2021 census, the Accra Metropolitan District, 20.4 km2 (7.9 sq mi), had a population of 284,124, and the larger Greater Accra Region, 3,245 km2 (1,253 sq mi), had a population of 5.46 million.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr la na'ana buolʋg, "Accra" anɛ zin'isia bɛ Accra Metropolitan District pʋʋgin ka di da bɛ ka yʋʋm 2008 , dinɛ ka di pɛ'ɛs 199.4 km2 (77.0 sq mi).
english: The name "Accra" sometimes refers to the territory of the Accra Metropolitan District as it existed before 2008, when it covered 199.4 km2 (77.0 sq mi).

kusaal: Zin'ikaŋa da pʋdʋgnɛ paam zi'is 13; 12 municipal sʋ'ʋlim banɛ sʋe ba mɛŋ (teŋ la bɛn: 179.0 km2) nɛ Accra Metropolitan District kani ka ba bʋ'oe (20.4 km2), dinɛ an sʋ'ʋlim kani bɛ teŋpʋʋg dinɛ ka ba tisi ba teŋpʋvɛnlim.
