english: This territory has since been split into 13 local government districts: 12 independent municipal districts (total area: 179.0 km2) and the reduced Accra Metropolitan District (20.4 km2), which is the only district within the capital to be granted city status.

kusaal: Teŋkani mɔr 199.4 km2 la mɔr nidib 1,782,150 nidib kanl kani da bɛ 2021 nidib kanl la ni, ka Ghana wʋsa teŋpʋtita'ar, ka sʋ'ʋlʋm bani bɛ Accra Metropolitan Assembly pʋʋgin la (20.4 km2) bɛɛ di kɔn' nɛ teŋpʋʋs bama la ni an "City of Accra".
english: This territory of 199.4 km2 contained 1,782,150 inhabitants at the 2021 census, and serves as the capital of Ghana, while the district under the jurisdiction of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly proper (20.4 km2) is distinguished from the rest of the capital as the "City of Accra".

kusaal: Di da pin'ilɛ yit sʋ'ʋlimnam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb bɛ British Fort James, Dutch Fort Crêvecoeur (Ussher Fort), nɛ Danish Fort Christiansborg saŋa bɛ Jamestown, Usshertown, nɛ Christiansborg ni, Accra da an teŋpʋtita'ar bɛ British Gold Coast saŋa yit yʋʋm 1877 nɛ 1957 ni, ka di yʋ'ʋn da nɔbignɛ an nanna metropolis.
english: Formed from the merger of separate settlements around British Fort James, Dutch Fort Crêvecoeur (Ussher Fort), and Danish Fort Christiansborg as Jamestown, Usshertown, and Christiansborg, respectively, Accra served as the capital of the British Gold Coast between 1877 and 1957 and has since transitioned into a more modern metropolis.

kusaal: Teŋpʋʋg la architecture bigisi di pin'ilʋg, pin'il 19th-century colonial architecture tis nanna skyscrapers nɛ dɔgbɛɛnda.
english: The capital's architecture reflects this history, ranging from 19th-century colonial architecture to modern skyscrapers and apartment blocks.

kusaal: 2020 nii, Globalization nɛ World Cities Research Network gaŋ Accra ka di an "Gamma" − teŋpʋʋg kani ka dunia nidib ken, bigisid ye nidib lʋga anaasi kpɛn'ɛdi anina.
english: Accra is the Greater Accra Region's economic and administrative hub, and serves as the anchor of the larger Greater Accra Metropolitan Area (GAMA), which is inhabited by about 4 million people, making it the thirteenth-largest metropolitan area in Africa. In 2020, the Globalization and World Cities Research Network think tank designated Accra as a "Gamma −" level global city, indicating a growing level of international influence and connectedness.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmʋn la, Accra da anɛ Kpiisʋg tensʋk, zin'ibanɛ ka ba da kpiisid la anɛ Ada nɛ Prampram, la'anɛ Dodowa nɛ Akuse.
english: Initially, Accra was not the most prominent trading centre; the trading hubs were the ports at Ada and Prampram, along with the inland centres of Dodowa and Akuse.

kusaal: Dutch nam la da mɛ Ussher Fort kanɛ kpi'e la, ka British nɛ Swedes mɛ da mɛ James Fort nɛ Christianburg castle nam.
english: The Dutch later built the nearby Fort Crèvecœur while the British and the Swedes built James Fort and Christiansborg castles, respectively, in the 17th century.

kusaal: British la yʋ'ʋn da zabi faaen Accra yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (1974) la ni ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1977) la ni, Anloga-Asante zabkanɛ paasi ayi' la nya'aŋ ka Accra yʋ'ʋn da di'e Cape Coasti an Gold Coast tempʋtita'ar.
english: The British then captured Accra in 1874, and in 1877, at the end of the second Anglo-Asante War, Accra replaced Cape Coast as the capital of the British Gold Coast.

kusaal: Ban da yis Gold Coast tempʋtita'ar la yi Cape Coast lɛbis Accra (yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1977) la ni la, Britain nɛ European dim kanl da maligim paas Accra hali Christianburg baba (Osu, Ministries, Ridge, Labone nɛ Cantonments) yʋ'ʋm pin'il, ka tempʋʋg la yʋ'ʋn yaligi paas ka nidib banɛ kena la nyaŋi kpɛn'.
english: As the newly established Gold Coast's administrative functions were moved to Accra (1877), an influx of British colonial administrators and European settlers grew around the Christiansborg (what later is Osu, Ministries, Ridge, Labone, and Cantonments) began, and the city began to expand to accommodate the new residents.

kusaal: Ba da maal Victoriaborg nɛ 19th Century la ni ka di an zin'ikanɛ ka Europe dim la bɛ ka sɔ' pʋ gɛndigidi baa, ka di bɛ tempʋʋg la ya-dagɔbʋg baba.
english: Victoriaborg was formed in the 19th century as an exclusively European residential neighbourhood, located to the east of the city limits of the time.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anii (1948) nii, Ghana kpɛlim bɛnɛ Britain dim nu'usin dɔlisid Dunia wʋsa zabkanɛ paasi ayi la.
english: In 1948, Ghana remained a colony of Great Britain following World War II.

kusaal: Wadmaannib yir, son depremler depremabi.com Supreme Court of Ghana, Black Star Square nɛ Bank of Ghana anɛ zin'ibanɛ mɛ bɛ Accra.
english: The Parliament, Supreme Court of Ghana, Black Star Square and the Bank of Ghana are located in Accra.

kusaal: Tempʋʋg la mɛ mɔr suobanɛ ka nidib dɔlli nwied, Kotoka International Airport, nɛ ziriga suoya banɛ tɔ'ɔŋ tembama Tema, Sekondi-Takoradi nɛ Kumasi.
english: The city is a transportation hub, home to Accra International Airport, and railway links to Tema, Sekondi-Takoradi and Kumasi.

kusaal: Accra yʋ'ʋn anɛ zin'ikanɛ ka Ghana nidib nɛ tensieba nidib wʋsa kpɛn'ɛdi maan kpikpiŋ ka sɔnsʋdi gban'ad kpiisʋg suoya nwɛnɛ, BarCamp Ghana series, ka Ghana Think Foundation da maal la.
english: Accra has become a location for national and international business conferences, such as the BarCamp Ghana series, organised by GhanaThink Foundation.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a gɔs din bɛ zin'isi'a, zin'ibanɛ bɛ Ring Road West ya-tuona la, yaligi paae northern nɛ eastern ti paae tempʋʋg la yinɛ saltponds ka Graphic Road lɛbid ya-dagɔbʋg, anɛ Accra West.
english: Geographically, the areas west of Ring Road West, extending as far west as the saltponds and south of Graphic Road, are considered Accra West.

kusaal: Pre-school anɛ nursery nɛ kindergarten.
english: Pre-school comprises nursery and kindergarten.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne (2001) la ni, bibanɛ da ken bibaanlʋg sakur Accra da anɛ Tusa Ayɔpɔi, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisi nɛ tan (7,923) (bipumis Tusa atan, kɔbʋsnii nɛ piswai nɛ atan (3,893) ka biribis an Tusa anaasi nɛ pistan' (4,030).
english: In 2001, there were 7,923 children (3,893 girls and 4,030 boys) in pre-schools in Accra.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) ni, banɛ da ken bibaanlʋg sakur la da anɛ piswai nɛ nii kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn (98%).
english: In 2010, the enrolment rate at Pre-school was 98%.

kusaal: Primary school sakur biis da zu'oe gaad biribis.
english: Primary school enrolment of girls is higher than that of boys.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2001/2002) gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yʋʋm la nii, biis Tusa pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne nɛ pisnii (61,080) banɛ bɛ Accra da ken sakur, kanl kaŋa zɛmnɛ pisnu nɛ yɔpɔi dʋ'al piinɛ yɔpɔi kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn (57.17%) yi biis Tusa Kɔbʋga nɛ pisi nɛ awa, kɔbʋsnaasi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yɔpɔi (129,467) banɛ yʋma an piinɛ ayi (12) keŋ paae piinɛ anaasi (14) ka di nar ye ba keŋ sakur la.
english: In the 2001/2002 academic year, 61,080 pupils had enrolled in Accra, representing 57.17% of the 129,467 school-age 12–to-14-year-olds.

kusaal: Biis banɛ naan junior high ken senior high school la paasi yi pistan kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn (30%) yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai (1990) keŋ pisnu kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn (50%) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne la ni (2001).
english: The transition rate between junior high and senior high school increased from 30% in 1990 to 50% in 2001.

kusaal: Ka ba kanl nɔbʋgʋ yi Tusa pisi nɛ atan', kɔbʋga nɛ ayi (23,102) din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ piswai la ni (1990) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) la ni, ka lɛm paas nwɛnɛ tusa ayi, kɔbʋstan nɛ piiga (2,310) yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgʋn, din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ni, senior high school sakur biis kanl anɛ piswai nɛ anu kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn (95%).
english: The number of students grew by 23,102 between 1990 and 2005, an increase of about 2,310 a year, since 2010 the senior high school enrolment rate has been 95%.

kusaal: Ghana International School (GIS), asʋ'ʋ-m-mɛŋ lʋgʋr kanɛ an A-Level school ka ba da pin'ili di yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anu (1955) tis bibanɛ an yʋma atan paae piinɛ anii la (3–18), bɛnɛ Accra Cantonments.
english: Ghana International School (GIS), a private non-profit A-Level school founded in 1955 for children from ages 3–18, is located in Accra's Cantonments.

kusaal: Abelemkpe an zin'ikanɛ ka Lincoln Community School, asʋ'ʋ-m-mɛŋ sakur kanɛ an International Baccalaureate (IB) tis bibanɛ an yʋma atan keŋ paae yʋʋm piinɛ anii la (3–18), da pin'ilnɛ Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (1968).
english: Abelemkpe is the home of Lincoln Community School, a private, non-profit International Baccalaureate (IB) school for students aged 3–18, established in 1968.

kusaal: Thomas Aquinas Senior High School, ck aba buon ye "Quinas"; Accra High School ka ba buon ye "Ahisco"; West Africa Secondary School, ka ba buon ye "WASS"; Accra Girls' Senior High School, ka ba buon ye "Agiss"; Kaneshie Secondary Technical School ("Kateco"); Armed Forces Secondary Technical; nɛ St.
english: A number of public secondary schools lie on the outskirts of Accra: Achimota School, also referred to as "Motown", which was founded in 1924 and opened in 1927; the Accra Academy, known as "Accra Aca"; the Presbyterian Boys' Secondary School in Legon, also known as "Presec"; Wesley Grammar School – WESS-G Dansoman, St. Mary's Senior High School, also referred to as "Merriez", is a girls' boarding school in Ghana; St. Thomas Aquinas Senior High School, also known as "Quinas"; Accra High School also known as "Ahisco"; West Africa Secondary School, also known as "WASS"; the Accra Girls' Senior High School, also known as "Agiss"; Kaneshie Secondary Technical School ("Kateco"); the Armed Forces Secondary Technical; and St. John's Grammar School; among others.

kusaal: University of Ghana anɛ 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) lɛbid Legon Ya-dagɔbʋg baba.
english: The University of Ghana is located 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) north of the city centre at Legon.

kusaal: Di bɛnɛ ya-dagɔbʋgi kpi'e Gulf of Guinea la, dinɛ pɛ'ɛs Atlantic Ocean ni.
english: Accra () is the capital and largest city of Ghana, located on the southern coast at the Gulf of Guinea, which is part of the Atlantic Ocean.

kusaal: Accra an Greater Accra Region's economic nɛ administrative hub, ka lɛm an anchor tis tita'ar Greater Accra Metropolitan Area (GAMA), dinɛ mɔr nidib wʋʋ miliyon 4, kɛt ka di an metropolitan kani pɛ'ɛs piinɛ atan' bɛ Africa ni.
english: Accra is the Greater Accra Region's economic and administrative hub, and serves as the anchor of the larger Greater Accra Metropolitan Area (GAMA), which is inhabited by about 4 million people, making it the thirteenth-largest metropolitan area in Africa. In 2020, the Globalization and World Cities Research Network think tank designated Accra as a "Gamma −" level global city, indicating a growing level of international influence and connectedness.

kusaal: Accra yinɛ Kambʋnnir pian'ʋk kanɛ an Nkran ka di gbin an "gunya" la, ka di yinɛ ban da nyɛ ka gunya mɛ dɔɔg Accra la.
english: The word Accra is derived from the Akan word Nkran meaning "ants", a reference to anthills seen in the countryside around Accra.

kusaal: Ga nam la buon Accra nɛ Ga bɛɛ Gaga, di anɛ yinne tis Ga nam la nɛ Kambʋmis la.
english: The name of Accra in the local Ga language is Ga or Gaga, the same name as that of the Ga people and a cognate with Nkran.

kusaal: Ka ba ɛɛnti mɛɛ (aklabatsa) giŋi di, mɛ wa' banɛ da dilig Accra la, ba da nyɛ di ka di anɛ nidib sʋ'ʋlim nam ka lɛn an dinɛ tɔ'ɔŋ banɛ vui nɛ banɛ kpi la.
english: Sometimes ringed by sacred fences (aklabatsa), the tall red mounds dotting Accra's hinterland were seen as microcosms of human community and as nodal points between the known world and the world of the dead.

kusaal: Ga nam la nɔk gunbanɛ an sabil-wiid la ye di pa'al paŋ nɛ ban da zabi nyaŋ banɛ pian'ad Guang ka bɛ Accra plains la.
english: The Gas used the reference to the invasive species of dark-red swarming ants to connote the military prowess of the Gas and their ancient conquest of Guang speakers residing in the Accra Plains.

kusaal: Ga mɛ nɔki di yʋ'ʋri tis Ga district nam banɛ bɛ Accra la.
english: This territory of 199.4 km2 contained 1,782,150 inhabitants at the 2021 census, and serves as the capital of Ghana, while the district under the jurisdiction of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly proper (20.4 km2) is distinguished from the rest of the capital as the "City of Accra".

kusaal: Accra sɔb la anɛ Kambʋmisi da nɔki tis Na'asaanam.
english: The spelling Accra was given to Nkran by Europeans.

kusaal: Dinzug ka Lartens la da buoli ba ye Nkran (gunya).
english: The spelling Accra was given to Nkran by Europeans.

kusaal: Nya'aŋ ka Na'asaanam la da san'ami Nkran la, ka ba yʋ'ʋm buoni Accra keŋ paae zina.
english: The spelling Accra was given to Nkran by Europeans.

kusaal: Nkran nɛ Ga pian'adin anɛ Gaga, din nya'aŋ ka ba pin'ili buoni ba mɛŋ ye Ga.
english: The name of Accra in the local Ga language is Ga or Gaga, the same name as that of the Ga people and a cognate with Nkran.

kusaal: 17th century la ni, Portugal, France nɛ Denmark, da mɛ fort nam tempʋʋg la ni.
english: The Dutch later built the nearby Fort Crèvecœur while the British and the Swedes built James Fort and Christiansborg castles, respectively, in the 17th century.

kusaal: Britain da anɛ tenkanɛ ka tɛɛns wʋsa da mɔr bɔɔdim din yi 1951 saŋa Denmarki da ku'os Christianburg (dinɛ ka ba da da' yi Swdes la) nɛ bam mɛŋ fortnami tis British la.
english: Britain gradually acquired the interests of all other countries beginning in 1851, when Denmark sold Christiansborg (which they had acquired from the Swedes) and their other forts to the British.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan (1983) la nii, British nɛ Kambʋmisi da zabid la yʋma piiga baba nya'aŋ, Na'asaanam la da zaba faaen Kumasi, ka san'am tempʋʋg la luosieba.
english: In 1873, after decades of tension between the British and Ashantis, the British captured Kumasi, destroying portions of the city.

kusaal: Keŋ paae zina, Accra sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa da mɛnɛ gilig din yi Ussher ti paaedi ya-nya'aŋ ka Korle Lagoon bɛ di ya-tuona.
english: Until this time, the settlement of Accra was confined between Ussher Fort to the east and the Korle Lagoon to the west.

kusaal: Accra titɔndig da lɛm maligim yalig ya'as yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ anii (1908) la ni.
english: The boundaries of Accra were further stretched in 1908, after a bubonic plague epidemic.

kusaal: Ani ka ba da maali Adabraka lɛbis tempʋʋg la ya-dagɔbʋg baba.
english: Adabraka was thus established to the north of the city.

kusaal: Gban'asʋŋ kanɛ ka ba da maal ka di tiak tempʋʋg la zi'esim anɛ ban da maal Accra nɛ Kumasi ziriga pal la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ anii (1908) la ni.
english: The boundaries of Accra were further stretched in 1908, after a bubonic plague epidemic.

kusaal: Nɛ' anɛ di tɔ'ɔŋ Accra, teŋ la tempʋtita'akanɛ mɔr port sankan la, nɛ Ghana region kanɛ kuod koko gaad banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa.
english: Accra is the Greater Accra region's tourist hub, sporting hotels, monuments, museums and nightclubs.

kusaal: Na'asaanam la da kɛ ka Accra an din da an si'em la sankan win.
english: Until this time, the settlement of Accra was confined between Ussher Fort to the east and the Korle Lagoon to the west.

kusaal: Nɛ' da kpɛlim anɛ ala hali ti paae Sir Frederick Gordon Guggisberg saŋa ka o zaŋ sʋ'ʋlkʋm atan' la (Osu, La nɛ Jamestown) la'as taaba ka di yʋ'ʋn lieb Accra an si'em nananna la.
english: Formed from the merger of separate settlements around British Fort James, Dutch Fort Crêvecoeur (Ussher Fort), and Danish Fort Christiansborg as Jamestown, Usshertown, and Christiansborg, respectively, Accra served as the capital of the British Gold Coast between 1877 and 1957 and has since transitioned into a more modern metropolis.

kusaal: Tʋʋmbanɛ ka Guggisberg da tʋm sieba anɛ o da mɛ teriko buŋ Korle Lagoon la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisi nɛ atan (1923) la ni ka di yɔ'ɔg paalʋ kanɛ bɛ di lɔ'ɔm la ka di lieb nidib bɛllim zin'ig.
english: Among the achievements of Guggisberg was the building of a bridge across the Korle Lagoon in 1923, which increased settlement at Korle Bu, Korle Gonno and Chokor, to the west of the lagoon.

kusaal: Guggisberg mɛ da gɔsya ka ba mɛ sibiti tita'ar dinɛ an Korle-Bu nɛ sekondari sakur kanɛ an Achimota.
english: Guggisberg also oversaw the building of a hospital (Korle-Bu) and secondary school (Achimota).

kusaal: Bʋnkaŋa da kɛya ka Accra nidib kanl maligim paas bɛdegʋ ka di yinɛ nidibi naan teŋkpɛmisin ken' tempʋʋgʋn na ka British kpikpikpinnib mɛ kpɛn'ɛna paas la.
english: As the newly established Gold Coast's administrative functions were moved to Accra (1877), an influx of British colonial administrators and European settlers grew around the Christiansborg (what later is Osu, Ministries, Ridge, Labone, and Cantonments) began, and the city began to expand to accommodate the new residents.

kusaal: Osu Alata Na'ab Nii Kobina Bonney onɛ paasi atan la, da gban'e ye ba da lɛm mɔr Europe la'adi kpɛn' teŋ la wʋsa nii la'ad ligiid dʋ la zug.
english: The chief of Osu Alata, Nii Kobina Bonney III, had set up a boycott of European goods across the country due to the rise of prices for essential commodities.

kusaal: Nkrumah da lieb Ghana yiiga gɔmena la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi la, o da gban'e on mɛŋ suokanɛ ka o bɔɔd ye dɔlisi maal Accra sʋ'ʋŋa.
english: After Kwame Nkrumah became Ghana's first Prime Minister in 1957, he created his own plan for Accra's development.

kusaal: On da na maal zin'igi tis banɛ nini nie la, Nkrumah da mɔɔɔdnɛ ye o maan dinɛ na kɛ ka o nidib la mɔr si'ir nɛ ban yi teŋsi'a nɛ Africa tɛmis wʋsa nidib.
english: Nkrumah proposed creating spaces to inspire pride and nationalism in his people and people throughout Africa.

kusaal: Accra tempʋʋg la mɛŋ-mɛŋ anɛ zin'ibanɛ ka British nam, Danish nɛ Dutch dim fort nam la da bɛ kʋdʋmin lal.
english: Formed from the merger of separate settlements around British Fort James, Dutch Fort Crêvecoeur (Ussher Fort), and Danish Fort Christiansborg as Jamestown, Usshertown, and Christiansborg, respectively, Accra served as the capital of the British Gold Coast between 1877 and 1957 and has since transitioned into a more modern metropolis.

kusaal: Dɔlisid din bɛ zin'isi'a Dahomey Gap la ni, zin'ikanɛ ka Gulf of Guinea nɛ Atlantic Occean la dɔl taaba ken ka pɛbisim da'ad la, Accra bɛnɛ zin'ikanɛ mɔr tʋʋlʋg bi'ela ka di mɔr ʋʋn nɛ sɛɛʋng.
english: Accra () is the capital and largest city of Ghana, located on the southern coast at the Gulf of Guinea, which is part of the Atlantic Ocean.

kusaal: Climate & Development Knowledge Network mɛ yɛl ye wada banɛ gɔsid mɛɛb yɛla nɛ, wa'adim suoya banɛ bɛ gɔmena nam ni la, gɔmena lʋga pʋ tisid taaba labayaa bɛɛ a-ba' kae nam ya mɛɛb yɛla kɛya ka Accra ku'osuoya ka' sʋm ka mɔr daaʋŋ.
english: Inadequate planning regulation and law enforcement, and perceived corruption in government processes, lack of communication across government departments and lack of concern or government co-ordination with respect to building codes are impediments to progressing the development of Accra's drainage infrastructure, according to the Climate & Development Knowledge Network.

kusaal: Accra Metropolitan District kʋdʋg la labisim da anɛ , 199.4 km2 (77.0 sq mi), din da bɛ keŋ paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) la, nananna, ba yʋ'ʋm pʋdʋgi dinɛ ka di yʋ'ʋm mɔr district nam piinɛ atan (13), ka ba gɔsidi ba mɛŋ yɛla ka mɔri ba la'asʋg zin'is nɛ ba diisinam banɛ ka Ghana gɔmena gaansi tisi ba.
english: The name "Accra" sometimes refers to the territory of the Accra Metropolitan District as it existed before 2008, when it covered 199.4 km2 (77.0 sq mi).

kusaal: Accra Metropolitan District kanɛ ka ba da sie la (ka ba mɛ buon ye City of Accra la), ka mɔr 20.4 km2 (7.9 sq mi), da anɛ Accra wʋsa, ti paae sankanɛ ka ba yis Ledzokuku, Krowor, La Dadekotopon, Ablekuma North, Ablekuma Central, Ablekuma West, Ayawaso East, Ayawaso North, Ayawaso Central, Ayawaso West, Okaikwei North, nɛ Korley Kottey districts ka ba liebi ba district nam yʋ'ʋm bɛ ba gʋnni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ nii (2008) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2019) saŋa.
english: This territory of 199.4 km2 contained 1,782,150 inhabitants at the 2021 census, and serves as the capital of Ghana, while the district under the jurisdiction of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly proper (20.4 km2) is distinguished from the rest of the capital as the "City of Accra".

kusaal: Accra Metropolitan Assembly, dinɛ gɔsid City of Accra titɔndis banɛ gilig Accra Metropolitan District, kpɛɛm anɛ Metropolitan Chief Executive onɛ ka Republic of Ghana zugraan gaŋ.
english: This territory of 199.4 km2 contained 1,782,150 inhabitants at the 2021 census, and serves as the capital of Ghana, while the district under the jurisdiction of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly proper (20.4 km2) is distinguished from the rest of the capital as the "City of Accra".

kusaal: La Dadekotopon Municipal District, ka di tempʋtita'ar bɛ La, da nwaae yinɛ Accra Metropolitan Districtin yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012).
english: This territory has since been split into 13 local government districts: 12 independent municipal districts (total area: 179.0 km2) and the reduced Accra Metropolitan District (20.4 km2), which is the only district within the capital to be granted city status.

kusaal: Kotoka International Airport, Airport City, Accra Mall, nɛ US Embassy anɛ banɛ bɛ district la ni, ka di labisim na an nwɛnɛ 32 km2 (12 sq mi).
english: This territory of 199.4 km2 contained 1,782,150 inhabitants at the 2021 census, and serves as the capital of Ghana, while the district under the jurisdiction of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly proper (20.4 km2) is distinguished from the rest of the capital as the "City of Accra".

kusaal: Ba da nwaae Korley Klottey Municipal District yinɛ Accra Metropolitan District yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019) la ni ka di labisim an wʋʋ 10 km2 (3.9 sq mi) tɛmbanɛ bɛ district la sʋ'ʋlʋm sieba anɛ Osu, Ringway Estates, Asylum Down, North Ridge, West Ridge, Ministries, Gold Coast City, North Adabraka, nɛ Tudu.
english: As the newly established Gold Coast's administrative functions were moved to Accra (1877), an influx of British colonial administrators and European settlers grew around the Christiansborg (what later is Osu, Ministries, Ridge, Labone, and Cantonments) began, and the city began to expand to accommodate the new residents.

kusaal: Ring Road yinɛ Korle Lagoon lɛbid ya-tuona baba, ka di ya-datiʋŋ baba an Kwame Nkrumah Circle, di ya-nya'aŋ baba anɛ Independence Avenue, ka tɔlis tuonɛ keŋ Osu, di maalnɛ baŋ gilig district kʋda banɛ da bɛ Accra, ka mɛ bak Accra pʋʋgʋn nɛ teŋkpɛmis banɛ bɛ di sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: Geographically, the areas west of Ring Road West, extending as far west as the saltponds and south of Graphic Road, are considered Accra West.

kusaal: Accra pʋʋgʋn anɛ CBD, dinɛ da mɔr district banɛ an Usshertown, Tudu, Victoriaborg, West Ridge, nɛ East Ridge, la'anɛ district banɛ ka nidib gbɛɛndi ani nwɛnɛ Jamestown, Adabraka, Asylum Down, North Ridge nɛ Christiansborg/Osu.
english: Formed from the merger of separate settlements around British Fort James, Dutch Fort Crêvecoeur (Ussher Fort), and Danish Fort Christiansborg as Jamestown, Usshertown, and Christiansborg, respectively, Accra served as the capital of the British Gold Coast between 1877 and 1957 and has since transitioned into a more modern metropolis.

kusaal: La'anɛ district banɛ ni ka ba kpiisid nwɛnɛ Airport City bɛnɛ gilig tempʋʋg la wʋsa, Accra Tempʋʋg la kpɛlim an kpi'eŋ zin'ig nɛ malima bɛ Accra tempʋʋgʋn, dinɛ mɔr gɔmena lʋga, yigbɛɛnda, kpikpiŋ nɛ ligiid sʋ'ak zin'is.
english: This territory of 199.4 km2 contained 1,782,150 inhabitants at the 2021 census, and serves as the capital of Ghana, while the district under the jurisdiction of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly proper (20.4 km2) is distinguished from the rest of the capital as the "City of Accra".

kusaal: Accra tempʋʋgʋn zin'ivɛnlla anɛ Kwame Nkrumah Mausoleum, National Museum, Independence Square, National Theatre, nɛ Ohene Djan Stadium.
english: After Kwame Nkrumah became Ghana's first Prime Minister in 1957, he created his own plan for Accra's development.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlʋm kan ka "37" Military Hospital, Flagstaff House, nɛ tensieba embassies, Achimota School, Achimota Golf Park, nɛ University of Ghana's Legon campus, dinɛ tɔnd nɛ Accra north la bɛ.
english: The University of Ghana is located 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) north of the city centre at Legon.

english: It was established in 1949 as a Technical School and commissioned in 1957 as Accra Technical Institute.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' ni, ba da pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Accra Polytechnic, sankan gomɛna zugraan kpɛɛm Dr.
english: By the Polytechnic Law of 1992 (PNDC 321), which became fully operative in the 1993/1994 academic year, Accra Technical University was elevated to a tertiary status.

kusaal: Ba ba dʋ'ʋs Accra Technical University ka li lieb sakur tita'ar.
english: Notwithstanding the difficulties that characterized the sudden change over from secondary to a tertiary status, Accra Technical University made a tremendous progress in its review and expansion of curricula to suit contemporary needs.

kusaal: Yelsi'eba da bɛ kati wa'ae ban da dʋ'ʋs sakur la ka li kilim sakur tita'ar la, la'an nɛ wala, Accra Technical University da muku kɛ ka ba zamisig nam la na nyaŋi mɔr sʋŋir bɛdigʋ zʋmaaŋ kaŋa nwa ni.
english: Accra Technical University began to offer Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical/Electronic Engineering, Building Technology, Civil Engineering, Furniture Design and Production, Secretaryship and Management Studies, Bilingual Secretaryship and Management Studies, Accountancy, Marketing, Purchasing and Supply, Hotel Catering and Institutional Management, Fashion Design and Textiles, Mathematics and Statistics, and Science Laboratory Technology.

kusaal: Ban an zamisig lʋgir tita'ar la zug, Accra Technical University dɔlisid nɛ wada banɛ gɔsid University banɛ zamisid nu'ug tʋʋma yela, wada kanɛ da yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ na (Wada kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anu).
english: As a tertiary institution, Accra Technical University is governed by a Council established under the Technical University Act 2016 (Act 745).

kusaal: Sakur la zamisid pa'ala bɛdigʋ anina, ka ba si'eba an na'asaasɔɔng zamisʋg, nu'ug tʋʋma zamisʋg, tɔlʋŋ zamisʋg, di'ema nɛ la'ad maalig zamisʋg.
english: The school offers a range of academic programs including applied sciences, engineering, business, arts, and design.

kusaal: Accra Sports Stadium, ka ba da buon ye Ohene Djan Stadium, anɛ Stadium kanɛ mɔr tʋʋmbabʋg ka nɔkid nidib nwɛnɛ tusa pisnaasi (40,000) pɛ'ɛn ka bɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana, ka ba mɔr nwɛ'ɛd association football maknam.
english: The Accra Sports Stadium, formerly named the Ohene Djan Stadium, is a multi-use stadium (40,000-capacity, all-seater) located in Accra, Ghana, mostly used for association football matches.

kusaal: Ba da zuŋ stadium lanɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi la ni (1962) dɔlisid bɔɔlkanɛ ka Accra XI nɛ Kumasi XI da nwɛ'.
english: The stadium was inaugurated in 1962 by a football match played between Accra XI and Kumasi XI.

kusaal: Di yʋ'ʋri da an Accra Sports Stadium, ba da tiaki stadium la yʋ'ʋri tis Ohene Djan, Ghana ninkanɛ da an yiiga Director of Sports, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni (2004) ban da tiaki di la nya'aŋ.
english: Originally known as the Accra Sports Stadium, the stadium was renamed after Ohene Djan, the country's first Director of Sports, in 2004 after renovations.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne nwadisa ayuobʋ dabpiinɛ ayuobʋ daar (16 June 2011), yʋ'ʋkanɛ ka ba da sɔbi tabil stadium la, 'Ohene Djan Stadium' da tiaki keŋ 'Accra Sports Stadium' ka Accra Metropolitan Assembly pʋ yina tis mɔɔlʋgʋ di yɛlaa ka National Democratic Congress Governmentmɛ sʋŋi di.
english: On 16 June 2011, the name 'Ohene Djan Stadium' on the stadium building was changed to 'Accra Sports Stadium' without any official announcement by the Accra Metropolitan Assembly supported by the National Democratic Congress Government.

kusaal: Din da an zin'ikanɛ ka ba na nwɛ' 2008 African Cup of Nations maknam la, ba da maligim mɛ, ka tiaki di ka di lieb nwɛnɛ FIFA zi'esim.
english: As a designated venue of some of the 2008 African Cup of Nations matches, the stadium was rebuilt, upgraded, and modernized to meet FIFA standards.

kusaal: Ba da tʋm tʋʋma stadium la nii naae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la nwadis piiga ni (October 2007).
english: Work on the stadium was completed in October 2007.

kusaal: Ba da zuŋi di nɛ four-nation tournament dinɛ ka Ghana da di (the Zenith Cup).
english: It was inaugurated with a four-nation tournament that Ghana won (the Zenith Cup).

kusaal: Stadium la mɛ anɛ Africa most popular kilabs, Hearts of Oak nɛ Accra Lions FC nɛ Great Olympics, la yin zin'ikanɛ ka ba nwɛ'ɛdi ba maknam ka Ghana national team maknam la sieba mɛ nwɛ'ɛda ani sansieba.
english: The stadium is also the home of one of Africa's most popular clubs, Hearts of Oak as well as Accra Lions FC and Great Olympics, but Ghana's national team matches are sometimes played there.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi (2000) African Cup of Nations dinɛ da bɛ Ghana nɛ Nigeria la, ba da nwɛ' maknami awai stadium la ni ka da lɛn an zin'ikanɛ ka ba da nwɛ' yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (1978) final.
english: During the 2000 African Cup of Nations in Ghana and Nigeria, the stadium hosted nine matches, and was also the venue of the 1978 final.

kusaal: Zin'ig la nib a mɛ nwɛ' professional boxing tʋʋma, dinɛ kanli na an nwɛnɛ piswai nɛ yinne (91 professional boxing programs) din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadisa anii la ni (August 2020).
english: The venue has also hosted important professional boxing events, numbering 91 professional boxing programs as of August 2020.

kusaal: Dinɛ gaadi da wʋsa anɛ dinɛ da naam Asibit daar yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ nwadis piinɛ yinne daba ayuobʋ daar la (Saturday, 6 November 1976), Ghana David Kotei, World Boxing Council's world Featherweight champion, da kɔ'ɔŋi o championship tis International Boxing Hall of Fame nid, Mexican-American Danny Lopez 15 rounds ka bi'esʋg kai la.
english: Perhaps the most famous one took place on Saturday, 6 November 1976, when Ghanaian David Kotei, the World Boxing Council's world Featherweight champion, lost his championship to future International Boxing Hall of Fame member, Mexican-American Danny Lopez by a 15 rounds unanimous decision.

kusaal: La'askaŋa mɛ da paas, 29–0 prospect Sulley Shittu nɛ Felix Figueroa, ka Shittu da di 8 rounds.
english: This program also featured a bout between undefeated, 29–0 prospect Sulley Shittu and Felix Figueroa, which Shittu won by 8 rounds decision.

kusaal: Ba mɛ lɛm mɔri di maan rugby union.
english: It is also used for rugby union.

kusaal: Nimabɛ da keŋ la'asʋg la kanl da na gaad nwɛnɛ tusa kɔbiga (100,000).
english: The crowd for this event has been estimated at over 100,000 fans.

kusaal: Di yʋ'ʋr la tiakir da mɔr daʋŋ bɛdegʋ kena ka Ga nidib la pʋ siakɛ.
english: Its renaming was quite controversial and opposed by the Ga people.

kusaal: Kwasi Akyem Apea-Kubi (du'ata) on da bɛnɛ NDC ni, ka Robert Kwasi Amoah da di lieb wadmaan.
english: The parliamentary seat was contested in 2012 by Robert Kwasi Amoah (a teacher) of the NPP and Dr. Kwasi Akyem Apea-Kubi (a specialist gynaecologist) of the NDC and was won by Robert Kwasi Amoah.

kusaal: Constituency la da la'asnɛ nɛ Akim Swedru constituency ka naam killim constituency li kɔn' an Achiase Constituency nɛ Akim Swedru Constituency.
english: The Constituency was born out of a re-demarcation of the Akim Swedru constituency, which became Achiase Constituency and Akim Swedru Constituency.

kusaal: Robert Amoah da pʋ paam suor ka o lɛn zi'en wadmaan dɔlisid NPP wadmaannib vɔɔtʋgin la, Kofi Ahenkorah Marfo da di'e.
english: Heading into the 2020 general elections, Mr. Robert Amoah had lost his mandate to contest as the MP at the NPP's primaries to Kofi Ahenkorah Marfo (the NPP's former constituency chairman).

kusaal: Achiase Constituency da sin'iŋnɛ yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadis piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: The Constituency was born out of a re-demarcation of the Akim Swedru constituency, which became Achiase Constituency and Akim Swedru Constituency.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi wadmaan kʋk la, banɛ da bɔɔd da anɛ Robert Kwasi Amoah (pa'an) on da bɛnɛ NPP nɛ Dr.
english: The parliamentary seat was contested in 2012 by Robert Kwasi Amoah (a teacher) of the NPP and Dr. Kwasi Akyem Apea-Kubi (a specialist gynaecologist) of the NDC and was won by Robert Kwasi Amoah.

kusaal: Achidago B. Akugri anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛ ka da an wadmaani paas Ghana 3rd parliament, 4th republic la ni.
english: Achidago B. Akugri is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the 3rd parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan kʋdʋgʋ tis Binduri constituency bɛ Upper East Region la ka an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress kanɛ bɛ Ghana la nid.
english: He is a former member of Parliament for the Binduri constituency in the Upper East Region and a member of the National Democratic Congress political party in Ghana.

kusaal: O poɔlitis tʋʋma da pin'ilnɛ on da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg (2000 Ghanaian General elections) ka di Ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug la.
english: His political career began when he contested in the 2000 Ghanaian General elections and won on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti Akugri ka o lieb wadmaani tis Binduri constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni (2000 Ghanaian general elections).
english: Akugri was elected as the member of parliament for the Binduri constituency in the 2000 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O constituency la da paas wadmaannib anii yi kʋgʋs piinɛ ayi banɛ ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress da di Vɔɔtkan ni Western Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: His constituency was a part of the 8 parliamentary seats out of 12 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election for the Western Region.

kusaal: Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress da di kʋgʋs bi'ela dinɛ an kʋgʋs piswai nɛ yi (92) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi pʋʋgin (200) 3rd parliament la Ghana 4th republic la ni.
english: The National Democratic Congress won a minority total of 92 parliamentary seats out of 200 seats in the 3rd parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Nɛ' da zɛmnɛ nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ naasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (64%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: This was equivalent to 64% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas Atubiga Mathias onɛ bɛ People's National Convention, James A. Anaba onɛ bɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party ni, nɛ Benjamin A. Asatanga onɛ bɛ National Reformed Party.
english: He was elected over Atubiga Mathias of the People's National Convention, James A. Anaba of the New Patriotic Party, and Benjamin A. Asatanga of the National Reformed Party.

kusaal: Akugri da paasnɛ 3rd parliament la Ghana 4th republic la ni.
english: Akugri was a member of the 3rd parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O paasnɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress ni.
english: He is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da zi'eni o na'adɔɔg la nɔba zugʋ nya' nya'a di Binduri constituency bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: He represented the political party at the Binduri constituency of the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: He won the elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da diya nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ yi', kɔbiga nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ naasi (12,174) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa an tusa piinɛ wai, kɔbiswai nɛ pisi nɛ yɔpɔi (19,927).
english: He was elected with 12,174 votes out of 19,927 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Bama da paamnɛ tusa atan', kɔbisnu nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi (3,562), tusa ayi, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi (2,937) nɛ kɔbistan' nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (349) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: These obtained 3,562, 2,937 and 349 votes respectively out of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Adaklu bɛnɛ Adaklu sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ghana Volta Region la.
english: Adaklu is located in the Adaklu district of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kwame Agbodza da lɛn di'e kʋk la yʋʋma 2016 vɔt la ni.
english: Kwame Agbodza retained his seat in the 2016 elections.

kusaal: Adaklu anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm yinne linɛ mɛ paas ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la.
english: Adaklu is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba yɔ'ɔg Adaklu yʋʋma 2012 la ni ka banɛ gɔsid vɔt yɛla ti Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm la da yɔ'ɔgi li ban da ye ba maal vɔt la yɛla.
english: It was created in 2012 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana prior to the Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Yiiga vɔt la da maalnɛ nwadis piina ayi la yʋʋma 2012 ka Ghana dim da maal.
english: It was created in 2012 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana prior to the Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Ba mɛ ɛɛnti vɔti gaŋ nid yinne ka o zi'enɛ ba nɔba zug n an wadmaan (MP) n tisi ba vɔt saŋa.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid da di mɔr vɔt ka li zu'oe wʋʋ bam 10,929.
english: The National Democratic Congress candidate won the seat with a 10,929 majority.

kusaal: Adama Sulemana anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tis Tain constituency bɛ Bono region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la dim.
english: Adama Sulemana is a Ghanaian politician and member of parliament for the Tain constituency in the Bono region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Adama nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii Nwadisa atan la daba ayuobʋ daar (6 March 1978) ka o yi Nsawkaw bɛ Bono region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Adama was born on 6 March 1978 and hails from Nsawkaw in the Bono region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da sɔbi o BECE nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ nɛ pisnii nɛ awai la ni (1989) nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la ni (1992).
english: He obtained his BECE in 1989 and also in 1992.

kusaal: O da sɔbi o SSSCE nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la ni (1995).
english: He also received his SSSCE in 1995.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maali o Bachelor of Education in Psychology yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2006) ka maal o Master in Philosophy in Psychology yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai ni (2009).
english: He received his Bachelor of Education in Psychology in 2006 and his Masters in Philosophy in Psychology in 2009.

kusaal: Adama da anɛ DCE tis Tain bɛ Ministry of Local Government ka lɛn an nimma'asim pa'an (Health Teacher) tis Ministry of Health.
english: Adama was the DCE of Tain under the Ministry of Local Government and also a Health Teacher under the Ministry of Health.

kusaal: Adama anɛ NDC nid ka an Wadmaani tis Tain Constituency.
english: Adama is a member of NDC and currently the MP for Tain Constituency.

kusaal: o da di o Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt Tusa pisi, kɔbistan nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (20,374) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ anu du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (45.4%) ka NPP nid la Gabriel Osei paam vɔɔt Tusa piinɛ anii, kɔbistan nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (18,346) dinɛ an pisnaasi dua'ali awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (40.9%).
english: He won the parliamentary seat with 20,374 votes making 45.4% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary aspirant Gabriel Osei had 18,346 votes making 40.9%.

kusaal: Adama paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Standing Orders ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid pian'ad yɛla (Communications) ya'as.
english: Adama is a member of the Standing Orders Committee and also a member of the Communications Committee.

kusaal: Adama anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Adama is a Christian.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis New Edubease linɛ bɛ Gaana Ashanti region la.
english: He is the member of Parliament for the New Edubease Constituency in the Ashanti region.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adams Abdul-Salam nɛ n bɛ New Edubiase linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sυ'υlυm la Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig la ni li dabisim piina yuobu yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ anu la ni.[8] O da keŋi o sakur n bɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, ti Gaana sυ'υlυm, ani ka o da naae o Bachelor of Arts digirɛɛ naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Political Studies yυυma tusa yi' nɛ awai la ni.
english: He attended Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana where he completed with a Bachelor of Arts degree in political studies in 2009.

kusaal: O da si'iŋi o sakuri Kumasi High Sakur la ni, yυυma tusa yi' nɛ atan' la ni ka o da naae.
english: He is also an alumnus of Kumasi High School which he completed in 2003.

kusaal: Abdul-Salam da tυmnɛ an Rural Policy Officer n bɛ Rural Development Institute, linɛ bɛ Canada ka lin nya'aŋ ka o lɛn tɔɔm n tυm Research Associate Rural Community nɛ Mental Health Lab, linɛ bɛ Brandon University Canada la ni.
english: Abdul-Salam served as a Rural Policy Officer at the Rural Development Institute, Canada and later as a Research Associate Rural Community and Mental Health Lab, Brandon University Canada.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Administrative Officer n bɛ New Edubiase United Bɔɔl Club la ni.
english: He also served as an Administrative Officer at New Edubiase United Football Club.

kusaal: O paas kpɛɛm banɛ Subsidiary Legislation ka mɛ lɛn paas Local Government nɛ Rural Development kpɛɛmnam la ni n bɛ wadmaanib yir la nit.
english: He serves as a member on the Subsidiary Legislation Committee and the Local Government and Rural Development Committee of Parliament.

kusaal: Abdul-Salam anɛ Muslim.
english: Abdul-Salam is a Muslim.

kusaal: O bier, Yakubu Abdul-Salam anɛ CEO, ka an onɛ yɔ'ɔg ka su'oe New Edubiase United Football Club la.
english: His elder brother, Yakubu Abdul-Salam is the CEO, Founder and President of New Edubiase United Football Club.

kusaal: Adams Abdul-Salam anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd, ba da du'anɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig la ni li dabisim piina yuobu yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ anu la ni, o anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Adams Abdul-Salam (born on Monday, 16 December 1985) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Abdul-Salam lɛn mɔr mastɛs digirɛɛ n bɛ Rural Development n zamis linɛ Rural Policy Brandon University, Canada sakur la ni, yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yuobu ni ka o da naae.
english: Abdul-Salam holds a master's degree in Rural Development with emphasis on Rural Policy from Brandon University, Canada, completing in 2016.

kusaal: Nannanna o anɛ kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Bɔɔl club la nid yinne.
english: He currently serves as a board member of the club.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris anu la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ ayi la ni ka o da da' sanitaiza nam bam 4,500 n tis New Edubiase sυ'υlυm COVID-19 ban'a la win la.
english: In May 2022, he presented over 4,500 pieces of hand sanitizers to the people of New Edubiase Constituency during the COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana.

kusaal: Adamu Daramani Sakande (Ba du'a o nɛ 6 May 1962 – ka o maal ka'alim 22 September 2020) da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Fifth Parliament la, Ghana Fourth Republic la ni tis Bawku Central Constituency, bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Adamu Daramani Sakande (6 May 1962 – 22 September 2020) was a Ghanaian politician and a member of the Fifth Parliament of the Fourth Republic for the Bawku Central Constituency, in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Portsmouth University, NHS-UK ka zamis Counter Fraud and Security Management Service Accredited SMS yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan' la ni (2003).
english: He attended the Portsmouth University, NHS-UK and studied Counter Fraud and Security Management Service Accredited SMS in 2003.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti Adamu yiiga ka o keŋ Parliament nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii nwadispiinɛ ayi (December 2008 )Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nɔba zug ka o lieb wadmaani tis Bawku Central Constituency bɛ Upper East Region.
english: Adamu was first elected into Parliament during the December 2008 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) as a member of Parliament for the Bawku Central Constituency in the Upper East Region.

kusaal: vɔɔtʋg la saŋa, o da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi, kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (20,157) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa an tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piinɛ wai (37,719) dinɛ zi'eni tis pisnu nɛ tan' du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (53.4%).
english: During the elections, he polled 20,157 votes out of the 37,719 votes representing 53.4%.

kusaal: Adamu da tʋmnɛ nɛ NHS Primary Case Trust, bɛ London.
english: Adamu worked with the NHS Primary Case Trust, London.

kusaal: Niigi da'abiig la da yɛl ye Daramani da mɔr British nɛ Burkinabe passport nam.
english: A cattle dealer stated that Daramani held both British and Burkinabe passports.

kusaal: Adamu da lu ban'a yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan la ni sa (2003), ka namisi paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadisa awai la dabpisi nɛ ayi daar (22 September 2020) ka o maal ka'alim London.
english: Adamu suffered from ill health since at least 2003, and died on 22 September 2020 in London.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adamu nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi nwadisa anu la daba ayuobʋ daar (6 May 1962), Bawku, bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Adamu was born on 6 May 1962, in Bawku, in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaani tis Bawku Central Constituency bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He was a member of Parliament for the Bawku Central Constituency in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Adamu da kɔ'ɔŋ bʋʋd perjury nɛ forgery ni.
english: Adamu was found guilty of perjury and forgery.

kusaal: Ba da zɛrig o ye, fassi ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii vɔɔt la paae (2008 elections) paae, o da pian' ziri pian'ad zaŋi keŋi o yʋ'ʋri na kpɛn' vɔɔt gbaʋŋ la ni ka da keŋ tuoni vɔɔt yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii vɔɔtʋg la ni ka di pʋ nar ye o vɔɔtɛ.
english: He was alleged to have, before the 2008 elections, made a false statement in an application to have his name registered in the voters' register and subsequently went ahead to vote in the December 2008 general elections when he was not entitled to do so.

kusaal: Adamu da mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa ayi.
english: Adamu was married with two children.

kusaal: Dinzug ba da kpɛn'ɛs o sanriga yʋma ayi bɛ'ɛd banɛ ka o maal la wʋsa zug.
english: He was therefore jailed for two years concurrently on all counts.

kusaal: O lɔya da bɛllim kɔɔtʋ la ye ba siem sariakadib la bi'ela o laafi ka'alim titu'aa yɛla.
english: His lawyer appealed to the court to lessen the intensity of the ruling due to some health concerns of Adamu.

kusaal: Adansi United Football Club ka si'eba buon yee Adansi Utd FC anɛ Ghanaian professional association football club linɛ bɛ Kumasi, Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: Adansi United Football Club is also known Adansi Utd FC is a Ghanaian professional association football club based in Kumasi, Ashanti Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba nya'adi bɛnɛ Division Two League linɛ bɛ Ghana di'ema pʋʋgin la.
english: They are currently competing in Division Two League of the Ghanaian league system.

kusaal: Ban an Second Division club la, ba mɔr suor ka ba nwɛn'ɛ Ghanaian FA Cup.
english: As a Second Division club, they are also entitled to play in the Ghanaian FA Cup.

kusaal: Team la da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai ni (1990) ka onɛ pin'ili li an George Amoako onɛ an Ghanaian professional player kʋdʋg.
english: The team was founded in 1990 by George Amoako a former Ghanaian professional player.

kusaal: Adansi United Football Club yin color nam anɛ dɔnbʋʋlim nɛ dɛn'ɛm (Yellow and Green).
english: Adansi United Football Club home colors are Yellow and Green.

kusaal: Adansi FC ya'a di'emid zin'ig si'eba ba fuud anɛ dɔnbʋʋlim ka ba mɛŋ yin lɛɛ an dɛn'ɛm.
english: Traditional away kit for Adansi FC is Yellow and home Green.

kusaal: Adansi-Asokwa bɛnɛ Adansi-Asokwa District bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: Adansi-Asokwa is located in the Adansi Asokwa District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Tɛŋ titada bane bɛ Adansi-Asokwa constituency anɛ Bodwesango, Fumso, Aboabo, Anhwiaso, Adiemra, Hwiremoase nɛ Pipiiso.
english: Prominent communities in the Adansi-Asokwa constituency include Bodwesango, Fumso, Aboabo, Anhwiaso, Adiemra, Hwiremoase, and Pipiiso.

kusaal: Ba kʋk la bɛ nɛ Adansi North District bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Adansi North District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Adejoké "Joké" Bakare anɛ na'asaara nɛ Nigeria nid ka o mi' dʋgib hali bɛ Africa ya'tʋona teŋin dugib ni.
english: Adejoké "Joké" Bakare is a British Nigerian-born chef specialising in West African cuisine.

kusaal: Bakare ba da dʋa o ka o nɔbignɛ Kaduna bɛ Nigeria.
english: Bakare was born and grew up in Kaduna, Nigeria.

kusaal: O ma da anɛ Yoruba nid ka o sa'am an Igbo nid, lin'nɛ da ke ka o zamis tens yela kon'ob kon'ob on da nobigid la.
english: She is Yoruba, her father is Yoruba and her mother is of Igbo ancestry, and she grew up in the northern part of Nigeria; which exposed her to a variety of cultural influences growing up.

kusaal: Yuma tusa ayi ne pisi ne ayi la, Time Out Magazine dim da put Chishuru ye diib zin'ig kanɛ an sʋm gaad zin'ig wusa bɛ London.
english: In 2022, Chishuru was named London's Best Restaurant by Time Out Magazine.

kusaal: Wadisa awai yuma tusa ayi ne pisi ne atan la, Bakare ne Chishuru da kɛŋi be Fitzrovia.
english: In September 2023, Bakare and Chishuru settled in Fitzrovia.

kusaal: On da zamisid nidib ti'ma yela bɛ Kaduna tɛŋ University la, o da sʋŋi o mɛŋnɛ ka kʋosid zimi nɛ kebis.
english: While studying biomedical sciences at [Ahamadu Bello University, Zaria, Kaduna state, she supported herself by running a fish-and-chips cart.

kusaal: Wadisa awai ni yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisi la, Bakare da yɔ'ɔg Chishuru, diib dʋgib zin'ig Brixton tɛŋ kane bɛ London la, o da dʋgidnɛ Africa ya'tʋona diib.
english: In September 2020, Bakare opened Chishuru, a pop-up restaurant in Brixton, London specialising in modern West African cuisine.

kusaal: Chishuru da yi zin'is kon'ob kon'ob London ka na'am nobigi o zin'ig line ba Brixton la.
english: Chishuru would appear in several other popup locations across London, before outgrowing their Brixton site.

kusaal: Wadisa ayi la yuma tusa ayi ne pisinɛ anaasi la, ba da tis Chishuru ne dʋgib kpɛ'ɛm Bakare piini Michelin-star.
english: On 5 February 2024, Chishuru and head chef Bakare were awarded a Michelin-star.

kusaal: O da kilim ninsabilis pua kanɛ paas ayi dʋnia wusa ka ba tis' o Michellin star dol France's Georgiana Viou yaʋŋ yuma tusa ayi ne pisi ne atan la.
english: She would become the second black woman in the world to be awarded a Michelin star after France's Georgiana Viou, who was awarded a Michelin star in 2023.

kusaal: onɛ an Wadmaani tis Nsuta-Kwaman-Beposo Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2021).
english: She has been the Member of Parliament representing the Nsuta-Kwaman-Beposo Constituency in the Ashanti Region since 7 January 2021.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adelaide Yaa Agyeiwaa Ntim nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne Nwadisa ayuobʋ la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 June 1971), o yinɛ Nsuta-Ashanti.
english: Adelaide Yaa Agyeiwaa Ntim was born on 24 June 1971 and hails from Nsuta-Ashanti.

kusaal: O mɔnrɛ Diplomanama ayi - Pharmacy Assistant (2017), and Basic Criminal Law (2019).
english: She holds two Diplomas - Pharmacy Assistant (2017), and Basic Criminal Law (2019).

kusaal: Ntim da yis onɛ da zin'i Nsuta-Kwaman-Beposo constituency kʋk la zug la, Kwame Asafu Adjei, yʋʋm tusa ay nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayuobʋ la ni, June 2020 New Patriotic Party (NPP) Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nidib la ni ka nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi, December 2020 vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Ntim ousted the then member of parliament for the Nsuta-Kwamang-Beposo constituency, Kwame Asafu Adjei, in the June 2020 New Patriotic Party (NPP) Parliamentary Primaries to become the party's candidate for the December 2020 election.

kusaal: O da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ atan, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisi nɛ ayi (23,622) dinɛ an pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne du'al ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (71.7%) ka o tiraan la, Newman Dapaah onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress(NDC) nid la paam vɔɔt tusa awai, kɔbistan nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (9,321) dinɛ an pisi nɛ anii du'al atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (28.3%).
english: She won the December 2020 parliamentary election with 23,622 votes representing 71.7% of the total votes cast, beating her opponent Newman Dapaah of the National Democratic Congress(NDC) who obtained 9,321 votes representing 28.3% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ Nwadisa ayuobʋ la ni, June 2021, Ntim da tis ligidi ka ba mɛ sakuya banɛ ka ba da mɛɛ paae suori bas Kruwi nɛ Asuafu bɛ Nsuta-Kwaman-Beposo Constituency.
english: In June 2021, Ntim funded abandoned school projects in Kruwi and Asuafu in the Nsuta-Kwaman-Beposo Constituency.

kusaal: O da lɛn tis Abrewa Anko nɛ Amangoase ku'om.
english: Communities such as Abrewa Anko and Amangoase also received water systems.

kusaal: Adelaide Yaa Agyeiwaa Ntim (du'anɛ 24 June 1971) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Adelaide Yaa Agyeiwaa Ntim (born 24 June 1971) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: Fassi ka o lieb Wadmaan la o da yisi o mɛŋ ye o lɛn ka' United States of America nid ya'asa yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la Nwadisa anii la ni, August 2020.
english: Prior to becoming a member of the Ghanaian Parliament, Ntim renounced her citizenship of the United States of America in August 2020.

kusaal: On da paae Wadmaan yin yiiga laa, o da anɛ kʋkgaan nya'andɔli la'askanɛ gɔsid Foreign Affairs ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Environment, Science and Technology yɛla.
english: As a first timer in Parliament, she serves as the Vice Chairperson and a Member of the Foreign Affairs and Environment, Science and Technology Committees in parliament respectively.

kusaal: Yʋma bɛdigʋ nii o da tʋmnɛ nɛ Brigade Concert Party nɛ Kusam Agoramba.
english: For over three decades she "worked at the cutting edge of popular theatre with the Brigade Concert Party and Kusam Agoromba".

kusaal: Buabeng da paas nɛ Workers' Brigade Concert Party, tʋmtʋmidib la sin'iŋi tʋm bi'el-bi'el nɛ ba, dinɛ anɛ buudi malima wa'ab dinɛ anɛ Atsiaghekor, Adowa, bɛɛ Takai ka yʋ'ʋm da kɛna pɛsigi o mɛŋi tʋm sini tʋʋma la anina.
english: Buabeng started as a part-time member of the Workers' Brigade Concert Party, performing traditional dances such as the Atsiaghekor, Adowa or Takai before becoming a full-time actress.

kusaal: Adenta anɛ sʋ'ʋlim yinne kanɛ bɛ Ghana wadmaanib yir kanɛ ka ti buon ye Parliament of Ghana la.
english: Adenta is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Adenta anɛ teŋ kane bɛ Adenta Municipa,l sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ bɛ Greater Accra sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Adenta is located in the Adentan Municipal District of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: ( Boundaries) Adenta sʋ'ʋlim kuk la bɛnɛ Adenta Municipal Assembly kanɛ bɛ Greater Accra sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana kpɛla.
english: The seat is located within the Adentan Municipal Assembly of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Adenta sʋ'ʋlim kuk la da bɛnɛ nɛ Ashaiman sʋ'ʋlim, 2024 burinya wadig la ni ka ba pʋdigi yisi Adenta yi Ashaiman sʋ'ʋlim ka di yʋ'ʋŋ bɛ di kɔn'ɔ.
english: It was formed prior to the 2004 December presidential and parliamentary elections by the division of the old Ashaiman constituency into the new Adenta and Ashaiman constituencies.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋid nid yinne ka o an ba wadmaan ka di yinɛ on paam vɔɔt ka di kanl gaadi o taaba la zug.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Aduana Football Club anɛ professional football club, kanɛ bɛ Dormaa Ahenkro, Bono Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Aduana Football Club (formerly Aduana Stars F.C) is a professional football club, based in Dormaa Ahenkro, Bono Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1984) la ni, nidiba anaasi banɛ yi Dormaa Ahenkro bɛ Bono Region ka Agya Donkor, onɛ an goldsmith ka da aan ba tuon gat ka Kofi Boahen, Iddrisa Issaka nɛ nid yinne onɛ ka ba pʋ buoli o yʋ'ʋr da sɔbi ba yʋda ye ba nwɛ' regional division 4 league bɛ Ghana, ani ka Aduana Stars Football Club da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu (1985).
english: In 1984, four natives of Dormaa Ahenkro, Bono Region led by Agya Donkor, a goldsmith and supported by Kofi Boahen, Iddrisa Issaka and one other unnamed person registered to play in the regional division 4 league of Ghana, bringing Aduana Football Club to birth in 1985.

kusaal: Aduana Stars da keŋi nwɛ' Ghana division 4 league la yʋma ayi ka naan nyaŋi keŋ nwɛ' division 3 league yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1986) la ni.
english: Aduana Football Club went on to play in the division 4 of the Ghana League for two years before gaining promotion to the Division 3 League in 1986.

kusaal: On da di'e la, kilab la da nwɛ' lower divisions ni yʋma bi'ela ka naan dʋ' ladda la ka ba'asʋg ka ba yʋ'ʋm bɛ Ghana Premier League yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai nwadisa anii la ni dabpiinɛ awai daar (19 August 2009) yiiga ban pin'il, Richard Addai da di goolkanɛ an naar gɛɛs Universal Stars la nya'aŋ ka di sʋŋi ba ka ba di 2–1 Baba Yara Sports Stadium la ni.
english: Subsequent to his take over, the club played in the lower divisions for some years moving up the ladder and finally getting promoted to the Ghana Premier League on 19 August 2009 for the first time in their history, after Richard Addai scored the winning goal in their last fixture against Universal Stars to help them to a 2–1 victory at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium.

kusaal: Sankaŋa Aduana Stars da di Ghana Premier League title nɔɔra ayi, yimmʋ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ni nɛ yinne yinne yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) la ni.
english: Within this period Aduana Football Club won the Ghana Premier League title two times, once in 2010 and once in 2017.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn di Ghana super cup yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2018) la ni ka da lɛn naae CAF Champions league la an Ghana champions nɔɔra ayi, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011) la ni nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la ni.
english: They also won the Ghana Super Cup in 2018 and competed in the CAF Champions League as champions of Ghana on two occasions, in 2011 and 2018.

kusaal: 17 October 2009, Aduana Stars da nwɛ' ba mak tita'ar nɛ Heart of Lions, Agyeman Badu I Pak la bɛ Dormaa la yit Richard Addae da nwɛ' si'el mitpisyɔpɔi nɛ atan la ni la (73rd-minute).
english: On 17 October 2009, Aduana Football Club won their first top flight in a match against Heart of Lions at the Agyeman Badu I Park in Dormaa through Richard Addae's 73rd-minute strike.

kusaal: Ba da dii ba yiiga title yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai nɛ piiga la ni la (2009–10) team la da naae siizin la ka an team kanɛ di goolnam bi'ela League la pʋʋgin la, ka da di goolnam piinɛ awa (19 goals) maknam pistan (30 matches) pʋʋgin.
english: They first won the title in 2009–10 when the team ended the season as the fewest-scoring side in the League, setting a world record for least productive champions with 19 goals in 30 matches.

kusaal: Turkish Süper Lig side da lieb champions 1979–80 nɛ goolnam pisi nɛ anu (25 goals) maknam pistan (30 matches) pʋʋgin.
english: The Turkish Süper Lig side became champions in 1979–80 with 25 goals in 30 matches (average of 0.8333).

kusaal: league kanɛ da mɔr 16 clubs dinɛ da kɛ ka ba paam 30 matches la, Aduana Stars da di 15 matches, drew 8 ka gʋ'ʋŋ 7, ba da di Obuase Ashanti Gold S.C ka di'e title la dɔlisid head-to-head dinɛ ka Ghana premier league board (PLB) da nɔk ba ya'a nwɛ' ka sɔ' pʋ di o tiraana, kilabnama ayi la da paam 53 points yi 30 matches banɛ ka ba nwɛ' paae siizin la naar.
english: In a league of 16 clubs that generated 30 matches, Aduana Football Club won 15 matches, drew 8, and lost 7 beating Obuase Ashanti Gold S.C to the title by the head-to-head margin which had been adopted by the Ghana premier league board (PLB) in case of a tie, after both clubs garnered 53 points from all the 30 matches played at the end of the season.

kusaal: Ba da di 2017/2018 Ghana Premier League la ban da nwɛ' 15 home matches siizin la ni ka sɔ' pʋ di ba ka da lɛm paam 2–1 victory ban nɛ Elmina Sharks ka nwɛ' Nana Agyeman Badu Park bɛ Dormaa-Ahenkro la.
english: They won the 2017/2018 Ghana Premier League after going undefeated in 15 home matches within the season with one game to spare after a 2–1 victory over Elmina Sharks at Nana Agyeman Badu Park at Dormaa-Ahenkro.

kusaal: Ghana coach Yussif Abubakar onɛ ka ba da ye onɛ zab zab sʋŋ la da mɔr team la keŋ di league title la.
english: The team was led by the late Ghanaian coach Yussif Abubakar who described their triumph at that time as a well hard fought league title victory.

kusaal: Ba da naae siizin la nɛ 6-point gap ban nɛ team kanɛ paasi ayi la, West African Football Academy (WAFA), mɔr 16 wins, 9 draws ka gʋ'ʋŋ 6.
english: They completed the season with a 6-point gap between them and the second place team West African Football Academy (WAFA), with 16 wins, 9 draws and 6 loses.

kusaal: Daaʋŋ bɛdegʋ paae Ghana premier league la din yi 2017 dɔlisid ban da widig GFA June 2018, 2018 league season da pʋ nwɛ' COVID-19 pandemic dinɛ da kɛ ka 2019–20 league la mɛ da gu'oe.
english: After several distractions to the Ghana Premier League from 2017 due to the dissolution of the GFA in June 2018, the 2018 league season was abandoned and the uprising of the deadly COVID-19 pandemic which also caused the 2019–20 league to be canceled abruptly.

kusaal: 2020–21 season da pin'ilnɛ November 2020.
english: The 2020–21 season started in November 2020.

kusaal: February 2020, Ghana coach Paa Kwesi Fabin da lieb head coach ka lɛm paae siizin la tensʋkʋ ye.
english: In February 2020, Ghanaian coach Paa Kwesi Fabin was signed as head coach who resigned midway through the season.

kusaal: March 2021 ni, kilab la da gaŋ Joseph Asare Bediako onɛ an coach kʋdʋgʋ tis Berekum Chelsea ye o naae siizin la.
english: In March 2021, the club appointed Joseph Asare Bediako a former coach of Berekum Chelsea to finish the season.

kusaal: Kilab la da naae 2020–21 season 4th yi 18 club ka da paam 54 points.
english: The club finished the 2020–21 season 4th out of 18 clubs and amassed 54 points.

kusaal: Aduana Stars anɛ Aduana tuŋ la zuraani sʋ'ɔe ka mɔr nimbanɛ gɔsidi di ka ba an na'abanɛ bɛ tɛɛns banɛ bɛ Bono region nɛ region sieba nwɛnɛ Kumawu nɛ Akwamu.
english: Aduana Football Club is a traditional club led by the head of the Aduana clan and has a board that comprises chiefs from towns in the Bono region and other regions like Kumawu, Agogo, Tepa, Bomaa, Abesim, Chiraa, Akwamu etc. The lifetime board chairman of the club is the Dormaa hene who doubles as the Aduana Piesie "Head of the Aduana Akan Clan".

kusaal: Kilab la nya'ad Ghanaian Premier League ni.
english: The club is competing in the Ghanaian Premier League.

kusaal: Di kɛ ka di kpɛn' labakʋda ni ye di Ghana Premier League la ban da keŋi ba yiiga nwɛ'ɛb la nɛ diib pisnu (53 points).
english: It made history by winning the Ghana Premier League at their first attempt with 53 points.

kusaal: Di da lieb kilab kanɛ paasi awa di Ghana Premier League di yʋma pisnu nɛ anaasi (54-year) saŋa.
english: It became the ninth club to win the Ghana Premier League in its 54-year-old history.

kusaal: Dɔlisid zanbin kanɛ an Aduana clan zanbin ka ba da nɔki maal kilab la, di da nar ye ba keŋ sɔs suori yi Aduanahene (onɛ an Na'atita'ari tis Aboabo no 3), ka o da siaki tisi ba suor.
english: Due to the decision to adopt the official emblem of the Aduana clan, the group had to seek for the permission from the Aduanahene (who was a paramount chief of Aboabo no 3), which he accepted.

kusaal: Ligidi ka'alim zug ka kilab la da lɛbid nya'aŋ la, da kɛ ka Omanhene of Dormaa, Osagyefo Oseadeeyo Dr.
english: Due to financial issues and the retrogressing of the club, led to the decision of the Omanhene of Dormaa Osagyefo Oseadeeyo Dr. Nana Agyeman Badu II who was also a High Court Judge in Tema and became an Appeal Court judge as of August 2025, to take over the management of the club.

kusaal: Nana Agyeman Badu II onɛ lɛn an High Court Judge bɛ Tema la, da gban'e ye o tiak kilab la kpɛɛmnam.
english: Due to financial issues and the retrogressing of the club, led to the decision of the Omanhene of Dormaa Osagyefo Oseadeeyo Dr. Nana Agyeman Badu II who was also a High Court Judge in Tema and became an Appeal Court judge as of August 2025, to take over the management of the club.

kusaal: Aduana's yiiga Ghana Premier League gool la, Richard Addai da di.
english: Aduana's first Ghana Premier League goal was scored by Richard Addai.

kusaal: 2017 ka kilab la da paae tuon ken ya'as ban da naae runners-up nɛ Wa All stars yʋʋmkanɛ gaad la.
english: The second triumph was 2017 after the team had finished as runners-up to Wa All stars in the previous year.

kusaal: Team la nɛ Herbert Addo da bak taaba yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne nwadisa anii (August 2011).
english: They were led by Ghanaian coach Herbert Addo, who helped them set the record of being the first newly promoted team to win the league.

kusaal: Din yi January 2021, Aduana Manager nam ban kpɛn' Ghana Premier League ni 2009.
english: In March 2021, the club appointed Joseph Asare Bediako a former coach of Berekum Chelsea to finish the season.

kusaal: Afadzato Anyigbe) anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ paas sʋ'ʋlʋm nam bam piina anii banɛ bɛ Ghana, Volta Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Afadzato Anyigbe) is one of the eighteen districts in Volta Region, Ghana.

kusaal: saŋ si'an la li da paasnɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm tita'ar la Hohoe District la ni nwadis atan' la dabisim piiga yʋʋma1989, hali ti paae saŋkanɛ ka ba daa ti pʋdʋg southern sʋ'ʋlʋm la pʋdi li ye Afadzato South District nwadis ayuobʋ la dabisim piisi nɛ anii (28) yʋʋma 2012 la ni; ka ala ka zi'in banɛ da kpɛlim la da kpɛlim an Hohoe Municipal District.
english: Originally it was formerly part of the then-larger Hohoe District on 10 March 1989, until the southern part of the district was split off to create Afadzato South District on 28 June 2012; thus the remaining portion has been retained as Hohoe Municipal District.

kusaal: district assembul la kpi'enɛ nɛ northern baba Volta Region sʋ'ʋlʋm ka mɔr Ve Golokwati ka li aan li temputita'ar.
english: The district assembly is located in the northern part of Volta Region and has Ve Golokwati as its capital town.

kusaal: District la tɔndnɛ tʋntɔndʋŋ nɛ Hohoe Municipal n lɛb ya-datiʋŋ, Kpando Municipal n lɛb ya-tuon, ka tɔnd nɛ ya-nya'aŋ nɛ Republic of Togo ka ya-dakɔbʋg n lɛb Ho West District nɛ ya-dakɔbʋg Dayi District mɛn.
english: The District shares boundaries with Hohoe Municipal District to the north, Kpando Municipal District to the west, to the east with the Togo and to the south with Ho West District and South Dayi District respectively.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlʋm la mɔr nidib hali pamm bɛ teŋkpɛmis la ni nidib wʋʋ(81.3%) mamis nɛ nidib bam (18.7%) banɛ bɛ tempʋʋsin la.
english: The District has majority of its people in the rural areas (83.6%) compared to (16.4%) in the urban areas.

english: Afigya Kwabre North is located in the Afigya Kwabre North District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Agnes Asangalisa Chigabatia (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yuobʋ nwadis piiga la dabpisi daar, October 20, 1956) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd pʋ'ak ka an wadmaan kʋdʋgʋ tis Builsa North Constituency.
english: Agnes Asangalisa Chigabatia (20 October 1956 – 9 January 2024) was a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the parliament for Builsa North Constituency.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Agnes Chigabatia nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yuobʋ nwadis piiga la dabpisi daar, (October 20, 1956) Chuchuliga bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Agnes Chigabatia was born on 20 October 1956 at Chuchuliga, Gold Coast (now Upper East Region, Ghana).

kusaal: O da maali o middle school education nɛ Adda Middle School bɛ Navrongo la nɛ Ayieta Middle School bɛ Sandema.
english: She acquired her middle school education at Adda Middle School in Navrongo and Ayieta Middle School in Sandema.

kusaal: Francis Girls' Senior High School, Jirapa.
english: Chigabatia later had her secondary school education at St. Francis Girls' Senior High School, Jirapa.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi o sakur la keŋ Accra Polytechnic maal Advance Level in Catering Certificate.
english: She furthered her education at the Accra Polytechnic where she acquired a Certificate at the Advanced Level in Catering.

kusaal: Agnes Chigabatia da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la (2004 parliamentary elections) Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party ka di.
english: Agnes Chigabatia contested in the 2004 parliamentary elections on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party which she won.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa yuobʋ, kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ (6,160) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pistan' nɛ tan du'al pisyɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (33.70%).
english: She pulled a total vote of 6,160 representing 33.70%.

kusaal: O da tʋmnɛ yʋma anaasi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu yʋʋmpaal nwadig daba yɔpɔi daar (7 January 2005) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai yʋʋmpaal nwadig daba yɔpɔi daar (7 January 2009).
english: She served for a period of four years (7 January 2005 – 7 January 2009).

kusaal: Sankaŋa ni ka Agnes da Deputy Minister tis Upper East Region.
english: Within this same period, Chigabatia was also the Deputy Minister for the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt Chigabatia ka o lieb wadmaani tis Builsa North constituency bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la yiiga nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni (2004 Ghanaian general elections).
english: Chigabatia was elected as the member of parliament for the Builsa North constituency of the Upper East Region of Ghana for the first time in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O constituency da paasnɛ wadmaannib kʋgʋsi ayi yi kʋgʋs piinɛ atan (13) banɛ ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party da di Upper East Region.
english: Her constituency was a part of the 2 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Upper East Region.

kusaal: The New Patriotic Party da di kʋgʋs bɛdigʋ dinɛ kanli an kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ nii (128) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan (230) pʋʋgin.
english: The New Patriotic Party won a majority total of 128 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa ayuobʋ, kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ (6,160) yi vɔɔt tusa piinɛ nii, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ tan' (18,273) pʋʋgin.
english: She was elected with 6,160 votes out of 18,273 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas Thomas Akum-Yong onɛ bɛ Peoples' National Convention, Awontiirim Ataboadey Timothy onɛ bɛ National Democratic Congress nɛ Abaayiak Ayulim Grace onɛ bɛ Convention People's Party.
english: She was elected over Thomas Akum-Yong of the Peoples' National Convention, Awontiirim Ataboadey Timothy of the National Democratic Congress and Abaayiak Ayulim Grace of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Bama da zɛmnɛ nɛ vɔɔt pistan' nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (31%), vɔɔt pistan nɛ tan du'ali ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (33.6%) nɛ yinne du'al ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.7%) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: These were equivalent to 31%, 33.6% and 1.7% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Chigabatia anɛ onɛ gɔsid diib dʋgʋb yɛla (caterer).
english: Chigabatia was a caterer by profession.

kusaal: Agnes da kɔ'ɔŋi o wadmaan kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii vɔɔtʋg la ni (2008 election) ka Timothy Awotiirim Ataboadey da di ka bas o.
english: Chigabatia lost her position as member of parliament during the 2008 election where she lost to Timothy Awotiirim Ataboadey.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zugʋ nya' ka di.
english: Her constituency was a part of the 2 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Nɛ' da zɛmnɛ vɔɔt pistan' nɛ tan du'al ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (33.7%).
english: This was equivalent to 33.7% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Chigabatia anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Agnes Chigabatia was a Christian.

kusaal: Bama da paamnɛ tusa anu, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnu nɛ yɔpɔi (5,657), tusa yuobʋ, kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yɔpɔi (6,147) nɛ vɔɔt kɔbistan' nɛ wai (309) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: These obtained 5,657, 6,147 and 309 votes respectively out of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Agnes Naa Momo Lartey anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Agnes Naa Momo Lartey is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pis (2020) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ka di Krowor Constituency sʋ'ʋlim kʋk la.
english: She contested in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election and won the parliamentary seat for the Krowor Constituency.

kusaal: Naa Momo da pin'ili o pɔlitiks tʋʋm yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni, 2000.
english: Naa Momo began her political career in 2000.

kusaal: din yi sankan, o da zi'en Krowor pu'ab nɔba zug Municipal Assembly la ni.
english: Since then, she has served as an assembly woman and a presiding member of the Krowor Municipal Assembly.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ Nwadis piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋg la (December 2016), o da zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la zugʋ nya' Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ka Elizabeth Afoley Quaye onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la di ka bas o.
english: In December 2016, she contested in the 2016 Ghanaian General Election under the ticket of the National Democratic Congress and lost to Elizabeth Afoley Quaye of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ yinne, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnu (41,850) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ anu du'ali pisnii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (55.80%).
english: She polled 41,850 votes which represents 55.80% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas onɛ zin'i kʋk la zug la, Elizabeth Afoley Quaye onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la, Hannah Bortey onɛ an Ghana Union Movement nid.
english: She was elected over incumbent Elizabeth Afoley Quaye of the New Patriotic Party and Hannah Bortey of the Ghana Union Movement.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa anaasi la dabpiinɛ ayuobʋ (16 April 1976).
english: She was born on 16 April 1976.

kusaal: O yinɛ Greater Accra tenkanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Krowor.
english: She holds qualifications from the University of Professional Studies, Accra, the University of Cape Coast, and Central University College, among other institutions.

kusaal: O da lɛn zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la zugʋ nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi, 2020 Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la.
english: She contested again in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election under the ticket of the National Democratic Congress and won.

kusaal: Nidiba ayi bama da paamnɛ tusa pistan nɛ ayi, kɔbis yuobʋ nɛ anaasi (32,604) nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anu (545) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ atan du'al pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (43.47%) nɛ nɛɛm du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan (0.73%).
english: Representing 43.47% and 0.73% respectively of total valid votes cast.
