kusaal: Region la da buaki yinɛ Brong Ahafo Region yatuona-datiʋŋand ka li da anɛ ka na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon New Patriotic Party da ziel nɔɔr ye ba die na'am ka pʋdʋgʋ li la.
english: The region was carved out of the south-eastern part of the Brong Ahafo Region and was in fulfilment of a campaign promise made by the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa yi' nɛ piinɛ ayuobu (2016) Ghanaian general election votug la, ka onɛ da an Nana Akufo-Addo da tis nɔɔr ye ba ya'a vɔɔti tis o, o na gɔs ka maal Region paala bɛdegʋ yi Region banɛ pʋn dɛŋim bɛ la ni ka li kɛ ka tɛŋ wʋsa nyaŋi sʋŋi ba mɛŋ.
english: Prior to the 2016 Ghanaian general election, the then candidate Nana Akufo-Addo declared that when elected, he would explore the possibility of creating new regions out of some of the existing regions in Ghana in order to bring government closer to citizens.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ da gɔsi maal regions la da anɛ sʋ'ʋlim paam kanɛ da an Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development, ka li tuongat an Girimadaan Daniel Botwe.
english: The execution of plans for the creation of the regions was assigned to the newly created Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development which is under the leadership of Hon. Dan Botwe, the Government of Ghana minister charged with the responsibility of supervising the creation of new regions in Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa yi' nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi, nwadis atan' (March 2017), ka ministry la da yis gbaʋŋi pa'al region nwa maalig nɛ o taaba wʋsa gbana kɛŋ tis Council of State.
english: In March 2017, the ministry sent the blueprint for the creation of the region, along with others, to the Council of State.

kusaal: Council la da la'as la'asa ka li tʋʋg wʋʋ nɔɔr pistan nɛ ayuobu gbaʋŋ la yiib saŋa ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi, nwadis anii (August 2017).
english: The council met over 36 times from the time of submission to August 2017.

kusaal: Nwa' anɛ yɛ, region la da pʋdʋgnɛ MMDA's nam ayuobu (ka li anɛ Metropolitan nam kai, Municipal nam atan' nɛ Assembly nam atan').
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into six MMDA's (made up of 0 Metropolitan, 3 Municipal and 3 Ordinary Assemblies).

kusaal: District, Municipal bɛɛ Metropolitan Assembly, bɛnɛ Chief Executive nʋ'ʋsin, one zie gɔmena nɔba zug amaa ka li paŋ bɛnɛ presiding member one ka Assembly members gaŋ o ba mɛŋ.
english: Each District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly, is administered by a Chief Executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an Assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Nidib banɛ daa na nyaŋi vot daa anɛ tusa kɔbis tan' nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbiga nɛ anii (307,108), nidib tusa kɔbis yi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyuobu nɛ pisyuobu nɛ atan' (277,663) da vɔɔt ka nidib tusa kɔbis yi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobu, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobu nɛ atan' (276,763) ka lin anɛ piswai nɛ awai nɛ pʋdigir ayuobu nɛ anii kɔbʋga pʋʋgin (99.68 per cent) da siak yɛ ba maalim region paalig la.
english: Out of a total of 307,108 registered votes, 277,663 took part in the referendum, with 276,763 (99.68 per cent) voting in favour of the creation of the new region.

kusaal: Ba da maal region la nɛ yʋʋm tusa yi' nɛ piinɛ awai, nwadis ayi' dabisa piinɛ atan' daar (13th February 2019) ka li dɔl nɛ wada kanɛ an kɔbʋga nɛ piinɛ anaasi (Constitutional Instrument 114).
english: The region was created on 13 February 2019 by Constitutional Instrument 114.

kusaal: Ahafo mɔr la'asʋma wʋʋ sanlima (Gold), pielis (Diamonds) nɛ daad (Timber) bɛdegʋ nɛ la'asieba.
english: The Region is endowed with rich natural resources such as Gold, Diamonds, Timber.

kusaal: Newmont Gold Ghana Limited banɛ tuud sanlima ka dunia wʋsa mi' ba yɛla, tuud samlima bɛ Kenyasi nɛ Yamfo sʋ'ʋlimnam.
english: Newmont Gold Ghana Limited, which is one of the biggest mining companies in the world, currently has its mining operations in Kenyasi and Yamfo zones.

kusaal: Ltd, Supremo-wood processing Co LTD, ban wʋsa bɛnɛ Mim sʋ'ʋlim, Ahafo.
english: Notable among the timber companies in the region are Ayum Forest Products Co. Ltd, Exbo wood Co. Ltd, Ocean-wood Co. Ltd, and Supremo-wood processing Co LTD, all in Mim, Ahafo.

kusaal: Asʋ'ʋ-m-mɛŋ tʋʋma yinne an Mim Cashew & Agric Products company LTD bɛ Mim, Ahafo sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The major agro-processing company in the region is the Mim Cashew & Agric Products company LTD, located at Mim, Ahafo.

kusaal: Ahafo Region Ya-datiʋŋ titɔdig anɛ Bono region, ka li Ya-ya'aŋ an Ashanti Region, ka li Ya-tuona an Bono region, ka li Ya-dagɔbʋg an Western North Region ka li mɔr district nam ayuobu.
english: The Ahafo Region is bordered on the north by the Bono Region, on the east by the Ashanti Region, on the west by the Bono Region, and on the south by the Western North Region and is made up of 6 districts.

kusaal: Yʋʋm wʋsa nwadis anaasi kɛŋ paae naar nwadig la an ʋʋn (December and April is the dry season).
english: Between December and April is the dry season.

kusaal: Sɛɛng saŋa anɛ lin yin nwadis ayɔpɔi (July) keŋ paae piinɛ yinne ni la (November) ka saa ɛɛnti ni' wʋʋ kɔbis yɔpɔi nɛ pisnu paae tusir nɛ pisnu (750 to 1050 mm or 30 to 40 inches).
english: The wet season is between about July and November, with an average annual rainfall of 750 to 1050 mm (30 to 40 inches).

kusaal: Li tʋʋlig bɛɛ li ma'ar anɛ wʋʋ 14 °C (59 °F) yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ 40 °C (104 °F) nintaŋ.
english: The temperatures can vary between 14 °C (59 °F) at night and 40 °C (104 °F) during the day.

kusaal: Region la mɔr wada ka mɛ tʋm nwɛnɛ region piinɛ anu bama la tʋm si'em Ghana la.
english: The Ahafo Region is a new region in Ghana, created on 27 December 2018, with Goaso as its capital.

kusaal: Government of Ghana , banɛ gɔsid regions nam maalig nɛ ba tʋʋma an si'em wʋsa Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The execution of plans for the creation of the regions was assigned to the newly created Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development which is under the leadership of Hon. Dan Botwe, the Government of Ghana minister charged with the responsibility of supervising the creation of new regions in Ghana.

kusaal: Linɛ da an naar linɛ da pa'al region la maalug yɛla da anɛ ye nidib banɛ da bɛ sʋ'ʋlim kan la da vɔtnɛ bas suor, yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ anii, nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27 December 2018).
english: The final stage for the creation of the region was decided through a referendum by the people within the catchment of the new region on 27 December 2018.

kusaal: Region la tʋmmi li tʋʋma dɔlisidnɛ local government system.
english: The political administration of the region is through the local government system.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa yi' nɛ piinɛ anii, nwadis samanpiid nwadig la dabisa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (27 December 2018) votug la da siak ye ba maalim Ahafo Region.
english: A referendum on 27 December 2018 approved the creation of the Ahafo Region.

kusaal: Ka nidib kɔbis yi' nɛ pisi nɛ anu (225) da pʋ vot ka li dɔl suorɛ, ka lin anɛ zaalim du'ali anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.08%) banɛ da vot la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: 675 (0.24 per cent) rejected the motion, and 225 rejected ballots represented 0.08% of total votes cast.

kusaal: Goaso ka ba da gaŋ ye li an region paal nwa' tempʋtita'ar.
english: Goaso was announced as the capital of the new region.

kusaal: Ahafo anɛ zin'ig yinne banɛ mɔr tiis Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, ba mɔr tiis bɛdegʋ.
english: Ahafo Region, which is one of the forest belts in Ghana, has a lot of forest reserves.

kusaal: Daad tʋmtʋmnib region la sieba an Ayum Forest Products Co.
english: Notable among the timber companies in the region are Ayum Forest Products Co. Ltd, Exbo wood Co. Ltd, Ocean-wood Co. Ltd, and Supremo-wood processing Co LTD, all in Mim, Ahafo.

kusaal: Ahafo Region ka diib bɛdegʋ yitna tisid Ghana dim.
english: Ahafo Region is known to be the breadbasket of Ghana.

kusaal: Ahafo Region anɛ zin'ig yinne kanɛ mɔr tiis Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, ba mɔr tiis bɛdegʋ ka li tɛŋ la mɔr kʋ'ʋlim nɛ mɔɔd ka li kas-kas anɛ savanna linɛ mɔr tiis banɛ tun'e sawak ka ba sieba an tɛ'ɛs bɛɛ acacias.
english: The Ahafo Region is part of the forest belt of Ghana and has vegetation consisting predominantly of fertile soil and grassland, especially savanna with clusters of drought-resistant trees such as baobabs or acacias.

kusaal: Amaa sisiepiilig saŋa linɛ yi Sahara la da'adnɛ yʋʋm naar nwadig ti paae yʋʋm paal nwadis ayi' pin'ilig.
english: However, the hot Harmattan wind from the Sahara blows frequently between December and the beginning of February.

kusaal: Ahmed Errachidi (ka ba lɛm bʋon o ye Ahmed Errachidi) yitnɛ Morocco ka na'asaatɛŋ dim Guantanamo Bay dim da gba'e o Cuba ka pʋ yel on maal siel la.
english: Ahmed Rashidi (also known as Ahmed Errachidi) is a citizen of Morocco who was held in extrajudicial detention in the United States Guantanamo Bay detainment camps, in Cuba.

kusaal: Rashidi pi'yam Clive Stafford Smith da sobi niŋ The Guardian gbana ni wadisa ayʋobo dabis piiga ne anaasi daar yʋma tusa ayi ne ayʋobo piandi pa'an na'asaatɛŋ di'mi maal Guantanamo nidiba atan la siem ka ba da kʋ ba mɛŋ wadisa ayʋobo dabis piiga daar yʋma tusa ayi ne ayuobo la.
english: Rashidi's lawyer, Clive Stafford Smith, wrote an article in The Guardian on June 14, 2006, commenting on the American reaction to the three Guantanamo detainees who committed suicide on June 10, 2006.

kusaal: O da pian Colonel Michael Bumgarner da mɔɔl ye o na tʋm zab'zabidib anu ka ba nɔk paŋɛ yo'og sanriga la ni ka yis Rashidi la'ad bane ka o ye' la wusa.
english: In particular he commented on Colonel Michael Bumgarner's announcement that he would send a five-man riot squad in to conduct a Forcible Cell Entry to forcibly strip Rashidi of his brown coveralls.

kusaal: Smith da lɛm yel ye Rashidi mɔr ne zuglɛbin ne pʋtenda yela bedigʋ ban da mɔr o kɛŋ camp la ni la.
english: Smith said that Rashidi had already had mental and emotional problems prior to being sent to the camp.

kusaal: Ahmed Ibrahim anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yir kanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anii la tis Banda Constituency bɛ Bono Region la Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug.
english: Ahmed Ibrahim is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Banda Constituency in the Bono Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Deputy Minority Chief Whip Ghana wadmaanib yir la.
english: He was the Deputy Minority Chief Whip in the Parliament of Ghana until his nomination as Minister of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a brahim nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi Nwadisa anu la daba ayuobʋ daar (6 May 1974), Banda Ahenkro bɛ Bono Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Ibrahim was born on 6 May 1974, in Banda Ahenkro in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ chief executive officer tis Flamingo Publications (Ghana) Limited.
english: He was the chief executive officer of Flamingo Publications (Ghana) Limited.

kusaal: ba da vɔɔti tis o yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anii (2008) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔdʋgin o sʋ'ʋlim la ni.
english: Ibrahim began his political career in 2009 after being declared the winner of the 2008 Ghanaian General Elections for his constituency.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka o keŋ paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anu la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni yʋʋm paal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (7 January 2009).
english: He was then elected into the 5th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana on 7 January 2009.

kusaal: O da naae o yiiga tʋʋma la, Ibrahim da gban'e ye o lɛn keŋ yinne paas yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' la (2013) ka di ka bas Joe Danquah ka lɛn zin'in kʋk la zug ya'as.
english: After the completion of his first term in office, Ibrahim decided to run for another term in 2013 and defeated Joe Danquah to retain his seat.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anu la ni (2015), o da nyi'a ya ka di Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg Wadmaanib vɔɔdʋg la Banda constituency bɛ Bono Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: In 2015 he contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Banda constituency in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di o sʋ'ʋlim kʋk la yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔdʋg la ni, paam vɔɔt kal tusa ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi (6,167) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi' du'al atan' kɔbiga pʋʋgin (52.03%) ka onɛ nyi'ad nɛ o la mɛ paam vɔɔt kal tusa anu nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyuobʋ (5,660) dinɛ an pisnaasi ne ayɔpɔi du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (47.76%).
english: He won this parliamentary seat during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections by getting 6,167 votes representing 52.03% against his opponent 5,660 votes representing 47.76%.

kusaal: Ibrahim paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Special Budget; ka lɛn paas Communications Committee; Local Government and Rural Development Committee; nɛ Business Committee.
english: Ibrahim is a member of the Special Budget Committee; a member of the Communications Committee; a member of the Local Government and Rural Development Committee; and a member of the Business Committee.

kusaal: Ibrahim da keŋ University of Ghana maali o bachelor's degree in Political Science and Philosophy yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ yinne la ni (2001).
english: Ibrahim was born on 6 May 1974, in Banda Ahenkro in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ibrahim pin'ili o pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: Ibrahim began his political career in 2009 after being declared the winner of the 2008 Ghanaian General Elections for his constituency.

kusaal: Ibrahim anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Ibrahim is a Christian.

kusaal: O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biig yinne.
english: He is married with one child.

kusaal: Di anɛ tɛmpʋtita'ar kanɛ bɛ Ajumako-Enyan-Esiam district la.
english: It is the capital of Ajumako-Enyan-Esiam district.

kusaal: Di ane zin' kanɛ ka nidib bɛrigʋ mi, bɔzugɔ, Ottobah Cugoano, onɛ ka ba da karʋ n yis tɛŋin la 18th century saŋa.
english: It is famous for being the birthplace of Ottobah Cugoano, an abolitionist of the 18th century.

kusaal: Sakur tita'ar kani ka ba buon ye University of Education, Winneba (Ajumako Campus) la bɛnɛ anina.
english: The University of Education, Winneba (Ajumako Campus) is situated there.

kusaal: Nim banɛ bɛ tɛŋin anɛ Fante dim m bɛ ani ka li ya' kanɛ ye Breman Essiam dim banɛ yit Breman Kumasi baba la.
english: The natives are Fante except the people of Breman Essiam who trace their lineage to Breman, near Kumasi.

kusaal: Ba tʋʋm anɛ kpaadib tʋʋma, ka ba mɔr da'as ka li bɛ Breman Essiam nɛ Ajumako.
english: The main occupation of the people is farming with emerging markets at Breman Essiam and Ajumako.

kusaal: Ba sʋ'ʋlim la tuongat Parliament nananna anɛ Cassiel Ato Forson.
english: The current Member of parliament of the district is Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson who hails from Ajumako Bisease.

kusaal: Ajumako/Enyan/Essiam anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm kanɛ paas ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni mɛn.
english: Ajumako-Enyan-Essiam is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: District assembul la da bɛnɛ northeast la baba linɛ bɛ Central Region la ka ba mɔri Ajumako linɛ aan ba temputita'ar.
english: Ajumako-Enyam-Essiam is located in the Ajumako/Enyan/Essiam district of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di tempʋtita'ar bɛnɛ Ajumako/Enyan/Essiam district dinɛ bɛ Central Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Ajumako/Enyan/Essiam district of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Akan constituency anɛ Ghana Parliament constituency nam la yinne.
english: The Akan constituency is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Di dagɔbʋkg anɛ Nkwanta South constituency bɛ Nkwanta District la, tuon anɛ Krachi East bɛ Krachi East District, datiʋŋ anɛ Jasikan District ka li nya'aŋ an Ghana nɛ Togo titɔdig.
english: To the north is the Nkwanta South constituency in the Nkwanta District, to the west, the Krachi East in the Krachi East District, to the south the Jasikan District and to the east, the Ghana - Togo border.

kusaal: Constituency la da bɛnɛ Volta Region ka ba naam pʋdig Region paala dɔlisid yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi (2018) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: The constituency was originally located within the Volta Region of Ghana until new Regions were created following the December 2018 referendum.

kusaal: Di bɛ nɛ Kadjebi districti bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: It is located in the Kadjebi district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛ nɛ Kadjebi districti bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: The constituency is located within the Kadjebi district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Lydia Akanvariba Lamisi anɛ Ghana laafi tʋmtʋm (awuriba), ka mɛ an onɛ nwɛ'ɛd pɔlitiks.
english: Akanvariva Lydia Lamisi (also known as Lydia Akanvariba Lamisi and Lydia Lamisi Akanvariva) is a Ghanaian nurse, a politician and a member of parliament for the Tempane Constituency of the Kusaug traditional area in the upper east region.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ Nasaa nwadig October dabsʋm ayɔpɔi, 1973 yʋʋmin.
english: She was born on 7 October, 1973.She was born at Tempane and she is a Christian.

kusaal: O paati anɛ National Democratic Congress bɛɛ NDC.
english: Lamisi is a member of the National Democratic Congress ( NDC).

kusaal: Nannanna, o anɛ Tempaan sʋ'ʋlim MP Wada Maalʋg Yir dinɛ paas anii (8th Parliament) Ghana Republic anaasi la ni (4th Republic).
english: In December 2020, she was elected member of Parliament for the Tempane Constituency after she competed in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election under the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da pin'íli o pɔlitics nwɛ'ɛbnɛ Nasaa yʋʋm 2020 votʋk la ni ka di.
english: She contested in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election at her constituency and won the parliamentary seat.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Lydia Akanvariba nɛ Nasaa nwadig piiga, li daba ayɔpɔi 1973 yʋʋm la ni.
english: Akanvariva Lydia Lamisi (also known as Lydia Akanvariba Lamisi and Lydia Lamisi Akanvariva) is a Ghanaian nurse, a politician and a member of parliament for the Tempane Constituency of the Kusaug traditional area in the upper east region.

kusaal: Ani ka madam Akanvariba pin'il pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛm ka zin'in primaries la di pisyuobʋ nɛ awai vaar kɔbiga pʋʋgin (69%).
english: Akanvariva Lydia Lamisi (also known as Lydia Akanvariba Lamisi and Lydia Lamisi Akanvariva) is a Ghanaian nurse, a politician and a member of parliament for the Tempane Constituency of the Kusaug traditional area in the upper east region.

kusaal: Nidib tusa pisi nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ awai (20,939) da vɔti tis o, ka li pa'al ye kɔbiga pʋʋgin, o da nyɛnɛ vaar pisnu nɛ a yuobʋ(56.0%) ka nidib tusa pii nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi' voti tis Joseph Dindiok Akpemka ka li pa'al ye ɔbiga pʋʋgin, oda paamnɛ vaar pisnaasi nɛ anaasi (44.0).
english: She polled 20,939 votes which represents 56.0% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Akatsi North kpi'enɛ nɛ Akatsi North district linɛ bɛ Ghana Volta Region la.
english: Akatsi North is located in the Akatsi North district of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Akatsi North Constituency anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ paas Sʋ'ʋlʋm banɛ paas ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la.
english: Akatsi North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2012 la ni ka tʋʋma lʋgʋr dim banɛ gɔsidi ti Ghana vɔt yɛla la da yɔ'ɔgi li kati wa'ae vɔt la yɛla la.
english: It was created in 2012 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana prior to the Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Yiiga vɔt la da pin'ili nwadis piina ayi la yʋʋma 2012 la Ghana wʋsa vɔt la ni.
english: It was created in 2012 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana prior to the Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nidi da di nɛ vɔtnam bam 8,908 pa'al ye onɛ mɔr worɔk.
english: The National Democratic Congress candidate won the seat with an 8,908 majority.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Abuakwa North Municipal District bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana.
english: The constituency is located in the Abuakwa North Municipal District of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Samuel Kwadwo Amoaka da an constituency la wadmaan din nɔk yʋʋmpaal nwadig la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai la ni paae yʋʋmpaal nwadig yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la ni.
english: Samuel Kwadwo Amoako was the member of parliament for the constituency between January 2009 and January 2013.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o nɛ dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) ka o da di nɛ vɔɔt tusa anu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ ka kilim wadmaan.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP)and won a majority of 5,046 votes to become the MP.

kusaal: Gifty Twum Ampofo an wadmaani tis constituency la nananna (yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan) ka tʋm tis 6th nɛ 7th parliament dɔlisidnɛ NPP ni.
english: Gifty Twum Ampofo then succeeded J. B. Danquah-Adu and became the member of Parliament of the constituency now (2023) and served in the 6th and 7th and parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the NPP.

kusaal: Akim Abuakwa North teŋtita'ar anɛ Kukurantumi.
english: The capital of Akim Abuakwa North is Kukurantumi.

kusaal: Di da bɛnɛ Abuakwa constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la.
english: It was created out of the Abuakwa constituency in 2004.

kusaal: Ba teŋ tita'ar bɛnɛ Kibi.
english: Its administrative capital is Kibi.

kusaal: O da di'e na'am la yinɛ J.B. Danquah-Adu san'an, onɛ da di kuk la nwadis piinɛ ayi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi dɔlisid NPP.
english: He succeeded J. B. Danquah-Adu who had won the seat in December 2004 with the NPP.

kusaal: O da di'e nɛ Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo onɛ da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug 4th Republic dlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) la ni.
english: He succeeded Samuel Atta Akyea who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Onɛ an constituency la wadmaan anɛ Samuel Atta Akyea.
english: He succeeded Samuel Atta Akyea who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) ka o da dii gaad o tiraan la, o da mɔr vɔɔt tusa anu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ gaad o tiraan la ka da di constituency la wadmaan.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and won a majority, with 27,011 votes to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: Ka mɔr vɔɔt nam tusa pisi nɛ anu, kɔbʋstan nɛ pisnii ka vɔɔt la wʋsa an tusa pistan' nɛ yinne, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ atan' ka di pa'al ye kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn o mɔr pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai pʋdʋg pisnaasi nɛ anu (79.45%), o da nyaŋi o tiraan la ka di kʋk la ka da an wadmaan kani paas anu Constituency la ni.
english: With a majority of 25,380 votes out of the 31,943 total votes cast (which represents 79.45%), he defeated his opponents and won the seat as the 5th MP for the Constituency.

kusaal: O da di'e kʋk la nɛ William Quaitoo san'an, onɛ da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug yʋma anii, din yi' yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi paae yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisi la dɔlisidnɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) la ni.
english: He succeeded William Quaitoo who represented the constituency for eight years from 2012 to 2020 on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: On da nan kae la, Yaw Owusu-Boateng da an wadmaan tis constituency la yʋma anaasi yʋma tusa ayi nɛ anii paae yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ka ba da maal constituency paal yi Akim Oda constituency yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ka on da zi'en constituency paal la nɔba zug, Asene Akoroso Manso dolisidnɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) yʋm kan.
english: Before him was Yaw Owusu-Boateng as the member of parliament for the constituency for four years (2008-2012) until a new constituency was created out of the Akim Oda constituency in 2012 which had him representing the newly created Constituency, Asene Akoroso Manso on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) that year.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋnɛ Alexander Akwasi Acquah ye o an wadmaan tis constituency la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anu, kɔbistan nɛ pisnii (25,380) dinɛ zi'eni tis pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai du'al pisnnasi nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (79.45%) wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug.
english: Alexander Akwasi Acquah was elected as MP for the constituency in 2020 with 25,380 votes representing 79.45% on the ticket of NPP.

kusaal: Ba yiiga wadmaan la da yine New Patriotic Party (NPP) ni na.
english: The first time MP was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Akim Swedru constituency bɛ nɛ Birim South District bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana.
english: The Akim Swedru constituency is located within the Birim South District of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Akiu no taue odori (秋保の田植踊) anɛ buudi malʋŋkanɛ an mi bʋdib wa'abi bɛ Akiu,dinɛ yʋ'ʋm paas Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan la.
english: Akiu no taue odori (秋保の田植踊) is a traditional rice-planting dance in Akiu, now part of Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi l (1970) la ni ka ba da maal suoya ye ba sɔb wa'a la yɛla digil ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (1976) la ni ka ba da zaŋi li paas Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni, Akiu no taue odori da paam suori paas UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity ni.
english: In 2009 Akiu no taue odori was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Busia bɛnɛ Accra bɛ 1966.
english: Busia was born in Accra in 1966.

kusaal: O da anɛ pu'ayuod tis Kofi Abrefa Busia, onɛ da an prime minister tis Republic of Ghana (din yi 1969 ti paae 1972) ka mɛ an nabiig bɛ royal buudi bɛ Wenchi, wɛlʋg yinne kanɛ pa'as Ashanti, linɛ kɛ ka Akosua an nabipu'a mɛ.
english: She is the daughter of Kofi Abrefa Busia, who was prime minister of the Republic of Ghana (from 1969 to 1972) and a prince of the royal family of Wenchi, a subgroup of the Ashanti, making Akosua a princess too.

kusaal: O taʋn, Abena Busia, anɛ sɛnlʋg sɔbit nɛ gbaʋŋ puugin, onɛ da mɔr baŋir tita'ar bɛ na'asaalin bɛ Rutgers University, ka din yi 2017 ni, ka o ziɛr Ghana nɔbazug bɛ Brazil.
english: Her sister, Abena Busia, is a poet and academic, who was a professor in English at Rutgers University, and since 2017 has been the Ghanaian ambassador to Brazil.

kusaal: Busia da nɔbig bɛnɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, ka sɛŋ o di'em-di'em tʋʋma la yʋʋm pii nɛ ayʋɔbu, o ken sakur bɛnɛ London's Central sakur kanɛ pa'an pia'and nɛ di'ema ka ba gɔsid o nɛɛm.
english: Busia grew up in Ghana, and began her acting career at the age of 16, attending London's Central School of Speech and Drama on scholarship.

kusaal: O yiiga di'ema da anɛ Juliet bɛ zin'igsia kanɛ an piɛlim kas, tʋʋmir Shakespeare's Romeo nɛ Juliet bɛ Oxford University, o taʋn biis mɛ da bɛ ani mɛ zamisid.
english: Her first acting role was as Juliet in an otherwise white cast, performing Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet at Oxford University, where her siblings were studying.

kusaal: Busia da maali o yiiga siini nɛ 1979 siini Ashanti, nɛ Michael Caine nɛ Peter Ustinov.
english: Busia made her film debut in the 1979 adventure film Ashanti, with Michael Caine and Peter Ustinov.

kusaal: On da yi kɛŋ Los Angeles bɛ in 1980s yʋʋm banɛ gaad la, o da di'em mɛ sʋŋir sɔ bɛ slasher siini li naae di'ema la ni, sɔ' nɛ da pa'an siini la anɛ Andrew Davis (The Fugitive).
english: After moving to Los Angeles in the early 1980s, she was cast to play a supporting role in the slasher film The Final Terror, directed by Andrew Davis (The Fugitive).

kusaal: Ba da pʋ nyaŋ yis siini la paalʋg, 1983 ni, ka ba yuon da paam li di'em-di'emnam(pa'as nɛ Daryl Hannah nɛ Rachel Ward) bɛdigʋ nɛ da mi'i ba la.
english: The film was not released until 1983, after several of its actors (including Daryl Hannah and Rachel Ward) had achieved public prominence.

kusaal: Busia's siini tʋʋma mɔr yɛlkpanna ɛntima bɛdigʋ wʋʋ Bessie bɛ 1986 siini pɛŋir bɛ Richard Wright's novel Native Son (nɛ Geraldine Page and Matt Dillon).
english: Busia's film roles include a notable performance as Bessie in a 1986 film adaptation of Richard Wright's novel Native Son (with Geraldine Page and Matt Dillon).

kusaal: O mɛ da la'as pa'as zamis kpiʋŋ la ni nɛ Denzel Washington nɛ Lynn Whitfield bɛ 1986.
english: She also starred in Hard Lessons alongside Denzel Washington and Lynn Whitfield in 1986.

kusaal: Busia da di'em nɛ Nettie, Whoopi Goldberg's taʋn di'em-di'em tiraan Celie Harris, bɛ Steven Spielberg's 1985 The Color Purple, nɔkir yi Alice Walker's di'ema ni ka pian'and zug la an yinne, nɛ Ruth bɛ Badge of the Assassin (1985), nwɛnɛ Jewel bɛ John Singleton's Rosewood (1997), nɛ Patience bɛ Antoine Fuqua's Tears of the Sun (2003).
english: Busia played Nettie, the younger sister of Whoopi Goldberg's character Celie Harris, in Steven Spielberg's 1985 The Color Purple, adapted from Alice Walker's novel of the same title, as Ruth in Badge of the Assassin (1985), as Jewel in John Singleton's Rosewood (1997), and as Patience in Antoine Fuqua's Tears of the Sun (2003).

kusaal: Busia sɔb gbaŋ kanɛ an The Seasons of Beento Blackbird: A Novel (Washington Square Press, 1997, ISBN 9780671014094).
english: Busia is the author of The Seasons of Beento Blackbird: A Novel (Washington Square Press, 1997, ISBN 9780671014094).

kusaal: O da paas nidib atan' banɛ da sɔb Toni Morrison yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi (1987) gbaŋ kanɛ buon Beloved tis yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998) ka nɔki maal sini kanɛ ka li tuongat da an Jonathan Demme la.
english: She was one of three co-writers for the screenplay adaptation of Toni Morrison's 1987 novel Beloved for the 1998 film version of the same name directed by Jonathan Demme.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anii ni (2008), Busia da gaad tuoni gɔs sini kanɛ da pa'an o saam yela: The Prof.
english: In 2008, Busia directed a film about her father: The Prof. A Man Remembered.

kusaal: Busia mɛ da paasi sɔb yʋʋma "Moon Blue" on nɛ Stevie Wonder mall yʋʋma album A Time 2 Love, ka ba da yisi li paalʋ yʋʋm tusayi ne anu (2005).
english: Busia also co-wrote the song "Moon Blue" with Stevie Wonder for his album A Time 2 Love, released in 2005.

kusaal: O yʋʋma kanɛ buon "Mama" da paas yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai (2019) ni yʋʋm kanɛ buon New Daughters of Africa, ka one da paasi sɔbi li an Margaret Busby.
english: Her poem "Mama" is included in the 2019 anthology New Daughters of Africa, edited by Margaret Busby.

kusaal: On da nɔk yʋʋm piinɛ nii ye o yuol o bipʋŋ la nya'aŋ, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ ni (2016) Busia da leb sini maalig ni bɛ off-Broadway nɛ Broadway production ka ba maal Danai Gurira di'em kanɛ buon Eclipsed, on nɛ Lupita Nyong'o.
english: After 18-year hiatus to raise her daughter, in 2016 Busia returned to acting in the off-Broadway and Broadway production of Danai Gurira's play Eclipsed, alongside Lupita Nyong'o.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi ni (2024), Busia da yis di'ema sini ka li buon In Search of a Blessed Life: He Who Hath, ya'amkan da yinɛ gbaŋ kanɛ buon He that Hath, to Him Shall Be Given ka one sɔb an Dag Heward-Mills la ni na.
english: In 2024 Busia released the drama film In Search of a Blessed Life: He Who Hath, which was inspired by the book He that Hath, to Him Shall Be Given by Dag Heward-Mills.

kusaal: Yʋʋmkan nya'aŋ, Busia sini kani buon Stevie Wonder in Ghana: In Search of a Blessed Life mɛ da yi paalʋ na.
english: Later that same year Busia's documentary Stevie Wonder in Ghana: In Search of a Blessed Life was also released.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ, nwadis piiga, dabpiinɛ yi daar (12 October 1996), Akosua Busia da kul sid, America tɛŋ nid kanɛ gɔsid sini maalig ka ba buon John Singleton, ba mɔr bipʋŋ yinne — Hadar Busia-Singleton (ba dʋ'a o nɛ 3 April 1997); ba da bas taaba yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi, nwadisayuobʋ, dabpii nɛ nu daar (15 June 1997).
english: On 12 October 1996, Akosua Busia married the American film director John Singleton, with whom she has a daughter — Hadar Busia-Singleton (born 3 April 1997); the couple divorced on 15 June 1997.

kusaal: On nɛ o pitu Abena Busia la'asi pin'il Busia Foundation International, ye "ba sʋŋ tadimnam".
english: She co-founded with her sister Abena Busia the Busia Foundation International, aiming "to provide assistance to the disadvantaged".

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ ka siini gɔsidib la mi'i o, on di'em siini di'ema linɛ da buon ye Nettie Harris bɛ yʋʋm 1985 siini linɛ yʋ'ʋri buonl ye The Color Purple.
english: She is known to film audiences for playing Nettie Harris in the 1985 film The Color Purple.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana prime minister onɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Kofi Abrefa Busia.
english: She is the daughter of Kofi Abrefa Busia, who was prime minister of the Republic of Ghana (from 1969 to 1972) and a prince of the royal family of Wenchi, a subgroup of the Ashanti, making Akosua a princess too.

kusaal: Ba pʋ'asadir la da kɛŋ sakur nɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, ka nyaan lɛb US.
english: Their daughter attended school in Ghana, before returning to the US.

kusaal: O da yi TV ni na bɛ ER.
english: She has also appeared on television in the series ER.

kusaal: Akrofi-Christaller Institute of Theology, Mission and Culture (ACI), ka ba da buoni li ye Akrofi-Christaller Memorial Centre for Mission Research and Applied Theology, anɛ kpɛɛmnam sakur kanɛ ka ba zamisid ka lɛn pa'an vɛɛnsʋg zamisig, ka li bɛ Akropong-Akuapem linɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: The Akrofi-Christaller Institute of Theology, Mission and Culture (ACI), formerly known as the Akrofi-Christaller Memorial Centre for Mission Research and Applied Theology, is a tertiary, postgraduate research and training institute located in Akropong-Akuapem in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba yʋda anɛ Johann Gottlieb Christaller nɛ Clement Anderson Akrofi banɛ da muk hali sɔb kambʋnir buudi pian'ad gbana ni.
english: The university was named after two Christian ethnologists, Johann Gottlieb Christaller and Clement Anderson Akrofi who carried out extensive literary work on the Twi language.

kusaal: Akrofi-Christaller Institute sakur paalʋ bɛnɛ Akropong Kristo biis Wina'am labaar pa'an-pa'anib zamisig zin'ig linɛ bɛ Akropong-Akuapem la, ba da mɛ' linɛ nineteenth century tɛnsʋk saŋa, ka da maligim maali li ka li lieb paalig, ka mɛ yaligi li paas.
english: Akrofi-Christaller Institute occupies the buildings of the historic Akropong Seminary including the Basel House in Akropong-Akuapem, a campus that was built in the mid-nineteenth century, renovated in the early nineties and expanded by the turn of the millennium.

kusaal: Sakur la da kɛna ye ba zamis Kristo biis gbana, ba malima nɛ ba pʋtɛnda bɛ Ghana nɛ Africa sʋ'ʋlim, ka mɛ tis nidib sʋŋir ka ba kɛŋ zamis tɛŋ si'eba malima.
english: With roots in the Pietistic tradition of the Basel Mission, the Institute combines academic study with propagation of the Gospel in Ghana and Africa.

kusaal: Akrofi-Christaller institute da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi ni, ka mɔri ba nyali, ka sʋŋidi ba mɛŋ ka ba tʋʋma kɛn tuon, ba da kpɛn'ɛsi ba yʋ'ʋr gbana ni anɛ sakur kanɛ pʋ bɔɔd nyɔɔdɛ.
english: Akrofi-Christaller institute was founded in 1987 as an independent, self-financing entity, a company limited by guarantee and registered under the Companies Code as a non-profit educational institution.

kusaal: Ba mɔr nyali nɛ ban na tis banɛ zamisi ba sa'an kasɛta gbana, ka Ghana Education Service mɛ tik nu'ugi tisi ba ye ba kɛm tuon.
english: It is fully accredited by the National Accreditation Board of Ghana's Ministry of Education, with a full Presidential Charter to award its own degrees.

kusaal: Ba da nɔk nɛ Kristo biis gbansɔbidib si'eba ayi' yʋda pʋd university la.
english: The university was named after two Christian ethnologists, Johann Gottlieb Christaller and Clement Anderson Akrofi who carried out extensive literary work on the Twi language.

kusaal: Sakur la la'as nɛ gbaŋ zamisig nɛ Wina'am labaar mɔɔlig zamisig bɛ Ghana nɛ Africa.
english: With roots in the Pietistic tradition of the Basel Mission, the Institute combines academic study with propagation of the Gospel in Ghana and Africa.

kusaal: Ba mɛ' dɔɔd tɔlis ka sakur la yʋ'ʋn mɔr diib zin'is, gbana la'asig zin'ig – ka ba buon zin'ig kan ye Johannes Zimmermann Library nɛ zamisig zin'is.
english: The upgrade of the facilities include residential and dining buildings, a specialist reference library - the Johannes Zimmermann Library and lecture halls.

kusaal: Ba gaŋidnɛ Member of Parliament yinne, onɛ gaade ba wusa vɔɔt la ni.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Akrofuom bɛ nɛ Obuasi Municipal district bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: Akrofuom is located in the Obuasi Municipal District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la da ani Ghana Electoral Commission ni sin'iŋidi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi paasnɛ pisinɛ awai sieba, dinni da kɛ ka constituency nam la paas kɔbusyi kɛŋ paae kɔbusyi nɛ pistan.
english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Ba kuk la bɛ nɛ Obuasi Municipal District bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Obuasi Municipal District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Akrofuom Senior High Technical School anɛ sɛkondiri sakur kani bɛ Akrofuom kani bɛ Adansi South District bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana la.
english: Akrofuom Senior High Technical School is a second cycle institution located in Akrofuom in the Adansi South District in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Sakur la da pin'ili yʋʋm 1991 la ni.
english: The school was established in 1991.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2011 nii, onɛ da an pa'an kpɛɛm da anɛ Mr.
english: In 2011, the headmaster of the school was Mr. Peter Amponsah.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2018 nii, Anglogold Ashanti Mining Company la da tis Akrofuom SHTS gbana pɛ'ɛsnɛ sakur sieba mɛn bɛ Obuasi Municipality la ni.
english: In 2018, Anglogold Ashanti Mining Company donated books to the Akrofuom SHTS and other schools in Obuasi Municipality.

kusaal: Sakur la pin'ilɛ nɛ sakurbiis 21 pɛ'ɛsnɛ pa'anib 8.
english: The school began with 21 Students and 8 Teachers.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2018 la ni, onɛ da pa'an kpɛɛm nya'andɔl tis sakur la an Mr.
english: In 2018, the assistant headmaster of the school was Mr. Jacob Anakpor.

kusaal: Akuka Albert Alalzuuga anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi ti Gaana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la nii tis Garu linɛ bɛ Upper East Region sυ'υlυm.
english: Akuka Albert Alalzuuga is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Garu Constituency in the Upper East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: O mɔr kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an BSC in Commerce yi University of Cape Coast sakur la ni ka mɛ lɛm mɔr kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an HND in Accounting yi Tamale Polytechnic.
english: He hold a BSC in Commerce from the University of Cape Coast and an HND in Accounting from the Tamale Polytechnic.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwadis ayi' la li dabisim piisi nɛ anii yυυm tυsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyuobu nɛ anii la ni ka ba da du'a Akuka Albert Alalzuuga.
english: Akuka Albert Alalzuuga was born on 28 February 1968.

kusaal: Akuka anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Akuka is a Christian.

kusaal: Akwapim South da anɛ Aburi-Nsawam constituency ka ba naam pudigi li kɔn' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi ka di yʋn an Akwapim South nɛ Nsawam Adoagyiri constituency la.
english: Akuapim South used to be known as the Aburi-Nsawam constituency until it was divided in 2012 which gave us Akuapim South and Nsawam Adoagyiri constituencies.

kusaal: Kʋk la bɛ nɛ Akuapem South Municipal Assembly bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana la.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Akuapem South Municipal Assembly of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Akwasi Konadu anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Akwasi Konadu is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Nannanna, onɛ an Director n gɔsid Ghana Water Company Limited yɛla.
english: He is currently the Director at the Ghana Water Company Limited.

kusaal: O da si'iŋi o secondary sakuri n bɛ Opoku Ware Secondary Sakur la ni.
english: He had his secondary education at Opoku Ware Secondary School.

kusaal: Ka o da tɔlisi o Diploma sakur n bɛ University of Education, Winneba sakurin la.
english: He had his Diploma in Education from the University of Education - Winneba.

kusaal: O da lɛn tɔlisi o Digirɛɛ zamisυg n bɛ University of Ghana yυυma tusa yi' nɛ anu la ni naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Sociology with Philosophy la.
english: He further had his bachelor's degree in Sociology with Philosophy in 2005 from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ, ka o lɛn tɔlisi maali o Masta Digirɛɛ n yi KNUST sakur la ni n naae di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Development Policy and Planning.
english: He also had his master's degree in Development Policy and Planning from KNUST.

kusaal: Konadu da anɛ Auditor for KDA Accounting Services linɛ bɛ Kumasi la kpɛɛm nya'andɔl.
english: Konadu was the Assistant Auditor for KDA Accounting Services in Kumasi.

kusaal: Onɛ mɛ da kaadi gɔsid Bonsafo Barwuah Foundation tυυma la ka li ken tituaa.
english: He was also the Project supervising officer for Bonsafo Barwuah Foundation.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Greenfield Company Limited tυυma la manager.
english: He was the Operations manager for Greenfield Company Limited.

kusaal: Vɔt la da naae ka ba mɔɔl ye onɛ di ya'an, o da paamɛ vɔt bam 39,562 kɔbiga pυυginɛ li anɛ 69.9% n gaad o tiraan onɛ da an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid Hamza Swallah onɛ mɛ da paam 15,943 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o mɛ da mɔri 28.2%.
english: He was declared winner in the parliamentary elections after securing 39,562 votes representing 69.9% against his closest contender the National Democratic Congress' candidate, Hamza Swallah had 15,943 votes representing 28.2%.

kusaal: Konadu paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid ban na niŋ si'em ka nɔŋ sɛɛrig (Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee) la ni ka mɛ lɛn paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid nimma'asim lυgυr yɛla la ni.
english: Konadu is a member of the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee and also a member of the Health Committee.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Konadu nɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris ayɔpɔi la li dabisim piisi nɛ anu yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ ayi la ni, o yinɛ Paakoso linɛ bɛ Kumasi sυ'υlυm.
english: Konadu was born on 25 July 1982 and hails from Paakoso in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Konadu da namisnɛ hali ka naam paam di, yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yi' la nɛ yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yuobυ la ni wusa ka on nɛ o tiraan Collins Owusu Amankwaah ka o pυ dii.

english: Aqyn or akyn (Kazakh: ақын, Kyrgyz: акын, pronounced [ɑˈqɯn]; both transcribed as aqın or اقىن), is an improvisational poet, singer, and oral repository within the Kazakh and Kyrgyz cultures.

kusaal: Yʋʋma nya'ab ka ba buon ye aytıs bɛɛ aytysh ni, aqyns anɛ nwɛnɛ sɛnlʋŋ yʋʋma ka ba yʋʋmidnɛ, ka ba ɛɛnti nwɛ'ɛd dombra (among Kazakhs) bɛɛ komuz (among Kyrgyz) gɛndigid.
english: In song competitions known as aytıs or aytysh, aqyns improvise in the form of a song-like recitative, usually to the accompaniment of a dombra (among Kazakhs) or a komuz (among Kyrgyz).

english: Famous historical Kazakh akyns include: Zhanak Kambaruluy (1760–1857), Makhambet Otemisuly (1804–1846), Suyunbai Aronuly (1815–1898), Shernyz Zharylgasov (1817–1881), Birzhan-Sal Khodgulov (1834–1897), Ziaus Baizhanov (1835–1929), Akan Sery Corramsauluy (1843–1913), Zhambyl Zhabayuly (1846–1945), Gaziz Firesoll (mind 1930), Kenen Azerbaev (1884–1976), and Aktan Kereiuly.

english: In the context of the nomadic lifestyle and illiteracy of most of the rural population in Central Asia in pre-Soviet times, akyns played an important role in terms of expressing people's thoughts and feelings, exposing social vices, and glorifying heroes.

english: Seal carving, also seal cutting, or zhuanke in Chinese (篆刻), is a traditional form of art that originated in China and later spread across East Asia.

kusaal: Zhou saŋa la mɛn, ba da mɔr scripts kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔbi tʋm (bɔzugɔ Chinese sɔbbiela la da nam pʋ naal taabaa), amaa dazhuan (大篆) bɛɛ jinwen (金文) scripts ka ba da mɔri tʋm.
english: During the Zhou period various scripts were used (because Chinese characters were still not unified), but mainly the dazhuan (大篆) or jinwen (金文) scripts were used.

kusaal: Qin dynasty saŋa la mɛn ka da mɔr seal script banɛ nar ka mɔr vɛnlim nwɛnɛ xiaozhuan (小篆) da an dinɛ ka ba da siak ye ba mɔri tʋm dɔlisid Chancellor Li Si ka Emperor Qinshihuang mɛ da gaŋi li, dinzug ba da siak ka Chinese sɔbbiela yʋ'ʋn naal taaba di yiiga saŋa.
english: During the Qin dynasty the more regular and formal seal script called xiaozhuan(described as the rabid dynasty) (小篆) was formalized by Chancellor Li Si and prescribed by the Emperor Qinshihuang, thus the written script of Chinese characters was unified for the first time.

kusaal: Kuga banɛ yi Qingtian, nananna di bɛnɛ Zhejiang Province, ka ba buon ye Qingtian kugir (青田印石) ka banɛ ka ba buon ye Shoushan stone (壽山印石) mɛ yi Fujian Province ka nidib bɛdegʋ mɛ tʋm.
english: Stones from Qingtian, currently in Zhejiang Province, are called Qingtian stone (青田印石) while those called Shoushan stone (壽山印石) from Fujian Province were also widely used.
