kusaal: Yʋʋmkanɛ dɔl la, o da nyaŋ Petey Scalzo onɛ yi New York la New York Golden Gloves tournament ni yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan nɛ anu (1935) la ni.
english: The following year he defeated Petey Scalzo of New York in the New York Golden Gloves tournament during 1935.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan nɛ ayuobʋ (1936) la ni, ba da yis o second round ni bantamweight class zaba ni yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan nɛ ayuobʋ (1936) Olympic Games, on da zab nɛ onɛ da di'e bronze medal, Fidel Ortiz ka gʋ'ʋŋ, Mexico.
english: In 1936 he was eliminated in the second round of the bantamweight class during the 1936 Olympic Games, after losing his fight to the upcoming bronze medalist Fidel Ortiz of Mexico.

kusaal: Albert Richard Barnes (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piinɛ atan nwadisa ayɔpɔi la daba ayi daar, 2 July 1913 ka o maal ka'alim yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nwadisa ayɔpɔi la daba anii daar, 8 July 1990).
english: Albert Richard Barnes (2 July 1913 – 8 July 1990) was a Welsh boxer who competed for Great Britain in the 1936 Summer Olympics.

kusaal: Albert Tetteh Nyakotey da dʋ'anɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu Nwadisa anii la dabpiiga daar (10 August 1965) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd onɛ bɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress la ni.
english: Albert Tetteh Nyakotey (born 10 August 1965) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Yilo Krobo constituency bɛ Eastern Region of Ghana.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Yilo Krobo constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Tetteh yinɛ Somanya, tenkanɛ bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Tetteh hails from Somanya, a town in the Eastern Region.

kusaal: O mɔr Commonwealth Executive MBA in Management.
english: He holds a Commonwealth Executive MBA in Management.

kusaal: Alençon lace (UK: /ˈælənsɒn, æˈlɒ̃sɒ̃/, US: /əˈlɛnsɒn, -sən/) or point d'Alençon (French: [pwɛ̃ dalɑ̃sɔ̃]) anɛ kparibpiim lace kanɛ ka ba da pin'ili di maalug Alençon bɛ France la.
english: Alençon lace (UK: , US: ) or point d'Alençon (French: [pwɛ̃ dalɑ̃sɔ̃]) is a needle lace that originated in Alençon, France.

kusaal: Sansieba ba buoni di ye "Queen of lace." Lace maalʋg da pin'ili Alençon nɛ 16th century la nid ka zin'ikanɛ ka ba da maan la da yaligi nɔbʋg Louis XIV saŋa yinɛ Jean-Baptiste Colbert, onɛ da pin'il Royal Workshop teŋin la ka ba sin'iŋi maan lace Venetian style yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu (1665).
english: It is sometimes called the "Queen of lace." Lace making began in Alençon during the 16th century and the local industry was rapidly expanded during the reign of Louis XIV by Jean-Baptiste Colbert, who established a Royal Workshop in the town to produce lace in the Venetian style in 1665.

kusaal: Marthe La Perrière da tiak Venetian suokanɛ ka ba dɔlisidi maal la ka Alençon da yina nɛ sitaai saaŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (1675) la ni Colbert monopoly da naae la nya'aŋ.
english: Marthe La Perrière had modified the Venetian technique and Alençon emerged as a unique style around 1675 after Colbert's monopoly ended.

kusaal: La'anɛ lace bɔɔdim da sie hali ka di yinɛ French Revolution yɛla la, di da lɛm paam paŋ ya'as Second French Empire saŋa.
english: Though the demand for lace went into sharp decline following the French Revolution, it recovered some of its popularity during the Second French Empire.

kusaal: Bamba Müller, Maharaja Duleep Singh pʋ'a, ka ba da yɛ Alençon trimmed gown o sid kulig malʋŋ ni bɛ Alexandria, Egypt yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi (1864) la ni.
english: Bamba Müller, the wife of the Maharaja Duleep Singh, wore an Alençon trimmed gown on the occasion of her wedding in Alexandria, Egypt in 1864.

kusaal: Onɛ da maali Alençon lace la da pin'ili sied 19th century la naari ka ba yʋ'ʋm pin'ili tia'as fuud nɛ ban da maal masin banɛ maan lace nam la.
english: The manufacture of Alençon lace entered terminal decline at the end of the 19th century with changes in fashion and the development of cheaper, machine-made lace.

kusaal: Lace banɛ ka ba nɔk nu'usi maal da anɛ banɛ maan bi'el-bi'el ka Carmelite nuns ka gu' baŋir kan Alençon.
english: Hand-made lace-making survived on a small scale and the technique was preserved by Carmelite nuns in Alençon.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (1976) la ni, ba da pin'il National Lace Workshop teŋ la ni ye di sʋŋ ka lace maalʋŋ baŋir la kpɛm bɛ ka da kpii bɔdigɛ.
english: In 1976 a National Lace Workshop was established in the town to ensure that this lace-making technique survives.

kusaal: Dinɛ zug ka ba da mpin'il workshop kaŋa anɛ di sie French kɔɔtʋ da zi'e kimm ka ba ziid la'ad tensieba kpɛn'ɛd na la.
english: The purpose of establishing this workshop was to reduce the French court's dependence on expensive foreign imports.

kusaal: St.Marie-Azélie Guérin Martin, onɛ an ma tis St.
english: The pattern represented the arms of the empire surrounded by bees.St. Marie-Azélie Guérin Martin, the mother of St. Thérèse of Lisieux was a famous lace-maker at Alençon.

kusaal: Therese onɛ yi Lisieux ka da maan lace ka nidib bɛdegʋ mi' o Alençon.
english: The pattern represented the arms of the empire surrounded by bees.St. Marie-Azélie Guérin Martin, the mother of St. Thérèse of Lisieux was a famous lace-maker at Alençon.

kusaal: Zin'isi'a bɛ pa'an lace an si'em nɛ ban maani li si'em bɛ Musée des Beaux Arts et de la Dentelle, ka di bɛ tempʋʋg la sʋʋgin ka pʋ lal nɛ Workshop la.
english: There is a permanent exhibition of lace and a display showing how it is made in the Musée des Beaux Arts et de la Dentelle, located in the town centre and adjoining the Workshop.

kusaal: Alex Adomako-Mensah (ba da du'a o nɛ 5 sapal nwadig1962) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ nwɛ'ɛd pɔlitis ka an Wadmaani tis Sekyere Afram Plains Constituency teŋkanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana la.
english: Alex Adomako-Mensah (born 5 November 1962) is a Ghanaian politician and Member of Parliament for Sekyere Afram Plains Constituency in the Ashanti Region, Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Kumawu teŋkanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: He was born on 5 November 1962 and hails from Kumawu in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Alex Adomako-Mensah maal o MBA m bɛnɛ (UK), University of Leicester la, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne la ni (2001).
english: Alex Adomako-Mensah earned his MBA in (UK) from the University of Leicester, in 2001.

kusaal: O da lieb Chartered Institute of Marketing (ACIM) tʋmtʋn yinne bɛ UK yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la ni (2003) ka ba piinl o Chartered Management Institute (MCMI) by Chartered Institute of Marketing bɛ UK la yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2006).
english: He became an Associate Member (ACIM) of the Chartered Institute of Marketing, UK in 2003 and was honored as a Member of the Chartered Management Institute (MCMI) by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, UK in 2006.

kusaal: O bɛnɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la ni, ka ba da vɔɔt ka o lieb wadmaan yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la ni ka o zi'eni tis Sekyere Afram plains.
english: He is a member of the National Democratic Congress who was voted as part of the MPs elected in the Ghanaian parliamentary election in 2016 to represent Sekyere Afram plains.

kusaal: O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Employment, Social Welfare and State Enterprises la nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla, (Finance).
english: He is a member of the Employment, Social Welfare, and State Enterprises Committee and also a member of the Finance Committee.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi' la li Nwadis pii nɛ yinne la daba anu daar (5 sapal nwadig 1962).
english: He was born on 5 November 1962 and hails from Kumawu in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la Nwadisa anii la dabpii nɛ anaas daar (mɔtul nwadig 14, 2017), faandib banɛ ka sɔ' zi'i baa da daam wadmaan la on da dɔl suori naan Kumasi wa'ae Kumawu zaam nɔɔr la.
english: On 14 August 2017, the MP was attacked by some unidentified armed robbers on his way from Kumasi heading towards Kumawu in the evening.

kusaal: O da di kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa anu nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi (5,664) n yi vɔɔt tusa awai nɛ kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (9,275) ni, k li an pisyuobʋ du'al pisnii nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (60.85%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He won the seat with 5,664 votes out of the 9,275 valid votes cast generating 60.85% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Alex Blankson (Ba da du'a o nɛ 26 December 1980) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaan tisi Akrofuom Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Alex Blankson (born 26 December 1980) is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of the eight parliament of the republic of Ghana who represented Akrofuom constituency of the Ashanti region.

kusaal: o paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party la ni.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Blankson da naaenɛ Adisadel College ka da naae o Senior Secondary School Certificate yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ wai la ni (1999).
english: Blankson attended Adisadel College and obtained his Senior Secondary School Certificate in 1999.

kusaal: Alex da anɛ CEO tis Day by Day Health Limited.
english: Alex was the CEO for Day by Day Healthcare Limited.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, Blankson da nya' Akrofuom kʋk la nɛ Joseph Azumah onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC nid la nɛ Prosper Maar onɛ da zi'en NDP zug.
english: During the 2020 Ghanaian general election, Blankson contested for the Akrofuom seat with Joseph Azumah of the NDC, and Prosper Maar of NDP.

kusaal: O da vɛ'ɛg vɔɔt tusa piinɛ yinne, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (11,992) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ anii du'al pisnu nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (58.51%) ka Joseph Azumah paam vɔɔt tusa anii nɛ kɔbisnaasi (8,400) ka Prosper Maar mɛ paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ atan (103) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ yinne du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (41.5%) nɛ nɛɛm du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.5%) nwɛnɛ ba yuda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: He polled 11,992 votes representing 58.51% of the total valid votes against Joseph Azumah 8400 votes and Prosper Maar 103 votes, representing 41.5% and 0.5% of the total valid votes cast respectively.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne 2021, Alan Kyeremanten da gaad tuoni nɔka Alex Blankson paas nidiba ayɔpɔi banɛ ka ba da gan ye ba gɔs masin bɛda yɛl la (Ghana Heavy Equipment Limited).
english: In 2021, Alan Kyeremanten sworn in Alex Blankson as a board member in a seven-member governing body of Ghana Heavy Equipment Limited.

kusaal: Alex paas la'askanɛ gɔsid dasam nɛ pʋ'asada, ninwisigir nɛ buudi malima yɛla (Youth, Sports and Culture Committee) ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid gɔmena ligidiisim suor (Special Budget Committee).
english: Alex is a member of the Youth, Sports and Culture Committee and also a member of the Special Budget Committee.

kusaal: O anɛ Nana Okai Ababio yaaŋ.
english: He is the grandson of Nana Okai Ababio.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadisa ayuobʋ la ni 2021, o da sʋŋya ka ba sɛ tiis nwɛnɛ tusa awai (9,000 trees) Adansi Akrofuom sʋ'ʋlim.
english: In June 2021, he aided in the planting of over 9,000 trees in the Adansi Akrofuom area.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Blankson nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii Nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ ayuobʋ daar (26 December 1980).
english: Blankson was born on 26 December 1980.

kusaal: O yinɛ Adansi Akrofuom.
english: He hails from Adansi Akrofuom.

kusaal: Alex anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Alex is a Christian.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadispiinɛ ayi la nii, December 2021, o da tis kɛmisi vaand nwɛnɛ kɔbis naasi tis ye di sʋŋi kpa' Grumesa community center.
english: In December 2021, he presented about 400 pieces of roofing sheets to aid in the completion of the Grumesa community center.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Fourth Republic of Ghana wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas ayɔpɔi la nid yinne, ka an wadmaan tis Mpohor sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Western Region la ni.
english: Alex Kofi Agyekum (born 18 August 1962) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Mpohor constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O mɔr o B.A kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit University of Cape Coast sakur tita'ar la ni, ka mɛ mɔr M.ED kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ 'management' ni nɛ 'diploma' kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ Education ni.
english: He obtained a BA degree from the University of Cape Coast, as well as an M.ED in Management and a diploma in Education.

kusaal: Agyekum da anɛ University of Cape Coast sakur tita'ar la pa'alʋg nɛ gbaʋŋ vɛɛnsʋg tʋʋma kpɛɛm nya'andɔl, din yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991) la ni ken paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' (' (1992 la ni.
english: Agyekum was a teaching and research assistant at University of Cape Coast from 1991 to 1992.

kusaal: O da anɛ kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid nu'ug tʋʋma zamisʋg lʋgir n bɛ Holy Child sakur la ni, din pin'il yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' la ni (1993) ken paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la ni (2003).
english: He was the head of the department for economics in Holy Child School from 1993 to 2003, and was the assistant headmaster at Holy Child School from 2003 to 2013.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) la ni la, Agyekum da zi'en wabʋg na'adɔɔg la ni nyi'a Mpohor teŋ sʋ'ʋlʋm wadmaan na'am kʋk la ka di nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (7,114) ka li an pisnaasi nɛ du'alʋg pisnaasi nɛ atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (40.43%).
english: Agyekum contested the 2012 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party and won the Mpohor parliamentary seat with 7,114 votes out of the total votes, equivalent to 40.43%.

kusaal: O da di na'am la ka bas ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid Anthony Bassaw kanɛ da mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbistan' nɛ pistan' nɛ atan' ' (6,333) ka li an pistan' nɛ anu nɛ du'alʋg piswai nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (35.99%), nɛ Mary Ankoman onɛ da zi'en nyi'a tis PPP dim na'adɔɔg la ka mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa anaasi nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne (4,151) ka li an pisi nɛ atan' nɛ du'alʋg pisnu nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (23.59%).
english: He won the election over the National Democratic Congress parliamentary candidate Anthony Bassaw, who polled 6,333 votes, representing 35.99%, while Mary Ankoman, the parliamentary candidate for the PPP, had 4, 151 votes, representing 23.59% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Vɔɔdʋg la wʋsa kal ni o da di na'am la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa anii nɛ kɔbistan' nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi (8,364) ka li an pisnaasi nɛ anii nɛ du'alʋg pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' ' (48.72%) kɔbʋg pʋʋgin, ka bas ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid Eric Kweku Kyeremah onɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi (6,947) ka li an kal pisnaasi nɛ du'alʋg pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (40.46%) kɔbʋg pʋʋgin la, nɛ Joseph Benedict Auby onɛ an PPP na'adɔɔg nid ka mɔr vɔɔt kal tusir nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (1,857) ka li an piiga nɛ du'alʋg pisnii nɛ ayi' ' (10.82%) kɔbʋg pʋʋgin.
english: He won the election with 8,364 votes out of the total votes representing 48.72% over the National Democratic Congress parliamentary candidate Eric Kweku Kyeremah, who polled 6,947 votes which is equivalent to 40.46%, while Joseph Benedict Auby of the PPP had 1,857 votes, representing 10.82% of the total votes.

kusaal: O anɛ karimbiig ka pʋ'ʋsid Methodist.
english: He is a Christian and fellowships at Methodist.

kusaal: Alex Kofi Agyekum (Ba da du'a o nɛ burnya nya'aŋ mɔraʋg nwadig la ni dabisim pii nɛ anii daar yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi' la ni).
english: Alex Kofi Agyekum (born 18 August 1962) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Mpohor constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: .Ba da du'a Agyekum nɛ burnya nya'aŋ mɔraʋg nwadig la ni li dabisim pii nɛ anii daar yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi' la ni (8th mɔraʋg nwadig, 1962).
english: Agyekum was born on 18 August 1962.

kusaal: Din da yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' (2003) la ni ken paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' la ni la, o da anɛ Holy Child sakur la zudaan kpɛɛm nya'andɔl.
english: He was the head of the department for economics in Holy Child School from 1993 to 2003, and was the assistant headmaster at Holy Child School from 2003 to 2013.

kusaal: Agyekum da lieb Mpohor teŋ sʋ'ʋlʋm wadmaan bɛ wadmaanib yir la ni nɛ yʋʋm paal nwadig la li daba ayɔpɔi daar yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' la ni, ka an wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid (NPP).
english: Agyekum contested the 2012 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party and won the Mpohor parliamentary seat with 7,114 votes out of the total votes, equivalent to 40.43%.

kusaal: Ala ka o kpɛlim wadmaanib yir la ni ka dit na'am kʋk la yʋʋma vɔɔdʋg banɛ ti'al la wʋsa ni (2012 nɛ 2016) din yi 2012 ni sa.
english: He has remained in parliament, winning the subsequent elections (2012 and 2016) since 2012.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayuobu (2016) ni la, Agyekum da lɛn zi'en wabʋg na'adɔɔg nɔba zug nyi'a Mpohor teŋ sʋ'ʋlʋm wadmaan na'am kʋk la ka dii li.
english: During the 2016 Ghanaian general election, Agyekum again contested the Mpohor parliamentary seat on the ticket of New Patriotic Party and won, therefore representing the constituency in the Parliament of Ghana for two consecutive terms (2012 and 2016).

kusaal: Dinzug o zi'en tis teŋ la nɛ nɔ'ɔr ayi' bɛ wadmaanib yirin la (2012 nɛ 2016).
english: During the 2016 Ghanaian general election, Agyekum again contested the Mpohor parliamentary seat on the ticket of New Patriotic Party and won, therefore representing the constituency in the Parliament of Ghana for two consecutive terms (2012 and 2016).

kusaal: Wadmaanib yir la nidib da vɔɔt gaŋ o ka o an kpɛɛm tis pu'asada nɛ dasam, nɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb nɛ buudi malima kpɛɛmnam kpɛɛm ye o gɔs yɛlbanɛ bɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb la'aʋŋ lʋgir la ni.
english: He was elected by parliament as the chairman of the youth, sports and culture committee to look into issues of the Ghana Football Association.

kusaal: Agyekum di pu'a du'a biisa anaasi.
english: Agyekum is married, and has four children.

kusaal: Alex Djornobuah Tetteh anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Alex Tetteh Djornobuah is a member of the New Patriotic Party, representing Sefwi-Akontombra constituency in the Seventh and Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ deputy minister tis Western North ka an Wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Sefwi-Akontombra Constituency teŋ kanɛ bɛ Western North Region la.
english: He is a deputy minister for Western North and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Sefwi-Akontombra Constituency in the Western North Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da nwɛ' suoya ka ba maali Wiawso-Akontombra suokanɛ ka gɔmena kanɛ gaad la da bas la.
english: He lobbied for the construction of the Wiawso-Akontombra road, which the previous government had abandoned.

kusaal: Alexander Agyare dʋ'anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayuobʋ daar (6 January 1979) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party ni.
english: Alexander Agyare (born 8 January 1979) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Agyare Pramkese.
english: Agyare was born in Pramkese.

kusaal: Alexander Akwasi Acquah Ba da du'a o nɛ buniya nwarig la li daba nii yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi la ni, o anɛ pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd Gaana ka an Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Alexander Akwasi Acquah (born Sunday 8 December 1974) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party and a member of parliament for the Akim Oda constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr Mastɛs Digirɛɛ linɛ an Peace and Security yɛla yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi la ni.
english: He holds Masters Degree in Peace and Security in 2020.

kusaal: O mɛ da maali o Diploma n bɛ Political Reporting yυυma tusa yi' la ni.
english: He also had his Diploma in Political Reporting in 2000.

kusaal: Akwasi anɛ kυk daan nya'andɔl n tis Trade, Industry and Tourism tυυma la; O mɛ paas Government Assurance nɛ Health kpɛɛmnam la ni.
english: Akwasi is the Vice Chairperson of the Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee; a member of the Government Assurance Committee and also a member of Health Committee.

kusaal: O mɛ da da' mathematical sets n tis JHS sakur bibis sυ'υlυm la ni.
english: He also donated mathematical sets to JHS students in his constituency.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Akim Oda linɛ bɛ Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Alexander Akwasi Acquah (born Sunday 8 December 1974) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party and a member of parliament for the Akim Oda constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Akwasi nɛ du'anɛ buniya nwarig la li daba nii yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi la ni, o yinɛ Akim Oda.
english: Akwasi was born on 8 December 1974 and hails from Akim Oda.

kusaal: Akwasi da anɛ Chief executive officer of the n bɛ Sibiti banɛ bɛ Teŋkpɛmis la.
english: Akwasi was the chief executive officer of the Community Hospitals Group.

kusaal: O anɛ entrepreneur nɛ business analyst sɔb.
english: He is an entrepreneur and a business analyst.

kusaal: Nannanna o anɛ wadmaan n tis Akim Oda linɛ Gaana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: He is currently the Member of Parliament for Akim Oda Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris piinɛ yinne la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ ayi la ni, ka o da nɔk ligidi linɛ an 100,000 cedis Akyem Oda dim ye ba di'e maal Municipal park la.
english: In November 2022, he presented 100,000 cedis to aid in the renovation of the Akyem Oda Municipal park.

kusaal: kwasi anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Akwasi is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Alexander Gyan anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani tis Kintampo South n bɛ Bono East sʋ'ʋlim, Gaana.
english: Alexander Gyan is a Ghanaian politician and member of parliament for the Kintampo South constituency in the Bono East region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Alexander nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii la Nwadisa atan la, dab pisi nɛ ayuobʋ la daar, 26 March 1980.
english: Alexander was born on 26 March 1980 and hails from Ampoma-Kintampo South in the Bono East region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da naae o SSSCE nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999) la ni.
english: He had his SSSCE in 1999.

kusaal: Ka tɔlisi maali o BSc.
english: He further had his BSc.

kusaal: in Agriculture Education yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012).
english: in Agriculture Education in 2012.

kusaal: Alexander da anɛ Diisi (District Chief Executive) bɛ Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development bɛ Kintampo South District.
english: Alexander was the District Chief Executive at the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development for Kintampo South District.

kusaal: Alexander anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP la nid ka an Wadmaani tis, MP Kintampo South Constituency.
english: Alexander is a member of NPP and currently the MP for Kintampo South Constituency.

kusaal: Alexander paassnɛ la'askanɛ an Government Assurance Committee ka lɛn paas banɛ gɔsid pian'ad yɛla la (Communications Committee).
english: Alexander is a member of the Government Assurance Committee and also a member of the Communications Committee.

kusaal: O yinɛ Ampomah-Kintampo South n bɛ Bono East region sʋ'ʋlim Gaana la.
english: Alexander was born on 26 March 1980 and hails from Ampoma-Kintampo South in the Bono East region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne la Nwadis piinɛ yinne (November 2021) la, Alexander da pʋdig sakur biis banɛ bɛ Kintampo South sʋ'ʋlkim nwɛnɛ tusir, kɔbistan nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (1357) banɛ da ye ba sɔbi ba karim gaat taaba (BECE) la diib nɛ lɔnam ka ba zii ba keŋ.
english: In November 2021, Alexander provided free food and transportation to about 1357 students who were BECE candidates in the Kintampo South constituency.

kusaal: Alexander Kodwo Kom Abban anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka mɛ paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n zi'enɛ tis Gomoa West sʋ'ʋlʋm teŋkanɛ bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Alexander Kodwo Kom Abban (born 6 December 1973) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Gomoa West Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Gomoa Dawurampong, teŋkanɛ bɛ Ghana, Central Region sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: Abban was born on 6 December 1973 and hails from Gomoa Dawurampong in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o masta Digirii bɛ wada zamisʋg linɛ an Bankin nɛ Ligidi wada zamisʋg yɛla la n yi Boston University, sakur linɛ zamisid Wada yɛla la yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) la ni.
english: He had his Master of Law degree in Banking and Financial law from the Boston University School of Law in 2008.

kusaal: O da di'e o tiim kasɛta gbaʋŋ n yi lʋgir kanɛ ka ba buon ye Medical and Dental Council la ni.
english: He had his Medical License from the Medical and Dental Council.

kusaal: O da maali o yiiga digirii zamisʋg linɛ ka ba buon ye Human Biology lanɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, ka yii anina keŋ Sakur kan ni ya'asi maal Digirii linɛ zamisʋgʋ an na'asaatima nɛ Pɛrisin maalʋg yɛla.
english: He also had his Bachelor of Science degree in Human Biology from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Bachelor of Science degree in Medicine and Surgery from the same institution.

kusaal: O da lɛn Keŋ tuon ya'as maal masta digirii linɛ an nimma'asim zamisʋg yɛla yi Hamburg School of Applied Science sakur la ni.
english: He further had his master's degree in public health from the Hamburg School of Applied Science.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn paam kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi German sakur Goethe Institute linɛ bɛ Ankara sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: He also had a certificate in German from the Goethe Institut in Accra.

kusaal: Abban da anɛ onɛ an san'an-san'an kati wa'ae wada yɛla lin da yi yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ atan' (2013) ti paae yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (2014) la ni, n bɛ Ghana Stock Exchange.
english: Abban was a Legal Advisor from 2013 to 2014 at Ghana Stock Exchange.

kusaal: O mɛ da anɛ pa'an n bɛ Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration lin da yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2009) la ti paae yuum tusa ayi' nɛ piiga (2010).
english: He was also a lecturer at the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration from 2009 to 2010.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri pisnaasi ne awi dʋ'ali ayuobʋ (49.6%) n yi vɔɔt la wʋsa ni ka o tiraan Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid Samuel Fletcher la mɔr vɔɔt bam 21,004 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri pisnaasi nɛ anu dʋ'ali anii (45.8%) n yi vɔɔt la wʋsa ni, ka PPP nid Charles Yawson la mɛ mɔr vɔt bam 2,086 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 4.6% n yi vɔt la wʋsa ni ka CPP nid Stephen Afriyie la mɛ da mɔr vɔt bam zaalim ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 0 0.0% n yi vɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He won with 22,741 votes making 49.6% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Samuel Fletcher had 21,004 votes making 45.8% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Charles Yawson had 2,086 votes making 4.6% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Stephen Afriyie had 0 vote making 0.0% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Abban da kɔ'ɔŋ Gomoa West sʋ'ʋlʋm kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi ne pisi (2020) kanɛ ka Ghana dim da maal vɔt ka o li ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la Richard Gyan Mensah di ka bas o.
english: Abban lost the Gomoa West Constituency parliamentary seat during the 2020 Ghanaian general elections to the NDC parliamentary candidate Richard Gyan Mensah.

kusaal: O da paamnɛ vɔt bam 25,235 linɛ bigis ye kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da paamnɛ 44.9% n yi vɔt kanl wʋsa ka Richard mɔr vɔt bam 29,822 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da paamnɛ 53.0% n yi vɔt la wʋsa ni, ka GUM nid la Edmond Panyin Enchill mɛ mɔr 716 kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o paam 1.3% n yi vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni, ala ka PPP nid la Charles Yawson da mɔr 481 kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɛ paam 0.9% n yi vɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: He lost with 25,235 votes making 44.9% of the total votes cast whilst Richard had 29,822 votes making 53.0% of the total votes cast, the GUM parliamentary candidate Edmond Panyin Enchill had 716 votes making 1.3% of the total votes cast, and the PPP parliamentary candidate Charles Yawson had 481 votes making 0.9% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O mɔr pu'a ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Anastasia Antoinette Abban, ka ba mɔr biis anaasi.
english: A Catholic, he and his wife, Anastasia Antoinette Abban, have four children.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Abban nɛ nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la daba ayuobʋ daar yʋʋm tusir kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan (1973) la ni.
english: Abban was born on 6 December 1973 and hails from Gomoa Dawurampong in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn anɛ pa'an n bɛ Ghana School of Law la ni lin da yi yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii ti paae yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anu la ni.
english: He was also a Part-time lecturer at the Ghana School of Law from 2010 to 2015.

kusaal: O da anɛ yir tʋʋma kariki kpɛɛm lin da yi yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai ti paae tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' n bɛ Ghana.
english: He was also a Part-time lecturer at the Ghana School of Law from 2010 to 2015.

kusaal: Abban anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Abban is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaan kʋdʋg n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n tis Gomoa West Sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ghana, Central Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: He was the former Member of Parliament in Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana for Gomoa West Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) ka Ghana dim da maal vɔɔt la, ka Abban di Gomoa West sʋ'ʋlʋm kʋk la.
english: During the 2016 Ghanaian general election, Abban won the Gomoa West Constituency parliamentary seat.

kusaal: Abban da anɛ Gɔmina la kpɛɛmnam yinne ka mɛ paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid nimma'asim lʋgʋr yɛla la.
english: Abban was a member of the Government Assurance Committee and also a member of the Health Committee.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig onɛ an Catholic karim biig.
english: A Catholic, he and his wife, Anastasia Antoinette Abban, have four children.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Minista kanɛ gɔsid laafi lʋgʋr yɛla kpɛɛm nya'andɔl.
english: He is the former Deputy Minister for Health.

kusaal: Alexander Kwamina Afenyo-Markin (27 sigsaa 1978) anɛ Wadmaani bɛ Ghana wadmaanib yir la tis Effutu constituency bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: Alexander Kwamina Afenyo-Markin (born 27 May 1978) is the Member of Parliament for the Effutu constituency, Central Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Nannanna, onɛ an Wadmaanib banɛ gat la kpɛɛm nya'adɔl (Deputy Majority Leader) Ghana Wadmaanib yin la.
english: He was the Deputy Majority Leader in the eighth Parliament of Ghana until February 2024, when he was promoted to Majority Leader as part of a reshuffle by President Nana Akufo-Addo and the leadership of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da zamis wada yɛla lɔyanam (tʋʋma) University of Buckingham, (LLB/mgt, yʋma tusa ayi nɛ atan' keŋ paae yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2003–2006), Ghana School of Law la ni ka o da di'e Barrister at Law kasɛtta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2007-2009), ka di'e M.A in international politics nɛ security studies University of Bradford yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piiga (2009-2010).
english: He studied law at the University of Buckingham (LLB/MGT, 2003–2006) and the Ghana School of Law, where he received a Barrister at Law certification (2007–2009), and received an MA in international politics and security studies at the University of Bradford (2009–2011).

kusaal: Yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999) nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' (2003) sʋʋgʋn, Effutu wadmaan la da anɛ Principal Postal Officer tis Ghana Post Company Limited.
english: Between the years 1999 and 2003, the Effutu legislator worked as a Principal Postal Officer at the Ghana Post Company Limited.

kusaal: Ya'asa, o da lɛn tʋm Excel Courier Ghana Limited aan ba Director yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi (2004) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ yinne (2011) ka lɛn an Associate bɛɛ Dehenya Chambers yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piiga (2010) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la ni.
english: Also, he worked at the Excel Courier Ghana Limited as the Director between 2004 and 2011 and as an Associate at Dehenya Chambers from 2010 to 2016.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) la nii, Afenyo-Markin da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg NPP la zug nyi'a nɛ Ma'asim tiig (NDC) nid la, Mike Allen Hammah ka di.
english: In 2016, on the ticket of the NPP, Afenyo-Markin contested the NDC parliamentary candidate, Mike Allen Hammah and won.

kusaal: O da an kʋkdaani tis Ghana Water Company Ltd (GWCL) yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) la ni.
english: He became the chairman of Ghana Water Company Ltd (GWCL) in 2017.

kusaal: O paas la'asʋg kanɛ gɔsid fuud dim la (Defense and the Interior Finance Committee) Ghana Wadmaanib yin la.
english: He has been on the Committees of Defence, Interior and Finance in Ghana's Parliament respectively.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne la ni (2021), Afenyo-Markinnɛ nimbama; Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah, Johnson Kwaku Adu, Laadi Ayii Ayamba nɛ Emmanuel Kwasi Bedzrah da paam suori paas Extraordinary Session yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) ECOWAS Wadmaanib dinɛ da naam Freetown bɛ Sierra Leone la.
english: In 2021, Afenyo-Markin, together with Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah, Johnson Kwaku Adu, Laadi Ayii Ayamba and Emmanuel Kwasi Bedzrah, was sworn in during the Extraordinary Session 2021 of the Parliament of the ECOWAS, which happened in Freetown in Sierra Leone.

kusaal: Pa'an yinne kɔmputa yinne la da zuŋnɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anii Nwadis piiga la dabpiinɛ atan' la daar (13 October 2018), o da tis pa'anib banɛ bɛ Effutuman kɔmputanam kɔbiga (100 laptops) Ebenezer Methodist Church bɛ Winneba la.
english: The One Teacher, One Laptop initiative was launched on 13 October 2018, during the donation of 100 laptops to teachers within the Effutuman at the Ebenezer Methodist Church in Winneba.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋm paal Nwadig la (January, 2021), pa'anib banɛ an saam pisnaasi (40 newly posted teachers) da di'e kɔmputanam la (laptops) ye di sʋŋ pa'alʋg nɛ zamisʋg.
english: In January 2021, 40 newly posted teachers received laptops to enhance teaching and learning.

kusaal: Gban'ar kaŋa yɛlaa, o tis pa'anib banɛ bɛ gɔmena nɛ asʋ'oe-m-mɛŋ sakuya banɛ bɛ o sʋ'ʋlimin la kɔmputanam tusir yinne (1000 laptops)
english: Through this initiative, about 1000 laptops have been donated to teachers of both private and public schools in the constituency.

kusaal: The Effutu Dream da pin'ilnɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayi' la ni (February 2020) ye di sʋŋ ka Effutuman buudi malima dinɛ na kɛ ka pu'asada nɛ dasam na mi'i ba buudi malima ka mi' ban yi zin'isia na.
english: The Effutu Dream was initiated in February 2023 to promote the Effutuman culture, which will create a sense of belonging among the youth in its constituency.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadisa atan daba ayɔpɔi (7 March 2020), Afenyo-Markin da sɛ abɛ tiis (Royal Palm trees) Winneba tempʋʋgin.
english: On 7 March 2020, Afenyo-Markin planted Royal Palm trees in the Winneba capital.

kusaal: Afenyo-Markin mɔr pʋ'a, Dianne Markin ka ba mɔr biis.
english: Afenyo-Markin is married to Dianne Markin.

kusaal: O paasnɛ la'askanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Freemason.
english: He is a Freemason.

kusaal: O da paas la'asʋg kanɛ gɔsid fuud dim yɛla la (Defense and Interior Committee) Ghana Wadmaanib yin la.
english: He serves on several committees, including the Committee on Defence and Interior.

kusaal: Di da anɛ ye di tiak Effutu Constituency ka saam nɛ kpikpinnib kena.
english: The dream aimed at branding Effutu Constituency to attract tourists and investors.

kusaal: Nɛ' zug da kɛya ka ba buol la'asʋg ka sigi di ye "Actualizing the Effutu Dream; the role of Effutu youth".
english: The Effutu Dream was initiated in February 2023 to promote the Effutuman culture, which will create a sense of belonging among the youth in its constituency.

kusaal: O nwɛ'ɛd tennis nɛ golf.
english: He plays table tennis and golf.

kusaal: Hottordze anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni zi'eni tis Central Tongu Constituency bɛ Volta Region la ka zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la zug.
english: Hottordze (born 9 May 1969) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Central Tongu Constituency in the Volta Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Hottordze yinɛ Mafi- Kumase sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: Born on 9 May 1969, Hottordze hails from Mafi-Kumase.

kusaal: O mɔr M.B.A kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Cape Coast University la ni.
english: He holds an M.B.A from the Cape Coast University and an M.A from the University of Social Studies.

kusaal: Ka lɛn mɔr M.A kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi University of Social Studies.
english: He holds an M.B.A from the Cape Coast University and an M.A from the University of Social Studies.

kusaal: Alfred Obeng-Boateng dʋ'anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan Nwadis piinɛ ayi dabpisi nɛ atan daar (23 November 1973) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid.
english: Alfred Obeng-Boateng (born 23 November 1973) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Bibiani-Anhwiaso-Bekwai constituency bɛ Western North Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Bibiani-Anhwiaso-Bekwai constituency in the Western North Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Obeng-Boateng yinɛ Subiri Nkwanta.
english: Obeng-Boateng hails from Subiri Nkwanta.

kusaal: O da naae Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, ka mɔr masters of law (Oil and Gas).
english: A graduate of Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, he holds masters of law (Oil and Gas).

kusaal: Alfred Oko Vanderpuije anɛ onɛ ka ba da du'a o daba anaasi daar, nwadis piiga nɛ yinne, yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anu la ni (4 sapal nwadig 1955) anɛ Ghana nid nɛ gbaʋŋ mi'id nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd, ka an wadmaan bɛ wadmaanib yin la.
english: Alfred Oko Vanderpuije (born 4 November 1955) is a Ghanaian educationist and politician who currently serves as a member of parliament.

kusaal: Dutch du'am yʋ'ʋr anɛ Dutch Surname ka li pa'ali o kpinnim nɛ Euro-African du'am tuŋ n an si'em.
english: His Dutch surname reflects his Euro-African descent.

kusaal: Vanderpuiji yaanam da yinɛ Sint- Maartensdijk teŋ kanɛ ka ba da buon nɛ li ye Tholen ka li bɛ Netherlands teŋgbaυŋ sυ'υlυmin la.
english: The ancestors of Vanderpuije originally came from Sint-Maartensdijk on the former island of Tholen in the Netherlands.

kusaal: O yaaba Jacobus van de Puije da anɛ gɔmma bɛ Dutch Gold Coast kanɛ ka ba buon nɛ Li nannana ye Ghana la, 1780 yʋʋm la ni.
english: His ancestor, Jacobus van der Puije, was governor of the Dutch Gold Coast in 1780.

kusaal: Vanderpuije zamisnɛ Postsecendary degree in Education, Accra Teacher Training College la yʋʋma atan' pʋʋgin.
english: Vanderpuije studied at Accra Teacher Training College for a 3-year Postsecondary degree in education.

kusaal: O mɔr nɛ Mid America Nazarene College kaset gbaʋŋi an Masters in Education la, ka mɔr University of Missouri, Kansas City U.S.A kasɛt gbaʋŋi an, Specialist in Education Administration la.
english: He holds a Masters in Education from Mid America Nazarene College and a Specialist in Education Administration from the University of Missouri, Kansas City, U.S.A.

kusaal: O da anɛ Accra Mayor la, sa kan la Ghana Gɔmina Zugraan kʋdʋg President John Atta Mills da gaŋ o zin'il 2009 yʋʋm la ni ka ti gɔmina Zugraan kʋdʋg, President John Dramani Mahama da kɛ ka o tʋm anina ti paae yʋʋm 2017 la ni.
english: He was the former Mayor of Accra, installed in that office by President John Atta Mills in 2009 and he was maintained in that office by President John Dramani Mahama, completing his second term in 2017.

kusaal: Vanderpuije da zi'en ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) la nɔba zug n nyi'a di Ablekuma South n bɛ Greater Accra Region la wadmaan kυk la keŋ Parliament Ghana vɔɔtʋg kanɛ da maal 2016 yυʋm la, n zaŋi li yʋʋma anaasi bɛn la.
english: Vanderpuije was elected to the Parliament of Ghana in the 2016 elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to represent the Ablekuma South Constituency in the Greater Accra Region for a four-year term.

kusaal: O da di Vɔɔtʋg la nɛ vɔɔtnam 31.927 n yi 59.041 vɔɔtnam pʋʋgin, ka lin an 54.36%.
english: He won the elections with 31,927 votes out of the 59,041 valid votes cast representing 54.36% of the votes.

kusaal: O wadmaan tʋʋmin la, o paasnɛ Foreign Affairs Committee, ka paas House Committee of Parliament Kpɛɛmnam la ni.
english: As an MP, he is a member of Foreign Affairs Committee and House Committee of Parliament.

kusaal: Vanderpuije da kɔ'ɔŋ o pu'a Gifty Naa Adei Vanderpuije 2012 yʋma la ni, o da kpinɛ Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital.
english: Vanderpuije lost his wife Gifty Naa Adei Vanderpuije in 2012, when she died at Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital.

kusaal: 2019 yʋʋm la ni, yʋʋma ayɔpɔi o pu'a kum la nya'aŋ, Vanderpuije da lɛn zaŋ Cynthia Amerley Ayiku k'o aan o pu'a.(wife)
english: In 2019, Vanderpuije got remarried to Cynthia Amerley Ayiku after seven years of losing his wife.

kusaal: 2021 yʋʋm la, nwadisa awai daba awai da an Lamsi daarɛ, o da zi'en Sakaman Junction nɛn n sʋo suokenib ba da dɔla ani ken Dansoman roundabout suotita'ar la ni.
english: On the night of Thursday 9 September 2021, he directed traffic on the Sakaman Junction to the Dansoman roundabout stretch.

kusaal: Alfred oko vanderpuiji an Ablekuma Suoth Constituency MP la, da kpɛn zi'e nɛ kiŋkiŋi nɛ Parliament n zan'as ye LGBTQ+ wada la da zi'en Ghana.
english: Alfred Oko Vanderpuije, MP for Ablekuma South Constituency, in October 2021 reaffirmed Parliament's rejection of LGBTQ+ legalization in Ghana.

kusaal: O ye, Ghana pʋ gban'ae ye ba na siak ka kpɛn'ɛs LGBTQ+ nyadi la wada ni, woo U S nɛ Europe dimɛ siak ka di'e li si'em la.
english: He affirmed Ghana's decision against enacting laws that endorse LGBTQ+ rights, marking a distinction from the perspectives in the U.S. and Europe.

kusaal: Nananna, o anɛ Ablekuma South Constituency wadmaan bɛ Greater Accra Region, Ghana.
english: He is currently the member of parliament for Ablekuma South Constituency in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Jamestown nid.
english: A Jamestown native, he was born and bred at Mamprobi, Darkuman, and Dansoman at various stages of his childhood.

kusaal: O nɔbig nɛ Mamprobi, Darkuman nɛ Dansoman tensin.
english: A Jamestown native, he was born and bred at Mamprobi, Darkuman, and Dansoman at various stages of his childhood.

kusaal: O da yii anina lɛn tɔlisi keŋ University of Missouri Kansas City bɛ U.S.A la naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Specialist in Education Administration.
english: He holds a Masters in Education from Mid America Nazarene College and a Specialist in Education Administration from the University of Missouri, Kansas City, U.S.A.

kusaal: O da tʋm nɛ'ɛŋa nɛ suorin la langima namɛ da ka' ani la yɛla, ye li sʋŋ ka suokennib (users using that road) la paam yɔlsʋm suor la zug.
english: His actions brought relief to users using that road.

kusaal: O da yɛl ye tinamɛ paae si'el buudi malimanam wʋsa Ghana pʋʋgin nɛɛ, ti pʋ nyɛ ka pu'a zaŋi o pu'a tiraanɛ niŋi o pu'aa, bɛɛ dau mɛ niŋ ala nɛ o dau tiraana.
english: He expressed the view that throughout Ghana's cultural history, the concept of same-sex marriage has been met with strong disapproval, transcending geographical and tribal distinctions.

kusaal: Vanderpuiji, onɛ an Ablekuma South wadmaan la yɛl ye, li sʋm ka ban gaŋ sɔ' la tʋm nɛ Accra Regional Minister lin na niŋ si'em ka Accra sadʋʋma yɛl la paam maalʋg o ya'a tʋʋma ba ya'a siaki tis o tʋʋm la ( confirmed)
english: He urged Madam Elizabeth Sackey to cooperate with the Accra Regional Minister upon taking office.

kusaal: Alhassan Bashir Fuseini ka bɛdigʋ mi'i o ye Alhaji A.B.A Fuseini (fuluŋfug nwadig 2, 1956) la anɛ labaya tʋntʋn ka lɛn an pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Hon. Alhassan Bashir Alhassan Fuseini (born 2 February 1956), popularly known as Alhaji A. B. A. Fuseini, is a Ghanaian journalist and politician, who is the former deputy Northern Regional Minister of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Tamale, tenkanɛ bɛ Northern Region n bɛ Ghana la sʋ'ʋlim.
english: He hails from Tamale, a town in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Yendi secondary school nɛ T.I. Ahmadiyya Senior High School, Kumasi.
english: He had his secondary education at Yendi secondary school and T.I. Ahmadiyya Senior High School, Kumasi.

kusaal: O da maal o yiiga digrii nɛ University of Ghana, ka lin nya'aŋ ka o keŋ Essex University bɛ UK la ka di'e master's digirii in Human Rights yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' (1993) la ni.
english: He earned his first degree at the University of Ghana, after which he entered the University of Essex, UK, obtaining a master's degree in Human Rights in 1993.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛm mɔr Post Graduate Diploma linɛ ka o paam yi International Institute of Journalism bɛ Berlin.
english: He also holds a Postgraduate Diploma from the International Institute of Journalism, Berlin.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana Northern Region la minista nya'adɔl kʋdʋg.
english: He is a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Sagnarigu (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O paas Ghana wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: He is a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Sagnarigu (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Sagnarigu teŋkanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He is a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Sagnarigu (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Fuseini nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ la Nwadisi ayi' la daba ayi' daar (Fuluŋfug nwadig 2, 1956).
english: Fuseini was born on 2 February 1956.

kusaal: Fuseini anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid (NDC).
english: During the 2023 NDC primaries, Fuseini lost the election to Attah Issah with 333 votes after the delegates give him 801 votes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni (2012), o da zi'en Ma'asim tiig nɔba zugʋ nyi'a Sagnarigu wadmaan kʋk la ka di, ka keŋ paas Ghana wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayuobʋ la, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He is a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Sagnarigu (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da anɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim Minista nya'andɔl yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' (2013) keŋ paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017).
english: Member Parliament (7 January 2013–present; 2nd term)

kusaal: Wadmaan yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ atan' yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar ken paae zina (yʋʋmpaal nwadig 7, 2013–paae zina ; 2nd term)
english: Member Parliament (7 January 2013–present; 2nd term)

kusaal: Alhaji Alhassan Kobina Ghansah anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka da naae Breman Asikuma Senior High School ka bɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress la ni.
english: Alhaji Alhassan Kobina Ghansah is a Ghanaian politician and an old student of Breman Asikuma Senior High School who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa (AOB) Constituency bɛ Central region.
english: He is the member of Parliament for the Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa (AOB) Constituency in the Central Region.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Ghansahnɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ Nwadis piinɛ yinne la dabpisi nɛ awai daar (29 November 1960), o yinɛ Breman Bedum bɛ Central Region, Ghana la.
english: Ghansah was born on 29 November 1960 and hails from Breman Bedum in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O maal Masters' degree in Business Administration yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu la ni (2015).
english: He had his master's degree in business administration in 2015.

kusaal: Ghansah da anɛ Managing Proprietor tis Classic Rahman Enterprise.
english: Ghansah was the managing proprietor of Classic Rahman Enterprise.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016 ) vɔɔtʋgin la Ghansah da zi'en National Democratic Congress bɛ Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa Constituency ka li ka New Patriotic Party nid, Anthony Effah da gaad o vɔɔt kɔbisnaasi nɛ pistan (430).
english: In the 2016 elections Ghansah represented the National Democratic Congress in the Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa Constituency but lost to the New Patriotic Party's candidate Anthony Effah with a difference of 430 votes.

kusaal: Vɔɔtkan nii o da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ atan, kɔbistan nɛ pistan (23,330) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai du'al pisi kɔbiga (49.20%) ka o tiraan la, Effah paam tusa tusa pisi nɛ atan, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobʋ (23,760) dinɛ an pisnu du'al piinɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.11%).
english: In that election he had 23,330 votes representing 49.20% and against Effah's 23,760 votes representing 50.11%.

kusaal: Ghansah da kpɛn' o na'am nya'ab nɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg NDC vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa Constituency gur yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Ghansah entered the race for the parliamentary candidate again in the NDC primaries in the Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa Constituency ahead of the 2020 elections.

kusaal: Ghansah da di wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la, National Democratic Congress tis Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa Constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la yʋʋm tusa ani nɛ piinɛ awai Nwadisa anii la ni (August 2019) nɛ vɔɔt kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (886) gaadi o taaba Michael Harry Yamson nɛ Eric Kwesi Taylor banɛ paam kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nɛ atan (153) nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayi (42).
english: Ghansah won the parliamentary bid to represent the National Democratic Congress for the Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa Constituency ahead of the 2020 elections in August 2019 after securing 886 votes to beat his two other opponents Michael Harry Yamson and Eric Kwesi Taylor who had 153 votes and 42 votes respectively.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la Nwadis piinɛ ayi la (December 2020),Ghansah da di kʋk la Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwat Constituency nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anii, kɔbiga nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (28,175) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ ayi pisnu nɛ ayi du'al pisnu nɛ anaasi (52.54%) ka onɛ da nya' nɛ o la, Emmanuel Domson Adjei onɛ an New Patriotic Party paam tusa pisi nɛ anu, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi (25,454) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (47.46%).
english: In December 2020, Ghansah won the seat for Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwat Constituency in the parliamentary elections after polling 28,175 votes representing 52.54% against his only opponent, Emmanuel Domson Adjei of the New Patriotic Party who had 25,454 votes representing 47.46%.

kusaal: Ghansah paas Special Budget Committee ka lɛn paas Environment, Science and Technology Committee.
english: Ghansah is a member of the Special Budget Committee and also a member of the Environment, Science and Technology Committee.

kusaal: Ghansah bɛnɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress ni.
english: Ghansah is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Alhassan Sayibu Suhuyini (ba da du'a o nɛ 12 mɔtul nwadig 1979) anɛ Ghana labadi'es nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Alhassan Sayibu Suhuyini (born 12 September 1979) is a Ghanaian broadcast journalist and politician.

kusaal: O paas nɛ Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Tamale North sʋ'ʋlʋm dim.
english: He is currently a member of the eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing Tamale North.

kusaal: Alhassan Suhuyini da keŋnɛ Ghana Secondary School dinɛ yʋ'ʋn an Ghana Senior High School, GHANASCO bɛ Tamale sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: Alhassan Suhuyini attended Ghana Secondary School now Ghana Senior High School (Tamale), GHANASCO in Tamale.

kusaal: Development management kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration.
english: Development management from Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration.

kusaal: O da pin'ili o labadi'esʋg tʋʋma nɛ Diamond FM bɛ Tamale la ka naan yi keŋ Ghana tenpʋtita'arin la.
english: His career as a radio presenter started at Diamond FM in Tamale before he moved to the capital of Ghana.

kusaal: O da tʋm bi'ela bɛ Citi FM nɛ Metro TV bɛ Accra la ka naan keŋ tʋm nɛ Radio Gold.
english: He had brief stints with Citi FM and Metro TV in Accra before settling with Radio Gold.

kusaal: Banɛ kɛlisid labaya da vɔɔt o ka o di Talk Show Host yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ yinne, (2011), yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' (2013) la.
english: He was voted Talk Show Host of the year in 2011, 2012 and 2013 by Radio listeners in Ghana at the Ghana Radio and Television Personality Awards.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' la (2013), South Korean government da gaŋ o, ka yɔ tis o ye o keŋ South Korea paas Next Generational Leaders from Africa program.
english: In 2013 he was selected and sponsored by the South Korean government to tour South Korea as part of its Next Generational Leaders from Africa program.

kusaal: O da anɛ delegate yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (2014) International Visitor Leadership Program, a United States Department of State professional exchange program.
english: He was a delegate at the 2014 International Visitor Leadership Program, a United States Department of State professional exchange program.

kusaal: O da tʋm Radio Gold bɛ Accra la, anina o da tʋm zin'isa ayi' the morning show called the "Gold Power Drive" nɛ weekend socio-economic and political current affairs program - Alhaji and Alhaji talk show.
english: He worked at Radio Gold in Accra, where he was the host of two of the station's flagship programs; the morning show called the "Gold Power Drive" and the weekend socio-economic and political current affairs program - Alhaji and Alhaji talk show.

kusaal: Pirɛsidɛn John Dramani Mahama da gaŋ o yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' la ni (2013) ye o paas Ghana Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA) ni.
english: He was appointed in 2013 by president John Dramani Mahama as board member of Ghana Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA).

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi la ni (2014) onɛ da an banɛ gɔsid pian'ad yɛla tis (Communications Manager) National Hajj Council (Ghana).
english: As of 2014 he was the Communications Manager for the National Hajj Council (Ghana).

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnii (21,280) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (67.79%).
english: He won the seat by getting 21,280 votes representing 67.79% of the total number.

kusaal: O da dii o pʋ'a Hamdiya Amadu Yakubu Vorsk nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' 2013 la ni.
english: He married Hamdiya Amadu Yakubu Vorsky in 2013.

kusaal: Public Administration nɛ M.Sc.
english: Public Administration and an M.Sc.

kusaal: (Ghana Radio and Television Personality Awards).
english: He was voted Talk Show Host of the year in 2011, 2012 and 2013 by Radio listeners in Ghana at the Ghana Radio and Television Personality Awards.

kusaal: O da zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zugʋ nya' ka di Tamale North kʋk la yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi Ghana wʋsa vɔɔdʋg la ka lieb Wadmaan.
english: He is currently a member of the eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing Tamale North.

kusaal: Alaazi Alhassan Tampuli Sulemana anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Gushegu Constituency bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid.
english: Alhassan Sulemana Tampuli sometimes Hassan Tampuli, is a Ghanaian politician, lawyer, energy expert and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Gushegu Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ban da du'a Sulemana nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ, Nwadisa anu la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27 May, 1976) o ynɛ Zinindo bɛ Northern region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Sulemana was born on 27 May 1976 in Gushegu in the Northern Region of Ghana, and hails from Zinindo in the Northern region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maali o DPA in Public Administration yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi la ni (2002).
english: He further had his DPA in Public Administration in 2002.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ ka o maali o bachelor's degree in Public Administration yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: He later obtained his bachelor's degree in Public Administration in 2005.

kusaal: O da lɛn maali o LLB in General Law yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awa la ni (2009).
english: He again had his LLB in General Law in 2009.

kusaal: Sulemana anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, NPP nid ka an Wadmaani MP tis Gusheigu Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Northern region la.
english: Tampuli is a member of the NPP and currently the MP for the Gusheigu Constituency in the Northern region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Gaana vɔɔtʋg la, o da di Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan, kɔbisnaasi nɛ yinne (30,401) ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC nid la, Mohammed Yussif Malimali da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anii nɛ pisnu nɛ anu (28,055) ka NDP nid la, Abdulai Abdul-Razak da paam vɔɔt kɔbis yi nɛ pisnu (250).
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 30,401 votes whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Mohammed Yussif Malimali had 28,055 votes and the NDP parliamentary candidate Abdulai Abdul-Razak had 250 votes.

kusaal: O da maali o O Level nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994) nɛ o QCL in Barrister and Solicitor yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011).
english: He completed his O Level in 1994 graduating from the University of Ghana with a bachelor's degree in business administration.

kusaal: Sulemana da anɛ Chief Executive tis National Petroleum Authority.
english: From 2017 to 2021, Tampuli served as Chief Executive Officer of the National Petroleum Authority.

kusaal: Sulemana paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Wadmaanib yin suor dɔlisʋg la (Standing Orders), ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid kpikpiŋ yɛla (Business Committee) nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid tʋʋma tisid/ kpɛɛmnam gaansʋg yɛla (Appointments Committee).
english: Tampuli is a member of the Standing Orders Committee, also a member of the Business Committee and also a member of the Appointments Committee.

kusaal: O anɛ Minista nya'adɔl tis la'adi naanid zin'ig yinne wa'ae zin'ig yinne yɛla.
english: He is a former Deputy Minister for Transport.

kusaal: Alhassan Umar anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an pɔlitis wɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la, n bɛ Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Alhassan Umar (born 29 June 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Zabzugu Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Alhassan nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ nwadisa ayuobʋ li dabisim pisi nɛ awai daar (29 sigir nwadig 1966) m bɛ Zabzugu kanɛ bɛ Northern region Ghana nwa.
english: Alhassan was born on 29 June 1966 in Zabzugu on the Northern region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr Master of Business Administration n yit University of Phoenix, nɛ B.A Biological Science n yit State University of NJ ni, nɛ Rutgers University ni.
english: He holds a Master of Business Administration from the University of Phoenix, a BA Biological Science the State University of NJ, Rutgers University.

kusaal: O Lɛn mɔr pa'annib kasɛtta gbaʋŋ yit Gambaga Training College.
english: He also holds a Diploma Teachers Certificate from Gambaga Training College.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Zabzugu Constituency teŋkanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ulim la.
english: Alhassan Umar (born 29 June 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Zabzugu Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ali Maiga Halidu anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas ayɔpɔi, Ghana Republic kanɛ aan anaasi la, o anɛ wadmaan tis Dormaa West Constituency kanɛ bɛ Brong-Ahafo Region la ka zi'e wabʋg na'adɔɔg, nɔba zug.
english: Ali Maiga Halidu is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Dormaa West Constituency in the Brong-Ahafo Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ali Maiga Halidu nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii li nwadisa atanˈ la dabpii nɛ yinne daar (dawalig nwadig 11, 1980).
english: Ali Maiga Halidu was born on March 11, 1980.

kusaal: O yinɛ Nkrankwanta, bɛ Brong Ahafo Region.
english: He is from the Nkrankwanta, in the Brong Ahafo Region.

kusaal: Halidu da maali o bachelor's digirii bɛnɛ University of Cape Coast; O da tɔlis o gbaʋŋ zamisʋg la n keŋ maal o Master of Philosophy bɛ Cambridge dinɛ bɛ United Kingdom la.
english: Halidu acquired his bachelor's degree at the University of Cape Coast; he then furthered his education with a Master of Philosophy at the Cambridge in the United Kingdom.

kusaal: Ka Rome ya-dagɔbʋg dim zaba da naae yʋma tusa anu saŋa si'a la, ka Egypt dim yin dɔɔbiig buudi la pʋn yadigi paae tembanɛ bɛ Baltic mu'ar gbɛʋk linɛ bɛ German ya-nya'aŋ baba la.
english: By the end of the Western Roman Empire in the 5th century, the Egyptian domestic cat lineage had arrived in a Baltic Sea port in northern Germany.

kusaal: Li wa'alim nɛ niŋgbiŋ la anɛ wʋʋ 46cm nɛ, ka na nyaŋi dɔnlʋg agɔl wʋʋ 23-25 cm, ka zʋʋr la mɛ wa'am wʋʋ 30 cm nɛ.
english: It averages about 46 cm (18 in) in head-to-body length and 23–25 cm (9.1–9.8 in) in height, with about 30 cm (12 in) long tails.

kusaal: Fɛntidi o mɛŋ nwa buon nɛ cat righting reflex.
english: This reflex is known as the cat righting reflex.

kusaal: Ba vɛɛnsi nyɛ ka amus nami niŋig si'em tun'oe fɛntidi ba niŋgbina ba liib saŋa ni la, ka li anɛ "falling cat problem".
english: This has been investigated as the "falling cat problem".

kusaal: Amus buudi (Felidae) la tun'oe sikki ba nya'aŋ dim nɛ si'im, nɛ li gʋlʋb buudi bɛdigʋ.
english: The genus Felis genetically diverged from other Felidae around 6 to 7 million years ago.

kusaal: Feline ASIP gene la mɔrɛ coding exons nam atan'.
english: The feline ASIP gene consists of three coding exons.

kusaal: Yin amus buudi la nɛ ASIP allele la da tun'oe sikki gɛd nɛ si'im sabilig.
english: The domestic cat family demonstrated a cosegregation between the ASIP allele and black coloration of the coat.

kusaal: Nɛŋa nwa an linɛ bi'ela kɛ ka amus nini mɔr tapetum lucidum, linɛ tʋ'ʋsid bugum wʋsa linɛ kpɛn retina nii lɛbis nifin la, ka lin tisid nini la nyɛɛb la paŋ zibisigin.
english: This is partly the result of cat eyes having a tapetum lucidum, which reflects any light that passes through the retina back into the eye, thereby increasing the eye's sensitivity to dim light.

kusaal: Yin amus la lɛɛ mɔrɛ color vision kanɛ ka'a sʋmm, ka mɔr cone cells buudi nam ayi ma'aa, banɛ nyɛt nɛ saa saŋgbaʋŋ si'im nɛ dɔnbʋʋlʋm kanɛ gɛnd nɛ dɛn'ɛm si'im; o pʋ tun'oe nyɛt bakid si'im zian nɛ dɛn'ɛm sʋ'ʋŋaa.
english: The domestic cat has rather poor color vision and only two types of cone cells, optimized for sensitivity to blue and yellowish green; its ability to distinguish between red and green is limited.

kusaal: On tun'e tʋm middle wavelengths zin'isi'a li ya'a ka' rod cells la, tun'e anɛ cone kanɛ paas atan' si'a.
english: A response to middle wavelengths from a system other than the rod cells might be due to a third type of cone.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛŋa nwɛn wʋʋ li nyaŋi nyɛt zibisigin ka lɛɛ pʋ pa'an trichromatic nini nyɛɛbi an si'em.
english: This appears to be an adaptation to low light levels rather than representing true trichromatic vision.

kusaal: Amus nam mɛ mɔr nictitating membrane, ka li kɛt ka ba amisid ba nini la ka li pʋ lusidi ba gɔsigɔ.
english: Cats have a nictitating membrane, allowing them to blink without hindering their vision.

kusaal: Yin amus la kɛlisʋg ni mɔrɛ paŋ kɛ ka o wʋm vuud 500 Hz paae 32 KHz.
english: The domestic cat's hearing is most acute in the range of 500 Hz to 32 kHz.

kusaal: Li na nyaŋi baŋ ultrasound kanɛ kɛt ka li baŋid ultrasinic buolʋg nam banɛ ka dayuus naam.
english: It can detect ultrasound, including ultrasonic calls from rodent prey.

kusaal: Amus nam tun'oe wʋm nyuug sʋ'ʋŋa, ka li anɛ ba olfactory bulb la mɔrɛ paŋ nɛ olfactory mucosa la nindaa la yalim la, li zɛm wʋʋ 5.8 cm2 (0.90 in2), li zɛm ninsaal din la nɔɔra ayi.
english: Cats have an acute sense of smell, due in part to their well-developed olfactory bulb and a large surface of olfactory mucosa, about 5.8 cm2 (0.90 in2) in area, which is about twice that of humans.

kusaal: Amus nam anɛ banɛ nyaŋidi baŋid pheromones wʋʋ 3-mercapto-3-mythlbutan-1-ol, kanɛ ka ba mɔri pian'adi dɔlisid dʋ'ʋnim ni, ka bɛŋid niŋgbiʋŋ la lua kanɛ wʋm nyuug la.
english: Cats are sensitive to pheromones such as 3-mercapto-3-methylbutan-1-ol, which they use to communicate through urine spraying and marking with scent glands.

kusaal: Amus nam bɛdigʋ sɔsid sʋ'ʋŋa nɛ tiis banɛ mɔr nepetalactone, kas kas catnip, ban tun'oe baŋid bʋn kan la pʋdigir yinne million pʋʋgin la.
english: Many cats also respond strongly to plants that contain nepetalactone, especially catnip, which they can detect at less than one part per billion.

kusaal: Tiis sieba wʋʋ silver vine (Actinidia polygama) nɛ valerian tiim vaang la mɛ siakid sɔsig nwa.
english: This response is also produced by other plants, such as silver vine (Actinidia polygama) and the herb valerian; it may be caused by the smell of these plants mimicking a pheromone and stimulating cats' social or sexual behaviors.

kusaal: Ninsaalib mɔri amino acid glutamic acid nɛ aspartic acid malisim, amaa dɔɔgbiis mɔri bʋnkpiilʋŋ nyuug nɛ I-Histidine malisim.
english: In humans, they detect the amino acids glutamic acid and aspartic acid; but in cats, they instead detect inosine monophosphate and histidine.

kusaal: Dɔɔgbiis mɛ mɔr saŋa kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb banɛ ni ka ba bɔɔd diib, Saŋkanɛ ka ba bɔɔd diib anɛ tʋʋlʋg ya'a ti an wʋʋ 38 °c (100 °F) linɛ an yinnɛ nɛ linɛ kpi paalim; dɔɔgbiis sieba zan'asid dima'asir (linɛ pa'an amus la ye, "bʋnkɔnb kanɛ kpi" la pʋn dɛŋim kpinɛ ka lieb bʋn bɛ'ɛd).
english: Cats distinctly prefer food temperature around 38 °C (100 °F), similar to a fresh kill.

kusaal: Yin amus nam 'scent rubbing' ittʋŋ nɛ nidib bɛɛ ba taaba, pʋtɛn'ɛr anɛ ye li dɔlisidi feline ittima ba taaba sʋʋgin.
english: Domestic cats' scent rubbing behavior toward humans or other cats is thought to be a feline means of social bonding.

kusaal: Ka linɛ lɛm pɛ'ɛs anɛ ye dumug la an yɛlkpan bʋn kanɛ ta'asidi feline immunodeficiency virus wiim kanɛ lɔɔsid amus nam bɛdegʋ la.
english: Bites are probably the main route of transmission of the feline immunodeficiency virus.

kusaal: Yin Amus nam anɛ banɛ gban'ad ka kʋʋd mɔɔgin niimis wʋʋ 1.3 ti paae 4.0 billion nɛ bʋnkɔnbid wʋʋ 6.3 ti paae 22.3 billion yʋʋm wʋsa bɛ America tɛɛnsin.
english: Domestic cats are a major predators of wildlife in the United States, killing an estimated 1.3 to 4.0 billion birds and 6.3 to 22.3 billion mammals annually.

kusaal: Ba da nyɛnɛ niimis banɛ ian'ad ka baŋ kɔli ba ningɔɔnrin, ka amus nam kʋʋ ba bam 31% bɛ Britain sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: In the recovery of ringed robins (Erithacus rubecula) and dunnocks (Prunella modularis) in Britain, 31% of deaths were a result of cat predation.

kusaal: Amus nya'asi buon pu'ana'anam la anɛ polyestrous, ka sigid nɛ nɔɔrim babiga yʋʋm yinne pʋʋgin, li zaŋid nɛ dabisa 21 sigib la saŋa.
english: Female cats, called queens, are polyestrous with several estrus cycles during a year, lasting usually 21 days.

kusaal: Bʋnnya'aŋ la na bʋʋlʋm agɔla bʋndaʋg la ya'a yisidi o yʋ'ori o ni la, bɔzugɔ amus daʋg yʋ'or la viligi nɛ si'eli kanɛ zɛmi nɛ wʋʋ120-150 bɛŋi lɛbid tutula ka kpa'ad penile spines ni, ka ba wa'alim an wʋʋ 1 mm (0.039 in); yu'or la yisib la ni, spines la paasid nɛ bʋnnya'aŋ la malisim la, linɛ yisid gɛl la niŋid du'asir la ni.
english: The female utters a loud yowl as the male pulls out of her because a male cat's penis has a band of about 120–150 backward-pointing penile spines, which are about 1 mm (0.04 in) long; upon withdrawal of the penis, the spines may provide the female with increased sexual stimulation, which acts to induce ovulation.

kusaal: Niŋgbina luos zaŋid nɛ dabisa 10 paad dabisa 12, tugud Pu'ana'anam pʋʋg mɔrim zaŋid nɛ dabisa 64 mɔri kenɛ paad dabisa 67 ni, ka saŋa la kiapi anɛ dabisa 65.
english: The gestation of queens lasts between 64 and 67 days, with an average of 65 days.

kusaal: United States teŋi nɛ, yin amus nam 80% anɛbanɛ ka' du'amm.
english: In the United States, about 80% of household cats are neutered.

kusaal: Sɔ' pʋ baŋ mɔɔgin amus nam kali zɛm si'em, amaa United States mak ye kal anɛ million nam 25 ken paad 60.
english: The numbers of feral cats are not known, but estimates of the United States feral population range from 25 to 60 million.

kusaal: United States teŋin, mɔɔgin amus nam nɛ yin amus gɔɔnda da kʋʋdi bʋnkɔnbid billion nam 6.3-22.3 yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: In the United States, feral and free-ranging domestic cats kill an estimated 6.3–22.3 billion mammals annually.

kusaal: Amus nam da kɛ ya ka Navassa curly-tailed lizard nɛ Chioninia coctel.
english: Cats have contributed to the extinction of the Navassa curly-tailed lizard and Chioninia coctei.

kusaal: United Kingdom teŋin, kpɛɛmnam 26% mɔrɛ amus, ka amus zuanam kal da an million nam 10.9 2020 yʋʋm la saŋa.
english: In the United Kingdom, 26% of adults have a cat, with an estimated population of 10.9 million pet cats as of 2020.

kusaal: 2021 yʋʋm la saŋa, ba da mak ye nidib da mɔri wʋʋ amus amus nam million 220, ka amus nam banɛ yii bɔdig zɛm wʋʋ million nam 480.
english: As of 2021, there were an estimated 220 million owned and 480 million stray cats in the world.

kusaal: Li bɔɔd wʋʋ amus anu ye li zaŋi maal kɔnbʋlʋg fuug Li tʋʋm kaŋa nwa wada la pʋlɛn tʋm United States teŋinɛ, 2000 yʋʋm la ni sa, ka European Union (la'am nɛ United Kingdom) 2007 la ni sa.
english: This use has been outlawed in the United States since 2000 and in the European Union (as well as the United Kingdom) since 2007.

kusaal: Ba makid yin amus nam kal dunia ni wʋsa zu'oe zɛm nɛ lin zaŋ million nam 200 ti paae million nam 600.
english: General estimates for the global population of domestic cats range widely from anywhere between 200 million to 600 million.

kusaal: O da yɛl ye o da ki'e amus nam 90,000 foto nam o tʋʋma la saŋa ni, ka da yis foto nam 255,000 banɛ da bɛ suakin, k'o da ki'e ba o vʋm saŋa la.
english: He is reported to have photographed 90,000 cats during his career and maintained an archive of 225,000 images that he drew from for publications during his lifetime.

kusaal: Amus nam tun'oe paam ban'as, bɛɛ tis ban'as nɛ viruses, bacteria, fungus, protozoans, arthropods bɛɛ zuzunya banɛ kɛt ka ban'as lɔ'ɔŋ nidib.
english: Cats can be infected or infested with viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungus, protozoans, arthropods or worms that can transmit diseases to humans; infections of most concern include salmonella, cat-scratch disease, and toxoplasmosis.

kusaal: Ban'as banɛ daanmid hali anɛ salmonella, cat--scratch disease, nɛ toxoplasmosis.
english: Cats can be infected or infested with viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungus, protozoans, arthropods or worms that can transmit diseases to humans; infections of most concern include salmonella, cat-scratch disease, and toxoplasmosis.

kusaal: Egypt kʋdʋg teŋi nɛ, ba da na'asid amus nam nɛ, ka pu'ana'ab ɛɛnti (basted) wʋʋ amus nɛ, saŋa sieba ni, o liebid nɛ wʋʋ gbigim nya'aŋi bɛ zaba ni.
english: In ancient Egypt, cats were revered.

kusaal: Greek nid, Herodotus onɛ mɔr si'iŋirin baŋir la da yɛl ye, amus kʋʋb da anɛ kisʋg, ka yi si'a amus ya da kpi, yi kan dim da bɛnɛ sunsan'aŋin, ka na pʋn ba ninkan'ad.
english: The Greek historian Herodotus reported that killing a cat was forbidden, and when a household cat died, the entire family mourned and shaved their eyebrows.

kusaal: Nidib da zaŋi di ba amus banɛ kpi la ken Bubastis tenpʋtita'ari an pʋ'ʋsim zin'ig la, ani ka ba na maal niŋgbiuŋ la linɛ na kɛ ka li kʋ san'am tɔ'ɔ, ka su'a li pʋ'ʋsim su'ak zin'igin.
english: Families took their dead cats to the sacred city of Bubastis, where they were embalmed and buried in sacred repositories.

kusaal: Herodotus da pa'al lin da an pakiri tis o si'em Egypt teŋin amus la yɛla, bɔzugɔ o da nan mi' nyɛnɛ mɔɔgin amus la.
english: Herodotus expressed astonishment at the domestic cats in Egypt, because he had only ever seen wildcats.

kusaal: Greek dim yiigin sa yɛlsida kanɛ ka nwa'asig kae ye Greek dim da mɔr amus nam ka ba yinɛ zin'is ayi ni, Magna Brescia, century piinɛ anu teŋsʋk la BC saŋa ni, ka ba an lokastos nɛ Phalanthos, banɛ da pin'il Rhegion nɛ nɛ Taras, ka di'em nɛ amus zuanam la.
english: The earliest unmistakable evidence of the Greeks having domestic cats comes from two coins from Magna Graecia dating to the mid-fifth century BC showing Iokastos and Phalanthos, the legendary founders of Rhegion and Taras respectively, playing with their pet cats.

kusaal: Greek kʋdʋg da bʋon 'amus' la ye ailouros, li gbin an ye, 'bʋn linɛ mɛnnim o zʋʋr la'.
english: The usual ancient Greek word for 'cat' was ailouros, meaning 'thing with the waving tail'.

kusaal: Aristotle yɛl ya, o bʋnkɔnbid si'iŋir gbaʋŋʋn la, ye "amus nya'as anɛ lecherous".
english: Aristotle remarked in his History of Animals that "female cats are naturally lecherous".

kusaal: Ka Greek dim la yuolim nya'aŋi la'asi ba mɛŋ winpuaki an Artsmis la, nɛ Egypt dim winpuaki an Bastet la naalim, ka zaŋ Bastet la'asa nɛ amus nam la paas Artemis la.
english: The Greeks later syncretized their own goddess Artemis with the Egyptian goddess Bastet, adopting Bastet's associations with cats and ascribing them to Artemis.

kusaal: Ovid's Metamorphoses, teŋgbana la da zɔɔ keŋ Egypt teŋinɛ lie bʋnkɔnbid sansi'a la, winpuak Diana la, da lieb nɛ amus.
english: In Ovid's Metamorphoses, when the deities flee to Egypt and take animal forms, the goddess Diana turns into a cat.

kusaal: Amus nam yʋʋn da ti nyaŋi kad weasels yis, ka lin anɛ bʋn dumma banɛ da san'amid bʋnbʋtta nɛ gʋ'ʋl yisib, bɔzugɔ ba bɛllim yaan da an sʋm ka ba mɛ da tɔn'ɔ tɔn'ɔsidi gban'ad dayuus sʋŋa.
english: Ancient Greeks and Romans kept weasels as pets, which were seen as the ideal rodent-killers.

kusaal: Amus nam anɛ Annunciation zanbina nɛ Holy Family, Italy dim sɔlima pa'al ye yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ nɔɔ ka Mary du'a Yeesu la, amus da du'a o biig Bethlehem teŋin.
english: Cats are often shown in icons of Annunciation and of the Holy Family and, according to Italian folklore, on the same night that Mary gave birth to Jesus, a cat in Bethlehem gave birth to a kitten.

kusaal: Japan teŋin, maneki neko amus la anɛ zanbin kanɛ tisid zugsʋŋ.
english: In Japan, the maneki neko cat is a symbol of good fortune.

kusaal: Jewish legend ni, yiiga amus la da bɛnɛ yiiga dau la Adam yin, kanɛ da bʋnkɔnbʋg zua, ka da yis kuus ka lɛn ka' yin na.
english: In Jewish legend, the first cat was living in the house of the first man Adam as a pet that got rid of mice.

kusaal: Bʋnkɔnbʋg si'a buudi pʋ bɛ Islam pʋ'ʋsimi nɛ, Muslims tisid amus nam girima.
english: Although no species are sacred in Islam, cats are revered by Muslims.

kusaal: Medievial Ypres, Belgium teŋin, ba tiendi linɛ innocuous dʋnbama Kattenstoet (amus pa'alʋg malima).
english: The killing of cats in medieval Ypres, Belgium, is commemorated in the innocuous present-day Kattenstoet (cat parade).

kusaal: Temis bɛdigʋ ni, ba ye ba vʋm la anɛ vʋm buudi ayɔpɔi.
english: In many countries, they are believed to have nine lives, but in Italy, Germany, Greece, Brazil, and some Spanish-speaking regions, they are said to have seven lives, while in Arabic traditions, the number of lives is six.

kusaal: Li da yuug ya hali ka ba baŋ ye Egypt teŋin ka ba da pin'ili nɔk amus ka o lieb yin bʋn yiiga, ani ka ba na'asid dɔɔbiis hali yit 3100 BC saŋa sa.
english: It was long thought that the domestication of the cat began in ancient Egypt, where cats were venerated from around 3100 BCE.

kusaal: Awa nam 148 saŋa ni, ka vir la naam.
english: At 148 hours, early blastocysts form.

kusaal: Biis 169 pʋʋgin, 127 da kpi ya ka nam pʋ paae nwadis ayuobʋ, ka li yinɛ baasi zabid nɛ ba pu'alimi ba, nɛ suor zugsapu'ad.
english: Of 169 kittens, 127 died before they were six months old due to a trauma caused in most cases by dog attacks and road accidents.

kusaal: Piank la "cat nap" kanɛ an vʋ'ʋsim fiinf la, anɛ amus ka gbɛɛm zɛɛgid o saŋa bi'ela pʋʋgin la.
english: The term "cat nap" for a short rest refers to the cat's tendency to fall asleep (lightly) for a brief period.

kusaal: Sieba mɛ bɛ ka an banɛ pʋ dit diibɔ ka lɛɛ diti wʋʋ daad, rɔbanam, kʋnt nwiis, gbana, guŋguma, kʋnt banɛ pigi, hali la'am nɛ kugsabilig.
english: Some also develop odd eating habits and like to eat or chew on things such as wool, plastic, cables, paper, string, aluminum foil, or even coal.

kusaal: Andrew Asiamah Amoako (24 February 1966) o anɛ Ghana lɔya, pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ aan anii la, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi annaasi la ni.
english: Andrew Asiamah Amoako (24 February 1966) is a Ghanaian lawyer, politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, elected to office in December 2020 as an independent candidate.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Amoako nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ 24-02-1966, Wioso-Adansi n bɛ Kumasi sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Amoako was born on 24 February 1966 at Wioso-Adansi in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O mɔr MSc in |r of Arts Zaba pansigir (Conflict Resolution) nɛ LLB (Law) yi Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology nɛ lɔyanam kasɛta gbaʋŋ (professional law licence (BL) yi Ghana lɔyanam sakurin la.
english: He holds an MSc in Environmental Resources Management, Master of Arts in Conflict Resolution and an LLB (Law) from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology and a professional law licence (BL) from the Ghana School of Law.

kusaal: On daa nam pʋ kpɛn' pɔlitis la, o daa anɛ lɔya bɛ Minka Premo and Co.
english: Before entering politics, he was a legal practitioner at the Minka Premo and Co. (Akosombo Chambers).

kusaal: O daa lɛn an Estates Officer, Land Officer nɛ Valuer Kumasi Metropolitant Assembly la ni.
english: He was the Estates Officer, Land Officer and Valuer at the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly.

kusaal: Wabʋg na'adɔɔg (NPP) gbansɔbid, John Boadu, yɛl ye Amoako na nyaŋi sɔb gbaʋŋ ka ba lɛn di'e o ya'as.
english: The General Secretary of the NPP, John Boadu, has suggested that Amoako could reapply for his NPP membership subject to specific party regulations and conditions.
