kusaal: Amoako an kʋkdaani tis la'askanɛ yʋ'ʋri an banɛ bɛ ɔfis banɛ mɔr nyɔɔd la, o daa paas banɛ gɔsid wadmaan yin suoya dɔlisʋg, la'as kanɛ gɔsid Subsidiary Legislation, la'as kanɛ gɔsid gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yɛla, nɛ banɛ gɔsid sanlimanam nɛ bugum yɛla.
english: Amoako is the chairperson of the Members Holding Offices of Profit Committee, a member of the Standing Orders Committee, a member of the Subsidiary Legislation Committee, a member of the Education Committee and a member of the Mines and Energy Committee.

kusaal: Nannanna, onɛ an Fomena n bɛ Kumasi sʋ'ʋlim la wadmaan.
english: He was the Estates Officer, Land Officer and Valuer at the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly.

kusaal: On da gban'e ye o kʋ nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi 2020 vɔɔtʋg la ka di yinɛ o mɛŋ na'adɔɔg dim la pʋ maal o sʋ'ʋŋa la, nya'aŋ o da gban'e ye o na nya'a o kɔn'ɔ-kɔn'ɔ ka o kʋ dɔl na'adɔsi'aa.
english: After deciding not to contest in the party's primaries prior to the 2020 general elections due to the unfair treatment he received from his own party, he decided to run as an independent candidate.

kusaal: Amoako da di Fomena kʋk la yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋg la nɛ vɔɔtnam tusa piinɛ Ayi, kɔbisnii nɛ anu ka onɛ dɔl o ka aan o mɛŋ na'adɔɔg nid la paam tusa piiga, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piswai nɛ anii.
english: Amoako first won the Fomena parliamentary seat during the December 2016 elections with 14,823 representing 72.7% under the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar, ba da gaŋ Asiamah ye paas Wadmaanib yir kpɛɛm nya'andɔl onɛ paas ayi.
english: On 7 January 2021, Asiamah was elected as the Second Deputy Speaker of Parliament.

kusaal: Ka di kpɛn' Ghana gbana pʋʋgin ye on ma'a an onɛ pʋ dɔl na'adɔɔg keŋɛ ka lieb kpɛɛm nya'adɔl.
english: He is the only independent member of parliament to have been elected to that position in the history of Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nid, ka dɔlisi ba wada gbaʋŋ la zug 3(9), daa yisi o mɛŋ ka yɛl Wadmaan yikpɛɛm la ka o tien yidim la ye o kʋk la yʋ'ʋŋ anɛ zaalim yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ pisi la nwadis anii la dabpiinɛ atan daar dɔlisid wada gbaʋŋ la yɛl si'em zug 97(1) .
english: He had been a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), which, citing Article 3(9) of its constitution, revoked his membership and notified the Speaker of Parliament, who duly declared his seat vacant on 13 October 2020 under the provisions of Article 97 (1)g of the Constitution.

kusaal: Lɔya Kwaku Asare da siaki Amoako yɛl si'el la, ka yɛl ye gba'akanɛ ka ba gban'e la anɛ ba dɔlis wada suor, ka di anɛ ba keŋ kɔɔtʋ nwɛnɛ wada gbaʋŋ la 99(1) yɛl si'em la.
english: Legal practitioner Kwaku Asare agreed with Amoako, arguing that such a decision is a legal matter which falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court, as specified by Article 99(1) of the Constitution.

kusaal: Onɛ lɛn an Wadmaanib yikpɛɛm kanɛ paas ayi'.
english: He is also the Second Deputy Speaker of the 8th Parliament of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Chiwitey yinɛ Nakoiyiri teŋkanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim Ghana la.
english: Chiwitey hails from Nakoiyiri in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: o mɔr HND in Sec/Management Studies dinɛ ka o maal bɛ Tamale Polytechnic nɛ Masters in Human Resource Development nɛ B.A, Master of Arts ka o maal bɛ University of Cape Coast.
english: He holds an HND in Sec/Management Studies from Tamale Polytechnic, Masters in Human Resource Development and a B.A, Master of Arts from the University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: Andrew Dari Chiwitey ( ba da du'a o nɛ 27 senlʋŋ nwadig 1970) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yir kanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Sawla-Tuna Kalba Constituency kanɛ bɛNorthern Region sʋ'ʋlim la, o zi'ennɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg zug.
english: Chiwitey was re-elected as a member of parliament for Sawla-Tuba Kalba constituency during the 2020 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress with 21,382 votes, equivalent to 65.9%.

kusaal: Andrew Kofi Egyapa Mercer (25 May 1973) anɛ Gaana lɔya nɛ pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Andrew Kofi Egyapa Mercer (born 25 May 1973) is a Ghanaian lawyer and politician.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Andrew Kofi Egyapa Mercer nɛ Sekondi n bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Andrew Kofi Egyapa Mercer was born in Sekondi in the Western Region of Ghana to James Mercer, a Ghanaian lawyer and diplomat.

kusaal: O da keŋ Chapel Hill Preparatory Schooli bɛ Takoradi la o primary saŋa.
english: He attended Chapel Hill Preparatory School in Takoradi for his primary education.

kusaal: Ka tɔlis keŋi Adisadel College n bɛ Cape Coast la, ani ka o da di'e o GCE Ordinary level nɛ GCE Advanced level kasɛtta gbana.
english: He proceeded to the Adisadel College in Cape Coast, where he obtained both his GCE Ordinary level and GCE Advanced level certificates.

kusaal: O da paam suori kpɛn' University of Ghana, o da naae ani ka di'e Bachelor of Arts in Humanities nɛ Bachelor of Laws kasɛtta gbana.
english: He gained entrance into the University of Ghana, graduating with Honours in Bachelor of Arts in Humanities and Bachelor of Laws.

kusaal: O da lɛn keŋ Ghana School of Law zamis ka yʋ'ʋm paam suori lieb lɔya Gaana kpɛla on da sɔbi ba karim gaad taaba ka di bʋʋt la yɛla.
english: He studied at the Ghana School of Law and qualified as a lawyer in Ghana after passing his bar examination.

kusaal: Acquah-Sampon and Associates, banɛ maan sininami bɛ Accra la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni.
english: Acquah-Sampon and Associates, a firm of solicitors based in Accra in 2004.

kusaal: O da naal First Atlantic Bank n bɛ Ankara la yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2007) tʋmi assistant manager tʋʋma ka tɔlis tuoni yʋ'ʋn lieb kpɛɛm tis banɛ gɔsid wada yɛla la (head of the legal department).
english: He joined First Atlantic Bank in Accra in 2007 as an assistant manager and advanced to become the head of the legal department.

kusaal: Mercer and Company, banɛ tʋm lɔyanam tʋʋma, Ankara.
english: Mercer and Company, a corporate and investment law firm based in Accra.

kusaal: Egyapa Mercer da zuŋi o pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛbnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa anii la ni dabpiinɛ anaasi daar (14 August 2016) Sekondi pʋʋgʋn.
english: Egyapa Mercer launched his campaign on 14 August 2016 in Sekondi.

kusaal: O zuŋir la nii, nidib bɛdigʋ da nwɛnɛ Alan John Kyerematen, da pian' ya ka sa'al nidib la ye ba vɔɔtim tisi Egyapa Mercer nɛ Nana Akuffo-Addo ka ba liebi ba Wadmaanib nɛ ba pirɛsidɛn.
english: During the launch, various speakers, including Alan John Kyerematen, advised the constituents to vote for Egyapa Mercer and Nana Akuffo-Addo as their parliamentarian and president respectively.

kusaal: Egyapa Mercer da nyaŋi Emmanuel Assifuah onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid la, Daniel Essuman onɛ an Progressive People's Party nid la, nɛ Peter Arthur onɛ bɛ Convention People's Party la.
english: Egyapa Mercer won the parliamentary election by defeating Emmanuel Assifuah of the National Democratic Congress, Daniel Essuman of the Progressive People's Party, and Peter Arthur of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Egyapa Mercer da paam vɔɔtnam tusa piinɛ ayuobʋ, kɔbisnii nɛ pistan nɛ awai (16,839) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ awai du'al pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (59.47%) yi vɔɔtnam la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Egyapa Mercer polled 16,839 votes, representing 59.47% of the total valid votes.

kusaal: Tʋʋmbanɛ ka o daa tʋm la sieba anɛ o da tis kɔmputanam anu (five desktop computers) nɛ d la'ad ka di sam na an nwɛnɛ Dolar tusa anaasi (US$4,000) Sekondi gbana buorig (Library).
english: Some of his engagements included the donation of five desktop computers and accessories costing US$4,000 to the Sekondi Library.

kusaal: O da lɛn sʋŋi yɔ Gaana siidi tusa anu GH₵5,000 sam kanɛ ka Sekondi Eleven Wise, a Division 1 league club bɛ o sʋ'ʋlim la da mɔr bɛ Ghana Football Association; ka banɛ bɔɔd bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib la yɔ sam kanɛ kpɛlim la, Gaana siidi tusir yinne nɛ kɔbis tan GH₵1,300.
english: He also helped repay the debt owed the Ghana Football Association by Sekondi Eleven Wise, a Division 1 league club based in the constituency, with a contribution of GH₵5,000; other supporters paid the remaining GH₵1,300 toward officiating fees.

kusaal: Onɛ an Wadmaani tis Secondi sʋ'ʋlim n bɛ Westhern Region, Gaana la.
english: He is the immediate past Member of Parliament for the Sekondi Constituency in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di'e Na'am la yinɛ Papa Owusu-Ankomah, onɛ da an Wadmaan yʋma pisi la nu'ugin.
english: He succeeded Papa Owusu-Ankomah, who had been MP for 20 years.

kusaal: O saam da anɛ James Mercer, onɛ an Gaana lɔya nɛ Gbammi'id la.
english: Andrew Kofi Egyapa Mercer was born in Sekondi in the Western Region of Ghana to James Mercer, a Ghanaian lawyer and diplomat.

kusaal: Egyapa Mercer da pin'ili o tʋʋma nɛ nwɛnɛ sakur bilnɛ Messrs.
english: Egyapa Mercer commenced his working life as a pupil with Messrs.

kusaal: On da bɛ First Atlantic, o da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ynne (2011) la ni nɛ Na'adɔɔg nidib ka Papa Owusu-Ankomah di ka bas o.
english: Whilst at First Atlantic, he contested and lost the 2011 Parliamentary primaries of the New Patriotic Party in Sekondi to the incumbent Papa Owusu-Ankomah.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, December 2016 vɔɔt la da nan bɔɔd paar la Na'anya'adib la da tʋm tʋʋma bɛdigʋ pa'al nidib la ye ba vɔɔtim tisi ba.
english: Prior to the December 2016 elections, several activities were organized to showcase the various candidates to the constituents.

kusaal: Yinne, Na'anya'adib la da nwa'as taaba Sekondi Methodist Park la ni.
english: One of these was the constituency debate for the various candidates of the political parties at the Sekondi Methodist Park.

kusaal: Nɛ' da anɛ ye di sʋŋ pa'alʋg nɛ zamisʋg o sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: This was to improve teaching and learning in the constituency.

kusaal: Andy Kwame Appiah-Kubi (7 sigir nwadig 1957) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi nɛ anii la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni ka zi'e tis Asante-Akim North Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region ka zi'e wabʋg na'adɔɔg nɔba zug.
english: Andy Kwame Appiah-Kubi (7 July 1957) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament and 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Asante-Akim North Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Andy mɔr BA (Hons), MBA nɛ LLB University of Ghana, bɛ Legon.
english: Appiah-Kubi holds BA (Hons), MBA and LLB from the University of Ghana, Legon.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai la ni (1989), Andy da anɛ chief executive officer tis Ideal Veterinary Supply ti paae yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi la ni (1994).
english: In 1989, Appiah-Kubi was the chief executive officer for Ideal Veterinary Supply until 1994.

kusaal: O da tiaki lieb country Director tis AFEX International group tʋʋma la ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ yinne (2001) ka o da lɛn bas ka tiaki an Deputy Executive Secretary tis Free Zones Board, o da tʋmnɛ ala ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: He assumed a new position as the country Director for AFEX International group until 2001 when he left to assume a new role as the Deputy Executive Secretary for the Free Zones Board, a position he held till 2009.

kusaal: O da tiak tʋʋma ya'asi an Chief Executive Office tis Appiah-Kubi and Associates.
english: He assumes a new role as the Chief Executive Office of Appiah-Kubi and Associates.

kusaal: Andy da nya' wabʋg na'adɔɔg wadmaanib kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) ka di zi'eni tis Asante-Akim North Constituency wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Appiah-Kubi stood on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party and won the 2016 Parliamentary Election to represent the people of Asante-Akim North Constituency in the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Pirɛsidɛn, Nana Addo Dankwah Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an Deputy Minister tis Railways Development .
english: He was then appointed as the Deputy Minister for Railways Development by the President, Nana Addo Dankwah Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt tis o yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋgin la ya'as paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Ghana Fourth Republic la ni.
english: He was re-elected in the 2020 general election to represent his constituents in the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anu nɛ awai (25,009) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' du'al piswai nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (63.91%) ka NDC nid Alhaji Adams Sulley Yussif paam vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ anaasi nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ atan' (14,123) ka li an pistan' nɛ ayuobʋ du'al yinne kɔbʋga pʋʋgin (36.1%).
english: He polled 25,009 representing 63.91% of the valid vote cast whiles the NDC parliamentary candidate Alhaji Adams Sulley Yussif had 14,123 votes representing 36.1% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Andy paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Holding Offices of Profit Committee ka lɛn paas Foreign Affairs Committee.
english: Appiah-Kubi is a member of the Members Holding Offices of Profit Committee and also a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr kasɛtta gbaʋŋ tita'ar bɛ wada tʋʋma n yit Ghana wada sakur ni.
english: He holds a professional certificate in Law from the Ghana school of Law.

kusaal: Angela Oforiwa Alorwu-Tay anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la, zi'eni tisi Afadjato South n bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Angela Oforiwa Alorwu-Tay is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Afadjato South Constituency in the Volta Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (Ghana).

kusaal: O mɔr (Hons) BA yi University of Ghana ni, diploma yi West Africa Computer Science Institute ka mɔr GCE O'level yii Nkonya Secondary School.
english: She has a (Hons) BA from University of Ghana, a diploma from West Africa Computer Science Institute and has a GCE O'level from Nkonya Secondary School.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛm mɔr MA degree in Democracy, Governance, Law & Development dinɛ ka o paam yi University of Cape Coast.
english: She also has an MA degree in Democracy, Governance, Law & Development from the University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015) ni, o da nya' nɛ o ma'asim tiig (NDC) nidib sieba ka o di ka basi ba ka zi'en o na'adɔɔg nɔba zugʋ nya' Afadjato South Constituency n bɛ Volta Region la kʋk la ka paam vɔɔtnam tusa anu, kɔbiga nɛ pistan nɛ anii (5,138) gaad Mr Reuben Kornu onɛ da paam vɔɔtnam tusir yine, kɔbisnaasi nɛ piinɛ awai (1,419), Miss Kafui Takyi da paam vɔɔt tusir yinne kɔbistan nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (1,366), Mr Eben Kay Hodo mɛ da paam kɔbisnii nɛ pisi (820), Mr Victus Agbesi mɛ da paam vɔɔt kɔbis nu nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (577) ka Miss Susie Adoboe mɛ da paam vɔɔt kɔbisnu nɛ pisnu nɛ awai (559).
english: In 2015, she contested and won the NDC parliamentary seat for the Afadjato South Constituency in the Volta Region and polled 5,138 votes to beat Mr Reuben Kornu with 1,419 votes, Miss Kafui Takyi −1,366 votes, Mr Eben Kay Hodo – 820 votes, Mr Victus Agbesi with 577 votes and Miss Susie Adoboe with 559 votes.

kusaal: O da anɛ gbaʋŋ sɔbidi tis Unique Insurance CO.
english: She served as a secretary Unique Insurance CO.

kusaal: O da lɛn an Manager Tahnaf Service yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012).
english: She also served as a Manager at Tahnaf Service between 2004 and 2012.

kusaal: O anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la nid (Ghana ).
english: She has a (Hons) BA from University of Ghana, a diploma from West Africa Computer Science Institute and has a GCE O'level from Nkonya Secondary School.

kusaal: O da paas pu'aba anu banɛ ka ba da vɔɔti tisi ba yi pu'aba awai banɛ da nya'a Volta Region la pʋʋgin.
english: She was one of the five women elected out of nine that contested during the 2016 general elections in the Volta Region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2003).
english: between the period of 1999 to 2003.

kusaal: Anlo bɛnɛ Keta district dinɛ bɛ Volta Region, Ghana teŋgbauŋun.
english: Anlo is located in the Keta district of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: District la bɛnɛ Keta sʋ'ʋlim linɛ bɛ Volta Region Ghana teŋgbauŋun.
english: The seat is located within the Keta District of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Anthony Akoto Osei anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an banker, ba da du'a o nɛ nwadis anaasi la ni dabisim piinɛ anii yʋʋma 1953 ti paae nwadis atan' la ni dabisim piisi yʋʋma 2023 la ni.
english: Anthony Akoto Osei (18 April 1953 – 20 March 2023) was a Ghanaian banker and politician.

kusaal: John Agyekum Kufuor Gɔmina diib win la ka Osei da an minista kanɛ gɔsid ligidi Ghana teŋ nɔbigir yɛla la ka da lɛn an minista kanɛ gɔsid ligidi nam yɛla.
english: Osei was in the cabinet of President John Agyekum Kufuor first as Minister of State for Finance and Economic Planning and then Acting Minister of Finance.

kusaal: Ba du'a Osei nɛ bɛ Kumasi, tempʋʋg tita'ar linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm, nwadis anaasi la ni dabisim piina anii yʋʋma 1953.O da keŋi o secondary sakuri bɛ Achimota nɛ Opoku Ware Senior High Sakurin la.
english: He had his secondary level education at Achimota School and Opoku Ware Senior High School.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o tɔlis Oberlin College n bɛ Ohio ani ka o paam o digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an economics la.
english: He continued at Oberlin College in Ohio where he obtained a Bachelor's degree in economics.

kusaal: Ka lɛn tɔlisi maali o mastɛs digirii linɛ an applied economics la yi American University linɛ bɛ USA la.
english: He earned a Master of Arts degree in applied economics from the American University in the USA.

kusaal: Ka lin nya'aŋ ka o lɛn tɔlis Howard University ni yʋʋma 1987 la ni n maal PhD zamisʋg linɛ an economics la.
english: He also graduated from Howard University in 1987 with a PhD in economics.

kusaal: Osei da anɛ onɛ an da an Profɛsa n bɛ economics zamisʋg ni.Nwadis atan' la dabisim piisi nɛ ayɔpɔi la yʋʋma 2002, ka Osei da paas kpɛɛm banɛ tʋm n bɛ Merchant Bank (Ghana) Ltd la ni.
english: On 27 March 2002, Osei became a member of the management board of Merchant Bank (Ghana) Ltd. Previously, he worked as associate professor at Dillard University (USA) and before that as a research assistant at the Centre for Policy Analysis (Ghana).

kusaal: Nwadis ayi la ni yʋʋma 2017 la ni, ka da zʋŋ Osei ye o an minista kanɛ an Monitoring and Evaluation Nana Akufo-Addo n da vɛɛnsi gɔsi o yɛla naae la, vɛɛnsʋg la da maali bɛ Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni.Monitoring nɛ Evaluation minista tʋʋma la ba da nan yɔ'ɔgi li nɛ paalim ye li sʋŋ ka ba gɔsid Ghana tʋʋma nɛ ken si'em nɛ gban'asʋma yɛla lin nan si'em ka gɔmina la nɔzi'ela la nyaŋi tʋm sʋŋa nɛ li tuon ken.
english: In February 2017, Osei was sworn in as Minister of Monitoring and Evaluation after being nominated by President Nana Akufo-Addo and going through the vetting process in the parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Nwadis anu la yʋʋma 2017, ka gɔmina Nana Akufo-Addo da put Anthony Akoto Osei ye o paas ministanam bam piina awai (19) la ni.
english: In May 2017, President Nana Akufo-Addo named Anthony Akoto Osei as one of 19 ministers who would form his cabinet.

kusaal: Ba da zaŋ Ministanam piina awai 19 nwa yʋda tis Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni ka Profɛsa Aaron Mike Oquaye onɛ an wadmaanib yir kpɛɛm onɛ gɔsid wadmaanib pian'ad la mɔɔli tis yir la.
english: The names of the 19 ministers were submitted to the Parliament of Ghana and announced by the Speaker of the House, Right Honourable Professor Aaron Mike Oquaye.

kusaal: O da anɛ Centre for Policy Analysis (CEPA) kpɛɛm, Accra; o da anɛ World Bank (Korean Division) kpɛɛm, yʋʋma 1987 la ni.
english: Centre for Policy Analysis (CEPA), Accra; consultant to the World Bank (Korean Division), 1987; associate professor in economics at Howard University from 1984 to 1995; Special Advisor, Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning, 2001–2003; Deputy Minister of Finance, 2003–2007; Minister of State, 2007–2008; Acting Minister of Finance, September 2008 - 6 January 2009; MP for Old Tafo-Pankrono and MP for Old Tafo (January 2005 to January 2017).

kusaal: Ba da vɔti gaŋ Osei o ye o an wadmaan n tis Old Tafo sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ Ashanti Region Ghana la, o yiiga ken da anɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni ka o da kpɛn' wadmaanib yir la.
english: Osei was elected as the member of parliament for the Old Tafo constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana for the first time in the 2004 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kanna Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg wadmaanib la da zu'oe gat, ba da anɛ 128 n yi wadmaanib la kanl wʋsa linɛ da an 230 la ni.Yʋʋma 2004 la ni la O da paamnɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ anaasi, kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (34,957) yi vɔɔt la kanl wʋsa linɛ da an Tusa pisnaasi nɛ anaasi (44,000) la ni.
english: He was elected in 2004 with 34,957 votes out of 44,000 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Onɛ Salu Ibrahim Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid, Andrews K Asamoah-Akoto onɛ da an CPP nid la nɛ Amediku Dominic D Quarshie onɛ da zi'e o nyari la ka o di ka basi ba.Wadmaanib bama tan' nwa da paamnɛ vɔt bam 7,116 (16.2%), 426 (1%) nɛ 1,501 (3.4%), wʋʋ ba yʋda la tʋʋnl dɔl taab si'em la, n yi vɔt la kanl ni.
english: He was elected over Salu Ibrahim of the National Democratic Congress, Andrews K Asamoah-Akoto of the Convention People's Party and Amediku Dominic D Quarshie an independent candidate.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2012 vɔɔt la ni la ka ba vɔt ka Osei lɛn di n bɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm ni ya'as.
english: In 2012, Osei won the general election once again for the same constituency.

kusaal: On nɛ Memuna Kabore Abu-Bakr Ma'asim Tiig nid, Faruk Muhammed Tankoh PNC nid nɛ Issah Abdul Salam onɛ da an CPP nid la da zi'en ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over Memuna Kabore Abu-Bakr Siddique of the National Democratic Congress, Faruk Muhammed Tankoh of People's National Convention and Issah Abdul Salam of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Ba wʋsa da paamnɛ vɔt bam 13,454, 149 nɛ 314 votes, wʋʋ ba yʋda la tʋʋnl taaba si'em la, n yi vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ ba da mɔri 23.41%, 0.26% and 0.55%, wʋʋ ba yʋda tʋʋnl taaba si'em la, vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: These obtained 13,454, 149 and 314 votes, respectively, of the total valid votes cast: equivalent to 23.41%, 0.26% and 0.55%, respectively, of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Osei da anɛ Kristo biig onɛ an Catholic nid.O da di pu'a mɔr biis atan'.
english: Osei was a Catholic.

kusaal: O da kpinɛ nwadis atan' la dabisim piisi la yʋʋma 2023 la ni, o nyɛ yʋʋma piisyuobʋ nɛ awai (69).
english: He died on 20 March 2023 at the age of 69.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaan n tis Old Tafo linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Osei was elected as the member of parliament for the Old Tafo constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana for the first time in the 2004 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Pɔi ka o naan tʋm ani la o da dɛŋim tʋmnɛ n bɛ Dillard University (USA) n an profɛsa, hali o da dɛŋim anɛ onɛ maan vɛɛnsʋg n bɛ Centre for Policy Analysis (Ghana) la ni.
english: On 27 March 2002, Osei became a member of the management board of Merchant Bank (Ghana) Ltd. Previously, he worked as associate professor at Dillard University (USA) and before that as a research assistant at the Centre for Policy Analysis (Ghana).

kusaal: Osei da tʋmnɛ an Minista kanɛ gɔsid ligidi nam nɛ ti Ghana bɛllim nɔbigir yɛla la nya'andɔl nwadis anu la ni yʋʋma 2003 la ni ka da lɛn an tʋm n an onɛ san'an gɔmina kati ti teŋ la bɛllim sʋŋ yɛla.
english: Osei worked as the deputy minister of Finance and Economic Planning in May 2003 and was an economic advisor to the government.

kusaal: Minista kanɛ da gɔsid ligidi nam Ghana bɛllim nɔbigir yɛla Kwadwo Baah Wiredu da kpila la nya'aŋ ka ba gaŋ Osei ye o an minista kanɛ na gɔsid ligidi nam Ghana bɛllim nɔbigir yɛla.
english: He was elevated to substantive acting Minister for Finance and Economic Planning after the death of the then Minister of Finance, Kwadwo Baah Wiredu.

kusaal: Osei an minista kpɛɛm la zug da bɛ gɔmina la tuon saŋa wʋsa sʋŋid nɛ gban'asa banɛ da ken wʋsa kati wa'ae Ghana nɔbigir yɛla.
english: As a cabinet minister, Osei was part of the president's inner circle and assisted in key decision-making in Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ profɛsa linɛ economics la nya'andɔl n bɛ Howard Nyunivɛsiti la lin da yi yʋʋma 1984 ti paae 1995 la ni.O da lɛn tʋm an onɛ san'an, ka an Minista onɛ gɔsid ligidi nɛ teŋ la nɔbigir yɛla yʋʋma 2001 ti paae 2003 la ni ka lɛn Minista onɛ gɔsid ligidi nɛ teŋ la nɔbigir yɛla nya'andɔl yʋʋma 2003 la ni ti paae yʋʋma 2007 la ni ka da lɛn kena an Minister of State, lin da yi yʋʋm 2007 ti paae yʋʋma 2008 la ni.
english: Centre for Policy Analysis (CEPA), Accra; consultant to the World Bank (Korean Division), 1987; associate professor in economics at Howard University from 1984 to 1995; Special Advisor, Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning, 2001–2003; Deputy Minister of Finance, 2003–2007; Minister of State, 2007–2008; Acting Minister of Finance, September 2008 - 6 January 2009; MP for Old Tafo-Pankrono and MP for Old Tafo (January 2005 to January 2017).

kusaal: Onɛ da an minista onɛ gɔsid ligidi nam yɛla la lin da yi nwadis awai la ni yʋʋma 2008 ti paae nwadig yinne la li daba yuobʋ yʋʋma 2009; onɛ da lɛn an wadmaan n tis Old Tafo-Pankrono sʋ'ʋlʋm la lin da yi nwadig yinne la ni yʋʋma 2005 ti nwadig yinne la ni yʋʋma 2017 la ni.
english: Centre for Policy Analysis (CEPA), Accra; consultant to the World Bank (Korean Division), 1987; associate professor in economics at Howard University from 1984 to 1995; Special Advisor, Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning, 2001–2003; Deputy Minister of Finance, 2003–2007; Minister of State, 2007–2008; Acting Minister of Finance, September 2008 - 6 January 2009; MP for Old Tafo-Pankrono and MP for Old Tafo (January 2005 to January 2017).

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai du'al anaasi (79.4%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: This was equivalent to 79.4% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2008 la ni, ka ba da lɛn vɔt ka Osei di Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug n bɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm kan noo ni.O sʋ'ʋlʋm la da paas kʋkʋs bam piistan' nɛ anaasi banɛ ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg dim da paam n bɛ la ni Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Osei was elected as the member of parliament for the Old Tafo constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana for the first time in the 2004 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Osei da paamnɛ vɔt bam 36,171 n yi vɔt la kanl wʋsa linɛ da an 47,478 la ni.
english: Osei was elected with 36,171 votes out of 47,478 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 76.18% vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 76.18% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Onɛ Swallah Ali PNC nid, Dominic Kwabena Anomah Ma'asim Tiig nid, Issah Abdul Salam CPP nid, nɛ Mohammed Rabui Umar RPD da zi'en ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over Swallah Ali of the People's National Convention, Dominic Kwabena Anomah of the National Democratic Congress, Issah Abdul Salam of the Convention People's Party and Mohammed Rabui Umar of the Reformed Patriotic Democrats.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ ba da paamnɛ 37.59%, 5.43% nɛ 1.28%, wʋʋ ba yʋda tʋʋnl dɔl si'em la, , n yi vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: These candidates obtained 427, 10,386, 375 and 119 votes, respectively, out of the total valid votes cast: equivalent to 37.59%, 5.43% and 1.28%, respectively, of the total vote.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔr 75.79% vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 75.79% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kanna Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg wadmaanib la da zu'oe gat, ba da anɛ 109 n yi wadmaanib la kanl wʋsa linɛ da an 230 la ni.
english: The New Patriotic Party won a minority total of 109 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: O da paamnɛ vɔt bam 43,561 yi vɔt la wʋsa linɛ da an 57,478 la ni.
english: He was elected with 43,561 votes out of 57,478 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Anthony Gildas Kofi Annan (du'am yʋʋm- 21 July 1986) anɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd onɛ nwɛ'ɛdi midfilda.
english: Anthony Gildas Kofi Annan (born 21 July 1986) is a Ghanaian professional footballer who plays as a midfielder for DJK Arminia Lirich.

kusaal: Bani da du'a o Accra laa, Anthony Annan pin'ili nwɛ'ɛd bɔɔl nɛ Super Rainbow Stars dinɛ bɛ Cape Coast, Ghana.
english: Born in Accra, Anthony Annan began playing football with a local Colts Super Rainbow Stars in Cape Coast, Ghana.

kusaal: O lɛm nwɛ' tis Cape Coast Venomous Vipers dinɛ bɛ Ghana Division one league ka naam pɛ'ɛs Sekondi Hasaacas yʋʋm 2003 ka nya'aŋ ka o kɛŋ Accra Hearts of Oak yʋʋm 2005 la ni.
english: He also played for Cape Coast Venomous Vipers in the Ghanaian Division one league before joined Sekondi Hasaacas in 2003 and later moving to Accra Hearts of Oak in 2005.

kusaal: O mɔri midfilda baŋir nɛ gɔɔl diib baŋir wʋsa, ka maali o mɛŋ ka nidib nɔŋ o bɛdigʋ Ghana ni.Annan pɛ'ɛs Accra Hearts of Oak dinɛ yi Sekondi Hasaacas FC bɛ 2005–06 league yʋʋm la ni.
english: Annan joined Accra Hearts of Oak from Sekondi Hasaacas FC in the 2005–06 league season.

kusaal: Onɛ bɛ Accra Hearts of Oak la nii, Annan da anɛ dasan kani an midfilda tita'ar Ghana wʋsa ni.
english: Annan signed for the Norwegian club Start on 26 January 2007, after a promising career in Ghana with his local club Accra Hearts of Oak.

kusaal: Anthony Effah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa Constituency linɛ bɛ Central Region la Wabg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Anthony Effah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Asikuma-Odoben-Brakwa Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Effah nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ yʋʋmpaal nwadig dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 January 1960) ka o yi Breman-Brakwa bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Effah was born on 24 January 1960 and hails from Breman-Brakwa in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o Bachelors' degree in Economics yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu la ni (1985) ka lɛm maali o Executive Masters' in Business Administration (Finance) University of Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan' (2003) la ni.
english: He had his bachelor's degree in economics in 1985 and also his Executive Masters' in Business Administration (Finance) from the University of Ghana in 2003.

kusaal: Effah da anɛ Director of Risk Management and Compliance tis Fidelity Bank dinɛ bɛ Accra.
english: Effah was the Director of Risk Management and Compliance at Fidelity Bank in Accra.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Board of Governors kʋkdaani tis Brakwa-Breman Rural Bank.
english: He was also the chairman of the Board of Governors of the Brakwa-Breman Rural Bank.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaani tis Asikuma Odoben Brakwa Constituency dinɛ bɛ Central Region la din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la (2017) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021).
english: He was the member of Parliament for Asikuma Odoben Brakwa Constituency in the Central Region from 2017 to 2021.

kusaal: O da di wadmaan kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ atan, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobʋ (23,760) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisnu du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.1%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, NDC wadmaan na'anya'ad la, Alhassan Kobina Ghansah da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ atan' kɔbistan' nɛ pistan (23,330) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin dinɛ an vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ awai du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (49.2%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin, PPP wadmaan na'anya'ad la, Richard Ato Quinoo da paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan nɛ ayɔpɔi (237) dinɛ an vɔɔt nɛɛm du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.5%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka CPP wadmaan na'anya'ad la, Hayford Amoakoh da paam vɔɔt piswai (90) dinɛ zɛm nɛ nɛɛm du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.2%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He won the parliamentary seat in the 2016 Ghanaian general elections with 23,760 votes making 50.1% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Alhassan Kobina Ghansah had 23,330 votes making 49.2% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Richard Ato Quinoo had 237 votes making 0.5% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Hayford Amoakoh had 90 votes making 0.2% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019) la ni, O da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid ligid-diisim yɛla (Finance Committee).
english: In 2019, he was a member of the Finance Committee.

kusaal: Effah anɛ Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid.
english: Effah is a member of New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Effah anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Effah is a Christian.

kusaal: Anthony Abayifaa Karbo anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan tis Lawra linɛ bɛ Ghana upper west region la, ba da du'a o nɛ nwadis anii la dabisim piina ayi yʋʋma 1979.
english: Anthony Abayifaa Karbo (born 12 August 1979) is a Ghanaian politician and member of Parliament of the Lawra constituency in the upper west region of Ghana.

kusaal: Karbo buudi anɛ Dagaadnam buudi, o yinɛ Lawra linɛ bɛ Ghana Upper West Region la.
english: Karbo is a member of the Dagaaba ethnic group and hails from Lawra in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba du'a o nɛ n bɛ Jekarayili tempubil linɛ bɛ Tamale, Ghana Northern regional capital sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: He was born in Jekarayili a small town located in Tamale, Ghana's Northern regional capital.

kusaal: Li anɛ o saam Abeifaa Karbo n da yɔ'ɔg pɔlitis na'adɔɔg linɛ da buon ye Northern People's Party la, onɛ da an yiiga wadmaan n tis Lawra- Nandom sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: His father, Abeifaa Karbo was a founding member of the Northern People's Party, eventually becoming the first Member of Parliament for the Lawra- Nandom constituency.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da an gɔmina la.
english: He was a leading voice during the oppressive reign of Ghana 's first President Dr. Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Karbo da keŋi o sakuri bɛ University for Development Studies, di'e o digirii zamisʋg linɛ an Integrated Development Studies yʋʋma 2005 la ni.
english: Karbo studied at the University for Development Studies, receiving a bachelor's degree in Integrated Development Studies in 2005.

kusaal: O da an sakur bil, Karbo bɛllim da bɛɛ o kɔn' hali nɛ o taaba la onɛ da an Central Student Representative Council la zugdaan n bɛ University for Development Studies la yʋʋma 2004 la ni.
english: As a student, Karbo distinguished himself as a student leader and rose through the ranks to become the Central Student Representative Council President of the University for Development Studies in 2004.

kusaal: Pɔi ka o naan di'e zi'esim kan la ka o pun anɛ zugdaan n tis TESCON linɛ anɛ Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la'asʋg linɛ bɛ Nyunivɛsiti nam ni la n bɛ Navrongo sakurin.
english: Before then, he was President of TESCON, Navrongo Campus.

kusaal: Karbo da lɛn paasi kpɛɛm banɛ da tʋm National Union of Ghana Students la ni bɛ University Students Association of Ghana.
english: Karbo also served on the Central Committees of both the National Union of Ghana Students and the University Students Association of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2006 la ni, ka o naae o Mastɛs zamisʋg ka di'e kasɛta linɛ an Economic Policy nɛ International Business n yi University of Birmingham.
english: In 2006, he graduated with a Masters in Economic Policy and International Business from University of Birmingham.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2007 la ni, ka o da zi'e wabʋg nɔba zug ye o nya'a Ghana na'am, Nana Akufo-Addo nɛ Karbo da lɛb Ghana na ye ba tʋm pɔlitis tʋʋma la.
english: In 2007, at the behest of then flag bearer of the New Patriotic Party, Nana Akufo-Addo Karbo returned to Ghana to pursue active politics.

kusaal: Karbo da bɛ kpiʋŋ nwa pʋʋgin ti paae yʋʋma 2012 ka lɛn nya'aŋ ka o sig ye o bɔɔdi zi'en wadmaan Lawra sʋ'ʋlʋm n dɔl nɛ ba na'adɔɔg la wada la.Amaa ka o da zi'en ka pʋ dii, Karbo da lɛn lɛbi tʋm n an ba na'adɔɔg la onɛ gɔsid ba pian'ad yɛla Darɛta nya'andɔl n tis Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ka an onɛ pian'adi tisid onɛ da zi'en gɔmina nya'andɔl.
english: Karbo held this role until 2012 when he resigned to pursue his bid of becoming the Party's Parliamentary candidate for the newly created Lawra Constituency in keeping with the Party's policy.

kusaal: Abayifaa Karbo da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la zugu nya'a di o yiiga saŋa nwadis piina ayi yʋʋma 2016 Vɔt la ni onɛ Sampson Abu nɛ Upper West Regional Minista la Bede Ziedeng.
english: Abayifaa Karbo was first elected to the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the NPP in December 2016 after defeating the incumbent Sampson Abu and Upper West Regional Minister Bede Ziedeng.

kusaal: Nwadis anaasi la yʋʋma 2017 la ni, ka ba Karbo ye o an Minista kanɛ gɔsidi ti Ghana suoya la nya'andɔl.
english: In April 2017, Karbo was appointed as Deputy Minister for Roads and Highways.

kusaal: On da an Minista nya'andɔl la, Karbo da an onɛ an tuongat n gɔsid kpɛɛm banɛ da tʋm Sinohydro kati wa'ae suoya yɛla la n bɛ Minista banɛ gɔsid suoya yɛla la ni, o tʋʋma an linɛ an zanbin hali dig Ghana kpɛla ka pʋ kpiinda.
english: As Deputy Minister, Karbo chaired the working committee on the Sinohydro deal at the Ministry for Road and Highways, the biggest infrastructure barter in the history of Ghana.

kusaal: Karbo mɔr pu'a ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Awenlue Kante-Karbo (née Kante) ka ba mɔr biis atan'.
english: Karbo is married to Awenlue Kante-Karbo (née Kante) and has three children.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig, ba da du'a o nɛ Catholic karimdɔɔgin ka o nɔbig ani ka an onɛ pʋ di'emid pʋ'ʋsim yɛla baa bi'ela n bɛ Lawra Parish Catholic pʋ'ʋsʋm la nii.
english: He is a Christian, born and raised a Catholic and is a devout member of the Lawra Parish of the Catholic Church.

kusaal: O anɛ Abayifaa na'adɔɔg nid, Karbo si'iŋ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb ka li yʋʋg hali.
english: A member of the Abayifaa royal family, Karbo was introduced at an early age to political activism.

kusaal: O da mɔr kpiʋŋ nɛ pian'ad pʋʋgin hali saŋkanɛ ka Ghana gɔmina Dr.
english: He was a leading voice during the oppressive reign of Ghana 's first President Dr. Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Nwadis atan' la yʋʋma 2008 la ni, ka ba da gaŋ Karbo ye o an wabʋg nidib banɛ vɛɛnsidi gɔsidi ba yɛla la.
english: In March 2008, Karbo was appointed a member of the national research team of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'os o hali nwadis piina yi yʋʋma 2008 la ni ye o an onɛ kaadi gɔsidi ba pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛdib banɛ dɔl Gɔmina nya'andɔl Dr.
english: He was promoted in December 2008 to be the Campaign Coordinator for the vice presidential candidate of the New Patriotic Party Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia.

kusaal: Ba na'adɔɔg la da lu yʋʋma 2008 vɔt la ni la, ka Karbo lɛb ba na'adɔɔg la tʋʋma dɔɔgin an kpɛɛm tirig hali n tʋmɛ tisi o na'adɔɔg la.
english: After the defeat of the Party in the 2008 elections, Karbo returned to the Party 's office and served as a key member of the Party's communication unit.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2010 la ni, Karbo da anɛ ba na'adɔɔg la Ghana kpɛla bipula kpɛɛm.
english: In 2010, Karbo was elected National Youth Organizer of the Party.

kusaal: Ban da zuŋ o naae ye o anɛ wadmaan la li pʋ yʋʋgɛ ka labaar yarig Ghana wʋsa ye ba gaŋ o ye o an minista nya'andɔl.
english: Abayifaa Karbo was first elected to the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the NPP in December 2016 after defeating the incumbent Sampson Abu and Upper West Regional Minister Bede Ziedeng.

kusaal: Pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb ya'a yi, Karbo anɛ onɛ an kpaad amɛŋa hali ka la'am bɔɔd ye onɛ o sʋ'ʋlʋm la nidib la'asi kua la'amnɛ on an pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd la.
english: Besides politics, Karbo actively pursues farming and likes to take advantage of opportunities to engage in communal farming activities with his constituents and thus further consolidating his persona as a grassroots politician.

kusaal: Nidib nyɛ Anthony Karbo nɛ ka o an ninkanɛ bɛ tis Africa dim nɛ nɔŋ dim.
english: Anthony Karbo is generally viewed as pro-African and pro-poor in his beliefs.

kusaal: , Karbo ɛɛnti pian'ad ye bɔɔ maal ka ti zan'as ka zɔti dɔl na'asaa nam la'ad ka basi ti mɛŋ la'adɛ o ɛɛnti pian'a nɛ' tis ninsabilis Africa dim wʋsa.
english: Anthony Karbo is generally viewed as pro-African and pro-poor in his beliefs.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid ka an Minista kanɛ gɔsid suoya yɛla la nya'andɔl n bɛ Ghanan.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the deputy minister for Roads and Highways in Ghana.

kusaal: Anthony Mwinkaara Sumah (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi, Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig dabpiinɛ ayɔpɔi daar, 17 January 1982) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: Anthony Mwinkaara Sumah (born 17 January 1982) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Mwinkaara yinɛ Charikpong bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Mwinkaara hails from Charikpong in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Anthony's primary school ka tɔlis keŋ Tuolu Senior High School.
english: He attended St. Anthony's primary school and proceeded to Tuolu Senior High School.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da keŋ University of Ghana bɛ Legon la maal Bachelor of Science Degree in Health service administration.
english: He later gained admission to the University of Ghana, Legon, where he graduated with Bachelor of Science Degree in Health service administration.

kusaal: Anthony osei Boakye (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai, sawa'ar nwadig dabpiinɛ anu daar ka an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Ghana republic kanɛ aan anaasi la wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas ayuobʋ la nid, ka zi'e tis Atwi Nwabiagya south teŋ kanɛ bɛ Ahanti region Ghana nwa ni la.
english: Anthony Osei Boakye (born 15 October 1949) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the Sixth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing Atwima Nwabiagya South in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O keŋɛ university of cape coast naae nɛ o Bachelor of science digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1977) la ni.
english: He earned his Bachelor of Science degree in education from the University of Cape Coast in 1977.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt gaŋ Boakye ka o an wadmaan bɛ Ghana republic kanɛ aan anaasi wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas ayuobʋ la ni, 7 yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2013 la ni, Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2012 la nya'aŋ la ka o da mɔr 74.29% yit vɔɔtnam la wʋsa kallin.
english: Boakye was elected into the sixth parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana on 7 January 2013 after the completion of the 2012 Ghanaian general election, where he obtained 74.29% of the valid votes cast.

kusaal: O an wadmaan tʋm ala hali ti paae 6 yʋʋmpaal nwadig la 2017.
english: He served until 6 January 2017.

kusaal: Onɛ daa an kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid produce buying company limited la.
english: Boakye was the immediate past managing director of Produce Buying Company Limited.

kusaal: Anthony Abayifaa Karbo: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbʋswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai, nwadis anii la dapii nɛ ayi' daar (12 August, 1979) la, anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛn'ɛd.
english: Anthony Abayifaa Karbo (born 12 August 1979) is a Ghanaian politician and member of Parliament of the Lawra constituency in the upper west region of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ deputy minister for Roads and Highways, Ghana.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the deputy minister for Roads and Highways in Ghana.

kusaal: Karbo anɛ Dagaaba buudi la bɛ Lawra, upper west sʋ'ʋlim la nid.
english: Karbo is a member of the Dagaaba ethnic group and hails from Lawra in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O teŋ du'adir anɛ Jekarayili an tempʋbili bɛ Tamale, Ghana Northern region sʋ'ʋlim tempʋtita'ar la ni.
english: He was born in Jekarayili a small town located in Tamale, Ghana's Northern regional capital.

kusaal: O saam, Abeifaa Karbo paas nimbanɛ da pin'il Northern People's Party la, ka yʋ'ʋn da ti naam Lawra-Nandom constituency yiiga wadmaan la.
english: His father, Abeifaa Karbo was a founding member of the Northern People's Party, eventually becoming the first Member of Parliament for the Lawra- Nandom constituency.

kusaal: O da anɛ onɛ ka o kʋkɔr dʋt hali ti yiiga Ghana Zugraan, Dr Kwame Nkrumah saŋa la.
english: He was a leading voice during the oppressive reign of Ghana 's first President Dr. Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Karbo zamis nɛ University for Development Studies, ka yina nɛ bachelar's degree bɛ Integrated Development Studies yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anu (2005) la ni.
english: Karbo studied at the University for Development Studies, receiving a bachelor's degree in Integrated Development Studies in 2005.

kusaal: On da an sakur bil la, karbo da yi paalʋ nii an sakur bibis tuongat, ka da ti dʋʋ ti lieb Central Student Representative Council Zugraan, University for Development Studies, yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni.
english: As a student, Karbo distinguished himself as a student leader and rose through the ranks to become the Central Student Representative Council President of the University for Development Studies in 2004.

kusaal: Karbo da lɛn tʋm nɛ National Union of Ghana Students nɛ University Students Association of Ghana.
english: Karbo also served on the Central Committees of both the National Union of Ghana Students and the University Students Association of Ghana.

kusaal: O tʋʋma la'asʋg bama ni da an sʋm hali kɛ ka ba da gaŋ o paas banɛ da gɔsidd NPP party la Upper West Region nya'ab yɛla, yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi (2004) vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: His performance in these roles earned him an appointment on the Upper West Regional Campaign Team ahead of the NPP 2004 general elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayuobʋ (2006) la nii, o da yi nɛ Masters in Economic Policy and International Business, Uniersity of Birmingham la ni na.
english: In 2006, he graduated with a Masters in Economic Policy and International Business from University of Birmingham.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la nii, New Patrotic Party, Nana Akufo-Addo da an wabʋg party tuongat la, o da tʋm buol Karbo ye o kul Ghana na nwɛn' politiks.
english: In 2007, at the behest of then flag bearer of the New Patriotic Party, Nana Akufo-Addo Karbo returned to Ghana to pursue active politics.

kusaal: O nya'ad nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piisi (2020) Ghanaian General Election la ni, New Patrotic Party la zug.
english: He is contesting in the 2020 Ghanaian general election as the parliamentary candidate for the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa anaasi (April 2017) la ni, ba da gaŋ Karbo niŋ o Deputy Minister for Roads and Highways.
english: In April 2017, Karbo was appointed as Deputy Minister for Roads and Highways.

kusaal: Karbo pu'a anɛ Awenlue Kante-Karbo (Nee-Kante), ba mɔr biis atan'.
english: Karbo is married to Awenlue Kante-Karbo (née Kante) and has three children.

kusaal: O pʋ'ʋsid nɛ Lawra Parish Catholic Church ni.
english: He is a Christian, born and raised a Catholic and is a devout member of the Lawra Parish of the Catholic Church.

kusaal: O anɛ Lawra constituency linɛ bɛ upper west Region, Ghana la wadmaan, ka paas wadmaannib yikanɛ paas ayɔpɔi (7th) la, ka bɛnɛ nɛ New Patrotic Party la.
english: Anthony Abayifaa Karbo (born 12 August 1979) is a Ghanaian politician and member of Parliament of the Lawra constituency in the upper west region of Ghana.

kusaal: Karbo zamis politiks nwɛ'ɛb tʋʋma ka anɛ biig.
english: His father, Abeifaa Karbo was a founding member of the Northern People's Party, eventually becoming the first Member of Parliament for the Lawra- Nandom constituency.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii (2008)) la nii, ba da gaŋ Karbo paas nimbanɛ da vɛɛnsid New Patrotic Party ghana wʋsa yɛla.
english: In March 2008, Karbo was appointed a member of the national research team of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan la nwadis piinɛ ayi' la nii, o da paam kpɛʋŋʋ an New Patrotic Party la na'anya'ad tuongat nya'andɔl, Dr.
english: He was promoted in December 2008 to be the Campaign Coordinator for the vice presidential candidate of the New Patriotic Party Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia.

kusaal: Party la da lʋ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii (2008) vɔɔtʋg la, Karbo da lɛb party la tʋʋma ni aan ba tuongattib yinne onɛ da gɔsid party la labaya lʋgʋr la yɛla.
english: After the defeat of the Party in the 2008 elections, Karbo returned to the Party 's office and served as a key member of the Party's communication unit.

kusaal: Abayifaa Karbo da zi'en wabʋg party NPP la zugʋ di ya'annɛ ken Ghana wadmaannib yin la o yiiga ken la ni nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la ni.
english: Abayifaa Karbo was first elected to the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the NPP in December 2016 after defeating the incumbent Sampson Abu and Upper West Regional Minister Bede Ziedeng.

kusaal: O da lubnɛ Sampson Abu onɛ da an wadmaan saŋkan la nɛ Upper East Regional Minister Bede Ziedeng ka vɔɔtʋg nyaan paae.
english: Abayifaa Karbo was first elected to the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the NPP in December 2016 after defeating the incumbent Sampson Abu and Upper West Regional Minister Bede Ziedeng.

kusaal: Bɛdigʋ da bi'esid o ya'an diib la nɛ, li da anɛ ma'asim tiig (National Democratic Congress) NDC da zin' kʋk kan la zug yʋʋma anii.
english: Prior to the elections, many had doubted his chances of success since the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC) had held the seat for eight years.

kusaal: Anina la, o da anɛ working committee on sinohydro deal kʋkraan.
english: As Deputy Minister, Karbo chaired the working committee on the Sinohydro deal at the Ministry for Road and Highways, the biggest infrastructure barter in the history of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Catholic Christabiig.
english: He is a Christian, born and raised a Catholic and is a devout member of the Lawra Parish of the Catholic Church.

kusaal: Aprapransa, ba da buoni li ye 'akplijii' bԑԑ 'akplidzi') anԑ Ghana dim GaDangme bԑԑ Ga dim buudi diib kanԑ ka ba mͻr abԑ' zԑԑnd nԑ kawԑnna zͻ'ͻm maan.
english: Aprapransa, originally called 'akplijii' (or 'akplidzi') is a Ghanaian GaDangme(or Ga) dish prepared by heat mixing (or blending) roasted corn flour with palm nut soup.

kusaal: Li mԑ anԑ zԑԑnd kanԑ ka GaDangme dim maan saŋa wʋsa dit nԑ kawԑnna zͻ'ͻm diib kanԑ ka ba buon Kpokpoi bԑԑ Kpekpele, sankanԑ ka ba maani ba bunib malʋŋ kanԑ buon Homowo la.
english: It is also an ancient sacred soup of the GaDangme people and is always prepared as a complement to another sacred corn flour meal called Kpokpoi (or Kpekpele) during an Ancient Religious Hebraic Harvest Festival called Homowo.

kusaal: Buudsi'eba banԑ bԑ Nigeria wan wʋʋ Yorubas, Igbos mԑ mͻr abԑ' zԑԑnd kanԑ ka ba dʋgʋd ka buoni li ye Banga Soup.
english: Outside Ghana, other tribes in Nigeria such as the Yorubas, Igbos have a variation of palm nut soup called Banga Soup.

kusaal: Aprapransa ka'a dikanԑ ka fʋ na kpԑlim nyԑԑ li Ghana tԑnpʋʋsin da'a li, ba mԑ pʋ maani li daar wʋsaa.
english: Aprapransa as a complete meal is not a food that is commonly found on the streets of Ghana or is prepared every day in the house.

kusaal: Akan buudi dimi pʋdʋgʋdi li tisid saam malʋŋ si'eba ni wan wʋʋ pʋ'adiir nԑ sidkulug, biig yʋ'ʋr pʋdib, nԑ dʋ'am dabisir malima dabisa.
english: It is usually served by the Akan tribe on special occasions such as marriage ceremonies, naming ceremonies, birthday celebrations, family cookouts, etc. Its name derived from the fact that it is a complete meal with its soup/stew integrated that one only needs to wipe their hand (prapra wo nsa) to eat.

kusaal: Ban mͻr la'ad si'eba maan anԑ kawԑnna zͻ'ͻm (Tom brown) nԑ abԑ' kpaam.
english: The main ingredients are roasted corn flour (Tom brown) and palmnut or palm oil.

kusaal: La'ad banԑ ka ba paasidi maan si'eba anԑ bԑŋa, tomatos, gabʋ, nanzʋ'ʋs, kakaduro bԑԑ garlic.
english: Other ingredients include beans, vegetables such as tomatoes, onion, pepper, ginger, or garlic.

kusaal: Onɛ an Volta Regional minister tis Ghana.
english: He was the Volta Regional minister of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paamnɛ gaŋir yi Zugdaan Nana Addo Danquah Akuffo-Addo bɛ January 2017 ka da paam tuon gaadʋg yit bani bɛ palimet la ni bɛ February 2017 ni.
english: He was appointed by President Nana Addo Danquah Akuffo-Addo in January 2017 and was approved by the Members of Parliament in February 2017.

kusaal: Letsa keŋi o secondary sakurnɛ bɛ St.Peter's Senior high school Nkwatia Kwahu Ghana.
english: Letsa had his secondary school education at St. Peter's Boys Senior High School Nkwatia Kwahu Ghana.

kusaal: Scandinavian buudi pian'ad an fredag bɛ Swedish, Norwegian, nɛ Danish dim buudi pian'ad ni, ka di gbin an Freyja dabisir.
english: The modern Scandinavian form is fredag in Swedish, Norwegian, and Danish, meaning Freyja's day.

kusaal: Nidib bɛdigʋ yɛl ye Freyja and Frigg ka'a kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔba bɛ Germanic buudi ni.
english: The distinction between Freyja and Frigg in some Germanic mythologies is contested.

kusaal: Arizum daar yinɛ yʋda banɛ bɛ Roman buudi pian'ad naming la yinɛ Latin dies Veneris bɛɛ "Venus dabisir" (dinɛ yi Greek pian'ad Aphrodī́tēs hēméra, Ἀφροδίτης Ἡμέρα ni), ka si'eba an vendredi Fariŋ pian'ad ni, venres, Galician buudi pian'ad ni, divendres, Catalan buudi pian'ad ni, vennari, Corsican buudi pian'ad ni, venerdì, Italian buudi pian'ad ni, vineri, Romanian buudi pian'ad ni, nɛ viernes, Spanish buudi pian'ad ni, ka Filipino buon ye biyernes bɛɛ byernes, ka Chamorro buudi pian'ad mɛ buon betnes.
english: The word for Friday in most Romance languages is derived from Latin dies Veneris or "day of Venus" (a translation of Greek Aphrodī́tēs hēméra, Ἀφροδῑ́της Ἡμέρα), such as vendredi in French, venres in Galician, divendres in Catalan, vennari in Corsican, venerdì in Italian, vineri in Romanian, and viernes in Spanish and influencing the Filipino biyernes or byernes, and the Chamorro betnes.

kusaal: Ka p-Celtic Welsh buudi pian'ad ni mɛ an Gwener.
english: This is also reflected in the p-Celtic Welsh language as Gwener.

kusaal: Fu ya'a yis Portuguese buudi pian'ad, dinɛ mɛ paas Romance buudi ni la, ban buon ye sexta-feira, ka di gbin an "dabisa ayuobʋ daari bɛ liturgical di'ema pʋʋgin", ka ba nyɛ pian'a kan nɛ yi Latin buudi pian'ad feria sexta ni, dinɛ ka ba mɔr winpʋ'ʋs gbana ni zin'is banɛ ka ba da pʋ si'akid ka ba dɔl tɛnsi'eba winaa.
english: An exception is Portuguese, also a Romance language, which uses the word sexta-feira, meaning "sixth day of liturgical celebration", derived from the Latin feria sexta used in religious texts where it was not allowed to consecrate days to pagan gods.

kusaal: Buudi pian'ad kanɛ mɛ an wala buudi bɛ Romance buudi pian'adnam puugin anɛ Sardinian, ban da buonɛ chenàpura pian'ad kanɛ yinɛ Latin buudi yʋ'ʋr kanɛ an cena pura.
english: Another exception among the Romance languages is also Sardinian, in which the word chenàpura is derived from Latin cena pura.

kusaal: Wan wʋʋ Asibid daari an (Savvato, Σάββατο) ka Alasid daar mɛ an (Kyriaki, Κυριακή), ba pʋd Arizum daar nɛ din kanɛ ka ba ti'ebidi gur vʋ'ʋsim dabisir malima la, dinɛ da pin'il nɛ Greek dim banɛ an Kristo biis da bɛ la malima ni na.
english: Like Saturday (Savvato, Σάββατο) and Sunday (Kyriaki, Κυριακή), Friday is named for its liturgical significance as the day of preparation before Sabbath, which was inherited by Greek Christian Orthodox culture from Jewish practices.

kusaal: Arizum daar da pin'ili anɛ Kristo biis nɔlɔɔr dabisir; anina ka Irish buudi buon ye Dé hAoine, Scottish Gaelic buudi buon Di-Haoine, Manx buudi buon Jeheiney ka Icelandic dim pian'ad mɛ an föstudagur, ba wʋsa gbin anɛ "nɔlɔɔr dabisir".
english: Friday was formerly a Christian fast day; this is the origin of the Irish Dé hAoine, Scottish Gaelic Di-Haoine, Manx Jeheiney and Icelandic föstudagur, all meaning "fast day".

kusaal: Wina'am gbaʋŋin nɛ Hebrew tɛŋin, ba buon Arizum daar ye יום שישי Yom Shishi ka di gbin paal ye "daba yuobʋ daar".
english: In both biblical and modern Hebrew, Friday is יום שישי Yom Shishi meaning "the sixth day."

kusaal: Indian dim buudi pian'ad bɛdigʋ ni, ba buon Arizum daar ye Shukravāra, ba pʋd nɛ tis Shukra, Venus.
english: In most Indian languages, Friday is Shukravāra, named for Shukra, the planet Venus.

kusaal: Bengali buudi pian'ad buon ye শুক্রবার bɛɛ Shukrobar anɛ dabisir kanɛ paas ayuobʋ, Bengali bakwai kanl pʋʋgin nɛ ba gbana ni, ka mɛ an dabisir kanɛ pin'il vʋ'ʋsim dabisa la, bɛ Bangladesh.
english: In Bengali শুক্রবার or Shukrobar is the 6th day in the Bengali week of Bengali Calendar and is the beginning of the weekend in Bangladesh.

kusaal: Japanese tɛŋin, ba buon ye 金曜日 (きんようび, kinyōbi) ba nyɛ yʋ'ʋr kannɛ yi 金星 (きんせい, kinsei) ni, ka di gbin an Venus (lit.
english: In Japanese, 金曜日 (きんようび, kinyōbi) is formed from the words 金星 (きんせい, kinsei) meaning Venus (lit.

kusaal: Korean dim buudi pian'ad pʋʋgin, ba buon ye 금요일, Korean pʋʋgin Hangul sɔb (Romanization: geumyoil), ka ba buoni di 金曜日 dinɛ an Chinese tɛŋ sɔb, bɛɛ Japanese.
english: In the Korean language, it is 금요일 in Korean Hangul writing (Romanization: geumyoil), and is the pronounced form of the written word 金曜日 in Chinese characters, as in Japanese.

kusaal: Nahuatl buudi pian'ad ni, ba buon Arizum daar ye quetzalcōātōnal ([ket͡saɬkoːaːˈtoːnaɬ]) ka di gbin an "Quetzalcoatl dabisir".
english: In the Nahuatl language, Friday is quetzalcōātōnal ([ket͡saɬkoːaːˈtoːnaɬ]) meaning "day of Quetzalcoatl".

kusaal: Slavic buudi pian'ad bɛdigʋ buon Arizum daar ye "dabisa anu daar": Belarusian dim buon ye пятніца – pyatnitsa, Bulgarian dim buon ye петък – petŭk, Czech dim buon ye pátek, Polish dim buon ye piątek, Russian dim buon ye пятница – pyatnitsa, Serbo-Croatian dim buon ye петак – petak, Slovak dim buon ye piatok, Slovene dim buon ye petek, ka Ukrainian pian'ad pʋʋgin mɛ an п'ятниця – p'yatnitsya.
english: Most Slavic languages call Friday the "fifth (day)": Belarusian пятніца – pyatnitsa, Bulgarian петък – petŭk, Czech pátek, Polish piątek, Russian пятница – pyatnitsa, Serbo-Croatian петак – petak, Slovak piatok, Slovene petek, and Ukrainian п'ятниця – p'yatnitsya.

kusaal: Hungarian dim buon ye péntek yʋ'ʋr kan yinɛ Slavic Pannonian buudi pian'ad ni na.
english: The Hungarian word péntek is a loan from Pannonian dialect of Slavic language.

kusaal: (Dies Infaustus gbin anɛ "zutoog dabisir".) Nwa' anɛ maliŋ kanɛ ni ka maliŋ kanɛ ka ba buon HMS Friday la yina.
english: (Dies Infaustus means "unlucky day".) This superstition is the root of the well-known urban legend of HMS Friday.

kusaal: Kristo pʋ'ʋs-pʋ'ʋsidib bɛdigʋ ka ba si'eba an Roman Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Methodist, nɛ Anglican mɔr maliŋ kanɛ an ye ba lɔ nɔɔr Arizum daar, sankan ka ba pʋ dit diib, bɛɛ ni'im bɛɛ bin'isim bɛɛ pataasii Arizum daar wʋsa yʋʋm pʋʋgin.
english: As such, adherents of many Christian denominations including the Roman Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Methodist and Anglican traditions, observe the Friday Fast, which traditionally includes abstinence from meat, lacticinia, and alcohol on Fridays of the year.

kusaal: Filet-O-Fish diib la da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi (1962), ka one da mɔri di kɛna an Lou Groen, McDonald's tʋʋma zin'ig yinnɛ kanɛ bɛ Cincinnati, Ohio sʋ'ʋlim, bɔzugɔ, diki'ima da'a da lut nɛ hali Arizum daar wʋsa, ka di anɛ Roman Catholic dimi da pʋ dit ni'im Arizum daar wʋsa la zug.
english: The Filet-O-Fish was invented in 1962 by Lou Groen, a McDonald's franchise owner in Cincinnati, Ohio, in response to falling hamburger sales on Fridays resulting from the Roman Catholic practice of abstaining from meat on Fridays.

kusaal: Ba pʋd dabisir kaŋa nɛ yi Shukra onɛ an Bhrigu biig nɛ Kavyamata (Usana).
english: The day is named after the Shukracharya, son of Bhrigu and Kavyamata (Usana).

kusaal: Arizum daar mɛ len anɛ vʋ'ʋsim dabisir Bahá'í pʋ'ʋsim dim ni.
english: Friday is also the day of rest in the Bahá'í Faith.

kusaal: Malaysian tɛŋ si'eba pʋʋgin, Arizum daar anɛ vʋ'ʋsim dabisa pin'ilig daar, ka Asibid daar ti'al, ye di bas suor ka mɔɔm nyaŋi pʋ'ʋsi ba Arizum daar pʋ'ʋsim.
english: In some Malaysian states, Friday is the first week-end day, with Saturday the second, to allow Muslims to perform their religious obligations on Friday.

kusaal: Jew dim la maliŋ anɛ ye ba lɔ nɔɔr Arizum daar kanɛ lu Chukat bakwai la ni.
english: There is a Jewish custom to fast on the Friday of the week of Chukat.

kusaal: Iran tɛŋin, Arizum daar anɛ bakwai vʋ'ʋsim dabisa naar, ka Asibid daar an bakwai pʋʋgin tʋʋma dabisa pin'ilig.
english: In Iran, Friday is the last day of the weekend, with Saturday as the first day of the working week.

kusaal: German dim buudi pian'ad pin'ilig ni, ba da buoni di ye friggjar-dagr.
english: The expected cognate name in Old Norse would be friggjar-dagr.

kusaal: Arizum daar German buudi pian'adi da pin'il si'em anɛ frjá-dagr, ka din pa'al nɛ ye ba da pɛ'ɛŋ bakwai pʋʋgin dabisa la nɛ yi Low German buudi ni; Amaa, Faroese buudi buon ye fríggjadagur.
english: The name of Friday in Old Norse is frjá-dagr instead, indicating a loan of the week-day names from Low German.

kusaal: Banɛ an Jewish buudi tɛŋ dimi da tis yʋ'ʋr kaŋa, ban da zɔɔ kɛŋ bɛ mɔɔgin la, ye ba tisi ba dikanɛ ka bad diti ba maliŋ kani buon Shabbat ni la.
english: This name had been given by the Jewish community exiled to the island in order to designate the food specifically prepared for Shabbat eve.

kusaal: Arabic buudi pian'ad pʋʋgin, Arizum daar anɛ الجمعة al-jumʿah, ka di gbin an " nidib la'asig." Buudi banɛ bɛ mɔɔm tɛɛnsin, ka ba lɛɛ ka' Arab tɛŋin la, Arizum daar nyɛ di yʋ'ʋr nɛ yi: (Malay Jumaat (Malaysia) bɛɛ Jumat (Indonesian), Turkish cuma, Persian/Urdu جمعه, jumʿa) Swahili (Ijumaa).
english: In Arabic, Friday is الجمعة al-jumʿah, from a root meaning "congregation/gathering." In languages of Islamic countries outside the Arab world, the word for Friday is commonly a derivation of this: (Malay Jumaat (Malaysia) or Jumat (Indonesian), Turkish cuma, Persian/Urdu جمعه, jumʿa).

kusaal: Greek tɛŋin, bakwai pʋʋgin dabisa anaasi yʋda yinɛ yɛlsi'eba ni na.
english: Like Saturday (Savvato, Σάββατο) and Sunday (Kyriaki, Κυριακή), Friday is named for its liturgical significance as the day of preparation before Sabbath, which was inherited by Greek Christian Orthodox culture from Jewish practices.

kusaal: Amaa, Greek dim buudi pian'ad ni, Arizum daar anɛ Paraskevi (Παρασκευή) ka di gbin anɛ ye "ti'ebig" (παρασκευάζω).
english: The Greek word for Friday is Paraskevi (Παρασκευή) and is derived from a word meaning "to prepare" (παρασκευάζω).

kusaal: gold + planet) nɛ 曜日 (ようび, yōbi) ka di gbin an dabisir (kanɛ bɛ bakwai pʋʋgin).
english: gold + planet) and 曜日 (ようび, yōbi) meaning day of the week.

kusaal: Kristo pʋ'ʋsim ni, Good Friday anɛ Arizum daar kanɛ kɛnna ka Easter nyaan paad la.
english: In Christianity, Good Friday is the Friday before Easter.

kusaal: Malima pʋʋgin, Roman Catholics dim da kis ni'im kanɛ yi bʋnkɔnbid banɛ mɔr zi'tʋʋla ni Arizum daar wʋsa, amaa, ziiŋ pʋ paasɛ.
english: Traditionally, Roman Catholics were obliged to refrain from eating the meat of warm-blooded animals on Fridays, although fish was allowed.

kusaal: Arizum daar tʋʋma si'eba anɛ ban na kɛŋ Masjid (masaliki ni) ye ba la'as taaba pʋ'ʋs bɛ maal Salat Al Jumu'ah.
english: Friday observance includes attendance at a mosque for congregation prayer or Salat AlJumu'ah.

kusaal: Islam dim malima pʋʋgin, Arizum daar anɛ dabisir kanɛ an kasi yi wina'am sa'ana, amaa, Jew dim nɛ Kristo biis lee gɔs ka di anɛ dabisa banɛ bɛ tuon la.
english: In Islam, Friday, is the day of communion, of praying together.

kusaal: Bakwai pin'in Asibid daar ka naad Arizum daar, mɔɔm tɛnsi'eba ni, wan wʋʋ Somalia, nɛ Iran tɛɛnsin.
english: The week begins on Saturday and ends on Friday in most other Islamic countries, such as Somalia, and Iran.

kusaal: Tɛɛns banɛ dunia kaanlig kanɛ buon ISO 8601-ka ban gban'e nɛ ye "Atinɛ daar yiiga" la ni, Arizum daar paas nɛ dabisa anu bakwai pʋʋgin.
english: In countries adopting the "Monday-first" convention it is the fifth day of the week.

kusaal: Na'asaatɛɛnsin la, Arizum daar anɛ dabisir kanɛ paas anu nɛ naar dabisiri tis tʋmtʋmnib.
english: In most Western countries, Friday is the fifth and final day of the working week.

kusaal: Armed Forces Revolutionary Council (AFRC) da anɛ military Junta dinɛ da faaen paŋ Ghana din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai nwadisa ayuobʋ daba anaasi daar (June 4, 1979), paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai nwadisa awai dabpisi nɛ anaasi (September 24, 1979).
english: The Armed Forces Revolutionary Council (AFRC) was the military junta that seized power in Ghana from June 4, 1979, to September 24, 1979.

kusaal: AFRC da di'e na'am dɔlisid coup dinɛ da yis Supreme Military Council, dinɛ mɛ an military regime.
english: The AFRC came to power in a coup that removed the Supreme Military Council, another military regime, from power.

kusaal: Fassi ka June 4 coup da maal, ba da mɔnɛ ye ba maal May 15, 1979, ka ba da gban'e Flt.
english: The June 4 coup was preceded by an abortive attempt on May 15, 1979, when Flt.

kusaal: Soogia banɛ da kpi daakan anɛ Colonel Joseph Enningful onɛ da an Commander kʋdʋgʋ tis Support Services bɛ Ghana Armed Forces.
english: These include Major General Odartey-Wellington, who led the government's resistance to the coup d'état, and Colonel Joseph Enningful, who was a former Commander of the Support Services of the Ghana Armed Forces.

kusaal: Soogia banɛ da kpi sieba anɛ Second-Lieutenant J. Agyemang Bio, Corporal William Tingan, Lance Corporal Sorkpor, Trooper Samuel Larsey, Trooper Emmanuel Koranteng-Apau, Lance Corporal Gabriel Follivi nɛ Lance Corporal Mamudu Kalifa.
english: Other soldiers who died that day include Second-Lieutenant J. Agyemang Bio, Corporal William Tingan, Lance Corporal Sorkpor, Trooper Samuel Larsey, Trooper Emmanuel Koranteng-Apau, Lance Corporal Gilbert Kwabla Folivi-Tayko and Lance Corporal Mamudu Kalifa.

kusaal: Ba da mumi ba wʋsa nwɛnɛ military honours nɛ Osu Military Cemetery bɛ Accra la.
english: They were all buried with full military honours at the Osu Military Cemetery in Accra.

kusaal: AFRC gɔmena la da gban'e lʋgʋr sieba faan ba la'ad ka J. K. Siaw da paas.
english: Numerous business entrepreneurs were also targeted and unlawfully had their assets confiscated by the AFRC government, including J. K. Siaw.

kusaal: Hilla Limann onɛ da bɛ People's National Party da lieb zuraan Ghana Third Republic la ni.
english: The AFRC allowed the already scheduled elections to go ahead and handed over to the duly elected Dr. Hilla Limann of the People's National Party, who became the only president of the Third Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: AFRC mɔr nidib piinɛ anu ka ba bɛ di pʋʋgin (15 members).
english: The AFRC consisted of 15 members.

kusaal: Jerry Rawlings nɛ sieba.
english: Lt. Jerry Rawlings and other ranks were arrested.

kusaal: Bama anɛ Major General Odartey-Welllington onɛ da gaad gɔmena nimbanɛ da pʋ siak ye bam aal coup d'état la.
english: These include Major General Odartey-Wellington, who led the government's resistance to the coup d'état, and Colonel Joseph Enningful, who was a former Commander of the Support Services of the Ghana Armed Forces.

kusaal: Sankan la ba da pin'il ya piisʋg, 'House cleaning' tʋʋmkanɛ an ye di yis na'ayiigim nɛ faaŋ.
english: The regime started a 'house cleaning' exercise against corruption.

kusaal: Commissioner nam da bɛnɛ Minister of state nɛ banɛ tʋm gɔmena kʋda ni.
english: Commissioners were in place of Ministers of state and most carried on from the previous government.

kusaal: Commissioner nam sieba tʋm ministries sieba ni AFRC saŋa.
english: A number of commissioners had to cover additional ministries during the period of the AFRC.

kusaal: Zaba kanɛ da naam dabisir la wʋsa la nii, soogianam bɛdegʋ da kɔ'ɔŋi ba nyɔvʋr.
english: During the fighting that ensued throughout the day, a number of military personnel died.

kusaal: Arthur Ahmed anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ pɔlitis wɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan tis Okaikwei South Constituency n bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) o anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Arthur Ahmed is a Ghanaian politician who was Member of Parliament for Okaikwei South Constituency in the Greater Accra Region from 2013 to 2017 on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Nsuta Mampong n bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: He comes from Nsuta Mampong in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Arthur daa di'e o kasɛtta gbaʋg kane bounye Ordinary level certificate bɛ Accra Academy nɛ o GCE Advanced Level certificate bɛ Abuakwa State College.
english: Arthur received his Ordinary level certificate from Accra Academy and his GCE Advanced Level certificate from Abuakwa State College.

kusaal: On na an kpɛɛm bɛ Ackwell Entreprise nɛ contracts tʋʋma.
english: He is the managing director of Ackwell Entreprise and contracts works.

kusaal: Ba daa vɔɔti tis o ka o lieb wadmaan tis Okaikwei South Constituency lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) ka ba lɛn vɔɔti tis o ya'as bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: He was elected Member of Parliament for Okaikwei South Constituency from 2013 and was re-elected in 2016.

kusaal: O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis atan'.
english: He is married with three children.

kusaal: Gyan pin'ili o nwɛ'ɛb la nɛ bɛ 2003 nɛ Ghana Premier League club Liberty Professionals ka dit gɔɔlnam piiga yi nwɛ'ɛb piinɛ ayuobʋ pʋʋgʋn ka bɛnɛ yʋma atan' nɛ Serie A club Udinese dɔlisnɛ yʋma ayi' lɔɔn bɛ Modena netting bɛ zin'is piinɛ anu yit leknam 53 nwɛ'ɛb ka Udinese nii, dinɛ ka o di gɔɔlnam pii nɛ yinne (11) bɛ likmam pistan' nɛ awai (39) nwɛ'ɛb.
english: A club Udinese via two seasons loan at Modena, netting on fifteen occasions in 53 league matches and at Udinese where he scored 11 times in 39 league matches.

kusaal: Gyan an onɛ mɔr gɔɔlnami gati bɛ Ghana national team la ni, ka mɔr gɔɔlnam pisnu nɛ yinne (51).
english: Gyan is the all-time leading goalscorer of the Ghana national team, with 51 goals.

kusaal: O da an Ghana Kabiten bɛ FIFA World Cups banɛ ka ba DA nwɛ' yʋʋm Tusa Ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2006), nɛ yʋʋm Tusa Ayi nɛ pii nɛ Anaasi (2014) la ni.
english: He represented Ghana at the 2006, 2010 and 2014 FIFA World Cups.

kusaal: Gyan lɛn da nɔk Ghana keŋ 2004 Summer Olympics nɛ nɔɔr ayɔpɔi bɛ Africa Cup of Nations banɛ ka ba DA nwɛ' bɛ Yʋʋm Tusabayi' nɛ Anii (2008), yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga (2010), yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012), yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013), yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015), yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) nɛ yʋʋm Tusa Ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019), kɛt ka ba naad ni bɛ 2008 nu runner-up bɛ 2010 nɛ 2015.
english: Gyan also represented Ghana at the 2004 Summer Olympics and in seven Africa Cup of Nations (2008, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2015, 2017 and 2019), helping them finish in third place in 2008 and as runners-up in 2010 and 2015.

kusaal: O nɔki o " LeGYANdry" piinɛ la bigis nidib bɛ Kempinski Gold Coast Hotel bɛ Accra la.
english: He launched his memoir, titled "LeGYANdry" at the Kempinski Gold Coast Hotel in Accra.

kusaal: Gyan anɛ o ma bikpaan, Baffour Gyan Mensah (saam) nɛ o ma kanɛ digi o nu'ug zug, Madam Cecilia Amoako.
english: Gyan is the last born of his parents, Baffour Gyan Mensah (Father) and the late Madam Cecilia Amoako (Mother).

kusaal: Gyan pʋ'a anɛ Gifty Gyan ka ba mɔr biis atan' ka ba yʋ'ʋra an; Rafael Gyan, Frederick Gyan, nɛ Floyd Gyan.
english: Gyan was married to Gifty Sandra Dzamesi and together, they had three children, namely, Rafael Gyan, Frederick Gyan, Floyd Gyan.

kusaal: Onɛ da an kabitin tis Ghana national team la.
english: Gyan is the all-time leading goalscorer of the Ghana national team, with 51 goals.

kusaal: Ka Tusa Ayi' nɛ anii (2008) nii, Gyan pɛ'ɛs Ligue 1 club Rennes ni, ka di gɔɔlnam piinɛ anaasi bɛ leknam nwɛ'ɛb pisnaasi nɛ anii bɛ yʋma ayi' ni.
english: In 2008, Gyan joined Ligue 1 club Rennes, netting fourteen times in forty-eight league matches during two seasons.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir nɛ piiga (2010) pʋʋgʋn nɛɛ, Gyan yʋ'ʋn pɛ'ɛs Premier League club Sunderland, o da digil kʋ'ʋg zabin kilab la ni ka di gɔɔlnam piiga bɛ Premier League nwɛ'ɛb pistan' nɛ anaasi ni bɛ yʋma ayi' ni.
english: On 31 August 2010, Gyan signed for Premier League club Sunderland on a four-year deal for a club record £13 million.

kusaal: Ka mɔr gɔɔlnam 6, onɛ mɔr gɔɔlnam gati sɔ' wʋsa bɛ African wʋsa bɛ World Cup pin'ilʋg.
english: In the final group match, he became the top African goalscorer in World Cup finals history by scoring the Black Stars' goal as they were defeated 2–1 by Portugal.

kusaal: Ka 20 June 2023 nii, Gyan da yɛl ye o kʋ lɛm nwɛ' bɔɔl ya'asɛ ka o gɛn' ya.
english: Gyan announced his retirement from active football on 20 June 2023, marking the end of a career spanning two decades.

kusaal: O bier Baffour Gyan mɛn da anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd.
english: On 24 January 2008, during the Africa Cup of Nations, Gyan and his brother Baffour decided to walk out on the Black Stars following criticism after their unconvincing 1–0 win over Namibia.

kusaal: Asante Kotoko Sporting Club, ka ba buon ye Asante Kotoko giŋa la, anɛ professional football club kanɛ ka ba da pin'i I 31 August 1935 ka di bɛ Kumasi bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Asante Kotoko Sporting Club, simply known as Asante Kotoko, is a professional football club founded on 31 August 1935 and based in Kumasi in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di zab yʋ'ʋr anɛ Porcupine Warriors, ba nya'ad Ghana Premier League ka nwɛ'ɛdi ba yin maknam Baba Yara Stadium in Amakom, Kumasi.
english: Nicknamed the Porcupine Warriors, they compete in the Ghana Premier League and play their home matches at the Baba Yara Stadium in Amakom, Kumasi.

kusaal: Ba di league record nɔɔrim pisi nɛ anaasi (24 times) ka di CAF Champions League nɔɔra ayi ka International Federation of Football History and Statistics (IFFHS) da yɛl ye banɛ di African club of the century.
english: They have won the league a record 24 times, the CAF Champions League twice, and were adjudged the African club of the century by the International Federation of Football History and Statistics (IFFHS).

kusaal: Kwasi Kumah, onɛ yit Nyankyerenease linɛ kpi'e nɛ Kumasi tɛnpʋʋg linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, da anɛ dɔriba tis na'asaa daʋ kanɛ da an soogia, Colonel Ross.
english: Mr. Kwasi Kumah, a native of Nyankyerenease near Kumasi in the Ashanti Region, was a chauffeur to an English man and military officer, Colonel Ross.

kusaal: Colonel Ross da lɛb yinna la, Kumah da da'a nɛ jerseys nam ye o pin'il o football team.
english: When Colonel Ross returned home for good, Kumah bought a set of jerseys to start his football team.

kusaal: O zua sʋŋ, L.Y.Asamoah, mɛ da sʋŋ ya ka ba pin'il Ashanti United Football Club yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisi nɛ ayuobʋ ni (1926).
english: With cooperation from his good friend, L.Y. Asamoah, he formed the Ashanti United Football Club in 1926.

kusaal: "Kumasi Titanics" da pʋ nyɛ zugsʋŋi ba yʋʋr saaʋŋ la nii, ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ anaasi ni (1934), ba da gaŋ yʋ'ʋr kanɛ mɔr paŋ ye Mighty Atoms.
english: "Kumasi Titanics" did not find enough luck in their new name, and in 1934, they adopted a more powerful name, Mighty Atoms.

kusaal: Nɛwala, li sʋ'ʋm da kai, ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ anu ni (1935), Mr J.S.K. Frimpong, kanɛ ka ba da buon o ye Teacher Frimpong, onɛ da an pa'an-pa'ani bɛ Kumasi Government School onɛ da mɔr o pʋtɛn'ɛr club la yela, da la'as dab bi'ela o sakur la ni ka ye ba ti'akim yʋ'ʋr la yi "Kumasi Titanics" lɛbis Kumasi Asante Kotoko Football Club.
english: Still, the club did not see much progress, and in 1935, Mr. J.S.K. Frimpong, popularly called Teacher Frimpong, then a teacher at the Kumasi Government School who had all the time shown interest in the club, organized some men from his school and proposed a change of name from "Kumasi Titanics" to Kumasi Asante Kotoko Football Club.

kusaal: Ba da sɔs suori yi Asantehene (Na'ab parinyaŋ Kingdom of Ashanti) bɔzugɔ, yʋʋr kanɛ an "Kotoko" la, gbin anɛ "Porcupine" ka linɛ an Ashanti tɛŋ la zanbin.
english: Permission had to be obtained from the Asantehene (King of the Kingdom of Ashanti) because the name "Kotoko", meaning "Porcupine" is the official symbol of the Ashanti nation.

kusaal: Asantehene, Nana Sir Osei Agyeman Prempeh II, da pin'ili an yiiga an patron tis club la.
english: The Asantehene, Nana Sir Osei Agyeman Prempeh II, became the first life patron of the club.

kusaal: Accra Sport Stadium ni yelsi'a da sig na bɛ Ohene Djan Stadium, Accra, Ghana yʋʋm tusayi nɛ yinnɛ, sigsaa nwadig, daba wai daar (9 May, 2001).
english: The Accra Sport Stadium disaster occurred at the Ohene Djan Stadium, Accra, Ghana on 9 May 2001.

kusaal: Ghana football teams banɛ nyɛ yʋ'ʋr la da nwɛn'ɛ daar kan, Accra Hearts of Oak (The Phobians) Sporting Club nɛ Asante Kotoko.
english: Ghana's most successful football teams played that day: the Accra Hearts of Oak Sporting Club and the Asante Kotoko.

kusaal: Yʋʋm paal nwadig, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi la ni (January 2020), ba da kad team la ye ba da lɛn nwɛn'ɛ bɛ Baba Yara stadium, saŋa bi'ela, ka li da yinɛ nya'andɔlib banɛ da duod zabir ka pʋlʋs da nwɛn'ɛ rubber bullet da di gban'ae sɔ' ka o da kpi la.
english: In January 2020, the team was banned from the Baba Yara stadium temporarily after violent reactions by supporters led to a fan being hit by a rubber bullet fired by the police.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ, mɔraʋg nwadig la (July 2011), Asante Kotoko nɛ English Premier League club kanɛ buon Sunderland da maal nɔɔr naalig, ani ka Sunderland da sʋŋi sa'al Asante Kotoko, kati wa'ae tuon kɛn yela, laafi yela, nɛ di'ema la yela an si'em.
english: In July 2011, Asante Kotoko and English Premier League club Sunderland signed a partnership agreement, which will see Sunderland offering practical support and advice in youth coaching, player development, fitness, and medical matters, as well as football business strategy, to Asante Kotoko.

kusaal: Yʋʋm paal nwadig, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayi ni (January 2002), ba da gaŋ P V Obeng ye o an board chairman of the Board of Directors tis club la.
english: In January 2002, P V Obeng was appointed as the board chairman of the Board of Directors of the club.

kusaal: Asante Kotoko's zanbin la dolnɛ tɛngbaŋ zanbin kanɛ bɛɛ tis Kingdom of Ashanti ka di colour nam an sabilig, dɛn'ɛm nɛ dɔnbʋʋlim la, kpɛn dɔl nɛ national flag ; Asante Kotoko zanbin la pa'al nɛ yugudir kanɛ ka o nindaa kpi'ɛm ka b aba yelkpan an ba buudi pian'ad "Ashanti Twi ni ye: Kum apem a, apem beba", linɛ gbini pa'al ye "fʋ ya'a ku tusir, tusir na yina ya'as".
english: Asante Kotoko's emblem symbolizes the national emblem of the Kingdom of Ashanti (Kingdom of Asante) with the colours black, green and yellow enclosing the colours on the national flag and ethnic flag of the Kingdom of Asante and Asante Kotoko's emblem; the Asante Kotoko emblem features a remarkably threatening looking porcupine and the motto "Ashanti Twi: Kum apem a, apem beba", which means "If you kill a thousand, a thousand more will come".

kusaal: Nidib tusa pisnaasi, kɔbisnu nɛ pisi nɛ anii (40,528) kpɛn'ɛd anina, ba da mɛ Baba Yara Stadium nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (1957), ka linɛ an stadium kanɛ yalimi bɛ Ghana.
english: With a 40,528 capacity, Baba Yara Stadium, which was built in 1957, is the largest stadium in Ghana.
