kusaal: Stadium la yʋ'ʋri buon Baba Yara, ka ba nɔk nɛ Ghana Footballer kʋdig kanɛ da nwɛn'ɛ tis Kotoko lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anu (1955) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinnɛ (1961).
english: The stadium is named after a former Ghanaian footballer who played for Kotoko between 1955 and 1961.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga ni (2010), ba da tis labaar ye Rlg Communications dim di'e Asante Kotoko ka na tisi ba di'ema zin'ig(stadium) tita'ar ka li yʋ'ʋr na buon Rlg Fabulous Arena.
english: In 2010, it was reported that as part of an endorsement by Rlg Communications, Asante Kotoko will get a multi-purpose stadium called the Rlg Fabulous Arena.

kusaal: Asante Kotoko paas nɛ abʋyuobʋ, football team bɛɛ club banɛ bɛ Africa sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa, ka lin pa'al ye li gati li taaba Ghana sʋ'ʋlim; Asante Kotoko mɔr nya'andɔlib 10 million, ka yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ la, Asante Kotoko nɛ Sunderland AFC tuongatib da sɔns ban na maal nɔnaalig yela.
english: Asante Kotoko is the 6th biggest football team and professional club in Continental Africa and arguably the biggest club in Ghana; Asante Kotoko has a speculated 10 million followers and in the year 2011, Asante Kotoko and Sunderland AFC respective club executive Chairmen's engaged in strategic and positive discussions on both clubs collaborating.

kusaal: Onɛ sʋ'ʋe nɛ tuongat kanɛ nan vʋe tis Asante Kotoko sports club anɛ Asantehene, Zugraan Na'ab tis Ashantis/ Asantes banɛ bɛ Ghana, Osei Tutu II.
english: The owner and life patron of Asante Kotoko sports club is the Asantehene, King of the Asantes of Ghana, Osei Tutu II.

kusaal: Ashanti anɛ tɛŋ kanɛ paas piiga ka ba maan sanlima dunia sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa, bɔzugɔ, Ashanti anɛ zin'ig yinnɛ kanɛ ka ba tuud sanlima ka li paas tɛns piiga banɛ ka ba tuud sanlima anina dunia sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa; The Obuasi Gold Mine.
english: Ashanti is a top-10 producer of gold bars and gold bullions in the world as Ashanti is also a major site of the world's gold-mining industry with Ashanti being home to the world's 10th largest producing gold mine on Earth; The Obuasi Gold Mine.

kusaal: Sanlim 1 ton nɛ Gold (Bullion) anɛ $64.3 Million dollars (US$64,300,000) at $2000/oz.
english: The 1 ton of Gold bars and Gold (Bullion) is worth $64.3 million (US$64,300,000) at $2000/oz.

kusaal: Asante Kotoko tʋm nɛ si'eba an technology corporations Interplast, Smart TV, Iei nɛ giant Rlg Communications; financial institution Fidelity Bank; water company Everpure limited, Peppis Pizza limited, nɛ Vit's Noodles limited; telecommunication companies Millicom nɛ MTN Group; mass media company Sports Pro Media limited; worldwide major electricity generation and electricity construction incorporation Symbion Power; nɛ Singaporean kit manufacturer Kubba.
english: Asante Kotoko's diverse endorsements portfolio includes technology corporations Interplast, Smart TV, Iei and giant Rlg Communications; financial institution Fidelity Bank; water company Everpure limited, Peppis Pizza limited, and Vit's Noodles limited; telecommunication companies Millicom and MTN Group; mass media company SportsPro Media limited; worldwide major electricity generation and electricity construction incorporation Symbion Power; and Singaporean kit manufacturer Kubba.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, sapal nwadig (November 2020) ba da maal nɔnaalig nɛ Hisense Ghana.
english: In November 2020 a partnership agreement was signed between the club and Hisense Ghana.

kusaal: Ba maan "Asante Kotoko Adako-Jachie Training Complex" ka li ya'a naae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu (2015) li na mɔr di'ema zamisig zin'ig, mɔɔg zin'ig, di'ema zin'ig tita'ar, Olympic-size swimming pool nɛ zin'ig kanɛ mɔr gbɛɛnsa dɔɔd pisi tis Asante Kotoko bɛ Adako Jachie, linɛ bɛ Kumasi tɛnkpɛŋ.
english: There is ongoing construction of the "Asante Kotoko Adako-Jachie Training Complex" which when completed in 2015 will consist of three training pitches, one artificial grass pitch, multi-functional sports hall, Olympic-size swimming pool and a 20-bedroom camping facility for Asante Kotoko at Adako Jachie suburb situated on the outskirts of Kumasi.

kusaal: "Asante Kotoko Adako-Jachie Training Complex" la; zamisig zin'is atan' nɛ gbɛɛnsa dɔɔd pisi, ningbina maalig zin'ig, ti'ebig zin'ig, technical staff and coaches nam zin'ig, nɛ la'asig zin'ig, nɛ dɔɔd banɛ bɛ tis Asante Kotoko Chief operating officers (Operations Director) nɛ technical bench.
english: The "Asante Kotoko Adako-Jachie Training Complex"; three training pitches and the 20 bedroom facility will come with a large multi-operational health club and gym, weights for strength training and physical fitness area, a massage unit, dressing rooms, the technical staff's and coaches' office, as well as a conference room with screening facilities and offices for the Asante Kotoko Chief operating officers (Operations Director) and the technical bench.

kusaal: Asante Kotoko executive board da pin'il ya ye onɛ sʋe Asante Kotoko ka an li kpɛɛm kanɛ vue, Asantehene Na'ab Otumfuo Osei Tutu II tis Ashanti tɛŋ dim nar ka o sʋŋ "Asante Kotoko Adako-Jachie Training Complex" nɛ ligidiba mɛɛbnam nɛ ligidi nɛ sa'alig.
english: The Asante Kotoko executive board intimated that the Asante Kotoko Owner and Life Patron of Asante Kotoko, Asantehene King Otumfuo Osei Tutu II of the Ashanti nation is to provide both financial and moral support to the "Asante Kotoko Adako-Jachie Training Complex" and mega training facility construction project.

kusaal: Asante Kotoko nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛdib la yit Asante Kotoko stadium dɔlisid Asante Kotoko squad coach (bus) lɔr linɛ ka banɛ maal an Tata Motors linɛ bɛ conglomerate Tata Group paadi ba zamisig zin'ig tita'arin la.
english: The Asante Kotoko squad players are driven from the Asante Kotoko stadium on the Asante Kotoko squad coach (bus) manufactured by Tata Motors of conglomerate Tata Group to the training headquarters of Asante Kotoko.

kusaal: Nidib si'eba banɛ naan Asante Kotoko Youth academy development program and system yi si'eba anɛ Karim Abdul Razak, Tony Yeboah, Isaac Vorsah, Samuel Inkoom, Godwin Antwi.
english: Former products of the Asante Kotoko Youth academy development program and system include Karim Abdul Razak, Tony Yeboah, Isaac Vorsah, Samuel Inkoom, Godwin Antwi.

kusaal: sʋŋid: Bright Yeboah Taylor (Ghanaian Sports Historian)
english: Contributor: Bright Yeboah Taylor (Ghanaian Sports Historian)(KUMASI)

kusaal: Maxwell Konadu (December 2019 – December 2020)
english: Maxwell Konadu ( December 2019 – December 2020)

kusaal: Prosper Narteh Ogum (September 2021 – August 2022)
english: Prosper Narteh Ogum(September 2021 – August 2022)

kusaal: Kumasi Asante Kotoko Sporting Club ɛɛnbir da pin'il ya nɛ dasam piinɛ tan' banɛ yit Ashanti ka ba tuongat da an lor dɔriba, Mr.
english: The foundation of Kumasi Asante Kotoko Sporting Club was laid by 13 young Ashanti men led by a young driver, Mr. Kwasi Kumah, ably supported by L.Y. Asamoah, an electrician.

kusaal: Kwasi Kumah da paam pʋtɛnr kanɛ an ye o pin'il football team yinɛ on da gɔsidi li di'ema la ni.
english: Kwasi Kumah nurtured the idea of forming a football team when he watched an exciting football match.

kusaal: Yʋʋma anu nya'aŋ ka ba ti'aki li yʋ'ʋri lɛb Kumasi Titanics.
english: Still, the club did not see much progress, and in 1935, Mr. J.S.K. Frimpong, popularly called Teacher Frimpong, then a teacher at the Kumasi Government School who had all the time shown interest in the club, organized some men from his school and proposed a change of name from "Kumasi Titanics" to Kumasi Asante Kotoko Football Club.

kusaal: Ba da pin'il Kumasi Asante Kotoko Football Club nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ anu ni (1935).

kusaal: Constituency la da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni, yinɛ Ghana vɔɔtʋg lʋgʋr la ni, ka li da paas constituency nam pisi nɛ awai la ni, li da kɛ ka constituency nam la kal paasi yi kɔbisyi' keŋ kɔbis yi' nɛ pistan'.
english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Nurein migyimah aan ba wadmaal la bɛ Ghana lʋgʋr kanna ni.
english: Nurein Shaibu Migyimah is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: Assin Central bɛnɛ Assin municipal district n be Ghana lʋg bɛdir kanɛ an Central region la ni.
english: The seat is located within the Assin North Municipal District of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Assin North bɛni Assin North district n bɛ Central Region of Ghana.
english: The Assin North constituency is located in the Assin North district of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Naa'am kʋk la bɛni Assin North Municipality n bɛ Central Region of Ghana.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Assin North Municipality of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piisi nɛ ayi la, li nwadis a anaasi li dabisim piinɛ atan' daar , ka Ghana kɔɔtʋ tita'ar la daa kad saria zaŋi keŋ nidiba anu gat nidiba ayi siak ye, James Gyakye Quayson kʋ lɛm an wadmaan tis Assin North ka mɛ kʋ lɛm zin' wadmaanib yir la ya'asɛ.
english: The Supreme Court of Ghana ruled by 5-2 majority decision on 13 April 2022 that James Gyakye Quayson could not continue to sit in the house as MP for Assin North.

kusaal: Ken Ohene Agyapong, wadmaan tis Assin North constituency yi 2000 vɔtʋg la, ti paae 2008 vɔtʋg yʋ'ʋn lieb wadmaan tis Assin Central constituency bɛ 2012.
english: Ken Ohene Agyapong, the MP for the Assin North constituency from the 2000 parliamentary election to the 2008 parliamentary election became the MP for Assin Central constituency in 2012.

kusaal: Assin North anɛ constituencies nam la yinne ka mɔr wadmaan ka o zi'el tis ba bɛ wadmaanib yir la Ghana nwa.Ba vɔtʋg gaŋ wadmaan yinne ka an linɛ ka nidib la vɔɔt gaŋ nid yinne ma'a.
english: Assin North () is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Assin South constituency la bɛnɛ the Assin South district linɛ bɛ Ghana Central Region la.
english: The Assin South constituency is located in the Assin South district of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Assin South Constituency anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm kanɛ paas ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni mɛn.
english: Assin South is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Assin South District la anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ paas sʋ'ʋlʋm nam bam piisi nɛ ayi banɛ bɛ Central Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Assin South district of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Aston Villa anɛ English kilab kanɛ ka ba mi' ba yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nam saŋa (1880s), ban da an banɛ gat tuon di'ema pʋʋgin la.
english: Aston Villa has been a leading English club since the 1880s, when it was a pioneer of the modern passing game.

kusaal: George Ramsay da di ya'an League Championships nama ayuobʋ nɛ FA Cups nama ayuobʋ la da kɛ ka Aston Villa an kilab kanɛ kɛn tuoni bɛ England, ba da mɔr ya'an kanɛ yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nam saŋa (1890s) kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nam saŋa (1970s).
english: George Ramsay's trophy haul of six League Championships and six FA Cups established Aston Villa as the most successful club in England, a position it held from the 1890s until the 1970s.

kusaal: Villa da di goal nam kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ anii (128) bɛ season 1930–31, ba bʋ lɛn nyɛɛ li buudi ya'asɛ paae zina, amaa kilab la da pin'ili lɛbis nya'aŋ nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nam saŋa (1930s); yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nam saŋa (1940s) nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nam saŋa (1950s) ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nam saŋa la (1960s) ka ba lu tɛŋin ka lini da kɛ ka Doug Ellis da kɛna di'e kilab la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii ni (1968) ka Villa da lɛb nya'aŋ kɛŋ relegation English football ni yʋʋm 1969–70.
english: Villa scored 128 goals in 1930–31, which remains the all-time top-flight record, however the club began its first decline in the mid-1930s; the 1940s and 1950s were generally a period of mediocrity followed by a steep decline in the 1960s which culminated in a takeover of the club by Doug Ellis in 1968 and Villa's first and only relegation to the third tier of English football in 1969–70.

kusaal: Villa da lɛn duoe bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nam tɛnsʋk (1970s) ka ba manager da an Ron Saunders, onɛ da kɛ ka kilab la paas 1980–81 di'ema pʋʋgin.
english: Villa returned to the elite from the mid-1970s under manager Ron Saunders, who led the club to a seventh top-flight league title in 1980–81.

kusaal: Unai Emery da an tuongat yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi ni la (2024), kilab la da nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋi kɛŋ UEFA Champions League ba yiiga daan lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnii paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi la ni 1982/83 sa.
english: Under Unai Emery, the club qualified for the UEFA Champions League for the first time since 1982–83 and won the Europa League in 2025–26.

kusaal: Ba di'ema pʋʋgin, Villa di'em yʋʋm kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ (111) ka bɛnɛ agɔla, fʋ ya'a nɔki mak nɛ si'eba li anɛ abʋyi' daani tisi ba, ka mɛ di ya'an 78 England internationals, ka di ya'ani gaadi ba taaba.
english: During their history, Villa has spent 112 seasons in the top-flight, the second highest of any club, and provided 78 England internationals, also the second highest of any club.

kusaal: Villa nya'ad nɛ Birmingham City bɛɛ ba tɛŋin ka ba dataas banɛ ti'al ayi an City derby ban di'em nɛ kilab si'eba yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii saŋa sa (1879).
english: Villa have a fierce local rivalry with Birmingham City and the Second City derby between the teams has been played since 1879.

kusaal: Aston Villa Football Club da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi, sapal nwadig, dabpisi nɛ yinnɛ daar (21 November 1874), ka banɛ da pin'ili li an Villa Cross Wesleyan Chapel nidib banɛ bɛ Handsworth: linɛ yʋ'ʋn bɛ Birmingham sʋ'ʋli la.
english: Aston Villa are believed to have formed on 21 November 1874, by members of the Aston Villa Wesleyan Chapel in Handsworth: which is now part of Birmingham.

kusaal: Nidib anaasi banɛ da pin'il Aston Villa da anɛ Jack Hughes, Frederick Matthews, Walter Price nɛ William Scattergood, banɛ da paas chapel's cricket team banɛ da ied suor kanɛ ka ba na wisigi ba ningbina waad saŋa.
english: The four founders of Aston Villa Football Club were Jack Hughes, Frederick Matthews, Walter Price and William Scattergood, who were members of the chapel's cricket team looking for a way to stay fit during the winter months.

kusaal: Footballkilab nami da kae la zug Aston Villa yiiga nwɛ'ɛb da anɛ ban nɛ Aston Brook St Mary's Rugby team.
english: Due to the lack of local football teams Aston Villa's first match was against the local Aston Brook St Mary's Rugby team.

kusaal: Kilab la da nyɛ zugsʋŋ ban da nyɛ Scotland dim daʋ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon George Ramsay ka o da kɛna nyɛ ka Villa nwɛ'ɛ-nwɛ'ɛdib bɛ ba di'ema pʋʋgin bɛ Aston Park yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii ne pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayʋobʋ ni (1876).
english: The infant club's fortunes changed forever when a young Scotsman called George Ramsay stumbled across the Villa players' practice match in Aston Park in 1876.

kusaal: Labaar da yi lalli Ramsay baŋir yela, nidib bɛdigʋ da la'asid ye ba gɔs ninkanɛ ka ba da pʋd o giŋa ye 'Scotty' la.
english: Word spread about how fine a player Ramsay was, spectators began turning up to watch the little man nicknamed "Scotty".

kusaal: Ramsay da paam kpɛmisigi yi Scottish dim kilab, Queen's Park, onɛ da gaad tuoni gɔs bʋnlinɛ ka ba buon 'combination football' linɛ da bɛ Glasgow, ban da tɔmisid bɔɔl la si'em la da ti'ak English kilab nam 1870s.
english: On the other hand, Ramsay had been influenced by the Scottish club Queen's Park, who pioneered what became known as "combination football" in his native Glasgow.

kusaal: Villa da pin'ili maali ba mɛŋi an banɛ gati ba taaba bɛ Midlands, ka da di ba ya'an piini, Birmingham Senior Cup in 1880.
english: Villa began to establish themselves as one of the best teams in the Midlands, winning their first honour, the Birmingham Senior Cup in 1880.

kusaal: banɛ bɔɔd na mɔr gbana tis Aston Villa Club House kpɛɛmnam la bɛ 6 Witton Road, Aston' la, ka da ke ka di yʋʋgi gaad Sigir Nwadig la dabisim pisyi nɛ atan' daare.
english: Applications with reference must be made not later than June 23rd to Chairman of the Committee, Aston Villa Club House, 6 Witton Road, Aston' Villa received 150 applicants for the role, but with his strong association with the club George Ramsay was the overwhelming choice of the membership.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis nii nɛ pisnii nɛ anii la Dɔnwalig Nwadig (March 1888) la ni, o da sɔbi tis club la kpɛɛmnam, Aston Villa, la'am nɛ Blackburn Rovers, Bolton Wanderers, Preston North End nɛ West Bromwich Albion, pian'adi pa'an yee ba ya'a maal team yinne pɛɛs di na sʋŋ ka ba mɔr nidibi tis clab ka ba nwɛ'ɛd saŋa wʋsa.
english: In March 1888, he wrote to the committee of his own club, Aston Villa, as well as to those of Blackburn Rovers, Bolton Wanderers, Preston North End and West Bromwich Albion, suggesting the creation of a league competition that would provide a number of guaranteed fixtures for its member clubs each season.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a gɔsi ba la'asʋg nami ayi ka ba kpɛɛmnam la da mɔri ba keŋ dunia wʋsa yiiga Football League season dinɛ da sin'iŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis nii nɛ pisnii nɛ anii Sɛnlʋŋ Nwadig (September 1888) la ni nɛ club la nwɛ'ɛdibi piiga nɛ ayi (12) banɛ yit Midlands nɛ north of England: Accrington, Aston Villa, Blackburn Rovers, Bolton Wanderers, Burnley, Derby County, Everton, Notts County, Preston North End, Stoke, West Bromwich Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderer.
english: Following two meetings between representatives of the leading clubs, the world's first Football League season began in September 1888 with 12 member clubs from the Midlands and north of England: Accrington, Aston Villa, Blackburn Rovers, Bolton Wanderers, Burnley, Derby County, Everton, Notts County, Preston North End, Stoke, West Bromwich Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderers.

kusaal: Villa tuongatib kpɛɛmnam la ni yinne Frederick Rinder an onɛ da sin'iŋ club la la'asʋg bɛ Barwick Street yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis nii nɛ piswai nɛ atan' Fulumfug Nwadig (February 1893) la ni yis tuongatib kpɛɛmnam banɛ da da bɛ saŋkan la gɔsid club la yɛla.
english: Villa Committee Member Frederick Rinder was the instigator of a club meeting at Barwick Street in February 1893 that removed the committee running the club at the time.

kusaal: Pitch la ni ka manager George Ramsay gʋn'ʋl team la banɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋr yi hali giŋa, tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ la'asi gaadi nyɛ' Villa ka o di ya'an yiiga league dinɛ pia'nzug nɛ bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai atan' keŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai anaasi (1893 - 94) la ni nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai ayuobu keŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswa ayɔpoi (1896 - 1897) la ni.
english: On the pitch, manager George Ramsay was moulding a team that became renowned for its short, quick combination passing which saw Villa win its first league title in 1893–94; the season after that the club won its second FA Cup in 1894-95.

kusaal: Aston villa da yi an banɛ yina ken tuon hali English club, Victorian era saŋa la, ba da di ya'anam ka di pʋ pɔɔd di gad League nami anu pian'azut nɛ FA Cups nam atan' Queen Victoria's reign la naarin bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ ayinne 1901 la ni.
english: Aston Villa emerged as the most successful English club of the Victorian era, winning no fewer than five League titles and three FA Cups by the end of Queen Victoria's reign in 1901.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Villa kpɛɛm saŋa kaŋa da anɛ Birmingham-born forward John Devey, onɛ da ken tuon bɛ lightning-fast winger Charlie Athersmith nɛ marshalling Villa's gudim da anɛ tough-tackling Scotsman James Cowan onɛ da mɔr ya'am mi'i saŋa kanɛ ka ba na nwɛ'.
english: Villa's captain during this era was Birmingham-born forward John Devey, who enjoyed a successful partnership with the lightning-fast winger Charlie Athersmith and marshalling Villa's defence was the tough-tackling Scotsman James Cowan, who had an unrivalled sense of timing and anticipation.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai ayɔpoi 1897 la, yʋʋm kan la ka Villa da di ya'an nam abʋyi la (The Double), ba da yii lɛb ba yin dinɛ ka ba bɛ nananna, Aston Lower Grounds la.
english: In 1897, the year Villa won The Double, they moved into their present home, the Aston Lower Grounds.

kusaal: Ba tuon ken la da kpɛm kenɛ ala ti paae Edwardian era, nɛ Villa ti kenna ʋk FA Cup dinɛ pɛɛsidi abʋnaasi bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ anaasi paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ anu (1904 - 1905) la ni, nɛ league kanɛ pɛɛsi ayuobʋ bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ awai paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piiga (1909 - 1910) la ni.
english: Success continued into the Edwardian era, with Villa lifting the FA Cup for the fourth time in 1904–05, and a sixth league title in 1909–10.

kusaal: Ti ya'a keŋ tuon FA Cup yaŋir la da nyaŋi tʋm eve First World War bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piiga nɛ atan' 1913 la ni club la da kɔ'ɔŋ nɛ ban na di ya'an abʋyi (Double) la, naar league.
english: A further FA Cup triumph was achieved on the eve of the First World War in 1913, with the club narrowly missing out on winning a second Double, finishing runners-up in the league.

kusaal: Banɛ da nwɛ'ɛd bool la paam anɛɛ Howard Spencer, ka gur cultured onɛ an kpɛɛm da an Villa nɛ England, nɛ banɛ an prolific strike force of Joe Bache nɛɛ Harry Hampton onɛ da bɛ batbetween them scored 382 goals bɛclaret nɛblue.
english: Star players during this era included Howard Spencer, the cultured defender who captained both Villa and England, and the prolific strike force of Joe Bache and Harry Hampton who between them scored 382 goals in claret and blue.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyi (January1920), Billy Walker da di goals nam abʋyi o Villa nya'aŋi ba 2-1 FA Cup la first round la ni k aba di ya'aŋ ka bas QPR; Club la da di FA Cub la ya'aŋ dinɛ pɛɛŋi abʋtan' la saŋkan la ka Walker keŋ pa'al yee on anɛ Villa's star player bɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ psyi (1920s) saŋa, ka di goals nam kɔbisyi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anaasi (244) bɛ o nwɛ'ɛbnam kɔbisnu nɛ pistan'nɛ yinne (531), onɛ da an kpɛɛm tis Villa nɛ England.
english: In January 1920, Billy Walker scored twice on his Villa debut in a 2–1 FA Cup first-round win over QPR; the club won the FA Cup for the sixth time that season and Walker went on to establish himself as Villa's star player of the 1920s, scoring a record 244 goals in 531 appearances, captaining Villa and England.

kusaal: Goals pisnaaasi nɛ anaasi (49) sieba ka ba da di ka li bɛɛ di kɔn' hali saŋakan la tɛŋsʋk tuon sɔb Tom 'Pongo' Warning la da di goals ban la, nɛ goals pistan' sieba mɛn ka kpɛn-kpɛn sɔb Eric Houghton la da dii li.
english: A remarkable 49 of the league goals that season were scored by centre-forward Tom 'Pongo' Waring, with another 30 goals from winger Eric Houghton.

kusaal: Club la da gaŋ Jimmy McMullan ye o an kpɛɛm kani gɔsid bool la nwɛ'ɛb yɛla bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ anaasi (1934), amaa ba gban'ar kaŋa da naae ba sʋmm, din ka ke ka ba gʋ'ʋŋ ka lʋ teŋin hali yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ anu (1935) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ ayuobu (1936) la nib a da did ya'an ha yʋma anii (48 years) yɛla la.
english: The club appointed Jimmy McMullan as manager in 1934, however, the move proved disastrous, resulting in Villa's first ever relegation in 1935–36 after 48 years in the top flight.

kusaal: Villa da namisnɛ hali gʋ'ʋŋir la yɛla: ba da di kɔbiga nɛ piiga (110) bɛ nwɛ'ɛb pisnaasi ni, ka ayɔpɔi (7) yit Arsenal's Ted Drake dinɛ an infamous 1–7 nyaŋir bɛ Villa Park la ni.
english: Villa struggled largely due to a dismal defensive record: they conceded 110 goals in 42 games, 7 of them coming from Arsenal's Ted Drake in an infamous 1–7 defeat at Villa Park.

kusaal: Club la da tik nu'ug nwɛnɛ bam baba ayɔpɔi ka sa'am ligidi saŋkan la £35,500 mɔɔd ban na niŋ siem ka nyaŋi keŋ tuo din kun tun'oe ka an siem wʋsa, amaa ba da pʋ yaŋi da' ba mɛŋi yɛla la nii.
english: The club made seven signings and spent a staggering sum for the time of £35,500 trying to retain top-flight status at all costs, but were unable to buy their way out of trouble.

kusaal: Saŋa kan la Aston Villa da an boolnwɛ'ɛdi banɛ k aba yʋ'ʋr yi hali k aba ken tuon hali bɛ dunia wʋsa ni boolnwɛ'ɛbin la, ba da yʋ'ʋm sigi bɛ teŋin bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ ayuobu (1936) la ni yɛlkuda dinɛ nan zi maal kudim.
english: Aston Villa, at the time one of the most famous and successful clubs in world football, was relegated in 1936 for the first time in its history.

kusaal: Dɔlisidi kɛn tuon sa bɛ ba Second Division la ni, Villa board dim la da gʋ'ʋŋ ka ken mɔri ba club chairman Fred Rinder onɛ ann ba kpɛɛm kudig la lɛb na, o da o ya'a lɛb na Villa na lɛm du agola ka kɛŋ tuon nwɛni on da bɛ k aba da kɛn tuon ka did ya'an siem la.
english: Following relegation to the Second Division, the Villa board brought back the ageing former club chairman Fred Rinder, who said on his return "Villa have been a great club, are still a great club, and always will be a great club".

kusaal: Rinder's yiiga tumir dinɛ ka o da tum anɛ on da nwieɛ kɛŋ Austria mɔr coach Jimmy Hogan ka o an ba manager.
english: Rinder's first act was to travel to Austria to recruit the progressive coach Jimmy Hogan as manager.

kusaal: Hogan da pa'al nyain o yam kanɛ ka mɔr boolnwɛ'ɛbin yee: "I am a teacher and lover of constructive football with every pass, every kick, every movement an object." O daa ɛɛnt yɛti o nidib la saŋa wʋsa yee boolnwɛ'ɛb nwɛnɛ Viennese waltz, rhapsody nɛ.
english: Hogan outlined his philosophy: "I am a teacher and lover of constructive football with every pass, every kick, every movement an object." He used to tell his players that "football was like a Viennese waltz, a rhapsody.

kusaal: Bumper nidib bɛdigʋ da kɛŋ Villa Park dɔlisid nwɛ'ɛb ka na la, nidib tusa kɔbispisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobu, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (76,588) da kɛŋ FA Cup quarter-final, Villa nɛ Derby County da nwɛ'ɛd bɛ yʋʋm tusa kɔbiswai nɛ pisnasi ayuobu Dɔnwalig nwadig la ni (March 1946), nɛ'ɛŋa an dinɛ ka nidib da kɛŋ zuo hali bɛ Villa Park la ni.
english: Bumper crowds flocked to Villa Park following the war, 76,588 people attended the FA Cup quarter-final between Villa and Derby County in March 1946, which is the all-time record attendance at Villa Park.

kusaal: Star players da anɛ club dau yinne ma'aa onɛ an Harry Parkes, Welsh ɛ tɛŋsʋk tuon Trevor Ford nɛ pʋʋgin - tuon Johnny Dixon, fʋ ya'a gɔs club la da di ya'aŋ dinɛ an ba mid-table ka naas wʋsa ba pisnaasi nam ni bɛɛ ba pisnu nam ni din bɛɛ agɔl bɛdigʋ gat 6th place league ni.
english: Star players of this era included the one-club man Harry Parkes, the Welsh centre forward Trevor Ford and inside-forward Johnny Dixon, however the club only achieved mid-table finishes throughout the forties and fifties, never finishing higher than 6th place in the league.

kusaal: Board la da kpɛ' pʋʋgin na ban da nyɛ ka nidib la sin'iŋi fieɛɛd saŋa kan la nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' (1953) la AGM ka Sports Argus pa'ali di yɛla yee "the longest and liveliest Villa meeting".
english: The board came in for increasing criticism during this time, with the 1953 AGM described by the Sports Argus as "the longest and liveliest Villa meeting".

kusaal: La'am nɛ ba ban daa pʋ bɔɔd ye ba sik teŋin la wʋsa saŋa kanɛ da dɔl la, Aston Villa's first trophy ba yʋma pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi (37 years) la ni, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu ayuobu (1956) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu ayɔpɔi (1957) la ni, saŋa kanɛ Villa boolnwɛ'ɛd niŋ kudʋg, Eric Houghton onɛ da Gaad Manchester United 2-1 nɛ Northern Irish winger Peter McParland kanɛ ka ba da la'am la'asi di goal la.
english: Despite narrowly avoiding relegation the season before, Aston Villa's first trophy for 37 years came in the 1956–57 season when another former Villa player, Eric Houghton led the club to a then record seventh FA Cup Final win, defeating the 'Busby Babes' of Manchester United 2–1 with Northern Irish winger Peter McParland scoring both goals.

kusaal: Team la da kpɛm kɛnɛ tuoni namisid ka pʋ bata league la, ka dinzug ka ba da yis Eric Houghton bɛ , yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii Samampiid Nwadig (December 1958) la ni.Ban da yis o ka nɔk Joe mercer la pʋ sʋŋ siel-siel ka yaŋi ke ka team nɔɔrim abʋtan' dinɛ nan zi naam kudim bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii (1958) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai (1959) la ni.
english: The team continued to struggle for consistency in the league though, which led to Eric Houghton being sacked in December 1958.

kusaal: Amaa fd ya'a gts Mercer saŋa la o da nyaŋi ke ka Villa ken tuon bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnyuobʋ (1960) ka an Second Division Champions dasam paalis yʋ'ʋs ja ba da buoni ba ye 'Mercer's Minors' Aston Villa yʋ'ʋm da an team kanɛ an yiiga di Football League Cup nɛ England teŋʋk-tuon Gerry Hitchens di goals vɛnna pisnaasi nɛ ayi bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnyuobʋ (1960) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnyuobʋ ayinne (1961).
english: However, under the stewardship of Mercer, Villa returned to the top-flight in 1960 as Second Division Champions with a talented young side which became known as 'Mercer's Minors'.

kusaal: Hitchens' goal si da ke ka Italian club Inter Milan, da wdm o yɛla ka tis o ligidi bɛdigʋ ka tik nu'ug.
english: Hitchens' goals brought him to the attention of Italian club Inter Milan, who offered him a large financial incentive to sign.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi, nɛ piiga ayuobʋ, sigir nwadig la ni (June 2016), Chinese kpikpiŋ daan kanɛ ka ba buon Tony Xia da da' kilab la £76 million.
english: In June 2016, Chinese businessman Tony Xia bought the club for £76 million.

kusaal: Kpɛɛm kanɛ da sʋ'ʋe Chelsea ka ba buon o Roberto Di Matteo ka ba da gaŋ ye o an kilab la manager, amaa ba da kad o yis di'ema piinɛ yi pʋʋgin, ban da pʋ nyaŋi pin'il sʋ'ʋŋa la zug.
english: Former Chelsea boss Roberto Di Matteo was appointed as the club's new manager, but was dismissed after just 12 games following a poor start to the season.

kusaal: Bruce da gaadi ba tuon ka ba da naae bɛ abʋnaasi 2017–18 season la ni, amaa ka da lɛb nya'aŋi bɛ 2018 EFL Championship play-off final ban da nwɛ'ɛd nɛ Fulham la.
english: Bruce led the team to finish fourth in the 2017–18 season, but lost in the 2018 EFL Championship play-off final to Fulham.

kusaal: Ba da da' kilab la faar pisnu nɛ anu, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (55%), ka Sawiris da di'e kpɛŋi an chairman, ka da gaŋ Christian Purslow ye o an CEO.
english: They purchased a controlling 55% stake in the club, and Sawiris took over the role of club chairman, appointing Christian Purslow as CEO.

kusaal: Onɛ da di'e o nɔbir anɛ Brentford manager kudug nɛ boyhood Villa nya'andɔl Dean Smith, onɛ da gaad kilab la tuon ka ba paas abʋnu zin'ig, ka kɛ ka ba di ya'an nɔɔr piiga banɛ ka ba da nwɛ'ɛ la wʋsa ka nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋ playoffs ya'as.
english: He was replaced by Brentford manager and boyhood Villa fan Dean Smith, who led the team to fifth place, and reaching the playoffs again—helped on by a club-record 10 league game winning streak.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ ka Villa lɛb Premier League ni la, Recon Group faar kanɛ ka ba mɔr kilab la ni la, NSWE da da' li, ka li pa'al ye Xia pʋ lɛn mɔr si'el kilab la nii.
english: On the eve of Villa's Premier League return, Recon Group's minority share ownership was bought out by NSWE, meaning Xia no longer had any stake in the club.

kusaal: Villa da lɛb Premier League ni abʋyi daan la, Smith nɛ o nidib la da naae bɛnɛ piinɛ yinnɛ zin'igin, amaa o da pʋ nyaŋi muk ka ba nwɛ'ɛ-nwɛ'ɛd kanɛ mɔr baŋir ka an captain ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Jack Grealish la ka o kpɛlim kilab la nii, Manchester City dimi da ye ba da'a o £100 million la da kɛ ka o gaad tɔ'ɔtɔ'.
english: In Villa's second season back in the Premier League, Smith oversaw an 11th-place finish, but was unable to persuade star player and captain Jack Grealish to remain at the club after Manchester City's British-record £100 million bid triggered his release clause.

kusaal: Ban da pʋ nwɛ'ɛ sʋ'ʋm bɛ 2021–22 season ni la, ba da nwɛ'ɛ nɔɔr piinɛ yinnɛ ka kɔ'ɔŋ ayɔpɔi, linzug ka ba da yis Dean Smith.
english: Following a poor start to the 2021–22 season, which saw seven losses in the club's opening 11 games, Dean Smith was dismissed.

kusaal: Aston Villa da gaŋ Liverpool nɛ England captain kudug kanɛ ka ba buon o Steven Gerrard ka o an head coach yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ, sapal nwadig, dapiinɛ yinne daar (11 November 2021).
english: Aston Villa appointed former Liverpool and England captain Steven Gerrard as head coach on 11 November 2021.

kusaal: Ban da pʋ pin'il 2022–23 season titua la, ba da di goal nɔɔra yi ma'a ka ba goal nam kanl la'asa ayɔpɔi, ba da yis Gerrard yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yi, Sawaar nwadig la ni (October 2022), ka onɛ da di'e o nɔbir an Ninkanɛ gaad tuoni di ya'an nɔɔra anaasi bɛ Europa League ni ka an Spain nid ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Unai Emery.
english: After a poor start to the 2022–23 season, in which Villa won just twice and scored only seven goals in their opening 11 games, Gerrard was sacked in October 2022, and replaced by four-time Europa League-winning Spanish manager Unai Emery.

kusaal: 2023–24 season la ni, Emery da gaad kilab la tuoni paae Conference League semi-finals, anina ka Olympiacos da yisi ba, ka ba da naae anaasi zin'ig league la ni, ka da paam suori kpɛn'ɛ UEFA Champions League ni lin yi 1982–83 saŋa sa.
english: In the 2023–24 season, Emery led the club to the Conference League semi-finals, where they were knocked out by Olympiacos, and a fourth-place finish in the league, securing participation in the UEFA Champions League for the first time since 1982–83.

kusaal: Aston Villa fuud la ba da maani bɛnɛ tɛnkan ni ti paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi ni (1974), sankan ka Umbro da an yiiga maali li zanbini niŋ Villa fuugin la.
english: Aston Villa's kit was produced by local manufacturers until 1974, when Umbro became the first kit supplier to have its logo on a Villa shirt.

kusaal: Banɛ da sʋŋ Aston Villa tisi ba fuud la yiiga da anɛ Davenports Breweries bɛ 1982–83 season.
english: Aston Villa's first shirt sponsor was Davenports Breweries in the 1982–83 season.

kusaal: Aston Villa di'emidi ba yin di'ema bɛ nɛ Villa Park; ba da di'emid yiiga bɛnɛ Aston Park (1874–1876) nɛ Wellington Road (1876–1897).
english: Aston Villa's current home venue is Villa Park; the team previously played at Aston Park (1874–1876) and Wellington Road (1876–1897).

kusaal: England di'ema nam piinɛ yuobʋ ka ba da di'em anina, pin'ilig saŋa da anɛ 1899, ka linɛ nan pʋ yʋʋgɛ an 2005.
english: It has hosted 16 England internationals at senior level, the first in 1899, and the most recent in 2025.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi ni (2022), club la da yis labaar na ye ba ye ba maligim mɛ North Stand ka maal Trinity Road zin'ig si'eba ka li nyaŋi nɔk nidib tusa pisnu (50,000).
english: In 2022, the club announced plans to rebuild the North Stand and part of the Trinity Road stand, which will take the maximum capacity over 50,000.

kusaal: Ban wisigidi ba mɛŋ zin'ig si'a an Bodymoor Heath linɛ kpi'e Kingsbury linɛ bɛ north Warwickshire, zin'ig kan ka chairman kudug Doug Ellis da da'a bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔinam pin'ilig saŋa la (1970s) o da da' yi nɛ kpaad sɔ' ni.
english: The current training ground is located at Bodymoor Heath near Kingsbury in north Warwickshire, the site for which was purchased by former chairman Doug Ellis in the early 1970s from a local farmer.

kusaal: Bodymoor Heath da anɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka la'avɛnla bɛ ka nidib kɛnni gɔsid yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi saŋa (1970s), amaa yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai naar saŋa la (1990s) zin'ig la da pʋ lɛn vɛnl ya'asɛ.
english: Although Bodymoor Heath was state-of-the-art in the 1970s, by the late 1990s the facilities had started to look dated.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu, kusanwadis piiga ni la (November 2005), Ellis nɛ Aston Villa plc da yis labaar na ye ba ye ba nɔk nɛ £13 million maligim maal Bodymoor zin'is ayi.
english: In November 2005, Ellis and Aston Villa plc announced a state of the art £13 million redevelopment of Bodymoor in two phases.

kusaal: Zin'ig paalig nwa' da yi paalʋ na yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kusanwadis anaasi, daba yuobʋ daar (6 May 2007), ka banɛ da gaad tuoni gɔsi li yela an onɛ da an manager sankan ka ba buon o Martin O'Neill, team captain ka ba buon o Gareth Barry nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi (1982) captain kanɛ da gaad tuon ka ba di'e European Cup ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Dennis Mortimer, ka Aston Villa nwɛ'ɛ-nwɛ'ɛdib da nyaŋi paas 2007–08 season la ni.
english: The new training ground was officially unveiled on 6 May 2007, by then manager Martin O'Neill, then-team captain Gareth Barry and 1982 European Cup winning team captain Dennis Mortimer, with the Aston Villa squad moving in for the 2007–08 season.

kusaal: O da anɛ chairman ka lɛn an sʋ'ʋe (shareholder) "Aston Villa F.C." gaad o taaba lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii ni (1968) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu ni (1975) ka lɛn gaad o taaba lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiwai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi (1982) paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ ni (2006).
english: He was chairman and substantial shareholder of "Aston Villa F.C." from 1968 to 1975 and the majority shareholder from 1982 to 2006.

kusaal: Ba da la'asi pɛ'ɛli bɛ London Stock Exchange (LSE) bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ ni (1996), ka ba ligidi da lu hali yʋʋm piiga pʋʋgin.
english: The club were floated on the London Stock Exchange (LSE) in 1996, and the share price fluctuated in the ten years after the flotation.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ, kusanwadis ayɔpɔi ni, dabpiinɛ anaasi ni (14 August 2006), ba da yel ye Randy Lerner, onɛ da sʋ'ʋe National Football League ka ba buon o Cleveland Browns la, da naal nɔɔr nɛ taaba ligidi £62.6 million nɛ Aston Villa ye o di'e club la.
english: On 14 August 2006, it was confirmed that Randy Lerner, then owner of the National Football League's Cleveland Browns, had reached an agreement of £62.6 million with Aston Villa for a takeover of the club.

kusaal: Lerner da gaŋ o mɛŋ ka o an chairman tis club la ka Charles Krulak an director ka Ellis da di'e kpɛŋ kanɛ ka ba pʋd ye Chairman Emeritus.
english: Lerner appointed himself chairman of the club with Charles Krulak as a non-executive director and Ellis awarded the honorary position of Chairman Emeritus.

kusaal: Lerner da ti'eb ye o kuos club la bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ naasi, kusanwadis anaasi ni (May 2014), ka ligidi kanɛ ka o da bɔɔd an £200 million.
english: Lerner put the club up for sale in May 2014, valuing it at an estimated £200 million.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, kusanwadis anaasi, dabpiinɛ nii daar (18 May 2016), Randy Lerner da si'ak ye o kuos Aston Villa tis Recon Group, tʋʋma zin'ig kanɛ ka onɛ sʋ'ʋe an Chinese kpikpiŋ daan Tony Xia.
english: On 18 May 2016, Randy Lerner agreed the sale of Aston Villa to Recon Group, owned by Chinese businessman Tony Xia.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai, kusanwadis ayɔpɔi, daba wai daar (9 August 2019), ban da tɔlis tuoni yʋ'ʋn wa'ae Premier League ni la, Companies House da yis labaar ye Xia sʋ'ʋd la ba da'a li ka o pʋ lɛn sʋ'ʋe si'el kilab la ni ya'asɛ.
english: On 9 August 2019, following Villa's promotion to the Premier League, Companies House revealed that the remainder of Xia's shares had been bought out, and that Xia no longer had any stake in the club.

kusaal: Nɔɔrnaalig nwa, linɛ da kɛ ka Atairos paam ya'ani sʋ'ʋe V Sport pʋdigir pisi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (20%), ka Villa ligidi da gaad £500 million.
english: The agreement, which saw Atairos obtain a stake of approximately 20% in V Sports, valued Villa at more than £500 million.

kusaal: Nɔɔrnaalig kanɛ da bɛ ban nɛ Atairos tɛnsʋk la da pin'il tʋʋma nɛ yʋʋm tusayii nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi, na'asaanwadis anaasi, dabpiinɛ yi daar (12 April 2024), ka onɛ sʋ'ʋe Atairos la nɛ Comcast CFO kudug kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Michael Angelakis da paas Villa tuongatib la pʋʋgin.
english: The deal with Atairos was finalised on 12 April 2024, with Atairos CEO and former Comcast CFO Michael Angelakis appointed to Villa's board of directors.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga, nwadisawai ni (September 2010), Aston Villa da pin'il gban'ar si'a bɛ Villa Park ka ba da buol ye Villa Midlands Food (VMF) ye kilab la nɔk yʋma yi pa'al sakur biis Aston Villa hospitality and events ban nɛ Birmingham City Council.
english: In September 2010, Aston Villa launched an initiative at Villa Park called Villa Midlands Food (VMF) where the club will spend two years training students with Aston Villa hospitality and events in association with Birmingham City Council.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ, sigsaa nwadig la ni (May 2021), Prince William, Duke of Cambridge da la'as banɛ paas lugir nwa ni bɛ Aston Villa dim zin'ig kanɛ buon Bodymoor Heath Training Ground la.
english: In May 2021, Prince William, Duke of Cambridge, met with members of the Foundation at Aston Villa's Bodymoor Heath Training Ground.

kusaal: Nwa' da anɛ ban da maan diibi tisid nidib tusir yel, ka lin anɛ tɛŋin tʋmtʋmnib, COVID-19 pandemic kanɛ da paae United Kingdom saŋa la ka mɛ bas suor ka sibiti dim ka ba buon NHS Trust ka ba kpɛn'ɛ ka mɛ nɔk Villa Park la'ad la tum tuuma.
english: This was following the Foundation providing 1000 hot meals a week to local organisations during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom, as well as allowing a local NHS Trust to make use of Villa Park's facilities.

kusaal: John Devey onɛ da an captain lin da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ yinnɛ (1891) paae tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ anii ni la (1898), da an captain kanɛ gaad o taaba, da gaad Villa tuon ka ba di ya'an di'ema nama anu ni nɛ FA Cup nama ayi kilab la pin'ilig saŋa la.
english: John Devey who was captain from 1891 to 1898, is their most successful captain, leading Villa to five league titles and two FA Cup triumphs during the club's "Golden Age".

kusaal: Onɛ an captain nannanna anɛ onɛ yit Scotland ka o yʋ'ʋr buon John McGinn.
english: The present captain is Scotland international John McGinn.

kusaal: Tuongatib bama da di ya'an piini yinnɛ bɛɛ babik ban da bɛ tʋʋma ni la ka Villa dim mi' ba yela League la pʋʋgin, Nid yinnɛ anɛ Jozef Vengloš onɛ da kɛ ka ba di ya'an.
english: The following managers have all won at least one trophy when in charge or have been notable for Villa in the context of the League, for example Jozef Vengloš who holds a League record.

kusaal: Gbambʋʋg la ka ba da pin'il 1874, zab nɛ Premier League, solemiine tita'ar la zu'oe.
english: Founded in 1874, it competes in the Premier League, the top tier of English football, and has played at its home ground, Villa Park, since 1897.

kusaal: Tiim la di'emnɛ ba yaan, Villa Park, din yi 1897.
english: Founded in 1874, it competes in the Premier League, the top tier of English football, and has played at its home ground, Villa Park, since 1897.

kusaal: Aston Villa anɛ kpɛɛmnam nɛ banɛ nyaŋid bɛ England la yinne, ka di nwɛnɛ Boole Diction yiiga diib ayɔpɔi, FA kupi la nɔɔnɛ nɔɔra ayɔpɔi, nɛ European Cup nɛ European Cup yimmʋ.
english: Aston Villa is one of the oldest and most successful clubs in England, having won the Football League First Division seven times, the FA Cup seven times, the League Cup five times, as well as the European Cup, European Super Cup, and Europa League once.

kusaal: A-nwɛn'ɛtɔlis taaba giŋa-giŋa baŋir da pin'ili yinɛ daʋ kanɛ yit Scotland George Ramsay, onɛ ka ba da gaŋ o ka o an dunia wʋsa football kilab yiiga tuongat yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1886).
english: This short, slick combination passing style was introduced by Scotsman George Ramsay, who was appointed as the world's first professional football manager in 1886.

kusaal: Kilab la da tʋmtʋʋma nɛ bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ anu (1885), ka li da anɛ Villa director, William McGregor, da gaad tuoni gɔs dunia wʋsa yiiga Football League yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ anii ni (1888).
english: The club was influential in the sport's move to professionalism in 1885, and it was a Villa director, William McGregor, who founded the world's first Football League in 1888.

kusaal: Banɛ da paas English kilab nama anaasi ni da di European Cup, bɛ 1981–82, nɛ European Super Cup bɛ 1982.
english: They became only the fourth English club to win the European Cup, in 1981–82, followed by the European Super Cup in 1982.

kusaal: Aston Villa da paasi pin'il Premier League bɛ 1992, ba da paasi ba taaba atan' banɛ da pin'il Football League nɛ Premier League la.
english: Aston Villa were a founding member of the Premier League in 1992, one of just three clubs to have been a founding member of both the Football League and the Premier League.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai saŋa lanɛ yʋʋm tusayi saŋa, Villa da kɛn tuoni nwɛ'ɛd European football, amaa ka Martin O'Neill da gaad la ka kilab la da lɛb nya'aŋ ka da lɛb relegation Premier League ni 2015–16.
english: Throughout the 1990s and early 2000s, Villa regularly qualified for European football, but following a period of decline after the departure of Martin O'Neill the club suffered its only relegation from the Premier League in 2015–16.

kusaal: Ban di'em yʋma atan' bɛ EFL Championship ka mɛ ti'as tuongatiba ayi nya'aŋ la, kilab la da lɛb Premier League yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai ni (2019).
english: After three seasons in the EFL Championship and two ownership changes, the club returned to the Premier League in 2019.

kusaal: Aston Villa yʋ'ʋn anɛ abʋnu English di'ema pʋʋgin, lin da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ anii saŋ la sa (1888) ka an kilab kanɛ paas ayɔpɔi bɛ English football ni nya'a di ya'an.
english: Aston Villa is ranked fifth in the all-time English top flight table since its creation in 1888, and is the seventh most successful club in English football by competitive honours.

kusaal: Ba mɛ lɛn mɔr dataalig nɛ West Bromwich Albion, ka di'em banɛ ka ba di'emid nidib pʋdi ba ye West Midlands derby.
english: There is also a local rivalry with West Bromwich Albion, with matches between the sides known as the West Midlands derby.

kusaal: Kilab la fuud colours anɛ wiig nɛ dɛn'ɛm, kurug giŋ pi'el nɛ socks banɛ an dɛ'ɛm wʋʋ sangbaŋ nɛ.
english: The club's traditional kit colours are claret shirts with sky blue sleeves, white shorts and sky blue socks.

kusaal: Banɛ sʋ'ʋe kilab la nannanna anɛ V Sports, tʋʋmkanɛ an Egypt dim ligid daan Nassef Sawiris, America ligid daan Wes Edens, nɛ America da'adiib tʋʋma kanɛ buon Atairos.
english: The club is currently owned by V Sports, a company owned by the Egyptian billionaire Nassef Sawiris, the American billionaire Wes Edens, and American investment company Atairos.

kusaal: Di'ema la pʋʋgin, Villa dim da di'em nɛ dɔlis Rugby dim wada ka nyaan kɛŋ vʋ'ʋs ka ban da vʋ'ʋsi lɛb na la ka dɔlis Association la wada.
english: As a condition of the match, the Villa side had to agree to play the first half under Rugby rules and the second half under Association rules.

kusaal: Di'ema la da naae la, Villa nwɛ'ɛ-nwɛ'ɛdib da la'asi gilig o ka buol o ye o paasi ba an ba captain.
english: Villa's captain during this era was Birmingham-born forward John Devey, who enjoyed a successful partnership with the lightning-fast winger Charlie Athersmith and marshalling Villa's defence was the tough-tackling Scotsman James Cowan, who had an unrivalled sense of timing and anticipation.

kusaal: 'Bɔɔdi sɔ': Aston Villa dim Football Club kpɛɛm iɛɛdi onɛ na nyaŋi pɛsigi o mɛŋi pa'al nwɛ'dib la tituaa.
english: 'Wanted: manager for Aston Villa Football Club, who will be required to devote his whole time under direction of the committee.

kusaal: Din yi saŋkan la Aston Villa da tuon hali dunia nwa' ni ka an yiiga bɛ Midlands teamla ni ka di ya'an ni bɛ FA Cup bɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbis nii nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpoi bɛ1887 la ni.
english: During the following season Aston Villa rose to national prominence, as the first Midlands team to win the FA Cup in 1887.

kusaal: Villa tuoni gaadʋg, powerful Scottish centre-forward Archie Hunter yʋ'on da anɛ yir la yiiga yʋ'ʋr, ba da an yiiga dim banɛ di goal la yiiga ba nwɛ'ɛd FA Cupsaŋa wʋsa.
english: Villa's captain, the powerful Scottish centre-forward Archie Hunter, became one of the game's first household names, being the first player to score in every round of the FA Cup.

kusaal: Aston Villa da anɛ team yinne kanɛ pɛɛs team nam bɛdigʋ ni da keŋ nwɛ' zʋŋir nwɛ'ɛb dinɛ anɛ inaugural Football League bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis nii nɛ pisnii nɛ anii 1888 la ni pɛɛs nɛ ba clab la pa'an-pa'an yinne, William McGregor onɛ da sin'iŋ league la.
english: Aston Villa were one of the dozen teams that competed in the inaugural Football League in 1888 with one of the club's directors, William McGregor being the league's founder.

kusaal: saŋa wʋsa zuod friendlies la daa san'amnɛ ka di dɔlisnɛ ban da ɛɛnti nwɛ'ɛdi geesid taaba FA Cup bɛɛ county cup matches bɛɛ clubs da pʋ ka ba paam zugsʋŋɔ la'am nɛ ba nwɛ'ɛb la da an sʋm la wʋsa bab ka ni wʋsa ka keŋi nwɛ'.
english: Frequently friendlies were cancelled due to opponents' FA Cup or county cup matches or clubs simply failed to honour a fixture in favour of a more lucrative match elsewhere.

kusaal: McGregor da nyɛ' ka ba kad Villa matches la bas ka ba nwɛ'ɛd-nwɛ'ɛdib yʋ'ʋm namis la o da nɔk sɔŋkpi'em bɛ Asibiddaar nami anu la ni.
english: McGregor took action after seeing Villa matches cancelled, to the increasing frustration of the club's fans, on five consecutive Saturdays.

kusaal: George Ramsay da bas boolwɛ'ɛb nɛ bɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyi nɛ ayuobu (1926) la ni, ka mɔr yʋma pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayinne la'am nɛ on da nɔk Billy Smith lɛdig la wʋsa o da pʋ nyaŋi keŋ wʋʋ on da kn tuon siem laa, di an sida mɛŋa football clubs da kena yʋ'ʋm pʋm nwɛ'ɛdi gat Aston Villa, kaskas anɛ Arsenal, banɛ da pʋ nyaŋi keŋ tuon ya'as bɛ league yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan'(1930) kɛm paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ ayinne (1931) nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ ayi (1932) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ atan' (1933) la.
english: George Ramsay retired in 1926, at the age of 71, and his replacement Billy Smith was unable to continue Ramsay's success.

kusaal: La'am nɛ bam da pʋ nya'ŋi di ya'an la, wʋrʋg la da bɛ Villa Park la ni da mɔri nɔŋgbanwa'ar nɛ boolwɛ'ɛb yɛl, goals banɛ ka ba da di kɔbiga nɛ pisyi nɛ anii la bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' (1930) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' ayinne (1931) an dinɛ ka sɔ'ɔ nam pʋ nyaŋi dii tʋʋg wala hali ti kɛna paae zina.
english: Despite missing out on the league title, Villa Park crowds were entertained by attacking football; the 128 goals scored in the 1930–31 season remains the all-time top-flight record.

kusaal: Ka saansa ayi ma'aa ka Hogan da nyaŋi sʋŋi pa'al Villa tituaa ka ba keŋ tuon yʋ'ʋm pɛɛs banɛ nwɛ'ɛd bool sʋŋa la ba ayi ni Second Division champions k aba yʋ'ʋm kpɛm boola tituaa yim.
english: Within two seasons, Hogan had guided Villa back to the top flight as Second Division champions playing attractive free-flowing football.

kusaal: Ka di nar yee ba nwɛ'ɛdi tisid taaba saŋa wʋsa ka kɛn tuon (One-two-three, one-two-three, pass-move-pass, pass-move-pas.") amaa, Second World War da naae la ka Hogan's pʋtɛn'ɛr kanɛ ka o da mɔr ye o ke ka Aston Villa yaŋ di ya'aŋ bɛ English game la ni da pʋ nyaŋi tʋmm.
english: One-two-three, one-two-three, pass-move-pass, pass-move-pass." However, the Second World War ended Hogan's project to restore Aston Villa to the top of the English game.

kusaal: Nwɛni English clubs nam ɛɛnti pʋn lut siem la, Villa mɛ da gʋ'ʋŋ bɛ Second World War la ka di da ke ka sielnam bɛdigʋ sa'am ba bɛlim pʋʋgin.
english: Like all English clubs, Villa lost seven seasons to the Second World War, and that conflict brought several careers to a premature end.

kusaal: Alex Massie onɛ an ba nwɛ'ɛd kudug la da sʋŋi zamis ka kpa'al li ba titua din nar siem bɛ yʋʋm tusa kɔbiswai nɛ pisnasi (1940s) saŋa la.
english: The team was rebuilt under the guidance of former player Alex Massie for the remainder of the 1940s.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi (1954) la ni, Danny Blanchflower da bɔɔd ye ba nɔk o tɔɔm tɛŋ o da ye "club la nɔbignɛ mɔr kpaam ka gbanya'am mɔri banɛ ban na lɛbi sin'iŋ ban da maan siel la ka li kɛ ka ɛɛnnbir pʋoɛe san'amid".
english: When Danny Blanchflower submitted a transfer request in 1954 he said that "the club had grown fat and lazy on its old traditions and the decay was eating at the once solid foundations".

kusaal: Ka ban da nɔk Derek Dougan nytdig la di da pʋ sʋŋi ba Villa lɛb nya'aŋ.
english: He was sold for £85,000 in summer of 1961, his replacement, Derek Dougan was not a success and Villa slid backwards.

kusaal: Onɛ da kɛna di'e o nɔbir anɛ Birmingham manager kudug kanɛ buon Steve Bruce.
english: He was replaced by former Birmingham manager Steve Bruce.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, Mɔraug nwadig la, dabpisi daar (20 July 2018) labaar da yina ye NSWE Group, tʋʋma kanɛ an Egypt tɛŋ ligid daan kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Nassef Sawiris nɛ America ligid daan kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Wes Edens din la, da si'ak ye ba kpɛn'ɛsi ba ligidi bɔɔl kilab la ni.
english: On 20 July 2018 it was announced that the NSWE Group, a consortium consisting of Egyptian billionaire Nassef Sawiris and the American billionaire Wes Edens, were to invest in the football club.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, Sawaar nwadig la ni (October 2018), ba da yis Bruce on da gaad tuon ka ba nwɛ'ɛ bɔɔl nɔɔra awai ka di ya'an nɔɔra ayinnɛ ma'a la yela.
english: In October 2018, Bruce was dismissed after winning only once in a nine match stretch.

kusaal: Ba da paae 2019 EFL Championship play-off final ka da di Derby County 2–1 ka da paam suori kpɛn'ɛ Premier League ni ya'as, ban da pʋ nyaŋi paasɛ yʋma atan' pʋʋgin nya'aŋ la.
english: They reached the 2019 EFL Championship play-off final and defeated Derby County 2–1 to gain promotion back to the Premier League after a three-year absence.

kusaal: Ba da lɛb nya'aŋi bɛ relegation ni season nam bɛdigʋ ni, amaa ka li naarin la ka ba da paas nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi zin'igin.
english: The team battled relegation for most of the season, but stayed up on the final day with a 17th-place finish.

kusaal: Aston Villa da gaad tuoni ia banɛ na sʋŋi ba fuud la yela bɛ 2008–09 nɛ 2009–10 season nam; ka da pin'ad asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ lugir kanɛ ka ba buon Acorns Children's Hospice yela, banɛ da an yiiga ba Premier League bɛilim pʋʋgin.
english: Aston Villa forwent commercial kit sponsorship for the 2008–09 and 2009–10 seasons; instead advertising the charity Acorns Children's Hospice, the first deal of its kind in Premier League history.

kusaal: Nɔnaalig nwa da kɛŋ tuoni paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga ni (2010) anina ka lugir si'a da di'e Acorns nɔbir, ka hospice kilim kilab la sʋŋid.
english: The partnership continued until 2010 when a commercial sponsor replaced Acorns, with the hospice becoming the club's Official Charity Partner.

kusaal: Ba da maal fuug kanɛ mɔr nu'us yiiga nɛ 2019–20 season ni ka pa'an BR88s.
english: A shirt sleeve sponsor was used for the first time in the 2019–20 season with BR88 being displayed.

kusaal: Villa Park anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb zin'ig kanɛ yalim hali bɛ English Midlands sʋ'ʋlim, ka paasa anii daani zuoe gaad o taaba bɛ England.
english: Villa Park is the largest football stadium in the English Midlands, and the eighth largest stadium in England.

kusaal: Villa Park anɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka ba di'emid anina tita'am FA Cup semi-final pin'ilig sa paae zina, di'emanam pisnu nɛ anu, 55 semi-finals nam.
english: Villa Park is the most used stadium in FA Cup semi-final history, having hosted 55 semi-finals.

kusaal: Ba da yis labaar yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi, kusanwadis anii, daba yuobʋ daar (6 August 2014), ye Villa Park da yi FIFA video game ni na bɛ FIFA 15, ka Premier League stadiums banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa mɛ da bas suor ye ba paas di'emkan ni mɛn.
english: It was announced on 6 August 2014, that Villa Park would appear in the FIFA video game from FIFA 15, with all other Premier League stadiums also fully licensed from this game onwards.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili bas suor ka nidib paam suori paasi sʋ'ʋe club la bɛ 19th century naar saŋa ka li yina wada kanɛ da kɛna ye li la'as nwɛ'ɛ-nwɛ'ɛdib nɛ teams nam banɛ bɛ Association Football leagues ni la.
english: The first shares in the club were issued towards the end of the 19th century as a result of legislation that was intended to codify the growing numbers of professional teams and players in the Association Football leagues.

kusaal: Da' diib nwa tɔlis ala paae 20th century sankanɛ ka Ellis da pin'ili da'ad faar la bɛdigʋ bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ saŋa (1960s) la.
english: This trading continued for much of the 20th century until Ellis started buying up many of the shares in the 1960s.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ ni (2006), ba da yis labaar na ye tʋʋma zin'is bɛdigʋ nɛ Nidib bɛdigʋ bɔɔd ye ba da Aston Villa.
english: On 14 August 2006, it was confirmed that Randy Lerner, then owner of the National Football League's Cleveland Browns, had reached an agreement of £62.6 million with Aston Villa for a takeover of the club.

kusaal: Lerner da pin'ili sʋ'ʋe nɛ kusanwadis piinɛ nii, dabpiinɛ nii daar (18 September) nɛ Ellis ka o kpɛɛmnam la mɛ da gaad ka Lerner bɔ kpɛɛm paala kusanwadis piinɛ nii, dabpiinɛ awai, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ (19 September 2006).
english: Lerner took full control on 18 September with Ellis and his board replaced with a new board by Lerner on 19 September 2006.

kusaal: Ba da naae kuosig la gbana nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ, kusanwadis anu, piinɛ anaasi daar (14 June 2016) ka ligidi la da an £76 million, Football League la da bas suor la nya'aŋ.
english: The sale was completed on 14 June 2016 for a reported £76 million, after being approved by the Football League.

kusaal: Ban da da'a la'ad bɛdigʋ ka mɛ pʋ lɛn nyaŋi kɛŋ Premier League pʋʋginɛ 2017–18 Championship final, ka ligidi yela yʋ'ʋn muki ba.
english: After a period of high expenditure and failing to secure promotion to the Premier League in the 2017–18 Championship playoff final, financial difficulties at the club began to mount.

kusaal: Ba da tisid labaya ye Villa mɔr sama ka pʋ nyaŋi yɔ la, Xia da pin'ili ied suoya ye o kuos club la yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, kusanwadis anu ni (June 2018).
english: Amid rumours that Villa risked entering administration, Xia entered talks to sell the club in June 2018.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, kusanwadis ayuobʋ, dabpisi daar (20 July 2018), ba da yis labaar ye V Sports (sankan li da anɛ NSWE Group), tʋʋma zin'ig kanɛ ka Egypt dim dau kanɛ an ligid daan ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Nassef Sawiris nɛ America nid kanɛ an ligid daan ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Wes Edens, da ye ba kpɛn'ɛs ligidi bɔɔl kilab la ni.
english: On 20 July 2018, it was announced that V Sports (at the time known as NSWE Group), a consortium consisting of Egyptian billionaire Nassef Sawiris and the American billionaire Wes Edens, were to invest in the football club.

kusaal: Ba da da' kilab la sʋ'ʋd pisnu nɛ nu, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (55%), ka Sawiris da di'e an kilab la chairman.
english: They purchased a controlling 55% stake in the club, and Sawiris took over the role of club chairman.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan', samanpiid nwadig, dabpiinɛ nu daar (15 December 2023), Aston Villa da yis labaar ye America tʋmtʋmnib zin'ig kanɛ ka ba buon Atairos la na kpɛn'ɛs ligidi V Sports, kilab la sʋ'ʋe tʋʋma zin'ig si'a la.
english: On 15 December 2023, Aston Villa announced that Comcast-backed American investment firm Atairos would invest in V Sports, the ultimate parent company of the club.

kusaal: Aston Villa mɔr nɔnaalig nɛ Acorns Children's Hospice lugur kanɛ sʋŋid bɔɔl yela banɛ tʋm tʋʋma English bɔɔl ni.
english: Aston Villa has a unique relationship with the Acorns Children's Hospice charity that is groundbreaking in English football.

kusaal: Ba yiiga Premier League, Aston Villa da sʋŋ nɛ ba fuud la tuon zanbina la maalig, banɛ maan ala pa'al ye ba yɔ ligid tita'ar, tis Acorns Hospice lin na niŋ si'em ka lugur kan dim yʋ'ʋr yi ka ba mɛ paam ligidi.
english: In a first for the Premier League, Aston Villa donated the front of its kit shirts, usually reserved for high-paying sponsorships, to Acorns Hospice so that the charity would gain significant additional visibility and more funds.

kusaal: Kilab la da yɔ'ɔg diib zin'igi bɛ Trinity Road Stand ka nɔk biis piinɛyi banɛ pʋ lal la wʋʋ 10-mile (16 km) nɛ Villa Park ka diib banɛ ka ba kuosid anina la da an ba tɛŋ la diib.
english: The club opened a restaurant in the Trinity Road Stand staffed with twelve students recruited from within a ten-mile (16 km) radius of Villa Park, with most of the food served in the restaurant sourced locally.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ ni (2016), Aston Villa da mɔr gbaŋ ye ba maal sʋŋir lugir, ka li yʋ'ʋr an Aston Villa Foundation.
english: In 2016, Aston Villa created a registered charity, the Aston Villa Foundation.

kusaal: Aston Villa Football Club di'e European nɛ ba mɛŋ tɛŋin league nam piini.
english: Aston Villa have won both European and domestic league honours.

kusaal: Kilab la piini kanɛ ba da di'e yi English ni da anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ ni (1996) sankan ka ba da di'e League Cup la, ba daa lɛn di'e 2001 UEFA Intertoto Cup.
english: The club's last English honour was in 1996 when they won the League Cup, and most recently they won the 2025–26 UEFA Europa League.

kusaal: Kilab la pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi ni (1874) paae zina, Nwɛ'ɛ-nwɛ'ɛdib pisnaasi nɛ atan' kɛna an captain tis Aston Villa.
english: Since the foundation of the club in 1874, forty-five players have been club captain of Aston Villa.

kusaal: Asunafo North Constituency anɛ constituency banɛ bɛ Parliament of Ghana la yinne ka mɛ paas nɛ constituency nam ayuobʋ banɛ bɛ Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Asunafo North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana and also one of the six constituencies in the Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ anaasi, kɔbis yuobu nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (34,684) ka din zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ ayi' du'al pisi nɛ yinne', kɔbiga pʋʋgin (52.21%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin, ka o di ya'an ka bas Mohammed Haruna onɛ da zi'en Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug la.
english: Winning the election with a total of 34,684 votes (52.21%) of the total votes cast beating his rival Mohammed Haruna of the National Democratic Party (NDC).

kusaal: Constituency la da pin'ilnɛ bɛ Brong-Ahafo Region, ka nannanna ka li yʋ'ʋn bɛ Ahafo Region dinɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: This constituency was originally located in the Brong-Ahafo Region, now in the Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Evans Opoku Bobie ka ba da vɔɔti gaŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋg la ni ka o an wadmaani tis constituency la, o da zi'enɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug.
english: Evans Opoku Bobie was voted and elected in the 2020 general election as the Member of Parliament for the constituency form the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Asunafo North constituency da paas constituency banɛ ka ba da maali ba yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' vɔɔtʋg yʋʋm la ni.
english: The Asunafo North constituency was one of the constituencies created prior to the 1992 Ghanaian parliamentary election.

kusaal: Eric Opoku an wadmaan nananna tis constituency la.
english: Eric Opoku is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlim, Republic of Ghana ni.
english: The constituency is located in the Ahafo Region of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ an wadmaan constituency la ni nananna anɛ Patrick Banor.
english: Ebenezer Kwaku Addo is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: O da zi'eni nya'a na'am lanɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug ka nidib bɛdegʋ da vɔɔti gaŋ o ka o paam vɔɔt wʋʋ tusa piinɛ anii, kɔbisnu nɛ anu (18,505).
english: He was elected on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress and won a majority of 18,584 votes.

kusaal: Asutifi South constituency bɛnɛ Asutifi Districti bɛ Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Asutifi South is located in the Asutifi District of the Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk bɛnɛ Asutifi district pʋʋgin, linɛ bɛ Ahafo Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Asutifi district of the Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Philip Kofi Adjapong Amoah, onɛ da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug ka da maal ka'alim la, da kɛ ka ba tɔlis vɔɔtʋg la constituency kan ni,ka ba da vɔɔt yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ yinne, yʋʋmpaal nwadig daba atan' daar (3 January 2001).
english: Due to the death of Philip Kofi Adjapong Amoah, (NPP) candidate standing for parliament, the elections in this constituency were postponed to 3 January 2001.

kusaal: Cecilia Djan Amoah, onɛ da an o pʋkɔɔnr la da di'e o sid nɔbiri zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni, ka da di ya'ani gaad o taaba wʋʋ vɔɔt kɔbisnu nɛ pisnu nɛ anu.
english: Cecilia Djan Amoah, the (NPP) replacement candidate and also the widow of the deceased, won the seat with a majority of 550.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka o aan wadmaan zi'eni tisi ba.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Diib nɛ zʋkuosa da bɛ la zug , dinzug Europe dim la da zabid nɛ taaba onɛ na gaad tuoni gɔs Gold Coast la'abanɛ ka ba da mɔr la, ka yʋʋm 1874 la, Biritish dim la da paam ikku bɛ Gold Coast dim la'ad la bam ni, la,anɛ Portugal dim la da la'am dɛŋi ba ka zin'in Elmina teŋ kanɛ bɛ Gold Coast yʋʋm 1482 la ni, British dim la da mɔr ikku la zugɔɔ, ba yʋ'ʋn da pʋd Gold Coast nɛ ye British Gold Coast.
english: In 1874, the British took control over parts of Gold Coast although the Portuguese were the first to settle at Elmina in the Gold Coast in 1482.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah la da di, dinzugɔɔ onɛ da an Gold Coast dim tuongat yʋʋm 1952 la ni, o da pʋn dɛŋim dinɛ wadmaanib kpɛɛm yʋʋm 1951 sa, ka nimbɛda ayuobʋ sieba da sʋŋ o.
english: Osagyefo in 1952, Dr. Kwame Nkrumah won the election to lead the Gold Coast administration after he won the Gold Coast legislative election in 1951.

kusaal: Asʋ'ʋ-m-mɛŋ dabisir anɛ dabiskanɛ an di'ema nɛ vʋ'ʋsʋm daari tis Ghana wʋsa yʋʋm wʋsa.
english: The Independence Day of Ghana is a national holiday celebrated yearly.

kusaal: Daakan anɛ vʋ'ʋsʋm daar tis Ghana nid wʋsa banɛ bɛ Ghana nɛ banɛ ka' Ghana ye ba na'as tuongatib banɛ da kɛ ka Ghana paam yɔlisim la.
english: This day is an official state holiday for the citizens of Ghana both within and in the diaspora to honour and celebrate the heroes of Ghana who led the country to attain its independence.

kusaal: Onɛ da an yiiga Piram minista da anɛ Kwame Nkrumah, onɛ da an Ghaana gɔmma kpɛɛm din yi yʋʋm tusa piine awai n paa yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: On Wednesday, 6 March 1957, Kwame Nkrumah declared to the people of Ghana about their freedom, he added that, "the African People are capable of managing their own affairs and Ghana our beloved country is free forever." Ghana was the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to achieve its independence from European colonial rule.

kusaal: Nwadis atan' la ni li daba ayuobʋ daar la, Kwame Nkrumah da yɛl nyain tis Ghana dim ye, ba paam yɔlisim ka lɛn ye, Afirikadim na nyaŋi mɔri ba mɛŋ tituaa.
english: Many presidents from other African countries and Europe have been invited to Ghana to join in the celebration either as guest speakers or invited guests, since the reign of former President Kwame Nkrumah till now.

kusaal: Ghana da an tɛŋkanɛ da bɛ Sub-Sahara Afirica paami o yɔlisim yiiga yi Na'asaanam nu'usin.
english: Ghana, formerly known as the Gold Coast, had many natural resources categorized into two as minerals and forest resources.

kusaal: Pirɛsidɛnnam bɛdigʋ banɛ bɛ Afirika tɛɛns ne Europe tɛɛns la, Ghana ɛɛnti kaanbi buoliba ye ba kena ka ba la'asi di'em ka li malis.
english: Many presidents from other African countries and Europe have been invited to Ghana to join in the celebration either as guest speakers or invited guests, since the reign of former President Kwame Nkrumah till now.

kusaal: Gold Coast dim da paamɛ asʋ'ʋ-m-mɛŋ paŋ la nɛ yi British dim san'nɛ yʋʋm 1957 nwadisa atan' la li daba ayuobʋ daar, ka ba yʋ'ʋn tiaki buon Gold Coast ye Ghana.
english: Led by Kwame Nkrumah and the Convention People's Party (CPP), the Gold Coast declared its independence from the British on Wednesday, 6 March 1957.

kusaal: Dunia wʋsa sɔb wada ISO 8601 pa'al ye, Atɛni daari an bakwai pin'ilig dabisir; ka Atalata paas dabisa ayi bakwai pʋʋgin.
english: According to international standard ISO 8601, Monday is the first day of the week; thus, Tuesday is the second day of the week.

kusaal: Di na'asaal yʋ'ʋr la yinɛ Middle English Tewesday, ka Old English mɛ an Tiwesdæg, di gbin anɛ "Tīw's Dabisir", Tiw bɛɛ Týr dabisir, ba ba'ar kanɛ gɔsid zaba, wada, nɛ sida sarikadib bɛ ba sɔlima banɛ pa'ani ba bada nami da an si'em la ni.
english: The English name is derived from Middle English Tewesday, from Old English Tiwesdæg meaning "Tīw's Day", the day of Tiw or Týr, the god of single combat, law, and justice in Norse mythology.

kusaal: Atalata daar bɛɛ Tuesday yinɛ Old English Tiwesdæg ni ka di gbin an "Tiw Dabisir".
english: The name Tuesday derives from the Old English Tiwesdæg and literally means "Tiw's Day".

kusaal: *Tîwaz yinɛ sɔb kanɛ an *dei-, *deyā-, *dīdyā-, ka di gbin an 'ni'e nyain', ani ka sɔb kanɛ an "wina" mɛ yina.
english: *Tîwaz derives from the Proto-Indo-European base *dei-, *deyā-, *dīdyā-, meaning 'to shine', whence come such words as "deity".

kusaal: Indo-Aryan bʋʋdi pian'ad Pali nɛ Sanskrit, ba nyɛ dabisir la yʋ'ʋr nɛ yi Angaraka ('one an wiig'), style (suor pa'alig) tis Mangala, one an zaba ba'ar, nɛ Mars, planet kanɛ an wiig la.
english: In the Indo-Aryan languages Pali and Sanskrit the name of the day is taken from Angaraka ('one who is red in colour'), a style (manner of address) for Mangala, the god of war, and for Mars, the red planet.

kusaal: Hinduism wina pʋ'ʋsim ni, Atalata daar anɛ dabisir kanɛ ka ba zʋn'ɔd ka pʋ'ʋsid Hanuman ka si'eba mɛ zʋn'ɔd Kartikeya, Kali, Durga, Parvati, nɛ Ganesha.
english: In Hinduism, Tuesday is a popular day for worshipping and praying to Hanuman and Kartikeya, some also worship Kali, Durga, Parvati, and Ganesha.

kusaal: Hindus pʋ'ʋsim dim bɛdigʋ lɔɔd nɔɔr Atalata daar.
english: Many Hindus fast during Tuesday.

kusaal: Hindu pʋ'ab banɛ mɔr sidib maan maliŋ kanɛ buon Mangala Gauri Vrat ka an nɔlɔɔr la, Atalata daar wʋsa, ba nwadig kanɛ buon Shravana la ni, nwadig kan anɛ ba wina Gauri nɛ Shiva nwadis.
english: Many Hindu married women also observe the Mangala Gauri Vrat of fasting every Tuesday in the Hindu month of Shravana, as the month is dedicated to Gauri and Shiva.

kusaal: Greek dim tɛŋin, Atalata daar (the day of the week of the Fall of Constantinople) anɛ zutoog dabisir.
english: In the Greek world, Tuesday (the day of the week of the Fall of Constantinople) is considered an unlucky day.

kusaal: Tiw da anɛ ba zaba paŋ bada nam la pʋʋgin, ka ba nɔki pʋd dabisir la yinɛ latin yʋ'ʋr dies Martis ni.
english: Tiw was equated with Mars in the interpretatio germanica, and the name of the day is a translation of Latin dies Martis.

kusaal: Ba malima ya'a naae Atalata daar la, ba na yel ye: "Kiristo one an Wina'am asida la, dɔlisid o ma kanɛ an kasi la ni, nɛ nɔdi'es kanɛ mɔr girima, one gaad tuon nɛ John one sʋʋd nidib wina'am kuom la…" ka nyaan kul.
english: At the end of Divine Services on Tuesday, the dismissal begins with the words: "May Christ our True God, through the intercessions of his most-pure Mother, of the honorable and glorious Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John…"

kusaal: Atalata daar anɛ dabisir kanɛ an Mangala (Mars) din, banɛ pʋ'ʋsid Hinduism la ni.
english: Tuesday is also viewed as the day ruled by Mangala (Mars) in Hinduism.

kusaal: Judaism winpʋ'ʋsim dim ni, Atalata daar anɛ zusuŋ dabisir, bɔzugɔ, Bereshit (parashah), ka Kiristo biis malima ni an Genesis gbaʋŋ pin'ilig la, di sɔb anina ye "di da an sum" abʋyi'.
english: In Judaism, on the other hand, Tuesday is considered a particularly lucky day, because in Bereshit (parashah), known in the Christian tradition as the first chapters of Genesis, the paragraph about this day contains the phrase "it was good" twice.

kusaal: Gbana banɛ pa'an dabisa la ni, Alasid daari an bakwai pin'ilig dabisir, ka di pa'al ye Atalata daar paas nɛ dabisa atan' bakwai pʋʋgin.
english: According to many traditional calendars, however, Sunday is the first day of the week, so Tuesday is the third day of the week.

kusaal: Atebubu-Amantin Constituency anɛ linɛ bɛ Atebubu-Amantin district ka ba da buon ye Atebubu district yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la (2003).
english: Atebubu-Amantin constituency of the Atebubu-Amantin district formerly the Atebubu district in 2003.

kusaal: Atebubu-Amantin district da maal nɛ dɔlisid wada, LI 1770.
english: The Atebubu-Amantin district was formed by the legislative instrument LI 1770.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Bono East Region, linɛ paas zin'ikanɛ ka ba da buon ye Brong Ahafo region la, Ghana.
english: The constituency can be found in the Bono East region, which was part of the former Brong Ahafo region of Ghana.

kusaal: Emmanuel Owusu-Mainu da an wadmaani tis constituency la lin da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan' la ni la (2003).
english: Emmanuel Owusu-Mainu was the member of parliament for the constituency after its creation in 2003.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o nɔɔr ayi', yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi (2004) nɛ yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ anii la (2008) wadmaannib vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: He was elected twice in the 2004 and 2008 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: Linzug ka o da zi'en constituency la nɔba zugʋ aan li wadmaan 4th nɛ 5th parliaments of the 4th republic of Ghana.
english: As a result, he represented the constituency as its member of parliament in the 4th and 5th parliaments of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Sanja Nanja da di'e Emmanuel Owusu-Mainu nɔbir yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayi' vɔɔtʋg la ni, ka da zi'enɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress mɛn, 5th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana saŋa da paae la.
english: Sanja Nanja succeeded Emmanuel Owusu-Mainu in the 2012 parliamentary elections also on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress after the dissolution of the 5th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Kofi Amoakohene onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la da di'e na'am la yi Sanja Nanja san'an yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la ni, 6th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.
english: Kofi Amoakohene of the New Patriotic Party succeeded Sanja Nanja in the 2016 parliamentary elections after the dissolution of the 6th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Din pa'al ye o da zi'en Atebubu-Amantin nidib nɔba zugʋ an wadmaani paas 7th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.
english: He thus represented Atebubu-Amantin constituents as their member of parliament in the 7th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) nɔba zug.
english: This was on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Linzugɔ, o da zi'en constituency la nɔba zugʋ an wadmaani paas 6th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.
english: He therefore represented the constituency as the member of parliament in the 6th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii vɔɔtʋgin la ka o da di gaadi o taaba la nɛ vɔɔt tusa atan' nɛ kɔbistan' nɛ piswai nɛ anu (3,395).
english: In the 2008 parliamentary elections he won by a majority of 3,395 votes.

kusaal: Ba da la'asi pʋr bakɔi la dabisa yʋda nɛ Roman saŋa la, ka Greek nɛ Latin pian'ad ni ka ba buon Atinɛ daar ye ἡμέρᾱ Σελήνης, diēs Lūnae.
english: ἡμέρᾱ Σελήνης, diēs Lūnae "day of the Moon".

kusaal: Buudi pian'ad bɛdegʋ ni ba sieba pʋdi ba dabisa yʋda ka li yinɛ yʋ'ʋbama ni bɛɛb pɛ'ɛŋi yi pian'asieba lɛbigidin.
english: Many languages use either terms directly derived from these names or loan translations based on them.

kusaal: Abena Osei Asare an wadmaan nannanna n bɛ Atiwa East constituency la.
english: Abena Osei Asare the current MP for the Atiwa East constituency.

kusaal: Atiwa East Constituency sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ paasi ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni mɛn.
english: Atiwa East is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Atiwa West constituency bɛnɛ Atiwa district bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana.
english: The Atiwa West constituency is located in the Atiwa District of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: kuk la bɛ nɛ Atiwa district bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Atiwa District of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaan zi'eni tisi ba, onɛ paa vɔɔti gaadi o taaba la wʋsa.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Din da paad yʋʋm tusa nɛ pisi (2020) wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la, wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) da maali ba vɔɔtʋg ye ba gaansi ba wadmaan na'anya'adib ka ba zi'en na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug.
english: Building up to the 2020 parliamentary elections, the New Patriotic Party (NPP) organized its parliamentary primaries to elect a candidate to represent the party.

kusaal: Ato Panford da paas banɛ nya'ad la ni ka pʋ diika onɛ nya' nɛ o la, Lawyer Samuel Erickson Abakah da di ka keŋ tuoni di vɔɔt la mɛŋ.
english: Ato Panford participated but lost to his contender Lawyer Samuel Erickson Abakah who later won in the general elections.

kusaal: Ato Panford anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da paas Ghana wadmaanib yir Linɛ paas ayɔpɔi li Republic kanɛ aan anaasi la, o da zi'eni tis Constituency.org Shama Constituency kanɛ bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim la wabʋg na'adɔɔg nɔba zug.
english: Ato Panford (born on 28 August 1962) was a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana who represented the Shama Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Atwima-Kwanwoma constituency bɛnɛ Botsomtwe/Atwima/Kwanhuma district linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Atwima-Kwanwoma is located in the Botsomtwe/Atwima/Kwanhuma district of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk bɛnɛ Botsomtwe/Atwima/Kwanhuma District linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la pʋʋgin, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The seat is located within the Botsomtwe/Atwima/Kwanhuma District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋi nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaan zi'eni ba nɔba zug.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Atwima-Mponua constituency bɛnɛ Atwima Mponua district dinɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Atwima-Mponua is located in the Atwima Mponua district of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk bɛnɛ Atwima Mponua District pʋʋgin linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: The seat is located within the Atwima Mponua District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Atwima-Nwabiagya North bɛnɛ Atwima Nwabiagya District linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Atwima-Nwabiagya North is located in the Atwima Nwabiagya District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency kan nɛ Atwima-Nwabiagya South anɛ banɛ ka ba nwaae yi Atwima-Nwabiagya constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) vɔɔtug la ni.
english: The constituency and Atwima-Nwabiagya South are sister constituencies born out of the Atwima-Nwabiagya constituency in 2012.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk la bɛnɛ Atwima District pʋʋgin linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
