english: The seat is located within the Atwima District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Atwima-Nwabiagya South constituency bɛnɛ Atwima Nwabiagya District linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Atwima-Nwabiagya South is located in the Atwima Nwabiagya District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency kaŋa nɛ Atwima-Nwabiagya North constituency anɛ banɛ ka ban waae ba yi Atwima-Nwabiagya constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) vɔɔtug la ni.
english: The constituency and Atwima-Nwabiagya North are sister constituencies born out of the Atwima-Nwabiagya constituency in 2012.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk la bɛnɛ Atwima District linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The seat is located within the Atwima District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili li, lin na niŋ si'em ka Audit Service nyaŋi tʋmi ba tʋʋma lin nar si'em dɔlisnɛ Article 188 linɛ bɛ 1992 Constitution of Ghana ni la, ka li paas tʋʋma lʋgir Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: It was established as part of the Audit Service through Article 188 of the 1992 Constitution of Ghana as part of the Public Services of Ghana.

kusaal: Auditor-general dɔlisid Audit service ni vɛɛnsid Ghana ligid diisim nɛ ba tʋʋma, ba nyɛ paŋi yinɛ Article 187 linɛ bɛ 1992 Constitution of Ghana ni la.
english: The auditor-general through the Audit service undertakes audits of the public accounts of Ghana and all public offices as mandated by Article 187 of the 1992 Constitution of Ghana.

kusaal: Tɛɛns si'eba ni, ba buon auditor-general ye Comptroller General, wan wʋʋ US dimi buon ye Comptroller General of the United States ka UK dim mɛ buon ye Comptroller and Auditor General (United Kingdom).
english: In other jurisdictions, the auditor-general is referred to as Comptroller General, as referred to in US as Comptroller General of the United States and UK as Comptroller and Auditor General (United Kingdom).

kusaal: British dimi da nan sʋ'ʋe Ghana la, ba kpɛɛm kanɛ da tʋmi li tʋʋma ka ba buon Colonial Audit Office ka li bɛ London la da pin'il vɛɛnsig lʋgir la Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka li kpɛŋ yʋ'ʋr da an Director, ka on tʋʋma da an ye o maal vɛɛnsig ligidi diib yela yʋʋm wʋsa ka sɔb gbaŋi tisi ba wʋsa kpɛɛm kanɛ bɛ London la.
english: During the colonial era the British Colonial Administration under the direction of the Colonial Audit Office in London established a local Audit Office headed by a Director, whose duty was to annually submit an audit report to the Director of Colonial Audit in London.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinnɛ ni, Kwame Nkrumah da kilim gɔmɛna zugraan la, onɛ da gɔsid lʋgir nwa yi Director of Audit lɛbis Director-General (D-G) of Gold Coast Audit Department.
english: In 1951, after Kwame Nkrumah became Prime Minister, the designation of the head of the Audit Department was modified from Director of Audit to Director-General (D-G) of Gold Coast Audit Department.

kusaal: Neville Warde Sabine ka ba da gaŋ ka o an Director-General yiiga yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinnɛ ni.
english: Neville Warde Sabine was appointed as the first Director-General in 1951.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi ni, ban da maal vootʋg ka li nya'aŋ ka ba maal 1954 Constitution of the Gold Coast, sankan ka ba da ti'ak kpɛŋ la yʋ'ʋri lɛbis Auditor-General (A-G) ye o di'e Director-General of Gold Coast Audit Department nɔbir, ka li dɔl 1954 Constitution la.
english: In 1954, after another legislative election birthing the 1954 Constitution of the Gold Coast, the position was changed to Auditor-General (A-G) in order to replace the Director-General of Gold Coast Audit Department in line with the adoption of the 1954 Constitution.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' ni, Ahenkora Osei ka ba da gaŋ ka o an yiiga sɔbi an Ghana nid kanɛ ka ba gaŋ o ye o an auditor-general ye o an tuongatti tis Auditor-General's Department.
english: In 1963, Ahenkora Osei was appointed as the first Ghanaian auditor-general to lead the Auditor-General's Department.

kusaal: O da tʋm o tʋʋma yʋma piinɛ anii ti paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinnɛ ni, o da tʋm nɛ gɔmɛna nam atan' banɛ ka ba da vooti tisi ba (1960–1966, 1969–1972, nɛ 1979–1981) ka nɔɔra ayi' da an soogianami da faan na'am ka o nan kpɛlim tʋm o tʋʋma (1966–1969 nɛ 1972–1979).
english: He held the position for 18 years till 1981, serving through three constitutional eras (1960–1966, 1969–1972, and 1979–1981) and two military regimes (1966–1969 and 1972–1979) respectively.

kusaal: Ahenkora Osei da yiya ka James Benoni Haizel-Coleman di'e o nɔbir yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinnɛ ni, o da tʋm yʋma atan' ka yi ka Richard Tello-Nelson da di'e o nɔbiri bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan' ni.
english: Ahenkora Osei was succeeded by James Benoni Haizel-Coleman in 1981 who served for 3 years and was subsequently replaced by Richard Tello-Nelson in 1983.

kusaal: Prempeh da tʋmnɛ yʋʋm piiga, o da tʋm paae yʋʋm tusayi la ni ka Edward Dua Agyeman kɛna di'e o nɔbir yʋʋm tusayi nɛ yinnɛ la ni tʋm ka li an ye o tʋm saŋa bi'ela nɛ lin ti paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ atan' ni ka ba bas o suor ye onɛ an kpɛɛm.
english: Prempeh served for 10 years, serving till 2000 and was succeeded by Edward Dua Agyeman in 2001 as Acting A-G till he was confirmed in 2003.

kusaal: Agyeman da tʋm ala ti paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ awai la ni ka Richard Quartei Quartey kɛna di'e o nɔbiri tʋm yʋma ayɔpɔi ti paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ ni, o vʋ'ʋsʋm saŋa da paae ya ka o kul ka Daniel Yaw Domelevo di'e o nɔbir.
english: Agyeman served till 2009 and was replaced by Richard Quartei Quartey who also served for 7 years till 2016, when he retired and was replaced by Daniel Yaw Domelevo.

kusaal: Neville Warde Sabine da nan kpɛlim kɛn tuoni tʋm o tʋʋma ti paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' ni.
english: Neville Warde Sabine maintained his role until 1963.

kusaal: Tello-Nelson da tʋm o tʋʋma yinɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan' paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai ni, li nya'aŋ ka Osei Tutu Prempeh di'e o nɔbir yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai ni.
english: Tello-Nelson served from 1983 to 1989 and was later replaced by Osei Tutu Prempeh in 1990.

kusaal: Augustine Collins Ntim (ba da du'a o nɛ selʋŋ 24, 1964) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka tʋm gbaʋŋ zamisʋg tʋʋma.
english: Augustine Collins Ntim (born September 24, 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and an educationist.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Augustine nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi la ni nwadisa awai la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 Selʋŋ 1964) tenkanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Nkenkaasu ka bɛ Ashanti Region.
english: Augustine was born on 24 September 1964 in a town called Nkenkaasu in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O mɔr Bachelor of Science degree nɛ Master of Science degree in Reproductive Biology yi Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology ni.
english: He holds a Bachelor of Science degree and a Master of Science degree in Reproductive Biology from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr kasɛtta gbana ayi yi Harvard Kennedy School.
english: He also holds two academic certificates from Harvard Kennedy School.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka o keŋ wadmaanib yin la yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009), ka o da mɔr kal gaadi o taaba la nwɛnnɛ vɔɔt tusa atan' (3000).
english: He was elected into parliament in 2009 where he won with over 3000 votes.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) vɔɔtʋg la nya'aŋ la, o da lɛn di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la ka kpɛn' wadmaan yin la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 Yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2017), o da mɔri vɔɔt pisnu nɛ atan' du'al pii nɛ anu kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (53.15%).
english: He was re-elected on 7 January 2013 after the 2012 Ghanaian General Elections and reelected to enter parliament on 7 January 2017 after the completion of the 2016 Ghanaian General Elections where he obtained 53.15% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt o ya'as yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la ni ka o mɔr vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ anii du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (48.67%).
english: He was again elected in the 2020 General elections where he obtained 48.67% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O da anɛ District Chief Executive tis Ministry of Local Government yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) la ni ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: He was the District Chief Executive for the Ministry of Local Government from the year 2005 to 2009.

kusaal: O paasnɛ Government Assurance Committee lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid ka ministanam pɛ'ɛnnɛ ba nɔzi'ela banɛ ka ba kaanb pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb saŋa la.
english: He is a member of the Government Assurance Committee which sees to the fulfilment of all promises and assurances given by ministers.

kusaal: O lɛn paas nɛ Health Committee.
english: He is also a member of the Health Committee.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt o yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ atan' la Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2013).
english: He was re-elected on 7 January 2013 after the 2012 Ghanaian General Elections and reelected to enter parliament on 7 January 2017 after the completion of the 2016 Ghanaian General Elections where he obtained 53.15% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ntim bɛ Ghana wadmaanib yin la din yi yʋʋm 2009 ni ti paae zina.
english: Ntim has been in the parliament of Ghana from 2009 till date.

kusaal: Augustine Tawiah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi ti Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni n tis Bia West linɛ bɛ Western North Region sυ'υlυm la, o anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Augustine Tawiah (born 27 September 1961) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Bia West Constituency in the Western North Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Thomas Aquinas Senior High Sakur linɛ da an Ordinary Level ka la, ka lin nya'aŋ ka o tɔlis Labone Senior High Sakur la ni n naae o Advanced Level la.
english: The Secondary School Augustine Tawiah attended are St. Thomas Aquinas Senior High School (SHS Ordinary Level) and later at Labone Senior High School (SHS Advanced Level).

kusaal: Augustine Tawiah da tɔlis sakur bɛda ni naae ka di'e kasɛtta gbaʋŋ linɛ an Doctor of Ministry yυυma tυsa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ la ni, ka lɛn di'e kasɛtta gbaυŋ linɛ an Doctor of Education zamisυg linɛ an kpiυŋ nɛ wada maalυg yɛla yυυm tυsa ayi nɛ awai la pυυgin, ka lin nya'aŋ o lɛn di'e kasɛtta gbana banɛ an Master of Theology nɛ Master of Science n yi University of Memphis sakurin la.
english: Augustine Tawiah gained Doctor of Ministry (Applied Theology) in 2006, Doctor of Education Certificate (Leadership and Policy Studies) in 2009, Master of Theology, a Master of Science from the University of Memphis as well as a Certificate in University Teaching.

kusaal: Augustine Tawiah da lɛn di'e kasɛtta gbaυŋ linɛ an Doctor of Ministry n yi Harding University la ni, ka mɛ lɛn di'e Master of Arts kasɛtta gbaʋŋ n yi Lipscomb University.
english: Augustine Tawiah also has a Doctor of Ministry from Harding University, a Master of Arts from Lipscomb University, and a Cert-Hr Training from the University of Oklahoma.

kusaal: O anɛ pa'an ka lɛn an kpɛɛm n bɛ Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) la ni.
english: He is a Lecturer and Consultant at Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).

kusaal: Onɛ da an gbaυŋ sɔbid tis National Teaching Council Ghana nwa, onɛ an Ghana Christian University College la Academic Kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid sakur gbaυŋ zamisυg yɛla.
english: He held the position as the Executive Secretary for the National Teaching Council in Ghana and also the Academic Dean at Ghana Christian University College.

kusaal: Augustine yinɛ Tawiah yinɛ Sefwi Asuopiri linɛ bɛ Western Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Augustine Tawiah started his basic school in the Bia District in the current Western North Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Augustine Tawiah pin'ili o biilim sakur nɛ Bia teŋ kanɛ bɛ Ghana Western North Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Augustine Tawiah started his basic school in the Bia District in the current Western North Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Secondary sakur kanɛ ka Augustine Tawiah da keŋ la anɛ St.
english: The Secondary School Augustine Tawiah attended are St. Thomas Aquinas Senior High School (SHS Ordinary Level) and later at Labone Senior High School (SHS Advanced Level).

kusaal: Ala mɛn o da lɛn di'e Cert-Hr Training kasɛtta gbaʋŋ n yi University of Oklahoma.
english: Augustine Tawiah also has a Doctor of Ministry from Harding University, a Master of Arts from Lipscomb University, and a Cert-Hr Training from the University of Oklahoma.

kusaal: Augustine Tawiah anɛ tυmtυm bɛ Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni n an wadmaan.
english: Augustine Tawiah works at the Parliament of Ghana as a Member of Parliament (MP).

kusaal: Augustine Tawiah anɛ wadmaan n tis Bia West linɛ bɛ Western North Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Augustine Tawiah is the Member of Parliament (MP) for Bia West Constituency in the Western North Region.

kusaal: Awutu-Senya Constituency anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ paasi ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni mɛn.
english: Awutu-Senya is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba mɛ ɛɛnti vɔti gaŋ nid yinne ka o zi'enɛ ba nɔba zug n an wadmaan n tisi ba vɔt saŋa Cape Coast constituency la bɛnɛ Cape Coast Municipal district la linɛ bɛ Ghana Central Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Awutu-Senya is located in the Awutu/Effutu/Senya district of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Cape Coast constituency la bɛnɛ Cape Coast Municipal district la linɛ bɛ Ghana Central Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Awutu-Senya is located in the Awutu/Effutu/Senya district of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlʋm la da ti kena pʋdigi ayi n an Cape Coast North nɛ Cape Coast South constituencies yʋʋma 2012.
english: Leading into the 2012 elections the constituency was divided into two Awutu-Senya East and Awutu-Senya West.

kusaal: Ayawaso North sʋ'ʋlim m bɛ Greater Accra sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana ni.
english: The Ayawaso North constituency is located in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Accra Metropolis District dinɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region, Ghana la pʋʋgin.
english: The constituency is located within the Accra Metropolis District of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaan bɛ wadmaanib yin la ni vɔɔtʋg saŋa.
english: It elects one member of parliament (MP) by the first-past-the-post system of election.

kusaal: Ayawaso West bɛɛ Ayawaso west Wuogon anɛ sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ paas sʋ'ʋlim banɛ bɛ Accra ni la, ka mɔr wadmaam Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni, first past the post vɔɔt buudi saŋa sa.
english: Ayawaso West or Ayawaso West Wuogon is one of the constituencies in Accra represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ayawaso West bɛnɛ Accra Metropolitan Area n an Greater Accra region, Ghana.
english: Ayawaso West is located in the Accra Metropolitan Area of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Dɔnwalig nwadig la 15 daar, 2018 yʋʋm la ni, ka ba da dɔlis wada (LI) 2312 zuginɛ zi'el Ayawaso West Municipal Assembly (AWMA) la, ka li bɛɛ li kɔn' nɛ Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA).
english: On the 15th of March, 2018, the Ayawaso West Municipal Assembly (AWMA) was established as a distinct entity, separated from the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA), through the enactment of Legislative Instrument (LI) 2312.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlim la zɛmisim kanɛ an 385 square kilometers la, Ayawaso West Municipal assembly (AWMA) zaŋ nɛ Greater Accra Region faalʋ zɛmis wʋʋ 3.0%.
english: Covering an area of 385 square kilometers, the Ayawaso West Municipal Assembly (AWMA) encompasses approximately 3.0% of the total land area of the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Teŋ la dim la anɛ Ga nidib, banɛ buudi malima an Homowo Festival, ka teŋ la mɛ mɔr Ga-Dangme nidib, Akan nidib banɛ yi Tudu sʋ'ʋlim, Ewe nidib, Nageria nidib nɛ buudsieba banɛ ya'a bɛnɛ teŋin la bɛɛ ba tʋm nɛ sʋ'ʋlim la ni.
english: The local populace primarily consists of Ga people who observe the Homowo Festival, while the area also accommodates Ga-Dangme, Akan with Northern heritage, Ewe, Nigerian, and other ethnic groups who either reside or work within its boundaries.

kusaal: Ban pian'ad buudi seiba anɛ Twi, Ga, Ewe nɛ buudsieba bi'ela pian'ad.
english: The prevalent languages spoken encompass Twi, Ga, Ewe, and a spectrum of other dialects.

kusaal: Benard Kwesi Pari sakyiama, onɛ an assembly la Coordinating Director nananna nwa.
english: Leading the administrative affairs is Mr. Bernard Kwesi Pari Sakyiama, serving as the present Municipal Coordinating Director for the assembly.

kusaal: Teŋ banɛ da paam anɛ Legon Staff Village School, Mamobi Prison School, Abelenkpe Primary 1 Basic School.
english: Beneficiary Communities includes Legon Staff Village School, Mamobi Prisons School, Abelenkpe Primary 1 Basic School.

kusaal: SƲ'ƲLIM LA SUO-SIEBA MAALIG – Ba nam bɛnɛ tʋʋm kan ni sʋ'ʋlim la zin'isieba, ka kɛ ka Westland By-Pass Link sealing tʋʋma la naae zin'isieba.
english: PARTIAL RECONSTRUCTION OF LOCAL ROADS - The project is currently underway in certain sections of the assembly, while sealing on the Westland By-Pass Link has been finished in other areas.

kusaal: Ayawaso West Municipality bɛ nananna nwa la, sʋ'ʋlim la dim anɛ banɛ tens kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb kpɛn' bɛ ani, ka nidib bɛɛ ani la anɛ banɛ mɔri buudi malima nam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb.
english: The Ayawaso West Municipality stands as a contemporary and cosmopolitan region, boasting a rich tapestry of individuals from various socio-cultural backgrounds.

kusaal: Westland teŋ la paas tens banɛ paam tʋʋm kaŋa nwa nyɔɔd la.
english: The Westland community is among the beneficiaries of this initiative.

kusaal: Ayensuano Constituency bɛnɛ Eastern region Sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The Ayensuano constituency is in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni ka Ayeh-Paye Samuel da lieb wadmaanni tis constituency la.
english: The current member of Parliament for the constituency is Ida Adjoa Asiedu.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o dɔlisid New Patriotic Party, ka o da mɔr vɔɔt tusa atan, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ ayi gaadi o taaba la ka di constituency la wadmaan.
english: She was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and won a majority of 18,229 to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: Godfred Kwame Otsere onɛ da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug 4th Republic parliament dɔlisid New Patriotic Party ni da sig ka o di'e.
english: She succeeded Teddy Safori Addi who had represented the constituency in the 8th parliament of the 4th Republican parliament on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) nii, Azerbaijani carpet weaving tʋʋma bɛ Azerbaijan la da paam suori paas UNESCO List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
english: Azerbaijan successfully lobbied to inscribe the traditional art of Azerbaijani carpet weaving on the representative list of UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Yʋʋmkanɛ da tia'ali Azerbaijani da paami asʋ'ʋ-m- mɛŋi yi Soviet Union la, Azerbaijani carpet weaving malʋŋ la da anɛ bʋŋkanɛ mu'oe ba nini ka Azerbaijani gɔmena la da mɔɔd ye o gu', pa'al/gɔsim, sʋŋ kadi keŋ tuon ka nɔbʋg carpet weaving malʋŋ la.
english: In the years following Azerbaijan's independence from the Soviet Union, Azerbaijani carpet weaving tradition has been the subject to the special attention of the Azerbaijani government's efforts to preserve, study, promote and develop carpet weaving traditions.

kusaal: Wada kanɛ an ye ba gu' ka kɛ ka carpet tʋʋmkanɛ ka Azerbaijan dim tʋm la nɔbʋg la" ka Zugraan Ilham Aliyev da pin'ili di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni, "Azerkhalcha" OJSC (Azerbaijani: "Azərxalça" ASC) da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) nwadisa anu la ni, Ka ba yʋ'ʋn pin'ili tiend Carpet Weaver Day nwadisa anu la daba anu daar dɔlisid Zugraan la da tis nɔɔr yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ nwadis piinɛ yinne dabpisi nɛ anu daar la,Austrian architect Franz Janz da maal Azerbaijan Carpet Museum ka di nwɛnɛ kaapɛt ka ba kpilimnɛ ka li da sin'iŋ tʋʋma yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi nwadisa anii la ni.
english: The Law "On the protection and development of carpet art of Azerbaijan" was adopted by the President Ilham Aliyev in December 2004, "Azerkhalcha" OJSC (Azerbaijani: "Azərxalça" ASC) was established in May 2016, Carpet Weaver Day started to be celebrated on May 5 according to the Presidential Decree dated 25.11.2016, the new building for Azerbaijan Carpet Museum designed by an Austrian architect Franz Janz in the shape of a rolled carpet was put into use in August 2014.

kusaal: Ya'asa, State Program kanɛ da an "ye ba gu' ka ka kɛ ka carpet tʋʋma kanɛ bɛ Republic of Azerbaijan la keŋ tuon, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la ni paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi (2022) la ni" da paam suori tʋm yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadisa ayi la ni ka di yinɛ zugraan Ilham Aliyev zug, ye ba nyaŋi paam la'adi tis industry la, ka sʋŋ carpet-weaving ka di keŋ tuon, ka lɛn sʋŋi yɔ'ɔs tʋʋma zin'is paala ka bam aal kaapɛt paala.
english: In addition, State Program on the "Protection and development of carpet art in the Republic of Azerbaijan 2018-2022" was approved in February 2018 by President Ilham Aliyev with the aim to create raw material supply for this industry, improve the infrastructure for carpet-weaving, support the establishment of new workplaces and carry out qualified personnel training in the field of carpet-weaving.

kusaal: Azerbaijani carpet anɛ malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba mɔr nu'usu ʋgʋd fuud ka ba labisim, tɛbisim bɛ kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb ka ba pa'ali agɔl la bɛɛ pʋ pa'alɛ ka ba bɔɔnsim la aan Azerbaijan zi'esim yi region bɛdegʋ banɛ maan carpetnam nɛ nu'us la ni.
english: The Azerbaijani carpet is a traditional handmade textile of various sizes, with dense texture and a pile or pile-less surface, whose patterns are characteristic of Azerbaijan's many carpet-making regions.

kusaal: Carpet maalʋg anɛ buudi malʋŋ kanɛ lɔmisid yit tuŋ yinne lɛbid yinne ni dɔlisid nɔɔr pian'ad bɛɛ zamisʋg.
english: Carpet making is a family tradition transferred orally and through practice.

kusaal: Aziz Abdul Muniru anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Akan Constituency bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim la ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: Aziz Abdul Muniru is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Akan Constituency in the Volta Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da naae nɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology nɛ M.S.C. ka lɛn da maal B.S.C. in procurement management.
english: He graduated from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology with an M.S.C. and a B.S.C. in procurement management.

kusaal: Dinɛ paas anɛ ye, o mɔr gbaʋŋ kanɛ pa'al ye o paas Ghana Institute of Surveyors (MGhIS) nɛ Ghana Institute of Construction (MGIOC).
english: Additionally, he holds professional memberships with the Ghana Institute of Surveyors (MGhIS) and the Ghana Institute of Construction (MGIOC).

kusaal: O da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni, ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, ka da di Akan constituency bɛ Volta Region kʋk la.
english: He contested for the 2016 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of National Democratic Congress and won the Akan constituency in the Volta Region.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔt kal tusa piinɛ atan' nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yinne (13, 941) ka li zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ yinne du'al nɛɛm anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.05%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He won the election with 13,941 which is equivalent to 51.05% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔt la ka bas Kofi Adjei Ntim onɛ da an wadmaan na'anya'ad tis wabʋg na'adɔɔg la, ka da paam vɔɔt tusa awai nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pistan' (9, 730) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pistan' nɛ anu du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' kɔbiga pʋʋgin (35.63%), ka IND wadmaan na'anya'ad Joseph Kwadwo Ofori da paam vɔɔt tusa atan' nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (3, 486) ka li an vɔɔt pii nɛ ayi' du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (12.77%), ka Jonathan Tetteh onɛ da an APC wadmaan na'anya'ad la da paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (149) ka li zɛm nɛ nɛɛm du'al pisnu nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.55%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: He won the election over Kofi Adjei Ntim who was a parliamentary candidate for New Patriotic Party who polled 9,730 representing 35.63%, IND parliamentary candidate Joseph Kwadwo Ofori had 3,486 representing 12.77% and Jonathan Tetteh who was APC parliamentary candidate polled 149 representing 0.55% of the total votes.

kusaal: Li dɔlis nɛ yi Ga wa'a Kpanlogo, linɛ bɛ Chorkor, James Town, Teshie, Nungua nɛ Tema sʋ'ʋlim nam la, ba wʋsa bɛnɛ Greater Accra Region.
english: It is connected to the traditional Ga dance Kpanlogo, associated with the coastal towns in the country such as Chorkor, James Town, Teshie, Nungua and Tema, in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Azonto anɛ wa'a nɛ yʋʋma buudi pin'il Ghana.
english: Azonto is a dance and music genre from Ghana.

kusaal: Tɛɛns bam ani, ba da pin'ili buon Azonto nɛ ye 'Apaa'.
english: Azonto is a communicative dance believed to originate from "Apaa" which literally means to work.

kusaal: Apaa wa'a, linɛ an Azonto wa'a la anɛ linɛ ka ba la'asid taaba ka lɔbid nu'us yinnɛ, ka li pa'an nidib tʋʋma yela, bɛɛ ba lɔbid nu'us la ye nidib gɔsid ka li vɛn ni ba.
english: Azonto is a communicative dance believed to originate from "Apaa" which literally means to work.

kusaal: O da anɛ two-weight world champion, onɛ da paam WBC bɛ 1984 ti paae 1987 nɛ WBC super-featherweight taetil la nɔɔr ayi' bɛ1988 nɛ 1997.
english: He was a two-weight world champion, having held the World Boxing Council (WBC) featherweight title from 1984 to 1987 and the WBC super-featherweight title twice between 1988 and 1997.

kusaal: O da lɛm keŋ tuon nya'a WBC nɛ IBF lightweight taetil bɛ 1990 ni.
english: He also challenged once for the unified WBC and International Boxing Federation (IBF) lightweight titles in 1990.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlʋm pʋʋgʋnɛ, onɛ da mɔr ABU, nɛ Commonwealth featherweight taetil bɛ 1980 nɛ 1982.
english: At regional level, he held the ABU, and Commonwealth featherweight titles between 1980 and 1982.

kusaal: Nelson naae All-Africa Games nɛ 1978 ka 1978 mɛn an Commonwealth Games, da di sanlim nwiig bɛ featherweight saŋa ayi' la ni.
english: Nelson competed at the 1978 All-Africa Games and 1978 Commonwealth Games, winning gold medals in featherweight at both events.

kusaal: Ba da tis o Amateur Boxer bɛ yʋʋm kan, ka di yinɛ Sports Writers Association of Ghana (SWAG) yʋʋm kanna.
english: He was awarded Amateur Boxer of the year by the Sports Writers Association of Ghana (SWAG) that same year.

kusaal: Dunia wʋsa da yɛl ye o anɛ bɔgisa nwɛ'ɛd tita'ar Africa ni, nannana onɛ pɛ'ɛs 31 onɛ nwɛ'ɛd pound for pound bɔgisa bɛ BoxRec bɛ dunia wʋsa.
english: Widely considered one of the greatest African boxers of all time, he is currently ranked as the 69th greatest pound for pound boxer of all time by BoxRec.

kusaal: Baddoo anɛ yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba mɔri pʋd Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Baddoo is a Ghanaian surname.

kusaal: Badu anɛ Ninsaal yʋ'ʋr ka ba mɔri pʋd nidib tɛɛns banɛ bɛ Asia nɛ Africa sʋ'ʋlim nam.
english: Badu is a surname or title found in various regions of Asia and Africa.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr la da bɛ Brahmin tɛɛns banɛ bɛ western region Nepal tɛŋ sʋ'ʋlim, li kaskas anɛ Darchula, doti nɛ Baitadi districts, Kanchanpur, Dhangadhi, nɛ Gorkha district linɛ bɛ Nepal ya'nya'aŋ baba la.
english: The surname बडू is found in the Brahmin community in the far western region of Nepal mainly in the Darchula, doti and Baitadi districts,Kanchanpur, Dhangadhi, also in Gorkha district eastern part of Nepal .Also in eastern regions of Indian states like West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh & Jharkhand which are unrelated to one found in Nepal.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr kan buudi mɛ bɛ Ghana.
english: An unrelated surname is found in Ghana.

kusaal: Nidib banɛ bɛ Lingaraja Temple linɛ bɛ Bhubaneswar, Odisha sʋ'ʋlim la, maanmaanib banɛ bɛ anina la yit nɛ tɛnkpɛmis atan' bama: Pujapanda Nijog, Brahman Nijog nɛ Badu Nijog, ka banɛ an Badu an sankpan'as nam, ka ba buoli ba ye Vadu bɛ chapter 62, gbaŋ kanɛ buon Ekamrapurana la ni.
english: In modern times, in the Lingaraja Temple of Bhubaneswar, Odisha priests belonged to three communities, namely Pujapanda Nijog, Brahman Nijog and Badu Nijog out of which the Badu are non-Brahmin servant groups [section of the Kshatriya (क्षत्रिय)] while they are described as Vadu in chapter 62 of the Ekamrapurana.

kusaal: Tuŋ kanɛ buon Badu la ba buoni ba ye Niyoga, ka banɛ gaansid kpɛɛmnam yʋʋm wʋsa bɛ malima kanɛ ka ba buon Sandalwood festival la ni.
english: The caste group of Badu is called Niyoga, which elects the officers every year during the Sandalwood festival.

kusaal: Li mɛ bɛ Indian tɛɛns si'eba banɛ bɛ ya'nya'aŋ wan wʋʋ West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh nɛ Jharkhand tɛɛns nɛ.
english: The surname बडू is found in the Brahmin community in the far western region of Nepal mainly in the Darchula, doti and Baitadi districts,Kanchanpur, Dhangadhi, also in Gorkha district eastern part of Nepal .Also in eastern regions of Indian states like West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh & Jharkhand which are unrelated to one found in Nepal.

kusaal: Banɛ buon Badu wʋsa maan malima atan' bama, ba vʋti ba tʋba, ka kun sidib bɛɛ dit pʋ'ab ka mɛ lɛn an banɛ maan wina nam la.
english: Every Badu undergoes three distinct rites, namely, ear-piercing, marriage, and god-touching.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmin saŋa la, banɛ da an Badu nam la da tʋm tʋʋma anu bɛ wina dɔɔgin - Paliabadu nɛ Pharaka, banɛ da an malim banɛ pak hali.
english: Historically, the Badu's performed five different temple duties - Paliabadu and Pharaka, which were considered important and Pochha, Pahada and Khataseja, which were considered inferior.

kusaal: Badu dim la mɛ piesidi ba mɛŋ ka yɛɛni ba wina Siddhaganesh nɛ Gopalini fuud.
english: The Badus also carry out ablution and dressing of the images of Siddhaganesh and Gopalini.

kusaal: Di da paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity la'ad ni nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017).
english: It was inscribed on the UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list in 2017.

kusaal: Bài Chòi ka Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism da nyɛ ka di an Vietnam national intangible cultural heritage din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014)- paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la ni.
english: Bài Chòi was recognised as Vietnam's national intangible cultural heritage during 2014-2016 by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism.

kusaal: Bài Chòi di'ema nɛ di tʋʋma anɛ di'em kanɛ mɔr gbana yʋda nwɛnɛ bingo nɛ, ka Hieu artist nam nwɛ'ɛdi li ka yʋ'ʋm yʋʋma, Tết Nguyên Đán saŋa.
english: Bài Chòi games and performances involve a card game similar to bingo, played with songs and music performed by Hieu artists, during the Tết Nguyên Đán.

kusaal: Bài Chòi anɛ tʋʋma banɛ ka ba la'asi bɛ Central Vietnam ka di an yʋʋma, sɛnlʋŋ, di'ema, pɛntʋg nɛ pʋtɛn'ɛr pian'ad yɛla, ka ba tisid nyaasim, di'ema ka lɛn kɛ ka nimbanɛ bɛ teŋkpɛmis sʋ'ʋlimin la baŋid taaba.
english: Bài Chòi (aka Bài tới in Huế) is a combination of arts in Central Vietnam including music, poetry, acting, painting and literature, providing recreation, entertainment and socialising within village communities.

kusaal: Turkmen bakshy malʋŋ la nwɛnɛ Turkic Ashik buudi malima an si'em la.
english: The Turkmen bakshy tradition is closely related to the larger Turkic Ashik tradition.

kusaal: Bakshy (Persian: بخشی, romanized: baxši) anɛ buudi malʋŋ kanɛ ka Turkmen yʋʋmyʋʋmnib yʋ'ʋm.
english: The bakshy (Uzbek: baxshi, Turkmen: bagşy) are traditional Central Asian folk singers.

kusaal: Ba yʋʋmidnɛ cappella bɛɛ ba nɔk buudi malima la'adi nwɛ'ɛdi suakid (nwiisa ayi' lute kanɛ ka ba buon ye dutar la).
english: The bakshy may sing either a cappella or to the accompaniment of traditional instruments (primarily the dutar).

kusaal: Yiiga ba da maali linɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (1869) ni bɛ Estonia (Estonian Song Festival), ka lɛm maal yinne ya'as yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' (1873) la ni Latvia (Latvian yʋʋma nɛ wa'ab malʋŋ).
english: The first national celebrations were held in Estonia in 1869 and Latvia in 1873; Lithuania held its first celebration in 1924.

kusaal: Baltic song festivals (Estonian: laulupidu, Latvian: dziesmu svētki, Lithuanian: dainų šventė) anɛ amateur malʋŋ yʋʋma nɛ wa'ab kanɛ ka ba maanɛ bɛ Baltic states ka ba zaŋi li paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List.
english: The Baltic song and dance celebrations, also known as the Baltic song festivals (Estonian: laulupidu, Latvian: dziesmu svētki, Lithuanian: dainų šventė), form a transnational tradition of mass amateur choral, dance, instrumental and folk-art celebrations in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

kusaal: Ba'asʋgɔ malʋŋ la da paae Lithuania (Lithuanian Song Festival) nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi (1924) la ni.
english: The first Lithuanian Song Celebration was held in Kaunas in August 1924.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014) la ni, Estonian Song Festival da la'as nidib ka ba kal nwɛnɛ nidib tusa kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nɛ awai nɛ kɔbis tan' (159 300).
english: A comparative study by Guntis Šmidchens inventoried 1,964 works performed at 70 Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian national song celebrations between 1869 and 2014.

kusaal: Bambara, ka ba lɛn buon Malian, Bamana bɛɛ Bamanankan anɛ buudi pian'ad ka ba pian'adi bɛ Mali tɛŋin, nidib banɛ pian'adi li an wʋʋ miliyɔn piinɛ anaasi, banɛ an buud kan an nidib 4.2 million ka miliyɔŋ piiga lɛɛ an buud si'eba ka wʋmi li.
english: Bambara, also known as Malian, Bamana (N'Ko script: ߓߡߊߣߊ߲) or Bamanankan (N'Ko script: ߓߡߊߣߊ߲ߞߊ߲; Arabic script: بَمَنَنكَن), is a lingua franca and national language of Mali spoken by perhaps 14 million people, natively by 4.2 million Bambara people and about 10 million second-language users.

kusaal: Vɛɛnsig pa'al ye nidib banɛ bɛ Mali tɛŋin pisnii, kɔbiga pʋʋgin pian'ad Bambara ka li an ba buudi pian'ad bɛɛ pian'ad kanɛ ka ba wʋmi paasi ba buudi pian'ad ni.
english: Bambara was until 2023 one of several languages designated by Mali as a national language.

kusaal: Akple anɛ dikanɛ ka banɛ bɛ Ghana dagɔbʋg sʋ'ʋlim dim nɔŋi li hali— Ewe buudi, Fante buudi nɛ Ga-Dangme—amaa ba diti li tɛɛns wʋsa Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Akple is preferred by the people of the southern regions of Ghana—the Ewe people, the Fante people and the Ga-Dangme—but it is also eaten across other regions in Ghana.

kusaal: Banku anɛ dikanɛ bʋk ka Ga-Dangme (Ga bɛɛ Dangbe) diti li, ka Fante nam la mɛ mɔr diid wala buudi ka li lɛɛ kpiem ka ba buoni li ye ɛtsew.
english: Banku is a softer variety eaten by the Ga-Dangme (Ga or Dangbe), while the Fante people also have a drier variant of the dish they call ɛtsew.

kusaal: Banku anɛ yʋ'ʋr kanɛ yi Ga-Dangme pian'ad ni na.
english: Banku is a distinctively Ga-Dangme term.

kusaal: Banku anɛ linɛ ka ba paami li yinɛ Dangbe pian'a giŋ "ba mi ku" ni.
english: Banku is coined from the Dangbe phrase "ba mi ku".

kusaal: 'Ku' anɛ bʋnlinɛ ka Ga-Dangbe dim nɔki pʋd diib buudi wʋsa banɛ wan taaba.
english: "Ku" is the generic Ga-Dangbe term for all food of similar texture and prepared in a similar manner.

kusaal: Ba buon la'ad bɛdigʋ ka li kɛŋ wan yʋ'ʋr nwa' bɛ Ga buudi pian'ad ni, si'eba an inku (lin anɛ kpasɔɔndim bɛ Ga buudi pian'ad ni), ashanku nɛ la'ad si'eba yʋda bɛdigʋ banɛ ba buudi pian'ad ni ka ba naad ye 'ku'.
english: There are similar tonal terms with different meanings in the Ga language, such as inku (for pomade in the Ga language), ashanku (for a variant of a plantain fritter called tatale), and many other names ending in "ku".

kusaal: Banku nɛ akple anɛ diib banɛ ka ba dit nɛ nu'us.
english: Banku and akple are traditionally eaten with the hands.

kusaal: 'Ba' gbin an 'vaang(bɛɛ vaand)'.
english: "Ba" means "leaf(ves)".

kusaal: Ba mɛ diti li nɛ zɛɛnd, sitiw bɛɛ nanzʋ'ʋs nɛ ni'im bɛɛ zimi.
english: It can be served with soup, stew or pepper sauce with meat or fish.

english: The Barbra Asher Foundation, in collaboration with Cape Coast Technical University's Entrepreneurship Development and Innovation, has trained more than 200 youth in the Cape Coast constituency in entrepreneurial skills.

english: Barbara Asher Ayisi (born 12 February 1976) is a Ghanaian politician and a former member of parliament for the Cape Coast North constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

english: She is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and was the former deputy minister for education in Ghana.

english: Barbara Asher Ayisi was born on 12 February 1976 in Effutu, Central Region of Ghana.

english: Before her election to parliament, she worked as a form mistress between 2003 and 2006 with the Ghana Education Service (GES) and also as a housemistress from 2010 to 2016 at Wesley Girls High School.

kusaal: Onɛ sʋ'oe Barbara Asher Foundation lʋgir gɔsid pu'asada nɛ na'akim nu'ug tʋʋma yɛla bɛ o constituency la.
english: She has a foundation called the Barbra Asher Foundation, which focuses on reducing unemployment among the youth in her constituency.

english: She is Christian and attends Victory Bible Church International.

english: Barbara Oteng Gyasi (born 5 October 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and a former Member of Parliament for Prestea-Huni Valley constituency of the Western Region of Ghana.

english: As the NPP candidate, Gyasi was elected to represent the Prestea-Huni Valley Constituency in 2016, but failed to retain the seat in the 2020 Ghanaian elections, as she lost to Robert Wisdom Cudjoe of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Gyasi nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ anaasi (1964).
english: Gyasi was born on 5 October 1964.

kusaal: Barewa College anɛ sakur kanɛ bɛ Zaria, Kaduna State, Nigeria yaya'aŋ baba.
english: Barewa College is a college in Zaria, Kaduna State, northern Nigeria.

kusaal: British Governor General Hugh Clifford, da sin'iŋ sakur la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyi nɛ ayinne(1921) la ni, sakur la yʋ'ʋri da anɛ Katsina College sin'iŋirin la.
english: Founded in 1921 by British Governor General Hugh Clifford, it was originally known as Katsina College.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr la tiaknɛ lɛbisi buon ye Kaduna College yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ anii (1938) la ni, ka lɛ tiaki lɛb Government College, Zaria yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (1949) la ni, ka yʋ'm da lɛm tiaki li yʋ'ʋr la lɛbis Barewa College dinɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋm buoni li zina la.
english: It switched its name to Kaduna College in 1938 and to Government College, Zaria in 1949 before settling on Barewa College.

kusaal: Sakur la pɛɛs sakur titada dinɛ ka sakur bibis gbɛɛnd bɛ Nigeria yaya'aŋ baba, ka mɛ lɛ an sakur kanɛ ka di yʋ'ʋr yi hali ka nidib mi'i di hali diŋ yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu(1960s) sin'isirin.
english: It is one of the largest boarding schools in Northern Nigeria and was the most-celebrated post-primary schools there up to the early 1960s.

kusaal: Sakur la yʋ'ʋr yinɛ pamm ka di anɛ teŋ la nidib bɛdigʋ da naae sakur la ni ka yʋ'ʋm an nimbɛda zina la zug, nimbama anɛ Tafawa Balewa onɛ da Prime Minister of Nigeria diŋ yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu(1960) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu(1966) la ni gɔsid Nigeria teŋtitada anaasi heads of state of Nigeria.
english: The school is known for the large number of elites from the region who attended and counts among its alumni include Tafawa Balewa who was Prime Minister of Nigeria from 1960 to 1966, four heads of state of Nigeria.

kusaal: Sakur la bɛni Gaskiya suorin dinɛ bɛ Tukur -Tukur Zaria sʋ'ʋlim baba la.
english: The school is located along Gaskiya road in the Tukur -Tukur area of Zaria.

kusaal: Hugh Clifford, onɛ an British dim governor-general, sin'iŋ Katsina College sakur la nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyi nɛ ayinne(1921) la ni.
english: Hugh Clifford, a British governor-general, founded Katsina College in 1921.

kusaal: Emir Muhammadu Dikko da dɛgim mɛɛ li yiiga bɛ Katsina ka yɔ'ɔgi li yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyi nɛ ayi(1922) la ni.
english: It was first built in Katsina by Emir Muhammadu Dikko and officially opened in 1922.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobu(1956) ni la k aba da nyɛ sakuyanam bɛdigʋ kena ka an sʋm la zug ba da lɛm tiak sakur la yd'dr ya'asi lɛ Zaria Secondary School.
english: When some of the provincial secondary schools were poised to become full secondary schools in 1956, the college was renamed Zaria Secondary School.

kusaal: Alhaji Ahmadu Bello, kanɛ da an nintirin bɛ Northern Nigeria (Premier of Northern Nigeria) ka da mɛ lɛm onɛ naae kakur kanla,labaar kanɛ ka o sɔbi digil ka di pian'adi o mɛŋ yɛla ye sakur la anɛ sakur kanɛ an na'abiis sakur o pian'a nɛ mamis nɛ sakur kanɛ ka British dim bɛ India (schools set up by the British in India) la.
english: Alhaji Ahmadu Bello, the first Premier of Northern Nigeria and an alumnus of the college, described it in his autobiography as a training ground for princes, likening it to the schools set up by the British in India.

kusaal: Sakur ya la yʋ'ʋ banɛ an tier zin'ig anɛ Bello Kagara House, Lugard House, Clifford House, Dan Hausa House, Mallam Smith House, Nagwamatse House, Bienemann House, Mort House nɛ, later, Jafaru House nɛ Suleiman Barau House, ka ba da buoni li kʋdimin la ye New House A nɛ New House di mɛɛp saŋa.
english: Memorable names of the dormitories include Bello Kagara House, Lugard House, Clifford House, Dan Hausa House, Mallam Smith House, Nagwamatse House, Bienemann House, Mort House and, later, Jafaru House and Suleiman Barau House, which were called New House A and New House B during their construction.

english: My second reason was that Katsina, though it is an important town and the administrative capital of an important Emirate, is not as yet so close to the railway and to the commercial centres of Nigeria as to make it unsuitable for that quiet and tranquillity and that freedom from distractions which are so necessary for young men who are devoting their lives to study.It is Northern Nigeria's first secondary school, initially catering to children of royalty and a select few from the aristocracy.

kusaal: O da tʋm nɛ yʋʋma anaasi bɛ Ningo-prampram constituency Jerry John Rawlings Gomɛna la ni.
english: He did only one term for the Ningo-prampram constituency under Jerry John Rawlings Government.

kusaal: Onɛ da di'e o nɔbir anɛ Enoch Teye Mensah ka o na'adɔɔg da an National Democratic Congress, o da di na'am la bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ vootʋg saŋa la, ka nidib tusa piinɛ anu, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi vooti tis o, lin anɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ pʋdigir yinnɛ kɔbiga pʋʋgin da vooti tsi o ka da di ya'an ka bas; Desmond Nene Quaynor on da paam mɛ nidib tusir, kɔbisnu nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai ka ba vooti is o, ka lin anɛ anu' nɛ pʋdigir ayuobʋ, kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka Gwendolyn Sara Addo da zi'en nɛ o mɛŋ nyali ka mɛ paam nidib tusir, kɔbisnu nɛ pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi ka ba vooti tis o, o da anɛ National Democratic Congress nid mɛn.
english: He was succeeded by Enoch Teye Mensah of the National Democratic Congress who won the seat during the 1996 Ghanaian general election with 15,677 votes representing 56.10% of the share defeating his opponents; Desmond Nene Quaynor who polled 1,569 which represent 5.60% of the total votes cast and Gwendolyn Sara Addo an Independent candidate who also polled 1,537 representing 5.50% under the membership of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Carboo nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi, Samanpiid nwadig, daba atan' daar bɛ Greater Accra Region Ghana tɛŋin.
english: Carboo was born on 3 December 1937 in Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Carboo anɛ onɛ da maan gbana ka nyaan kpɛn'ɛ parliament of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' ni da paas yiiga parliament kanɛ da bɛ fourth republic of Ghana ni la.
english: Carboo was a printer before entering the parliament in 1993 as a member of the first parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Carboo da paas yiiga parliament kanɛ da bɛ fourth republic of Ghana la ni.
english: Carboo was a member of the first parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paam na'am kʋk la yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' Ghana vootʋg saŋa la, ka o na'adɔɔg da an National Democratic Congress.
english: He took seat during the 1992 Ghanaian parliamentary election on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Carboo anɛ Kristo nid.
english: Carboo is a Christian.

kusaal: Batakari Day anɛ dabisir kanɛ ka Ghana nidib wʋsa diti li Ghana sʋ'ʋim wʋsa, dabisir la lu daasi'er anɛ Arizum daar kanɛ pin'in nwadig wʋsa.
english: National Batakari Day (or simply Batakari Day) is a national day of celebration across Ghana, held on the first Friday of every month.

kusaal: Li ka'a bʋnlinɛ an tilas ye sɔ' wʋsa maalɛ, amaa banɛ bɛ Ghana wʋsa nark a ba ye Banaa Batakari kɛŋ tʋʋma zin'isin bɛɛ sakur nam ni.
english: Though not mandatory, everybody living in Ghana is expected to wear the Batakari smock to their various workplaces or schools.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anu, Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig la, daba anaasi daar ka Ministry of Tourism da tis nɔɔr kan, dabisir la anɛ ye banɛ bɛ Ghana yadatiʋŋ baba dim pa'ali ba fʋʋd yɛɛb ka li anɛ Ghana nidib banɛ bɛ ya'datiʋŋ baba tɛŋ nɔbigir yela.
english: First declared on September 4, 2015, by the Ministry of Tourism, the day is meant to expose the culture of northerners as part of SADA's comprehensive development agenda for Ghana's three most deprived regions.

kusaal: Batakari Festival anɛ di'ema malima kanɛ ka King Ayisoba pin'ili li ye o pa'al Batakari, Ghana banaa Batakari, o yit nɛ Upper East Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The Batakari Festival is a cultural event organised by King Ayisoba to showcase Batakari, a traditional handmade Ghanaian smock from the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Accra sʋ'ʋlim, ba maal di'ema malima kaŋa zin'is kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb, zin'is la si'eba anɛ; National Theater nɛ Alliance Française.
english: In Accra, various venues have hosted the event, some of which include; the National Theater and Alliance Française.

kusaal: Li yiiga daan la da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ atan' ni ka yʋʋm wʋsa ka Ghana dim yʋ'ʋn di'em mi li.
english: The inaugural event was held in 2013 and the festival has since become an annual event in Ghana.

kusaal: O gban'e ye o ya'a pian'adi tisid nidib fuud nwa' yɛɛb yela, nidib banɛ tʋmmi li tʋʋma tʋʋma na kɛŋ tuon ka nidib paam tʋʋma tʋm ka pʋ'asada nɛ dasam la paam ligidi Ghana.
english: He believed that propagating the wearing of the fashion through programs like his will consequently create jobs for people thereby reducing the rate of unemployment and also serve as a source income for the youth in Northern Ghana.

kusaal: Malima nwa bɛnɛ yʋʋm wʋsa tɛnpʋʋg si'eba Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka dabisa la lɛɛ ka'a yinnɛ.
english: The festival is held on an annual basis in specific cities in Ghana at specific dates.

kusaal: Saam kɛn zin'igin la pa'ani ba Batakari fuud yɛɛb, amaa banɛ maan di'ema daarkan anɛ King Ayisoba nɛ o nya'andɔlib.
english: Guest artistes are invited to perform and showcase their Batakari attires, however, the main performers are King Ayisoba and his team of Kologo players.

kusaal: Ba kaanbidi buon yʋ'ʋmyʋ'ʋmidib si'eba la'asig nwa' ni, ba si'eba anɛ; Wiyaala, Wanlov the Kubolor, Kwaw Kese, Yaa Pono, Atongo Zimba nɛ Zea onɛ yit Netherlands.
english: Some guest artistes that have been invited to grace the occasion include; Wiyaala, Wanlov the Kubolor, Kwaw Kese, Yaa Pono, Atongo Zimba and Zea from the Netherlands.

kusaal: Bɔk anɛ tɛmpʋʋg, ka an Bɔk sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa tɛmpʋtita'ari bɛ Upper East tudu ni, Ghana ya-dagɔbʋg.
english: Bawku is a town in and the capital of Bawku Municipal District, Upper East Region, in north Ghana, adjacent to the border with Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Bawku Central constituency dinɛ bɛ Bawku Municipal district ka bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, dinɛ bɛ Ghana la.
english: Bawku Central is located in the Bawku Municipal district of the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Fassi ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la (2004 parliamentary election la), ba da buak Pusiga constituency yi Bawku Central constituency dinɛ ka ba da buon ye Bawku East District la.
english: Prior to the 2004 parliamentary election, the Pusiga constituency was carved out of the pre-existing Bawku Central constituency in what was then known as the Bawku East District.

kusaal: Onɛ an wadmaani tis Bawku Central constituency nannanna anɛ Mahama Ayariga onɛ ka ba da vɔɔt o yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadis piinɛ yi vɔɔtʋgin la (December 2020 elections).
english: The current MP is Mahama Ayariga who was elected in the December 2020 elections.

kusaal: Ayariga da anɛ wadmaani tis Bawku Central constituency din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005) amaa ka da li yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii vɔɔtʋg la (2008 Elections) tis Adamu Dramani Sakande onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP nid la.
english: Ayariga was the member of Ghana's parliament for the Bawku Central constituency from 2005 but lost his seat in the 2008 Elections to Adamu Dramani Sakande of the NPP.

kusaal: Ayariga da lɛn di kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yi vɔɔtʋg la (2012 General Elections) ni.
english: Ayariga recaptured the seat in the 2012 General Elections.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o an wadmaani tis constituency la Ghana fourth, sixth, seventh nɛ eighth parliament la Ghana fourth Republic la ni.
english: He has been elected as the member of parliament for this constituency in the fourth, sixth, seventh and eighth parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana Supreme Court da kpari Adamu Dramani Sakande sanriga yʋma ayi (2 years) din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi' la nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi la daar (27 July 2012).
english: Adamu Dramani Sakande was jailed for 2 years by the Supreme Court of Ghana for forgery on 27 July 2012.

kusaal: Nɛ' yinɛ Mr Sumaila Biebel onɛ kuosid niigi, da mɔr pian'ad la keŋ kɔɔtʋ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni pa'al ye Dramani da pʋ mɔr suor ye o nya' wadmaana ka o mɔri British nɛ Burkinabé passport.
english: This follows a case brought in the High court by Mr Sumaila Biebel, a cattle dealer in 2009 stating that Dramani did not qualify to be an MP as he held both a British and a Burkinabé passport.

kusaal: Ofis tita'ar linɛ an Bawku Municipal Assembly la bɛnɛ Bawku linɛ bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: The seat is located within the Bawku Municipal District in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la pʋ lɛn zu'oe sʋ'ʋlim la nii din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi vɔɔtʋg la (2004 election).
english: The current constituency is thus smaller in area than that preceding the 2004 election.

kusaal: Kʋk la da lieb zaalim ban da mɔr Adamu keŋ kɔɔt ka ba kpɛn'ɛs o sanriga ye o anɛ tensi'a nid ka di gɛɛns Ghana wada gbaʋŋ la.
english: The seat became vacant when Adamu was convicted and jailed by a court for having stood for the election while being the citizen of another country which is against the Ghana constitution.

kusaal: Li da tɛŋin anɛ Bawku East 1439 yʋʋm dinɛ ka Legislative Instrument (L.I) da pʋdi li, ka 1988 li da anɛ district ma'a, ka piresiden John Agyekum Kufuor yʋ'ʋn da kena pʋdʋgi li Ya-dagɔbʋg la ni yʋ'ʋn paam Garu-Tempane District August 2004; ka dinɛ yʋ'ʋn da kpɛlim la ka kilim Bawku Municipal District.
english: Originally created as an ordinary district assembly in 1988 when it was known as Bawku East District; which was established by Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 1439, until the southern part of the district was split off by a decree of president John Agyekum Kufuor in August 2004 to create Garu-Tempane District; thus the remaining part was elevated to municipal district assembly status on the same year to become Bawku Municipal District.

kusaal: 28 June 2012, ba da lɛm pʋdʋg zin'is ayi' paam Binduri District yi Ya-tuon nɛ Pusiga District yi Ya-nya'aŋ; ka dinɛ kpɛlim la an Bawku Minicipal District.
english: However, on 28 June 2012, two parts of the district were later split off to create Binduri District (from the west) and Pusiga District (from the east) respectively; thus the remaining part has been retained as Bawku Municipal District.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga Nidib nɛ ya kaanlʋg la pa'al ye Bawku Municipal Distrct mɔr nidib kal anɛ tusa piswai nɛ nii, kɔbis nu nɛ pistan' nɛ nii dinɛ zi'eni tis awai du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin nimbanɛ bɛ Upper East Region pʋʋgin wʋsa.
english: Bawku Municipal District is one of the fifteen districts in Upper East Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Dap anɛ piasnaasi nɛ nii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (48.0%) ka pʋ'ab an pisnu' nɛ ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (52.0%).
english: Males constitute 48.0 percent and females represent 52.0 percent.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋgin, nidib pistan' nɛ ayuobʋ du'ali anaasi (36.4%) bɛ tenkpɛŋ ka pisyuobʋ nɛ atan du'ali ayuobʋ (63.6%) bɛ tempʋʋgin.
english: 36.4 percent of the population is rural and 63.6 percent is urban.

kusaal: Di tɔdnɛ nɛ Pusiga District lɛbid Ya-datiʋŋ, Binduri District lɛbid Ya-dagɔbʋg, Garu- Tempane District lɛbid Ya-nya'aŋ nɛ Bawku West District lɛbid Ya-tuon baba.
english: It shares boundaries with Pusiga District to the north, Binduri District to the south, Garu-Tempane District to the east and Bawku West District to the west.

kusaal: Nɛ wala wʋsa, ba nidib bɛdegʋ bɛ Nouthern nɛ Southern Ghana la'an nɛ Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Togo, Niger nɛ Nigeria.
english: The other tribes in the area are the Bisas, Mossi, Mamprusis, Hausas etc. There are however large immigrant populations from other locations in northern and southern Ghana as well as from Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Togo, Niger and Nigeria.

kusaal: Niib la kanl wʋsa pʋʋgin, banɛ an yʋʋm piinɛ yinne bɛɛ gaad ala, kɔbiga pʋʋgin pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al anii (47.8%) keŋ sakur ka pisnu nɛ yi du'ali ayi (52.2%) pʋ keŋ sakurɛ.
english: Of the population 11 years and above, 47.8% are literate and 52.2% are nonliterate.

kusaal: Bawku Mincipal sʋ'ʋlʋm anɛ dinɛ pɛ'ɛs sʋ'ʋlʋmnam piinɛ anu Upper East,.Ghana nwa ni.
english: Bawku Municipal District is one of the fifteen districts in Upper East Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Minicipal la bɛnɛ Upper East Sʋ'ʋlʋm Ya-nya'aŋ ka Bawku an ba tɛmpʋtita'ar.
english: The municipality is located in the eastern part of Upper East Region and has Bawku as its capital town.

kusaal: Buudbanɛ kpɛlim paas zin'igin la sieba anɛ Mamprusis, Bisas, Mossi, Hausas nɛ banɛ kpɛlim, banɛ kena zin'in.
english: The other tribes in the area are the Bisas, Mossi, Mamprusis, Hausas etc. There are however large immigrant populations from other locations in northern and southern Ghana as well as from Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Togo, Niger and Nigeria.

kusaal: Dap banɛ keŋ sakur kɔbiga pʋʋgin anɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al ayuobʋ (57.6%) gad pʋ'abi an pistan nɛ wai du'ali atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (39.3%).
english: The proportion of literate males is higher (57.6%) than that of females (39.3%).

kusaal: Bʋnkɔbid nwɛnɛ niigi, pɛ'ɛs, bʋʋs, bʋmis nɛ banɛ kpɛlim bɛ district la ni.
english: Livestock such as cattle, sheep, goats, donkeys etc. are also kept in the district.

kusaal: Kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋli an nimbanɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlmin la tʋʋmkpɛŋ, dinɛ ta'as ka nidib pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin tʋmid kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl tʋʋma.
english: Agriculture is the dominant occupation of the people of the municipality, accounting for about 47.0 percent of the total occupation in the municipality.

kusaal: Bawku West District anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm yinne kanɛ pɛ'ɛs sʋ'ʋlʋmnam piinɛ anu la Upper East nwa.
english: Bawku West District is one of the fifteen districts in Upper East Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlʋm kaŋa da pʋdignɛ 1988, dinɛ ka Legislative Instrument (L.I.) yʋ'ʋn da zi'eli di 1442.
english: Originally created as an ordinary district assembly in 1988; which was established by Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 1442.

kusaal: Di bɛnɛ ya-dagɔbʋgi kpi'e Kurkina Faso Republic, ka tɔd nɛ Bindur ya-nya'aŋ, kɛŋ tuonɛ tɔdi bɛ Talensi District nɛ Nabdam District ya-tuon ka bɛ East Mamprusi District ya-datiʋŋ.
english: It is bordered to the north by the Republic of Burkina Faso, to the east by Binduri District, to the west by Talensi District and Nabdam District and to the south by East Mamprusi District.

kusaal: Tɛŋgbaʋŋ la anɛ wʋʋ 1,070 square kilimetres dinɛ an 12% Upper East sʋ'ʋlʋmnɛ.
english: The district covers an area of approximately 1,070 square kilometres, which constitutes about 12% of the total land area of the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Municipal la bɛnɛ ya-nya'aŋ Upper East sʋ'ʋlʋm, ka di tɛŋ̍pʋtita'ar an Zebilla (Sabil)
english: The municipality is located in the eastern part of Upper East Region and has Zebilla as its capital town.

kusaal: Bawku West bɛnɛ Kusaʋg tɛŋgbaʋŋ la ni.
english: Bawku West is part of the traditional kingdom of Kusaug.

kusaal: Di anɛ bab kanɛ pɛ'ɛsa anaasi mɔr tɛŋ paalʋ Upper East sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni.
english: The district covers an area of approximately 1,070 square kilometres, which constitutes about 12% of the total land area of the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Beasts of No Nation anɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu (2015) American zaba di'ema sini ka one sɔbi li la, ka paasi maal ka an li tuongat an Cary Joji Fukunaga.
english: Beasts of No Nation is a 2015 American war drama film written, co-produced, shot, and directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga.

kusaal: Ba da maal di'ema nwa nɛ Ghana ka banɛ paas an Idris Elba, Abraham Attah, Ama K. Abebrese, Grace Nortey, David Dontoh, nɛ Opeyemi Fagbohungbe, sini kan da dɔl nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu (2005) di'ema gbaŋ kanɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr mɛ an ala ka one sɔb an Uzodinma Iweala, ba da pʋd gbaŋ la yʋ'ʋr nɛ dɔlis nɛ Fela Kuti album.
english: Shot in Ghana and starring Idris Elba, Abraham Attah, Ama K. Abebrese, Grace Nortey, David Dontoh, and Opeyemi Fagbohungbe, the film is based on the 2005 novel of the same name by Uzodinma Iweala, the book itself being named after a Fela Kuti album.

kusaal: Ba da gɔsi li yela di'ema nya'ab sankanɛ an 72nd Venice International Film Festival, anina ka Attah ya'a ni bɛ Marcello Mastroianni Award.
english: It was screened in the main competition section of the 72nd Venice International Film Festival, where Attah won the Marcello Mastroianni Award.

kusaal: Ba da gɔsid sini nwa' bɛ 2015 Toronto International Film Festival, ka nɔki li niŋ Netflix ye dunia wʋsa nyɛ ka lʋgir kanɛ buon Bleecker Street la mɛ yɔ'ɔgi li yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu, nwadis piiga ni (October 16, 2015).
english: The film was shown in the Special Presentation section of the 2015 Toronto International Film Festival, and released on Netflix globally and in a limited release by Bleecker Street on October 16, 2015.

kusaal: Elba baŋir la da kɛ ka ba gaŋ o ye o paas banɛ nar ye ba di'e ya'an piini bɛ BAFTA, Golden Globe, Spirit, nɛ SAG Award for Best Supporting Actor, ka o da di'e piini nwa'.
english: Elba's performance earned nominations for the BAFTA, Golden Globe, Spirit, and SAG Award for Best Supporting Actor, winning the latter two.

kusaal: Dasaŋ bil kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Agu, da bɛ nɛ o dʋ'adib nɛ o pitib tɛnkpɛŋ kanɛ bɛ West Africa, linɛ bɛ zaba tɛnsʋk kanɛ ka ECOMOG zabzabidib bɛ.
english: A young boy, Agu, lives in a small West African village with his parents and siblings, located within a "buffer zone" enforced by ECOMOG troops.

kusaal: Ka ba yʋ'ʋr an Native Defense Forces (NDF), ba anɛ tʋbzian'asim dim banɛ bɛ tɛŋin la zabid nɛ gɔmɛna, ba zamis Agu ka o paasi ba nidib ni.
english: The Native Defense Forces (NDF), a rising rebel faction in the country, adopt Agu into their ranks.

kusaal: Zabzabidib nwa' ya'an kanɛ ka ba di zaba pʋʋgin la kɛ ka tʋbzian'asim dim zabzabidib kpɛɛm la buoli ba o zin'igin, anina ka Commandant, nɛ Agu, Strika, nɛ soogia si'eba dɔl o kɛŋ si'al NDF zaba kpɛɛm la, ka o yʋ'ʋr an Dada Goodblood.
english: The battalion's many victories earn them a summons to the rebel headquarters, where the Commandant, accompanied by Agu, Strika, and a few other soldiers, goes to meet with the NDF leader, Dada Goodblood.

kusaal: Ba mɔr banɛ an biis la kɛŋ kpɛn'ɛs winpʋ'ʋsim sakur tɛŋ la zin'ig kanɛ ka zaba kae, amaa ka Preacher nɛ Randy zɔɔ gaad ye ba len kɛŋ zab.
english: The younger members of the battalion are sent to a missionary school in a safe part of the country, while Preacher and Randy decide to run away to rejoin the war.

kusaal: O da nam pʋ pin'ilɛ nɛ yʋma ayuobʋ vɛɛnsig ka o da vɛn'ɛs Sierra Leone Civil War la ka Fukunaga yʋ'ʋn si'al Beasts of No Nation gbaŋ.
english: It was not until after six years of research on the Sierra Leone Civil War that Fukunaga came across the Beasts of No Nation novel.

kusaal: Pian'ad kanɛ ka ba pian'ad di'ema nwa' ni la anɛ gbaŋ ka ba dɔlis, ka ba da sɔbi li Nigerian Pidgin English buudi pian'ad kanɛ buon Krio la ni yiiga.
english: The dialogue in the screenplay is faithful in form to the novel, originally written in a lighter form of Nigerian Pidgin English known as Krio.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan', nwadis anii, dabpisi (August 20, 2013), Idris Elba da paas banɛ na maal sini.
english: On August 20, 2013, Idris Elba joined the cast of the film adaptation.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ naasi, nwadis ayuobʋ, daba yuobʋ daar (June 6, 2014), Ghana sini maanib Ama K. Abebrese, Grace Nortey nɛ David Dontoh da paas sini la ni.
english: On June 6, 2014, Ghanaian actors Ama K. Abebrese, Grace Nortey and David Dontoh joined the film.

kusaal: Red Crown Productions da an banɛ gɔsid sini nwa' nɛ li ligidi yela, ban nɛ Primary Productions and Parliament of Owls.
english: Red Crown Productions was the financier and producer, along with Primary Productions and Parliament of Owls.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ naasi, nwadis ayuobʋ, daba nu daar (June 5, 2014), principal photography da pʋn bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim Ghana.
english: On June 5, 2014, principal photography was underway in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da maal sini la zin'is si'eba Koforidua nɛ Ezile Bay linɛ bɛ Akwidaa.
english: The film was shot at locations in Koforidua and Ezile Bay at Akwidaa.

kusaal: Dan Romer da gɔs sini la vuud yela.
english: Dan Romer scored the film.

kusaal: Netflix da da' ya'an kanɛ ka ba na pa'al sini la tis dunia wʋsa nɛ $12 million.
english: Netflix bought the worldwide distribution rights for around $12 million.

kusaal: ban da nɔki niŋ foon nam ni la da san'am wada kanɛ ye li nar ka ba gɔsi li sini zin'isin dabpiswai la, AMC Cinemas, Carmike Cinemas, Cinemark, nɛ Regal Entertainment Group—sini gɔsig zin'is anaasi banɛ bɛ United States—da yis labaar na ye ba na bas Beasts of No Nation yisig, ka li kɛ ka sini zin'is bibis la ni ma'a yisi di li.
english: Considering the online release a violation of the traditional 90-day release window of exclusivity to theatres, AMC Cinemas, Carmike Cinemas, Cinemark, and Regal Entertainment Group—four of the largest theater chains in the United States—announced that they would boycott Beasts of No Nation, effectively downgrading it to a limited release at smaller and independent theatres.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili gɔsid sini la sini zin'isin UK tɛŋin nɛ (October 16, 2015), bɛ Curzon Cinemas.
english: The film was also theatrically released in the UK on October 16, 2015, in Curzon Cinemas.

kusaal: Gɔmɛna soogianam la kad tita'alnam la yis ka kʋʋd nidib, amaa Agu nyaŋi zɔɔ kpɛn'ɛ mɔɔg.
english: Rebel and government forces fight in and around Agu's village.

english: Agu's battalion is led by the Commandant, who takes Agu under his wing.

kusaal: Ba dɔlis nɛ suor kpi'eŋ hali zamisi ba ka Agu fi'ig sankpan'as kanɛ ka ba gban'ae zug nɛ sʋ'ʋraʋg, ka yʋ'ʋn kilim zabzabid yinne.
english: Agu's battalion is led by the Commandant, who takes Agu under his wing.

english: Strika, another of the Commandant's rape victims, comforts him.

english: Preacher, an older soldier, gives Agu brown-brown to lift his mood.

kusaal: Agu nɛ Strika paasi kʋ zab zaba ka ku nidib bɛdigʋ.
english: Agu and Strika take part in a number of bloody battles and ambushes.

english: The Commandant's lieutenant, Two I-C, will take control of the battalion, and the Commandant will be made Deputy Chief of Security under the leader.

kusaal: Two I-C nɔki ziil Commandant ye one kɛ ka ba kʋʋ o ka nyaan kpi, ka Commandant lɛɛ ye ba gban'e nɛ gɛɛs on ka li ka'a one kʋʋ o.
english: While the adult soldiers spend the night with the brothel's women, one of the women shoots Two I-C. Two I-C accuses the Commandant of orchestrating the incident before dying, while the Commandant insists it must have been a botched attempt against himself.

kusaal: Pʋ'agɔɔndir la si'aki tʋ'as ye li anɛ sapʋ'ad, amaa Commandant nɛ o nidib la kʋ pʋ'ab la ka bas tɛnpʋʋg kan.
english: The prostitute professes that it was an accident, but the Commandant and his men shoot the women and leave the city.

kusaal: Zaba lɔpir nam nɛ diib ka'alim kɛ ka Strika nɛ o taaba bɛdigʋ kpi.
english: Air strikes and supply shortages kill Strika and many others.

english: Following a confrontation between a frustrated Preacher and a paranoid Commandant, Agu and the soldiers abandon the Commandant to surrender, ignoring his warnings that they will merely be thrown in jail and disowned by their families.

english: On May 17, 2014, Participant Media, along with Mammoth Entertainment, came on board to co-finance the film, initially budgeted at $4.3 million but which ultimately cost about $6 million.

kusaal: Pʋtɛn'ɛr kanɛ kɛ ka ba gaŋ soogianam banɛ an biis la fʋʋd la yinɛ Kamajors kʋdʋmin dim tɔn'ɔsnam fʋʋd, ka fʋʋd la bam zanligi lʋsi ba tuoni an gu'ud.
english: The costumes for the child soldiers were inspired by the uniforms of the Kamajors, who wore fabric patches on their shirts as a form of protection.

english: The film was simultaneously released theatrically and online through its subscription video on demand service on October 16, 2015, with Bleecker Street handling the theatrical release.

kusaal: Labaya zin'ig kan gbaŋ la da anɛ ye, "Beasts of No Nation nyɛ gbansɔbid nɛ one gɔsidi li, director Cary Fukunaga ka o tʋm nɛ sini maanib banɛ mɔr baŋir ye bama maal sini kanɛ dɛŋ kanɛ bɛ ninsaalib zaba pʋʋgin." english: The website's critical consensus reads, "Beasts of No Nation finds writer-director Cary Fukunaga working with a talented cast to offer a sobering, uncompromising, yet still somehow hopeful picture of war's human cost." On Metacritic, the film has a score of 79 out of 100, based on 30 critics, indicating "generally favourable" reviews.
