english: As the parliamentary member for Hohoe Constituency, Heloo criticized the president of the Republic of Ghana Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo for not addressing the kidnapping of the Takoradi girls in the 2019 state of the nation address.

kusaal: John Dramani Mahama da gaŋ o yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piin atan (2013) la ni ye o an Minister of Environment, Science and Technology and Innovation nya'andɔl.
english: Heloo was appointed by President John Dramani Mahama in 2013 to serve as deputy Minister of Environment, Science and Technology and Innovation.

kusaal: O da tʋm zin'ikan John Mahama gɔmena la ni din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017).
english: She served in that role in the John Mahama administration from 2013 to 2017.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Heloo nɛ Hohoe, Volta Region, o saam anɛ Rev.
english: Heloo was born in Hohoe, Volta Region, Gold Coast on 24 September 1954, to Rev. E. T. Adiku and Comfort Adiku.

kusaal: Nananna, o anɛ wadmaani tis Hohoe constituency.
english: Hon. Heloo contested the Hohoe constituency parliamentary seat in the Volta Region on the ticket of National Democratic Congress during the 2012 Ghanaian general election and won the parliamentary seat with 40, 486 votes representing 81.58% of the total votes.

kusaal: Heloo anɛ Kristo biig ka mɔr sid.
english: Heloo was a Christian and was married.

kusaal: Bertus Hendrik Basson (o dʋ'am dabisir anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awi, Vaala nwadig, dabpiinɛ ayi daar) O anɛ Ninkanɛ yit South Africa ka dʋgʋd diib, ka sʋ'ʋe diib kuosig zin'ig, ka an kpikpiŋ daan ka lɛn an onɛ tisid labaya bɛ TV ni ka nidib mi' o nɛ ye o anɛ kpɛɛm tis banɛ dʋgʋd diib bɛ Overture linɛ bɛ Stellenbosch, Western Cape.
english: Bertus Hendrik Basson (born 12 April 1979) is a South African chef, restaurateur, entrepreneur and TV personality best known for his work as head chef of Overture in Stellenbosch, Western Cape.

kusaal: Ban da dʋ'a o Cape Town tɛŋin yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai nya'aŋ la, Bertus da nɔbigi bɛ nɛ Polokwane, Nelspruit nɛ Witbank.
english: After being born in Cape Town in 1979, Bertus was brought up in Polokwane, Nelspruit and Witbank.

kusaal: On da nɔbigid la, Basson da tʋm nɛ bɛ Spur Steak Ranches ziid diib nɛ dama tisid banɛ kɛnn anina na da'a si'el, ba mɛ da kuosid dama nɛ biis di'ema la'ad anina.
english: Growing up, Basson also worked as a waiter at Spur Steak Ranches, as well as at a liquor store and a toy store.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ London tɛŋin ka an yʋʋm piinɛ awai ye o tʋm diib kuosig zin'ig kanɛ ka Michelin da sʋ'ʋe ka li buon Chez Bruce.
english: He moved to London at the age of 19 to work at the Michelin starred restaurant Chez Bruce.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi ni, ba da tis Bertus ya'an ye onɛ dʋg diib gaad o taaba bɛ Unilever yʋʋm kan pʋʋgin, ka o nyaan da pin'il o mɛŋ diib kuosig zin'igi bɛ Sapal nwadig la ni.
english: In 2007, Bertus was named Unilever Chef of the Year, before establishing his first restaurant, Overture in November.

kusaal: On da gaad tuoni gɔsid Overture diib kuosig zin'ig la, ba da paam ya'an piini yi Eat Out Guide nɛ Rossouws Restaurant Guide ni.
english: Overture has been awarded distinguished accolades from both the Eat Out Guide and Rossouws Restaurant Guide while under his leadership.

kusaal: O da pian'ad TV di'ema kanɛ buon Top Billing nɛ daar wʋsa sɔnsig di'ema kanɛ da buon Expresso la pʋʋgin.
english: He also appears as a guest on the lifestyle TV show Top Billing as well as the daily talk show Expresso.

kusaal: Basson da di ya'ani an "Onɛ dʋg diib gaad o taaba" bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ awai South Africa ya'an piini kanɛ ka ba buon EatOut piini la, o tʋʋm kanɛ ka o da tʋm bɛ Eike nɛ Overture ni la yela.
english: Basson was crowned with "Chef of the Year" at the 2019 South African EatOut Awards for his work at Eike and Overture.

kusaal: Bertus Basson da pin'ili tʋm diib tʋʋma nɛ on da an yʋʋm piinɛ ayɔpɔi la saŋa.
english: Bertus Basson began working in the culinary career when he was 17 years old.

kusaal: Basson da pin'il o diib kuosig yiiga linɛ ka o da pʋd ye, Diib wʋsa zin'ig bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu ni.
english: Basson began his first catering business, All Things Culinary, in 2005.

kusaal: Basson da paasi an sariakati bɛ diib dʋgʋb nya'ab pin'ilig yʋʋm la ti paae yʋma anaasi, di'em kaŋa yʋ'ʋr da anɛ The Ultimate Braai Master ka ba yisidi li TV ni bɛ SABC 3.
english: Basson appeared as a judge on Season 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the national cooking show The Ultimate Braai Master on SABC 3.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Betty Nana Efua Krosbi Mensah (lɛn tʋn'e sɔb Crosby bɛɛ Krosby) Nasaa nwadisa Anii la dabpisi nɛ awai yʋʋm 1980 (August 29, 1980) la ni.
english: Betty Nana Efua Krosbi (also spelled Crosby and Krosby) Mensah, (born August 29, 1980) is a Ghanaian politician and a former Member of Parliament for the 7th and 8th parliament of the republic of Ghana for the Afram Plains North constituency in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: O paasnɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg (National Democratic Congress) la ni.
english: She is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Mensah nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii li Nwadisa anii la dab pisi nɛ awai daar (29 August 1980) Donkorkrom, bɛ Eastern Region.
english: Mensah was born on 29 August 1980 in Donkorkrom, Eastern Region.

kusaal: O mɔr bachelor's degree in Business Administration yi Zenith University College, nɛ Higher National Diploma (HND) in Accounting, Koforidua Technical University la ni.
english: She holds a bachelor's degree in Business Administration from the Zenith University College, and a Higher National Diploma (HND) in Accounting from Koforidua Technical University.

kusaal: Fassi ka o lieb Wadmaan la, Mensah da anɛ managing director tis Best Pat Ghana Limited din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan' la (2013) paae yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: Before she became a Member of Parliament, Mensah was the managing director of Best Pat Ghana Limited from the year 2013 to the year 2016.

kusaal: O da lɛn an Second Deputy Coordinator tis National Youth Employment din yi yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ awai (2009) paae yʋʋm tusaayi' nɛ piinɛ atan' (2013).
english: She also served as the Second Deputy Coordinator for the National Youth Employment from 2009 to 2013.

kusaal: Mensah da lɛn an Gender and Development Coordinator tis Ghana Cooperative Credit Union yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ atan' (2003) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: Mensah was also the Gender and Development Coordinator of Ghana Cooperative Credit Union from 2003 to 2005.

kusaal: O anɛ Vice President tis Parliamentarians Forum, Ghana Chapter.
english: She is the Vice President of the Young Parliamentarians Forum, Ghana Chapter.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni, o da dii Afram Plains North Constituency sʋ'ʋlim Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anii nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ atan' (18,543) ka li pa'al ye kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da paamnɛ vaar pisyuobʋ nɛ anii du'al pistan' (68.30%) ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg NPP nid la, Isaac Ofori-Koree paam vɔɔt tusa anii nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ anu (8,605) ka li pa'al ye kɔbiga pʋʋgin o paamnɛ vaar pistan' nɛ yinne du'al pisyɔpɔi (31.70%) ka NDP nid la, Ferguson Asare paam nɛɛm (0) dinɛ an nɛɛm bɔbiga pʋʋgin (0%).
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general election, she again won the Afram Plains North Constituency parliamentary seat with 18,543 votes making 68.30% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Isaac Ofori-Koree had 8,605 votes making 31.70% of the total votes cast and the NDP parliamentary candidate Ferguson Asare had 0 vote making 0% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ Krosbi Mensah, o anɛ yiiga Wadmaani tis Afram Plains Constituency la pʋ'ayua.
english: She is the daughter of Krosbi Mensah, the first MP for Afram Plains Constituency.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig ka pʋ'ʋsid nɛ Roman Catholic.
english: She is a Christian and worships as a Roman Catholic.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadisa ayɔpɔi la nii (July 2021), Mensah da nɔk kompiuta linɛ an laptop tis Michael Awingura, onɛ an sakur bili bɛ University of Ghana.
english: In July 2021, Mensah donated a laptop to Michael Awingura, a student of the University of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tisi Afram Plains North constituency linɛ bɛ Eastern region Ghana sʋ'ʋlimin.
english: Betty Nana Efua Krosbi (also spelled Crosby and Krosby) Mensah, (born August 29, 1980) is a Ghanaian politician and a former Member of Parliament for the 7th and 8th parliament of the republic of Ghana for the Afram Plains North constituency in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, 2016 Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋgin la, Afram Plains kʋk la, Mensah da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anii nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (8,121) yi vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (23,606).
english: In Ghana's 2016 general elections for the Parliamentary seat of Afram Plains, Mensah pulled a total vote count of 18,121 out of 23,606 votes cast representing 78.44% to beat Isaac Ofori-Koree of the New Patriotic Party who had 4,795 votes making 20.8% of the total votes cast, Cornelius Agbeku of the National Democratic Party who had 94 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast, and Micheal Ampontia of the Convention People's Party who had 91 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast to win the seat in 7th Parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Dina pa'al ye vaar kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da paamnɛ vaar piisyɔpɔi nɛ pa'ali (78.44%) ka Isaac Ofori-Koree onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg Paati la, (New Patriotic Party) nid la paam tusa anaasi nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piswai nɛ anu (4,795).
english: In Ghana's 2016 general elections for the Parliamentary seat of Afram Plains, Mensah pulled a total vote count of 18,121 out of 23,606 votes cast representing 78.44% to beat Isaac Ofori-Koree of the New Patriotic Party who had 4,795 votes making 20.8% of the total votes cast, Cornelius Agbeku of the National Democratic Party who had 94 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast, and Micheal Ampontia of the Convention People's Party who had 91 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast to win the seat in 7th Parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Li pa'al ye kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da paamnɛ vaar pisi nɛ pa'ali (20.8%), Cornelius Agbeku onɛ zi'eni tis Danwan Pielig Paati, National Democratic Party nid la da paamnɛ vɔɔt piswai nɛ anaasi (94) dinɛ an nɛɛm du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.4%) ka Micheal Ampontia onɛ an Convention People's Party nid la paam piswai nɛ yinne (91) dinɛ an nɛɛm du'ali anaasi (0.4%) la.
english: In Ghana's 2016 general elections for the Parliamentary seat of Afram Plains, Mensah pulled a total vote count of 18,121 out of 23,606 votes cast representing 78.44% to beat Isaac Ofori-Koree of the New Patriotic Party who had 4,795 votes making 20.8% of the total votes cast, Cornelius Agbeku of the National Democratic Party who had 94 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast, and Micheal Ampontia of the Convention People's Party who had 91 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast to win the seat in 7th Parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Mensah da ka dii keŋ paas Gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: In Ghana's 2016 general elections for the Parliamentary seat of Afram Plains, Mensah pulled a total vote count of 18,121 out of 23,606 votes cast representing 78.44% to beat Isaac Ofori-Koree of the New Patriotic Party who had 4,795 votes making 20.8% of the total votes cast, Cornelius Agbeku of the National Democratic Party who had 94 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast, and Micheal Ampontia of the Convention People's Party who had 91 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast to win the seat in 7th Parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Mensah mɔr sid nɛ biig yinne.
english: Mensah is married with one child.

kusaal: Biakoye Constituency anɛ Ghana Parliament constituency nam la yinne.
english: The Biakoye constituency is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Di dagɔbʋg anɛ Krachi East district, tuon anɛ Volta Kɔldaʋg, datiʋŋ anɛ Hohoe Municipal nɛ Kpando Municipal district dinne bɛ Volta Region ka nya'aŋ an Ghana nɛ Togo titɔdig.
english: To the north is the Krachi East district, to the west, the Volta River, to the south the Hohoe Municipal and Kpando Municipal districts which are both in the Volta Region and to the east, the Ghana - Togo border.

kusaal: Di bɛnɛ Biakoye districti bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: It is located in the Biakoye district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛ nɛ Biakoye district bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: The constituency is located within the Biakoye district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la da bɛnɛ Volta Region ka ba naam pʋdig Region paala dɔlisid yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi (2012) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: The constituency was originally located within the Volta Region of Ghana until new Regions were created following the December 2018 referendum.

kusaal: Bilia yiti anɛ biig kani dua zina to paae nwadis ayi' bɛɛ atan'.
english: The term infant is typically applied to very young children under one year of age; however, definitions may vary and may include children up to two years of age.

kusaal: On da tʋm The Dorchester linɛ London nya'aŋ la, Gallagher da lɛb South Africa yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' ni ka an banɛ dʋgʋd kpɛɛm bɛ hotel chain Southern Sun.
english: After having worked at The Dorchester in London, Gallagher arrived in South Africa in 1973 to take up an executive sous-chef position with local hotel chain Southern Sun.

kusaal: Lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi ni sa ka o da an kpɛɛm ka lɛn an onɛ pian'adi tisid Southern Sun Hotel Group kanɛ bɛ Johannesburg; lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu ni, ka o an kpɛɛm tis banɛ gɔsid diib dʋgʋb titua yela bɛ Johannesburg, ka lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ ni, ka o da an kugraani tis sakur kanɛ zamisid tɛŋ kaar yela nɛ nidib sʋŋir yela bɛ Johannesburg.
english: From 2004 he was Director of Communication and PR for the Southern Sun Hotel Group in Johannesburg; from 2005, executive director for the Centre for Culinary Excellence in Johannesburg, and from 2006, Chairman of the School for Tourism and Hospitality Studies in Johannesburg.

kusaal: Gallagher da kɛŋ sakur ka paam gbaŋ kanɛ ka ba buon Doctorate bɛ diib dʋgʋb pʋʋgin bɛ Johnson & Wales University linɛ bɛ Miami la.
english: Gallagher earned a Doctorate of Culinary Arts from the Johnson & Wales University, Miami.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi ni, ba da gaŋ Gallagher ye o an kpɛɛm tis lʋgir kanɛ gɔsid diib dʋgʋb yela sʋ'ʋlim, o an ba kpɛɛm wala paae yʋma pisi nɛ yinnɛ nɛ ban ti tis o na'asi bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ atan' ni.
english: In 1982, Gallagher was elected president of the South African Chefs Association (SACA), and held that position for 21 years before becoming its honorary life president in 2003.

kusaal: Sansi'en na sa di da anɛ yinne nɛ Bawaku municipal district 1988 sa'aŋa; di yʋ'ʋn daa ti kɛna paae saŋa kanɛ an ye ba pʋdʋgi di yʋ'ʋn paam Binduri district n yi (Ya- tuona) nɛ Pusiga district n yi (Ya- nya'aŋ) 28 June 2012 yʋʋŋ.
english: Originally it was formerly part of the then-larger Bawku Municipal District in 1988; until two parts of the district were later split off to create Binduri District (from the west) and Pusiga District (from the east) respectively on 28 June 2012.

kusaal: Binduri anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm kanɛ pɛ'ɛs sʋ'ʋlʋm piinɛ anu (15) la zug Upper East sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana nwa ni.
english: Binduri District is one of the fifteen districts in Upper East Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba sʋ'ʋlʋm la'asʋg zin'iŋ kanɛ ka ba buon ye 'District assembly' la bɛnɛ Ya-nya'aŋ Upper East sʋ'ʋlʋm ka Binduri an di teŋpʋʋg tita'ar.
english: Binduri District is one of the fifteen districts in Upper East Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Binduri da paasnɛ Bawku Municipal district bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana amaa din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa yuobʋ la ni (June 2012) ka di liebi di mɛŋ district.
english: Binduri was part of in the Bawku Municipal District of the Upper East Region of Ghana but has since June 2012 become a full district.

kusaal: Binduri tɔdnɛ nɛ Garu Tempane District lɛbid ya-nya'aŋ nɛ ya-tuon, Bawku Municipality lɛbid ya-datiʋŋ baba nɛ Bawku West District bɛbid ya-tuona baba bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Binduri shares boundaries with Garu Tempane district to the east and south, Bawku municipality to the north and Bawku West district to the west in the Upper East region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di gaŋid nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaani zi'eni tisi ba wadmaannib yin la dɔlisid Ghana vɔɔtʋg suor.
english: Binduri is a constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Bismark Tetteh Nyarko (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan Nwadis piinɛ ayi dabpiinɛ anu daar, 15 December 1973) ka o an Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tis Upper Manya Krobo Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: Bismark Tetteh Nyarko (born 15 December 1973) is a Ghanaian politician who currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Upper Manya Krobo Constituency.

kusaal: Bissa (bɛɛ Bisa (yinnɛ), Bisan, Bissanno (babig)), anɛ Mande buudi banɛ bɛ ya'dagɔbʋg tɛnsʋk baba Burkina Faso, ya'datiʋŋ-nya'aŋ Ghana nɛ ya'datiʋŋ baba Togo.
english: Bissa or Bisa (endonym: Bɩsa) is the language of the Bissa people, a Mande ethnic group of south-central Burkina Faso, northeastern Ghana and the northernmost tip of Togo.

kusaal: Ba buudi pian'ad Bissa, anɛ Mande language buudi pian'ad kanɛ wan pian'a si'eba bɛ Borgu Kingdom kʋdʋg kanɛ bɛ ya'nya'aŋ-datiʋŋ Benin ya'nya'aŋ-dagɔbʋg Nigeria, ka ba si'eba an Busa, Boko, nɛ Kyenga.
english: It is a Mande language that is related to, but not the same as, a cluster of languages in the old Borgu Kingdom area of Northeast Benin and Northwest Nigeria, including Busa, Boko, and Kyenga.

kusaal: Yʋʋr kanɛ ka lɛn mɔri buon Bissa nam anɛ Busansi, ka banɛ buon ala anɛ Mossi nɛ Kusasi pian'ad ni, bɛɛ ban buol ye Busanga.
english: Alternate names for the Bissa are Busansi, which is used by the Mossi people and Kusasi people, or Busanga.

kusaal: Si'eba mɛ sɔbidi li ye Bisa, ka Mossi pian'ad ni an Busansi (babig) bɛɛ Busanga (yinnɛ); nwa' bɛɛ li kɔn' nɛ Bisa pian'ad kanɛ bɛ Zambia bɛɛ Busa pian'ad kanɛ bɛ Nigeria nɛ Benin la.
english: It can also be spelled Bisa, and the name in the Mossi language is Busansi (singular) or Busanga (plural); This should not be confused with the Bisa language of Zambia or the Busa language of Nigeria and Benin.

kusaal: Burkina Faso tɛŋin, ba pian'ad Bissa bɛ Boulgou, Koulpélogo, nɛ Kouritenga tɛɛn banɛ bɛ Centre-Est Region, ka lɛn bɛ Bazaga nɛ Zoundwéogo sʋ'ʋlim nam banɛ bɛ Centre–Sud Region (Garango, Gomboussougou, Zabré, nɛ Tenkodogo tɛnpʋʋs), nɛ tɛŋ titɔndig baba linɛ bɛ Ganzargou Province Plateau-Central Region.
english: In Burkina Faso, Bissa is spoken in Boulgou, Koulpélogo, and Kouritenga Provinces of the Centre-Est Region, in Bazaga and Zoundwéogo Provinces of the Centre–Sud Region (Garango, Gomboussougou, Zabré, and Tenkodogo Cities), and in the Boudry Department of Ganzargou Province of the Plateau-Central Region.

kusaal: Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ni, ba pian'ad Bissa bɛ Bawku Municipal District, si'eba mɛ bɛ districts nam anu banɛ bɛ Bawku traditional sʋ'ʋlim linɛ bɛ Upper East Region ka bam mɛ bɛ North East Region.
english: In Ghana, Bissa is spoken in Bawku Municipal District, some other parts five districts in Bawku traditional area in the Upper East Region and also some parts in the North East Region.

kusaal: Togo tɛŋin, ba pian'ad Bissa bɛnɛ Tône Prefecture linɛ bɛ Savanes Region la.
english: In Togo, Bissa is spoken in Tône Prefecture of the Savanes Region.

kusaal: Nidib si'eba mɛ pian'ad Bissa bɛ Ivory Coast.
english: There are also some Bissa speakers in Ivory Coast.

kusaal: Li paas nɛ Eastern Mande buudi pian'ad ni, linɛ ka buudi babig pian'ad paasi li pʋʋgin, banɛ ka ba pian'adi bɛ Volta River nɛ Borgu Kingdom, ka ba si'eba an Boko, Busa, Samo, nɛ Bokobaru.
english: It is part of the Eastern Mande group, which also includes several other languages spoken across the Volta River and the Borgu Kingdom, including Boko, Busa, Samo, and Bokobaru.

kusaal: Barka bɛɛ Baraka (ka si'eba buon Eastern Bissa)
english: Barka or Baraka (also known as Eastern Bissa)

kusaal: Lebre bɛɛ Zeba (ka si'eba buon Western Bissa)
english: Lebre or Zeba (also known as Western Bissa)

kusaal: Leere (ka si'eba buon Northern Bissa)
english: Leere (also known as Northern Bissa)

kusaal: Banɛ bɛ ya'tiʋŋ la pian'ad anɛ Lere.
english: To the North the Lere dialect is used.

kusaal: Duoe wala: Domireh ki (lɛbisig: Domireh zain)
english: Good morning: Domireh ki (Response: Domireh zain)

kusaal: Nintaŋ an wala: Sundareh ki (lɛbisig: Sundareh zain)
english: Good afternoon: Sundareh ki (Response: Sundareh zain)

kusaal: Busa nɛ Boko dim, Bissa buudi ayi', yinnɛ bɛnɛ Nigeria ka yinnɛ bɛ Benin kpi'e nɛ Borgu, Nigerian zin'is banɛ an Niger, Kebbi nɛ Kwara nɛ Benin tɛɛns banɛ an Alibori nɛ Borgou.
english: The Busa and Boko peoples, two subgroups of the Bissa people, live in Northwestern Nigeria and Northern Benin near Borgu in the Nigerian States of Niger, Kebbi and Kwara (mostly Bokobaru subgroup) and in the Beninese Departments of Alibori and Borgou.

kusaal: Ban pian'ad nɛ Busa (ka ba lɛn buoni ba Bisã) nɛ Boko (ka ba lɛn buoni ba Boo).
english: They speak Busa (also known as Bisã) and Boko (also known as Boo).

kusaal: Ba buon bama ye Bussawa bɛ Hausa pian'adin.
english: This peoples are referred to as Bussawa in Hausa.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr la sɔbid gbaʋŋin si'em anɛ Bissa.
english: The name is usually spelled Bissa.

kusaal: Bissa buudi ppian'ad la an linɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr yi paalʋ bɛ Mande buudi nam banɛ bɛ Ghana nɛ Togo.
english: Bissa language is the most populous of the Mande languages of Ghana and Togo.

kusaal: Bissa buudi kanɛ ka ba pian'adi li zin'is bɛdigʋ anɛ Barka nɛ Lebre.
english: The most widely spoken dialects of Bissa are Barka and Lebre.

kusaal: Bissa nidib banɛ bɛ ya'nya'aŋ la pian'ad anɛ Barka/Baraka.
english: To the East the Bissa people speak Barka/Baraka.

kusaal: Banɛ bɛ ya'tuona la piana'ad anɛ Lebre/Zeba.
english: To The West people speak Lebre/Zeba.

kusaal: Black Girl anԑ sini kanԑ ka ba da maal 1966, onԑ da sͻbi li ka gͻsi li maalʋg yela anԑ Senegal dim sini maan kanԑ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Ousmane Sembène.
english: 'Black girl of...') is a 1966 drama film, written and directed by Senegalese filmmaker Ousmane Sembène in his feature directorial debut.

kusaal: Li da dͻlis nԑ sͻlima kanԑ bԑ Sembène's 1962 gbaʋŋ Voltaique pʋʋgin, ka li anԑ bʋnlinԑ sit da maal ka ba nͻki li maal sini la.
english: It is based on a short story from Sembène's 1962 collection Voltaique, which was in turn inspired by a real life incident.

kusaal: Lin pin'il si'em anԑ Mbissine Thérèse Diop ka buon o Diouana sini la ni, pʋ'asadir kanԑ yit Senegal tԑŋ kanԑ buon Dakar tu suori kԑŋ Antibes, France, ye o tʋm tʋʋma tis daʋ nԑ o pʋ'a banԑ yit Fariŋ.
english: It stars Mbissine Thérèse Diop as Diouana, a young Senegalese woman who moves from her native Dakar to Antibes, France, to work for a French couple.

kusaal: Black Girl anԑ yiiga sini kanԑ yi Sub-Saharan African ka banԑ maali li yit Africa ka li yʋ'ʋr paae tԑŋ-tԑŋ.
english: Black Girl is often considered the first Sub-Saharan African film by an African filmmaker to receive international attention.

kusaal: Sini la maalig ni, onԑ gban'ad footo ka tʋm nԑ Actualitiés Sénégalaises da nͻk Mbissine Thérèse Diop footo, ka onԑ maan sini ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Sembène nyԑ li, o da kԑŋi sial Diop kati wa'ae Black Girl yela.
english: During casting, a photographer working at the Actualitiés Sénégalaises took a photograph of Mbissine Thérèse Diop, which was seen by filmmaker Sembène, who contacted Diop regarding Black Girl.

kusaal: Onԑ da an kpԑԑm bԑ Ministry of Cooperation's Cinema Bureau da zan'as Black Girl lin wa'am la zug, banԑ da gͻsid sini banԑ ka ba maam Fariŋ buudi pian'ad ni yela ka yͻͻdi ba.
english: The screenplay of Black Girl was rejected by the then-head of the Ministry of Cooperation's Cinema Bureau, which provided funding for French-speaking films, likely because of the film's subject matter.

kusaal: Gbaʋŋ kanԑ ka Jonathan Rosenbaum da sͻb yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ ayͻpͻi ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Movies as Politics, la da pa'al ye Black Girl anԑ sini kanԑ pini sini maalig bԑ sub-Saharan Africa, hali ka onԑ da gͻsi l yela an onԑ ka ba dʋ'a o ka o nͻbig Africa sʋ'ʋlim.
english: In his 1997 book Movies as Politics, Jonathan Rosenbaum argues that Black Girl is the symbolic genesis of sub-Saharan African filmmaking, at least to the extent that its authorship belonged to a born-and-bred African.

kusaal: Amaa, on kԑŋ paae Antibes la, Diouana nyԑ namisigi yi pʋ'a la nԑ o sid la ni, ba kԑ ka o tʋm tʋʋma wan wʋʋ yamig nԑ.
english: However, upon her arrival in Antibes, Diouana experiences harsh treatment from the couple, who force her to work as a servant.

kusaal: Sini la pin'il nԑ ka Diouana tԑn'ԑsid o bԑilim kanԑ ka o bԑ France, tʋm yammʋg tʋʋma nԑ on da bԑ o mԑŋ tԑŋin Senegal la.
english: The plot continually shifts back and forth between Diouana's present life in France, where she works as a domestic servant, and flashbacks to her previous life in Senegal.

kusaal: Daar yinnԑ ka Fariŋ dim pʋ'a kanԑ ka ba buon o 'Madame' kԑn ba tԑŋin la na bͻͻd tʋmtʋm ka gaŋ Diouana yii o pʋ'ataaba banԑ da bͻͻd tʋʋma ni.
english: Madame treats her unkindly, and Diouana is confused about her role.

kusaal: Pin'ilig la, Madame da nͻk Diouana tʋʋma ye o an biyuol bԑ Dakar.
english: Initially, Madame hires Diouana to care for her children in Dakar.

kusaal: Diouana da tis pʋ'a la piigin kanԑ ka o da da' dasaŋbil sͻ' ni 50 guineas, ka ba nͻki li ya'ali ba yin la.
english: As a gift, Diouana gives her employers a traditional mask that she had bought from a small boy for 50 guineas, and they display it in their home.

kusaal: Monsieur nԑ Madame da gban'a ye ba mͻr Diouana kԑŋ ka o tʋm tʋʋma bԑ France.
english: Monsieur and Madame then offer Diouana a job working for them in France.

kusaal: Amaa on da paae France, o da pʋ yit yin la yi'iŋͻ, o da bԑnԑ yin la dʋgʋd diib ka piisid ma'a—anina ka'a wan wʋʋ on da bԑ Senegal ka nyaŋidi yit yi'iŋ la.
english: However, in France, she does not leave the apartment and only cooks and cleans inside the house—a stark contrast to her previous life in Senegal, where she spent much time outdoors.

kusaal: Diouana ma da sͻb gbaʋŋi tͻlim tud na ka Monsieur karimi li tis o.
english: Due to her illiteracy, when a letter is sent to Diouana by her mother, Madame and Monsieur take it upon themselves to write Diouana's response for her, asking her to correct them if they get anything wrong.

kusaal: Diouana da aans gbaʋŋ la bas.
english: Diouana is not dead.

kusaal: Sini la naar la Monsieur da lԑb Senegal nԑ Diouana baagi, piini kanԑ ka o daa tisi ba la, nԑ ligidi ye o tis o yir dim.
english: The film ends with Monsieur journeying to Senegal to return Diouana's suitcase, mask, and money to her family.

kusaal: Diop yir-dim da pʋ siak ye Diop maal sini, amaa, Sembène kԑn la da kԑ ka Diop si'ak ye o na paasi maal.
english: Diop's family was very opposed to Diop's interest in film, but after Sembène visited with Diop she decided to accept the role.

kusaal: Sini la tita'am da nͻk nԑ Senegal, ka Diouana pian'ad la ka sͻ' da tuasi lԑbis Fariŋ buudi pian'ad ni.
english: While Senegal had gained independence in 1960 (before the film takes place), colonial oppression persists throughout the film.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayuobʋ k aba da sͻns nԑ Diop la, o da pa'al ye fuud banԑ ka o yԑ bԑ sini la ni la wʋsa da anԑ o mԑŋi maal, li ya'a ka'a fuug kanԑ da lʋm la ma'anԑ, bͻzugͻ, o da anԑ onԑ sԑԑnd fuud.
english: According to a 2016 interview of Diop, all of the outfits she wears in the film except for the polka-dot dress were her own, as she was a dressmaker.

kusaal: Linԑ paas ya'as, sini la ka Senegal dim pʋ'a sͻ' da pa'ali li gbin ye li pa'al nԑ nidib nԑ tԑԑns banԑ ka na'asaanam di'e ba tԑŋ ka namisidi ba la yela.
english: While Senegal had gained independence in 1960 (before the film takes place), colonial oppression persists throughout the film.

kusaal: Black Star Square, linɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr lɛm buon ye Independence Square la, anɛ nimbabig la'asʋg zin'igi bɛ Accra, Ghana, n tɔnd Accra niŋwisigir di'ema zin'ig nɛ Nkwame Nkrumah Memorial Park la.
english: Black Star Square, also known as Independence Square, is a public square in Accra, Ghana, bordered by the Accra Sports Stadium and the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park.

kusaal: Gold Coast linɛ yʋ'ʋŋ an nananna Ghana independence yan'aŋ la, Kwame Nkrumah da an yiiga piram minista nɛ pirɛsiden yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (1957) saŋkan.
english: In 1957, Kwame Nkrumah became the first prime minister and president of Gold Coast, now Ghana, after gaining independence from the British.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da gaad Ghana dim tuon ka ba paam Independence n yi Britain dim nu'usin dinɛ ka ba da buon ye Gold Coast la.
english: Kwame Nkrumah was the one who led Ghana, formerly Gold Coast, to gain independence from Britain.

kusaal: Linɛ zi'ie viki ka pʋ tanmid anɛ Golden Jubilee, Ghana yʋma pisnu (50th) annivɛsiri Independence la'asʋg dinɛ ka ti faan ti mɛŋi yi British dim nu'usin la.
english: A particularly notable parade was the Golden Jubilee, which was Ghana's 50th anniversary of independence from British colonial rule.

kusaal: Golden Jubilee la'asʋg di'ema la da naamnɛ March 6, 2007 ka di da anɛ Pirɛsiden John Kuffour da gaad tuon.
english: The Golden Jubilee celebration occurred on March 6, 2007, and it was led by President John Kuffour.

kusaal: Independence Square la ni mɔr zin'isa, dinɛ na yaŋŋi nɔk nidib tusa pistan (30,000).
english: In Independence Square there are stands that can seat 30,000 people.

kusaal: Banɛ an Independence Arch nɛ, Liberation Dabisir Monument nɛ Black Star Square za'anɔɔr la, ba lɛm buoni li nɛ ye Black Star Monuments.
english: This includes the Independence Arch, the Liberation Day Monument, and the Black Star Gate, also known as the Black Star Monument.

kusaal: March 24, Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998), nidib da la'asi tʋʋg tusa kɔbisnu square la ni ye ba di'e U.S Pirɛsidɛn kudug Bill Clinton.
english: On March 24, 1998, over 500,000 people gathered at the square to welcome former U.S. President Bill Clinton and First Lady Hillary Clinton.

kusaal: August 10, yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayi (2012), ba da maal Ghana pirɛsidɛn kudug John Atta Mills kuur la nɛ Square la ni.
english: The state funerals for presidents John Atta Mills and Jerry Rawlings, and for vice-president Aliu Mahama, were held at the square.

kusaal: Black Star Square anɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka yʋʋm wusa ka ba maan Independence di'ema nɛ di'em titada bani bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Black Star Square, also known as Independence Square, is a public square in Accra, Ghana, bordered by the Accra Sports Stadium and the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park.

kusaal: Black Star Square bɛnɛ 28th Febuary suor la nɛ Accra ya dagɔbʋg baba la tɛŋsʋk.
english: Black Star Square, also known as Independence Square, is a public square in Accra, Ghana, bordered by the Accra Sports Stadium and the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da tis nɔɔr ka ba mɛ' Black Star Square la ye ba nɔki di'em tɛŋ la Independence dabisir di'ema la.
english: Black Star Square, also known as Independence Square, is a public square in Accra, Ghana, bordered by the Accra Sports Stadium and the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park.

kusaal: Di da sialnɛ nɛ Queen Elizabeth onɛ pɛɛsa ayi (II) o kʋg zug la kɛn saŋŋa Ghana na.
english: It was completed in 1961, in time for the state visit of Queen Elizabeth II to Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ yinnɛ saŋŋa ka ba da mɛ' Black Star Square la naae.
english: Construction ended in 1961, and it was named Black Star Square.

kusaal: Black Star Square anɛ Ghana dim Independence la'asʋg zin'ig kani ɛnti lut 6th March yʋʋm wʋsa.
english: Black Star Square is a site for Ghana's Independence Day parade, which falls on 6 March every year.

kusaal: Sanlim soogia dinɛ ka ba ya'abi zi'eli kpa' Independence Arch la pa'annɛ Ghana nidib banɛ da kɔ'ɔŋi ba nyɔvʋya Asʋ'ʋ-m-mɛŋ zaba la ni.
english: A statue of a soldier facing the Independence Arch symbolizes the Ghanaians who lost their lives fighting for Ghana's independence.

kusaal: November 18, yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayi (2012), ba da maal Ghana Pirɛsidɛn nyaŋdɔl kudug Aliu Mahama kuur la nɛ Square la ni.
english: The state funerals for presidents John Atta Mills and Jerry Rawlings, and for vice-president Aliu Mahama, were held at the square.

kusaal: January 27, yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ la ni, Ghana Pirɛsidɛn kudug Jerry Rawlings kuur la, Square la ni ka ba da maal.
english: The state funerals for presidents John Atta Mills and Jerry Rawlings, and for vice-president Aliu Mahama, were held at the square.

kusaal: Black Volta bɛɛ Mouhoun anɛ kɔlʋg kanɛ pʋbigidi yit Burkina Faso ka di wa'alim na an nwɛnɛ km tusir yinne, kɔbistan nɛ pisnu nɛ yi' (1,352 km) bɛɛ mɛɛla kɔbisnii nɛ pisnaasi (840 mi) kem paae atɛʋk piel (White Volta) bɛ Dagbon, Ghana, Volta Lake la naarin.
english: The Black Volta or Mouhoun (French: Volta noire) is a river that flows through Burkina Faso for approximately 1,352 km (840 mi) to the White Volta in Dagbon, Ghana, the upper end of Lake Volta.

kusaal: Black Volta la ku'om yitnɛ Cascades Region bɛ Burkina Faso la, kpi'e nɛ Mount Tenakourou, teŋ la wa'alim naarin.
english: The source of the Black Volta is in the Cascades Region of Burkina Faso, close to Mount Tenakourou, the highest point of the country.

kusaal: Ghana pʋʋgin, di anɛ titɔdʋg tis Savannah nɛ Bono region nam.
english: Within Ghana, it marks the border between the Savannah and Bono regions.

kusaal: Bui Mu'ar la, hydroelectric power plant, mɛnɛ kɔlʋg la ni, kpɛm bɛ Bui National Park dagɔbʋg baba, ka kɔlʋg la pʋdigi di ay.
english: The Bui Dam, a hydroelectric power plant, is built on the river, just south of the Bui National Park, which the river bisects.

kusaal: Di teŋir bi'ela anɛ Ghana nɛ Burkina Faso titɔdʋg, ka Burkina Faso mɛ bɛ Côte d'Ivoire nɛ Ghana titɔdʋgʋn.
english: The river flows generally southward, then forms international boundaries between Ghana and Burkina Faso, and between Ghana and Ivory Coast.

kusaal: Boadu anɛ yʋ'ʋr kanɛ gbin ni an tɔn'ɔs kanɛ sʋŋid, onɛ mɔr paŋ.
english: Boadu is a surname meaning Helper hunter the one who is strong.

kusaal: Boakye-Yiadom anɛ yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba pʋd nidibi bɛ Ghana.
english: Boakye-Yiadom is a Ghanaian surname.

kusaal: Boamah anɛ kambʋŋ bɛɛ Akan yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba mɔri pʋd ka li gbin an tɛɛns sʋŋid'.
english: Boamah is a surname of Akan origin meaning 'helper of nations'.

kusaal: Ba nyɛ dizora banɛ ka ba gɔs ka ye di paae yʋʋma tusa pistan' banɛ gaad la (30,000) ka di bɛ Europe nɛ Austrilia su'ulim ka di taae kuga banɛ ka ba da mɔri nɛɛmid bunbuttta.
english: Evidence from 30,000 years ago in Europe and Australia revealed starch residue on rocks used for pounding plants.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a tɛn'ɛsi di yɛla bɛdigʋ, bodobodo banɛ ka ba kuosid la ba paasid si'elnami di pʋʋgin ye ba paasi di malisim, tɛbisim, si'im, di yuugir, di ningbiŋ maalig, ka mɛ ye ba kɛ ka di maalig an na'ana'.
english: This produces a more flavorful bread with better texture.

kusaal: Bole anɛ tempʋbil ka an tempʋtita'ari tis Bole district, district kanɛ bɛ Savannah Region sʋ'ʋlim, northern Ghana.
english: Bole is a small town and is the capital of Bole district, a district in the Savannah Region of northern Ghana.

kusaal: Bole bɛnɛ suorini tɔ'ɔŋ Sawla tempʋʋg nɛ Bamboi tempʋʋg.
english: Bole is connected by road to the town of Sawla and the town of Bamboi.

kusaal: Bole an zin'ikanɛ ka Bole District Hospital nɛ post office bɛ.
english: Bole is home to the Bole District Hospital and post office.

kusaal: Bole District labisim anɛ wʋʋ 4800 km2 ka di nidib kal an wʋʋ tusa pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (87,656).
english: The Bole District covers an area of 4800 km2 land mass and has a population of about 87,656.

kusaal: Suor ken bɛ Bolgatanga ken teŋpʋtita'ara wʋʋ Accra, Kumasi, Mim, Ahafo, Cape Coast, Sunyani, Tamale, Tema, Ho, Wa, Elubo, Aflao, and Techiman.
english: There is public transportation from Bolgatanga to major cities such as Accra, Kumasi, Mim, Ahafo, Cape Coast, Sunyani, Tamale, Tema, Ho, Wa, Elubo, Aflao, and Techiman.

kusaal: Bolgatanga Nursing Training College (dab nɛ pʋ'ab)
english: Bolgatanga Nursing Training College (Mixed)

kusaal: Bolgatanga Girls' Senior High School (pʋ'ab)
english: Bolgatanga Girls' Senior High School (Girls)

kusaal: Zamse Senior High/Technical School (dab nɛ pʋ'ab)
english: Zamse Senior High/Technical School (Mixed)

kusaal: Bolgatanga Gbana bʋʋr la ka onɛ da di'e piini nɛ on mɛ' di la, American architect J. Max Bond, Jr., dinɛ ka Le Corbusier da sʋŋ o.
english: The Bolgatanga Library is a notable design of award-winning American architect J. Max Bond Jr., who was influenced by Le Corbusier.

kusaal: Bond dinɛ bɛ Ghana yʋma anaasi gaad yʋʋm1960s ni.
english: Bond lived in Ghana for four years in the 1960s.

kusaal: Bolgatanga anɛ 161 km (wʋʋ 100 miles) bɛ Tamale ya-datiʋŋ.
english: The town lies in the Red Volta Valley, 161 km (100 mi) north of Tamale, with the White Volta and the cliffs of the southern Gambaga escarpment forming the southern boundary of the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Bolgatanga bɛnɛ Red Volta River Valley (dinɛ an vɛnlim zi'ig suor kani ka wabid dɔli gat), nɛ White Volta River nɛ Gambaga tampiis dinʋ bɛ teŋpʋʋg la ya-dagɔbʋg ka maan ya-dagɔbʋg titɔrʋg tisid Upper East Region.
english: The town lies in the Red Volta Valley, 161 km (100 mi) north of Tamale, with the White Volta and the cliffs of the southern Gambaga escarpment forming the southern boundary of the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr Bolgatanga (Bolbatanga) da paamnɛ yi Guresi pian'ad "Boole" Yak nɛ "tanga" tampiig.
english: Siddharth Kara writes that Bolgatanga served as a market where captives from the Sahel were sold to Hausa merchants as part of the African slave trade.

kusaal: Upper East Region, dinɛ ka Bolgatanga bɛ la, pɛ'ʋsi kɛ' ka ba buon ye Upper Region la.
english: Bolgatanga is known as the crafts centre of the Upper East Region, with a large central market.

kusaal: Ba ya'a ye ba zi la'ad ba mɔri dinɛ ka ba mi' ka buon ye 'motor king'.
english: For the transportation of goods, an uncovered tricycle popularly known as "motor king" is used.

kusaal: Bolgatanga anɛ zi'ikani ka nidib mi' nu'us tʋʋm bɛ Upper East Region ni, ka mɔr da' tita'ar kani bɛ teŋsʋg.
english: Apart from items found elsewhere in the Upper East Region, the so-called "Bolga hats" are made and sold in Bolgatanga.

kusaal: Upper East Region mɔr la'ad bɛdigʋ lʋsiaba la, dinɛ ka ba ye "Bolga hats" la maanɛ ka kuosid Bolgatanga.
english: Apart from items found elsewhere in the Upper East Region, the so-called "Bolga hats" are made and sold in Bolgatanga.

kusaal: La'avɛnla dɔɔg mɛn bɛ anina, dinɛ an ya' bani an kʋdʋmɛn tɛrigir bɛ Upper East Region la ni.
english: There is also a museum in the town, which houses objects of historical importance of the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Bolgatanga mɔri teŋtʋʋlʋg (Köppen climate classification BSh).
english: The town has a hot semi-arid climate (Köppen climate classification BSh), experiencing a rainy season and a dry season per year.

kusaal: Bolgatanga Senior High School (dab nɛ pʋ'ab)
english: Bolgatanga Senior High School (Mixed)

kusaal: Zuarungu Senior High School (dab nɛ pʋ'ab)
english: Bolgatanga Senior High School (Mixed)

kusaal: Bolgatanga gbana bʋʋr la da an o yiiga tʋʋm onɛ da bɛ national construction compan la ni.
english: The Bolgatanga library was his first major project while working for the national construction company.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka ba maali li pʋ'ab kɔlɛgi bɛ yʋʋm 1965 la ni ka ka 1973 yʋʋm la ka li lieb pʋ'asada sakur bɛɛ Bolgatanga Girls Senior High School.
english: Bolgatanga Girls Senior High School (also known as BOGISS, Lily of the North) is an all female second cycle institution in the Bolgatanga Municipality in Bolgatanga in the Upper East Region of Ghana, established in 1956 as a girls' middle boarding school to expand opportunities for girls in northern Ghana and converted to Bolgatanga Women's Training college in 1965 to train female teachers.

kusaal: Bolgatanga Technical University Sakura BTU la, (kanɛ da dɛŋi buon Bolgatanga Politechnic) anɛ zama sakur tita'ar n bɛ Upper East Region Ghana, West Africa.
english: The Bolgatanga Technical University BTU, (formerly Bolgatanga Polytechnic) is a public tertiary institution in the Upper East Region of Ghana, West Africa. It is gradually increasing its courses and facilities following the achievement of university status.

kusaal: Li da lieb Technical University nɛ Ghana zugraan kʋdʋg, John Dramani Mahama.
english: It was converted into a Technical University during the administration of the former president of Ghana, John Dramani Mahama.

kusaal: Ba da zi'el zakur la nɛ 1999 amaa ka pin'ili ba zamisa la nɛ 2003 Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig la ni, lin da an Bolgatanga Politechnic la.
english: The institution was established in 1999 but started rolling out its academic programs in September 2003 as Bolgatanga Polytechnic.

kusaal: Nananna nwa, sakur la bɛnɛ zin'is ayi, ka Sakura tʋʋma la mɛŋ niŋid nɛ Sumbrungu n bɛ Bolgatanga nɛ Navrongo suoraug tita'arin la, ka ba da yɔ'ɔgi li 2007.
english: Currently, the university has two campuses, with the main operations at Sumbrungu on the Bolgatanga–Navrongo highway, opened in 2007.

kusaal: Bolgatanga an Upper East Region Ghana tenpʋʋg tita'ar, ka li nidib la kal kanɛ pʋ paae 70, 000 teŋin la.
english: Bolgatanga is the capital of the Upper East Region of Ghana and has a population of under 70,000 people.

kusaal: Ka Technical University nam tɛnrigir tʋʋm 2020, Act 1016 5?
english: It was converted into a Technical University in April, 2020, by the Technical Universities amendment Act 2020 (Act 1016).

kusaal: Ecological Agriculture an ba zamis kpan sakurin la, ka li bɛnɛ zin' I kpieŋin kanɛ ka ba gʋ'ʋn bʋnkɔnbid, zin'i kan la li'eli nɛ Togo nɛ Burkina Faso.
english: Ecological Agriculture is the niche area of the university, situated in a dryland region with extensive cropping and livestock herding, relatively close to Togo and Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Tʋʋma la zin'iginɛɛ sakura zaŋ zuod nɛ kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl lʋgʋr la nɛ Savanah Agriculture Research Institude (SARI), nɛ Skills Development Fund (SDF), ye li sʋŋ ka kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋlʋg tʋʋma Savanah sʋ'ʋlim Ghana nyɛ paŋ ka nɔbig.
english: The university has built industrial partnerships with the Ministry of Agriculture, the Savanah Agriculture Research Institute (SARI), and the Skills Development Fund (SDF) to improve agriculture in the savannah region of Ghana.

kusaal: Bolgatanga Technical University la la'am tʋmmɛ nɛ sakur sieba, ban anɛ Ouagadougou University n bɛ Burkina Faso, linɛ kpie nɛ Accra, Ghana tempʋ-tita'arin la, ye fariŋ sakurbibis zamis na'asaal pian'ad, nɛ tʋʋma zaŋir zin'igin.
english: These include the University of Ouagadougou in Burkina Faso, closer than Ghana's capital Accra, for English Language immersion training for francophone students, and industrial placements.

kusaal: Ba mɛ la'am zamisid nɛ Apidon Academy of Science, Burkina faso.
english: Another association is with the Apidon Academy of Science, Burkina Faso.

kusaal: AAS anɛ banɛ mɔr baŋir bɛdigʋ management zamisʋg nɛ statistical zamisʋg sociology ni.
english: AAS specialises in management studies and statistical training in sociology.

kusaal: University la da pin'ili anɛ sakuri bɛ Bukere an tenbili Bolgatanga pʋʋgin.
english: The university began as a School in Bukere, a suburb of Bolgatanga.

kusaal: Yiiga tʋmtʋmnib la da tʋm nɛ ani hali ti paae Sumbrungu din la da ti mɛɛ naae la.
english: The pioneer staff worked from there until the Sumbrungu campus was finished.

kusaal: Nananna nwa, Bukere Sakura mɔri zamisa ka sakur bɛda nɛ sakur bibis wʋsa ken yʋ'ʋŋi zamisid.
english: Bukere currently has an Evening School where both tertiary and non-tertiary programs are run.

kusaal: PNDC wada 321 (1992), ka ba da tɛnrigi li 2007 yʋʋmin ka li an Parliament tʋʋm, (Act 745).
english: The school was founded in 1999 under PNDC Law 321(1992) which was amended in 2007 with an Act of Parliament (Act 745).

kusaal: la da tiak Sakura niŋi li Technical University 2020 yʋʋm la, Vaala nwadigin la.
english: It was converted into a Technical University in April, 2020, by the Technical Universities amendment Act 2020 (Act 1016).

kusaal: Maryland University, Eastern Shore, USA la'as nɛ ba n gɔt gbana banɛ ka ba mɔri zamisid, nɛ suo-sʋma banɛ sʋm ye ba dɔlisi zamisid zaŋi ken saam di'esig nɛ gɔɔnbin.
english: The University of Maryland, Eastern Shore, USA collaborates on curriculum assessment and international best practice and standards for the hospitality and tourism curricula.

kusaal: University la da gaŋ nidibi tisi ba paŋ, ka ba da kɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa da dɔlis COVID-19 lu'asig suoyala.
english: The university created a COVID-19 taskforce to make sure there was adherence to the safety protocols.

kusaal: nɛŋa da ye li sʋŋ nɛ gu' corona virus sakurin la, sakurbibis la da ti'ebid ye ba lɔ'ɔŋ yʋʋmkanɛ da bɛ tuon zamisʋg la.
english: This was to curb corona virus on campus as students get ready for the next academic year.

kusaal: Zamisa da si'iŋ nɛ Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig la 2003 yʋʋm la ni, Bukere teŋin.
english: Academic programmes began in September 2003 in Bukere.

kusaal: Ba da zi'eli di nɛ ka di an distirik asambil yʋʋm 1988 la ni; dinɛ ka Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 1446 la kɛ ka di zi'en.
english: Originally created as an ordinary district assembly in 1988, which was established by Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 1446.

kusaal: Bongo District bɛnɛis Bolgatanga babir, dinɛ an Upper East Region teŋpʋtita'ar la.
english: Bongo District is near the town of Bolgatanga, the Upper East Region's capital.

kusaal: Di tɔndnɛ Kassena-Nankana District ya-tuona ka Bolgatanga Municipal District mɛn bɛ ya-dagɔbʋg.
english: It shares borders with Kassena-Nankana District in the west, the Bolgatanga Municipal District in the south, the Nabdam District to the east and Burkina Faso to the north.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlʋm la wʋsa anɛ wʋʋ 459 square kilometers.
english: The total area is 459 square kilometers.

kusaal: Zi'ig la bɛnɛ Sudan Savannah Zone, zi'ig la pɔti anɛ Guinea Savannah Zone.
english: The landscape borders on the Sudan Savannah Zone although technically in the Guinea Savannah Zone.

kusaal: Bongo Rocks anɛ zi'ivɛnlʋg tita'ar zi'ig, dinɛ mɔr vɛnlim tis Bongo district wʋsa, ka kɛ ka nidib dʋti gɔsid.
english: The Bongo Rocks is a top tourism site, which provides a beautiful view of all the Bongo district landscape and allows an easy ascent.

kusaal: Bongo District mɔri District Hospital yinne nɛ laafi zi'ins ayuobo (6) bɛ sʋ'ʋlim la pʋʋgʋn.
english: The Bongo District has one District Hospital, One Catholic Health Centre (St. Theresa Health Centre, Zorkor) with 6 health centres located in majoy communities and CHPS compounds throughout the district.

kusaal: Di da anɛ Presbyterian Church of Ghana dimi zi'eli di ka di sʋŋid northern nam atan' la wʋsa bɛ Ghana.
english: It was founded by the Presbyterian Church of Ghana and it caters to people from all 3 regions in the northern part of Ghana.

kusaal: Bongo anɛ teŋkani an tɛɛd tiis ba'ayir.
english: The predominant occupation in Bongo District is subsistence farming along with some handicraft production.

kusaal: Di mɔri senior secondary schools nam ayi', junior secondary schools nam piinɛ atan' nɛ primary schools nam pisnaasi.
english: The Bongo District can boast of Six (6) senior high schools, several junior high and primary schools.

kusaal: Region paal nwa maalʋg yinɛ nɔzi'el kanɛ ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party da yɛli zi'el kati wa'ae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: This creation of this new region was in fulfillment of a promise made by the New Patriotic Party prior to the 2016 Ghana general election.

kusaal: On da di vɔɔt la, Zugraan, Nana Akuffo Addo da maal lʋgʋr paal Ministry of Regional Reorganization ye di gɔs ka si'el wʋsa nyaŋi maal sʋ'ʋŋa.
english: Upon winning the elections, the President, Nana Akuffo Addo created the Ministry of Regional Reorganization to oversee policy formulation and implementation.

kusaal: Rregion banɛ kpɛlim la anɛ Bono, Western North, Ahafo, Savannah, North East, nɛ Oti region nam.
english: The other regions are Ahafo, Western North, Savannah, North East, and Oti regions.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔs ka tʋʋma la tʋm ka region paala la maal anɛ Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development dinɛ ka Hon.
english: The execution of plans for the creation of the regions was seeded to the newly created Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development which is under the leadership of Hon. Dan Botwe.

kusaal: Dinɛ an Government of Ghana ministry kanɛ gɔsid ka ba maan region paala Ghana.
english: Government of Ghana ministry charged with the responsibility of supervising the creation of new regions in Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa atan (March 2017) la ni, ministry la da tis suor region paala la maalʋg la'asnɛ Council of State.
english: In March 2017, the ministry sent the blue print for the creation of the region along with others to the Council of State.

kusaal: Council la da la'as taaba gaad nɔɔrim pistan nɛ ayuobʋ (36) din yi sankanɛ ka ba da tis gbaʋŋ la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa anii (August 2017) la ni.
english: The council met over 36 times from the time of submission to August 2017.

kusaal: Vɔɔtʋg la da bɛnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27 December 2018) ka nidib tusa kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnu, kɔbisnii nɛ piinɛ ayi (450,812) yina vɔɔt dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisnii nɛ anu du'al pisnii nɛ ayi kɔbiga pʋʋga (85.82%) yi nidib tusa kɔbisnu nɛ pisi nɛ anu, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (525,275) banɛ sɔbi ba yʋda ye ba vɔɔt.
english: A referendum on 27 December 2018 resulted in 450,812 casting their votes representing 85.82 per cent of 525,275 registered voters.

kusaal: Nidib 448,545 la pʋʋgin, kɔbiga pʋʋgin piswai nɛ awai du'al pisnu (99.50 per cent) da siak ye ɛɛn ka ba maalim region paal la; ka nidib tusir, kɔbistan nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1,384) zɛm nɛ vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pistan nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.31%) pʋ siak region paal la maaligɔ.
english: 448,545 (99.50 per cent); voted in favour of the creation of the new region with 1,384 (0.31 per cent) voting against.

kusaal: Vɔɔt banɛ da san'am anɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ atan (883) dinɛ zɛm nɛ nɛɛm du'al pisi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.20 per cent).
english: A total of 883 (0.20 per cent) ballots were rejected.

kusaal: Bono East Region tɔtnɛ nɛ Savannah Region, Bono Region, Ashanti Region nɛ Volta Lake la.
english: The Bono East Region borders on the north the Savannah Region, on the west the Bono Region, on the south the Ashanti region and on the east the Volta Lake.

kusaal: Region la pʋnɛ piinɛ 11 MMDA's (ba pʋ mɔr Metropolitanɛ, Municipal nam anaasi (4) ka Ordinary Assembly nam aan ayɔpɔi (7)).
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into 11 MMDA's (made up of 0 Metropolitan, 4 Municipal and 7 Ordinary Assemblies).

kusaal: District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly, wʋsa mɔri ba Chief Executive, onɛ zi'eni tis central government ama aba paamidi ba paŋnɛ Assembly kpɛɛmkanɛ an presiding member, ka Assembly members themselves vɔɔti gaŋ la.
english: Each District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly, is administered by a Chief Executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an Assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Region paal la maalʋg naar suor anɛ ba bas suor ka nimbanɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlim kan la vɔɔt new region paal la yɛla yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27 December 2018).
english: The final stage for the creation of the region was decided through a referendum by the people within the catchment of the new region on 27 December 2018.

kusaal: Busa an zʋkanɛ ka ba kuod pamm Savannah zone la bɛ Techiman, Yeji, Nkoranza, Kintampo, Kwame Danso, Prang nɛ zin'ibanɛ kpɛlim.
english: The production of yam is very high in the woodland Savannah zone in Techiman, Yeji, Nkoranza, Kintampo, Kwame Danso, Prang and others.

kusaal: · Kristo Boase Monastery.
english: Kristo Boase Monastery is home to a small community of eleven Benedictine monks.

kusaal: Bono East region mɔrnɛ nidib kal bi'ela ka nimbanɛ bɛ anina la tita'am pian'adnɛ Bono dialect.
english: The Bono East region has a low population density, and most inhabitants speak the Bono dialect.

kusaal: Bono ancestral worship and spirituality ka Kristo biis pʋ'ʋsim an pʋ'ʋskanɛ zu'oe sʋ'ʋlim la ni.
english: Bono ancestral worship and spirituality and Christianity form the dominant religions of the region.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr paal kanɛ an Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development, ka Hon.
english: The implementation of plans for the creation of this region is seeded to the newly created Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development under the leadership of Hon. Dan Botwe.

kusaal: Brong Ahafo Region da lɛn kae ya'asa din ka ba buon ye Brong Ahafo Region Co-ordinating Council (BARCC).
english: Brong Ahafo Region in effect ceased to exist and so does the Brong Ahafo Region Co-ordinating Council (BARCC).

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ, dɔlisid 1992 wada gbaʋŋ la, Article 255 nɛ Article 186 of the Local Governance Act, 2016 (Act 936 as Amended), Bono Regional Co-ordinating Council (BRCC) anɛ bʋn saaŋ ka di'e BARCC nɔbir.
english: Consequently, in the spirit of Article 255 of the 1992 constitution and Article 186 of the Local Governance Act, 2016 (Act 936 as Amended), the Bono Regional Co-ordinating Council (BRCC) is a new entity and thus replaces the BARCC.

kusaal: Region la pʋnɛ MMDA's piinɛ ayi (12) (Di pʋ mɔr Metropolitanɛ, Municipal nam anu (5) nɛ Ordinary Assembly nam ayɔpɔi (7).
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into 12 MMDA's (made up of 0 Metropolitan, 5 Municipal and 7 Ordinary Assemblies).

kusaal: District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly, wʋsa mɔr Chief Executive, onɛ zi'eni tis gɔmena la ka lɛɛ tʋmmi dɔlisid presiding member onɛ ka assembly members gaŋ ye o aan ba tuon gat la.
english: Each District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly, is administered by a Chief Executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an Assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Teŋ la topography anɛ dinɛ bɛ teŋin ka pʋ gaad 152 metresɛ.
english: This area's topography is mainly characterized by a low elevation not exceeding 152 metres above sea level.

kusaal: Region la kuod zʋkuosa (Cash crops) nwɛnɛ atinya, timber, nɛ banɛ kpɛlim, nɛ diibnam nwɛnɛ kawɛnna, banki, bɔɔdia, baŋkan, kamantɔɔsi/toosi nɛ sieba bɛdegʋ.
english: The region produces Cash crops like cashew, timber, etc., and food crops such as maize, cassava, plantain, cocoyam, tomatoes, and many others.

kusaal: Bono Region tɔtnɛ Savannah Region lɛbid Ya-datiʋŋ,ka tɔt nɛ Ghana-Côte d'Ivoire lɛbid Ya-tuona, Ya-nya'aŋ anɛ Bono East, ka Ya-nya'aŋ an Ahafo Region.
english: Bono Region shares a border at the north with the Savannah Region, is bordered on the west by Ghana-Côte d'Ivoire international border, on the east by Bono East, and on the south by Ahafo Region.

kusaal: Di mɔr nidib kal nwɛnɛ miliyɔŋ yinne, tusa kɔbisyi nɛ anii, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (1,208,649) dɔlisid Ghana statistical service yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) nidib kaalʋg la.
english: It has a population of about 1,208,649 according to Ghana statistical service in 2021 census.

kusaal: Sunyani Business High School.
english: Sunyani Business High School etc.

kusaal: Bono Ancestral Worship and spirituality ka Kristo biis pʋ'ʋsim an pʋ'ʋskanɛ gat banɛ kpɛlim la.
english: Bono Ancestral Worship and spirituality and Christianity is the dominant religion within this domain.

kusaal: Kwafie an dinɛ ka Dormaa, Berekum nɛ Nsoatre dim maan nwadis piinɛ yinne, nwadis piinɛ ayi nɛ yʋʋmpaal nwadig la mi ka Munufie mɛ an dinɛ ka Drobo nam maan.
english: Kwafie is celebrated by the Dormaa, Berekum and Nsoatre people in November, December or January.

kusaal: Nidib niŋ yadda ye di anɛ Dormaa Ahenkro (Aduana) dim mɔr bugum kpɛn' Ghana na,din ka ba tiend nintita'akaŋa yɛla.
english: It is believed that the people of Dormaa Ahenkro (Aduana) brought fire to Ghana, hence this legend is symbolically re-enacted.

kusaal: Brong-Ahafo region anɛ region kanɛ da kpɛlim ban da nwaae Bono East region nɛ Ahafo region maal region paala la.
english: It is as a result of the remainder of Brong-Ahafo region when Bono East region and Ahafo region were created.

kusaal: Sunyani, ka sieba buon ye green city ka di bɛ Ghana la, aan di tempʋtita'ar.
english: Sunyani, also known as the green city of Ghana, is the regional capital.

kusaal: Ba da maal region lanɛ ban da nwaae Ahafo region nɛ Bono East region nami yi Brong-Ahafo region la.
english: The region was created after the Ahafo region and Bono East region respectively have been carved out of the then Brong-Ahafo region.

kusaal: Region la maalʋg dɔlisnɛ Nana Akuffo Addo da nwɛ'ɛdi o pɔlitis ka yɛl si'em yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la.
english: This was in fulfillment of a promise made by candidate Nana Akuffo Addo in his 2016 campaign activities.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛŋa zug, di da mɔr suor ye ba zuŋ BRCC ka di nyaŋi tʋmi di tʋʋma din nar si'em.
english: Because of this, it became necessary to inaugurate the BRCC to enable it to perform its functions accordingly.

kusaal: Region la tʋmnɛ pɔlitical administration dɔlisid local government system.
english: The political administration of the region is through the local government system.

kusaal: Buudi malima nɛ tiga bɛdegʋ bɛ region la ni.
english: There are several cultural practices and festivals within this region.

kusaal: Bono, ka si'eba buon ye Abron, Brong, bɛɛ Bono kambʋnir, anɛ buudi pian'ad kanɛ la'as nɛ buudi babiga ka li lieb yinnɛ ka ba pian'adi bɛ Akan buudi banɛ an Bono dɔɔg dim.
english: Bono, also known as Abron, Brong, and Bono Twi, is a dialect cluster within the Twi-Fante dialect continuum that is spoken by the Bono people.

kusaal: Banɛ pian'ad Bono anɛ wan wʋʋ nidib 1.2 million bɛ Ghana, li kaskas anɛ Bono Region, Bono East Region, ka nidib wan wʋʋ tusa kɔbistan' mɛ pian'ad buud kanɛ bɛ Côte d'Ivoire.
english: Bono is spoken by approximately 1.2 million people in Ghana, primarily in the Bono Region, Bono East Region, and by over 300,000 in eastern Côte d'Ivoire.

kusaal: Bono pian'ad la zamisig tɔi, li la'as nɛ Akan buudi pian'a si'eba wan wʋʋ Asante, amaa fʋ ya'a yii ba tɛŋin la ka li kɛŋ naalim nɛ pian'a si'eba ka Fante mɛ anɛ pian'a kanɛ bɛɛ li kɔn'.
english: Bono is mutually intelligible with neighboring dialects of Akan such as Asante, but the degree of intelligibility drops off with geographical distance, and Fante is effectively a different language.

kusaal: Bono nɛ Wasa anɛ pian'a banɛ bɛɛ ba kɔn' bɛ Akan buudi ni.
english: Bono and Wasa are the most divergent dialects of Twi-Fante.

kusaal: Borborbor anɛ Ghana nɛ Togo dim wa'a kanɛ ka Ewe dim buudi banɛ bɛ Volta region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim nɛ Togo ya'dagɔbʋg baba dim wa'ad, ba si'eba anɛ Kpalime nɛ Lomé.
english: Borborbor (also known as Akpese) is a Ghanaian and Togolese traditional dance performed by the Ewe people from the Volta region of Ghana and Southern Togo , including Kpalime and Lomé.

kusaal: Li anɛ wa'a kanɛ pa'an malima banɛ ka Ewe dim banɛ bɛ Volta Region Ghana la maan, zin'ig kanɛ ka Anlo Ewe nam bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim nɛ Togo tɛŋin.
english: It's a cultural and social recreational dance performed by the Ewe people in the Volta Region of Ghana, an area north of the Anlo Ewe of southeastern Ghana and some Togolese.

kusaal: Borborbor wa'a la nyɛ yʋ'ʋr hali lin yi yʋʋma pisnu banɛ gaad la bɛ Nketia, Jones nɛ Amu nɛ lin nyaan ti yadig zin'igi paae Chernoff, Agawu, Avorgbedor, Burns, Fiagbedzi, Dor, Pantaleoni, Locke nɛ zin'ig si'eba bɛdigʋ.
english: The borborbor music has been internationally recognized for the past half a century by Nketia, Jones, and Amu before spreading to the ends of Chernoff, Agawu, Avorgbedor, Burns, Fiagbedzi, Dor, Pantaleoni, Locke, and many others.

kusaal: O zi'en constituency la nɔba zug 4th Republic of Ghana parliament la ni.
english: He had also represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament.

kusaal: Akwasi Boateng an wadmaani tis constituency la.
english: Nana Asafo-Adjei Ayeh is the current member of parliament (MP) for the constituency.

kusaal: Di bɛnɛ Bosomtwe Districti bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: It is located in the Bosomtwe District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Bosomtwe constituency bɛnɛ Bosomtwe District linɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Bosomtwe is located in the Bosomtwe District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaan ka o zi'eni tisi ba.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Bowili (Bowiri) language, Tuwuli (Liwuli, Siwuri, Tuwili, Tora), anɛ buudi pian'ad kanɛ ka ba pian'ad bɛ Volta Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The Bowili (Bowiri) language, Tuwuli (Liwuli, Siwuri, Tuwili, Tora), is spoken in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li paas nɛ buudi pian'ad banɛ ka Ghana nɛ Togo dim la'as ka li dɔl Kwa tʋŋ pian'ad.
english: It is considered one of the Ghana–Togo Mountain languages of the Kwa family.

kusaal: Braised rice anԑ Ghana dim mui dʋgʋb suor.
english: Braised rice is a Ghanaian style of cooking rice.

kusaal: Ba buoni li nԑ angwa moo bԑ Akan buudi pian'ad ni, "mui ka ba niŋ kpaam kiim" bԑԑ omɔ kɛ fɔ bԑ Ga buudi pian'ad ni.
english: It is known as angwa moo in the Akan language, literally "oil rice" or omɔ kɛ fɔ(omor ker for) in the Ga language.

kusaal: Ba dit mui ki'ima la nԑ Nanzu'us bԑԑ siito, ka paasid gԑl ki'ima bԑԑ sardine.
english: The braised rice is served with ground pepper or shito, and served with fried eggs, omelette or sardine.

kusaal: Brandford Kwame Daniel Adu (dʋ'am 2 Sigir 1942) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ maan kpikpiŋ, politis, ka lɛn an Member of Parliament zi'en Okere Constituency linɛ bɛ Eastern Region Ghana nɔba zug.
english: Brandford Kwame Daniel Adu (born 2 June 1942) is a Ghanaian businessman, politician, and Member of Parliament of the third and fourth parliaments of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Okere Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ sakur bɛ Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration, GIMPA ka di'e kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an Diploma in Paint Technology.
english: He attended the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration, GIMPA and obtained his Diploma in Paint Technology.

kusaal: O nɔɔra atan' ni ka o nya'a na'am ka ninkanɛ mɛ da zi'en o na'adɔɔg New Patriotic Party ni, Daniel Botwe, da di ka bas o.
english: He was however oust after his second term as the member of parliament for the same constituency by another representative of the New Patriotic Party, Daniel Botwe.

kusaal: Ba da vooti tis o ka bas Fuzzy Dapaah Torbay onɛ da zi'en National Democratic Congress na'adɔɔg zug la, Seth Otibu Mpare onɛ da zi'en Convention People's Party na'adɔɔg ni la, David Opare onɛ da zi'en National Reform Party na'adɔɔg zug nɛ Simson Samuel Duodu onɛ da zi'en People's National Convention na'adɔɔg zug.
english: He was elected over Fuzzy Dapaah Torbay of the National Democratic Congress, Seth Otibu Mpare of the Convention People's Party, David Opare of the National Reform Party and Simson Samuel Duodu of the People's National Convention.

kusaal: Adu da zi'en New Patriotic Party na'adɔɔg zug ka ba vooti tis o bɛ Samanpiid nwadig, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi Ghana wʋsa vootʋg la ni tis Okere Constituency linɛ bɛ Eastern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Adu was elected into Parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party during the December 2004 Ghanaian General elections for the Okere Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da vooti tis o ka bas Gloria Adu Nartey onɛ da zi'eni tis National Democratic Congress nɛ Akoto Kwasi onɛ da zi'eni tis Convention People's Party.
english: He was elected over Gloria Adu Nartey of the National Democratic Congress and Akoto Kwasi of the Convention People's Party.
