english: The Black Volta, one of the most important rivers in the country passes through the town, making Buipe one of the leading market centres in the northern part of Ghana.

kusaal: Buli, bɛɛ Kanjaga, paas nɛ Gur pian'ad nam banɛ bɛ Ghana la ni ka banɛ pian'adi li bɛ Builsa North District nɛ Builsa South District, linɛ bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Buli, or Kanjaga, is a Gur language of Ghana primarily spoken in the Builsa North District and Builsa South District, located in the Upper East Region of the country.

kusaal: Pina'ad yinnɛ anɛ Chuchuliga, ka banɛ pian'ad bɛ Ghana ya'nya'aŋ baba kpi'e nɛ Navrongo.
english: One dialect is Chuchuliga, spoken in the northern part of Ghana close to Navrongo.

kusaal: Pian'akaŋa mɔr Kasem li pʋʋgin, lin mɛ paas nɛ Gur pian'ad banɛ ka ba pian'ad Upper East Region nɛ Burkina Faso la ni.
english: This dialect is influenced by Kasem, which is another Gur language spoken in the Upper East Region of northern Ghana and in Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Banɛ gɔsid buudi pian'ad yela pa'al ye, Buli wan wʋʋ Konni, buud banɛ ka ba pian'adi bɛ Nangurima nɛ Yikpabongo District nam ni la.
english: According to Ethnologue, Buli does not show dialectal variation and is reportedly similar to Konni, which is spoken in the districts of Nangurima and Yikpabongo.

kusaal: Chuchuliga pʋ mɔr pian'a tɛɛgir, bɛɛ pian'a bila, linɛ kɛ ka li wan Buli.
english: Chuchuliga has specific morphological features such as the lack of diphthongs, a richer nominal morphology and the lack of low tones, which are similar to other varieties of Buli.

kusaal: Linɛ paas ya'as, Buli wan Mampruli bɛdigʋ.
english: Moreover, Buli is lexically similar to Mampruli (77%).

kusaal: Nidib tusa kɔbisyi' pian'adi li.
english: It is an SVO language and has 200,000 speakers.

kusaal: Bunkpurugu bɛnɛ Bunkpurugu-Yunyoo District bɛ North East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Bunkpurugu is located in the Bunkpurugu-Yunyoo District of the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba yelkpan anɛ buudi piinɛ yinnɛ yela: Akuapem Twi, Asante Twi, Ewe, Mfantse, Ga, Dangme, Nzema, Dagbani, Dagaare, Gonja nɛ Kasem.
english: It focuses on 11 languages: Akuapem Twi, Asante Twi, Ewe, Mfantse, Ga, Dangme, Nzema, Dagbani, Dagaare, Gonja and Kasem.

kusaal: Ba mɔr tʋʋma zin'ig dɔɔd ayi', yinnɛ bɛ Accra ka yinnɛ la mɛ bɛ Tamale.
english: It has two offices, one in Accra and the other in Tamale.

kusaal: Lʋgir la da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinnɛ ni ka ba da buoni li yiiga ye Vernacular Literature Bureau, ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi ni ka ba tisi li yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ti buon zina nwa'.
english: The bureau was founded in 1951, originally as the Gold Coast Vernacular Literature Bureau, and later given its current name in 1957.

kusaal: Ba da ti'aki li yi Ministry of Information lɛbis Ministry of Education yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' ni.
english: It was later transferred from the Ministry of Information to the Ministry of Education in 1963.

kusaal: Bureau of Ghana Languages lʋgir kanɛ bɛ Ghana gomɛna nu'usin gɔsid buudi pian'ad banɛ bɛ Ghana nɔbigir yela, ba gban'a si'eba anɛ ba sɔbid gbana dɔlisid buudi nam la ni.
english: The Bureau of Ghana Languages (BGL) is an agency of the government of Ghana that promotes Ghanaian languages, including publication of materials in them.

kusaal: Lʋgir la sʋŋid ka nidib zamisid Ghana buudi pian'ad nam banɛ bɛ Ghana, ka mɛ vɛɛnsidi li yela, ka sɔbid gbana li yela niŋid gbana ni, ka kɛt ka buudi nam la kpɛn'ɛd gbana ni.
english: The Bureau of Ghana Languages (BGL) is an agency of the government of Ghana that promotes Ghanaian languages, including publication of materials in them.

kusaal: Lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai, Samanpiid nwadig pin'ilig daar, li da yʋ'ʋn bɛnɛ banɛ gɔsid buudi malima nu'usin da dɔlis PNDC wada 238.
english: The Bureau has since 1 December 1989 been under the National Commission on Culture by the PNDC Law 238.

kusaal: Bureau of Ghana Languages anɛ gomɛna lʋgir kanɛ tʋʋma an ye ba gɔs tɛŋ la zamisig nɛ malima yela.
english: The Bureau of Ghana Languages is a government institution involved in the educational and cultural effort of the nation.

kusaal: Anina ka zabtita'ar da bɛ June 1979 coup linɛ da kɛ ka Jerry Rawlings faae na'am la.
english: It was the site of fighting during the June 1979 coup that placed Jerry Rawlings in power.

kusaal: Ba da maal Flower Pot interchange ye li kɛ ka suor kanɛ wa'ae Burma Camp da kpiadi galisɛ.
english: The Flower Pot interchange was constructed to ease traffic to Burma Camp.

kusaal: Li anɛ dɔɔg tita'ar kanɛ ka Ghana Armed Forces nɛ Ministry of Defence bɛ ka li mɔr dabiem, bɔzugɔ anina ka soogianam banɛ da faae tɛŋ la da bɛ, ka banɛ ka' soogianam ya'a da kpɛn'ɛ anina, ba da pʋ yit nɛ laafi ya'asɛ.
english: Burma Camp is the headquarters of the Ghana Armed Forces and the Ghanaian Ministry of Defence.

kusaal: Burma Camp mɔr sakur nam ban pisi nɛ anaasi, ka banɛ zamisid an nidib tusa piinɛ anaasi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piinɛ ayi'.
english: Burma Camp has twenty-four (24) schools, with a learner population of 14,712.

kusaal: Burkina Faso tɔndnɛ titɔndis nɛ Mali, Niger, Benin, Togo, Ghana nɛ Ivory Cost.
english: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa. It is bordered by Mali to the northwest, Niger to the northeast, Benin to the southeast, Togo and Ghana to the south, and Ivory Coast to the southwest.

kusaal: Bʋʋd kanɛ zu'oe Burkina Faso paam anɛ Mosi, banɛ zin'in ani 11th and 13th centries sa.
english: The largest ethnic group in Burkina Faso is the Mossi people, who settled the area in the 11th and 13th centuries.

kusaal: French da colonized ba paas French West Africa sʋ'ʋlim ,1896 saŋa.
english: In 1896, it was colonized- by the French as part of French West Africa; in 1958, Upper Volta became a self-governing colony within the French Community.

kusaal: Din nyaŋ la coups nam bɛdigʋ paad teŋ din yi 1966,1980,1982,1983,1987, ka nam ayisa 2022.
english: There have been various coups d'état, in 1966, 1980, 1982, 1983, 1987, and twice in 2022, in January and September.

kusaal: Ka din nɔk 1989,2015,nɛ 2023, ba da mɔɔ coup yɛla paam ka di pʋ tʋm.
english: There were also unsuccessful coup attempts in 1989, 2015, and 2023.

kusaal: Franco-British Convention of 14 june, 1898 da maal Burnkina Faso titɔndis.
english: The Franco-British Convention of 14 June 1898 created the country's modern borders.

kusaal: Ba da nam Republic of Upper Volta(French: Republic de Haute_Volta bɛnɛ Burinya wadig la dabis piiga nɛ yinne daar, 1958 ka buoli di ye self-governing colony ka di bɛnɛ French Community sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The Republic of Upper Volta (French: République de Haute-Volta) was established on 11 December 1958 as a self-governing colony within the French Community.

kusaal: Din nyaŋ la Maurice Yameogo da tuongat tis Voltalic Democratic Union(VDU)
english: The first president, Maurice Yaméogo, was the leader of the Voltaic Democratic Union (UDV).

kusaal: Voltans la da du'oe tiak wada ka di bas suor ye ba dim gɔmmina na'am la yʋʋma anaas-naas nɛ da maal nɛ burinya nyaŋ wadis ayɔpɔi la dabis piiga nɛ anaasi, yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbis wai nɛ piisyɔpɔi nɛ ayʋobʋ la ni(14th July,1976) ye di sʋŋ ka naae bɛɛ kad soogianam la ɛnti faan si'em la.
english: On 14 June 1976, the Voltans ratified a new constitution that established a four-year transition period toward complete civilian rule.

kusaal: Burkina Faso anɛ teŋ kanɛ bɛ West Africa sʋ'ʋlim kpɛla.
english: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa. It is bordered by Mali to the northwest, Niger to the northeast, Benin to the southeast, Togo and Ghana to the south, and Ivory Coast to the southwest.

kusaal: Burkina Faso mɔr paalʋ ka di labisim na aan wʋʋ (1958-1984) saŋa.
english: Formerly the Republic of Upper Volta, the country was renamed "Burkina Faso" on 4 August 1984 by then-President Thomas Sankara.

kusaal: Upper Volta nwa da paami ba mɛŋ yi ba French Colony 1960 saŋa, ka Maurice Yameogo aan ba gɔmmina.
english: The French Colony of Upper Volta was named for its location on the upper courses of the Volta River (the Black, Red and White Volta).

kusaal: Thomas Sankara, da ki'ilim teŋ la gɔmmina yinɛ coup ni,1983 saŋa amaa o da tʋm ya, ka on da mɔɔd ye o maal bʋn si'aba la sieba anɛ, sakʋr yɛla, alɛbis teŋ tisi ba dim, amʋg biig tis sid, nɛ yɛla bɛdigʋ.
english: The leader of the leftists, Capt. Thomas Sankara, was appointed prime minister in January 1983, but was subsequently arrested.

kusaal: Captain Ibrahim Traore da yis Paul -Henri Sandaoge Damiba nɛ coup bɛ wadis awai la dabis piistan daar, 2022 ka aan gɔmmina nannanna tis Burkina Faso.
english: The rationale given by Traoré for the coup d'état was the purported inability of Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba to deal with an Islamist insurgency.

kusaal: French da aan ba pian'ʋk kanɛ ka mɔri tʋm bɛ gɔmma tʋʋma lʋga ni wʋsa ka yʋʋn da paas English ye di tʋm bɛ ba gɔmma tʋʋma zin;'insin 2024 la ni.
english: The former government and business language was French until January 2024 when, alongside English, its status was demoted to that of a "working language" by ratification of a constitutional amendment.

kusaal: Burkina Faso da yis o mɛŋ yi dinɛ anɛ ECOWAS nɛ Africa Union ni.
english: In the aftermath of the coup, ECOWAS and the African Union suspended Burkina Faso's membership.

kusaal: Republic of Upper Volta da paam yʋʋr paal kanɛ an Burkina Faso burinya nya'aŋ nwadig daba anaasi daar, 1984 saŋa.
english: Formerly the Republic of Upper Volta, the country was renamed "Burkina Faso" on 4 August 1984 by then-President Thomas Sankara.

kusaal: Burnkina Faso anɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka French colony da kpen 1896 saŋa sa.
english: In 1896, it was colonized- by the French as part of French West Africa; in 1958, Upper Volta became a self-governing colony within the French Community.

kusaal: Maurice Yameogo anɛ da yiiga gɔmmina tis Upper Volta, da gɔs gbananam kati wae ba da di'e ba mɛŋ 1960 la yɛla.
english: In 1960, it gained full independence with Maurice Yaméogo as the president.

kusaal: Ba da pud zin'ig la ye Upper Volta ka di yinɛ din bɛ zin'ig si'a la yɛla.
english: The country owes its former name of Upper Volta to three rivers which cross it: the Black Volta (or Mouhoun), the White Volta (Nakambé) and the Red Volta (Nazinon).

kusaal: Kɔlis banɛ da bɛ anina da anɛ kɔlisa atan, banɛ aan, White, Black nɛ Red Volta.
english: The country owes its former name of Upper Volta to three rivers which cross it: the Black Volta (or Mouhoun), the White Volta (Nakambé) and the Red Volta (Nazinon).

kusaal: 1960 saŋa la ka ba yʋʋn da sʋ'oe ba mɛŋ ka pʋ lɛn bɛ French dim banɛ colonized b ani ya'asa.
english: In 1896, it was colonized- by the French as part of French West Africa; in 1958, Upper Volta became a self-governing colony within the French Community.

kusaal: Thomas Sankara da mɔr zi'elis paala keena, yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbis wai nɛ piisnii nɛ naasi,wadis Anni la dabis piiga nɛ anaasi daar, ye ba tiak teŋ la yʋur yi Upper Volta keŋ Burnkina Faso bɛɛ ban pʋdi li ye land of honest men.
english: On 2 August 1984, on Sankara's initiative, the country's name changed from "Upper Volta" to "Burkina Faso", or land of the honest men; (the literal translation is land of the upright men).

kusaal: Sankara da paas tuongatib bi'ela Africa sʋ'ʋlim nwa ni, da sin'ig dinɛ ka ti buon ye environmental protection a priority.
english: In the 1980s, when ecological awareness was still very low, Sankara was one of the few African leaders to consider environmental protection a priority.

kusaal: Soogianam nwa da bɛ na'am la zugʋ paae yʋʋma anaasi.
english: The army remained in power for four years.

kusaal: Ba pian'ad la (Busandir) anɛ Mande pian'ad ka wɛn wʋʋ kudumin Borgu na'am teŋi bɛ ya-dagɔbug Benin teŋin ka mɛ bɛ ya-dagobug Nigeria teŋin la'am nɛ Busa, Boko, nɛ Kyenga.
english: Their language, Bissa, is a Mande language that is related to, but not the same as, a cluster of languages in the old Borgu Kingdom area of Northeast Benin and Northwest Nigeria, including Busa, Boko, and Kyenga.

kusaal: Yu'ur kani lem bɛ tis Busans ka Mossi dim buon anɛ Busansi bɛɛ Busanga.
english: An alternate name for the Bissa is Busansi or Busanga which is used by the Mossi people.

kusaal: Ninsi'eba yɛt ye Rialle, Nakomse ya'anam yinni onɛ da an Mossi tuɔngat mɛn, da anɛ Busaŋ".
english: According to some traditions, Rialle, progenitor of the Nakomse line of Mossi rulers was Busansi."

kusaal: Busans anɛ nidiba ayi, anʋ pʋʋgin (2/5th) Burkina Faso nidib la wʋsa.
english: Bissa make up 2/5th of the Burkina Faso population.

kusaal: Busa nɛ Boko dim anɛ Busans zin'is bʋ'ʋdi ayi yit ya-gɔbʋg Nigeria nɛ ya-dagɔbʋg Benin kpi'ɛnɛ Borgu n bɛ Nigeria tensin Niger, Kebbi nɛ Kwara (Bokobaru dim) ka mɛ bɛ Beninese Alibori nɛ Borgou.
english: The Busa and Boko peoples, two subgroups of the Bissa people, live in Northwestern Nigeria and Northern Benin near Borgu in the Nigerian States of Niger, Kebbi and Kwara (mostly Bokobaru subgroup) and in the Beninese Departments of Alibori and Borgou.

kusaal: Ba piantnɛ Busa (mɛ an Busandir) nɛ Boko (ka mɛ lem bʋon yɛ Boo).
english: They speak Busa (also known as Bisã) and Boko (also known as Boo).

kusaal: Hausa dim buoni banɛ Bussawa.
english: This peoples are referred to as Bussawa in Hausa.

kusaal: Garango teŋ anɛ Busans teuŋu nbɛɛ ba kɔ ya-dagɔbʋg, ka banɛ bɛ ya'tʋona sakpidir la wusa bɛ Tutelage (Mossi na'amsɔɔlim) Ouagadougou dim nʋ'ʋsin, banɛ mɛ bɛ ya'yaŋ sakpidir la wusa mɛ bɛ Tenkodogo (Mossi na'amsɔɔlim).
english: The township of Garango, which serves as the center of the northern Bissa population, remained independent, while the northwestern districts fell under the influence of the Mossi Kingdom of Ouagadougou and the northeastern townships under the supervision of the Mossi Kingdom of Tenkodogo.

kusaal: Barso onɛ an Busans yaanam yinni la da anɛ tɔn'ɔs.
english: According to Bissa tradition, their ancestor Barso was a hunter.

kusaal: Daniel McFarland gbauŋ kani bɛ volta yɛt yɛ Busans anɛ "bugusim mande buudi banɛ zi'in koldaʋg pi'el kani bɛ Tenkodogo teŋir (by 1300).
english: Daniel McFarland's Historical Dictionary of Upper Volta refers to them as "intrusive Mande who settled the area along the White Volta below Tenkodogo by 1300.

kusaal: Ba nidib bam kidik Ghana titɔdugu kɛŋi bɛ hali Togo sa.
english: Some live across the border in modern northern Ghana and Togo.

kusaal: Ba pian'ad bʋʋdi la anɛ Barka, Lebir nɛ Lere.
english: The Bissa are divided in three language groups, that is the Barka, the Lebir and the Lere.

kusaal: Tʋŋ kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb la zak wʋsa mɔri ba yʋ'ʋr nɛ ba kɛliŋ ka Busans la bʋon din yɛ dedaa.
english: Each clan has a name and an appellation normally called dedaa by the Bissa.

kusaal: Ba kɛliŋ la yʋn anɛ sɔ yʋ'ur Burkina Faso.
english: Bissa make up 2/5th of the Burkina Faso population.

kusaal: Accra, Ghana tɛŋ banɛ ka Busans bɛ anɛ Busanga line nbɛ Kaneshie din'ni nbɛ Okai Koi sɔ'ɔlim la.
english: These include Busanga Line in the North Kaneshie area of the Okai Koi constituency, as well as Town Council Line (Lartebiokorshie) and Shukura in the Ablekuma Central constituency.

kusaal: Tɛŋ banɛ lɛm pas anɛ Town Council line bɛɛ Lartebiokorshie nɛ shukura nbɛ Ablekuma tɛŋpʋʋgin nɛ Nima, Ayawaso tɛŋsʋ'ʋgin.
english: These include Busanga Line in the North Kaneshie area of the Okai Koi constituency, as well as Town Council Line (Lartebiokorshie) and Shukura in the Ablekuma Central constituency.

kusaal: Busandir'rin Lingani dimi mɔr na'am paŋ ka lɛm mɔr tima paŋ.
english: Within Bissa society, the Lingani clan holds both political and mystical power.

kusaal: Sɔ kai mɔr paŋ kanɛ ka ʋ na nyaŋi pit zʋpibʋg kanɛ ka Lingan banɛ bɛ Tangaré tɛŋkpiŋin Garango yit Boulgou (Burkina Faso) dim mal nɛ ti'im laa.
english: No one can assume power or wear the crown without first undergoing mystical preparation by the Lingani clan in Tangaré (a village in Garango, Boulgou Province, Burkina Faso).

kusaal: Lingani anɛ tɔn'ɔs dim ka ba malʋŋ kanɛ ain kikaŋ nɛ ba yaanam tɔn'ɔs kpan la nan kpɛm bɛ zina Tangaré zuɔrini kpa nɛ Lingani yin.
english: The Lingani are traditionally hunters, and a ceremonial fig tree, along with an ancestral hunting spear dating back centuries, remains near Tangaré Mountain, facing the Lingani family residence.

kusaal: Bani mɔr na'am paŋ la kai banɛ zanl na'am zupibʋg laa amaa banɛ tisid na'am zʋpibʋg la.
english: The authority does not rest with the individual who wears the crown, but rather with the one who bestows it.

kusaal: Busans bɛdigʋ anɛ mɔɔm (muslims).
english: Most Bissa people are Muslim.

kusaal: Nanny goat, bʋ nyan'aŋ (bʋn-nyan'as) da pin'ili bɛ nɛ 18th century la ni, ka billy goat, bʋ raʋg (bʋn raad) bɛllim da pin'il 19th century la ni.
english: Nanny goat (adult female) originated in the 18th century, and billy goat (adult male) in the 19th century.

kusaal: Bʋʋs buudi vɛnsʋg yɛla yina pa'al ye mɔɔgin bʋʋg, bezoar ibex kanɛ yi nɛ Zagros Mountains, Zagros zuoya ni la, onɛ tun'oe an yin bʋʋs wʋsa bɛɛ ba paamm sa, naam nɛ on ni ka bɛ zina la.
english: A genetic analysis confirms the archaeological evidence that the wild bezoar ibex, found today in the Zagros Mountains, but formerly widespread in Anatolia, is the likely original ancestor of all or most domestic goats today.

kusaal: Neolithic kpaadib da pin'ili kim kɔnbid nɛ bin'isim nɛ ni'im zug, la'am nɛ ba bina bugulum kanɛ da an bugum; ka mɔri ba kɔnba, nɛ kɔnbʋd/zuobʋd nɛ ba giinla la maan fuud, ka mɔri mɛɛd, ka ba lɛn am tʋʋma la'ad.
english: Neolithic farmers began to herd wild goats primarily for easy access to milk and meat, as well as to their dung, which was used as fuel; and their bones, hair, and sinew were used for clothing, building, and tools.

kusaal: Yiigin paa la, bʋʋs banɛ da lieb yin bʋnam la, yʋʋma 10,000 ni sa la bɛ nɛ Ganj Dareh, Iran teŋin.
english: The earliest remnants of domesticated goats dating 10,000 years Before Present are found in Ganj Dareh in Iran.

kusaal: Ba nyɛ bʋ-kpiilima niŋgbina vɛɛnsigʋn Jericho, Choga, Mami, Djeitun, nɛ Çayönü teesin ka bʋʋs mɛ da kpɛn' yaanɛ bɛi, hali 8,000 nɛ 9,000 yʋʋma la ni sa.
english: Goat remains have been found at archaeological sites in Jericho, Choga Mami, Djeitun, and Çayönü, dating the domestication of goats in Western Asia at between 8,000 and 9,000 years ago.

kusaal: DNA vɛɛnsʋs yɛt ye, bʋʋs yin miinlʋŋ da bɛ 10,000 yʋʋma la ni sa.
english: DNA evidence suggests that goats were domesticated around 10,000 years ago.

kusaal: zɛmisim nam la nii, African Pygmy buudi kanɛ an 41 paae 58cm (16 paae 23 in) ka makidi nɛ kpɛɛm bankimpiing nɛ.
english: At the bottom of the size range are miniature breeds such as the African Pygmy, which stand 41 to 58 cm (16 to 23 in) at the shoulder as adults.

kusaal: Dutch/Frisian bok and giving modern buck) until ousted by hegote, hegoote in the late 12th century.
english: To refer to the male goat, Old English used bucca (cf. Dutch/Frisian bok, modern English buck) until ousted by hegote, hegoote ('he-goat') in the late 12th century.

kusaal: Norse kʋdʋmin sa labaya pa'al ye, teŋgban kanɛ gɔsid sa-tansʋg yɛla, Thor, mɔrnɛ tɛriko kanɛ ka Tanngrisnir nɛ Tanngnjóstr bʋʋs tɛɛdi di.
english: In Norse mythology, the god of thunder, Thor, has a chariot that is pulled by the goats Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjóstr At night when he sets up camp, Thor eats the meat of the goats, but takes care that all bones remain whole.

kusaal: Gävle Goat anɛ Yule Goat bʋntita'ar, ka ba duodi di agɔla yʋʋm wʋsa Gavle dinɛ bɛ Swedish la tempʋʋgʋn.
english: The Gävle goat is a giant version of the yule goat, erected every year in the Swedish city of Gävle.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmin sa labaya bɛdegʋ pa'al ye bʋʋg paas si'elnam bɛdegʋ ni, la'anɛ Chimera.
english: Several mythological hybrid creatures contain goat parts, including the Chimera.

kusaal: Capricorn zanbin kanɛ bɛ Westhern zodiac la pa'annɛ bʋʋgʋ na mɔr ziŋ zʋʋr.
english: The Capricorn constellation sign in the Western zodiac is usually depicted as a goat with a fish's tail.

kusaal: Fauns nɛ satyrs anɛ kʋdʋmin sa labaya la'ad banɛ ka pʋsʋg an nid ka pʋsʋg mɛ an bʋʋg.
english: Fauns and satyrs are mythological creatures with human bodies and goats' legs.

kusaal: Finland ni, Nuuttipukki malʋŋ la nam bɛ zin'is nwɛnɛ Satakunta, Southwest Finland nɛ Ostrobothnia.
english: In Finland the Nuuttipukki tradition is kept alive in areas of Satakunta, Southwest Finland and Ostrobothnia.

kusaal: Ba bɛ Australia, New Zealand, Great Britain, Galapagos nɛ zin'is bɛdegʋ.
english: Feral goats have established themselves in many areas: they occur in Australia, New Zealand, Great Britain, the Galapagos and many other places.

kusaal: Bʋʋs bin'isim ka ba mɔri maal diid kanɛ ka buon ye bʋʋg cheese.
english: Milk from goats is often turned into cheese.

kusaal: Ban da ki'aki gɔs COVID-19 la wi'akidi tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ si'em yʋʋm tusir, nɛ pisi, pin'ilig nwadig la (January 2020) da anɛ 1.4 nɛ 2.5 tɛnsʋk, amaa, nya'aŋ ka ba vɛn'ɛsi gɔs ka di pa'al ye di anɛ 5.7 (ka lin anɛ piswai nɛ anu, kɔbiga pʋʋgin 95% percent confidence interval of 3.8 to 8.9).
english: Initial estimates of the basic reproduction number (R0) for COVID-19 in January 2020 were between 1.4 and 2.5, but a subsequent analysis claimed that it may be about 5.7 (with a 95 per cent confidence interval of 3.8 to 8.9).

kusaal: Nwadig kan dabisa pisi nɛ anii saŋa la (28 December), nidib million nam kɔbisyi nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi, tusayɔpɔi nɛ piswai, kɔbisnii nɛ pisi nɛ ayi (282,790,822) dunia wʋsa ka ban'as la da gban'ae ba.
english: As of that 28 December, 282,790,822 individuals worldwide had been confirmed as infected.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi nɛ ayi, nwadis anaasi, dabisa piinɛ anaasi (14 April 2022) daar la, dunia wʋsa, banɛ ka ban'a la da gban'ae ba da tʋʋg million nam kɔbisnu (500 million).
english: As of 14 April 2022, over 500 million cases were confirmed globally.

kusaal: COVID-19 pandemic (ka ba buon ye coronavirus pandemic bɛɛ COVID pandemic), ban'as la yinɛ vʋ'ʋsim ban'as kanɛ an coronavirus 2 ( bɛɛ SARS-CoV-2), li da pin'il nɛ Wuhan, China sʋ'ʋlim, yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛ awai (December 2019).
english: The global COVID-19 pandemic (also known as the coronavirus pandemic), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), began with an outbreak in Wuhan, China, in December 2019.

kusaal: Di di'e zin'igi paae Asia, nɛ dunia wʋsa yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi pin'ilig la (2020).
english: It spread to other parts of Asia and then worldwide in early 2020.

kusaal: Ba da maal COVID-19 pin'ima tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ tis dunia wʋsa pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi, naar nwadig la ni (December 2020), ka tɛns gɔmɛna nam nɛ lʋg si'eba wʋʋ COVAX dim, da paas nʋ'ʋg ka bɔɔd ye di paae zin'ig wʋsa.
english: COVID-19 vaccines were developed rapidly and deployed to the general public beginning in December 2020, made available through government and international programmes such as COVAX, aiming to provide vaccine equity.

kusaal: Banɛ gɔsid dunia wʋsa laafi yela la da yis dabi'em kanɛ bɛ COVID-19 ban'as la yela la yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi nɛ atan', nwadis anu, dabisa anu daar (5 May 2023).
english: The WHO declared that the public health emergency caused by COVID-19 had ended in May 2023, while noting that COVID-19 continued to be a global health threat.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi, nwadis piiga, dabisa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (27 October 2024) saŋa la, COVID-19 da kʋ nidib milliyɔnnam ayɔpɔi, tusa pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne, kɔbistan' nɛ piinɛ yinne (7,071,311).
english: Using such data, estimates of the true number of deaths from COVID-19 worldwide have included a range from 18.5 to 35.2 million (≈27.4 million) by 25 January 2024 by The Economist, as well as over 18.5 million by 1 April 2023 by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation and ≈18.2 million (earlier) deaths between 1 January 2020, and 31 December 2021, by a comprehensive international study.

kusaal: Saŋa: ba da nyɛɛ di nɛ yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi nɛ anu, nwadis atan' (March 2024) ka ya'am dim mɔr pʋtɛnda kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ye COVID-19 anɛ pandemic bɛɛ di ka' ala, ka banɛ gɔsid dunia wʋsa laafi yela la buoni di ye dunia ban'abɛ'ɛd bɛɛ pandemic, ba labaya zin'is wʋsa.
english: Time reported in March 2024 that expert opinions differ on whether COVID-19 is currently considered endemic or pandemic, and that the WHO continued to call the disease a pandemic on its website.

kusaal: Din da pin'il Wuhan la, ba da buon ban'as nwa' ye "coronavirus", "Wuhan coronavirus", "the coronavirus outbreak" nɛ "Wuhan coronavirus outbreak", ka saŋ si'eba ka ba buoni li "Wuhan pneumonia".
english: During the initial outbreak in Wuhan, the virus and disease were commonly referred to as "coronavirus", "Wuhan coronavirus", "the coronavirus outbreak" and the "Wuhan coronavirus outbreak", with the disease sometimes called "Wuhan pneumonia".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi, yiiga nwadig la (January 2020), banɛ gɔsid dunia wʋsa laafi yela la da tisi di yʋ'ʋr si'a pin'ilig la da anɛ 2019-nCoV nɛ 2019-nCoV vʋ'ʋsim ban'as da an yʋ'ʋr banɛ ka ba tis buon ban'a la bɔzugɔ, yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛnu ka ba da gban'ae ye ba da mɔr tɛŋ yʋ'ʋr,(wʋʋ Wuhan, China), bʋnkɔnbig yʋ'ʋr, bɛɛ nidib la'asig yʋ'ʋri pʋd ban'asɛ, ala ka nyan kʋ mɔr sɔ'ɔ.
english: In January 2020, the WHO recommended 2019-nCoV and 2019-nCoV acute respiratory disease as interim names for the virus and disease per 2015 international guidelines against using geographical locations (e.g. Wuhan, China), animal species, or groups of people in disease and virus names in part to prevent social stigma.

kusaal: banɛ gɔsid dunia laafi yela la da si'ak ye ba buolim ban'as la ye COVID-19 bɛɛ SARS-CoV-2 yʋʋm tusir, nɛ pisi, nwadis ayi, dabisa piinɛ yinne daar (11 February 2020).
english: The WHO finalised the official names COVID-19 and SARS-CoV-2 on 11 February 2020.

kusaal: Ninkanɛ ka ba buon Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus da pa'al yʋ'ʋr la gbin: CO anɛ corona, VI an virus, D an ban'as ka piinɛ wai (19) la mɛ pa'an yʋʋm kanɛ ka ban'as la kɛna (yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛ wai, naar nwadig, dabisa pistan' nɛ yinne daar, 31 December 2019).
english: WHO Director-General Tedros Ghebreyesus explained: CO for corona, VI for virus, D for disease and 19 for when the outbreak was first identified (31 December 2019).

kusaal: Yiigin ka ba da pʋd yʋda la ka di yinɛ ban nyɛ ban'as la buudi lɔsi'a (wʋʋ Delta da pin'ili anɛ "Indian ban'a buudi") yʋ'ʋr ban buudi lɛn kae.
english: The initial practice of naming them according to where the variants were identified (e.g. Delta began as the "Indian variant") is no longer common.

kusaal: SARS-CoV-2 anɛ ban'a kanɛ pa'as nɛ zinzaŋ coronavirus, pangolin coronavirus, nɛ SARS-CoV nam ni.
english: SARS-CoV-2 is a virus closely related to bat coronaviruses, pangolin coronaviruses, and SARS-CoV.

kusaal: Zamis kanɛ ka ba da zamis China la da pa'al ye biis nɛ bʋnkʋda ka ban'a la na gban'ae tita'am.
english: Reports from February 2020, when most confirmed cases were confined to China, cited racist sentiments about Chinese people 'deserving' the virus.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, naar nwadig la (December 2021), nidib banɛ ka ban'as la gban'ae ba kanl da kpɛm paasid nɛ yɛlsi'eba yela, wan wʋʋ COVID-19 buudi paala da kɛna la zug.
english: It was reported on 11 December 2021, that China had vaccinated 1.162 billion of its citizens, or 82.5% of the total population of the country against COVID-19.

kusaal: Ba da pʋ tɛɛs ninsi'eba gɔsɛ, ka Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation da yina yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi nɛ ayi ni la ye nidib banɛ ka ban'as la gban'ae wa'ae nɛ billion nam.
english: On 24 January, the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation estimated that about 57% of the world's population had been infected by COVID-19.

kusaal: Yɛlbanɛ bɛ ka ninsaal na nyaŋi paam ban'as tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ anɛ nintita'ar kanɛ an bɛdir, sikir ban'as ya'a namis sɔ', sʋnsa'aŋ, nɛ yɛlsi'eba banɛ bɛ.
english: The strongest risk factors for severe illness are obesity, complications of diabetes, anxiety disorders, and the total number of conditions.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2009) la ni, ka United Nations Education, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) da nɔk candombe paas Representation List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity ni.
english: In 2009, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) inscribed candombe in its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Candombe bɛɛ Argentina nɛ Paraguay nɛ Brazil mɛn.
english: To a lesser extent, candombe is practiced in Argentina, Paraguay, and Brazil.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a keŋ Argentina, li bɛnɛ Buenos Aires, Santa Fe, Parana nɛ Corrientes.
english: In Argentina, it can be found in Buenos Aires, Santa Fe, Paraná, and Corrientes.

kusaal: Ka fʋ ya'a keŋ Brazil, candombe nan kpɛlim zi'e li zi'esimin ka fʋ tun'e ye li anɛ Minas Gerais.
english: In Brazil, candombe retains its religious character and can be found in the states of Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a dɔlisid George Reid Andres, kʋdʋmin la teŋ sabilis banɛ bɛ Latin America la, 19th century tɛŋsug ka ninsabilis dasam da si'iŋi basid candombe ka ye ba wa'a Europe's dim wa'a banɛ an waltz, schottische, nɛ mazurka.
english: According to George Reid Andrews, a historian of black communities in Latin America, after the middle of the 19th century younger black people began to abandon the candombe in favor of practicing European dances such as the waltz, schottische, and mazurka.

kusaal: Ka buoni ba mɛŋ ye Los Negros, upper class portenos yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyʋobu (1860) la ni nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi (1870) da di'em blackface ka maal malʋŋ yinne yʋʋm wusa ni.
english: Calling themselves Los Negros, upper class porteños in the 1860s and 1870s performed blackface and formed one of the carnival processions each year.

kusaal: African-Uruguay da la'asidnɛ wa'ad candombe wa'ab la Alasid daar wʋsa nɛ vʋ'ʋsim dabisa nwɛnɛ Yʋʋm paal yʋ'ʋŋ, Bunia, Saint Baltasar, Rosary Virgin nɛ Saint Benito.
english: African-Uruguayans organized candombe dances every Sunday and on special holidays such as New Year's Eve, Christmas, Saint Baltasar, Rosary Virgin and Saint Benito.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piinɛ atan' (1913) la ni, wa'akanɛ ka' yʋ'ʋrɛ ka kʋdʋmin dim buon ye "Viejo Tanguero" onɛ da sɔb yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1877) wa'ab kanɛ an tango ka mɛ la'as candombe la.
english: In 1913, an anonymous dance historian identified only as "Viejo Tanguero" ("Old Tangoer") wrote about the 1877 creation of a dance referred to as a tango but featuring ideas from the candombe.

kusaal: Robert Farris Thompson onɛ yi Tango la, da pa'al Lynch pian'ad la gbin ye: The Art of Love ka li pa'al ye tɛmpʋʋg kanɛ an compadritos wa'adnɛ milonga ka kae teŋkpɛŋa, gauchos.
english: Lynch's report was interpreted by Robert Farris Thompson in Tango: The Art of Love as meaning that city compadritos danced milonga, not rural gauchos.

kusaal: Biili linɛ bɛ candombe la da yinɛ tɛŋkanɛ ka ba buon ye Angola zina la, lin ka ba da mɔri keŋ South America 17th century nɛ 18th century la ni.
english: The seeds of candombe originated in present-day Angola, where it was taken to South America during the 17th and 18th centuries by people who had been sold as slaves in the kingdom of Kongo, Anziqua, Nyong, Quang and others, mainly by Portuguese slave traders.

kusaal: Banɛ malʋŋʋ an candombe la da nyaŋ Brazil (li kas-kas anɛ zin'ibanɛ bɛ Salvador de Bahia), Cuba, nɛ Rio de la Plata nɛ li tɛmpʋʋg Buens Aires nɛ Montevideo.
english: The same cultural carriers of candombe colonized Brazil (especially in the area of Salvador de Bahia), Cuba, and the Río de la Plata with its capital Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

kusaal: Buenos Aire, li ya'a an gomena nama ayi banɛ da bɛ Juan Manuel de Rosas la, li anɛ na'ana nɛ "afroportenos" (ninsabilis banɛ bɛ Buenos Aires) na wa'an candombe la nidibin, ka Rosas nɛ o pu'ayʋa Manuel la'am kaae ba ka kpɛmisi ba mɛn.
english: In Buenos Aires, during the two governments of Juan Manuel de Rosas, it was common for "afroporteños" (black people of Buenos Aires) to perform candombe in public, even encouraged and visited by Rosas and his daughter, Manuela.

kusaal: Ba da nyaŋ Rosas zaba ni Caseros yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi (1852) la ni, ka Buenos Aires da pin'ili maan malʋŋ ka li kpɛn yaligid Europe dim malima ni.
english: Rosas was defeated at the battle of Caseros in 1852, and Buenos Aires began a profound and rapid cultural shift which saw a bigger emphasis on European culture.

kusaal: Candombe anɛ yʋʋma nɛ wa'ab bʋʋdi ka ba da pin'ili di Uruguay banɛ da an African sankpan'asnam banɛ da faaɛn ba mɛŋ la.
english: Candombe is a style of music and dance that originated in Uruguay, among the descendants of liberated African slaves.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a keŋ Paraguay, li bɛnɛ Camba Cuá nɛ Fernando de la Mora linɛ kpi'e Asuncion.
english: In Paraguay, this tradition continues in Camba Cuá and in Fernando de la Mora near Asunción.

kusaal: Ba ɛɛnti nwɛ'ɛdi linɛ nwadisa ayi' la ni, Montevideo malʋŋ ka nidib wa'ad ka ba buonɛ li ye llamadas nɛ desfile inaugural del carnaval.
english: It is usually played in February during carnival in Montevideo at dance parades called llamadas and desfile inaugural del carnaval.

kusaal: Ba na yiiti nyu'od bugum ka li tʋlig binnanam la ka ba nwɛ'ɛd ka yʋ'ʋm candombe yʋʋma, di kas-kas anɛ yʋ'ʋŋ-yʋ'ʋŋ kpi'es ya, wʋʋ Barrio Sur nɛ Palermo bɛ Montevideo.
english: They would set a fire to heat the drums and play candombe music, especially during the night in certain neighborhoods such as Barrio Sur and Palermo in Montevideo.

kusaal: Wa'akaŋa yʋ'ʋr da anɛ "soft tango," ka African Argentina dim da maal.
english: This dance, which later became known as "soft tango," was created by African Argentines.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbusnii nɛ pisnii nɛ atan (1883) ni, wa'ad wa'ad onɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr an Ventura Lynch da pian' Argentina dim wa'awa'adib la yɛla ye ba anɛ compadritos ka bɛɛ Argentina wa'ab zin'is wʋsa.
english: Writing in 1883, dance scholar and folklorist Ventura Lynch described the influence of Afro-Argentine dancers on the compadritos ("tough guys") who apparently frequented Afro-Argentine dance venues.

kusaal: Thompson da nyɛ ka nidib banɛ wa'ad milonga la sieba an ninsabilis ka sieba mɛ an ninsabilis pʋsʋk ka banɛ wa'ad la pʋ lɛm mɔr ninla'asim ya'asɛ.
english: Thompson notes that the population of city toughs dancing milonga would have included blacks and mulattoes, and that it would not have been danced as a mockery by all the dancers.

kusaal: Africa ninsabilis banɛ ka ba da da'a ba ka ba bɛ Buenos zina la da bɛ anina hali yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnii (1580) la ni sa.
english: A population of black African slaves had been present in Buenos Aires since around 1580.

kusaal: Afroportenos dim tʋasnɛ ba yaanam malima da an si'em ye ba nɔbigi ba mɛŋ bɛllimin ka dinzʋg ka din yi yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyʋobʋ nɛ ayi' (1862) la nii wa'ae sa, banɛ tisid labaya, gbaŋmi'idib nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛdib pʋ tami li tʋʋma.
english: For this reason, onwards from 1862, the press, intellectuals and politicians began to assert the misconception of Afro-Argentine disappearance that has remained in the imagination of ordinary people from Argentina.

kusaal: Cape Coast North Sʋ'ʋlim la bɛnɛ Cape Coast Metropolis District kanɛ bɛ Central Region, Ghana.
english: The Cape Coast North constituency is located in the Cape Coast Metropolitan District of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Zin'ig la bɛn zaŋ nɛ Cape Coast Metropolitan district n bɛ Central Region Ghana la.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Cape Coast Metropolitan district of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kwamena Minta Nyarku, onɛ an Cape Coast North Constituency Wadmaan nananna nwa.
english: Dr. Kwamena Mintah Nyarku the current MP for the Cape Coast North constituency.

kusaal: Cape Coast North Constituency anɛ sʋ'ʋlim yinne kanɛ paas sʋ'ʋlim banɛ mɔr wadmaan-nam wadmaannib yir Ghana.
english: Cape Coast North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔti yisi ba wadmaan (MP) yinne dɔlis nɛ first past the post vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Ka ba da buoni li Cape Coast Polytechnic anɛ gomɛna sakur kanɛ an kpɛɛmnam din ka ba Central Region tɛŋ kanɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Formally Cape Coast Polytechnic is a public tertiary institution in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li da pin'il tʋʋma bɛ Ghana Education Service pʋʋgin bɛnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ ni.
english: In began operating under Ghana Education Service in 1986.

kusaal: Nwa' da anɛ Cyber Ghana la'as nɛ Royal Academy of Engineering, linɛ bɛ United Kingdom la, nɛ Lloyds Register Foundation, ban wʋsa bɛnɛ UK sʋ'ʋlim.
english: It is the brain child of Cyber Ghana in conjunction with the Royal Academy of Engineering, United Kingdom and the Lloyds Register Foundation, all in the UK.

kusaal: Cape Coast Polytechnic da dɛŋin bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi saŋa ka da anɛ banɛ naae JSS ban tɔlisim kɛŋ sakur kan.
english: Cape Coast Polytechnic was in existence in 1984 as a second cycle institution.

kusaal: Wada kanɛ buon PNDCL kɔbistan' nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ, da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi saŋa la, da tis sakur nwa paŋ ye ba pa'al ka mɛ tis kasɛta gbana banɛ buon Higher National Diploma.
english: After the enactment of the PNDCL 321 in 1992, the Technical University was upgraded to a tertiary level that allowed it to run programmes associated with the award of Higher National Diploma.

kusaal: Cape Coast Technical University pʋʋgin mɔr zamisig lʋga atan' banɛ ka ba buon sakurnam li pʋʋgin, ka sakurnam la pʋʋgin ka ba mɔr zamisig kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb piinɛ ayi'.
english: Cape Coast Technical University as an institution have twelve (12) academic departments and three schools.

kusaal: Zamisa banɛ ka Cape Coast Technical University pa'an anina anɛ kpikpiŋ zamisig, na'asaasɔɔng zamisig nɛ li la'ad maalig, fiita zamisig, la'ad da'ab nɛ kuosig zamisig, ya' mɛɛb zamisig, kaanlig nɛ na'asaasɔɔng zamisig, la'ad maalig, gbansɔbidib nɛ tuongaadig zamisig, da'adiib nɛ baŋ-wiins zamisig.
english: The courses run by Cape Coast Technical University are Arts, Business, applied sciences, and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Procurement & Supply Chain Management Building Technology, Bachelor of Science in Statistics Accounting with Computing, Civil Engineering, Secretaryship & Management Studies, Marketing and Telecommunication Engineering.

kusaal: Gban'ar kaŋa da anɛ ye ba pa'al nidib nu'ug tʋʋma, ka tis nidib tʋʋma ka ba tʋm, ka mɛ lɛn sʋŋi gu' na'asaasɔɔng filim-filim tʋʋma Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: This was to provide skills training, jobs creation and to curb cyber crime in Ghana.

kusaal: Ahenkorah da keŋi Tema Secondary sakur la nɛ Abuakwa State College.
english: Ahenkorah attended Tema Secondary School and Abuakwa State College.

kusaal: O da paam Arts master kasɛta gbauŋ (Ports ni Kuomin suor ken tʋʋma) nyi kasɛta gbauŋ tita'ar kanɛ ka ba buon degree Na'asaalin la Maritime University n bɛ Nungua Accra /Ghana Kpe-kpeŋ University la ni 2013.
english: He obtained a Master of Arts (Ports and Shipping Administration) degree from the Regional Maritime University, Nungua-Accra and the University of Ghana Business School in 2013.

kusaal: O da tʋmnɛ Jospong Consortium.
english: He worked at Jospong Consortium as a sales executive from 2004 to 2006.

kusaal: O da anɛ Zoomlion Ghana Limited nɛ Director tis J.A. Plant Pool Limited 2007 nɛ 2012 tensʋg.
english: He was the marketing manager of Zoomlion Ghana Limited and the manager director of J. A. Plant Pool Limited between 2007 and 2012.

kusaal: O da anɛ pa'an bɛ Ghana Maritime University hali 2005 ka an pa'an bɛ Ghana Institute nɛ Public Administration (GIMPA) hali 2010.
english: He has been a lecturer at the Regional Maritime University since 2005 and lectured at Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) since 2010.

kusaal: O nan gɔt Carlos King Freight Tʋʋma hali 1992.
english: He has been running Carlos King Freight Services since 1992.

kusaal: Nɛ zugɔɔ, la'asʋg dim banɛ an Occupy Ghana da bɔɔd isib gɔmma sa'an.
english: For this action pressure group Occupy Ghana demanded his expulsion from government.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2021 parliament pian'ad-pian'ad vootʋg la ni, ba da nyii Ahenkorah TV ni ka o su'a nɔk vootʋg gbana ka fut dim nga'a o.
english: In January 2021, during a national live telecast of the election of the Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana, Ahenkorah was seen snatching ballot sheets from the chamber during the voting process, before they were retrieved by security personnel and opposition lawmakers, as he bolted for the exit.

kusaal: Ya'asee, o da anɛ Trade nɛ Industry Minista nyaaŋdɔl tis Ghana.
english: Also, he was a Deputy Minister for Trade and Industry in Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛm anɛ kpeem tis Carlos King Freight Service la ni.
english: He is also the CEO of Carlos King Freight Services.

kusaal: 3 June 2020 la nii, o da sigya.
english: On the 3rd of July 2020, he resigned from office.

kusaal: Ba Majority kpeem Osei Kyei-Mensah Bonsu da ke'es ye on pʋ yɛl o ye Carlos Ahenkorah zɔkim vootʋg gbana.
english: The Majority Leader of the eight parliament of Ghana, Osei Kyei-Mensah Bonsu denied speculations that he had instructed Carlos Ahenkorah to snatch ballot papers.

kusaal: Cassiel Ato Baah Forson anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi nɛ anii la Gaana rpublic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Ajumako-Enyan-Esiam Constituency bɛ Central Region la Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg National Democratic Congress (NDC) nɔba zug.
english: Forson first joined the Fifth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, before retaining his seat for the Sixth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ajumako-Enyan-Esiam Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Forson nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii Nwadisa anii la daba anu daar (5 August 1978) o yinɛ Ajumako Bisease bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Forson was born on 5 August 1978 and hails from Ajumako Bisease in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: o da maali o PhD in Business and Management (finance option) Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadisa awai la ni (September 2020) Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) bɛ Ghana la.
english: He obtained a PhD in Business and Management (finance option) in September 2020 from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Ghana.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ maal doctorate la, Wadmaan la, MP da mɔr master's degrees nama ayi: master of Science in Taxation, University of Oxford, UK nɛ Master of Science degree in economics, KNUST.
english: Prior to getting the doctorate, the MP had two master's degrees: A master of Science in Taxation from the University of Oxford, UK and another Master of Science degree in economics from KNUST.

kusaal: O da maali o yiiga degree in accountingnɛ South Bank University bɛ London.
english: He had his first degree in accounting at the South Bank University in London.

kusaal: Forson paas Institute of Chartered Accountants, Ghana nɛ Chartered Institute of Taxation.
english: Forson is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants, Ghana and a fellow of Chartered Institute of Taxation.

kusaal: Forson anɛ Ghana Wadmaan, Fiscal Economist, Chartered Accountant, Tax practitioner nɛ Entrepreneur onɛ mɔr baŋir hali nwɛnɛ yʋma pisi yɛla tʋmmi tisid gɔmena nɛ asʋ'oe-m-mɛŋ lʋga.
english: Forson is a Ghanaian Legislator, Fiscal Economist, Chartered Accountant, Tax practitioner and Entrepreneur with professional experience spanning two decades in both private and public sectors.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ chief executive officer tis Omega Africa Holding Limited.
english: He also served as the chief executive officer for Omega Africa Holding Limited.

kusaal: O paas NDC Wadmaanib la zi'eni tis Ajumako-Enyan-Esiam constituency hali yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: He has been the NDC Member of Parliament for Ajumako-Enyan-Esiam constituency since 2009.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008), o da nya' Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ka di.
english: In 2008, he contested in the Ghanaian General Elections and won.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anii, kɔbisnu nɛ piswai nɛ atan (18, 593) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne dua'al pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.66%) ka bas banɛ nya' nɛ o la, William Kow Arthur-Baiden, Alex Arthur, Rexford Mensah nɛ Evans Addo-Nkum.
english: He garnered 18, 593 votes which represents 51.66% of the total votes cast and hence defeated the other contestants including William Kow Arthur-Baiden, Alex Arthur, Rexford Mensah and Evans Addo-Nkum.

kusaal: O da zi'en National Democratic Congress ya'as, nya Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ka di nɛ vɔɔt Tusa pisi nɛ anaasi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi (24,752) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi dua'al pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi (52.67%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Under the ticket of the National Democratic Congress again, he contested in the 2012 Ghanaian General Elections and won by obtaining 24,752 votes which represented 52.67% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋgin la, o da nya' nɛ Ransford Emmanuel Kwesi Nyarko, Jerry Henry Quansah, Sarah Mensah nɛ Monica Daapong.
english: In that election, he contested against Ransford Emmanuel Kwesi Nyarko, Jerry Henry Quansah, Sarah Mensah and Monica Daapong.

kusaal: O da diya ka basi ba nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anu, kɔbisyuobʋ (25,601) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ atan dua'al pisnu nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (53.55%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He defeated them by obtaining 25,601 votes which represented 53.55% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghanaian wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, o da lɛn di o sʋ'ʋlim Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt Tusa pistan nɛ awai, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisi nɛ awai (39,229) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnu nɛ anii dua'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (58.1%) ka NPP nid Etuaful Rashid Kwesi paam vɔɔt Tusa pisi nɛ anii, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisi nɛ awai (28,229) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnnasi nɛ yinne dua'al anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (41.8%) ka NDP nid la, Samuel Akombisa paam kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (117) dinɛ an nɛɛm dua'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.2%) vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he again won the parliamentary seat with 39,229 votes making 58.1% of the total votes cast whiles the NPP parliamentary candidate Etuaful Rashid Kwesi had 28,229 votes making 41.8% of the total votes cast and the NDP parliamentary candidate Samuel Akombisa had 117 votes making 0.2% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) ni ka o lieb wadmaani kpɛn' Wadmaanib yin la ka lieb Minista onɛ gɔsid Gaana ligidi yɛla nya'adɔl yʋʋm Tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013).
english: In 2009, he became a member of the Parliament of Ghana and served as the deputy minister for Finance in 2013.

kusaal: On da an deputy Minista la, o da paas Ghana Economic Management Team la ni.
english: As deputy Minister he served as a member of Ghana's Economic Management Team.

kusaal: O da lɛn tʋm boardnam kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb ni ya'as nwɛnɛ, Bank of Ghana nɛ Ghana Cocoa Board.
english: He has also served on several boards including that of the Bank of Ghana and Ghana Cocoa Board.

kusaal: O da lɛn an Ghana Alternate Governor tis International Monetary Fund (IMF) nɛ World Bank.
english: He was also Ghana's Alternate Governor at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.

kusaal: O baŋir da nie paalʋ on da an kʋkdaani tis la'askanɛ da maal Ghana Integrated Financial Management Information System Reforms (GIFMIS) la.
english: His expertise was also brought to light when he chaired the Committee that implemented the Ghana Integrated Financial Management Information System Reforms (GIFMIS).

kusaal: Forson anɛ Ranking Member tis la'askanɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla (Finance Committee); o paas House Committee, Foreign Affairs Committee ka lɛn paas Selection Committee.
english: Forson is a Ranking Member of the Finance Committee; a member of the House Committee; a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee and also a member of the Committee of Selection Committee; special budget committee; House committee.

kusaal: Ba da zɛrig Forson ye o san'am Gaana ligidi, on da da ambulancena ban Kobisyi (200) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) sʋʋgʋn la.
english: Forson was alleged to have caused financial loss to Ghana in a procurement of 200 ambulances between 2014 and 2016.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la ni (2013) o da anɛ minista onɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla nya'adɔl.
english: In 2013 he served as the deputy minister for Finance.

kusaal: Forson anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) nid.
english: Forson is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la nii, nya Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ka di ka paam suori zi'eni tis o sʋ'ʋlim dim nɔɔra atan ya'as.
english: Under the ticket of the National Democratic Congress again, he contested in the 2012 Ghanaian General Elections and won by obtaining 24,752 votes which represented 52.67% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa ayi.
english: He is married and has two children.

kusaal: Catherine Ablema Afeku (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 27 Sigir/Nwadisayɔpɔi 1967) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an pɔlitis wɛ'ɛd.
english: Catherine Ablema Afeku (born June 27, 1967) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nid nɛ wadmaan tis Evalue Gwira Constituency n bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: She is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the Member of Parliament for the Evalue Gwira Constituency in the Western Region.

kusaal: O daa yi minista bɛ Tourism keŋ teŋ zugdaa ɔfis Ghana Republic bɛ 28 February 2019.Nannana on na an minista teŋ zugdaan ɔfis.
english: She was reshuffled from the Ministry of Tourism to the Presidency of the Republic of Ghana on 28 February 2019.

kusaal: O mɔr Master of Business Administration n yit Keller Graduate School of Management of DeVry University in Atlanta, Georgia n bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni.
english: She obtained a Master of Business Administration from the Keller Graduate School of Management of DeVry University in Atlanta, Georgia in the year 2000.

kusaal: Afeku daa tʋʋm nɛ dunia wʋsa Bank ni nɛ Stico Petroleum bɛ Kenya, ani ka o daa an business development consultant.
english: Afeku has worked with the World Bank and Stico Petroleum in Kenya, where she served as a business development consultant.

kusaal: O daa lɛm tʋʋm bɛ Inlingua School of languages bɛ Brescia, Italy.
english: She was also employed at the Inlingua School of languages in Brescia, Italy.

kusaal: Afeku kpɛn' Ghana dim politiks n bɛ 2000s bɛ Ghana gɔmena zudaan John Agyekum Kufuor saŋa.O daa anɛ gɔmma zʋgdaan pian'adi'es .
english: Afeku entered Ghanaian politics in the early 2000s during the presidency of John Agyekum Kufuor.

kusaal: O daa nya'ad yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Evalue Gwira constituency.
english: She contested in the 2008 general election for the Evalue Gwira constituency.

kusaal: O daa lɛm nya'ad na'am ya'as bɛ o constituency bɛ 2016 vɔtʋg la ni , ani Ka o daa nyaŋ on daa mɔr, Kweku Tanikyi Kesse onɛ zi'enɛ tis ma'asim tiig paati la, onɛ paam 11,641 vɔɔts yit 20,179, ka kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ ka o paam 57.7% yit vɔɔts la wʋsa ni.
english: She again contested the constituency's seat during the 2016 Parliamentary election, where she defeated the incumbent, Kweku Tanikyi Kesse of the National Democratic Congress, obtaining 11,641 votes out of the 20,179, representing 57.7% of total votes cast.

kusaal: O daa keŋ People's Republic of China bɛ March 2017, ani ka o daa si'el investors nɛ exhibitors ye ba sʋŋ iɛɛ tourist nam nɛ arts nɛ culture Ghana nwan.
english: In March 2017, she travelled to The People's Republic of China, where she held meetings with investors and exhibitors to showcase tourist sites and the arts and culture of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba gaan Afeku ka o an kukdaan nɛ kpɛɛm bɛ Taskforce n bɛ United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO).
english: Afeku was appointed Chairperson of the Leadership Taskforce of the United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO).

kusaal: Ba yɛl lina ka li bɛ 25 January 2018.
english: This was announced on 25 January 2018.

kusaal: Asu'oe-m-mɛŋ la'asʋg buon ye (Truth and Accountable Governance)daa fabil tis gɔmena zugdaan Akuffo-Addo ye o yisʋg minista ni bas.
english: A pressure group calling itself Truth and Accountable Governance petitioned President Akuffo-Addo to remove her from her ministerial position.

kusaal: Yʋum tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la, li nwadis anu (May 2017), ka gɔmena zugdaan Akufo-Addo gaŋi Afeku paas o minista nam piinɛ awai la ni ye ba an cabinet mimista.
english: In May 2017, President Akufo-Addo named Afeku as one of the 19 ministers who would form his cabinet.

kusaal: Catherine daa ɛli Seth Afeku ka ba mɔr biis atan'.
english: Catherine is married to Seth Afeku with whom she has three children.

kusaal: o daa di ka bas onɛ daa mɔr la, Kojo Armah onɛ daa zi'enɛ tis nɔraug paati, o paami 11,671 vɔɔts .N pass wadmaandib yikanɛ paasi anu la be Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la, yiiga o daa paasi nidiba gɔsid ti suoya nam maanlʋg yɛla anɛ ya'andɔl tis ti pian'ad nam la'asʋg .[6] nya'aŋa o daa lɛm anɛ k la'asʋg kanɛ ka ti boun business committee nid yinne .O da lʋ onɛ lɛn zi'el la bɛ 2008 vɔɔtʋg tita'a la ni.
english: She defeated the incumbent, Kojo Armah of the Convention People's Party, by obtaining 11,671 votes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la, li nwadi yinne la ni ka gɔmma zugdaan Nana Akuffo-Addo gaan Afeku onɛ Tourism minista.
english: She was a cabinet minister in the Nana Akuffo-Addo administration and served as the Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts of Ghana from February 2017 to February 2019.

kusaal: Onɛ daa an tourism minista, o daa keŋ ken bɛdigʋ ye o ku'os ti teŋ la zin'iŋ banɛ an nyalima ka teŋ si'eba kena gɔs.
english: As tourism minister, she has embarked on several trips to market the country's tourist attractions and potential.

kusaal: Vɛɛnsʋg la pʋʋginɛ wadmaanib yir la'asʋg kanɛ gɔsid vɛɛnsʋg yɛla la, daa mɔr labaar ye, Catherine nɛ o sid , ka kɔɔtʋ zɛrigir ba ye gɛɛns wada bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni ( 2007).
english: Prior to being vetted by the Parliamentary Appointment Committee, reports emerged that Catherine and her husband were defendants in a civil case of breach of contract in 2007.

kusaal: pɔɔtim pa'al ye, Accra kɔɔtʋʋ tita'ar la daa yɛl Afekus sʋm ka yɔ ligikaŋa $217,464.00 paas nɛ 50% nyɔɔd tis American couple, Patricia nɛ Bill Gick, ban daa baŋ ye gbɛlʋŋ la yinɛ ba ni la.
english: The reports showed that the Afekus had been directed by an Accra High Court to pay $217,464.00 plus 50% interest to an American couple, Patricia and Bill Gick, after charges of fraud had been brought against them.

kusaal: Catherine nɛ o sid la daa pʋ yɔ ligidi la nwɛnɛ kɔɔtʋ la yɛl si'em la.
english: Catherine and her husband had failed to honour the instructions of the court.

kusaal: On daa lɛbis si'el zaŋi keŋ yɛlkan anɛ ye o daa bɛnɛ Nairobi, Kenya nɛ o du'adib saŋa,lin ka o daa pʋ nyaŋ maalɛ.
english: Her defense for not honouring her constitutional obligation was due to her being in Nairobi, Kenya, with her parents at the stipulated time.

kusaal: o daa tis ya'a la nɛ 11 February 2017 on daa paam gbaʋŋ yi National service secretariat, ka o zaŋi tis vɛɛnsʋg la'asʋg banɛ gɔsid minista nam gaansʋg yɛla nya'aŋ.Ba daa bas o suor yinɛ ba wʋsa daa siak la.
english: Her nomination was approved on 11 February 2017 after she presented the Appointments Committee with a waiver letter given her by the National Service Secretariat.

kusaal: Mike Ocquaye ye o zaŋi ba bigis.
english: Hon. Prof. Mike Ocquaye.

kusaal: on daa cabinet minista la, Afeku daa paasi gɔmena zugdaani nɛ ba zin'il gban'e gban'asa tis teŋ la.
english: As a cabinet minister, Afeku was part of the president's inner circle and is to aid in key decision-making activities in the country.

kusaal: O an kristio biig ka Catholic Church nid.
english: She is a Christian and a member of the Catholic Church, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba daa nɔk minista nam piinɛ awai la yʋ'ʋra tis wadmaanib yir kpɛɛm Rt.
english: The names of the 19 ministers were submitted to the Parliament of Ghana and announced by the Speaker of the House, Rt.

kusaal: Catholic University College of Ghana anɛ asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ sakur kanɛ bɛ Ghana.
english: The Catholic University College of Ghana is a private universities in Ghana.

kusaal: Li bɛnɛ Fiapre, Sunyani linɛ bɛ Bono Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: It is located at Fiapre, Sunyani in the Bono Region.

kusaal: Zin'ig kaŋa ka ba gɔsid vɛɛnsig yela bɛ university la ni ka mɛ dɔlisid anina ka tɛŋ la nidib kɛn sakur la ni.
english: The centre promotes research within the university and be a creative link with the local communities.

kusaal: Di anɛ catholic jubilee malʋŋkanɛ ka Pope Celestine V nɛ o bull Inter sanctorum solemnia (ka sieba mɛ buon ye Bull of Pardon bɛɛ Bull of Forgiveness) da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyi' nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1294) la ni.
english: It is a Catholic jubilee celebration, established in 1294 by pope Celestine V with his bull Inter sanctorum solemnia (also known as Bull of Pardon or Bull of Forgiveness).

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011) la ni, malʋŋ la mɛ yʋ'ʋm paas "Heritage of Italy for tradition" ("Patrimonio d'Italia per la tradizione") ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019) la ni, ka ba da zaŋi li paas UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity ni.
english: Since 2011 the celebration is a "Heritage of Italy for tradition" ("Patrimonio d'Italia per la tradizione") and in 2019 it was inscribed in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Tembanɛ giligi di anɛ Ashanti nɛ Eastern region, ba ni bɛ li dagɔbuk ka Western region bɛɛ li tuon ka Greater Accra region bɛɛ li nya'aŋ ka Gulf of Guinea bɛɛ li datiuŋ.
english: Ashanti and Eastern regions border it to the north, Western region to the west, Greater Accra region to the east, and the Gulf of Guinea to the south.

kusaal: Cape Coast Castle nɛ Elmina Castle anɛ UNESCO World Heritage Sites tiend Trans-Atlantic slave trade la.
english: Cape Coast Castle and Elmina Castle are prominent UNESCO World Heritage Sites and serve as a reminder of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade.

kusaal: Ghana zin'ivɛnlla paa bɛnɛ Central Region ka ba mɔr beach nam nɛ national park nam (Kakum National Park).
english: The Central Region is a center for tourism within Ghana, with Kakum National Park and beach developments.

kusaal: Region la pʋnɛ MMDA's nam pisinɛ ayi ka mɔr Metropolitan yinne, Municipal nama ayɔpɔi nɛ distric assembly nam piinɛ anaasi.
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into 22 MMDA's (made up of 1 Metropolitan, 7 Municipal and 14 District Assemblies).

kusaal: Central region yʋ'ʋr laligya nɛ ban mɔr sakur sʋma nɛ ba ligidi zu'oe ka li yitnɛ ba industrial minerals nɛ tourism yɛla.
english: The Central Region has an economy based on industrial minerals and tourism.

kusaal: Central region dim na nyaŋɛ nwɛ' nyɔ'ɔg ye ba mɔr castle nam, forts nɛ beach nam ka li bɛ mu'ar la nɔɔrin.
english: The Central region has tourist attractions including castles, forts and beaches along the region's coastline.

kusaal: Ba da mɛ dinɛ yiiga ye ba mɔri kpiisid ka li nya'aŋ ka li yʋ'ʋn an suokanɛ ka Atlantic slave trade dim ɛɛnti zi'en.
english: Cape Coast Castle and Elmina Castle are prominent UNESCO World Heritage Sites and serve as a reminder of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade.

kusaal: UNESCO mi' castle la ye World Heritage Site.
english: Cape Coast Castle and Elmina Castle are prominent UNESCO World Heritage Sites and serve as a reminder of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade.

kusaal: Central Tongu kpi'enɛ nɛ North Tongu district linɛ Ghana Volta Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Central Tongu is located in the North Tongu district of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kʋk la kpi'enɛ nɛ North Tongu District linɛ bɛ Ghana Volta Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: The seat is located within the North Tongu District of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Pɔi ka yʋʋma 2004 nwadis piina ayi ni ka ba maal Gɔmina nɛ Wadmaanib vɔt la, ka Old North Tongu constituency la da pʋdignɛ linɛ ka ba buon nannanna ye North Tongu nɛ Central Tongu constituencies la.
english: Before the 2004 December presidential and parliamentary elections, old North Tongu constituency was divided into the current North Tongu and the Central Tongu constituencies.

kusaal: Central Tongu Constituency anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm kanɛ paas ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni mɛn.
english: Central Tongu is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlʋm punɛ buudi nam zi'is atan' banɛ an; Bakpa, Mafi nɛ Kpoviedzi.
english: It is made up of three Traditional areas; Bakpa, Mafi and Kpoviedzi.

kusaal: Mensah Otabil da pin'il ka di an pastanam zamisʋg sakur bɛ yʋʋm 1988 la ni.
english: It was founded as a pastoral training institute by Mensah Otabil in 1988.

kusaal: Ka June 1991 la ni ba da tiaki li yʋ'ʋn tis Central Bible College.
english: In June 1991, it was known as the Central Bible College.

kusaal: Ba da lɛm tiaki li yʋ'ʋr ka di an Central Christian College yʋʋm 1993 la ni, ba yʋ'ʋn tiaki an Central University College bɛ yʋʋm 1998 la ni.
english: In 1993, it became the Christian University College and became the Central University College (CUC) in the year 1998 after a change of name.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2016 la ni, Central University College paam su'or ye di yʋ'ʋn an University ka di yʋ'ʋr an Central University.
english: In January 2016, the University College received the long-awaited Presidential Charter to become an autonomous and a fully-fledged university as Central University.

kusaal: Dinnɛ an asʋe-mɛŋ kɔligi tita'ar bɛ Ghana ni.
english: The vice-chancellor of the university, Kwesi Yankah, is awarded Laureate for Education in Ghana by Impact Africa Summit.

kusaal: Cephas Narh Omenyo anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ mi' Wina'am gbaʋŋ ka da paas piinɛ ayɔpɔi daani an kpɛɛm tis Presbyterian Church of Ghana lin da yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, Mɔtul nwadig ni paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anii, Mɔtul nwadig la ni.
english: Cephas Narh Omenyo is a Ghanaian theologian and academic who was the 17th Moderator of the Presbyterian Church of Ghana from August 2016 to August 2018.

kusaal: Omenyo dʋ'adib anɛ Cephas Tettey Mate Omenyo nɛ Felicia Namo Omenyo.
english: Omenyo was born to Cephas Tettey Mate Omenyo and Felicia Namo Omenyo.

kusaal: Omenyo da pin'il sakur nɛ Presbyterian Primary, Middle and Secondary schools bɛ Bechem linɛ bɛ Brong Ahafo Region la.
english: Omenyo had his basic and secondary education at the Presbyterian Primary, Middle and Secondary schools at Bechem in the Brong Ahafo Region respectively.

kusaal: O da naae o sixth-form education in Science bɛ nɛ Sunyani Secondary School.
english: He completed his sixth-form education in Science at the Sunyani Secondary School.

kusaal: Omenyo da pin'il Wina'am gbaʋŋ zamisig nɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka ba da buon Trinity College (ka yʋ'ʋn buon Trinity Theological Seminary) li yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi' paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi' ni.
english: Omenyo started his theological education at the then Trinity College (now Trinity Theological Seminary) from 1982 to 1985.

kusaal: O da maal o M.Phil.
english: He obtained his M.Phil.

kusaal: (Winpʋ'ʋsʋg zamisig) bɛ University of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi ka maal Ph.D. bɛ University of Utrecht, Netherlands, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayi' ni.
english: (Study of Religions) from the University of Ghana in 1994 and his Ph.D. from the University of Utrecht, the Netherlands, in 2002.

kusaal: Ba da tik nu'ug ye Omenyo pin'il o Wina'am tʋʋma bɛ Presbyterian Church of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu ni bɛ Teshie ka da maligim paas o paŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi ni bɛ Unity Congregation, Tamale.
english: Omenyo was commissioned into the ministry of the Presbyterian Church of Ghana in June 1985 at Teshie and ordained in 1987 at the Unity Congregation, Tamale.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anii, Mɔtul nwadig dabpisi nɛ atan' daar, Joseph Obiri Yeboah Mante kanɛ da an kpɛɛm tis Trinity Theological Seminary dim la ka ba da gaŋ ye o di'e Omenyo an kpɛɛm kanɛ paas piinɛ anii daan tis Presbyterian Church of Ghana, Akropong-Akuapem.
english: On 23 August 2018 Joseph Obiri Yeboah Mante, immediate past President of the Trinity Theological Seminary, was elected to succeed Omenyo as the 18th Moderator of the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church of Ghana at the end of the 18th General Assembly in Akropong-Akuapem.

kusaal: Omenyo pʋ'a yʋ'ʋri buon Rosekel, o anɛ pa'an pa'an.
english: Omenyo is married to Rosekel, a teacher and librarian.

kusaal: O da naae University of Ghana ka paam gbaʋŋi bɛ tɛŋgbaŋ nɛ Winpʋ'ʋsʋg yela.
english: (Study of Religions) from the University of Ghana in 1994 and his Ph.D. from the University of Utrecht, the Netherlands, in 2002.

kusaal: Ba da vooti tis Omenyo ye o an tuongati bɛ Presbyterian Church of Ghana yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, Mɔtul nwadig ni.
english: Omenyo was elected Moderator of the Presbyterian Church of Ghana in August 2016.

kusaal: O paas nɛ anu' daan, o dʋ'adib biis piiga la pʋʋgin (dasam ayɔpɔi nɛ pʋ'asada atan').
english: He is the fifth among 10 children (seven male and three female).

kusaal: Ba mɔr biribis ayi' nɛ bipʋŋ yinnɛ.
english: They have two sons and a daughter.

kusaal: Chakalaka anԑ South African dikanԑ an vaand, ka ba maan ka kpaam wʋm sʋ'ʋŋa, ka ba dit nԑ bodobodo, pap, dafaduka, bԑԑ sitiw.
english: Chakalaka is a South African vegetable relish, usually spicy, that is traditionally served with bread, pap, samp, stews, or curries.

kusaal: Chakalaka yinԑ tԑԑns banԑ bԑ Johannesburg, zin'is banԑ ka ba tuud sanlima la ni, sanlim tuudib sieba banԑ an Mozambic dim da nͻki ba tamantoos bԑԑ bԑŋa dibanԑ ka ba su' kͻliba ni dugu gԑndig Nanzʋ'ʋs ka li yʋ'ʋn wan wʋʋ Portuguese-tԑŋ dim diib, ye ba tʋ'ʋs nԑ pap.
english: Chakalaka is said to have originated in the townships of Johannesburg or in the gold mines surrounding Johannesburg, when Mozambican mineworkers leaving their shift cooked tinned produce (tomatoes, beans) with chili to produce a spicy Portuguese-style relish to accompany pap.

kusaal: Ba mͻr bԑŋa, cabbage bԑԑ tomato maan si'eba.
english: Some versions include beans, cabbage and butternut squash.

kusaal: Sieba mͻr bԑŋa banԑ ka ba dʋgʋ sʋ kͻliba ni kuosid, bԑԑ tomatoos, bԑԑ gabʋ bԑԑ garlic, bԑԑ Nanzʋ'ʋs ma'asa maani li.
english: For example, canned baked beans, canned tomatoes, onion, garlic, and curry paste can be used to make the dish.

kusaal: Chakali anɛ Gur pian'ad nam banɛ bɛ Ghana la yinnɛ, ka nidib banɛ pian'adi li an tʋsa atan' nɛ kɔbisnu yela bɛ tɛnkpɛmis banɛ bɛ Wa East District linɛ bɛ Upper West Region.
english: Chakali (tʃàkálɪ́ɪ́) is a Gur language of Ghana, spoken by almost 3,500 individuals in several villages in the Wa East District of the Upper West Region.

kusaal: Tɛɛns banɛ pian'ad Chakali anɛ Tiisa, Sogla, Tousa, Motigu, Ducie, Katua nɛ Gurumbele.
english: More specifically, Chakali is spoken by inhabitants of the Tiisa, Sogla, Tousa, Motigu, Ducie, Katua and Gurumbele villages.

kusaal: Nidib banɛ pian'ad Chakali la tita'am mɛ pian'ad Wali bɛɛ Bulengi.
english: Some believe that the language of Chakali is soon to be extinct, with Wali and Bulengi becoming the only languages that will be spoken in those villages.

kusaal: Si'eba ye saŋa na kɛna ka Chakali pian'ad la kʋ lɛn bɛ ya'asɛ, ka nidib banɛ tɛŋ ban ni la yʋ'ʋn na pian'ad nɛ Wali nɛ Bulengi.
english: Some believe that the language of Chakali is soon to be extinct, with Wali and Bulengi becoming the only languages that will be spoken in those villages.

kusaal: Chakkirako (Japanese: チャッキラコ) anɛ wa'a kanɛ ka ba wa'ad malima nam ni bɛ Miura, Japan sʋ'ʋlim, yʋʋmpaal malima ye ba nyɛ zugsʋŋ, li kas-kas anɛ ba zimi gban'ab yɛla.
english: Chakkirako (Japanese: チャッキラコ) is a dance performed at a festival in Miura, Japan, to celebrate the New Year and bring good fortune, especially in fishing.

kusaal: Chala (Cala) anɛ Gur pian'ad buudi yinnɛ bɛ Ghana.
english: Chala (Cala) is a Gur language of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) la ni, Chamamé da paas UNESCO Intangible cultural heritage la'ad la ni Argentina da gaŋi li yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) ni la.
english: In 2020, Chamamé was inscribed in UNESCO's Intangible cultural heritage list after it was nominated by Argentina in 2018.

kusaal: Jesuit reductions dinɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlimin la kpɛmisid buudi malima nɔbʋgir ka di da an ala keŋ paae sankanɛ ka Spanish Crown da yis Jesuits la 18th century naarin.
english: Jesuit reductions in the area encouraged cultural growth that lasted until the Jesuits were expelled by the Spanish Crown in the late 18th century.

kusaal: Zin'ikaŋa ni, Yapeyú, Corrientes da an buudi malima yʋʋma wʋsa tensʋk centre ka nidib bɛdegʋ tiesidi pa'an ye Chamamé yinɛ anina.
english: Within this area, Yapeyú, Corrientes was a centre of musical culture that many point to as the birthplace of the original Chamamé.

kusaal: Ban da maan Chamamé si'em kʋdʋmin la nwɛnɛ 20th century la ni nam bɛ nananna, ka ban yʋ'ʋr la ye 'Chamamé' da pʋm bɛnɛ hali yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan nɛ yinne (1931) la ni; yʋʋm bama buudi, din da nan kae la, ba da buoni linɛ Corrientes Polka.
english: There are recordings of Chamamé dating back to the early 20th century, and the term 'Chamamé' was already used in 1931; this type of music, prior to that, was often referred to as the Corrientes Polka.

kusaal: Chamamé, yinɛ schottische ka Volga German immigrants da mɔri li kena, ka di mɔr Guaraní tiakir, la'asnɛ Spanish guitar nɛ European accordion yi nimbanɛ da mɔri li ken' zin'igin la na 20th century la saŋa.
english: The Chamamé, originally schottische brought by the Volga German immigrants, has considerable Guaraní influence, mixed with the Spanish guitar and the European accordion from those immigrants that arrived in the area at the beginning of the 20th century.

kusaal: Chamamé kaalʋg wʋsa pʋʋgin anɛ Teresa Parodi, Tránsito Cocomarola, Ramona Galarza nɛ Chango Spasiuk.
english: Among chamamé figures of note are Teresa Parodi, Tránsito Cocomarola, Alejandro Brittes, Ramona Galarza, and Chango Spasiuk.

kusaal: Chamamé lɛn anɛ buudi malima yʋʋma ka ba nwɛ'ɛdi li South America titɔdig baba, nwɛnɛ Paraguay nɛ Uruguay.
english: In 2020, Chamamé was inscribed in UNESCO's Intangible cultural heritage list after it was nominated by Argentina in 2018.

kusaal: Ka ban nwɛ'ɛd nɛ bʋnnwɛ'ɛdanam nwɛnɛ Spanish guitar, nɛ googi nɛ accordion nami gɛndigid la, dinɛ kɛ ka ba pʋdi li ye "Chamamé".
english: Further mixing with instruments such as the Spanish guitar, then the violin and the accordion, finally resulted in what is currently known as "Chamamé".

kusaal: Charles Acheampong anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Lower West Akim Constituency bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim la Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Charles Acheampong is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Lower West Akim Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O anɛ board member tis Ghana News Agency.
english: He is currently a board member of the Ghana News Agency.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Acheampong nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne Nwadisa anu daba awai daar (9 May, 1981) ka o yi Osenase bɛ Eastern region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Acheampong was born on 9 May 1981 and hails from Osenase in the Eastern Region.

kusaal: o da maali o Masters degree in Wireless Communication yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012).
english: He had his Masters degree in Wireless Communication in 2012.

kusaal: Acheampong da anɛ manager tis National Communications Authority.
english: Acheampong was the manager of the National Communications Authority.

kusaal: Acheampong bɛnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, NPP ni ka an Wadmaani tis Lower Akim West Constituency bɛ Eastern region.
english: Acheampong is a member of NPP and currently the MP for the Lower Akim West Constituency in the Eastern region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, o da di kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisnu nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (27,527) ka NDC nid la, Micheal Adu-Sei paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ awai, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anaasi (19,744) GUM nid la, Baidoo Seth Nicholas Kwame paam vɔɔt kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi (464).
english: In the 2020 Ghana general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 27,527 votes whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Micheal Adu-Sei had 19,744 votes and the GUM parliamentary aspirant Baidoo Seth Nicholas Kwame had 464 votes.

kusaal: Acheampong paasnɛ Public Accounts Committee nɛ Communications Committee.
english: Acheampong is a member of the Public Accounts Committee and also a member of Communications Committee.

kusaal: Acheampong anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Acheampong is a Christian.

kusaal: Charles Akwesi Agbeve du'anɛ nwadisa ayɔpɔi dapisi nɛ yinne yʋʋm 1970 la ni anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛn'ɛd (Ghanaian politician) ka an Agotime-Ziope wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la ni Republic of Ghana kanɛ paasi anaasi la sʋ'ʋlimi bɛ Volta Region la.
english: Charles Akwesi Agbeve (born 21 July 1970) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Agotime-Ziope Constituency in the Volta Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Charles Agbeve nɛ Ziope Honugo bɛ Volta Region, Ghana.
english: Charles Agbeve was born in Ziope Honugo in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Charles Agbeve da sɔbi o Common Entrance Examination nɛ yʋʋm tusir, yinne, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi (1982) ka lin da tis o suor k'o da maali o Ordinary Level yʋʋm tusir, yinne kɔbis wai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi (1987) la, ka maali o Advanced Level yʋʋm tusir yinne kɔbis wai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (1989) la ni.
english: Charles Agbeve passed his Common Entrance Examination in 1982 which enabled him to obtain his Ordinary Level in 1987 and Advanced Level in 1989.

kusaal: O da tɔlis tuoni maali o Bachelor of Science(Bsc) nɛ Maths Diploma In Education yʋʋm tusir yinne kɔbis wai nɛ piswai nɛ anu (1995) la University of Cape Coast.
english: He then proceeded to have his Bachelor of Science(Bsc) and Maths Diploma In Education in 1995 from University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: Charles Agbeve da tɔlisi maali o Master of Business Administration – Finance Option (Health Insurance) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2002) la ni, University of Ghana, Legon – Ghana.
english: Charles Agbeve continued to have his Master of Business Administration – Finance Option (Health Insurance) in 2002 from University of Ghana, Legon – Ghana.

kusaal: Charles Agbeve mɛ da lɛn maali o Master of Arts (Economic Policy Management) din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la ni.
english: Charles Agbeve also obtained his Master of Arts (Economic Policy Management) from 2017–2018.

kusaal: Charles Agbeve da anɛ Maths and Science Teacher, Ghanatta Senior High School.
english: Charles Agbeve served as a Maths and Science Teacher at Ghanatta Senior High School.

kusaal: Charles Agbeve da lɛn anɛ Ghana Aluminium Products Limited Commercial Manager.
english: Charles Agbeve has also worked as the Commercial Manager for Ghana Alumnium Products Limited.

kusaal: O da lɛn niŋ District/Municipal manager Ho municipal National Health Insurance Authority, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni, ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la.
english: He also worked as the District /Municipal Manager of National Health Insurance Authority, Ho Municipal Office from 2009 to 2016.

kusaal: Nananna nwa, Charles Agbeve anɛ Agotime-Ziope wadmaan (Member of Parliament MP) lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ anu (2025) la.
english: Charles Agbeve is now working as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Agotime-Ziope Constituency from 2021 to 2025.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015) la, Charles Agbeve da nya' Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg vɔɔtʋg la Agotime-Ziope Constituency bɛ Volta Region, Ghana la.
english: In 2015, Charles Agbeve contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Agotime-Ziope Constituency in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Charles Agbeve da zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la zugʋ nya' ka di Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ka da di ya'anɛ ken paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi 7th Parliament of the Fouth Republic of Ghana .
english: Charles Agbeve also won the parliamentary seat in his constituency during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress to join the Seventh (7th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn di ya'an nɛ vɔɔtnam (19143) dinɛ an pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al pisnii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (87.80%) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi 2020 vɔɔtʋg la ni ken paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He won again with 19143 vote (87.80%) in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament which is the current Parliament now until 2025.

kusaal: 2019 yʋʋm la ni, on nɛ o wadmaan taaba da keŋ Tepaye ba kaae ka gɔs Kumawu Sekeyere District Hospital nɛ Fomena District Hispital banɛ ka ba nyɔrigi li bas la, ks la'am paas ye li sʋm ks Gɔbina la mɔr nimmua nɛ sibiti bibis (health centre) la yɛla.
english: In 2019, he, with other members of Parliament, visited Tepa to tour the abandoned Kumawu Sekeyere District Hospital and the Fomena District Hospital concluding that the government should pay attention to the health center.

kusaal: Charles Agbeve paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Government Assurance Committee la nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid nimma'asim yɛla (Health Committee) Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Republic of Ghana kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Charles Agbeve is a member of the Government Assurance Committee and Health Committee of the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: MP Charles Agbeve kpɛmis langima nam kpɛɛm la, IGP George Dampare ye o vɛɛnsim langima nam daamigi daa kɛ ka dau kanɛ daa an woo yʋʋma pistan' (30s) kpi la, kum la yɛla.
english: MP Charles Agbeve urged IGP George Dampare to investigate a suspected case of police brutality that led to the death of a man in his 30s.

kusaal: O daa pian' nɛŋa nɛ zaŋi kenɛ dau nwa Felix Azibodzi onɛ kpi yidimɛ daa yɛl ye, ba daa gban'ae nid nwa la nɛ ka ye o paas nɛ nimbanɛ faaen sɔ' lɔr Ho teŋ la ni, ka man' o kpɛn'ɛsi li vɛɛnsʋg nii ti kʋʋ o.
english: This comment was made after the family of the late Felix azibodzi says, he was arrested for allegedly being part of a car-snatching incident in Ho, after being lured into an investigative issues.

kusaal: Charles Agbeve anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Charles Agbeve is a Christian.

kusaal: Charles Binipom Bintin anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Saboba Constituency bɛ Northern Region la wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
