english: Charles Binipom Bintin is a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Saboba Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Charles Binipom Bintin nɛ Kuntuli-Saboba dinɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi nwadis anii dabpisi nɛ ayi daar (22 August 1964).
english: Charles Binipom Bintin was born in Kuntuli-Saboba in the Northern Region of Ghana on 22 August 1964.

kusaal: O da keŋ University of Ghana maal Diploma in Adult Education yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999) la ni ka da tɔlisi keŋ University of Cape Coast maali o post graduate studies in Arts yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la ni.
english: He went to University of Ghana and obtained a Diploma in Adult Education in 1999 and later proceeded to the University of Cape Coast for his post graduate studies in Arts in the year 2007.

kusaal: Charles Binipom Bintin da kpɛn' wadmaannib yin la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu yʋʋmpaal nwadig daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2005) wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug ban da vɔɔt o ye o lieb wadmaan tis Saboba Constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) (nwadis piinɛ ayi' la ni).
english: Charles Binipom Bintin entered parliament on 7 January 2005 on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party and he was elected as the member of parliament for the Saboba Constituency in the 2004 Ghanaian general election in December.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ye o lieb wadmaani tsi Saboba Constituency fourth parliament la fourth republic of Ghana zugraan kʋdʋg J.A Kufour saŋa.
english: He was elected as the member of parliament for the Saboba Constituency in the fourth parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana under His excellency the Ex-President J.A Kufour's administration.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa piiga, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yinne (10,441) dinɛ zi'eni tis vɔɔt pisnu nɛ atan' du'al pisyuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (53.60%) ka oa taaba la, Bilijo Nayon onɛ bɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress la da paam vɔɔt tusa ayɔpɔi, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (7,892) dinɛ zi'eni tis vɔɔt pisnaasi du'al pisnu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (40.50%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka Kenneth Wujangi onɛ bɛ People's National Convention la da paam vɔɔt tusir yinne, kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (1,157) din mɛ zɛmnɛ vɔɔti anu du'al piswai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (5.90%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He obtain a total vote cast of 10,441 which represent 53.60% whiles his opponent candidates, Bilijo Nayon of the National Democratic Congress polled 7,892 representing 40.50% of the vote and Kenneth Wujangi of the People's National Convention obtained 1,157 also representing 5.90% of the total vote cast.

kusaal: Charles Binipom Bintim da tʋmnɛ Ghana gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la, Ghana Education Service an pa'an (Tutor) bɛ Evangelical Presbyterian Secondary School yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne (2001) la ni.
english: Charles Binipom Bintim worked with Ghana Education Service as a Tutor in Evangelical Presbyterian Secondary School in the year 1999 to 2001.

kusaal: O da anɛ Diisi (District Chief Executive) tis Saboba-Chereponi District yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne (2001) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan (2003) la ni.
english: He was the District Chief Executive for Saboba-Chereponi District in the 2001 to 2003.

kusaal: O da anɛ Northern Region minister nya'andɔl yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan (2003) la keŋ paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) ka da lieb wadmaani tis Saboba Constituency din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009).
english: He was the Deputy Minister for Northern Region in the year 2003 to 2005 and the Member of Parliament for Saboba Constituency in the year 2005 to 2009.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Minister for Local Government din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009).
english: He was also the Minister for Local Government in the year 2005 to 2009.

kusaal: Charles Binipom Bintin da diya lieb wadmaani tis Saboba Constituency.
english: Charles Binipom Bintin emerged as the winner of the Saboba Constituency.

kusaal: Charles Binipom Bintim mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa atan ka an Kristo biig.
english: Charles Binipom Bintim worked with Ghana Education Service as a Tutor in Evangelical Presbyterian Secondary School in the year 1999 to 2001.

kusaal: Charles Forson (dʋ'am 12 Vaala 1974) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ maan politis ka lɛn maan kpikpiŋ.
english: Charles Forson (born 12 April 1974) is a Ghanaian politician and business executive.

kusaal: O paas New Patriotic Party (NPP) na'adɔɔg ni ka an wadmaani tis Tema Central Constituency bɛ Parliament of Ghana.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Tema Central Constituency in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Forson yit nɛ Taido linɛ bɛ Western Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Forson hails from Taido in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr da'adiib gbaʋŋ yi Institute of Professional Studies yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi Mɔtul nwadig la ni.
english: He obtained a Certificate in Marketing from the Institute of Professional Studies in August 2007.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ tuoni zamis tuongaadig zamisig bɛ Oxford University Department of Continuing Education yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai, Sigir nwadig la ni.
english: He later completed a leadership programme at the Oxford University Department of Continuing Education in October 2019.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ, Sigir nwadig la ni, o da paam gbaʋŋ kanɛ an Master's in Business Administration bɛ Accra Business School, banɛ la'asi ba mɛŋ nɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology la.
english: In June 2021, he earned a Master's in Business Administration from Accra Business School, affiliated with the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology.

kusaal: Forson da tʋm da'adiib tʋʋma bɛ Voting Technik Motors and Honda Place.
english: Forson has held marketing roles at Voting Technik Motors and Honda Place, where he worked as a marketing manager and consultant.

kusaal: O da tʋm da'adiib tʋʋma ya'asi bɛ Primeland Estates Limited ka da lɛn an Executive Chairman tis Prime Pharmacy Limited.
english: He later served as managing director of Primeland Estates Limited and is the Executive Chairman of Prime Pharmacy Limited.

kusaal: Parliament of Ghana pʋʋgin, o paas banɛ gɔsid tʋmtʋmnib nɛ banɛ tʋmi ba tʋʋma paae ba kʋli vʋ'ʋs, ka lɛn an tuongati tis Backbenchers' Business Committee.
english: In Parliament, he is a member of the Employment, Labour Relations and Pensions Committee and the Chairperson of the Backbenchers' Business Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi vootʋg la ni, ba da vooti tis o ye o kɛŋ Parliament of Ghana dɔlis nɛ New Patriotic Party na'adɔɔg la ni, ka o da zi'eni tis nɛ Tema Central Constituency.
english: In the 2024 general elections, he was elected to the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party to represent the Tema Central Constituency.

kusaal: Charles Konadu-Yiadom (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 24 Sigsaa/Nwadisayuobʋ 1968) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni n tis Nkoranza South linɛ bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Charles Konadu-Yiadom is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Nkoranza South Constituency in the Bono East Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da di'e o Diploma kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ zamisʋg linɛ an Democracy, Na'am diib yɛla, kpɛmbir nɛ Nɔbigir n yi University of Ghana sakurin la.
english: He had his Diploma in Democracy, Governance, Leadership and Development from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Konadu-Yiadom da an Darɛta n bɛ Brite Life Microfinance tʋʋma la ni.
english: Konadu-Yiadom was the Director at Brite Life Microfinance.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaan n tis Nkoranza South sʋ'ʋlʋm lin da yi 2017 ti paae yʋʋma la ni 2021.
english: He was the Member of Parliament for Nkoranza South Constituency from 2017 to 2021.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2016 vootʋg la ni ka Ghana dim da maal vɔt la ka o di, o da paamnɛ vɔt bam 22,300 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 50.7% vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni ka Ma'asim Na'adɔɔg Tiig nid la Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum mɛ da mɔr vɔt bam 21,315 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 48.5% yi vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni, ka PPP nid la Emmanuel Osei Antwi mɛ da mɔr 227 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 0.5% n yi vootʋg la kanl wʋsa ni, ka CPP nid Justice Baah Mathuselah da mɔr 100 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 0.2% yi vootʋg la wʋsa ni, ka PNC nid Florence Ampour da mɔr vɔt bam 25 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 0.1% vɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 22,300 votes making 50.7% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum had 21,315 votes making 48.5% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Emmanuel Osei Antwi had 227 votes making 0.5% of the total votes cast, the CPP parliamentary candidate Justice Baah Mathuselah had 100 votes making 0.2% of the total votes cast, the PNC parliamentary candidate Florence Ampour had 25 votes making 0.1% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn da' kʋkʋs wʋʋ bam kɔbis yi (200) n tis Nkoranza Senior High Technical Sakur la.Yʋʋma 2019 la ni, ka o da nɔk ligidi GHS 26,000.00 n sʋŋ ka ba tu bulis n tis Nkoranza Senior High Technical Sakur.
english: In 2019, he also donated about GHS 26,000.00 to support the construction of a borehole to the Nkoranza Senior High Technical School.

kusaal: Nwadis piinɛ yinne la ni yʋʋma 2017 la ni, ka ba da yinɛ pian'a ye Konadu-Yiadom nwɛ'ɛ Diana Attaa Kissiwaa malifu, Nkoranza sʋ'ʋlʋm D.E.C. la ba da yinɛ nɛ pian'adnam bɛdigʋ na'asaa sɔɔngin.
english: In November 2017, it was alleged Konadu-Yiadom fired gunshot at Diana Attaa Kissiwaa, the then Municipal Chief Executive of Nkoranza on social media.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Konadu-Yiadom nɛ nwadis anu la dabisim piisi nɛ anaasi la yʋʋma1968 o yinɛ Nkoranza linɛ bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana la.
english: Konadu-Yiadom was born on 24 May 1968 and hails from Nkoranza in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Konadu-Yiadom anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Konadu-Yiadom is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2020 vɔt la ni ka Ghana dim da maal la ka o kɔŋ kʋk la ka Ma'asim Tiig nid Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum di ka bas o.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he lost the parliamentary seat to the NDC parliamentary candidate Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum.

kusaal: Konadu-Yiadom da mɔri vɔt bam 22,219 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 43.04% n yi vɔt la wʋsa ni ka Ma'asim Tiig nid la Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum mɛ da mɔr 29,408 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 56.96% vɔt la wʋsa ni, ka PNC nid la Florence Ampour da mɔr zaalim 0 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 0% vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: Konadu-Yiadom had 22,219 votes making 43.04% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum had 29,408 votes making 56.96% of the total votes cast, the PNC parliamentary candidate Florence Ampour had 0 votes making 0% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Konadu-Yiadom anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Konadu-Yiadom is a Christian.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2018 la ni, ka o da tis sakur bibis banɛ sɔbidi akarim gaad taaba (BECE) la diib n bɛ o sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni ba sɔbʋg saŋa la.
english: In 2018, he provided food to the BECE candidates in his constituency during the exams period.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka ti Ghana pulis da yina yɛl ye li ka'a sidaa.
english: The Ghana Police later denied those allegations.

kusaal: Charles Omar Nyanor (1 Sɛnlʋŋ 1935 – 30 Vaala 2004) da anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ mi' da'a diib yela, mi' politis yela, ka tʋm banki ni, ka mi' wada, ka da zi'en Upper Denkyira constituency nɔba zug.
english: Charles Omar Nyanor (1 September 1935 – 30 April 2004) was a Ghanaian economist, political scientist, banker, lawyer, industrialist and politician who represented the Upper Denkyira constituency.

kusaal: O da yit nɛ Dunkwa-on-Offin.
english: He was from Dunkwa-on-Offin.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ sakur nɛ University College, London nɛ Lincoln's Inn, London, anina ka o paam kasɛta gbaʋŋ kanɛ an Bachelor of Science degree in economics yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi ni.
english: He attended University College, London and Lincoln's Inn, London, where he attained a Bachelor of Science degree in economics in 1964.

kusaal: O da kilim banki ni tʋmtʋm bɛ Institute of Bankers (AIB), London yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu ni.
english: He also became an Associate of the Institute of Bankers (AIB), London in 1965.

kusaal: Nyanor da lɛb Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi ni, ka da tʋm tʋʋma bɛ National Investment Bank.
english: Nyanor returned to Ghana in 1967, and worked as the Senior Project Officer in the Project Appraisal and Implementation and legal work associated with project implementation at the National Investment Bank.

kusaal: On da an minista kanɛ gɔsid ligidi yela la, o da paasi muk ka Merchant Bank kɛn na, ba da mɔr sʋŋiri tis ninbanɛ maan kpikpiŋ.
english: In the ministry of finance he was instrumental in the establishment of the Merchant Bank, the small business promotion scheme and the bank for housing and construction.

kusaal: Ba da vooti tis o ka o kɛŋ Parliament of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ ni, o na'adɔɔg da anɛ New Patriotic Party.
english: He was later elected into the Parliament of Ghana in 1996, as a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Nyanor da lɛn an minista kanɛ gɔsid asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ dim tʋʋma nɔbigir yela bɛ President J.A. Kuffour Gomɛna la ni ka lɛn kɛŋ tuoni an minista kanɛ gɔsid asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ tʋʋma tuon kɛn yela.
english: Nyanor also served as minister of private sector development under President J.A. Kuffour and subsequently as minister of state in charge of Divestiture implementation committee.

kusaal: On da nan vʋe la, Nana Kwaku Ofori II, Dunkwahene, da ye C.O. Nyanor na di'e o zin'ig, o vʋ'ʋsʋg saŋa ya'a ti paae.
english: During his lifetime, the late uncle, Nana Kwaku Ofori II, Dunkwahene, proposed C.O. Nyanor to succeed him after his reign.

kusaal: Ba da vooti tis o bɛ yʋʋm tusayi vootʋg la ni, nidib banɛ da vooti tis o da anɛ tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi; o da di ya'an ka bas o kpia Kwaku Oduro-Bonsu onɛ da zi'en National Democratic Congress na'adɔɔg zug la, nidib tusa piinɛ atan', kɔbistan' nɛ pistan' nɛ anu da vooti tis o, nɛ Beatrice Buadu onɛ da zi'en Convention Peoples Party na'adɔɔg zug ka nidib kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ yinnɛ vooti tis o, nɛ Apeko-Kow Anderson onɛ da zi'en National Reform Party na'adɔɔg zug ka nidib kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnii nɛ awai da vooti tis o, nɛ Kwasi Antoban Joseph onɛ da zi'eni tis United Ghana Movement ka nidib kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi da vooti tis o la, bama wʋsa da nya'a na'am bɛ Upper Denkyira constituency.
english: He was elected during the 2000 Ghanaian General Elections where he polled 25,994 of votes cast which represents 63.90 of the total votes cast over his opponents; Kwaku Oduro-Bonsu of the National Democratic Congress who polled 13,335 votes representing 32.80% of the total votes cast, Beatrice Buadu of the Convention Peoples Party who obtained 891 votes representing 2.20% of the total votes cast, Apeko-Kow Anderson of the National Reform Party who also polled 289 representing 0.70% of the total votes cast and Kwasi Antoban Joseph of the United Ghana Movement polling 167 votes which represent 0.40% of the total votes cast for the Upper Denkyira constituency.

kusaal: Nyanor tʋʋma da anɛ onɛ sa'an nidib ligidi digilig yela bɛ National Investment Bank, Accra.
english: Nyanor worked as the Senior Investment development officer of the National Investment Bank, Accra.

kusaal: Nyanor da anɛ Methodist Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg nid, ka mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis.
english: Nyanor was a devout Methodist, and was married with children.

kusaal: O da paas Parliament of Ghana.
english: He was a member of the 1st Parliament of the 2nd Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Charles Omar Nyanor nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ anu, Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig la pin'ilig daar.
english: Charles Omar Nyanor was born on 1 September 1935.

kusaal: O da kilim Barrister-at-Law yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ ni.
english: He became a Barrister-at-Law in 1966.

kusaal: K.A. Busia Gomɛna saŋa, lin da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' (Progress Party).
english: C.O. as affectionately called by his colleagues served as the deputy minister, Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning under the government of Dr. K.A. Busia from 1969 to 1972 (Progress Party).

kusaal: O da pa'al ye lin yela ka o kʋ nyaŋi di'e Dunkwa-hene na'am kʋk la zin'inɛ.
english: He offered the excuse as one of the main reasons why he refused acceding to the Dunkwa-hene throne.

kusaal: O da paas wadmaanib Parliament of Ghana.
english: He was also a member of the Third Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Charlotte Kesson-Smith Osei, Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm 1969 nwadisa ayi la ni li dabisir yinnɛ daar, o anɛ kɔmisina vɔtʋʋg la ni, o lɛn anɛ Ghana wadmaan ka mɛ kʋkdaan kʋdʋg kanɛ da tʋm vɔɔtʋg tʋʋma Ghana nil in yi yʋm 2015 keŋ paae yʋm 2018 nwadisa ayuobʋ la nika ba da yisʋ tʋʋma la ni.
english: Charlotte Kesson-Smith Osei (born 1 February 1969) is a Ghanaian lawyer and former chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Ghana from 2015 until she was dismissed in June 2018 on grounds of financial malfeasance.

kusaal: Osei da kɛŋ nɛ sakur bɛ Ghana National College linɛ bɛ Cape Coast.
english: Charlotte Osei had her secondary education at the Ghana National College in Cape Coast.

kusaal: O da tɔlis nɛ kɛŋ University of Ghana zin'g kanɛ ka o paam o LLB yʋm 1992 la ni nɛ Ghana sakur kanɛ ka ba maan wadanam la anina ka o paam mi'ilim k aba buolʋ yɛ o tʋm yʋm 1994.
english: She proceeded to the University of Ghana where she obtained her LLB in 1992 and Ghana School of Law to be called to the bar in 1994.

kusaal: O mɛ mɔri Master of Business Leadeaship ka li yinɛ University of South Africa, Pretoria yʋm 2006, Master of (LLM), yitnɛ Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario, Canada.
english: She also holds Master of Business Leadership (MBL) from the University of South Africa, Pretoria (2006), Master of Laws, (LLM), from Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario, Canada.

kusaal: o da tʋmnɛ wʋʋ wadmaanɛ bɛ Laryea kɔmpen Accra lin yi yʋm 1994 kɛŋ paae 1997, o mɛ da anɛ kpɛɛm bɛ Ghana Commercial Bank lin yi yʋm 1997 keŋ paae yʋm 2002.
english: She worked as a lawyer for Laryea Company in Accra from 1994 to 1997, then as Senior Legal Officer at the Ghana Commercial Bank from 1997 until 2002.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn pa'anɛ Commicial Law bɛ University yʋm 1997 paae 2003.
english: She also lectured part-time in commercial law at the university from 1997 until 2003.

kusaal: Lin yi yʋm 2002 paae yʋm 2005, Osei da tʋm nɛ generai counsel tʋʋma bɛ Ghana Unibank la ni, ka lin yi yʋm 2005 paae yʋm 2011 ka an onɛ pin'il nɛ tuongat bɛ Business Lawyers.
english: From 2002 to 2005, Osei worked as general counsel for Unibank Ghana, and then from 2005 to 2011 as founder and lead counsel for business lawyers, Prime Attorneys.

kusaal: O da anɛ kʋkdaan bɛ National Commissioner for Civil Education yʋm 2011 paae yʋm 2015.
english: She was chairperson of the National Commission for Civic Education from 2011 to 2015.

kusaal: Yʋm 2015, ba da gaŋ o nɛ yɛ o an kʋkdaan bɛ Electoral Commission of Ghana ka o tʋm zugraan tʋʋma tis Ghana yʋm 2016 Presidential and Parliamentary Elections la ni yʋm 2019 nwadisa anu la ni, United Nations da gaŋi Charlotte Osei ka o an International Non-Voting Electoral Commissioner tis Ashraf Ghani.
english: In May 2019, the United Nations appointed Charlotte Osei as an International Non-Voting Electoral Commissioner to Afghanistan.

kusaal: Ghana supreme court dim da mɔnɛ pian'ad tuam wadanam kɔn'kɔnb ayi.
english: She became the first female to serve in the office of the Electoral Commission of Ghana since the country's independence.

kusaal: O da anɛ pʋ'akanɛ an yiiga sɔb tum Electoral Commission of Ghana lin yi saŋkanɛ ka Ghana da paam Asʋmmɛŋ la ni.
english: She became the first female to serve in the office of the Electoral Commission of Ghana since the country's independence.

kusaal: Ban da nan pʋ nɔkʋ tʋʋma la ni la, o da anɛ kʋkdaan bɛ National Comission for Civil Education.
english: She was previously the chairperson of the National Commission for Civic Education.

kusaal: Yʋm 2019 nwadisa anu la ni, ka United Nations dim da gaŋi o yɛ o an pian'azug sa'alisna ni, ka mɛ sʋŋ ka yʋm 2019 pɛrizidɛn vɔɔt la tʋʋma kɛŋ sʋm bɛ Afghanistan.
english: In May 2019, she was appointed by the United Nations to be on a team of international advisors, to assist in managing the 2019 presidential elections in Afghanistan.

kusaal: Ba da dua Osei nɛ Nigeria, o ma kanɛ da la'as nɛ West Africa teŋ la da ka' Ghana nida ka o saam mɛ la'as nɛ West Africa tɛŋ, o mɔr duadib banɛ an Ghana nidib.
english: Charlotte Osei was born in Nigeria.

kusaal: Osei da anɛ pa'an nyandɔl bɛ wadmaanib ni, University of Legon, Legon yʋm 1994 kɛŋ paae yʋm 1995.
english: Charlotte Osei was a teaching assistant at the Faculty of Law, University of Ghana, Legon in 1994 to 1995.

kusaal: On an Non-Voting Electoral Commissioner o da tis nɛ gu'ud bɛ Commissioner la ni ka ti'ebid vɔɔtʋg kanɛ wʋsa lɛb anina baba, o da sʋŋʋd yɛ o kɛ' ka dinɛ wʋsa bɛ vɔɔtʋg ni ka an daʋŋ, o na kɛ' k aba maal si'el wʋsa sʋŋa ka daaʋŋ kae li ni.
english: As a Non-Voting Electoral Commissioner, she provided guidance to the Commission in the preparation and drafting of all election-related regulations and policies, and support in the adjudication of complaints in a fair, independent and legal manner to ensure electoral justice throughout the entire electoral cycle.

kusaal: Ba kʋk la bɛnɛ Saboba/Chereponi district bɛ North East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Saboba/Chereponi district of the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Doris Asibi Asiedu da maal ka'alimnɛ yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ awai nwadisa ayɔpɔi dabpistan nɛ yinne daar (31st July, 2009) on da lu ban'a bi'ela nya'aŋ.
english: Doris Asibi Asiedu died on 31 July 2009 after an illness.

kusaal: Electoral Commission of Ghana da lɛn maal vɔɔtʋg anina ya'as yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ awai nwadisa awai la ni dabispisi nɛ awai daar.
english: The Electoral Commission of Ghana organised a by-election for 29 September 2009.

kusaal: Chereponi bɛnɛ Chereponi District bɛ North East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Chereponi is located in the Chereponi district of the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ban da dʋ'a o bɛ Singapore la, o da zamisi lieb onɛ dʋgʋt diibi kuosid, ka on da tiak zin'ig keŋ United Kingdom la, o da dʋg diib Saam dɔgbɛɛnda nɛ Diib kuosʋg zin'isin ka di ya'an piini bɛdigʋ.
english: Born in Singapore, she trained to become a pastry chef and after moving to the United Kingdom, has worked as an executive chef at various hotels and restaurants and has won a plethora of awards for her work.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la nii, o tʋm sariakad tʋʋma bɛ Bake Off: The Professionals.
english: Since 2016, she has served as a judge on Bake Off: The Professionals.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Finden nɛ 20 Samampiid 1967 bɛ Singapore.
english: Finden was born on 20 December 1967 in Singapore.

kusaal: Saŋkanɛ ka Finden da paae yʋʋm piinɛ ayuobʋ (16) la, o da keŋ naal nɛ Shatec Institutes zin'ikanɛ ka o da zamis diib dʋgʋb nɛ kuosʋg ka din nya'aŋ ka o da keŋ pin'ili maan tɔfinam ka naan pin'ili an pastry chef, bɛ Raffles Hotel nɛ Pan Pacific Singapore Hotel.
english: When Finden was 16, she joined Shatec Institutes where enrolled on a course in pastry making, and later began working as a chocolatier before becoming a pastry chef, at Raffles Hotel and Pan Pacific Singapore Hotel.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi (2000) la ni, Finden da gaad tuonɛ dɔl o taaba ka ba di ya'an bɛ IKA Culinary Olympics ni.
english: In 2000, Finden led a team of pastry chefs to win the IKA Culinary Olympics.

kusaal: Finden ɛlnɛ daʋ kanɛ gɔsid ligiid yɛla ka ba mɔr pʋ'ayu'a yinne; ba da duoe keŋ London bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne (2001) la ni.
english: Finden is married to a financial director and they have a daughter together; they moved to London in 2001.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) nɛ tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) la tensʋk, onɛ da an executive pastry chef tis Langham Hotel, tʋʋmkanɛ ni ka o da di'es ya'an piini bɛdigʋ.
english: Between 2009 and 2017, she worked as an executive pastry chef at the Langham Hotel, a role which has earned her numerous awards.

kusaal: O yiiga yʋʋma saŋa, o da di'e ya'an piini kanɛ pa'al ye onɛ an "Yʋʋm la wʋsa onɛ dʋg zaamnɔɔr diib gaad sɔ' wʋsa" ka Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ni, dɔlisid Finden's tuon gaadʋg ni, The Langham's Palm Court da di Tea Guild's "Top London Afternoon Tea" ya'an piini.
english: During her first year, she won "Dessert of the Year" and in 2010, under Finden's leadership, The Langham's Palm Court won Tea Guild's "Top London Afternoon Tea" award.

kusaal: O da lɛn di'e "Pastry Chef of the Year" ya'an piini dinɛ da yi Craft Guild of Chefs yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) la ni ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015) la nii, Finden da lɛn di'e The Macallan Lifetime Achievement ya'an piini bɛ World Gourmet Summit.
english: She was also awarded "Pastry Chef of the Year" by the Craft Guild of Chefs in 2012 and in 2015, Finden was awarded The Macallan Lifetime Achievement Award at the World Gourmet Summit.

kusaal: Yuʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la ni, ba da gaŋ Finden ye onɛ an creative development chef tis luxury chocolatier Godiva ka yʋʋm kanɛ dɔl la ka o maal dunia wʋsa gɛla suusʋg kanɛ ligidi gati ba wʋsa, dinɛ ka o da nɔk Belgian chocolate maal ka di sam da an wʋʋ £10,000.
english: In 2018, Finden was appointed creative development chef at luxury chocolatier Godiva and the following year created the world's most expensive easter egg, made entirely of Belgian chocolate that cost £10,000.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) la nii, Finden da lieb executive pastry chef tis Pan Pacific London, dinɛ ka ba da yɔ'ɔg bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) nwadisa awai ni la.
english: In 2020, Finden became the executive pastry chef at the Pan Pacific London, which opened in September 2021.

kusaal: O da bas tʋʋma bɛ Pan Pacific nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan (2023) la ni.
english: She left her role at Pan Pacific in April 2023.

kusaal: Cherish da yi Pan Pacific Hotel London ye o gɔsi o tʋʋma ka di keŋ tuon.
english: Cherish parted ways with the Pan Pacific Hotel London to concentrate on other ventures.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la nii, Finden da an onɛ pian'adi tisid Master Chef Australia nɛ Master Chef: The Professionals.
english: In 2010, Finden appeared as a guest chef on MasterChef Australia and MasterChef: The Professionals.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) nii, Finden da lieb sariakati bɛ BBC bodobodo maalʋg nya'ab Bake Off: Crème de la Crème, dinɛ da pin'ili yi The Great British Bake Off.
english: In 2016, Finden became a judge on the BBC baking competition Bake Off: Crème de la Crème, a spin-off of The Great British Bake Off.

kusaal: O maalʋg nɔɔri ayi BBC ni nya'aŋ, ba da yis sɔnsʋg la ani keŋ Channel 4 bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la ni ka tiaki di yʋ'ʋm buon ye Bake Off: The Professionals, ka Finden kpɛlim sɔnsʋg la ni kem paae zina.
english: After two series on the BBC, the show moved to Channel 4 in 2018 and was renamed Bake Off: The Professionals, and Finden has remained with show since.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (In 2017) la ni, Finden da lieb onɛ pa'an bɛ Celebrity Master Chef, saŋkanɛ ka o da mɔri o nidibi keŋ ka ba maligim maal o diib laas.
english: In 2017, Finden appeared as a mentor on Celebrity MasterChef, during an episode in which she led a team of contestants who had to re-create her pastry dishes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) la nii, Finden da lieb onɛ an baŋir sɔb bɛ BBC di'ema sɔnsʋg di bɛ The Wheel.
english: In 2020, Finden appeared as a celebrity expert on an episode of the BBC game show The Wheel.

kusaal: O mɛ da yi Heston's Great British Food, Junior Bake Off, The Great British Bake Off: An Extra Slice nɛ Saturday Kitchen ni na.
english: She has also made appearances on Heston's Great British Food, Junior Bake Off, The Great British Bake Off: An Extra Slice and Saturday Kitchen.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Cherish Finden nɛ 20 Samampiid 1967 bɛ Singapore ka o an dikuos.
english: Cherish Finden (born 20 December 1967) is a Singaporean-born pastry chef.

kusaal: On da bɛ anina la, o da yɔ'ɔgi o mɛŋ pâtisserie Shiok!
english: Whilst there, she opened her own pâtisserie Shiok!

kusaal: Dinɛ ka o da yɔ'ɔg bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi (2022) nwadisa anu la ni.
english: which launched in May 2022.

kusaal: Paper-cutting, paper-cutting an paper-nwwaasg tʋʋma la (Chinese: … pinyin …) China teŋin tun'oe kaali lɛb 2nd century CE, yʋʋma kɔbʋs yi la saŋa ni, saŋkanɛ ni ka li da an Cai Lun onɛ da an kɔɔtʋ tʋmtʋn, Eastern Han Dynasty la maal paper.
english: The traditional art of paper cutting (Chinese: 剪紙; pinyin: jiǎnzhǐ) in China may date back to the 2nd century CE, when paper was invented by Cai Lun, a court official of the Eastern Han dynasty.

kusaal: Archaeological vɛɛnsʋg gbana pa'al ye paper-nwaasʋg da pin'il lɛ 6th century, yʋʋma kɔbʋs yuobʋ la ni, la'am nɛ sieba tis sida ye li pin'ilʋg tun'oe tuunsi lɛb nya'aŋi paae nɛ Warring States period (around 3 BC), saŋa bɛdigʋ ka ba nyaan maal paper.
english: According to archaeological records, paper-cutting originates from the 6th century, although some believe that its history could be traced back as far as the Warring States period (around 3 BC), long before paper was invented.

kusaal: Paper nwaasʋg kanɛ an artform paam nɔbigir nɛ Tang dynasty la saŋa, kanɛ da ka' nɛ handcraft tʋʋma buudi ma'aa nɛ, ka anɛ artwork, ani ka ba da dɔlsid paper nwaasʋg la ni pa'an yam nɛ baŋir.
english: Paper-cutting as an artform matured during the Tang dynasty, where it became considered not only a type of handicraft, but also a type of artwork, as ideas and concepts were expressed through the pattern cut into the paper.

kusaal: Folk paper nwaasʋg da widigi paae nidib bɛdigʋ, ka ba da pa'ali ba baŋir nɛ min'ilim tʋʋma li ni.
english: Folk paper-cutting spread to a wider range of people and expressed an abundance of artistic expression.

kusaal: Ming nɛ Qing dynasties nam la saŋa (1368-1912), tʋʋm nwa da nyɛ nɔbigir nɛ nyɔɔdi gaad saŋa banɛ da gaad la.
english: In the Ming and Qing dynasty (1368-1912), paper-cutting reached a developmental peak and became a more popular Chinese art.

kusaal: Amaa li ka' ala northeast China teŋin nɛ an kpi'emisɛ, ka fʋ tun'oe nyɛ paper nwaasʋg tʋʋma la'ad ka li yit Northern dynasties Turpan, Sinkiang province.
english: In contrast, the weather in the northwest of China is usually dry, making it possible to find cut-paper art made in the Northern dynasties in Turpan, Sinkiang province.

kusaal: Southern maalig la yit nɛ Yangzhou bɛ Jiangsu Province nɛ Yueqing bɛ Zhejiang Province, ba maan nɛ bʋn vɛnlla hali kanɛ ka mi'ilim nɛ baŋir bɛdigʋ kpɛn' ba maaligin.
english: Representative works are from Yangzhou in Jiangsu Province and Yueqing in Zhejiang Province.

kusaal: Northern maalig la, ka tita'am yit nɛ Yuxian nɛ Fengning bɛ Hebel Province, ka northern Shaanxi dimi maani ba bɛdigʋ, ka ba nwaasʋg la mɔr vɛnllim nɛ si'esim buudi buudi kanɛ gban'ad bɛdigʋ yam.
english: The northern style, mainly from Yuxian and Fengning in Hebei Province, and best represented by works from northern Shaanxi, features exaggerated shapes, vigorousness, vivid depictions and diverse patterns.

kusaal: China zin'is bɛdigʋ, kas kas ya-datiuŋ, ba tabin paper nwaasʋg la dɔɔd vɔnya ni, ka li pa'an nɛ ba sunma'asim yʋʋm paal la yɛla, malʋŋ kaŋa da pʋn bɛnɛ Song nɛ Yuan dynasties la saŋa sa.
english: In many areas of China, especially in the north, paper-cuttings are pasted to windows to express happiness for the new season, a tradition that has been practiced since the Song and Yuan dynasties.

kusaal: Chinese paper cutting anɛ buudi malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba yam gban'ae hali, ka li titti ba ligidi sʋŋa ka da naam nɛ saŋkanɛ ka ba da pin'il paper maalig la.
english: The traditional art of paper cutting (Chinese: 剪紙; pinyin: jiǎnzhǐ) in China may date back to the 2nd century CE, when paper was invented by Cai Lun, a court official of the Eastern Han dynasty.

kusaal: Nidib bɛdigʋ da ti kena baŋ paper nwaasʋg tʋʋma la ka li paasidi dɔɔg za'anɔɔr nɛ dɔɔg vɔɔnr vɛnlim, paper paamʋg yʋʋn da an na'ana saŋsi'a la.
english: Paper cutting became popular as a way of decorating doors and windows as paper became more accessible.

kusaal: Paper da'agi da pʋ lɛn kpi'em la, paper nwaasʋg yʋʋn da liebi Chinese folk art kpeŋ yinne.
english: Paper-cutting is one of the oldest and the most popular folk arts in China.

kusaal: Ban mɔri nwaasʋg nam la niŋid za'anɔnya nɛ vɔɔnya paasidi ba vɛnlim la zugɔɔ, ba buonɛ ba sansi'a ye "window flowers" (…) bɛɛ "window paper cuts".
english: The paper cuts that used to decorate the window, it is called "window flowers" (窗花; chuāng huā) or "window paper-cuts".

kusaal: Paper banɛ ka ba nwaas nwa ye ti tabil nɛ dɔɔg vɔnya la yiŋ, kɛ ka dɔɔg la pʋʋgin nɛɛsim la gaadi tɔlig paper la nwaai, cutout la vɔɔnrin.
english: Finally, the paper cutout is opened up to reveal the exquisite design, which can be further enhanced with additional details such as coloring and shading.

kusaal: Chinese paper-nwaasʋg pin'ilig yinɛ ba ansestors, yaannam nɛ wina pʋ'ʋsim pʋʋgin kanɛ an malʋŋ kanɛ paas Chinese buudi malima ni ka pin'ili woo millennia nama ayi banɛ gaad la sa.
english: Chinese paper-cutting originated from the practice of worship of both ancestors and gods, a traditional part of Chinese culture dating back roughly two millennia.

kusaal: Saŋkan la, nidib da mɔri la'asieba, woo, vaand, silver foil, silk hali nɛ leather, gbaʋŋ n maan negative-space patterns.
english: At that time, people used other thin materials, like leaves, silver foil, silk and even leather, to carve negative-space patterns.

kusaal: Tang dynasty la saŋa, paper nwaasʋg da nyɛ nɔbigir hali ka sɔ' wʋsa mi' li China teŋin, kanɛ da kpab nɛ li si'ib ka pa'an nɛ siigin yɛla.
english: During the Tang dynasty, paper cutting developed rapidly and became popular in China, which typically combined paper cutting with painting to illustrate spiritual ideas.

kusaal: Song dynasty la saŋa, Chinese paper-nwaasʋg la da paam tiakir ka nɔbigir bɛdigʋ da naam, ka ba da paam zamisigi yʋʋn tʋm li nɛ baŋir bɛdigʋ.
english: During the Song dynasty, Chinese papercutting developed into a more advanced technique, with trained artisans creating more complex artworks.

kusaal: Ba da zaŋ baŋir la kpɛn' ya'abig ni ka maal shadow puppets.
english: The technique was used to decorate ceramics and make shadow puppets.

kusaal: Ba ka gʋligid oily cardboarb naming, ka nwwɛn'ɛd gʋlib la nigid yaadi namin, blue-printed fabric came about.
english: By carving patterns onto oily cardboard and scraping patterns onto the fabric, blue-printed fabric came about.

kusaal: Ming nɛ Qing dynasty nam la ni, paper-nwaasʋg da paae li nɔbigir bɛn.
english: In the Ming and Qing dynasty (1368-1912), paper-cutting reached a developmental peak and became a more popular Chinese art.

kusaal: Ming nɛ Qing dynasties nam la ni, paper nwaasʋg da kena an Chinese artform tʋʋm kpɛŋ.
english: This artistry witnessed its most prosperous period in Ming and Qing dynasties.

kusaal: li tʋʋma zu'oe ya, ka ba anɛ, lantern nɛ fan ornaments, needlework patterns, nɛ window flowers.
english: It developed a variety of uses, including lantern and fan ornaments, needlework patterns, and window flowers.

kusaal: Imperial zak dim la mɛ da mɔr paper nwaasʋg la'ad nam la nigidi ba yaan, ka ya'al paper nam la Forbidden City la emperor, zugdaan la, pu'adir saŋa ni.
english: The imperial family also utilized papercutting, with the Forbidden City decorated with papercuts during the emperor's wedding ceremony.

kusaal: Nɛŋa zugu kɛ ka dʋn kaŋa nwa China nidib baŋ paper-nwaasʋg tʋʋma.
english: Yuxian paper-cutting, produced in Hebei province, China, is famous for its color printing techniques and bold and unrestrained style.

kusaal: Lin an lak la, paper pʋ ya'asida ka na pʋn'oe, mildews ka bɛdig.
english: As a material, paper mildews and rots easily.

kusaal: Southeast China ka Sigsaa nɛ Sigir nwadis la mɔr saku'om bɛdigʋ, kɛt ka paper pun'od ka bɛdigid tɔ'ɔtɔ; kɛ ka suotheast China dim da pʋ maan paper-nwaasʋg tʋʋma, kɛ ka li da tɔi nɛ kʋdimin yʋʋma dimi na tʋmi li.
english: Yuxian paper-cutting, produced in Hebei province, China, is famous for its color printing techniques and bold and unrestrained style.

kusaal: Paper nwaasʋg anɛ tʋʋm kʋdʋg ka an folk arts kanɛ ka nidib mi' li yɛla China teŋin gaad tʋʋma wʋsa.
english: Paper-cutting is one of the oldest and the most popular folk arts in China.

kusaal: Chinese paper-nwaasʋg la anɛ tʋʋm kanɛ yi Chinese buudi malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba di'e yi ba yaanamin, ka li mɔri nwaasʋg buudi bɛdigʋ li zaŋ banɛ gʋlibi an bi'ela ka mɔri fɔɔtʋ yimmir, nɛ banɛ mɔri fɔɔtʋ nama ayi ka kpɛn nwɛnɛ taab yim, ka lin maalʋg pɔɔnbin nɛ paper la bɛn bɛn ka nyaan nwwaas, kɛ ka li ya'a pɔnbil, fɔɔtʋ nam la ba' nwɛnɛ taab hali, ka li pɔnbini ta'an woo nɔɔr ayi bɛɛ anaasi.
english: The symbolic language of Chinese paper-cutting is deeply rooted in traditional culture.

kusaal: Ban tabini ba kpi'en yaŋa la anɛ ye li mɔr zugsʋŋi ken.ba da mɔr paper nwaasʋg nam la duorimɛ kas kas, a mɔri niŋid embroidery nɛ lacquer tʋʋma ni.
english: Paper cuttings used to be used as patterns, especially for embroidery and lacquer work.

kusaal: Sieba bɔɔd ye ba kuo ka paam zʋʋd bɛdigʋ, bɛɛ ba paam kpan'am ba vʋmin, nɛŋa pa'anɛ ba pʋtɛnda ni ban bɔɔd bun sʋŋ si'em, bʋnkɔnbid nɛ bʋnbʋtta nɔbigir, la'am nɛ yɛlsʋma, ka carp ianki gaŋ dragon yaŋir ( Chinese buudi kpɛŋ kanɛ pa'an ye vʋm sʋŋ bɛɛ ba tuon), polecats, lions, kylins ( a mythical Chinese creature), jade rabbits (an animal taken from Chinese legend), pomegranates and peonies.
english: Some express wishes for a harvest or a wealthy life, shown through the imagery of a golden harvest, thriving domestic animals and plants, as well as good fortunes, a carp jumping over a dragon gate (a traditional Chinese story, indicating a leap towards a better life), polecats, lions, qilins (a mythical Chinese creature), jade rabbits (an animal taken from Chinese legend), pomegranates and peonies.

kusaal: Naasʋg la sieba pa'anɛ nidib banɛ tʋm hali ka ba yʋ'ʋr yi, bɛɛ ba yaanam yɛla, bɛɛ ban da tʋm si'em, woo Yellow Emperor la nwaasʋg la, cowherd la si'alʋg (…) nɛ Weaver Girl (…) nɛ filial piety sɔlima 24 la.
english: Other designs feature legendary figures, or scenes from traditional myths or stories, such as designs of the Yellow Emperor, the meeting of [[The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl|Cowherd(牛郎; niúláng) and Weaver Girl(织女; zhīnǚ)]], and the 24 stories of filial piety.

kusaal: Nwaasʋg banɛ yʋ'ʋri yi hali Chinese characters anɛ characters bama… (li gbin an 'zugsʋŋ') nɛ …(li gbin an 'sunma'asim a bʋyi').
english: The most popular paper-cutting Chinese characters are the characters 福 (meaning 'lucky') and 囍; xǐ (meaning 'double happiness'), which respectively used in the scenario of Chinese New Year Celebrations and weddings.

kusaal: Chinese paper nwaasʋg motifs nam woo bunib, bʋnkɔnbid, nɛ malima kuga pa'alʋg woo carp n in'aki gaŋ dragon yaŋir la.
english: Common Chinese papercutting motifs include representations of harvests, animals, and mythical stories such as the carp jumping over the dragon gate.

kusaal: Chinese paper naasʋg mɔr zamisʋg tʋʋma ka li pa'an biis Chinese buudi malima nɛ paper nwaasʋg la vɛnllim ka zamisid paper nwaasʋg la pin'ilʋg yɛla.
english: As a traditional Chinese folk art, paper cutting not only carries emotional expression and cultural symbol, but also has a certain healing function.

kusaal: A nwaasid paper nam la sʋŋid biis ka ba paamid nwaasʋg la baŋir, nifi gɔt nu'us la tʋm si'em, hand-eye coordination, a nwai ka maal, cutting and creativity.
english: Practicing paper cuts also helps children enhance their fine motor skills, hand-eye coordination, cutting and creativity.

kusaal: Chinese-paper nwaasʋg tʋmmi nɛ baŋir bɛdigʋ, nwaasʋg banɛ vɛn hali, banɛ ka ba zaŋ sʋ'ʋs, knives bɛɛ ma'adins maal yinne bɛɛ maal ba pa'al taaba zut.
english: Chinese paper-cutting involves cutting intricate, exquisite designs from a single or multiple layers of paper with scissors or artwork knives.

kusaal: A la'as paper nam bɛdigʋ ka nwai la kɛt ka nwaar la an yinne, consistent pattern.
english: This cutting of multiple paper layers at the same time enables a more consistent pattern.

kusaal: Li nya'aŋa, tʋʋm nwa da giligi tiing dunia la zin' sieba, ka sʋ'ʋlim sieba zaŋi ba buudi malima kpɛn'ɛsi li ni.
english: Later, this art form spread to other parts of the world, with different regions adopting their own cultural styles.

kusaal: Christ Apostolic Church (CAC) anɛ yiiga Pentecostal Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg kanɛ da kɛn Nigeria na.
english: Christ Apostolic Church (CAC) is the first Pentecostal church present in Nigeria.

kusaal: Li da pin'il nɛ 20th century pʋsʋk saŋa, bɛ British Empire.
english: It arose in the first half of the 20th century, in the then-British Empire.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili li bɛ Ijebu-ode ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Precious Stone Society bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piinɛ anii amaa li da kpɛn'ɛ gbana ni nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yinnɛ ni, ban da bak ki yi Apostolic Church banɛ ka Aladura organization (Faith Tabernacle) dim da kaanbi buoli ba ye ba kɛn Nigeria na la.
english: It was founded in Ijebu-ode named Precious Stone Society in 1918 but was formally established in 1941 after a split from the Apostolic Church which the original Aladura organization (Faith Tabernacle) had invited to Nigeria.

kusaal: Christ Apostolic Church mɛ' secondary school nam nɛ Univɛsity kanɛ ka ba da nɔki pʋd ye Joseph Ayo Babalola University (JABU) ka li bɛ Ikeji Arakeji, Osun State Nigeria.
english: Christ Apostolic Church operates secondary schools and an Entrepreneurial University named after the first General Evangelist, Joseph Ayo Babalola University (JABU) right in Ikeji Arakeji, Osun State in Nigeria.

kusaal: Christ Apostolic Church anɛ Africa Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg kanɛ ka Precious Stone Society (Faith Tabernacle) karembiis da pin'il, ban da baki ba mɛŋi yi The Apostolic Church ni yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi la ni.
english: Christ Apostolic Church is an indigenous African church founded by members of Precious Stone Society (Faith Tabernacle) after separating from The Apostolic Church in 1940.

kusaal: Karindɔɔg la pin'il si'em dɔl nɛ banɛ pin'ili li la, ba anɛ Isaac Babalola Akinyele, Joseph Ayo Babalola, David Odubanjo, Joseph Esinsinade, nɛ Miss Sophia Odunlami.
english: The church's history is linked to its founders, namely Isaac Babalola Akinyele, Joseph Ayo Babalola, David Odubanjo, Joseph Esinsinade, and Miss Sophia Odunlami.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmin la, Christ Apostolic Church nɛ The Apostolic Church (ka ba da buon Diamond or Precious Stone sankan la) da pin'ili bɛ zin'ig si'eba Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim, amaa ka lɛɛ da si'an taaba bɛ St Savior's Anglican Church.
english: Before then, Christ Apostolic Church and The Apostolic Church (called Diamond or Precious Stone at that time) were found in some places in Nigeria but met mainly at St Savior's Anglican Church.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ yinnɛ ni, Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig, dabpisi nɛ atan' daar, Pastors D.P Williams, A. Turnbull, nɛ W.J Williams da kɛn Nigeria na ka bas Karinsaam nam ayɔpɔi la suor ye ba tʋm karindɔɔg la ni.
english: On 23 September 1931, Pastors D.P Williams, A. Turnbull, and W.J Williams came to Nigeria and ordained the first seven Pastors of the church.

kusaal: Nɔŋgbanwa'ar da kɛn karindɔɔg la ni na din da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ awai paae tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi ni la da kɛ ka karindɔɔg la pʋdʋg zin'is ayi', yiiga la anɛ The Apostolic Church Nigeria ka ba tuongat an Pastor Samuel Adegboyega ka onɛ kpɛlim la mɛ an Christ Apostolic Church.
english: Then during the crisis that occurred in 1939–1940 in the church that led to the emergence of two groups, the first is The Apostolic Church Nigeria led by Pastor Samuel Adegboyega while the second is Christ Apostolic Church.

kusaal: Baba Abiye da anɛ kpɛɛmnam banɛ da bɛ Christ Apostolic Church ni la yinnɛ, onɛ da an Assistant General Evangelist tis karindɔɔg la, ka on nɛ Joseph Ayo Babalola da la'asi tʋmmid.
english: Baba Abiye was one of the leaders of the Christ Apostolic Church who served as the Assistant General Evangelist of the church, working closely with Joseph Ayo Babalola during his lifetime.

kusaal: Pastor Isaac Babalola Akinyele (1943–1964) – yiiga tuongat onɛ da tʋm paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi ni.
english: Pastor Isaac Babalola Akinyele (1943–1964) – served as the first president from incorporation until 1964.

kusaal: Pastor Jacob Soyege Bartholomew Odusona (1964–1966) – da di'e Akinyele nɔbiri an tuongat yʋʋma ayi'.
english: Pastor Jacob Soyege Bartholomew Odusona (1964–1966) – succeeded Akinyele and led for two years.

kusaal: Pastor Elijah Titus Latunde (1966–1983) – tuongat yʋʋma piinɛ ayɔpɔi.
english: Pastor Elijah Titus Latunde (1966–1983) – presided over the church for 17 years.

kusaal: Pastor John Dada Obafemi – o paas nidib ayi' banɛ da kilim tuongatib ka pʋ kilim General Superintendent yiiga.
english: Pastor John Dada Obafemi – one of the only two leaders who became president without previously serving as General Superintendent.

kusaal: Pastor Joseph Bolade Orogun (1983–1991) – da di'e Latunde nɔbir.
english: Pastor Joseph Bolade Orogun (1983–1991) – succeeded Latunde.

kusaal: Pastor John Dada Obafemi (1993–1997) – da an tuongat yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' ka kɛŋ vʋ'ʋs yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi ni.
english: Pastor John Dada Obafemi (1993–1997) – appointed president in 1993 and retired in 1997.

kusaal: Pastor Elijah Howard Lajuwomi Olusheye (1997–2011) – da di'e Obafemi nɔbir ka tʋm o tʋʋma paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ, Samanpiid nwadig la ni.
english: Pastor Elijah Howard Lajuwomi Olusheye (1997–2011) – succeeded Obafemi and served until December 2011.

kusaal: Joseph Ayo Babalola da kɛ ka li nɔbig, o da anɛ onɛ maan pal, ka da kilim yiiga tʋmtʋm kpɛɛm anina.
english: Its growth was led by Joseph Ayo Babalola, a road construction driver who became its first General Evangelist.

kusaal: Pastor Samuel Olusegun Oladele ka ba da gaŋ ye o an kpɛɛm kanɛ paas anii daani tis Christ Apostolic Church dunia wʋsa yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ, Dɔnwalig nwadig, dabpisi daar la.
english: Pastor Samuel Olusegun Oladele was inaugurated as the 8th president of Christ Apostolic Church Worldwide on 20 March 2021.

kusaal: The Anglican Church da pʋ si'ak wala ka banɛ da paas ka an tʋmtʋmnibi bɛ Anglican Church ni la da bas ka ti'aki lɛb anina.
english: The Anglican Church were opposed to the practices of the group and members of the group who are workers in the Anglican Church were forced to resign.

kusaal: O da an tuongat ya'adɔl yiiga Odusona saŋa.
english: Prior to his presidency, he had served as vice president under Odusona.

kusaal: Kpɛɛm kanɛ buon Pastor E.A. Faniyan da di'e o nɔbir lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinnɛ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' ni.
english: An interim administration headed by Pastor E.A. Faniyan was in place between 1991 and June 1993.

kusaal: Pastor Samuel Olusegun Oladele (2021 paae zina) – tuongat kanɛ bɛ zina, o da pin'il tʋʋma yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ ni.
english: Pastor Samuel Olusegun Oladele was inaugurated as the 8th president of Christ Apostolic Church Worldwide on 20 March 2021.

kusaal: Christ Apostolic Church International anɛ Pentecostal Evangelical Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg kanɛ ka ninkanɛ lɛn ka' dunia, Apostle Peter Anim kanɛ da pin'il Penticostal Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la da mɔri li kɛna.
english: Is a Pentecostal Evangelical church which traces its existence from the ministry of the late Apostle Peter Anim, the originator of Ghanaian Pentecostalism.

kusaal: Peter Anim Newman da pin'ilig o Wina'am tʋʋma kanɛ an ye o ti'eb nidib la bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi ni ka o karindɔɔg yʋ'ʋr da an Faith Tabernacle, on da karim gbaʋŋi nyɛ ka Wina'am da ti'eb ninkanɛ mɔr pʋ'ban'as nɛ ban'as si'eba la, o da karimi li yi nɛ gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka Faith Tabernacle USA dim da yis na ka pʋdi li ye Sword of Spirit la.
english: Peter Anim Newman began a healing ministry in 1917 under the name Faith Tabernacle as a result of healing received from acute stomach upset and guinea worms infections after he read a magazine published by Faith Tabernacle USA called Sword of Spirit.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ yinnɛ ni, Anim da dɔlis o Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg Faith Tabernacle ni kɛŋ mɔɔl Wina'am labaar Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim, David O. Odubanjo, da buol tʋmtʋmnib banɛ bɛ Apostolic Church of Bradford, ye ba kaae o.
english: In 1931, Anim, through a fellow Faith Tabernacle minister in Nigeria, David O. Odubanjo, contacted missionaries of the Apostolic Church of Bradford, to pay his team a visit.

kusaal: Rev George Perfect, tʋmtʋm kanɛ ka Apostolic Church Bradford da tʋm o ye o kɛn Nigeria na la, da dɔl Asamankese linɛ bɛ Ghana la ka bɛ nɛ Faith Tabernacle Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg la bakwai ayi'.
english: Rev George Perfect, a missionary sent by Apostolic Church Bradford to Nigeria, passed by Asamankese in Ghana and stayed with the Faith Tabernacle church for two weeks.

kusaal: Li da dɔlis nɛ al aka Anim karindɔɔg la yʋ'ʋn kilim The Apostolic Church Gold Coast.
english: Hence, Anim's church became The Apostolic Church Gold Coast.

kusaal: Banɛ da dɔl McKeown da ti'aki ba yʋʋri lɛbis Apostolic Church Bradford ka banɛ da dɔl Anim mɛ yʋ'ʋn da an Christ Apostolic Church.
english: The followers of McKeown remained the name Apostolic Church Bradford whilst the followers of Anim became Christ Apostolic Church.

kusaal: Anim nɛ o Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg dim da siak ya ka dɔl Apostolic Church Bradford dɔlisa.
english: Anim and his members fully embraced the doctrine and practices of the Apostolic Church Bradford.

kusaal: Ba da yel ye kpɛɛm sɔ' naan Bradford na, ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi ni: James McKeown da an onɛ ka ba da tʋm o ka o naan UK kɛn Asamankese na.
english: They requested an external missionary from Bradford, and the request was granted in 1937: James McKeown was sent as the first Pentecostal missionary from the UK to Asamankese.

kusaal: McKeown da lu ban'a ka kɛŋ Europe dim sibiti kanɛ da bɛ Ghana.
english: The church by then practiced strictly divine healing.When McKeown contracted malaria and was subsequently hospitalized in the European Hospital in Ghana.

kusaal: Christabel Ekeh anɛ onɛ an ti Ghana sini di'em-di'em yinne, ba da du'a o n bɛ Sawa'ar nwadig la ni li dabisim pii nɛ ayuobυ, 1990.
english: Christabel Ekeh (born October 16, 1990) is a Ghanaian actress and model.

kusaal: Ekeh si'iŋnɛ n paasidi o mɛŋ di'em nam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb banɛ da bɛ wυυ, Miss Malaika Ghana 2008 ka da di ti'eli ayi daan.
english: Ekeh started her career as a model and participated at the beauty pageant, Miss Malaika Ghana 2008 and won the second position.

kusaal: O paam yυ'υr hali n kati wa'ae wυυ sini nam ban kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb bɛdigυ pυυgυn n bɛ Ghana and Nageriya sini maalυg pυυgυn.
english: Ekeh started her career as a model and participated at the beauty pageant, Miss Malaika Ghana 2008 and won the second position.

kusaal: O sini maalig tʋʋma da pin'il nɛ on da paasi maal Nigeria sini kanɛ buon College Girls la ni.
english: Her acting career began when she featured in the Nigerian movie College Girls.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋr yinɛ on paasi maal sini kanɛ buon Potomanto la.
english: She is also known for the movie Potomanto.

kusaal: College Girls (2008)
english: Her acting career began when she featured in the Nigerian movie College Girls.

kusaal: Christian Corleytey Otuteye (dʋ'anɛ October 23, 1973) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Sege constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress zug.
english: Christian Corleytey Otuteye (born October 23, 1973) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Sege constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da keŋi University of Kaiserslautern, bɛ Germany la maal o Master of Science degree in Financial Mathematics yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni (2004).
english: He entered University of Kaiserslautern, Germany and obtained his Master of Science degree in Financial Mathematics in 2004.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana vɔɔtʋg la ni, o da lɛn di Sege Constituency Wadmaan kʋk la ya'as.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian elections, he retained the Sege Constituency parliamentary seat.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Otuteye nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan Nwadis piiga la dabpisi nɛ atan daar (October 23, 1973), Sege, tenkanɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Otuteye was born on October 23, 1973, in Sege, a town in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Otuteye anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) nid.
english: Otuteye is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni 2012, o da nya' Sege kʋk la Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, NDC zugʋ paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayuobʋ la ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Sege seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: Christian Council of Ghana (CCG) anɛ la'asig kanɛ ka karindɔɔg pistan' nɛ yinnɛ la'asi bɛ Ghana.
english: The Christian Council of Ghana (CCG) is an umbrella group that unites 31 churches and denominations in Ghana.

kusaal: Nidib banɛ paas la yit nɛ Church of Power World Ministry, Charismatic, Pentecostal, Orthodox, Inside God Christian college, nɛ karindɔɔd si'eba.
english: The council has its members from Church of Power World Ministry, Charismatic, Pentecostal, Orthodox, Inside God Christian college, and other churches.

kusaal: Methodist Church Ghana (ka ba ba buon Wesleyan Methodist Church)
english: the Methodist Church Ghana (then the Wesleyan Methodist Church)

kusaal: La'asig la tʋm tʋʋm si'eba bɛ Ghana.
english: The council undertakes various projects in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba tʋʋma yinnɛ anɛ ye ba yis nyan kanɛ bɛnɛ nidib banɛ mɔr HIV/AIDS la.
english: The project trained community members in areas of the country that had high HIV/AIDS prevalence of 8–9%.

kusaal: Ba da kɛŋ tɛɛns banɛ ni ka HIV/AIDS bɛ bɛdigʋ sa'ali ba.
english: The training involved basic facts about HIV/AIDS, stigma and discrimination among others.

kusaal: Christian Kwabena Asante anɛ Ghana politis nwɛ'ɛd ka bɛ parliament of Ghana zi'en nɛ Bia Constituency dim nɔbazug ka o na'adɔɔg an National Democratic Congress.
english: Christian Kwabena Asante is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the first parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana representing Bia Constituency under the membership of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ sakur bɛ Government Training College ka naae o GCE Ordinary Level.
english: He studied at Government Training College where he obtained his GCE Ordinary Level.

kusaal: Asante da pin'il o politis tʋʋma nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' ni, sakan ka o da zi'e National Democratic Congress (NDC) zugu nya'a na'am bɛ Asokwa East constituency yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' vootʋg la ni.
english: Asante began his political career in 1992 when he became the parliamentary candidate for the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to represent Asokwa East constituency prior to the commencement of the 1992 Ghanaian parliamentary election.

kusaal: O da di ya'an ka bas Benjamin Armah onɛ mɛ da zi'eni tis New Patriotic Party la ka nidib tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyi nɛ pisnu da vooti tis o.
english: He defeated Benjamin Armah of the New Patriotic Party by obtaining 51.60% of the total valid votes which was equivalent to 37,250 votes.

kusaal: O da di'e nɛ Michael Coffie Boampong onɛ da an NDC nid la nɔbir.
english: He was succeeded by Michael Coffie Boampong of NDC.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Christian Kwabena Asante nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi, Sawaar nwadig, dabpisi nɛ atan' daar.
english: Christian Kwabena Asante was born on 23 October 1940.

kusaal: Ba da vooti tis o ka o kpɛn'ɛ parliament of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan', yʋʋm paal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar, on da di ya'ani bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi, Samanpiid nwadig, dabpisi nɛ awai daar vootʋg la.
english: He was elected into the first parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana on 7 January 1993 after being pronounced winner at the 1992 Ghanaian election held on 29 December 1992.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vooti tis Asante yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ vootʋg la ni, ka o da lɛn zi'en nɛ tis National Democratic Congress.
english: Asante was re-elected into the 2nd parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana during the 1996 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Christian Service University college la anɛ university colleges yinne ka National Accreditation Board bas sour ka ba tʋum.li paasi University of Ghana,nɛ University of Cape Coast.
english: The Christian Service University is one of the university accredited by the National Accreditation Board in the past decade.

kusaal: li bɛni Kumasi, teŋpʋʋg tita'ar kanɛ paasi ayi Ghana nwa.
english: It is located in Kumasi, the second largest city in Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi li nwadis piinɛ yinne la ni, ba yiiga karimdɔɔg la daa sin'iŋ nɛ karimbiis anaasi ;yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piisi la, koligi la daa yʋ'ʋn tiak an evangelical Christian university.
english: In October 1974, the first residential classes started with four students; by 2020, the college had become an evangelical Christian university.

kusaal: University campus bɛni Kumasi, teŋpʋʋg tita'ar bɛ Ashanti Region nwa.
english: The university is based on a main campus within Kumasi, the capital of the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: University la mɔr nidib kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobo nɛ yinne (161) banɛ sʋŋi nɛ faculty pa'adib.
english: The university has 161 support and faculty staff.

kusaal: University la mɔr sakur biis nɔyinne la'asʋg ka ti buon ye Students Representative Council.
english: The university has a students union known as the Students Representative Council.

kusaal: Di da pin'iinɛ 1983 sa.
english: This has existed since 1983.

kusaal: Kanl kanɛ ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusayi ni la, Ghana nidib banɛ an 18.8 million la pʋʋgin, Kristo biis anɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai, kɔbiga pʋʋgin.
english: According to the census figures of the year 2000, out of Ghana's 18.8 million people, Christians made up 69 percent of the population of Ghana.

kusaal: Na'asaanam la ka 15th century ka ba da kɛn Gold Coast na la da mɔr Kristo pʋ'ʋsʋm kɛn tɛŋ la zug na.
english: The arrival of the Europeans in 15th century into the then Gold Coast brought Christianity to the land.

kusaal: Nidib bɛdigʋ banɛ bɛ West African da maani ba malima kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb ka dɔlli ba wina nam.
english: There were many different cultural groups across the West African region who were practicing different forms of spirituality.

kusaal: Methodist Church Ghana da pin'il Ghana yinɛ tʋʋm kanɛ ka Wesleyan Methodist Church da tʋm la, li da pin'il ya, yinɛ Joseph Rhodes Dunwell da kɛn Gold Coast (Ghana) na yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pistan' nɛ anu ni la.
english: The Methodist Church Ghana came into existence as a result of the missionary activities of the Wesleyan Methodist Church, inaugurated with the arrival of Joseph Rhodes Dunwell to the Gold Coast (Ghana) in 1835.

kusaal: Methodist Church linɛ bɛ Ghana la da pin'il nɛ dɔl Anglican suor.
english: Like the mother church, the Methodist Church in Ghana was established by people of Anglican background.

kusaal: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints mɔr nidib tusa kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ atan' banɛ la'asid zin'is kɔbistan' nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi pʋ'ʋsid bɛ Ghana.
english: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has 113,000 members in 387 congregations in Ghana.

kusaal: Seventh-day Adventist tʋmtʋmnib da kɛn Ghana na yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ anii.
english: Seventh-day Adventist missionaries arrived in Ghana in 1888.

kusaal: Ba karinbiis la pisyuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin banɛ bɛ Ghana anɛ Ashanti.
english: 60 percent of its members in Ghana are Ashanti.

kusaal: Grand Orange Lodge of Ghana, ka ba lɛn buon The Loyal Orange Institution of Ghana, an kpɛɛmnam banɛ gɔsid Orange Order tʋʋma Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The Grand Orange Lodge of Ghana, also known as The Loyal Orange Institution of Ghana, governs the Orange Order in the country.

kusaal: Christianity anɛ Wina'am pʋ'ʋsʋg suor kanɛ ka nidib bɛdigʋ dɔlisid bɛ Ghana.
english: Christianity is the religion with the largest Denomination in Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga kanl la da pa'al ye Ghana nidib wʋsa anɛ 24 million ka pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinnɛ kɔbiga pʋʋgina an Kristo biis.
english: The 2010 Population and Housing Census puts the figure at slightly over 71 percent of the total population of over 24 million people.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ kaanlig la da pa'al ye 71.3% anɛ Kristo biis.
english: According to the 2021 census, 71.3% of the population belonged to a Christian denomination.

kusaal: Ba mɔr kʋdʋmin labaya zin'is pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ, missions ayuobʋ, nɛ Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg temple tita'ar yinnɛ Ghana, k aba lɛn paas ayi' ya'as.
english: They also have 86 family history centers, 6 missions, and 1 temple in Ghana, with 2 more announced.

kusaal: Ba mɔr sakur nam kɔbiswai nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, sibiti nam piinɛ atan', nɛ sibiti bibis piinɛ ayi' bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Mawuli School – Evangelical Presbyterian Church Ghana (Ho)

kusaal: Zin'is bɛdigʋ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim kɛn titua ka li yinɛ Kristo biisi paasi sʋŋ la yela.
english: Mawuli School – Evangelical Presbyterian Church Ghana (Ho)

kusaal: Ba la'asid taaba ka mɔr nɔɔr yinnɛ nɛ pʋtɛn'ɛr yinnɛ, William of Orange anɛ banɛ pʋ paas politis pʋʋginɛ.
english: The organization, once predominantly white, began admitting Ghanaian locals, leading to its full integration and making it the most active Orange community in Africa. In its current form, the fraternity has created a network of like-minded individuals who share a common faith, William of Orange is viewed as a symbol of civil and religious freedom rather than a political one.

kusaal: Ghana dim banɛ paas Order pʋʋgin la sʋŋid nidib ka dɔlisid anina mɔɔn labaari tisidi ba.
english: The Grand Orange Lodge of Ghana, also known as The Loyal Orange Institution of Ghana, governs the Orange Order in the country.

kusaal: O anɛ ka bɛdigʋ mi' ye o anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd tita'ar, Ronaldo di Ballon d'Or piinɛ anu, o anɛ UEFA nwɛ'ɛd tita'ar bɛ Europe ni, nɛ European Golden Shoes anaasi, o lɛm anɛ European nwɛ'ɛd tita'ar.
english: Nicknamed CR7, he is widely regarded as one of the greatest players in history, having won numerous individual accolades throughout his career including five Ballon d'Or awards, a record three UEFA Men's Player of the Year Awards, and four European Golden Shoes.

kusaal: Ronaldo mɔr yʋ'ʋr pʋdigir bɛ yiib (183), gɔɔlnam (140) nɛ sʋŋ ka ba di mɛn an (42) bɛ Champions League ni, gɔɔlnami bɛ European Championship (14), international gɔɔlnam (127) nɛ international yiib (203).
english: He holds the records for most goals (140) and assists (42) in the Champions League, most goals (14) and assists (8) in the European Championship, most international appearances (233), most men's international goals (146), and most international victories (141).

kusaal: Ronaldo da an saŋkan bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd kani ligidi kpi'em ka tiki wa'ae Real Madrid yʋʋm 2009 la ni nɛ tiakir ligidi wʋʋ €94 million (£80 million).
english: In 2009, he joined Real Madrid in a deal worth €94 million (£80 million), which was the most expensive transfer in history at the time.

kusaal: O di tirifisnam 34 o nwɛ'ɛb ni wʋsa, pɛ'ɛsnɛ lik piinɛ ayɔpɔi, UEFA Champions Leagues anu, UEFA European Championship nɛ UEFA Nations League.
english: Ronaldo is one of the most decorated players in the history of professional football, having won 35 trophies in his career, including five UEFA Champions Leagues, two UEFA Nations Leagues and the UEFA European Championship.

kusaal: O anɛ nwɛ'ɛdib bi'ela bani yi gaad 1,200 yinne o nwɛ'ɛb pʋʋgʋn, ka dii gaad kpɛɛm gɔɔlnam 850 tis kilab nɛ o tɛŋ, kɛt ka o an gɔɔl dit kpɛɛm tisi o saŋa ni.
english: Ronaldo made his international debut for Portugal in 2003 at the age of 18, and has earned more than 200 caps, making him history's most-capped male player.

kusaal: Ronaldo pin'ili o nwɛ'ɛb la nɛ bɛ Sporting CP, ka naam tik Manchester United bɛ yʋʋm 2003 ni, onɛ di FA Kab o yiiga nwɛ'ɛb ni.
english: After Sporting defeated Manchester United 3–1 in a friendly on 6 August 2003, United manager Alex Ferguson was determined to acquire Ronaldo, describing him as "one of the most exciting young players" he had ever seen.

kusaal: O lɛm keŋ tuoni di piininam atan' bɛ Premier League ni, Champions League nɛ FIFA Club World Cup; onɛ da an yʋma 23 la, o di o yiiga Ballon d'Or.
english: He gradually established himself as an integral player for the club, winning three consecutive Premier League titles, the 2007–08 Champions League, and the 2008 FIFA Club World Cup.

kusaal: Saŋkaŋa nwa, o di back-to-back Ballons d'Or bɛ yʋʋm 2013 nɛ yʋʋm 2014 la ni, nɛ yʋʋm 2016 nɛ 2017 ya'as, ka bɛ runner-up Lionel Messi nya'aŋ nɔɔr atan', o nintaa bɔɔl mwɛ'ɛb ni.
english: With Madrid, he also won two La Liga titles, won the Ballon d'Or in 2013, 2014, 2016, and 2017, and became the club's all-time top goalscorer.

kusaal: O lɛm an kilab la saŋa wʋsa bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd gɔɔl dit bɛ Champions League ni, ka an onɛ naae o yigilim-yigilim gɔɔl dit onɛ bɛ agɔla tis yʋma ayuobʋ yit 2012 nɛ 2018 pʋʋgʋn.
english: In the 2012–13 season, Ronaldo scored his first hat-trick in the Champions League in a 4–1 win over Ajax.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2018 nii, o tiki tis Juventus ka yɔɔd an €100 million (£88 million), dinɛ an tiakir kani ligidi kpi'ɛm bɛ Italian kilab tis nwɛ'ɛd onɛ gaad yʋma 30.
english: Ronaldo joined Juventus in 2018 for €100 million, the transfer was the highest ever for a player over 30 years old and the highest paid by an Italian club.

kusaal: O lɛb Manchester United yʋʋm 2021, ka naae yʋʋm yinne ka an onɛ gɔɔli gat sɔ' wʋsa, ka o kɔntirak la kʋ'ʋg yʋʋm 2022.
english: In 2021, he returned to Manchester United, but his contract was terminated in 2022 after a public dispute with the club's management.

kusaal: Ronaldo nwɛ'ɛb tita'ar international tis Portugal bɛ yʋʋm 2003 ka an yʋʋm 18 ka mɔri gaad kabnam wʋʋ 200, kɛt ka o an nid kaani an o teŋ la wʋsa nɛ yʋ'ʋri digi an bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd kani mɔr baŋir gat sɔ' wʋsa, ka Guinness World Records mi' o.
english: Ronaldo made his international debut for Portugal in 2003 at the age of 18, and has earned more than 200 caps, making him history's most-capped male player.

kusaal: ^ Does not include one goal scored on 18 September 2010 against Real Sociedad.
english: He scored his 100th league goal for Madrid in a 5–1 win over Real Sociedad on 24 March 2012, breaking the previous club record held by Ferenc Puskás.

kusaal: Marca, which awards the Pichichi Trophy, attribute it to Ronaldo, while La Liga and UEFA attribute it to Pepe.
english: He scored 31 goals in 30 league games during the season, which earned him the the European Golden Shoe (shared with Luis Suárez) and the Pichichi Trophy.

kusaal: Christopher Addae anɛ tuongat ka lɛn maan politis Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, o da kilim wadmaan tis Bibiani-Anhwiaso-Bekwai Constituency linɛ bɛ Western Region Ghana la.
english: Christopher Addae is an administrator and Ghanaian politician who served as the member of the Fifth parliament of the Fourth Republic representing the Bibiani-Anhwiaso-Bekwai Constituency of the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yit nɛ Nambro-Sefwi Anhwiaso linɛ bɛ Western Region Ghana.
english: He hails from Nambro-Sefwi Anhwiaso in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paam Master of Arts degree in international affairs yit University of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' la ni.
english: He obtained his Master of Arts degree in international affairs from University of Ghana in 1992.

kusaal: O da an District Chief Executive tis Bibiani-Anhwiaso-Bekwai lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ yinnɛ paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu la ni.
english: He was the District Chief Executive of Bibiani-Anhwiaso-Bekwai from 2001 to 2005.

kusaal: Ba da vooti tis Addae ka o kɛŋ Parliament of Ghana yiiga nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi, Samanpiid nwadig la ni, ban da voot yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi vootʋg la nya'aŋ.
english: Addae was first elected into Parliament in December 2004 after the completion of the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Humado tis John Kobla Humado nɛ o pʋ'a Grace Abla Humado.Ba wʋsa yinɛ Alakple n bɛ Keta Municipality bɛ Volta Region Ghana nwa.

kusaal: Bɛ 1985, o daa naae yina nɛ Certificate bɛ Monitoring bɛ Evaluation of Public Sector Projects nɛ Programmes course n bɛ University of East Anglia, Norwich, England.
english: In 1985, he completed a Certificate in Monitoring and Evaluation of Public Sector Projects and Programmes course at the University of East Anglia, Norwich, England.

english: Humado has worked in various capacities and as a consultant in agriculture and finance in various organisations such as U SAID WEST AFRICA.

kusaal: O anɛ kpɛɛm bɛ monitoring bɛ Evaluation ka an nka an nya'andɔl tis Project manager for International Fund for Agricultural Development bɛ 1991 ti paae 1999.
english: He was also the Head monitoring and Evaluation Deputy Project manager for International Fund for Agricultural Development from 1991 to 1999.

kusaal: O daa an kpɛɛm bɛ World Food Program yit 1990 to paae 1991.
english: He was also the National Officer for World Food Program from 1990 to 1991.

kusaal: O daa kpɛn' politiks we'ɛd bɛ 2000 onɛ daa la'as nɛ Alakple branch bɛ ma'asim tiig paati la.

kusaal: O daa di lieb wadmaan tis Anlo December 2004 vɔtʋg tita'ar la ni.

kusaal: Ba daa lɛm gaan o ye o an youth nɛ Sports minista yi gɔmma zugdaan kʋdʋg Atta-Mills saŋa.

kusaal: O an kristo biig ka pʋʋsid bɛ Catholic.

english: Clement Kofi Humado (born 18 December 1953) is the Member of Parliament for the Anlo constituency in Ghana.

english: He was the Minister for Interior in the National Democratic Congress government of John Atta Mills in Ghana until January 2010.

english: He was formerly the Member of Parliament for Bawku West constituency in the Upper East region of Ghana from 1993 to 2005.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2008 la ni ka o da wadamaanib vɔɔtʋg la ka kpɛn Wadmaanib yin la zi'en Sabil (Zebilla) sʋ'ʋlimin la ziek.
english: In the 2008 parliamentary election, he re-entered parliament as the second MP for the Zebilla constituency and assumed office in January 2009.

kusaal: Avoka anɛ Catholic Pʋ'ʋsʋm nid ka mɔr pu'a nɛ biis anaasi.
english: Avoka is a Catholic Christian and is married with four children.

kusaal: O anɛ Gaana (Ghana) Lɔya ka mɛ nwɛ'ɛd pɔlitiks ka an Gaana Wadmaanɛ zie tis Sabil teŋin (Zebilla East constituency) linɛ bɛ Upper East sʋ'ʋlimin la.
english: Cletus Apul Avoka (born 20 November 1951) is a Ghanaian lawyer, politician and member of the Parliament of Ghana representing the Zebilla constituency in the Upper East region.

kusaal: Cletus Apul Avoka anɛ onɛ nyit Tesh teŋkpɛŋ linɛ bɛ Sabil sʋ'ʋlimin.

english: After the 2012 general elections, he was replaced by Benjamin Kunbuor for the 6th Parliament of the 4th Republic as Majority Leader.

english: Cletus Seidu Dapilah (born 2 April 1980) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Jirapa Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Upper West Region la dim.

kusaal: Dapilah yinɛ Tizza-Nimbare.
english: Dapilah hails from Tizza-Nimbare.

kusaal: O mɔr Bachelor of Business Administration kasɛtta gbaʋŋ.
