kusaal: Yʋʋm 2024 la ni, kooko kuob dunia la wʋsa daa anɛ 5.8 million tonnes, Ivory Coast daa mɔrnɛ kɔbiga pʋʋgin pistan nɛ anii (38%) ka Ghana dɔl nɛ Indonesia.
english: In 2024, global cocoa bean production reached 5.8 million tonnes, with Ivory Coast leading at 38% of the total, followed by Ghana and Indonesia.

kusaal: Kooko biIili, kooko kpaam, nɛ kooko zɔ'ɔm la ba kuosidi li nɛ da'asin, ka London dim nini nɛ bɛ West Africa dim kooko nɛ New York dinɛ an' Southeast Asian dim kooko la ni.
english: Cocoa beans, cocoa butter, and cocoa powder are traded on futures markets, with London focusing on West African cocoa and New York on Southeast Asian cocoa.

kusaal: Di yinɛ kakaw(a) ni, amaa pian'ʋk la yinɛ Nahuatl bɛɛ Mixe-Zoquean buudi pian'ad ni la anɛ nɔŋgbannwa'ar bɛ buudi pian'ad nam ni.
english: It is ultimately derived from kakaw(a), but whether that word originates in Nahuatl or a Mixe-Zoquean language is the subject of substantial linguistic debate.

kusaal: Kooko biili da pin'ili yinɛ 19th century la ni; 18th century la saŋa ba da buoni banɛ chocolate nuts, cocoa nuts bɛɛ kooko.
english: The term cocoa beans originated in the 19th century; during the 18th century they were called chocolate nuts, cocoa nuts or just cocoa.

kusaal: Ba da mɔri li yinɛ Santa Ana-La Florida (SALF) site dinɛ yʋ'ʋm bɛ Ecuador (Zamora-Chinchipe Province)Ya-tun Nya'aŋ pʋ lal nɛ Mayo-Chinchipe, ka naan pin'il bɛ Mesoamerica.
english: It was first domesticated at least 5,300 years ago, in equatorial South America at the Santa Ana-La Florida (SALF) site in what is present-day southeast Ecuador (Zamora-Chinchipe Province) by the Mayo-Chinchipe culture, before being introduced in Mesoamerica.

kusaal: Di mɛ da nɔbʋgʋ bɛ foothills of Andes dinɛ bɛ Amazon region la nɛd the Orinoco basins dinɛ bɛ South America, nwɛnɛ Colombia nɛ Venezuela.
english: It also grows in the foothills of the Andes in the Amazon region and the Orinoco basins of South America, such as in Colombia and Venezuela.

kusaal: Kooko tiis la ni ka ti paamɛt laad banɛ ka nɔk Kooko maal nɛ di kpaam dinɛ ka buon ye cocoa butter la.
english: Cocoa beans, cocoa butter, and cocoa powder are traded on futures markets, with London focusing on West African cocoa and New York on Southeast Asian cocoa.

kusaal: Kooko tiis la pɛ'ɛsnɛ Amazon rainforest ni.
english: The cacao tree is native to the Amazon rainforest.

kusaal: Kooko tiig la kena wʋʋ yʋʋma tusa anu nɛ kɔbistan banɛ gaad la (5,300 )dɔlisid Mayo-Chinchipe buudi kanɛ bɛ South America la ka di yaan paae Mesoamerica.
english: It was first domesticated at least 5,300 years ago, in equatorial South America at the Santa Ana-La Florida (SALF) site in what is present-day southeast Ecuador (Zamora-Chinchipe Province) by the Mayo-Chinchipe culture, before being introduced in Mesoamerica.

kusaal: Pre-Hispanic dim da dɛŋim mɔrnɛ kooko maanɛ ba malima , ka di biis la nwenɛ ligidi bɛɛ linɛ ka ba na nyaŋi nɔki da' siel Mesoamerica sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: The cacao tree was first domesticated at least 5,300 years ago by the Mayo-Chinchipe culture in South America before it was introduced in Mesoamerica. Cacao was consumed by pre-Hispanic cultures in spiritual ceremonies, and its beans were a common currency in Mesoamerica. The cacao tree grows in a limited geographical zone; today, West Africa produces nearly 81% of the world's crop.

kusaal: Ba anɛ, Forastero, Criollo, nɛ Trinitario, ka Forastero la ka ba kuod bɛdigʋ.
english: They are generally of the Amelonado type and are associated with West Africa. Trinitario refers to any hybrid between Criollo and Forastero.

kusaal: Zin'is bɛdigʋ mukidnɛ ye ba sʋŋ ka Kooko nɔbig.La'am nɛ Swiss Platform for Sustainable Cocoa (SWISSCO), German Initiative on Sustainable Cocoa (GISCO), nɛ Belgium's Beyond Chocolate.
english: These include the Swiss Platform for Sustainable Cocoa (SWISSCO), the German Initiative on Sustainable Cocoa (GISCO), and Beyond Chocolate, Belgium.

kusaal: Dunia wʋsa kooko sʋŋid nɛ kɔbiga pʋʋgin pisi nɛ awai chocolate yisibin yʋʋm 2016 la.
english: As of 2016, at least 29% of global cocoa production was compliant with voluntary sustainability standards.

kusaal: Tiis banɛ ka ba waan'ad bɛɛ kʋʋd West Africa la mɔrnɛ daan'ʋŋ pamm na tisid cocoa kuob.
english: In late 2000, a BBC documentary reported the use of enslaved children in the production of cocoa in West Africa. Other media followed by reporting widespread child slavery and child trafficking in the production of cocoa.

kusaal: Kooko sʋŋid nɛ ligidi zin'igin wʋʋ Nigeria dim la bɔɔd laad banɛ ka ba nɔk kooko maal siem la.
english: Cocoa contributes significantly to economies such as Nigeria's, and demand for cocoa products has grown at over 3% annually since 2008.

kusaal: Cocoa mɔr laad nam wʋʋ flavanols, procyanidins, nɛ flavonoids, nɛ flavanol-rich chocolate nɛ Kooko la'ad la sieba mɔr sieli di ni ka di na tʋne sie zidʋtʋm.
english: Cocoa contains phytochemicals like flavanols, procyanidins, and other flavonoids, and flavanol-rich chocolate and cocoa products may have a small blood pressure lowering effect.

kusaal: Di mɛ lɛn mɔr theobromine nɛ caffeine biela.
english: The beans contain theobromine, and between 0.1% and 0.7% caffeine, whereas dry coffee beans are about 1.2% caffeine.

kusaal: Kooko anɛ cacao buudi, din tun'e an ye di yinɛ pian'ʋk coco zug.
english: Cocoa is a variant of cacao, likely due to confusion with the word coco.

kusaal: Kooko tiig anɛ dinɛ yi Amazon rainforest ni.
english: The cacao tree is native to the Amazon rainforest.

kusaal: Ba da mɔri li kul yin nwɛnɛ yʋma tusa anu nɛ kɔbistan' banɛ gaad la saŋa bɛ equatorial South America.
english: As of 2018, evidence suggests that cacao was first domesticated in equatorial South America, before being domesticated in Central America roughly 1,500 years later.

kusaal: Nwɛnnɛ yʋma tusa atan' (3,000) banɛ gaad la, di anɛ bʋnkanɛ ka kʋdʋmin dim da diti li dɔlisid Yucatán, la'an nɛ Maya dim buudi nam ni, ka fʋ ya'a gɔsi ,lɛb nya'aŋ nwɛnɛ Olmeca civilization dinɛ ka ba da maan ka di an siigin malima.
english: More than 3,000 years ago, it was consumed by pre-Hispanic cultures along the Yucatán, including the Maya, and as far back as Olmeca civilization in spiritual ceremonies.

kusaal: Collins Adomako-Mensah (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 2 Sapal/Nwadispii 1983) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg New Patriotic Party nid.
english: Collins Adomako-Mensah (born 2 November 1983) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O zi'enɛ tis Afigya Kwabre North Constituency ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He represents Afigya Kwabre North Constituency in the 8th parliament of the 4th Republic in Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Boaman Maase bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Adomako Mensah was born on 2 November 1983 and hails from Boaman Maase in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Presbyterian Boy's Senior Secondary School bɛ Legon la.
english: He attended the Presbyterian Boy's Senior Secondary School, Legon for his secondary school education.

kusaal: O da maali o Bachelor of Arts degree in banking and finance nɛ Executive Master of Business Administration yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la na (2007) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016).
english: He was awarded a Bachelor of Arts degree in banking and finance and an Executive Master of Business Administration in 2007 and 2016 respectively and Master of Arts in economics at the University of Ghana (Legon).

kusaal: Adomako-Mensah tʋmya nɛ ligidi zin'is bɛdigʋ nwɛnɛ GCB, Fidelity bank an deputy manager nɛ relationship manager.
english: Adomako-Mensah has worked with financial institutions such as GCB, Fidelity bank as deputy manager, associate member of chattered institute of banking and relationship manager and member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ay nɛ pisi Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg vɔɔtʋgin la, Adomako-Mensah da nya'a Afigya Kwabre North kʋk la nɛ ba Wadmaan la, Nana Marfo Amaniampong ka di.
english: During the 2020 NPP parliamentary primaries Adomako-Mensah contested for the Afigya Kwabre North seat against the then MP, Nana Marfo Amaniampong and won.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, Adomako- Mensah da di kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yinne (20,441) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ anu du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (65.75%) ka onɛ ti'al o la, Emmanuel Jackson Agumah onɛ an Ma'asim tiig nid la paam vɔɔt tusa piiga, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (10,646) dinɛ an pistan nɛ anaasi du'al pisi nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (34.25%).
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, Adomako- Mensah won the seat with 20,441 votes representing 65.75% as against his opponent Emmanuel Jackson Agumah of the NDC who polled 10646 representing 34.25% of votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadis piinɛ yinne la pʋʋgin (November 2021), Adomako-Mensah da tis sakur biis banɛ ye ba sɔbi akarim gaat taab mathematical sets nɛ gbaʋŋ zamisʋg la'asieba Afigya Kwabre North Constituency sʋ'ʋlim n bɛ Ashanti region la.
english: In November 2021, Adomako-Mensah donated mathematical sets and other stationery to candidates in the Afigya Kwabre North Constituency in the Ashanti region.

english: He is the nephew of Albert Kan-Dapaah.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adomako Mensah nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan Nwadis piinɛ yinne daba ayi daar (2 November 1983).
english: Adomako Mensah was born on 2 November 1983 and hails from Boaman Maase in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Adomako-Mensah paas la'askanɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla (finance committee) nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid nimma'asim yɛla (health committee).

english: Adomako-Mensah is a Christian.

english: In 2020, he was alleged to have been involved in a GHS264,094 theft.

english: Alhaji Collins Dauda (born 13 February 1957) is a teacher, politician, former Ghanaian Minister for Lands and Natural Resources; and Water Resources, Works and Housing and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing Asutifi South Constituency He is from Mahame in the Brong Ahafo Region.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Collins Dauda nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadisa ayi' la dabpiinɛ atan' daar (13 February 1957) Mehame bɛ Ahafo region (dinɛ da an, Brong Ahafo Region) sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Collins Dauda was born on 13 February 1957 in Mehame in the Ahafo region (formerly, Brong Ahafo Region).

kusaal: o da keŋnɛ Mim Senior High School maal GCE Ordinary Level nɛ GCE Advanced Level yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' (1973) nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981) sʋʋgʋn.
english: His secondary education was at Mim Senior High School where he obtained both the GCE Ordinary Level and the GCE Advanced Level between 1973 and 1981.

kusaal: Dauda da pa'anɛ Kukuom Agricultural Senior High School din yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu saŋa (1985).
english: Dauda taught at the Kukuom Agricultural Senior High School from 1985.

kusaal: Yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1986) la nii, o da lieb pa'ani tis Ahafoman Senior High School tʋgʋs tuon nɛ o pa'alʋg la hali ti paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' la ni (1992).
english: In 1986, he joined the teaching staff at the Ahafoman Senior High School where he continued to teach until 1992.

kusaal: Dauda da lieb Asutifi District Assembly la nid yinne yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (1978) nɛ yʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981) sʋʋgʋn.
english: Dauda became a member of the Asutifi District Assembly between 1978 and 1981.

kusaal: O da di kʋk la din yi wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anaasi (4th) paae ayɔpɔi daan (7th) republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He has maintained the seat from the 4th to the 7th parliament of the 4th republic.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ ayi (2002) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la o da pʋ kpɛn' Wadmaanib yin la, o da anɛ Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) bɛ Brong Ahafo Region.
english: During 2002 and 2004 when he was out of parliament, he was the Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Brong Ahafo Region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai Nwadisa ayi la (February 2009) ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016), ba da gaŋ Collins Dauda ye o an Minista tis Lands and Mineral Resources ka da lɛn tiak o ye o tʋm Ministry of Water Resources, Works and Housing.
english: From February 2009 to 2016, Collins Dauda was appointed Minister for Lands and Mineral Resources and reshuffled to the Ministry of Water Resources, Works and Housing.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ kʋkdaan nya'adɔli tis la'askanɛ gɔsid tam nɛ tiis yɛla la (Lands and Forestry) din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ (1996).
english: He was also the Vice president of the committee on Lands and Forestry between 1994 and 1996.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt Dauda paas nɔɔr atan (3rd time) ka o an wadmaani tis Asutifi South constituency bɛ Brong Ahafo Region la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Dauda was elected for the 3rd time as the member of parliament for the Asutifi South constituency of the Brong Ahafo Region in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Asutifi South constituency dim da vɔɔtnɛ pʋlʋmir, ba da vɔɔti tis John Kufour onɛ an New Patriotic Party nid.
english: The Asutifi South constituency saw a 'skirt and blouse' voting by electorates in that election as the presidential candidate elected by the constituency electorates was John Kufour of the major opposition New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress la da di kʋgʋs piswai nɛ anaasi (94) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi nɛ pistan pʋʋgin (230).
english: The National Democratic Congress won a minority total of 94 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Dauda da paam vɔɔt tusa awai, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (9,668) yi vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anii nɛ kɔbis yɔpɔi (18,700) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne du'al pisyɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.70%).
english: Dauda was elected with 9,668 votes out of 18700 total valid votes cast, equivalent to 51.70% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas Thomas Broni onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la, Nana Nsiah Ababio Williams Cosmus onɛ an People's National Convention nid nɛ Adu Adjei Augustine onɛ an Convention People's Party.
english: He was elected over Thomas Broni of the New Patriotic Party, Nana Nsiah Ababio Williams Cosmus of the People's National Convention and Adu Adjei Augustine of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la nii, ba da lɛn vɔɔt Dauda ka o keŋ nɔɔr anaasi daan (4th) an wadmaani tis Asutifi South constituency.
english: In the 2008 Ghanaian general elections, Dauda was elected for the 4th time as the member of parliament for the Asutifi South constituency.

kusaal: Dauda da paam vɔɔt tusa piiga, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (10,984) yi vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ ayi nɛ pistan nɛ ayi pʋʋgin (22,032) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai du'al pisnii nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (49.85%).
english: Dauda was elected with 10,984 votes out of 22,032 total valid votes cast, equivalent to 49.85% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas Yiadom Boakye onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid nɛ Okyere George onɛ an Democratic People's Party nid la.
english: He was elected over Yiadom Boakye of the New Patriotic Party and Okyere George of the Democratic People's Party.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋgin ba da paamnɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (49.79%) nɛ nɛɛm du'al pistan nɛ anu (0.35%).
english: These obtained 49.79% and 0.35% of total valid votes cast respectively.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlim dim da lɛn vɔɔt o ya'as yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la ni ye o zi'eni tisi ba Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He was re-elected by his constituents in the 2020 General election, to represent them in the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Dauda paas la'askanɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla, (Finance committee), o lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid tam nɛ tiis yɛla (Lands and Forestry Committee) nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid gaansʋg yɛla (Selection Committee).
english: Dauda is a member of the Finance committee, also a member of the Lands and Forestry Committee and also a member of Committee of Selection Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa anii la ni (August 2016), Dauda da pian'adi tisidi o Na'adɔɔg nidib ka ye wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party mɔr barigaŋ nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ Zongo ka ye "ti kɛl ka ba baŋ ye tinam pʋ bɛ nɛ baa".
english: In August 2016, Dauda in addressing party supporters at Koforidua said that the then opposition New Patriotic Party had a long history of discriminating against Zongo people and that "We should let them know that we are not with them".

kusaal: O yinɛ Mehame bɛ Brong-Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Collins Dauda was born on 13 February 1957 in Mehame in the Ahafo region (formerly, Brong Ahafo Region).

kusaal: O du'adib anɛ Issaka Naaba nɛ Mariama Issah.
english: His parents were Issaka Naaba and Mariama Issah.

kusaal: wadmaanib vɔɔdʋg la ni, o da zi'enɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba Zug ka di lieb yiiga Wadmaani tis Asutifi South constituency Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni (Fourth Republic).
english: He was first elected to parliament in the 1992 parliamentary election on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress making him the first MP for the Asutifi South constituency in the Fourth Republic.

kusaal: O da lɛn di ya'as yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ (1996) wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: He won a second term in the 1996 parliamentary election.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da lieb kʋkdaani tis la'askan din yi yʋʋm tusir kɔbisyi nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1997) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi la (2000) ka da lɛn tʋm la'asbanɛ gɔsid ligidi nɛ pʋ'asada nɛ dasam, ninwisigir nɛ buudi malima yɛla.
english: He later became chairman of the same committee between 1997 and 2000 and also served as member of the Finance and Youth, Sports and Culture Committees.

kusaal: O da lɛn zi'en tisi o sʋ'ʋlim dim Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anaasi la Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He was re-elected by his constituents in the 2020 General election, to represent them in the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋgin bama da paamnɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ du'al piswai (46.90%), yinne du'al pisi (1.20%) nɛ nɛɛm du'al pistan (0.30%).
english: These obtained 46.90%, 1.20% and 0.30% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Dauda mɔr pʋ'aba ayi nɛ biis piinɛ yinne.
english: Dauda is married with two wives and eleven children.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlim la paas sʋ'ʋlimam kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ anaasi (114) banɛ ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la da di yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi nɛ pistan (230) pʋʋgin la.
english: His constituency was part of the majority total of 114 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats in that election.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Manhyia North Constituency n bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, o anɛ wabʋg paati la nid.
english: Collins Owusu Amankwah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Manhyia North Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Collins nɛ 21 August 1980, o yinɛ Gyinyase n bɛ Ashanti Region.
english: Collins was born on 21 August 1980 and hails from Gyinyase in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O mɔr Bachelor of Arts degree in sociology bɛ University of Ghana, Legon ka lɛm mɔr LLB yi GIMPA.
english: He had his Bachelor of Arts degree in sociology from University of Ghana, Legon and also had his LLB from GIMPA.

kusaal: o anɛ student of Kumasi High Sakur biig kʋdʋg.
english: He is an old student of Kumasi High School.

kusaal: Collins daa an kpɛem bɛ All Friends FM (94.5 MHz), Kumasi yi 2011 ti paae 2013 apɔi ka o na lɛm lieb wadmaan.
english: Collins worked as the General Manager for All Friends FM (94.5 MHz), Kumasi from 2011 to 2013 before going into Parliament.

kusaal: o daa mɛ lɛm an kpɛɛm bɛ Jakwapo Express Limited bɛ 2002 ti paae 2004.
english: He was also a scale manager at Jakwapo Express Limited from 2002 to 2004.

kusaal: O daa lɛm an kpɛɛm bɛ Clean City Initiative yi 2008 ti paae 2018.
english: He was also the Executive Director for Clean City Initiative from 2008 to 2018.

kusaal: Ba daa vɔɔt ti o ka lieb wadmaan yiiga saŋa bɛ 2013 bɛ 2012 Ghana dim vɔtʋg tita'ar la nya'aŋ.
english: He was voted into Parliament for the first time in 2013 after the completion of the 2012 Ghanaian General Election.

kusaal: On daa naae o yʋma anaasi la, ba daa lɛm vɔɔt ti tis o ya'as on daa nyaŋi onɛ daa nya'andnɛ o la ka kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ ka o paam 71.80% yit nidiba nɛ wʋsa vɔɔt la ni.
english: After serving his four years term, he was re-elected again after defeating his opposition with a dominating percentage of 71.80% of the total valid vote, his political went down after the election in january 2024.

kusaal: Collins Owusu Amankwah anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ politiks wɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan bɛ wadmaanib yikanɛ paas ayɔpɔi la n bɛ Gbana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: Collins Owusu Amankwah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Manhyia North Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Collins anɛ kristo biig .O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis anii.
english: Collins is a Christian.

kusaal: O anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid.
english: He is a member of the NPP.

kusaal: Comfort Doyoe Cudjoe-Ghansah anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd n an wadmaan n tis Ada sυ'υlυm.
english: Hon. Comfort Doyoe Cudjoe-Ghansah (born 3 November 1967) is a Ghanaian politician and the Member of Parliament for Ada constituency.

kusaal: Nannanna onɛ an Chief Whip kpɛɛm nya'andɔl n bɛ Gaana wadmaanib yir la ni.
english: She was, as of 2023, the Deputy Government Chief Whip in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Comfort da keŋ sakur n bɛ Royal Academy of Accounting sakur linɛ Ankara sυ'υlυm naae ka di'e Diploma kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Stenographership yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ atan' la ni.
english: Comfort earned her diploma in stenographership from Royal Academy of Accounting, Accra in 1983.

kusaal: O da lɛn tɔlis Ghana Institute of Journalism sakurin la naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Walisnam nɛ TV namin pian'ad yɛla la yυυma tusa yi nɛ piinɛ yinne la ni.
english: She earned a certificate in radio and television presentation from the Ghana Institute of Journalism in 2011.

kusaal: Nidib atan' banɛ ka on nɛ ban da nya'and la anɛ Kanor Saakey Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid, Asupah Manasseh National Democratic Party nid nɛ Daniel Katey Ossah Convention People's Party nid yυυma yi nɛ piina yuobu la ni.
english: Three other candidates namely Kanor Saakey of the New Patriotic Party, Asupah Manasseh of National Democratic Party and Daniel Katey Ossah of Convention People's Party also contested in the 2016 by-election of Ada constituency held in 2016.

kusaal: O da anɛ Minister of State n gɔsid ti Gaana tem maalυg yɛla.
english: She served as the Minister of State in charge of Social and Allied Institutions.

kusaal: Cudjoe-Ghansah anɛ wadmaan n tis Ada sυ'υlυm la, ka paas kpɛɛmnam banɛ gɔsid dap nɛ pu'ab nɛ biis yɛla la ni.
english: Cudjoe-Ghansah is the Member of Parliament for Ada constituency, and sits on the committees for gender and children, and on foreign affairs.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Minister of State n tis Gaana Gɔmina.
english: She was the Minister of State for the Ghanaian government on Social and Allied Institutions, having been named to the role in January 2013 by President of Ghana John Dramani Mahama.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la yυυma tusa yi nɛ piina naasi la ni ka ti Gaana Gɔmina John Dramani Mahama da gaŋ o ye o an Minista kan.
english: She was the Minister of State for the Ghanaian government on Social and Allied Institutions, having been named to the role in January 2013 by President of Ghana John Dramani Mahama.

kusaal: Cudjoe-Ghansah da zi'enɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la zugu nya'a di Ada linɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region sυ'υlυm la wadmaanib kυk la.
english: Cudjoe-Ghansah contested and won the National Democratic Congress parliamentary seat for Ada Constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Cudjoe-Ghansah da paamɛ vɔt 18,954 n yi vɔt la kanl wυsa ni linɛ 23,570 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da paamɛ 80.42 vɔt.
english: Cudjoe-Ghansah won the election by obtaining 18,954 votes out of the 23,570 cast, representing 80.42 percent of total valid votes.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi nɛ piina yuobu la ni ka o da zi'en Gɔmina nɔba zugu tɔnd kɔmputanam bam kɔbisnu (500) o sυ'υlυm la ni.
english: In 2016, she presented computers on behalf of the government to the head of the Ghanaian civil service, and over 500 desks to schools within her constituency.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi nɛ piisi la ni ka da ba lɛn vɔt ka o di, o da vɔtnam bam 27,591 kɔbiga pυυnɛ o da mɔri 82.14% vɔt.
english: In 2020 Cudjoe-Ghansah retained her seat, with 27,591 votes, gaining 82.14% of the votes cast for the Ada seat in Parliament.

kusaal: Comfort Owusu (dʋ'am 28 Vaala 1940) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ maan politis ka da an wadmaan bɛ Parliament of Ghana tis Mfantsiman East Constituency linɛ bɛ Central Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Owusu is a Beautician and a Former member of Parliament for the Mfantsiman East Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ sakur bɛ Morris School of Hairdressing & Culture anina ka o paam gbaʋŋ kanɛ an Diploma degree in Culture & Beauty.
english: She attended Morris School of Hairdressing & Culture where she obtained her Diploma degree in Culture & Beauty.

kusaal: O da pin'il politis nwɛ'ɛb nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' ni, sankan ka o da kilim wadmaan tis Mfantsiman constituency linɛ bɛ central region la dɔlis National Convention party na'adɔɔg la ni.
english: Her political career started in 1992 when she became a member of parliament for the Mfantsiman constituency of the central region on the Ticket of the National Convention party.

kusaal: O da lɛn nya'a na'am ya'as yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ yʋʋm tusayi' vootʋg nam la ni, kpɛlim zi'e nɛ tis Mfantsiman East Constituency dim ka paam na'am kuk la dɔlisid National Democratic Congress na'adɔɔg ni.
english: She contested again in the 1996 and 2000 Ghanaian General elections representing the Mfantsiman East Constituency and retained her seat on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da di ya'an ka an wadmaan tis Mfanstiman East constituency nɔɔra atan'.
english: She has won the seat of the Member of Parliament for the Mfanstiman East constituency three consecutive times.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Owusu nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi la ni bɛ Mfantsiman East linɛ bɛ Central region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Owusu was born in 1940 in the Mfantsiman East in the Central region of Ghana.

kusaal: Owusu kilim wadmaan nɔɔra atan' bɛ parliament of Ghana.
english: Owusu is a member of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Owusu anɛ onɛ mi' vɛnlim tʋʋma ka lɛn an wadmaan kʋdʋg tis Mfantsiman East Constituency linɛ bɛ Central Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Owusu is a Beautician and a Former member of Parliament for the Mfantsiman East Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Owusu anɛ Kristo nid.
english: Owusu is a Christian.

kusaal: Dasaʋŋ pɔl kanɛ an lɔya, Ebenezer Ako Adjei ka ba da gaŋ ye o tʋm gbaʋnsɔbid tʋʋma la tis (UGCC) ka ba yɔɔd o, ka o zan'as ka lɛɛ pa'al o pʋtɛn'ɛr ye ba gaŋim Kwame Nkrumah onɛ da bɛ na'asaateŋ (London) ka mɔr Gɔmma na'am nya'ab baŋir la ka o kena di'e kpɛʋŋ la.
english: Ebenezer Ako Adjei, then a young lawyer, was offered the paid secretaryship of the UGCC but he declined the position and instead proposed Kwame Nkrumah, a political activist then in London, for the position.

kusaal: Ako Adjei da mi'i Nkrumah nɛ ye o tiraan bɛ Lincoln University linɛ bɛ United State, Lincoln School of Economics la ni.
english: Ako Adjei had known Nkrumah as a fellow at Lincoln University in the United States and at the London School of Economics.

kusaal: Onɛ mɛ da lɛm an zugraan kʋdʋg tis West African Students' Union (WASU) bɛ London zin'ikanɛ ka ba da an yiiga dim di'e o Britain pʋʋgin on da naam United State kena la.
english: He was also the past President of the West African Students Union (WASU) in London which first hosted Nkrumah when he arrived in Britain from the United States.

kusaal: O da pʋn dɛŋim la'as nɛ George Padmore nɛ ninsieba ka ba buol Pan-African Congress la'asʋg linɛ paas anu bɛ Manchester 1945 saŋa England pʋʋgin.
english: Together with George Padmore and others he had organised in 1945 the Fifth Pan-African Congress in Manchester, England.

kusaal: Pin'ligin la, Nkrumah da pʋ bɔɔd ye o siaki di'e kpɛʋŋ la, on da pʋm mi' ye UGCC la la'asʋg la mɛŋ nɛ ba gban'abanɛ bɛ la pʋ bi'igi paae onɛ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr nɛ gban'asia bɔɔdin ye o maali ti Ghana nɛ Africa wʋsa la.
english: Initially, Nkrumah was hesitant about accepting the position, being aware that both the composition and objectives of the UGCC fell far short of the radical, political program he envisaged for the Gold Coast and for Africa. But after discussion with his colleagues he decided to accept, knowing that it might not be long before he would find it impossible to continue working within the UGCC.

kusaal: Sapal 14,1947 daar, Kwame Nkrumah da gban'e pʋtɛn'ɛpaalig bɛ Liverpool na'asaateŋ on nɛ o zua Kojo Botsio onɛ da paas WASU la ni ka ba an suor, ani ka ba pin'il pʋtɛn'ɛpaalig kati ken Ghana Gɔmma na'am labaya yɛla.
english: On 14 November 1947, Kwame Nkrumah set sail from Liverpool aboard the SS Accra, accompanied by Kojo Botsio, another friend from London who was also member of WASU and with that, the beginning of a new chapter in the modern political history of Ghana begun.

kusaal: Pin'lʋgʋn la, UGCC la da mɔr o nidib bi'ela la ka ba bɛ kɔlʋgnɔɔr tempʋtitada la ni nɛ Kibi pʋʋgʋn.
english: In the beginning, the UGCC had only a handful of branches in the larger coastal towns and Kibi.

kusaal: Convention people's Patty (CPP) dinɛ ka ti boun ye ''Anɔraʋg Paati'' la anɛ nidib la pʋtɛn'ɛrin Gɔmma na'am nya'ab dɔɔg bɛ Ghana kpɛla fʋ ya'a gɔsi ba yiiga Gɔmma tis Ghana, Kwame Nkrumah la pʋtɛn'ɛr da gban'e si'el la.
english: The Convention People's Party (CPP) is a socialist political party in Ghana based on the ideas of the first President of Ghana, Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Ba da zi'el Anɔraʋg paati (CPP) la nɛ Sigir 1949 saŋa ka Nkrumah da aan yi United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) ni la.
english: The CPP was formed in June 1949 after Nkrumah broke away from the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC).

kusaal: Convention people's Patty (CPP) ''Anɔraʋg Paati'' la da yinɛ Gɔmma na'anya'ab la'asʋg kanɛ ka na da sin'iŋi li bɛ 20th sintiri la pin'ilʋgʋn baba ye ba zab I kad na'asaanam la Ghana kpɛla la.
english: The Convention People's Party is descended from a line of political movements formed in the early half of the 20th century to spearhead the anti-colonial struggle in the Gold Coast.

kusaal: La'asʋg kanɛ da dɔl din nya'aŋ da anɛ United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) line ka ba da zi'eli li Mɔttʋl 1947 la ni ka Gbammi'idib nɛ Da'aditib kpɛɛmnam da an li tuoŋgatib la.
english: The movement that preceded it was the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) formed in August 1947 and led predominantly by members of the professional and business classes.

kusaal: UGCC tuongatib la da pʋ ki'is Ako Adjei pian'ad la ka sid siak ye ba na buol Kwame Nkrumah onɛ pʋn dɛŋim mɔr baŋir bɛdigʋ kati wa'ae Gɔmena na'am nya'ab dɔɔg tigisʋg nɛ tuon gaadʋg piini la.
english: Leaders of the UGCC — J. B. Danquah, Ofori Atta, Akufo Addo, Ako Adjei, Obetsebi Lamptey and Kwame Nkrumah, subsequently known as The Big Six – were arrested and flown to the Northern Territories, where they were detained for six weeks before being taken to Accra to appear at a Commission of Enquiry set up by the Governor under the chairmanship of Aiken Watson Q.C.

kusaal: Ba da nɔki Nkrumah pa'ali ba UGCC komatii tʋntʋnib la ye onɛ an ba gbansɔbid la nɛ samampiid 28,1947 daar, ka li pʋ yʋʋgɛ ka pin'il UGCC yaligir nɛ sʋŋir ieb tʋʋma la la'asid na'akim nɛ pʋ'asada dɔlisid teŋkpɛmis banɛ bɛ na'asaanam nu'usin la na'akim nɛ pʋ'asada la'asʋgnam ni.
english: Kwame Nkrumah was officially introduced to the UGCC's Working Committee as their Secretary on 28 December 1947 and soon got to work seeking to expand the support base of the UGCC by mobilizing the youth through local youth societies in the Colony (e.g., Apowa Literary and Social Club) and the Ashanti Confederacy (e.g., Asante Youth Association- AYA), whose members were farmers, petty-traders, drivers, artisans, school, teachers, clerks and letter-writers, many of whom were the growing number of elementary-school-leavers.

kusaal: (Tʋntʋʋnli, Apowa Literary and Social Club) nɛ Ashanti Confederacy (tʋntʋʋnli Asante Youth Association -AYA) dinɛ ka ba nidib da anɛ, kpaadib, da' ditib, dɔrʋbanam, sakuya, pa'anib, gbansɔbidib banɛ ka ba bɛdigʋ naae nɛ ''elementary school'' bɛn.
english: Kwame Nkrumah was officially introduced to the UGCC's Working Committee as their Secretary on 28 December 1947 and soon got to work seeking to expand the support base of the UGCC by mobilizing the youth through local youth societies in the Colony (e.g., Apowa Literary and Social Club) and the Ashanti Confederacy (e.g., Asante Youth Association- AYA), whose members were farmers, petty-traders, drivers, artisans, school, teachers, clerks and letter-writers, many of whom were the growing number of elementary-school-leavers.

kusaal: Nkrumah da ied tiakir la zug, o da duoe giligi paae zin'is la wʋsa buol la'asʋgnam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ka nwadis ayuobʋ bɛn ma'a ka UGCC la paam ya'ada Ghana kpɛla wʋsa.
english: At midnight on 5/6 March 1957, on the Polo Ground in Accra, Nkrumah proclaimed the Independence of Ghana, To cries of FREEDOM!

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da ti paae Ghana kpɛla 1947 naarin na la, ka nɔŋgbanwa'abaanlʋg sieba pʋn dɛŋ'm bɛ nidib la teŋ la zi'esim yɛla kati ken bumbɔɔdim nam kar ka di ligidinam mɛ dʋt la yɛla.
english: On 14 November 1947, Kwame Nkrumah set sail from Liverpool aboard the SS Accra, accompanied by Kojo Botsio, another friend from London who was also member of WASU and with that, the beginning of a new chapter in the modern political history of Ghana begun.

kusaal: Na'anam la nɛ Gɔmma na'adɔɔg la sɔsɔ da pʋ kɛlig nidib la daʋŋ an si'el teŋin la ka li ti kena anɛ ye Nii Kwabena Bonne II, nɛ Osu Alata Mantse li tuonɛ zabi tis nidib la kati ken teŋ la tʋlʋgʋr nɛ si'elnam ligidi dʋt tɔ'ɔtɔ si'em la.
english: Neither the chiefs nor the political class championed the growing disaffection in the country and it fell to Nii Kwabena Bonne II, Osu Alata Mantse, to lead the agitation against the growing economic hardship and especially the rising prices of consumer goods.

kusaal: Nkrumah da ti paae Ghana na la, the nwadig bɛn ka nidib la sʋndaʋŋ la wʋsa paam kʋkɔr pian'a ye ba kad kʋkpiʋŋ lʋga banɛ ka na'asaanam bɛɛ saam sʋ'ʋe la bas, Nii Kwabena Bonne II da buol la'asʋg la Yʋʋmpaal 26, 1948.
english: Just over a month after Nkrumah's arrival in the Gold Coast, the growing discontent found expression in a boycott of mostly foreign-owned trading firms organized by Nii Kwabena Bonne on 26 January 1948.

kusaal: Kadib la da tɔlisnɛ alaa ti paae wʋʋ nwadig ka tuoŋgatib la nɛ Gɔmma la nɛ kʋkpiʋŋ lʋga banɛ anɛ Association West African Merchants (AWAM) sɔnsid la'ad la ligidi sier yɛla.
english: The boycott continued for a month, while its leaders negotiated price reductions with the government and the trading firms in the Association of West African Merchants (AWAM).

kusaal: Joseph Boakye Danquah nɛ ban ti yina pian'a tis nidib la Ankara pʋʋgʋn ba na'adɔɔg la'asʋg daar, Fʋlʋnfʋʋg 20, 1948 daar.
english: There was unrest also among the ex-servicemen and both Kwame Nkrumah and Dr Joseph Boakye Danquah addressed them at a rally in Accra on 20 February 1948.

kusaal: Council of State anɛ Ghana lʋgʋr bil kanɛ ka nintitada bɛ di ni, nwɛnɛ Council of Elders bɛ pɔlitis na'anya'ar pʋʋgin sa'an Zuraan la teŋ la yɛla.
english: The Council of State in Ghana is a body of prominent citizens, analogous to the Council of Elders in the traditional political system, which advises the president on national issues.

kusaal: Council of State da pin'ilnɛ dɔlisid Articles 89 paae 92 dinɛ bɛ Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yi wada gbaʋŋʋn la (1992 Constitution of Ghana): "Council of State na bɛ ka sa'an Zuraan la on na tʋmi o tʋʋma si'em."
english: The Council of State was established by Articles 89 to 92 of the 1992 Constitution of Ghana: "There shall be a Council of State to counsel the President in the performance of his functions."

kusaal: Nimbanɛ bɛ Council of State ni anɛ Chief Justice kʋdʋg tis Ghana, Chief of the Defence Staff kʋdʋg nɛ Inspector General of Police kʋdʋg paasnɛ onɛ an Zuraani tis National House of Chiefs.
english: The Council of State should include a former Chief Justice of Ghana, a former Chief of the Defence Staff and a former Inspector General of Police and the president of the National House of Chiefs.

kusaal: Zuraan Nana Akufo-Addo da zuŋ banɛ paasi di ni nananna la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne nwadisa ayi la dabpisi nɛ tan' daar (23 February 2021) Jubilee House.
english: The membership from the past four years was sworn in by President Nana Akufo-Addo on 23 February 2021 at the Jubilee House.

kusaal: Ka fal kanɛ kpɛlim tis Ghana Chief Justice kʋdʋg la Georgina Theodora Wood da li'i di on da naae o tʋʋma la.
english: The vacant position reserved for former Chief Justice of Ghana was filled following the appointment of Georgina Theodora Wood following her retirement.

kusaal: Ba mɛ lɛn tʋn'e la'as Ghana Zuraan, Parliament of Ghana bɛɛ nidib anu bɛ gaadnidib anu bɛ gaadʋg banɛ paas la'asʋg la ni ya'a yɛl ye ba zin'inim.
english: It can also meet if requested by the President of Ghana, the Parliament of Ghana or by at least five sitting members of the council.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr la nar ye ba la'asi zi'en nɔɔr anaasi yʋʋm pʋʋgin.
english: The council is required to meet four times a year.

kusaal: Di nar ye nidib pʋsʋg bɛɛ gaadʋg bɛ la'asʋg la ni.
english: There should be more than half the members of the Council at a meeting to form a quorum.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni UNESCO da gaŋi li la'am nɛ Water Tribunal of the plain of Valencia ye di an intangible cultural heritage.
english: In 2009 it was chosen along with the Water Tribunal of the plain of Valencia as an intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO.

english: It is chaired by the Mayor or his delegate.

english: The Council holds its hearings in public every Thursday in the salon of the city hall of Murcia, from nine until noon.

kusaal: Sankanɛ ka ba pin'il dinɛ ka ti buon cruiserweight class la, ba da buon "light heavyweight" nɛ "cruiserweight" nɛ tiasid sansieba United Kingdom.
english: Before the advent of the current cruiserweight class, "light heavyweight" and "cruiserweight" were sometimes used interchangeably in the United Kingdom.

kusaal: Tɛbisim kanɛ ka ba mɔri makid division kaŋa nananna anɛ 200 pounds (90.7 kg; 14 st 4.0 lb).
english: The current weight limit for the division is 200 pounds (90.7 kg; 14 st 4.0 lb).

kusaal: La'anɛ heavyweight champions (nwɛnɛ Rocky Marciano nɛ Joe Louis) tɛbisim da an nwɛnɛ 190 poundsi ba tʋʋma ni la, 1970s la nii di da an zi'esim kanɛ nyaŋi siak heavyweight boxers banɛ tɛbisim an bɛɛ gaad 210 pounds (95 kg; 15 st 0 lb).
english: While many heavyweight champions (such as Rocky Marciano and Joe Louis) weighed around 190 pounds during their careers, during the 1970s it became fairly standard that fit heavyweight boxers weighed at least 210 pounds (95 kg; 15 st 0 lb).

kusaal: Kpɛɛm sieba da yɛt ye fʋn na yɛl onɛ mɔr 176 pounds (80 kg; 12 st 8 lb) nɛ 190 pounds (86 kg; 13 st 8 lb) ye ba zab nɛ nintitada bama pʋ dɔl suorɛ.
english: Many boxing authorities felt that asking men weighing between 176 pounds (80 kg; 12 st 8 lb) and 190 pounds (86 kg; 13 st 8 lb) to fight these larger men was unfair.

kusaal: World Boxing Council da an lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid zaba nɛ mɔɔr yɛla ka siaki tis cruiserweight division ban da tɛɛg Marvin Camel nɛ Mate Parlov tʋbir December 8, 1979, ban da tulig title la.
english: Camel won the match, which led to the World Boxing Council (WBC) sanctioning its first cruiserweight title fight between Marvin Camel and Mate Parlov on December 8, 1979.

kusaal: zabkan ni sɔ' da pʋ nyaŋi tiraana, amaa ban da lɛn zzab si'el March 1980 la, Camel da diya ka lieb yiiga daan di'e cruiserweight champion.
english: That fight was a draw, but in the rematch in March 1980 Camel won and became the first cruiserweight champion.

kusaal: 1982 World Boxing Association da nyɛ Ossie Ocasio ka o an yiiga daani di'e cruiserweight champion on da nyaŋi bʋ' South Africa dim daʋ Robbie Williams la.
english: In 1982 the World Boxing Association (WBA) recognized Ossie Ocasio as its first cruiserweight champion when he defeated South African Robbie Williams (although at that time the WBA called the division "junior heavyweight").

kusaal: International Boxing Federation da dɔl wala nɔɔ 1983 ban da kɛ ka WBC champion kʋdʋg Marvin Camel zab nɛ Rick Sekorski ba zuŋir title la.
english: The International Boxing Federation followed suit in 1983 when it matched former WBC champion Marvin Camel against Rick Sekorski for its inaugural title.

kusaal: Evander Holyfield onɛ da mɔr WBA, WBC, nɛ IBF title nam la da lieb yiiga daani mɔr title nama atan la ka dʋ' keŋ heavyweight division 1988.
english: Evander Holyfield unified the WBA, WBC, and IBF titles to become undisputed champion, the first to do so, and then moved up to the heavyweight division in 1988.

kusaal: 2006 ni, daʋ kanɛ da ti'ali ayi daan ka sɔ' pʋ nya'a o anɛ O'Neil Bell, onɛ ka nya'aŋ ka ba da faaen IBF title la ka bas o.
english: In 2006, the second man to become undisputed champion was O'Neil Bell, who was later stripped of the IBF title.

kusaal: Banɛ da an champions division kaŋa ni sieba anɛ Bobby Czyz, Dwight Muhammad Qawi, Tomasz Adamek, Virgil Hill, Al Cole, Orlin Norris, James Toney, David Haye, Tony Bellew nɛ Oleksandr Usyk.
english: Other notable champions in the division have been Bobby Czyz, Dwight Muhammad Qawi, Tomasz Adamek, Virgil Hill, Al Cole, Orlin Norris, James Toney, David Haye, Tony Bellew, Gilberto Ramirez, Jai Opetaia, David Benavidez, Noel Mikaelian, Chris Billam-Smith, Badou Jack, and Lawrence Okolie.

kusaal: Din da nam pin'il la, tɛbisim kanɛ ka ba da gɔsid bɛ da anɛ 190 pounds (86.2 kg; 13 st 8.0 lb).
english: When originally established, the weight limit was 190 pounds (86.2 kg; 13 st 8.0 lb).

kusaal: Division la da pin'ilnɛ ye di gɔs zabzabidib banɛ tɛmisim pʋ zu'oe paae heavyweight boxers ka kʋ nyaŋi nya' division kan nii.
english: The division was established in order to accommodate smaller heavyweight boxers who could not compete with the growing size of boxers in that division.

kusaal: Camel da diya ka an yiiga daani di'e IBF cruiserweight champion.
english: Camel won and became the first IBF cruiserweight champion.

kusaal: Zabzabidib bɛdegʋ duoe paae heavyweight ba ya'a di dunia wʋsa title bɛ cruiserweight zaba ni.
english: Oleksandr Usyk became undisputed cruiserweight champion in 2018; he moved to heavyweight in 2019, becoming the undisputed champion in 2024.

kusaal: Cynthia Mamle Morrison, ba da du'a o nɛ Yʋʋmtusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi, yʋʋmpaal nwadig la dabpiinɛ ayɔpɔi daar, Elmina n bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Cynthia Morrison was born on 17 January 1964 in Elmina in the Central Region.

kusaal: O da paami o pa'anib zamisʋgnɛ Maria Montessori Training School yʋʋmtusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la ni (1992) nɛ Hepziba Montessori.
english: She acquired a Teacher Training Certificate at Maria Montessori Training School in 1992 and also in Hepziba Montessori.

kusaal: O da lɛm paami o dʋgʋb kasɛtta gbaʋŋ yinɛ Flair Catering.
english: She also has certificates in catering from Flair Catering.

kusaal: O daa lɛn an pa'annib kpɛɛm tis Maryland Montessori bɛ Dansoman la.
english: She was also the Proprietress of Maryland Montessori in Dansoman.

kusaal: Nannanna onɛ an Wadmaani tis Agona West n bɛ Central Region.
english: She is currently the Member of parliament for Agona West Constituency in the Central Region.

kusaal: Nidib tusa pisnu nɛ awai, kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ atan' da vɔɔt, ka o paam tusa pisntan, kɔbisnu nɛ piinɛ atan ka onɛ kpi'e o la Paul Ofori-Amoah paam tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan ka onɛ da zi'eni o kɔn'ɔ kɔn' ka pʋ mɔr na'adɔɔg la Ishmael Kofi Tekyi Turkson da paam tusir yinne nɛ ayɔpɔi.
english: She polled 30,513 out of a total of 59,193 valid votes cast as against Paul Ofori-Amoah of the opposition National Democratic Congress who had 27,673 votes, and an Independent candidate Ishmael Kofi Tekyi Turkson had 1,007 votes.

kusaal: Onɛ an kʋkdaan tis la'askanɛ yʋ'ʋri an "Government Assurance Committee" ka lɛn an kʋkdaani tis banɛ gɔsid pian'ad yɛla.
english: She is the Chairperson of the Government Assurance Committee and also the Chairperson of the Communications Committee.

kusaal: O ɛlnɛ Herbert Morrison ka mɔr biis ayɔpɔi.
english: She is married to Herbert Morrison with seven children.

kusaal: Cynthia Mamle Morrison, ba da du'a o nɛ Yʋʋmtusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi, yʋʋmpaal nwadig la dabpiinɛ ayɔpɔi daar.
english: Cynthia Mamle Morrison (born 17 January 1964) is a Ghanaian politician from Elimina.

kusaal: O anɛ Awabʋg na'adɔɔg nid ka lɛn aan Agona West Wadmaan.
english: She was a member of parliament representing Agona West Constituency for the New Patriotic Party until she announced her independent candidacy for the 2024 General Elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii, nwadis anii la ni daba awai daar ka pirɛsidɛn Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an minista onɛ gɔsid pʋ'ab, biis nɛ ba bɛlim yɛla.
english: On 9 August 2018, she was appointed Minister designate for Gender, Children and Social Protection by President Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: O da di Agona West kʋk la yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ vɔɔtʋgʋn lanidib nayi banɛ da la'asi nya'and na'am la nɛ o anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid Charles Obeng-Inkoom nɛ Akubɛ na'adɔɔg hid Evans Idan Coffie.
english: Two other candidates namely Charles Obeng-Inkoom of National Democratic Congress and Evans Idan Coffie of Convention People's Party also contested in the 2016 by-election of the Agona West constituency held in 2016.

kusaal: Onɛ an minista kʋdʋg kanɛ gɔsid pu'ab nɛ biis yɛla.
english: She was the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection.

kusaal: Daboya an tempʋtita'ari tis North Gonja district, district kanɛ bɛ Savannah Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana Ya-datiʋŋ.
english: Daboya is the capital of the North Gonja district, a district in the Savannah Region of north Ghana.

english: It was previously called Burugu by the Dagomba people.

english: It was important in the trade route the stretched from Yendi to Bouna.

english: Today Daboya is represented by the Daboya-Mankarigu constituency.

english: There is an Army Special Operations Training School at Daboya.

english: Daboya is inhabited by the Gonja, Tampulma, Dagomba, and Hanga.

kusaal: Daboya da anɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ba kpiisid yaarim bɛ Kingdom of Dagbon.
english: Daboya was an important salt trading settlement in the Kingdom of Dagbon.

kusaal: Di anɛ tenkanɛ mɔr labakʋda bɛdegʋ Ghana.
english: It is considered a historical place in Ghana.

english: To the north is the Jirapa and Sissala West to the east the Sissala East and to the south east the and Wa East to the south the Wa.

english: The constituency was changed in 2012 when the initial Nadowli District was divided into the Nadowli-Kaleo District and Daffiama-Bussie-Issa District.

kusaal: Ka Nadowli-Kaleo yʋ'ʋŋ lieb constituency paal,pin'lʋg la daa anɛ Nadawli West nɛ Nadowli East constituency ka yʋ'ʋŋ tiak an Daffiama-Bussie-Issa constituency.
english: Therefore, the Nadowli-Kaleo became the new constituency for the initial Nadawli West and the Nadowli East constituency was also changed to Daffiama-Bussie-Issa constituency.

kusaal: pin'ilʋg la nɛ for 1992–2000 (Nadawli South) 2004–2008 (Nadowli East)
english: for initial 1992–2000 (Nadawli South) 2004–2008 (see Nadowli East)

english: Daffiama-Bussie-Issa is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

english: Daffiama-Bussie-Issa is located in the Daffiama-Bussie-Issa District of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

english: Its western neighbour is Nadowli-Kaleo District.

kusaal: Dag Heward-Mills (dʋam dabisir 14 May 1963) anɛ Ghana nid ka lɛn an Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg kpɛɛm bɛ Accra, Ghana.
english: Dag Heward-Mills (born 14 May 1963) is a world renowned healing evangelist, megachurch pastor, best-selling author, and international conference speaker based in Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ pin'il ka lɛn an Bishop tis Lighthouse Group of Churches.
english: He is the founder and presiding Bishop of the United Denominations Originating from the Lighthouse Group of Churches.

kusaal: Onɛ lɛn sʋ'ʋe Anagkazo Bible and Ministry Training Center linɛ bɛ Eastern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He is also the founder of the Anagkazo Bible and Ministry Training Center in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Dag Heward-Mills da dʋ'a nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuob nɛ atan', Sigsaa nwadig, dabpiinɛ anaasi daar bɛ London sʋ'ʋlim, o ma' anɛ Elizabeth ka o saam an Nathaniel Heward-Mills.
english: Dag Heward-Mills was born on May 14, 1963, in London to his parents, Elizabeth and Nathaniel Heward-Mills.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii la ni, Heward-Mills da pin'il Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg kanɛ buon Lighthouse Chapel International.
english: In 1988, Heward-Mills started Lighthouse Chapel International.

kusaal: Heward-Mills da pin'il "Healing Jesus Campaign" lin na niŋ si'em ka o nyaŋi faan'e nidib million kɔbiga yela tis Kristo.
english: Heward-Mills founded the "Healing Jesus Campaign" with the aim of reaching 100 million souls for Christ.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ la ni, Heward-Mills da kilim karinsaam tis First Love Church, linɛ ka o da tiaki li yʋ'ʋr ya'as yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nii lɛbis United Organization of First Love Churches (UO-FLC 190).
english: In 2011, Heward-Mills became pastor of First Love Church, which was later renamed by Heward-Mills in 2020 to the United Organization of First Love Churches (UO-FLC 190).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan', yʋʋm paal nwadig la ni, Dag Heward-Mills da paas nidib kɔbiga banɛ bɛ Africa ka ba yʋ'ʋr yi' pʋʋgin, lʋgir kanɛ da vɛɛns anɛ Reputation Poll International.
english: In January 2023, Dag Heward-Mills was recognized among the 100 most reputable Africans by Reputation Poll International.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinnɛ saŋa la, Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg la da da' di'ema zin'igi bɛ Korle-Gonno, anina ka ba mɛ ba Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg yiiga.
english: By 1991, the church had bought a local cinema hall in Korle-Gonno, where they built their first cathedral.

kusaal: Daimokutate (題目立) anɛ yʋʋma bɛɛ pian'ad tʋasʋg kanɛ ka ba maani li bɛ Yahashira Shrine la ni Kami-fukawa teŋkpɛŋ linɛ kpi'e tempʋʋg kanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Nara.
english: The Daimokutate (題目立) is a recitation show that is performed at Yahashira Shrine in Kami-fukawa village, near the city of Nara.

kusaal: Shinto Temple linɛ bɛ Kamifukawa malʋŋ la anɛ ye ba di'esid dasam banɛ an yʋʋm piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi ka ba paasidi ba wimpʋ'ʋsim pʋʋgin, ka maan maana ba la'asʋg zin'is ni.
english: The Shinto Temple in Kamifukawa has a tradition of accepting a 17-year-old boy as a member of a religious organization that carries out religious ceremonies at the temple.

kusaal: Daimokutate da bɛnɛ Muromachi naar saŋa la.
english: The Daimokutate was performed around the end of the Muromachi period.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni ka Daimokutate da paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists kaal pʋʋgin.
english: Daimokutate was inscribed in 2009 on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists.

kusaal: Dasam banɛ mɔr yʋʋm piinɛ ayɔpɔi (ka dasam ban bʋʋdi ya'a kae, banɛ yʋʋma gaad ala nɛ banɛ yʋʋma pʋ paae ala na maani li) ban a zien bɔn'ɔlim gbiligin kpa'a taaba ka yɛ samurai fʋʋd ka ziid la'as.
english: Young men, aged 17 (If there are not enough boys aged 17 years, boys who are not yet 17 years old or are over 17 years old are also included in the performance) stand in a semi-circle dressed in samurai clothes and carrying bows.

kusaal: Bunkʋdʋg na zi'eni ba tɛnsʋk ka buoni ba yinne yinne ka ba yit tɛnsʋk na ka buol nidib banɛ bɛ sɔlima banɛ bɛ Minamoto nɛ Taira clans tʋŋin la yinne yʋ'ʋr.
english: One by one, they are called to the centre by an old man who reads the name of a character in the tales of the feud between the Minamoto and Taira clans.

kusaal: Li bɛɛ li kɔn' Japan sʋ'ʋlim ka ba maani li ka pʋ nwɛ'ɛd yʋʋma la'adɛ, Daimokutate anɛ zanbin linɛ ka ba baŋid taaba ka mɛ lɛn kɛ ka nɔɔr yinne bɛ tɛŋ banɛ bɛ kʋkʋna ni la.
english: Unique in Japan as a dramatic performance without acting or music, the Daimokutate is an important marker of identity and plays an indispensable role in maintaining solidarity in this mountainous town.

kusaal: Linɛ bɛ sɔlima Hosen Jungo gbana ni yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' (1953) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anu (1955) la ba gʋ' li, amaa banɛ wʋmi li yɛla zu'oe gaad ban mi' si'el la.
english: Documents collected by the folklore specialist Hosen Jungo between 1953 and 1955, have been preserved, but it is likely that the repertoire was much larger.

kusaal: Daimokutate anɛ maan kanɛ an naari tis maan banɛ an ye ba yʋʋm yʋʋma, linɛ ka nidib la mɛŋ da maan, ka yiiga ka li da kpɛn'ɛ gbaʋŋin anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋsnu nɛ pistan' nɛ anaasi (1534) la ni.
english: Daimokutate is the last living example of a tradition of reciting in sanctuary performed by ordinary people, attested for the first time in a document of 1534.

kusaal: Dainichido Bugaku (Japanese: 大日堂舞楽, ka li gbin an: Vairocana Temple Dance nɛ Entertainment) la anɛ yʋʋm yʋʋm malima awai banɛ an yʋʋma nɛ wa'ab, ka ba pʋdi li yinɛ imperial palace ensemble maalʋg "bugaku", ka na'ayidim na kɛŋ kaae Hachimantai, Kazuno District, Akita Prefecture, sankanɛ ka ba maligim maan ba'ar kanɛ an, "Dainichido", yuuma Kobus nii (eighth century), ka pa'an nidib la wa'a.
english: Dainichido Bugaku (Japanese: 大日堂舞楽, meaning: Vairocana Temple Dance and Entertainment) is a yearly set of nine sacred ritual dances and music, named for the imperial palace ensemble performances, "bugaku", and from the palace's ensemble's visit to Hachimantai, Kazuno District, Akita Prefecture, during the reconstruction of the local shrine pavilion, "Dainichido", in the early eighth century, and their teaching of dances to the locals.

kusaal: Wa'a la tiakid nɛ saŋa wʋsa, ka nannanna wa'a nam la anɛ ayɔpɔi, ka ba anɛ Gongen-mai, Koma-mai, Uhen-mai, Tori-mai, Godaison-mai, Kōshō-mai, nɛ Dengaku-mai wa'a nam.
english: The order and number of dances has changed over time, with the current order of seven dances being the Gongen-mai, Koma-mai, Uhen-mai, Tori-mai, Godaison-mai, Kōshō-mai, and Dengaku-mai dances.

kusaal: Wa'a la mor yʋʋma tusir nɛ Kobustan' 1300-year history (Nara period), ba da basi li ka li paae yʋʋma pisyuobu (sixty years) yʋʋm Kɔbis piiga nɛ anii saŋa la (eighteenth century), wa'a la sieba nan bɛ zina nwa ka ba maani li yʋʋm yiiga nwadig dabisa ayi' ni bɛugʋn ma'ae zaam bɛ tembanɛ an Osato, Azukisawa, Nagamine, nɛ Taniuchi, Hachimantai.
english: The dances have a 1300-year history (Nara period), and though interrupted for nearly sixty years in the late eighteenth century, the dances, some of which may include children or masks, are still practiced on January second from sunrise to noon in shrines throughout communities in Osato, Azukisawa, Nagamine, and Taniuchi, including Hachimantai.

kusaal: Yamaji Kōzō saŋa Dainichido Bugaku da pin'ilnɛ Nara saŋa nɛ li nya'aŋ(CE 710 to 794) nɛ Heian periods tɛnsʋk (CE 794 to 1185), teŋ la da sʋŋ Shinto temple la (li da pin'ili yinɛ Emperor Shōmu (CE 701 – 756)).
english: Yamaji Kōzō dates Dainichido Bugaku as arising during and after the Nara (CE 710 to 794) and mid-Heian periods (CE 794 to 1185), after state support of Shinto temple complexes (originally ordered by Emperor Shōmu (CE 701 – 756)) began to decline and court and temple performers took residence in local communities, which then preserved genres such as Dainichido Bugaku as folk arts.

kusaal: La'ad banɛ ka ba mori nwɛ'ɛd la sieba an flute nɛ taiko.
english: Instruments include the flute and taiko.

kusaal: Li da pin'ili lɛbid nya'aŋ ka court nɛ temple wa'a-wa'adib la da gbɛɛndnɛ tɛnkpɛmisin linɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋn gu' li paae zina, ka ba sieba an Dainichido Bugaku.
english: Yamaji Kōzō dates Dainichido Bugaku as arising during and after the Nara (CE 710 to 794) and mid-Heian periods (CE 794 to 1185), after state support of Shinto temple complexes (originally ordered by Emperor Shōmu (CE 701 – 756)) began to decline and court and temple performers took residence in local communities, which then preserved genres such as Dainichido Bugaku as folk arts.

kusaal: Dakoa Newman (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 6 Sigir/Nwadisayɔpɔi 1985) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd kanɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nid New Patriotic Party (NPP).
english: Dakoa Newman (born 6 June 1985) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: o da naae Wesley Girls Senior High School, bɛ Cape Coast la.
english: She completed Wesley Girls Senior High School, Cape Coast.

kusaal: O anɛ chartered Project Management Professional (PMP) nɛ chartered Risk Management Professional (RMP).
english: She is a chartered Project Management Professional (PMP)and a chartered Risk Management Professional (RMP) certified by the Project Management Institute, USA(2017.

kusaal: o lɛn mɔr Bachelor's Degree in Political Science, University of Ghana, Legon nɛ Master's Degree in Program and Project Management yi University of Warwick, bɛ United Kingdom.
english: She also holds a Bachelor's Degree in Political Science from the University of Ghana, Legon and a Master's Degree in Program and Project Management from the University of Warwick, United Kingdom.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa yi nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayuobʋ la ni, June 2020, o da nya' Wabʋg Naa'adɔɔg New Patriotic Party kʋk la bɛ Okaikwei South.
english: In June 2020, she stood for the New Patriotic Party primaries for Okaikwei South.

kusaal: O da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Nwadis piinɛ ayi Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Okaikwei South Constituency.
english: She won the 2020 December parliamentary elections for the Okaikwei South Constituency.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi, kɔbistan nɛ piswai nɛ atan (40,393) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ du'al pisnii nɛ ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (60.82%) ka onɛ ti'al o la, Abraham Kotei Neequaye onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) nid la paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ piinɛ awai (26,019) dinɛ an pistan nɛ awai du'al piinɛ anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (39.18%).
english: She obtained 40,393 votes, representing 60.82% against her closest contender Abraham Kotei Neequaye of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) who had 26,019 votes representing 39.18%.

kusaal: o anɛ Wadmaani tis Okaikwei South Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: She is the member of parliament for the Okaikwei South Constituency.

kusaal: o anɛ Victor Newman onɛ da an pɔlitks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas banɛ da pin'il Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la yinne pʋ'ayua.
english: She is the daughter of Victor Newman who was also a politician and founding member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ Akropong ka o lɛɛ yi Osu.
english: She was born on 6 June 1985 into a Christian family and hails from Akropong and Osu.

kusaal: Project Management Institute, bɛ USA la da tis o kasɛtta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2017).
english: She is a chartered Project Management Professional (PMP)and a chartered Risk Management Professional (RMP) certified by the Project Management Institute, USA(2017.

kusaal: Newman da diya ka bas onɛ da zin'i kʋk la zug Arthur Ahmed nɛ Nana Fredua.
english: Newman defeated incumbent member of parliament Arthur Ahmed and Nana Fredua by getting 440 votes, whilst the two others got 327 votes and 27 votes respectively.

kusaal: O anɛ Victor Newman onɛ da an Gaana pɔlitks nwɛ'ɛd la pʋ'ayua.
english: She is the daughter of Ghanaian politician Victor Newman.

kusaal: Damango Constituency anɛ constituency kanɛ mɔr sɔ' ka o zi'e di nɔba zug bɛ Parliament of Ghana.
english: Damango is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Damango constituency bɛnɛ West Gonja District linɛ bɛ Savannah Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The Damango constituency is located in the West Gonja District of the Savannah Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk bɛnɛ West Gonja District linɛ bɛ Savannah Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: The seat is located entirely within the West Gonja District of the Savannah Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Dan Abdul-latif (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 1 Yʋʋmpaal/Nwadisayi 1970) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Dan Abdul-latif (born 1 January 1970) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O bɛ Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni zi'eni tisi Ablekuma Central Constituency bɛɛ Ablekuma Central Municipal District bɛ Greater Accra Region, Ghana.
english: He is a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ablekuma Central Constituency in the Ablekuma Central Municipal District in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Tamale bɛ Northern region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Tamale in the Northern region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔnrɛ Degree in Communication Management yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni (2020).
english: He holds Degree in Communication Management (2020).

kusaal: O da anɛ Chief Executive office tis Ysan Cevre Isiklan Dirma Malzemeleri S. T. Ltd.
english: He was the Chief Executive office of Ysan Cevre Isiklan Dirma Malzemeleri S. T. Ltd.

kusaal: Abdul-latif paasnɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress(NDC) ni.
english: Abdul-latif is a member of the National Democratic Congress(NDC).

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwaisa anii la ni (August 2021), o da nya'aya ka di Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la Ablekuma Central Constituency sʋ'ʋlim ka zi'eni o Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Nwadis piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋg la.
english: In August 2021, he contest and won the NDC Parliamentary Primaries at Ablekuma Central Constituency to become the party's candidate for the December 2020 election.

kusaal: O da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Wadmaanib (December 2020) vɔɔtʋg la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ pisnaasi (47,040) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ awai dua'al ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (49.7%) ka onɛ tia'al o ka da pʋn dɛŋim zin'i kʋk la zug la, Ebenezer Gilbert Nii Narh Nartey onɛ bɛ Wabʋg N'adɔɔgin la, New patriotic Party paam vɔɔt Tusa pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ, kɔbisnii nɛ pistan nɛ ayuobʋ (46,836) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ awai dua'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgion (49.5%).
english: He won the December 2020 parliamentary election with 47,040 votes representing 49.7% of the total votes cast, beating his main opponent and incumbent member of parliament Ebenezer Gilbert Nii Narh Nartey of the New patriotic Party who obtained 46,836 votes representing 49.5% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid pian'ad yɛla la (Communication Committee) nɛla'askanɛ gɔsid ya yɛla (House Committee) Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni .
english: He serves as a member of Communication Committee and House Committee respectively in the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Abdul-latif nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi la yʋʋmpaal Nwadig yiiga daar (1 January 1970).
english: Abdul-latif was born on 1 January 1970.

kusaal: Dancing Devils of Corpus Christi zi'ennɛ tis Venezuelan dim buudi malʋŋ kanɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ mi' ka ba maani li Corpus Christi, maani li tiend Kristi bɛllim bɛ Eucharist.
english: Dancing Devils of Corpus Christi refers to a set of popular Venezuelan religious festivals held on Corpus Christi, celebrating the presence of Christ in the Eucharist.

kusaal: Di anɛ tʋʋmkanɛ ka 11 brotherhood nam bɛ regions kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb maan, dinɛ ka nidin nwɛnɛ banɛ gaad tusa anu (5,000), tʋmmi di tʋʋma ka onɛ ka nidib mi' bɛdegʋ an Dancing Devils of Yare.
english: It generally refers to the practices of 11 brotherhoods in various regions, which include more than 5,000 people, among which the best-known is the Dancing Devils of Yare.

kusaal: Ba tʋʋma da nieya ka UNESCO zaŋi ba paas Intangible Cultural Heritage yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) la ni.
english: These manifestations were recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2012.

kusaal: Brotherhood la'asʋgnam la da pin'ilnɛ seventeenth century tensʋk bɛ Aragua nɛ Vargas state pɔɔdin.
english: The brotherhood groups originated in the mid seventeenth century on the Aragua and Vargas state farms.

kusaal: Nwɛnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (1749) la saŋa sa, ka ba da maan Corpus Christi malʋŋ la ka dap, pʋ'ab nɛ biis ɛɛnti yɛɛ ba fuud nwɛnɛ suntaananam nɛ ye ba maal nɔɔr zi'ela banɛ ka ba zi'eli tis Blessed Sacrament.
english: As early as 1749, Corpus Christi was celebrated and men, women and children dressed as devils to fulfill promises made to the Blessed Sacrament.

kusaal: Labasieba banɛ bɛ Yare brotherhoods yɛla, di vɛɛnsa labaya sieba bɛ sɔlima gbaʋŋ Peonía dinɛ gbaʋŋ sɔbidi an Manuel Vicente Romero Garcia la ni, pa'an nyain nɛ bɔɔnlim wa'ad wa'adibi da maali ba mɛŋ Cúa devils yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi saŋa (1870s).
english: Regarding other stories about the Yare brotherhoods are, some references are in the novel Peonía by the writer Manuel Vicente Romero Garcia, describing in a clear and illustrative manner how the dancers were Cúa devils in the 1870s.

kusaal: Ti mɔr la'asʋgnam piinɛ yinne (11) ka nidib mi' ka di an guilds society nam bɛɛ association nam banɛ la'asid yʋʋm-yʋʋmi wa'ad ka zi'el nɔɔr ye ba zun'e Blessed Sacrament.
english: There are 11 groups recognized as guilds, societies or associations which constitute hierarchies to dance annually and make promises to worship the Blessed Sacrament.

kusaal: Din zug,ba da pin'il National Association of Dancing Devils of Corpus Christi ye di nyaŋi ye di mɔr la'asʋgnam kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb na ka ba lieb yinne bɛ la'asʋg yiine pʋʋgin.
english: As a result, the National Association of Dancing Devils of Corpus Christi was created to bring together most of the existing fraternities.

kusaal: Dancing Devils of Yare (Diablos Danzantes del Yare) anɛ yʋ'ʋkanɛ ka ba nɔki tisbuudi malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba maan San Francisco de Yare, dinɛ bɛ state of Miranda, Venezuela, Corpus Christi daar.
english: The Dancing Devils of Yare (Diablos Danzantes del Yare) is the name of a religious festival celebrated in San Francisco de Yare, in the state of Miranda, Venezuela, on the day of Corpus Christi.

kusaal: Sociedades del Santísimo (Societies of the Holiest) an banɛ gɔsid malʋŋ la di'ema.
english: The Sociedades del Santísimo (Societies of the Holiest) are in charge of the celebration.

kusaal: Din pin'il zin'iginsieba anɛ 18th century, ka an brotherhood of the American continent kanɛ yuugi gaadi ba wʋsa.
english: Its origins are traced back to the 18th century, being the oldest brotherhood of the American continent.

kusaal: Corpus Christi wʋsa (Holy Thursday ya'a gaad Alamisdaar nam awai ), ba na maal wa'ab malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba buon ye "Dancing Devils," banɛ yɛɛd fuud banɛ mɔr si'im kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb (ka sieba mɛ yɛɛd fuwiid), ka fuud la mɔr fuudbuudi gʋn gʋni li pʋʋgimn, yʋgʋd banɛ ka di nindaa kae sʋ'ʋm nɛ mɔr la'ad nwɛnɛ dapuudanam, scapular nam, rosary nam nɛ amulet kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb.
english: Every Corpus Christi (nine Thursdays after Holy Thursday), a ritual dance is performed by the so-called "Dancing Devils," who wear colorful garments (commonly all red), layers of stripped fabric, masks of grotesque appearance and also accessories like crosses, scapulars, rosaries and other sorts of amulets.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋsieba bɛɛ tis malʋŋ kaŋa ka di yʋ'ʋr yi din bɛ zin'isi'a, nwɛnɛ Devils of Naiguatá nɛ Devils of Chuao.
english: There are other expressions in this particular festival named according to the location, such as the Devils of Naiguatá and the Devils of Chuao.

kusaal: Malʋŋ kaŋa nii, ba ɛɛnti tien onɛ da pin'ili di la, Saint Francis of Paola nɛ Jesus Christ banɛ bɛ Blessed Sacrament la ni.
english: In this folkloric festival, devotion is given to the patron saint Saint Francis of Paola and to Jesus Christ in the Blessed Sacrament.

kusaal: Nidib pa'al ye Dancing Devils of Corpus Christi yinɛ zin'is kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb na.
english: Different origins have been attributed to the Dancing Devils of Corpus Christi.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a dɔlis labaya banɛ pa'al San Francisco de Yare brotherhood yɛla, yʋma kɔbisnaasi (400) banɛ gaad la win, maan maan kanɛ da zi' suokanɛ ka ba da pin'il Corpus Christi da yɛl ye: "Ligidi bɛɛ yadda niŋidib ya'a kae na zi' Blessed Sacrament giligɛ, ala suntaana kena!
english: According to a story about the San Francisco de Yare brotherhood, 400 years ago, a priest without the means to hold the procession of Corpus Christi said: "If there is no money nor believers to carry the Blessed Sacrament in procession, then the devils come!" After a storm, several devils presented themselves in front of the church.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la pin'innɛ Alaarib daar ka ba ɛɛnti isigi nwɛ' fulías (dinɛ aan ba buudi yʋʋma nwɛ'ɛb buudi) ka ba nwɛ'ɛd, décimas (ba buudi sɛnlʋŋ) ka ba sɛnlim nɛ rosary nam nɛ bʋnnwɛ'ɛdsieba ka ba nwɛ'ɛd nɛ yʋ'ʋŋi na ti sɔb.
english: The celebration starts Wednesday with a wake where fulías (a native music style) are played, décimas (native form of poetry) are recited and rosaries and other prayers are recited until dawn.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ, la'asʋg la na keŋ pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg la tuon ka mass la ya'a naae, ban a nɔk Eucharist la zi'el pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg la za'anɔɔrin ka ba pin'ili zabid ka di pa'al ye suntaana zabid nɛ Winanidib.
english: Later on, the group moves towards the front of the church and when the mass has ended, the Eucharist is placed at the church's entrance and a sort of fight representation begins between the devils and the guardians.

kusaal: Ba ziidnɛ dapuuda kanɛ ka ba nɔki abɛ vaandi maal, rosary, nɛ medallion dinɛ ka Kristo footo bɛ di ni (ka ba tun'e nɔk Kristo biis pʋ'ʋsim footo si'a zi'e di nɔba zug).
english: They carry a cross made out of blessed palm leaves, a rosary, and a medallion with the image of Christ (that can be substituted by another Christian religious image).

kusaal: Saŋkan winla, la'asʋgnam da ɛɛnti maal la'ag banɛ pʋ bɔɔd ied nyɔɔdɛ ye ba paam sʋŋir bɛdegʋ yi gɔmena nɛ asʋ'ʋ-m- mɛŋ nidibin sʋŋi ba tʋʋma ka di keŋ tuon ka mɛ sʋŋ ka nidib baŋi ba tʋʋma yɛla nɛ suoya banɛ ka ba dɔlli tʋm.
english: In contemporary times, groups have organized non-profit associations that access public and private funding to improve their organizational strategies and reach a wider audience.

kusaal: Daniel Kwaku Botwe (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 26 Fulumfug/Nwadisatan' 1958) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd, ba da du'a o nɛ Buriya nya'aŋ nwadis ayi' la li dabisim pisi nɛ ayuobʋ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnυ nɛ anii la ni.
english: Daniel Kwaku Botwe (born February 26, 1958) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaanɛ tis Okere linɛ bɛ ti Gaana Eastern Region sυ'υlυmin la.
english: He was the Member of Parliament of Okere constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ minista kanɛ gɔsid labaya yɛla John Agyekum Kufour saŋa la, ka da lɛn an Regional Reorganization and Development minista n tisi ba sυ'υlυm la, o mɛ da lɛn anɛ Minister for Local Government n gɔsid teŋkpɛmis nam nɔbigir yɛla Nana Akufo-Addo na'am la nɔɔr ayi la ni wυsa.
english: He served as Minister for Information and National Orientation in the John Agyekum Kufour administration and also served as the Minister for Regional Reorganization and Development and the Minister for Local Government, Decentralisation and Rural Development in the Nana Akufo-Addo first and second term of office respectively.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Dan Kwaku Botwe nɛ Buriya nya'aŋ nwadis ayi' la li dabisim pisi nɛ ayuobʋ yυυm tʋsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii la Gaana nwa Eastern Region sυ'υlυmin.
english: Dan Kwaku Botwe was born on February 26, 1958, in Abiriw-Akuapem, located in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da si'iŋi o sakur n Presbyterian Primary sakur la ni n bɛ Mabang linɛ bɛ Ahafo-Ano sυ'υlυm Ashanti Region la.
english: He hails from Abiriw Akuapem He was enrolled at the Presbyterian Primary and Middle Schools at Mabang in the Ahafo-Ano District of the Ashanti Region for his basic education.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ Kumasi Academy naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an GCE Ordinary level, ya'asɛ, o da lɛn tɔlis Achimota Sakur la ni naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an GCE Advanced level yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: He obtained his GCE Ordinary level certificate at Kumasi Academy and his GCE Advanced level certificate in 1977 from Achimota School.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o paam suori tɔlis Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology sakur la ni naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an computer science.
english: He gained admission into the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology to pursue a Bachelor of Science degree in computer science.

kusaal: A-su'oemɛŋ tυυma linɛ yυ'υri buon Danmaud Limited dim da gaŋ o ye o aan ba kpɛɛm n gɔs tυυma la.
english: He was appointed director of Danmaud Limited, a private company in Accra.

kusaal: On da bɛ KNUST, ka ba gaŋ o ye o an gbaυŋ sɔbid n tis National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) lin yi yυυm tυsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ ayi la ni n ti paae yυυm tυsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ atan' la ni.
english: While at KNUST, he was elected as the national secretary of the National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) from 1982 to 1983.

kusaal: Ba da yis o nɛ Gaana ninsieba kadi ba bas Ivory Coast.
english: He was sentenced to exile with other Ghanaians to the Ivory Coast.

kusaal: Dan Botwe da zi'en Wabυg Na'adɔɔg zugu nya'a Okere wadmaanib kυk la yuma tusa yi nɛ anii la ni Brandford Kwame Daniel Adu n da bas la.
english: Dan Botwe contested the parliamentary election in Okere in 2008 after the incumbent, Brandford Kwame Daniel Adu, had decided to step down as the constituency's parliamentarian.

kusaal: Botwe da paam vɔt 11,974 n yi vɔt la kanl wυsa linɛ da an 19,684 la ni, kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da paamnɛ 60.8% vɔt n kpɛn' wadmaanib dɔɔgin la o yiiga saŋa.
english: Dan Botwe obtained 11,974 votes out of the 19,684 total votes cast, representing 60.8% of the vote, to become the new member of parliament.

kusaal: On da an wadmaan la o da tυm tυυm nam hali kon'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb n tis o sυ'ulυm la, ba sieba anɛ , o da sυŋ niŋ-wisigir di'ema dim banɛ yυ'υri buon Dreams FC, a Ghana Premier League dim la, nɛ sieba bɛdigu.
english: He promised his support for Dreams FC, a Ghana Premier League team that plays their home game at Dawu, a town in his constituency.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaig yinne la yuma tusa nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni ka Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Botwe ye o an Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development.
english: In January 2017, President Akufo-Addo named Dan Botwe as the Minister for the newly created Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development.

kusaal: Yυυm tυsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ anu la ni ka Ghana Cocobod dim da nɔk Botwe ye o tυm nɛ ba linɛ an Kɔmpiita tυυma.
english: In 1985, Dan Botwe was employed by the Ghana Cocobod as a computer analyst.

kusaal: O na'am nya'anb la ni da an Provisional National Defence Council pin'ilυg sagianam wada na'am bɛllim la win.
english: His election coincided with the beginning of the military rule led by the Provisional National Defence Council.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o lɛb Gaana tυm nɛ Ghana cocoa board dim li yi yυυm tυsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ anu la ni n ti paae yυυm tυsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ atan' la ni.
english: He later returned to Ghana and worked as a computer analyst at the Ghana cocoa board from 1985 to 1993 before moving into a private business.

kusaal: Botwe da tυm minista kanɛ gɔsid labaya yɛlɛ tυυma la lin da yi yuma tusa yi nɛ ayuobu la ni n ti paae yuma tusa yi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni John Agyekum Kufour saŋa la.
english: From 2006 to 2007 Dan Botwe served as the Minister for Information (Ghana) in the John Agyekum Kufour administration.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris anu la yuma tusa yi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni ka ti Gaana Gɔmina Akufo-Addo gaŋ Dan Botwe ye o paas minista nam bam piina wai la ni.
english: In May 2017, President Nana Akufo-Addo named Dan Botwe as one of 19 ministers who would form his cabinet.

kusaal: Dan Kwaku Botwe di pu'a mɔr biis atan'.
english: Dan Kwaku Botwe is married with three children.

kusaal: Onɛ Kristo biig Presby karimdɔɔg la ni.
english: He is a Christian with the Presbyterian denomination.

kusaal: Daniel Kwesi Ashiamah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Buem Constituency bɛ Volta Region la ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: Daniel Kwesi Ashiamah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Buem Constituency in the Volta Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Daniel Nsala Wakpal (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 15 Dɔnwalig/Nwadisanaa 1975) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress ni.
english: Daniel Nsala Wakpal (born 15 March 1975) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Kpandai Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Northern Region, Ghana la.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Kpandai Constituency, in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Wakpal yinɛ Saboba.
english: Wakpal hails from Saboba.

kusaal: O mɔnrɛ Master of Arts in Local Government Administration and Organisation.
english: He holds a Master of Arts in Local Government Administration and Organisation.

kusaal: Daniel Obinim (o dʋ'am dabisir an Mɔtul nwadig, dabpisi nɛ awai daar, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi ni), ka ba lɛn buon o ye Angel Obinim, anɛ karensaam tis Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg kanɛ buon International God's Way Church, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Daniel Obinim (born 29 August 1977), also known as Angel Obinim, is a minister of the International God's Way Church in Ghana.

kusaal: Jon Benjamin, onɛ zie British dim nɔba zug Ghana tɛŋin, da la'ad o bɛ Twitter.
english: Jon Benjamin, the British High Commissioner to Ghana, ridiculed him for these claims over Twitter.

kusaal: Ghana nid kanɛ da an Minister of Gender, Children, and Social Protection ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Nana Oye Lithur mɛŋ da duoe dɔlis suoya lin na niŋ si'em ka ba gban'a o, o da kɛŋi fabili tis Ghana Police Service Domestic Violence and Victims' Support Unit (DOVVSU).
english: Ghana's Minister of Gender, Children, and Social Protection Nana Oye Lithur herself led a campaign for his arrest, by lodging a complaint to the Ghana Police Service Domestic Violence and Victims' Support Unit (DOVVSU).

kusaal: Obinim anɛ Kristo nid ka o pʋ'a a yʋ'ʋm-yʋ'ʋm kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Florence Obinim.
english: Obinim is a Christian and married to Ghanaian gospel musician, Florence Obinim.

kusaal: Nwa' da kɛ ka lʋgir kanɛ ka ba buon Amnesty International ka ba bɛ Ghana la yɛt ye o tu'ug wada ka li nar ye ba tɛɛg o tubirt.
