english: In 2014, Obinim was seen on television stepping on the belly of a woman in a "deliverance" This led the Amnesty International in Ghana to call for his prosecution for assault.

kusaal: Daniel Obinim yi yiŋ saŋa bɛdigʋ yis o nɔɔr pian'ad si'eba.
english: Daniel Obinim has made several public controversial declarations.

kusaal: O da pian'a ye o anɛ Wina'am maliak, ka linzug ka o karindɔɔg dim nɔk Maliaki paas o yʋ'ʋr la pʋʋgin ka yʋ'ʋn buon o ye "Maliak Obinim".
english: He declared he was an angel of God, which led to the name "Angel Obinim" given to him by his church.

kusaal: Ba da gban'a o.
english: He was subsequently arrested.

kusaal: Daniel Ohene Darko (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 18 Sigir/Nwadisayɔpɔi 1961) ka o an Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd onɛ an Wadmaani tis Upper Denkyira West Constituency.
english: Daniel Ohene Darko (born 18 June 1961) is a Ghanaian politician who currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Upper Denkyira West Constituency.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Daniel Ohene Darko nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne Nwadisa ayuobʋ dabpiinɛ anii daar (18 June 1961) ka o yi Ayanfuri bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Daniel Ohene Darko was born on 18 June 1961 and hails from Ayanfuri in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da sɔbi o Senior Secondary Certificate Examination (SSCE) nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1977).
english: He obtained his Senior Secondary Certificate Examination (SSCE) in 1977.

kusaal: O da maali o Ordinary Level yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1977) ka maali Advanced Level yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan la ni (1983).
english: He also obtained his Ordinary Level in 1977 and Advanced Level in 1983.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maal o Bachelor of Laws (Law) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinnew (2001) keŋ paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan la ni (2003), Barrister of Law yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan la ni (2003) ka maal Executive Master of Business Administration (EMBA) – Marketing yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011).
english: He proceeded in having his Bachelor of Laws (Law) from 2001 to 2003, Barrister of Law in 2003 and Executive Master of Business Administration(EMBA) – Marketing in 2011.

kusaal: Daniel Ohene Darko da tʋmnɛ Associate of a Law Firm "Kwasi Blay and Associates" Ghana.
english: Daniel Ohene Darko worked as an Associate of a Law Firm "Kwasi Blay and Associates" in Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn tʋm tis Amicus Legal Consult (Partner) bɛ Ghana.
english: He again worked at Amicus Legal Consult (Partner) in Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ Managing Partner tis Betta Law Consult.
english: He is the Managing Partner of Betta Law Consult.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋn anɛ Wadmaani tis Upper Denkyira West Constituency bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana, Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: He is currently working as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Upper Denkyira West Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Daniel Ohene Darko da nya' ka di NDC Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la Upper Denkyira West Constituency bɛ Central Region, Ghana la.
english: Daniel Ohene Darko contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Upper Denkyira West Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di Upper Denkyira West Constituency Wadmaan kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la, Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg National Democratic Congress nɔba zug nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anii, kɔbisaasi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (18,446) dinɛ an pisnu dua'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.7%) ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi nii la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni ka bas Samuel Nsowah-Djan onɛ bɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party ni ka paam vɔɔt Tusa piinɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbiswai nɛ pisi nɛ anu (17,925) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ awai dua'ali atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (49.3%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He won the Upper Denkyira West Constituency parliamentary seat in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress with 18,446 votes making 50.7% of the total votes cast to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana against Samuel Nsowah-Djan of the New Patriotic Party who had 17,925 votes making 49.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Daniel Ohene Darko paas Youth, Sports and Culture Committee la ni, ka lɛn paas Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee.
english: Daniel Ohene Darko is a member of the Youth, Sports and Culture Committee and also a member of the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee.

kusaal: Daniel Ohene Darko anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Daniel Ohene Darko is a Christian.

kusaal: Daniel Okyem Aboagye (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔɔpɔi nɛ, 31 December 1973 ka o maal ka'alim yuʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan nwadisa awai la dabpisi nɛ atan daar, (23 September 2023) da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, zi'eni tis Bantama Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim la, wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Daniel Okyem Aboagye (31 December 1973 – 23 September 2023) was a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Bantama Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Okyem Aboagye nɛ Atwima Boko bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la on yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔɔpɔi nɛ, 31 December 1973.
english: Okyem Aboagye was born in Atwima Boko in the Ashanti Region of Ghana on 31 December 1973.

kusaal: Aboagye da keŋnɛ University of Ghana zin'ikanɛ ka o da di'e o bachelor's degree in Business Administration.
english: Aboagye studied at the University of Ghana where he received a bachelor's degree in Business Administration.

kusaal: O da naae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2002) ka di'e MBA nɛ MIS in Accounting yi Troy University, Alabama, USA.
english: He graduated in 2002 with an MBA and MIS in Accounting from Troy University, Alabama, USA.

kusaal: Okyem Aboagye da di'e kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan (2003) la ni ka yʋ'ʋn an public accountant bɛ Certified Public Accountant of USA.
english: Okyem Aboagye was certified in 2003 as a public accountant at the Certified Public Accountant of USA.

kusaal: Aboagye da pin'ili tʋʋma ka anɛ branch manager tis SINAPI ABA TRUST yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998).
english: Aboagye started his career as the branch manager of SINAPI ABA TRUST in 1998.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da lieb project manager tis Opportunity International yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan (2003) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2006) la ni.
english: He later became the project manager of Opportunity International in 2003–2006.

kusaal: Okyem Aboagye wda an financial controller tis Globe Union bɛ US la ka lɛn a CEO tis MGI Microfinance yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii ( 2008) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012).
english: Okyem Aboagye was the financial controller of Globe Union in the US and CEO of MGI Microfinance in 2008–2012.

kusaal: O da anɛ CEO tis 2M Express Transport Services.
english: He was the CEO of 2M Express Transport Services.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015) o da nya'aya ka di wabʋg na'adɔɔg, NPP wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Bantama bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: In 2015 he contested and won the NPP parliamentary primaries for Bantama (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di wadmaan kʋk layʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: He won this parliamentary seat during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadisa ayuobʋ la ni (June 2020), O da nya' wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party wadmaan gaansʋg vɔɔtʋg la ka pʋ dii amaa ka Francis Asenso-Boakye, onɛ yʋ'ʋn an wadmaan tis Bantama constituency.
english: In June 2020, he lost the bid to represent the New Patriotic Party after losing in the primaries to Francis Asenso-Boakye, who is now the member of parliament for the Bantama (Ghana parliament constituency).

kusaal: Aboagye da paas Finance and Economic Committee, Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana la ni.
english: Aboagye served as a member of the Finance and Economic Committee in the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Okyem Aboagye da kpinɛ Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital yuʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan nwadisa awai la dabpisi nɛ atan daar, (23 September 2023), o da anɛ yʋma pisnaasi nɛ awai (49).
english: Okyem Aboagye died at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital on 23 September 2023, at the age of 49.

kusaal: Aboagye da mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis.
english: Aboagye was married with children.

kusaal: Ba buud si'eba busid til duta la ni ka li wa'alim paad 16 m (52 ft).
english: Some cultivars also form shoots up to 16 m (52 ft) in length.

kusaal: Daasi'erɛ tɛŋin la nidibi da tɔlisi li ka li paae Caribbean dim nɛ South America 2500 BCE.
english: The cultigen was most likely spread by local people to the Caribbean and South America by 2500 BCE.

kusaal: Ba vɛɛn ya gɔs ka ye dankal kanɛ ka ti mi' zina la, ba da nyɛ linɛ bɛ tampilɛma ni bɛ Chilca Canyon, linɛ bɛ south-central zone Peru tɛŋin, ka li pa'al ye li yuugi paae 8080 ± 170 BC.
english: The oldest radiocarbon dating remains of the sweet potato known today were discovered in caves from the Chilca Canyon, in the south-central zone of Peru, and yield an age of 8080 ± 170 BC.

kusaal: Ba vɛɛns nɛ ka ye da'asi'erɛ Polynesia dim da ansig nɛ vaand la mɔri kɛn Polynesia tɛŋin na, banɛ da kɛn South America ka lɛbid la, anina ka li widigi yi Polynesia paae Easter Island, Hawaii nɛ New Zealand.
english: A common hypothesis is that a vine cutting was brought to central Polynesia by Polynesians who had traveled to South America and back, and spread from there across Polynesia to Easter Island, Hawaii and New Zealand.

kusaal: Ba vɛɛnsi nyɛ ka Polynesian nidibi kuod dankal si'a la nɛ American dim ninkʋka din la wan bi'ela wʋʋ Zenú, bama anɛ nimbanɛ bɛ Colombia tɛŋin zina, ka li pa'al ye Polynesia dim tɔ'ɔn da kɛŋ South America ka paam dankal anina yi Europe dim la nu'usin.
english: Genetic similarities have been found between Polynesian peoples and indigenous Americans including the Zenú, a people inhabiting the Pacific coast of present-day Colombia, indicating that Polynesians may have visited South America and taken sweet potatoes prior to European contact.

kusaal: Adelaar nɛ Muysken da nyɛ ka yʋ'ʋr la pa'al ye Central Andes dim nɛ Polynesia dim tɔ'ɔn da si'al taaba zin'ig si'a.
english: Adelaar and Muysken assert that the similarity in the word for sweet potato is near proof of either incidental or sporadic contact between the Central Andes and Polynesia.

kusaal: Li da paae Fujian banɛ bɛ China la nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnu nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi ni (1594) saŋa yi Luzon, ba bʋnbʋtta da san'am la zug.
english: The plant was introduced to Fujian in about 1594 from Luzon, in response to a major crop failure.

kusaal: Dankal kuob da nyɛ kpɛmisigi yi onɛ da an Governor Chin Hsüeh-tseng (Jin Xuezeng) san'an.
english: Its cultivation was encouraged by the Governor Chin Hsüeh-tseng (Jin Xuezeng).

kusaal: Dankal da paae Ryukyu Kingdom, zin'ig kanɛ ka ba buon Okinawa, ka li bɛ Japan zina la, yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ saŋa (1600s) da yinɛ Portuguese ni na.
english: Sweet potatoes were also introduced to the Ryukyu Kingdom, present-day Okinawa, Japan, in the early 1600s by the Portuguese.

kusaal: Li da paae Korea nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi ni (1764).
english: The crop was introduced to Korea in 1764.

kusaal: Baa Hebrew dimi mɛ buon dankal ye batata (בטטה‎) ba buudi pian'adin la, li ka'a ye ba wʋm nɛ yi Taíno dim buolig nii.
english: Though the sweet potato is also called batata (בטטה) in Hebrew, this is not a direct loan of the Taíno word.

kusaal: Amaa, Spanish dimi buon patata la ka ba da ti'aki li lɛbis Arabic ka buon ye batata (بطاطا‎), bɔzugɔ, ba pʋ mɔr sɔb bil /p/ ka li bɛ Arabic nii, lin ka ba da buon dankal ye batata ḥilwa (بطاطا حلوة‎); ka li pʋn anɛ ('dankal').
english: Rather, the Spanish patata was loaned into Arabic as batata (بطاطا‎), owing to the lack of a /p/ sound in Arabic, while the sweet potato was called batata ḥilwa (بطاطا حلوة‎); literally ('sweet potato').

kusaal: Arabic dimi buon batata la Hebrew dim da zamisi li ka buon ka li anɛ dankal ma'a yʋ'ʋr, bɔzugɔ Hebrew dim da mɔr yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba pʋn tis potato sa ye, תפוח אדמה‎ (tapuakh adama, ka li gbin an 'dunia apple'; ka French pian'ad ni an pomme de terre).
english: The Arabic batata was loaned into Hebrew as designating the sweet potato only, as Hebrew had its own word for the common potato, תפוח אדמה (tapuakh adama, literally 'earth apple'; compare French pomme de terre).

kusaal: Mexico tɛŋin, Bolivia, Peru, Chile, Central America, nɛ Philippines tɛɛnsin, ba buon dankal ye camote (ka si'eba sɔbidi li kamote bɛ Philippines pian'adin), ba nyɛ yʋ'ʋr nwa' yinɛ Nahuatl buudi pian'ak camotli.
english: In Mexico, Bolivia, Peru, Chile, Central America, and the Philippines, the sweet potato is known as camote (alternatively spelled kamote in the Philippines), derived from the Nahuatl word camotli.

kusaal: Peru nɛ Bolivia, ban buoni li si'em anɛ apichu, amaa ba bɛ buudi buudi ka si'eba an khumara, kumar (Ayacucho Quechua), nɛ kumara (Bolivian Quechua), li wan nɛ Polynesian dimi buon ye kumara nɛ yʋ'ʋr banɛ paas (kumala, umala, ʻuala, etc.), linɛ kɛ ka vɛɛnsidib ye li yinɛ pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact ni.
english: In Peru and Bolivia, the general word in Quechua for the sweet potato is apichu, but there are variants used such as khumara, kumar (Ayacucho Quechua), and kumara (Bolivian Quechua), strikingly similar to the Polynesian name kumara and its regional Oceanic cognates (kumala, umala, ʻuala, etc.), which has led some scholars to suspect an instance of pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact.

kusaal: Australia tɛŋin, ban kuod dankal si'a anɛ abija 'Beauregard', linɛ da yi nɛ Louisiana Agricultural Experiment Station ni yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinnɛ ni (1981).
english: In Australia, about 90% of production is devoted to the orange cultivar 'Beauregard', which was originally developed by the Louisiana Agricultural Experiment Station in 1981.

kusaal: Ba buon ye kumara (yit nɛ Māori pian'ad ni, kūmara), ban kuod sɔ' saŋa nwa anɛ bʋnzi'an la 'Owairaka', amaa, ba mɛ kuod orange ('Beauregard'), gold, purple nɛ si'eba.
english: Known as kumara (from the Māori language kūmara), the most common cultivar now is the red 'Owairaka', but orange ('Beauregard'), gold, purple and other cultivars are also grown.

kusaal: Li nɔbigid sʋŋa zin'ig banɛ ka tʋʋlig zɛnmis wʋʋ 24 °C (75 °F), ka nintaŋ mɛ bɛ ka tʋʋlig bɛ yʋ'ʋŋyʋ'ʋŋ.
english: It grows best at an average temperature of 24 °C (75 °F), with abundant sunshine and warm nights.

kusaal: Boniatos pʋ malis ka mɔr kuom wan wʋʋ dankal si'ebaa, amaa ba malisim la bɛɛ li kɔn' nɛ onɛ mɔr orange color la.
english: Boniatos are not as sweet and moist as other sweet potatoes, but their consistency and delicate flavor are different from the common orange-colored sweet potato.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi ni (2020), dunia wʋsa dankal kuob da anɛ 89 million tonnes, ka tɛŋ kanɛ da kua gaad o taaba an China da mɔr nɛ pisnu nɛ anu, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (55%) dankal kanɛ bɛ dunia wʋsa.
english: In 2020, global production of sweet potatoes was 89 million tonnes, led by China with 55% of the world total (table).

kusaal: Banɛ da dɔl nya'aŋ da anɛ Malawi, Tanzania, nɛ Nigeria.
english: Secondary producers were Malawi, Tanzania, and Nigeria.

kusaal: Dankal ban'as anɛ Sweet potato chlorotic stunt virus (Crinivirus).
english: Sweet potato suffers from Sweet potato chlorotic stunt virus (a Crinivirus).

kusaal: Li ya'a la'as nɛ ban'as si'ebanam, Untiveros et al., 2007 da vɛɛnsi nyɛ ka SPCSV maligim mɔr paŋ hali san'amidi ba.
english: In synergy with other any of a large number of other viruses, Untiveros et al., 2007 finds SPCSV produces an even more severe symptomology.

kusaal: I. batatas namisid nɛ Phytophthoras ban'as ka ba si'eba an P. carotovorum, P. odoriferum, nɛ P. wasabiae.
english: I. batatas suffers from several Phytophthoras including P. carotovorum, P. odoriferum, and P. wasabiae.

kusaal: Dankal kanɛ ka ba dug (ka ba sɛn'ɛ) mɔr kuom 76%, 21% carbohydrates, 2% protein, nɛ kpaam finn).
english: Cooked sweet potato (baked in skin) is 76% water, 21% carbohydrates, 2% protein, and contains negligible fat (table).

kusaal: Ka la'abama mɛ bɛ bi'ela (10–19% DV) an B vitamins nɛ potassium.
english: It is a moderate source (10–19% DV) of some B vitamins and potassium.

kusaal: Maltose pʋ zuoe li pʋʋginɛ, amaa fʋ ya'a tʋligi li bugum ni, li na kɛ ka maltose kanɛ bɛ pʋʋgin la nɔbig an wʋʋ piiga paae pisi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (10% nɛ 20% tɛnsʋk).
english: Maltose content is very low, but baking can increase the maltose content from between 10% and 20%.

kusaal: Vɛɛnsig kanɛ ka United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization vɛɛns la pa'al ye dankal anɛ dikanɛ ka fʋ na nyaŋi sɛ' fʋ pɔɔgin, ka li nyɛ'ɛd wan wʋʋ 70,000 kcal hectare pʋʋgin (28,000/acre) / day.
english: According to a study by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, sweet potatoes are the most efficient staple food to grow in terms of farmland, yielding approximately 290,000 kilojoules per hectare (28,000 kcal/acre) daily.

kusaal: Amukeke (linɛ ka ba sɛ dɛlig ka li kʋdʋg) nɛ inginyo (linɛ ka ba bu'ari dɛlig ka li kʋdʋg) anɛ diibi tis ninbanɛ bɛ yadatiʋŋ-ya'nya'aŋ Uganda tɛŋin.
english: Amukeke (sun-dried slices of root) and inginyo (sun-dried crushed root) are a staple food for people in northeastern Uganda.

kusaal: Emukaru (earth-baked root) anɛ linɛ ka ba dit saŋa wʋsa lin nɛ tea bɛɛ suma zɛɛnd.
english: Emukaru (earth-baked root) is eaten as a snack anytime and is mostly served with tea or with peanut sauce.

kusaal: Ba mɛ mɔri li maan diib bɛdigʋ bɛ South Sudan.
english: Similar uses are also found in South Sudan.

kusaal: Ethiopia tɛŋin, dankal buudi kanɛ ka ba kuod anina tita'am anɛ banɛ ka ba pak la an sabilik, ka nyɛ'ɛlim la kala an wan wʋʋ cream ka ba buoni li bitatis bɛɛ mitatis.
english: In Ethiopia, the commonly found cultivars are black-skinned, cream-fleshed and called bitatis or mitatis.

kusaal: Indian sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ ka ba buon Tamil Nadu ni, ba buoni li ye sakkara valli kilangu.
english: In the Indian state of Tamil Nadu, it is known as sakkara valli kilangu.

kusaal: Pakistan tɛŋin, ba buon dankal ye shakarqandi ka ba mɛ dʋgʋdi li nɛ zɛnma'asa zɛn'ɛd ka lɛn an ni'im zɛn'ɛd (nua ni'im, pɛ'ɛg ni'im, bɛɛ naaf ni'im).
english: In Pakistan and northwestern India, sweet potato is known as shakarqandi and is cooked as a vegetable dish and also with meat dishes (chicken, mutton or beef).

kusaal: Shōchū, anɛ Japanese dim diib kanɛ ka ba mɔr mui kanɛ mi'igi maan, ba mɛ tɔ'ɔn nɔk Dankal li maal, ka ba buon lin ye imo-jōchū.
english: Shōchū, a Japanese spirit normally made from the fermentation of rice, can also be made from sweet potato, in which case it is called imo-jōchū.

kusaal: Pizza kuosig zin'is ni wan wʋʋ Pizza Hut nɛ Domino banɛ bɛ Korea tɛŋin mɔr dankal li pa'an zugin.
english: Pizza restaurants such as Pizza Hut and Domino's in Korea are using sweet potatoes as a popular topping.

kusaal: Malaysia nɛ Singapore, ba nwaasid dankal nɛ ban'alig ka dʋgi li nɛ taro nɛ kube kuom (santan) ka dikanɛ ka di kilimid la yʋ'ʋr an bubur cha cha.
english: In Malaysia and Singapore, sweet potato is often cut into small cubes and cooked with taro and coconut milk (santan) to make a sweet dessert called bubur cha cha.

kusaal: Indonesia tɛŋin, ba buon dankal ye ubi jalar (lit: "nyɛ'ɛlim kanɛ tɛɛnd") bɛɛ ubi giŋa, ka ba kiimid nɛ la'asi'eba dit nɛ kodu ki'imi, tempeh, tahu, breadfruit, bɛɛ cassava.
english: In Indonesia, sweet potatoes are locally known as ubi jalar (lit: "spreading tuber") or simply ubi and are frequently fried with batter and served as snacks with spicy condiments, along with other kinds of fritters such as fried bananas, tempeh, tahu, breadfruit, or cassava.

kusaal: Vietnamese cuisine tɛŋin, ba buon dankal ye khoai lang ka ba dʋgʋd nɛ la'amalisa wan wʋʋ corn syrup, siind, sikir, bɛɛ molasses.
english: In Vietnamese cuisine sweet potatoes are known as khoai lang and they are commonly cooked with a sweetener such as corn syrup, honey, sugar, or molasses.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi ni (1947), black rot (Ceratocystis fimbriata) da yi kūmara na bɛ Auckland tɛŋin baba ka nɔbig bɛdigʋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nam saŋa la (1950s).
english: In 1947, black rot (Ceratocystis fimbriata) appeared in kūmara around Auckland and increased in severity through the 1950s.

kusaal: Ba da nɔki li tis tɛŋ la kpɛɛmnam, ka li da kɛ ka ba di'e piini kanɛ buon Bledisloe Cup yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ atan' ni (2013).
english: They gave the strain to the nation, earning them the Bledisloe Cup in 2013.

kusaal: kūmara buudi la mɔr abʋtan' ka ba kuosid New Zealand tɛŋin: 'Owairaka Red' ("red"), 'Toka Toka Gold' ("gold"), nɛ 'Beauregard' ("orange").
english: There are three main cultivars of kūmara sold in New Zealand: 'Owairaka Red' ("red"), 'Toka Toka Gold' ("gold"), and 'Beauregard' ("orange").

kusaal: Tɛŋ la kuod dankal wan wʋʋ 24,000 metric tons yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin, ka li tita'am, piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (97%) ba kuodi bɛnɛ Northland Region.
english: The country grows around 24,000 metric tons of kūmara annually, with nearly all of it (97%) grown in the Northland Region.

kusaal: Nidib banɛ an Urapmin buudi bɛ Papua New Guinea, buon dankal ye taro (ka Urap pian'ad ni an ima) ka lɛn mɔr dankal yinnɛ (Urap: wan) anɛ dibanɛ sʋŋid hali, ka ban buon 'diib' nɛ sɔb si'a Urap pian'ad ni la la'as nɛ yʋda ayi' nwa.
english: Among the Urapmin people of Papua New Guinea, taro (known in Urap as ima) and the sweet potato (Urap: wan) are the main sources of sustenance, and in fact the word for 'food' in Urap is a compound of these two words.

kusaal: Veneto (northeast Italy) sʋ'ʋlim, ba buon dankal ye patata mericana, bɛ Venetian buudi pian'ad ni (patata americana bɛ Italian buudi pian'ad ni, ka li gbin an "America dankal"), ka ba kuodi li zin'is wʋsa bɛ yadagɔbʋg, region la ni;.
english: In the Veneto (northeast Italy), sweet potato is known as patata mericana in the Venetian language (patata americana in Italian, meaning "American potato"), and it is cultivated above all in the southern area of the region;.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ ka ba di'emid di'emkanɛ ka ba buon All Souls' Day, bɛ Catalonia (northeastern Spain) la, dikanɛ ka ba dit tita'am anɛ dankal sɛn'ɛda nɛ chestnuts, panellets nɛ damalisiŋ.
english: On the evening of All Souls' Day, in Catalonia (northeastern Spain) it is traditional to serve roasted sweet potato and chestnuts, panellets and sweet wine.

kusaal: Ba buon tigir nwa' ye La Castanyada.
english: The occasion is called La Castanyada.

kusaal: Dulce de batata anɛ dikanɛ ka Argentine, Paraguayan nɛ Uruguayan dit, ka li anɛ dankal ka ba nɔki maal.
english: Dulce de batata is a traditional Argentine, Paraguayan and Uruguayan dessert, which is made of sweet potatoes.

kusaal: Ba gɔsid o yʋʋm bɛn ni bɛ USDA hardiness Zone 9, ba nɔbigid tɔ'ɔtɔ' ka bʋsid vaandi yadigid tɔ'ɔtɔ'.
english: Grown as an annual in zones up to USDA hardiness Zone 9, they grow rapidly and spread quickly.

kusaal: Di bi'ela, starchy, sweet-tasting tuberous rootsmɔri maan nya'a diib (root vegetable).
english: Its sizeable, starchy, sweet-tasting tuberous roots are used as a root vegetable, which is a staple food in parts of the world.

kusaal: Di anɛ di kanɛ an staple food ka nidib nɔŋi li pamm dunia ni.
english: Its sizeable, starchy, sweet-tasting tuberous roots are used as a root vegetable, which is a staple food in parts of the world.

kusaal: Banɛ tʋmi li tʋʋma la (Cultivars of the sweet potato) zamis ban na niŋi ka sua li ka li kpɛm mɔr niŋgbiŋ paalig nɛ sin'imnam bɛdigʋ.
english: Cultivars of the sweet potato have been bred to bear tubers with flesh and skin of various colors.

kusaal: Dankal pin'il yinɛ tropical regions bɛ South America ka nananna di yʋ'ʋm bɛ Ecuador.
english: The sweet potato is native to the tropical regions of South America in modern Ecuador.

kusaal: Daʋg kakɛ zanl vaang la wa'alim anɛ wan wʋʋ 13 paae 51 centimetres (5 to 20 inches).
english: The leaf stalk is 13 to 51 centimetres (5 to 20 inches) long.

kusaal: Vaand la kpikpɛmis labisim pʋ zɛnmiya, 5 to 13 cm (2 to 5 in), li anɛ wan wʋʋ sʋsʋnf, siyanini bɛɛ gɛl nɛ, ka an gbilig bɛɛ lammirɛ bɛɛ lin on mɔr labisim atan', li kpikpɛmis la tɔ'ɔn an mummi, bʋ'asibʋ'as bɛɛ li pʋdipʋda abʋtan' bɛɛ li tɔ'ɔn pʋdi paae abʋyɔpɔi.
english: The leaf stalk is 13 to 51 centimetres (5 to 20 inches) long.

kusaal: Pak kanɛ lus puum la anɛ bi'ela ka wa'am, ka pʋlʋm ka an (wan wʋʋ ayɔpɔi bɛn) 10 to 15 millimetres (3⁄8 to 5⁄8 in) wa'alim pʋʋgin, ka mɔr zuob baanlig.
english: The small sepals are elongated and tapering to a point and spiky and (rarely only 7) 10 to 15 millimetres (3⁄8 to 5⁄8 in) long, usually finely haired or ciliate.

kusaal: Li bʋʋlim la kala si'eba anɛ beige, pi'elig, wiig, pink, violet, dɔnbʋʋlim, orange, bɛɛ purple.
english: Its flesh ranges from beige through white, red, pink, violet, yellow, orange, and purple.

kusaal: Dankal si'eba banɛ ka ba nyɛ'ɛlim bʋʋlim la an pi'elig bɛɛ waans dɔnbʋʋlim la pʋ malis ka mɔr kuom wan wʋʋ banɛ an wiig, pink bɛɛ orange la.
english: Its flesh ranges from beige through white, red, pink, violet, yellow, orange, and purple.

kusaal: Dankal li mɔr bʋn si'a li ni anɛ li DNA ka li yinɛ Agrobacterium, sensu lato; lin wanni Rhizobium rhizogenes buudi), ka ba da nyɛ ka bʋnbʋtir la an ala.
english: The genome of cultivated sweet potatoes contains sequences of DNA from Agrobacterium (sensu lato; specifically, one related to Rhizobium rhizogenes), with genes actively expressed by the plants.

kusaal: Europeans dimi da nan pʋ kɛn Americas tɛŋin la, dankal da bɛ Polynesia tɛŋin, ka ba kʋ'ʋt nɛ vaandi sɛɛd ka ka'a biilifɔ.
english: Before the arrival of Europeans to the Americas, sweet potato was grown in Polynesia, generally spread by vine cuttings rather than by seeds.

kusaal: Dankal da bɛ Cook Islands nɛ 1210–1400 CE.
english: Sweet potato has been radiocarbon-dated in the Cook Islands to 1210–1400 CE.

kusaal: Dutch buudi nid nɛ onɛ mi' Amerindian buudi pian'ad, Willem Adelaar nɛ Pieter Muysken ye dankal yʋ'ʋr la yinɛ Polynesian nɛ South America buudi pian'ad ni na: Proto-Polynesian *kumala (compare Rapa Nui kumara, Hawaiian ʻuala, Māori kūmara) tɔ'ɔn an yinnɛ nɛ Quechua bɛɛ Aymara k'umar ~ k'umara.
english: The Dutch linguists and specialists in Amerindian languages Willem Adelaar and Pieter Muysken have suggested that the word for sweet potato is shared by Polynesian languages and languages of South America: Proto-Polynesian *kumala (compare Rapa Nui kumara, Hawaiian ʻuala, Māori kūmara) may be connected with Quechua and Aymara k'umar ~ k'umara.

kusaal: Dankal da paae Europe dɔl nɛ nidibi da ti'as taaba la'ad saŋsi'a la, fʋ ya'a gɔs gbaŋ kanɛ ka Elinor Fettiplace sɔb ka pʋd Receipt Book la ni, linɛ ka ba da sɔbi li na'asaalin England tɛŋin yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi la ni (1604).
english: It is recorded, for example, in Elinor Fettiplace's Receipt Book, compiled in England in 1604.

kusaal: Dankal da paae Philippines dim tɛŋin nɛ Spanish colonial period (1521–1898) yi Manila galleons, nɛ dunia bʋnbʋta si'eba.
english: Sweet potatoes were introduced to the Philippines during the Spanish colonial period (1521–1898) via the Manila galleons, along with other New World crops.

kusaal: Aoki Konyō da sʋŋi kkɛ ka dankal yadig Japan tɛŋin, ka Tokugawa bakufu mɛ da sʋŋ, sɔb gbana, ka mɛ da tɔlis o vɛɛnsig kanɛ ka o da vɛɛns Japanese buudi pian'ad ni dankal yel la tis nidib ka li kɛ ka ba ku'a li bɛdigʋ.
english: Aoki Konyō helped popularize the cultivation of the sweet potato in Japan, and the Tokugawa bakufu sponsored, published, and disseminated a vernacular Japanese translation of his research monograph on sweet potatoes to encourage their growth more broadly.

kusaal: Ba da sɛɛd dankal nɛ Shōgun Tokugawa Yoshimune lɔmbɔn'ɔg ni.
english: Sweet potatoes were planted in Shōgun Tokugawa Yoshimune's private garden.

kusaal: Kang P'il-ri nɛ Yi Kwang-ryŏ da gban'a gba'ar ye ba tʋm dankal tʋʋma bɛ Seoul yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ ni (1766), mɔr nɛ ya'am kanɛ ka ba da zamisi yi Japanese dim ni yi Tongnae da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi ni (1764).
english: Kang P'il-ri and Yi Kwang-ryŏ embarked on a project to grow sweet potatoes in Seoul in 1766, using the knowledge of Japanese cultivators they learned in Tongnae starting in 1764.

kusaal: Baa la'anɛ lin pʋ kpi'em la, ba buon dankal si'eba nɛ "busa" bɛ North America zin'ig si'eba, dankal bɛɛ li kɔn' nɛ busa mɛŋir (Dioscorea), linɛ yadigid tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔs, ka paas nɛ monocot mɔɔd buudi Dioscoreaceae ni.
english: Although the soft, orange sweet potato is often called a "yam" in parts of North America, the sweet potato is distinct from the botanical yam (Dioscorea), which has a cosmopolitan distribution, and belongs to the monocot family Dioscoreaceae.

kusaal: Mɔɔg yinnɛ mɛn, ka ba buon oca (Oxalis tuberosa, ka li vaand mɛ labis), ka ba buon ye "busa" dunia zin'ig si'eba ni.
english: A different crop plant, the oca (Oxalis tuberosa, a species of wood sorrel), is called a "yam" in many parts of the world.

kusaal: Europe nidib banɛ da lɛm dankal yiiga da anɛ banɛ da paas Christopher Columbus ka ba tu suori bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnaasi nɛ piswai nɛ ayi ni (1492).
english: The first Europeans to taste sweet potatoes were members of Christopher Columbus's expedition in 1492.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka vɛɛnsidib nyɛ ka nidib kuodi li ka lɛɛ pʋdi li ba buudi yʋda, amaa yʋ'ʋr kanɛ da yʋʋg anɛ Taíno kudumin dimi da pʋd ye batata la.
english: Later explorers found many cultivars under an assortment of local names, but the name which stayed was the indigenous Taíno name of batata.

kusaal: Spanish dim da la'as nwa' nɛ Quechua dim yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba da pʋd dankal, ye papa, ani ka ba da buon dankal ye patata.
english: The Spanish combined this with the Quechua word for potato, papa, to create the word patata for the common potato.

kusaal: Luga si'eba nɛ vɛɛnvɛɛnsidib si'eba bɔɔd ye ba sɔm yʋ'ʋr la la'as mumi li na'asaalin la ye—sweetpotato—ka ka'a ba pʋdigi li ayiŋa, ka li nyaŋi pa'al ye li bɛ li kɔn' nɛ potatoes nɛ busa ka li mɛ kɛ ka nidib da nɔki li maal ye potato.
english: Some organizations and researchers advocate for the styling of the name as one word—sweetpotato—instead of two, to emphasize the plant's genetic uniqueness from both common potatoes and yams and to avoid confusion of it being classified as a type of common potato.

kusaal: Argentina, Colombia, Venezuela, Puerto Rico, nɛ Dominican Republic tɛɛnsin, ba buon dankal ye batata.
english: In Argentina, Colombia, Venezuela, Puerto Rico, and the Dominican Republic, the sweet potato is called batata.

kusaal: Brazil tɛŋin, ba buon dankal ye batata doce.
english: In Brazil, the sweet potato is called batata doce.

kusaal: New Zealand tɛŋin, Māori buudi da nyɛ'ɛd fʋomafʋoma ka ba pa'ad nɛ bʋʋlim la an pi'elig, linɛ ka ba gɔs ka ye li yinɛ European dim banɛ da tuud suor la ni na.
english: In New Zealand, the Māori varieties bore elongated tubers with white skin and a whitish flesh, which points to pre-European cross-Pacific travel.

kusaal: Tiim kanɛ ka ba mɔri puusidi yisid mɔɔd banɛ paas dankal pʋʋgin anɛ DCPA, ka ba mɛ lɛn buon ye Dacthal.
english: A commonly used herbicide to rid the soil of any unwelcome plants that may interfere with growth is DCPA, also known as Dacthal.

kusaal: Dankal da yi paalʋ na an diib bʋn bɛnɛ Pacific Ocean, South India, Uganda nɛ Africa tɛŋ si'eba ni.
english: Sweet potatoes became common as a food crop in the islands of the Pacific Ocean, South India, Uganda and other African countries.

kusaal: Ban did dankal si'em bɛ United States anɛ wan wʋʋ 1.5–2 kg (3.3–4.4 lb) yʋʋm pʋʋgin, kɛŋ paae 13 kg (29 lb) yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisi ni (1920).
english: The annual per capita consumption of sweet potatoes in the United States is only about 1.5–2 kg (3+1⁄2–4+1⁄2 lb), down from 13 kg (29 lb) in 1920.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a nɔk 100 gram, dankal sɛn'ɛda tisid 90 calories, ka mɔr (20% bɛɛ li gaad ala, Daily Value, DV) mɔr vitamin A (120% DV), vitamin C (24% DV), manganese (24% DV), nɛ vitamin B6 (20% DV).
english: In a 100-gram reference amount, baked sweet potato provides 359 kilojoules (86 kilocalories) of food energy, and rich content (20% or more of the Daily Value, DV) of vitamin A (120% DV), vitamin C (24% DV), manganese (24% DV), and vitamin B6 (20% DV).

kusaal: Sikir kanɛ bɛ pʋʋgin la wʋʋ pisnu paae piswai, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50% and 90% ) an sikir kanɛ ka ba buon sucrose.
english: Between 50% and 90% of the sugar content is sucrose.

kusaal: Amukeke anɛ bɛʋgin diib, ka ba dit nɛ sʋnma zɛɛnd.
english: Amukeke (sun-dried slices of root) and inginyo (sun-dried crushed root) are a staple food for people in northeastern Uganda.

kusaal: Inginyo anɛ linɛ ka ba la'asid nɛ bankyi zɔ'ɔm nɛ punsa maan atapa.
english: Inginyo is mixed with cassava flour and tamarind to make atapa.

kusaal: Kenya tɛŋin, Rhoda Nungo onɛ bɛ economics department Ministry of Agriculture sɔb gbaŋ kanɛ pa'an dankal ka ba mɔri maan disi'eba.
english: In Kenya, Rhoda Nungo of the home economics department of the Ministry of Agriculture has written a guide to using sweet potatoes in modern recipes.

kusaal: Nwa' pʋʋgin pa'anɛ linɛ ka ba tu'a ka li kʋdʋg nɛ linɛ ka ba nɛɛm ka li kilim zɔ'ɔm ka ba nɔki li ka li di'e sikir nɔbir ka ba mɔri sɛn'ɛd diib wan wʋʋ cake, chapatis, mandazis, bodobodo, buns nɛ cookies.
english: This includes uses both in the mashed form and as flour from the dried tubers to replace part of the wheat flour and sugar in baked products such as cakes, chapatis, mandazis, bread, buns and cookies.

kusaal: Yʋʋm banɛ gaad la, banɛ ka ba nyɛ'ɛlim kala an orange da yina, ka banɛ da yisi li na an Haramaya University ka ban da an sʋm ka sikir pʋ zuoe pʋʋginɛ ka mɛ mɔr vitamin A bɛdigʋ.
english: In recent years, better yielding orange-fleshed cultivars were released for cultivation by Haramaya University as a less sugary sweet potato with higher vitamin A content.

kusaal: South Africa tɛŋin, ba pʋ dit dankal ma'a nɛ, ba lɛɛ paasidi li nɛ disi'eba ni ka ba yinnɛ an soetpatats.
english: In South Africa, sweet potatoes are often eaten as a side dish such as soetpatats.

kusaal: Japan tɛŋin, ban maani li si'em ka li dɔl wʋʋ Korea dim maalig la, ban buon ye yaki-imo (dankal sɛn'ɛda), ba mɔr nɛ linɛ ka bʋʋlim an dɔnbʋʋlim la "Japanese dankal" bɛɛ onɛ an purple la "Okinawan dankal", ka ba buon ye beni-imo.
english: In Japan, a dish similar to the Korean preparation is called yaki-imo (roasted sweet potato), which typically uses either the yellow-fleshed "Japanese sweet potato" or the purple-fleshed "Okinawan sweet potato", which is known as beni-imo.

kusaal: Fujian cuisine nɛ Taiwanese cuisine ni, ba dʋgʋd dankal nɛ mui maan kɔɔkɔ.
english: In Fujian cuisine and Taiwanese cuisine, sweet potato is often cooked with rice to make congee.

kusaal: Dankal kanɛ ka ba waae nɛ dinɛ ka ba dɛlig ka li kʋdʋg anɛ diib hali tis Liancheng County.
english: Steamed and dried sweet potato is a specialty of Liancheng County.

kusaal: Nwa' nɛ dankal diib bɛdigʋ bɛ bento (Pe̍h-ōe-jī: piān-tong) diib kuosʋg zin'is ni.
english: They, as well as dishes featuring the sweet potato root, are commonly found at bento (Pe̍h-ōe-jī: piān-tong) restaurants.

kusaal: Northeastern Chinese cuisine ni, ba nwaasid dankal nɛ bi'elbi'el ka kiimid, ka nyaan kwa'ae niŋ zɛn'ɛd kanɛ pʋn dʋgʋd pʋʋgin.
english: In northeastern Chinese cuisine, sweet potatoes are often cut into chunks and fried, before being drenched into a pan of boiling syrup.

kusaal: India zin'ig si'eba ni, ba nwaasid dankal ma'asa nɛ dɛligid ka nɛɛmid ka li kilid dankal zɔ'ɔm; ka ba nɔk wheat zɔ'ɔm gɛndig ka sɛn'ɛ li ka li kilim chapatti (bodobodo).
english: In some parts of India, fresh sweet potato is chipped, dried and then ground into flour; this is then mixed with wheat flour and baked into chapatti (bread).

kusaal: Sri Lanka tɛŋin, ba buon dankal ye bathala, ka ba mɔri maan bɛʋgʋn diib (ba ɔnbid dankal dʋgʋda nɛ kube kuom) bɛɛ ba dʋgi li di kɔn' di nɛ mui.
english: In Sri Lanka, it is called bathala, and tubers are used mainly for breakfast (boiled sweet potato is commonly served with sambal or grated coconut) or as a supplementary curry dish for rice.

kusaal: Dankal nyɛ'ɛlim la, ka Dhivehi dim buon ye kattala, ba mɔri li ka li an dikpɛŋi bɛ Maldives.
english: The tubers of this plant, known as kattala in Dhivehi, have been used in the traditional diet of the Maldives.

kusaal: Japan tɛŋin, ba kuod dankal (ka ba buon satsuma-imo) nɛ busa (ka ba buon daijo bɛɛ beni-imo).
english: In Japan, both sweet potatoes (called satsuma-imo) and true purple yams (called daijo) are grown.

kusaal: Daigaku-imo (ja:大学芋) anɛ ba ya'a sɛn'ɛ dankal ka paas sikir bɛɛ bʋnmalisiŋ si'a.
english: Daigaku-imo (ja:大学芋) is a baked and caramel-syruped sweet potato dessert.

kusaal: Ka ba buoni li ye "sweet potato" (ja:スイートポテト) Japan tɛŋin, li anɛ cake kanɛ ka ba nɔk Dankali nɛɛm maal.
english: What is commonly called "sweet potato" (ja:スイートポテト) in Japan is a cake made by baking mashed sweet potatoes.

kusaal: Imo-gohan, ba ya'a dʋg dankal nɛ mui, anɛ dinɛ ka di yʋ'ʋr yi Guangdong, Taiwan nɛ Japan tɛɛns ni.
english: Imo-gohan, sweet potato cooked with rice, is popular in Guangdong, Taiwan and Japan.

kusaal: Ba diti li nimono bɛɛ nitsuke pʋʋg, dʋgʋ li ka paas soy sauce, mirin nɛ dashi.
english: It is also served in nimono or nitsuke, boiled and typically flavored with soy sauce, mirin and dashi.

kusaal: Korean cuisine ni, ba mɔr dankal titabid la maan dangmyeon (cellophane taliya).
english: In Korean cuisine, sweet potato starch is used to produce dangmyeon (cellophane noodles).

kusaal: Korean dim dikanɛ ka di yʋ'ʋr yi ka ba buon, goguma-mattang, ka ba lɛn buon ye Korean candied dankal la, ba kiimid dankal la nɛ nwaasi ba bɛdabɛda ka nɔk sikiri bʋlʋgi li.
english: A popular Korean side dish or snack, goguma-mattang, also known as Korean candied sweet potato, is made by deep-frying sweet potatoes that were cut into big chunks and coating them with caramelized sugar.

kusaal: Philippines tɛŋin, dankal (ka ba buudi pian'ad ni an camote bɛɛ kamote) anɛ dikpɛŋ hali tis banɛ bɛ tɛnkpɛmisin la.
english: In the Philippines, sweet potatoes (locally known as camote or kamote) are an important food crop in rural areas.

kusaal: Vanpɔla nɛ buspaala la (ka ba buon ye talbos ng kamote bɛɛ camote tops) anɛ diibi tisi ba ka ba sɛɛdi niŋid salad nii gɛndig nɛ zɛɛnd kanɛ ka ba nɔk zimi maal.
english: Young leaves and shoots (locally known as talbos ng kamote or camote tops) are eaten fresh in salads with shrimp paste (bagoong alamang) or fish sauce.

kusaal: Ba si'eba dʋgʋdi li kuomi'isim ni nɛ zɛn'ɛd kanɛ ka ba nɔk bɛŋa maal ka diti li nɛ ziŋki'ima (ka ba buon ye adobong talbos ng kamote), bɛɛ ba di nɛ bʋnlinɛ ka ba buon sinigang.
english: They can be cooked in vinegar and soy sauce and served with fried fish (a dish known as adobong talbos ng kamote), or with recipes such as sinigang.

kusaal: Kuom kanɛ ka ba siligidi yit camote tops ni la kala anɛ purple, ka ba gɛndigidi li nɛ lemon kuom nud.
english: The stew obtained from boiling camote tops is purple-colored, and is often mixed with lemon as juice.

kusaal: Ba mɔr dankal li maan halo-halo linɛ ka ba buon ginatan, lin anɛ ba dʋg dankal la nɛ kube kuom pʋʋgin nɛ sikir kanɛ ka ba gɛndig si'elnam wan wʋʋ rootcrops, sago, jackfruit, nɛ bilu-bilo (glutinous rice balls).
english: Sweet potatoes are also used in a variant of halo-halo called ginatan, where they are cooked in coconut milk and sugar and mixed with a variety of rootcrops, sago, jackfruit, and bilu-bilo (glutinous rice balls).

kusaal: Kʋkʋna banɛ bɛ West Papua ni la, dankal anɛ ba dikpɛŋ.
english: In the mountainous regions of West Papua, sweet potatoes are the staple food among the natives there.

kusaal: Dankal vanpɔla la ka ba mɔri maan biis diib, li kaskas anɛ Southeast Asia nɛ East Asia.
english: Young sweet potato leaves are also used as baby food, particularly in Southeast Asia and East Asia.

kusaal: Dankal kanɛ ka ba bʋlʋg sikir mɛ anɛ dikanɛ ka ba mɔri dit nɛ disi'eba ka ba maan nɛ brown sugar, marshmallows, maple syrup, molasses, orange juice, marron glacé, bɛɛ la'abanɛ malis si'eba.
english: Candied sweet potatoes are a side dish consisting mainly of sweet potatoes prepared with brown sugar, marshmallows, maple syrup, molasses, orange juice, marron glacé, or other sweet ingredients.

kusaal: Dankal casserole anɛ dikanɛ ka ba nɔk dankal kanɛ ka ba tu'a nɛ casserole maal, ka ba bʋlʋg nɛ sikir bɛɛ pecan.
english: Sweet potato casserole is a side dish of mashed sweet potatoes in a casserole dish, topped with a brown sugar and pecan topping.

kusaal: Tɛŋ banɛ gɔs ka dankal an tɛŋ la zɛnvaadi hali anɛ Alabama, Louisiana, nɛ North Carolina.
english: Sweet potatoes are recognized as the state vegetable of Alabama, Louisiana, and North Carolina.

kusaal: Dankal ki'ima la buudi si'a anɛ Okinawan sweet potato haupia pie, linɛ ka ba nɔk dankal kanɛ an purple la maal.
english: Another variation on the typical sweet potato pie is the Okinawan sweet potato haupia pie, which is made with purple sweet potatoes.

kusaal: Ba da pin'il dankal kiimig nɛ nineteenth century sa bɛ United States.
english: The fried sweet potatoes tradition dates to the early nineteenth century in the United States.

kusaal: Ba buon John Bettencourt Avila ye "dankal kpaadib yaab" bɛ North America.
english: John Bettencourt Avila, an Azorean immigrant to California, is known as the "father of the sweet potato industry" in North America. Avila planted sweet potatoes from the Azores on a small 20 acre plot of land near Merced in 1888, and eventually spread their cultivation throughout the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys.

kusaal: Māori dim buudi da kua ba kɔ'ɔbkɔ'ɔb bʋnbaalig, banɛ pa'adi an dɔnbʋʋlim, ka ba zɛm wʋʋ nu'ubil nɛ ka ba buon kūmara (ka li yʋda si'eba an taputini, taroamahoe, pehu, hutihuti, and rekamaroa) banɛ ka ba da mɔri yi Polynesia tɛŋin na.
english: Māori grew several varieties of small, yellow-skinned, finger-sized kūmara (with names including taputini, taroamahoe, pehu, hutihuti, and rekamaroa) that they had brought with them from east Polynesia.

kusaal: Lin da wa'ae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ ni la (2021), banɛ gɔsid kʋdʋmin la'ad yela da vɛɛns ya ka ye dankal da pʋ nyaŋi maal titua bɛ New Zealand south linɛ bɛ Christchurch sʋ'ʋlim la ba tɛŋ la mɔr waad la zug, ka li da kɛ ka Māori buudi nidib la an (ban nɛ Moriori dim banɛ bɛ Chatham Islands) nimbanɛ bɛ Polynesian sʋ'ʋlim an tɔn'ɔsnam.
english: Prior to 2021, archaeologists believed that the sweet potato failed to flourish in New Zealand south of Christchurch due to the colder climate, forcing Māori in those latitudes to become (along with the Moriori of the Chatham Islands) the only Polynesian people who subsisted solely on hunting and gathering.

kusaal: Amaa, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ (2021) vɛɛnsig kanɛ ka ba da vɛɛnsi yi la'abanɛ ka ba nyɛ bʋnbɔk si'a ni ka li kpie Dunedin, an wʋʋ 250 km (160 mi) ya'dagɔbʋg, da pa'al ye ba da kuod dankal ka su'adi li 15th century, ka li kuob nyaan da lɛb nya'aŋ ka ba ye li anɛ waad yela.
english: However, a 2021 analysis of material excavated from a site near Dunedin, some 250 km (160 mi) further south, revealed that sweet potatoes were grown and stored there during the 15th century, before the industry was disrupted by factors speculated to be due to the Little Ice Age.

kusaal: Māori dim buon dankal dʋgʋda ye kūmara ka ba ɛɛti sɛn'ɛ li bɛ hāngī (sɛn'ɛb dɔɔg).
english: Māori traditionally cooked kūmara in a hāngī (earth oven).

kusaal: Dankal ka ba buon Kūmara la bɛ New Zealand tɛŋin saŋa wʋsa yʋʋm pʋʋgin, ka anina ka ba di'e potatoes nɔbir.
english: Kūmara are widely available throughout New Zealand year-round, where they are a popular alternative to potatoes.

kusaal: Kūmara paas dibanɛ ka ba sɛn'ɛd pʋʋgin, ka ba diti li nɛ cream kanɛ pʋ Malisa nɛ nanzʋ'ʋs.
english: Kūmara are often included in roast meals, and served with sour cream and sweet chili sauce.

kusaal: Ba diti li nɛ zɛnma'asa wan wʋʋ potatoes nɛ yʋ'a ka ba maan si'em la, ka ba maani li nɛ la'abanɛ na paas ka zɛn'ɛd malis.
english: They are served alongside such vegetables as potatoes and pumpkin and as such, are generally prepared in a savory manner.

kusaal: Spain tɛŋin, ba buon dankal ye boniato.
english: In Spain, sweet potato is called boniato.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan' ni (2023), Spain da anɛ tɛŋ kanɛ kua dankal li gaadi o taaba bɛ Europe sʋ'ʋlim.
english: As of 2023 Spain is the largest sweet potato producer in Europe.

kusaal: Peru sʋ'ʋlim, ba buon dankal ye camote ka ba dit nɛ zimi diib.
english: In Peru, sweet potatoes are called camote and are frequently served alongside ceviche.

kusaal: South America tɛŋin, ba la'asid dankal wiig la kuom nɛ lime juice mɔri maan dye maan fuud.
english: In South America, the juice of red sweet potatoes is combined with lime juice to make a dye for cloth.

kusaal: Ba kuodi ba bɛ ya'nya'aŋ nɛ yadagɔbʋg kʋkʋna ni ka tuud saa wakad (Sigir/Mɔraug).
english: They are cultivated in the eastern and southern lower highlands and harvested during the rainy season (June/July).

kusaal: Ka yʋʋm wʋsa saa makir bɛn an wʋʋ 750–1,000 mm (30–39 in) zin'ig ban ka li bɔɔd, ka li nɔbigir saŋa la mɛ an wan wʋʋ 500 mm (20 in).
english: Annual rainfalls of 750–1,000 mm (30–39 in) are considered most suitable, with a minimum of 500 mm (20 in) in the growing season.

kusaal: Bʋnbʋtir la pʋ bɔɔd kuonɔŋɔ, li ya'a pin'in nyɛ'ɛb la, wan wʋʋ dabpisnu paae dabpisyuobʋ saŋa (50–60 days) ka sɛɛb nya'aŋ, li mɛ pʋ lɛn bɔɔd kuom alasaa, li ya'a ka'a ala nyɛ'ɛlim la na pʋn'ɔe ka san'am nya'a la pɛbisim kae la zug.
english: The crop is sensitive to drought at the tuber initiation stage 50–60 days after planting, and it is not tolerant to waterlogging, which may cause tuber rots and reduce the growth of storage roots if aeration is poor.

kusaal: Ba nɔkid vaand bɛdigʋ pa'ani li zugin, ka dʋgi li hour nam bɛdigʋ ka li kɛ ka tʋʋlig la nyaŋi nwɛ'ɛ dʋg la'abanɛ bɛ pʋʋgin la.
english: The top of the pile is then insulated with more leaves, creating a pressure of heat and steam inside which cooks all food within the pile after several hours.

kusaal: Yoruba pian'ʋk "dashiki" yinɛ Hausa pian'ʋk kanɛ an "dan ciki," ka di gbin an fuug la ni.
english: The word "dashiki" comes from dàńṣíkí, a Yoruba loanword from the Hausa dan ciki, literally meaning 'shirt' or 'inner garment' (as compared to the outer garment, babariga).

kusaal: "Dashiki" yinɛ Yoruba buudi pian'ad ni, zin'kanɛ ka ba da mɔri pa'an fuwɔk kanɛ ka ba da maali bɛ West Africa ka di an dap sieba nu'ug tʋʋm.
english: The word "dashiki" comes from dàńṣíkí, a Yoruba loanword from the Hausa dan ciki, literally meaning 'shirt' or 'inner garment' (as compared to the outer garment, babariga).

kusaal: Fukaŋa kɛtnɛ ka onɛ yɛɛ li la niŋgbina ma'ae sankanɛ ka tʋʋlʋg bɛ Africa.
english: It is frequently worn with a brimless kufi cap (which is worn in Islamic communities in Africa and the African diaspora) and pants.

kusaal: Dashiki da anɛ tʋʋma fuug saŋa bi'ela.
english: Dashiki formally appeared in the Webster's New World Dictionary, 1st College Edition of 1970/72.

kusaal: David Adakudugu (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii nwadis piiga la dab pisi nɛ atan daar (October 23, 1968) – ka o kpi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai nwadisa awai la dabpiinɛ awai daar (September 19, 2019) o da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Sixth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Tempane (New) Constituency bɛ Upper East Region la Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: David Adakudugu (October 23, 1968 – September 19, 2019) was a Ghanaian politician and member of the Sixth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Tempane (New) Constituency in the Upper East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Adakudugu da anɛ Kristo biig ka kenni Assemblies of God Church.
english: Adakudugu was a Christian (Assemblies of God Church).

kusaal: O pʋ'a da anɛ Akanvariva Lydia Lamisi ka ba mɔr biisa anu.
english: He was married to Akanvariva Lydia Lamisi with five children.

kusaal: O yinɛ Basyonde, tenkanɛ bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Basyonde, a town in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Methodist University, Accra ka da di'e o bachelor's degree in marketing kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: He entered Methodist University, Accra and obtained his bachelor's degree in marketing.

kusaal: Adakudugu da paasnɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) nidib ni.
english: Adakudugu was a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012), o da zi'eni nya' Tempane (New) kʋk la Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, NDC nɔba zug sixth parliament of the fourth republic ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Tempane (New) seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: Managing Director, Noryini Commercial Limited, Kasoa (2005–2009).
english: Managing Director, Noryini Commercial Limited, Kasoa (2005–2009)

kusaal: District Chief Executive, Garu-Tempane Director (April, 2009–January, 2013).
english: District Chief Executive, Garu-Tempane Director (April, 2009–January, 2013)

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adakudugu nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ nwadis piiga la dabpisi nɛ atan daar (October 23, 1968).
english: Adakudugu was born on October 23, 1968.

kusaal: David Kwame Dontoh (dʋ'am dabisir, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi, 1964) ka ba buon o ye Uncle David, "Ghanaman" nɛ "Kofi Abranteɛ" (Kofi Gentleman), anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an sini maan ka tʋm TV ni, ka paasi maal sini di'ema bɛdigʋ ni.
english: David Kwame Dontoh (born 1964) and affectionately called Uncle David, "Ghanaman" and "Kofi Abranteɛ" (Kofi Gentleman), is a veteran Ghanaian actor and television personality who has starred in numerous local and international films, drama, theatre and other stage productions.

kusaal: O yiiga sini da anɛ The Way To Shame, sini giŋ kanɛ an minute ayɔpɔi ka one da gɔsi li yela an Alex Bannerman ka li paas o di'ema zamisig pʋʋgin.
english: His first NAFTI film was The Way To Shame, a short seven minute stage production which was directed by Alex Bannerman as part of his formal assessment in drama production.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ, Dontoh sini di'ema baŋir da kɛn tuon on da paas di'em kanɛ buon Gus : The Theatre Cat, sini giŋ kanɛ dɔlis yʋʋma kanɛ ka T. S. Eliot da yʋʋm la.
english: Subsequently, Dontoh's acting potential became more noticed when he played the lead role in Gus: The Theatre Cat, a short stage adaptation of a poem by T. S. Eliot.

kusaal: One da gɔs di'ema nwa yela anɛ George Andoh Wilson one da yit Wilson Acting Academy fame.
english: The play was directed by George Andoh Wilson of Wilson Acting Academy fame.

kusaal: One an kpɛɛm kanɛ ka ba buon ye board chairman tis Ghana National Film Authority (NFA) linɛ ka ba da pin'ili li bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai, naar nwadig ni la (December 2019).
english: He is currently the board chairman of the newly formed Ghana National Film Authority (NFA) which was inaugurated in December 2019.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu (2015), o da pin'il o DAS Professional Acting Institute ka li bɛ Zenith University College, Ghana.
english: In 2015, he launched his DAS Professional Acting Institute at the Zenith University College, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a David Dontoh bɛnɛ Gyegyeano, tɛnkpɛŋ kanɛ bɛ Cape Coast linɛ bɛ Central Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: David Dontoh was born at Gyegyeano, a suburb of Cape Coast in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O ma - Elizabeth Victoria Ackon Green (Efua Beduwa) – da anɛ one kuosid zimi.
english: His mother - Elizabeth Victoria Ackon Green (Efua Beduwa) - was a fish monger.

kusaal: David Dontoh da pin'ili kɛŋ sakurnam bɛdigʋ bɛ Cape Coast, Winneba, nɛ Abakrampa linɛ bɛ Central Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: David Dontoh's primary education was at various schools in Cape Coast, Winneba, and Abakrampa in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ secondary school bɛnɛ Apam Senior High School.
english: He had his secondary education at Apam Senior High School.

kusaal: O da zamis nɛ science, English nɛ poetry.
english: He studied science, English and poetry.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka nidib baŋ o bɛdigʋ dɔlisid o sini maalig pʋʋgin, on nɛ one da maan sini saŋkan la - Grace Omaboe (Maame Dokono) one da paas Obra fame ni – da kpɛmis o ye o ieem tʋʋma gbaŋi bɛ sini maalig pʋʋgin, on da di ya'an piini kanɛ an Best Actor Award bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii ne anaasi ni la (1984).
english: In later years when his popularity began to soar on the acting scene, his co-actor at the time - Grace Omaboe (Maame Dokono) of Obra fame - encouraged him to obtain formal qualifications in theatre and drama after he won the Best Actor Award in 1984.

kusaal: Dontoh da zamis sini di'ema maaligi bɛnɛ School of Performing Arts University of Ghana lin da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu (1985) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988), anina ka o zamiskpan da an sini di'ema gbana sɔb ka di'e o tʋʋma gbaŋ kanɛ buon diploma.
english: Dontoh therefore studied Drama and Theatre at the School of Performing Arts University of Ghana between 1985 and 1988, where he majored in playwriting and obtained a diploma.

kusaal: · Ghana Peace Award (2017)
english: Ghana Peace Award (2017)

kusaal: O anɛ one tʋm bɛdigʋ sini tʋʋma nɛ li maalig ni, li kaskas anɛ kʋdʋmin sa la di'ema zin'is Ghana sʋ'ʋlim yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ piswai saŋa la (80s and 90s).
english: He has been very influential in the development of television and drama, especially during the golden age of theatre in Ghana in the 80s and 90s.

kusaal: O da pin'il sini di'ema nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii (1980) on da wʋm ka National Film and Television Institute (NAFTI) labaya ni ye ba bɔɔd banɛ na maan sini ye ba zamisi ba la.
english: He took up acting in 1980 after seeing a National Film and Television Institute (NAFTI) newspaper advert inviting potential actors to come forward for training in stage and film acting.

kusaal: Bannerman one da kɛn sakur NAFTI sankan la ka si'al Dontoh o mugusu ye o an gaad di'ema la tuon, bɔzugɔ, ninkanɛ da nar ye o di'em di'emkan la da pʋ kɛnaa.
english: Bannerman who was a student of NAFTI at the time had chanced upon Dontoh and persuaded him to play the lead role, as the intended person had not showed up during shooting.

kusaal: Banɛ da gɔs sini kan la, li kaskas anɛ Mike Hagan, da baŋ ye Dontoh baŋir di'emkan pʋʋgin ka zaŋi yel Alex Bannerman, one da an dasaŋ la.
english: The film's assessment panel, especially Mike Hagan, recognised Dontoh's potential in theatre and drama and highlighted this to the young Alex Bannerman.

kusaal: National Film Authority an banɛ gɔsid banɛ maan sininam yela.
english: The National Film Authority provides general oversight and quality control for the film industry.

kusaal: Lʋgir kaŋa bɛnɛ Bureau of Ghana Languages tʋʋma zin'ig pʋʋgin, ka tʋmtʋmnib la si'eba nan kae.
english: The skeleton organisation is currently housed within the premises of the Bureau of Ghana Languages and yet to be fully staffed.

kusaal: O da maal sini si'eba on da nam bɛ secondary school la.
english: He performed in several amateur productions during his secondary school days.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ ka nidib mi' o yee o anɛ onɛ da gaad GHComedy tuoni zabi tis ba ka li sʋŋ ka Ghana dim zi'en tituaa ba galima sini tʋʋma la ni.
english: He is known for leading the movement GHComedy, that fought to gain visibility and acceptance for upcoming Ghanaian Stand-up comedians.

kusaal: David Oscar yʋ'ʋm da nɔki o galima sini tʋʋma la nɛ nɛ nimuaa, ka Kenna kilim raggae yʋm-yʋm yʋ'ʋs.O da la'asi tʋm nɛ Ghana nidib banɛ k aba ʋ'ʋr yi hali, ba yʋda anɛɛ Afriyie Wutah ka dunia wʋsa pʋʋgin yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anaasi(2014) BEFFTA Awards (UK) Winner onɛ da di bɛ pian'adin, Lyric Da Nkechi.
english: He has collaborated with other popular Ghanaian stars, namely, Afriyie Wutah and internationally with the 2014 BEFFTA Awards (UK) Winner for spoken word, Lyric Da Nkechi.

kusaal: Ba du'a David nɛ Koforidua dinɛ bɛ yadaten Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la (Eastern Region of Ghana), o du'adib da anɛ Mr Oscar Yaovi Adukpo nɛ Mrs Faustina Mary Asamoah Adukpo.
english: David was born at Koforidua in the Eastern Region of Ghana to Mr Oscar Yaovi Adukpo and Mrs Faustina Mary Asamoah Adukpo.

kusaal: O da mɔr pitib atan', ayi an biribis banɛ an Isaac Oscar Ohene Adukpo nɛ Bright Nana Osei Oscar Adukpo nɛ bipuŋ ayinne onɛ an Felicia Mawuena Oscar.
english: He has 3 siblings; two brothers, Isaac Oscar Ohene Adukpo and Bright Nana Osei Oscar Adukpo and a sister Felicia Mawuena Oscar.

kusaal: David da sin'iŋi o sakur la nɛ biilimin sa ka ta kenna sɔb bɛ Freeman Methodist sakurin dinɛ bɛ Koforidua la ni.
english: David attended Nursery, Primary and Junior High School education at Freeman Methodist School in Koforidua.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi kɛŋi o dɔɔda awai, piiga nɛ piiga nɛ ayinne la nɛ bɛ Pope John Senior High School la ni, anina ka o mɛ da lɛm zamis dinɛ anɛ Visual Arts la.
english: He then continued to Pope John Senior High School and Junior Seminary where he studied Visual Arts.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007)la ni, David Oscar da naae dinɛ anɛ School of Performing Arts bɛ University of Ghana in the Bachelor of Fine Arts Program la ni.
english: In 2007, David Oscar graduated from the School of Performing Arts at University of Ghana in the Bachelor of Fine Arts Program.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayuobu (2006) la ni ka o da nam bɛ University la ni la ba da voot David nɛ ka o an Ghana wʋsa onɛ mi galima di'ema kali ka onɛ da pɛɛs sini di'ema dinɛ da an "Stars of the Future" ka di anɛ Charter Hose Ghana da gɔsi di li yɛla, anina ka David yiiga na nidib tusir pʋʋgin(1000) banɛ da di'emid la ni.
english: In 2006 while still at the university, David was voted Ghana's Best Comedy Icon when he participated in the comedy reality series "Stars of the Future" that was organized by Charter House Ghana, where he came top out of over 1000 upcoming comedians.

kusaal: Ba voot o yee onɛ di ya'an Ghana kpala galima di'ema dine da anɛ, "Stars of the Future", dinɛ ka Charter House Ghana da gɔsi di li yɛla la.
english: He was voted Ghana's Best Comedy Icon in a show, "Stars of the Future", organized by Charter House Ghana.

kusaal: David T. D. Vondee (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 2 Mɔtul/Nwadisawai 1978) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tis Twifo-Atii Morkwaa Constituency bɛ Central Region, Ghana.
english: David T. D. Vondee (born 2 August 1978) is a Ghanaian politician who currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Twifo-Atii Morkwaa Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a David Vondee nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii Nwadisa anii la daba ayi daar (2 August 1978) ka o yi Mafi Adidome bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: David Vondee was born on 2 August 1978 and hails from Mafi Adidome in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: David Vondee da maali o Associate Degree in (Marketing, Administration and Communication) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni (2020).
english: David Vondee had his Associate Degree in Marketing, Business administration, and Communication in 2020.

kusaal: David Vondee anɛ Wadmaani tis Twifo-Atii Morkwaa Constituency bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: David Vondee is working as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Twifo-Atii Morkwaa Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: David Vondee da nya' ka di NDC Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la Twifo-Atii Morkwaa Constituency n bɛ Central Region, Ghana.
english: David Vondee contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Twifo-Atii Morkwaa Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: David Vondee da lɛn di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la National Democratic Congress nɔba zug nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne, kɔbisnaasi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (21,416) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'al anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.5%) ka keŋ paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni ka bas Ebenezer Obeng Dwamena onɛ bɛ New Patriotic Party ka da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ awai, kɔbisnu nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (19,594) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi dua'al ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (47.2%) Samuel Kofi Essel onɛ bɛ GUM la paam vɔɔt kɔbisnu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yinne (541) dinɛ an yinne dua'al atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.3%).
english: David Vondee won again in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress with 21,416 votes making 51.5% of the total votes cast to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana against Ebenezer Obeng Dwamena of the New Patriotic Party who had 19,594 votes (47.2%) Samuel Kofi Essel of GUM who also had 541 votes (1.3%).

kusaal: David Vondee paas Works and Housing Committee Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: David Vondee is a member of the Works and Housing Committee of the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: David Vondee anɛ Ewe ka an Kristo biig.
english: Vondee is an Ewe.

kusaal: Ba da zɛrig David Vondee ye zu $2.4 million din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu Nwadisa anii la ni (August 2015) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu Nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni (July 2016) sʋʋgʋn ka ma' ye o na kuos paalʋ tis asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ lʋgʋr kanɛ yʋ'ʋri an "REI Ghana Limited" ka o da bɛlim kɔɔtʋ la ye on pʋ tʋmi di.
english: David Vondee was born on 2 August 1978 and hails from Mafi Adidome in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Davis Ansah Opoku (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 13 Sɛnlʋŋ/Nwadispiigin 1984) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd, ba da dᴜ'a o nɛ yᴜᴜm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ anaasi la nwaris anii li dabisim piina tan' la ni, O anɛ wadmaan n tis Mpraeso sᴜ'ᴜlᴜm linɛ bɛ Gaana Eastern Region sᴜ'ᴜlᴜm la.
english: Davis Ansah Opoku (born 13 September 1984) is a Ghanaian politician, and a member of Parliament for Mpraeso Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Deputy Ranking kpɛɛm n paas Public Accounts Committee la ni ka lɛn paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid works & Housing n bɛ wadmaanib yir la ni Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris piiga la yᴜᴜma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ yinne la ni, ka 40 under 40 yɔɔd barika pᴜ'ᴜsim la da maal ka ba du'os Davis yᴜ'ur bɛdigᴜ pamm ye bikpiuŋ hali n bɛ Gɔmina tᴜmtᴜmnib la ni.
english: He serves as the Deputy Ranking Member of the Public Accounts Committee and a member of the works & Housing Committee of Parliament In October 2021, the 40 under 40 awards ceremony adjudged Davis as a young leader in Governance and Government agencies.

kusaal: O saam yᴜ'ᴜr buon ye, Sampson Opoku Kwahu Asakraka ka o ma aan Helena Opoku Obomeng Kwahu.
english: Opuku was born in Accra, 13 September 1984 to Sampson Opoku of Kwahu Asakraka and Helena Opoku of Obomeng Kwahu.

kusaal: Opuku da keŋi sakuri Nkwatia Secondary Sakur linɛ bɛ Gaana la ka tɔlisi keŋ University of Cape Coast naae ka di'e digirɛɛ gbaᴜŋ linɛ bigs ye o zamisnɛ laboratory technology.
english: Opuku attended Nkwatia Secondary School in Ghana and graduated from the University of Cape Coast with a degree in laboratory technology.

kusaal: O da lɛn tɔlisi keŋ University of London n keŋ zamis wada yɛla ka yii ani lɛn keŋ University of Leicester ani ka o naae o zamisᴜg linɛ pian'ad mi'ilim yɛla la.
english: He continued to the University of London to study Law and then to University of Leicester where he completed his course in communication.

kusaal: O mɔr kasɛta gbaᴜŋ linɛ an strategic political communication n yi' International Academy for Leadership (IAF), linɛ bɛ Germany sᴜ'ᴜlᴜm la Nannanna bɛɛ ani n zamisid linɛ an wada tᴜᴜma yɛla nɛ Masters in Law n bɛ University of Law.
english: He holds a certificate in strategic political communication from the International Academy for Leadership (IAF), Germany and currently in the final stage of his Legal Practice Course and Masters in Law at the University of Law.

kusaal: Opoku da tᴜmnɛ n an director of communications, ka lin nya'aŋ ka o lɛn kena an director of operations n tis Alliance for Accountable Governance (AFAG) dim.
english: Opoku was director of communications, then later director of operations for the Alliance for Accountable Governance whose role was to expose some alleged rots during the NDC term in office.

kusaal: Opoku an pressure group la tuongat, nɛ Let My Vote Count Movement (LMVC) la.
english: Opoku is a member of the pressure group Let My Vote Count Movement.

kusaal: Yᴜᴜma tusa yi' nɛ piina wai la ni ka o da maal a-pɛsigi tum yᴜᴜm yinne tis Gɔmina la tᴜᴜma n bɛ wadmaanib yir la ni ka da National Mock wadmaanib yir la ni linɛ an Ghana @ 50 celebrations yᴜᴜma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ yinne la ka lin nya'aŋ ka o kena lieb wadmaan n tis Mpreaso sᴜ'ᴜlᴜm la.
english: In 2019 he did his national service at the parliament and was part of the National Mock Parliament of the Ghana @ 50 celebrations and in 2021 became a full member of parliament for the Mpreaso Constituency.

kusaal: Deadly Voyage da anɛ sini di'ema dinɛ ka John Machkenzie da an tuongat ka Stuart Urban sɔbi di yυυma 1996 la ni.
english: Deadly Voyage is a 1996 television film directed by John Mackenzie and written by Stuart Urban.

kusaal: Aboard cargo ship MC Ruby la, zi'en New York Tempυυgυn, ayuobυ zɔ bɔdig n yi laa ayinne ni yidigi li.
english: Aboard the cargo ship MC Ruby, docked in New York City, six stowaways burst from one of the containers being unloaded.

kusaal: Nɛ' ka tυmtυm kpɛɛm Andreas Vlachos kena ye o gɔs bɛog tυυma yɛla ka pian'a sa'al ye ban a nwɛ'ɛ crew la sam ka di gaad ala.Din nya'aŋ, ka MC Ruby ken Ghana na, ani ka dock tυm Kingsley Ofosu.
english: Later, the MC Ruby is docked in Ghana, where dock worker Kingsley Ofosu plans to some day stow away aboard a cargo ship to pursue a better life for himself and his pregnant wife in the United States.

kusaal: Union Pictures nɛ John Goldschmidt's Viva Films dimi da la'asi maan n pυdigidi tisid BBC Films nɛ HBO dim.
english: Produced by Union Pictures and John Goldschmidt's Viva Films for joint distribution to BBC Films and HBO.

kusaal: MC Ruby's Ukrainian dim la da gɔsid yɛlbama wυsa ka di an la'adi tisi ba, amaa ka aanrυg la kpɛɛm nɛ o yiiga nya'andɔl la, lon Pesin, di da pυ malisi baa, ba mi' ye banɛ su'a zɔɔ kena la na nwɛ'ɛ sam kati wa'ae aanrυg tυυma ni wυυ tusa kɔbis nɛ zak yɛl dolla nam ni.
english: The MC Ruby's Ukrainian crew watches the detention with some amusement, but the ship's captain and his first mate, Ion Plesin, are displeased, aware that the illegal immigrants will cost the shipping company hundreds of thousands of dollars in fines.

kusaal: Hùng Kings' Temple Festival (Vietnamese: Giỗ Tổ Hùng Vương or Lễ hội đền Hùng) anɛ Vietnamese malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba maan yʋʋm yʋʋm 8th paae 11th daar, third lunar month la ni tis Hùng Vương bɛɛ Hùng Na'anam.
english: The Hùng Kings' Temple Festival (Vietnamese: Giỗ Tổ Hùng Vương or Lễ hội đền Hùng) is a Vietnamese festival held annually from the 1st to the 10th day of the third lunar month in honor of the Hùng King (Hùng Vương in Vietnamese).

kusaal: Malʋŋ la mɛŋ daar, dinɛ an vʋ'ʋsim daar Vietnam din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la ni, bɛnɛ dabpiiga la daar.
english: The main festival day, which is a public holiday in Vietnam since 2007, is on the 10th day.

kusaal: La'anɛ di yʋ'ʋkanɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ mi' an Death Anniversary of the Hùng Kings la (Vietnamese: Giỗ Tổ Hùng Vương), malʋŋ la pʋ pa'an dabisir vikki kanɛ ka Na'asi'a maal ka'alim Hùng King pʋʋginɛ.
english: Although the official name is the Death Anniversary of the Hùng Kings (Vietnamese: Giỗ Tổ Hùng Vương), the festival does not mark any specific date of death for any Hùng King.

kusaal: Dinɛ zug ka ba maan malʋŋ kaŋa anɛ ye ba tien' ka yɔ' lampo tis Hung kings banɛ an kpɛɛmbanɛ da pin'il sʋ'ʋlim la ka an yiiga na'anam tis teŋ la.
english: The purpose of this ceremony is to remember and pay tribute to the Hung king who are the traditional founders and first kings of the nation.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la ni, banɛ da an saami keŋ teŋ la malʋŋ kaŋa nina kal na an nwɛnɛ miliyɔŋa ayɔpɔi.
english: In 2016, the total number of visitors to the festival numbered seven million.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la ɛɛnti pin'ilnɛ teŋin la mɛŋ vʋ'ʋsim daar, amaa ka di yʋ'ʋn lieb teŋ la wʋsa vʋ'ʋsim daar ka din da pin'il yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la ni.
english: The festival began as a local holiday, but has become recognized as a national holiday starting in 2007.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la bɛnɛ dabisa bɛdegʋ amaa nwadig la dabpiiga daar anɛ dabiskanɛ bɛɛ di kɔn'.
english: The ceremony takes place over several days, but the 10th day of the month is considered the most important.
