kusaal: 2011 la nii, Ayew da paamnɛ BBC Afrika bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd tis yʋʋm kana nɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdtita'ar tis yʋʋm kanna.
english: In 2011, Ayew was named the BBC African Footballer of the Year and Ghanaian Footballer of the Year.

kusaal: Ayew da pin'ili o tʋmkaŋa Germany, nwɛ'ɛdi tisid 1860 München, ka an yʋma 7.
english: Ayew began his career in Germany, playing for 1860 Munich, while debuting for the club at age seven.

kusaal: Ka 2006 la nii, o da keŋnɛ o saami da nwɛ'ɛd Kilab sia la ni dinɛ an Marseille, ka nwɛ' anina yʋma ayi' ka yʋ'ʋn da bas ka tɔlis 2007–08 nwɛ'ɛb la ni.
english: In 2006, he signed with his father's former club, Marseille, and spent two seasons in the club's youth academy before making his debut in the 2007–08 season.

kusaal: Ayew da bɛnɛ loon tis Lorient nɛ Arles-Avignon yʋma ayi' sʋŋid tiim kan la ye ba nyaŋi paae Ligue 1 ba yiiga din.
english: Ayew spent the following two seasons on loan with Lorient and Arles-Avignon, helping the latter team earn promotion to Ligue 1 for the first time.

kusaal: Ka 2010 la nii, o da lɛb Marseille ka da an nwɛ'ɛd tita'ar bɛ manager Didier Deschamps ni, nyaŋidi nwɛ'ɛd zin'is 200 ka dit dit Trophée des Champions and Coupe de la Ligues bɛ 2010 nɛ 2011 wʋsa ni.
english: In 2010, he returned to Marseille and became an integral part of the first team under manager Didier Deschamps, making over 200 appearances and winning consecutive Trophée des Champions and Coupe de la Ligues in both 2010 and 2011.

kusaal: O mwɛ' nɔɔr atan' tis FIFA World Cups (2010, 2014 nɛ 2022), pɛ'ɛsnɛ Afrika kap tis tɛɛns (2008, 2010, 2012, 2015, 2017, 2019 nɛ 2021), sʋŋidi ba ka ba naad runners-up bɛ 2010 nɛ 2015, ka da an onɛ di goolnami gaad nwɛ' kana ni.
english: He has played in three FIFA World Cups (2010, 2014 and 2022), as well as eight Africa Cup of Nations (2008, 2010, 2012, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2023), helping them finish runners-up in 2010 and 2015, and was top goalscorer at the latter tournament.

kusaal: O anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd kanɛ nwɛ'ɛd dagɔbʋg kpikpɛŋ ka an kaptin tisid Ghana national team la.
english: At the youth level, Ayew represented Ghana at under-20 level and captained the team to victory at both the 2009 African Youth Championship and the 2009 FIFA U-20 World Cup.

kusaal: O anɛ daʋkanɛ da di'e Afrika bɔɔlnwɛ'ɛdib wʋsa kpɛɛm bɛ ootballer FIFA la ni onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Abedi Pele Ayew ka mɔr ba'abiis ayi', Ibrahim nɛ Jordan, banɛ wʋsa mɛn an bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib.
english: Ayew is the second-born son of three-time African Footballer of the Year and FIFA 100 member Abedi "Pele" Ayew and has two brothers, Ibrahim and Jordan, who also are professional footballers.

kusaal: Onɛ da du'a France laa, Ayew anɛ international tis Ghana dinɛ pin'il 2008 ka paam kapnam wʋʋ 110 nɛ.
english: Born in France, Ayew has been a full international for Ghana since 2008 and has earned 120 caps.

kusaal: Onɛ da an na'akin la, o da an kapitin tis under-20 tiim kanɛ da di'e 2009 African Youth Championship la nɛ 2009 FIFA U-20 World Cup la.
english: At the youth level, Ayew represented Ghana at under-20 level and captained the team to victory at both the 2009 African Youth Championship and the 2009 FIFA U-20 World Cup.

kusaal: Della Sowah (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 23 Sapal/Nwadispii 1959) da anɛ ti Gaana Minista banɛ gɔsid dap, pu'ab, biis nɛ teŋ la nidib bɛllim sυŋ yɛla la nya'andɔl.
english: Della Adjoa Sowah (born 23 November 1959) is a Ghanaian former Deputy Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection.

kusaal: Sowah da naae o sakur yuma 1981 la ni n yi Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology ka di'e o kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an degree in Social Sciences.
english: Sowah earned her degree in Social Sciences from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology in 1981.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Diploma in Finance and Master of business administration.
english: She holds a Diploma in Finance and Master of business administration.

kusaal: wadmaan ti Gaana kpɛla lin yi yυυma 2012 ti paae 2016.
english: Member of Parliament, 2012–2016 (government of Ghana)

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Marketing, MD lin yi 1990 ti paas 2000 (DAPEG LTD).
english: Marketing, MD, 1990–2000 (DAPEG LTD)

kusaal: Onɛ da lɛn an Research, lin yi 1986 ti paae 1990 (ESSOR LTD).
english: Research, 1986–1990 (ESSOR LTD)

kusaal: Sowah anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Sowah is a Christian.

kusaal: O kul sid n mɔr biis atan'.
english: She is married, and has three children.

kusaal: Derek Darko Ohene Assifo Bekoe (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 6 Vaala/Nwadisanu 1967) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Upper West Akim Constituency bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim la ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: Derek Darko Ohene Assifo Bekoe (born 6 April 1967) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Upper West Akim Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Derrick Oduro (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii nwaisa ayi dabpisi nɛ atan daar, (23 February 1958) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd onɛ da an soogia da bɛ Ghana Army ka o kpɛŋ da an major.
english: Derrick Oduro (born 23 February 1958) is a Ghanaian politician who is also a retired military personnel with the Ghana Army and has a rank of major.

kusaal: O anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid ka da an deputy Minister tis Defence, Ghana.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the deputy Minister for Defence in Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ wadmaani tisi Nkoranza North Constituency dinɛ bɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ti da buon ye Brong Ahafo region ka yʋ'ʋn an Bono East Region la.
english: He is also a member of parliament for Nkoranza North Constituency in the then Brong Ahafo region now Bono East Region.

kusaal: Oduro yinɛ Dromankese bɛ Brong Ahafo Region ka dio yʋ'ʋr yʋ'ʋn an Bono East Region bɛ Ghana.
english: Oduro hails from Dromankese in the then Brong Ahafo Region now Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔrnɛ Masters of Arts, governance and leadership yi Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).
english: He holds a Masters of Arts in governance and leadership from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).

kusaal: O lɛm mɔr Diploma in Public Finance yi Institute of Accountancy Training nɛ kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Cranfield University.
english: He also holds a Diploma in Public Finance from the Institute of Accountancy Training and a Certificate from Cranfield University.

kusaal: Oduro da pin'ili o tʋʋma ka anɛ onɛ gɔsid ligiid yɛla (bursar) bɛ Akosas Business College din yi yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1977) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1979).
english: Oduro begun his career as a bursar at Akosas Business College from 1977 to 1979.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ ka o da yi keŋ kpɛn' military yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1979) paae tʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005).
english: After which he was drafted into the military from 1979 to 2005.

kusaal: O da naae o soogia tʋʋma ka lieb presiding member tis Nkoranza District Assembly din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007).
english: He retired from the military and became a presiding member of the Nkoranza District Assembly from 2005 to 2007.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la ni, Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid, Derrick Oduro da nyaŋi o taaba nɛ na'adɔbanɛ da nya' nɛ o la ka keŋ zi'eni tisi Nkoranza North Constituency ka nan kpɛn an wadmaani paae zina.
english: In 2007, under the ticket of the New Patriotic Party, Derrick Oduro defeated his opponents from other political parties to represent the Nkoranza North Constituency and has represented his constituency to date.

kusaal: O da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party ka kɔ'ɔŋ tis Joseph Kwasi Mensah onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress.
english: He contested in the 2020 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party and lost to Joseph Kwasi Mensah of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Joseph Mensah da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anu, kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi (15,124) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka Oduro paam vɔɔt tusa piiga, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (10,978).
english: Joseph Mensah obtained 15,124 of the valid vote cast while Oduro polled 10,978 votes.

kusaal: Derrick Oduro mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa ayuobʋ o anɛ Kristo biig ka keŋ Seventh Day Adventist.
english: Derrick Oduro is married with six children and is a practising Seventh Day Adventist.

kusaal: O da paas Gender and Children Committee, Business Committee nɛ Youth, Sports and Culture Committee.
english: He is part of Gender and Children Committee, Business Committee and also the Youth, Sports and Culture Committee.

kusaal: Desmond De-Graft Paitoo anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd, ba da du'anɛ nwaris anii la yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyuobυ nɛ awai li dabisim piisi nɛ yinne la ni.
english: Desmond De-Graft Paitoo (born 21 August 1969) is a Ghanaian politician who currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Gomoa East Constituency.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Desmond De-Graft nɛ nwaris anii la yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyuobυ nɛ awai li dabisim piisi nɛ yinne la ni, o yinɛ Gomoa Dasum linɛ bɛ Gaana Central Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Desmond De-Graft was born on 21 August 1969 and hails from Gomoa Dasum in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Desmond De-Graft da naae o MSLC yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni, ka lɛn naae linɛ an Mechanical Engineering yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ yinne la ni ka maal o Digirɛɛ linɛ an Supply Chain Management (Procurement) yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina nii la ni.
english: Desmond De-Graft had his MSLC in 1987, City and Guild Intermediate in Mechanical Engineering in 1991 and his Degree in Supply Chain Management (Procurement) in 2018.

kusaal: Desmond De-Graft anɛ Chief Executive Officer (CEO) n tis Desreen Shipping and Logistics tυυma.
english: Desmond De-Graft is the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Desreen Shipping and Logistics.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi la ni ka ba da vɔt ka Desmond De-Graft da zi'en Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug nya'a di Gomoa East sυ'υlυm wadmaanib kυk la, o da paamnɛ vɔt bam 36,637 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 49.46% n yi vɔt la kanl wυsa ni n keŋi paas ti wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anii la ti Gaana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la onɛ Wabυg nid Kojo Asemanyi la zi'en ka o di ka bas o, Wabυg nid la da mɔri vɔt bam 135,873 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 48.42% n yi vɔt la kanl wυsa ni, Samuel Kofi Essel onɛ da an GUM nid la mɛ da paam vɔt bam 1,397 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da paamnɛ 1.89% n yi vɔt la wυsa pυυgin ka Emmanuel Otchere onɛ an UPP nid la mɛ da mɔri vɔt bam 173 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 0.23% vɔt la wυsa pυυgin.
english: Desmond De-Graft won the parliamentary seat for the Gomoa East Constituency during the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress with 36,637 votes making 49.46% of the total votes cast to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana against Kojo Asemanyi of the New Patriotic Party who had 135,873 votes making 48.42% of the total votes cast, Samuel Kofi Essel of GUM who had 1,397 votes making 1.89% of the total votes cast and Emmanuel Otchere of UPP who also had 173 votes making 0.23% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Gomoa East sυ'υlυm la.
english: Desmond De-Graft Paitoo (born 21 August 1969) is a Ghanaian politician who currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Gomoa East Constituency.

english: Desmond De-Graft is a member of the House Committee.

english: He is also a member of the Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs Committee of the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

english: In January 2022, he pledged to support the construction of a health facility with hospital furniture and other items at Dampase in the Central Region.

english: The Diamond Stars became the champions of the 2012 and 2013 Premier League season, and the first club outside Freetown to ever won the Premier League.

english: The club have won the Sierra Leonean FA Cup once, in 1992 and they are one of the most popular football clubs in Sierra Leone.

english: The club got the name the Diamond Stars due to the rich diamond reserves in Kono district, where it is based.

english: Diamond stars have one of the largest fan bases among Sierra Leonean football clubs and its supporters are primarily from Kono District.

english: It is a multi-use 2,000 capacity soccer stadium located in Koidu Town, Kono District, Sierra Leone.

english: Adomako Kissi was born on 23 August 1981 to Dr. Emanuel Abu Kissi, a medical doctor and Madam Elizabeth Bamfo Kissi, a Midwife nurse.

english: Digya National Park was created in 1900 as a protected area, the first in Ghana.

kusaal: di bɛnɛ Bono ya-tuona sʋ'ʋlʋmin.
english: It is located in the Bono East Region.

kusaal: saŋkanɛ ka gɔmma da di'e li la, ya da bɛ park la ni, ba da anɛ zingban'adib nɛ kpaadib bɛdigʋ da mɛ' ya zin' ani.Yʋʋm 2006 la ni la, nidib da mɛ ya 49 zin' ani, ka gɔmma da pin'ili yiisidi ba yinne-yinne yit park la ni.
english: In 2006, there were 49 settlements and the government of Ghana began evicting settlement residents from the park.

kusaal: Pɛbis kaŋa ka ba buon Ammonia la tisid proteins, nucleic acids, nɛ vitamins bɛdigʋ.
english: Ammonia is the precursor to proteins, nucleic acids, and most vitamins.

kusaal: Ban pin'ili maan vɛɛnsig kanɛ buon Haber-Bosch Process, ka ba dɔlisidi maan ammonia la, ninsaal mɛŋi yʋ'ʋn maani li bɛdigʋ.
english: Since the advent of the industrial process for nitrogen fixation, the Haber-Bosch Process, the majority of ammonia in the world is human-made.

kusaal: Bi'elim anɛ biili banɛ ka ninsaalib dit bɛɛ kuod, ka mɔɔg biili (oats, wheat, mui, kawɛnna, barley, rye, sorghum nɛ ki) paas nɛ Poaceae (mɔɔg) buudi nɛ biili banɛ yit Fabaceae (legume) buudi.
english: Grains can be defined as seeds that humans eat or harvest, with cereal grains (oats, wheat, rice, corn, barley, rye, sorghum and millet) belonging to the Poaceae (grass) family and pulses coming from the Fabaceae (legume) family.

kusaal: Wal banɛ pʋ kʋdʋgɛ (ban bɛɛ ba kɔn'ɔ nɛ banɛ an kpi'ema wan wʋʋ bi'elim, biili bɛɛ banɛ pigid) lɛn mɔr kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb pʋdʋgir ka ban an stone fruits (cherries nɛ peaches), pome fruits (apples, pears), berries (blackberry, strawberry), citrus (oranges, lemon), melons (watermelon, cantaloupe), Mediterranean fruits (grapes, fig), tropical fruits (banana, pineapple).
english: Fleshy fruits (distinguishable from dry fruits like grain, seeds and nuts) can be further classified as stone fruits (cherries and peaches), pome fruits (apples, pears), berries (blackberry, strawberry), citrus (oranges, lemon), melons (watermelon, cantaloupe), Mediterranean fruits (grapes, fig), tropical fruits (banana, pineapple).

kusaal: Phytates anɛ bʋnlinɛ na nyaŋi kɛ ka sikir buudi si'eba nɛ vitamins pʋ zuoe bʋnbʋta la nii.
english: Phytates can prevent the release of some sugars and vitamins.

kusaal: One 4-ounce (110 g) steak, nua bin'isa bɛɛ kurkur ni'im mɔr protein 30 grams.
english: One 4-ounce (110 g) steak, chicken breast or pork chop contains about 30 grams of protein.

kusaal: A 4-ounce (110 g) ba ya'a mak cheese wala bɛn tisid protein 15 grams.
english: A 4-ounce (110 g) serving of cheese has about 15 grams of protein.

kusaal: Ka milik kɔp yinnɛ (~240 mL) mɛ mɔr protein 8 grams.
english: And 1 cup (~240 mL) of milk has about 8 grams of protein.

kusaal: Niŋgbiŋ biim buudi banɛ ka ninsaal paamidi yit bʋnkɔnbid ni si'eba anɛ kpaam, vitamins (ka B12 paas) nɛ (ka zinc, iron, calcium, magnesium paas).
english: Other nutrients found in animal products include calories, fat, essential vitamins (including B12) and minerals (including zinc, iron, calcium, magnesium).

kusaal: Diarrhea, ban'a kanɛ ka ba tiind ka saand la anɛ wikanɛ yinɛ fʋn na di dikanɛ san'am, ka nidib 550 million ka li gban'adi ba, ka ba pʋʋgin, nidib 230,000 dɔlisid anina kɔ'ɔŋidi ba nyɔɔrr yʋʋm wʋsa.
english: Diarrhea is the most common illness caused by consuming contaminated food, with about 550 million cases and 230,000 deaths from diarrhea each year.

kusaal: Linɛ lɛn paas ya'as, yʋʋm bama saŋa, diib ban'as kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb 1,007 ka ba da nyɛ ka lin da gban'a nidib si'eba an 30,395.
english: In addition, during this period, 1,007 food poisoning outbreaks with 30,395 cases of food poisoning were reported.

kusaal: Diib pʋʋgin mɔr ku'om, lipids, proteins, nɛ carbohydrates.
english: Food is mainly composed of water, lipids, proteins, and carbohydrates.

kusaal: Minerals (wʋʋ yaarim) nɛ organic substances (wʋʋ vitamins) mɛ bɛ diib pʋʋgin.
english: Other organic substances (e.g., vitamins) and minerals (e.g., salts) can also be found in food.

kusaal: Lugur Kane gosid diib, kuob ne gu'ul yela nɛ World Health Organization la'as diibi pʋdʋg nɛ zin'is piinɛ awai: mɔɔg biili, nya'a, yam nɛ biili banɛ kpi'em, bin'isim, gɛla, zimi, ni'im, bʋni'anda, vegetables, wala, kpaam, sikir, spices, daam, diib banɛ tisid niŋgbiŋ biim, la'abanɛ paasid malisim nɛ vɛnlim, diib banɛ ka ba maali la'as nɛ bʋnɔnbida.
english: The Food and Agriculture Organization and World Health Organization use a system with eighteen or nineteen food classifications, including: cereals and their products; roots, tubers, plantains and their products; pulses, seeds and nuts and their products; milk and milk products; eggs and their products; fish, shellfish and their products; meat and meat products; insects, grubs and their products; vegetables and their products; fruits and their products; fats and oils; sweets and sugars; spices and condiments; beverages; foods for particular nutritional uses; food additives; composite dishes; and savory snacks.

kusaal: Bʋnbʋta banɛ paas buudi bam ani bɛ kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb, ka banɛ an tiig wala si'eba an tomato, squash, nanzʋ'ʋs nɛ nyaadua bɛɛ biili wan wʋʋ bʋnlinɛ ka ba buon peas anɛ vaand buudi.
english: Where plants fall within these categories can vary, with botanically described fruits such as the tomato, squash, pepper and eggplant or seeds like peas commonly considered vegetables.

kusaal: Bi'el mum anɛ diib banɛ ka bi'elif la an si'em la kpɛlim aan ala ka pʋ ti'akɛ (bran, germ, and endosperm).
english: Whole grains are foods that contain all the elements of the original seed (bran, germ, and endosperm).

kusaal: Nuts mɛ anɛ wala banɛ kʋdʋg, ka pak kanɛ ligili ba la an wan wʋʋ daag nɛ.
english: Nuts are dry fruits, distinguishable by their woody shell.

kusaal: Vegetables anɛ bʋnbʋtir la lɔkanɛ ka fʋ na nyaŋi di, wan wʋʋ nya'a, til, vaand, puum, pak bɛɛ tiig la wʋsa.
english: Vegetables refer to any other part of the plant that can be eaten, including roots, stems, leaves, flowers, bark or the entire plant itself.

kusaal: Bama si'eba anɛ banɛ ka ba dit nya'a (potatoes nɛ carrots), bʋngbila (gabʋ buudi), banɛ maan puum (cauliflower nɛ broccoli), banɛ ka ba dit vaand (spinach nɛ lettuce) nɛ banɛ ka ba diti ba til (celery nɛ asparagus).
english: These include root vegetables (potatoes and carrots), bulbs (onion family), flowers (cauliflower and broccoli), leaf vegetables (spinach and lettuce) and stem vegetables (celery and asparagus).

kusaal: Zin'ig banɛ tisid paŋ la anɛ starch, fructose, glucose bɛɛ sikir buudi si'eba.
english: Carbohydrates are mainly in the form of starch, fructose, glucose and other sugars.

kusaal: Linɛ gu'ud ninsaal niŋgbiŋ ban'as pʋʋgin ka ba buon vitamins la yinɛ bʋnbʋta ni, ba si'eba banɛ pʋ yi bʋnbʋta ni anɛ vitamin D nɛ vitamin B12.
english: Most vitamins are found from plant sources, with the exception of vitamin D and vitamin B12.

kusaal: Bʋnlinɛ maan niŋgbina ka ba buon Minerals la tɔ'ɔn zuoe bɛɛ lin an finn.
english: Minerals can also be plentiful or not.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a mak nɛ wal banɛ nan pʋ kʋdʋgɛ (ka yis kodu) vegetables mɔr starch, potassium, dietary fiber, folate nɛ vitamins bɛdigʋ ka lɛɛ mɔr kpaam finn.
english: Compared to fleshy fruit (excepting bananas) vegetables are high in starch, potassium, dietary fiber, folate and vitamins and low in fat and calories.

kusaal: Bi'elim anɛ banɛ mɔr diib bʋʋlim bɛdigʋ ka banɛ ka ba pak kpi'em la mɛ tisid protein, fiber, vitamin E nɛ B bɛdigʋ.
english: Grains are more starch based and nuts have a high protein, fiber, vitamin E and B content.

kusaal: Biili anɛ diib hali tis bʋnkɔnbid bɔzugɔ, ba mɔr pa'ad nɛ kpaam kanɛ zɛnmis, wan wʋʋ omega-3 fats.
english: Seeds are a good source of food for animals because they are abundant and contain fiber and healthful fats, such as omega-3 fats.

kusaal: Ba buon bʋnkɔnbid banɛ an yam bɛɛ mɔɔg ma'a la nɛ ye herbivores, ka banɛ dit tiis wala ka ba buoni ba ye frugivores, ka banɛ dit vaand nɛ li daad la mɛ an folivores (pandas) ka banɛ ɔnbid daad la an xylophages (termites).
english: Animals that only eat plants are called herbivores, with those that mostly just eat fruits known as frugivores, while leaf and shoot eaters are folivores (pandas) and wood eaters termed xylophages (termites).

kusaal: Ba mɔr bʋnbʋta maan bodobodo, pasta, cereals, daam nɛ jams bɛɛ la'asi'eba wan wʋʋ sikir, ti'nya'a, linɛ niŋid diib ka ba buon spices la nɛ kpaam.
english: Plants can be processed into breads, pasta, cereals, juices and jams or raw ingredients such as sugar, herbs, spices and oils can be extracted.

kusaal: Biili banɛ tisid kpaam mɔr kpaam bɛdigʋ ba pʋʋgin – sunflower, flaxseed, rapeseed (ka si'eba an canola oil) nɛ sesame.
english: Oilseeds are pressed to produce rich oils – ⁣sunflower, flaxseed, rapeseed (including canola oil) and sesame.

kusaal: Nwa' si'eba anɛ ni'im, gɛla, shellfish nɛ li kpaam wan wʋʋ milk nɛ cheese.
english: This includes meat, eggs, shellfish and dairy products like milk and cheese.

kusaal: Gɛl tita'ar yinnɛ mɔr protein 7 grams.
english: One 4-ounce (110 g) steak, chicken breast or pork chop contains about 30 grams of protein.

kusaal: Diib banɛ ka ti nyɛti yit bʋnkɔnbid ni si'eba anɛ milik, lin yit nɛ bin'isa ni, ka si'eba nuud ala ka si'eba mɛ mɔri li maan disi'eba (cheese, butter, etc.).
english: Food products produced by animals include milk produced by mammary glands, which in many cultures is drunk or processed into dairy products (cheese, butter, etc.).

kusaal: Buud si'eba nud ziim, diib wan wʋʋ ziim ni'im, ziim ka ba mɔri bʋligid ni'im ka paasid yaarim digin ka di yʋʋgin, ka si'eba mɛ mɔr ziim maan stew wan wʋʋ dikanɛ ka ba buon jugged hare la.
english: Some cultures consume blood, such as in blood sausage, as a thickener for sauces, or in a cured, salted form for times of food scarcity, and others use blood in stews such as jugged hare.

kusaal: Bʋnlinɛ kɛt ka si'el malis ninsaal nɔɔrin anɛ sikir buudi banɛ ka ba si'eba an glucose, fructose, bɛɛ disaccharides ka ban si'eba mɛ an sucrose, lin la'as nɛ glucose nɛ fructose.
english: Sweetness is almost always caused by a type of simple sugar, such as glucose or fructose, or disaccharides, such as sucrose, a molecule combining glucose and fructose.

kusaal: Dibama buudi si'eba an citrus, li kaskas anɛ lemons nɛ limes.
english: Sour foods include citrus, especially lemons and limes.

kusaal: Diib ya'a an yaarimyaarim, li pa'al ye yaarim kuguri paasi li pʋʋgin wan wʋʋ sodium nɛ potassium.
english: Saltiness is the taste of alkali metal ions such as sodium and potassium.

kusaal: Umami, mɛ anɛ malisim kanɛ bɛ fʋn na dʋg ni'im pʋʋgin.Fleming, Amy (9 April 2013).
english: Umami, commonly described as savory, is a marker of proteins and characteristic of broths and cooked meats.

kusaal: "Umami: why the fifth taste is so important".
english: Umami, commonly described as savory, is a marker of proteins and characteristic of broths and cooked meats.

kusaal: Labaar bɛ World Health Organization (WHO), ye nidib 600 million dunia wʋsa bɛn'ɛd ka 420,000 ɛɛti kɔ'ɔŋi ba nyɔɔr dɔlisid nɛ ban di dibanɛ sa'am pʋʋgin.
english: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), about 600 million people worldwide get sick, and 420,000 die each year, from eating contaminated food.

kusaal: Biis banɛ pʋ paae yʋma anu anɛ pisnaasi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka li dɔlisid nɛ diib ban'as ni ka ba kɔ'ɔŋidi ba nyɔɔr, biis 125,000 kɔ'ɔŋidi ba nyɔɔr yʋʋm wʋsa.
english: Children under five years of age account for 40% of the burden of foodborne illness, with 125,000 deaths each year.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ atan' ni (2003) World Health Organization (WHO) da yis labaar na ka ye nidib banɛ dit diib kanɛ san'am ka ban'as mɔri ba bɛ WHO European Region pistan' kɔbiga pʋʋgin (30%) yitnɛ nidib yaan.
english: A 2003 World Health Organization (WHO) report concluded that about 30% of reported food poisoning outbreaks in the WHO European Region occur in private homes.

kusaal: WHO nɛ CDC gbana pʋʋgin, US tɛŋin ma'a, yʋʋm wʋsa, nidib 76 million ka ban'as gban'adi ba dɔlisid diib ni, nidib 325,000 pʋ lɛn nyaŋidi tʋm si'ela ka nidib 5,000 ɛɛnti kɔ'ɔŋid ba nyɔɔr.
english: According to the WHO and CDC, in the US alone, annually, there are 76 million cases of foodborne illness leading to 325,000 hospitalizations and 5,000 deaths.

kusaal: Bʋnbʋta nɛ bʋnvʋya si'eba maani ba mɛŋ diib.
english: Animals are used as food either directly or indirectly.

kusaal: Ku'om bɛ diib bɛdigʋ ni ka lin mɛŋ mɛ anɛ diibi la.
english: Water is found in nearly all foods and has been defined as food by itself.

kusaal: Ku'om an bʋnlinɛ ya'a kae ka vʋ'ʋm kae la pʋ mɔr malisim bɛɛ tɔɔlim nɔɔrinɛ.
english: Water, while important for survival, has no taste.

kusaal: Li bɛ diib bɛdigʋ ni zɛnmis nɛ ye li kɛ ka li diib malis.
english: It is found in almost every food in low to moderate proportions and enhances flavor.

kusaal: Zimi wan wʋʋ kɔbiga nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi (182) dit wala bɛɛ biili.
english: About 182 fish consume seeds or fruit.

kusaal: Ninsaalib dit bʋnbʋta buudi-buudi tusa-tusa; bʋnbʋta banɛ maan puum anɛ wan wʋʋ ban buudi-buudi tusa pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (75,000), ka ba dit wan wʋʋ ban tusa yɔpɔi (7,000).
english: Humans eat thousands of plant species; there may be as many as 75,000 edible species of angiosperms, of which perhaps 7,000 are often eaten.

kusaal: Diib bɛɛ Diid anɛ bunkanɛ ka bunvuya dit ka di tisidi ba niŋgbina biim nɛ paŋ.
english: Food is any substance consumed to provide nutritional support and energy to an organism.

kusaal: Diib anɛ bʋnlinɛ ka ba did ka li maan ningbina biim nɛ paŋi tisid ningbiŋ la.
english: Food is any substance consumed to provide nutritional support and energy to an organism.

kusaal: Division One League yʋ'ʋn anɛ dinɛ ka ba buon ye Access Bank Division One League ban yɔɔd ligidi la zug ka an second tier football league bɛ Ghana ka Ghana Football Association gɔsidi di yɛla.
english: The Division One League is the second tier football league in Ghana organized by the Ghana Football Association.

kusaal: Onɛ di zonenama atan la ɛɛnti paam tuon keni paas Ghana Premier League.
english: The winner of each of the three zones will be promoted to the Ghana Premier League.

kusaal: League la pʋdignɛ zin'isa atan (three zones) ka zone yinne bɛ teŋ la tuon (southern), sʋʋgʋn (middle) nɛ nya'aŋ (northern) sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.
english: The league is divided into three zones with a zone in the southern, middle and northern sectors of the country.

kusaal: Domeabra-obom bɛnɛ Ga south minisipal kanɛ bɛ Accra region Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm nwa.
english: Domeabra-Obom is located in the Ga South Municipal of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da naam constituency la nɛ ka li dɔlisi ban da wɛlig bɛɛ pʋdig Ga south constituency kʋdʋg n yiis Domeabra-obom nɛ waija nɛ Trobu-Amasaman constituency nam la ba kɔn la, ka li anɛ yʋʋm 2004 samanpiid nwadig kanɛ da an gɔmma nɛ wadmaanib gaansʋg vɔɔt saŋa la.
english: It was formed prior to the 2004 December presidential and parliamentary elections by the division of the old Ga South constituency into the new Domeabra-Obom, Weija and the Trobu-Amasaman constituencies.

kusaal: Kʋk la bɛnɛ wa Accra mɛtɔrɔpɔlis distrik sʋ'ʋlʋm kanɛ bɛ Accra region tita'ar Ghana nwa ni.
english: The seat is located within the Accra Metropolis District of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

english: The Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) is a unit in the Ghana Police Service.

en_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit

kusaal: Lʋgʋr la sʋnidnɛ ka gu'ud nimbanɛ ka ba mugusidi ba ka la'asid nɛ Department of Social Welfare, International Federation of Women Lawyers nɛ Legal Aid Board.
english: The unit provides support and protection for victims of domestic abuse by interrelating activities with the Department of Social Welfare, the International Federation of Women Lawyers and the Legal Aid Board.

en_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit

english: DOVVSU is mandated by, The 1992 Constitution of the Republic of Ghana, the Police Service Act, the Criminal and other Offences Act, Act 29/60, the Children's Act, Act, 560 /98, the Juvenile Justice Act, Act 653/2003, Ghana Domestic Violence Act (Act 732) 2007.
kus_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU)
en_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit

english: DOVVSU previously Women and Juvenile Unit (WAJU) was introduced in October 1998 as a special unit to handle violence against the vulnerable.
kus_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU)
en_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit

english: Assigned a new name to Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit in 2005, is composed of police personnel with offices in all regional capitals and desks in majority of districts in Ghana.
kus_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU)
en_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit

kusaal: DOVVSU mɔnrɛ gban'ar ye ba gu', gban' ka kpar nimbanɛ mugusidi ba taaba bɛɛ namisid pʋ'ab nɛ biisi ba yaan.
english: DOVVSU has a mission to prevent, apprehend and prosecute culprits of domestic violence and child abuse.
kus_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU)
en_article: Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit

kusaal: DOVVSU sʋŋid nimbanɛ ka ba digin nɛ ba ka di ka' ban mɛŋ bɔɔdim, banɛ ka ba saansidi ba, banɛ ka ba faan ba nɛ banɛ ka ba nidib kɛɛsi ba bas.
english: DOVVSU assists victims of sexual abuse, physical assault, fraud and neglect.

kusaal: Dominic Akuritinga Ayine onɛ ka ba dua o yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuʋbʋ la, Sapal nwadig daba ayuobʋ daar la,(06-01-1966) anɛ Ghana nid ka an wadmaani bɛ Ghana Parliament kanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la ni Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la, zi'e tisid Bolgatanga East teŋ n bɛ Bolgatanga sʋ'ʋlim ni la, ka zi'e tid man'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la(NDC).
english: Dominic Akuritinga Ayine (born 6 January 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the Sixth, Seventh, Eighth, and Ninth Parliaments of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Bolgatanga East Constituency in the Upper East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba du'a Ayine nɛ yʋʋm tusur yinne la, kɔbʋs wai pisyuʋbʋ nɛ ayuʋbʋ la, sapal nwadig, daba ayuobʋ daar la nɛ Zuarungu teŋ n bɛ tudu sʋ'ʋlim ni (Upper east region), Ghana kpɛ.
english: Ayine was born on 6 January 1966 in Zuarungu, Upper east region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da naae University of Ghana ka yinɛ nɛ gbauŋ bama, Bachelor of Arts degree, lɔɔ ni, nɛ GSL, yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ anu(1995) la ni.
english: He earned a Bachelor of Arts in law from the University of Ghana, Legon, in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana and GSL in 1995.

kusaal: Ka lɛn da paam LLM kasɛt International Economic Law ni, n yi University of Michigan Law Sakurin la, yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ anii(1998) la ni.
english: He earned his LLM in International Economic Law at the University of Michigan Law School in 1998.

kusaal: Ka o da lɛn tʋgʋs n keŋ Stanƒord University lɔɔ sakurin n bɛ California teŋin, USA la, n yi nɛ Trade and Democracy kasɛt bgauŋ, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuʋbʋ(2006) la ni.
english: He then went to Stanford University Law School, in California, USA, for an LLM in International Trade Law in 2003 and subsequently a JSD (Trade and Democracy) in 2006.

kusaal: O teŋ: O anɛ Ghana nid.
english: He earned a Bachelor of Arts in law from the University of Ghana, Legon, in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana and GSL in 1995.

kusaal: O lɛm anɛ pa'an law zamisʋg lʋgʋr la University of Ghana, Legon, Accra.
english: He earned a Bachelor of Arts in law from the University of Ghana, Legon, in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana and GSL in 1995.

kusaal: Ka lɛm an Minista nya'andɔli tis Justice.
english: In January 2025, President John Mahamma appointed Ayine as the Attorney General and Justice Minister-Designate.

kusaal: Dominic Azimbe Azumah (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 1 January 1950) anɛ Ghana nid onɛ an politiks daan onɛ da an yiiga nɛ ayi' nɛ anaasi nɛ anu nɛ ayuobu daan M.P. tis Fourth Republic of Ghana.
english: Dominic Azimbe Azumah (born 1 January 1950) is a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the first, second, fourth, fifth and sixth Parliaments of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Azumah anɛ Accountant (banɛ kaan ligidi bankin la).
english: Azumah is an Accountant by profession.

kusaal: O da nya' na'am bɔɔd MP o teŋin 2004 vɔɔtʋg la, ka paam kuk la yʋ'ʋn da an MP bɛ, 4th parliament tis 4th Republic of Ghana bɛ January 2005 yʋʋm la ni.
english: He contested for the parliamentary seat of his constituency in the 2004 general election and subsequently regained the seat, becoming a member of the 4th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana in January 2005.

kusaal: Onɛ da an MP ti paae 6 January 2017.
english: He served in this capacity after winning subsequent elections until 6 January 2017.

kusaal: Akuka Albert Alalzuuga da di'e kuk la o nu'usin onɛ mɛ da an NDC nid.
english: He was succeeded by Akuka Albert Alalzuuga, also of the NDC.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayi' la ni (2012), Azumah da an MP nɛ Minister of State tis Atta Mills yʋʋm la ni.
english: In 2012, Azumah doubled as a Minister of State in the Atta Mills government.

kusaal: On ka ba da vɔɔt o ye o an MP tis yiiga MP bɛ gɔmɛnanam anaasi Ghana nwa ni 7 January 1993, banɛ da vɔɔt 1992 Ghana MP nam vɔɔtʋg kanɛ da maal 29 December 1992 la ni.
english: He was elected into the first parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana on 7 January 1993, after he was pronounced winner at the 1992 Ghanaian parliamentary election held on 29 December 1992.

kusaal: On da li 2000 yʋʋm vɔɔtʋg la ni, Azumah da lɛm di kuk la an MP tis Garu-Tempane sʋ'ʋlʋm bɛ Upper East Region, Ghana bɛ 2004 yʋʋm vɔɔtʋg la ni nɛ Ma'asim-tiig pati.
english: Following his loss in the 2000 general election, Azumah later reclaimed the seat as the member of parliament for the Garu-Tempane constituency of the Upper East Region of Ghana in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlʋm la da an dinɛ pɛ'ɛs sʋ'ʋlʋmnam 9 banɛ di Mp bɛ Ma'asim-tiig paati yit sʋ'ʋlʋmnam 13 banɛ bɛ Upper East Region nwa ni.
english: His constituency was a part of the 9 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election in the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress da di kʋgʋs bi'ela dinɛ an piswai nɛ anu (94) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi nɛ pistan' pʋʋgin (230).
english: The National Democratic Congress won a minority total of 94 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ nii nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (18,705) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa an tusa pistan' nɛ naasi nɛ pisi pʋʋgin (34,020).
english: He was elected with 18,705 votes out of 34,020 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Nɛ' da zɛmnɛ pisnu nɛ nu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (55%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: This was equivalent to 55% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o ka bas Pullam William onɛ bɛ Peoples' National Convention, Joseph Akudbilla onɛ bɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party ni la nɛ Anabah Joseph Benibah onɛ bɛ Convention People's Party.
english: He was elected over Pullam William of the Peoples' National Convention, Joseph Akudbillahh of the New Patriotic Party and Anabah Joseph Benibah of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔt la zɛmnɛ anu du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin 5.5%), pistan nɛ anii du'al anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (38.4%) nɛ yinne du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.1%) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: These were equivalent to 5.5%, 38.4% and 1.1% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Azumah anɛ Kristo biig (Catholic).
english: Azumah is a Christian (Catholic).

kusaal: Azumah du'am yʋʋm anɛ 1 January 1950.
english: Azumah was born on 1 January 1950.

kusaal: O nɔbignɛ Garu, teŋbil banɛ bɛ Upper East Region bɛ Ghana la.
english: He hails from Garu, a town in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Azumah anɛ Ma'asim-tiig dinɛ ka ba buon ye NDC la nid.
english: EAzumah is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: O yiiga na'am ka o di MP bɛnɛ January 1993 dinɛ ka ba da vɔɔt 1992 MP nam vɔɔtʋg la.
english: He first became a member of the parliament in January 1993 following the 1992 Ghanaian parliamentary election.

kusaal: O da bɛnɛ ani ti paae December 2000 ka Akuka Albert Alalzuuga, yʋ'ʋn kena di'e ka bas o, ka o lɛn keŋ zi'en o kɔn'ɔnkɔn' ya'as.
english: He retained the seat until December 2000 when he lost the seat to Akuka Albert Alalzuuga, who then contested as an independent candidate.

kusaal: O yitnɛ Kajaji, tempʋʋg kanɛ bɛ Bono East Region Ghana nwa.
english: He hails from Kajaji, a town in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ sakur tita'ar linɛ buon University of Education, Winneba ka di'e Bachelor of Education degree Management ni nɛ Secretarial Studies kasɛta gbauŋ.
english: He entered University of Education, Winneba, where he obtained his Bachelor of Education degree in Management and Secretarial Studies.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vot Napare ye o an wadamaan Sene East yʋʋm 2020 nwadis pii nɛ ayi' vootigin la.
english: Napare was again elected member of parliament for Sene East in the 2020 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: O da di kʋk la ka li anɛ nidib tusa pii nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ yinne (13,401) lin pa'al ye kɔbiga pʋʋgin o paam nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi nɛ pʋsʋg (64.4%) ka wabʋg New Patriotic Party nid onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Luchoun Nicholas Bitagan ka o daa nya'ad nɛ o la paam nidib tusa ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbinaasi nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi (7,424) ka lin pa'al ye kɔbiga pʋʋgin, on daa nyɛnɛ vaar pistan' nɛ a nu nɛ linɛ gaad pʋdigir bi'ela (35.7%).
english: He was declared winner in the parliamentary elections after obtaining 13,401 votes, representing 64.4% against his closest contender the New Patriotic Party candidate Luchoun Nicholas Bitagan, who had 7,424 votes, representing 35.7%.

kusaal: Dominic Aduna Bingab Nitiwul (du'anɛ November 4, 1977) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani, (MP) tis Bimbilla constituency bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Dominic Aduna Bingab Nitiwul (born 4 November 1977) is a Ghanaian politician and a Member of Parliament (MP) for the Bimbilla constituency in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la (February 2017), Nitiwul an Minister of Defence tis Gaana.
english: Nitiwul has held the office of Minister of Defence of Ghana from February 2017 to January 2025.

kusaal: Dominic Nitiwul zamis bɛdigʋ sakuya kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb Ghana, Germany, nɛ United Kingdom.
english: Dominic Nitiwul studied in various educational institutions in Ghana, Germany, and the United Kingdom.

kusaal: Dominic da naae o O level nɛ St Charles Secondary nɛ Seminary School yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la ni (1992).
english: Dominic completed his O level at St Charles Secondary and Seminary School in 1992.

kusaal: Germany teŋinɛɛ, o da maal zaba gu'ub, (conflict prevention) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan la ni (2003) nɛ zaba pansigir (conflict management) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005 International Academy for Leadership sakur la ni.
english: In Germany he earned certificates in conflict prevention (2003) and conflict management (2005) from the International Academy for Leadership.

kusaal: O da maali o Master of Business Administration in finance University of South Wales, ka maal Master of Laws in corporate finance University of Westminster.
english: He obtained his Master of Business Administration in finance from the University of South Wales, and a Master of Laws in corporate finance from the University of Westminster.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt Nitiwul ka o lieb Gaana Wadmaan yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi la ni (2002) ka anɛ yʋma pisi nɛ anu (25 years).
english: Nitiwul was elected to the parliament of Ghana in 2002 at the age of 25.

kusaal: O da anɛ Deputy Minority Leader Gaana Wadmaanib yin la yʋʋm tusa ay nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: He was the Deputy Minority Leader of the Ghanaian Parliament from 2012 to 2016.

kusaal: Nitiwul da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la, on da nyaŋ National Democratic Congress nid la Dr Joseph Mamboah Rockson.
english: Nitiwul won the 2016 Parliamentary elections for his constituency by defeating the National Democratic Congress candidate Dr Joseph Mamboah Rockson.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ay nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la dabpiinɛ atan (13 January 2017) Nitiwul da paas minista banɛ ka Pirɛsidɛn Nana Akuffo-Addo ka gaans yiiga la.
english: On 13 January 2017, Nitiwul was part of the first group of ministers designate nominated by President Nana Akuffo-Addo.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o an minista bɛ Ministry of Defence.
english: His nomination was for the Ministry of Defence.

kusaal: Nɛ' da maalnɛ o Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party, da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Gaana vɔɔtʋg la.
english: This was done after his party, the New Patriotic Party, had won power in the 2016 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Pirɛsidɛn Akuffo-Addo da gaad tuon ka Nitiwul pɔ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔi yʋʋmpaal Nwadig dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27 January 2017) ka naan pin'il tʋʋma.
english: His oath of office was administered by President Akuffo-Addo on 27 January 2017.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal Nwadig dabpisi nɛ yinne daar (21 January 2021),pirɛsidɛn da bas Nitiwul ye o an minister of Defence.
english: on the list presented to parliament for approval on 21 January 2021, Mr. Nitiwul was nominated by the president to maintain his ministerial position as the minister of Defence.

english: Working with the military high command of the Ghana Armed Forces and the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Nitiwul helped roll out measures to seize machinery, drive out the miners, and restore degraded lands in the country.

kusaal: Ban da kʋ Major Maxwell Mahama yʋʋm tusa nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadisa anu la ni (May 2017), Nitiwul da zi'il nɔɔr ye ba na vɛɛnsi di yɛla ka gban'e banɛ tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la.
english: When Major Maxwell Mahama was lynched in May 2017, Nitiwul promised that a thorough investigation would be initiated to identify and arrest the culprits.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la Nwadisa anu la ni (May, 2017,) Pirɛsidɛn Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Dominic Nitiwul ye o paas ministanam piinɛ awai banɛ ka o gaŋ ye ba an cabinet.
english: In May, 2017, President Nana Akufo-Addo named Dominic Nitiwul as part of nineteen ministers who would form his cabinet.

english: As a Cabinet minister, Nitiwul is part of the inner circle of the president and is to aid in key decision-making activities in the country.

english: Nitiwul has embarked on developmental projects in Bimbilla to better the lot of his constituents.

english: She returned to Ghana in 2012 to continue her entrepreneurship career of which she is currently the chief executive officer and Country Representative for Nano Fix IT Company, and Sebastian Closet Inc respectively.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt Affo-Toffey ye o zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress la Wadmaanib nya'ab la ni bɛ Jomoro Constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai Nwadis anii la ni (August 2019).
english: Affo-Toffey was elected as the National Democratic Congress parliamentary candidate for the Jomoro Constituency in August 2019.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusir yinne, kɔbistan nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi (1,324) dinɛ an pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (87.4%) ka nidib ayi banɛ kpɛlim la, Akatia Kwaidoo nɛ Nda Blay Armah paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (188) dinɛ an piinɛ ayi du'al anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (12.4%) nɛ anaasi (4) dinɛ an nɛɛm du'al ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.2%).
english: She got 1,324 votes (87.4%) whilst the other two candidates Akatia Kwaidoo receiving 188 votes (12.4%), and Nda Blay Armah receiving 4 votes (0.2%).

kusaal: Affo-Toffey da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Jomoro Constituency sʋ'ʋlim nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anaasi, kɔbistan nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (24,356) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnu nɛ anu du'al anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (55.5%) ka onɛ dɛŋim zin'i kʋk la zug la, Paul Essien onɛ bɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔgin, New Patriotic Party ni la paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ awai, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (19,889) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anaasi du'al piswai nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (44.95%).
english: Affo-Toffey won the 2020 parliamentary elections for Jomoro Constituency after receiving 24,356 votes representing 55.5% against the incumbent member of parliament Paul Essien of the New Patriotic Party who had 19,889 votes (44.95%).

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2021), o paas pʋ'ab pisnaasi (40) ka an on ma'a an pʋ'a yi Western Region zi'eni tisi ba sʋ'ʋlim dim wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la ni.
english: Since 7 January 2021, she has been one of the 40 women and the only one from the Western Region representing their respective constituencies in the 8th Parliament.

kusaal: O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Gender and Children nɛ Lands and Forestry Committee wadmaanib yin la.
english: She serves as a member on the Gender and Children Committee and the Lands and Forestry Committee of Parliament.

kusaal: On da ye o pian' yiiga wadmaanib yin la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadisa atan dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar la (24 March 2021), o da ye gɔmena mukim ka yɔ'ɔg border nam la ka ba yɔ COVID-19 pandemic yɛl la ka di sʋŋ ka nidib nyaŋi tʋm.
english: In her maiden address on the floor of parliament on 24 March 2021, she urged the government to reopen land borders which had been closed due to the COVID-19 pandemic to boost economic activities.

kusaal: O da pian' bɛdigʋ din nar dinɛ kɛ ka di nar ye ba yɔ'ɔg border la Jomoro Constituency zin'isieba anɛ dinɛ ka ba yɔ ka nidib pʋ nyaŋidi lɔ'ɔŋida nwɛnɛ Elubo, Jaway wharf, Newtown, Ellenda wharf nɛ tɛɛns bɛdigʋ Gaana.
english: She stressed on the urgent need to reopen and regularize land border crossing at key entry points in the Jomoro Constituency such as Elubo, Jaway wharf, Newtown, Ellenda wharf and other border towns in Ghana.

kusaal: Nɛ wala wʋsa, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadispiinɛ ayi daba awai daar (December 9th, 2021), Affo-Toffey da keŋ kɔɔtʋ la ni nɛ o lɔya, Edudzi Kudzo Tamaklo, nɛ onɛ an wadmaani tis Ellembelle, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah.
english: However, on December 9, 2021, Affo-Toffey appeared in court with her lawyer, Edudzi Kudzo Tamaklo, and the MP for Ellembelle, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, Nwadisa atan la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 March 2021), Affo-Toffey da da' Ghana Division One League club Proud United.
english: On 24 March 2021, Affo-Toffey completed the purchase of the Ghana Division One League club Proud United.

kusaal: O da tiak club la yʋ'ʋri tis Jomoro FC ka tiaki di yi Accra, Greater Accra Region keŋ Jomoro bɛ Western Region.
english: The club's name was changed to Jomoro FC and relocated from Accra, Greater Accra Region to Jomoro in the Western Region.

kusaal: Club la da ti'ebnɛ ye ba nwɛ' nɛ Crosby Awuah Memorial Park (CAM), bɛ Aiyinase, zin'ikanɛ ka Karela United yi la ban da tiak onɛ sʋ'oe la.
english: The club was set to play its home games at the Crosby Awuah Memorial Park (CAM), in Aiyinase, home grounds of Karela United following the takeover.

english: She is married and has two daughters: Francine Koffi (Fantana, a musician in Ghana) and Lynelle Koffi (a cybersecurity professional in the USA).

english: Annual production of seeds in northern Nigeria is estimated at around 200,000 t.

kusaal: Di bɛ ye biili ɛɛnti bun siem anɛ 75%, biili la bulib tun'e keŋ ba fʋgis biili la pa'akpimis la 7 minutes ka nɔki li wʋ'ʋl kuotʋʋligin nieɛ bɛo ka naam nyaŋi bʋdi di biili la.
english: Although the seeds' usual germination rate has been reported at 75%, germination can be improved by scalding for about 7 minutes, then soaking seeds in hot water overnight prior to planting.

kusaal: Ba na sin'iŋi puud yʋma atan' nɛ ayɔpɔi la teŋsʋk (5-7) ʋʋn saŋa bɛ Sahel Samampiid Nwadig la kem paae Vaala Nwadig la (December to April), amaa ka lɛɛ pʋ puud bɛ teŋbanɛ kudigid la ni.
english: They will begin to flower at 5–7 years during the dry season in the Sahel (December to April), while occurring slightly earlier in less dry regions.

kusaal: Zanzana sʋŋid ti kaŋa ka o puum la widigid, bʋnvʋbanɛ mɛ sʋŋid ka li puumla nɔbigid anɛ "siins, pʋmpɔɔs, tangbɛɛlnam, kusin'is, tenebrionid beetles nɛ tettigometid bugs." Tiig la tun'e wɛl wɛla din kʋnyi yʋma anu paae yʋma piiga la ni (5-10 years) ka li yʋ'ʋm sin'iŋi bi'igid hali ka yiiga saa la naam ti ni, ala ta kem paae sɛɛn'ʋg.
english: The tree is pollinated primarily by bats, but can also occur by way of "honeybees, flies, wasps, ants, tenebrionid beetles and tettigometid bugs." Fruiting can occur at anywhere from 5–10 years, and they will start to ripen just before the first rains and continue over most of the season.

kusaal: Ba ɛɛnti tiaki dinɛ ka di lieb seasoning, ka ba pʋdi di yʋ'ʋr ye sikomu nɛ dodowa Yoruba nɛ Hausa nidib sʋʋgʋn.
english: The seeds are processed into a seasoning, known as sikomu and dodowa/ dawadawa among the Yoruba and Hausa people respectively, and sunbala in the Inner Niger Delta.

kusaal: Ba mɔr lipid nam bɛdigʋ, nwɛnɛ pisi nɛ awai kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn (29%), protein anɛ pistan nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgʋn(35%), carbohydrates anɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn (16%), ka mɛ an bʋmbanɛ tisid kpaam nɛ calcium tis banɛ bɛ teŋkpɛmisin.
english: They are high in lipids (29%), protein (35%), carbohydrates (16%), and are a good source of fat and calcium for rural dwellers.

kusaal: Néré wala anɛ dinɛ ka ba da'ad hali bɛ Burkina Faso; "kɔbiga pʋʋgʋn, nidib gaad pisnu (50%) vɛɛnsʋg pʋʋgʋn da siak ye ba paasi di kpiisig ni.
english: Néré fruits are highly commercialized in Burkina Faso; "over 50% of respondents in a nation-wide survey said they participated in its trade." In general, women are wholly responsible for the sale of fermented seeds (dawadawa) even though men and women are equally responsible for the sale of dry seeds.

kusaal: Fʋ na nyɛ tiig kaŋa nɛ ka ba bɛ Africa bɛdigʋ ka mɔr o diib la ka li malis hali ka mɔr biilsʋma.
english: It is found in a wide range of environments in Africa and is primarily grown for its pods that contain both a sweet pulp and valuable seeds.

kusaal: di anɛ deciduous perennial dinɛ nɔbigi ka o wa'alim an 7 nɛ 20 metres, Saŋa sieba ba wa'alim tun'e paae 30 metres.
english: It is a deciduous perennial that grows to between 7 and 20 metres high, in some cases up to 30 metres.

kusaal: Tiig la wɛla la, anɛ dinɛ ka tia'am buoni li ye locust beans, ka mɔr zɛnwiid sin'im di sin'iŋirin, ka ti lɛ kilim sabil wiiʋ di ya'a ti yʋ'ʋm gu tituaa la.
english: The pods of the tree, commonly referred to as locust beans, are pink in the beginning and turn dark brown when fully mature.

kusaal: West Africa kpala nii, tiig la pak, nya'a, vaand, puum, wɛla, nɛ li biili la mɔri maan buudi tima bɛdigʋ tiebid wiim bɛdigʋ, puugin nɛ yiŋ wʋsa, saŋa sieba ka ba nɔ ti sieba gɛdigi li.
english: In West Africa, the bark, roots, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds are commonly used in traditional medicine to treat a wide diversity of complaints, both internally and externally, sometimes in combination with other medicinal plants.

kusaal: veterinary timanam ni o nya'ag la mɔri ti'ebid coccidiosis bɛ nɔɔs wimanam ni.
english: In veterinary medicine, a root decoction is used to treat coccidiosis in poultry.

kusaal: Tiig la locust mɔ tun;e mɛ lɛm buol ye "arbre à farine, fern leaf, irú, monkey cutlass tree, two ball nitta-tree, nété and néré").
english: The tree locust bean is also known as "arbre à farine, fern leaf, irú, monkey cutlass tree, two ball nitta-tree, nété and néré").

kusaal: Bam sin'iŋi mɔr wɛl pa'ad la mi'ilimid la da sin'iŋ nɛ West Africa ka ba sɔbi digil bɛ 14th century, Michel Adanson da pa'al li yɛla bɛ o Histoire naturelle du Sénégal, ka zaŋi li pa'al bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbi yɔpɔi nɛ pisnu ayɔpɔi (1757) la ni.
english: The use of fermented locust beans in West Africa was documented as early as the 14th century, and described by Michel Adanson in his Histoire naturelle du Sénégal, published in 1757.

kusaal: Amaa nananna tiig la yʋ'ʋm bɛ zin'ig wʋsa kas-kas anɛ anthropic communities anthropic communities – zin'ig kanɛ ka ba kuodi li la di ka bʋn.
english: The tree currently exists within a wide range of natural communities but is most abundant in anthropic communities – places where cultivation is semi-permanent.

kusaal: ka bam mɔr tiig la maan siel la fʋ kʋ nyɛɛ li bɛ international trade la nii, amaa ba anɛ yɛlkpan ka pʋ gʋ'ʋŋida bɛ West Africa kuam-kuam la.
english: While the products of the tree are not common in international trade, they form an important part of local and regional trade in West Africa. The seeds are especially prized, and much trade occurs locally in the Sahel region where they are transferred between borders.

kusaal: Ba bʋm biig la walim anɛ 20-25cm bakwainami pisi saŋa bɛ nursery, di anɛ saŋa kanɛ ka ba na nyaŋi nɔki ba se pɔɔding; fʋ mɛ tun'e bʋdi ba pɔɔdin la ka pʋ waali ba se, dina sʋm anɛ teŋ la sʋm an siem nɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ bɛ pʋʋgin la an siem.
english: Seedlings typically reach 20-25 centimetres tall after 20 weeks in the nursery, at which point they can be planted out into the field; direct sowing is possible, but its viability largely depends on soil moisture and the degree of insect/rodent threats.

kusaal: Yʋma ayi ka ba maal kpansib vɛɛnsigi o gbinin ma'asim la, ba kpans ya ka duan la (Parkia biglobosa) ba da "nyɛ ka o ma'asim la pʋ sʋŋid la'asiebaa ka lɛɛ sʋŋid ki yʋʋm yinne ni." Eggplant mɛ daa pʋ nyaŋi maal tituaa nɛ, ka bam paam zʋʋd la siem la atan' pʋʋgi an yinne maa nɛ yinne piiga pʋʋgin banɛ ka ba bʋdi ba yiŋ ka saa sa'ami ba.
english: In a 2-year experiment on shading, Parkia biglobosa was "found to have suppressive effects on vegetative growth and yield of pearl millet in both years." Eggplant yields were also suppressed by trees to between one third and one tenth of the yield in controlled plots, which themselves were damaged by rain.

kusaal: African dim duan la bɛdim an 0-300 metres, ka saa niib an wʋʋ 400-700 millimetre ka li tʋʋlim an 24-28°C." Di bɔɔdi zin'ikanɛ ka saa kuom la na nyaŋi silig tɔ'ɔtɔ, ya'ad tintan kanɛ tɛbis amaa di mɛ tun'e mɛ lɛm bɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka tintan la pʋ tɛbisa, tintan bi'isʋg ni.
english: The tree of the African locust bean requires "between 0-300 metres of altitude, a mean annual rainfall of between 400-700 millimetres and a mean annual temperature of about 24-28°C." It prefers well-drained, thick clay soils but can also be found on shallow, thin sandy soils.

kusaal: Ba mɔr pulp la maan danmalisa.
english: The pulp is also used to make beverages.

kusaal: Vɛɛnskanɛ ka ba da maal kpalʋg mi'igir yɛla la, vɛɛnsʋg la da pa'al ye Gmelina arborea nɛ kou kɛt ka biili la mi'igir, ka mɛ paasid kpaam, protein nɛ ma'asʋgʋ zɛm si'em, ka lɛɛ sied carbohydrate zɛm si'em.
english: In a study conducted on the fermentation of dawadawa, it was found that Gmelina arborea and banana leaves accelerated fermentation of seeds, while increasing fat, protein and moisture content, but also decreasing carbohydrate content.

kusaal: Puum la anɛ dinɛ ka siins bɛ nɔŋ hali ka lɛn an zin'ikanɛ ka di paamid nectar.
english: The flowers are attractive to bees and a good source of nectar.

kusaal: Tikaŋa kuob anɛ dinɛ mɔr nyɔɔd hali tis Africa tɛmis bɛdigʋ, la'an nɛ pʋ'ab.
english: The cultivation of this tree is an important economic activity for many in Africa, including many women.

kusaal: Tiig la mɛ lɛn anɛ dinɛ paasi ayi ni tibanɛ tibanɛ ka ba mɔri ti'ebid fɛn'ɛd bɛ South-Western Nigeria, ka kɛ ka proliferation of dermal fibroblasts paasid tɔ'ɔtɔ." Ala ka vɛɛnskan buudi mɛ da maali bɛ Guinea zaŋi keŋ tibanɛ ka ba mɔri ti'ebid dumis ban'a ba sʋ'ʋlʋm ni, ba da pa'al ye duan anɛ tikanɛ paas banɛ ka ba mɔri ti'ebid dumis ban'a la ni.
english: The tree was also one of two plants "listed as having real wound-healing properties in South-Western Nigeria, influencing the proliferation of dermal fibroblasts significantly." In a similar survey conducted in Guinea relating to their use of antimalarial plants, Parkia biglobosa was cited among those most often successfully used.

kusaal: Ban da lɛn vɛɛnsid tibanɛ kʋʋd bʋnvʋya ni, mak nɛ tibanɛ mɔr streptomycin, duan da mɔr ka di kɛ ka di paas tibanɛ na nyaŋi ti'eb bʋnvʋya ban'as.
english: In an analysis on the antibacterial properties of the plant, another study found that "these properties compare favourably with those of streptomycin, making it a potential source of compounds used in the management of bacterial infections."

kusaal: Tiig kaŋa anɛ tiig kanɛ pʋ zɔt bugim ka li anɛ om mɔr pak kanɛ an sabili wilim-wilim ka kpi'em la zu.
english: The tree is a fire-resistant heliophyte characterized by a thick dark gray-brown bark.

kusaal: Di tibanɛ waal la ɛɛnti nɔbigid tɔ'ɔtɔ' - ba tun'e nɔbig ka li wa'alim paae 1metre yʋʋm pʋʋgin.
english: Seedlings grow comparatively fast – they can reach a height of 1 metre in just 1 year.

kusaal: Zamisʋg kpansib kani ka ba yʋma atan' ka nye ka teŋ la kʋ'ʋlim kanl an 86% mamisi li nɛ sisibig kan wɛni li la ka li an 138%.
english: In one experiment, the isolated relative effect of locust bean in the third year of the experiment was 86%, compared to 138% for neem, a related tree.

kusaal: Dutar (ka sieba buon dotar; Persian: دوتار, romanized: dutâr; Russian: Дутар; Tajik: Дутор; Uzbek: Дутор; Uyghur: دۇتار, romanized: Dutar; simplified Chinese: 都塔尔; traditional Chinese: 都塔爾; pinyin: Dū tǎ ěr; Dungan: Дутар) anɛ Iranian dim buudi malʋŋ kanɛ na'asaa googi kanɛ mɔr nwiisa ayi ka niŋgɔɔnr wa'am hali ka di bɛ Iran nɛ Central Asia.
english: The dutar (also dotar; Persian: دوتار, romanized: dutâr; Russian: Дутар; Tajik: Дутор; Uzbek: Дутор; Uyghur: دۇتار, Дутар, romanized: Dutar; Dungan: Дутар) is a traditional Iranian long-necked two-stringed lute found in Iran and Central Asia.

kusaal: Di yʋ'ʋr la yinɛ Persia dim piana'akanɛ an "nwiisa ayi la", دوتار do tār (< دو do "ayi",تار tār "nwiins"), la'anɛ Herati dutar of Afghanistan mɔr nwiis piinɛ anaasi la.
english: Its name comes from the Persian word for "two strings", دوتار do tār (< دو do "two",تار tār "string"), although the Herati dutar of Afghanistan has fourteen strings.

kusaal: Dutar anɛ dinɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ mi'i di yɛla Tajikistan nɛ Khorasan province of Iran.
english: Dutar is very popular in Tajikistan and Khorasan province of Iran.

kusaal: La'abanɛ nwɛnɛ li anɛ Kazakh dombra.
english: Related instruments include the Kazakh dombra.

kusaal: Dutar la mɛ anɛ bʋnkanɛ yela pak hali bɛ Kurds of Khorasan la'ad la pʋʋgin ka Haj Ghorban Soleimani dinɛ yi Quchan la gati ba wʋsa.
english: The dutar is also an important instrument among the tork of Khorasan amongst whom Haj Ghorban Soleimani of Quchan was a noted virtuoso.

kusaal: Kurdish teŋin ba buon onɛ nwɛ'ɛd dutar la nɛ bakci (bakhshi) yinne nɛ Turkmen bagşy, ka Azeri teŋin ba buonɛ ye ashiq.
english: In tork one who plays the dutar is known as a bakci (bakhshi) similar to Turkmen bagşy, while in Azeri the term is ashiq.

kusaal: Khorasan bakhshi music mɛ paasnɛ Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
english: Khorasan bakhshi music is recognized on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Nɛ wala wʋsa ban da yɔ'ɔg Silk Road, catgut da bas suori tis banɛ ka ba maali ba ban na vilig nwiins la ka zaŋi li tud China.
english: However, with the opening up of the Silk Road, catgut gave way to strings made from twisted silk imported from China.

kusaal: Front and back views of Dutar Haj Ghorban Soleimani (1920–2008)
english: Haj Ghorban Soleimani (1920–2008)

kusaal: Ba ya'a nwɛ' di,nwiis la ɛɛnti gu' nɛ Uyghurs dinɛ bɛ Western China la ka gu' ka suoen Tajiks, Turkmen, Uzbeks.
english: When played, the strings are usually plucked by the Uyghurs of Western China and strummed and plucked by the Tajiks, Turkmen, Uzbeks.

kusaal: Hali nɛ zina ba ɛɛnti nɔknɛ nwiisi viligi maal, la'anɛ nylon nwiisi bɛ zin'ig wʋsa la.
english: To this day some instruments still feature silk strings, although nylon or steel strings are also commonly used.

kusaal: Dutar la mɔr kʋkuma kanɛ dʋt, dulcet tone.
english: The dutar has a warm, dulcet tone.

kusaal: Di kʋkuma ɛɛnti dɔlnɛ La Re bɛɛ A D, amaa di bɛnɛ region la ni.
english: Typically it is tuned La Re or A D, but it also depends on the region.

kusaal: Dutar maaalʋg mi'ilim nɛ buudi malima yʋʋma ka ba la'asi di nɛ asi di nɛ asi di nɛ yʋʋma aditional music performing art combined with singing from 2021 representative on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists.
english: Khorasan bakhshi music is recognized on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
