english: Haj Ghorban Soleimani (1920–2008)

kusaal: O da anɛ Tourism minista nya'andɔl ka ba buon Na'asaalin ye Deputy Minista la n tis Ma'asim Tiig paati (NDC) saŋkanɛ ka ba paati la da an Ghana gɔmina la yʋʋm 2013 nɛ 2017.
english: She was the Deputy Minister of Tourism between 2013 and 2017 during President John Mahama's first term and the substantive sector minister in the Mahama government from 2025.

kusaal: Patrick Dotse Gomashie nɛ o Pu'a Helen Gomashie da du'a Gomashie nɛ Ankara (Accra).
english: Gomashie was born in Accra to Mr Patrick Dotse Gomashie and Helen Gomashie.

kusaal: O yitnɛ Aflo n bɛ Volta Region la.
english: She hails from Aflao in the Volta region and was born on July 5, 1965.

kusaal: Gomashie da pin'ili o sigiilima itima yɛla nɛ yʋʋm 1985 saŋkanɛ ka o da la'asnɛ Talents Theatre Company la.
english: Gomashie's began her actress career in 1985 when she joined the Talents Theatre Company.

kusaal: O da la'amnɛ nɛ sigiilim nwa'adib n maal sigiilima banɛ an 'Black Star', 'Mambo', 'Chaka the Zulu', 'Jogolo' nɛ The Third Woman.
english: She has featured in plays like Black Star, Mambo, Chaka the Zulu, Jogolo and The Third Woman.

kusaal: Li ya'a yi sigiilima itima ni, o mɔr diib kuosug zi'ig ka li buon ye 'Mama's Kitchen' bɛ Ashale Botwe, [1] linɛ pʋ lɛm bɛ tʋʋma nii.
english: Aside acting, she owned a restaurant called 'Mama's Kitchen' at Ashale Botwe, which is no longer in operation.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2013 la ni, Zugraan John Dramani Mahama da gaŋi o ka o an deputy Minista tis Tourism, Arts nɛ Culture, kpeŋ kanɛ ka o zanl hali ti paae o paati saŋa la.
english: In 2013, she was nominated and appointed into office as the deputy Minister of Tourism, Arts & Culture by President John Dramani Mahama, a position she held until her party, the NDC lost the elections and handed over to the next government in 2017.

kusaal: Gomashie da anɛ Poverty Reduction Strategy kpɛɛm ka mɛ da lɛn an banɛ gɔsid Tɔlʋŋ nɛ Lʋgir kanɛ maan la'ad nɛ Zin'ibanɛ ka nidib kennɛ gɔsid (Tʋʋm Trade, Industry nɛ Tourism) kpɛɛm yinne.
english: Gomashie is a member of the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee and also a member of the Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee.

kusaal: Gomashie da ɛlnɛ Martin K. Ahiaglo onɛ kpi la.
english: Gomashie was married to the late Martin K.G Ahiaglo.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ Na'asaa nwadis ayɔpɔi an Mɔraug Nwadig la dabis 25 yʋʋm 1965.
english: She hails from Aflao in the Volta region and was born on July 5, 1965.

kusaal: Ba da pʋ du'a biisɛ.
english: The couple had no child together.

kusaal: Anasazi nif ni'ɛr saŋa ba mɛ da mɛ dɔbɛda, li si'eba an dɔkʋda bɛ North America, nɛ Maya bɛ Central America linɛ da mɔr dɔɔd banɛ ka ba mɛ tituaaa yʋʋma kɔbiga (hundred AD) saŋa.
english: The Anasazi civilization also had an early complex development of room structures, probably the oldest in North America, while the Maya of Central America had very advanced room configurations as early as several hundred AD.

kusaal: United Kingdom tɛŋin, ya' bɛdigʋ mɔr dɔbibis ka ba buon box-room (box room bɛɛ boxroom) ka din bɛɛ di kɔn'ɔ baŋid, ban pɔɔdi gati ba taaba.
english: In the United Kingdom, many houses are built to contain a box-room (box room or boxroom) that is easily identifiable, being smaller than the others.

kusaal: Pin'ilig sa, tita'am anɛ country houses nɛ suburban houses bɛda ni, di da anɛ ala kɛŋ paae yʋʋma tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' (1930s) saŋa, Britain, ka box room la yʋ'ʋn da anɛ ye ba sʋ'a box nam, trunks, portmanteaux, nɛ la'ad si'eba, ka lɛn ka'a dɔgbɛn'ɛda ya'asɛ.
english: Traditionally, and often seen in country houses and larger suburban houses up until the 1930s in Britain, the box room was for the storage of boxes, trunks, portmanteaux, and the like, rather than for bedroom use.

kusaal: Ireland tɛŋin, return room anɛ box room kanɛ ka ba mɛ' girimbiisi zug nɛ tɛŋin wʋsa, zin'ig kanɛ dɔlli dʋt la gɔnligir ni nɔɔ.
english: In Ireland, a return room is a box room added between floors at the turn ("return") of a staircase.

kusaal: Mɛɛb pʋʋgin bɛɛ ship pʋʋgin, dɔɔg anɛ paalʋ kanɛ ka zanguoma bɛdigʋ lus ka mɔr za'anɔɔr zin'ig kanɛ dɔlli yit ka kpɛn'ɛd, bɛɛ ba gbi'e zin'ig si'a bas.
english: In a building or a ship, a room is any enclosed space within a structure, typically bounded by walls to which entry is possible only via a door or other dividing structure.

kusaal: Din pin'il si'em la, ba da pin'ili bɛ dɔɔdin ka li gaad Minoan cultures pin'ilig saŋa sa, yʋʋma tusayi', nɛ kɔbisyi (2200 BC) ya'aŋ, ba da lɛɛk titan Akrotiri linɛ bɛ Santorini ka nyɛ ka li pa'al yɛ dɔɔd da bɛ mɛ'sieba pʋʋgin.
english: Historically, the use of rooms dates at least to early Minoan cultures about 2200 BC, where excavations at Akrotiri on Santorini reveal clearly defined rooms within certain structures.

kusaal: Akrotiri linɛ ka ti pian' li yɛla yiiga la, ba da nyɛ dɔɔd ka ba mɛ pa'ali ba taaba zug ka mɛ ban dɔl lɔsia dʋt ka sigid, sʋʋb dɔɔd ka la'asi'eba bɛɛ anina wan wʋʋ sʋʋb tan laas, ku'onwiins, nɛ dʋʋnim dɔɔd, ka li wʋsa tɔ'ɔŋ nɛ tan kuosuoya banɛ ka ba maali paae ku'omin, ka li mɔr ku'oma'asig bʋn nɛ ku'otʋʋlig bʋn.
english: The aforementioned Akrotiri excavations reveal rooms sometimes built above other rooms connected by staircases, bathrooms with alabaster appliances such as washbasins, bathing tubs, and toilets, all connected to an elaborate twin plumbing systems of ceramic pipes for cold and hot water separately.

kusaal: Han dynasty pin'ilig, China sʋ'ʋlim (na wan wʋʋ wan wʋʋ yʋʋma kɔbisyi, 200 BC)], dɔsʋma bɛda da pin'il ya, li kas-kas zin'is banɛ ka nidib bɛdigʋ la'asid nɛ winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔd; ba da mɛ dɔɔd la bʋʋdi kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ka mɛ lɛn mɛ' dɔsi'eb pa'ali ba taaba zug.
english: By at least the early Han dynasty in China (e.g. approximately 200 BC), comfort room complex multi-level building forms emerged, particularly for religious and public purposes; these designs featured many roomed structures and included vertical connections of rooms.

kusaal: 17th, 18th, nɛ 19th centuries ni, banɛ da an kpan'am dim la da mɛɛd dɔbama kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb, ka pʋ la'asidi baa.
english: In the 17th, 18th, and 19th centuries, among those who could afford it, these facilities were kept in separate areas.

kusaal: Dɔɔg yinne da bɛ an dau la dɔɔg ka ba buon man cave; ka kʋdimin dim da buon cabinet , banɛ bɔɔd ye ba mɔri ba dɔɔdi ba kɔn'ɔ la.
english: One decorated to appeal to a man might be called a man cave; in an older style, the cabinet was used by men who wanted a separate room.

kusaal: Ya'bɛda da mɔr dɔɔd banɛ bɛɛ ba kɔn'ɔ, ka ban an di'ema dɔɔd; bama si'eba an library, home theater, billiard room, game room, nɛ yʋʋma dɔɔg.
english: Some large homes have special rooms for entertainment; these may include a library, a home theater, a billiard room, a game room, or a music room.

kusaal: Master bedroom mɔr dɔɔd bɛdigʋ di pʋʋgin.
english: A master bedroom may have an en suite bathroom.

kusaal: Bedsit, communal apartment, bɛɛ studio apartment pʋʋsin, ba tɔn'ɔ nɔk dɔɔg tita'ar yinne tʋm tʋʋma bɛdigʋ di pʋʋgin, ya'a ka'a sʋʋb dɔɔg nɛ bin dɔɔd la ma'a kʋ nyaŋ ala.
english: In a bedsit, communal apartment, or studio apartment, a single main room may serve most functions, except usually the toilet and bath.

kusaal: Zin'isieba, lady's boudoir da la'as nɛ pʋ'ab dɔgbɛn'ɛdig nɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka on nɛ o zu'a nam bi'ela na nyaŋi kpɛ'ɛ anina.
english: In some places, a lady's boudoir was a combination sleeping room and place to entertain small numbers of friends.

kusaal: "En-suite" pa'al ye nid yinne zin'ig, li kas-kas anɛ li ya'a an sakur bil dɔɔg.
english: "En-suite" usually indicates a private space, especially if it is student accommodation.

kusaal: En-suite rooms banɛ ka sakur biis bɛɛ anina anɛ ye li mɔr paalʋ ka o zamisid ka zin'ig la mɛ an lamm.
english: En-suite rooms for students are intended to provide study space and a peaceful environment.

kusaal: Nursery anɛ biis dɔɔg gbɛn'ɛdig.
english: The nursery is a bedroom for babies or young children.

kusaal: Za'anɔɔr la dɔlnɛ suori yit bɛɛ kpɛn'ɛd dɔɔd sieba ni, bɛ dɔlli yit yaŋirin.
english: The entrance connects it to either a passageway, another room, or the outdoors.

kusaal: Eastern region Ya-Ya'aŋ titɔdig anɛ Lake Volta kuom la, ka li datiʋŋ an Bono East Region nɛ Ashanti region, ka li Ya-tuona titɔndig lɛn an Ashanti region, ka li dagɔbʋg an Central region nɛ Greater Accra Region.
english: Eastern Region is bordered to the east by the Lake Volta, to the north by Bono East Region and Ashanti region, to the west by Ashanti Region, to the south by Central Region and Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Akans buudi la an banɛ zu'oe bɛ Eastern region, ka Akan, Ewe, Krobo, Hausa nɛ na'asaal an buudi pian'ad banɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ pian'ad ani.
english: Akans are the dominant inhabitants and natives of Eastern Region, and Akan, Ewe, Krobo, Hausa and English are the main spoken languages.

kusaal: Eastern Region tɛmpʋʋg anɛ Koforidua.
english: The capital town of Eastern Region is Koforidua.

kusaal: Eastern region tɛŋgbaʋŋ bɛn labisim anɛ 19,323 square kilometres, ka lin anɛ wʋʋ anii nɛ pʋdigir yinne kɔbʋga pʋʋgin (8.1%) Ghana tɛŋgbaʋŋ sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.
english: Eastern Region covers an area of 19,323 square kilometres, which is about 8.1% of Ghana's total landform.

kusaal: Na'asaa bugum, Akosombo kuom la bɛdegʋ yitnɛ zin'is atan' bama: the Black Volta; White Volta nɛ Red Volta ka Akosombo kuom nwa pʋbʋdi kpɛ'ɛd Gulf of Guinea linɛ bɛ Atlantic Ocean.
english: High-capacity electricity generation Akosombo Hydroelectric Project contains three main tributaries: the Black Volta; the White Volta and the Red Volta and the Akosombo Hydroelectric Project flows into the Gulf of Guinea on the Atlantic Ocean.

kusaal: Akosombo Dam da si'iŋ tʋʋma nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai, nɛ pisyuobu nɛ anu 1(965), li da anɛ Volta River dim tʋʋma.
english: The Akosombo Dam was completed in 1965 as part of the Volta River Project.

kusaal: Kɔlʋg la zuluŋ anɛ nɔbir yakir kɔbʋs naasi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anaasi (440 ft same as134 m).
english: The dam measures at 440 ft (134 m) above ground level.

kusaal: Li kuom la mɔr paŋi yaŋidi vɛ'ɛgid na'asaa bugum wʋʋ kɔbʋs wai nɛ piiga nɛ ayi' (912 megawatts).
english: The large electric power generating capacity is 912 megawatts.

kusaal: Pʋ'ʋsim la na nyaŋi nwɛ'ɛ nyɔ'ɔg ye ba mɔr sakurnam ka sieba an Hecta School Complex, linɛ da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayi' (1962), ka sieba lɛn paas.
english: The region also boasts of some quality basic schools, one of which is Hecta School Complex, established in 1962, and others.

kusaal: · Presbyterian University College (Abetifi Kwahu)
english: Presbyterian University College (Abetifi Kwahu)

kusaal: · Presbyterian University college (Akropong)
english: Presbyterian University college (Akropong)

kusaal: Ba da nwaae Achiase District nɛ yi Birim South District linɛ da bɛ la ka pin'il o tʋʋma yʋʋma tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ awai, yʋʋm paal nwadig, dabisa pisi nɛ ayi' daar (22 February 2019).
english: Achiase District was carved out of the existing Birim South District and inaugurated on 22 February 2019.

kusaal: Afram Plains District mɛ pʋdʋg nɛ zin'is ayi' ka ba tiaki li yʋ'ʋr yɛ Kwahu Afram Plains North District ka li tɛnpʋʋg an Donkorkrom, nɛ Kwahu Afram Plains South District ka li tɛnpʋʋg an Tease.
english: The Afram Plains District has since been split into two and renamed as Kwahu Afram Plains North District with its capital being Donkorkrom and Kwahu Afram Plains South District with its capital also being Tease.

kusaal: Akuapim South District, East Akim District nɛ Kwahu West Districts nyɛ nɔbigiri yʋ'ʋn anɛ Municipal ka Birim Central Municipal District linɛ nan an paal la.
english: The Akuapim South District, East Akim District and Kwahu West Districts have been upgraded to municipal status with the addition of Birim Central Municipal District, which is entirely new.

kusaal: Districts paala sieba an Akyemansa District nɛ Kwahu East District.
english: Other new districts include Akyemansa District and Kwahu East District.

kusaal: Manya Krobo District mɛ pʋdʋgnɛ yʋ'ʋn an Lower Manya Krobo District nɛ Upper Manya Krobo District.
english: The Manya Krobo District has been split into Lower Manya Krobo District and Upper Manya Krobo District.

kusaal: MMDA's la da nɔbigi yii awai nii paae piiga nɛ anu (9 to 15), yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii la (1988); ka lɛn nɔbigi yi piiga nɛ anu la nii kɛŋ piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi (15 to 17) yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ anaasi la (2004); ka lɛŋ yi piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi kɛŋ paae pisi nɛ ayinne (17 to 21) yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ anii la (2008); li da lɛn nɔbigi yi pisi nɛ yinne la kɛŋ paae pisi nɛ ayuobu (21 to 26) yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayi' la (2012); li pʋ yʋʋgɛ ka li yi pisi nɛ ayi' kɛŋ pistan' nɛ atan' (26 to 33) yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii la (2018).
english: The MMDAs were increased from 9 to 15 in 1988, then from 15 to 17 in 2004, then from 17 to 21 in 2008, then from 21 to 26 in 2012, and recently from 26 to 33 in 2018.

kusaal: Eastern Region bɛnɛ Ya-ya'aŋ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka anɛ administrative region nam pii nɛ ayuobu banɛ bɛ Ghana la yinnɛ.
english: The Eastern Region is located in the eastern part of Ghana and is one of the sixteen administrative regions of Ghana.

kusaal: Eastern region ka Akosombo dam bɛ ka linɛ sʋŋidi ba da'a diib anɛ na'asaa bugum linɛ buon electricity generation la.
english: The Eastern Region is the location of the Akosombo Dam, and the economy of the Eastern Region is dominated by its high-capacity electricity generation.

kusaal: Region la tʋmmi li tʋʋma nɛ dɔlisid local government system.
english: The political administration of the region is through the local government system.

kusaal: Ka lin pa'al siem la anɛ yɛ, region la pʋdʋg nɛ MMDA's ban pistan' nɛ atan' (33), ka nidib la mɛŋ gaŋi ba kpɛɛm.
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into 33 MMDAs, each headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Ebenezer Begyina Sekyi Hughes (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pistan' nɛ wai nwadis awai la daba anaasi daar, 4 September 1939) ka o da ane gɔmena wada maanib kpɛɛm (Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana) yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ anu la ni, (2005) kem paae yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: Ebenezer Begyina Sekyi Hughes (born 4 September 1939) was the Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana between 2005 and 2009.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ebenezer Sekyi-Hughes nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pistan' nɛ wai nwadis awai la daba anaasi daar, (4 September 1939) bɛ Cape Coast, line bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Ebenezer Sekyi-Hughes was born on 4 September 1939 at Cape Coast, the capital of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da pin'il o sakur kennɛ Cape Coast Government dasam sakur la ni (line yʋn an Philip Quaque dasam sakur la).
english: From 1945 to 1953, he had his basic education at Cape Coast Government Boys School (now the Philip Quaque Boys School), founded c.

kusaal: O da keŋ o secondary education nɛ Adisadel College, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisnu' nɛ anaasi la nii (1954) keŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu la ni (1960).
english: His secondary education was at Adisadel College between 1954 and 1960.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ yinne la ni (1961), O da paam suori keŋ University of Ghana, Legon, ka da zamisi paam Bachelor of Arts kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ anaasi la ni (1964).
english: In 1961 he gained admission to the University of Ghana, Legon, where he obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1964.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ Ghana School of Law, zamisi yina nɛ kasɛta gbaʋŋ (LLB) yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu la ni (1966).
english: He then attended the Ghana School of Law, graduating with an LLB in 1966.

kusaal: Ebenezer Sekyi-Hughes da kilim Ghana kɔɔtʋ ni tʋmtʋm, da anɛ barrister nɛ solicitor tis nɛ Supreme Court of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu la ni (1966).
english: Ebenezer Sekyi-Hughes was admitted to the Ghana Bar as a barrister and solicitor of the Supreme Court of Ghana in 1966.

kusaal: O da tum kɔɔtɔ tʋʋma nɛ wada tʋʋma bɛ Accra nɛ Takoradi linɛ bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim la yʋʋmtusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu nwadis piiga la ni (October 1966).
english: He was in private legal practice in Accra and Takoradi in the Western Region from October 1966.

kusaal: O da paam kpɛŋ kanɛ yʋʋri buon Notary Public yitnɛ Ghana banɛ gɔsid wada tʋʋma kpɛɛm (Chief Justice of Ghana) yʋʋmtusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi la ni (1974).
english: He was appointed notary public by the Chief Justice of Ghana in 1974.

kusaal: O da nɔbigi lieb Senior Advocate yʋʋmtusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai la ni (1990).
english: He rose to the level of Senior Advocate in 1990.

kusaal: Sekyi-Hughes da anɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim kpɛɛm tis Ghana Bar Association yʋʋmtusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1977) kem paae yʋʋmtusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnii la ni (1981).
english: Sekyi-Hughes was the President of the Western Region Branch of the Ghana Bar Association from 1977 to 1981.

kusaal: O da paas Judicial Council of Ghana yʋʋm kan la.
english: He was also a member of the Judicial Council of Ghana during the same period.

kusaal: Sekyi-Hughes tɛŋ na'anam nɛ o tɛŋ nidib (Western Region sʋ'ʋlim) da gaŋ o ye o paasi sa'an Ghana teŋ nɔbigir yɛla (Council of State of Ghana), yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ yinne la ni (2001).
english: Sekyi-Hughes was elected by the chiefs and people of the Western Region to the Council of State of Ghana in 2001.

kusaal: On da nya' na'adɔɔg First National Vice-Chairman ka da kɔ'ɔŋ yʋʋmtusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai saŋa la (1990), o da kpɛn bɛ o na'adɔɔg la ni', nɛ on ti nya' na'am ka yʋ'ʋn di' ya'an, ka da an National Council of Elders ka lin nya'aŋ ka ba gaŋ o ye o an Ghana wada maanib kpɛɛm (Speaker of Parliament), na'adɔɔg kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon NPP na'am saŋa la.
english: Although he lost elections as the first National Vice-Chairman in the late 1990s, he remained loyal to the party until he was re-elected to the National Council of Elders and subsequently appointed as the Speaker of Parliament during the NPP Administration.

kusaal: Philip Quaque, da pin'il sakur nwa' yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs yɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayʋobu la ni' (1766), onɛ da an yiiga sɔb, ninsabilis teŋin ka Anglican winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg dim da maal o kpɛɛm.
english: 1766 by Philip Quaque, the first African to be ordained an Anglican vicar.

kusaal: Sekyi-Hughes Mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis ayuobʋ.
english: Sekyi-Hughes is married with six children.

kusaal: Ebenezer Gilbert Nii Narh Nartey anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Ablekuma Central Constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim la wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Ebenezer Gilbert Nii Narh Nartey (born 16 July 1979) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ablekuma Central Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Ningo bɛ Greater Accra Region la.
english: He hails from Ningo in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: O mɔrnɛ Diploma in Human Resource Management dinɛ ka paam yi Institute of Commercial Management, Diploma in Architectural Draftsmanship yi Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology nɛ NVTI kasɛta gbaʋŋ ka da paam yi Modern School of Draftsmanship.
english: A Diploma in Architectural Draftsmanship from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology and NVTI Certificate from the Modern School of Draftsmanship.

kusaal: O da pa'anɛ Islamic Education Programme din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005).
english: Nartey taught at Islamic Education Programme from 2004 to 2005.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Executive Secretary tis Hands that Care Asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ lʋgʋr.
english: He was also the Executive Secretary for Hands that Care NGO.

kusaal: Onɛ da lɛn an Deputy Clients Service Manager nya'andɔl din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011) bɛ Lands Commission ka lɛn an managing director tis Ednark Limited din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: He was the Deputy Clients Service Manager from 2007 to 2011 at Lands Commission and the managing director of Ednark Limited from 2011 to 2016.

kusaal: O paasnɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic party.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Ablekuma Central Constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region.
english: He is the member of parliament for Ablekuma Central Constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo Kum (dʋ'anɛ Tini daar 17 April 1967) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd, lɔya nɛ wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi nɛ anii Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Ahanta West Constituency bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party zug.
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum (born Monday 17 April 1967) is a Ghanaian politician, a lawyer who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and currently a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ahanta West Constituency in the Western Region of Ghana on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Ebenezer Kojo Kum nɛ Dixcove ka o mɛ yii anina n bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum was born and hails from Dixcove in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo Kum da maali o Ordinary Level (O - Level) yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1984) ka maal Advanced Level (A - Level) yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1986).
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum obtained his Ordinary Level(O - Level) in 1984 and Advanced Level(A - Level) in 1986.

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo Kum da tɔlisi maali Bachelor of Arts(Hons) nɛ Diploma in Education, bama wʋsa yi University of Cape Coast yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne la ni (1991) ka maal Barrister-at-Law (General Practice) Ghana School of Law ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni (2020).
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum proceeded to have his Bachelor of Arts(Hons) and Diploma in Education, all from the University of Cape Coast in 1991 and Barrister-at-Law (General Practice) at Ghana School of Law in the year 2020.

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo Kum da anɛ Deputy Director/Principal Cultural Officer/Senior Cultural Officer din yi yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) tis Centre for National Culture.
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum was the Deputy Director/Principal Cultural Officer/Senior Cultural Officer from 1992 to 2005 at the Centre for National Culture.

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo Kum da lɛn anɛ junior lawyer yʋʋm tusa ayi (2000) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi la ni (2002) bɛ Kendicks Law Firm, an Associate partner yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2002) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2007) mɛn ka lɛn an General Manager yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2007) paae yʋʋm rusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016) bɛ Kendicks Law Firm.
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum was also a junior lawyer from 2000 to 2002 at Kendicks Law Firm, an Associate partner from 2002 to 2007 as well as the General Manager from 2007 to 2016 at the Kendicks Law Firm.

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo yʋ'ʋn anɛ Wadmaani, Member of Parliament (MP) tis Ahanta West Constituency bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la dim Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party la zug.
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum is now working as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Ahanta West Constituency in the Western Region of Ghana on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo Kum da nya' ka di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Ahanta West Constituency in the Western Region, Ghana.
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum contested and won the 2016 NPP parliamentary primaries for Ahanta West Constituency in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo Kum da keŋ tuoni di sʋ'ʋlim la kʋk la (Ahanta West Constituency) bɛ Western Region, Ghana yʋʋm tysa yi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la (2016 Ghanaian general elections) Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la zug, New Patriotic Party ka keŋ paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan, kɔbisnu nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ (30,596) pisyuobʋ nɛ anii du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (68.1%) ka George Kwame Aboagye(onɛ maal ka'alim) onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid la paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ atan, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (13,784) pistan du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (30.7%) ka Isaac Kweku Annan onɛ an Convention People's Party(CPP) nid la paam vɔɔt kɔbisnu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (546) yinne du'al ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.2%).
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum proceeded to win the parliamentary seat in his constituency (Ahanta West Constituency) in the Western Region of Ghana during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party to join the Seventh (7th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana with 30,596 votes (68.1%) against George Kwame Aboagye(Late) of the National Democratic Congress who had 13,784 votes (30.7%) and Isaac Kweku Annan of the Convention People's Party(CPP) who had 546 votes (1.2%).

kusaal: Ebenezer Kojo Kum da lɛn nya' ka di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la tis Ahanta West Constituency bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana nɛ vɔɔt kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi (472) pisyuobʋ nɛ anu du'al pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (65.46%) ka Kwesi Biney paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (249) pistan nɛ anaasi du'al pisnu nɛ anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (34.54%).
english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum again contested and won the 2020 NPP parliamentary primaries for Ahanta West Constituency in the Western Region of Ghana with 472 votes(65.46%) against Kwesi Biney who had 249 votes (34.54%).

english: Ebenezer Kojo Kum again proceeded to win in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana with 27,946 votes (51.60%) against Dr. Emmanuel Okumi Andoh (a former Pro-Vice Chancellor of the Takoradi Technical University) of the National Democratic Congress who had 23,957 votes (44.24%), Ismail Buadii of the Ghana Union Movement (GUM) who had 1,797 votes (3.32%), Ebo Mensah of the Convention People's Party (CPP) who had 214 votes (0.40%), Nathaniel Adusei of the All People's Congress (APC) who had 139 votes (0.25%) and Dominic Akalga of the People's National Convention (PNC) who also had 101 votes (0.18%).

kusaal: Ba tɛnr Tagoe yela nɛ on da paasi maal sininam ayi banɛ an: As the hippie "Presuming Ed" yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yɔpɔi (1987) nɛ Withnail and I, tʋʋm kanɛ ka o da pin'ili tʋm sini kan pʋʋgin yʋʋm tusayi la (2000); ka lɛn maali sini kanɛ ka o an kuomin faandi bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne ka ba pʋd ye Raiders of the Lost Ark.
english: Tagoe is best-remembered for minor supporting roles in two film classics: As the hippie "Presuming Ed" in the 1987 film production of Withnail and I, a role that he resumed in 2000 in a stage production of the same work; and as one of the pirates in the 1981 movie Raiders of the Lost Ark.

kusaal: Tagoe da yi sini kanɛ ka ba pʋd yʋ'ʋr ye, Who Is Killing the Great Chefs of Europe?
english: Tagoe had a significantly larger part in his film debut, Who Is Killing the Great Chefs of Europe?

kusaal: (1978) la, ka lɛn an "Chocolate Mousse" yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnasi nɛ anaasi (1984) sini kanɛ an, Top Secret!
english: (1978), and as "Chocolate Mousse" in the 1984 farce, Top Secret!.

kusaal: Gwambe bɛ Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend (1985), nɛ The Dogs of War (1980), Pink Floyd The Wall (1982) nɛ Spaghetti House (1982).
english: He appeared in various other roles such as Sgt. Gwambe in Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend (1985), as well as The Dogs of War (1980), Pink Floyd The Wall (1982) and Spaghetti House (1982).

kusaal: Tagoe mɛ paasi maal sininam bɛdigʋ bɛ British television ni, ba si'eba an Legacy of Murder, Prospects, nɛ The Bill, ka li kɛ ka nidib bɛdigʋ baŋ o bɛ British TV ni ye o anɛ sini maan.
english: Tagoe also appeared in episodes of a number of British television series, including Legacy of Murder, Prospects, and The Bill, becoming "a well-known face on British television as an actor".

kusaal: In yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu (1995) la, o da lɛb o nu'us nɛ nɔba laafi zamisig la pʋʋgin, ka ba gaŋ o ye o aan li tʋmtʋmi bɛ Newcastle United F.C.
english: In 1995, he returned to his original career choice when he was recruited to serve as team reflexologist for Newcastle United F.C.

kusaal: O da paasi maal sininam bɛdigʋ wʋʋ ban da pʋd o Sgt.
english: He appeared in various other roles such as Sgt. Gwambe in Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend (1985), as well as The Dogs of War (1980), Pink Floyd The Wall (1982) and Spaghetti House (1982).

kusaal: Edward Abamire Bawa (n du'a Sibiddaar, 1 September, 1973) la anɛ Ghana Na'am nya'ad onɛ da Parliament kpeem Yinne ka nan paas ba ni n tit Bongo sʋ'ʋlimin n bɛ Upper East Ghana Teŋin n tisid Ma'asim tiig (NDC) la'asʋg la.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa (born 1 September 1973) is a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and served as a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Bongo (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Upper East Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Edward Abamire Bawa anɛ ka ba da du'a o ka o yit Bongo-Lungu n bɛ Upper East Ghana la.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa was born and hails from Bongo-Lungu in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Edward Abamire Bawa da n sɔb akarimgaadtaaba 1886 linɛ da sʋŋ o ka o nyaŋ kasɛta gbana (O-ziesim) 1991 ni nɛ Tuon kasɛta gbauŋ (A-ziesim) 1993 ni.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa passed his Common Entrance Examination in 1986 which enabled him obtain his Ordinary Level(O – Level) in 1991 and Advanced Level(A – Level) in 1993.

kusaal: Edward Abamire Bawa da tɔlisi keŋ Cape Coast University la ni yʋʋm 2002 ka lɛm keŋ Liverpool University la nii yʋʋm 2007 n zamis ligidi yela.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa proceeded to have his Bachelor of Education in Chemistry from the University of Cape Coast, Ghana in the year 2002, Master of Business Administration in Business Finance from the University of Liverpool in the year 2007, Certificate in Development Communications in the year 2012, Certificate in Risk Communications in the year 2014.

kusaal: Edward Abambire Bawa anɛ tuongat tis pian'ad-pia'an Dunia wusa Ligid dɔɔgin Tʋʋma (kpaam nɛ nyɔ'ɔns tʋʋma) n bɛ Kpaam tʋʋma Lʋgir Accra la.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa is the Head of Communication for World Bank project (oil and gas capacity building project) of the Ministry of Petroleum in Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: Edward Abambire da zien tis NDC kʋk la 2016 Bongo sʋ'ʋlim ka di.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa contested and won the 2016 NDC parliamentary primaries for Bongo Constituency in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Edward Abambire Bawa da lɛm paam NDC kʋk la 2020 tis Bongo sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa again contested and won the 2020 NDC parliamentary primaries for Bongo Constituency in the Upper East Region of Ghana with 590 votes against Dr. Rainer Akumperigya who had 291 votes.

kusaal: Edward Abambire Bawa yʋʋn anɛ MP nananna n tit Bongo teŋin Upper East Ghana ni Ma'asim Tiig na'am Lʋgir la.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa again contested and won the 2020 NDC parliamentary primaries for Bongo Constituency in the Upper East Region of Ghana with 590 votes against Dr. Rainer Akumperigya who had 291 votes.

kusaal: Edward Abambire Bawa anɛ Asie Nɔŋ suoya kpeem yinne.
english: Edward Abambire Bawa was a member of the Poverty Reduction strategy Committee.

kusaal: Akufo-Addo du'am yʋʋm anɛ 26 June 1906 bɛ Dodowa, Greater Accra Region tis o saam William Martin Addo-Danquah nɛ o ma Theodora Amuafi.
english: Akufo-Addo was born on 26 June 1906 at Dodowa in the Greater Accra Region to William Martin Addo-Danquah and Theodora Amuafi.

kusaal: O da kɛŋi o primary sakur nɛ bɛ Presbyterian Primary nɛ Middle Schools bɛ Akropong.
english: He had his primary education at Presbyterian Primary and Middle Schools at Akropong.

kusaal: O kɛŋi o kɔligi nɛ Presbyterian Training College, Akropong nɛ Abetifi Theological Training College.
english: He continued to Presbyterian Training College, Akropong and Abetifi Theological Training College.

kusaal: Ka 1929 ni, o kpɛn' Achimota College, dinɛ ka o da paam scholarship kɛŋ St Peter's College, Oxford.
english: In 1929, he entered Achimota College, where he won a scholarship to St Peter's College, Oxford.

kusaal: O da zamisnɛ mathematics, Politics nɛ Philosophy ka da naae nɛ kasɛta gbana bɛ philosophy nɛ politics bɛ1933 ni.
english: He studied mathematics, Politics and Philosophy and he went on to graduate with honours in philosophy and politics in 1933.

kusaal: Akufo-Addo ka ba da buol o bɛ Middle Temple Bar, London, UK, bɛ 1940 ni ka naami anina lɛb dinɛ ka ba buon ye Gold Coast la ye o pin'il private legal practice bɛ yʋʋm kan bɛ Accra.
english: Akufo-Addo was called to the Middle Temple Bar, London, UK, in 1940 and returned to what was then the Gold Coast to start a private legal practice a year later in Accra.

kusaal: 1947 nii, o da an onɛ pin'il United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) la ka da pɛ'ɛs "Big Six" la ni (ba yʋda nwa dɔlis dinɛ an si'em, Ebenezer Ako-Adjei, Joseph Boakye Danquah, Kwame Nkrumah, Emmanuel Obetsebi-Lamptey kɛ William Ofori Atta) ka ba da lɛbisid o nɛ nya'aŋ nɛ daamʋg bɛ Accra 1948 ni.
english: In 1947, he became a founding member of the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) and was one of the "Big Six" (the others being Ebenezer Ako-Adjei, Joseph Boakye Danquah, Kwame Nkrumah, Emmanuel Obetsebi-Lamptey and William Ofori Atta) detained after disturbances in Accra in 1948.

kusaal: Dinɛ yi 1949 ti paae 1950 ni, onɛ da pɛ'ɛs Gold Coast Legislative Council nɛ Coussey Constitutional Commission.
english: From 1949 to 1950, he was a member of the Gold Coast Legislative Council and the Coussey Constitutional Commission.

kusaal: Edward Kaale-Ewola Dery (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (6 March 1969) ka o da an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Lambussie Constituency bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: Edward Kaale-Ewola Dery (born 6 March 1969) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Lambussie constituency in the Upper West Region, on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Kpare bɛ Upper West region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Kpare in the Upper West region of Ghana.

kusaal: Dery da maalnɛ diploma, University of Professional Studies.
english: Dery earned a diploma from University of Professional Studies.

kusaal: O da lɛm maal Certified Information Systems Auditor yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012) bɛ US.
english: He also graduated as a Certified Information Systems Auditor in 2012 in the United States.

kusaal: Wadmaan (January 7, 2013–present; 2nd term)
english: Member of Parliament (7 January 2013–present; 2nd term)

kusaal: Ba da Dery nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (6 March 1969).
english: Dery was born on 6 March 1969.

kusaal: Edward Nasigrie Mahama du'am dabisir anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anu la nwadis anaasi, dabisa piiga nɛ anu la ni (born 15 April 1945) o anɛ dʋa'ata ka lɛn an pɔlitis na'anya'ad.
english: Edward Nasigrie Mahama (born 15 April 1945) is a Ghanaian medical doctor and politician.

kusaal: Saŋakan la, o da lɛn anɛ onɛ pa'an ziim dɔɔgin paalig bɛ Northwestern University.
english: During this period, he was also a Clinical Instructor at Northwestern University.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai la (1990), ba da gaŋ Mahama ye o an pa'an-pa'an bɛ University of Ghana Medical School dʋa'atanam sakurin la, ka lɛn an onana), yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anu la (1945).
english: In 1990, Mahama was appointed a lecturer at the University of Ghana Medical School and consultant at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra.

kusaal: Mahama da kɛŋ sakur nɛ Nalerigu Primary and Middle School lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' la, kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai la ni (1953 to 1959).
english: Born in the village of Sumniboma (northern Ghana) in 1945, Mahama attended Nalerigu Primary and Middle School from 1953 to 1959.

kusaal: O da tɔlis nɛ kɛŋ kpɛɛmnam sakur kanɛ an Secondary School bɛ Tamale sʋ'ʋlim, lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ yinne, paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ yinne (1961 to 1965).
english: He then attended Secondary School in Tamale from 1961 to 1965.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan pʋʋgin ka o da tɔlisi kɛŋ University of Ghana bɛ Legon la ka naae sakur kan yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' la (1972) nɛ kasɛta gbaʋŋ kanɛ pa'al ye o anɛ dua'ata.
english: Later that year, he was admitted to the University of Ghana in Legon and graduated in 1972 with a medical degree.

kusaal: Mahama da lɛb Nalerigu yʋn an dua'ata nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' la, nwadis awai la ni (September 1973), ka li yʋʋma anaasi nya'aŋ ka o bas Ghana ka kɛŋ na'asaatɛŋ kanɛ buon Chicago, Illinois tʋm tʋʋm kanɛ an pʋ'adʋas bɛɛ biisdʋ'am yɛla (Obstetrics and Gynecology) ka banɛ bɛn'ɛd wɛn'ɛdʋ suora ka ba buon ye consultant bɛ Accra's Korle Bu Teaching Hospital.
english: Mahama went back to Nalerigu as a medical doctor in September 1973 and four years later, he left Ghana to become an Obstetrics and Gynecology Physician in Chicago, Illinois.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋʋ ye o paas banɛ an ya'tuona ninsabilis teŋ banɛ gɔsid pʋ'adʋ'asʋg yɛla (West African College of Surgeons) yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi la (1994).
english: He was elected a fellow of the West African College of Surgeons in 1994.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobu la (1996), on da zi'en nya'a Ghana zugraan na'am, zi'enɛ na'adɔɔg kanɛ an People's National Convention (PNC) la, nidib biela da tɔn'ɔ tis o, ka ba da anɛ atan' yit kɔbʋga pʋʋgin (3.0%) banɛ da tɔn'ɔ la wʋsa.
english: In 1996, running as the presidential candidate of the People's National Convention (PNC), he received 3.0% of the vote.

kusaal: Banɛ da tiebid ye ba nya'a na'am yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la (2004 presidential election), na'adɔɔg PNC nɛ ba taaba ayi' banɛ an – Every Ghanaian Living Everywhere (EGLE) nɛ Great Consolidated Popular Party (GCPP) – da la'as taaba ka buoli ba mɛŋ ye Grand Coalition ka gaŋ Mahama ye o gaadi ba tuoni an kʋgdaan tisi ba na'adɔɔg la.
english: In preparation for the 2004 presidential election, the PNC and two other parties – Every Ghanaian Living Everywhere (EGLE) and the Great Consolidated Popular Party (GCPP) – formed an alliance known as the Grand Coalition and chose Mahama as its presidential candidate.

kusaal: Mahama da lɛn paam gaŋir ye o gaad na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon PNC la tuoni nya'a na'am yʋʋm tʋsa ayi' nɛ anii, nwadis piiga nɛ ayi' la dabisa ayɔpɔi da'ar vɔɔtʋg la (December 7, 2008 presidential elections).
english: Mahama was elected as the candidate for the PNC for the December 7, 2008 presidential elections.

kusaal: Edward Mahama da kɔ'ɔŋ ya'an nɛ on nan an ba na'adɔɔg PNC kugdaan tis nɛ Hassan Ayariga yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayi' na'am nya'ab yʋʋŋ la (2012 general election).
english: Edward Mahama lost the position of presidential candidate of the PNC to Hassan Ayariga in the run up to the 2012 general election.

kusaal: Ayariga da kɔ'ɔŋ la o da bas PNC kɛŋ pin'il o mɛŋ na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon All People's Congress (APC) la.
english: After the defeat, Ayariga left the PNC to form another party, the All People's Congress (APC).

kusaal: Nannanna Edward Mahama anɛ kpɛɛm kanɛ ka gɔmina gaŋ yɛ o gɔs Ghana nɛ tɛŋ zʋmis belim sʋŋ yɛla (Ghana's Ambassador-at-Large).
english: Edward Mahama is currently Ghana's Ambassador-at-Large.

kusaal: Ba da du'a' o nɛ tɛŋkpɛŋ kanɛ an Sumniboma (northern Gh.
english: Born in the village of Sumniboma (northern Ghana) in 1945, Mahama attended Nalerigu Primary and Middle School from 1953 to 1959.

kusaal: Abuyi' daan ka o da nya'a na'am la da anɛ yʋʋm tusayi' la ni (2000), saŋkan ka o da paam nidib ayi' nɛ pʋdigir anu kɔbʋga pʋʋgin (2.5%) banɛ da tɔn'ɔ la wʋsa.
english: In his second attempt at the presidency, in 2000, he won 2.5% of the vote.

kusaal: Li da an wʋʋ nid yinne nɛ pʋdigir awai kɔbʋga pʋʋgin (1.9%), da tɔn' tis o, banɛ da vote la wʋsa.
english: He placed third out of four candidates, winning 1.9% of the vote.

kusaal: Nɛ wala o da lɛn di' ya'ani yii Ayariga nuusin, da an ba kugdaani nya'a yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobʋ na'am nya'ab saŋa la (2016 election).
english: However, he won the position back from Ayariga for the 2016 election.

kusaal: Mahama mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa anaasi.
english: Mahama is married and the father of four children.

kusaal: John Dramani Mahama na'am saŋa, o da anɛ Minister of Youth and sports ka mɛ an deputy minister of Trade and industry.
english: He served as Minister of Youth and Sports and as Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry in the John Dramani Mahama's government.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Bechem Presbyterian dap Secondary sakurin la n nɛ Mfantsipim sakurin, Cape Coast.
english: He is an alumnus of Bechem Presbyterian Boys' Secondary School and Mfantsipim School, Cape Coast.

kusaal: O sanlɛ master degree government nɛ Leadership nyi Ghana institute of Management nɛ public Administration (GIMPA) nɛ B.A. Na'asaalin Pian'ad gbauŋin, Philosophy nɛ Classics nyit University of Ghana la ni.
english: He holds a master's degree in Governance & Leadership from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) and a B.A. in English, philosophy and classics from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Lin yi 1990 ti paae 2004 la, o tʋmnɛ Ghana Broadcasting Corporation zi'ig kanɛ ka o da lieb Deputy head of Sports.
english: From 1990 to 2004, he worked at the Ghana Broadcasting Corporation, where he became the Deputy Head of Sports.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu(2005) la nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ aii (2008) la, onɛ da tuongad tit sports n bɛ Network Broadcasting Limited la.
english: Between 2005 and 2008, he was the Head of Sports at Network Broadcasting Limited.

kusaal: O da anɛ onɛ bɛ o gʋnne ka an director of Operations n bɛ presidency Atta Mills na'amin ka mɛ an deputy minister tis Trade and Industry John Mahama saŋa.
english: He was a special aide and director of operations at the presidency under former President of Ghana President Mills and also the former Deputy Minister for Trade and Industry under John Mahama.

kusaal: Ba da vooti gaŋ o MP linɛ an 2012 vootʋg la, zi'ig kanɛ ka onɛ Nwabʋg paati nid Victor Okaikoi da li'ad na'am la.
english: He was elected as MP during the 2012 elections, where he faced off against Victor Okaikoi of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Samanpiid Nwadig la ni 2016, o da lɛn di na'am la n lieb Parliament nidi tis Odododiodio constituency la nɛ vootʋg kanl 36,606 linɛ zi'e tis 57.04% la.
english: In December 2016, he was retained as the member of Parliament for the Odododiodio Constituency with 36,606 votes, representing 57.04% against his closest contender, the New Patriotic Party, whose candidate had 26,671 votes, representing 41.56%.

kusaal: O da tʋʋmnɛ Parliament n an Ranking member linɛ anɛ Local Government nɛ Rural Development Committee nɛ member on the Privileges Committee nɛ Appointment Committee la ni.
english: He served in Parliament as the ranking member on the Local Government and Rural Development Committee and as a member on the Privileges committee and Appointments committee.

kusaal: Vaala Nwadig la March 2013 la ni, ba da gaŋ o ka o an Deputy minister for Trade and Industry John Mahama Na'am saŋa.
english: In March 2013, he was appointed as Deputy Minister for Trade and Industry under the John Mahama government.

kusaal: O da tʋmnɛ kpeŋ kan la ni hali ti paae 2014 ka tɔlisi keŋ lieb deputy minister for Local Government nɛ Rural Development la ti paae 2015.
english: He served in that role until 2014, when he was moved to serve as Deputy Minister for Local Government and Rural Development, where he served until 2015.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk bɛnɛ Sekyere East District pʋʋgin, linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: The seat is located within the Sekyere East District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Alex Afenya Markin anɛ Effutu constituency wadmaan, ka an wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Alex Afenyo Markin is the member of parliament of Effutu constituency, he is on the ticket of NPP.

kusaal: O da di'e kʋk la yinɛ Mike Allen onɛ da an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid ka da di nɛ vɔɔt kal 13,114 n lieb wadmaan la ni.
english: He took over from Mike Allen Hammah who was elected on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and won a majority of 13,114 votes to become the MP.

kusaal: Samuel owusu Agyei onɛ da an wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid ka da zi'en tis constituency bɛ, wadmaanib yir linɛ da paas anaasi la ni la, da sig ya ka o di'e.
english: He succeeded Samuel Owusu Agyei who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Ejisu constituency bɛnɛ Ejisu-Juaben Municipal District bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Ejisu is located in the Ejisu-Juaben Municipal District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk la bɛnɛ Ejura-Sekyedumase District pʋʋgin, Ashanti Region linɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: The seat is located within the Ejura–Sekyedumase District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li tɔdnɛ titɔdig nɛ Mampong Constituency, Nkoranza south constituency nɛ Atebubu Amantin constituency.
english: It shares boundaries with Mampong Constituency, Nkoranza south constituency and Atebubu Amantin constituency respectively.

kusaal: Ejura-Sekyedumase constituency bɛnɛ Ejura-Sekyedumase districti bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Ejura-Sekyedumase is located in the Ejura-Sekyedumase district of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ekow Hayford (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 December 1970 ka o maal ka'alim yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadis piiga daba awai daar (9 October 2020) o da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da lɛn an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Mfantseman Constituency bɛ Central Region la Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nɔba zug.
english: Ekow Hayford (24 December 1970 – 9 October 2020) was a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Mfantseman Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Ba da kʋʋ o nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadis piiga la daba awai daar (9 October 2020) O da lɛn anɛ chief executive officer tis Apam Football Club.
english: He was also the chief executive officer of Apam Football Club.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Hayford yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 December 1970) Mankessim, Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Hayford was born on 24 December 1970 in Mankessim, Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: On ma'aa da aan o ma, Madam Mena Aba Attah biig.
english: He was the only child of his mother, Madam Mena Aba Attah.

kusaal: O da mɔrnɛ Bachelor of Business Administration degree yi Methodist University College.
english: He held a Bachelor of Business Administration degree from the Methodist University College.

kusaal: O da lɛm mɔr Master of Business Administration (Supply Chain Management) degree yi Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).
english: He also held a Master of Business Administration (Supply Chain Management) degree from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).

kusaal: Hayford's yiiga tʋʋma da bɛnɛ Ghana Police Service, ani ka o da tʋm yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan (1993) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998).
english: Hayford's first career was in the Ghana Police Service, in which he served from 1993 to 1998.

kusaal: O da dɔlis kpɛma la ti paae Corporal.
english: He rose to the rank of Corporal.

kusaal: Onɛ da an chief executive officer ka an Manager tis MODISA Lodge nɛ MANTRAC Ghana Limited nwɛnɛ ban tun' taaba si'em la ka naan kpɛn' pɔlitis.

english: The name of the play comes from its main character, El Güegüense, which is derived from the Nahuat word Wewej, meaning 'old man' or 'wise man'.

english: "El Güegüense" represents folklore of Nicaragua, therefore, UNESCO proclaimed it a "Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity" in 2005 making Nicaragua the only country in Central America and one of six in Latin America to have two proclaimed masterpieces by UNESCO.

english: The theatrical play was written by an anonymous author in the 16th century, making it one of the oldest indigenous theatrical/dance works of the Western Hemisphere.

kusaal: Ba da sɔbi li nɛ Nahuat nɛ Spanish bʋʋdi ni.

english: Because deception for monetary gain is central to the plot of "El Güegüense", the play frequently is cited by newspaper editorials as a kind of symbolic archetype for perceived corrupt politicians or unaccountable public institutions.
