english: The Energy Commission is the key regulator for Ghana's energy sectors and advises the government on energy matters.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr kaŋa zug kpan anɛ ye o tis Ghana nidib na'ansa-bugʋm dinɛ nar si'ɛm ka kɛ ka pʋdaas la mɛ paam Gɔmina bugʋm.
english: The company's main focus is providing electricity to Ghana's people with commercial integrity and overseeing rural electrification projects for the government.

kusaal: Elijah Amoo Addo (dʋ'am dabisir 1 Mɔtul 1990) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ dʋgʋd diib ka lɛn an kpikpiŋ daan ka pin'il lʋgir kanɛ buon ye Africa wʋsa diib la.
english: Elijah Amoo Addo (born 1 August 1990) is a Ghanaian chef and food stylist who has become a social entrepreneur through his creation of Food for All Africa. He is the Co-Founder of Okumkom Biodigital Investment Ltd and the Founder of Biodigital Tech Solutions Ltd in UK.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni, ba da tis Addo ya'an piini yi lʋgir kanɛ buon Queen's Young Leaders Award ka li yit nɛ zugraan pʋ'ana'ab Queen Elizabeth II san'an bɛ Buckingham Palace on nyaŋi sʋŋi ti'ak Ghana diib pʋdigir la yela, lin na niŋ si'em ka di'saʋŋ da bɛ, ka yis kɔ'ɔm, ka mɛ sʋŋi yis nɔŋ nɛ banɛ did diib banɛ pʋ tisid laafi la.
english: In 2017, Addo was awarded a Queen's Young Leaders Award by Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II at Buckingham Palace for his contribution towards the reforming of Ghana's food distribution system to reduce waste, overcome hunger, and alleviate poverty and malnutrition.

kusaal: O da lɛn di'e ya'a piini kanɛ buon Takeda Young Entrepreneurship Award yit lʋgir kanɛ buon Takeda Foundation la ni yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anii la ni.
english: He also received a Takeda Young Entrepreneurship Award from the Takeda Foundation in 2018.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Addo nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai, Sapal nwadig, yiiga dabisir la daar bɛ Accra, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka o lɛɛ yit Akuapem-Mampong.
english: Addo was born on 1 August 1990 in Accra, Ghana but comes from Akuapem-Mampong.

kusaal: Thomas Aquinas Secondary School linɛ bɛ Accra, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la ka mɛ zamis diib dʋgʋb bɛ Sphinx Hospitality school and catering services bɛ Lagos, Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim.
english: He continued his educational journey at St. Thomas Aquinas Secondary School in Accra, Ghana and then completed a course in culinary studies at Sphinx Hospitality school and catering services in Lagos, Nigeria.

kusaal: O mɔr gbaŋ kanɛ pa'al ye o zamis da'a diib yela ka na nyaŋi gɔs o taaba bɛ YALI West Africa RLC-GIMPA ka lɛn paam kasɛta gbaŋi bɛ University of Cambridge on nyaŋi mɔr ti'akiri kɛna la yela, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi ni.
english: He holds a certificate in entrepreneurship and management from YALI West Africa RLC-GIMPA and earned a Leading Change certificate from the University of Cambridge in 2017.

kusaal: O da pin'ili kaasi ka tansidi yet ye, "fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye mam dʋ'adib ya'a nan vʋen mam na bɛ kpala dʋʋsid ka pi'esid ka mam taaba bɛ sakur nii?" Nwa da si'is banɛ dʋgʋd kpɛɛm la sʋʋnr ka o si'ak ye o sʋŋ o ka o zamis diib dʋgʋb bɛ Sphinx Vocational Training School linɛ bɛ Lagos.
english: He started crying and yelled out, "Do you think if my parents were alive, I would be here as a cleaner while my colleagues are in school?" This touched the Head Chef, who decided to mentor him and supported him through culinary studies at Sphinx Vocational Training School in Lagos.

kusaal: Zamisig la nya'aŋ, ba da nɔk o tʋʋma bɛ Marios diib kuosig zin'ig, zin'ig kan da anɛ diib kuosig zin'ig kanɛ ka vʋ'ʋsʋm kae bɛ Lagos, ka yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga la ni ka o lɛb Ghana na ye o sʋŋ Lebanese kpikpiŋ daan kanɛ da nyɛ o tʋʋma Lagos tɛŋin ka o yɔ'ɔg diib kuosig zin'ig.
english: After training, he got a job in Marios restaurant, then one of the busiest restaurants in Lagos, and in 2010 returned to Ghana to help a Lebanese businessman who had seen his work in Lagos to open Chase Restaurant.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayi ni, ba da gaŋ o ye o an kpɛɛm sʋ'ʋe da'aŋi bɛ +233 Jazz Bar zin'ig kanɛ ka ba kuosid diibi bɛ Accra la ka o da kilim kpɛɛm lɛn tis banɛ dʋgʋd diibi bɛ Greater Accra sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa, anina ka o da tʋm nɛ lʋgir la tuongatib ka ba nyaŋi pa'al bibaanlig la baŋir nɛ ban na niŋ si'em ka diib paae banɛ bɔɔd titua.
english: In 2012, he was selected to head the kitchen at +233 Jazz Bar in Accra and became Secretary of the Greater Accra Chefs Association, where he worked with the leadership of the Association to rebrand and focus on training student chefs to improve the standards of delivery in the job market.

kusaal: O da lɛn tʋm bɛ Burger nɛ Relish amaa yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anu la ni ka o bas tʋʋmkan ye o gaad tuoni gɔs lʋgir kanɛ gɔsid diibi na paae Africa sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa la ni.
english: He also worked at Burger and Relish but in 2015 resigned to focus on heading the Food For All Africa programme.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni, o da pin'il Okumkom ("li yis kɔ'ɔm") linɛ an na'asaasɔɔng laʋg kanɛ niŋid foon pʋʋgin lin na niŋ si'em ka nidib banɛ bɛ tɛɛns kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb paam diibi da'a ka li ligidi pʋ kpi'ema, zin'ig kanɛ ka ba da la'as diib la kuosid yiiga da bɛnɛ Teshie, Accra.
english: In 2017, he started the Okumkom ("It Ends Hunger") mobile app as a platform to bring affordable local food products to target communities, with its first community store located in Teshie, Accra.

kusaal: On sʋ'ʋe lʋgir sia nwa ka li yʋ'ʋr buon Africa wʋsa paam diib la da paam diib wan wʋʋ $8,000 nɛ 10,000 na'asaatɛn ligidi yela yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin ka li sʋŋ nidib tusanu, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnii nɛ anu Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi ni ka ba da gaŋ o lʋgir la ye ba tʋʋma la paas kɔbiga pʋʋgin suoya banɛ ka ba na nyaŋi dɔlisi sʋŋ ka diib nɔŋ nɛ kɔ'ɔm gaad Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, lʋgir kanɛ da tisi ba zʋn'or nwa da anɛ Dubai tɛŋ lʋgir kanɛ piin tɛŋ-tɛŋ banɛ tʋm titua.
english: His organization Food for All Africa recovers between $8,000 and $10,000 worth of food annually to support over 5485 beneficiaries across Ghana and in 2014 was selected as one of the 100 Global Best practices to end hunger and poverty in Ghana by Dubai International Awards for Best practices.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi ni, ba da gaŋ o ka o paasi di'e ya'an on nyaŋi mɔr tiakiri kɛn Africa na, ka piini lʋgir kanɛ da tis o piini la an Queen's Young Leaders Award ka onɛ sʋ'ʋe li an Pʋ'ana'ab Pariyaŋ Queen Elizabeth II onɛ an zugraani tis United Kingdom bɛ na'ayir kanɛ ka ba buon Buckingham Palace la ni, piini nwa da anɛ ye li pa'al on nyaŋi sʋŋ si'em mɔr nɔbigiri kɛn tɛɛns bɛdigʋ nina ka mɛ nyaŋi diis nidib banɛ pʋ mɔr diibɔ ka an nɔŋ dim la ka mɛ sʋŋi ti'ak Ghana diib pʋdʋgir yela ka li nyaŋi guoe disaʋŋ, kɔ'ɔm, nɔŋ nɛ a-dit-dikanɛ pʋ maan niŋgbinaa.
english: In 2017, he was selected as one of change-makers from Africa in the Commonwealth for the Queen's Young Leaders Award by Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom at Buckingham Palace in recognition of his work towards social development across the Commonwealth, feeding the less privileged and reforming Ghana's food distribution system to overcome food waste, hunger, poverty and malnutrition.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anii ni, ba da tis o ya'an piini bɛ Takeda piinkanɛ ka ba tisid dap banɛ mɔr paŋ ka an kpikpinib piini kanɛ ka ba tisid yʋʋm wʋsa bɛ Takeda symposium linɛ bɛ Tokyo, Japan sʋ'ʋlim, on da maal na'asaasɔɔng laʋg kanɛ ka ba buon Okumkom mobile app ka lɛn nyaŋi sʋŋ nidib ka ba sʋa ba diib titua, ka li kɛ ka nidib nyaŋi paam da'a diibi dɔlisi na'asaasɔɔng la pʋʋgin nɛ zin'is banɛ ka ba da sʋ'ad diib la ni.
english: In 2018, he was awarded the 2018 Takeda Young Entrepreneurship Award at the annual Takeda symposium in Tokyo, Japan for his Okumkom mobile app and community food stores initiative, which brings affordable and convenient local food products to communities through a mobile app, website and community target stores.

kusaal: Lin da pin'il yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi ni la, Africa wʋsa diib lʋgʋr la anɛ asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ lʋgʋr kanɛ tʋm tʋʋma bɛ West Africa ka an yiiga mɔr diib sʋŋir na.
english: Established in 2014, Food for All Africa is a non-profit social enterprise that operates West Africa's first community food support center.

kusaal: Ba zin'ig anɛ Ghana tɛŋpʋʋg kanɛ buon Accra, lʋgir la mɔr na'asaasɔɔng laʋg kanɛ bɛ foon pʋʋgin nyaŋidi pʋdʋgid diib ka li diisid biis banɛ pʋ mɔr sʋŋirɛ ban tusa yela,nyaŋidi sʋ'ad diib ka pʋdʋgid ka li paad zin'is bɛdigʋ.
english: Based in the capital of Ghana, Accra, the organization uses advocacy and a food-sharing mobile phone app to feed thousands of vulnerable children through food recovery and redistribution.

kusaal: Ba tʋm nɛ diib kuosig zin'is banɛ bɛ, banɛ kuosid la'ad, tʋʋma zin'is banɛ pʋdigid diib, nɛ tɛŋkpɛŋin kpaadib, Addo tʋʋma lʋgir nwa di'esid diib banɛ bɔɔd bɔɔd saʋŋ, nɛ diib banɛ ka ba di ka nya'al la pʋdʋgidi tisid biis bɛ kpiibis ya, sibiti nam ni, nɛ sakur zamisig zin'is banɛ ka tadimnam bɛ.
english: Working with local restaurants, supermarkets, food distribution companies, and rural small-hold farmers, Addo's organization collects leftover food or unwanted food that is close to its use-by date and redistributes it to disadvantaged children in orphanages, hospitals and lower-income schools.

kusaal: Linɛ lɛn paas ya'as, ban baŋ ye diib banɛ ka ba kuod Ghana sʋ'ʋlim kɔbiga pʋʋgin, pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ san'amid nɛ kati wa'ae suoya la ka'a sʋ'ʋm, ka si'eba lɔɔm san'amid suoya ni nɛ ban pʋ nyɛt da'a kuosid la, Africa wʋsa diib lʋgir la la'asid nɛ banɛ gɔsid diib yela wʋsa lin na niŋ si'em ka ka paam suoya ka diib da lɛn san'amid wala ya'asɛ.
english: Additionally, after discovering that as much as 46% of the food produced on farms in Ghana goes to waste because of poor roads, broken-down trucks and inefficient marketing, Food for All Africa is collaborating with a range of stakeholders in the Ghanaian food industry to find ways to reduce food wastage.

kusaal: On ma'a da an o dʋ'adib biribiŋ biisa anaasi pʋʋgin, on da an yʋʋm piinɛ ayi' la ni ka o da kɔ'ɔŋ o saam ka kɛŋ bɛ nɛ o pʋgʋdʋb Lagos tɛŋin, anina ka o da kɛŋ sakur.
english: The only boy among four children, he lost his parents at the age of 12 and went to live with his aunt in Lagos, where he attended school.

kusaal: Addo da pin'il o diib dʋgʋb nɛ Lagos, Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim on da tʋm diib kuosʋg zin'igin ye o paam ligidi gɔs o sakur yela la.
english: Addo's journey as a chef started in Lagos, Nigeria when he took up a job in a restaurant as a kitchen porter to support his education.

kusaal: Yʋʋm yinnɛ nya'aŋ ka o lɛb Lagos onɛ da sʋŋ o la da buol o la zug ye o kɛna sʋŋi ba hotel nwadis ayuobʋ ka o da kilim onɛ dʋgʋd diib hali.
english: After one year he returned to Lagos at the invitation of his mentor to work in their hotel for six months and rose to become the Sous Chef.

kusaal: Addo da lɛb Ghana sʋ'ʋlim na ka yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ ni ka o da si'al daʋ kanɛ mɔr zuglɛbin ban'as ka o vaad di'yaama banɛ kuosid diib sa'an ye o kɛŋ tis o taaba.
english: Addo came back to Ghana and in 2011, he met a mentally challenged man who was recovering leftover food from street vendors to feed his mentally challenged colleagues on the streets.

kusaal: Anina ka o da pin'il lʋgir kanɛ buon diib dʋgʋdib banɛ bɔɔd ye ba tiak Ghana, a-sʋ'ʋmmɛŋ lʋgir kanɛ di'esid diibi yit ninsʋma nɛ sʋŋidib sa'ani tisid banɛ ka'a sʋŋirɛ ka nyaŋi kɛ ka diib nɔŋ bɛɛ kɔ'ɔm da da bɛɛ.
english: This inspired him to start the Chefs for Change Ghana Foundation, an NGO that recovered excess food from hospitality companies to feed the vulnerable and advocate against food wastage and hunger.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anu ni, diib dʋgʋdib banɛ bɔɔd ti'akir la da ti'aki ba yʋ'ʋri lieb Africa wʋsa diib la'asig, nwa anɛ tɛŋgbaŋ diib sʋ'ak kanɛ an yiiga bɛ West Africa linɛ ye li sʋŋ biis banɛ ka'a sʋŋidiba, bʋnkʋda nɛ banɛ mɔr zuglɛbin ban'as dɔlis diib pʋʋgin, kuob pʋʋgin ka kɛ ka nidib banɛ pʋdʋgid diib Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la paas bɛdigʋ.
english: In 2015, Chefs for Change became the Food for All Africa programme, a social enterprise that operates West Africa's first food bank by creating sustainable means of nutrition for vulnerable children, the elderly and the mentally challenged through food banking, farming and a forum for stakeholders within Ghana's food supply chain.

kusaal: Ba gban'ar da an ye ba nyaŋi sʋŋ nidib banɛ an nɔŋ dim wan wʋʋ nidib 1 million yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi la ni.
english: It hopes to reach and impact 1 million low-income people by 2020.

kusaal: Elizabeth mɔr Bachelor of Science degree bɛ Agribusiness n yit Central University College.
english: Elizabeth holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Agribusiness from the Central University College.

kusaal: O lɛm paam National Diploma bɛ General Agriculture n bɛ University of Ghana, nɛ certificate bɛ General Agriculture n yit Kwadaso Agricultural College.
english: She obtained a National Diploma in General Agriculture from the University of Ghana, and also a certificate in General Agriculture from the Kwadaso Agricultural College.

kusaal: Elizabeth daa tʋʋmi bɛ kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl lʋgir la ni, nɛ o an Principal Production Officer yit 20 years.
english: Elizabeth has worked with Ministry of Food and Agriculture as Principal Production Officer for 20 years.

kusaal: Afoley Quaye daa li'a na'am la ka nɛ o di lieb wadmaan tis Krowor Constituency n bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋúlim yit 2015.
english: Afoley Quaye contested and won the New Patriotic Party parliamentary elections for the Krowor Constituency in the Greater Accra Region in 2015.

kusaal: O daa li'a na'am la nɛ nidiba atan', ba yʋ'ʋra nwana Agnes Naa Momo Lartey onɛ zi'enɛ tis ma'asim tiig paati la, Hugo Kofi Huppenbauer onɛ zi'enɛ tis Progressive People's Paati la nɛ Amartey Fanny onɛ zi'enɛ tis nɔraug paati.
english: She contested with three other candidates, namely Agnes Naa Momo Lartey of the National Democratic Congress, Hugo Kofi Huppenbauer of the Progressive People's Party and Amartey Fanny of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Afoley Quaye daa paam 32,463 vɔɔts yit 63,555 vɔɔts kɔbiga pʋʋgin daa paami 51.08 percent yi nidiba wʋsa vɔɔt la.
english: Afoley Quaye won the elections with 32,463 votes out of 63,555 votes cast, representing 51.08 percent of total valid votes.

kusaal: O anɛ Minista tis gɔmɛna lʋgir kanɛ buon ye Fisheries nɛ Aquaculture.
english: She is also a former Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture.

kusaal: O daa lɛm li'a na'am la yaas ka nɛ o di lieb wadmaan tis Krowor Constituency.
english: During the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, she won this same parliamentary seat to become the Member of Parliament for the Krowor Constituency.

kusaal: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare (March 1, 1974) anɛ Gaana lɔya nɛ pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛdi.
english: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare (born March 1, 1974) is a Ghanaian lawyer and politician who served as Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts.

kusaal: Nannanna o anɛ Wadmaani paas Gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la, Gaana Republic ka nɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Techiman North Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: and currently a member for the 8th and 9th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana representing the Techiman North Constituency.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ St Monica's Secondary School bɛ Mampong, Kumasi sʋ'ʋlim la, ani ka da maali o O & A level certificates.
english: She attended St Monica's Secondary School in Mampong, Kumasi, where she obtained both her O & A level certificates.

kusaal: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare da tɔlisi keŋ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology ka paami Bachelor of Arts in Social Science kasɛtta gbaʋŋ.
english: Ofosu-Adjare then proceeded to the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology where she obtained a Bachelor of Arts in Social Science.

kusaal: O da lɛn tɔlisi keŋ University of Ghana, Legon zamis lɔyanam yɛla tʋgʋ tuon ka di'e LLB yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2002) la ni.
english: She continued to the University of Ghana, Legon to pursue further studies in the field of Law and obtained honors in LLB in 2002.

kusaal: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare da pin'ili o lɔya tʋʋmanɛ Holy Trinity Chambers n bɛ Kumasi, Ashanti Region la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni ka tɔlis onɛ sʋ'oe zin'ig la yinne.
english: Ofosu-Adjare started her legal practice with the Holy Trinity Chambers in Kumasi, Ashanti Region in 2004 and rose to become a partner of the Firm.

kusaal: O da lɛn an Lɔya (lawyer) tis Legal Aid Scheme, Ashanti Region.
english: She also became a lawyer for the Legal Aid Scheme in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: o paas banɛ gɔsid Multi Trust Financial Company kanɛ bɛ Kumasi la, din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) paae zina.
english: She has been a board member of the Multi Trust Financial Company in Kumasi from 2004 till date.

kusaal: Nannanna o lɛn paas banɛ gɔsid Federation Commodities Limited.
english: She is currently a board member of the Federation Commodities Limited.

kusaal: Gaana pirɛsidɛn da lɛn gaŋ o ye paas banɛ gɔsid Tema Oil Refinery yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) ni.
english: She was appointed to the Board of the Tema Oil Refinery in 2009 by the President of the Republic of Ghana and served from 2009 to 2013.

kusaal: On da an minista la,o da tʋmya nɛ lʋga piinɛ anaasi (14) Agencies ka pin'il innovative,novelty tourism programsi paas Ghana's Tourism products & Offerings.
english: As the sector minister, she worked creditably with fourteen (14) Agencies under her ministry introduced innovative, novelty tourism programs as an addition to Ghana's Tourism products & Offerings.

kusaal: Dinɛ nar nɛ pʋdigir anɛ Explore Ghana project ka o da zuŋi di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014) ye di kɛ ka nidib mɔr bɔɔdim tisi akaae zin'ivɛnla Gaana kpɛla.
english: The Explore Ghana project, launched in 2014, aimed to stimulate domestic tourism in the country.

kusaal: o da lɛn tiak National Festival for Arts & Culture (NAFAC) ka Ghana Carnival da sin'iŋnɛ sankanɛ ka o kpɛn ɔfis la.
english: She also restructured the National Festival for Arts & Culture (NAFAC) and the famous Ghana Carnival introduced in her maiden year in office.

kusaal: Wad paal kaŋa da keŋi tiak wadkʋdʋg kanɛ da bɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiwai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne la (Act of 1961) yiiga la ka bʋnkaŋa buudi naam ka Film and Television sʋ'ʋlim la paam wada ye ba tʋm Gaana.
english: This new bill replaced the old Film Act of 1961 and was the first time such a new legislative framework was introduced to ensure the Film and Television sector got the much-needed legal backing in Ghana.

kusaal: O da gaad nimbanɛ ka gɔmena da tʋm la tuon (Government Delegation ) ye ba bi'el Kambʋn Na'ab Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II keŋ Seychelles Islands zin'ikanɛ ka ba da kad Kambʋn Na'ab (King of Ashanti), Nana Prempeh I kpɛn'ɛs mɔɔg sankanɛ ka Kambumis nɛ Na'asaanam da zabid yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbis wai la (Ashanti-British war in 1900).
english: She led a high-powered Government Delegation to accompany the return of the King of Ashanti Kingdom, Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II to the Seychelles Islands where the King of Ashanti, Nana Prempeh I was sent to exile during the Ashanti-British war in 1900.

kusaal: Tɛɛns kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb tʋʋma ni, o mɔr Gaana zin'ivɛnlla la keŋ zin'is kbɛdigʋ nwɛnɛ World Travel Market, International Tourism Bourse (ITB), FITUR International Travel Fair, Vakantiebeurs Holiday Fair, & China Outbound Tourism & Travel Market (COTTM).
english: On the International level, she has led Ghana's tourism sector by consistently appearing at the major Tourism fairs and exhibitions like the World Travel Market, International Tourism Bourse (ITB), FITUR International Travel Fair, Vakantiebeurs Holiday Fair, & China Outbound Tourism & Travel Market (COTTM).

kusaal: O da pian'a tisi o taaba banɛ bɛ ninsabilis teŋin nɛ United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) ye ba kɛ ka ba maal Brand Africa conference Ankara, Ghana kpɛla yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu Nwadisa anii la ni (August 2015).
english: She lobbied her colleague African Ministers & the top echelons of the United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) to have Ghana host the first ever Brand Africa conference in Accra in August 2015.

kusaal: Nidibi mi' o nɛ tʋʋmkanɛ ka o tʋm International Tourism yɛla la da kɛya ka ba da vɔɔt Gaana paas Executive Council tis UN Tourism body di UNWTO Session kanɛ paas pisi nɛ yinne la (21st) Medellini bɛ Colombia.
english: Her popularity and energetic role in the International Tourism matters helped Ghana to be elected on to the Executive Council of the UN Tourism body at its 21st UNWTO Session in Medellin Colombia.

kusaal: O da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid nimma'asim yɛla la (Health Committee) nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid tʋʋma nyɛɛm yɛla la (Appointments Committee).
english: She is a member of the Health Committee and also a member of the Appointments Committee.

kusaal: O ɛlnɛ Lawrence Ofosu-Adjare.
english: She is married to Lawrence Ofosu-Adjare.

kusaal: O anɛ Isaac Kwadwo Adjei-Mensah da kpi la, onɛ da an Minista gɔsid ku'om, tʋʋma nɛ ya yɛla Rawlings gɔmena la ni, ka da an Wadmaani tis Techiman North zin'ikanɛ ka o nan an wadmaan la.
english: She is the daughter of the late Isaac Kwadwo Adjei-Mensah, who served as Minister of Water Resources, Works and Housing during the Rawlings government, and was also Member of Parliament for Techiman North where she currently is a member of parliament.

kusaal: Pirɛsidɛn John Mahama da gaansi o nidib ye ba tʋmi o gɔmena la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) la ka gaŋ o ye o an Minista tis Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts.
english: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare was appointed on 1 March 2013 by President John Dramani Mahama to the newly created/realigned Ministry of Tourism, Culture & Creative Arts.

kusaal: O anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la (National Democratic Congress).
english: She is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare an onɛ paasi atan o du'adib bipumis piiga la pʋʋgin.
english: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare (born March 1, 1974) is a Ghanaian lawyer and politician who served as Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts.

kusaal: O du'adib anɛ Girimadaan Adjei-Mensah onɛ an lɔya, kpikpin nɛ Pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd nɛ o pʋ'a Adjei-Mensah onɛ an kpikpin.
english: Ofosu-Adjare is the third of ten girls born to Isaac Kwadwo Adjei Mensah, a lawyer, businessman and politician, and his wife, a businesswoman.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ ka o maali o degree in law yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2004) la ni.
english: She later obtained a degree in law in 2004.

kusaal: Pirɛsidɛn John Mahama da gaŋ Elizabeth Ofosu yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan Nwadisa atan la yiiga daar(1 March 2013) la ni ye o an Minista tis Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts zin'ikanɛ ka ba nan maal paal.
english: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare was appointed on 1 March 2013 by President John Dramani Mahama to the newly created/realigned Ministry of Tourism, Culture & Creative Arts.

kusaal: On da an minista tis Tourism, Culture & Creative Arts la yɛla.
english: Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare was appointed on 1 March 2013 by President John Dramani Mahama to the newly created/realigned Ministry of Tourism, Culture & Creative Arts.

kusaal: Ghana pin'il, nɛ'ɛ da an yiiga ka lʋgʋkaŋa nyaŋi maal tigir malʋŋ kaŋa Ankara sʋ'ʋlim, Greater Accra Region.
english: For the first time in Ghana, the ministry nurtured this Homogeneous Festival to ensure the Greater Accra Region has its own brand festival.

kusaal: Onɛ da lɛn pin'il Tourism levy secretariat la ye di sʋŋ Tourism lampo an yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (1%) di'esʋg nɛ yɔɔb.
english: She is also credited with the setting up of Tourism levy secretariat to help improve the collection & payment of the 1% Tourism levy.

kusaal: Dinɛ ka Ofosu-Adjare da lɛn nyaŋi tʋm on da an Wadmaan la anɛ on da sʋŋ banɛ kpi'ed bɛɛ ya'abid nam tʋʋma nɛ ba tʋʋma zin'ig.
english: Other achievements of Mrs. Ofosu-Adjare were done in the area of a legislative framework to support the work of the creative Arts industry She led the passage of the Film Bill, which went through cabinet and was approved by Parliament into become law.

kusaal: O da kɛya ka ba sin'iŋ Film Bill, dinɛ da keŋ Wadmaanibin ka ba tik ka di lieb wada la.
english: Other achievements of Mrs. Ofosu-Adjare were done in the area of a legislative framework to support the work of the creative Arts industry She led the passage of the Film Bill, which went through cabinet and was approved by Parliament into become law.

kusaal: Dinɛ da an yiiga ka Kambʋn Na'akanɛ nan zin'i kʋk la zug kaae Seychelles Islands.
english: It was the first time a sitting Ashanti King has visited the Seychelles Islands.

kusaal: Elmina Sharks F.C. anɛ football club kanɛ yit Ghana ka bɛ Elmina, Central Region.
english: Elmina Sharks F.C. is a football club from Ghana based in Elmina, Central Region.

kusaal: Ba da nya'a 2018 Ghanaian Premier League.
english: The club is competing in the 2018 Ghanaian Premier League.

kusaal: Ba nwɛn'ɛdi ba yin di'ema nɛ Nduom Sports Stadium.
english: Home games are played at Nduom Sports Stadium.

kusaal: Elmina Sharks F.C. da pin'ili yinɛ Coconut Grove Beach Resort yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai ni (1999).
english: Elmina Sharks F.C. was born out of Coconut Grove Beach Resort in 1999.

kusaal: Ba da buon Elmina Sharks yiiga nɛ ye Coconut Grove Sharks C ka team la da pin'ili anɛ division one league team.
english: Elmina Sharks was formerly known as Coconut Grove Sharks FC and the team started as division one league team.

kusaal: Ba da bɛ division two league yʋma ayɔpɔi pʋʋgin ka nyaan lɔ'ɔŋ division one yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ (2011).
english: The team was in the division two league for seven years and later on moved to division one in 2011.

kusaal: Elmina Sharks nwɛn'ɛ yʋʋma ayi nɛ fan' bɛ Ghana Premier League, ka naae nɛ table la tɛnsʋk yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi ni (2017) ka pʋ nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋ playoff stage yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wain nii (2019), ka ba da gu'e ba 2018 nwɛn'ɛb ye na'ayiigim bɛɛ li pʋʋgin.
english: Elmina Sharks played two and a half seasons in the Ghana Premier League, finishing mid-table in 2017 and failing to make the playoff stage in 2019, with the 2018 season suspended due to corruption.

kusaal: yʋma yi, 2019–20 season nɛ 2020–21 season la, Benjamin Bernard Boateng da naae anɛ onɛ di goal nami gaad o taaba club la ni.
english: In both the 2019–20 season and 2020–21 season, Benjamin Bernard Boateng finished as the club's top goal scorer.

kusaal: Ba daa pʋ maali ba mɛŋ titua nɛ ban daa nwɛn'ɛd nɛ Swedru All Blacks United FC yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ anu, fulumfug nwadig ni la (February 2025).
english: They had been found guilty of misconduct during a league match with Swedru All Blacks United FC in February 2025.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ nu, dɔnwalig nwadig la ni (March 2025),club la nidib anu daa kpɛn'ɛ sam pʋʋgin GHS 10,000 nid wʋsa ka ba zin'ili ba di'ema la wʋsa pʋʋgin ye ba da paasɛ.
english: In March 2025, 5 of the club's officials were fined GHS 10,000 each and banned for the rest of the season.

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh (dʋ'anɛ 25 February 1983) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi nɛ anii la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni zi'eni tis Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Central Region la, Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party zug.
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh (born 25 February 1983) is a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and currently a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Elvis Morris Donkoh nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan Nwadisa ayi la dabpisi nɛ anu daar (25 February 1983) ka o yi Cape Coast bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh was born on 25 February 1983 and hails from Cape Coast in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh da maali o Diploma (Youth In Development Work) nɛ University of Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008) ka maal o Post Graduate Diploma (Project and Quality Management) Business University of Costa Rica yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016).
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh obtained his Diploma (Youth In Development Work) from the University of Ghana in the year 2008 and Post Graduate Diploma (Project and Quality Management) from Business University of Costa Rica in the year 2016.

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh anɛ Executive Director tis Alliance for Youth Development.
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh is the Executive Director of Alliance for Youth Development.

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh da nya'aya ka di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la ni bɛɛ Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency bɛ Central Region, Ghana la.
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh contested and won the 2016 NPP parliamentary primaries for Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh da keŋ tuoni di wadmaan kʋk la o sʋ'ʋlim la (Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency) bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni, Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg Nɔba zug ka o paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi atɔpɔi la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ninɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ ayi, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anu (22,245) dinɛ an pisnu du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (50.7%) ka Samuel K. Hayford onɛ bɛ National Democratic Congress paam vɔɔt tusa pisi, kɔbisnu nɛ anii (20,508) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (46.7%), Clement Abaidoo onɛ bɛ Progressive People's Party (PPP - Ghana) da paam vɔɔt tusir yinne nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi (1,054) dinɛ an ayi du'al anaasi (2.4%) ka Kwame Edu Ofori onɛ bɛ People's National Convention (PNC - Ghana) paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (116) dinɛ an nɛɛm du'al atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.3%).
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh proceeded to win the parliamentary seat in his constituency (Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency) during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party to join the Seventh (7th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana with 22,245 votes (50.7%) against Samuel K. Hayford of the National Democratic Congress who had 20,508 votes (46.7%), Clement Abaidoo of the Progressive People's Party (PPP - Ghana) who had 1,054 votes (2.4%) and Kwame Edu Ofori of the People's National Convention (PNC - Ghana) who also had 116 votes (0.3%).

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh da lɛn nya' ka di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la nɛ vɔɔt kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (475) ka Kobina Nyanteh paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi nɛ pisi (220).
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh again contested and won the 2020 NPP parliamentary primaries for Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana with 475 votes against Kobina Nyanteh who had 220 votes.

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh da lɛn keŋ tuoni di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi tusa pisi nɛ anu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anii (25,048) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ awai du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (49.2%) ka Felix Ofosu Kwakye onɛ bɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anaasi, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi (24,872) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ anii du'ali anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (48.8%) ka Francis Eghan onɛ bɛ Ghana Union Movement (GUM) paam vɔɔt tusir yinne nɛ yinne (1,001) dinɛ an ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (2.0%).
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh again proceeded to win in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana with 25,048 votes (49.2%) against Felix Ofosu Kwakye of the National Democratic Congress who had 24,872 votes (48.8%) and Francis Eghan of the Ghana Union Movement (GUM) who had also 1,001 votes (2.0%).

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh anɛ kʋkdaan nya'adɔli tis Mines and Energy Committee.
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh is a member (Vice Chairperson) of Mines and Energy Committee.

kusaal: O lɛn paas la'askanɛ an Privileges Committee la nɛ Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He is also a member of Privileges Committee as well as the Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee of the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Elvis Morris Donkoh anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Seventh Day Adventist Church (SDA).
english: Elvis Morris Donkoh is a Christian and a member of the Seventh Day Adventist Church (SDA).

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋn anɛ Wadmaani tis Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency bɛ Central Region Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg zug.
english: He is now working as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Abura-Asebu-Kwamankese Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Emanuel Navarrete Martínez (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ 17 January 1995) anɛ Mexico zabzabid (professional boxer).
english: Emanuel Navarrete Martínez (born 17 January 1995) is a Mexican professional boxer.

kusaal: Navarrete da paam o amateur record nɛ 108–7.
english: Navarrete had an amateur record of 108–7.

kusaal: Ba da mɔɔl October 17, 2018, ye Navarrete na zab nɛ onɛ an WBO junior featherweight champion la, Isaac Dogboe, dinɛ da an Dogboe nɔɔra ayi ka o zabid ye o gu' title la.
english: It was announced on 17 October 2018, that Navarrete would challenge the reigning WBO junior featherweight champion Isaac Dogboe, in what was Dogboe's second title defense.

kusaal: Zaba la da bɛnɛ December 8, 2018, Top Rank card headlined dinɛ da la'as lightweight title zaba kanɛ da bɛ tis Vasyl Lomachenko nɛ Jose Pedraza.
english: The bout was scheduled for the undercard of a 8 December 2018, Top Rank card headlined by a unified lightweight title fight between Vasyl Lomachenko and Jose Pedraza.

kusaal: Zaba la da naan nɛ Hulu Theater bɛ New York City ka ESPN dinɛ bɛ America la da dɔlis VITV dinɛ bɛ Dogboe's teŋin, Ghana.
english: The event took place at the Hulu Theater in New York City and was broadcast by ESPN in the Americas and by VITV in Dogboe's native Ghana.

kusaal: Navarrete da kpɛn' first title bout tʋʋma nɛ odds-makers ka mɔr +500 underdog, ba da nyɛ' Dogboe ka o anɛ -800.
english: Navarrete entered the first title bout of his career as a significant underdog, with most odds-makers having him a +500 underdog, while Dogboe was seen as a –800 favorite.

kusaal: Dogboe da nwɛ' Navarrete digil nɛ nu'udatiʋŋ ninth round la ni, amaa knockdown da pʋ buolɛ, zabpansid (referee) Benjy Esteves Jr.
english: Dogboe dropped Navarrete with a right hand in the ninth round, but no knockdown was called, as referee Benjy Esteves Jr. deemed it an illegal punch.

kusaal: Zaba la da naaeya ka Navarrete paam (221 paae 176) ka lɔb (804 to 686) kpisinkpila gaad Dogboe.
english: The fight ended with Navarrete having landed (221 to 176) and thrown (804 to 686) more punches than Dogboe.

kusaal: June 14, 2019, ESPN da pa'al ye Navarrete da nar ye o lɛn zabi gu' title nɔɔra ayi daan gɛɛs Francisco De Vaca dabisir, dabisir kanl, nɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ba nan ye ba yɛl.
english: It was revealed by ESPN on 14 June 2019, that Navarrete was expected to make his second title defense against the undefeated Francisco De Vaca at a date, location and venue which would be announced later.

kusaal: nɛ Luis Collazo zaba daar, amaa ka da tɔlisi di ka di tud August 17 Top Rank card, Benavidez da bfuoe o mɛŋ sapu'ad zug la.
english: The fight was originally scheduled for the José Benavidez Jr. and Luis Collazo undercard, but was later promoted to headline the 17 August Top Rank card, after Benavidez withdrew due to injury.

kusaal: Ba da zabnɛ Banc of California Stadium bɛ Los Angeles, California la, ka ESPN da kɛ ka di yi paalʋ na.
english: The fight took place at the Banc of California Stadium on Los Angeles, California, and was broadcast by ESPN.

kusaal: Five days Navarrete da zabi gu'u o title, daba anu nya'aŋ ka Top Rank vice-president Carl Moretti da mɔɔl ye Navarrete na zab gu' title la nɔɔra atan gɛɛs #2 ranked WBO junior featherweight Juan Miguel Elorde.
english: Five days after Navarrete made his second title defense, Top Rank vice-president Carl Moretti confirmed that Navarrete would make his third title defense against the #2 ranked WBO junior featherweight Juan Miguel Elorde.

kusaal: Zaba la da booknɛ Tyson Fury nɛ Otto Wallin heavyweight bout daar, dinɛ da naam September 14, 2019, Navarrete zabkʋdʋg la dabpisi nɛ ayuobʋ daar.
english: The fight was booked for the undercard of the Tyson Fury vs. Otto Wallin heavyweight bout at the T-Mobile Arena, Paradise, Nevada which took place on 14 September 2019, just 28 days after Navarrete's previous fight.

kusaal: BT Sport nɛ ESPN+ pay per view da kɛ ka zaba la yina ka sɔ' wʋsa nyɛ.
english: The fight was broadcast on BT Sport and ESPN+ pay-per-view.

kusaal: Navarrete da kpɛn' zaba la nɛ -3000 favorite.
english: Navarrete came into the fight as a –3000 favorite.

kusaal: Navarrete da lɛn zab nɔɔra anaasi daan ye o gu' WBO junior featherweight title la gɛɛs nɛ Francisco Horta, o zabkanɛ paasi anaasi yʋʋm la pʋʋgin.
english: Navarrete was booked to make his fourth title WBO junior featherweight title defense against Francisco Horta, in his fourth fight of the year.

kusaal: Zaba la da bɛnɛ December 7, 2019, Auditorio GNP Seguros bɛ Puebla, Mexico.
english: The fight was scheduled as for the undercard of an ESPN broadcast Top Rank card which took place on 7 December 2019, at the Auditorio GNP Seguros in Puebla, Mexico.

kusaal: On da pin'il bi'el-bi'el la, Navarrete da sin'iŋi tisid Horta kpisinkpilbɛda, ka da nyaŋi o tiraan la 2:09 minute, fourth round la ni.
english: After a slow start, Navarrete began catching Horta with looping punches, finally stopping his opponent at the 2:09 minute mark of the fourth round.

kusaal: January 30, 2020, da zabi o nɔɔra anu zabkanɛ an ye o gu' title la gɛɛs Jeo Santisima.
english: On 30 January 2020, it was announced that Navarrete would make the fifth defense of his title against Jeo Santisima.

kusaal: Zaba la da naamnɛ MGM Grand Garden Arena bɛ Paradise, Nevada, February 22, 2020.
english: The fight was booked for the Deontay Wilder vs. Tyson Fury II pay-per-view undercard, which took place at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Paradise, Nevada on 22 February 2020.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ mɔr three-division world champion, o da mɔr WBO junior featherweight title di yi 2018 paae 2020, ka mɔr WBO featherweight title din yi 2020 paae 2023, ka lɛm mɔr WBO junior lightweight title din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan nwadisa ayi la ni (February 2023).
english: He is a three-division world champion, having held the unified International Boxing Federation (IBF) and World Boxing Organization (WBO) junior lightweight titles since February 2026.

kusaal: Navarrete da pin'ili o zaba nɛ gɛɛs Misael Ramirez, February 18, 2012.
english: Navarrete made his professional debut, at the age of 16, against Misael Ramirez on 18 February 2012.

kusaal: O da nyaŋ zaba la nɛ first-round technical knockout.
english: He won the fight by a first-round technical knockout.

kusaal: Navarrete da paam 25–1 record yʋma ayuobʋ banɛ ria'al la ni, ka nyaŋ zab-ban atan dɔlisid on ɛɛnti kpɛm bʋ' nyaŋ ka ba gu'oe ba la.
english: Navarrete amassed a 25–1 record during the first six years of his professional career, winning all but three of those fights by way of stoppage and all fights taking place in Mexico.

kusaal: Ba da zi'el zaba lanɛ José Benavidez Jr.
english: The fight was originally scheduled for the José Benavidez Jr. and Luis Collazo undercard, but was later promoted to headline the 17 August Top Rank card, after Benavidez withdrew due to injury.

kusaal: Navarrete da di zaba la fourth-round technical knockout.
english: Navarrete won the fight by a fourth-round technical knockout.

kusaal: Di da anɛ Navarrete yiiga zaba ka o zabi o mɛŋ teŋin, Mexico.
english: Navarrete encountered passport issues in Mexico which delayed his travel to Arizona for the fight.

kusaal: Navarrete da di zaba la nɛ fourth-round technical knockout.
english: Navarrete won the fight by a fourth-round technical knockout.

kusaal: Navarrete da lɛn pa'al banɛ nɔŋ o la ye o sid anɛ zabzabid, ka di zaba la eleventh-round stoppage.
english: He came close to securing a stoppage in the eleventh round as the referee moved closer to the action, but Conceição remained resilient.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Emelia Brobbey nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yi', pin'ilig nwadig daba yu'obʋ daar (6 January 1982) ka o nɔbigi bɛ Akyem Swedru linɛ bɛ Eastern region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Emelia Brobbey was born on 6 January 1982 and grew up in Akyem Swedru to Mr Samuel P Brobbey in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da zamis gbaŋi bɛnɛ Akyem Swedru Secondary School, o O-level ka kɛŋ tuoni paae Presbyterian Teacher's Training College, anina ka o paae pa'an-pa'an baŋir.
english: She studied at Akyem Swedru Secondary School for her O-level and continued to Presbyterian Teacher's Training College to acquire teaching skills.

kusaal: On paam pa'an-pa'anib tʋʋma gbaŋ, Teacher's Certificate 'A' nya'aŋ la, ba da tud Emelia nɛ Obuasi, anina ka o pa'al biis agricultural science.
english: After completing Teacher's Certificate 'A', Emelia was posted to Obuasi, where she taught agricultural science.

kusaal: O mɛ mɔr labaya di'esidib gbaŋ, diploma in Journalism, bachelor's degree bɛ Human Resource Management nɛ ICM certificate bɛ Broadcast Journalism.
english: She also holds a diploma in Journalism, a bachelor's degree in Human Resource Management and an ICM certificate in Broadcast Journalism.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piiga (2010), Emelia da el o sid Dr Kofi Adu Boateng one sʋ'ʋe End Point Homeopathy Clinic amaa ka ba bas taaba yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yi (2012).
english: In 2010, Emelia married Dr Kofi Adu Boateng who is the founder of End Point Homeopathy Clinic but the couple divorced in 2012.

kusaal: O biig dasaŋ kanɛ paas ayi la, da anɛ o sid Doctor Kofi biig ka o da dʋ'a on nɛ yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛ tan', nwadis ayʋobʋ, dabpiinɛ atan' daar (13th, June 2013).
english: Her second son was from her marriage with Doctor Kofi and was born on 13th, June 2013.

kusaal: Emelia Brobbey (ba dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yi', pin'ilig nwadig daba yu'obʋ daar, 6 January 1982) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an sini maan, one tisid labaya TV ni ka len an yʋmyʋm.
english: Emelia Brobbey was born on 6 January 1982 and grew up in Akyem Swedru to Mr Samuel P Brobbey in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da len di ya'ani bɛ yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛ wai (2019) an Best Actor Female indigenous bɛ ZAFAA Global Award ka banɛ da tis piini nwa' an African Film Academy Awards.
english: Best International Act; Royal Africa Awards 2015.

kusaal: O anɛ Samuel P Brobbey pʋ'ayʋa.
english: Emelia Brobbey was born on 6 January 1982 and grew up in Akyem Swedru to Mr Samuel P Brobbey in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da yis o kɔn'ɔ-kɔn'ɔ ma'a yiiga yʋʋma kanɛ an "Fa me ko" nɛ yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛ wai (2019).
english: She released her first single song "Fa me ko" in 2019.

english: In 2021, Bedzrah together with Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin, Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah, Johnson Kwaku Adu and Laadi Ayii Ayamba were sworn in during the Extraordinary Session 2021 of the Parliament of the ECOWAS which happened in Freetown in Sierra Leone.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Norgbey nɛ Ho-Ziavi bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Norgbey was born in Ho-Ziavi in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da zamisnɛ Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply, ka di'e diploma kasɛtta gbaʋŋ.
english: He studied at the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply, where he received a diploma.

kusaal: O da lɛn di'e diploma kasɛtta gbaʋŋʋ yi International School of Aviation.
english: He also received a diploma at the International School of Aviation.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan la ni (2003), o da maal o MSC in Supply Chain Management Coventry University yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne la ni (2011), ka lɛn naae nɛ BBA yi University of Professional Studies, Accra.
english: In 2003, he graduated with an MSC in Supply Chain Management from Coventry University In 2011, he graduated with a BBA from the University of Professional Studies, Accra.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu ni (2015), ka o da maali o Postgraduate Certificate bɛ Public Procurement Law and Policy University of Nottingham,bɛ UK la ni.
english: In 2015, he acquired a Postgraduate Certificate in Public Procurement Law and Policy at the University of Nottingham, UK.

kusaal: Norgbey da anɛ pa'an (teacher) Happy Home Basic School yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2006) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) din nya'aŋ ka o lieb procurement officer tis National Disaster Management Organization.
english: Norgbey worked as a teacher at Happy Home Basic School in 2006–2009 and later became the procurement officer at the National Disaster Management Organization.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu la ni (2015), o da nya' ya ka di Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC wadmaanib kʋk la bɛ Ashiaman constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region la.
english: In 2015, he contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Ashiaman constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: O da di Wadmaan kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la.
english: He won this parliamentary seat during the 2016 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Asibid daari, Nwaidisa anu la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan la (Saturday 13 May 2023), Ernest Henry Norgbey daa nya'aya ka di NDC wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la Ashiaman constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region nɛ vɔɔt tusir yinne, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1,627) gaad Tony Afenyo onɛ daa paam vɔɔt tusir yinne, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (1,221) ka David Worwui-Brown paam vɔɔt pisnu (50).
english: On Saturday 13 May 2023, Ernest Henry Norgbey contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Ashiaman constituency in the Greater Accra Region with 1,627 votes by beating Tony Afenyo who polled 1,221 votes and David Worwui-Brown who also polled 50 votes.

kusaal: O da lieb chartered member tis Supply Chain Management, bɛ UK, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi la ni (2014).
english: In 2014, he became a chartered member of the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply.

kusaal: Norgbey mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biig yinne.
english: Norgbey is married with one child.

kusaal: Otor anԑ diib kanԑ an GaDangme (Ga) buudi banԑ bԑ Ghana la dikpԑŋ kanԑ ka ba maani bԑ "Liiba malʋŋ" ni, bԑԑ biig yʋ'ʋr pʋdib ni.
english: Otor (also Eto, Oto or Otoor) is a food formulated by the GaDangme (Ga) tribe of Ghana for special occasions such as the "Twins Festival" (Akweley Suma), Outdooring Naming Ceremony and 8th Day Abrahamic circumcision.

kusaal: Eto (ka si'eba sͻbidili etor) anԑ Akan dimi tiak ka li sͻb mԑŋ anԑ oto (or otoor), nwa anԑ Ga-buudi pian'ad ni ka an sͻb kanԑ da bԑ hali yʋʋm tusir, kͻbisniinam saŋa sa.
english: Eto (also spelled etor) is an Akan corruption of the actual name oto (or otoor), a Ga-language word dating to the 1800s.

kusaal: GaDangme Etor an dikanԑ yʋ'ʋri yi hali bԑ "Liiba malʋŋ" ni.
english: GaDangme Etor is the most popular of the sacred foods prepared during the "Twins Festival".

kusaal: Eugene Boakye Antwi da du'anɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi.
english: Eugene Boakye Antwi (born 1970) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Subin Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da paami o PGDIP kasɛtta gbaʋŋnɛ Post Certificate Market Research.
english: He had his PGDIP from the Post Certificate Market Research.

kusaal: O da paami o Higher National Diploma yinɛ Westminster College, UK.
english: He had his Higher National Diploma from Westminster College, UK.

kusaal: Ka mɛ paami o B A Business Administration yi University of Westminster.
english: He further had his BA in Business Administration from the University of Westminster.

kusaal: O tʋmnɛ Barclays Banki dinɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋm buon ye ABSA lin yi yʋʋmtusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai paae yʋʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ ayi.
english: He is a banker at the Barclays Bank now ABSA from 1999 to 2002.

kusaal: O daa anɛ tʋntʋnnɛ bɛ Lord Chancellors Department lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi ken paae yʋʋmatusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ.
english: He was the Administrator of Lord Chancellors Department from 2002 to 2006.

kusaal: Onɛ da an kpɛɛm tis EUGASS Limited, lin yi yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ ken paae yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ.
english: He was the Director of EUGASS Limited from 2006 to 2016.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani bɛ tis Subin bɛ Kumasi sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Subin Constituency in the Ashanti region.

kusaal: O anɛ Gaana nid ka an onɛ tʋm pɔlitiks tʋʋma.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Subin Constituency in the Ashanti region.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ tʋm banki ni.
english: He is a banker at the Barclays Bank now ABSA from 1999 to 2002.

kusaal: Evans Bobie Opoku anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la nɛ anii la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni zi'eni tis Asunafo North Constituency bɛ Ahafo Region.
english: Evans Bobie Opoku is a Ghanaian politician who served as a member of the Seventh Parliament and Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Asunafo North Constituency in the Ahafo Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) la, Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o lieb minista kanɛ gɔsid pʋ'asada nɛ dasam nɛ ninwisigir nya'andɔl.
english: In 2021, Nana Akufo-Addo appointed and swore him in as the Deputy Minister for Youth and Sports.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Evans Bobie Opoku nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi Nwadis piinɛ ayi la yiiga daar (1 December 1974).
english: Evans Bobie Opoku was born on 1 December 1974 and hails from Dadiesoaba in the Ahafo region.

kusaal: O da sɔbi o BECE yʋʋm tusir kɔbiwai nɛ piswai la ni (1990) ka naae o SSSCE yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan la ni (1993).
english: He completed his BECE in 1990 and his SSSCE in 1993 at Gyamfi Kumanin senior High school/ Ahafoman senior High Technical school.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maali o GCE yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1996).
english: He further had his GCE in 1996.

kusaal: Ka yʋ'ʋn maali o diploma in Adults Education University of Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi la ni (2002).
english: He later obtained his diploma in Adult education from the University of Ghana in 2002.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la nii (2012), o da naae o master's degree in Development Management University of Cape Coast ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni (2020), o da maali o lɔyanam zamisʋg (LLB in Law).
english: In 2012, he had his master's degree in Development Management from the University of Cape Coast and in 2020, he had his LLB in Law.

kusaal: Evans da anɛ General manager din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) ka da lɛn an kpɛɛmkanɛ gɔsid ligidpɛmisa yɛla Ahafo Community Bank Limited yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2002) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2006).
english: Evans was the General manager from 2010 to 2016 and also the Credit manager for the Ahafo Community Bank Limited from 2002 to 2006.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'an din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1997) paae yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999).
english: He was a tutor from 1997 to 1999.

kusaal: Evans anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la (NPP) nid ka an Wadmaani (MP) tis Asunafo North Constituency bɛ Ahafo region.
english: Evans is a member of NPP and currently the MP for the Asunafo North Constituency in the Ahafo region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la,o da di kʋk la nɛ vɔɔtnam tusa pistan nɛ anaasi, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (34,684) ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg (NDC) nid la, Mohammed Haruna paam tusa pistan nɛ yinne, kɔbistan nɛ pisnaasi (31,340).
english: In the 2020 Ghana general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 34,684 votes whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Mohammed Haruna had 31,340 votes.

kusaal: O anɛ Regional Minista kʋdʋgʋ tis Bono Ahafo region ka an Regional minista tis Ahafo region.
english: He was formerly the Regional Minister for the Bono Ahafo region and the Regional minister for the Ahafo region.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn gaŋ o ye o gɔsid Bono-East region la nɛ ban na ti paam minista tis sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He was also appointed the care-taker as regional minister for the Bono-East region.

kusaal: Evans paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Government Assurance ka lɛn paas banɛ gɔsid Environment, Science and Technology Committee.
english: Evans is a member of the Government Assurance committee and also a member of Environment, Science and Technology Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la (2020), Evans da nɔk bu'ata banɛ piesid nu'us la, ki'ibʋnam nɛ la'ad bɛdigʋ tis Asunafo North Constituency Na'anam nɛ ba nidib ban'akanɛ yʋ'ʋri an COVID-19 la saŋa.
english: In 2020, Evans presented veronica buckets, soaps and other items to the people of the Asunafo North Constituency during the COVID-19 pandemic.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maali o bachelor's degree in Social Work nɛ Psychology yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008).
english: He further continued his education to gain his bachelor's degree in Social work and Psychology in 2008 from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o minister kanɛ gɔsid pʋ'asada, nɛ dasam nɛ ninwisigir yɛla la nya'andɔl.
english: He was appointed as the deputy minister for Youth and sports.

kusaal: Evans anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Evans is a Christian.

kusaal: Every Ghanaian Living Everywhere (EGLE) anɛ pɔlitis na'adɔkanɛ pʋ kpi'em sʋ'ʋŋa vɔɔtʋginɛ Ghana.
english: Every Ghanaian Living Everywhere (EGLE) is an inactive political party in terms of elections in Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana wada pa'al ye, pɔlitis na'adɔɔg wʋsa nar ye di bɛ district naming ka di sʋŋ ka ba vʋi, amaa lax enforcement zug, EGLE nam kpɛn anɛ pɔlitis na'adɔɔg din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai la ni (2019).
english: According to Ghanaian law, political parties must have a presence in all districts in order to remain registered, but due to lax enforcement, EGLE remains registered as a party as of 2019.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi nwadis piinɛ ayi la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 December 2004) vɔɔtʋgin la, EGLE da paas Grand Coalition dinɛ da di kʋgʋsa anaasi (4) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan (230 seats) pʋʋgin.
english: In the 7 December 2004 general elections, EGLE was part of the Grand Coalition which won 4 out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Edward Mahama, onɛ da an Grand Coalition na'anya'ad la, da di vɔɔt la yinne du'ali awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.9%) yi zuraan vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: Edward Mahama, the Grand Coalition candidate, won 1.9% of the vote in the presidential elections.

kusaal: EGLE, dinɛ tuon gati an Owuraku Amofa, da nya' yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) zuraan vɔɔtʋg la, o da naal nɛ Ma'asim tiid na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) dinɛ ka Jerry Rawlings da an di tuon gat la.
english: EGLE, led by Owuraku Amofa, contested the 1992 presidential election in an alliance with the National Democratic Congress (NDC) led by Jerry Rawlings.

kusaal: Progressive Alliance, nwɛnɛ ban da buoni di si'em la, da yis zuraan na'anya'ad yinne onɛ da an, Rawlings, nɛ o nya'adɔl yinne onɛ da an, Kow Nkensen Arkaah, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi nwadis piinɛ yinne la daba atan daar (3 November 1992).
english: The Progressive Alliance, as it was called, put forward a single candidate for president, Rawlings, and a single vice presidential candidate, Kow Nkensen Arkaah, on 3 November 1992.

kusaal: Ba da diya nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ anii du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (58.4%) ka da an yiiga zuraan nɛ o nya'andɔl Fourth Republic of Ghana la ni.
english: They won 58.4% of the popular vote and became the first president and vice president of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayin wadis piinɛ ayi dabpisi nɛ awai daar (29 December 1992) wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg, EGLE da di kʋg yinne (1) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi (200 constituencies) pʋʋgin, ka lieb na'adɔkanɛ zu'oe paasi atan daa wadmaannib yin la.
english: In the 29 December 1992 parliamentary election, EGLE won 1 out of 200 constituencies, becoming the third-largest party in parliament.

kusaal: Di pʋ nyaŋi nya' vɔɔtsi'a ya'asa din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la.
english: It has not contested any elections since the 2004 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Eyiah Kyei Baffour anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ politiks wɛ'ɛd nɛ wdamaan pass wadamaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la bɛ Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la,o anɛ wadmaan tis Lower West Akim Constituency n bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Eyiah Kyei Baffour (born 1 February 1968) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Lower West Akim Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O daa di'e CA n yi Institute of Chartered Accountants, Ghana, nɛ MBA n bɛ University of Ghana, ka di'e o CTA n bɛ Chartered Institute of Tax Accountants.
english: He earned his CA from the Institute of Chartered Accountants, Ghana, his MBA from the University of Ghana, and his CTA from the Chartered Institute of Tax Accountants.

kusaal: Luis de Ossó, Bartomeu Terradas, Otto Kunzle, Otto Maier, Enric Ducal, Pere Cabot, Carles Pujol, Josep Llobet, John Parsons, and William Parsons bama an banɛ da la'as taaba ka Barcelona la'asʋg nwa naam.
english: Eleven players attended – Walter Wild (the first president of the club), Luis de Ossó, Bartomeu Terradas, Otto Kunzle, Otto Maier, Enric Ducal, Pere Cabot, Carles Pujol, Josep Llobet, John Parsons, and William Parsons – and formed Foot-Ball Club Barcelona.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kʋbis wai nɛ yinnɛ la nii la, an yʋʋm kanɛ ka Barcelona pin'il ba nwɛ'ɛb n bɛ Iberian Peninsula, nɛ Copa Macaya ka lɛ da mɔ gʋ'ʋŋ ka Hispania AC di ya'an kan, amaa yʋʋm kan nya'aŋ laa, Barca da di ba yiiga ya'an kanɛ anɛ piece of silverware, ka lɛn paas mɛ nwɛ' dinɛ da ka ti boun yɛ first Copa del Rey ka lɛ pʋ nyaŋi di ya'anɛ, ba di nɛ yinnɛ ka Bizcaya dinɛ la'as anɛ, Athletic Club nɛ Bilbao FC) da di ayi ka di ya'an ka bas Barcelona FC.
english: In 1901, the club participated in the first football competition played on the Iberian Peninsula, the Copa Macaya, narrowly losing to Hispania AC, but in the following year, Barça won the tournament, the club's first-ever piece of silverware, and then participated in the first Copa del Rey, losing 1–2 to Bizcaya (a combination of players from Athletic Club and Bilbao FC) in the final.

kusaal: Ba da pʋ nam mi' di ya'an di yi Campionat de Catalunya bɛ 1905 saŋa sa.
english: They had not won a competition since the Campionat de Catalunya in 1905.

kusaal: Di da ŋɔk nɛ team suma banɛ yid Languedoc, Midi nɛ Aquitaine (Southern France), nɛ Basque Country.
english: It consisted of the best teams of Languedoc, Midi and Aquitaine (Southern France), the Basque Country and Catalonia, all former members of the Marca Hispanica region.

kusaal: FC Barcelona team tita'ada nam da anɛ Carles Comamala, Alfredo Massana, Amechazurra, Paco Bru, and Jack Greenwell.
english: Notable figures of Barça's first great team include Carles Comamala, Alfredo Massana, Amechazurra, Paco Bru, and Jack Greenwell.

kusaal: Kilab da lɛn tiaki ba pian'uk yi ba pian'ʋk kʋdʋg la yi Castilian lɛb Catalan.
english: During the same period, the club changed its official language from Castilian to Catalan and gradually evolved into an important symbol of Catalan identity.

kusaal: Fulunfuk waidig la dabis anaasi, yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kʋbis wai nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi, kilab la da di yiiga ball yɛ ba girim Ramón Torralba onɛ da nwɛ' din yi 1913 keŋ paae 1928.
english: On 4 February 1917, the club held its first tribute match to honour Ramón Torralba, who played from 1913 to 1928.

kusaal: Gamper da nɔk Paulino Alcántara 1912 ye onɛ an onɛ di gɔal nami gad nwɛ'ɛdib wʋsa, ka mɛ nɔk Jack Greenwell ye o an Barcelona's first full-time manager.
english: In 1912, Gamper recruited Paulino Alcántara, the club's seventh all-time top-scorer.

kusaal: Alcántara nɛ Barça team da bɛ Greenwell da anɛ Sagibarba, Ricardo Zamora, Josep Samitier, Félix Sesúmaga, nɛ Franz Platko.
english: Along with Alcántara, the Barça team under Greenwell also included Sagibarba, Ricardo Zamora, Josep Samitier, Félix Sesúmaga, and Franz Platko.

kusaal: Barca yʋʋn da nyaŋi di awai yi nwɛ'ɛb piiga pʋʋgin anɛ dinɛ bɛ Campionats de Catalunyadin yi 1919 keŋ paae 1928 ka lɛn mɛ di ayi dinɛ anɛ Copa del Rey din yi 1920 ti paae 1922.
english: This team won nine out of ten Campionats de Catalunya between 1919 and 1928 and two Copa del Rey titles in 1920 and 1922.

kusaal: Bɔɔl lʋgʋr kaŋa da pin'ili yʋʋm 1899 la ni.
english: Founded in 1899 by a group of Swiss, Catalan, German, and English footballers led by Joan Gamper, the club has become a symbol of Catalan culture and Catalanism, hence the motto Més que un club ("More than a club").

kusaal: Ban nɛ swiss, catalan, German nɛ na'asaal bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib kanɛ ka John Gamper aan by tuongat, bɔɔl lʋgʋr kaŋa yʋ'ʋn anɛ zanbinɛ tis catalan dim malima nɛ ba itima.
english: Founded in 1899 by a group of Swiss, Catalan, German, and English footballers led by Joan Gamper, the club has become a symbol of Catalan culture and Catalanism, hence the motto Més que un club ("More than a club").

kusaal: Di pɛ'ɛsi zin'is atan ni fɔtbɔɔl lʋgʋr kanɛ mɔr ziesim nɛ tɛbisim dunia zug.ka di ligidi gɛligir na an' wʋʋ $5.6 billion nam.Ka lɛn pɛ'ɛs zin'is anaasi ni dunia ni, ti ya'a gɔs ligidi gɛligir pʋʋgʋn.
english: It is the third-most valuable football club in the world, worth $5.6 billion, and the world's fourth richest football club in terms of revenue, with an annual turnover of €800.1 million.

kusaal: Barcelona yʋ'ʋma anɛ "Cant del Barça", onɛ sɔbi li la anɛ Jaume Picas nɛ Josep Maria Espinàs.
english: The official Barcelona anthem is the "Cant del Barça", written by Jaume Picas i Guiu and Josep Maria Espinàs.

kusaal: Barcelona da dɛŋnɛ nwɛ'ɛd nɛ ningɔtis banɛ an' bʋlʋ nɛ fusieba banɛ ka ba pʋd ye Blaugrana.
english: Barcelona traditionally play in dark shades of blue and garnet stripes, hence nicknamed Blaugrana.

kusaal: Pisi nɛ anii (28) La Liga, pistan nɛ ayi (32) Copa del Rey, ayi (2) Copa de la Liga, piinanu (15) Supercopa de España nɛ atan (3) Copa Eva Duarte ni.
english: Domestically, Barcelona has won a record 82 trophies: 29 La Liga, 32 Copa del Rey, 2 Copa de la Liga, 16 Supercopa de España and 3 Copa Eva Duarte titles, as well as being the record holder for the latter four competitions.

kusaal: Teŋgbaŋ wʋsa fɔtbɔɔl nam la, Barca dinɛ pisi nɛ ayi (22) Europe nɛ dunia wʋsa ya'an diib nɛ bam banu (5) UEFA Champions League ya'an diib, bam anaasi (4) four UEFA Cup Winners' Cups, a record bʋnam atan Inter-Cities Fairs Cups, bʋnama anu UEFA Super Cups, nɛ ya'an diib banɛ tɔn'ɔg taaba , ayi Latin Cups nɛ atan FIFA Club World Cap nam.
english: In international club football, Barça has won 22 European and worldwide titles: five UEFA Champions League titles, a record four UEFA Cup Winners' Cups, a record three Inter-Cities Fairs Cups, five UEFA Super Cups, a joint record two Latin Cups and three FIFA Club World Cups.

kusaal: Bɔɔl lʋgʋr kaŋa nɛ Real madrid bɔɔl lʋgʋr la yʋʋnnɛ taaba bɛɛ pʋ siakid taaba nɔɔrɛ.Ka ba yʋ'ʋn buonɛ ba ye, El Clásico.
english: In November 2010, Barcelona defeated their main rival Real Madrid 5–0 in El Clásico.

kusaal: Barcelona bɔɔl nwɛdib la nya'aŋi di alas taaba ya'an diib piini Ballon d'or bam piiga nɛ ayi.
english: He was crowned European Footballer of the Year in 1973 during his first season with Barcelona (his second Ballon d'Or win; he won his first while playing for Ajax in 1971).

kusaal: Ka banɛ di anɛ Romário, Ronaldo, Rivaldo, Ronaldinho nɛ Lionel Messi.
english: Barcelona players have won a joint record twelve Ballon d'Or awards, with recipients including Johan Cruyff, as well as a record six FIFA World Player of the Year awards, with winners including Romário, Ronaldo, Rivaldo, Ronaldinho and Lionel Messi.

kusaal: Barcelona anɛ lʋgʋr yinnɛ kanɛ pɛ'ɛs nidib atan banɛ yɔ'ɔg Primera División la.
english: In 1999, the club celebrated its centenari, winning the Primera División title, and Rivaldo became the fourth Barcelona player to be awarded European Footballer of the Year.

kusaal: Din yi hali 1929 nɛ banɛ zɔt wʋsa wʋʋ Bilbao and Real Madrid la.
english: Barcelona is one of three founding members of the Primera División that have never been relegated from the top division since its inception in 1929, along with Athletic Bilbao and Real Madrid.

kusaal: Yʋʋma Tusa nɛ awai (2009) la Barcelona da an' yiiga bɔɔl lugʋr kanɛ an' Spanish dim la di tɛn'ɛs wʋsa to win the continental treble diema la.
english: In 2009, Barcelona became the first Spanish club to win the continental treble consisting of La Liga, Copa del Rey and UEFA Champions League titles, and also became the first European football club to win six competitions in a single year.

kusaal: Dinɛ ka tiim / bɔɔl lʋga bamɛ pɛ'ɛs , La Liga, Copa del Rey and UEFA Champions League titles, ka lɛn di yiiga ya'an Europe dim bɔɔl nam bam ba ayuobu yʋʋm yinnɛ pʋʋgʋn.
english: In 2009, Barcelona became the first Spanish club to win the continental treble consisting of La Liga, Copa del Rey and UEFA Champions League titles, and also became the first European football club to win six competitions in a single year.

kusaal: Spanish Super Cup, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup.
english: In international club football, Barça has won 22 European and worldwide titles: five UEFA Champions League titles, a record four UEFA Cup Winners' Cups, a record three Inter-Cities Fairs Cups, five UEFA Super Cups, a joint record two Latin Cups and three FIFA Club World Cups.

kusaal: Ka ba lɛn di yʋʋm 2015 bɔɔl la ya'as la ka di pɛ'ɛs nɔɔra anu kɛ ka ba an' yiiga banɛ di ya'an Europe bɔɔl nwɛb pʋʋgʋn nɔɔrim bʋyi sa.
english: On 11 August, Barcelona started the 2015–16 season winning a joint record fifth European Super Cup by beating Sevilla 5–4 in the 2015 UEFA Super Cup.

kusaal: FC Barcelona da pamm pin'il suŋ bɛnɛ ba sʋ'ʋlʋmin nɛ ba teŋ la wʋsa nɔba ball nwɛ' pʋʋgin, ba da di ya'an ban, Campionat de Catalunya nɛ Copa del Rey pʋʋgin.
english: Barcelona had a successful start in regional and national cups, competing in the Campionat de Catalunya and the Copa del Rey.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋm tʋsir nɛ kʋbis wai nɛ anii la ka , Hans Gamper kanɛ ka ti buon nannanna yɛ Joan Gamper da ki'ilim nwɛ'ɛdib la tuongat kanɛ da kena mʋkid din na niŋ si'em kaFC Barcelona da kpi.
english: In 1908, Hans Gamper – now known as Joan Gamper – became club president, attempting to prevent Barcelona from shutting down.

kusaal: FC Barcelona da namisid nɛ ligidi yɛla, nidib yɛla hali nɛ ban nwɛ' si'em.
english: On 14 April 2026, Barcelona were eliminated from the Champions League quarter-finals again by Atlético Madrid, falling 3–2 on aggregate after a 2–0 first-leg deficit.

kusaal: Hans Gamper da ye Barcelona kʋ tunɛ kpi ka mɛ kʋ kpi.
english: In 1908, Hans Gamper – now known as Joan Gamper – became club president, attempting to prevent Barcelona from shutting down.

kusaal: Stadium kan yʋun da an dinɛ bɛɛ onɛ sʋŋ kilab la ka o zi'en ka yalig din yi yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kʋbis wai nɛ piiga saŋa sa ka ki'ilim kilab kanɛ bɛ zin'ig wʋsa, ka di ya'an din an Campionats de Catalunya nɔɔri atan ka daʋŋ kae din yi yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kʋbis wai nɛ awai awai keŋ paae yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kʋbis wai nɛ pii nɛ yinnɛ, ka di Copa del del Rey nɔɔri atan yʋʋma anaasi pʋʋgin, din yi yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kʋbis wai nɛ piiga keŋ paae yʋum tʋsir nɛ kubis wai nɛ pii nɛ atan, ka lɛn di Pyrenees Cup din yi yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kʋbis wai nɛ piig la keŋ paae yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kubis wai nɛ pii nɛ atan la.
english: The stadium is regarded as the main element that helped the club grow in the 1910s and become a dominant team, winning three successive Campionats de Catalunya between 1909 and 1911, three Copa del del Rey in four years between 1910 and 1913, and four successive Pyrenees Cup between the inaugural year in 1910 and 1913.

kusaal: Pyrenees Cup la da anɛ kap yinnɛ kanɛ da anɛ yiiga international kap kanɛ da bɛ Europe sʋ'ʋlimin.
english: The Pyrenees Cup was one of the earliest international club cups in Europe.

kusaal: Kilab la nidib kʋda banɛ da bɛ Marca Hispanica.
english: It consisted of the best teams of Languedoc, Midi and Aquitaine (Southern France), the Basque Country and Catalonia, all former members of the Marca Hispanica region.

kusaal: Gamper onɛ da gɔs kilab la yɛla la da yɔ'ɔg sour ye o nɔk nidib paas kilab ni, ka din yi 1922 la ka kilab mɔr nidib wʋʋ tʋsa piis, banɛ sʋŋid ye ba gɔs stadium pa'al la yɛla.
english: Gamper simultaneously launched a campaign to recruit more club members, and by 1922, the club had more than 20,000, who helped finance a new stadium.

kusaal: Gamper tuongadʋg saŋa la wʋsa Barcelona nyaŋi di ya'an ba nwɛ'ɛb pʋʋgin, yinnɛ yinne piiga nɛ yinne din anɛ Campionats de Catalunya,ka di Copa del Rey nami ayuobʋ nɛ Pyrenees kap nami anaasi.
english: In total, during the Gamper-led era, Barcelona won eleven Campionats de Catalunya, six Copa del Rey and four Pyrenees Cups.
