kusaal: Mahama da si'iŋi o biilim sakuri bɛ Sakasaka Presby Experimental Sakur linɛ bɛ Tamale nɛ Achimota sakurin la.
english: Mahama had his basic education at Sakasaka Presby Experimental School in Tamale and Achimota schools.

kusaal: O da keŋi o secondary sakuri bɛ Prempeh College Kumasi, Ashanti Region la.
english: He attended secondary school at Prempeh College in Kumasi, Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O da paamnɛ vɔt bam 40,624 ka o tiraan Alhassan Abdul Fatawu onɛ da an Ma'asim Tiig nid la mɛ mɔr vɔt bam 24,755.[10] Mahama da faaen kυk la nɛ yi Mohammed Habib Tijani, onɛ da Minister for Foreign Affairs nya'andɔl la san'an Akufo-Addo na'am win, onɛ da faaen kυk la hali zi'in tis Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la lin yi yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yi'ka yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi la ni ka o zan'as ye o kυ lɛn zi'enɛ.
english: Mahama succeeded Mohammed Habib Tijani, Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs under the Akufo-Addo government, who had been member of parliament since recapturing the seat for the New Patriotic Party in the 2012 elections.

kusaal: Fati Seidu anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas Second parliament of the Fourth republic ni zi'eni tis Bawku Central constituency bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Fati Seidu is a Ghanaian politician who was the member of the Second parliament of the Fourth republic representing the Bawku Central constituency in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da zi'en Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zugʋ nya' Bawku Central kʋk la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yuobʋ (1996) vɔɔtʋg la ni ka da di nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan, nɛ pisnaasi nɛnu (30,045) yi vɔɔt tusa pisnu nɛ naasi, kɔbistan nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (54,327) pʋʋgin dinɛ zɛmnɛ vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ ayi du'ali pisnii kɔbiga pʋʋgi (42.80%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka o na'anya'ad tiraan la Hawa Yakubu da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne, kɔbisnaasi nɛ piswai nɛ tan (21,493) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pistan' du'al pisyuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (30.60%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka Awini Emmanuel Akami onɛ da paam vɔɔt tusa ayi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (2,789) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔta anaasi du'al nɛɛmkɔbiga pʋʋgin (4.00%).
english: She contested for the Bawku Central seat on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) during the 1996 parliamentary election and won polling 30,045 votes out of the 54,327 valid votes cast which represented 42.80% of the entire votes cast against Hawa Yakubu who polled 21,493 votes which represented 30.60% of the entire votes cast and Awini Emmanuel Akami who polled 2,789 votes representing 4.00%.

kusaal: O da kɔ'ɔŋi o kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la ni (2000 parliamentary election) ka Hawa Yakubu da di amaa o da ye ba maligim kaanl vɔɔt la ya'as bɔzugɔ o da pa'al ye Electoral Commission kaanin vɔɔt la zaba la pa'a kɛya ka daʋŋ bɛ di pʋʋgin.
english: She lost the seat however during the 2000 parliamentary election to Hawa Yakubu but demanded a recount of the votes as she claimed counting of the votes by the Electoral Commission had been interrupted by violence in the area.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni (2004), Mahama Ayariga da di'e o zi'esim Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg nɔba zugʋ nya' Bawku Central constituency.
english: In 2004, she was replaced by Mahama Ayariga as the parliamentary candidate of the NDC for the Bawku Central constituency.

kusaal: Ayariga da keŋ tuoni di kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la ni (2004 parliamentary election) ka din nya'aŋ ka o yis onɛ dɛŋim zin' I kʋk la zug la Hawa Yakubu.
english: Ayariga went on to win the seat during the 2004 parliamentary election and consequently unseated the then incumbent member of parliament, Hawa Yakubu.

kusaal: O da paas council bɛ University for Development Studies.
english: She once served on the council of the University for Development Studies.

kusaal: Pʋlis pa'al ye zaba an pɔlitis zaba la, di tiaki lieb buudi zaba ka Mamprusis nɛ Kusasi zabid.
english: The violence according to the police even though political, had evolved into a tribal conflict between the Mamprusis and the Kusasis.

kusaal: Felicia Adjei (Ba da du'a o nɛ yuum tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi nwadisa atan la daba atan daar, 3 March 1974) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an pɔlitis wɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan tis Kintampo South Constituency bɛ Brong Ahafo Region Ghana nwa ni.O anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Felicia Adjei (born 3 March 1974) is a Ghanaian politician and was the Member of Parliament for Kintampo South Constituency in the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adjei bɛ Anyima, Brong Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Adjei was born in Anyima, Brong Ahafo Region.

kusaal: O da pin'ili o sakur bɛ Kintampo Methodist Sakur la ni.O mɔr kasɛtta gbaʋŋ kanɛ buon ye advanced diploma bɛ Catering, Food and Nutrition n bɛ Adventist Vocational Institution ka nannana ka li tiak an Techiman Campus of the Valley View University.
english: She holds an advanced diploma in Catering, Food and Nutrition from the Adventist Vocational Institution now Techiman Campus of the Valley View University.

kusaal: O lɛm mɔr kasɛtta gbaʋŋ kanɛ buon ye Cookery for Catering Industry diploma yi Sunyani Polytechnic ka nannana ka li an Sunyani Technical University.
english: She also holds a Cookery for Catering Industry diploma from the Sunyani Polytechnic now Sunyani Technical University.

kusaal: O daa di 2016 vɔɔtʋg la nɛ o lieb wadmaan tis Kintampo South Constituency n paas wadmaandib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kane paasi anaasi la.
english: She won the 2016 parliamentary elections to become a member of parliament for Kintampo South Constituency in the 7th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: On daa di la, ka paam 15,266 vɔɔts kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o paami 51.79% ka basi o na'anya'ad tiraan na Gyan Alexander on zi'enɛ tis wabʋg na'adɔɔg la, on mɛ daa paami 14,210 vɔɔts kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o paami 48.21%.
english: She won after garnering 15,266 votes representing 51.79% against her contender Gyan Alexander of the New Patriotic Party who had 14,210 representing 48.21%.

kusaal: wadmaandib yikane paasi ayɔpɔi la ni, o bɛnɛ la'asʋg bama ni Gender nɛ Children committee nɛ communications committee.
english: In the 7th parliament she served on the Gender and Children committee and the communications committee.

kusaal: O daa keŋ na'asaateŋ on daa tʋʋm bɛ Catering Guest House bɛ Sunyani nya'aŋ la.O daa lɛb Ghana na nɛ o an kpɛɛm bɛ Addfal FA Limited.
english: She moved to the United States of America for a while after working at the Catering Guest House in Sunyani.

kusaal: O daa lɛm ɛɛnb o la'asʋg kanɛ buon ye Felicia Adjei foundation ka o gban'ar daa anɛ ye o tis pʋ'ab paŋ kanɛ nɛ kɛ ka ba zamis nuug tʋʋma , nɛ na'akim nɛ pʋ'asada bɛ sakur nɛ niŋwisigir, kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl , ka ti'el winzug tarim nam nɛ alaafi yɛla ka mɛ sʋŋ teŋmaalʋg yɛla.
english: She also founded the Felicia Adjei foundation with the objective of to empower women through vocational training, youth development through education and sports, farming, supporting the physically challenged and the provision of healthcare and other of community development.

kusaal: Felicia anɛ kristo biig .
english: Felicia is a Christian.

kusaal: La'am nɛ lin an na'ana hali nɛ ban na nwɛdig fest nɛ fêtes folkloriques ka li lieb nananna bʋn, fest noz buudi wa'a la bɛdigʋ anɛ bʋn kʋda, bam da pʋn bɛnɛ Middle Ages saŋa sa, lin da kɛt ka teŋ la nidib gban'ad linɛ da naamid gbin ka mɔr suma'asim ye ba bɛnɛ ba yaanam zin'ig la, relish a deep sense of being with ansestors and with place.
english: Although easy to write off the fest nozou and fêtes folkloriques as modern inventions, most of the traditional dances of the fest noz are ancient, some dating back to the Middle Ages, providing a way for the community to grasp hold of its past and relish a deep sense of being with ancestors and with place.

kusaal: Breton ya' an babiga ba buon ye festoú noz, amaa Goadeg sisters (anɛ nidib banɛ yʋʋm la'asig) da ye buon ye festnozoú, ka French dim mɛ tun'oe yɛl ye des fest-noz.
english: The plural in Breton is festoù noz, but the Goadec Sisters (a family of traditional singers) used to say festnozoù, and the French may also say in French des fest-noz.

kusaal: Daba anu daar, Samampiid nwadig la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi, 5 December, 2012 UNESCO da paas fest noz Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity gbaʋŋin.
english: On 5 December 2012 the fest noz was added by UNESCO to the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Ba baŋ yʋ' kaŋa nɛ 19th century la ni sa, amaa li an woo yʋ'ʋr la tis nɛ yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu,1950s naming la.
english: This term is known since the end of the 19th century but is given as a name only since the 1950s.

kusaal: Buudi wa'a paae kɔbis si'em, ka banɛ ka nidib mi' la anɛ gavottes, an , dro, 'hanter dro,plinn, and Scottish.
english: There are hundreds of traditional dances, of which the most well-known are gavottes, an dro, 'hanter dro, plinn, and Scottish.

kusaal: Jean Michel Guilcher da zamis Breton wa'a la yɛla ka sɔbi li o gbaʋŋ nwa ni"La tradition populaire de dance en Basse-Bretagne (new edition by coop-Breizh/Armen, 1995).
english: The major study on Breton dancing is "La tradition populaire de danse en Basse-Bretagne", book written from his thesis dissertation, by Jean-Michel Guilcher (new edition by Coop-Breizh, Chasse-Marée/Armen, 1995).

kusaal: Second World War la nya'aŋ, Scottish bagpipes (binioú brass) mɛ yʋʋn da bɛ Brittany pʋ'ʋsim kenɛ tit bagadoú (pipes bands) ka lin zugɔ binioú-kozh la lɛdigi li.
english: After the Second World War, the Scottish bagpipes (binioù bras) also became common in Brittany thanks to bagadoù (pipe bands) and thus often replaced the binioù-kozh.

kusaal: Nwiig yʋʋma la'ad, (violin la, double-bass la, acoustic guitar la, bass guitar la) nɛ North American percussion instruments, ba zaŋi ba paasi ba din la ni.
english: String instruments (the violin, the double-bass, the acoustic guitar, the electric guitar, the bass guitar) and North African percussion instruments have long since been adopted.

kusaal: Fest noz la'asig sieba yʋʋm nɛ electronic keyboards nɛ synthesisers (Strobinell, Sonerien Du, Les Baragouineurs, Plantec, etc.).
english: To varying degrees, some fest noz groups also use electronic keyboards and synthesisers (Strobinell, Sonerien Du, Les Baragouineurs, Plantec, etc.).

kusaal: Fest noz (ka sansia ka pian'ak la ye pʋdig zin'isa ayi woo fest-noz, "yʋ'ʋŋ malima" Breton teŋin) anɛ Breton teŋ buudi malima, ka ba la'as bi'el bi'el wa'ad ka yʋʋm-yʋmnib nwɛn'ɛd bʋn nwɛn'ɛda.
english: A fest noz (sometimes hyphenated as fest-noz; "night festival" in Breton) is a Breton traditional festival, with dancing in groups and live musicians playing acoustic instruments.

kusaal: (pl: festtoú noz) anɛ buudi malima wa'a Brittany teŋin.
english: A fest noz (pl.: festoù noz) is a traditional dance festival in Brittany.

kusaal: Nananna, ba mɛ lɛn wa'ad festoú noz kateŋ kɛ ka zin'i sieba baŋi Breton malima la.
english: Currently, many festoù noz are also held outside Brittany within diaspora, bringing the Breton culture to life outside Breton territory.

kusaal: Sansi'en la, ba da ye wa'ad saŋa sieba ka bʋ'ʋdi teŋ la ka li lieb sassi kaba kuod (the "aire neuve"dances ), ani ka ban a buol teŋ la nidib la, linɛ pa'an linɛ kɛ ka ba mɔr nɔba bʋ'ʋd teŋ la wa'a sieba ni la.
english: In the past, the dances were sometimes used to trample the ground to make a firm earth floor in a house or a solid surface for farm work (the "aire neuve" dances), to which people from the neighbourhood were invited, which explains the presence of stamping movements in some of the dances.

kusaal: Teŋ bibis la bɛdigʋ mɔr fest noz nɔɔra ayinne yʋʋm pʋʋgin wʋsa, ninwisigir di'ema la'asig dimi, sakuya nɛ sieba ye gɔsidi li yɛla.
english: Most of the villages have a fest noz at least once a year, organised by the sports clubs, the school, etc. It is a way to express their culture and identity, and to share common values with friends of a night.

kusaal: Tʋʋlʋg saŋa nɛ gɔɔndim saŋa, suoya bɛdigʋ ni, a keŋ fest noz malima nidib bɛdigʋ ni li anɛ woo ban na keŋ yʋ'ʋŋ di'ema gɔsʋg.
english: During the summer and tourist season, in many ways, taking part in a fest noz is for many people like an alternative way of going to a night club.

kusaal: Fest noz la saŋa, ba tuundi gbandaa wɔk bɛɛ gbandaa gbilidi zamisid wa'a nam la ( ba wʋsa zanl nu'us); amaa wa'a la sieba anɛ nidiba ayi yi wa'ad nɛ "choreographed" wa'a nam buudi, ka lin anɛ wa'a buudi banɛ ka baŋir bɛdigʋ kpɛn li pʋʋgin (sequence, figure, etc.).
english: During the fest noz, most dances are practised in a chain or in a circle (everyone holds hands), but there are also dances in pairs and "choreographed" dances, meaning dances enriched with precise artistic elements (sequences, figures, etc.).

kusaal: Ka ba nyaan maal microphones nɛ amplified yʋʋma la'ad, Yʋʋma la'a bama ka ba da mɔri yʋʋm talabard (a sort of oboe or shawm) nɛ Breton bagpipes (binioú kozh), ka li anɛ ba yʋʋma dʋt hali la zug.
english: Before the invention of microphones and amplified instruments, common instruments included the talabard (a sort of oboe or shawm) and the Breton bagpipes (binioù kozh), due to their high volume.

kusaal: Linɛ nam ka nidib mɛ da lɛn mi' ba yɛla anɛ diatonic accordion, clarinet la, ka sanai'a violin la nɛ hardy-gurdy.
english: Also popular was the diatonic accordion, the clarinet, and occasionally the violin and the hurdy-gurdy.

kusaal: clarinet la (treujenn-gaol, 'gabbage core' in Breton) da bɛ ka bɔdig amaa yuoliŋ la ba lɛbna ka lɛn pin'ili widigid.
english: The basic clarinet (treujenn-gaol, 'cabbage core' in Breton) had all but disappeared but has regained popularity over the past few years.

kusaal: Li ka' ban mi' yʋʋma la'asieba la ma'aa bɛɛ, dʋn bama nwa yʋʋma buudi zuoya, lin yi rock, jazz, keŋ punk ka gɛntit teŋ sieba yʋʋma yam.
english: Other than the traditional instruments, there are nowadays groups with many different styles of music ranging from rock, jazz, to punk and also mixes with styles from other countries.

kusaal: Fʋ da nyɛt "free stages".
english: It was common to see the holding of "free stages".

kusaal: Wa'a buudi atan' sʋʋgin wʋsa "suite" (three dances), ba ye gʋoe zi'en ka pian'a nɛ banɛ wa'ad la sieba bɛɛ kenɛ kaad buffet of local dishes woo crêpes, galettes-saucisses, far Breton, nɛ kouign-amann, with local cider, beer, nɛ chouchenn, a mead-like drink ka ba zaŋ siind kanɛ ka ba min'ilim maal.
english: Between every "suite" (three dances), there are short breaks where dancers socialise by chatting to other dancers or visiting the traditional buffet of local dishes like crêpes, galettes-saucisses, far Breton, and kouign-amann, with local cider, beer, and chouchenn, a mead-like drink made from fermented honey.

kusaal: Nidib bɛdigʋ kenɛ malʋŋ la, dinɛ nɔk tɛŋpʋʋg la dim, zi'is bani kpi'e anina, teŋpʋsieba bani bɛ Croatia, nɛ tɛŋkpimis, bani gɔɔnd, nɛ Roman Catholic Church la lʋgʋr wʋsa kpɛmnam.
english: It is attended by many people, including residents of the city, surrounding areas, other parts of Croatia, and neighboring countries, tourists, and representatives of state and local authorities of the Roman Catholic Church.

kusaal: Blaise, onɛ sʋŋ Dubrovnik nidib dinɛ ka o da gʋr teŋ la yi Venice nu'usin.
english: The festivity is based on the legend of the appearance of St. Blaise, who helped the people of Dubrovnik in defending their town against the Republic of Venice.

kusaal: Festus Awuah Kwofie anɛ pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd Gaana, ba da du'anɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la li dabisim anii yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyuobυ nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: Dr. Festus Awuah Kwofie (born 8 January 1967) is a Ghanaian Politician.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anii la Gaana Republic linɛ paas anaasi n zi'enɛ tis Upper Denkyira East Gaana Central Region sυ'υlυm, o anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid(NPP).
english: He was a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Upper Denkyira East Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party(NPP).

kusaal: O yinɛ Buabinso-Dunkwa-Offin linɛ bɛ Gaana Central Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: He hails from Buabinso-Dunkwa-Offin in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O pin'ili o secondary gbaυŋ zamisυg nɛ bɛ Tarkwa Secondary School and Fijai Secondary sakur la ni yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ anii la ni.
english: He had is secondary education at Tarkwa Secondary School and Fijai Secondary school in 1988.

kusaal: O da naae University of Ghana nɛ University of Leicester, ani ka o maal Bachelor of Art Digirɛɛ n bɛ (Statistics, Economics AND Geography) yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ ayi la nika maal o Mastɛs n bɛ line an Business Administration) nɛ Finance yυυma tusa yi' nɛ atan' la ni.
english: He is a graduate of University of Ghana and University of Leicester, where he obtained a Bachelor of Art Degree (Statistics, Economics AND Geography) in 1992 and a Masters in Business Administration) with Finance in 2003 respectively.

kusaal: O da maali o Mastɛs n bɛ linɛ an Applied Business Research nɛ post graduate certificate linɛ an Contemporary management yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yɔpɔi la ni ka maal Swiss Business Sakur n bɛ Zurich linɛ bɛ Switzerland la.
english: He has Masters in Applied Business Research and post graduate certificate in Contemporary management in 2017 with the Swiss Business School in Zurich in Switzerland.

kusaal: Festus n da an CEO tis Jeseque Company Limited tυυma la.
english: Festus was the CEO of Jeseque Company Limited.

kusaal: Onɛ mɛ da an Director n tis Bank of Africa, Ghana.
english: He was also the Director of Risk Management at the Bank of Africa, Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn anɛ Managing Director nya'andɔl n tis Cocoa Merchant Limited tυυma la.
english: He was also the Deputy Managing Director at Cocoa Merchant Limited.

kusaal: Onɛ mɛ da an Chief Finance Officer n tis First African Group Limited tυυma la.
english: He was also the Chief Finance Officer at First African Group Limited.

kusaal: Nannanna o anɛ Board Member tis Ghana Shippers Authority tυυma.
english: He currently a Board Member of the Ghana Shippers Authority.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi la vɔt la ni ka Gaana dim da vɔt ka o di Upper Denkyira East sυ'υlυm kυk la, o da paamnɛ vɔt bam 26,771 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 54.76% n yi kanl la wυsa ni ala ka Ma'asim Tiig nid la Emelia Ankomah da mɔr vɔt bam 22,121 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 45.24% vɔt la kanl wυsa ni, ka GUM nid la Christiana Asante mɛ da mɔr vɔt bam 337 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 0.7% vɔt la kanl wυsa ni, PNC nid Amaniampong Owusu Offin da mɔri 0 vɔt kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 0.0% vɔt la kanl wυsa ni ka PPP nid Fredrick Enchile da mɔr 0 vɔt kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 0.0% vɔt la wυsa kanl pυυgin.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he won the Upper Denkyira East Constituency parliamentary seat with 26,771 votes making 54.76% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Emelia Ankomah had 22,121 votes making 45.24% of the total votes cast, the GUM parliamentary candidate Christiana Asante had 337 votes making 0.7% of the total votes cast, the PNC parliamentary candidate Amaniampong Owusu Offin had 0 vote making 0.0% of the total votes cast and the PPP parliamentary candidate Fredrick Enchile had 0 vote making 0.0% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Festus nɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la li dabisim anii yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyuobυ nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: Festus was born on January 8, 1967.

kusaal: Festus anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid (NPP).
english: Festus is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O da tυmnɛ an kυkdaan nya'andɔl n tis Gender and Children ka paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Bipɔla, Ninwisigir nɛ Buudi malima yɛla la ni n bɛ wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anii la Gaana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la.[1] O mɛ paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid AD-HOC ka ba gaansi Auditor ka ba maal audit the Auditor-General la ni.
english: He was also a member of the AD-HOC Committee that would appoint an Auditor to audit the Auditor-General.

kusaal: Festus anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Festus is a Christian.

kusaal: Di lɛm bɛ Lividim gbaʋŋɔn 12 nii pa'an yɛ ba ya'a yɛ ba zʋŋ pʋa ba nɔkid nɛ pɛ'ɛɔg bɛɛ niiŋkani an kasi bɛɛ dawan ka li an tʋmmbɛ'ɛd malʋŋ ka ba nyuoeɛ bugimin ba ya'a koɛn'ɛs biribiŋ la baŋɔ dapistan' nɛ at an' (33) aya'aŋ.
english: According to the Old Testament rules in Leviticus 12, a woman was to be purified by presenting a lamb as a burnt offering, and either a young pigeon or dove as sin offering, 33 days after a boy's circumcision.

kusaal: Fiifi Fiavi Kwetey ka ba du'a o daba ayi nwadisa ayuobʋ la yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi (1967) la anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd, nɛ National Democratic Congress party la gbaŋ sɔbid (General Secretary) Ghana wʋsa.
english: Fifi Fiavi Kwetey (born 2 June 1967) is a Ghanaian politician and general secretary of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba du'a Kwetey nɛ Hohoe, ka o lɛɛ yinɛ Nogokpo.
english: Kwetey was born in Hohoe but comes from Nogokpo both in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O keŋi o sakur nɛ Bishop Herman College bɛ Kpando la nɛ yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi (1987), ani ka o paam O level gbaʋŋ (Certificate).
english: He attended Bishop Herman College in Kpando in 1987, where he acquired his O level certificate.

kusaal: O tɔlisi keŋ Achimota School n zamisi yi nɛ A level gbaʋŋ (Certificate).
english: He further moved to Achimota School for his A level certificate.

kusaal: O keŋ University of Ghana mɔr Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Psychology.
english: He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Psychology from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994) la nii, o da paam Doplomes de la Chambre de Commerceet d'industrie de Paris (CCIP) (Chamber of Commerce and Industry's Higher Diploma, Paris).
english: In 1994, he obtained the Diplômes de la Chambre de Commerce et d'industrie de Paris.

kusaal: University la ya'aŋa, Kwetey da maal National Service nɛ Parliament office ni, nwadis piiga la yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' (1993) la ni ti paae nwadisa ayɔpɔi la yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994) la ni.
english: After university, Kwetey did his national service with the office of Parliament from October 1993 to July 1994.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋaa, o keŋ Investment Bank Strategic African Securities tʋʋma zin'iginɛ an Financial Analyst nɛ stockbroker.
english: After the mandatory one-year national service, heworked as a financial analyst and a stockbroker at the investment banking firm Strategic African Securities Ltd in July 1995.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la nwadisa ayuobʋ la ni, o da lɛn tʋm nɛ CDH Financial Holdings Ltd n aan ba Funds Manager, Investment Analyst nɛ Stockbroker, lin yi yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ anii la nwadis anaasi (April 1998) nii ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi la, nwadisa ayi la ni.
english: He subsequently moved to CDH Financial Holdings Ltd as a funds manager, investment analyst and stockbroker.

kusaal: Tʋʋm bama saŋa, o da lɛn an pa'an nɛ ligidi yɛla zamisʋg, Ghana Stock Exchange.
english: He worked there from April 1998 to February 2002, whilst also serving as a tutor for some financial courses at the Ghana Stock Exchange.

kusaal: On nan bɛ sakurin ka an sakurbibis la tuongat la, o da anɛ National Democratic Congress wili bɛ University of Ghana Legon Campus la kʋkraan.
english: In university, Kwetey was as a student leader, serving as the chairman for the National Democratic Congress branch on the University of Legon Campus.

kusaal: Nwadis piinɛ ayi la, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) la ni, Kwetey da nya' NDC kpɛŋ vɔɔtʋg ka da di ya'ani da lieb banɛ da pian'adi tit NDC la zan' kpɛɛm.
english: In December 2005, he contested in the national NDC executive elections and won to become the chief communicator for the NDC.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛ nyya'aŋ ka ba tiak yʋ'ʋr la yis Propaganda Secretary la ni n yʋʋn an National Communication Officer.
english: The position of propaganda secretary was subsequently rebranded into the National Communications Officer.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la nii, John Atta Mills da gaŋ o k'o aan Finance Minister, nya'andɔl Kwabea Dufour da an Finance Minister saŋa si'a la.
english: In 2009, Kwetey was appointed by John Atta Mills to serve as deputy minister for finance to Kwabena Duffuor, who was then minister for finance.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012) la ni, Kwetey da di ya'an Ketu South National Democratic Congress tuongat vɔɔtʋg kanɛ da na kɛ k'o paas yʋʋm kan wadmaanib vɔɔtʋgʋn la.
english: In 2012, Kwetey won the Ketu South National Democratic Congress primaries in the 2012 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: Vɔɔt kan nii, o da paam vɔɔtnam 403 nyaŋi lub Albert Ziga, sankan wadmaan onɛ da paam vɔɔtnam 60 n niŋa atan' daan nɛ Raphael Alorwu, onɛ da paam vɔɔtnam 82 n da niŋa ayi daan, ka Nyphson Agbagedy mɛ da paam vɔɔtnam 30.
english: He won the primaries by receiving 403 votes, against 60 votes polled by the then incumbent Albert Ziga, who came third, Raphael Alorwu who polled 82 votes, and Nyphson Agbagedy who got 30 votes.

kusaal: Kwetey da ti di ya'an Keyu South wadmaannam gaansʋg la nɛ 77,837 vɔɔtnam linɛ an 88.92% Ghana wadmaannam vɔɔtʋgʋn la, n lɔb New Patriotic Party Godwin Yayra Nkuawu, onɛ da paam 4,122 vɔɔtnam linɛ an 4.71%.
english: Kwetey subsequently won the Ketu South parliamentary elections by getting 77,837 votes, which represented 88.92% of the votes cast against his closest contender, Godwin Yayra Nkuawu of the New Patriotic Party, who got 4,122 votes representing 4.71%.

kusaal: 2015 yʋʋm la ni, Fiifi Kwetey da lɛn zi'en National Democratic Congress party la zugu nya'a Ketu South wadmaannam vɔɔtʋgʋn la.
english: In 2015, Kwetey was maintained as the National Democratic Congress candidate for the Ketu South constituency going into the 2016 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔtnam 146,10 linɛ an 86.13% n lɔb Sylvanu Amedorme onɛ da paam 1,375 vɔɔtnam, ka Kuadugah paam 637 vɔɔtnam Denu teŋi bɛ Volta region la.
english: He won the primaries by polling 146,10 votes representing 86.13%, to beat Sylvanus Amedorme, who received 1,375 votes, and Famous Kuadugah, who received 637 votes at Denu in the Volta Region.

kusaal: John Dramani Mahama da gaŋ Kwetey niŋ o Minister of State at the Presidency onɛ gɔt Financial and Allied Istitutions nwadisa ayi la yʋʋm 2013 ni.
english: Kwetey was appointed by President John Dramani Mahama to serve as minister of state at the presidency in charge of financial and allied institutions in February 2013.

kusaal: Tʋʋm kan ni la o da gaans nidiba anu la'as ye ba gɔs National Pension Regulatory Authority (NPRA).
english: In that capacity, he inaugurated a five-member steering committee for the National Pensions Regulatory Authority (NPRA) to oversee the implementation of a three-year capacity building agreement with the Swiss government.

kusaal: O pu'a anɛ Naomi Kwetey ka ba mɔr biisa anaasi.
english: Kwetey is married to Naomi Kwetey, and they have four children.

kusaal: O niŋ Ketu South sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana wadmaan nɔɔr ayi.
english: He is a former two-term member of Parliament for the Ketu South constituency in Ghana.

kusaal: O da an National Democratic Congress (NDC) party la Propaganda Secretary.
english: He was propaganda secretary for the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Temisa ayi bɛnɛ Volta Region, Ghana.
english: Kwetey was born in Hohoe but comes from Nogokpo both in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kwetey mɔr University of Ghana la B A HONS.
english: He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Psychology from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: kpɛŋ nwa tʋʋma nii, kan ka o party la da pʋdi li ye, Propaganda Secretary la, o tʋʋm da anɛ o zɛrigid party banɛ kpɛlim bɛ'ɛd yɛla, ka lɛɛ pian'adi kɛt ka o party la tʋʋm sʋma nied paalʋ platforms ni.
english: Serving as the chief communicator, which his party dubbed as the party's propaganda secretary, he was seen as the person to criticize the other parties and raise pertinent issues regarding their parties, whilst defending his party on the necessary platforms.

kusaal: O da digil nɔɔri zi'el ka pin'il tʋʋma nɛ nadisa anaasi la yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai (April 2009) la ni, ban da vɛɛns o Parliament nii naae la.
english: Kwetey was sworn into office in April 2009 after going through vetting in parliament.

kusaal: O da di ya'an 2016 vɔɔtʋgʋn la n niŋ Ketu South wadmaan yʋʋma anaasi ya'as Parliament of Ghana.
english: Kwetey was elected in the 2016 elections to serve as member of parliament for Ketu South for another term in the parliament of Ghana after getting 48,723 votes, representing 65.47% of the total votes against his closest contender, Jim Yao Morti, an independent candidate who got 18,643 votes representing 25.04%.

kusaal: O da paam nɛ 48,723 vɔɔtnam linɛ an 65.47% n lɔbi o tiraan Jim Yao Morti, onɛ da zi'enɛ o mɛŋ zugu nya'a la 18,643 vɔɔtnam linɛ an 25.04%.
english: Kwetey was elected in the 2016 elections to serve as member of parliament for Ketu South for another term in the parliament of Ghana after getting 48,723 votes, representing 65.47% of the total votes against his closest contender, Jim Yao Morti, an independent candidate who got 18,643 votes representing 25.04%.

kusaal: O da tʋm nɛ nɛ' ka da ti lɛn di'e Minister of Food and Agriculture tʋʋma ya'as Clement Kofi Humado nu'ugun.
english: Kwetey was reassigned to serve as minister of food and agriculture to replace Clement Kofi Humado.

kusaal: O pʋtɛn'ɛr da anɛ o kɛ ka kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl lʋgʋr (agriculture sector) la kpɛ' kpikpiʋŋʋn nɛ zʋʋd la ka ka' ye ba kuod nɛ diid yɛla ma'a nɛ.
english: His vision was to push the agricultural ministry into an agribusiness-oriented rather than just a food production-oriented sector.

kusaal: On da an NDC propaganda secretary nɛ onɛda sa'an zugraan kʋdʋg Rawlings, saŋa si'a la, 2007 yʋʋm la ni, o da yɛl banɛ da tʋm US Embassy yʋʋm kan la on nɛ ban sɔnsʋgin ye, ''mɔr kʋ tun'oe niŋ zugraan Republic of Ghana'' nwa nii.
english: In his capacity as propaganda secretary of the NDC and adviser to former President Rawlings, Kwetey in 2007 stated during an interaction with US embassy officials that a Muslim could never become the president of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Amaa o da pʋ nwɛn' nu'ug muslim communuty la hali ti pass nwadisa atan' la 2015 yʋʋm la ni.
english: As of March 2015, he had yet to do so.

kusaal: O tʋʋm da anɛ o tʋm nɛ ligidi zanlim yɛla lʋgʋr la'am nɛ zugraan ɔfissin ka li gɔsid ligidi zanlim tʋʋma zin'is.
english: His role was to work with the finance ministry through the office of the president to monitor and regulate the financial and allied institutions.

kusaal: Fomena bɛ nɛ Adansi North District bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: Fomena is located in the Adansi North District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba kuk la bɛ nɛ Adansi North district bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Adansi North district of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency kaŋa mɔr MP nam anu fourth republic la sin'iŋirin na.
english: This constituency has had five MPs since the beginning of the fourth republic.

kusaal: Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) tʋmmi ba tʋʋma dɔlisid nɛ wada Parts 6, 7, nɛ 8 bɛ Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851).
english: The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) operates under the authority granted by Parts 6, 7, and 8 of the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851).

kusaal: Delese A. A. Darko an CEO tis FDA.
english: Delese A. A. Darko is the CEO of FDA.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, nwadisanu ni (May 2020), FDA da bɛ World Health Organization gbana ni ye li anɛ Level Three lʋgir kanɛ ka ba mi' li ti'ir.
english: In May 2020, the FDA was recognized by the World Health Organization as a Level Three listed institution.

kusaal: Food and Drugs Board da pin'il yiiga nɛ yi Food and Drugs Law of 1992 (PNDCL 305B) ka nya'aŋ ka Food and Drugs (ti'akir) Act 523 of 1996 ka li yʋ'ʋn pa'al ye li nar ka ba maal yaarim sʋŋa ka li nyaŋi maal ningbina, ka mɛ da nɔki li dɔlis 1992 Constitution of Ghana wada la.
english: The Food and Drugs Board was initially established under the Food and Drugs Law of 1992 (PNDCL 305B) and later amended by the Food and Drugs (Amendment) Act 523 of 1996 to mandate salt fortification for addressing nutritional deficiencies and align the law with the 1992 Constitution of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai (1990) da bɔɔd paar la, wada kanɛ da gɔsid tima yela da anɛ Pharmacy and Drugs Act (Act 64) of 1961.
english: Prior to 1990, the regulation of drugs and pharmacy practice was governed by the Pharmacy and Drugs Act (Act 64) of 1961.

kusaal: Amaa, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai ni (1990), Provisional National Defense Council (PNDC) da maal wada kanɛ an Narcotics Drugs Control, Enforcement and Sanctions Law (PNDCL 236), anina ka ba pin'il Narcotics Control Board ye ba gɔs ka gu' ka nidib da nu tiim tʋʋma ba bennɛ ka mɛ sʋŋi gɔs banɛ zuud tima lɔmisid tɛɛns la yela.
english: However, in 1990, the Provisional National Defense Council (PNDC) enacted the Narcotics Drugs Control, Enforcement and Sanctions Law (PNDCL 236), establishing the Narcotics Control Board to combat the growing issue of drug abuse and the international challenges posed by illicit drug trafficking.

kusaal: Li nya'aŋ ka Pharmacy Act, 1994 (Act 489), da pin'il Pharmacy Council ye ba gɔs banɛ zamisid tima yela, nɛ ba kasɛta gbana yela.
english: Later, the Pharmacy Act, 1994 (Act 489), established the Pharmacy Council to oversee the pharmacy profession and pharmacist registration.

kusaal: Baa Food and Drugs Law wada la da kɛn yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi na la (1992), ba kpɛɛmnam la da nan kae ti paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi, nwadisanii, dabpisi nɛ ayuobʋ daar (August 26, 1997).
english: Although the Food and Drugs Law was passed in 1992, the inaugural board was not formed until August 26, 1997.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan' (2023) la, FDA da bas suor ye ba tɔn'e kʋns nidib nɛ malaria pin'im kanɛ ka University of Oxford vɛɛns-vɛɛnsidib da maal la, li da kɛ ka Ghana da an tɛŋ kanɛ an yiiga bas suor ye ba nɔkim kʋns nidib.
english: In 2023, the FDA approved a malaria vaccine created by University of Oxford researchers, making Ghana the first country to approve it for use.

kusaal: Food and Drugs Authority (bɛɛ FDA, da ba da buon ye Food and Drugs Board) anɛ Ghana gɔmɛna lʋgir kanɛ vɛɛnsidi gɔsid diib yela, banɛ kuosid diib, nɛ ban na niŋ si'em ka diib nɛ laafi tima nyaŋi paae Ghana sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.
english: The Food and Drugs Authority (or FDA, formerly known as the Food and Drugs Board) is a Ghanaian government agency responsible for the inspection, certification, and proper distribution of foods and food products as well as drugs in Ghana.The FDA exists to ensure the safety, quality and efficacy of both human and veterinary products.

kusaal: FDA bɛnɛ ye ba gɔs diib yela, laafi tima nɛ li la'ad yela, nɛ la'abane ka ba maani sɔn'ɔd ningbina bɛɛ mɔri kpɛn'ɛd yaan.
english: The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) operates under the authority granted by Parts 6, 7, and 8 of the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851).

kusaal: Wada kanɛ ka ba dɔlis ka gaŋi ba tuongatib anɛ Food and Drugs Law 1992, PNDC Law 305B.
english: The board was established by the Food and Drugs Law 1992, PNDC Law 305B.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992), PNDC da bak tikpi'ema wada yis tiim banɛ kpɛlim la ni, linzug ka ba mɔr wada kanɛ an Food and Drugs Law, 1992 (PNDC 305B) la kɛna.
english: In 1992, the PNDC separated the regulation of non-narcotic drugs from the practice of pharmacy, leading to the enactment of the Food and Drugs Law, 1992 (PNDC 305B).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yi ni (2012), Food and Drugs Board da ti'aki kilim Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) ban da yis wada kanɛ an Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851) la.
english: In 2012, the Food and Drugs Board transitioned into the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) with the enactment of the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851).

kusaal: Ba tʋʋma anɛ ye ba nɔk wada dɔlisi gɔs laafi tima nɛ diib maalig, ban ziidi kpɛn'ɛd ka yit si'em, li kuosig nɛ lin nyaŋidi paad zin'ig wʋsa yela (ti nya'a, ti'vɔnnim, nɛ bʋnkɔnbid tima), tison'odim, tima la'ad, tima banɛ bɛ yaan, taba la'ad, ziim, nɛ ziim la'ad, ka lin gɔsid ka mɛ len gɔsid sibiti ni vɛɛnsanam, lin wʋsa anɛ ye li gu' nidib laafi nɛ bɛilim sʋŋ yela.
english: Its role includes establishing and enforcing standards for the production, importation, exportation, sale, and distribution of food, drugs (herbal, allopathic, and veterinary), cosmetics, medical devices, household chemicals, tobacco products, blood, and blood products, as well as overseeing the regulation of clinical trials, all aimed at protecting public health and safety.

kusaal: Fortunate Atubiga (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar, 27 July 1950) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Fortunate Atubiga (born 27 July 1950) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O da paasnɛ Ghana Fourth Republic wadmaanib yikanɛ an yiiga nɛ ayi la ni zi'eni tis Binduri Constituency bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He was member of the First and Second Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Binduri Constituency in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Atubiga nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar, (27 July 1950), Upper East Regioni bɛ Ghana la.
english: Atubiga was born on 27 July 1950, in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da zamis gbaʋŋʋ paaenɛ GCE Ordinary Level.
english: He was educated to GCE Ordinary Level.

kusaal: Atubiga da zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zugʋ nya' Binduri Constituency kʋk la ka kpɛn' wadmaannib yin yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan yʋʋmpaal nwadig daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 1993) ban da yɛl ye o di yʋʋm tusi, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi Ghana wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la da bɛ nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la.
english: Atubiga was first elected into parliament on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress on 7 January 1993 after he was pronounced winner at the 1992 Ghanaian parliamentary election held on 29 December 1992.

kusaal: O da lɛn di kʋk la ya'as yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ Ghana dim vɔɔtʋgin la, o da paam vɔɔt tusa piiga, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (10,704) yi vɔɔt tusa pisi, kɔbistan' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan pʋʋgin (20,373) dinɛ zɛmnɛ pisnaasi du'al pisyɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (40.70%) ka bas Asaana Dunstan Ayaribilla onɛ da paam vɔɔt tusa anu, kɔbisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (5,806) dinɛ zɛmnɛ pisi nɛ ayi du'al piiga kɔbiga pʋʋgin (22.10%), Mustafa onɛ da paam vɔɔt tusa ayi, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi (2,654) dinɛ zɛmnɛ piiga du'al piiga kɔbiga pʋʋgin (10.10%) nɛ Francis Aboko Ayariga onɛ da paam vɔɔt tusir yinne, kɔbisyi' nɛ awai (1,209) dinɛ zɛmnɛ anaasi du'al pisyuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (4.60%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He then retained his seat in the 1996 Ghanaian general election, polling 10,704 votes out of the 20,373 valid votes cast representing 40.70% over Asaana Dunstan Ayaribilla who polled 5,806 votes representing 22.10%, Mustafa who polled 2,654 votes representing 10.10% and Francis Aboko Ayariga who polled 1,209 votes representing 4.60% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Achidago Bernard Akugri onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nidi da di'e o zi'esim yʋʋm tusa ayi Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni (2000 Ghanaian general elections).
english: He was succeeded by Achidago Bernard Akugri of the National Democratic Congress in the 2000 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Ninbani da paas ninbɛda ayuobʋ la da anɛ Edward Akufo-Addo, Joseph Boakye Danquah, Emmanuel Obetsebi-Lamptey, William Ofori Atta, nɛ Ebenezer Ako-Adjei.
english: Other members of the "Big Six" were Edward Akufo-Addo, Joseph Boakye Danquah, Emmanuel Obetsebi-Lamptey, William Ofori Atta, and Ebenezer Ako-Adjei.

english: Firstly, on 4 August 1897, Gold Coast Aborigines' Rights Protection Society led by John Mensah Sarbah was formed.

kusaal: Founders' Day da sin'iŋ yiiga nɛ dabisa anaasi nwadisa anii yuma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai ka da li bakwai naar ka interior Minister, Ambrose Dery da yel ye dabisir la li Alasid daar la, President Nana Addo Danquah Akufo-Addo dolisidnɛ Executive Instrument (EI) ke ya ka Atini daar daba anu nwadisa anii la an vu'usim dabisir zin'ig wusa.
english: The first Founders' Day, which is 4 August 2019 fell on a weekend therefore the Interior Minister, Ambrose Dery, in a statement said in view of the day falling on a Sunday, the President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo by Executive Instrument (EI), declared Monday, 5 August, as a public holiday to be observed as such throughout the country, he held a Luncheon in honor of Senior citizens at Accra International Conference Centre.

english: The Speaker of Parliament, Prof. Aaron Mike Oquaye delivered a public lecture.

kusaal: Ninkir sieba wennɛ Chief of Staff, Mrs Akosua Frema Opare; Majority Leader nɛ Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Mr Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu; Minister of Food and Agriculture, Dr Owusu Afriyie Akoto; Minister of Information, Mr Kojo Oppong Nkrumah; kpeem kani be Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), Mr Roland Affail Monney da laam be la'asigin la.
english: Key personalities such as the Chief of Staff, Mrs Akosua Frema Opare; the Majority Leader and Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Mr Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu; the Minister of Food and Agriculture, Dr Owusu Afriyie Akoto; the Minister of Information, Mr Kojo Oppong Nkrumah; the President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), Mr Roland Affail Monney were present at the lecture.

kusaal: Open Foundation West Africa da sin'iŋi ba Founders' Day Ghana ye ba gos onɛ yaŋe sobi gaadi o tiran ye ba suŋ Ghana nidib ba zamisug ni dolisidnɛ Wikipedia ni.
english: The Open Foundation West Africa launched its Founders Day Ghana writing contest to increase Ghanaian literature of personalities and events on Wikipedia.

kusaal: Alemis daar dini an daba anaasi nwadisa anii yuma tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi la an Ghana yaanam tendigir, Danquah Institute da la'asnɛ zamisug sia ka li piazug an "The Independence Struggle: Our Heroes and Fight for Democracy".
english: On Thursday 4 August 2022, to commemorate Ghana's Founding Fathers, the Danquah Institute held a lecture on the theme "The Independence Struggle: Our Heroes and the Fight for Democracy".

kusaal: Nwa'asig enti be National Democratic Congress (NDC) nɛ Convention People's Party (CPP) ni an ye ba yisimi li bas ka li anɛ ye vu'usim daar kan pu ta'al nɛ yelsia kudumin nɛ ka li kudun anɛ Akufo-Addo gomena meŋ bɔɔdim ye o tiak kudimin yela.
english: However, there has been some contention by the opposition National Democratic Congress (NDC) and Convention People's Party's (CPP) to cancel it with their premise being that the new holiday is not a true representation of historical facts and is a deliberate attempt by the Akufo-Addo government to rewrite the country's history.

kusaal: Samuel Adu-Gyamfi, pa'an pa'an kpeem onɛ pa'an kudumin nɛ politis zamisug be Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) yel ye president la maannɛ suor ye o yalig United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) dini ka J.B Danquah nɛ George Alfred "Paa Grant" da sin'iŋ yum tusir, koboswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayopoi la.
english: Dr. Samuel Adu-Gyamfi, a senior lecturer in the history and political studies program at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), claims that the president appears to be pursuing an agenda to overexpand the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC), which was founded in 1947 by J.B. Danquah and George Alfred "Paa" Grant.

kusaal: Founders' day anɛ teŋla wusa vʋ'ʋsʋm daar ka li maal ye li tiɛn nimbɛda ayuobʋ banɛ da zabi faaen Ghana la.
english: Founders' Day is a national public holiday observed to commemorate the contributions of all the people, notably the "Big Six" who led the struggle for Ghana's independence.

kusaal: Ba da buoni li nɛ ye "Founder's Day" ka ba da maani li maluŋ pa'an Osagyefo Dr.
english: Founders' Day was formerly called "Founder's Day" (with the letter "S" appearing after an apostrophe) and it was celebrated to commemorate the achievements of Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da nyaŋe maal si'elnam la.
english: Kwame Nkrumah was the first President of Ghana and a member of the "Big Six".

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da an Ghana yiiga President ka da len paas nimbɛda ayuobʋ la.
english: Kwame Nkrumah was the first President of Ghana and a member of the "Big Six".

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ dabis pisinɛ yinnɛ nwadisa awai daar, dinzug ka maluŋ kani an Founder's Day me be dabis pisinɛ yinne nwadisa awai daar yʋʋm wusa ni ye ba na'as on da paas ka ba nyaŋe faan'e Ghana yi naasaanam la nuusin la.
english: The Founders' Day (which was formerly spelt as "Founder's Day") was observed in Ghana on 21 September in year each to mark the birthdate of Ghana's first president, Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, and in remembrance of the struggle for independence by Ghana's brave "Big Six" as the name implies.

kusaal: Dini len paas anɛ piantbani ka speaker of parliament Aaron Mike Oquaye yet, maluŋ kani gaad la o da yel ye li anɛ ziri tita'ar.
english: Notably, this included strong statements made by the former speaker of parliament, Aaron Mike Oquaye, who said that it was "palpably false" to claim that Nkrumah was the founder of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da tiak yuur la nɛ "Founder's Day" ka li yun an "Founders' Day " ka li paal ye ninbeda ayuobo la wusa paas maluŋ la ni ka mor naasi men.
english: As a result, the name was changed from "Founder's Day" to "Founders' Day" – making the word plural to honour the other members of the "Big Six", and include them in the Founders' Day celebrations.

kusaal: Founder's Day be nɛ Ghana ka an yuum wusa dabis pisinɛ yinne nwadisa awai daar dini ann Ghana yiiga president duam dabisir, Osagyefo Dr.
english: The Founders' Day (which was formerly spelt as "Founder's Day") was observed in Ghana on 21 September in year each to mark the birthdate of Ghana's first president, Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, and in remembrance of the struggle for independence by Ghana's brave "Big Six" as the name implies.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah ka me tendig ninbeda ayuobo ("Big Six") la genlis nɛ ban muki faae Ghana nwenni di yuur la pun yel la.
english: The Founders' Day (which was formerly spelt as "Founder's Day") was observed in Ghana on 21 September in year each to mark the birthdate of Ghana's first president, Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, and in remembrance of the struggle for independence by Ghana's brave "Big Six" as the name implies.

kusaal: Zugdaan Nana Addo Danquah Akufo-Addo da die kuk la nɛ ban da bɔɔd ye maluŋ la kpamp ninbeda ayuobo la da ke ya ka o yel parliament ye ba tiakim dabisir la lebis daba anaasi daar nwadisa anii la ni ka li nyaŋe yalik maluŋ la ka kpamp bani da suŋe faae teŋ la wusa.
english: President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo upon assuming office and based on the call to celebrate other members of the "Big Six" proposed a legislation to Parliament to designate 4 August as a new date of the Founders' Day celebration, to widen the scope of the celebration to cover all people who played a key role in the liberation of the country.

kusaal: Nwadisa anii daba anaasi daar ka ba da gaŋ ye li yun an founders' day, di len zabilnɛ dabis suma ayi Ghana kudumin yela.
english: 4 August was apparently chosen as the substantive date to mark founders' day to purposely mark two important days or events in the history of Ghana.

kusaal: Dini len paas la, United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) da sin'iŋ nɛ nwadisa anii daba anaasi daar, yuma tusir, koboswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayopoi ka J.B Danquah nɛ George Alfred Paa Grant da gaad tuon.
english: Furthermore, the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) was formed on 4 August 1947 by J.B. Danquah and George Alfred Paa Grant.

kusaal: Kukdaan Nana Addo Danquah Akufo-Addo da len yel ye dabis pisine yinne nwadisa awai daar na an Kwame Nkrumah tendigir daar ye ba na'asi o duam daar.
english: President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo again proposed that 21 September however should be instituted as Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Day, to commemorate his birthdate.

kusaal: O gba'ar la pudig "Founder's Day" ka di naasid ninbeda ayuobo la "Big Six" ka Osagyefo Dr.
english: The Founders' Day (which was formerly spelt as "Founder's Day") was observed in Ghana on 21 September in year each to mark the birthdate of Ghana's first president, Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, and in remembrance of the struggle for independence by Ghana's brave "Big Six" as the name implies.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah tendigir daar me be li ko o duam daar on da maal sieli tis Ghana ka len an Ghana President kudug la.
english: The decision separated the "Founder's Day" celebration as an honour of the "Big Six" from Dr. Kwame Nkrumah's Memorial Day celebration on his birthdate at the heroic leader of Ghana's independence attainment and a former President of Ghana.

kusaal: Nwadisa atan yuma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai la, Ghana gomena da yis vu'usim daar la ka nwadisa anii daba anaasi daar la yun an "Founders' Day" dabis kani sial nɛ paati dim sin'iŋir – United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) nwadisa anii daba anaasi yum tusir koboswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayopoi.
english: In March 2019, the public holiday amendments bill was passed into law by the Ghanaian government and 4 August was instituted as the "Founders' Day," a day which coincides with the formation of the first political party in the country – the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) on 4 August 1947.

kusaal: Founder's Day la be nɛ ye li na'as ninbeda ayuobo la "The Big Six", bani da faae Ghana yi naasaanam la nu'usim la, ka ke ka Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Day ann Osagyefo Dr.
english: The Founders' Day is reserved to celebrate and honour the people (The Big Six) who led Ghana to independence whilst Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Day is reserved for Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah's birthdate the leader of the movement towards independence.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah duam dabisir, onɛ da gaad tuon ka ba faae ti teŋ la.
english: The Founders' Day is reserved to celebrate and honour the people (The Big Six) who led Ghana to independence whilst Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Day is reserved for Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah's birthdate the leader of the movement towards independence.

kusaal: "Founder's Day" anɛ dabis kani ka Ghana dim tensidi ti yaanam la da zabi ti la'am kpi ye ba faae Ghana ka li be li ko la.
english: The decision separated the "Founder's Day" celebration as an honour of the "Big Six" from Dr. Kwame Nkrumah's Memorial Day celebration on his birthdate at the heroic leader of Ghana's independence attainment and a former President of Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana dim len maan "Founder's Day" ka paasid tuum bani na kpemis Ghana dim teŋ nwa ni nɛ ban be zin'isia wusa ye ba gos ka Ghana ann ba teŋ.
english: The decision separated the "Founder's Day" celebration as an honour of the "Big Six" from Dr. Kwame Nkrumah's Memorial Day celebration on his birthdate at the heroic leader of Ghana's independence attainment and a former President of Ghana.

kusaal: Kae "Founders' Day" la kpemisidnɛ Ghana dim la maa nɛ amaa di ket ka ba gosid ka tuoŋatib la da kpi siem la, ba me pesigi ba meŋi tis teŋ la ban be zin'sia wusa.
english: Activities during the celebration and observance of the "Founders' Day" are meant to encourage the Ghanaians within the country and in the diaspora to accept Ghana as their homeland.

english: The public lecture was chaired by the Overlord of Dagbon, Yaa Naa Abubakari Mahama II, with other traditional rulers from Dagbon being present.

kusaal: Aaron Mike Oquaye da tis public lecture la.
english: The Speaker of Parliament, Prof. Aaron Mike Oquaye delivered a public lecture.

kusaal: Jacob Mahama, da girim nidib wusa bani da paas zaba ye ba faae Ghana la, ka len pian din naar ye ba girimi ba wusa ka kae Kwame Nkrumah maa nɛ.
english: The spokesperson of Yaa Naa, Zamgbali Naa, Dr Jacob Mahama, in his tribute hailed all persons who contributed to the fight for independence and reiterated the essence of honoring all and sundry without focusing entirely on Kwame Nkrumah.

english: According to the NDC, Akufo-Addo seeks to give prominence to his uncle JB Danquah who was a leader in the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC), the political party from which Kwame Nkrumah broke away to form the CPP which won him the election that saw him become Leader of Government Business and Prime Minister and eventually the first president of Ghana.

english: Francis Asenso-Boakye (born 24 September 1977) is a Ghanaian politician and businessman.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Bantama Constituency Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Bantama Constituency in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ deputy Chief of Staff and Political Assistant tis Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo; onɛ an Gaana Pirɛsidɛn la.
english: He was the deputy Chief of Staff and Political Assistant to Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo; President of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadisa awai la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 September 1977) o yinɛ Maase bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: He was born on 24 September 1977 and hails from Maase in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ da an la'asʋg la kʋkdaan on da bɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST).
english: He served as its Founding President while pursuing his undergraduate studies at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST).

kusaal: Asenso-Boakye da naae Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology la, o da lɛn tɔlis tuoni maali o master's degree in Public Policy and Administration as a Rotary Scholar, Michigan State University, Michigan, USA.
english: Asenso-Boakye after completing a degree program at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, pursued a master's degree in Public Policy and Administration as a Rotary Scholar at the Michigan State University, Michigan, USA.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ dɔli H.E Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo nwɛ'ɛd pɔlitiks la, o da tʋmnɛ Gaana lʋg kanɛ gɔsida abɔ tʋʋma tis nidib ka mɛ gɔsid nidib bɛlim sʋŋ yɛla (Ministry of Employment and Social Welfare (MESW), Global Media Alliance (GMA), Delta Acquisitions and Development, Delaware, USA, Michigan House of Representatives, Michigan, USA, Planning Officer at Ghana Free Zones Board (GFZB), a Project Manager for the Tema Export Processing Zone (TEPZ)and a Research Analyst, Ghana Investment Promotion Center (GIPC).
english: Prior to joining the staff and campaign of Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, Asenso-Boakye had worked at the Ministry of Employment and Social Welfare, Global Media Alliance, Delta Acquisitions and Development, Delaware, USA, Michigan House of Representatives, Michigan, USA, been a planning officer at Ghana Free Zones Board, a project manager for the Tema Export Processing Zone and a research analyst at the Ghana Investment Promotion Center.

kusaal: Asenso-Boakye da ln an policy and research associate bɛ Office of State Representative nɛ Michigan Legislative Black Caucus (MLBC) – Michigan House of Representatives, USA, ani ka da gɔsid daʋn banɛ paasid Na'asaa banɛ an ninsabila nɛ buud banɛ pɔɔd sʋ'ʋlim nam la ni.
english: Asenso-Boakye has been a policy and research associate in the Office of State Representative and for the Michigan Legislative Black Caucus, Michigan House of Representatives, USA, where his work focused on policy and legislative issues affecting the interests of African American and minority communities.

kusaal: On da lɛ Gaana la, Asenso-Boakye da tʋm tis Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg NPP ninkanɛ zi'en pirɛsidɛn la ka an pirɛsidɛn tis Gaana la; Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo.
english: On his return to Ghana, Asenso-Boakye worked for the then NPP Presidential Candidate and current president of the Republic of Ghana, Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, as political assistant, a position he held until elected into office as a member of parliament.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la, January 2017, Gaana Zugraan Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Francis Asenso-Boakye ye o an political assistant nɛ Deputy Chief of Staff bɛ Zugraan ɔfisin, Flagstaff House.
english: In January 2017, Francis Asenso-Boakye was appointed the political assistant and Deputy Chief of Staff at the Flagstaff House by President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayuobʋ la ni, June 2020, Asenso-Boakye da di Bantama Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP vɔɔtʋg la ka bas Daniel Okyem Aboagye onɛ da zin'i kʋk la zug la.
english: In June 2020, Asenso-Boakye won the Bantama NPP primaries against the incumbent Daniel Okyem Aboagye in a bid to contest for a seat in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Yuʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, vaar kɔbiga pʋʋgin, o da paamnɛ pisnii nɛ anii nɛ pa'ali (88.84%) ka lieb Wadmaani tis Bantama (Ghana parliament constituency) sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: In the 2020 General Elections, he polled 88.84% of total votes cast to emerge as the parliamentary representative of Bantama (Ghana parliament constituency).He served as the Minister for Ministry of Works and Housing (Ghana) before being appointed as the Minister of Roads and Highways.

kusaal: Asenso-Boakye paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Government Assurance Committee la nɛ la'as kanɛ gɔsid tam nɛ tiis yɛla (Lands and Forestry)
english: Asenso-Boakye is a member of Government Assurance Committee and also a member of Lands and Forestry Committee.

kusaal: O paas Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nidib la ni.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Jerry Rawlings Na'adɔɔg, Provisional National Defence Council da kad Hilla Limann gɔmena yis na'amin yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ Nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpistan nɛ yinne daar la (31 December 1981), Ayariga da zɔ keŋ su'a Nigeria.
english: Following the overthrow of Hilla Limann's government by the Jerry Rawlings-led Provisional National Defence Council on 31 December 1981, Ayariga left for exile in Nigeria.

kusaal: O da bɛ anina yʋma ayuobʋ, ka da fɛndigi lɛb Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1987) ban da yisi o yʋ'ʋr ye o pʋ zu la nya'aŋ.
english: He stayed there for six years, only returning to Ghana in 1987 after he had been cleared of corruption.

kusaal: Ayariga buudi bɛnɛ Tinsungo bɛ Bawku sʋ'ʋlim Upper East Region, Ghana la.
english: Ayariga's family hails from Tinsungo in Bawku in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛm paas Kusasi Royal Family ni.
english: He was also a member of the Kusasi Royal Family.

kusaal: O bikanɛ paasi atan la, Hassan Ayariga da zi'en People's National Convention nɔba zugʋ nya' Ghanaian zuraan vɔɔtʋg kanɛ da naam yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayin wadis piinɛ ayi la ni, December 2012.
english: His third child, Hassan Ayariga was the presidential candidate for the People's National Convention in the Ghanaian presidential election in December 2012.

kusaal: Mahama Ayariga, onɛ an o pʋ'akanɛ paasi ayi la bikpaanr la an wadmaani tis Bawku ka lɛn an Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry kʋdʋg ka nya'aŋ ka o da lieb gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la minister nya'adɔl.
english: Mahama Ayariga, a younger son of his 2nd Wife is the MP for Bawku and a former Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry and later Education.

kusaal: O pʋ'a da anɛ Anatu Ayariga.
english: He was married to Anatu Ayariga.

kusaal: Ka da mɔr biis piinɛ yinne.
english: He had eleven children.

kusaal: Frank Annoh-Dompreh (dʋ'anɛ 25 October 1977) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd nɛ consultant.
english: Frank Annoh-Dompreh (born 25 October 1977) is a Ghanaian politician and consultant.

kusaal: o bɛnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party ka an Wadmaani Nsawam-Adoagyiri.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and was the Member of Parliament for Nsawam-Adoagyiri between Jan 2013 and Jan 2025.

kusaal: O anɛ kʋkdaani tis Parliamentary Select Committee on Foreign Affairs ka lɛn paas banɛ gɔsid Subsidiary Legislation and Roads and Transport Committee.
english: He is the chairperson for the Parliamentary Select Committee on Foreign Affairs and a member of the Subsidiary Legislation and Roads and Transport Committee.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Annoh-Dompreh nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1977) Nsawam-Adoagyiri, bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana la.
english: Annoh-Dompreh was born in 1977 at Nsawam-Adoagyiri, Eastern Region, Ghana.

kusaal: O da naaenɛ University of Cape Coast nɛ Bachelor of Science in agriculture.
english: He graduated from the University of Cape Coast with a Bachelor of Science in agriculture.

kusaal: O da lɛn keŋ Mountcrest University zamis o LLB and LLM.
english: He also studied at Mountcrest University where he obtained an LLB and LLM.

kusaal: Annoh-Dompreh da pin'ili o pɔlitiks nɛ sakurin, on da nya' ka ka ba vɔɔti tis o ka o lieb Pirɛsidɛn tis National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) sankanɛ ka o da an sakur biig bɛ university of Cape Coast yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2000).
english: Annoh-Dompreh started his engagement in politics as a student politician when he contested and was elected as president of the National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) while a student of the university of Cape Coast in 2000.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye an Eastern regional Youth Organizer tis Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party.
english: He was selected as the Eastern regional Youth Organizer for the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la nii (2012), o da nya' Nsawam/Adoagyiri Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la ni nɛ Seth Wiafe Danquah ka da paam suor ye zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) Gaana dim wʋsa wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la nɛ vɔɔt kɔbistan nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (366) yi vɔɔt kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi pʋʋgin (482).
english: In 2012, He contested in the Nsawam/Adoagyiri NPP Parliamentary primaries against Seth Wiafe Danquah and was given the nod by delegates in the constituency, to represent them in the 2012 Ghanaian parliamentary election, by obtaining 366 out of the 482 votes cast.

kusaal: O da lɛn di kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Gaana wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la.
english: He retained his seat in the 2016 Ghanaian parliamentary election.

kusaal: O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Parliamentary Select Committees on Subsidiary Legislation nɛ Roads & Transport.
english: He is also a member of the Parliamentary Select Committees on Subsidiary Legislation and Roads & Transport.

kusaal: Annoh-Dompreh anɛ kʋkdaan nya'andɔli tis Housing Committee.
english: Annoh-Dompreh is the vice-chairperson of the Housing Committee.

kusaal: O lɛn paas banɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla (Finance Committee); banɛ gɔsid gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yɛla (Education Committee); ka paas banɛ gɔsid Foreign Affairs Committee, nɛ Appointments Committee, ka paas Business Committee nɛ Selection Committee.
english: He is also a member of the Finance Committee; a member of the Education Committee; a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, a member of the Appointments Committee, a member of the Business Committee and also a member of the Committee of Selection Committee.

kusaal: Annoh-Dompreh anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Church of Pentecost.
english: Annoh-Dompreh is a Christian and attends the Church of Pentecost.

kusaal: O da keŋ tuoni di kʋk la ka bas Ben Ohene-ayeh onɛ dɔl NDC la.
english: He proceed to win the seat against Ben Ohene-ayeh of the NDC.

kusaal: O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa atan.
english: He is married with three children.

kusaal: Frank Fuseini Adongo anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani, Member of Parliament bɛ wadmaannib yin.
english: Frank Fuseini Adongo is a Ghanaian politician and a [Member of the 7th Parliament of Ghana].

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la nwadisa atan' la ni (March 2017), Zuraan Nana Akufo-Addo, da buoli o yʋ'ʋr ye o paas nidib piiga ye ba an minister nya'andɔlib banɛ na paasi o gɔmena la ni.
english: In March 2017, President Nana Akufo-Addo, named him one of the ten deputy regional ministers who would form part of his government.

kusaal: Appointments Committee of the Parliament of Ghana da vɛɛnsi o yɛla ka bu'os o bu'osa nwadkan ni.
english: He was vetted by the Appointments Committee of the Parliament of Ghana in the same month.

kusaal: Ba da tis o suor ka nɔki o yʋ'ʋri tis Speaker of Parliament ye wadmaanib la wʋsa ya'a siak ka o naan pin'il tʋʋma.
english: He was approved by the committee and his name was forwarded to Speaker of Parliament for further approval by the general house of parliament.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid ka da an Upper East Region dinɛ bɛ Ghana la minister nya'andɔl.
english: Frank Fuseini Adongo is a Ghanaian politician and a [Member of the 7th Parliament of Ghana].

kusaal: Freda Akosua Oheneafrewo Prempeh (du'anɛ 23 January 1966) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni n tis Tano North Constituency bɛ Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la dim.
english: Freda Akosua Oheneafrewo Prempeh (born 23 January 1966) is a Ghanaian politician, and Member of Parliament in the Seventh Parliament and Eighth Parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana representing Tano North Constituency in the Ahafo Region, Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ minista nya'adɔli tis minister kanɛ gɔsid dap nɛ pʋ'ab yɛla la ka lɛ aan Assembly member – "Assembly Woman" yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2002) paae yʋʋm tusa ati nɛ piiga (2010) tis Lakoo Electoral Area sʋ'ʋlim bɛ La-Dade kotopo Constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region.
english: She was the Minister of State, for the Ministry of works and housing, Ghana and previously served as the Deputy Gender Minister and also Assembly member – "Assembly Woman" from 2002 to 2010 for the Lakoo Electoral Area of the La-Dadekotopo Constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2017), ba da gaŋ o ye o an kʋkdaani tis nidib piinɛ yinne banɛ ka ba da gaansi ba ye ba gɔsi maal si'elnam ka ba nya'ŋi nwɛ' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii ninsabilis tɛɛns pʋ'ab bɔɔl la (2018 African Women Cup of Nations).
english: In 2017, she was appointed chairperson of an 11-member local organising committee tasked to organise the 2018 African Women Cup of Nations.

kusaal: O anɛ Ohenenana Akwasi Agyeman Dua-Prempeh, onɛ da maal ka'alim la pʋ'ayua kanɛ paasi atan onɛ an kambʋʋs Na'adɔɔg la nɛ Nana Amma Serwaa, Kontihemaa onɛ bɛ Duayaw Nkwanta ka da maal ka'alim la,( ka bɛdigʋ mi'i o ye Madam Georgina Ansah).
english: She is the third daughter of the late Ohenenana Akwasi Agyeman Dua-Prempeh, of the Ashanti Royal Family and the late Nana Amma Serwaa, Kontihemaa of Duayaw Nkwanta( known in private life as Madam Georgina Ansah).

kusaal: Ka tɔlisi maali o Ordinary(O) level Technology Secondary School (dinɛ yʋ'ʋn an KNUST Senior High School la) bɛ Kumasi, Ghana la.
english: Freda started her basic education at University Primary School, Kumasi and furthered with her Ordinary(O) level at Technology Secondary School (now KNUST Senior High School) in Kumasi, Ghana and continued with her Advanced level Certificate (A level) at the Accra Workers College in Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋ Ghana Institute of Journalism, maali o Diploma in Public Relations and Advertising.
english: She then proceeded to the Ghana Institute of Journalism, where she pursued a Diploma in Public Relations and Advertising.

kusaal: Ba da tis o Certified Public Accountant yi Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii la ni (1998).
english: She was honored a Certified Public Accountant by Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration in 1998.

kusaal: O lɛm mɔr Certificate nɛ Advanced Certificate in Marketing, DipM, MCIM, Chartered Marketer Professional Postgraduate Diploma in Marketing, o da maal bama wʋsa nɛ Chartered Institute of Marketing, United Kingdom.
english: She holds both a Certificate and an Advanced Certificate in Marketing, DipM, MCIM, Chartered Marketer Professional Postgraduate Diploma in Marketing, all from the Chartered Institute of Marketing, United Kingdom.

kusaal: O da lɛn maali o degree in (Business Administration), Human Resource Management Option University of Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2006).
english: She obtained her degree in (Business Administration), Human Resource Management Option from the University of Ghana in 2006.

kusaal: O da lɛn maal M. A Comms, Media and Public Relations University of Leicester bɛ UK la ka maali o PhD in Business Administration Ghana Technology University College.
english: She also studied MA Comms, Media and Public Relations at the University of Leicester, UK and also has a PhD in Business Administration from the Ghana Technology University College.

kusaal: Freda Akosua Prempeh yinɛ Duayaw Nkwanta, dinɛ an tentita'ari tsi o sʋ'ʋlim la Tano North, bɛ Ahafo Region, Ghana.
english: Freda Akosua Prempeh hails from Duayaw Nkwanta, the capital of her parliamentary Constituency, Tano North, in the Ahafo Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Di da kpɛlim bi'ela ka Freda kɔ'ɔŋi o nyɔvʋr yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu Nwadisa ayuobʋ daba atan daar (June 3, 2015) sapuat kanɛ da maal ka ku'om ʋak zin'ig la ka bugum mɛ lɛn did ya'as (flood and fire disaster) bɛ circle, Accra.
english: Freda almost lost her life to the June 3, 2015 flood and fire disaster at circle, Accra.

kusaal: Ban da nam pʋ vɔɔt Freda ka o kpɛn' Wadmaanib yin yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la, o da anɛ manageressi tis Point Four Hotel bɛ Sunyani la, ka lɛn tʋm nɛ Prison Service ya'as yʋma piiga (10 years).
english: Prior to Freda's election into office as a Member in parliament in 2013, she was a manageress at the Point Four Hotel in Sunyani and had also worked with Prison Service for 10 years.

kusaal: Freda Prempeh paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni, New Patriotic Party (N.P.P.).
english: Freda Prempeh belongs to the New Patriotic Party (N.P.P.).

kusaal: O pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛb pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayui la ni, (2002), o da anɛ Assembly member tis Lakoo Electoral Area bɛ La-Dadekotopo Constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region la, yʋma anii (8 years), yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa ayi la ni (February 2006), ba da buol o ye o tʋm tis National Reconciliation Commission an Public Affairs Officer Nwadisa awai (9 months).
english: Her political career started back in 2002, as an Assembly member for the Lakoo Electoral Area of the La-Dadekotopo Constituency in the Greater Accra Region, for 8 years, In February 2006, she was called to serve on the National Reconciliation Commission as a Public Affairs Officer for a period of 9 months.

kusaal: Nannanna, o anɛ Wadmaani tis Tano North Constituency, ka paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Mines and Energy, Government Assurance Committee Wadmaanib yin la.
english: She's is currently the member of Parliament for Tano North Constituency, and serves on the Mines and Energy, Government Assurance Committee in parliament.

kusaal: Pirɛsidɛn Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an Deputy Minister of Works and Housing, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la la (2017).
english: She was appointed the Deputy Minister of Works and Housing, in 2017 by President Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: O da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la Tano North seat wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nɔbir zug ka di nɛ vɔɔt ka di tʋʋg pisnu nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51%).
english: She contested in the 2020 Ghanaian general election as the parliamentary candidate for the Tano North seat on the ticket of New Patriotic Party and won by more than 51%.

english: 2002–2006 Chairperson, Development Sub-Committee (Accra Metropolitan Assembly)

english: 2006–2008 Chairperson, Women & Children Sub-Committee (Accra Metropolitan Assembly)

english: 31 October 2003 to date Institute of Public Relations (IPR, Ghana) – Accredited Member.

kusaal: O anɛ Minista of State, tis Ministry of works and housing, Ghana.
english: She was the Minister of State, for the Ministry of works and housing, Ghana and previously served as the Deputy Gender Minister and also Assembly member – "Assembly Woman" from 2002 to 2010 for the Lakoo Electoral Area of the La-Dadekotopo Constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la dabpisi nɛ atan daar (23 January 1966) Ankara, Gaana Na'adɔɔgin.
english: She was born on 23 January 1966 in Accra to a Ghanaian Royal family.

kusaal: Freda da pin'ili o basic educationnɛ University Primary School bɛ Kumasi la.
english: Freda started her basic education at University Primary School, Kumasi and furthered with her Ordinary(O) level at Technology Secondary School (now KNUST Senior High School) in Kumasi, Ghana and continued with her Advanced level Certificate (A level) at the Accra Workers College in Accra, Ghana.

english: Freda started her basic education at University Primary School, Kumasi and furthered with her Ordinary(O) level at Technology Secondary School (now KNUST Senior High School) in Kumasi, Ghana and continued with her Advanced level Certificate (A level) at the Accra Workers College in Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋn anɛ minista nya'adɔli tis dap nɛ pʋ'ab, biis nɛ nidib bɛlim yɛla (Deputy Minister of Gender, Children and Social Protection).
english: She was the Minister of State, for the Ministry of works and housing, Ghana and previously served as the Deputy Gender Minister and also Assembly member – "Assembly Woman" from 2002 to 2010 for the Lakoo Electoral Area of the La-Dadekotopo Constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Frederick Obeng Adom (ka bba da du'a o 11 January 1984) anɛ Ghana Pɔlitks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Frederick Obeng Adom (born 11 January 1984) is a Ghanaian Politician.

kusaal: O paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Upper West Akim Constituency bɛ Eastern Region, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nid.
english: He is a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Upper West Akim Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O da naaenɛ Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration, ka ba tis o Bachelor of Science marketing kasɛtta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) la ni.
english: He is a graduate of Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration, where he was awarded a Bachelor of Science marketing in 2013.

kusaal: O da anɛ business development officer tis Fonak Technologies Ltd ka an Chief Executive Officer tis Surveying Precision Market Ltd.
english: He was the business development officer of Fonak Technologies Ltd and Chief Executive Officer of Surveying Precision Market Ltd.

kusaal: Adom anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nid.
english: Adom is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O da di Upper West Akim Constituency sʋ'ʋlim kʋk la ka sigis onɛ pʋn dɛŋim zin'i di zug la, Ohene Assifo Derek Bekoe onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg NDC nid la, o da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan (21,863).
english: He won the Upper West Akim Constituency seat in the general elections to unseat the incumbent member of parliament Ohene Assifo Derek Bekoe of the NDC, He polled 21,863 of the valid vote cast.

kusaal: Pirɛsidɛn Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye an minista onɛ gɔsid transportation nya'adɔl.
english: He was nominated and appointed as the deputy minister of transportation by President Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: O anɛ minista onɛ gɔsid transportation nya'adɔl.
english: He is the deputy minister of transportation.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adom nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi, yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la dabpiinɛ yinne daar (11 January 1984).
english: Adom was born on 11 January 1984.

kusaal: O da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid ya yɛla, la'askanɛ gɔsid sanlima tuub nɛ bugum yɛla Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He serves as member of House Committee and Mines and Energy Committee respectively in the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayuobʋ la (June 2020) o da nya' Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg Na'am la ka di zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug yʋʋ tusa ayi nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋg la.
english: In June 2020 NPP parliamentary primaries, he contested and won to represent the NPP in the 2020 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Frederick Opare-Ansah anɛ na'asaa bugum tʋmtʋm ka an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd onɛ paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n tis Suhum sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Frederick Opare-Ansah (born September 5, 1968) is an Electrical Engineer and Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Fourth to Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the peole of Suhum Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O yinɛ Amankokrom-Akuapem, tempʋʋg linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: He hails from Amankokrom-Akuapem, a town in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da naae o sakuri bɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology sakur la ni ka di'e Digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ pa'al ye o zamisnɛ na'asaa bugum yɛla yʋʋma 1993 la ni.
english: He graduated from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology and obtained his Bachelor of Science degree in electrical engineering in 1994.

kusaal: Opare-Ansah da an manɛgia darɛta n tis Third Rail (Ghana) Limited tʋʋma dim la.
english: Opare-Ansah worked as the managing director of Third Rail (Ghana) Limited.

kusaal: Onɛ Jacob Kwaku Arkoh onɛ da PNC nid, Samuel Fleischer Kwabi onɛ da Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la nid, Francis Darby Kobena Inkoom onɛ da an CPP nid la, Matilda Garbrah onɛ mɛ da zi'enɛ o mɛŋ nyari la da zi'en ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over Jacob Kwaku Arkoh of the People's National Convention, Samuel Fleischer Kwabi of the National Democratic Congress, Francis Darby Kobena Inkoom of the Convention People's Party, Matilda Garbrah an independent candidate.

kusaal: Opare-Ansah anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Opare-Ansah is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: New Patriotic Party (NPP).
english: Opare-Ansah is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: He is a member of the 4th, 5th, 6th nɛ 7th Suhum Sʋ'ʋlʋm nwadig yinne la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) on da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) ban da maal vɔt nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni la.
english: He is a member of the 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Parliaments of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ wʋsa da paamnɛ 0.75%, 41.02%, 0.77% and 12.20% wʋʋ ba yʋda la tʋʋnl si'em la.O da kɔ'ɔg na'am la yʋʋma 2021 vɔt la ni ka Kwadjo Asante da di ka bas o 272 n yi 666 vɔt la ni.
english: These obtained 0.75%, 41.02%, 0.77% and 12.20% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Opare-Ansah anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Opare-Ansah is a Christian.

kusaal: Frederick Yaw Ahenkwah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan tis Jaman North linɛ bɛ Ghana Bono region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Frederick Yaw Ahenkwah is a Ghanaian politician and member of parliament for the 8th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana representing the Jaman North constituency in the Bono region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Frederick nɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris ayuobυ la li dabisim piisi nɛ anaasi yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ ayi la ni, o yinɛ Sampa linɛ bɛ Ghana Bono Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Frederick was born on 24 June 1982 and hails from Sampa in the Bono region of Ghana.
