kusaal: O da tɔlisi maal o Digirɛɛ linɛ an Agriculture Education mɛn yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piiga la ni 2010.
english: He further had his Degree in Agriculture Education in 2010.

kusaal: Frederick paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Privileges la ni ka mɛ paas Land and Forestry kpɛɛmnam la ni.
english: Frederick is a member of the Privileges Committee and also a member of the Land and Forestry Committee.

kusaal: O da keŋi o sakur linɛ an SSSCE la nɛ yυυma tusa yi' la ni.
english: He had his SSSCE in 2000.

kusaal: Frederick da anɛ ti Ghana gbaυŋ zamisυg lugυr la kpɛɛm yinne.
english: Frederick was a form master in the Ghana Education Service.

kusaal: Frederick anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid ka nannanna onɛ an wadmaan n tis Jaman North sυ'υlυm la.
english: Frederick is a member of NDC and currently the MP for Jaman North Constituency.

kusaal: Ban da vɔt ka o paam vɔt si'a la da anɛ 22,375 ka o tiraan Siaka Stevens onɛ an Wabυg nid la mɛ da paam18,206 vɔt.
english: He won the parliamentary seat with 22,375 votes whilst the NPP parliamentary aspirant Siaka Stevens had 18,206 votes.

kusaal: Frederick anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Frederick is a Christian.

kusaal: O kpa'am la paamʋg anɛ saŋkanɛ ka o tʋʋmid nɛɛ the Doctor's Companion Martha Jones bɛ BBC science fiction series Doctor who, yʋʋm tʋsir, nɛ ayɔpɔi la paae yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ piiga(2007 - 2010) la ni, ka di paae saŋasia yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ piiga nɛ anii la ni Torchwood(2018) ka lɛm di ya'an nɛ on da nwɛ' Crown Persecutor Alesha Phillips bɛ ITV Crime Procedural Law & Order: UK(2009-2012), Ananita Caphan bɛ Netflix science fiction drama scene8(2015 - 2018) nɛ Doctor Helen Sharpe bɛ NBC medical drama New Amsterdam(2018 - 2023).
english: She rose to fame with her role as the Doctor's companion Martha Jones in the BBC science fiction series Doctor Who (2007–2010) and its spin-off Torchwood (2008), and received further recognition for playing Crown Prosecutor Alesha Phillips in the ITV crime procedural Law & Order: UK (2009–2012), Amanita Caplan in the Netflix science fiction drama Sense8 (2015–2018) and Dr. Helen Sharpe in the NBC medical drama New Amsterdam (2018–2023).

kusaal: O mɛŋ TV da pɛɛsnɛ mile High(2005), Bizarre ER(2008), nɛ Dreamland(2023).
english: Her other television appearances include Mile High (2005), Bizarre ER (2008), and Dreamland (2023).

kusaal: Ba da nɔŋ o sininam gɔsʋ pamm pɛɛs North nɛ South (2015) nɛ da nya'ad taaba o sininam la yɛla, Eat Locals(2017), nɛ The Matrix Resurrection (2021).
english: Agyeman has also appeared in films, including North v South (2015), Eat Locals (2017), and The Matrix Resurrections (2021).

kusaal: Ba dʋ'aa Agyeman nɛ Hackney teŋin East London yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai Dɔnwalig nwadig la ni dabisa pisyi(1979) la ni.
english: Agyeman was born on 20 March 1979 in Hackney, East London.

kusaal: Azar Azizian-Kohan ka ba du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anii(1948) ka yi Iranian Kurdish, ka o saam Osei Agyeman anɛ Ghana nid.
english: Her mother, Azar Azizian-Kohan, born in 1948, is Iranian, and her father, Osei Agyeman, is Ghanaian.

kusaal: Agyeman da mɔr taʋ kpɛɛm Leila nɛ o pitʋ Dominic.
english: Agyeman has an older sister, Leila, and a younger brother, Dominic.

kusaal: O ma da anɛ Muslim ka o saam an Christian Methodist pʋ'ʋsim la ni, Agyeman nɔbignɛ Roman Catholic pʋ'ʋsim la ni.
english: Although her mother was raised as a Muslim and her father was raised as a Methodist, Agyeman grew up to be a practising Roman Catholic.

kusaal: Agyeman da keŋɛ Our Lady's Convent RC High School la ni, Catholic school ka di bɛ Stamford Hill.
english: Agyeman attended Our Lady's Convent RC High School, a Catholic school in Stamford Hill.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ yʋʋm tʋsir kɔbiswai nɛ pisawai nɛ ayuobʋ (1996) la ni o keŋ Anna Scher Theater School in Islington, North London, zamis arts nɛ drama bɛ Middlesex University, ka naae yʋma tʋsa ayi(2000) la ni.
english: Later, during the summer of 1996, she attended the Anna Scher Theatre School in Islington, North London, and studied performing arts and drama at Middlesex University, graduating in 2000.

kusaal: O da lɛm zamisnɛ Theatrical bɛ Radford University bɛ Virginia yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii(1998) la ni hali ka pɛsigi ye tʋm sʋŋid ba ka an box-office assistant tis sakur biis la Diana malʋg ka ba da pʋ zan'sʋʋ.
english: She also took a theatrical course at Radford University in Virginia in 1998, even volunteering to work as a box-office assistant for student drama productions in which she was not cast.

kusaal: On da paam sʋŋir Martha Jones ni bɛ Doctor Who la, Agyeman kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr hali yi ka nidib mi' o la, o T V ni tʋʋma da anɛ Lola Wise dinɛ ka ba maligim gɔsi yɛla bɛ ITV soap opera Crossroads la ni.
english: Before securing the part of Martha Jones in Doctor Who, Agyeman's most famous television role was playing Lola Wise in the revived series of the ITV soap opera Crossroads.

kusaal: Ba da nɔk o nɛ pɛɛs gaansʋgʋ ayi ni pa'ala yɛɛ onɛ an Best Newcomer nɛ Sexiest Female yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ atan'(2003) la saŋa dinɛ da anɛ British Soap Awards la.
english: For her performance, she was nominated in two categories, Best Newcomer and Sexiest Female, at the 2003 British Soap Awards.

kusaal: Agyeman da lɛm pɛɛs nidib biela nwa' da sʋŋid ka ba tʋm bɛ TV series ka an BBC's long running medical drama Casualty, Sky one airline drama Mile High and ITV's police procedural The Bill, anina ka o yina mɔr itimanami a ayi.
english: Agyeman also had small guest roles in such TV series as BBC's long-running medical drama Casualty, Sky One's airline drama Mile High and ITV's police procedural The Bill, in which she appeared twice as two separate characters.

kusaal: Agyeman da maali o film Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobu(2006) la ni, di'emid Nana in the independent drama Rulers and dealers yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobu(2006) la ni, dinɛ ka Stephen Lloyd Jackson da sɔbi li ka lɛm gɔsi li yɛla.
english: Agyeman made her feature film debut in 2006, playing Nana in the independent drama Rulers and Dealers (2006), written and directed by Stephen Lloyd Jackson.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu sigir nwadig la ni dabisa pisyi nɛ anaasi la ni(24th June, 2005), o da di'em Sally Jacobs bɛ "The Christmas Invasion", amaa Anita Briem da di'e li tʋm bɔzugɔ onɛ da mɔri li ya'am bɛdigʋ ka li nar o nɛ on na maal sini la, dinɛ an "ice cool blinde".
english: On 24 June 2005, she auditioned for the part of Sally Jacobs in "The Christmas Invasion", but the role went to Anita Briem, who better fitted the production team's concept of the character as an "ice cool blonde".

kusaal: Agyeman da lɛm kene na tʋmnɛ Esme nɛɛ Adeola Oshodi, bɛ "Rise of the Cybermen"/"The age of steel" nɛɛ "Army of Ghosts", nwɛnɛ din nar ye di dɔl siem.
english: Agyeman later auditioned for the roles of Esme and Adeola Oshodi, in the "Rise of the Cybermen"/"The Age of Steel" and "Army of Ghosts", respectively.

kusaal: O da lɛm maal sini yinne (ostensibly for an episode of Torchwood) ka naam kɛ ka Tenth Doctor actor David Tennant naam kpansʋ gɔs.
english: She attended another audition (ostensibly for an episode of Torchwood) before a final screen test with Tenth Doctor actor David Tennant.

kusaal: Ka ba da nam bi'esis onɛ na to di'e Billie Piper, ka nɔk Agyeman ka o tʋm nɛ Martha Jones bɛ yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ ayuobu Mɔraʋg nwadig la dabisa anu daar(2006).
english: Following extensive speculation on who would replace Billie Piper, Agyeman was confirmed to the press as new companion Martha Jones on 5 July 2006.

kusaal: Agyeman da sin'iŋnɛ o sininam la maalʋg dinɛ pɛɛs atan' la ni, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobu mʋtʋl nwadig(August 2006) la ka naae Vaala nwadig la yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi(March 2007) la ni.
english: Agyeman began filming for the third series in August 2006 and finished in March 2007.

kusaal: O da maali o sini la nwɛnɛ medical sakur biig nɛ Martha bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi Mɔraʋg nwadig la dabisim pistan' nɛ yinne(31st March 2007) la ni, o sini kanɛ da an ''Smith nɛ Joans''.
english: She made her screen debut as medical student Martha on 31 March 2007 in the episode "Smith and Jones".

kusaal: Agyeman ni da sin'iŋi o siini la maalʋg la o da tiakʋ o dʋ'am yʋ'ʋr Frema, ka li aan o sini maalʋg yʋ'ʋr din na niŋsiem ka nidib namisid ye ba buolɛ.
english: When Agyeman began her professional acting career, she chose to use a different spelling of her birth name, Frema, as her professional name, to avoid pronunciation problems.

kusaal: Agyeman da tʋmnɛ Tʋʋma atan' bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobu dinɛ anɛ series of Doctor Who.
english: In between the third and fourth series of Doctor Who, Agyeman appeared in three episodes of the show's spin-off drama Torchwood, namely "Reset", "Dead Man Walking" and "A Day in the Death".

kusaal: Esme da anɛ dinɛ ka ba yisʋ nyain yis naarin la, amaa Agyeman da nyaŋi maali o din la tis Adeola.
english: Esme was ultimately cut from the final script, but Agyeman was successful in her audition for Adeola.

kusaal: Ka screen la ni pa'al yee Adeola yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobu (2006) Mɔraʋg nwadig la dabisir yinne la ni.
english: She filmed her role in the series in December 2005 and appeared on screen as Adeola on 1 July 2006.

kusaal: Tennant la da da nɔk sʋmalisim gbaʋŋɔ digil Agyeman za'anɔɔrin ka li da an dinɛ da sʋŋɔ ka o suunr ma'ae.
english: Tennant left a reassuring note under the door of Agyeman's hotel room, and this helped calm any nerves the actress had.

kusaal: O dʋ'adib la da basnɛ taaba saŋkanɛ ka o biig la.
english: They divorced when she was young.

kusaal: Frevo anɛ wa'a nɛ yʋʋma si'a buudi ka li yit nɛ Recife, Pernambuco Brazil, ka mɛ bɛ Brazilian Carnival.
english: Frevo is a dance and musical style originating from Recife, Pernambuco, Brazil, traditionally associated with Brazilian Carnival.

kusaal: 19th century la naar saŋa, Brazilian Army yʋʋm-yʋmnib banɛ da bɛ Recife tenpʋ tita'arin la da pin'ili yʋʋm mɛ giligid Carnival saŋa la.
english: By the end of the 19th century, bands from the Brazilian Army regiments based in the city of Recife started a tradition of parading during the Carnival.

kusaal: Carnival la mɔr kpinnim nɛ Catholicism laa, ba da yʋʋm nɛ wina'am pʋ'ʋsim yʋʋma, religious procession giligid la'am nɛ zaba yʋʋma nam, sida siakidib nɛ banɛ ban'ad widi zabib la bi'ela da mɔr banɛ yʋʋmid ka nidib bɛdigʋ mi' kɛ ka ba yʋlɛɛg bɛnɛ ba la da paas nɛ ba.
english: Since the Carnival is originally linked to Catholicism, they played religious procession marches and martial music, as well.

kusaal: Ayi banɛ ka bɛdigʋ da mi' la da anɛ Espanna (meaning Spain) ka lin anɛ Spain, ka ba kpɛɛm onɛ da pa'an nɛ ba la da anɛ Spanish nid, ka an piinɛ anaasi sɔbi (14) yi 14th Infantry Regiment ni na.
english: The two most famous bands were the Espanha (meaning Spain), whose conductor was of Spanish origin, and the 14, from the 14th Infantry Regiment.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnu,1950s la pin'ilʋg, banɛ da sʋŋ passo la nid yinne, anɛ master Nascimento do passo.
english: Starting in the 1950s, one of the biggest contributors to the passo is the master Nascimento do Passo.

kusaal: America pop-star Cyndi Laupa wa'ad nɛ frevo la o ya' yʋʋmidi o yʋʋm "Maybe He'll Know"
english: American pop-star Cyndi Lauper is dancing the frevo when she sings her song "Maybe He'll Know".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi, 2000s ambassadors banɛ ka ba da min' hali da anɛ Recife dim, Recife-based yʋʋma dim Spokfrevo Orquestra ka ba tuongat an Inaldo Cavalcante de Albuquerque, ka ba min' o sʋŋa nɛ Spok.
english: In the 2000s the best-known ambassadors of the frevo is the Recife-based big band SpokFrevo Orquestra, led by sax player Inaldo Cavalcante de Albuquerque, better known as Spok.

kusaal: Ba anɛ 17-18 professional musicians nɛ nidiba ayi nwɛnɛd lʋns, virtuoso drummers nɛ percussionist- onɛ zaŋi li ka li aan ba tʋʋm ye dunia la baŋ frevo yʋʋma.
english: These are 17-18 professional musicians - including two virtuoso drummers and a percussionist - who have made it their mission to introduce the world to frevo music.

kusaal: Frevo-de-Bloco yʋʋm nɛ ka di'emid nɛ string instruments.
english: Frevo de Bloco is also sung and played with string instruments.

kusaal: Capiba ka ba da min' yʋʋm kaŋa buudi ni, amaa sɔ mɛ tun'oe kaal Getulio Cavalcante, Cluodionor Germano (singer) nɛ Antonio Nobrega (singer and dancer) nidiba ayi bama an ya'an dittib Frevo de Bloco ni.
english: Claudionor Germano (singer) and Antonio Nóbrega (singer and dancer) are two of Frevo de Bloco greatest performers.

kusaal: La'as bibis pɛ'ɛg frevo malima, ka ba lɛɛ pʋ paas brass section la, ka mɔri Bahian-guitars, drums, bass, electric guitars, keyboards and a singer.
english: Adaptation of frevo compositions for smaller formations, commonly without a brass section and made up of Bahian-guitars, drums, bass, electric guitars, keyboards and a singer.

kusaal: Li da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir yinne kɔbis wai nɛ pisnu, 1950 ni la pin'ilʋg saŋa Bahia teŋin "Carnvalesco Clube di'ema Misto Vassuorinhas of Olinda" Salvador tɛŋin (Bahia State) ka nya'aŋa Trio Eletrico Armandinho, Dodo & Osmar tis trio eletrico an Bahian Carnival la malʋŋ ka frevo kpɛn Western pop rock ni.
english: The style developed in the early 1950s in Bahia, spurred by a performance given by the "Clube Carnvalesco Misto Vassourinhas of Olinda" in Salvador (Bahia State) and later by the band Trio Elétrico Armandinho, Dodô & Osmar, gave origin to the trio eléctrico tradition of the Bahian carnival, which fused the frevo with Western pop rock.

kusaal: Ba ye frevo pian'k la yinɛ frever ni na, ka lin mɛ yinɛ Porpugueses pian'k frever nina (to boil), li lɛ'ɛg.
english: The word frevo is said to come from frever, a variant of the Portuguese word ferver (to boil).

kusaal: Ba yɛl ye frevo yʋʋma la vʋʋd la na kɛ ka banɛ kɛlisid nɛ banɛ wa'ad tɛn'ɛs ye ba lɛ'ɛgid nɛ.
english: It is said that the sound of the frevo will make listeners and dancers feel as if they are boiling on the ground.

kusaal: Frevo bɛllim gaad yʋʋma kɔbiga (1907) woo lin nar si'em, li nɔbig ya ti paae li bɛ si'em saŋkaŋa nwa ni.
english: Frevo is more than 100 years old (1907) and naturally it has developed throughout this time to reach its current form.

kusaal: Yigilig siig kanɛ da naami li laa, Frevo da pin'ili yinɛ Capoeira tʋʋma ni ti lieb quasi-acrobatical movement of the dance.
english: In the same spirit of competition that created it, Frevo was developed by transforming the capoeira movements into the quasi-acrobatical movements of the dance.

kusaal: Nananna ba yʋʋn buon frevo wa'a ye passo ka buon frevo wawa'adib la ye passistas.
english: Frevo dance is now known as passo and Frevo dancers as passistas.

kusaal: Ba mɛ maal passistas la fuud la ka li anɛ bi'ela zɛmis kɛ ka li an na'ana nɛ wa'a la bɔɔd si'em.
english: The clothes of the passistas also developed from regular clothing to a skimpy attire that is more appropriate for the movements.

kusaal: Passista yʋ'ʋri an bʋn kanɛ ka ba min' I li sʋŋa carnival of Pernambuco.
english: The image of the passista is one of the most prominent icons of the carnival of Pernambuco.

kusaal: Frevo de-rua (street frevo) "frevo" pian'ak la gbin nɛ an si'em anɛ bʋn-nwɛn'ɛdir nwɛn'ɛb buudi, ka li nwɛn'ɛb an tʋʋlli nɛ brass intruments bama, trumpets, trombones, saxophones, nɛ tuba.
english: Frevo-de-Rua (Street Frevo), the most common meaning of the word "frevo", is an instrumental style, played in a fiery fast tempo with brass instruments, namely trumpets, trombones, saxophones, and tuba.

kusaal: America dim ye li nwɛn nɛ polka.
english: It is frequently perceived by American ears as resembling polka.

kusaal: Frevo de-Rua tun'oe nwɛn football di'ema saŋa Recife teŋin, ka li an woo pep band.
english: Frevo-de-Rua bands can often be found playing during football matches in Recife, forming a sort of pep band.

kusaal: Onɛ pa'an yʋʋma la anɛ Maestro Duda.
english: A famous conductor in this style is Maestro Duda.

kusaal: Ba da keŋ nwɛn'ɛb US nɛ Donwalig nwadig la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi, 2012 la ni.
english: They embarked on their first US tour in March 2012.

kusaal: Ti mɛ mɔr Japanese chāhan kanɛ an' Japanese dim diib ka ba nyɛ li yi Chinese diibin bɛɛ China dim mui ki'ima ni.
english: Japanese chāhan is considered a Japanese Chinese dish, having derived from Chinese fried rice dishes.

kusaal: Mui ki'ima anɛ di kanɛ mɔr yʋ'ʋr hali teŋ gbaŋ zug wʋʋ East Asian, Southeast Asian nɛ zin'isieba bɛ South Asian diib zin'isin .
english: Fried rice is a popular component of East Asian, Southeast Asian and South Asian cuisines.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a gɔs diib zin'igin wʋʋ teŋ banɛ pʋ pɛ'ɛs Asia sʋ'ʋlʋmin la mui ki'ima pɛ'ɛsi ba diib buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb la ni.Di mɛ lɛm bɛ Latin American teŋin diib zin'isin nɛ ba buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb wʋʋ, Ecuadorian chaulafan, Peruvian arroz chaufa, Cuban arroz frito, nɛ Puerto Rican arroz mampostea(d)
english: Additionally, the cuisine of some Latin American countries includes variations on fried rice, including Ecuadorian chaulafan, Peruvian arroz chaufa, Cuban arroz frito, and Puerto Rican arroz mampostea(d)o.

kusaal: Frimpong Yaw Addo anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib ykinaɛ paasi ayɔpɔi nɛ anii la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Manso Adubia Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region la New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Frimpong Yaw Addo (born 2 September 1962) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and Eight parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Manso Adubia constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O anɛ Deputy Minista tis Food and Agriculture.
english: He is currently the Deputy Minister for Food and Agriculture.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Addonɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi Nwadisa awai la daba ayi daar (2 September 1962) tenkanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Manso Gyeduako bɛ Amansie South District n bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: Addo was born on Sunday, 2 September 1962 in the town of Manso Gyeduako in the Amansie South District in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O da maali o Bachelor of Arts degree in Sociology nɛ Diploma in English University of Cape Coast.
english: He earned his Bachelor of Arts degree in Sociology and Diploma in English from University of Cape Coast in 1990.

kusaal: O da lɛn maali o Executive Masters certificate in Conflict, Peace and Security yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016) Kofi Annan International Peace Keeping Training Center bɛ Accra la.
english: He also obtained an Executive Master's certificate in Conflict, Peace and Security in 2016 at the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre in Accra.

kusaal: Addo da anɛ Manager tis corporate affairs department bɛ Private Ent.
english: Addo was the Manager of Corporate Social Responsibility Department, Private Enterprise Foundation.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Social and Environment impact expert bɛ Comptran Engineering.
english: He was also the Social and Environment impact expert at Comptran Engineering.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Social and Environment impact expert tis Transtel Consult.
english: He was also the Social and Environment impact expert at Transtel Consult.

kusaal: Onɛ da lɛn an programs liaison officer tis National Democratic Institute for International Affairs.
english: He was also the programme's liaison officer at National Democratic Institute for International Affairs.

kusaal: Addo paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party ka lɛn an Wadmaani tis Manso Adubia Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: Addo is a member of the New Patriotic Party and currently the member of parliament for Manso Adubia Constituency in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt o yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana vɔɔtʋg la, ka o paam vɔɔt pisyuobʋ nɛ awai dua'al pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (69.86%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Addo was re-elected as a member of parliament for the Manso Adubia constituency on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party during the 2016 Ghanaian general election with 24,074 votes, representing 69.86% of the total votes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la ni, o da lɛn di wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi (17,652) dinɛ an pisntan nɛ anii dua'al anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (38.8%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka NDC nid la, Simon Kwaku Agyei paam vɔɔt tusa piiga, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ atan (10,753) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisi nɛ atan dua'ali ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (23.6%).
english: In the 2020 General elections, Addo won the parliamentary seat with 17,652 votes making 38.8% of the total votes cast whiles the NDC parliamentary candidate Simon Kwaku Agyei had 10,753 votes making 23.6% of the total votes.

kusaal: Onɛ pʋ mɔr Na'adɔɔg la, Independent, Kofi Osei-Afoakwa mɛ da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (17,149) dinɛ an pistan nɛ ayɔpɔi dua'ali ayɔpɔikɔbiga pʋʋgin (37.7%) vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: The Independent candidate Kofi Osei-Afoakwa also had 17,149 votes making 37.7% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Addo paas Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee ka lɛn paas Environment, Science and Technology Committee.
english: Addo is a member of Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee and also a member of Environment, Science and Technology Committee.

kusaal: O da lieb Wadmaan (MP) tisi o sʋ'ʋlim la yʋʋm tusa yi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) Ghana vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Hon. Addo first contested the Manso Adubia constituency parliamentary seat on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party during the 2012 Ghanaian general election and won with 26,368 votes representing 74.97% of the total votes.

kusaal: O nɔŋnɛ ku'ob nɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb.
english: He likes farming and soccer.

kusaal: Tiasig banɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlim la anɛ Gozo ftira, kanɛ ka ba maanɛ li ka diti li tita'am woo pizza n gaad sandwich nɛ.
english: Regional variations include Gozo ftira, which is served more like a pizza than a sandwich.

kusaal: Li da dɔlis nɛ Maltese Parliament, wadmaannim yir la da niŋ nɔɔryinne siak ka naam li wada ye UNESCO's Convention for the safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii, 2018 la ka Malta's Cultural Directorate da zaŋi ba fabʋlig tis ye ba bɔɔd ye ba paas Maltese ftira la UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) gbaʋŋin, list.
english: Following the Maltese Parliament's unanimous approval to ratify UNESCO's Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, in 2018 Malta's Culture Directorate launched a petition to include the Maltese Ftira as part of UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) list.

kusaal: Teŋ la gbammit yinne, Ftira Maltija naamʋg la woo lin bɛ Directorate la National Inventory ni la, da pʋn bɛ Sixteenth Century la ni sa.
english: According to a local expert, 'The Making of the Ftira Maltija' dates back to the sixteenth century.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi, 2020 la ni Maltese ftira kpɛn paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage gbaʋŋin, list.
english: In 2020, "Il-Ftira, culinary art and culture of flattened sourdough bread in Malta" was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage List.

kusaal: Ftira anɛ Maltese dim bod obodo kanɛ ka ba maali li ka li nwɛn nɛ baŋ nɛ ka niŋi li daambin, leavened, ka ba taa diti li nɛ sardines, tuna, potato, tomato ma'asa, onion, capers nɛ olives.
english: Ftira (plural: ftajjar) is a ring-shaped, leavened, Maltese bread, usually eaten with fillings such as sardines, tuna, potato, fresh tomato, onion, capers and olives.

kusaal: Li da dɔlis nɛ nidib la bɛdigʋ bɔɔdim, Malta gɔbina zugraan la da siak ka tik nu'ugu ye o na zaŋ Maltese ftira paae UNESCO ye ba siak ka paasi li intangible cultural heritage.
english: Following a strong public call, the Government of Malta announced that it would be submitting the culinary art and culture of the Maltese ftira to UNESCO for consideration as intangible cultural heritage.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr nwa paae Africa tɛɛns si'eba mɛn ka ba mɔri pʋd diib banɛ ka ba tuod, tɛɛns la si'eba anɛ Sierra Leone, Liberia, Cote D'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Benin, Togo, Nigeria, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Central African Republic, Republic of Congo, Angola nɛ Gabon.
english: It is a Twi word originating from the Akans in Ghana, but the word has been expanded to include several variations of the pounded meal found in other African countries including Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso, Benin, Togo, Nigeria, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Central African Republic, the Republic of Congo, Angola and Gabon.

kusaal: Côte d'Ivoire tɛŋin, ba buon diib la ye foutou.
english: In Côte d'Ivoire, the word foutou is also used.

kusaal: Ivorian foufou anɛ diib kanɛ ka ba mɔr bɔɔdiɛ kanɛ malisi maan, foutou anɛ dikanɛ mɔr paŋ, ka mɔr tɛbisim yit busa, banki, bɔɔdiɛ bɛɛ ba la'as bama maal.
english: Ivorian foufou is specifically mashed sweet plantains, whereas foutou is a stronger, heavier paste made of various staple foods such as yam, cassava, plantains, taro or a mix of any of those.

kusaal: Cameroon sʋ'ʋlim banɛ ka ba pian'ad Fariŋ buudi pian'ad la ni, ba buoni li ye "couscous" (nwa bɛɛ li kɔn' nɛ dikanɛ bɛ North African ka ba buon couscous la).
english: In the French-speaking regions of Cameroon, it is called "couscous" (not to be confused with the North African dish couscous).

kusaal: Ba gban'ae ye li yinɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim na, dɔlis nɛ Asante, Akuapem, Akyem, Bono, nɛ Fante nidib banɛ paas kanbʋmʋs buudi banɛ bɛ Ghana la, ka tɛŋ la wʋsa yʋ'ʋn diti li.
english: It is believed to originate in what is now modern-day Ghana, by the Asante, the Akuapem, the Akyem, the Bono, and the Fante people of the Akan ethnic group of Ghana and now generally accepted across the country.

kusaal: Zina nwa, li buudi mɛ bɛ Beninese diib pʋʋgin, Cameroon dim diib pʋʋgin, Guinea dim diib pʋʋgin, Congolese diib pʋʋgin, Nigeria diib pʋʋgin, nɛ Togo dim diib pʋʋgin, anina ka ba diti li nɛ nanzʋ'ʋs, ma'ana, bɛɛ stew.
english: Today, it also features in Beninese cuisine, Cameroonian cuisine, Guinean cuisine, Congolese cuisine, Nigerian cuisine, and Togolese cuisine, where it is eaten with hot pepper soup, okra, or other kinds of stew.

kusaal: Akpu, anɛ yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba pʋd banki bɛ Igbo buudi pian'ad ni.
english: Akpu, properly punctuated as akpụ in Igbo, is the Igbo word for cassava.

kusaal: Caribbean tɛɛns la ni ka nidib banɛ zuoe anina la tita'am yit West African (wan wʋʋ Cuba, Jamaica, Dominican Republic, Haiti nɛ Puerto Rico), ba tuod banki bɛɛ busa gɛndigid nɛ bʋnsi'eba.
english: In Caribbean nations with substantial populations of West African origin (such as Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Haiti and Puerto Rico), plantains, cassava or yams are mashed with other ingredients.

kusaal: Banɛ diti li bɛdigʋ anɛ banɛ bɛ Haiti ya'dagɔbʋg tɛɛns la wʋʋ Grand' Anse nɛ Sud nam ni.
english: It is primarily consumed in the southernmost regions of Haiti namely the Grand'Anse and Sud departments.

kusaal: Tɛŋpʋʋg kanɛ ka ba buon Jérémie anɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka ba gɔs ka anina an tonmtonm tɛŋpʋʋgi bɛ Haiti.
english: The city of Jérémie is regarded as the tonmtonm capital of Haiti.

kusaal: Fufu (bɛɛ fufuo, sa'atuodim) anɛ diib kanɛ ka ba tuodi bɛ West African sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Fufu (or fufuo, foofoo, foufou foo-foo ) is a pounded meal found in West African cuisine originally made from boiled cassava, plantains, and cocoyam.

kusaal: Li buudi mɛ bɛ na'asaatɛŋ nɛ banɛ bɛ America tɛnsʋk, zin'is banɛ ka Africa nidib bɛɛ anina zuoe.
english: It also includes variations in the Greater Antilles and Central America, where African culinary influence is high.

kusaal: Nigeria tɛŋin, ba buon diib nwa nɛ ye akpu, ka banɛ nɔŋi li hali anɛ Igbo buudi banɛ bɛ Nigeria.
english: In Nigeria, cassava-based fufu, referred to as akpu (Igbo), is common among various ethnic groups in Nigeria.

kusaal: Onɛ gɔsid kʋdʋmin yela ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Miller pa'al ye, "yʋ'ʋr la ka ba pʋd ye Fufu la gbin anɛ Twi." Ka li yinɛ banki an pi'eligi paas Ghana dim fufu la ni la.
english: According to historian Miller, "the word Fufu literally means white in Twi." and is likely derived from the whitish colour of the cassava component in Ghanaian fufu.

kusaal: Onɛ ka ba buon ye Chinua Achebe ka o sɔb gbaŋ ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye "si'el wʋsa widig nɛ la pʋdigi li yʋ'ʋr, Fufu anɛ dikpɛŋ hali tis kambʋmʋs banɛ da bɛ Ashanti Empire.
english: Fufu was a major cuisine of the Ashanti Empire.

kusaal: Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, fufu yʋ'ʋr yinnɛ lɛn anɛ fufuo, li anɛ pi'elig ka tabid (ba ya'a pʋ la'as banki nɛ bɔɔdiɛ tua).
english: In Ghana, fufu, also known as fufuo, is white and sticky, if plantain is not mixed with the cassava when pounding.

kusaal: Nigeria tɛŋin, fufu bɛɛ akpu anɛ dikanɛ nyɛ yʋ'ʋr hali ka ba mɔr banki ma'asa bɛɛ banɛ ka ba mi'ilim.
english: In Nigeria, cassava-based fufu, referred to as akpu (Igbo), is common among various ethnic groups in Nigeria.

kusaal: Nigeria tɛŋin, fufu kanɛ ka ba nɔk banki maal, ba buon ye akpu, ka li da yinɛ Igbo buudi ni na Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim ka buud banɛ kpɛlim la mɛ yʋ'ʋn baŋ.
english: In Nigeria, cassava-based fufu, referred to as akpu (Igbo), is common among various ethnic groups in Nigeria.

kusaal: Cuba tɛŋin, ba buon diib la lin yi si'el na African sʋ'ʋlim ka ba tisi li yʋ'ʋr sia la ye fufú bɛɛ ban paas pian'ad si'eba pa'al lin an si'em wan wʋʋ fufú de plátano bɛɛ fufú de plátano pintón.
english: In Cuba, the dish retains its original African stem name, termed simply as fufú or with added descriptive extensions like fufú de plátano or fufú de plátano pintón.

kusaal: Dominican Republic tɛŋ sʋ'ʋlim ni, diib buudi kanɛ ka ba nɔŋ hai ka buon mangú, anɛ linɛ wan fufú.
english: In the Dominican Republic, mangú is very similar to fufú.

kusaal: Tɛŋ si'eba ni, ba buon fufú ye funche bɛ Puerto Rico pian'ad ni.
english: A dish called funche made with taro, green and yellow plantains boiled and mashed with butter, garlic, and pork fat was once popular in Puerto Rico.

kusaal: Haiti tɛŋin, ba buoni li ye tonm tonm nɛ foofoo.
english: In Haiti, it is called tonm tonm and foofoo.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a nɔk fufu zɔ'ɔm makir 100 g (dinɛ ka ba nɔk bankan maal) mɔr niŋgbina maalig laʋg makir 2 g, ka kpaam kanɛ bɛ li pʋʋgin makir an 0.1 g ka lin tisid niŋgbiŋ paŋ si'em an 84 g, bɛɛ 267 calories.
english: 100 g dry fufu flour (made from cocoyam) contains 2 g of protein, 0.1 g of fat and 84 g of carbohydrates, and 267 calories.

kusaal: Fuseini Issah (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu nwadisa ayi daba ayi daar (orn 2 February 1975) ka o da an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Okaikwei North Constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region la wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Fuseini Issah (born 2 February 1975) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Okaikwei North constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ University of Ghana maal B.S.C., an EMBA, an FCCA yi Association of Chartered Accountants dinɛ bɛ United Kingdom la, nɛ venture capital and private equity kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Harvard University bɛ United States.
english: He graduated from the University of Ghana with a B.S.C., an EMBA, an FCCA from the Association of Chartered Accountants in the United Kingdom, and a certificate in venture capital and private equity from Harvard University in the United States.

kusaal: Fɔnɛtiks anɛ linguistiks lʋgʋr kanɛ zamisid pian'ad buudi wʋsa vuudnam an si'em.
english: Phonetics is a branch of linguistics that mainly concerns the articulation, sound wave properties, and perception of speech sounds.

kusaal: Fɔnɛtiks gɔsidnɛ vuudi naamid si'em (ninsaal nɔɔrin ken paae o kʋkɔr nya'arin), lin naanid zin'ig yinne paad yinne nɛ ninsaal tubiri wʋmi li si'em.
english: Phonetics is a branch of linguistics that mainly concerns the articulation, sound wave properties, and perception of speech sounds.

kusaal: Akiʋstik fɔnɛtiks anɛ fɔnɛtiks lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid pian'ad vuudnami an si'em ba ya'a yi nɔɔrin na.
english: Acoustic phonetics deals with the acoustic properties of speech sounds.

kusaal: Atikuletiri fɔnɛtiks anɛ lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid pian'ad vuudnami naamid si'em.
english: Articulatory phonetics deals with the ways in which speech sounds are made.

kusaal: Ɔditiri fɔnɛtiks anɛ fɔnɛtiks lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid kɛlisid la wʋmmid pian'ad vuud la si'em.
english: Auditory phonetics studies how humans perceive speech sounds.

kusaal: Gabriel Ayum Teye (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tuisr yinne kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ naasi yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni, January 1964) ka o an Ghana gbaʋŋ zamisid ka an pa'an (lecturer) ka lɛn an onɛ zi'eni tis vice dean of students bɛ University for Development Studies.
english: Gabriel Ayum Teye (born January 1964) is a Ghanaian educationist who is a lecturer and currently acting as the vice dean of students of the University for Development Studies.

kusaal: Teye da paami o basic educationnɛ Abertiso Roman Catholic Primary School yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai la ni (1969).
english: Teye had his basic education at Abertiso Roman Catholic Primary School in 1969.

kusaal: Ka keŋi o middle school Korwhere Roman Catholic Middle School bɛ Upper Manya district la, din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ nu (1975) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ wai la ni (1979).
english: He had his middle school education at the Korwhere Roman Catholic Middle School in the Upper Manya district, from 1975 to 1979.

kusaal: O da paami o secondary education bɛ nɛ Manya Krobo nɛ Kpando Senior High School din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ wai la ni (1979) kem paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yuobʋ la ni (1986) maali o GCE 'O' level nɛ GCE 'A' nwɛnɛ yʋma la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: He then attained his secondary education at the Manya Krobo and Kpando Senior High School from 1979 to 1986 for his GCE 'O' level and GCE 'A' respectively.

kusaal: O da naae Kwame Nkrumah University of Science And Technology nɛ Bsc degree in agriculture (Animal Science) yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991), ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yuobʋ la ni (1996), o da maali o Msc degree yi yunivɛsiti kan nɔɔ ni.
english: He graduated from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science And Technology with a Bsc degree in agriculture (Animal Science) in 1991 and in 1996, he obtained his Msc degree from the same university.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋm mɔrnɛ PhD in Meat Science and Technology dinɛ yi University of Bristol, UK nɛ diploma in Modern Management and Administration dinɛ yi Cambridge International College din mɛ bɛnɛ UK.
english: He holds a PhD in Meat Science and Technology from the University of Bristol, UK and a diploma in Modern Management and Administration from Cambridge International College also in the UK.

kusaal: O bɛ yunivɛsiti la ni ka lieb head of the Animal Science Department din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008).
english: He has since been with the university and became the head of the Animal Science Department from 2005 to 2008.

kusaal: O da anɛ Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012) ka yʋ'ʋn lieb Pro-Vice-Chancellor yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012) kem paae sankanɛ ka ba nɔk o ye o an Vice Chancellor yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ nu nwadis piiga yiiga daar la (October 1, 2015).
english: He was Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture from 2008 to 2012 and became the Pro-Vice-Chancellor from 2012 until he was appointed the Vice Chancellor on October 1, 2015.

kusaal: Ayum mɛ lɛn anɛ reviewer of the Ghana Journal of Animal Science, Journal of Food, Animal and Food Research, African Journal of Food, Agriculture, Nutrition and Development nɛ Ghana Journal of Agricultural Science.
english: Ayum is also a reviewer of the Ghana Journal of Animal Science, Journal of Food, Animal and Food Research, African Journal of Food, Agriculture, Nutrition and Development and the Ghana Journal of Agricultural Science.

kusaal: Ayum tʋʋma da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yuobʋ la ni (1986) ba da nɔk o ye o pa'an (lecturer) tis university for development studies la.
english: Ayum career began in 1996 when he was appointed a lecturer at the university for development studies.

kusaal: Gabriel Kweku Osei anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni n zi'enɛ tis Tain sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ Brong-Ahafo Region la, onɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Gabriel Kweku Osei is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Tain Constituency in the Brong-Ahafo Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Badu linɛ bɛ Brong Ahafo Region la lin ka nannanna ka ba yu'un buon ye Bono Region la.
english: Osei was born on 2 June 1974 and hails from Badu in the then Brong Ahafo Region, now Bono Region.

kusaal: O maali o Digirii zamisʋg linɛ an economics n yi Catholic University College in Fiapre sakurin la yʋʋma 2008 la ni.
english: He had his Bachelor of Science degree in economics at the Catholic University College in Fiapre in 2008.

kusaal: O da lɛn maal o mastas kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an kpikpiʋŋ zamisʋg (CEMBA) n yi KNUST sakurin la.
english: He also had his certificate in Executive Master of Business Administration (CEMBA) from KNUST.

kusaal: Ambrose College of Education linɛ bɛ Dormaa Akwamu sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Osei was the finance officer at St. Ambrose College of Education in Dormaa Akwamu.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan kʋdʋg n tis Tain sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ghana Bono Region la.
english: He is the former MP for Tain Constituency in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Osei nɛ nwadis ayuobʋ li daba ayi daar, yʋʋma 1974.
english: Osei was born on 2 June 1974 and hails from Badu in the then Brong Ahafo Region, now Bono Region.

kusaal: Osei da tʋmnɛ ligidi kpɛɛm n bɛ St.
english: Osei was the finance officer at St. Ambrose College of Education in Dormaa Akwamu.

kusaal: Osei anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Osei is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2020 Ghana da maal vɔt la, ka o kɔ'ɔgi o kʋk la ka Adama Sulemana di ka bas o.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he lost his seat to Adama Sulemana.

kusaal: O da mɔri vɔt bam 18,346 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 40.87% n yi vɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: He had 18,346 votes making 40.87% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Nwadis piiga la ni yʋʋm 2020 la ni, ka o da nɔk samɛti bɔtnam bam kɔbiga nɛ piisnu150 n maal Brodi Senior High Sakur la nɛ Pʋlis tʋʋma dɔt la tituaa sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni.
english: In October 2020, he presented about 150 bags of cement to help in the construction of the Brodi Senior High School and a Police Post in the constituency.

kusaal: Osei anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Osei is a Christian.

kusaal: Carl Linnaeus da pa'al lin an si'em bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' ni (1753) tʋʋmkanɛ ka o da pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Species Plantarum.
english: It was first officially described by Carl Linnaeus in his 1753 work Species Plantarum.

kusaal: Buudkanɛ wan paa anɛ A. vavilovii linɛ bɛ Turkmenistan nɛ A. asarense linɛ bɛ Iran.
english: The most closely related include A. vavilovii from Turkmenistan and A. asarense from Iran.

kusaal: Aggregatum buudi banɛ ka ba kuod (A. cepa var.
english: The Aggregatum Group of cultivars (A. cepa var.

kusaal: Cepa anɛ yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba tis "gabʋ"; di buudi yʋ'ʋri an Allium ka linɛ an Latin yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba tis garlic.
english: Cepa is commonly accepted as Latin for "onion"; the generic name Allium is the classical Latin name for garlic.

kusaal: di wan Spanish: cebolla, Italian: cipolla, Polish: cebula, nɛ German Zwiebel (kisig san'am nwa').
english: It has an affinity with Spanish: cebolla, Italian: cipolla, Polish: cebula, and the German Zwiebel (this last altered by folk etymology).

kusaal: Na'asaal buudi pian'ad "chive" yinɛ Old French chive, ka lin mɛ yi cepa.
english: The English word "chive" is from the Old French chive, in turn from cepa.

kusaal: zʋmaʋŋ kaŋa gabʋ la nat tun'e nɔbʋg wa'alim wʋʋ 15 to 45 cm (6 to 18 in).
english: Modern varieties typically grow to a height of 15 to 45 cm (6 to 18 in).

kusaal: Assyriologist la nɛ "gourmet cook" Jean Bottero yɛl "a cuisine of striking richness, refinement, sophistication and artistry".
english: The Assyriologist and "gourmet cook" Jean Bottero stated this was "a cuisine of striking richness, refinement, sophistication and artistry".

kusaal: Yʋʋm-pʋ-kʋdigin Ancient Egyptians la da na'as gabʋ tɛŋsʋg diib la ka ye li anɛ zanbin kanɛ pa'al nyɔvʋr kanɛ kaae naare.
english: Ancient Egyptians revered the onion bulb, viewing its spherical shape and concentric rings as symbols of eternal life.

kusaal: Pliny kanɛ da an yiiga kpɛɛm bɛ first century AD la da sɔbi pa'al gabʋ nɛ cabbage tʋʋma an siem bɛ Pompeii.
english: Pliny the Elder of the first century AD wrote about the use of onions and cabbage in Pompeii.

kusaal: chaeologists vɛɛnsid Pompeii saŋa bɛdigʋ its 79 AD volcanic burial la ya'aŋ ba da nyɛ labʋn'ɔg nwɛnɛ Pliny da pa'al siem la tituaa.
english: Archaeologists unearthing Pompeii long after its 79 AD volcanic burial have found gardens resembling those in Pliny's detailed narratives.

kusaal: Amaa fʋ labaar kanɛ ka ba da paam da fifth/sixth century AD bɛ authorial aegis of "Apicius" saŋa la (yɛl ye di anɛ gourmet) roman dim la da mɔr gabʋ nam la ba diib namin saŋa bɛdigʋ ni.
english: According to texts collected in the fifth/sixth century AD under the authorial aegis of "Apicius" (said to have been a gourmet), onions were used in many Roman recipes.

kusaal: Age of Discovery saŋa la, European dim banɛ da dɛŋim bɛ Columbian exchange lada mɔr gabʋ keŋ North America.
english: In the Age of Discovery, onions were taken to North America by the first European settlers in the Columbian exchange.

kusaal: Ba da nyɛ Allium tricoccum kanɛ nwɛnɛ gabʋ ka mɔr dit bɛdigʋ bɛ Native American gastronomy.
english: They found close relatives such as Allium tricoccum readily available and widely used in Native American gastronomy.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a gɔs yiiga English colonists dim la sɔb sieli digil la pa'al ye gabʋ pʋʋgin diib la ka Pilgrim fathers la da nɔki li bʋt bɛ North America.
english: According to diaries kept by early English colonists, the bulb onion was one of the first crops planted in North America by the Pilgrim fathers.

kusaal: Gab dɔnbʋʋlim bɛɛ zɛn'ɛd la (Yellow or brown onions) malisnɛ hali, ka li ke k aba kuod o bɛdigʋ di malisim la yɛla kas-kas anɛ Vidalia, Walla Walla, Cévennes, nɛ Bermuda.
english: Yellow or brown onions are sweet, with many cultivars bred specifically to accentuate this sweetness, such as Vidalia, Walla Walla, Cévennes, and Bermuda.

kusaal: Gab wiid la(Red or purple onions) ba mi'iʋ ka di nyuusid malis hali, ka ba mɔr dʋgid diib nam, di ya'a an kansa bɛɛ di ya'a nɛɛm nɛ.
english: Red or purple onions, known for their sharp pungent flavour, are commonly cooked in many cuisines, and used raw and in grilling.

kusaal: Shallot anɛ na'asaabuulug yinne kanɛ ka ba da gɛligi li ye o anɛ o kɔn hali ti paae 2011.
english: The shallot is a botanical variety of the onion which was classified as a separate species until 2011.

kusaal: Gabʋ la mabiis la sieba anɛ garlic, scallion, leek nɛ chieves.
english: The onion's close relatives include garlic, scallion, leek, and chives.

kusaal: Ba gbin la mɔr buudi nam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ka ba buonɛ ba ye gabʋnam ka kuodi ba mɔri maan diib, ba anɛ Japanese bunching onion Allium fistulosum, the tree onion Allium × proliferum, nɛ Canada onion Allium canadense la.
english: cultivated for food, such as the Japanese bunching onion Allium fistulosum, the tree onion Allium × proliferum, and the Canada onion Allium canadense.

kusaal: Ti pʋ nyaŋi baŋ li pin'ilʋg Gabʋ dinɛ ka Latin dim buon ye (Allium cepa L.Tooltip Carl Linnaeus, from Latin cepa), ka mɛ buon ye gab gbilʋg bɛɛ gabna'ana anɛ tivaand nyɛ'ɛlim kanɛ dit ka nyusid zan'ezan'e.
english: The onion (Allium cepa L.Tooltip Carl Linnaeus, from Latin cepa), also known as the bulb onion or common onion, is a vegetable that is the most widely cultivated species of the genus Allium.

kusaal: Ka gab gbil nyɛ'ɛlim la da pɛ'ɛs nɛ gab nyɛ'lima buud sieba ni hali ti paae yʋʋm 2011.Gabʋ kpin nɛ sieba paa anɛ garlic, scallion, leek, nɛ chives.
english: The onion's close relatives include garlic, scallion, leek, and chives.

kusaal: Ba wʋsa mɔrnɛ buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb amaa ti yiti ye di anɛ gabʋ nɛ diib banɛ ka kuod wʋʋ Japanese bunching gabʋ nyu'sa wʋʋ Allium fistulosum, the tree onion Allium × proliferum, nɛ Canada gabʋ nyu'sa Allium canadense.
english: cultivated for food, such as the Japanese bunching onion Allium fistulosum, the tree onion Allium × proliferum, and the Canada onion Allium canadense.

kusaal: Di anɛ kudimɛn mɔɔgin bʋn sʋŋ kanɛ yʋ'ʋn ba'a nya'a teŋ sieba.Gabʋ yiti taa anɛ biennial bɛɛ perennial tivaand amaa gɔsidi ka kuodi li yʋʋm yʋʋm ka vɔɔndi li saŋa kanɛ nar.
english: The onion is most frequently a biennial or a perennial plant, but is usually treated as an annual and harvested in its first growing season.

kusaal: · Allium cepa var.
english: Allium cepa var.

kusaal: A. cepa anɛ buudkanɛ ka ba kuod, amaa ba mɔɔgin bʋnam bɛ Central Asia nɛ Iran.
english: A. cepa is known exclusively from cultivation, but related wild species occur in Central Asia and Iran.

kusaal: Buudi kanɛ an Allium la ni ka gabʋ buudi la bɛ ka ba kuodi maan diib, wan wʋʋ Japanese gabʋ (A. fistulosum), Egyptian gabʋ (A. × proliferum), nɛ Canada gabʋ (A. canadense).
english: The genus Allium contains other species variously called onions and cultivated for food, such as the Japanese bunching onion (A. fistulosum), Egyptian onion (A. × proliferum), and Canada onion (A. canadense).

kusaal: aggregatum) si'eba anɛ shallots, ba da la'asid din buudi nɛ di kɔn', nɛ potato onions.
english: aggregatum) includes both shallots, formerly classed as a separate species, and potato onions.

kusaal: Buud banɛ wan si'eba anɛ garlic, leek, nɛ chives.
english: Related species include garlic, leek, and chives.

kusaal: Ninsaalibi baŋ ka gaŋ gabʋ pin'ili kuodi li wʋʋ yʋma 7,000 nwa.
english: Humans have grown and selectively bred onions in cultivation for at least 7,000 years.

kusaal: Li bʋdʋb la da na pin'ilnɛ yi West bɛɛ Central Asia.
english: Domestication likely took place in West or Central Asia.

kusaal: Ba pa'al zin'is babʋga ka li anɛ ye gabʋ yinɛ Iran, western Pakistan nɛ western Asia na.
english: Onions have been variously described as having originated in Iran, western Pakistan and Central Asia.

kusaal: gabʋ buudkanɛ ka ba buon ye allium fistulosum nɛ Allium tubarosum la, ba pin'ili di kuob bɛ China nɛ zʋʋd sieba wʋʋ zɛnma'asa, bielim nɛ tiwɛla nɛ 6,000 BC.
english: The onion species Allium fistulosum (spring onion, bunching onion) and Allium tuberosum (Chinese leek) were domesticated in China around 6000 BC alongside other vegetables, grains, and fruits.

kusaal: Recipes sieba da mɔr gabʋ tʋm nɛ Allium species la da anɛ dinɛ ka ba da nyɛ li bɛ cuneiform sɔb ni ka ba sɔbi li niŋ dinɛ ka ba nɔk ya'adi ya'abi li bɛ yʋʋm-pʋ-kʋdigin Mesopotamia, yʋʋm tusa ayi 2000 BC la ni.
english: The tablets, dating from around 2000 BC, are the oldest known recipes in the world.

kusaal: Egyptian dim la da la'am mɔr gabʋ mumi ba kum ban da di kaseta ye ba nyɛ ka gabʋ la Ramesses IV nifin.
english: Onions were used in Egyptian burials, as evidenced by onion traces found in the eye sockets of Ramesses IV.

kusaal: O da sɔbi pa'al Roman dimi tis gabʋ sida siem ye li mɔri ti'ebid nini wiim, ka mɛ lɛm sʋŋid gbɛɛm, nɛ dinɛ wʋsa anɛ nɔɔrin fɛn'ɛd nɛ baa na dʋm sɔ', lumbago, nɛ hali la'am nɛ dysentery.
english: He documented Roman beliefs about the onion's ability to improve ocular ailments, aid in sleep, and heal everything from oral sores and toothaches to dog bites, lumbago, and even dysentery.

kusaal: Gabʋ mɛ yuoe bʋt k aba yina gun,'u ka lɛɛ an finsa-finsa, k aba buoni li ye pearl, boiler, bɛ pickler gabʋ; nɛ' kaae gab mɛŋir la laa (pearl onions), bama bɛɛ ba kɔn.
english: Onions may be bred and grown to mature at smaller sizes, known as pearl, boiler, or pickler onions; these are not true pearl onions which are a different species.

kusaal: Gab banɛ ka kuomi'isim sua li la, ba tuoe dii li ala ti bam ɛɛnti pʋm dʋgiddi siem ka li an nintaŋin diib la (ploughman's lunch).
english: Onions pickled in vinegar are eaten as a side serving with traditional pub food such as a ploughman's lunch.

kusaal: Gagok anɛ Korean vocal music lʋgʋr kanɛ la'asid dap nɛ pʋ'ab kʋkɔya.
english: Gagok (Korean: 가곡; Hanja: 歌曲) is a genre of traditional Korean vocal music, derived from jeong-ak, for mixed female and male voices.

kusaal: Di da paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List ni nɛ din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (201)0 la ni ka mɛ paas South Korean Intangible Cultural Property din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (1969) la ni.
english: Gagok is considered one of the most refined forms of Korean court music and was designated a national cultural heritage in the 1960s and an UNESCO intangible heritage in 2010.

kusaal: Ba zaŋi li ka li paas nɛ South Korea ka UNESCO paasi li Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity ni, Sapal nwadi la dapisi nɛ anu, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu,November 25, 2005 la ni.
english: Since 1967, it has been a National Intangible Cultural Heritage of South Korea, and since 2005 it has been on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, 2021 la ni, Gangneung Dano Festival malima piinɛ atan' ni la na pin'il Sigir nwadig la dapiiga daar ka na zaŋ nɛ daba anii ti paae piinɛ ayɔpɔi, 17th la.
english: In 2021, the 13th Gangneung Dano Festival opened on June 10 and ran for eight days until the 17th.

kusaal: Gangneung Danoje Committee la ye, la anɛ malima nam banɛ pa'an Danoje ken si'em in the post-corona era, yʋʋda ban'as la nya'aŋ nɛ Danoje siig ka nɛ da bɛ yʋʋma 1,000 nɛ nwa la.
english: According to the Gangneung Danoje Committee, it consists of programs that present the direction of Danoje in the post-corona era.

kusaal: Li maalig hali bɛnɛ nwadisa anu la daba anu la ni yʋʋm la pʋʋgin woo lunisolar calender la pa'al si'am, Gangneung , Gangwon Province.
english: Gangneung Danoje (Korean: 강릉 단오제; Hanja: 江陵端午祭), called by locals Danogut (단오굿), is a yearly celebration of the Korean holiday Dano, in Gangneung, Gangwon Province, South Korea.

kusaal: Danoje gbini an Suritnal la gbin anɛ dabis tita'ar ka an Wina'am dabisir.
english: While the holiday Dano is celebrated elsewhere in Korea and even in China (Dragon Boat Festival), Gangneung Danoje is distinguished by its unique practices and long historical continuity.

kusaal: Gangneung Danoje yʋʋgi gaad Korea buudi malima banɛ mɛ lɛn bɛ ka li tʋʋm anɛ a pʋ'ʋsidi wɔ'ɔgid siig kanɛ gur zuokanɛ tisid teŋ la gurim ka pʋ'ʋsid teŋ la suma'asim yɛla nɛ ya nɛ ba kuob pʋʋgin.
english: While the holiday Dano is celebrated elsewhere in Korea and even in China (Dragon Boat Festival), Gangneung Danoje is distinguished by its unique practices and long historical continuity.

kusaal: Ya'asɛ, Heo-gyun da sɔbi o gbaʋŋin ye o da nyɛ Gangneung Danoje la nɛ yʋʋm tusir yiunne, kɔbus yuobʋ nɛ atan', 1603 yʋʋm la ni.
english: There is a definite attestation to the festival occurring in 1603; the scholar-official Hŏ Kyun recorded that he saw the festival then in his 1611 text Sŏngsobubugo.

kusaal: Gangneung Dano Festival pin'iligʋn sa da anɛ nidibin la'asig malima ka lɛn an public-private malʋŋ kanɛ ka gɔbina la basid sour ka ba maan, active coorperation from the government.
english: While the holiday Dano is celebrated elsewhere in Korea and even in China (Dragon Boat Festival), Gangneung Danoje is distinguished by its unique practices and long historical continuity.

kusaal: Ba da zaŋ Gangneung ka li anɛ Important Intangible Cultural Heritage No.
english: In 1967, the festival was made National Important Intangible Cultural Property No. 13.

kusaal: Ba mɛ lɛn maan shaman malima bʋnbɔɔr mɔrim yɛla ba kuob zin'igin nɛ teŋ la suma'asim.
english: After a series of rituals, the head shaman goes up to a tree on the mountain, and brings from it a sacred branch (신목; 神木).

kusaal: Buudi bɛdigʋ bɛ Garu sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Garu is the only town in Ghana which is bordered by two countries: Republic of Togo to the east and Burkina Faso to the north.

kusaal: Garu constituency bɛnɛ Garu-Tempane district I bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The Garu constituency is located in the Garu-Tempane District of the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di gaŋid nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaani zi'eni tisi ba wadmaannib yin la dɔlisid Ghana vɔɔtʋg suor.
english: Garu is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Kʋk la bɛnɛ Garu-Tempane Districti bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Garu-Tempane District of the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni, ba da nwaae di nɛ ye Garu-Tempane sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: Originally it was formerly part of the then-larger Garu-Tempane District in 2004.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlʋm la ya-dagɔbʋg da pʋdʋgnɛ yʋ'ʋn paam Tempane sʋ'ʋlʋm la 15 February 2018 ka babir kanɛ kpɛlim la mɛn an Garu sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: The southeast part of the district was split off to create Tempane District on 15 February 2018 and the remaining part has been renamed as Garu District.

kusaal: Di sʋ'ʋlʋm la'asʋg zin'ig kanɛ ka ba buon ye 'district assembly' la bɛnɛ ya-nya'aŋ Upper East sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: The district assembly is located in the eastern part of Upper East Region.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini (du'anɛ Alamisi daar 1 yʋʋmpaal nwadig 1970) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas Wadmaanb yikanɛ paasi anii Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Nkwanta South Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Oti Region Ghana la.
english: Geoffrey Kini (born Thursday 1 January 1970) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Nkwanta South Constituency in the Oti Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Geoffrey Kini nɛ Bakpa New Town bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: Geoffrey Kini was born and hails from Bakpa New Town in the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini da maali o Middle School Leaving Certificate (MSLC) nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu la ni (1985), ka maali o 2nd Division yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991) ka maali o Bachelor's degree in Human resource management (2nd Class Upper) yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2017).
english: Geoffrey Kini had his Middle School Leaving Certificate (MSLC) in 1985, 2nd Division in 1991 and his Bachelor's degree in Human resource management (2nd Class Upper) in 2017.

kusaal: O da lɛn naae Conflict Peace and Security yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi la ni (2020).
english: He is also a Graduate (Conflict Peace and Security) in the year 2020.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini anɛ chief executive officer (CEO) tis Kini Geoffrey.
english: Geoffrey Kini is the chief executive officer (CEO) of Kini Geoffrey.

kusaal: O da anɛ managing director tis Fair Com (A Database Technology Company) yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: He worked as a managing director for FairCom (A Database Technology Company) from 1994 to 2016.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016), Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg NDC gaansʋg la ni ka o da di Nkwanta South Constituency bɛ Oti Region, Ghana la.
english: Geoffrey Kini contested and won the 2016 NDC parliamentary primaries for Nkwanta South Constituency in the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O di nɛ vɔɔt kal tʋsa pisi nɛ ayi' nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (21,691) ka li an pisnu nɛ awai du'ali atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (59.3%) ka Edusei Cephas Kujo onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid la paam vɔɔt kal tusa anii nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ atan' (8,903) ka li an pisi nɛ anaasi du'ali anaasi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (24.4%), Njonam Wisdom Wagy onɛ zi'e o mɛŋ nyadi la mɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyɔpɔi (670) ka li an pii nɛ anu du'al anu kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (15.5%) nɛ Nyame Maxwell onɛ an Anɔraʋg na'adɔɔg (CPP) nid la paam kɔbisyi' nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (297) ka li an nɛɛm du'ali anii (0.8%).
english: Geoffrey Kini proceeded to win the parliamentary seat in his constituency (Nkwanta South Constituency) in the Oti Region of Ghana during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress to join the Seventh (7th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana with 21,691 votes (59.3%) against Edusei Cephas Kujo of the New Patriotic Party who had 8,903 votes (24.4%), Njonam Wisdom Wagya (An Independent Candidate) who also had 5,670 votes (15.5%) and Nyame Maxwell of the Convention People's Party(CPP) who had 297 votes (0.8%).

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini da keŋ tuoni di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la nɛ vɔɔt tusa ayi nɛ, kɔbiga nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (29,189) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (57.7%) ka Sherifa Sekyere-Tijani onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la paam vɔɔt tusa ayi, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi (20,272) dinɛ an pisnaasi du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (40.1%) ka Ograh Felix William onɛ bɛ Progressive People's Party(PPP) mɛ paam vɔɔt tusir yinne, kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1,127) dinɛ an ayi' du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (2.2%).
english: Geoffrey Kini again proceeded to win in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana with 29,189 votes (57.7%) against Sherifa Sekyere-Tijani of the New Patriotic Party who had 20,272 votes (40.1%) and Ograh Felix William of the Progressive People's Party(PPP) who had 1,127 votes (2.2%).

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Wadmaanib yir suoya dɔlisʋg (Standing Orders Committee).
english: Geoffrey Kini is a member of the Standing Orders Committee.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini da tis Bonakye bɛ Nkwanta South Constituency la dim samɛt bɔtʋ kɔbiga ye ba nɔki mɛ dɔɔdi paas sibiti la Bonakye Na'anb nɛ nidib la da bɛlim o ye o mɛɛ tisi ba ka di sʋŋ ka nidib da ɛɛnti duoe keŋi Nkwanta ka naan paam ti'ebʋg la.
english: Geoffrey Kini donated Hundred(100) Bags of Cement to the Bonakye community in the Nkwanta South Constituency to support the building of an additional facility at the Health Center since Chief and people of Bonakye made an appeal that they want to put up additional facilities to expand their health center so that people will not have to travel to Nkwanta before accessing primary health care.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini da lɛn tis Sibiti la ligidi nwɛ'nɛ Gaana sidi tusa piiga (GHc10,000) ye ba da' la'ad, Personal Protective Equipment (PPEs) gu'u ba mɛŋ.
english: Aside from the motorbike, Geoffrey Kini also donated an amount of GHc10,000 to the hospital to help them buy Personal Protective Equipment (PPEs) to protect themselves.

kusaal: Nannanna o anɛ Wadmaani tis Nkwanta South Constituency bɛ Oti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la dim.
english: He is now working as the Member of parliament (MP) for Nkwanta South Constituency in the Oti Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini da keŋ tuoni nya' ka di Wadmaan kʋk la o sʋ'ʋlim la, (Nkwanta South Constituency) bɛ Oti Region, Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni ka da dii keŋ Wadmaan yikanɛ paasa ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: Geoffrey Kini contested and won the 2016 NDC parliamentary primaries for Nkwanta South Constituency in the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini da lɛn nya' ka di yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la Nkwanta South Constituency bɛ Oti Region, Ghana la sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Geoffrey Kini again contested and won the 2020 NDC parliamentary primaries for Nkwanta South Constituency in the Oti Region of Ghana with 891 votes against Richard Manuribe who had 189 votes.

kusaal: O lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid pian'ad yɛla (Communications Committee) Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la ni.
english: He is also a member of the Communications Committee of the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Geoffrey Kini is a Christian.

kusaal: Joseph Catholic Hospital nɛd Municipal Hospital banɛ bɛ o sʋ'ʋlim (Nkwanta South Constituency) n bɛ Oti Region, Ghana la.
english: Geoffrey Kini again donated a motorbike to St. Joseph Catholic Hospital and the Municipal Hospital in his constituency(Nkwanta South Constituency) in the Oti Region of Ghana because they lacked any vehicle to attend to emergencies and also facilitate the movement of health officials attending the COVID-19 outbreak.

kusaal: Geoffrey Kini da lɛn keŋ tuoni tisi tiim ye ba puuus (gallons of disinfectants), kpakanɛ sɔɔnd nu'us (hand sanitizers), ki'ibʋ ku'omnam (liquid soaps) nɛ la'asieba (other items).
english: Geoffrey Kini further donated gallons of disinfectants, hand sanitizers, liquid soaps and other items.

kusaal: George Akuffo Dampare anɛ Ghana chartered accountant ka lɛn an pʋliŋ ya'as.
english: George Akuffo Dampare (born July 14, 1970) is a Ghanaian chartered accountant and police officer.

kusaal: Dampare da kpɛn' Ghana Police Service ninɛ yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nwadis piinɛ yi la ni, December 1990 ka an yʋʋma pisi (20) ka an Police Constable ka ba da tisi o piini ye onɛ an overall Best Recruit bɛ National Police Training School ka da di ya'an piini la wʋsa ka nya'al Best Marksman ma'aa.
english: Dampare was named the overall Best Recruit at the National Police Training School in 1991, after completing his recruit training, and won all awards except the 'Best Marksman' award.

kusaal: Fassi ka ba nɔk o ye o an IGP la, Dampare da tʋm zin'is kɔn'ɔnb kɔn'ɔb komanug nɛ kpɛŋ ni nwɛnɛ Aide-de-camp tis zuraan nya'andɔl, Director General (Finance), Director General (Welfare), Director General (ICT), Commandant of the Police Command and Staff College, Accra Regional Police Commander and Director General (Operations).
english: Dampare rose through the ranks, serving as the Vice President's Aide-de-camp to John Evans Atta Mills, Vice President of Ghana (1997–2001) for 18 months, the GPS's Chief Internal Auditor, the Municipal Commander for Cape Coast, the Regional Commander for Railways, Ports and Harbour (now the Police Marine Department), the Accra Regional Police Commander, and the Commandant of the Police Command and Staff College.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'an tis University of Cape-Coast (UCC), Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA), Regent University College, nɛ Data Link University College.
english: Dampare has served as a lecturer at the University of Cape Coast (UCC), Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA), Regent University College, and the DataLink University College.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛn anɛ banɛ da pin'ili pa'al Business School kanɛ bɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi.
english: He is also one of the pioneer lecturers at the Business School of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi.

kusaal: George Akuffo Dampare paas nidiba anii banɛ pʋ kʋdʋgɛ ka lieb Acting Inspector-General of Police (IGP) ka ba gaŋ din yi Ghana da paam asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ la ka an onɛ an biigi ba wʋsa sʋʋgʋn Fourth Republic la ni.
english: Dampare was the youngest Inspector-General of Police (IGP) to be appointed in the Fourth Republic of Ghana and the eighth youngest since Ghana gained independence.

kusaal: Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o nan zi'eni an Inspector General of Police tis Ghana Police Service Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dab pisi nɛ yinne daar (21 July 2021) ye o pin'il tʋʋma nwadisa anii la yiiga daar (1 August 2021), o da di'e yi James Oppong-Boanuh onɛ da an IGP din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ wai nwadis piiga ni la.
english: He was appointed the acting Inspector General of Police of the Ghana Police Service by President Nana Akufo-Addo on 21 July 2021, effective 1 August 2021, taking over from James Oppong-Boanuh who had been serving since October 2019.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne nwadisa nii la daba anii daar (October 8, 2021), ba da zuŋi o ye o an Inspector General of Police (IGP) tis Ghana Police Service.
english: On 8 October 2021, he was sworn in as the substantive Inspector General of Police (IGP) of the Ghana Police Service.

kusaal: George Nenyi Kojo Andah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan kʋdʋg n tis Awutu Senya West sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ghana Central Region sʋ'ʋlʋm, ba da du'a o nɛ nwadis anaasi la ni dabisim pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar yʋʋm 1970 la ni.
english: George Nenyi Kojo Andah (born 27 April 1970) is a Ghanaian politician and a former Member of Parliament for the Awutu Senya West Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Nwadis ayuobʋ la ni yʋʋma 2021 la nii, ka ba da diis o na'am n tis Akyempim Odefey linɛ bɛ Senya Beraku na'am sʋ'ʋlʋm ka o na'am yʋ'ʋr anɛ Nenyi Kobena Andakwei onɛ paas ayuobʋ.
english: In June 2021, he was installed as the Akyempim Odefey (Chief) of the Senya Beraku Traditional Area and goes by the stool name, Nenyi Kobena Andakwei VI.

kusaal: Ba da du'a George nɛ nwadis anaasi la ni dabisim piisi nɛ ayɔpɔi la yʋʋma 1970 la ni, o yinɛ Senya Beraku linɛ bɛ Ghana Central Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: George was born on 27 April 1970 and hails from Senya Beraku in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋi o secondary sakur n bɛ Achimota sakurin la ka tɔlisi keŋ KNUST ani ka o maal o Digirii linɛ ka ba buon ye Biochemistry.
english: He had his secondary education at Achimota School and proceeded to KNUST where he studied for a bachelor's degree in Biochemistry.

kusaal: George mɛ lɛn mɔr kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an MBA zamisʋg linɛ an kuosʋg yɛla n yi the University of Ghana kpikpiʋŋ sakurl.
english: George also holds an MBA degree in marketing from the University of Ghana Business School.

kusaal: George tʋm zi'ibɛda bɛdigu ni hali; onɛ da an kuosʋg darɛta n tis Guinness Ghana Breweries Ltd, onɛ da an tʋʋma la kpɛɛm n tis Scancom Limited.
english: George has worked for several reputable companies; from being the marketing director of Guinness Ghana Breweries Ltd to being the Chief Marketing Officer for Scancom Limited.

kusaal: O da paas MTN Tʋmtʋmnib la n tʋmmɛ an kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid kuosʋg yɛla n tis Bharti Airtel Nigeria, o da anɛ Bharti tʋmtʋm ka da lɛn an Ghana wʋsa taŋarʋŋ wʋsa kpɛɛm Ghana to the Regional Darɛcta, ka onɛ gɔsid kuosim nɔbigir yɛla, Globacom (Nigeria, Ghana and Benin).
english: He was a member of the MTN Group to being the Chief Marketing Officer of Bharti Airtel Nigeria, a member of the Bharti Group to Chief Operating Officer (Country Manager) of Glo Mobile Ghana to the Regional Director, Marketing Promotions, Globacom (Nigeria, Ghana and Benin).

kusaal: O da yɔ'ɔgi o mɛŋ tʋʋma linɛ yʋ'ʋr buon RUDDER Solutions, li da anɛ tʋʋm kanɛ ka o da yɔ'ɔg ye o zamis nidib ban na niŋ si'em ka kpikpiʋŋ nɔbig, li da anɛ kpikpiʋŋ nɔbigir yɛla, pa'an ban na pian'a si'em nɛ ban na di'e da'adib nɛ ban na sɔnsidi ba si'em-si'em, kuosʋg, ban na dɔl suosi'a ka kuos nɛ kpiʋŋ bɛllim pa'alʋg nam wʋsa.
english: He then went on to establish his own company called, RUDDER Solutions, a Ghanaian-based market-development management consultancy service.

kusaal: O mɛ da tʋm n bɛ Ankara SG-SSB tʋʋma la ni lin da yi nwadis atan' yʋʋm 2001 ti paae nwadis anaasi la yʋʋm 2002 la ni.
english: He also worked at the Accra main branch of SG-SSB from March 2001 to April 2002.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛn anɛ wadmaan n tis Awutu Senya West sʋ'ʋlʋm n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi ka lɛn an minista kanɛ gɔsid sɔnsʋg yɛla nya'andɔl.
english: He was also the Member of Parliament for the Awutu Senya West Constituency in the 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic and the Deputy Minister for Communications.

kusaal: O da paam yɔɔd nam hali yi MTN dim ni yʋʋm 2019 pʋʋgin.
english: He was honored as the MTN Mobile Money Builder Award in 2019.

kusaal: George anɛ onɛ da yɔ'ɔg Occupy Ghana a political pressure kpɛɛmnam la.
english: George is a founding member of Occupy Ghana a political pressure group.

kusaal: Nwadis anaasi la ni, yʋʋm 2022 la ni, ka o da sɔb gbaʋŋ ka li pian'azug an 'gban'e pʋtɛn'ɛr tʋm bɛdegʋ'.
english: In April 2022, he launched his book called 'Determined to do more'.

kusaal: Nwadis anaasi la, yʋʋm 2019 la ni, ka George da' na'asaa kʋkʋs banɛ ligidi kpi'em bam pii nɛ ayi' tis Department of Marketing and Entrepreneurship linɛ bɛ University of Ghana Business Sakur la ni.
english: In April 2019, George presented about 12 executive chairs to the Department of Marketing and Entrepreneurship at the University of Ghana Business School.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid ka an minista kanɛ gɔsid sɔnsʋg yɛla nya'andɔl n bɛ Ghana.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and was the Deputy Minister for communications in Ghana.

kusaal: O da di'e CIMG linɛ pa'al ye diib da'a pʋʋgin onɛ di yiiga yʋʋm 2008 la ni.
english: Received the CIMG Marketing man of the year in 2008.

kusaal: O da anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid n tis Awutu-Senya West Sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: In June, 2020 he was elected by the delegates of the NPP to represent Awutu-Senya West Constituency in the 2020 Ghanaian general election as their parliamentary candidate.

kusaal: Nwadis ayuobʋ la ni, yʋʋm 2020 la ni ka ba da vɔɔt ka o di tis Awutu-Senya West sʋ'ʋlʋm la O da Kɔ'ɔŋ kʋk la ka Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid di ka bas o.
english: He lost his parliamentary seat to Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: George di pu'a mɔr biis anaasi onɛ buudi la wʋsa zi'ini Accra.
english: George is married with four children and lives in Accra with his family.

kusaal: O da anɛ minista kanɛ gɔsid sɔnsʋg yɛla la nya'andɔl.
english: He is a former Deputy Minister for Communications.

kusaal: George Boahen Oduro anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi n tis New Edubease sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: George Boahen Oduro is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the New Edubease Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Atobiase linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: George Oduro was born on October 10, 1965, he hails from Atobiase in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O maal o Digirii zamisʋg linɛ an Project Management yi Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) sakur la ni yʋʋma 2013 la ni.
english: He had his Bachelor of Science degree in Operations and Project Management from Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) in 2013.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2015 ni, ka ba da tis o yɔɔd linɛ pa'an ye o tʋʋma linɛ Masters In Business Administrations (MBA) bɛ International Trade fair yi Analt University sakur la ni.
english: In 2015, he was awarded a Masters In Business Administrations(MBA) in International Trade from the Analt University.

kusaal: Oduro da an Darɛta tis Operations/Project of Cedar Seal Company Limited linɛ bɛ Ankara.
english: Oduro was the Director of Operations/Project of Cedar Seal Company Limited in Accra.

kusaal: Ba da du'a George nɛ nwadis piiga la ni li dabisim piiga, yʋʋma 1965.
english: George Oduro was born on October 10, 1965, he hails from Atobiase in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Oduro anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Oduro is a Christian.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nid ka wadmaan kʋdʋg tis New Edubease Sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: He is a member of New Patriotic Party and was the former Member of Parliament (MP) for New Edubease Constituency.

kusaal: Nwadis ayuobʋ la ni, yʋʋm 2019, ka o da da' moto anii tis tʋʋma kpɛɛmnam tis Ghana Education Service.
english: In June 2019, he presented motorcycles to about 8 circuit supervisors of GES.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Minista kanɛ gɔsid kuob nɛ diib yɛla nya'andɔl.
english: He was the Deputy Minister for Food and Agriculture.

kusaal: Ka nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la, 2020, ka o da nɔk makis wʋʋ bam tis sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: In December 2020, he donated sewing machines to about 40 apprentices in his constituency.

kusaal: George Kwame Aboagye ( du'anɛ 24 mɔtul nwadig 1968) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la tisi Asene-Akroso-Manso Constituency sʋ'ʋlim n bɛ Eastern Region la.
english: George Kwame Aboagye (born 24 August 1968) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Asene-Akroso-Manso Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Aboagye nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii Nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 mɔtul nwadig 1968) bɛ Akim Manso kanɛ bɛ Eastern region sʋ'ʋlim Ghana.
english: Aboagye was born on 24 August 1968 at Akim Manso in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o diploma nɛ Zenith University college ka maali o LLB at Lancaster University, Ghana campus.
english: In 1987, he obtained a certificate in mechanical engineering, he also earned his diploma at Zenith University college and his LLB at Lancaster University, Ghana campus.

kusaal: O da anɛ chief executive officer Geospence Ghana Limited din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii (2008) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: He was the chief executive officer at Geospence Ghana Limited from 2008 to 2016.

kusaal: Aboagye anɛ Kristo biig ka an Pentecost pʋ'ʋsʋm la kpɛɛm, O mɔr pu'a nɛ biis anaasi.
english: Aboagye identifies as a Christian and an elder at the Church of Pentecost.

kusaal: Aboagye da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg zug nyi'a ka di Asene-Akroso-Manso constituency sʋ'ʋlim kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne, kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anii (21,148) yi vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ yinne nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (31,078), ka li an pisyuobʋ nɛ anii du'al pisnaasi nɛ anaasi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (68.44%).
english: Aboagye won the seat of Asene-Akroso-Manso constituency on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party by obtaining 21,148 votes out of 31,078 valid votes cast, which is equal to 68.44%.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o paas la'askanɛ gɔsid tam nɛ tiis yɛla ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid banɛ mɔr ɔfiskanɛ mɔr nyɔɔd la.
english: He was then nominated to join the land and forestry committee and members holding offices of profits committee.

kusaal: George Mireku Duker (du'am; 9 sigsaa nwadig 1975)ka an Ghana nid , ka yi Dompim Pepesa bɛ Tarkwa Nsuaem Constituency, o anɛ politis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛm an wadmaan bɛ wadmaanib yikanɛ paas ayɔpɔi bɛ Ghana nwa anaasi Repulic la, ka mɛ an wadmaan zi'eli tis Tarkwa-Nsuaem Constituency bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlum, o zi'eli tis wabʋg na'adɔɔg la.
english: George Mireku Duker was born on May 9, 1975 in Dompim-Pepesa in the Tarkwa municipality.

kusaal: Duker zamis gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka ti buon ye, B.ED Accounting University of Education bɛ Kumasi Campus, ka nya'aŋ ka o zamis linɛ ka ti buon ye, MSC Oil and Gas Management University of Plymouth bɛUK.
english: Duker obtained a master's degree in Business Management from the University of Plymouth in 2010.

kusaal: O da anɛ pa'an bɛ gbana zamisʋg lʋgir la ni, yi yʋʋm 1998 ti paa yʋʋm 2006 ka nyaan lieb wadmaan nɛ Special Aide yi yʋʋm 2007 ti paa yʋʋm 2008 (Minista of Local Government, Ghana), o da lɛn anɛ Municipal Chief Executive bɛ Ghana gɔmena zugdaan John Agyekum Kuffour saŋa kanɛ da an yʋʋm 2008 la.
english: In 2007, he became a Special Aide at Ghana's Ministry of Local Government before being appointed in 2008 as Municipal Chief Executive for Tarkwa-Nsuaem by President John Kufuor.

kusaal: Duker da lɛm anɛ Programs Manager of Integrated Social Development Centre (ISODEC) lin yi yʋʋm 2011 ti paae yʋʋm 2012 la ni.
english: Duker was also the Programs Manager of Integrated Social Development Centre (ISODEC) from 2011 to 2012.

kusaal: Ghana gɔmena zugdaan Akuffo Addo da siak di'e Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF) bɛ are zugdaan nwadis anii la ni,li dabisim pisi nɛ anii daar, yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi la ni, ka da gaŋ George Mireku Duker ka o an yiiga kʋkdaan .
english: In 2019, President Nana Akufo-Addo appointed Duker as first chairperson of the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF).

kusaal: O da kɛ ka wabʋg na'adɔɔg la paam vɔɔtnam bɛdigu bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlum Ghana nwa ni.
english: In 2007, he became a Special Aide at Ghana's Ministry of Local Government before being appointed in 2008 as Municipal Chief Executive for Tarkwa-Nsuaem by President John Kufuor.

kusaal: la'asʋg kanɛ ka ba buon ye, fund la anɛ ye li tɛnb tɔb Ghana Repulic sanlima tʋʋma ni la, ka nyaan di'e ligidi nɛ linɛ wʋsa sʋm la , yit republic sanlima tʋʋma ni.
english: The fund manages the equity interest of the Republic of Ghana mining companies to receive minerals royalties and other related income due Ghana from mining operations.

kusaal: George Kwabena Obeng Takyi (ba da dʋ'a o nɛ 29 March 1965) anɛ chartered accountant ka lɛn an wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Manso Nkwanta Constituency bɛɛ Ashanti Region.
english: George Kwabena Obeng Takyi (born 29 March 1965) is a chartered accountant and currently a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana for Manso Nkwanta Constituency in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Takyi nɛ yʋʋm yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu Nwadisa atan la dabpisi nɛ awai daar (29 March 1965) bɛ Mpatuam, n bɛ Amansie West District kanɛ bɛ hali yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988).
english: Takyi was born on 29 March 1965 at Mpatuam, in Amansie West District since 1988.

kusaal: O mɔr MBA in Chartered Accountancy, Business Communication.
english: He has an MBA in Chartered Accountancy, Business Communication.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr PhD Accounting, Finance and Taxation.
english: He also has a PhD candidate in the area of Accounting, Finance and Taxation.

kusaal: On da nan pʋ kpɛn' pɔlitiks la, Takyi da anɛ pa'anɛ (lecturer) bɛ Kumasi campus, University of Education, Winneba.
english: Prior to entering politics, Takyi worked as a lecturer at the Kumasi campus of the University of Education, Winneba.

kusaal: O paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party dim ni ka an Wadmaani tis Manso Nkwanta Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and currently the member of parliament for the Manso Nkwanta Constituency in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O da di Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Manso Nkwanta kʋk la ka bas Joseph Albert Quarm.
english: He won the NPP Parliamentary primaries for the Manso Nkwanta seat against Joseph Albert Quarm.

kusaal: O da keŋ tuoni nya' nɛ Bance Musah Osmane, onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC nid yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi (December 2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: He subsequently contested against Bance Musah Osmane, an NDC candidate in the December 2020 election.

kusaal: Takyi da paam vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ anaasi, kɔbisnaasi nɛ anii (34,408) dinɛ an pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (76.1%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka di Manso Nkwanta Constituency kʋk la, o da zi'enɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) zug ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC nid la paam vɔɔt tusa piiga, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piswai nɛ anii (10,798) dinɛ an pisi nɛ atan du'ali awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (23.9%).
