english: Takyi had 34,408 votes making 76.1% of the total votes cast to win the Manso Nkwanta Constituency seat on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant had 10,798 votes making 23.9% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Government Assurance ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid diib, kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl nɛ kooko bɛlim yɛla (Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs).
english: He is a member of the Government Assurance Committee and also a member of the Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs Committee.

kusaal: PPE tis sakur sieba Manso Nkwanta Constituency bɛɛ Ashanti Region.
english: In February 2021, he presented some school uniforms and PPE to some schools in the Manso Nkwanta Constituency in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan kʋdʋg n tis Wenchi sʋ'ʋlʋm lin da yi yʋʋm 2005 ti paae yʋʋm 2021.
english: He is a former Member of Parliament who represented Wenchi constituency from 2005 to 2021.

kusaal: O da anɛ profɛsa n bɛ Howard Nyunivɛsiti linɛ bɛ Washington, D.C., lin da yi yʋʋm 1993 ti paae yʋʋm 2001 la ni.
english: He was a professor at Howard University in Washington, D.C., from 1993 to 2001.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ Helsinki sakur la ni n bɛ Finland ani ka o paam o diloma kasɛta gbaʋŋ n bɛ Economics ni ya'as.
english: He proceeded to Helsinki School of Economics in Finland where he obtained a Diploma in Economics.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o maal o mastɛs digirii n bɛ Wisconsin Nyunivɛsiti sakurin la.
english: He later obtained his master's degree and Doctor of Philosophy degrees after enrolling at University of Wisconsin, Madison.

kusaal: Vɔɔt kanɛ ka Ghana da maal yʋʋm 2000 ni la, ka o da di ya'an ka lɛb Ghana ka Gɔmina John Kufour da gaŋ o ye o an Darɛta onɛ gɔsid gban'asa yɛla kati wa'ae nɔbigir yɛla, o si'iŋ tʋʋma nɛ yʋʋm 2002 la ni.
english: Upon the election victory of the New Patriotic Party in Ghanaian general election in 2000, he returned to Ghana and was appointed by President John Kufour as the Director General of the National Development Planning Commission in 2002.

kusaal: Ba da vɔti ya ka o di ka da lɛn tɔlis tuonɛ di yʋʋm 2008, 2012, nɛ yʋʋm 2016 vɔɔt la ni ka di yʋʋm ban ni wʋsa.
english: He won the election and went on to win the three subsequent elections in 2008, 2012 and 2016.

kusaal: Onɛ da an minista kanɛ gɔsid Ghana ligidi yɛla la nya'andɔl lin da yi yʋʋm 2005 la ni ti paae nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la yʋʋm 2008 la ni Gɔmina Kufour win la.
english: He was appointed a Deputy Minister for Finance and Economic Planning from March 2005 to December 2008 by President Kufour.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2015 la ni, ka o yi yiŋ pian'a zab nɛ Mahama da gɔmina la ye li pʋ suor ye ba keŋ pɛŋ ligidi n yi IMF ni.
english: In 2015, he publicly opposed the Mahama administration's plan to seek a government bailout from the International Monetary Fund.

kusaal: Gyan-Bafour yiiga gaŋir ye o an wadmaan n tis Wenchi sʋ'ʋlʋm saŋkanɛ ka sʋ'ʋlʋm la da pʋdigi an Wenchi East nɛ Wenchi west sʋ'ʋlʋm la.yʋʋma 2004 Ka ba da vɔt ka o di.
english: Gyan-Baffour was first elected as the Member of Parliament for the Wenchi constituency after it was created from the then Wenchi East and Wenchi West constituencies.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 53.8% n yi vɔt wʋsa kanl ni.Onɛ Abdul-Latif Umar Abdullah onɛ an CPP nid, Alhassan Bene, onɛ an EGLEP nid nɛ Osei Kwadwo Hayford onɛ da zi'en o nyari.
english: He was elected over Abdul-Latif Umar Abdullah of the Convention People's Party, Alhaji Alhassan Bene of the Every Ghanaian Living Everywhere Party and Osei Kwadwo Hayford an independent candidate.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ ba wusa da paamnɛ 3.8%, 22.7%, nɛ 19.7% n yi vɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: These were equivalent to 3.8%, 22.7% and 19.7% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlʋm la da paas Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg wadmaanib bam piina anaasi 14 la banɛ da di n yi wadmaanib ban piisi nɛ anaasi 24 la ni n bɛ Brong Ahafo Region linɛ bɛ Ghana la.
english: His constituency was a part of 14 parliamentary seats out of a total 24 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ Yaw Osei Agyei onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la, Akotia Kwaky Thompson onɛ da an DFP nɛ Abdul-Latif Omaru Abdullay onɛ da an CPP nid la da nya'and nɛ taaba.
english: He was elected over Yaw Osei Agyei of the National Democratic Congress, Akotia Kwaky Thompson of the Democratic Freedom Party and Abdul-Latif Omaru Abdullay of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2012 la ni ka ba vɔɔt ka Gyan-Bafour lɛn di nɛ vɔɔt bam 50.83% kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka bas Yaw Osei Agyei onɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la nid, Ebenezer Gyimah Koomson onɛ da an PPP nɛ Jacob Steve Kojo Akasampah Gyan onɛ mɛ da an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid la da nya'a ka o di ka basi ba.
english: During the 2012 parliamentary elections, Gyan-Baffour obtained 50.83% of all valid votes by defeating Yaw Osei Agyei of the National Democratic Congress, Ebenezer Gyimah Koomson of the Progressive Peoples' Party and Jacob Steve Kojo Akasampah Gyan of the National Democratic Party.

kusaal: Gyan-Baffour da tʋm nɛ Institute of Chartered Economists of Ghana.
english: Gyan-Baffour is a fellow of the Institute of Chartered Economists of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paas Gɔmina tʋʋma kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ni, ba sieba anɛ Ghana bank, Council for Scientific and Industrial Research nɛ Ghana Institute of Management nɛ Public Administration.
english: He has been a board member of various Government of Ghana agencies including the Bank of Ghana, Council for Scientific and Industrial Research and the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration.

kusaal: O anɛ Catholic Karim biig n bɛ Ghana.
english: He is a member of the Catholic Church in Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid ka an minista kʋdʋg onɛ da gɔsid gban'e suma kati wa'ae nɛ nɔbigir yɛla Ghana kpɛla.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the former Minister of Planning in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Gyan-Baffour nɛ n bɛ Wenchi linɛ bɛ Brong Ahafo Region linɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Gyan-Baffour was born in Wenchi in the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋi o sakuri nɛ Nyunivɛsiti of Ghana sakur la ni, ani ka o da maal o digirii zamisʋg n bɛ economics la.
english: He attended the University of Ghana where he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in economics.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan kʋdʋg n tis Wenchi sʋ'ʋlʋm lin da yi yʋʋma 2005 ti paae yʋʋma 2021.
english: He is a former Member of Parliament who represented Wenchi constituency from 2005 to 2021.

kusaal: O da anɛ profɛsa n bɛ Howard Nyunivɛsiti linɛ bɛ Washington, D.C., lin da yi yʋʋma 1993 ti paae yʋʋma 2001 la ni.
english: He was a professor at Howard University in Washington, D.C., from 1993 to 2001.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid ka an minista kʋdʋg onɛ da gɔsid gban'e suma kati nɔbigir yɛla Ghana kpɛla.
english: Upon the election victory of the New Patriotic Party in Ghanaian general election in 2000, he returned to Ghana and was appointed by President John Kufour as the Director General of the National Development Planning Commission in 2002.

kusaal: O da keŋi o sakuri Nyunivɛsiti of Ghana sakur la ni, ani ka o da maal o digirii zamisʋg n bɛ economics la.
english: He attended the University of Ghana where he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in economics.

kusaal: Ka o lɛn maali o doctoral diploma kasɛta gbaʋŋ n bɛ Harvad Nyunivɛsiti sakur la ni.
english: He also has a post doctoral diploma from Harvard University.

kusaal: George Gyan-Baffour da anɛ profɛsa n bɛ Howard Nyunivɛsiti la ni lin da yi yʋʋm 1993 ti paae yʋʋm 2001.
english: George Gyan-Baffour was a professor of management at Howard University from 1993 to 2001.

kusaal: O da nyaŋi gɔs Ghana bɛllim nɛ li nɔbigir yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa hali.
english: He oversaw the development of the Coordinated Program for the Economic and Social Development of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan ni, ka o da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg zugu nya'a Wenchi Sʋ'ʋlʋm wadmaanib kʋk la.
english: Gyan-Baffour was first elected as the Member of Parliament for the Wenchi constituency after it was created from the then Wenchi East and Wenchi West constituencies.

kusaal: N paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anaasi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi.
english: He thus represented the constituency in the 4th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔt ka Gyan Bafour di ya'as yʋʋma 2008 la ni n an wadmaan n tis Wenchi sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: Gyan-Baffour was re-elected as the Member of Parliament for the Wenchi constituency in the 2008 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O da lɛn zi'en Sʋ'ʋlʋm la nɔba zug n bɛ wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anu la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la.
english: He thus represented the constituency again in the 5th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da paamnɛ 56.84% n yi vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 56.84% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ ba wʋsa da paamnɛ 41.43%, 0.87%, nɛ 0.85 n yi vɔt kanl wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 41.43%, 0.87% and 0.85% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlʋm la da paas Wabʋg wadmaanib bam piina ayuobʋ n yi wadmaanib la wʋsa kanl bam piisi nɛ anaasi banɛ bɛ Brong Ahafo Region Sʋ'ʋlʋm la.Wabʋg wadmaanib la wusa Ghana ni da la'asnɛ 107 n yi wadmaanib kanl la wʋsa ni linɛ an bam 230 n paas wadmaanib yir line paas anu la Gbana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: In all the New Patriotic Party won a minority total of 107 parliamentary representation out of 230 seats in the 5th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: On mɔr mi'ilim ka an Economist la zug, Gyan-Bafour da kpɛɛm banɛ tʋʋma kpin nɛ o zamisʋg la ni.
english: Being an economist, Gyan-Baffour has mainly sat on parliamentary committees that relate to his field.

kusaal: Nwadig yinne la dabisim piinɛ nɛ ayi la yʋʋma 2017 la ni, ka Gɔmina Nana Akuffo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an minista kanɛ gɔsid gban'asa kati wa'ae nɔbigir yɛla la.
english: On 12 January 2017, President Nana Akuffo-Addo nominated him as minister designate for planning.

kusaal: Wadmaanib kpɛɛmnam da vɛɛnsi o gɔs nwadis ayi la ni yʋʋma 2017 la ni.
english: He was vetted by the Appointments Committee of Parliament in February 2017.

kusaal: Gɔmina Akuffo-Addo da zʋŋi o nwadis ayi dabisim piinɛ nɛ yinne daar yʋʋma 2017 la ni.
english: He was sworn in by the President Akuffo-Addo on 11 February 2017.

kusaal: George Gyan-Baffour di pu'a mɔr biis ayɔpɔi.
english: George Gyan-Baffour is married with seven children.

kusaal: Li wʋsa nii, Wabʋg wadmaanib la da mɔr worʋg n gaad sɔ' wʋsa ba da mɔr wadmaanib bam 128 n yir wadmaanib kanl wʋsa linɛ an 230 la ni ka paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: In all, the New Patriotic Party won a majority total of 128 parliamentary representation out of a total 230 seats in the 4th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da paamnɛ vɔt bam 13495, 284, nɛ 278 wʋʋ ba yʋda la tʋʋnl dɔl si'em la.
english: These obtained 13,495votes, 284 votes and 278votes respectively of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Justice Getrude Torkornoo yitnɛ Winneba dinɛ bɛ Central Region of Ghana ni la.
english: Torkornoo hails from Winneba in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O du'am yʋʋm anɛ 11 September 1962 Cape Coast ni tis Abraham Kofi Sackey nɛ Comfort Aba Sackey, banɛ wʋsa da an pa'anib.
english: She was born on 11 September 1962 in Cape Coast to Abraham Kofi Sackey and Comfort Aba Sackey, who were both teachers at the time.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Suhum Presby Primary School yʋʋm 1966 la ni tɔlisi keŋ Ajumako Catholic School 1969 ni, dinɛ ka o naae o primary education.
english: She attended Suhum Presby Primary School in 1966 and continued to Ajumako Catholic School in 1969, where she completed her primary education.

kusaal: Dinɛ yi 1969 ti paae 1973, o keŋ tuon bɛ Ajumako Methodist School ka na keŋ Wesley Girls' High School bɛ 1973 ni dinɛ ka o paami o ordinary level certificate bɛ 1978 ni.
english: From 1969 to 1973, she continued at Ajumako Methodist School, prior to entering Wesley Girls' High School in 1973 where she obtained her ordinary level certificate in 1978.

kusaal: O keŋ tuoni bɛ Achimota School dinɛ yi 1978 ti paae 1980 paami o advanced level certificate.
english: She continued at Achimota School from 1978 to 1980 for her advanced level certificate.

kusaal: O paam B. A. in Law and Sociology bɛ University of Ghana yʋʋm 1984 ka naae Ghana School of Law yʋʋm 1986 ni.
english: She gained a B. A. in Law and Sociology at University of Ghana in 1984 and graduated from the Ghana School of Law in 1986.

kusaal: 2001 ni o paam Postgraduate Diploma bɛ International Law and Organization yit International Institute of Social Studies, dinɛ pɛ'ɛs Erasmus University Rotterdam dinɛ bɛ Netherland ni.
english: In 2001, she obtained a Postgraduate Diploma in International Law and Organization from the International Institute of Social Studies, which is part of Erasmus University Rotterdam in the Netherlands.

kusaal: 2011 ka o naae Golden Gate University School of Law, bɛ USA nɛ Master Of Laws (LLM) bɛ Intellectual Property Law.
english: In 2011, she graduated from Golden Gate University School of Law, in USA with a Master of Laws (LLM) in Intellectual Property Law.

kusaal: la, wada lʋgʋr dinɛ bɛ Accra onɛ da dɔl nya'aŋ la, Justice Torkornoo tʋmi an sʋŋid bɛ FIDA Legal Aid Service ka maali o internship nɛ Nabarro Nathanson bɛ London la.
english: Prior to joining Fugar & Co., a law firm in Accra, as an associate, Torkornoo worked as a volunteer at the FIDA Legal Aid Service and later worked there for her national service.

kusaal: O lɛb lʋgʋr la (Fugar & Co.) bɛ 1994 ni ye o an director.
english: She returned to Fugar & Co. in 1994 to become a director.

kusaal: January 1997, o pɛ'ɛsi sʋ'oe Sozo Law Consult dinɛ ka o an Managing Partner ti paae 14 May 2004 ka da paam gaŋir ye o an Justice tis High Court of Ghana.
english: In January 1997, she co-founded Sozo Law Consult, where she worked as Managing Partner until 14 May 2004 when she was appointed a Justice of the High Court of Ghana.

kusaal: O tʋmi bɛ High Court judge ti paae October 2012 ka da paam dʋ'ʋsʋg keŋ Court of Appeal.
english: She worked as a High Court judge until October 2012 when she was elevated to the Court of Appeal.

kusaal: Onɛ da mɔɔl labaar la da anɛ sankan Speaker of Parliament, Professor Aaron Mike Oquaye, dinɛ ka o ye ba gaŋir la ye di pɛ'ɛl fal kani ka pʋ'ab ayi'; Justice Vida Akoto-Bamfo nɛ Justice Sophia Adinyira banɛ gɛn' ka kul la zi'is, pɛ'ɛs nɛ onɛ ka di kʋ yʋʋgɛ ka o mɛn ma gɛn', Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo.
english: The announcement was made by the then Speaker of Parliament, Professor Aaron Mike Oquaye, who stated that the nominations were intended to fill the vacancies left by the retirement of two female justices; Justice Vida Akoto-Bamfo and Justice Sophia Adinyira, and the impending retirement of the then Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo.

kusaal: Justice Gertrude Torkonoo, pɛ'ɛs nɛ Justice Mariama Owusu nɛ Justice Avril Lovelace-Johnson, wʋsa keŋnɛ kpansib gɔsʋgi bɛ Gaŋir Kɔmitii bɛ wada dim la ni Atilata daar, December 10.
english: Gertrude Torkonoo, along with Justices Mariama Owusu and Avril Lovelace-Johnson, underwent the vetting process before the Appointments Committee of Parliament on December 10, 2019.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o bɛ Supreme Court yʋʋm November 2019 ka paam suori yi parliamentary yʋʋm December 2019 la ni.
english: She was nominated to the Supreme Court in November 2019 and received parliamentary approval in December 2019.

kusaal: O da zi'in kuk la zug 17 December 2019.
english: She was sworn in on 17 December 2019.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ bɛ office of Chief Justice yʋʋm April 2023 ye o zi'en Justice Kwasi Anin-Yeboah nɔba zug onɛ keŋ gɛɛb an Chief Justice bɛ May 24, 2023 yʋʋm ni.
english: She was nominated to the office of Chief Justice in April 2023 to replace Justice Kwasi Anin-Yeboah who retired as Chief Justice on 24 May 2023.

kusaal: O da zi'in kuk la zugi an 15th Chief Justice of Ghana yʋʋm 12 June 2023 la ni.
english: She was the 15th Chief Justice of Ghana from 12 June 2023 until her dismissal on 1 September 2025.

kusaal: Justice Torkornoo da paam gaŋir la bɛ Supreme Court of Ghana yʋʋm November 2019 la ni.
english: Torkornoo was nominated to the Supreme Court of Ghana in November 2019.

kusaal: Onɛ tʋmi an kukraan bɛ E-Justice Committee ni la, o gaad tuoni gba'e gba'ar kati wa'e automation bɛ kɔɔtɔ zi'ibibis ni wʋsa, da'aug yɛla nɛ na'asaasɔɔg tʋʋma la'ad nɛ software bɛ Judicial Service tʋʋma ni wʋsa.
english: In her work as chair of the E-Justice Committee, she led the planning of automation of all levels of courts, procurement and incorporation of the electronic resources and software in the work of the Judicial Service.

kusaal: November 12, 2019 nii, Zugdaan Nana Akufo-Addo gaŋ Justice Torkornoo pɛ'ɛs nɛ Justice Mariama Owusu nɛ Justice Lovelace-Johnson, pɛ'ɛs Appeal Court Judges.
english: On November 12, 2019, President Nana Akufo-Addo nominated Torkornoo together with Justices Mariama Owusu and Avril Lovelace-Johnson, then Appeal Court Judges.

kusaal: Onɛ da nyɛɛ Council of State la naae la, Zugdaan la da paam suori yi Parliament ye ka ba gaŋ o, nɛ o taaba ayi' la.
english: After the completion of consultations with the Council of State, the President sought the approval of Parliament for her appointment with her two other colleagues.

kusaal: O pɛ'ɛsnɛ ayi' o ma biis anu la ni.
english: She is the second of five siblings.

kusaal: Di kpi'enɛ Gulf of Guinea ka Atlantic Ocean bɛ di ya-dagɔbʋg, ka ban nɛ Ivory Coast tɔnd taaba bɛ ya-tuon, Burkina Faso mɛn bɛ ya-datiʋŋ, ka Togo bɛ ya-nya'aŋ.
english: Ghana, officially the Republic of Ghana, is a country in West Africa. It is situated with the Gulf of Guinea and the Atlantic Ocean to the south, and shares borders with Ivory Coast to the west, Burkina Faso to the north, and Togo to the east.

kusaal: Ghana mɔri paalʋ ka di labisim an wʋʋ 239,567 km2 (92,497 sq mi).
english: Ghana covers an area of 239,567 km2 (92,497 sq mi), spanning various ecologies, from coastal savannas to tropical rainforests.

kusaal: Bani da bɛ yamʋg ni wʋʋ yʋma bɛdigʋ la ka pʋ sʋ'e ba mɛŋ la, bani da bɛ yamʋg pʋʋgʋn la British colonial da mɔr sʋ'ʋlʋm kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb nam 4: Gold Coast, Ashanti, the Northern Territories, nɛ British Togoland.
english: Following more than a century of colonial resistance, the later borders of the country took shape, encompassing four separate British colonial territories: Gold Coast, Ashanti, the Northern Territories, and British Togoland.

kusaal: Ghana bɛnɛ Gulf of Guinea la baba, digriis bi'ela bɛ Equator ya-datiʋŋ.
english: Ghana lies on the Gulf of Guinea in West Africa, a few degrees north of the Equator.

kusaal: Di gilig nɛ wʋʋ 239,535 km2 (92,485 sq mi) ka mɔr Atlantic coastline dinɛ wa'am wʋʋ 560 kilometres (350 miles) bɛ Guinea ni dinɛ bɛ Atlantic Ocean ya-dagɔbʋg.
english: It covers 238,540 km2 (92,101 sq mi) and has an Atlantic coastline of about 560 kilometres (350 miles).

kusaal: Mɔɔgteŋ da gɛndig nɛ south coastal shrublands nɛ baŋɔ sʋ'ʋg Ghana, baŋɔ (wɛog) bɛnɛ northward yit coast 320 kilometres (200 miles) nɛ eastward nɛ maximum of 270 kilometres (170 miles) nɛ bɛllim zi'ig an sanlima tuub nɛ industrial minerals nɛ timbanam.
english: Grasslands mixed with south coastal shrublands and forests dominate Ghana, with forest extending northward from the coast 320 kilometres (200 miles) and eastward for a maximum of about 270 kilometres (170 miles) with locations for mining of industrial minerals and timber.

kusaal: Ghana anɛ 5 terrestrial ecoregions: Eastern Guinean forests, Guinean forest–savanna mosaic, West Sudanian savanna, Central African mangroves, nɛ Guinean mangroves.
english: Ghana is home to five terrestrial ecoregions: Eastern Guinean forests, Guinean forest–savanna mosaic, West Sudanian savanna, Central African mangroves, and Guinean mangroves.

kusaal: White Volta River nɛ di kɔdaag kani pʋbidi kenna Black Volta, pʋbidnɛ ya-dagɔbʋg dɔl Ghana ken Lake Volta, ku'otita'ar kani pɛ'ɛs atan' di bɛdim nɛ di yaliŋ wʋsa, dinɛ ka hydroelectric Akosombo Dam dim maal, di naae yʋʋm 1965 la ni.
english: The White Volta River and its tributary Black Volta, flow south through Ghana to Lake Volta, the world's third-largest reservoir by volume and largest by surface area, formed by the hydroelectric Akosombo Dam, completed in 1965.

kusaal: Ka 2015 nii, gɔmma la da tis gbaʋŋ ka di pian'azut an "Ghana's Intended Nationally Determined Contribution." Bani dɔlisid nɛ', Ghana si'ak ka tik nɛ Paris Climate Agreement bɛ yʋʋm 2016 la ni.
english: Ghana signed the Paris Agreement in 2016.

kusaal: Nidib wʋʋ 29% bɛnɛ yʋma 15 tɛŋir, ka nidib bani bɛ yʋma 15–64 an 57.8 yi kɔbiga nidib kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn.
english: As of 2018, around 29% of the population is under the age of 15, while persons aged 15–64 make up 57.8% of the population.

kusaal: 2010 kanlʋg la da bigis ye buudinam kanl anɛ Akan (47.3%), Mole-Dagbani (16.6%), Ewe (13.9%), Ga-Dangme (7.4%), Gurma (5.7%) ka Guan la mɛn mɔr (3.7%).
english: The 2010 census reported that the largest ethnic groups are the Akan (47.3%), the Mole-Dagbani (18.5%), the Ewe (13.9%), the Ga-Dangme (7.4%), the Gurma (5.7%) and the Guan (3.7%).

kusaal: Teŋgbaʋŋ banɛ la'asʋg an Ghana la anɛ Dagbon teŋgbaʋŋ nɛ Bono sʋ'ʋlʋm, dinɛ ka Bono state bɛ di pʋʋgʋn dinɛ yi 11th century la sa.
english: The earliest kingdoms to emerge in Ghana were Bonoman in the south and the Kingdom of Dagbon in the north, with Bonoman existing in the area during the 11th century.

kusaal: Teŋgbana nwɛnnɛ Dagbon teŋgbaʋŋ dinɛ bɛ ya-datiʋŋ nɛ Ashanti Empire dinɛ bɛ ya-dabɔbʋg la mɛn da bɛ yʋma tʋsa bɛdigʋ.
english: The earliest kingdoms to emerge in Ghana were Bonoman in the south and the Kingdom of Dagbon in the north, with Bonoman existing in the area during the 11th century.

kusaal: Dinɛ yi 15th century, Portuguese Empire la dɔl pɛ'ɛs nɛ European powers, da sɔs suor ye tɔlim ninsaal suor bɛllim, ka British la yʋ'ʋn da di'e suori sʋ'ʋg coast la bɛ 19th century la ni.
english: Beginning in the 15th century, the Portuguese Empire, followed by other European powers, contested the area for trading rights, until the British ultimately established control of the coast by the 19th century.

kusaal: Ka 6 March 1957, Ghana da an yiiga teŋi bɛ Sub-Saharan Africa ye ba paami ba sʋ'ʋ-m-mɛŋ.
english: On 6 March 1957, Ghana became the first colony in Sub-Saharan Africa to achieve sovereignty.

kusaal: Di bɛnɛ latitudes 4°45'N nɛ 11°N pʋʋgʋn, nɛ longitudes 1°15'E and 3°15'W pʋʋgʋn mɛn.
english: It is situated between latitudes 4°45'N and 11°N, and longitudes 1°15'E and 3°15'W. The Prime Meridian passes through Tema, near Accra, making Ghana the country closest to the intersection of the Prime Meridian and the Equator (0°, 0°), located offshore in the Atlantic.

kusaal: Prime meridian la dɔli Ghana gaad, zi'ig la anɛ Tema.
english: It is situated between latitudes 4°45'N and 11°N, and longitudes 1°15'E and 3°15'W. The Prime Meridian passes through Tema, near Accra, making Ghana the country closest to the intersection of the Prime Meridian and the Equator (0°, 0°), located offshore in the Atlantic.

kusaal: Volta ku'om la pʋbidnɛ dɔl Lake Volta kpɛn'ɛd Gulf of Guinea.
english: Its main geographical units are: the Coastal Plain along the Gulf of Guinea, the Ashanti uplands in the centre, the Volta Basin in the east, which is dominated by Lake Volta, and the Northern Plains stretching to Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Ghana ya-datiʋŋ mɛŋir anɛ Pulmakong ka di ya-dagɔbʋg mɛŋir an Cape Three Points.
english: The northernmost settlement in Ghana is Pulmakong near the Burkina Faso border, while the southernmost point is Cape Three Points.

kusaal: Ghana bɛnɛ hydro-climatic zi'es atan'.
english: Ghana sits at the intersection of three hydro-climatic zones.

kusaal: Ghana 1979 vɔɔtʋg la da bɛnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai nwadis ayuobʋ la dabpiinɛ anii daar (18 June 1979), ka ba da lɛn vɔɔt zuraannam la ya'as yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiwai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai nwadis ayɔpɔi la daba awai daar (9 July 1979).
english: General elections were held in Ghana on 18 June 1979, with a second round of the presidential election on 9 July 1979.

kusaal: Ba da lɛm maligim vɔɔt zuraan vɔɔt lanɛ ka di nya'aŋ ka Hilla Limann onɛ da bɛ People's National Party la di.
english: The presidential election resulted in victory for Hilla Limann of the People's National Party, who received 62% of the vote in the run-off, whilst his PNP won 71 of the 140 seats in Parliament.

kusaal: Electoral Commissioner vɔɔtʋg la saŋa da anɛ Joseph Kingsley-Nyinah, onɛ da an Appeal Court Piyam ka Supreme Military Council (SMC) da gaŋ o.
english: The Electoral Commissioner during the elections was Joseph Kingsley-Nyinah, an Appeal Court Judge who was appointed by the Supreme Military Council (SMC).

kusaal: La'anɛ ban da yis SMC yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai nwadisa ayuobʋ daba anaasi daar (4 June 1979) la, Armed Forces Revolutionary Council dinɛ da di'e kpɛŋ la da bas suor ka ba maal vɔɔtʋg bakɔi ayi nya'aŋ.
english: Although the SMC was overthrown on 4 June 1979, the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council military government which replaced it allowed the elections to proceed just two weeks later.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (62%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin vɔɔtkanɛ da paasi ayi la ni ka o PNP da di kʋgʋs pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne (71) yi wadmaannib kʋgʋs kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi pʋʋgin (140).
english: The presidential election resulted in victory for Hilla Limann of the People's National Party, who received 62% of the vote in the run-off, whilst his PNP won 71 of the 140 seats in Parliament.

kusaal: Nidib nwɛnɛ miliyɔŋa anu nɛ tusa pisyɔpɔi (5, 070,000) yʋda da bɛ vɔɔtʋg gbaʋŋ la ni.
english: Around 5,070,000 people were registered to vote.

kusaal: Vɔɔt kaŋa da an yiiga daa din yi ban da maal yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1979) ni la, ka an vɔɔtkanɛ paasi anaasi maali ala buudi teŋ la paami asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1957).
english: They were the first contested elections held in the country since 1979, and only the fourth contested elections of any sort since the country gained independence in 1957.

kusaal: Jerry Rawlings, onɛ da an zuraan din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981) coup la, da siak ye na'adɔɔg kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb tʋn'e bɛ Ghana yʋʋm la pin'ilʋgin.
english: Jerry Rawlings, who had led the country since taking power in a 1981 coup, had grudgingly agreed to hold multiparty elections earlier in the year.

kusaal: Rawlings da zi'en Progressive Alliance na'adɔɔg nɔba zugʋ nya' dinɛ ka o mɛŋ na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress da paas, ka di nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ anii du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (58.4%) ka di paam on na di ka ba pʋ maligim vɔɔt ya'asa.
english: Rawlings ran as the candidate of the Progressive Alliance, which included his National Democratic Congress, and won 58.4% of the vote, enough to win without the need for a runoff.

kusaal: Banɛ da yina vɔɔt da anɛ nidib pisnu du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.2%).
english: Voter turnout was 50.2%.

kusaal: Na'adɔɔg banɛ kpɛlim la da zɛrig Rawlings nɛ o nidib la ye ba fan' vɔɔt lanɛ, ka zu vɔɔt dakanam ka lɛn ti'as vɔɔt kanl ya'as.
english: The opposition accused Rawlings and his supporters of engaging in massive fraud, including ballot-box stuffing and altering results after they were certified.

kusaal: Zuraannam vɔɔtʋgin la, ba da lɛn vɔɔt onɛ da dɛŋim an zuraan la, Jerry Rawlings onɛ bɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) vɔɔt yimmʋ ni, ka o di ka bas John Kufuor onɛ bɛ Great Alliance (ka Kufuor da gaad Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party tuon), o da paam vɔɔt pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (57%).
english: In the presidential elections, incumbent Jerry Rawlings of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) was re-elected in a single round, defeating John Kufuor of the Great Alliance (led by Kufuor's New Patriotic Party) with 57% of the vote.

kusaal: Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la, NDC da di kʋgʋs bɛdigʋ, ba da di kʋgʋs kʋgʋs kɔbiga nɛ pistan nɛ atan (133) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' (200 seats) pʋʋgin.
english: The NDC retained its majority in Parliament, winning 133 of the 200 seats.

kusaal: Ghana 2000 wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la da bɛnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nwadis piinɛ ayi daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 December 2000), ka ba da lɛn maligim vɔɔt zuraan vɔɔtʋg la ya'as nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ anii daar, 28 December.
english: General elections were held in Ghana on 7 December 2000, with a second round of the presidential election on 28 December.

kusaal: Zugdaan vɔɔtʋg la nii, John Kufuor onɛ bɛ wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party (NPP) da bɛ tuon nɛ vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ anii kɔbiga pʋʋgio (48 percent) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: In the presidential election, John Kufuor of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) led the field in the first round of voting, taking 48 percent of the vote.

kusaal: Zugdaan nya'adɔl John Atta Mills onɛ da bɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress (NDC) da paasi ayi, nɛ vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (44 percent).
english: Vice President John Atta Mills of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) finished second, with 44 percent.

kusaal: Ban da lɛn vɔɔt vɔɔtkanɛ paasi ayi la Kufuor da diya ka basi Atta-Mills.
english: Kufuor defeated Atta-Mills in the second round with 57 percent of the vote.

kusaal: Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, NPP da lɛn di kʋgʋs bɛdegʋ di wadmaannib kʋgʋs la bɛdegʋ vɔɔtkan ni, ka da gu'oe yʋma anii banɛ ka ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, NDC zin'i kʋg la zug.
english: The NPP also won the most seats in the parliamentary elections, ending eight years of NDC dominance.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (57 percent) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Kufuor defeated Atta-Mills in the second round with 57 percent of the vote.

kusaal: Nɛ wala wʋsa, ban da mɔr kʋgʋs piswai nɛ wai (99) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' (200 seats) pʋʋgin la, di da pasig kʋgʋsa ayi nɛ ban na zu'oe gaad na'adɔbama la.
english: However, with 99 of the 200 seats, it was two seats short of a majority.

kusaal: Zuraan vɔɔtʋg la ni, John Kufuor onɛ bɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party (NPP), da diya ka bas John Atta-Mills onɛ da bɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (52 percent) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin yiiga vɔɔt la ni ka amaligim vɔɔt lɛn ka'asigɛ.
english: The presidential elections resulted in a victory for incumbent John Kufuor of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), who defeated John Atta-Mills of the National Democratic Congress with 52 percent of the vote in the first round, enough to win without the need for a runoff.

kusaal: Wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la ni, Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la, NPP wda di kʋgʋs kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ anii (128 seats) yi kʋgus kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan (230-seat) pʋʋgin, ka zu'oe gaad na'adɔbanɛ kpɛlim la wadmaannib yin.
english: The parliamentary elections saw the NPP win 128 seats in the expanded 230-seat Parliament, an outright majority.

kusaal: Ka na'aya'ad sɔ' pʋ paam ka di paae vɔɔt pisnu kɔbiga pʋʋginla (50%) ba da maligim, vɔɔt ya'as (run-off election) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 December 2008) na'anya'adib ayi banɛ da gaad tuon la, Nana Akufo-Addo onɛ bɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɛ John Atta Mills onɛ bɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress.
english: Since no candidate received more than 50% of the votes, a run-off election was held on 28 December 2008 between the two candidates who received the most votes, Nana Akufo-Addo of the governing New Patriotic Party and John Atta Mills of the opposition National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: 21 December 2006, Zuraan nya'andɔl kʋdʋg John Atta Mills, onɛ da nya' National Democratic Congress (NDC) zuraan vɔɔtʋg yʋʋm tusa ayi la (2000) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni (2004), Ma'asim tig na'adɔɔg nidibi da gaŋ o ye o aan ba zuraan na'anya'ad yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) vɔɔtʋgin la da diya.
english: On 21 December 2006, former Vice-President John Atta Mills, who unsuccessfully ran as the National Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate in 2000 and 2004, was overwhelmingly elected by NDC as its candidate for the 2008 presidential election.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ Foreign Minister kʋdʋg Nana Akufo-Addo ye o an yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi la (2008) zi'en wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nɔba zug ba na'adɔɔg la congress ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la nwadis piinɛ ayi dabpisi nɛ atan daar (23 December 2007).
english: Former Foreign Minister Nana Akufo-Addo was elected as the 2008 presidential candidate of the governing New Patriotic Party (NPP) at a party congress on 23 December 2007.

kusaal: La'anɛ on da pʋ paam vɔɔt pisnu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50%) la, onɛ da ti'ali ayi daan ka an Trade Minister kʋdʋg John Alan Kyeremanten, da siak ye on liya ka sʋŋi Akufo-Addo.
english: Although he fell short of the required 50%, the second-place candidate, former Trade Minister John Alan Kyeremanten, conceded defeat and backed Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Ya'asa, ba da lɛn zɛrig nidib vɔɔt na'ayiigim dinɛ da ta'as zaba Kenya nɛ Zimbabwe, ka military coups d'état, dinɛ naam Mauritania nɛ Guinea la mɛ kɛ ka nidib wʋsa nindaa yʋ'ʋm bɛ Ghana dim vɔɔtʋgin la ye ba na mɔr constitutional democracy lɛb Africa na.
english: Additionally, allegations of electoral fraud that resulted in violence following elections in Kenya and Zimbabwe and military coups d'état in Mauritania and Guinea caused international election monitors to hope the Ghanaian elections would refurbish the image of constitutional democracy in Africa.

kusaal: Nana Akufo-Addo –Attorney General and Minister for Justice, Minister for Foreign Affairs, zi'eni tis New Patriotic Party (NPP)
english: Nana Akufo-Addo – The former Attorney General and Minister for Justice, Minister for Foreign Affairs, and a current member of Parliament representing the New Patriotic Party (NPP)

kusaal: Emmanuel Ansah-Antwi – zi'eni tis Democratic Freedom Party (DFP)
english: Emmanuel Ansah-Antwi – Representing the Democratic Freedom Party (DFP)

kusaal: Edward Nasigri Mahama – zi'eni tis People's National Convention (PNC)
english: Edward Nasigri Mahama – Representing the People's National Convention (PNC)

kusaal: Paa Kwesi Nduom –Minister for Economic Planning & Regional Cooperation, Minister for Energy, Minister for Public Sector Reform kʋdʋg zi'eni tis Convention People's Party (CPP)
english: Paa Kwesi Nduom – The former Minister for Economic Planning & Regional Cooperation, Minister for Energy, Minister for Public Sector Reform, and a current member of Parliament representing the Convention People's Party (CPP)

kusaal: Thomas Nuako Ward-Brew – zi'eni tis Democratic People's Party (DPP)
english: Thomas Nuako Ward-Brew – Representing the Democratic People's Party (DPP)

kusaal: Vɔɔtkanɛ ka ba da maal April 2008 da pa'al ye Mills da bɛ Akufo-Addo tuon bi'ela.
english: A poll conducted in April 2008 showed Mills slightly ahead of Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: National Commission for Civic Education da maal vɔɔtkaŋa nɛ nidib tusa anu, kɔbistan nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (5,327).
english: The National Commission for Civic Education conducted the poll which sampled 5,327 people.

kusaal: Angus Reid Global Monitor da lɛm maal vɔɔtʋg yinne October 2008 ka nyɛ ka Akufo-Addo bɛ tuon.
english: Another poll conducted in October 2008 by the Angus Reid Global Monitor saw Akufo-Addo leading.

kusaal: Mills da di vɔɔt la gaadi o tiraan la nɛ vɔɔt yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin, o da di vɔɔt kan on da mɔ nɔɔra atan ka pʋ di la.
english: On 21 December 2006, former Vice-President John Atta Mills, who unsuccessfully ran as the National Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate in 2000 and 2004, was overwhelmingly elected by NDC as its candidate for the 2008 presidential election.

kusaal: Dinɛ an vɔɔt kanɛ pʋ lal taaba labakʋda ni Ghana pin'il vɔɔtʋg.
english: The stakes of the election were raised by the discovery of oil in Ghana and an expectation for incoming oil revenues to begin in 2010.

kusaal: Na'anya;adiba anii (eight candidates) da sɔbi ba yʋda tis Electoral Commission of Ghana ye ba nya' zuraan vɔɔtʋg la.
english: The following eight candidates formally registered with the Electoral Commission of Ghana.

kusaal: John Atta Mills – Vice-President kʋdʋg zi'eni tis National Democratic Congress (NDC)
english: John Atta Mills – The former Vice-President representing the National Democratic Congress (NDC)

kusaal: Vɔɔtʋg la mɛ da pa'al ye nidib piswai nɛ ayuobʋ du'ali awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (96.9%) na yina vɔɔt, vɔɔtʋg daar.
english: The poll also predicted a high voter turnout of 96.9%.

kusaal: Ghana 2012 vɔɔtʋg la da bɛnɛ Arizum daar, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadis piinɛ ayi la daba ayɔpɔi daar ye ba vɔɔti gaŋ zugraan nɛ wadmaannib kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (275) constituency nam la ni.
english: General elections were held in Ghana on Friday 7 December 2012 to elect a president and members of Parliament in 275 electoral constituencies.

kusaal: Banɛ da nya' zugraan na'am la anɛ onɛ da zin'i kʋk la zug, Zugraan John Dramani Mahama onɛ bɛ National Democratic Congress (NDC), nɛ Nana Akufo-Addo onɛ bɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) nɛ na'anya'adiba ayuobʋ sieba.
english: Competing for presidency were incumbent president John Dramani Mahama of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), his main challenger Nana Akufo-Addo of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and six other candidates.

kusaal: Nana Akufo-Addo da paam vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (47.74%).
english: Nana Akufo-Addo received 47.74%.

kusaal: Banɛ da pʋ di la da yɛl ye Electoral Commission (EC) da fɛndis vɔɔt lanɛ, ka da mɔr pian'ad la keŋ Ghana Supreme Court ye ba maligim gɔs vɔɔt la kaalʋg la da an si'em.
english: The opposition alleged tampering with results by the Electoral Commission (EC), and filed a petition in a 2012 Ghanaian Presidential Election Petition at the Ghanaian Supreme Court to review the election results.

kusaal: NPP da mɔr dinɛ ka ba ye "pink sheets" ka di paae ban tusa piinɛ yinne (11,000) ka di nar ye piyamnam la maki ba nɛ gbambanɛ ka EC, NDC nɛ na'adɔbanɛ kpɛlim la.
english: The NPP produced more than 11,000 so-called "pink sheets" to the judges who had to compare them to similar papers from the EC, NDC and possibly other parties.

kusaal: Ba da paasnɛ constituency nam pisnaasi nɛ anu (45) constituency nam kɔbisyi nɛ pistan (230) Ghana 2008 vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: Controversially, 45 additional constituencies were added to the 230 of the 2008 general election.

kusaal: Ba da maal vɔɔtʋg lanɛ constituency nam kɔbisyi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (275) la wʋsa nɛ vɔɔtʋg zin'is tusa pisi nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ ayi (26002).
english: Voting therefore took place in a total of 275 constituencies and 26002 polling stations.

kusaal: Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO) da pa'al nidib ye ba gɔs ye vɔɔtʋg la ken wala ka da tʋm nidib tusa anaasi 4000 Ghana wʋsa ye ba gɔs vɔɔtʋg la yɛla.
english: The Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO) trained election observers and deployed 4000 of them to monitor the elections nationwide.

kusaal: Nidib mɛ da naan ECOWAS Observer Mission dinɛ ka Nigeria zugraan kʋdʋg, General Olusegun Obasanjo da aan ba tuon gat la kena ye ba gɔs vɔɔtʋg la ken si'em.
english: Observers from ECOWAS Observer Mission led by former Nigerian president, General Olusegun Obasanjo also monitored the elections.

kusaal: Zugraan John Atta Mills da maal ka'alim la nya'aŋ, Electoral Commission of Ghana tuon gat Kwadwo Afari-Gyan da yɛl ye vɔɔtʋg suor la pʋ tiakɛ ka di anɛ na'adɔɔg yɛl ka National Democratic Congress dim mɔr suor ka ba gaŋ onɛ ka ba bɔɔd ka o aan ba zugraan na'anya'ad.
english: Following the death of incumbent President John Atta Mills amid concerns for the election, leader of the Electoral Commission of Ghana Kwadwo Afari-Gyan said that "the election calendar remains unchanged—it's purely a party matter" and the National Democratic Congress had to decide whom to nominate as its new candidate.

kusaal: Dinɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ da pian'ad anɛ ban da pʋ tis Nana Konadu Agyeman Rawlings, tuon gati tis na'adɔkanɛ ka ban am maal, National Democratic Party la.
english: The main talking point following the close of nominations was the disqualification of Nana Konadu Agyeman Rawlings, leader of the newly formed National Democratic Party.

kusaal: Onɛ da zin'i kʋk la zug, Zugraan John Dramani Mahama da di zugraan vɔɔtʋg la nɛ vɔɔt pisnu du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.7%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin, o da gaad zi'esim kanɛ ka ba mak la nɛ vɔɔt tusa bi'ela gu' ka amaligim vɔɔt lɛn kae.
english: Incumbent president John Mahama was declared winner of the presidential contest with 50.7% of the vote, just a few thousand votes over the threshold for avoiding a run-off election.

kusaal: Pink sheets bama pa'al ye ba kaalnɛ vɔɔtʋg zin'ig yinne ka naan la'asi ba ken tuon, nwɛnɛ municipality, district nɛ region nam.
english: These pink sheets state the results as counted in single polling stations, before aggregating them to any higher level, such as municipality, district and region.

kusaal: NPP da yɛl ye kal la pʋ zɛm taaba nwɛnɛ din nar si'em vɔɔtʋg zin'igin la, nɛ banɛ ka ba kaali la'as la, ka ye "pink sheets" la na nyaŋi pa'al nɛ'.
english: The NPP claimed that there were differences between the results as stated immediately after their counting in polling stations, and those which were used in aggregations, and that this can be proven by the pink sheets.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt Mahama ka o yʋ'ʋn keŋi o mɛŋ on da lieb zugraan nwadisa anu John Atta Mills, onɛ da gbirigi maal ka'alim tʋʋma ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: Mahama was elected to a full term less than five months as president having succeeded John Atta Mills, who died suddenly in office in July 2012.

kusaal: Electoral Commission of Ghana da maal biometric vɔɔtʋg yʋda sɔbʋg nwadisa atan dabpisi nɛ anaasi, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa anu la daba anu daar.
english: The Electoral Commission of Ghana successfully held a biometric system of registration for the electorate from 24 March 2012 to 5 May 2012.

kusaal: Masinbanɛ ka ba mɔri tɛɛsid nidib la da san'am la zug, banɛ nar ye ba vɔɔt la bɛdegʋ da pʋ nyaŋi vɔɔtɛ ka ba da tɔlisi keŋ Asibit daar yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayin wadis piinɛ ayi la daba anii daar.
english: Owing to the breakdown of some biometric verification machines, some voters could not vote, and voting was extended to Saturday 8 December 2012.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn maligim vɔɔt ya'as yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayin wadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ anii daar zugraan na'anya'ad sɔ' ya'a pʋ paam vɔɔt la ka di paae pisnu kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ.
english: A run-off was scheduled for 28 December 2012 if no presidential candidate received an absolute majority of 50% plus one vote.

kusaal: Ghana Armed Forces kpɛɛm anɛ Ghana gɔmena zuraan, o nɔɔr ka banɛ gɔsid titɔndis ka ba buon Border Guard Unit (BGU) dim dɔl.
english: The Commander-in-Chief of the Ghana Armed Forces is the president of Ghana, who is also the supreme military commander of the Border Guard Unit (BGU).

kusaal: Banɛ gɔsidi ba tʋʋma anɛ Minister of Defence nɛ Chief of Defence Staff.
english: The armed forces are managed by the Minister of Defence and the Chief of Defence Staff.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir,kɔbis nii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1879), Gold Coast soogianam lʋgʋr da pin'il ya, ka li da yinɛ Hausa soogianam san'an Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim, ka ba tʋʋma an ye ba gɔs ka zin'in baanlim bɛ teŋ la pʋʋgin na'asaanam la da sʋ'oe Gold Coast saŋa si'a la.
english: In 1879, the Gold Coast Constabulary was established by personnel of the Hausa Constabulary of Southern Nigeria, to perform internal security and police duties in the British colony of the Gold Coast.

kusaal: Gold Coast Constabulary da nyɛ yʋ'ʋr yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ yinne (1901) ka li da an Gold Coast soogianam lʋgʋr la, li da paam nya'ar West African Frontier Force ni la, ka Colonial Office tis British Government da gɔsidi li yɛla.
english: The Gold Coast Constabulary was renamed in 1901 as the Gold Coast Regiment, following the foundation of the West African Frontier Force, under the direction of the Colonial Office of the British Government.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr nwa da zamis soogianam ye ba tʋm tʋʋma dunia wʋsa zabkanɛ da an yiiga daan la ( First World War) zin'is-zin'is anu (five battalions) , ban wʋsa da tʋm tʋʋma East Africa campaign saŋa la.
english: The regiment raised a total of five battalions for service during the First World War, all of which served during the East Africa campaign.

kusaal: Dunia wʋsa zabkanɛ da paas ayi' la (Second World War), soogianam lʋgʋr nwa da zamis soogianam la zin'is-zin'is awai, ba da tʋm tʋʋma Kenya Northern Frontier District nɛ Italian Somaliland nɛ Abyssinia nɛ Burma ka li da paas nɛ 2nd (West Africa) Infantry Brigade.
english: During the Second World War, the regiment raised nine battalions, and saw action in Kenya's Northern Frontier District, Italian Somaliland, Abyssinia and Burma as part of the 2nd (West Africa) Infantry Brigade.

kusaal: Major General Stephen Otu ka ba da gaŋ ye o an onɛ gɔsidi ba tʋʋma yɛla yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ yinne, nwadis awai la (September 1961).
english: Major General Stephen Otu was appointed Chief of Defence Staff in September 1961.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da an yiiga zugraan (first prime minister), tɛŋ la da sʋ'ʋgi ba mɛŋ na'asaanam nu'usin yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi la (1957).
english: Kwame Nkrumah had become Ghana's first prime minister when the country became independent in 1957.

kusaal: Nkrumah na'am saŋa da wa'ae naar la, o da pin'il nɛ gba'ad gba'a sieba linɛ da daam armed forces kpɛɛmnam, yinne anɛ on da pin'il President's Own Guard Regiment (POGR) la.
english: As Nkrumah's rule wore on, he began to take actions which disquieted the leadership of the armed forces, including the creation and expansion of the President's Own Guard Regiment (POGR).

kusaal: Linɛ da kɛ ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu, nwadis ayi', dabisa pisi nɛ anaasi la (February 24, 1966), soogianam biela nɛ pʋlis, ka ba tuongat an Emmanuel Kotoka, o da anɛ tuongat tis soogianam la'asʋg kanɛ an Second Brigade bɛ Kumasi sʋ'ʋlim, Major Akwasi Afrifa, (one da an one zamisid o taaba nɛ ba tʋʋmanam yɛla), Lieutenant General (one da naae o tʋʋma bɛn) Joseph Ankrah, nɛ J.W.K. Harlley, (one da sʋ'ʋe pʋlʋs lʋgʋr la), da faae na'am ka ba da buoli li ye "Operation Cold Chop", linɛ da an yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu (1966 Ghanaian coup d'état) , ka ba da faae zugraan, Nkrumah na'am di' la .
english: As a result, on February 24, 1966, a small number of Army personnel and senior police officials, led by Colonel Emmanuel Kotoka, commander of the Second Brigade at Kumasi, Major Akwasi Afrifa, (staff officer in charge of army training and operations), Lieutenant General (retired) Joseph Ankrah, and J.W.K. Harlley, (the police inspector general), successfully launched "Operation Cold Chop", the 1966 Ghanaian coup d'état, against the Nkrumah regime.

kusaal: Bama da la'as nɛ pʋdi ba na'adɔɔg yʋ'ʋr yeNational Liberation Council, Ba da mɔr na'am Ghana sʋ'ʋlim lin pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ awai (1966 to 1969).
english: The group formed the National Liberation Council, which ruled Ghana from 1966 to 1969.

kusaal: Lieutenant Colonel Ignatius Kutu Acheampong (one da an kpɛɛm saŋa biela tis nɛ First Brigade bɛ Accra) da faae na'am ka ziim da lɛɛ pʋ kpa'ae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' (1972 Ghanaian coup d'état) linɛ da paas ayi' daan ka soogianam faae na'am Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Lieutenant Colonel Ignatius Kutu Acheampong (temporary commander of the First Brigade around Accra) led the bloodless 1972 Ghanaian coup d'état that ended the Second Republic.

kusaal: Saŋa kan ka na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon National Redemption Council da pin'il.
english: Thus the National Redemption Council was formed.

kusaal: Acheampong da anɛ gɔmena zugraan ka NRC di' na'am pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (1972 to 1975).
english: Acheampong became head of state, and the NRC ruled from 1972 to 1975.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu, nwadis piiga, dabisa awai daar (October 9, 1975), Supreme Military Council (SMC) da die NRC nɔbir.
english: On October 9, 1975, the NRC was replaced by the Supreme Military Council (SMC).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii, nwadis ayɔpɔi (July 1978) ni la,tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ, ka SMC kpɛɛmnam la la'as taaba la da mugus Acheampong ka o bas o zugraan na'am la, ka Lt.
english: In July 1978, in a sudden move, the other SMC officers forced Acheampong to resign, replacing him with Lt. Gen. Akuffo.

kusaal: Amaa, li nwadis ayuobu la (June), lin da kpɛlim bi'ela ka Ghana dim gaŋ zugraan wʋʋ ban yɛl siem la, soogia banɛ mɔr paŋ nɛ Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings, da faae na'am Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka ba buon Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai, na'am fan'ar la (1979 Ghanaian coup d'état).
english: However, in June, just before the scheduled resumption of civilian rule, a group of young armed forces officers, led by Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings, mounted the 1979 Ghanaian coup d'état.

kusaal: Ba na'adɔɔg da anɛ Armed Forces Revolutionary Council, ba da mɔr na'am ti paae Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai, nwadis awai (September 1979).
english: They put in place the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council, which governed until September 1979.

kusaal: Amaa, Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981), Rawlings da lɛn faae na'am gɔmena zugraan kanɛ ka Ghana dim gaŋ la ka ba buon lin ye Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne na'am fan'ar la (1981 Ghanaian coup d'état).
english: However, in 1981, Rawlings deposed the new civilian government again, in the 1981 Ghanaian coup d'état.

kusaal: Saŋa kan la Rawlings da pin'il na'adɔɔg kanɛ an Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC).
english: This time Rawlings established the Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC).

kusaal: Na'adɔɔg PNDC naar saŋa la, Jerry Rawlings da die na'am ka li anɛ Ghana dimi da gaŋ o; ba da gaŋ o ye o an gɔmena zugraan Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' (1993) ka o mɔr na'am ti paae yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ yinne la ni.
english: In the last years of the PNDC, Jerry Rawlings assumed civilian status; he was elected as a civilian President in 1993 and continued as president until 2001.

kusaal: Armed Forces (soogianam) la da pin'ili ba yiiga tʋʋma nɛ United Nations Operation, Congo sʋ'ʋlim, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nam saŋa la (early 1960s).
english: The Armed Forces' first external operation was the United Nations Operation in the Congo in the early 1960s.

kusaal: GAF da tʋm zin'ig kanɛ an Balkans, nɛ UNMIK.
english: The GAF operated in the Balkans, including with UNMIK.

kusaal: Gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka o da sɔb yʋ'ʋr an Shake Hands with the Devil, Canada soogianam kpɛɛm Romeo Dallaire da tis Ghana soogianam zuor bedego tʋʋm kanɛ ka ba da tʋm la yɛla.
english: In his book Shake Hands with the Devil, Canadian Forces commander Romeo Dallaire gave the Ghanaian soldiers high praise for their work during that deployment.

kusaal: Liberia zaba saŋa la (Liberian Civil War), Ghana soogianam tʋʋma da sʋŋi maal suor ka Accra Comprehensive Peace Agreement, nɛ tʋʋm sieba.
english: During the Liberian Civil War, Ghanaian activities helped pave the way for the Accra Comprehensive Peace Agreement, among others.

kusaal: Tʋʋm banɛ ka ba da tʋm Asia sieba an Iran nɛ Iraq ban da zabid la (Iran–Iraq War), Kuwait nɛ Lebanon zaba nam nɛ tʋʋm sieba bedego.
english: Additional operations in Asia have included Iran and Iraq in the Iran–Iraq War, Kuwait and Lebanon civil war among others.

kusaal: Ghana soogianam tusatan', kɔbʋs tan' nɛ pisnu nɛ awai (3,359), nɛ soogianam banɛ an pʋlʋs ban kɔbʋsyi' nɛ pisnii nɛ atan' (283) da tʋm tʋʋma linɛ da an of UNTAC la Cambodia sʋ'ʋlim.
english: A total of 3,359 Ghana Army soldiers and 283 Ghana Military Police operated as part of UNTAC in Cambodia.

kusaal: UNTAC tʋʋma da anɛ yʋma ayi' bɛn, da pin'il nɛ Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi', kɛŋ paae Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' (1992−1993).
english: The UNTAC operation lasted two years, 1992−1993.

kusaal: UNTAC tʋʋma la ni da an yiiga tʋʋma kanɛ ka Ghana soogianam da yii ba mɛŋ tɛŋin pansig zaba, ONUC Congo sʋ'ʋlim mɛn yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nam saŋa la (1960s).
english: Operation UNTAC was the largest Ghanaian external operation since Ghana's first external military operation, ONUC in the Congo in the 1960s.

kusaal: Tʋʋm kanɛ da buon UNTAC nɛ li tiraan linɛ an UNAMIC, da la'asi san'am ligidi ka li gaad na'asaatɛŋ ligidi billion yinnɛ nɛ pʋdʋgir ayuobu ($1.6 billion).
english: Operation UNTAC and its contingent UNAMIC had a combined budget of more than $1.6 billion.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayi' (2012) la ni, soogianam la da naal nɔɔr nɛ Armed Forces of the Russian Federation.
english: In 2012, closer military cooperation was agreed with the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ atan' (2013), Ghana soogianam la da naal nɔɔr nɛ China People's Liberation Army, nɛ Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran.
english: In 2013, the Armed Forces agreed closer military cooperation with the China People's Liberation Army, and with the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran.

kusaal: · Ghana ya'datiŋ soogianam nɛ ba kpɛɛmnam (northern commands) ka ba dɔtita'ar bɛ Tamale, Central Command ba dɔtita'ar bɛ Kumasi nɛ Southern Command ba dɔtita'ar bɛ Accra.
english: The Northern Command with headquarters in Tamale, Central Command with headquarters in Kumasi and the Southern Command with headquarters in Accra.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' la nwadis atan' (March 2000) ka Northern nɛ Southern Commands da pin'il ban da nɔbig la nya'aŋ.
english: In March 2000 Northern and Southern Commands were formed after the two infantry brigades were upgraded in status.

kusaal: Yiigin la, ba daa anɛ pʋdigir atn' (three brigades): 1st Infantry Brigade (ba dɔtita'ar bɛ Teshie), 2nd Infantry Brigade (ba dɔtita'ar bɛ Kumasi) nɛ Support Services Brigade (ba dɔtita'ar bɛ Burma Camp).
english: Previously there were three brigades: 1st Infantry Brigade (HQ in Teshie), 2nd Infantry Brigade (HQ in Kumasi) and Support Services Brigade (HQ in Burma Camp).

kusaal: · 6 Infantry Battalions bɛ Ghana Regiment.
english: 6 Infantry Battalions of the Ghana Regiment.

kusaal: 3rd Battalion of Infantry, 4th Battalion of Infantry and 6th Battalion of Infantry bɛ Northern Command, 1st Battalion of Infantry, 2nd Battalion of Infantry and 5th Battalion of Infantry bɛ Southern Command.
english: 3rd Battalion of Infantry, 4th Battalion of Infantry and 6th Battalion of Infantry in the Northern Command, 1st Battalion of Infantry, 2nd Battalion of Infantry and 5th Battalion of Infantry in the Southern Command.

kusaal: · 64 Infantry Regiment, a presidential guard force (ka ba da buon yiiga ye President's Own Guard Regiment)
english: 64 Infantry Regiment, a presidential guard force (formerly known as President's Own Guard Regiment)

kusaal: · Reconnaissance Armoured Regiment (armoured reconnaissance squadrons nam ayi')
english: Reconnaissance Armoured Regiment (two armoured reconnaissance squadrons)

kusaal: · Two Engineer Regiments (48 Engineer Regiment nɛ 49 Engineer Regiment)
english: Two Engineer Regiments (48 Engineer Regiment and 49 Engineer Regiment)

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobu la (1996), ka Support Services Brigade yʋ'ʋr da yi' ka ba da tɔlisi li soogianam lʋgʋrin la ye li tʋʋma an ye li gɔs Ghana soogianam dɔtitada la yɛla (Armed Forces GHQ).
english: In 1996, the Support Services Brigade was reorganized and transferred from the Army to be responsible to the Armed Forces GHQ.

kusaal: Lin da yi' saŋa kan, li pʋdig kɔn'ɔb,kɔn'ɔb ka li pʋdigir sieba nwa; 49 Engineer Regiment, nɛ Ghana Military Police, nɛ Defence Signal Regiment (Ghana), nɛ FRO, nɛ Forces Pay Office, nɛ 37 Military Hospital, nɛ Defence Mechanical Transport Battalion (Def MT Bn), nɛ Base Ordnance Depot, nɛ Base Ammunition Depot, nɛ Base Supply Depot, nɛ Base Workshop, nɛ Armed Forces Printing Press (AFPP), nɛ Armed Forces Fire Service (AFFS), nɛ Ghana Armed Forces Central Band, nɛ Ghana Armed Forces Institution (GAFI), nɛ 1 Forces Movement Unit (Tema Port), nɛ 5 Forces Movement Unit, nɛ Base Engineer Technical Services (BETS), nɛ 5 Garrison Education Centre (5 GEC), nɛ the Armed Forces Museum, nɛ Army Signals Training School, nɛ Armed Forces Secondary Technical School (AFSTS).
english: From that point its units included 49 Engineer Regiment, the Ghana Military Police, Defence Signal Regiment (Ghana), FRO, Forces Pay Office, 37 Military Hospital, Defence Mechanical Transport Battalion (Def MT Bn), Base Ordnance Depot, Base Ammunition Depot, Base Supply Depot, Base Workshop, Armed Forces Printing Press (AFPP), Armed Forces Fire Service (AFFS), the Ghana Armed Forces Central Band, Ghana Armed Forces Institution (GAFI), 1 Forces Movement Unit (Tema Port), 5 Forces Movement Unit, Base Engineer Technical Services (BETS), 5 Garrison Education Centre (5 GEC), the Armed Forces Museum, Army Signals Training School, and the Armed Forces Secondary Technical School (AFSTS).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu (2016) ka ba dɔkanɛ buon ye Forces Pay Office nɔbig ka ba yʋ'ʋn buon ye Forces Pay Regiment.
english: By 2016 the Forces Pay Office had been upgraded to the Forces Pay Regiment.

kusaal: M16 rifles, nɛ AK-47s, nɛ Type 56 assault rifles, nɛ ballistic vests nɛ personal armor bɛnɛ zin'ig wʋsa, ka la'ad bedego banɛ ka soogianam la nɛ Air Force dim mɔri tʋm la maal nɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, ka banɛ maal nwa' la an Defence Industries Holding Company (DIHOC).
english: M16 rifles, AK-47s, Type 56 assault rifles, ballistic vests and personal armor are standard issue, while much of the secondary equipment used by the Army and Air Force are manufactured internally by the Defence Industries Holding Company (DIHOC).

kusaal: Amaa United Nations nɔk Ghana soogianam ka ba kɛŋ pans zaba tɛn's bedego, ka ba sieba an Afghanistan, nɛ Iraq, nɛ Kosovo, nɛ Georgia, nɛ Nepal, nɛ Cambodia nɛ Lebanon.
english: Ghana prefers to send its troops to operations in Africa. However the United Nations has used Ghanaian forces in countries as diverse as Afghanistan, Iraq, Kosovo, Georgia, Nepal, Cambodia and Lebanon.

kusaal: Ghana armed forces dim yinne da an Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) kpɛɛm kanɛ da an yiiga sɔb, ka o yʋ'ʋr an Lieutenant General Arnold Quainoo.
english: Ghana armed forces provided the first Force Commander of the Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG), Lieutenant General Arnold Quainoo.

kusaal: Nidib la'as taaba nɛ tʋmtʋmnib la'as sieba nam , ka ba sieba an National Democratic Congress (NDC) nɛ Ghana Union Movement (GUM), la'as taaba yɛla Akufo-Addo nɛ o tuongatib ye ba da kɛ ka Ghana Armed Forces kɛŋ ye ba zabi faae Niger, Mohamed Bazoum, ba gɔmena zugraan kanɛ ka nidib la gaŋ o ka General Abdourahamane Tchiani faae na'am nɛ paŋ ka bas o la.
english: A group of opposition political parties and civil society organizations, comprising the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and Ghana Union Movement (GUM), has jointly urged the Akufo-Addo administration to refrain from deploying the Ghana Armed Forces to restore the democratically elected president of Niger, Mohamed Bazoum, who was ousted from power by General Abdourahamane Tchiani.

kusaal: Kennedy Ohene Agyapong, one an kpɛɛm tis nɛ Interior and Defense Committee in Parliament, ye on siak ye soogianam la kɛm Niger zab.
english: However, Hon. Kennedy Ohene Agyapong, the Chairperson of the Interior and Defense Committee in Parliament, has expressed his endorsement of the nation's deployment of troops to Niger.

kusaal: Ghana soogia banɛ gɔsid pɛbisimin suoya yɛla (Ghana Air Force) tʋʋma dɔtita'ar bɛnɛ Burma Camp bɛ Accra la, ka li tʋm zin'is kɔn'ɔb,kɔn'ɔb ka yiiga anɛ li zin'igin Accra, Tamale (anina anɛ zamisʋg zin'ig) nɛ Sekondi-Takoradi (zamisʋg zin'ig).
english: The Ghana Air Force is headquartered in Burma Camp in Accra, and operates from bases in Accra (main transport base), Tamale (combat and training base)and Sekondi-Takoradi (training base).

kusaal: GHF wada pʋʋgin (military doctrine) nɛ ban gba'ae gban'a sieba anɛ ye ba tʋʋma Ghana sʋ'ʋlim bɛɛ Ghana yiŋ, ye li sʋŋ Ghana Army nɛ tʋʋma la'ad.
english: The GHF military doctrine and stated mission is to perform counterinsurgency operations within Ghana or externally and to provide logistical support to the Ghana Army.

kusaal: Ghana Navy tʋʋma anɛ ye li gur Ghana nɛ li kuom sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa, gur kuomin zimi nam, ka gɔs da' diib nɔbigir yɛla (exclusive economic zone), ka gur Ghana sʋ'ʋlim kuokanɛ buon Lake Volta la.
english: The Ghana Navy's mission is to provide defence of Ghana and its territorial waters, fishery protection, exclusive economic zone, and internal security on Lake Volta.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1994) Navy dim da paas Eastern command, ka ba tʋʋma dɔtita'ar bɛ Tema, ka lɛn paas Western command, ka ba tʋʋma dɔtita'ar bɛ Sekondi-Takoradi.
english: In 1994 the Navy was re-organized into an Eastern command, with headquarters at Tema, and a Western command, with headquarters at Sekondi-Takoradi.

kusaal: Ghana Armed Forces sʋ'ʋe arms industry weapons nɛ military technology and equipment manufacturer (DIHOC − Defence Industries Holding Company) ma'a nɛ, li mɔri li mɛŋ banki (private bank).
english: The Ghana Armed Forces, in addition to owning its own arms industry weapons and military technology and equipment manufacturer (DIHOC − Defence Industries Holding Company), operates its own private bank.

kusaal: 37 Military Hospital nyɛ nɔbigir ka li nan bʋ yʋʋgɛ bozugo ba yʋ'ʋn mɔr zin'ig anina ka li tʋm bɛogin sɔbʋd yʋ'ʋŋi lɛn nied bɛog ka vʋʋsʋm kae, ka li bɛnɛ tis banɛ bɔɔd tiebig tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ yɛla ka ba bʋon Emergency Department (ED).
english: The 37 Military Hospital has recently undergone expansion and its facilities include a twenty-four-hour Emergency Department (ED).

kusaal: Vyacheslav Lebedev, one an Supreme Court of Russia kpɛɛm, daa wɔ'ɔgi ba ban ti'ebid ban'adnam banɛ bɔɔd ti'ebig tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ wʋʋ banɛ paam sapʋ'ad nam la yɛla.
english: Vyacheslav Lebedev, Chairman of the Supreme Court of Russia, expressed gratitude following his emergency treatment at the hospital.

kusaal: Ghana Army sʋ'ʋe zamisig lʋgʋr (Cadet Corps) ka ba an GAF Cadets banɛ kɛn Military Education and Training nɛ Recruit Training zamisig, ka banɛ naae GAF Military Academy kɛŋ Army Recruit nɛ Seaman Recruit ka ba nyaan nyɛ suori tʋm nɛ soogianam, bɛɛ soogia banɛ gɔsid kuomin (Navy) bɛɛ banɛ gɔsid pɛbisim suoya ka dɔribid alɔpir nam la ni (Air Force).
english: The Ghana Army operates a Cadet Corps for GAF Cadets whom go on to Military Education and Training and Recruit Training graduation from the GAF Military Academy for Army Recruit and Seaman Recruit prior to enlistment into the Army, Navy or Air Force.

kusaal: Zin'is banɛ ka ba zamisidi ba, ka li sieba an Ghana Military Academy nɛ Ghana Army-sponsored Cadet Corps.
english: Training institutions include the Ghana Military Academy and the Ghana Army-sponsored Cadet Corps.

kusaal: Mɛ bɛ Accra la nyɛ sʋŋiri yi Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre, linɛ bʋ paas soogianam la tʋʋma nii amaa li zamisid zab'pansidib , nɛ GAF soogianam mɛn.
english: Also located in Accra is the internationally funded Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre, which is not part of the Armed Forces but provides a wide-ranging of peace operations training, including to GAF personnel.

kusaal: Ghana Armed Forces Command nɛ Staff College (GAFCSC) pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ atan' (1963).
english: The Ghana Armed Forces Command and Staff College (GAFCSC) dates back to 1963.

kusaal: Li zamisid soogianam, nɛ ban na gu' ba tɛŋ dim, ka li wʋsa bɛ Pass Staff College (PSC) kasɛta gbaʋŋ la ni.
english: It focuses on military and defense courses, culminating in the issuance of the Pass Staff College (PSC) certificate.

kusaal: Single Spine Salary Structure (SSSS) ka Ghana Arm Forces dim diesidi ba yɔɔd.
english: The Single Spine Salary Structure (SSSS) is the payment made to the Ghana Arm Forces.

kusaal: Line lɛn paas anɛ, Ghana wada pʋ bas suor ye sɔ' nyaŋi ki'a Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) bɛɛ Ghana Military Police (GMP) bɛɛ GAF soogianam la bɛɛ ba lornam la (vehicles) ba tʋʋma nii, li kas-kas anɛ ba ya'a bɛ tʋʋma ni Kotoka International Airport , nɛ Ghana gɔmena na'am kuk zin'ik Jubilee House.
english: In addition, Ghanaian law prohibits the photographing of Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) Ghana Military Police (GMP) police or GAF military personnel and vehicles while on duty, strategic sites such as Accra International Airport when in use, and the seat of the Ghanaian government, Jubilee House.

kusaal: Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) la'asnɛ an armed force of Ghana, li pʋdʋgir anɛ Army (GA), Navy (GN), nɛ Ghana Air Force.
english: The Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) is the state military organisation of Ghana, consisting of the Army (GA), Navy (GN), and Ghana Air Force.

kusaal: Gold Coast soogianam banɛ da naan ya-nya'aŋi lɛbna la da mɔr pʋtɛnda kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb ka nyaan yi.
english: Gold Coast soldiers returning from the Far East carried different perspectives from when they had departed.

kusaal: Ghana Armed Forces da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi la (1957).
english: The Ghana Armed Forces were formed in 1957.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu la (1966), Armed Forces da pin'ili paasidi li mɛŋ tɛŋ na'am pʋʋgin, ba da faae zugraan nam bɛdegʋ na'am di' ka basiba.
english: From 1966, the Armed Forces were extensively involved in politics, mounting several coups.

kusaal: Armed Forces seized da faae na'am ya'as yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi', pin'ilig nwadig la (January 1972), ban da bas suor ka Ghana dim voti gaŋi ba zugraan la, ba da sie soogianam la sumalisim, ka pin'ili tia'asid kpɛɛmnam banɛ bɛ soogianamin la.
english: The Armed Forces seized power again in January 1972, after the reinstated civilian government cut military privileges and started changing the leadership of the army's combat units.

kusaal: Banɛ da paas la'as kaŋa ni anɛ Colonel Acheampong, (kpɛɛm kanɛ ka ba da paas o kpɛŋ ka o yi Colonel tɔlis General), Lt.
english: Council members were Colonel Acheampong, (chairman, who was also promoted straight from Colonel to General), Lt. Gen. Fred Akuffo, (the Chief of Defence Staff), and the army, navy, air force and Border Guard Unit commanders.

kusaal: Akuffo, one da an na'adɔɔg SMC kpɛɛm la, da tis nɔɔr paalʋ ni ye o na bas suori tis gɔmena kanɛ ka Ghana dim wʋsa na gaŋ ye o gaadi ba tuon Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai, nwadis ayɔpɔi, dabisir yinne daar (July 1, 1979).
english: Akuffo, the new SMC chairman, promised publicly to hand over political power to a new government to be elected by July 1, 1979.

kusaal: PNDC da mɔr na'am ti paae Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ atan', pin'ilig nwadig, dabisa ayɔpɔi daar (January 7, 1993).
english: The PNDC remained in government until January 7, 1993.

kusaal: Ban da tʋm tʋʋm sieba ninsabilis sʋ'ʋlim sieba anɛ UNAMIR linɛ da paasi li mɛŋ Rwandan genocide la.
english: Ghanaian operations within Africa included the UNAMIR deployment which became entangled in the Rwandan genocide.

kusaal: Cambodia zaba la na'asaanami da sʋŋidi li ka li nɔbigid, lin nya'aŋ ka na'adɔɔd anaasi banɛ da zabid la da siak azi'in-ban'alim yɛla.
english: After the long running Cambodia civil war ignited by external interventions, a resolution was accepted by the four warring factional parties.

kusaal: Ghana soogia banɛ an poa'ab da la'as nɛ tɛn's la'asʋg soogianam linɛ buon United Nations Interim Force ka da kɛŋ zaba pansigir Lebanon ( UNIFIL) tɛŋin.
english: Ghana prefers to send its troops to operations in Africa. However the United Nations has used Ghanaian forces in countries as diverse as Afghanistan, Iraq, Kosovo, Georgia, Nepal, Cambodia and Lebanon.

kusaal: · Defence Signal Regiment (Ghana)

english: Ghana Senior High School (Ghanasco) is a co-educational second cycle institution located in Tamale, Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Sakur la da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu (1960) la ni, yitnɛ Ghana gɔmma kʋdʋg Kwame Nkrumah, ka di an Ghana Education Trust Schools.
english: The school was established in 1960 by the Government of Ghana, under Kwame Nkrumah, as one of the Ghana Education Trust Schools.

kusaal: Di mɔrɛ sakur biis kanl wʋʋ 2,800.
english: It has a student population of about more than 2,800.

kusaal: Dinɛ pɛ'ɛs sakur bɛda ayi pʋʋgʋn bɛ Northern region ka ti'el Tamale Senior High School (Tamasco).
english: It is the second largest school in the northern region after Tamale Senior High School (Tamasco).

kusaal: Yiiga sakur kpɛɛm da anɛ Kenneth Luther Purser, onɛ da an Jamaican nid.
english: The first headmaster of the school was Kenneth Luther Purser, a Jamaican.

kusaal: Master Abu Kassim Tahidu onɛ yit Kwame Danso dinɛ bɛ Brong Ahafo region Ghana la da an yiiga sakur biis kpɛɛm.
english: Master Abu Kassim Tahidu from Kwame Danso in the Brong Ahafo region of Ghana was the first Senior Prefect.

kusaal: Di kpɛmnan mɛnsir, diib dɔkʋdir, diib dɔpaalig/diema dɔɔg, maalʋg/ du'adib nɛ paanib La'asʋg dɔɔg, science dɔɔg, science labɔritiris anɛ yin ekɔnɔmis labɔritiri, mosque, Nkrumah yir, Gbewaa yir, Cabral/Gbanzaba yir, Dakpema nɛ purser yir wʋsa anɛ dab dɔɔd.
english: The administration block, the old dining hall, the new larger dining hall/ jams hall, the arts/ PTA block, the science block, the science laboratories including home economics laboratory, the mosque, Nkrumah house, Gbewaa house, Cabral/Gbanzaba house, Dakpema and purser house and also B.A fuseini house which was commissioned in 2024 are boys dormitories.

kusaal: Pʋ'ab dɔɔd la mɛn anɛ; indice 1, indice 2 yir, annex 1, annex 2 yir nɛ Lordina yir, pa'an kpɛɛm gbɛɛsir nɛ pa'anib gbɛɛsir.
english: The girls dormitories include; indice 1, indice 2 house, annex 1, annex 2 house and Lordina house, the headmaster's bungalow and the teachers' bungalows.

kusaal: Ghanasco bɛʋg la anɛ tɛŋ dim la mɔri tʋm ka sieba anɛ Kukuo dim nɛ Ghana Senior High School sakur biis.
english: The Ghanasco dam is used by surrounding communities including Kukuo and students of Ghana Senior High School.

kusaal: Ghanasco yʋ'ʋmɛŋir da anɛ Ghana koligi.
english: Ghanasco was originally called Ghana College.

kusaal: Ghana Super Cup anɛ football nya'ab kanɛ bɛ tis champion banɛ di Ghana Premier League nɛ banɛ di Ghanaian FA Cup la Ghana.
english: The Ghana Super Cup is a football competition involving a match played between the champion of the Ghana Premier League and the winner of the Ghanaian FA Cup in Ghana.

kusaal: Yiiga Ghana Super Cup competition da bɛnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1996) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1997) siizin la ni, din nya'aŋ yʋma piinɛ atan (thirteen-year hiatus) ba pʋ nwɛ', din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) siizin la ni.
english: The first Ghana Super Cup competition took place in the 1996–1997 season, after which there was a thirteen-year hiatus between the 1998 and 2010 seasons.

kusaal: Accra Hearts of Oak nɛ Kumasi Asante Kotoko an kilabnama ayi banɛ nwɛ' kap la din pin'ili paae zina.
english: Kumasi Asante Kotoko is the most successful club in the competition's history.

kusaal: Banɛ mɔr kap la nananna anɛ Accra Hearts of Oak, banɛ an champions 2020-21 Ghana Premier League la nɛ 2021 Ghanaian FA Cup la.
english: The Ghana Super Cup is a football competition involving a match played between the champion of the Ghana Premier League and the winner of the Ghanaian FA Cup in Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana Union Movement la anɛ pɔlitis na'adɔɔg linɛ bɛ Ghana.
english: The Ghana Union Movement is a political party in Ghana.

kusaal: Li anɛ Christian Kwabena Andrews onɛ yɔ'ɔg ka su'oe Life Assembly Worship Center linɛ bɛ Ankara la da yɔ'ɔgi li.
english: It was founded by Christian Kwabena Andrews who is also the founder of the Life Assembly Worship Center in Accra.

kusaal: Daakanɛ ka ba da zʋŋid na'adɔɔg la, o da pian'a zi'el ye on anɛ "Kwame Nkrumah paal" ka lɛn ye "Nkrumah siig la lɛn lɛbna ya'as."Na'adɔɔg la gban'asa nɛ ba yɛlkpana linɛ ka ba da mɔri yina la, Samia Nkrumah, onɛ an Kwame Nkrumah bipʋŋ la da pian'a kpɛmis ye ba gban'asa an sʋm pamm.
english: During the launch of the party, he declared that he is "new Kwame Nkrumah" and also that the "spirit of Nkrumah is back." The party's agenda received some backing from Samia Nkrumah, daughter of Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Andrews mɛ anɛ na'anya'and yinne onɛ da zi'enɛ nya'a ti Ghana vɔt linɛ da maal yʋʋma 2020 la ni.
english: Andrews is one of the presidential candidates for the 2020 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Andrew da gaŋnɛ Abu Grant Lukeman ye o aan o nya'andɔl.
english: Andrew nominated Abu Grant Lukeman as his running mate for the election.

kusaal: O da sɔbi o gbaʋŋ la nɛ tisnɛ Sawa'ar nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi la yʋʋma 2020 la ni.
english: He filed his nomination papers on 7 October 2020.

kusaal: Dinɛ da yi 1957 nii, ba da anɛ Gold Coast.
english: Prior to 1957, it played as the Gold Coast.

kusaal: Ba mɛn di nya'an ye ba kɛŋ CHAN nɔɔr anaasi, ka naae runners-up nɔɔr ayi' mɛn (2009 nɛ 2014).
english: Ghana have qualified for the CHAN four times, finishing as runners-up twice (2009 and 2014).

kusaal: 19 August 1962 Accra Sports Stadium la nii, ba da di'e saam Real Madrid, bani yʋ'ʋr da buon Spanish champions sankan, European champions kʋdʋg nɛ intercontinental champions ka nwɛ' alira 3–3.
english: On 19 August 1962 at the Accra Sports Stadium, Ghana hosted Real Madrid, who were at the time Spanish champions, drawing 3–3.

kusaal: Charles Kumi Gyamfi da an kɔch 1961 yʋʋm la ni, ka nɔki ba di'e African Cup of Nations, bɛ 1963 nɛ 1965 ni.
english: Charles Kumi Gyamfi became coach in 1961, leading Ghana to successive African Cup of Nations titles, in 1963 and 1965.

kusaal: Ba da paae naae nwɛ'ɛb la bɛ 1968 nɛ 1970 ni, ka li nɛ 1–0 bɛ nwɛ'ɛb ayi' la ni, yit DR Congo bɛ 1968 nɛ Sudan 1970 yʋʋm la ni.
english: It reached the final of the tournament in 1968 and 1970, losing 1–0 on both occasions, to DR Congo and Sudan respectively.

kusaal: Bani mɔr bɛog la ka ba paam ye Black Stars la, bani da pʋ nyaŋi paas nɔɔr atan' bɛ African Cup of Nations dinɛ bɛ 1970s ni la.
english: Fortunes changed for the Black Stars after it failed to qualify for three successive AFCON's in the 1970s.

kusaal: 1980s pin'ilʋg nii, nɛ nwɛ'ɛdib titara wʋʋ Abedi Pele, Black Stars di nya'an ka bas Libya bɛ 1982 African Cup of Nations naar nwɛ'ɛb dinɛ ka Libya da di'es saam la wʋsa la, Ghana da di ba nɔɔr anaasi nɛ ka lɛm an ba naar ti paae zina win.
english: In the 1980s, with emerging talents such as Abedi Pele, the Black Stars defeated 1982 AFCON hosts Libya in the final to win its fourth continental title.

kusaal: 1992 nii, Black Stars da kɛŋ runners-up nɛ Ivory Coast bɛ penalty shootout dinɛ ka ba da nwɛ' alira, dinɛ ka nwɛ'ɛd wʋsa bani da bɛ pakin la da nwɛ' penati, dinɛ ka ba da dii ba nɛ 11-10.
english: In 1992, the Black Stars would finish runners-up to the Ivory Coast in a penalty shootout after a goalless draw, which saw every player on the pitch take a penalty, in which they were beaten 11-10, with African Footballer of the Year Abedi Pele suspended for the final.

kusaal: 1990s nii, nɛ' tɔn'ɔn da pɛ'ɛs ka team la pʋ nyaŋi ziel teambani nan du'od la naa.
english: In the 1990s, this may have played some part in the failure of the team to build on the successes of the national underage teams.

kusaal: Ala zugɔ, Black Stars nwɛ'ɛdib bani da kɛŋ 2001 FIFA World Youth Championship naae la da li'eb "core" tis team la bɛ 2002 African Cup of Nations, ken ka sɔ' pʋ nyaŋidi ba 2005 yʋʋm la ni ka paasid naar nwɛ'ɛb dinɛ bɛ 2006 FIFA World Cup la ni.
english: The generation of Black Stars players who went to the 2001 FIFA World Youth Championship final became the "core" of the team at the 2002 African Cup of Nations, going undefeated for a year in 2005 and qualifying for the final tournament of the 2006 FIFA World Cup.

kusaal: Black Stars la da si'igi nyaŋid nɛ 2–0 liib nɛ champions Italy, ka di Czech Republic (2–0) nɛ United States (2–1).
english: The Black Stars started by succumbing to a 2–0 defeat to eventual champions Italy, and wins over Czech Republic (2–0) and the United States (2–1).

kusaal: Kɔch kpɛɛm Milovan Rajevac, Black Stars la da kɛŋi di'e 100% nya'an bɛ qualification campaign, ka di yi ba gurub la ni ka an yiiga African team na paasi bɛ 2010 FIFA World Cup la ni.
english: Under head coach Milovan Rajevac, the Black Stars went on to secure a 100% win record in its qualification campaign, winning its group and becoming the first African team to qualify for the 2010 FIFA World Cup.

kusaal: Ba pʋr team la yʋ'ʋr ye Black Stars kadi yinɛ nwadibil sabil kani bɛ Afrika ka bɛ Ghana flak la ni.
english: It is nicknamed the Black Stars after the Black Star of Africa in the flag of Ghana.

kusaal: Di anɛ Ghana Football Association la gʋri di, dinɛ bɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb lʋgʋr Ghana nwa ni.
english: The team is governed by the Ghana Football Association.

kusaal: Ghana da nyaŋi di ya'an ye ba kɛŋ FIFA World Cup ba yiiga daan bɛ 2006 yʋʋm la ni.
english: Ghana qualified for the FIFA World Cup for the first time in 2006.

kusaal: Black Stars paami ba nya'an diib la nɛ 13–2 yit Kenya nɛ' nya'aŋ ni.
english: The Black Stars achieved their record win, 13–2 away to Kenya, in the latter.

kusaal: Bani da mɔr paŋ la zug ka ba pʋdi ba ye "the Black Stars of Africa" dinɛ bɛ 1960s yʋʋm la ni.
english: Its domination of the tournament earned it the nickname "the Black Stars of Africa" in the 1960s.

kusaal: Black Stars da bɛnɛ gʋ'ʋgir ni, dinɛ ka African Footballer bɛ yʋʋm kanna, Abedi Pele ka ba da ye o kʋ nwɛ' bɛ naae nwɛ'ɛb la ni.
english: In 1992, the Black Stars would finish runners-up to the Ivory Coast in a penalty shootout after a goalless draw, which saw every player on the pitch take a penalty, in which they were beaten 11-10, with African Footballer of the Year Abedi Pele suspended for the final.

kusaal: 2000 saŋa laa, dabiemi da kpɛn' nwɛ'ɛdib la zug ka kɛ' ya ka mpnam nɛ zugdaan la da kpɛ'ɛs nu'ugi yɔ'ɔg suor ka Abedi Pele nɛ Tony Yeboah yʋ'ʋn nwɛ'.
english: Tensions among the squad led to the parliamentary and executive to intervene and settle issues between players Abedi Pele and Tony Yeboah.

kusaal: Ghana wada gbaʋŋ anɛ gbaʋŋkanɛ pa'an Ghana da paami o mɛŋi yi na'asaanam nu'usin ka yʋ'ʋn zanli ba dɔlisid wada sieba.
english: The Constitution of Ghana is the supreme law of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Di sɔbnɛ ye li sʋŋi ti ka ti nyaŋi paam karim ka baŋ linɛ bɛ ti Ghana a-sʋ'ʋmmɛŋ teŋgbauŋ zi'ela la ni.
english: The Constitution of Ghana is the supreme law of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Zi'elsieba bɛ teŋgbauŋ zi'ela la ni ka li ya'a ka Ghana nidib wʋsa siakɛ, sɔ' kae na tun'e tiak bɛɛ dɛmisi lii bɔzugɔ, ba anɛ yɛlkpana zaŋi ken saalib vʋ'ʋm pʋʋgin.
english: In part, the constitution was designed to decentralize the government in Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana nid onɛ maal gbanaa an tensi'a nid kʋ tun'e zi'en Ghana Gɔmma nɔba zug tensi'a ni bɛɛ an Gɔmma kpanaraan bɛɛ an pʋlis wʋsa kpɛɛm bɛɛ tʋʋmbanɛ wʋsa an tʋʋmtitada Ghana nwaa.
english: Since its independence in 1957, Ghana has undergone several major changes in both the type of government and the democratic government itself.
