kusaal: Ghana n an a-sʋ'ʋmmɛŋ teŋ la, ti na mɔr yɔlisim ti pian'adin nɛ Gɔmma gaŋirin nɛ ti gɔɔdimin nɛ yɛla bɛdegʋ ni.
english: Before the inauguration of the first government of the Third Republic Constitution, Ghana established a "National Government" that would rule as a transitory government for "at least" four years.

kusaal: Onɛ na tun'e an Ghana zugdaan na anɛ on an teŋ la nid ka lɛm paae yʋʋʋm pisnaasi ka mɔr suor ka o bɛ teŋgbauŋ zi'ela zɔŋin la.
english: The 1992 constitution drew primarily from the lessons from the previous 1957, 1960, 1969 and the 1979 constitutions and the British and United States constitution models, the preamble states clearly what the 1992 Ghanaian Constitution will employ when incorporated as the supreme law of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Gifty Twum-Ampofo nɛ Burnya nya'aŋ nwaris ayuobʋ la li dabisim pii nɛ yinne, yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni n bɛ Kukurantumi linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm.
english: Gifty Twum-Ampofo was born on 11 June 1967 in Kukurantumi, in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ani ya'as ka o tɔlisi zamisi naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an MBA in Strategic Management la yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ nii la ni (2018).
english: She further had her MBA in Strategic Management in 2018.

kusaal: O da lɛn tɔlis University of Ghana n maal BSc ya'as.
english: She also had her BSc from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Ampofo da anɛ Science tutor tυmtυm n bɛ Akosombo International Sakurin la ka naan kena an wadmaan la Onɛ mɛ da lɛn an zugdaan n tis Science Department ka lɛn an zugdaan gɔsid karim gaad taaba yɛla n bɛ Volta River Authority tυυma la ni.
english: She was also the Head of Science Department and Head of Examinations at the Volta River Authority.

kusaal: Nannana onɛ an Minista kanɛ gɔsid gbaυŋ zamisυg lυgυr n kati wa'ae Technical and Vocational Education Training la yɛla la kpɛɛm nya'andɔl.
english: She is currently the Deputy Minister for Education in charge of Technical and Vocational Education Training.

kusaal: Burnya nya'aŋ nwaris atan' la yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ ka o da yina nyi'a nɛ o tiraan Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la ni n dii ani ka yυ'υn ti'eb ye o nyi'a Abuakwa North linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region wadmaanib kυk la Joseph|Abuakwa North linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region wadmaanib kυk la Joseph]] Boakye Danquah-Adu n da kpila la nya'aŋ.
english: In March 2016, she contested and won the NPP parliamentary primaries for the Abuakwa North Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana after the death of Joseph Boakye Danquah-Adu.

kusaal: Joseph Boakye Danquah-Adu n da kpi ka ba ye ba vɔɔti gaŋ sɔ' ka o di'e kυk ka ba vɔɔt ka Ampofo di Abuakwa North kυk la, o da mɔri vɔɔt kal 10,033 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 89.60% ka ala mɛn ka Ghana Freedom Party nid Samuel Frimpong mɛ da mɔr vɔɔt kal 263 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 2.35% ka United People's Party nid Isaac Kwarteng mɛn da mɔri vɔɔt kal 901 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 8.05.
english: She later won the Abuakwa North Constituency by-elections with 10,033 votes, making up 89.60% of the total votes cast, while the Ghana Freedom Party parliamentary candidate Samuel Frimpong had 263 votes making 2.35% of the total votes cast, and the United People's Party parliamentary candidate Isaac Kwarteng had 901 votes making 8.05% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O da paam nɛ vɔɔt kal 17,838 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 59.23% ka ala mɛn ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid Emmanuel Smith mɛ da mɔri vɔɔt kal 11,754 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 39.03% ka onɛ mɛ da zi'en o nyari ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Adjei Danquah Patrick la da mɔri vɔɔt kal 524 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 1.74%.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general election, she won the Abuakwa North Constituency parliamentary seat with 17,838 votes making 59.23% of the total votes cast, while the NDC parliamentary candidate Victor Emmanuel Smith had 11,754 votes making 39.03% of the total votes cast and an Independent candidate Adjei Danquah Patrick had 524 votes making 1.74% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi la vɔɔt la ni ya'as, ka o da lɛn di Abuakwa North wadmaanib kυk la nɛ vɔɔt bam 17,653 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 53.2% ka ala ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid Charles Yeboah Darko mɛn da paam 15,551 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 46.8% vɔɔt.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general election, she again won the Abuakwa North Constituency parliamentary seat with 17,653 votes making 53.2% of the total votes cast, while the NDC parliamentary candidate Charles Yeboah Darko had 15,551 votes making 46.8% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni ka o da keŋ University of Cape Coast n naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an BSc.
english: in Biology from the University of Cape Coast in 1997.

kusaal: Vɔɔt kanɛ da maal Yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la, ka o di Abuakwa North wadmaanib kυk la.
english: In March 2016, she contested and won the NPP parliamentary primaries for the Abuakwa North Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana after the death of Joseph Boakye Danquah-Adu.

kusaal: O paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Public Accounts yɛla la ni ka mɛ lɛn paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Foreign Affairs yɛla la ni.
english: She is a member of the Public Accounts Committee and also a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee.

kusaal: O anɛ pu'akɔɔnr mɔr biis atan'.
english: She is married with three children.

kusaal: Burnya nwarig la yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ ayi' la ni ka o da tis nidib diib wυυ bam tusa tan' nɛ kɔbisnu (35,000) n bɛ ba sυ'υlυm la ni.
english: In December 2022, she presented foodstuff to over 35,000 people in her constituency.

kusaal: Gizella Akushika Tetteh-Agbotui anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn an onɛ bɔɔnd ya nwaasim ka ba mɛɛd ya.
english: Gizella Akushika Tetteh-Agbotui is a Ghanaian architect and politician.

kusaal: O yinɛ Awutu Obrachire n bɛ Central Region, Ghana.
english: Agbotui was born on 30 November 1970 and hails from Awutu Obrachire in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o Bachelor's degree in Design nɛ Architecture, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1997).
english: She had her bachelor's degree in Design in Architecture in 1997.

kusaal: O tɔlisi maali o Masters degree in Business Administration nɛ Marketing yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la (2007) ni.
english: She further had her master's degree in Business Administration in Marketing in 2007.

kusaal: O lɛm mɔr PMP, Project Management kasɛtta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) la ni.
english: She also had a certified PMP in Project Management in 2008.

kusaal: O da lɛm paam International Airport Professional kasɛtta gbaʋŋ kanɛ tʋm Airport Management tʋʋma yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017).
english: She also had her International Airport Professional in Airport Management in 2017.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayin nɛ pisi, Nwadis piinɛ ayi (December 2020) la nii, ba da vɔɔti ti o ye o lieb Wadmaani tis Awutu Senya West Constituency dim.
english: In December 2020, she was elected member of Parliament for Awutu Senya West Constituency after she competed in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election under the ticket of the National Democratic Congress and won.

kusaal: Vɔɔt la nta'aŋ o da paam vɔɔtnam tusa pistan nɛ ayi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ anii, 32,708 dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'al pisnu nɛ anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.58%).
english: She pulled 32,708 votes which represents 51.58% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ka bas George Andah onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg New Patriotic Party nid, Edith Mansah Dzonyrah onɛ an Ghana Union Movement nid nɛ Samuel Yawson onɛ an Anɔraʋg Na'adɔɔg Conventions People's Party.
english: She was elected over George Andah of the New Patriotic Party, Edith Mansah Dzonyrah of the Ghana Union Movement and Samuel Yawson of the Conventions People's Party.

kusaal: Bama da paamnɛ vɔɔtnam tusa pisi nɛ awai, kɔbisnii nɛ pistan nɛ ayi 29,832, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii, 678 nɛ kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ atan, 193 yi banɛ da vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: These obtained 29,832, 678 and 193 votes respectively out of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Gizella Tetteh Agbotui sʋ'oe /an Principal Consultant tis Zella Architects, banɛ gɔsid ya mɛɛnb, Ghana kpɛla.
english: Tetteh-Agbotui is the CEO/ Principal Consultant of Zella Architects, an architectural firm in Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ astute Consulting Architect ka mɔr mɔ nwɛnɛ yʋma pisi nɛ yinne baŋir, 21 years, ya mɛɛb lʋgʋr la ni; ka lɛn an International Airport Professional (IAP) nɛ onɛ mɔr Project Management Professional (PMP) kasɛtta gbaʋŋ.
english: She is an astute Consulting Architect with over 21 years' experience in the Construction sector; an International Airport Professional (IAP) and a certified Project Management Professional (PMP).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne la, 2021, o da yɔya ka ba maal daba atan la'asʋgʋ tis dɔribanam nɛ punpun ba'adib kɔbis yi, 200 banɛ pʋ mɔr kasɛtta gbanaa zamis ka paam kasɛtta gbana, ka ba da pʋdi di ye GTA Licensing Project.
english: In 2021, she sponsored a 3-day program where more than 200 unlicensed drivers and motorists were trained, regularized and issued with licenses in her project dubbed GTA Licensing Project.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, 2021, ba da tis o piini nɛ sʋŋir on zabid pʋ'ab yɛla Gaana la, ban da maan Under 30 Women Awards la.
english: In 2021, she was honored with a citation for her contribution to women empowerment in Ghana during the Under 30 Women Awards.

kusaal: O da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Ghana gil vɔɔtʋg la Awutu Senya West sʋ'ʋlim ka di.
english: She contested in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election and won the parliamentary seat for the Awutu Senya West Constituency.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Agbotui nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi la nwadis piinɛ yinne la danpistan daar (30 November 1970).
english: Agbotui was born on 30 November 1970 and hails from Awutu Obrachire in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Agbotui anɛ ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress la nid.
english: Agbotui is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Di da anɛ UNESCO da pɛ'ɛs Giong Festival tis Intangible Cultural Heritage pʋʋgʋn.
english: The festival was listed on the UNESCO List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 2020), club la da ti'ak sʋ'ʋd ka Ninkanɛ bɛ Hong Kong ka ba buon Mazinyi da di'e li ka ti'aki li yʋ'ʋr la lɛb Global F.C. Amaa, nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛdib yɔɔd yela da nan mɔr daʋŋ Global ni ka Mazinyi da bad o mɛŋ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, Mɔtul nwadig la ni (August 2020), ka ye on pʋ di'e club la yi Jarvis nu'usinɛ.
english: In January 2020, the club reportedly underwent an ownership change with Hong Kong–based Mazinyi taking over and the club reverted its name back to Global F.C. However, player wage issues continued to hound Global with Mazinyi distancing itself from the club in August 2020, alleging it had never taken over the club from Jarvis.

kusaal: Global FC da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi ni, Dɔnwalig nwadig (March 2000) dɔlis nɛ Nimbanɛ da nɔŋ football yela ka yit Tacloban da la'asid taaba bakwai-bakwai di'emid la.
english: Global FC was founded in March 2000 when a group of football enthusiasts from Tacloban formed a weekly football practice as their leisure activity.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili ba yiiga di'ema bɛnɛ Quezon City Hall nya'aŋ, li nya'aŋ ka ba kɛŋ Sunken Garden football field linɛ bɛ University of the Philippines Diliman pʋʋgin la ni.
english: The group played their first weekly football games behind the Quezon City Hall, and later moving to the Sunken Garden football field inside the University of the Philippines Diliman.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili nya'aŋ di'em bibisnamin bɛ Manila, ba si'eba an Alaska Cup, Kia Cup, nɛ Ang Liga, ka ba yʋ'ʋr da an Laos F.C. Ban da paam nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛdib ka ba yi ziriga pal tʋmtʋmnib banɛ ka ba tʋʋma yʋ'ʋr an Autre Porte Technique Global (APT Global) nya'aŋ la, ba da gban'e yʋʋm tusayi nɛ awai la ni (2009) ye ba na ti'ak club la yʋ'ʋri lɛb Global Football Club.
english: Then they began to participate in minor tournaments around Manila, including the Alaska Cup, the Kia Cup, and Ang Liga, under the name Laos F.C. (Tagalog: [ˈlɐʔos]; "has-beens", no relation to the country of Laos).

kusaal: Ba da nya'a bɛ 2009 UFL Cup, ka Smartmatic da sʋŋi ba.
english: Eventually, they joined the 2009 UFL Cup, with Smartmatic as their corporate sponsor.

kusaal: Global da nya'a nɛ bɛ Group B ka naae atan' zin'igin group stages ni, ka li da kɛ ka ba tɔlis tuoni kɛŋ plate cup single-elimination tournament.
english: Global competed in Group B and finished third at the group stages, advancing them to the plate cup single-elimination tournament.

kusaal: Franklin Muescan, onɛ da an coach kpɛɛm sankan la da gɔsi ba ka ba ti'al abʋyi' daani bɛ ba 2011 United Football League pin'ilig di'ema ni la.
english: Franklin Muescan, the current head coach of that time then led his team to a second-place finish in their first appearance in the top-tier 2011 United Football League.

kusaal: Ba da di ya'an ka bas San Beda FC ba kpi'iliŋ nwɛ'ɛbin la, ka li kɛ ka ba an yiiga di ya'an di'emkan ni.
english: They won over San Beda FC in the finals making the first champion of the tournament.

kusaal: Ban da di ya'an la zug, Global da tɔlis tuoni kɛŋ 2013 AFC President's Cup ka da an Filipino football club kanɛ an yiiga paam suor ye ba nwɛn'ɛ anina, hali di'ema la pin'il yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu sa (2005), amaa ba da yisi ba bɛ group stages.
english: Because of their victory in the league, Global advanced to the 2013 AFC President's Cup and was the first Filipino football club to qualify for the tournament since its inception in 2005, but they were eliminated early in the group stages.

kusaal: Graeme Mackinnon da tik nu'ug ye o lɛn ka' Global coach ya'asɛ ban da naae 2012 UFL season bɔzugɔ, o yidim yela, sisi'etita'ari da kɛn Mindanao na, anina ka o yidim da bɛ.
english: Graeme Mackinnon resigned as the coach for Global at the end of the 2012 UFL season because of family concerns about the destruction of Tropical Storm Washi in Mindanao where his family lived.

kusaal: Ba da ia sɔ' ye o di'e o nɔbir nwadig mum, ka onɛ da an coach kudugi tis Ayr United ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Brian Reid la da di'e o zin'ig.
english: After a month-long search for a replacement, former Ayr United head coach Brian Reid was signed for the position.

kusaal: Ba da buol Global ye ba kɛna nwɛn'ɛ 2013 Singapore Cup an saam, ban nɛ ba UFL kpi'es Loyola Meralco Sparks.
english: Eventually, Global was invited to play in the 2013 Singapore Cup as a guest club, together with fellow UFL side Loyola Meralco Sparks.

kusaal: Amaa, Global da yi ya ka banɛ da yisi ba an Tanjong Pagar United.
english: However, Global would lose to Tanjong Pagar United.

kusaal: Ba da bas suori tis Philippines dim ye ba paas 2017 AFC Champions League pin'ilig la.
english: A slot was allocated for the Philippines in the preliminary stage of the 2017 AFC Champions League.

kusaal: Global da bʋ nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋ group stage gbaa, Brisbane Roar da di ba 6–0 ka ba da lɛbisi ba group stage 2017 AFC Cup ni.
english: Global fails to qualify for the group stage after losing to Brisbane Roar by 6–0 in the second round of the qualification phase, and was relegated to the group stage of the 2017 AFC Cup.

kusaal: Global da paam suor yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ, Sapal nwadig la ni (November 2016) ye ba paas banɛ na nwɛn'ɛ Philippines Football League pin'ilig la.
english: Global was confirmed in November 2016 to be one of the teams to participate in the inaugural season of the Philippines Football League.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ, Sapal nwadig, dabpistan' daar (December 30, 2016), ba da yis labaar ye Global gban'e ye ba ti'aki ba yʋ'ʋr la lɛbis "Global Queen City FC" ye ba di'e team kanɛ yit Cebu ka da paasi nwɛn'ɛ UFL, ka ba buon Cebu Queen City United F.C la.
english: On December 30, 2016, it was reported that Global planned to adopt the name "Global Queen City FC" as a nod to the defunct Cebu-based team that participated in the UFL, the Cebu Queen City United F.C. Global owner, Dan Palami also expressed openness to investments from Cebuanos in the same report.

kusaal: Alvin Carranza, Ninkanɛ da pin'il ka sʋ'ʋe MacGraphics Carranz International Corp ka lɛn an managing director tis Teen Azkals Foundation la da bas ya ka Dan Palami di'e o nɔbiri sʋ'ʋe club la.
english: Alvin Carranza, founder and owner of MacGraphics Carranz International Corp and managing director of the Teen Azkals Foundation, and replaced Dan Palami as the club's owner.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anii, sigsaa nwadig la (May 2018), Global da sɔs suor ye tɔlis di'emkanɛ ka ba da wa'ae ye ba di'em nɛ Kaya F.C.–Iloilo ka li da kɛ ka ba pʋ lɛn nwɛn'ɛ ya'asɛ.
english: In May 2018, Global was forced to request the league to postponed an away match against Kaya F.C.–Iloilo which led to the cancellation of the match.

kusaal: Bɔzugɔ PFL na kpɛlim nɛ clubs nama anu ma'a, Ilocos United nɛ Manila Meralco da yi la zug.
english: This is because the PFL would only be left with five clubs after the departure of Ilocos United and Manila Meralco.

kusaal: Di'ema la pʋʋgin, ba da di Global Cebu 1–11 ka banɛ da di ba da an JPV Marikina yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, Mɔtul nwadig yiiga dabisir, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii (August 1, 2018), bɔzugɔ ba goalkeeper da pʋ'alim nɛ sankan la.
english: At one point of the league season, Global Cebu suffered at 1–11 loss to JPV Marikina on August 1, 2018, due to being unable to field a natural goalkeeper due to injury of their only keeper in their squad at that time.

kusaal: Ba da paam sʋŋir yi Puma ka yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, mɔtul nwadig la ni (August 2018), labaar pa'al ye Mark Jarvis da sʋ'ʋe club la sankan.
english: The club later secured sponsorship from Puma and in August 2018, it was confirmed that by this time Mark Jarvis was now the owner of the club.

kusaal: Jarvis, onɛ da an Global defender Jordan Jarvis, da paasi sʋ'ʋe club la.
english: Jarvis, the father of Global defender Jordan Jarvis, had previous indirect ownership of the club.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai, yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 2019), ligidi yela da nan anɛ yela tis nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛdib si'eba an goalkeeper kudug Milan Nikolic onɛ da yet ye onɛ sʋ'ʋe team la ka o yʋ'ʋr an Jarvis pʋ yɔɔ ba.
english: However, in January 2019, financial issues remain with several players including former goalkeeper Milan Nikolic calling out team owner Jarvis for the non-payment of their wages.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai, Fulumfug nwadig, daba nu daar (February 5, 2019), club la da yis labaar na ye ba ti'akidi ba yin di'ema zin'ig la yit Cebu lɛbisid Makati linɛ bɛ Metro Manila la ka lɛn paas ye ba ye ba ti'aki ba yʋ'ʋri lɛb "Global Makati F.C." Ba ti'aki ba yʋ'ʋri pʋd "United Makati FC" ban da maal vootug Facebook ni ka bɛdigʋ si'ak ala la zug.
english: On February 5, 2019, the club announced that they would be changing their home locality from Cebu to Makati in Metro Manila and that they will be changing their name to "Global Makati F.C." The club then renamed themselves as "United Makati FC" as a result of a Facebook poll organized by the club.

kusaal: Nwadig la ni nɔɔ, club la tuongatib da yis labaar na ye ba maal nɔɔrnaalig nɛ MC Sportz ka paas ye ba na nyɛ sʋŋidi yi Makati city gɔmɛna ni.
english: Within the same month, the club management announced a partnership with MMC Sportz and stated that they will have support from the Makati city government.

kusaal: Ba da da' nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛdib ayɔpɔi bɛɛ anii yel, nɛ coach Dragutin Stević-Ranković ka paam nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛd saama paas.
english: The club re-signed seven to eight players and head coach Dragutin Stević-Ranković and made new player signings as well.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai, Dɔnwalig nwadig la ni (March 2019), United Makati da yis labaar na ye ba baki ba mɛŋ nɛ Global Makati F.C., ka baki ba mɛŋi bɛ Philippine Football Federation.
english: In March 2019, United Makati announced its legal disassociation with its past as Global Makati F.C., registering with the Philippine Football Federation as a distinct separate legal entity from its former iteration as Global.

kusaal: Global Makati nɛ Stallion Laguna da yisi ba mɛŋ league la pʋʋgin nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai, Vaala nwadig, dabpisi nɛ ayuobʋ daar (April 26, 2019), daar kanɛ yimbɛʋg ka na nwɛn'ɛ yiiga match, league la pʋʋgin bɔzugɔ, Stallion tuongatib da gɔs ka ye pʋʋnyain kae league la tuongatib nii.
english: Global Makati along with Stallion Laguna withdrew from the league on April 26, 2019, a day before the first match day of the league citing concerns regarding what the Stallion management see as a lack of professionalism and transparency regarding the league's management.

kusaal: Amaa, PPL da gaad ya ka Global maligim la'as nɛ PFL.
english: However, PPL dissolved with Global rejoining the PFL.

kusaal: Global da kɛŋ tuoni paas PFL ka lɛɛ pʋ mɔr zi'esim, ka da naae 2019 season la bɛ gbinin sa, ka bɛ debutantes Green Archers United nɛ Mendiola nya'aŋ sa.
english: Global continued its participation in the PFL but continued to struggle, finishing at the bottom of the 2019 season's table behind debutantes Green Archers United and Mendiola.

kusaal: Ti'ir da kae ye ba na di'em bɛ 2020 season la nii, nɛ Global li ti yis labaar na ye ba na paas league la pʋʋgin ka onɛ sʋ'ʋe club la ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Jarvis la da basi tis Hong Kong tʋʋma dɔkanɛ buon Mazinyi Management Ltd.
english: Their status for the 2020 season was left with uncertainty until Global announced its intent to continue its participation in the league and the reportedly the relinquishing of the club by its owner Jarvis to Hong Kong–based Mazinyi Management Ltd. In February 2020, Global Makati reverted its name back to Global F.C. and modified its crest to reflect the name change.

kusaal: English nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛd John Cofie onɛ ka ba da buol o ka o nwɛn'ɛ tis club la yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi ni, yʋʋmpaal nwadig ni la (January 2020), da yi paalʋ na ye Global mɔr o sam.
english: English footballer John Cofie who was signed in to play for the club in January 2020, came forward to the public of allegations that Global owed him unpaid wages.

kusaal: PFF da tis Global dabisa piiga lin da yi Mɔraʋg nwadig dabpisi nɛ atan' la (July 23), ye ba yɔɔ ba nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛdib nɛ tʋmtʋmnib wʋsa sama.
english: The PFF gave Global a ten-day ultimatum from July 23, to settle all its outstanding wages to its players and staff and other contractual obligations.

kusaal: Ban da pʋ nyaŋi yɔ tʋmtʋmnib la nɛ nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛdib zug, PFF da nɔk Global pian'ak la tis Licensing First Instance Body.
english: While Global managed to settle its obligations with the graphic designer, it failed to do so for its players and staff and the PFF will now refer Global's case to its Licensing First Instance Body.

kusaal: Games and Amusements Board (GAB) dim mɛ da pin'ili ba vɛɛnsʋg ka mɔɔl Mɔtul nwadig daba nii ni (August 8), ye ba tisi ba dabisa piiga ye ba yis labaar na pa'al ye sama la sid anɛ sida bɛ Amaa Mazinyi tuongatib da ye ban pʋ paas sama la pʋʋginɛ, ye Mark Jarvis nan kpɛlim sʋ'ʋe li, ka ban pʋ lɛn sʋ'ʋe club la ya'asɛ li gbana si'eba yela.
english: The Games and Amusements Board (GAB) on their part have started their on investigation announcing on August 8, that they have issued a show cause order to demanding them to air their side in writing within 10 days from receipt of such order regarding the unpaid wage allegations However Mazinyi Management reportedly distanced itself from the wage issues, saying that Mark Jarvis is still the owner, and that they have backed out from taking over as the club's new owner allegedly due to documentary issues.

kusaal: Games and Amusement Board dim mɛ da dɔlis nɛ ala kad club la tʋʋma Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig dabayɔpɔi daar (September 7).
english: The Games and Amusement Board followed suit by blacklisting the club on September 7.

kusaal: Ban da nan pʋ nya'ad nɛ Ceres la, Philippine Club Football wʋsa da mɔr nɛ "big three", ka ban anɛ Philippine Army, Philippine Air Force nɛ Philippine Navy football clubs.
english: Before the Global-Ceres rivalry, the Philippine Club Footballing Landscape was dominated by the "big three", composed of the Philippine Army, Philippine Air Force and Philippine Navy football clubs.

kusaal: Saŋa bɛdigʋ, football teams banɛ yi Armed Forces banɛ bɛ Philippines tɛŋin la da nwɛn'ɛdi gati ba taaba.
english: For the longest time, the various football teams of the Armed Forces of the Philippines were the best clubs in the country.

kusaal: Global dataalig nɛ Ceres da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan' yʋʋmpaal nwadig, dabpiinɛ wai daar (January 19, 2013), ban da si'al taaba quarter-finals di'ema ni 2012–13 PFF National Men's Club Championship la.
english: Global's rivalry with Ceres began to develop on January 19, 2013, when the two sides met in a quarter-finals match of the 2012–13 PFF National Men's Club Championship.

kusaal: Di'emkanɛ da bɛ tuon la, Global nɛ Ceres da si'al naar (Finals) linɛ da an ba yiiga bɛ 2013–14 PFF National Men's Club Championship ni.
english: In the next edition of the national tournament, Global and Ceres would meet in a Finals match up for the first time during the 2013–14 PFF National Men's Club Championship.

kusaal: Ba da di'em di'emkaŋa nɛ Negros Occidental FA,ka si'eba nwɛn'ɛ bɛ Panaad Sports Complex, University of St.
english: The tournament was hosted by Negros Occidental FA, with matches held at Panaad Sports Complex, University of St. La Salle in Bacolod City, and also in the Bago City Sports Complex.

kusaal: Ceres, da an banɛ yit Negros Occidental sʋ'ʋlim la ban yini la, ka Global nya'a yi Leyte FA nɔba zug.
english: Ceres, being the Negros Occidental–based club is therefore the home-team, while Global participated under Leyte FA.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ la, ban da di ya'an la, Ceres da paam suor ye ba nwɛn'ɛ bɛ 2015 AFC Cup Play-off.
english: In the aftermath, as national tournament winners, Ceres earn a guaranteed 'spot' in the 2015 AFC Cup Play-off.

kusaal: Ceres da paas nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛdib ka ba si'eba anPatrick Reichelt, Carlie De Murga nɛ banɛ an ba'abiis nɛ taaba la, Marwin nɛ Marvin Angeles ye ba sʋŋi ba.
english: Ceres signed a number of national team members such as Patrick Reichelt, Carlie De Murga and brothers Marwin and Marvin Angeles to boost its campaign.

kusaal: Naar zaba la ni, Ceres da pin'il ka Kim Jin Ho di goal yiiga minute la ni nɛ o zug ka li pa'al ye ba bɛ tuon nɛ goal yinnɛ.
english: During the finals, Ceres came out firing right at the opening whistle, with Kim Jin Ho scoring at the first minute after converting a header for an early 1-nil lead.

kusaal: Ban vʋ'ʋs ka lɛb na la, Global da nyɛ paŋ, Mark Hartmann da nwɛn'ɛ lalli sa ka li kɛŋ di goal ka li niŋ 2–1.
english: In the second half, Global got a boost when Mark Hartmann connected with a long-distance shot from outside the box off a Misagh Bahadoran feed to trim their deficit, 2–1.

kusaal: Di pʋ yʋʋgɛ ka Global lɛn paŋ ya'as nɛ Ceres team captain kanɛ an Juani Guirado ka ba da yis o nwɛn'ɛb la pʋʋgin on da pʋ'alim Global goalkeeper Patrick Deyto zug la yela.
english: Global then got another break a few minutes after as Ceres team captain Juani Guirado was sent off after being involved in a scuffle that saw Global goalkeeper Patrick Deyto hurt after a Ceres player accidentally hit him in the head.

kusaal: Global da paam suoya bɛdigʋ ka ba nyɛ goal, amaa ba da gʋ'ʋŋ ya, la'an nɛ naarin mukur kanɛ ka Ceres goalkeeper Louie Casas da pʋ bas suor ka li gaad o nya'aŋ la da kɛ ka ba di ya'an.
english: But Global, despite having plenty of chances at the goal, failed to convert its shots, including a last-second effort which was denied by the Ceres goalkeeper Louie Casas that sealed the result.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu ni (2015) Ceres da di ba yiiga ya'ani bɛ UFL League ni, Ceres tuongat da anɛ Adrián Gallardo 18 goals ka li kɛ ka ba mɔr points nama anii gaad banɛ ti'al Global.
english: In 2015 Ceres won their first UFL League title with two games to spare, Ceres led by Adrián Gallardo's 18 goals was eight points ahead of runners-up Global.

kusaal: Clubs nam atan' ma'a bɛ Philippines tɛŋin da nyaŋi di ya'an league la ni nɔɔr ayi, ka ba da anɛ – Philippine Air Force F.C. yʋʋm tusayi nɛ wai nɛ piiga (2009–10), Stallion Laguna F.C. yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yi, nɛ piinɛ tan' (2012–13) nɛ Global Makati F.C. yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ (2016).
english: Only three clubs in the Philippines have achieved a league double, and the members of that exclusive group were – Philippine Air Force F.C. in 2009–10, Stallion Laguna F.C. in 2012–13 and Global Makati F.C. in 2016.

kusaal: Global da lɛb na di'e ba zin'igi lɛn paas club banɛ bɛɛ agola yinɛ Azkals standout nɛ tournament Golden Ball Misagh Bahadoran.
english: Global came back to reclaim their place as one of the country's top clubs with the help of the brace of Azkals standout and tournament Golden Ball Misagh Bahadoran.

kusaal: Li pʋ yʋʋgɛ, defense da gbɛlig ya ka Bahadoran nyɛ Matthew Hartman tuon ka o paas goal ka li niŋ 2–0 ka ba nyaan kɛŋ vʋ'ʋs.
english: Not long after, the defense of the Bacolod-based club was left to pay with another goal as Bahadoran found Matthew Hartman on the edge of the box to elevate their squad's lead to 2–0 going into the break.

kusaal: Ban vʋ'ʋsi lɛb na la, Bahadoran da mugus o mɛŋ yʋ'ʋŋ kan ka da nyaŋi dam defender Jason Sabio ka paas goal ya'as minute pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ ni.
english: After the restart Bahadoran doubled his output in the night with an impressive effort inside the area to shake away defender Jason Sabio and put the ball to the back of the net in the 56th minute.

kusaal: Busmen la yʋ'ʋn da nyaŋi di goal bɛ minute pisyuobʋ nɛ yinnɛ ni ka li da yinɛ onɛ ka ba da ti'ak sɔ' ka kpɛn'ɛs o Nate Burkey sa'an ka li si'e ba sam la ka nya'al ayi.
english: The Busmen finally scratched a mark in their scorecard in the 61st minute with a shot courtesy of substitute Nate Burkey to cut the deficit down to just two goals.

kusaal: Season kanɛ paas ayɔpɔi ka da an naari tis UFL League la, lin yi ban da pin'il yʋʋm tusayi nɛ awai ni (2009), Global dim ka ba tuongat an da di'e UFL Golden Ball ka o yʋ'ʋr an Hikaru Minegishi, da di ya'an ka goal kpɛlim, Global da mɔr points ayuobʋ gaad banɛ da ti'al, Ceres.
english: In the seventh and last season of the UFL League since its establishment as a semi-professional league in 2009, Global led by UFL Golden Ball awardee Hikaru Minegishi, won the league title with one game to spare, Global was six points ahead of runners-up Ceres.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi ni (2017), PFF, banɛ da an kpɛɛmnam banɛ gɔsid Philippine Football, da gban'e ye ba ti'ak Metro Manila UFL ka li yʋ'ʋn an tɛŋ mum di'ema kanɛ na nyaŋi dɔl wada banɛ bɛ FIFA nɛ AFC.
english: In the calendar year of 2017, the PFF, the governing body of Philippine Football, decided to replace the Metro Manila–based UFL for a nationwide, community-based football league that is at par with the standards set by the FIFA and the AFC.

kusaal: Lin da an tɛŋtɛŋ league ka mɔr yin di'ema nɛ yiŋ di'ema la, clubs la da nar ka ba dɔlis PFF Club Licensing Regulations ka mɔr yʋ'ʋr ka ban yit zin'ig si'a paasi li ni ka mɛ mɔri ba yin di'ema zin'ig.
english: As a community-based league with a home-and-away double round robin format, clubs were required under the PFF Club Licensing Regulations to have a name that includes the name of their home locality and were also required to have a certified home stadium.

kusaal: Global da ti'ak ya, ban da pin'ili paas Leyte FA(EVRFA nannanna) ka onɛ sʋ'ʋe an Leyte FA Pres.Dan Palami, club la da tɔlisi kɛŋ Cebu City, ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye "Global Queen City FC." (nya'aŋ ka ba ti'aki lɛbis Global Cebu FC).
english: While Global made a switch, originally a regular member of Leyte FA(now EVRFA) and owned by Leyte FA Pres.Dan Palami, the club decided to relocate to Cebu City, and adopted the name "Global Queen City FC." (later renamed as Global Cebu FC).

kusaal: Iain Ramsay da di nɛ goal nama atan' ka ba di ya'an.
english: Iain Ramsay scored a hat-trick that sealed the victory.

kusaal: Kaya da yi Makati lɛb Iloilo la, PFL "Visayas derby" da maligim malis nɛ Kaya paas ya'an dim Ceres–Negros F.C. nɛ banɛ ti'al Global Cebu F.C. ye ba nya'a 2018 PFL season la.
english: With Kaya relocating from Makati to Iloilo, one of the country's football hotbed, the PFL's "Visayas derby" got all the more interesting and competitive as Kaya joined reigning champ Ceres–Negros F.C. and runner-up Global Cebu F.C. in the mix for the 2018 PFL season.

kusaal: Ba da nwɛn'ɛdi bɛ nɛ zin'ig banɛ ka sɔ' pʋ sʋ'ʋe ya bɛ Philippines, ka zin'ig ban si'eba an McKinley Hill Stadium linɛ bɛ Taguig nɛ Rizal Memorial Stadium linɛ bɛ Manila (lini an tɛŋ la la'asig zin'ig) ban da nan bɛ UFL la.
english: Instead, they played in neutral venues across the Philippines, such as the McKinley Hill Stadium in Taguig and the Rizal Memorial Stadium in Manila (considered as the national stadium of the country) when they were still in the UFL.

kusaal: Ban da gaŋ Filipino Franklin Muescan ye o an Global head coach la, o taaba head coaches piinɛ tan' da dɔl nya'aŋ.
english: Since the appointment of Global head coach Filipino Franklin Muescan, there have been 13 other recognized head coaches.

kusaal: Kilab la nyaŋi paam tatilnam anaasi, UFL kapnam ayi', UFL FA kap yinne, nɛ PFF National Men's Club Championship mɛn yinne.
english: The club has won four league titles, two UFL Cups, one UFL FA Cup, and one PFF National Men's Club Championship.

kusaal: Ba da pɛ'ɛs AFC kapnam la nɔɔra atan'.
english: They have participated in the AFC Cup three times.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2000 la ni ka sakur la da pin'il, Global FC da lɛm pɛ'ɛs wɛ'ɛbibis bɛ Metro Manila an Laos nɔbanwɛ'ɛb kikiʋg kilab.
english: Founded in 2000, Global FC participated in minor tournaments around Metro Manila as Laos Football Club.

kusaal: ka ba da gaans nwɛ'ɛdib paala yit zidiga maalʋg lʋgʋr kani ka ba buon ye APT Global, kilab la da tiaki di yʋ'ʋri an Global Football Club ka di da an United Football League (UFL) dimi da pin'ili di.
english: In 2009, after recruiting several players from the railway maintenance company APT Global, the club changed its name to Global Football Club and were one of the founding members of the United Football League (UFL).

kusaal: Global da nɔk yʋʋm 2010 UFL Division 2 kap la, ka paam dʋ'ʋsʋgi kpɛ' UFL Division 1— dinɛ an Philippine dim kila tita'ar.
english: Global won the 2010 UFL Division 2 with an undefeated season, earning promotion to UFL Division 1—the de facto top-level league of Philippine football back then.

kusaal: Ba da lɛm di kapnam atan' yi yʋʋm ayɔpɔi UFL ni.
english: They went on to win three of the seven UFL seasons (commemorated by the three stars on the club's crest)—becoming the most successful club in the league.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi ni (2017), club la da tɔlisi kɛŋ Cebu City ka da ti'aki ba yʋ'ʋri li'eb Global Cebu F.C. ka paasi nya'a Philippines Football League (PFL) ni, linɛ da an di'emkanɛ gati li taaba bɛ Philippine football ni.
english: In 2017, the club moved to Cebu City and renamed itself to Global Cebu F.C. to participate in the Philippines Football League (PFL), which was the official top flight of Philippine football.

kusaal: PFL di'ema la pʋʋgin, club la da naae nɛ abʋyi daani bɛ 2017 season ka season la wʋsa naarin, Alvin Carranza da an onɛ yʋ'ʋn sʋ'ʋe Global, da di'e yinɛ onɛ da pin'ili li ka o yʋ'ʋr an Dan Palami ni.
english: In the PFL, the club finished as runners-up of the 2017 season and by the end of the season, Alvin Carranza became owner of Global, succeeding founder Dan Palami.

kusaal: Di'ema la tɛnsʋk, club la da ti'ak nu'ug, ka Mark Jarvis da di'e li yi Carranza ni sʋ'ʋg.
english: Mid-season, the club had another ownership change with Mark Jarvis taking over from Carranza.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai ni (2019), club la da ti'ak tɛŋi lɛb Makati ka anina ka ba paam yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋn mɔr nwa.
english: In 2019, the club relocated to Makati and adopted their current name.

kusaal: Ba da gban'a ye ba na paas Philippine Premier League zuŋir ni, amaa ba da pʋ di'em baa di'ema yinnɛ anina kati wa'ae nɛ yelsi'eba yela.
english: They intended to participate in the inaugural season of the Philippine Premier League but withdrew from the league without playing a match due to various issues with the league management.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka ba lɛbi la'asi ba mɛŋ nɛ PFL ya'as.
english: They later joined the revived PFL.

kusaal: Nwa' da kɛ ka ba faae ba PFF tʋʋma gbaŋ ka Games and Amusement Board tis nɔɔr ye ba kʋ lɛn di'em di'ema ya'asɛ.
english: This led to the suspension of Global's PFF license as well as the blacklisting of the club by the Games and Amusement Board.

kusaal: Dan Palami, onɛ da sʋ'ʋe ziriga tʋʋma la, ka ba da nɔk ye o sʋ'ʋe Global.
english: Dan Palami, the chief executive officer of the railway company, was hired as the owner of Global.

kusaal: Nwa' yela, ba na nwɛn'ɛ Division II bɛ United Football League.
english: In 2010, Global made its debut in the inaugural season of the United Football League (UFL) as a Division II team.

kusaal: Global, United Football League bɛilim (2010–2016)
english: In 2010, Global made its debut in the inaugural season of the United Football League (UFL) as a Division II team.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga ni (2010), Global da pin'ili bɛ ban da zuŋid United Football League (UFL) la, da an Division II team.
english: In 2010, Global made its debut in the inaugural season of the United Football League (UFL) as a Division II team.

kusaal: Ba da naae anina ka sɔ' pʋ nyaŋi maki ba ka ba tɔlisi ba kɛŋ Division I. Ba da lɛn di ya'ani bɛ league cup ni, ban da nyaŋi ba kpi'es Philippine Air Force bɛ naar nya'abin la.
english: They went undefeated throughout the season to secure a promotion to Division I. They were also victorious in the league cup after defeating Philippine Air Force in the finals.

kusaal: Ban da nwɛn'ɛ yiiga di'ema ban nɛ Stallion bɛ 2011 UFL Cup ni la, onɛ sʋ'ʋe team la, Dan Palami, da gaŋ Australia nid kanɛ buon Graeme Mackinnon ka o an coach kpɛɛm.
english: After an opening match against Stallion in the 2011 UFL Cup, the owner of the team, Dan Palami, hired Australian Graeme Mackinnon as head coach.

kusaal: Global da lɛb nya'aŋ ka banɛ da yisi ba da an Philippine Air Force, ban da paae semi-finals la ni.
english: Global would be later eliminated by the Philippine Air Force in the semi-finals.

kusaal: Global da nwɛn'ɛ ba yiiga nwɛn'ɛb bɛ 2011 National Men's Club Championship di'ema ni, ban da pin'il di'emkan yʋʋm kan ni nɔɔ la.
english: Global also made their first appearance at the 2011 National Men's Club Championship after it was established in the same year.

kusaal: Global da naae 2012 league season ka ban nɛ Kaya an yinnɛ, amaa ba da di'e ba ya'an ye banɛ an yiiga bɛ Division I la ni ban da di goal nami gaadi ba la zug.
english: Global then finished the 2012 league season tied with Kaya but claimed their first Division I title in goal difference.

kusaal: Global da pin'ili nya'adi bɛ 2012 UFL Cup ka naae ka sɔ' pʋ nyaŋi ba.
english: Global began to compete at the 2012 UFL Cup in the second group and finished unbeaten.

kusaal: Onɛ da gɔsid club la yella President's Cup saŋa la.
english: He was in charge of the club's campaign in the President's Cup.

kusaal: Season kanɛ da paas anaasi UFL ni la, Global da naae nɛ abʋyi' daan, points nam atan' ka yiiga daan la da gati ba, ka li da kɛ ka Stallion di ya'ankan.
english: In the fourth season of the UFL, Global finished second, three points beneath the top, resulting in Stallion winning the championship trophy.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili nya'ad 2012–13 National Men's Club Championship, ka Ceres da di ba bɛ quarter-finals ni.
english: The team began to compete at the 2012–13 National Men's Club Championship, where they lost in the quarter-finals to Ceres.

kusaal: Linzug, ba da an Philippine club kanɛ paas ayi nyaŋi paae semi-finals di'emkan ni.
english: As a result, they became the second Philippine club to reach the semi-finals of the tournament.

kusaal: Ba da di 2014 season nɛ FA Cup yʋʋmkan ni.
english: They won both the 2014 season and the FA Cup on the same year.

kusaal: Global Cebu da paas Philippines Football League ni (2017–2019)
english: In 2017, the club moved to Cebu City and renamed itself to Global Cebu F.C. to participate in the Philippines Football League (PFL), which was the official top flight of Philippine football.

kusaal: Ban da di ya'an 2016 UFL season la yela banɛ da zi'en tɛŋ la nɔbazug di'ema la ni.
english: Global as winners of the 2016 UFL season represented the country in the tournament.

kusaal: Ba da ti'aki ba yʋ'ʋri lɛb Global Cebu FC.
english: The club also released an official statement that in January 2018, Global Cebu owner Alvin Carranza requested the PFL for the club not to participate in the league but the whole management of the club decided against withdrawing from the league.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi, Mɔraʋg nwadig, dabisa nu daar (July 5, 2017), Global Cebu da nwɛn'ɛ ba yiiga yin di'ema ba yin di'ema zin'ig kanɛ buon Cebu City Sports Complex la.
english: On July 5, 2017, Global Cebu played their first home match at their designated home venue, the Cebu City Sports Complex.

kusaal: Ba da paas nɛ abʋyi' daan ka banɛ an yiiga an Ceres-Negros bɛ PFL pin'ilig di'ema la.
english: The club went on to finish second to champions Ceres-Negros in the overall standings of the PFL inaugural season.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi, Samanpiid nwadig la ni (December 2017), PFL season la da naae la, football club la da ti'ak sʋ'ʋd.
english: In December 2017 after the PFL season concluded, the football club reportedly had a new owner.

kusaal: 2018 season, Global da nwɛn'ɛdi ba yin di'ema bɛ Rizal Memorial Stadium.
english: In the 2018 season, Global was playing its home matches in the Rizal Memorial Stadium.

kusaal: Ba da yis labaar paalʋ na ye yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 2018), onɛ sʋ'ʋe Global Cebu ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Alvin Carranza da bɛlim PFL lin na niŋ si'em ka club la da nwɛn'ɛ league la nii amaa tuongatib banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa da pʋ si'akɛ.
english: The club also released an official statement that in January 2018, Global Cebu owner Alvin Carranza requested the PFL for the club not to participate in the league but the whole management of the club decided against withdrawing from the league.

kusaal: Ba ya'a da nyaŋi yi, Philippines dim da kʋ nyaŋi paam suori paas AFC Cup ni ya'asɛ.
english: If the withdrawal pushed through, the Philippines would lose eligibility to have its clubs participate in the AFC Cup.

kusaal: Ba da ti'eb ye ba mɔɔl labakaŋa tis nidib wʋsa nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, Sigsaa nwadig la ni (May 2018).
english: This development would later be officially announced to the public by the club in May 2018.

kusaal: Ban da paas clubs banɛ bɛ agɔl PFL season ni la, Global Cebu da lɛb nya'aŋ gbinin sa yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii (2018) PFL table la ni.
english: From being among the top clubs in the previous PFL season, Global Cebu fell to the bottom of the 2018 PFL table.

kusaal: O nu'usin, club la da da' nidib bɛdigʋ ye ba nwɛn'ɛ tis Global Cebu yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii, Mɔraʋg nwadigin (July 2018) ti'asig yʋʋŋ la.
english: Under his watch, the club had a major overhaul, signing numerous players to play for Global Cebu in the July 2018 transfer window.

kusaal: Jarvis da yʋ'ʋn bɔɔdi on na niŋ si'em ka club la zi'en yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii kɛŋ tuon (2018).
english: The club under Jarvis planned to focus on the club's survival for the rest of 2018.

kusaal: Global Makati da bɛ Philippine Premier League (2019)
english: The Philippines Football League was revived in 2019 after the Philippine Premier League its supposed replacement was dissolved in same year.

kusaal: Global Cebu ti'eb ya ye ba paas Philippine Premier League linɛ kɛna di'e PFL nɔbir la, baa la'an nɛ ligidi yela an tʋʋmi tisi ba la.
english: Global Cebu are set to join the Philippine Premier League which replaced the PFL despite financial issues experiencing by the club.

kusaal: Amaa gban'akan da pʋ nyaŋi tʋm tʋʋmaa, ka ba ti'aki lɛb Global Makati.
english: Their status for the 2020 season was left with uncertainty until Global announced its intent to continue its participation in the league and the reportedly the relinquishing of the club by its owner Jarvis to Hong Kong–based Mazinyi Management Ltd. In February 2020, Global Makati reverted its name back to Global F.C. and modified its crest to reflect the name change.

kusaal: Global Makati bɛilim Philippines Football League (2019)
english: The Philippines Football League was revived in 2019 after the Philippine Premier League its supposed replacement was dissolved in same year.

kusaal: Philippines Football League da maligim duoe yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai ni (2019), Philippine Premier League ka gaad yʋʋmkan ni la.
english: The Philippines Football League was revived in 2019 after the Philippine Premier League its supposed replacement was dissolved in same year.

kusaal: 2019 season la ni, PFL da buol club la ye Global Cebu ka ka'a Global Makati kati wa'ae nɛ ba tʋʋma gbana yela.
english: During the 2019 season, the PFL referred to the club as Global Cebu instead of Global Makati in official league channels due to licensing issues.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, Fulumfug nwadig la ni (February 2020), Global Makati da ti'aki ba yʋ'ʋr la lɛbis Global F.C. ya'as ka ti'aki ba zanbin la ye li dɔl nɛ yʋ'ʋr la ti'akir la.
english: Their status for the 2020 season was left with uncertainty until Global announced its intent to continue its participation in the league and the reportedly the relinquishing of the club by its owner Jarvis to Hong Kong–based Mazinyi Management Ltd. In February 2020, Global Makati reverted its name back to Global F.C. and modified its crest to reflect the name change.

kusaal: O da bɛlim Games and Amusements Board ye ba sʋŋ o ka Philippines Football League tuongatib gba'ae dabisir ye ba si'al Global FC kpɛɛmnam yel la zug.
english: He has sought the Games and Amusements Board to help him deal with the situation and the Philippines Football League officials has scheduled to meet with representatives of Global FC regarding the matter.

kusaal: PFL dim da yel ye ba ya'a vɛɛns ka yel la an sida, ba na di'e Global tʋʋma gbaŋ ka ba kʋ di'em bɛ 2020 PFL season la nii.
english: If the allegations were proven, the PFL has said that Global's license may be revoked rendering them ineligible to participate in the 2020 PFL season.

kusaal: Nimbanɛ maan zanbina ka ba buoni ba na'asaalin ye graphic designer ka ba da bɛ Global ni la da yinɛ ye ba pʋ yɔɔ ba sam, tʋʋm kanɛ ka ba tʋm tis club laa.
english: A graphic designer commissioned by Global has also said that they have not been paid for services rendered to the club.

kusaal: PFF dim da di'em Global's PFL tʋʋma gbaŋ dabisa piswai.
english: The PFF suspended Global's PFL license for 90 days.

kusaal: Global da pin'il tɛŋin la di'ema ni nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga (2010) ka da an banɛ di ya'ani bɛ UFL Division 2 ni.
english: Global first arrived in the local football scene in 2010 as the undefeated UFL Division 2 champions.

kusaal: Ban da tɔlisi ba Division 1 la, ba da nya'a nɛ powerhouse Philippine Air Force ye ba di ya'ani an club kanɛ gaad o taaba tɛŋin la.
english: Then after gaining promotion to Division 1, they went on to challenge powerhouse Philippine Air Force for the crowned of being best club in the country.

kusaal: Ceres–Negros F.C. da kɛna paas Philippine football's powerhouse clubs yinnɛ la, club la da anɛ Global dataa hali ba tɛŋin la football di'ema ni.
english: Since the emergence of Ceres–Negros F.C. as one of Philippine football's powerhouse clubs, the club became a serious threat to Global's dominance in the local football scene.

kusaal: Clubs nama ayi' la paae finals nɔɔr atan' ba tɛŋin di'ema ni, ka nya'a nɔɔr atan' ba tɛŋin league ni.
english: Both club's have battle it out in a total of three finals showdown in domestic cup campaigns, and fought three tight battle's for the domestic league title's, two for the last two league titles of the UFL and the other being the first and only 2017 PFL "Finals Series".

kusaal: Amaa yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yi ni (2012), armed forces teams nam la nwɛn'ɛb da lɛb nya'aŋ.
english: But by 2012, the armed forces teams went through a period of rapid decline.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka Global nɛ Ceres yʋ'ʋn nya'ad nɛ taaba, babayi' la ye ba sʋ'ʋg Philippine Club Football yʋma anii banɛ bɛ tuon la.
english: The new rivalry between Global and Ceres proceeded thereafter, as both clubs would go on to dominate Philippine Club Football for the next eight years.

kusaal: Club kanɛ ka ba da zi'i li yelaa ka li bɛ Bacolod City, ka ba da buoni yiiga ye "Ceres-La Salle", Ceres da di goal 1–0 gees nɛ UFL league mi'ilim dim Global Football Club.
english: The then unknown club based in football hotbed Bacolod City, and formerly known as "Ceres-La Salle", Ceres scored a major 1–0 "upset" against UFL league champions Global Football Club.

kusaal: Global da anɛ yiiga di ya'ani bɛ di'emkan ni(2011), ka Ceres da ti'al ayi(2012–13).
english: Global was the first champion of the tournament(2011), while Ceres was the 2nd champion(2012–13).

kusaal: Ba da nya'a piini la zug nɛ ya'an kanɛ an club team kanɛ gaad o taaba bɛ Philippines.
english: They battled it out for the coveted title, the nice top prize and the distinction as the best club team in the Philippines.

kusaal: La Salle linɛ Bacolod City, ka si'eba nwɛn'ɛ bɛ Bago City Sports Complex.
english: The tournament was hosted by Negros Occidental FA, with matches held at Panaad Sports Complex, University of St. La Salle in Bacolod City, and also in the Bago City Sports Complex.

kusaal: Ban da nwɛn'ɛd naarin la, Ceres da di Global 3–1 ka sʋ'ʋg ya'an piini la.
english: Ceres would be runners-up to Global in both league and cup tournaments.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2014 UFL Season ni, Global da di ya'ani an UFL Division 1 bani gaadi ba taaba, ka Ceres nan paam nɛ suori kpɛn'ɛ Division 1 ban da nyaŋi di UFL Division 2 ya'an la.
english: In the 2014 UFL Season, Global was crowned UFL Division 1 champions, while Ceres have just earned their promotion to Division 1 after winning the UFL Division 2 title.

kusaal: Lin da nyalim la, Ceres nɛ Global da lɛn tʋ'ʋs taaba ya'as ye ba zabi di'e ya'ani bɛ UFL FA League Cup ni.
english: As fate would have it, Ceres and Global met again in the finals to battle for the first and only UFL FA League Cup trophy.

kusaal: Ceres da nyɛ yela hali Azkals veteran Carlie De Murga da yi nwɛn'ɛb zin'igin la on da paam sapʋ'ad dʋma ni la zug.
english: Ceres suffered a huge blow after Azkals veteran Carlie De Murga was stretchered out of the pitch due to a possible knee injury.

kusaal: Amaa Adrián Gallardo da sʋŋi kɛ ka Ceres lɛn di goal nɛ o zug minute pisi nɛ yi saŋa ka ba yʋ'ʋn mɔr goal nam ayi ka vʋ'ʋsim saŋa nyaan paae.
english: But Adrián Gallardo doubled Ceres' cushion with a header at the 22nd minute as they held a comfortable 2-nil halftime lead.

kusaal: Nwa' da kɛ ka Global lɛb nya'aŋ ka bʋ lɛn mugusid ye ba di ya'an ya'asi bɛ UFL nii, ka lɛɛ nyaŋid clubs banɛ bɛ Philippines tɛŋin la.
english: The victory halted Global's run of back-to-back trophies in the UFL, while effectively throwing into disarray the hierarchy of clubs in the Philippines' elite domestic competition.

kusaal: Global head coach Leigh Manson sʋʋnr da ma'ae nɛ nidibi da bɔɔd di'ema la.
english: Global head coach Leigh Manson was pleased at the interest generated by the spectacular affair.

kusaal: "yʋ'ʋŋa di'ema la, nya'andɔlib bɛdigʋ bɛ – baŋir bɛ, ka di'ema bɛ li pʋʋgin, ka malisim bɛ, nwa' an sʋm tis League la, tis Filipino football," on da yel si'eli nwa.
english: "Tonight's game, with the amount of fans – the passion, the drama, the excitement, that's got to be great for the League, for Filipino football," he said.

kusaal: Sankan la, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ naasi (2014) naarin paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu ni (2015), Global da di nyani bɛ season yinnɛ nɛ fann pʋʋgin, ɛɛnti paae di'ema naar ka pʋ nyaŋi dii.
english: During that period, from late 2014 to 2015, Global would endured a disappointing 1 and 1/2-season stretch, losing in three straight Finals.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2016 UFL Season nɛ 2016 UFL Cup ni, Global da nyaŋi faae ba mɛŋi yi ba dataas Ceres nu'usin.
english: In the 2016 UFL Season and the 2016 UFL Cup, Global would finally have its redemption against bitter rival Ceres.

kusaal: Club la da kɛŋ tuoni di'e ya'an nɔɔrayi, ba da di yʋʋm wʋsa UFL league nɛ cup tournaments.
english: The club would go on to achieve a league double, by winning the annual UFL league and cup tournaments.

kusaal: Ceres da dɔl Global nya'aŋi bɛ league la nɛ cup tournaments la ni.
english: Ceres would be runners-up to Global in both league and cup tournaments.

kusaal: UFL Cup naar dabisir la, Global da lɛb nɛ na ban da kadi ba ye ba da nwɛn'ɛ UFL Cup yʋʋm kanɛ da gaad la.
english: Global captured the 2016 UFL Cup title, on a 3–1 finals victory.

kusaal: Global da paam suori bɛ Ceres defense ni ban da bas Bahadoran ka o bɛɛ o kɔn' tuon la ka o da nwɛn'ɛ di goal minute pisi nɛ yinnɛ ni.
english: Global quickly capitalized on a distraught defense of Ceres in the consequent minutes of the affair with Bahadoran left unmarked inside the box to strike the rebound in the 21st minute and open the scoring.

kusaal: Sʋnya da duoe bɛ li pʋʋgin Ceres head coach Ali Go da kpɛn'ɛ nwɛn'ɛb zin'igi la ban da ye li anɛ handball ka li bɛ penalty box pʋʋgin la.
english: Tension flared in the match when Ceres head coach Ali Go was thrown off the playing area following an altercation on the pitch after the side's protest of a non-call of a handball in the penalty box.

kusaal: Global da di 2016 UFL Cup ya'an nɛ 3–1 nyaŋir.
english: Global captured the 2016 UFL Cup title, on a 3–1 finals victory.

kusaal: Misagh Bahadoran da di'e PSA 'Mr.
english: Misagh Bahadoran would later be awarded with the PSA 'Mr. Philippine football' award for his heroics in the last UFL Cup tournament.

kusaal: Philippine football' award on muk si'em bɛ UFL Cup tournament la ni.
english: Misagh Bahadoran would later be awarded with the PSA 'Mr. Philippine football' award for his heroics in the last UFL Cup tournament.

kusaal: Ban da di la zug, Global da lɛb AFC Cup ni ka paam suor ye ba paas continental club championship ni.
english: With the win, Global returns to the next edition of the AFC Cup with a sure slot in the qualification round of the continental club championship.

kusaal: Ba da buos buosa tɛŋ la nidib ka ba si'ak ye ba pʋdi li "Philippines Football League" ka li da an league paalig la yʋ'ʋr.
english: A nationwide survey have favored "Philippines Football League" as the name for the new league.

kusaal: Ceres dimi da bɛ Bacolod tɛmpʋʋgin la zug, ba da paas Negros ba club la yʋ'ʋrin.
english: Ceres being based in the city of Bacolod, added Negros in their club name.

kusaal: Nwa'a da kɛ ka nidib pʋd Global nɛ Ceres zabir la ye "Visayas derby" bɛɛ "Visayas Clásico".
english: These developments lead fans to dubbed the Global-Ceres rivalry as the "Visayas derby" or the "Visayas Clásico".

kusaal: PFL's inaugural season la ni, league la da pʋdig zin'is ayi, regular season, nɛ "Finals Series", onɛ ka ba di ka o lɛb nya'aŋ, anina ka team nama anaasi banɛ bɛ tuon regular season ni na nwɛn'ɛ nɛ taaba gɔs banɛ na nyaŋ.
english: During the PFL's inaugural season, the league had two phases, the regular season, and the "Finals Series", a play-off round where the top four teams of the regular season played each other to determine the champions of the league.

kusaal: Inaugural season la da paae naar la, bama ya'an da kirig taaba ya'asi bɛ PFL "Finals Series" ye ba nya'a.
english: As the inaugural season reach its finale, the archnemeses once again crossed paths during the PFL "Finals Series" to resume their fierce rivalry.

kusaal: Ceres–Negros F.C. da di league inaugural championship la ka li anɛ ba da di ba dataas Global Cebu F.C. 4–1.
english: Ceres–Negros F.C. won the league's inaugural championship by defeating archrivals Global Cebu F.C. in the Final, 4–1.

kusaal: Ba da paas PFL nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi (2017) ka ba yin di'ema zin'ig an Cebu City Sports Complex.
english: The club joined the PFL in 2017 and maintained as their home ground the Cebu City Sports Complex.

kusaal: Global da pin'ili nwɛn'ɛ zin'ig kan yʋʋm 2013 AFC President's Cup saŋa.
english: Global started play in the stadium during the 2013 AFC President's Cup.

kusaal: Ban da nam pʋ la'as nɛ Philippines Football League la, Global da pʋ mɔri ba mɛŋ yin di'ema zin'igɔ.
english: The club released its fourth logo on April 26, 2017, through its social media account when it joined the Philippines Football League as Global Cebu F.C. The new logo is derived from the third logo, with the text "Cebu" placed in the center of the crest.

kusaal: Yiiga zanbin la da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi (2000) paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ ni (2011), sankan ka ba da buon club la ye Global F.C. Ba zanbin la da anɛ fuug ka ba tabil ka sɔb "Global F.C." tabil.
english: The first team emblem was used from 2000 to 2011, during which time the club was known as Global F.C. The logo was a simple crest with the words "Global F.C." in front of a wireframe globe.

kusaal: Kpɛɛm kanɛ da ka' Philippines nida da anɛ Australian coach kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Graeme Mackinnon la.
english: The first head coach from outside the Philippines was Australian coach Graeme Mackinnon.

kusaal: Glosa pian'ad nam dɔlisnɛ Latin nɛ Greek ka di nya' bɛ European buudi pian'adnam la kpɛɛm ni; dɔl science, na'asaasɔɔng, nɛ tima yɛla, pian'abama kpɛn'ɛd buudi pian'ad wʋsa.
english: Being an a posteriori language, Glosa takes most of its vocabulary from Greek and Latin roots, seen by the authors as international in a sense by their usage in science.

kusaal: Godfred Seidu Jasaw (14 March 1977) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress la ni.
english: Godfred Seidu Jasaw (born 14 March 1977) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Wa East constituency n bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Wa East constituency in the Upper West Region of Ghana .

kusaal: Ba da du'a Jasaw nɛ Jeriyi Atini daari, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadsa atan la dabpiinɛ anaasi la daar (Monday, 14 March 1977).
english: Jasaw was born in Jeriyi on Monday, 14 March 1977.

kusaal: O mɔr PHD (Sustainability science) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016), nɛ BSc (Agricultural Economics) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: He holds a PHD (Sustainability science) – 2016, BSc (Agricultural Economics) – 2005.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt Jasaw ye o lieb Wadmaani tis Wa East constituency la nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Jasaw was elected as a member of parliament for the Wa East constituency during the 2020 general elections.

kusaal: Godfrey Tangu Bayon anɛ Ghana Pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la ni Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n tis Wa East linɛ bɛ Upper West Region la, onɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋma 1956 la ni.
english: Godfrey Tangu Bayon (born 1956) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Wa East Constituency in the Upper West Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O Yinɛ Ducie, tempʋʋg linɛ bɛ Upper West Ghana Sʋ'ʋlʋm la.O da tʋmnɛ an pa'an ka nyaan kpɛn' Pɔlitis tʋʋma ni yʋʋm 2001 la ni.
english: He hails from Ducie, a town in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paamɛ o A level kasɛta gbaʋŋ n bɛ Gbewa Training College la ni yʋʋm 1982.
english: He obtained an A Level Certificate at Gbewah Training College in 1982.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn keŋ Institute of Adult Education.
english: He also attended the Institute of Adult Education.

kusaal: Tʋʋma Bayon tʋmnɛ an pa'an n bɛ Ghana gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni lin da yi yʋʋm 1977 ti paae yʋʋm 2000.Onɛ da an Sakʋr zug daan n tis Ducia primary sakur la O tʋʋma anɛ pa'an tʋʋma.
english: Bayon worked as a teacher at the Ghana Education Service from 1977 to 2000.

kusaal: Onɛ da an D.C.E lin da yi yʋʋm 2001 nɛ yʋʋm 2005.
english: He was the Wa District Chief Executive between 2001 and 2005.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o an minista kanɛ gɔsid suoya yɛla la gɔmina John Kufour win la lin da yi yʋʋm 2007 ti paae yʋʋm 2008.
english: He was appointed Minister of States (Roads and Highways) under the government of the then President John Kufour between 2007 and 2008.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt ka Bayon di wadmaanib kʋk la tis Waz East sʋ'ʋlʋm yʋʋm 2004 vɔɔt la ni.
english: Bayon was elected as the member of parliament for the Wa East constituency in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ ba da mɔri 5.1%, nɛ 43.5% n yi vɔɔt kanl wusa ni.
english: These were equivalent to 5.1% and 43.5% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Bayon anɛ Kristo biig, o anɛ Baptist Karimbiig ka di pu'a mɔr biis ayi'.
english: Bayon is a Christian(Baptist) and is married with two children.

kusaal: Ba da du'a nɛ Bayon nwadis atan' la daba atan' la ni yʋʋm 1956.
english: Bayon was born on 3 March 1956.

kusaal: Bayon anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Bayon is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: o da anɛ wadmaan tis Wa East sʋ'ʋlʋm la wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anaasi, anu, nɛ ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la.
english: He represented Wa East Constituency in the 4th, 5th and 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da bɛ kʋk la zug n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anaasi Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la.
english: He represented Wa East Constituency in the 4th, 5th and 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: ka Albert Solomon Bawah Sulley onɛ da an PNC nid, nɛ Saliah Issaku Aljaji onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig nid la da la'asi nyi'ad ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over Albert Solomon Bawah Sulley of the People's National Convention and Saliah Issaku Alhaji of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da paam nɛ vɔɔt kal 10947 n yi vɔɔt kanl wʋsa linɛ da 21307 la.
english: He was elected with 10,947votes out of 21,307 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba wʋsa vɔɔt nam da anɛ 1085, nɛ 9275 n yi vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: He was elected with 10,947votes out of 21,307 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ka di da anɛ Gold Coast mɛŋ, Ashanti, Northern Territories nɛ British Togoland sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: The term Gold Coast may also refer collectively to the four separate jurisdictions administered by the Governor of the Gold Coast: the colony proper, Ashanti, the Northern Territories, and British Togoland.

kusaal: Din ka Gold Coast da an yʋ'ʋri tis sʋ'ʋlʋm la ka di yinɛ Europeans dim la ni bɔzʋgɔ la'asʋma da bɛ zi'ig la ni.
english: Gold, which initially brought Europeans to the Gold Coast, remained in the hands of Africans until the 1890s.

kusaal: Bibiani Gold Stars SC, ka ba da buon ye Complex Stars ka ɛɛnti kʋ'ʋgʋ di giŋa ye Gold Stars la anɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib kilab dinɛ bɛ Western North Region.
english: Bibiani GoldStars SC, formerly the Complex Stars and often shortened to and more commonly known as the Gold Stars, is a Ghanaian professional football team based in the Western North Region.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili dinɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswain nɛ piswai nɛ anii la ni (1998) ka nya'aŋ ka ba da nɔki di tis Bibiani Gold Mines.
english: It was founded in 1998 and later given to the Bibiani Gold Mines.

kusaal: Ba da nwɛ'ɛd 2A Zone dinɛ bɛ Division One League ni la.
english: They played in the 2A Zone of the Division One League.

kusaal: Tiimnam la sieba yinɛ Ashanti Region, Western Region nɛ Central Region banɛ bɛ Ghana.
english: Zone 2A has seven competing teams from the part of the Ashanti Region, Western Region and the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da paam suori kpɛn' Ghana Premier League la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) la ni.
english: They achieved promotion to the Ghana Premier League in 2021.

kusaal: Zone 2A mɔrnɛ tiimnam ayɔpɔi ka ba nya'ad.
english: Zone 2A has seven competing teams from the part of the Ashanti Region, Western Region and the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Francis kojo Arthur an constituency la wadmaan.
english: Francis Kojo Arthur was the member of parliament for the constituency for two terms between January 2009 to January 2017.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt gaŋ o nɛ ma'asim na'adɔɔg la ni ka o di vɔɔt la nɛ vɔɔt kal 3,474 n lieb wadmaan la.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and won a majority of 3,474 votes to become the MP.

kusaal: O da di'e kʋk la yinɛ Joe Kingsley Hackman onɛ da an wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid ka da zi'en tis teŋ la bɛ wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: He succeeded Joe Kingsley Hackman who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 1993), military gɔmena da bas suori tis Fourth Republic la ban da maal Wadmaannib nɛ zuraan vɔɔtʋg la nya'aŋ yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) naarin.
english: In January 1993, military government gave way to the Fourth Republic after presidential and parliamentary elections in late 1992.

kusaal: National Democratic Congress yinɛ Jerry John Rawlings' na'adɔkanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Provisional National Defence Council ka da bɛ kʋk la zug yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la (1992).
english: The National Democratic Congress is the successor organisation to Jerry John Rawlings' Provisional National Defence Council which was in power from 1981 to 1992.

kusaal: Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party, da sin'iŋnɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yi la ni (1992), da di'enɛ Gold Coast nɔba zug, The Big Six asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ Na'adɔɔg, United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC); People's National Convention, nɛ Convention People's Party, dinɛ di'e Kwame Nkrumah Na'adɔɔg la yʋ'ʋri la mɛn, dinɛ da zin'i kʋk la zug yʋʋma piiga (10 years) din yi asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ saŋa yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (1957) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (1966), ka da di vɔɔt la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (1956), yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ (1960), nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu (1965).
english: The New Patriotic Party, found in 1992, is the successor to the Gold Coast's The Big Six independence achiever party United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC); the People's National Convention, and the Convention People's Party, successor to Kwame Nkrumah's original party of the same name, which was the incumbent government of Ghana for 10 years from declaration of independence in 1957 to 1966, winning elections in 1956, 1960, and 1965.

kusaal: National Democratic Congress da di zuraan nɛ wadmaannib vɔɔt la yʋʋmbama ni 1992, 1996, 2008 and 2012.
english: The National Democratic Congress won the presidential and parliamentary elections in 1992, 1996, 2008 and 2012.

kusaal: New Patriotic Party da di zuraan nɛ wadmaannib vɔɔt la yʋʋmbama ni 2000, 2004, and 2016.
english: The New Patriotic Party won the presidential and parliamentary elections in 2000, 2004, and 2016.

kusaal: Ghana anɛ tenkanɛ zi'e kippi United Nations nɛ African Union ni.
english: Ghana favors international and regional political and economic co-operation, and is an active member of the United Nations and the African Union.

kusaal: Bama anɛ Ghana diplomat Secretary-General of the United Nations kʋdʋg Kofi Annan, International Criminal Court Judge Akua Kuenyehia, Zuraan kʋdʋg Jerry John Rawlings nɛ Zuraan kʋdʋg John Agyekum Kuffour banɛ tʋm diplomats tʋʋma tis United Nations.
english: These include Ghanaian diplomat and former Secretary-General of the United Nations Kofi Annan, International Criminal Court Judge Akua Kuenyehia, former President Jerry John Rawlings and former President John Agyekum Kuffour who have both served as diplomats of the United Nations.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga nwadisa awai la ni, (September 2010), Ghana Zuraan kʋdʋg John Atta Mills da zi'en Ghana nɔba zugʋ kaae China.
english: In September 2010, Ghana's former President John Atta Mills visited China on an official visit.

kusaal: Mills nɛ China Zuraan kʋdʋg Hu Jintao, da tien yʋʋm pisnu tienr malʋŋ (50th anniversary) tis diplomatic naalʋg kanɛ bɛ tɛɛnsa ayi la sʋʋgin la, bɛ Great Hall of the People yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga nwadisa awai la dabpisi daar (20 September 2010).
english: Mills and China's former President Hu Jintao, marked the 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two nations, at the Great Hall of the People on 20 September 2010.

kusaal: China da yɔ sam ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne nwadis piinɛ yinne la ni (November 2011), ka ba kʋkdaan nya'adɔl tis Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China, Zhou Tienong da kaae Ghana ka si'al Ghana Zuraan John Dramani Mahama.
english: China reciprocated with a visit in November 2011, by the vice-chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China, Zhou Tienong who visited Ghana and met with Ghana's President John Dramani Mahama.

kusaal: Wada tʋʋma la dɔlnɛ yʋʋmtusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi wada gbaʋŋ la (1992 constitution), buudi malima wada, nɛ British common law.
english: The legal system is based on the 1992 constitution, customary (traditional) law, and British common law.

kusaal: Kɔɔtʋ dɔlisid si'em anɛ Supreme Court of Ghana (highest court), courts of appeal, nɛ high courts of justice.
english: Court hierarchy consists of Supreme Court of Ghana (highest court), courts of appeal, and high courts of justice.

kusaal: Republic of Ghana mɔrnɛ regionnam piinɛ yuobʋ (sixteen administrative regions) dinɛ pʋdigi an 6 metropolitan assemblies; 55 Municipal assemblies; nɛ 216 districts, ka ba wʋsa yinne-yinne mɔri ba district assembly nam.
english: There are sixteen administrative regions of the Republic of Ghana which are divided into 6 metropolitan assemblies; 55 Municipal assemblies; and 216 districts, each with its own district assembly.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) wada gbaʋŋ la pʋ paŋ la nɛ tis, zuraan, wadmaannib yir la, cabinet council of state, nɛ asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ banɛ gɔsid wada maalʋg yɛla (Independent Judiciary).
english: The 1992 constitution divides powers among a president, parliament, cabinet, council of state, and an independent judiciary.

kusaal: Pɔlitis na'adɔɔd la da nie paalʋ nɛ yʋʋm yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) tensʋg din da gu' yʋʋm piiga la nya'aŋ.
english: Political parties became legal in mid-1992 after a ten-year hiatus.

kusaal: Na'adɔɔd banɛ bɛ Fourth Republic la gaad pisi.
english: There are more than 20 registered political parties under the Fourth Republic.

kusaal: Na'adɔɔda ayi banɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa mi' anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party.
english: The two main parties are the National Democratic Congress and the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ghana diplomat Kofi Annan da anɛ Secretary-General of the United Nations yʋma awai (nine years) hali ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2006).
english: These include Ghanaian diplomat and former Secretary-General of the United Nations Kofi Annan, International Criminal Court Judge Akua Kuenyehia, former President Jerry John Rawlings and former President John Agyekum Kuffour who have both served as diplomats of the United Nations.

kusaal: Din yi asʋ'po-m-mɛŋ saŋa, Ghana pɛsigi o mɛŋi gɔsid ideals of nonalignment yɛla ka paas nimbanɛ pin'il non-aligned movement.
english: Since independence, Ghana has been devoted to ideals of nonalignment and is a founding member of the non-aligned movement.

kusaal: Ghana diplomats nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛdib bɛdigʋ mɔr kpɛŋ tɛɛns nɛ la'asʋgnam kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb.
english: These include Ghanaian diplomat and former Secretary-General of the United Nations Kofi Annan, International Criminal Court Judge Akua Kuenyehia, former President Jerry John Rawlings and former President John Agyekum Kuffour who have both served as diplomats of the United Nations.

kusaal: Banɛ pʋ paae bama anɛ circuit, magisterial, and traditional courts.
english: Beneath these bodies are circuit, magisterial, and traditional courts.

kusaal: Banɛ lɛm paas anɛ public tribunals.
english: Extrajudicial institutions include public tribunals.

kusaal: Greater Accra Region pɔɔdi gat Ghana Region nam piinɛ ayuobʋ (16) la, di labisim anɛ wʋʋ 3,245 square kilometres.Nɛ' anɛ nwɛnɛ yinne du'al anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.4 per cent) yi Ghana teŋ la wʋsa ni.
english: The Greater Accra Region has the smallest area of Ghana's 16 administrative regions, occupying a total land surface of 3,245 square kilometres.

kusaal: Region la mɔr nidib bɛdegʋ ka ba kal an 5,455,692 in 2021, dinɛ zɛm nɛ 17.7 kɔbiga pʋʋgin.
english: It is the most populated region, with a population of 5,455,692 in 2021, accounting for 17.7% of Ghana's total population.

kusaal: 1960 ni, Greater Accra, ka ba da buon ye Accra Capital District, da paasnɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: In 1960, Greater Accra, then referred to as Accra Capital District, was geographically part of the Eastern Region.

kusaal: Amaa di da tʋmnɛ di kɔn' dɔlisid Minister kanɛ gɔsid local government la.
english: It was administered separately by the Minister responsible for local government.

kusaal: Greater Accra Region tɔtnɛ nɛ Eastern Region, Volta Region, Gulf of Guinea, nɛ Central Region.
english: The Greater Accra Region is bordered on the north by the Eastern Region, on the east by the Volta Region, on the south by the Gulf of Guinea, and on the west by the Central Region.

kusaal: Yuum tusa ay nɛ piiga (2010) nidib kaalʋg la pa'al ye, region la nidib kal anɛ miliyɔŋ anaasi, tusa piiga nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi (4,010,054), ka di an region of Ghana kanɛ tia'ali ayi bɛ Ashanti Region nya'aŋ.
english: According to the 2010 census, the region had a population of 4,010,054, making it the second most populous (total number of people) region of Ghana behind the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Banɛ zu'oe gaad buudi banɛ kpɛlim ka ska sʋ'oe Greater Accra Region, ba anɛ 18.9%.
english: They form the largest ethnic sub-group in the Greater Accra Region, with 18.9% of the population.

kusaal: Nimbanɛ zu'oe Accra gat buudbanɛ bɛ ani la anɛ Akan, ba anɛ pistan nɛ awai du'ali anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (39.8%).
english: The largest portion of the population of Accra is Akan, at 39.8% of the population.

kusaal: Nɛ' nya'aŋ 18% Ewe nam.
english: After this 18% of the population is Ewe.

kusaal: 1960 nidib kaalʋg la ni Greater Accra Region da anɛ 491,817.
english: In 1960 the population of the Greater Accra Region was 491,817.

kusaal: Greater Accra region mɔr Kotoka International Airport bɛ Accra.
english: The Greater Accra region is served by the Accra International Airport in Accra.

kusaal: Ba mɛ lɛm mɔr ziriga suor (railway line) dinɛ tɔ'ɔŋ Accra nɛ Tema.
english: There is an active railway line connecting Accra and Tema.

kusaal: Dinɛ an region kanɛ pɔɔdi gat Ghana region nam piinɛ ayuobu (16) la wusa nɛ labisim.
english: The Greater Accra Region has the smallest area of Ghana's 16 administrative regions, occupying a total land surface of 3,245 square kilometres.

kusaal: Ba maanɛ dinɛ tiend kɔm tita'akanɛ da paae Ga nidib sixteenth century la ni.
english: It is celebrated in remembrance of a famine that hit the Ga people in the 16th century.

kusaal: Ga banɛ paas Ga-Dangme an banɛ sʋ'oe Accra.
english: The Ga sub-group of the Ga-Dangme people is the historical population of Accra.

kusaal: Nidib yinne du'ali atan kɔbiga oʋʋgin (1.3%) banɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region la ka' Ghana nidiba.
english: The Greater Accra Region has the smallest area of Ghana's 16 administrative regions, occupying a total land surface of 3,245 square kilometres.

kusaal: Airport nɔ'ɔsid nidib ken zin'is kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb Ghana kpɛla, Africa continent la ni nɛ continent sieba.
english: The Greater Accra region is served by the Accra International Airport in Accra.

kusaal: Di mɔr National highways nam anaasi (4) – N1, N2, N4 nɛ N6 – ka mɔr Regional highway yinne (1) dinɛ an R40 – dɔl Greater Accra region tensʋk.
english: The Greater Accra region is served by the Accra International Airport in Accra.

kusaal: Habib Iddrisu anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni, New Patriotic Party (NPP).
english: Habib Iddrisu is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Tolon Constituency bɛ Northern Region, Ghana la sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Tolon Constituency in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Iddrisu anɛ Deputy Executive Secretary tis Ghana Free Zones Authority gɔsid Tema sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Iddrisu, before becoming MP, served as the Deputy Executive Secretary of Ghana Free Zones Authority in charge of Tema enclave.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋgin la, Iddrisu da zi'enɛ Sagnarigu Constituency sʋ'ʋlim nya' nɛ Alhassan Bashir Fuseini onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg (NDC) nd la ka pʋ dii nɛ vɔɔt tusa ayɔpɔi, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (7,888) dinɛ an pisi du'al ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (20.7%) ka Fuseini paam tusa pisi nɛ ayuobʋ, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ anii (26,898) dinɛ an pisyɔpɔi du'al ayɔpɔi (70.7%).
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general election, Iddrisu stood for the Sagnarigu Constituency against the member of parliament Alhassan Bashir Fuseini of the National Democratic Congress and lost with 7,888 votes representing 20.7% against Fuseini's 26,898 votes representing 70.7%.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayuobʋ la ni (June 2020) o da diya ka bas Wahab Wumbei Suhuyini onɛ da an Wadmaani tis Tolon Constituency nɔɔra ayi ka da kpɛn' Wadmaanib yin la hali yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la (2013).
english: In June 2020, he won the primaries for the Tolon Constituency after defeating incumbent member of parliament Wahab Wumbei Suhuyini who had served as member of parliament for two terms and been in parliament since January 2013.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt kɔbistan nɛ pistan nɛ anii (338) ka onɛ da zin'i kʋk la zug la paam kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi (164) ka nidiba atan banɛ kpɛlim la vɔɔt wʋsa kal an pistan nɛ ayi (32).
english: He won by getting 338 votes, while the incumbent had 164 votes and the rest of the three candidates had a total of 32 votes.

kusaal: Ba da yina yɛl ye onɛ di ka di yinɛ on paam vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ yinne, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisi nɛ awai (31,429) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ anii du'al pistan nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (58.37%) ka onɛ ti'al o la, Yussif Adam onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid la paam tusa pisi nɛ ayi,kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anu (22,145) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ yinne du'al piinɛ atan (41.13%).
english: He was declared winner in the parliamentary elections after obtaining 31,429 votes representing 58.37% against his closest contender Yussif Adam of the National Democratic Congress who had 22,145 votes representing 41.13%.

kusaal: On da ti'ebidi gur yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (202)0 vɔɔtʋg la, Iddrisu nɛ o Na'adɔɔg ninsieba da nya' onɛ na zi'en nya' Tolon Constituency kʋk la.
english: Ahead of the 2020 elections, Iddrisu entered the race for the parliamentary candidate in the NPP primaries, this time around in the Tolon Constituency.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt Iddrisu ye an Wadmaani tis Tolon sʋ'ʋlim yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi (2020 December) Wadmaanib vɔtʋg la ni.
english: Iddrisu was elected member of parliament for Tolon constituency during the 2020 Ghanaian general elections.
