kusaal: Habib Saad anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Bortianor-Ngleshie-Amanfro Constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim la wabʋg na'adɔɔg, nɔba zug.
english: Habib Saad (born 10 October 1968) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Bortianor-Ngleshie-Amanfro Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii nwadis piiga la dabpiiga daar (sawa'ar nwadig 10, 1968), Antoakrom, bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: Saad was born on 10 October 1968, in Antoakrom, in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O da maalnɛ Bachelor of Arts bɛ India's Techno Global University.
english: He graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree from India's Techno Global University.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' (2000) la ni, Habib Saad da anɛ managing director tis Go Enterprise.
english: Since 2000, Saad has served as managing director of Go Enterprise.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.
english: He is a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Hachinohe Sansha Taisai (八戸三社大祭) anɛ Japanese maʋŋ kanɛ ka ba maan nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpistan' nɛ yinne daar keŋ paae nwadisa anii la daba anaasi daar Hachinohe, Aomori Prefecture, bɛ Japan.
english: Hachinohe Sansha Taisai (八戸三社大祭) is a Japanese festival celebrated from July 31 to August 4 in Hachinohe, Aomori Prefecture, Japan.

kusaal: Di malima la dɛlimnɛ Shinto teŋgbana atan la: Ogami (霊神社), Shinra (新羅神社), nɛ Shinmei (神明宮) teŋgbana.
english: Its rites center on three Shinto shrines: Ogami (霊神社), Shinra (新羅神社), and Shinmei (神明宮) shrines.

kusaal: Labakʋda pa'al ye di yuugi nwɛnɛ yʋma kɔbisyi' nɛ piswai nɛ awai ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni, ka ba da zaŋi li paas Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property ni.
english: It has a two hundred and ninety-year history and in 2004 was designated an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.

kusaal: Nwadisa anii la daba ayi daar wʋsa Chojasan Shinra Shrine maan yʋʋm-yʋʋm malʋŋ kanɛ an Kiba Dakyuu (騎馬打球) la'asʋg.
english: On August 2, the Chojasan Shinra Shrine holds the annual Kiba Dakyuu (騎馬打球) tournament.

kusaal: Di anɛ malʋŋkanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Kagami-style dakyu an si'em la ka ba maani li Hachinohe ma'aa, Yamagata Prefecture, nɛ Imperial Household Agency.
english: It is the traditional Kagami-style dakyu and is held only in Hachinohe, Yamagata Prefecture, and the Imperial Household Agency.

kusaal: Ba mɔr procession kanɛ mɔr float nam pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ mikoshi nam atan ka ba mɛ ziidi li dɔl pala la zug.
english: There is a procession of twenty-seven floats and three mikoshi are also borne through the streets.

kusaal: Hakata Gion Yamakasa (博多祇園山笠) anɛ Japanɛse festival malʋŋ kanɛ maani pin'il nwadisa ayɔpɔi la yiiga dabisiri keŋ paae dabisa piiga nɛ anu daar (1st to 15th of July) bɛ Hakata, Fukuoka.
english: Hakata Gion Yamakasa (博多祇園山笠) is a Japanese festival celebrated from the 1st until the 15th of July in Hakata, Fukuoka.

kusaal: Ba da siak ye li paas Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property dinɛ bɛ Japan la yʋʋm tusir, Kɔbis wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1979).
english: It was designated an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Japan in 1979.

kusaal: Vuud kanɛ bɛ Yamakasa malʋŋ ni la, Ministry of the Environment ɛɛnti gaŋi li yi 100 Soundscapes of Japan.
english: The sound of the Yamakasa has also been selected by the Ministry of the Environment as one of the 100 Soundscapes of Japan.

kusaal: Hakata, da mɔri li mɛŋ tempuug, ka yu'un la'as nɛ Fukuoka yuum tusir, Kɔbis nii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobu (1876).
english: Hakata, once its own city, merged with Fukuoka in 1876.

kusaal: Hakata da pʋdʋgnɛ district nam ayɔpɔi, onɛ da pʋdʋg la an Toyotomi Hideyoshi 1586/1587.
english: Hakata was divided into seven districts by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1586/1587.

kusaal: Districts nam la anɛ Higashi-nagare, Nakasu-nagare, Nishi-nagare, Chiyo-nagare, Ebisu-nagare, Doi-nagare nɛ Daikoku-nagare.
english: The districts are Higashi-nagare, Nakasu-nagare, Nishi-nagare, Chiyo-nagare, Ebisu-nagare, Doi-nagare and Daikoku-nagare.

kusaal: Malima la la'as nɛ Kushida Jinja.
english: The festivities are centred on the Kushida Jinja.

kusaal: Kakiyama la'asug la an bʋmbil, ka ba zɔti giligid tempʋʋgin la, amaa Kazariyama zienɛ babir yinne, ka ba nɔk la'adi mɛ' ka li wa'ami paae 13 metres ka li pa'al nɛ Japanɛse malʋŋ.
english: The Kakiyama are the smaller, carryable floats, that are raced through the town, while the Kazariyama are stationary floats, that are built up to 13 metres high and often depict historic or mythical events of Japanese culture.

kusaal: Amaa Yamakasa da pʋdʋg nɛ yʋʋm tusir, Kɔbis nii nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1898) sankanɛ ka bugum nwiis linɛ be Hakata da ke ka ba ku nyaŋi zi Yamakasa kanɛ wa'am la gilig tempʋʋsin la.
english: However the Yamakasa were split up in 1898 when the electrical power lines in Hakata became too common for large Yamakasa to be carried through the streets.

kusaal: Malima la ɛɛnti bɛnɛ Hakata teŋin.
english: The festivities are mostly based in Hakata.

kusaal: Ban da pʋdʋg la nya'aŋ la, ban na zi Yamakasa yi ba mɛŋ districts ni la da yu'un anɛ nya'ab.
english: Soon after the division, carrying the Yamakasa through one's own district became a competition for speed.

kusaal: Nannanna, malʋŋ kanɛ an Oiyama la, yʋ'ʋn anɛ zɔɔs ka districts la nya'ad.
english: Today, the main event, the Oiyama, is a race between the districts.

kusaal: Districts nwa' sieba tiak yʋda nɛ titɔndis zin'is kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb, amaa ba nye ba mɛŋ ka ba anɛ Districts ayɔpɔi la nɔɔ.
english: Some of these districts have changed names and exact boundaries multiple times; they still see themselves as the original seven districts.

kusaal: Hamile anɛ tembili bɛ Jirapa/Lambussie district, district kanɛ bɛ lalli Ya-datiʋŋ tuon tis Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana Ya-datiʋŋ baba, ya'ad nɛ Burkina Faso titɔdig.
english: Hamile is a village in the northwestern corner of the Republic of Ghana, close to the border with Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Suoratita'ar yi Wa keŋ Hamile ka di wa'alim na an 88.5 km.
english: There is a 88.5 km highway from Wa-Hamile.

kusaal: Hamza Adam (dʋ'anɛ 30 October 1975) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: Hamza Adam (born 30 October 1975) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Kumbungu Constituency bɛ Northern Region.
english: He is the member of parliament for Kumbungu Constituency in the Northern Region.

kusaal: O mɔr PhD in Rural Livelihoods, MPhil in Agricultural Extension, nɛ BSc in Agriculture Technology.
english: He holds a PhD in Rural Livelihoods, an MPhil in Agricultural Extension, and a BSc in Agriculture Technology.

kusaal: Adam da anɛ pa'an (lecturer) ka an Head of Department University for Development Studies.
english: Adam has worked as a lecturer and a Head of Department at the University for Development Studies.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Adam nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu Nwadis piiga la dabpistan daar (October 30, 1975).
english: Adam was born on October 30, 1975.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2tusa pisi nɛ anaasi020) Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la ni, Adam paam vɔɔt , kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (24,278) ka di Kumbungu Constituency kʋk la.
english: He is the member of parliament for Kumbungu Constituency in the Northern Region.

kusaal: Iddrisu di'e zamisʋgʋ yi University of Ghana yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai na atan' nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayopɔi zin'ikanɛ ka o paam B.A. (Hons) Sociology ni.
english: Iddrisu studied at the University of Ghana between 1993 and 1997 where he obtained B.A. (Hons) in Sociology.

kusaal: Iddrisu mɛ lɛn da anɛ Lɔya ka an Ghana Bar La'asʋg la nid hali yʋʋm 2002.
english: Iddrisu is also a barrister and has been a member of the Ghana Bar Association since 2002.

kusaal: O da zi'en MP yʋʋm 2004 la ni Parliament vɔɔtʋg Saŋkanɛ ka ba da nyɔ'ɔg Tamar zin'ig yinne teŋ.
english: He stood for MP in the 2004 parliamentary election in the then newly formed Tamale South constituency.

kusaal: Iddrisu da anɛ Ranking member tisid parliamentary select Committee Pian'ad pʋʋgin ka lɛn da an NDC Parliament dim la pian'a-pian'ad.
english: Iddrisu served as the Ranking Member of the Parliamentary Select Committee on Communications and also the Minority Spokesman on Communications in the Fourth Parliament when the National Democratic Congress, his party was in opposition.

kusaal: O da lɛm paam Parliament kʋk la 2008 Parliament vɔɔtʋg saŋa.
english: He retained his seat in the 2008 parliamentary election by gaining 78.2% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O da zanl kpɛuŋ kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb, wʋʋ Communication minista Atta Mills nɛ Mahama nam Gɔmina na'am saŋa ka lɛm da an Trade minista 2013 nɛ 2014.
english: He has held various positions in government, including Minister for Communications under the Mills and Mahama administrations, and Minister for Trade and Industry from 2014 to 2017.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ka o an minista tis Employment nɛ Labour Relation President Mahama saŋa la 2014.
english: He was appointed the Minister for Employment and Labour Relations by President Mahama in July 2014.

kusaal: O mɔr biis atan' ka yit Tamale linɛ bɛ Northern Ghana.
english: He is a married Muslim, has 3 children, and hails from the Northern Region of Ghana., Tamale.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ an NDC dim la kpeem Ghana Parliament lin yi Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayopɔi.
english: He is a member of the ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing Tamale South.

kusaal: Haruna Iddrisu du'a nɛ Yʋʋm tusa piinɛ awai nɛ pisyɔpɔi (1970) la ni Tamar teŋin, Ghana.
english: Haruna Iddrisu was born in 1970 at Tamale, Ghana.He started his early education at Kulikuli school.

kusaal: La'an nɛ Ma'asim tiig NDC president la da pʋ di na'am laa, on da paam NDC na'am la 2016 ka ba da gaŋ o ka o an NDC Parliament dim la kpeem.
english: Even though his party lost the Presidential Elections, Haruna retained his seat in the 2016 Elections and was selected to lead the minority caucus as the Minority Leader of the 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic in Ghana.

kusaal: Haruna Iddrisu yʋʋm 2020 laa, o da tis piini linɛ an sibiti dɔɔg Duunyin teŋkpɛŋ Northern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim laafi yɛla teŋkpɛŋ kan la.
english: In January 2020, Haruna Iddrisu donated a CHPS compound to the Duunyin community in the Northern region of Ghana to provide healthcare services to the indigents of the community.

kusaal: Haruna Seidu anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tis Wenchi constituency bɛ Bono region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Alhaji Haruna Seidu is a Ghanaian politician and member of parliament for the Wenchi constituency in the Bono region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o Master's in Business Administration in Marketing nɛ yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015) la ni.
english: He had his Masters in Business Administration in Marketing in 2015.

kusaal: Haruna da anɛ Marketing and Administrative Manager tis Lamini Investment Ghana Limited.
english: Haruna was the Marketing and Administrative Manager for Lamini Investment Ghana Limited.

kusaal: Haruna paasnɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg (NDC) la ni ka an Wadmaani, MP tis Wenchi Constituency.
english: Haruna is a member of NDC and currently the MP for Wenchi Constituency.

kusaal: O da di kʋk la nɛ vɔɔtnam tusa pisi nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (26,068) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.1%) ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid la, George Yaw Gyan-Baffuor da paam vɔɔtnam tusa pisi nɛ atan, kɔbiga nɛ ayi (23,102) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ anu du'al atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (45.3%)
english: He won the parliamentary seat with 26,068 votes making 51.1% of the total vote whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate George Yaw Gyan-Baffuor had 23,102 votes making 45.3% of the total votes.

kusaal: Haruna paas la'askanɛ gɔsid gɔmena ligidiisim suor (Special Budget Committee).
english: Haruna is a member of the Special Budget Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la (January 2022), o da nɔk pɔn'ɔr keeke paala pistan nɛ ayuobʋ (36) tis tadimnam (PWDs) banɛ bɛ Wenchi Municipal la.
english: In January 2022, he donated 36 new wheelchairs to some PWDs in the Wenchi Municipal.

kusaal: O yinɛ Wenchi bɛ Bono region, Ghana la.
english: Haruna was born on 4 February 1974 and hails from Wenchi in the Bono region of Ghana.

kusaal: Haruna Yakubu (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ nu nwadis piiga la dabpisi nɛ naasi daar, 24 October 1955) ka o an Vice-Chancellor tis University for Development Studies.
english: Haruna Yakubu (born 24 October 1955) is a Vice-Chancellor of University for Development Studies.

kusaal: O da maali o Master of Science degree in Physics and Mathematics nɛ yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ naasi la ni (1984) ka tɔlisi maali o Doctor of Philosophy degree in Semiconductor Physics yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yi' la ni (1992), ayi la wʋsa o da maalnɛ Moldova State University, Kishinev, Moldova, USSR.
english: He obtained a Master of Science degree in Physics and Mathematics in 1984 and a Doctor of Philosophy degree in Semiconductor Physics in 1992, both at Moldova State University, Chișinău, Moldova (Moldavian SSR until 1991).

kusaal: O tʋʋm kʋda anɛ Pro-Vice Chancellor tis University of Cape Coast, Chairman of the Governing Council tis Centre for Renewable Energy Studies (CRES), executive member tis Ghana Solar Energy Society, fellow – Council tis Advancement and Support for Education-UK, Associate Member – International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP), and Member – Governing Council tis Foundation for Security and Development in Africa (FOSOA).
english: Previous appointments include Pro-Vice Chancellor of the University of Cape Coast, Chairman of the Governing Council of the Centre for Renewable Energy Studies (CRES), executive member – Ghana Solar Energy Society, fellow – Council for Advancement and Support for Education-UK, Associate Member – International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP), and Member – Governing Council of the Foundation for Security and Development in Africa (FOSOA).

kusaal: Hassan Ayariga (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 4 September 1972) ka o an Ghana nid, ka o nu'ug tʋʋm an onɛ kaan ligidi ka Na'asaal ye accountant la, ka lɛn an kpikpinkpin nɛ politiks nid.
english: Hassan Ayariga (born 4 September 1972) is a Ghanaian accountant and unsuccessful 2016 Ghanaian presidential aspirant.

kusaal: Ayariga da bɛnɛ Accra nɛ Bawku sankanɛ ka o da an biig la, o da kɛŋ Nigeria nɛ o du'adib, ban da lub Limann kuk la zug la.
english: Ayariga spent his childhood in Accra and Bawku, moving to Nigeria with his parents after the overthrow of the Limann administration.

kusaal: O da kɛŋnɛ Ghana Secondary School dinɛ bɛ Tamale la, ka Nigeria la mɛn o da kɛŋnɛ Barewa College dinɛ bɛ Zaria la.
english: He attended Ghana Secondary School in Tamale and then in Nigeria Barewa College in Zaria, but did not earn a degree at Barewa.

kusaal: Ban da ye ba gaŋ onɛ na zi'en an People's National Convention paati piresident 2016 vɔɔtʋg la ni laa, Ayariga da lu nɛ ka Edward Mahama onɛ ka o da nya' nɛ o 2012 vɔɔtʋg la di, ye o zi'enɛ tis paati kan la.
english: In the primaries of the People's National Convention (PNC) for the 2016 general election, Ayariga lost to Edward Mahama, whom he had beaten to become presidential candidate in 2012.

kusaal: O da gɔs ka faaung bɛ li ni ka o yii o mɛŋi zi'el o paati ka li an All People's Congress (APC) 2016 yʋʋm la ni.
english: Alleging electoral misconduct, he left the party to form a new party, the All People's Congress (APC), in 2016.

kusaal: Ka Electoral Commission of Ghana siaki tis o kasɛta gbaʋŋ, nɛ on dɔlis ka mɔr dinɛ nar ye o mɔr ka paam kasɛta gbaʋŋ la.
english: The Electoral Commission of Ghana handed the party a provisional certificate after he met the requisite requirements, and it had since been granted a final certificate.

kusaal: O saam, Frank Abdulai Ayariga, da an MP tisid Bawku Constituency, Hilla Limann yʋʋŋ la ni ka o ma Anatu Ayariga mɛ da anɛ kpikpinkpin pʋ'a.
english: His father, Frank Abdulai Ayariga, was a member of parliament for the Bawku Constituency during the third republic administration of Hilla Limann and his mother, Anatu Ayariga, a business woman.

kusaal: O pittʋ Mahama Ayariga mɛ da an Minister for Youth and Sports ka lɛn an MP tisid Bawku Central Constituency bɛ National Democratic Congress paati la ni.
english: His younger brother Mahama Ayariga was Ghanaian Minister for Youth and Sports from 2013-2015, and he is the current Ghanaian Member of Parliament for the Bawku Central Constituency.

kusaal: Hassan Ayariga bɛ ka tʋm Germany pʋʋgin yʋma bɛdigʋ ka mɔr kpiisʋg ya'amlɛog Ghana nɛ Germany tensʋk.
english: Hassan Ayariga lived and worked in Germany for many years and has business interests in both Ghana and Germany.

kusaal: Onɛ an onɛ zi'el All People's Congress (APC) paati la ka da paasi nya'ad nɛ People's National Convention paati December 2012 president vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Alleging electoral misconduct, he left the party to form a new party, the All People's Congress (APC), in 2016.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ tuonɛ zamis accounting London School of Accountancy ka paam PhD kasɛta gbaʋŋ la yi Atlantic International University ni, di anɛ American distance learning university.
english: Ayariga later attended Atlantic International University, an unaccredited university often described as a degree mill.

kusaal: Hawa Yakubu Ogede (Ba du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ nii nwadisa anu la dabpisi nɛ naasi daar, 24 March 1948 – ka o maal ka'alim yʋʋm yusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa atan la dabpisi daar, 20 March 2007) da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Hawa Yakubu Ogede (24 March 1948 – 20 March 2007) was a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaani paas Fourth Republic of Ghana ka da lɛn an Minister for Tourism ya'as.
english: She was a Member of Parliament in the Fourth Republic of Ghana and also served as Minister for Tourism.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Hawa Yakubu nɛ Tarkwa bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Hawa Yakubu was born at Tarkwa in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Pusiga bɛ Upper East Region.
english: She is a native of Pusiga in the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Yakubu da keŋi o sakur nɛ Zebilla Middle School ka keŋ o secondary school Navrongo Secondary School.
english: Yakubu had her early education at Zebilla Middle School and her secondary education at the Navrongo Secondary School.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ Accra Polytechnic (dinɛ yʋ'ʋn an Accra Technical University) ani ka o da maal diploma in Institutional Management.
english: She had her tertiary education at the Accra Polytechnic (now the Accra Technical University) where she obtained her diploma in Institutional Management.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai la ni (1979), Yakubu da kpɛn'o local council ka sɔ' pʋ nya' nɛ o, ka o da an biigi bɛ constituent assembly dinɛ da sɔb Ghana Third Republic wad gbaʋŋ la.
english: In 1979, Yakubu was elected unopposed to her local council and was the youngest member of the constituent assembly which wrote the constitution of the Ghana's Third Republic.

kusaal: O da lɛn an pʋ'ab kpɛɛm tis United National Convention, na'adɔɔg la da pin'il yʋʋm tuiisr, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai la (1979).
english: She also served as the Women's Leader for the United National Convention when the party was founded in 1979.

kusaal: Yakubu da ianki keŋ London ka lɛb Nigeria military coup da naam yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne la (1981).
english: Yakubu fled to London and later Nigeria when a military coup occurred in 1981.

kusaal: Yʋʋmkan ni, Yakubu da fɛndigi lɛb Ghana ka yʋʋmkanɛ tia'al la, ka o nya' wadmaanib kʋk la Bawku Central district, ka da di la'anɛ on pʋ mɔr na'adɔɔg la.
english: In that year, Yakubu returned to Ghana and, in the following year, contested a seat in parliament from the Bawku Central district, which she won despite being an independent candidate.

kusaal: O da paasnɛ first Parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ tan' yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba yɔpɔi daar (7 January 1993) ban da yɛl ye onɛ di yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi vɔɔtʋg dinɛ da bɛ 29 December 1992 la.
english: She was elected into the first parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana on 7 January 1993 after she was pronounced winner at the 1992 Ghanaian parliamentary election held on 29 December 1992.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da kɔ'ɔŋ kʋk la pian'abaanlʋg yɛla ka gaad Cotonou, Benin ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2000).
english: She then lost the seat under controversial circumstances and moved to Cotonou, Benin until 2000.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne (2001) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi la ni (2002), Zuraan John Kufuor da gaŋ o ye o an Minister of Tourism.
english: In 2001 and 2002, she was appointed to be Minister of Tourism under President John Kufuor.

kusaal: Onɛ da lɛn an Ghana nidib nɔba zugʋ keŋ Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Wadmaannib yin la.
english: She also served at this time as a Ghanaian representative to the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) parliament.

kusaal: O da kpinɛ London, England, dindiig ban'as zug.
english: She died in London, England, due to cancer.

kusaal: O bas nya'aŋnɛ biisa atan, Derek Ayebo o yiiga sid kulug la ni nɛ Amanda nɛ Didi Ogede o sid kulug kanɛ paasi ayi la ni.
english: She is survived by three children, Derek Ayebo from her first marriage and Amanda and Didi Ogede from her second marriage.

kusaal: Fassi ka o kpɛŋ' pɔlitis la, Yakubu da anɛ domestic bursar nɛ kpikpikpin.
english: Prior to entering politics, Yakubu was a |domestic bursar] and a businesswoman.

kusaal: O mɛŋi da zɔti su'ad ti paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne la ni (1991).
english: She lived in voluntary exile until 1991.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2000), o da fɛndigi lɛb Ghana ka lɛn di kʋk la ya'as.
english: In 2000, she returned to Ghana and won back her seat.

kusaal: O kum la saŋa yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2007), ba da pɔtim ye o bɛn'ɛdnɛ dindiig ban'a ka di yuug, din ka o ken London nɛ South Africa ti'ebidi o mɛŋ.
english: At the time of her death in 2007, it was reported that she had been suffering from cancer for quite some time and had sought treatment in London and South Africa.

kusaal: Yakubu da kɔ'ɔŋi o wadmaan kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni (2004).
english: Yakubu lost her parliament seat in 2004.

kusaal: Health Services Workers' Union (HSWU) anɛ trade union dinɛ zi'eni tis baŋir dim banɛ tʋm Ghana nimma'asim lʋgʋrin la.
english: The Health Services Workers' Union (HSWU) is a trade union representing skilled workers in the health sector in Ghana.

kusaal: HSWU paasnɛ Ghana Trades Union Congress.
english: The HSWU is affiliated to the Ghana Trades Union Congress.

kusaal: Kilab la da nya' Glo Premier League, ka da lɛb nya'aŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu la ni (2015).
english: The club participated in the Glo Premier League but was relegated in 2015.

kusaal: Kilab la nam mi'i di (2-time Winner) GHALCA top 4 Competition nɔɔra ayi, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: The club is a two-time winner of the GHALCA top 4 competition in 2005 and 2009, respectively.

kusaal: Banɛ da lɛn an kilab kanɛ an naari di Sports Writers Association of Ghana (SWAG) Cup yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: They are also the last club to win the Sports Writers Association Of Ghana (SWAG) Cup in 2009.

kusaal: Heart of Lions FC da paam tuob kennɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) paae piiga (10) Ghana Premier League la ni ka da naae paas team banɛ aan annsi la yʋʋmkan.
english: Heart of Lions FC were promoted to the Ghanaian Premier League in 2002/2003 league season.

kusaal: Helen Adjoa Ntoso anɛ onɛ ka ba da da du'a o yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii la ni nwadis ayi' la pʋʋgin.
english: Helen Adjoa Ntoso (born February 1958) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana to representing Krachi West constituency in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ntoso yinɛ Kete Krachi dinɛ bɛ Oti Region ka ba da buon ye Volta Region la.
english: Ntoso is from Kete Krachi which was located in the Volta Region until December 2018 when new regions were created.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ St Francis Training College.
english: She completed her post-secondary education at St Francis Training College.

kusaal: O da maali o Advanced Diploma in Education nɛ Lambeth College bɛ London la.
english: She has an Advanced Diploma in Education from Lambeth College in London.

kusaal: O lɛm mɔr Master of Arts (in Conflict Peace and Security) zaba, sumbʋgʋsim yi Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre.
english: She also holds a Master of Arts in Conflict Peace and Security from Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre.

kusaal: O da anɛ onɛ gur biis Elizabeth Hamwod Nursery School la ni din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni ken paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: She was a Senior Child Care taker at Elizabeth Hamwod Nursery School from 2005 to 2007.

kusaal: Helen Ntoso da di'e piini ka li pa'al ye onɛ an Region minista nam la wʋsa onɛ tʋm gaadi ba wʋsa yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu la ni, dinɛ ka African International Magazine da maal.
english: Helen Ntoso won an award for Regional Minister of the Year 2015, organized by West African International Magazine.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana nid ka mɛ nwɛ'ɛd pɔlitis.
english: Helen Adjoa Ntoso (born February 1958) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana to representing Krachi West constituency in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Krachi West n bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim ka an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Helen Adjoa Ntoso (born February 1958) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana to representing Krachi West constituency in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Girimadaan Ntoso anɛ Volta region sʋ'ʋlim minista kʋdʋg.
english: Ntoso is from Kete Krachi which was located in the Volta Region until December 2018 when new regions were created.

kusaal: O da anɛ Wina'am labaar mɔɔn-mɔɔn tis Bright Church Army lin yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni.
english: She was a Missionary for Bright Church Army from 2003 to 2005.

kusaal: Henry Perry (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii nwadisa anii daba awai daar, 9 August 1878 ka o maal ka'alim yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai nwadisa anaasi dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar, 24 April 1969) o da anɛ British bantamweight amateur boxer onɛ da nya'ad twentieth century la pin'ilʋgin.
english: Henry Perry (9 August 1878 – 24 April 1969) was a British bantamweight amateur boxer who competed in the early twentieth century.

kusaal: O da zabi paae quarterfinals yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ anii (1908) Summer Olympics- Bantamweight ni.
english: He lost in the quarterfinals in Boxing at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Bantamweight.

kusaal: O da zabidnɛ nwɛnɛ Harry Perry.
english: He fought as Harry Perry.

kusaal: Perry da di yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ atan (1903) nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ anaasi (1904) Amateur Boxing Association British bantamweight title, ban da zab Columbia ABC yiiŋ la.
english: Perry won the 1903 and 1904 Amateur Boxing Association British bantamweight title, when boxing out of the Columbia ABC.

kusaal: Perry wa'alim da anɛ four feet nine inches amaa ka ba da ye o anɛ hustling, bustling terrifying fighter.
english: Perry was just four feet nine inches in height but was described as a hustling, bustling terrifying fighter.

kusaal: Henry Quartey (ba da du'a o nɛ 12 dawalig nwadig 1971) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Ayawaso Central Constituency kanɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg zug.
english: Henry Quartey (born 12 March 1971) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ayawaso Central Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Otublohum-Accra, tenkanɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Otublohum-Accra, a town in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋi o secondary educations nɛ Hams Secondary School bɛ Dansoman la nɛ Zams Secondary/Technical Schooli bɛ Bolgatanga la.
english: He had his secondary educations at the Hams Secondary School in Dansoman and Zams Secondary/Technical School in Bolgatanga.

kusaal: O da maali o G.C.E. O' level nɛ Osu Presbyterian Senior High School.
english: He had his G.C.E. O'level at Osu Presbyterian Senior High School.

kusaal: O da keŋ Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration maali o postgraduate certificate in Public Administration.
english: He entered Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration and obtained his postgraduate certificate in Public Administration.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ay'i la ni (2012), o da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zugʋ nyi'a Ayawaso Central kʋk la sixth parliament of the fourth republic ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Ayawaso Central seat on the ticket of the NPP sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: O da paas la'asʋg kanɛ gɔsid suoya nɛ lɔɔm la'ad ziib yɛla la nɛ Gender and Children Committee.
english: He was a member of the Roads and Transport Committee as well as Gender and Children Committee.

kusaal: Quartey paas la'akanɛ gɔsid suoya nɛ lɔɔm la'ad ziib yɛla Committee nɛ Appointments Committee.
english: Quartey is a member of Roads and Transport Committee and also a member of the Appointments Committee.

kusaal: O da anɛ CEO tis Krafty Hospitality Services Limited bɛ Accra la din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la (2003) ti paae zina.
english: He was the CEO of Krafty Hospitality Services Limited in Accra from 2003 to date.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Sales and Marketing Manager tis B.B.C Trading din yi yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' (1992) ti paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ (1996).
english: He was also the Sales and Marketing Manager of B.B.C Trading from 1992 to 1996.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ ka o lieb Regional Director tis Dalebrook Company Limited din yi yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1997) ken paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998).
english: He later became the Regional Director of Dalebrook Company Limited from 1997 to 1998.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Sales Manager and Director tis Pecoll Aluminiuim Systems yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu (1995) ken paae yʋma tusa ayi' la ni (2000).
english: He was also the Sales Manager and Director of Pecoll Aluminium Systems from 1995 to 2000.

kusaal: O da anɛ Deputy Minista tis Interior.
english: He was the Deputy Minister for Interior.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Deputy Minister tis National Security.
english: He was the Deputy Minister for National Security.

kusaal: Ka yʋ'ʋn an Greater Accra Regional Minista.
english: He is currently the Greater Accra Regional Minister.

kusaal: O pu'a anɛ Sybil Ansah Quartey ka ba mɔr biisa ayuobʋ (Biis ayuobʋ).
english: He is married to Sybil Ansah Quartey with six children.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadisa awai la ni (senlʋŋ nwadig 2021), Henry da zi'el nɔɔr ye o na sʋŋ Psalm Adjeteyfio nɛ Ghana siidi tusir yinne nɛ kɔbisnu (GH¢1,500) Nwadig wʋsa.
english: In September 2021, Quartey pledged to support Psalm Adjeteyfio with a monthly stipend of GH¢1,500.

kusaal: Onɛ yʋ'ʋn an Minista tis Greater Accra Region.
english: He served as the Minister for Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Quartey nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne Nwadisa atan' la dabpii nɛ ayi' daar (12 dawalig nwadig 1971).
english: Quartey was born on 12 March 1971.

kusaal: Quartey anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (NPP) nid.
english: Quartey is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Quartey anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Quartey is a Christian.

kusaal: Henry da yɛl ye Psalm's tʋʋma film nɛ entertainment industry Ghana kpɛla ma'ae o suunr pamm ka zi'el nɔɔr.
english: Quartey claimed he was inspired by Psalm's impact in the film and entertainment industry in Ghana, hence the pledge.

kusaal: Henry Yeboah Yiadom-Boachie anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Techiman South Constituency bɛ Brong Ahafo Region kanɛ yʋ'ʋn buon ye Bono East Region la wabʋg na'adɔɔg nɔba zug.
english: Henry Yeboah Yiadom-Boachie is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Techiman South Constituency in the then Brong Ahafo Region now Bono East Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Yiadom-Boachie nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' nwadis anii la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 mɔtul nwadig 1972) ka o yi Nsuta-Techiman bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Yiadom-Boachie was born on 24 August 1972 and hails from Nsuta-Techiman in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di'e kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi GIMPA.
english: He has a certificate from GIMPA.

kusaal: O da maal Bachelor of Arts degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Catholic University Southeastern Africa dinɛ bɛ Nairobi la.
english: He had his Bachelor of Arts degree from the Catholic University Southeastern Africa in Nairobi.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maali o Master of Philosophy yi University of Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga la ni (2010).
english: He further had his Master of Philosophy from the University of Ghana in 2010.

kusaal: Yiadom-Boachie da anɛ Youth Animator tis Ondo-Nigeria don Bosco Center din yi yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai la mi (1999) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' (2000) la ni.
english: Yiadom-Boachie was the Youth Animator at the Ondo-Nigeria don Bosco Center from 1999 to 2000.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Vice Principal nɛ Youth Coordinator tis Don Bosco Technical School din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la ni (2003) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anu (2005).
english: He also was the Vice Principal and Youth Coordinator of Don Bosco Technical School from 2003 to 2005.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Project Coordinator nɛ Education Director tis Orphan Aid Africa din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009).
english: He was also the Project Coordinator and Education Director of Orphan Aid Africa from 2005 to 2009.

kusaal: O da anɛ Project Coordinator nɛ Community Development Officer tis Newmont Ahafo Development dinɛ bɛ Ntotroso la ka lɛn an Kenyasi Ahafo Mines din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2009) I paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: He was also the Project Coordinator and Community Development Officer of Newmont Ahafo Development in Ntotroso and also Kenyasi Ahafo Mines from 2009 to 2016.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaani tis Techiman South Constituency din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la mi (2017) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021).
english: He was the member of parliament of Techiman South Constituency from 2017 to 2021.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) kanɛ da an Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, o da di Techiman South wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (37,257) ka li an vɔɔt pisnu du'al pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (50.47%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin, ka ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, NDC wadmaan na'anyi'ad, Adjei Mensah da paam vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ anu nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (35,684) ka li an vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ anii du'al pistan' nɛ atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (48.33%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin, ka PPP wadmaan na'anyi'ad, Sumaila Ibrahim da paam vɔɔt kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (886) ka li an vɔɔt yinne du'al pisi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (1.20%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, he won the Techiman South parliamentary seat with 37,257 votes making 50.47% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Adjei Mensah had 35,684 votes making 48.33% of the total votes cast and the PPP parliamentary candidate Sumaila Ibrahim had 886 votes making 1.20% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Wabʋg na'adɔɔg wadmaannib vɔɔtʋgin kanɛ da bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) la, o da pʋ nyi'a ye ba lɛn vɔɔt o ya'asa ka da bas suori tis Martin Kwaku Adjei-Mensah Korsah ka o da nyi'a.
english: During the New Patriotic Party parliamentary primaries in 2020, he did not file his nomination for re-election which paved way for Martin Kwaku Adjei-Mensah Korsah.

english: Henry Yiadom Boakye (born 12 May 1969) is a Ghanaian politician who served as the Member of Parliament for the Akwatia Constituency in the Seventh Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Henry Yiadom Boakye da maali o Diploma in Engineering yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (1989).
english: He obtained his Diploma in Engineering in 1989.

kusaal: Henry Yiadom Boakye da lɛn di yʋʋm tusa ay nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la National Democratic Congress zug nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ awai, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ awai (19,899) pinu nɛ yinne dua'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.5%) ka keŋ paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la ni ka bas, Ernest Kumi onɛ bɛ New Patriotic Party ka paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anii, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayi (18,742) pisnaasi nɛ anii dua'al anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (48.5).
english: Henry Yiadom Boakye won again in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress with 19,899 votes (51.5%) to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana against Ernest Kumi of the New Patriotic Party who had 18,742 votes (48.5).

kusaal: Henry Yiadom Boakye paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Youth, Sports and Culture yɛla.
english: Boakye is a member of the Youth, Sports and Culture Committee.

kusaal: O lɛn paas Privileges Committee Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana republic kan ɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He is also a member of the Privileges Committee of the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Henry Yiadom Boakye nɛ ka yi Akwatia bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana.
english: Boakye was born and hails from Akwatia in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

english: Boakye contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Akwatia Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Hilda Effiong Bassey ba da dʋa ɔ nɛ dabis pisi wadisa awai la ni yʋʋm tʋsir kɔbuswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu ka ɔ yit Nsit Ubium Gomena zin'ig kane bɛ Akwa Ibom.
english: Hilda Effiong Bassey was born on 20 September 1995, and she is from the Nsit Ubium Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State.

kusaal: O da diɛ gbang nidib nɛ tɛns zamisug ni on da naae Madonna University linɛ bɛ Okija, Anambra State.
english: She graduated with a degree in sociology from Madonna University, Okija, Anambra State.

kusaal: Onɛ da sin'iŋ linɛ ka ba bʋon ye dim'mi fʋ ligidi bɛn ka ba gosidi li Pop Central TV.
english: She was the host of Dine on a Budget, a television show that airs on Pop Central TV.

kusaal: Tuɔngatib banɛ bɛ Nigeria ka mɛ da gɔsid Hilda dʋgib la anɛ Lagos Gomena, Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu; Harvester International pʋ'ʋsim dim karimsa'am kpɛɛm, Bolaji Idowu, Nigeria onɛ di'ɛ yʋ'ʋma piini, Tiwa Savage, Tim Godfrey, Ice Prince.
english: High-profile Nigerians who visited Hilda include Governor of Lagos State, Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu; Lead Pastor of Harvester International, Bolaji Idowu, Nigerian award-winning singer, Tiwa Savage, Tim Godfrey, Ice Prince.

kusaal: Nigeria zugdaan ya'andɔl saŋkan la, Professor Yemi Osinbajo mɛ da bʋɔl Hilda ye o kpɛmisʋ o dugigaadtaaba la ni.
english: Then-Vice President of Nigeria, Yemi Osinbajo, also called to cheer Hilda up during the cook-a-thon.

kusaal: Hilda Effiong Bassey (ba dʋa o nɛ dabis pisi wadisa awai la ni yʋʋm tʋsir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu), bɛdigu mi o nɛ Hilda Baci, o dʋgidnɛ diib ka yit Nigeria, o mɔr diib zi'ig, ka maan bʋŋosida, ka nam mi di Guiness dʋnia wusa onɛ dʋgi gaad sɔ wusa (adʋgi'gaadtaaba ni) awa nam piswai nɛ atan nɛ mid piinɛ yin'nɛ wadisa anʋ la ni yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ pisinɛ atan la, li pʋ yʋʋgɛ yʋʋm kan ni ka Alan Fisher ɔnɛ yit Irish da dugi gaad o nɛ awa nam kɔbuga nɛ piinɛ awai nɛ mid pisnʋ nɛ ayɔpoi.
english: In November 2023, Hilda Baci lost her Guinness World Record title for the longest cooking marathon by an individual to Alan Fisher, an Irish chef.

kusaal: Atilata daar, wadisa anʋ la dabis piinɛ ayʋobɔ, yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisinɛ atan ka onɛ piandi tisid Guinness dʋnia gbana ni la da yɛl ye "ti mi yɛ fʋ mukid, ti gʋr nɛ linɛ an kasɛta ye ti tisi ti gbana dim la yiiga ka na'an sɔb ye li anɛ sida".
english: On Tuesday, May 16, 2023, Guinness World Records spokesperson released an official statement on its website saying: "We are aware of the record attempt and are looking forward to receiving the evidence for our Records Management Team to review before we can confirm the record is official."

kusaal: Hilda da pa'am sʋŋir bɛdigʋ yit Nigeria dim banɛ da kɛŋa adugigaadtaaba la zin'igin la, ka bam mɛ mɔri o yu'uri bɛ nidib la'asig zin'ig.
english: Then-Vice President of Nigeria, Yemi Osinbajo, also called to cheer Hilda up during the cook-a-thon.

kusaal: Sapal saŋa yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisinɛ atan la, Hilda Baci da gʋ'oŋ Guinness dʋnia wusa adugigaadtaaba tis Alan Fisher onɛ yit Iris ka mɛ dʋgid.
english: In November 2023, Hilda Baci lost her Guinness World Record title for the longest cooking marathon by an individual to Alan Fisher, an Irish chef.

kusaal: Baci da pʋ'ʋs Fisher ye o mɔya nɛ on di la ka yel ye o sunr malisi o yela nɛ on nyaŋi gaadi o la.
english: Baci congratulated Fisher on his achievement and said she was proud of him for breaking her record.

kusaal: Ho Technical University, ka ba da buon Ho Polytechnic, anɛ gɔmɛna university sakur kanɛ bɛ Volta Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Ho Technical University, formerly Ho Polytechnic, is a public tertiary institution in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Polytechnic wada ni (PNDC wada kɔbistan' nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ) da gaad ya ka Polytechnics wada paal (Act 745) da kɛna di'e li nɔbiri bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi, Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig la ni.
english: The Polytechnic Law (PNDC Law 321) was replaced in September 2007 by the Polytechnics Act (Act 745).

kusaal: University la zi'elkpan anɛ Adanu Nazu kekeli, ka li gbin pa'al ye Adanu nie nyain.
english: The Motto of the University is Adanu Nazu kekeli which means Adanu become light.

kusaal: University la pa'an Master of Technology (MTech) zamisig , Bachelor of Technology (BTech) zamisig, Higher National Diploma (HND) nɛ nu'ug tʋʋma zamisa.
english: The University offers Master of Technology (MTech) Programmes, Bachelor of Technology (BTech) Programmes, Higher National Diploma (HND) and Non-Tertiary Programmes.

kusaal: Master of Technology (MTech) zamisig la tɔ'ɔŋ nɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) ka ba mɔr saŋa kɛn ka ba zamisidi ba, ka li pa'al ye ba zamisig la mɔr buudi ayi'.
english: Master of Technology (MTech) Programmes are affiliated to the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) on sandwich basis.

kusaal: Polytechnic la da pin'il tʋʋma bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii ka da anɛ nu'ug tʋʋma sakur ka ba zamisig da an nu'ug tʋʋma pa'alig.
english: The Polytechnic started in 1968 as a technical institute with the primary goal of providing pre-technical education.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ ni, sakur la da kilim Polytechnic.
english: In 1986, the institution was upgraded into a Polytechnic.

kusaal: Amaa, li da anɛ ala paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' ni ka wada da kɛna tisi li paŋ ka li yʋ'ʋn zi'en nyali ye li anɛ kpɛɛmnam sakur, ka mɔr suor ka ba zamis nidib banɛ paae Higher National Diploma (HND) nɛ Degree zin'is ni.
english: However, it was not until 1993 that it got full backing of the law (Polytechnic Law 321) to become a fully-fledged tertiary institution, charged with the responsibility of training students to the Higher National Diploma (HND) and Degree Levels.

kusaal: Ho Technical University anɛ tɛŋ la kpɛɛmnam sakur yinnɛ bɛ Volta Region.
english: Ho Technical University is one of the premier national tertiary institutions in the Volta Region.

kusaal: University la nya'ar da yinɛ Ho Technical Institute ni na, linɛ da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii ni, ye ba zamis nidib nu'ug tʋʋma pa'alig kati wa'ae la'ad maalig nɛ ya' mɛɛb ni.
english: The University has its antecedents in the former Ho Technical Institute, which was established in 1968 to provide pre-technical training courses in various engineering and building trades.

kusaal: Ban da ti'aki li yi Technical Institute lɛbis Polytechnic yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ ni la, li da nan pʋ pin'il tʋʋma, li da mɔr wala paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' ni ka wada da kɛna tisi li paŋ (PNDC wada 321 ACT 745) ka li yʋ'ʋn kilim kpɛɛmnam sakur ka tʋmi li tʋʋma lin nar si'em.
english: Though the Technical Institute was re-designated a Polytechnic in 1986, it was not until 1993 that it got the full backing of the law (PNDC Law 321 as amended by ACT 745) to become a tertiary institution with statutory objectives and functions.

english: Ho Technical University has five faculties and they are listed below.

english: Its capital is Dzolokpuita.

english: It shade a common boundary with the Ho municipality to the south, the south Dayi to the north west and the Afadzato south to the north east.

kusaal: Ho West yadigi paaenɛ li ya-dagɔbʋg lɛbid ya-nya'aŋ linɛ tɔn titɔndiŋ nɛ Adaklu ka North Tongu district linɛ bɛ Volta region la.
english: Ho West also stretches to its south eastern boundary with the Adaklu and the North Tongu district in there Volta region.

kusaal: Ho West Constituency anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm kanɛ paasi ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni mɛn.
english: Ho West is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ho West anɛ zi'ikanɛ kpi'e nɛ Ho West District linɛ bɛ Ghana Volta Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Ho West is located is in the Ho West District of the Volta Region of Ghana.

english: Hohoe North is located in the Hohoe Municipal district of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li ya-dagɔbʋg baba lɛbnɛ nɛ Hohoe South constituency baba.
english: Its southern neighbour is the Hohoe South constituency.

english: Hohoe North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Holy week procession, ken ni wʋsa ba ya'asidi yin-yin ka Passion of Christ bɛɛ Marian fɔɔtʋ nam bɛ, la'am nɛ bay is sieba bas woo allegorical step of saints.
english: Each procession of Holy Week has processional floats and steps, which are often religious images of the Passion of Christ, or Marian images, although there are exceptions, like the allegorical steps of saints.

kusaal: Catholic pʋ'ʋsim la nimbaanl zɔɔr kanɛ bɛ Guatemala nananna nwa la niŋ nɛ woo nyalʋŋ nɛ lieb si'im, si'is nidib la ka li anɛ syncretism kanɛ bɛ Mayan pʋ'ʋsim nɛ Catholic pʋ'ʋsim wada tensʋk.
english: The Catholic fervor that currently exists in Guatemala has almost magical and mystical dyes due to the syncretism between the Mayan religion and the Catholic doctrine; it combines elements dating from the old American cultures and from Catholicism imposed by the Spanish in the Colonial era.

kusaal: Syncretism kpɛn anɛ woo pipiʋŋ ka ba gʋli niŋ sawdust carpet ni Crista pʋ'ʋsim malʋŋ kenning, bɔzugɔ pipiʋŋ la da ka' nɛ bʋn-iandiri tis Maya.
english: Syncretism appears in subtle factors such as figure drawing of a butterfly on the sawdust carpet for a Christ procession, because the butterfly was more than a mere insect for the Maya.

kusaal: Li da pʋ tɔi tis teŋin dim la nɛ ban na si'ak Holy Trinity la bɛllim, bɔzugɔ ban mi' ye, banɛ naam dunia la anɛ atan', ka maya mittib mi' b aka ba anɛ "G1", "G2" and "G3", ka kʋ nwaasim Virgin Mary, bɔzugɔ ba da zaŋ o ka'o anɛ lxchel- nwadig la, vʋm daan- ma, the moon, creative life- mother.
english: For the natives it was not difficult to understand or accept the existence of the Holy Trinity because for them, the creators of this world were three, known by Mayan scholars as "G1", "G2" and "G3"; neither was to assimilate Virgin Mary, because they associated her with Ixchel -the moon, creative life- mother.

kusaal: Bakɔi Sʋŋ da naam nɛ Council of Nicea –Roman Emperor Constantine I da zi'eli li 325 A D yʋʋm la ni –bɔzugʋ council kan ni ba da gban'ae ka ban a maal la aluak kimsa malʋŋ nɛ ban na gɛlig kimsa la dabisa la si'em.
english: Holy Week was created in the Council of Nicea – set up by the Roman Emperor Constantine I in the year 325 A.D.- because in that council it was decided when to celebrate Passover and how to calculate the date for the celebration.

kusaal: Li nya'aŋa Knights Templar da tis wada kɛ ka li sʋŋ Passion of Christ ka li nɔbig.
english: Subsequently, the Order of the Knights Templar promoted the praise for the Passion of Christ.

kusaal: Wada la da lɛn kae la, -close order fourteenth century –Franciscans da pɛsigi ba mɛŋ tis ye ba na mɔr malʋŋ la li an si'em la ka ti'akir kʋ naami li nii, banɛ da mɔri Via Crucis kena, malʋŋ la sankanɛ nidib kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ye bɛ Holy Week festivities la ni.
english: After the disappearance of that order, -close order fourteenth century - the Franciscans were dedicated to preserve the traditions that had been acquired over time; they were the ones who developed the Via Crucis, one of the most representative aspects of the Holy Week festivities.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs yɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu, 1765 la ni, Spanish Crown da yis Bourbon reforms kanɛ da an ye ba lɛbi zaŋi ba paŋ la ka paas lampo di'esig teŋ banɛ ka ba kpɛn faan bɛla, power over the colonies and increase tax collection.
english: In 1765 the Bourbon reforms were published by the Spanish Crown, which sought to recover the real power over the colonies and increase tax collection.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan ni ya'as, ba da maal Royal Treasury la kpikpiŋ buudi anaasi San Salvador, Ciudad Real, Comayagua nɛ León ka Guatemala teŋgbaʋŋ la zanlim nɛ li pʋdigir tiaki an 15 provinces.
english: That same year, four sub-delegations of the Royal Treasury were created in San Salvador, Ciudad Real, Comayagua and León and the political and administrative structure of the Captaincy General of Guatemala changed to 15 provinces.

kusaal: These have sort to excessive economic power of some brotherhood, their large number, the lack of administrative and fiscal control by the authorities and public manisfestations of piety, the latter listed as signs of backwardness and fanaticism, especially those of Holy Week.
english: These laws sought to limit excessive economic power of some brotherhoods, their large number, the lack of administrative and fiscal control by the authorities and public manifestations of piety, the latter listed as signs of backwardness and fanaticism, especially those of Holy Week.

kusaal: Ban da kad Aycinena Clan n yisi ba bas yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs nii nɛ pisi nɛ awai 1829 ni la nya'aŋ, liberals la da kad regula orders la bas ka kɛ nɛ secular clergy la ma'aa teŋin la, ba lɛɛ da pʋ maki zi'el mandatory tithing na an si'em.
english: After the overthrow and expulsion of members of Aycinena Clan in 1829, the Liberals ousted the regular orders and just left the secular clergy in the country, although without the fixed income from mandatory tithing.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛŋa da gɛɛns Catholic pʋ'ʋsim la Guatemala teŋin, amaa liberal gɔbina zugraan Mariano Gȧlvez da gʋ'ʋŋ ye o kad cholera morbus wiim yis la nya'aŋ, maanmaan kpɛɛmnam da nya'as kpaadbibis la wʋsa ka ba zan'as o, ka Rafael Carrera kpɛŋ saŋa la, ka kad Gȧlvez nɛ liberal yis kpiʋŋin.
english: This greatly weakened the Catholic Church in Guatemala, but after the failure of liberal governor Mariano Gálvez to combat an epidema of cholera morbus, parish priests incited the peasant population against him, and under the leadership of Rafael Carrera, drove Gálvez and liberal out of power.

kusaal: Yʋʋm piiga nya'aŋ gɔbina ni, Carrera da bas sour ka regular orders nɛ conservative ellite Catholics lɛb na, ka yɛli digil ka compulsory tithing lɛbna ya'as, ka sʋŋii kpɛmis pʋ'ʋsim la teŋin la ka ba pa'ali ba yadda niŋir woo Holy Week n nyɛ nɔbigir si'em la.
english: After a decade of government, Carrera allowed the return of the regular orders and conservative elite Catholics and authorized compulsory tithing again, reinforcing the church in the country and the manifestations of faith such as Holy Week flourished.

kusaal: Sida, yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs nii nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi, 1852 ni la Guatemala nɛ Holy see la da tik nu'ug nɛ concordat ka li da bɛnɛ yuoliŋ la nu'usin ye ba gɔs ka Guatemala teŋ nidib la paam gbaʋŋ zamisig baŋir ka da sʋŋi kpɛmis pʋ'ʋsim dim sʋ'ʋlim nam la wʋsa ka ba naalim taab, church state union in the country was reinforced.
english: Indeed, in 1852, Guatemala and the Holy See signed a concordat in which the latter was entrusted with the education of the Guatemalan population and church-state union in the country was reinforced.

kusaal: Conservative saŋa la ni da gʋ'ʋŋ la nya'aŋ ka liberal da di ya'an yʋʋm yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs nii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne, 1871 ni la, Catholic pʋ'ʋsim la da nyɛ saansigi ba kpikpiŋ nɛ ba malima ni woo lin da naam si'em yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs nii nɛ pisi nɛ awai ni la ka ba da namis Francisco Morazȧn liberal gɔbina nu'usin si'em la.
english: After the fall of the Conservative regime and the Liberal victory in 1871, the Catholic Church suffered renewed attacks on its economic and political influence, as happened in 1829 when it was attacked by the Liberal government of Francisco Morazán.

kusaal: Sigsaa nwadig la ni, yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs nii nɛ piswai nɛ yinne, 1891 ni la, Pope Leo xIII da yisi o Rerum Novarum encyclical-tʋmtʋmnib la bɛ si'em-gbaʋŋ kanɛ da sʋŋ Catholic pʋ'ʋsim nidib ka ba paam tiakir ka nyaŋi bɛi nɛ liberal states la; Guatemala teŋin nɛɛ, yam paal da sʋŋi kpɛmis baŋir nwa nɛ fɔɔtʋ namin nɛ pian'ad namin kɛ ka li paae yadda ni ye li kɛ ka liberal state la tun'oe tɔlisid labaya sʋŋa.
english: In May 1891, Pope Leo XIII issued his Rerum Novarum encyclical -The situation of workers- key document that helped Catholic Church parishes gradually transform to fit in liberal states; in Guatemala this reorganization was reinforced by a new form of reproduction of ideas expressed in the press whose images and speeches were sent to the faithful for an efficient postal service developed by the Liberal State.

kusaal: Catholicism nɔbigir United States da pin'ili an zanbin in the reconquest of ideological power in totally liberal states.
english: The progress of Catholicism in the United States began to serve as an example in the reconquest of ideological power in totally liberal states.

kusaal: Catholicism da paam paŋ José Maria Reyna Barrios gɔbina la saŋa (1892-1898), barika pʋ'ʋsim kenɛ tisidi o gɔbina la saŋa kanɛ da bas sour tis secular clergy nɛ on da bɔɔd ye art nɛ defence of local culture widig zin'ig wʋsa, linɛ da kɛ k'o siak ka paas Berne Convention, ka na'asid yadda niŋir pa'alig kanɛ ka ba pa'an Passion of Christ sour ken malʋŋin la.
english: There was a strengthening of Catholicism during the government of General José María Reyna Barrios (1892–1898), thanks to the political opening of his government to secular clergy and his concern for the dissemination of art and the defense of local culture, which led him to subscribe to the Berne Convention, respecting the popular manifestations of faith, expressed primarily in the processions of the Passion of christ.

kusaal: Ba da nyaŋi maal nɛŋa nɛ la'an nɛ Reyna Barrios da an high degree Freemason.
english: And this was accomplished even though Reyna Barrios was a high degree Freemason.

kusaal: Jacobo Arbenz saŋa la luub nya'aŋa, Catholic pʋ'ʋsim la da lɛn di'e o kpi'ʋŋ kanɛ k'o da mɔri conservative government of Rafael Carrera in the 19th century la ya'as, lin pʋʋgin laa, a sʋ'ʋe m mɛŋ pʋ'ʋsim zamisig da paam nɔbigir lin da yi yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛpisnu nɛ anu, 1955 ni la ken, mittib da yɔ'ɔs sakuya bɛdigʋ tis biribis banɛ da pʋn ken secular gɔbina sukuya la ka ba kpɛn.
english: After the fall of Jacobo Arbenz regime, the Catholic Church regained some of the power he had had during the Conservative government of Rafael Carrera in the nineteenth century, and as part of it, private religious education boomed from 1955 on, with the founding of several elite schools for boys which absorbed the elite students who had previously attended classes in secular government institutions.

kusaal: Ba da yɛli zi'el ye pʋʋ'ʋsim zamisig anɛ fʋ yam ya' bɔɔdi li official premises zin'igin: teŋ la wada gbaʋŋin, article 97 pa'al ye wada la na gɔsid pʋ'ʋsim zamisig yɛla official premises ni, amaa ka teŋ la da pʋ titta ka lɛɛ ye li anɛ yam bɔɔdim.
english: religious education was declared optional in official premises: Article 97 of the Constitution states that the law would regulate regard to religious education in official premises and that the State did not impart but declared optional.

kusaal: Rossell y Areliano da pin'ili mɔɔn nɛ kpi'eʋŋi bɔɔd ye o lɛbis Catholicism Guatemala ya'as: o da keŋ paae nɛ Arcbishop palace nɛ Bishop Francisco Marroquin yinɛ bɛ San Juan del Obispo, Sacatepequez, Moraug nwadig la dapisi nɛ ayi daar, yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' July 22, 1953 ni la, o da di'e maanmaanib, fathers Antonio Rodriguez Pedrazuela nɛ José Maria Bȧscones banɛ da pin'il Opus Dei tʋʋma la Guatemala teŋin; ka yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai ni la ka ba da maal yiiga Central American Eucharistic Congress.
english: Rossell y Arellano started an aggressive campaign to get Catholicism back in Guatemala: he restored the Archbishop's Palace and the residence of Bishop Francisco Marroquín in San Juan del Obispo, Sacatepequez; on July 22, 1953 he received fathers Antonio Rodríguez Pedrazuela and José María Báscones who began the work of Opus Dei in Guatemala; and in 1959 held the First Central American Eucharistic Congress.

kusaal: Bibi'el o da ti paam kɛ ka regular orders lɛb Guatemala teŋin na paas Second Vatican Council, kan ka Pope John xxIII da gɔsi li yɛla.
english: Gradually he managed the get regular orders back to Guatemala and participated in several sessions of the Second Vatican Council, organized by Pope John XXIII.

kusaal: Yʋʋma ken aka gaad, ka sour ken nɛ labaya tisib yɛla paam nɔbigir, a ken ɛ kaad pʋ'ʋsim zink nɛ pʋ'ʋsidi tit Esquipulas Wina'am la ka the city "Latin American Capital of Faith" maal la yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ, 1956 la ni, Pope Pius xxIII da duoe Prelature Nullius Cristi of Esquipulas zi'el kanɛ ka Municipality of Esquipulas nɛ li Cathedral Sanctuary da pin'ili li.
english: In 1956 Pope Pius XII erected the Prelature Nullius Cristi of Esquipulas, which is formed by the Municipality of Esquipulas and its cathedral Sanctuary.

kusaal: Ban da gaŋ Pope la kʋ da an Prime Esquipulas Prelate Arcbishop Rossell y Arellano.
english: The Pope also appointed as Prime Esquipulas Prelate Archbishop Rossell y Arellano.

kusaal: Rossell yɛlkpan yiiga daan da anɛ o kɛ ka pʋ'ʋsim dim la gɔsid pʋ'ʋsim yir la yɛla; link a ba da mak bʋ si'em ka gʋ'ʋŋ, o da mɔɔ nyaŋi paam sʋŋir Benedictine Abbey of San José Louisiana teŋi bɛ United States la.
english: One of the first concerns of Rossell was seeking a religious community to take over the pastoral care of the temple; after many failed initiatives, he managed to find support from the Benedictine Abbey of San José in Louisiana, United States.

kusaal: On palm Sunday of 1959, Vanma'asa Lasiddaar yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai ni la, Benedictine monks nama atan' yiiga dim la da ken Esquipulas na pin'il Monastery.
english: On Palm Sunday of 1959, the first three Benedictine monks arrived at Esquipulas and founded the Benedictine Monastery.

kusaal: Holy week in Guatemala (Bakɔi Sʋŋ) Guatemala anɛ Wina'am pʋ'ʋsim kaanbʋg malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba maanɛ dɔlsid suoraʋg zugʋ pa'anɛ ba yadda nigir, ka ba buon ye prossesion (ken), "hermandad" n gɔti li yɛla.
english: Semana Santa or Holy Week in Guatemala is celebrated with street expressions of faith, called processions, usually organized by a "hermandad".

kusaal: Spanish in the colonial era da zaŋ America kʋdʋg buudi malima nɛ Catholic pʋ'ʋsim malima la'asi ba paas kaanbʋg la ni.
english: The Catholic fervor that currently exists in Guatemala has almost magical and mystical dyes due to the syncretism between the Mayan religion and the Catholic doctrine; it combines elements dating from the old American cultures and from Catholicism imposed by the Spanish in the Colonial era.

kusaal: Fɔɔtʋ kaŋa nwa pʋ bɛ zin'isia Bakɔi Sʋŋ kaanbʋg malʋŋ la ni Spain teŋin nɛ.
english: That image does not appear anywhere in Holy Week activities held in Spain.

kusaal: A na niŋ si'em ka gban'ae dʋnbama nwa Guatemala Bakɔi Sʋŋ la gbin anɛ fʋn na lɛb nya'aŋi gɔs Maya pʋ'ʋsim zin'igin, ka malima la da nwɛni li si'ali nɛ teŋ la din, ka linɛ da na kɛ ka America teŋ dim la si'ak Catholic pʋ'ʋsim malima la.
english: To understand the current Guatemalan Holy Week one must go back to the religion of the Maya, where there were amazing coincidences that perhaps helped the Catholic religion fit more with the beliefs of Native Americans.

kusaal: Nwɛnnim la yinne anɛ Guatemala teŋ dim la da ziidi ba nidib banɛ da mɔr arizak nɛ na'anam ken katens, palanquin pʋʋgin, transport wealthy citizens and rulers.
english: One of these similarities is that indigenous Guatemalans used a palanquin to transport wealthy citizens and rulers.

kusaal: Ya'aŋ ka ba da tiaki maani li dɔlisid suoya, ani ka nidib pa'ani ba taal, people took to the street to express their guilt.
english: Later they evolved into processions where people took to the streets to express their guilt.

kusaal: Tias bama nwa ni, ba da maal wada zi'el ye li gɔsid kpikpiŋ yɛla woo alcoholic beerages maalʋg, snuff, gunpowder, playing cards nɛ cock fights nam wʋsa maalʋg.
english: With these reforms, specific trade regulators were created to control the production of alcoholic beverages, snuff, gunpowder, playing cards and cock fights.

kusaal: Ban da pʋdig teŋ la tɔdi tis taab la, Spanish crown da zi'eli wada ka li sie Catholic windɔɔg pʋ'ʋsim la paŋ, to diminish the power of the Catholic Church, paŋ kanɛ da tiing Spanish vassals wʋsa.
english: In addition to this administrative redistribution, the Spanish crown established a policy to diminish the power of the Catholic Church, power that until then was virtually all over the Spanish vassals.

kusaal: Amaa, sour da pʋ bɛ ye regular orders la kpɛn gbaʋŋin nɛ, bɔzugɔ, Guatemala teŋ wada la da kisigi ba bɛllim teŋgbaʋŋ la zug sankan la at the time.
english: However, the official entry of the regular orders was not allowed because the Guatemalan constitution forbid their presence in its soil at the time.

kusaal: Wada na tis sour ka Catholic pʋ'ʋsim nɛ pʋ'ʋsim buudi wʋsa na tun'oe mɔri la'ad ka yisi ba, ka li anɛ ye la'ad la ye li zaŋi tʋm nɛ pʋ'ʋsim tʋʋma, nidib la'asig zin'igin bɛɛ zamisig yɛla, provided they are intended for religious and social work or education.
english: the legal capacity of the Catholic Church-and all other churches- to acquire, hold and dispose of property, provided they are intended for religious and social work or education.

kusaal: Li ye sour mɛ lɛn bɛ ye tʋʋma zin'ig wʋsa dim tun'oe zamis gbaʋŋ, freedom of education in all other establishments.
english: It also guarantees freedom of education in all other establishments.

kusaal: Teŋ la na sʋŋid nɛ pʋ'ʋsim sakuya la maalig: Article 111 yɛl ye a sʋ'ʋ m mɛ sakuya banɛ pa'an nidib la zaalim kʋ yɔɔd lampɔ sieba teɛin la ka lin anɛ piini ba tʋʋm zaal la zug, in compensation for their service.
english: the state would contribute to the maintenance of religious education: Article 111 states that private institutions providing free education will be exempt from certain state and municipal tax in compensation for their services.

kusaal: Freelance photojournalists Diane Summers nɛ Eric Valli yis gbaʋŋ zaŋi ken Honey hunters of Nepal sɔb ye Gurung banɛ bɛ west-central Nepal kpɛn'ɛd mɔɔgin la ye ba ia mɔɔgin siind ka mɔr kʋdʋmin sa la'adi taabid siind la.
english: A documentary by freelance photo journalists Diane Summers and Eric Valli on the Honey hunters of Nepal documents Gurung tribesmen of west-central Nepal entering the jungle in search of wild honey where they use indigenous tools under precarious conditions to collect honey.

kusaal: Honey hunting bɛɛ honey harvesting anɛ fʋn na la'as siindi yi mɔɔgin siins ni.
english: Honey hunting or honey harvesting is the gathering of honey from wild bee colonies.

kusaal: Di anɛ yʋʋmpʋkʋdʋgin tʋʋmanam la yinne ka ba nam maani li bɛ Africa zin'isieba, Asia, Australia nɛ South America.
english: It is one of the most ancient human activities and is still practiced by aboriginal societies in parts of Africa, Asia, Australia and South America. Some of the earliest evidence of gathering honey from wild colonies is from rock painting, dating to around 8,000 BC.

kusaal: Siind taabʋg Nepal mɛ anɛ dinɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ mi' ye wild honey hunting, di mɔr nyɔɔd pamm ba buudi malima ni tis Nepal dim, di kas-kas anɛ teŋin dim, Gurung nɛ Magar sʋ'ʋlimnamin.
english: For centuries the Gurung people of the country of Nepal risked their lives to collect wild cliff-honey.

kusaal: Horezu ceramics anɛ Romanian ya'abʋg malʋŋ kanɛ bɛ di kɔn' ka ba maani li nɛ nu'us tempʋkanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon ye Horezu ka di bɛ northern Oltenia (Vâlcea County), kpi'e nɛ Horezu Monastery teŋkanɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ mi'.
english: Horezu ceramics is a unique type of Romanian pottery that is traditionally produced by hand around the town of Horezu in northern Oltenia (Vâlcea County), close to the famous Horezu Monastery.

kusaal: Di pa'anɛ tuŋ bɛdegʋ mi'ilim nɛ baŋir ya'abʋg ni, dinɛ ta'as ka Horezu ya'abʋg tʋʋma la da paam suori kpɛn' paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) nwadisa ayi Samanpiid nwadig la ni.
english: It reflects many generations of knowledge and skills development of pottery, which is why the craftsmanship of Horezu pottery was inscribed on UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists in December 2012.

kusaal: Colors nam la anɛ brown, red, green, blue nɛ linɛ ka ba buon "Horezu ivory" la.
english: Colors are bright shades of brown, red, green, blue and so called "Horezu ivory".

kusaal: Horezu anɛ zin'ig yinne bɛ historical Romanian ceramic center ka nidib bɛdegʋ ya'abid ka nyɛt ligiidi li pʋʋgin ka ba sieba an: Ogrezeanu, Vicsoreanu, Iorga, Frigura, Mischiu, Popa ka sieba nan kpɛlim.
english: Horezu is a singular historical Romanian ceramic center in which this trade remained the main source of income for many families of potters such as: Ogrezeanu, Vicsoreanu, Iorga, Frigura, Mischiu, Popa etc. Today this craftsmanship is transmitted as always in the family circle, but also in workshops from master to apprentice, and pottery festivals and exhibitions.

kusaal: Horezu banɛ ya'abid la mɔri tʋʋma la'ad banɛ ka ba mɛŋ maal wʋʋ mixer linɛ ka ba mɔri pied ya'ad la, pottery wheel nɛ comb linɛ ka ba mɔri mɛɛd, naaf iil ka li pʋʋgin an vɔɔnr nɛ dakanɛ ka di nɔɔrin an baanlif ka ba mɔri bɔɔnd zabin vɛnla nɛ stove kanɛ ka ba mɔr daadi nyɔ'ɔdi li ye ba nɔki nyɔ'ɔ ba ya'ad la.
english: Horezu potters use many traditional tools like a mixer for cleaning the earth, a pottery wheel and comb for shaping, a hollowed-out bull's horn and a fine wire-tipped stick for decoration, and a wood-burning stove for firing.

kusaal: Ba sua la'ad la ka ba maal la zin'ig kanɛ ka ba buon ye Olari Street bɛ Horezu la, ka ba gɔsidi li ka ya'abid wʋʋ ba yaanami daa maan siem la.
english: This ancient craft is preserved in the ancestral hearth, now known as Olari Street of Horezu, where artisans shape the clay into the same painstaking process as their ancestors did.

kusaal: Huaconada (ka Spain dim buon ye: [wakoˈnaða]) anɛ wa'ab malʋŋ ka ba maani li teŋ kpɛŋ kanɛ yʋ'ʋr an Mito ka di bɛ province of ConcepciónI bɛ central Peruvian Andes.
english: Huaconada (Spanish pronunciation: [wakoˈnaða]) is a ritual dance performed in the village of Mito in the province of Concepción in the central Peruvian Andes.

kusaal: UNESCO da zaŋi li paas Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity ninɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ni.
english: It has been inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO in 2010.

kusaal: Yʋʋmpaal nwadig wʋsa daba atan' banɛ gaad tuon la, dap banɛ niŋ yʋgʋd ka ba buoni ba ye "huacones" wa'andɛ wa'a buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb teŋ la tensʋk.
english: On the first three days of every January, masked men known as "huacones" perform a choreographed series of dances in the center of the village.

kusaal: "Huacones" buudi ayi' bɛ: banɛ yɛɛt malima fuud ka niŋ yʋgʋd banɛ ka ba nwaae ba bi'el-bi'el "ka di pa'an na'asi nɛ zɔtim" nɛ banɛ yɛɛt fubanɛ ka ba maal ka ba maal nananna nwa, "ka di pa'an la'asan'aŋ, sunsan'aŋ, bɛɛ ninla'asim".
english: There are two types of "huacones": those that wear traditional costumes and finely carved masks "inspiring respect and fear," and those that wear modern costumes, "embodying terror, sadness, or mockery." A small indigenous drum called the "tinya" beats out time to which the dance is performed.

kusaal: Nidib baŋ o nɛ on di'e Ric Griffin itʋŋi maan di'ema bɛ BBC One medical drama Holby City (2001–20), nɛ on da maal sini zaba di'ema bɛ Episode I – The Phantom Menace (1999).
english: He is known for his long-running role as Ric Griffin on the BBC One medical drama Holby City (2001–20), and for playing Captain Panaka in the Star Wars film Episode I – The Phantom Menace (1999).

kusaal: Ba len mi' o ka o maan di'ema bɛ Royal Shakespeare Company, o paasi ba lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne sa (1981) ka mɛ an kpɛɛm, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu saŋa sa (2005).
english: He has been a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC) since 1981 and an associate since 2005 and has appeared in many stage productions.

kusaal: O sini si'eba anɛ: Highlander, Nightbreed nɛ Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald.
english: His film work includes Highlander, Nightbreed, and Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yɔpɔi (1987), ba da gaŋ o ye o di'e piini bɛ Laurence Olivier Award for Best Actor ka yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yi (2022), ba da gaŋ o ye o di'e piini bɛ British Academy Television Award for Best Actor di'em kanɛ ka o da di'em an Neville Lawrence ka li yʋ'ʋr an Stephen (2021) la yela.
english: In 1987, he was nominated for the Laurence Olivier Award for Best Actor and in 2022 he was nominated for the British Academy Television Award for Best Actor for playing Neville Lawrence in Stephen.

kusaal: O di'e ya'an piini bɛ Critics' Circle Theatre Award nɛ Emmy Award.
english: He has also won a Critics' Circle Theatre Award and an Emmy Award.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ Accra, Ghana, ka o ma an Emma Wilhelmina (née Phillips; 1917–2004) nɛ Richard Quarshie (1913–2006).
english: Hugh Quarshie was born in Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: Hugh da dɔl o yidimi kɛŋ United Kingdom on da an yʋma atan' la.
english: He emigrated with his family to the United Kingdom at the age of three.

kusaal: O paas Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC) nidib kanl ni, ka maal sini nam bɛdigʋ ka ba si'eba an: the serial Behaving Badly on nɛ Judi Dench.
english: He has also appeared in many television programmes, including the serial Behaving Badly with Judi Dench.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋr yi ya ne on da pʋd o mɛŋ Sunda Kastagir sini kanɛ buon Highlander ni, Captain Panaka sini kanɛ buon Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace ni, nɛ Ric Griffin TV ni di'ema kanɛ buon Holby City la.
english: He is well known for playing the roles of Sunda Kastagir in Highlander, Captain Panaka in Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace, and Ric Griffin on the television series Holby City.

kusaal: O da maal o mɛŋ ye Lieutenant Obutu bɛ sini kanɛ buon Wing Commander la ni.
english: He portrayed Lieutenant Obutu in Wing Commander.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la (2007) o da paas nɛ Doctor Who ka bama maal sini kanɛ an "Daleks in Manhattan"/"Evolution of the Daleks" ani ka ba da buon o ye Solomon, one an Hooverville dim tɛŋ kpɛɛm.
english: He appeared in the 2007 two-part Doctor Who episode "Daleks in Manhattan"/"Evolution of the Daleks" as Solomon, the leader of the shanty town Hooverville.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga, nwadis awai ni la (September 2010), Quarshie da paas sini kanɛ ka ba da maan TV ni ka ba buon ye Who Do You Think You Are?, anina ka o dɔlisi baŋ o Ghana nɛ Dutch buudi.
english: In September 2010, Quarshie featured in an episode of the television genealogy series Who Do You Think You Are?, in which he traced his Ghanaian and Dutch origins.

kusaal: Di'em kan pa'al ye Quarshie paas nimbanɛ mɔr tʋŋ bɛdigʋ, bɔzugɔ, o yaab yinne, Pieter Martinus Johannes Kamerling, da anɛ Dutch nidi bɛ Gold Coast kpala.
english: The episode revealed that Quarshie is part of his country's old mixed-race elite as one of his ancestors, Pieter Martinus Johannes Kamerling, was a Dutch official on the Gold Coast.

kusaal: Quarshie anɛ one bɛ Women's Equality Party na'adɔɔg nya'aŋ.
english: Quarshie was a supporter of the Women's Equality Party.

kusaal: Hugh Anthony Quarshie (ba dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ naasi, naar nwadig, dabpisi nɛ ayi, born 22 December 1954) o anɛ one ka ba dʋ'a o Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka o lɛɛ mɔr British gbaŋ ka an sini maan.
english: Hugh Quarshie was born in Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: Quarshie anɛ Euro-African nid kanɛ yit Ghana, ka lɛɛ mɔr Ghana, English nɛ Dutch ziim o ningbiŋin.
english: Hugh Quarshie was born in Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: O ma' da yinɛ na'anam tʋŋin na; o buudi an na'anami bɛ tɛnkpɛŋ kanɛ bɛ Ghana ka li yʋ'ʋr an Abii.
english: Hugh Quarshie was born in Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: Quarshie da bɔɔd ye o an labadi'es ka nyaan paas o mɛŋ sini maalig ni la.
english: Quarshie has also narrated for television.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ la'as kanɛ buon Star Wars fan event "Star Wars Celebration" la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ wai (1999).
english: He is known for his long-running role as Ric Griffin on the BBC One medical drama Holby City (2001–20), and for playing Captain Panaka in the Star Wars film Episode I – The Phantom Menace (1999).

kusaal: Nwa' da kɛ ka o maal zuod nɛ Dutch sini maan, Antonie Kamerling.
english: This also made him a distant relative of Dutch actor Antonie Kamerling.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛm paas nimbanɛ da yʋm GH Rap dinɛ zi'eni tis 'Hip-hop yʋma dinɛ ka ba maan Ghana' kpala.
english: He is also credited with being among the pioneers of GH Rap which is a term to denote 'Hip-hop made in Ghana'.

kusaal: Yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni ka, Jazzi da tʋmnɛ nɛ banɛ piin banɛ di ya'an TV Commercial by creative Eye, ka ba nɔkid sini la nɛ nu'ubibis tisid telekominikasin dim TIGO bɛ Mumbai, India.
english: In 2009, Jazzi worked on an award-winning TV Commercial by Creative Eye, shot by Fingerprint Films, for the telecommunication company TIGO in Mumbai, India.

kusaal: Jazzi da lɛm anɛ pa'ani bɛ The Unwind Agency, bɛ Ghana kpala ka ba mɔri mɔɔn yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ awai(2009) la ni.
english: Jazzi is also the creative director of The Unwind Agency, a model & advertising agency he founded in Ghana in 2009.

kusaal: Ian du'adib da anɛ Frederick Oshodi nɛ Patience Otuwaa Amponsah bɛ Osu, Accra bɛ Ghana.
english: Ian Jazzi was born to Frederick Oshodi and Patience Otuwaa Amponsah in Osu, Accra in Ghana.

kusaal: O ma la da fedigi yi Lagos lɛb Ghana na o sid Oshodi kum la ya'aŋ.
english: His mother moved back to Ghana after Oshodi's death in Lagos.

kusaal: Jazzi keŋŋɛ Datus Complex School, di DA anɛ sakur kani ka ba kenne gbɛɛd ka bɛ Tema.
english: Jazzi attended the Datus Complex School, a boarding school in Tema.

kusaal: On da an yʋma piiga nɛ ayi(12yrs) la o taʋ kpɛɛm Gifty Jenny onɛ da an yʋʋm piiga nɛ atan'(13yrs) saŋkan la, di da tɔinɛ pamm tis Ian bɔzugɔ ba miilimnɛ taaba hali.
english: When he was twelve, he lost his elder sister Gifty-Jenny who was thirteen at the time and it was very hard on him because they very close.

kusaal: Dinɛ da kpɛmisi o anɛ di'ema yʋ'ʋŋ nɛɛ Hip-hop malima dinɛ da bɛ ba sakurin la, nɛ 90's hip-hop la da kpɛmisʋ pamm.
english: Inspired by the vibrant entertainment nights and hip-hop culture in the school and heavily influenced by the 90's hip-hop scene, he would use his leisure time to beat his desk in the classroom and write rhymes.

kusaal: O da naae ya ka tɔlisi kɛŋ The University Of Ghana, Legon, ani ka o zamis Economis, Mathematics nɛ Theater Arts.
english: Upon graduation, he was admitted into The University of Ghana, Legon, where he studied economics, Mathematics & Theatre Arts.

kusaal: On da bɛ university la ni la o da tʋmnɛ saŋa wʋsa ka recoodi lidii digin, pian'ad campus Radio station la ni, Radio Universe ni.
english: While at university, he continued rapping and began recording and airing singles on the campus radio station, Radio Universe.

kusaal: Yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ piiga, Dɔnwalig Nwadig(March 2010) la ni, Jazzi fa yʋmi yiiga yʋma mixtape, In Stereo Vol.1.
english: In March 2010, Ian Jazzi released his first mixtape, In Stereo Vol.1.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga Sawa'ar Nwadig la ni, Ian Jazzi da yisi o yʋm gɛnda(mixtape) dinɛ pɛɛs ayi, Ian Jazzi da bɛ Heartbeats & other free styles.
english: In October 2010, Ian Jazzi released his second mixtape, Ian Jazzi on the Heartbeats & Other Freestyles.

kusaal: Di anɛ yʋʋm gɛnda (mixtape) kaŋa ni ka onɛ maal yʋmanami tisid nidib Ghana sʋ'ʋlim koala ka ba mi'i hali la Jayso, da pa'ala Ian Jazzi nɛ da maan si'em dɔlisid bʋmw'da la.
english: This mixtape primarily featured Ian Jazzi freestyling over beats by renowned Ghanaian producer Jayso.

kusaal: Di da anɛ yʋʋm gɛnda b anɛ buudi ka ba da maani li yʋm-yʋmidib nwɛnɛ Sarkodie, Sway DaSafo, R2Bees, nɛ Kwaw Kesse.
english: It was a remix of hits produced for artists like Sarkodie, Sway DaSafo, R2Bees, and Kwaw Kesse.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga Sawa'ar Nwadig la ni, Ian Jazzi da yisi o fa yisi o pʋtɛn'ɛri lɛb o tʋʋma zin'igin, din an The Unwind Agency, o da maal tʋʋm nami naae ka yʋ'ʋm mɔɔnɛ tisid tʋʋma zin'isnam nwɛnɛɛ TIGO, Ecobank, nɛɛ Coca-Cola.
english: In October 2010, Jazzi turned his attention to his new company, The Unwind Agency, completing several model and advertising related contracts for companies such as TIGO, Ecobank, and Coca-Cola.

kusaal: O mɛ da yis yʋm pa'ala bɛdigʋ ka banɛ da pɛɛs o anɛ EL, Trigmatic, Jay Foley, Senam E. Twin Gbeho, nɛ Radio Rock/rapper J.O.E.L. Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga(2010) la naarin la, on nɛ o zua EL da la'asi yis yʋm paal dinɛ yʋ'ʋri buon yee ''Envy''.
english: In addition he also released several singles featuring artists like EL, Trigmatic, Jay Foley, Senam E.Twin Gbeho, and Radio Jock/rapper J.O.E.L. In the latter part of 2010 he collaborated with his friend EL and released "Envy".

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ yinne, Fulumfug Nwadig la ni, Ian Jazzi da yis sini yʋm paalig dinɛ yʋ'ʋri buon yee ''The Real'', bɛ In Stereo Volume II - Turn The Volume Up ka niŋ tɔ'ɔ-tɔ'ɔ dɔl nɛɛ ''Envy'', bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ yinne Dɔnwalig Nwadig(March 2011) la ni.
english: In February 2011, Ian Jazzi released his first music video, "The Real", off his upcoming sequel In Stereo Volume II – Turn The Volume Up and quickly followed it up with "Envy", in March 2011.
