english: He ran for Member of Parliament for the Sunyani West constituency and won in the 2008 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt o ya'as ka o lieb Wadmani po sʋ'ʋlim la ni ya'as yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) nɛ tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la (2016).
english: He was re-elected as MP in the same constituency in 2012 and 2016, 2020.

kusaal: Yuʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la Nwadisa anu la ni (dawalig nwadig 2017), Pirɛsidɛn Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Baffour-Awuah ye o paas ministanam pii nɛ awai banɛ na aan o cabinet la.
english: In May 2017, President Nana Akufo-Addo named Baffour-Awuah as part of nineteen ministers who would form his cabinet.

kusaal: On da an Cabinet minista la, Baffour-Awuah da paas nimbanɛ pʋ lal nɛ pirɛsidɛntɛ ka lɛn sʋŋidi gban'ad gban'abanɛ na sʋŋ ka teŋ la nɔbʋg.
english: As a Cabinet minister, Baffour-Awuah is part of the inner circle of the president and is to aid in key decision-making activities in the country.

kusaal: Baffour-Awuah da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid ya yɛla la; o lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Privileges Committee ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Selection Committee.
english: Baffour-Awuah was a member of House Committee; a member of Privileges Committee and also a member of Committee of Selection Committee.

kusaal: O kennɛ Catholic pʋ'ʋsim.
english: He is a Catholic.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ Nwadis anii la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 mɔtul nwadig 1966).
english: He was born on 24 August 1966 and hails from Nsoatre in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn maali o post-graduate diploma in management consultancy nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayopɔi la ni (2017).
english: He also had his post-graduate diploma in management consultancy in 2017.

kusaal: O Na'adɔɔg la kanɛ an NPP la Pirɛsidɛn la da liya.
english: His party, the NPP however lost the presidential election.

kusaal: Onɛ an Wadmaani tis Sunyani West constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: He ran for Member of Parliament for the Sunyani West constituency and won in the 2008 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: Mike Ocquaye buoli ba yʋda.
english: Hon. Prof. Mike Ocquaye.

kusaal: Baffour-Awuah mɔr pu'a nɛ biisa atan'.
english: On February 3, 2025, Baffour-Awuah was arrested by Ghana police service on suspicion of murder.

kusaal: Ilse van Staden (ba da dʋ'a o nɛ 25 March 1983) ka ba da dʋ'a o South African ka o lɛɛ yi Ireland ka paas pʋ'ab rugby union nwɛ'ɛd ka ba dʋ'a o bɛ Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa.
english: Ilse van Staden (born 25 March 1983) is a South African-born Ireland women's rugby union player born in Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa.

kusaal: O nwɛ'ɛdnɛ tisid Cooke WRFC, Ulster Rugby nɛ Ireland pʋ'ab rugby union tiim la onɛ nwɛ'ɛd tuon ka lɛn an onɛ dʋgʋd diibi kuosid nɛ onɛ kʋʋd bʋnkɔnbid.
english: She plays for Cooke WRFC, Ulster Rugby and the Ireland women's national rugby union team as a front row player and is a qualified chef and butcher.

kusaal: Van Staden da pin'ili nwɛ'ɛd rugby tis Correction Services Rugby Club dinɛ bɛ Pretoria, ka naan tɔɔm tiaki keŋ Pretoria Harlequins.
english: Van Staden started playing rugby for Correction Services Rugby Club in Pretoria, before she moved to Pretoria Harlequins.

kusaal: O lɛm paas banɛ nwɛ'ɛdi tisid University of Pretoria(TUKS) zin'ikanɛ ka o nwɛ'ɛd bɛ 15s and 7s.
english: She also lined out for the University of Pretoria(TUKS) where she represented them in both 15s and 7s.

kusaal: O saŋa la ka o da nwɛ'ɛd bɛ Tuks la o da nwɛ'ɛ international 7s nya'ab kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb la'an nɛ Dubai, Reunion, Hong Kong nɛ Rome.
english: During her time at Tuks she played various international 7s tournaments including Dubai, Reunion, Hong Kong and Rome.

kusaal: O da nwɛ' provincial rugby tis Blue Bulls Rugby Union, zin'ikanɛ ka o da nwɛ' nɔɔrin kɔbiga nɛ awai tisi ba.
english: She played provincial rugby for the Blue Bulls Rugby Union, where she made 109 appearances for them.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011) la ni, o da tiaki yii keŋ Northern Ireland ka di paas ban da tiasid baŋir zamisʋg la ka o da pin'ili nwɛ'ɛdi tisid Belfast Harlequins Ladies Rugby ka naan yi keŋ Cooke WRFC bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan (2013) la ni, ka dda liebi ba kpɛɛm (kabiten).
english: In 2011, she moved to Northern Ireland as part of a talent exchange programme where she started playing for Belfast Harlequins Ladies Rugby before moving to Cooke WRFC in 2013, eventually becoming their captain.

kusaal: O da lɛn nwɛ' tis Ulster bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) la ni on da paam buolʋg ye o kena nwɛ' tis Ulster nɛ o tiraan, Claire McLaughlin la.
english: She made her provincial debut for Ulster in 2012 after being called up alongside fellow Ulster player Claire McLaughlin.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni ( 2017), O da nwɛ'ɛ ba Women's Six Nations Championship la gees Scotland women's national rugby union team.
english: In 2017, she made her debut in the Women's Six Nations Championship against the Scotland women's national rugby union team.

kusaal: Yʋʋmkan ni nya'aŋ, ba da pʋ gaŋ o yiiga ye o paasi nwɛ' tis Ireland's 2017 Women's Rugby World Cup la.
english: Later that year, she was not initially selected for Ireland's 2017 Women's Rugby World Cup campaign.

kusaal: Van Staden da anɛ onɛ kʋʋd bʋnkɔnbid bɛ pɔɔgʋn bɛ Straid, County Antrim, Northern Ireland.
english: Van Staden works as a butcher at a farm in Straid, County Antrim, Northern Ireland.

kusaal: Van Staden da paam suor ye o na nyaŋi nwɛ' tis Ireland dɔlisid on da maal gbana ka di pa'al ye o yʋ'ʋn anɛ teŋimbiig la, ba da buol o ye o kena nwɛ' tisi ba national tiim la.
english: Van Staden works as a butcher at a farm in Straid, County Antrim, Northern Ireland.

kusaal: Nɛ wala wʋsa, o tiraan, Ruth O'Reilly da paam sapʋ'at la, ba da yuolim nya'aŋi buol van Staden ye o kena lɛrig o ka o nwɛ nɔɔr ayi di'emkana ni.
english: However, due to an injury to prop Ruth O'Reilly, van Staden was called up as her replacement and played twice in the tournament.

kusaal: On da tʋm pɔɔgʋn la, o da sʋŋ kuod South Africa dim biltong n bɛ Northern Ireland.
english: While working at the farm, she helped to pioneer the production of South African biltong in Northern Ireland.

kusaal: O da bɛnɛ Belfast.
english: She lives in Belfast.

kusaal: Institute of Local Government Studies (ILGS) anɛ Government of Ghana tʋʋma zin'ikanɛ ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ wai la ni (1999) ye ba pa'al sakur biis ban na zanl gɔmena tʋʋma zin'is si'em ka mɔr tuon ken na.
english: The Institute of Local Government Studies (ILGS) is a Government of Ghana institution established in 1999 with the mandate to educate students in public management and development.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr kaŋa da dɔlisidnɛ Act of Parliament, 647 of 2003.
english: The institution is backed by Act of Parliament, 647 of 2003.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr la bɛnɛ Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development pʋʋgin.
english: The institute is under the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development.

kusaal: Din bɛ zin'isi'a anɛ Ogbojo kpi'e nɛ Ashalley Botwe, Accra.
english: The institute is located in Ogbojo near Ashalley Botwe, Accra.

kusaal: Ba da pin'il club la nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ, sawaar nwadig (October 1996) ka banɛ da pin'ili li an Omar Nasser El-Eter, Rabeh Nasser El-Eter nɛ onɛ lɛn kae ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Robert Tetteh, on da anɛ nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛd kʋdʋgi tis nɛ SS74 team banɛ da bɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ pisyɔpɔi nam saŋa la bɛ Accra Great Olympics nɛ Ghana Black Stars.
english: The club was founded in October 1996 by Omar Nasser El-Eter, Rabeh Nasser El-Eter and the late Robert Tetteh, a former player for SS74 team of the seventies, Accra Great Olympics and Ghana Black Stars.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi ni (1997), Inter Allies da paami ba nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛd kanɛ mi nwɛn'ɛb yiiga, ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Michael Coffie onɛ da paasi nwɛn'ɛ FIFA U-17 World Cup ni nɛ Ghana National team, banɛ an Black Starlets la.
english: In 1997, Inter Allies discovered International Allies FC's first player, Michael Coffie who played in the FIFA U-17 World Cup with the Ghana National team, The Black Starlets.

kusaal: O da pin'il club la nɛ third division league ka yʋʋm tusayi la (2000), ka club la da nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋ second division league.
english: He started the club in the third division league and by the year 2000, the club qualified to play in the second division league.

kusaal: Ba paasi nwɛ'ɛd Ghana Premier League ni.
english: In 2001, three players were transferred into the Ghana Premier League and for the second time, it had a player play in 2001 FIFA U-20 World Cup in Argentina with the Black Satellites Squad.

kusaal: IBF da gaadnɛ tuon ka United States Boxing Association (USBA) naan kena, dinɛ an regional championship lʋgʋr nwɛnɛ North American Boxing Federation (NABF).
english: The IBF was preceded by the United States Boxing Association (USBA), a regional championship organization like the North American Boxing Federation (NABF).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan, 1983 la ni, WBA yʋʋm-yʋʋm la'asʋg dinɛ da bɛ Puerto Rico, Robert W. "Bobby" Lee Sr., onɛ an USBA zuraan la, da nya' ye di'e WBA zuraan ka lu ka Gilberto Mendoza di.
english: In 1983, at the WBA's annual convention, held in Puerto Rico, Robert W. "Bobby" Lee Sr., president of the USBA, lost in his bid to become WBA president against Gilberto Mendoza.

kusaal: Ba da maali dinɛ ka pʋdi yʋ'ʋr USBA-International, dinɛ ka ba da tiaki di yʋ'ʋr ka di yʋ'ʋn an International Boxing Federation, ka di bɛ New Jersey, zin'ikanɛ ka di ɔfis tita'ar bɛ.
english: Formed as USBA-International, the fledgling organization was renamed the International Boxing Federation on November 6, 1983, based in New Jersey, where its main offices remain.

kusaal: Bobby Lee mɛ da anɛ New Jersey boxing commissioner kem paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu (1985), labaari da yina, "ka ba zɛrig o ka Ethical Standards Commission nwɛ' o sam on da siak ka di'e ligidi yi banɛ bɔɔd ninwisigir zaba yɛla nɛ casino tuon gatib ni la.
english: Bobby Lee had also been a New Jersey boxing commissioner until 1985, when, according to news reports, "he was suspended and fined by the Ethical Standards Commission for accepting contributions from fight promoters and casino executives."

kusaal: IBF dunia wʋsa champion da anɛ Marvin Camel, onɛ an WBC world cruiserweight champion kʋdʋg ka da di IBF's belt division kan ni ya'as.
english: The IBF's first world champion was Marvin Camel, a former WBC world cruiserweight champion who won the IBF's belt in the same division.

kusaal: IBF da bɛ yʋʋm yinne la, 1984 ka di da gban'e ye di nyɛ Larry Holmes, Aaron Pryor, Marvin Hagler nɛ Donald Curry, banɛ pʋn dɛŋim an champion nam la'asʋg la ni, IBF dunia wʋsa champion nam.
english: During its first year of existence the IBF remained largely obscure, but by 1984 it decided to recognize Larry Holmes, Aaron Pryor, Marvin Hagler and Donald Curry, already established champions from other organizations, as IBF world champions.

kusaal: Holmes' yɛl la ni, o da bas WBC title la ka di'e IBF din.
english: In Holmes' case, he relinquished his WBC title to accept the IBF's recognition.

kusaal: International Boxing Federation (IBF) anɛ lʋga anaasi banɛ gɔsid zaba ninwisigir di'ema ka International Boxing Hall of Fame (IBHOF) mi' ba yɛla la yinne banɛ tɛɛgid professional boxing bouts, ban nɛ World Boxing Association (WBA), World Boxing Council (WBC) nɛ World Boxing Organization (WBO).
english: The International Boxing Federation (IBF) is one of four major organizations recognized by the International Boxing Hall of Fame (IBHOF) which sanctions professional boxing bouts.

kusaal: Lee nɛ sieba da yisi ba mɛŋ la'asʋg la ni vɔɔt la nya'aŋ, ka gban'e ye ba maal la'askanɛ paasi atan, ka an dunia eʋsa la'asʋg ye di la'am bɛ nɛ WBA nɛ WBC.
english: Lee and others withdrew from the convention after the election, and decided to organize a third, world-level organization, to co-exist with the WBA and the WBC.

kusaal: IBF dap dunia wʋsa championship belts anɛ wiig, ka pʋ'ab dunia wʋsa championship belts an bʋlʋ pɛɛlig.
english: IBF men's world championship belts are red, whereas women's world championship belts are light blue.

kusaal: International CoCoa Farmers Organization anɛ lʋgʋr kanɛ ka ba da pin'ili bɛ Netherlands yʋʋm tasayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi ni kati wa'ae nɛ kpaadib banɛ kuod cocoa bean da bɔɔd ye ba nyɛ suor kanɛ ka ba na la'as tɛɛns-tɛɛns kpaadib ka ba nyaŋi sɔnsi ba tʋʋma nɔbigir yela.
english: The International CoCoa Farmers Organization (ICCFO) is an organization that was formed in the Netherlands in 2014 in response to cocoa bean farmers needing an international platform for discussing issues in the industry.

kusaal: Linɛ ka ba mɔr cocoa maan ka buoni li ye chocolate tisid ligidi sia yʋʋm wʋsa anɛ na'asaatɛŋ US ligidi Billion pisnii dunia wʋsa.
english: The chocolate confectionery market generate annually about $80 Billion worldwide.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi, Sigir nwadig la ni ka ba da la'as dunia wʋsa cocoa la'asʋg, linɛ da bɛ Amsterdam tɛŋin la, cocoa kpaadib banɛ yi tɛɛns piinɛ yinnɛ la'as kaŋa ni da si'ak ye ba pin'il lʋgir kanɛ gɔsid cocoa kpaadib yela.
english: In June 2014 during the World Cocoa Conference, that took place in Amsterdam, cocoa farmers from eleven producing countries met at the side line of this conference and agreed to establish an international cocoa farmers organization.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi, samanpiid nwadig la ni, lʋgir kanɛ zi'e li mɛŋ nyali gɔsid cocoa kpaadib yela ka ba buon International Cocoa Farmers Organization (ICCFO) da pin'il ya, bɛ Netherlands ka ba kpɛɛmnam da nan anɛ bi'ela saŋkan ka ba tuongat da an Warren Sako.
english: In December 2014 an independent and transparent cocoa farmers organization with the name International Cocoa Farmers Organization (ICCFO) was established in the Netherlands by an interim Board led by Warren Sako.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi saŋa la International CoCoa Farmers Organization(ICCFO) linɛ da bɛ Lelystad, tɛnpʋʋg tita'ar kanɛ paasa anaasi bɛ Netherlands, da yina nɔk International CoCoa Farmers Organization (ICCFO) kpɛn'ɛs wada pʋʋgin, ka yɔ'ɔgi ba dɔpaaligi bɛ Africa sʋ'ʋlim, Ivory Coast tɛŋin.
english: As of 2014 the International CoCoa Farmers Organization(ICCFO) based in Lelystad, the fourth-largest city of the Netherlands, merged with the International CoCoa Farmers Organization (ICCFO) legally, with branch and regional head office for Africa, in the Ivory Coast.

kusaal: ICCFO bɔɔdim anɛ ye cocoa kpaadib na paam ban bɔɔd si'el wʋsa ka li nyaŋi sʋŋi ba wʋsa ka ba tʋmi ba tʋʋma.
english: The ICCFO aims to make sure cocoa is sourced using sustainable methods and to improve the conditions of cocoa farmers and farm workers.

kusaal: Banɛ an kpɛɛmnamɛ tis ICCFO anɛ nidib piinɛ atan', yinnɛ wʋsa zi'e nɛ tɛɛns banɛ ka ba kuod cocoa yinnɛ.
english: The governing board of the ICCFO consists of 13 members, each representing a cocoa-producing country.

kusaal: Banɛ paasi li pʋʋgin nɛ lin an si'em wʋsa da yi paalʋ na ban da kɛŋ la'asʋg kanɛ bɛ Hague yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛnu, Fulumfug nwadig ni la.
english: The members and structure of the board were announced in a meeting held in The Hague in February 2015.

kusaal: Kpaadib banɛ kuod cocoa nyaŋidi kɛt ka ba kpaadib taaba wʋsa paamid cocoa beans la.
english: Cocoa farmers ensure that the entire cocoa industry is supplied with the raw material (cocoa beans).

kusaal: Cocoa kpaadib sʋŋid bɛdigʋ ban nyaŋidi kuod cocoa ka gɔsidi li titua la.
english: Cocoa farmers play a crucial role as producers and maintenance of cocoa production.

kusaal: Amaa linɛ bɛ li pʋʋgin lɛɛ anɛ ye cocoa kpaadib la nɔɔr kuom pʋ tɔn'e laligida tɛɛns kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb la'asa banɛ ka ba la'asidi pian'ad tʋʋm si'eba yelaa, ka li anɛ ban da pʋ mɔr tuongatib ka ba na pian'a ba yela la.
english: Unfortunately, cocoa farmers are underrepresented in the international round table discussions on issues concerning their profession because they were unable to represent themselves as a single voice.

kusaal: Wada la si'eba anɛ: Sustainable Cocoa Economy, Ethical Cocoa, Fine Flavour Cacao, nɛ Cocoa year.
english: Some notable terms include: Sustainable Cocoa Economy, Ethical Cocoa, Fine Flavour Cacao, and Cocoa year.

kusaal: International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' ni linn a niŋ si'em ka gban'ar kanɛ ka ba da la'asi ba yiiga la'asigi bɛ Geneva Switzerland tɛŋin la nyaŋi tʋm tʋʋma.
english: The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) was established in 1973 to put into effect the first International Cocoa Agreement which was negotiated in Geneva Switzerland at a United Nations International Cocoa Conference.

kusaal: ICCO dɔɔg tita'ar da bɛnɛ England London amaa yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anu, sɛnlʋŋ nwadig la, dabpisi nɛ anu daar, International Cocoa Council (ICC) banɛ an tuongatib la da bas suor ye ICCO dɔɔg tita'ar la yi London England nɛ ba gbansɔbidib zin'ig la wʋsa lɛbis Abidjan, Cote d'lvoire.
english: The International Cocoa Organization is a global organization composed of both cocoa producing and cocoa consuming countries with a membership Formerly, ICCO was headquartered in England London but on September 25, 2015, the International Cocoa Council (ICC) which is the highest authority, unanimously approved the relocation of ICCO from London England together with its secretariat to Abidjan, Cote d'lvoire.

kusaal: Linɛ yela ka ICCO dɔɔg titia'ar la da bɛ London la anɛ ye 19th century saŋa la, nidib bɛdigʋ da kpɛn'ɛ cocoa tʋʋma ni ka mɔri ba ya'am nɛ ba pʋtɛn'ɛr kanɛ na nyaŋi sʋŋ ka ba maal cocoa la'ad ka li ligidi da kpi'ema tis tɛnkpɛmisin dim.
english: The reason why originally ICCO was headquartered in London lies in the fact that in the 19th century the Quaker businessmen entered the Cocoa business and used their skills to improve the living conditions for factory workers as well as making both chocolate and Cocoa inexpensive and available to the locals.

kusaal: Ban vɛɛnsidi gɔsid nɔɔra atan' yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin la zug, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan' nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi la ni, dunia wʋsa cocoa kuob da lɛb nya'aŋ hali zien nɛ 4.461 million tonnes nɛ 4.855 million tonnes.
english: Quarterly Bulletin of Cocoa Statistics (QBCS) provides reliable and up-to-date data analysis of Cocoa economy since 1960 on both Cocoa producing and Cocoa consuming countries According to ICCO QBCS most recent revised forecasts for the year 2023/2024 global productions and grindings declined by -11.7% to 4.461 million tonnes and by -4.3% to 4.855 million tonnes Cote d'lvoire is the world's leading cocoa producing country followed by Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana cocoa biili la anɛ linɛ an sʋ'ʋm gati ba taaba, yʋʋm wʋsa vɛɛnsig la pa'al lʋgir kanɛ buon Quality Control Company QCC la pa'al, ban bɛnɛ COCOBOD ni.
english: Ghana produces the most quality Cocoa seeds by the help of Quality Control Company QCC which is a subsidiary of COCOBOD.

kusaal: International Cocoa Organization anɛ dunia wʋsa la'asig lʋgir kanɛ ka banɛ paasi li pʋʋgin an tɛɛns banɛ kuod cocoa nɛ tɛɛns banɛ da'ad cocoa.
english: The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) is a global organization, composed of both cocoa producing and cocoa consuming countries with a membership.

kusaal: ICCO anɛ suori maali tis banɛ gɔsid cocoa yela lin na niŋ si'em ka ba sɔns cocoa kuosig nɛ li da'ab yela.
english: The ICCO serves as a platform for stakeholders in the global cocoa industry to discuss topics relevant to international cocoa trade.

kusaal: Linɛ paas anɛ, ICCO sʋŋidi gɔsid cocoa da'adiib yela nɛ li bɛʋgʋ saa na an si'em, ka gban'ad gban'asi'eba ka mɛ lɛn sʋŋidi pa'an kpaadib suor paala.
english: The ICCO serves as a platform for stakeholders in the global cocoa industry to discuss topics relevant to international cocoa trade.

kusaal: Banɛ paas ICCO lʋgir la pʋʋgin anɛ wan wʋʋ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ, kɔbiga pʋʋgin tɛɛns banɛ kuod ka pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' kɔbiga pʋʋgin mɛ an tɛɛns banɛ da'adi li dit dunia wʋsa.
english: Additionally, the ICCO offers expertise in cocoa market analysis and forecasting, project development and implementation, as well as capacity-building programs for its member countries.

kusaal: Banɛ paas la wʋsa mɔr tuongat ka o bɛ International Cocoa Council, nwa' an kpɛɛmnam banɛ gɔsid ICCO.
english: All Members are represented in the International Cocoa Council, the highest governing body of the ICCO.

kusaal: Banɛ tisid sa'alʋg la anɛ piinɛ anaasi banɛ mi' cocoa tʋʋma hali sʋ'ʋŋa, ba wʋsa yinɛ asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ tʋʋma ni na (ayɔpɔi yinɛ tɛɛns banɛ kuod cocoa na ka ayɔpɔi mɛ yi tɛɛns banɛ da'ad cocoa).
english: ICCO Member countries represent roughly 86% of world cocoa production and more than 72% of world cocoa consumption.

kusaal: Amaa ban tʋʋma anɛ ye ba sa'ali ba, gban'a si'a ya'a bɛ, kpɛɛmnam banɛ bɛ International Cocoa Council la ka ba gɔsid.
english: All Members are represented in the International Cocoa Council, the highest governing body of the ICCO.

kusaal: Linɛ yela ka ba da pin'il sa'alig lʋgir nwa anɛ ye ba paas asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ dim dunia cocoa tʋʋma ni, ka banɛ tʋmi li tʋʋma wʋsa anɛ ICCO.
english: The Consultative Board was established in recognition of the importance of the private sector in the world cocoa economy and of the increasingly important role that trade and industry have been playing in the ICCO.

kusaal: International Cocoa Organization anɛ dunia wʋsa lʋgir kanɛ ka banɛ paasi li pʋʋgin an tɛɛns banɛ kuod nɛ tɛɛns banɛ da'ad cocoa.
english: The International Cocoa Organization is a global organization composed of both cocoa producing and cocoa consuming countries with a membership Formerly, ICCO was headquartered in England London but on September 25, 2015, the International Cocoa Council (ICC) which is the highest authority, unanimously approved the relocation of ICCO from London England together with its secretariat to Abidjan, Cote d'lvoire.

kusaal: ICCO gbansɔbig zin'ig la tʋʋma anɛ ba kɛ ka yʋma anu gban'ar kanɛ ka lʋgir la gban'ae bɛ dɔɔg tita'arin Abidjan Cote d'lvoire la niŋ amɛŋa.
english: The ICCO Secretariat is the executive body tasked with the responsibility for implementation of the Organization's five year strategic plan based in the organization's headquarters in Abidjan Cote d'lvoire.

kusaal: Ba gɔsid cocoa maan si'em nɔɔra anaasi yʋʋm pʋʋgin hali yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ saŋa sa ka ba pin'ili gɔsid tɛɛns banɛ ka ba kuod cocoa nɛ tɛɛns banɛ ka ba da'ad cocoa ni.
english: Quarterly Bulletin of Cocoa Statistics (QBCS) provides reliable and up-to-date data analysis of Cocoa economy since 1960 on both Cocoa producing and Cocoa consuming countries According to ICCO QBCS most recent revised forecasts for the year 2023/2024 global productions and grindings declined by -11.7% to 4.461 million tonnes and by -4.3% to 4.855 million tonnes Cote d'lvoire is the world's leading cocoa producing country followed by Ghana.

kusaal: Cote d'lvoire an tɛŋ kanɛ ka ba kuod cocoa gaadi ba taaba ka tɛŋ kanɛ tial an Ghana.
english: Quarterly Bulletin of Cocoa Statistics (QBCS) provides reliable and up-to-date data analysis of Cocoa economy since 1960 on both Cocoa producing and Cocoa consuming countries According to ICCO QBCS most recent revised forecasts for the year 2023/2024 global productions and grindings declined by -11.7% to 4.461 million tonnes and by -4.3% to 4.855 million tonnes Cote d'lvoire is the world's leading cocoa producing country followed by Ghana.

kusaal: COCOBOD dim sʋŋ ya hali bɛ cocoa kuob pʋʋgin Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka Ghana gɔmɛna zi'e ba nya'aŋ.
english: COCOBOD had played a significant role to tremendous increment in Cocoa production in Ghana as it gains its support measures from the Ghanaian government.

kusaal: Ban mɔr biis ka ba tʋm la nɛ banɛ mɔri ba taaba ka ba an sankpan'as nami tʋmi tisidi ba la an yelpaka bɛ west Africa li kaskas Ivory Coast nɛ Ghana.
english: Human slavery and child labor are some of the current challenges that ICCO is battling to solve in west Africa specifically Ivory Coast and Ghana.

kusaal: Dasam nɛ pʋ'asada banɛ mɔr yʋʋm piinɛyi paae piinɛ ayuobʋ ka ba ɛɛnti pan'asiba yisi ba yaani kuosi ba tis banɛ sʋ'ʋe cocoa pɔɔd bɛ Ivory Coast, anina ka ba bɛɛ tʋm pɔɔdin, bɛɛ yaan bɛɛ si'eba pʋn anɛ tutunam gba'.
english: Young boys and girls as young as 12 to 16 years old are lured from their homes then sold to cacao plantation owners in Ivory Coast where they worked as field hands, domestic workers and even prostitutes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ yinnɛ ni, chocolate kanɛ ka tɛŋbɛda da dit la pisnaasi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin anɛ biis ka ba mɔri ba tʋm tʋʋmban ka biis paae 1 million bɛ Ghana nɛ Ivory Coast tɛɛnsin an yʋʋm piiga yela tʋm cocoa beans pɔɔd la ni ka nan zi'e kpɛn'ɛ sakur dɔɔg nii.
english: In 2001, 40% of Chocolate consumed in the developed world was produced by child slavery and up to 1 million children in both Ghana and Ivory Coast as young as 10 years old are estimated to have been working on harvesting farms of cacao beans who had never attended school.

kusaal: ICCO la'as nɛ west Africa gɔmɛnanam nɛ asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ lʋga si'eba ye ba gɔs ban na niŋ si'em ka biis tʋʋma nɛ sankpan'asim tʋʋma la gaad.
english: Human slavery and child labor are some of the current challenges that ICCO is battling to solve in west Africa specifically Ivory Coast and Ghana.

kusaal: Inusah Abdulai Bistav Fuseini anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn an Lɔya.
english: Inusah Abdulai Bistav Fuseini (born 23 January 1962) is a Ghanaian lawyer and politician.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaan n tis Tamale Central sʋ'ʋlʋm ka mɛ an Minista kʋdʋg onɛ da gɔsid tam nam nɛ teŋ la la'ad, o mɛ da lɛn anɛ Minista kʋdʋg onɛ da gɔsid suoya yɛla n bɛ ti Ghana gɔmina pʋʋgin.
english: He is a former member of parliament for Tamale Central constituency and the former Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, former Minister of Roads and Highways in the Ghana government.

kusaal: Fuseini yinɛ Tishiegu-Tamale sʋ'ʋlʋm, Ghana Northern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: Fuseini is from Tishiegu-Tamale, in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ wada tʋmtʋm kpɛɛm n bɛ Law Trust Company linɛ bɛ Ankara sʋ'ʋlʋm ka naan ken pɔlitis ni la.O da keŋi pa'alʋg sakur linɛ bɛ Bagabaga Training College la (lin ka ba yʋ'ʋn buonɛ li zina ye Bagabaga College of Education la) Ani ka o da di'e kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ bigis ye o anɛ pa'an.
english: He attended teacher training college at Bagabaga Training College (now Bagabaga College of Education) where he obtained his teacher certification to be a professional teacher.

kusaal: Fuseini, da anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid o da lieb wadmaan saŋkanɛ ka Wayo Seini da yi Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la ni keŋ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni la.
english: Fuseini, who is a member of the National Democratic Congress, became a member of parliament when Wayo Seini defected from the NDC to the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O da yi ka bas kʋk la ka ba ye ba maligim vɔɔti yis sɔb n bɛ Tamale Central sʋ'ʋlʋm nwadis anaasi la daba anaasi la yʋʋm 2006.
english: This triggered a by-election in the Tamale Central constituency on 4 April 2006.

kusaal: Ban da vɔɔt la ka Fuseini di nɛ vɔɔt kal 17,502.
english: Fuseini won the election with a majority of 17,502.

kusaal: Fuseini anɛ Mɔr ka di pu'a ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Abiba Fuseini.
english: Fuseini is a Muslim and was married to Abiba Fuseini.

kusaal: Ka o yii ani keŋ University of Ghana, Legon sakurin la, m maal o digirii linɛ pa'al ye o zamis nɛ wada.Ka lɛn maal o mastɛs n bɛ wada zamisʋg yi University of Ghana sakurin la.
english: He then proceeded to the University of Ghana, Legon, for his bachelor's degree in law.

kusaal: O da lɛn di vɔɔt kanɛ ka Ghana dim da maal nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la yʋʋm 2008 kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da mɔri 66% vɔɔt la wʋsa kallin, Onɛ da an minista kanɛ gɔsid paŋ yɛla nya'andɔl lin da yi yʋʋm 2009 ti paae yʋʋm 2012, lin nya'aŋ ka o kena an minista kanɛ gɔsid Ghana Tam nɛ Teŋ la la'ad yɛla la lin da yi yʋʋm 2012 ti paae yʋʋm 2013, ka da lɛn an minista kanɛ gɔsid Ghana suoya yɛla lin da yi yʋʋm 2013 ti paae yʋʋm 2017.
english: He held positions as the Deputy Minister for Energy in 2009-2012, Minister for Land and Natural Resources in 2012-2013, Minister for Roads in 2013-2017.

kusaal: Fuseini mɔr biis.
english: Fuseini has children.

kusaal: Isaac Adjei Mensah anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd nɛ Wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Wassa East Constituency bɛ Western Region la Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, nɔba zug.
english: Isaac Adjei Mensah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Wassa East Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Isaac Adjei Mensah nɛ Atalata daar yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' Nwadisa atan' la dabpisi nɛ ayuobʋ daar (Atilata 26 dawalig nwadig 1963).
english: Isaac Adjei Mensah was born on Tuesday 26 March 1963.

kusaal: O yinɛ Dompim Number 1, tenkanɛ bɛ Western Region bɛ Ghana la.
english: He hails from Dompim Number 1, a town in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: o da kpɛn' University of Ghana nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) ka di'e o bachelor's degree in Sociology yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne la ni (1991).
english: He entered the University of Ghana in 1988 and obtained his bachelor's degree in Sociology in 1991.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ University of Tromsø, bɛ Norway yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' la ni (1992) maali o post graduate studies.
english: He later proceeded to the University of Tromsø, Norway in 1992 for his post graduate studies.

kusaal: O da naae yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1997) nɛ o MBA in Public Policy.
english: He graduated in 1997 with his MBA in Public Policy.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ kpɛn' pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb la, Isaac da anɛ Regional Human Resource Manager tis Newmont Ghana Limited yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayuobʋ (2006) ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012).
english: Prior to entering politics, Isaac was the Regional Human Resource Manager for Newmont Ghana Limited from 2006 to 2012.

kusaal: Isaac Adjei Mensah paas nɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, (NDC) nidib ni.
english: Isaac Adjei Mensah is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Wadmaanib yin la o da tʋm la'asʋgnam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb, ba sieba anɛ; gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni, lʋgkanɛ gɔsid ya yɛla nɛ Special Budget Committee.
english: In parliament he has served on various committees, some of which include; the Education Committee, the House Committee and the Special Budget Committee.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt gaŋ o yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) ka o zi'eni tis o sʋ'ʋlim dim Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Isaac Adjei Mensah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Wassa East Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O mɔr pu'a nɛ biisa anu ka an karimbiig ken pɛntikost pʋ'ʋsʋm .
english: He is married with five children and identifies as a Christian and a member of the Church of Pentecost.

kusaal: Isaac Adongo ( ba du'a o nɛ Sapal nwadig la 12, 1972) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd onɛ paas 8th Ghana wadmaanib namin la tis Bolgatanga teŋ kanɛ bɛ Upper East Sʋ'ʋlim la ni tis Ma'asim tiig Lʋgir la (NDC).
english: Isaac Adongo (born 12 October 1972) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the 8th Ghanaian Parliament representing the Bolgatanga Central Constituency in the Upper East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ naae o sakur bɛ sakur tita'ar kanɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr an 'Gɛligir sakurin nɛ University of Ghana ni.
english: He is a graduate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants and the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dɛŋi gaŋi o na'am yʋʋm 2016 ka ba da lɛn vɔɔt tis o yʋʋm 2020 la ni.
english: Adongo was first elected in 2016, was re-elected in 2020 and 2024.

kusaal: Adongo anɛ onɛ yit Bolgatanga teŋin.
english: Adongo hails from Bolgatanga.

kusaal: Isaac Ashai Odamtten (dʋ'anɛ 13 May 1972) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: Isaac Ashai Odamtten (born 13 May 1972) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017), o da anɛ Mayor nɛ Metropolitan Chief Executive tis Tema Metropolitan Area sʋ'ʋlim.
english: From 2013 to 2017, he served the Mayor and Metropolitan Chief Executive of Tema Metropolitan Area.

kusaal: O yinɛ Tema bɛ Greater Accra Region, Ghana.
english: He is a native of Tema in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: o da naae University of Cape Coast yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999) ka di'e bachelor of commerce degree (BCom).
english: He completed the University of Cape Coast in 1999 with bachelor of commerce degree (BCom).

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr Master of Business administration (MBA) in Accounting nɛ certificate in project management.
english: He holds a Master of Business administration (MBA) in Accounting, Master of Arts (MPT) from Oral Robert University in 2025 and a certificate in project management.

kusaal: Odamtten anɛ pa'an (teacher) o da sin'iŋi anɛ pa'an gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni Ghana Education Service ka naan duoe ti kilim Finance officer nɛ Bursar sakur kan nɔɔ ni.
english: Odamtten is a teacher by profession and started his career as a tutor for the Ghana Education Service before rising to become a Finance officer and Bursar under the same institution.

kusaal: o da yi anina keŋ International Commercial Banki aan ba head of finance nɛ senior manager of corporate services ka John Dramani Mahama naan gaŋ o ye an Mayor tis Tema sʋ'ʋlim yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la ni (2013).
english: He moved to the International Commercial Bank to serve as the head of finance and senior manager of corporate services before being nominated by John Dramani Mahama to serve as Mayor of Tema in 2013.

kusaal: O da anɛ Mayor nɛ Metropolitan Chief Executive tis Tema Metropolitan Assembly din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017).
english: He served as Mayor and Metropolitan Chief Executive of the Tema Metropolitan Assembly from 2013 to 2017.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa atan la daba atan daar (3 March 2016), ba da vɔɔt o ye o an pirɛsidɛn tis National Association of Local Authorities of Ghana (NALAG) ka da paam suor 19th biennial national delegates conference kanɛ da bɛ Sunyani pin'il tʋʋma.
english: On 3 March 2016, he was elected as the president of the National Association of Local Authorities of Ghana (NALAG) and sworn in during the 19th biennial national delegates conference held in Sunyani.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi (624) yi vɔɔt kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii pʋʋgin (980), gaad onɛ da nya'ad nɛ o la, James Gunu, onɛ da an district chief executive (DCE) tis Akatsi North, ka da paam vɔɔt kɔbistan nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (356).
english: He was sworn in after polling 624 votes out the 980 total valid votes cast to beat his sole contender, James Gunu, the district chief executive (DCE) for Akatsi North, who canvassed 356 votes.

kusaal: O da paas 16-member executive committee tis United Cities and Local Governments ninsabilis tɛɛnsin (Africa) (UCLG Africa).
english: He served as a member of the 16-member executive committee of the United Cities and Local Governments of Africa (UCLG Africa).

kusaal: o da lɛn anɛ nidib ayi banɛ da zi'en West Africa Commonwealth Local Government Forum (CLGF) la yinne.
english: He served as one of the two board members representing West Africa on the Commonwealth Local Government Forum (CLGF).

kusaal: World Cities Day yʋʋ tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016), ka on da dɔl Habitat III, o da anɛ nimbanɛ ka ba mɔr yi zin'is kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb na ka di yinɛ Overseas Development Institute (ODI) Global Challenges dinɛ gɔsid tenkpɛmisi na niŋ si'em ka paami ba global SDG goals.
english: On World Cities Day 2016, and following Habitat III, he was one of the speakers brought in from cities around the world as a result of Overseas Development Institute (ODI) Global Challenges event to explore how urban areas can deliver their global SDG goals.

kusaal: Din yi Nwadsa atan la dabpiinɛ ayuobʋ daar ken paae dabpisi nɛ ayi daar yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (16 to 22 March 2016), o da gaad nidib tuon ka ba kaae Royal Borough Of Greenwich ka GUBA Enterprise dinɛ kpɛɛm an Dentaa sʋŋi ba.
english: From the 16 to 22 March 2016, he led a delegation on a visit to the Royal Borough of Greenwich with support from GUBA Enterprise led by Dentaa.

kusaal: Odamtten da di Ma'asim tiig, National Democratic Congress tis Tema East Constituency gur yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: Odamtten won the parliamentary bid to represent the National Democratic Congress for the Tema East Constituency ahead of the 2020 elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi Nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni (December 2020), Odamtten da diya ka bas Wadmaankanɛ pʋn dɛŋim zin'i Tema East Constituency kʋk la zug, Daniel Titus Glover nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ yinne, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (41,692) ka o tiraan la nyɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ yinne, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (31,956) ka o di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: In December 2020, Odamtten beat the incumbent Member of Parliament for Tema East Constituency Daniel Titus Glover with 41,692 votes as against 31,956 votes to win the seat in the 2020 Elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2021), Odamtten da paam suori lieb Wadmaan, Member of Parliament tis Tema East Constituency paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: On 7 January 2021, Odamtten was sworn in as the Member of Parliament representing the Tema East Constituency in the 8th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Gender and Children nɛ tʋʋma nyɛɛb yɛla (Employment), Social Welfare and State Enterprises Committee of Parliament.
english: He serves as a member on the Gender and Children Committee and the Employment, Social Welfare and State Enterprises Committee of Parliament.

kusaal: O anɛwadmaan kanɛ b aba gaŋ tis Tema East Constituency.
english: He is the member of Parliament Elect for the Tema East Constituency.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Odamtten nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi Nwadisa anu la dabpiinɛ atan daar (13 May 1972).
english: Odamtten was born on 13 May 1972.

kusaal: Tʋʋm tita'akanɛ ka o tʋm anɛ on da sʋŋ ziŋgban'adib ka zimi tʋʋma la keŋ tuon ka di kɛ ka teŋ la paam ligidi yi ziŋgban'adib la'asʋg kanɛ bɛ Tema la da paam outboard motors la.
english: One of his achievements was connected to helping fishermen and boosting the fisheries and aquaculture sector to generate more income through the provision of outboard motors to fishermen associations within Tema.

kusaal: Kaar la yinɛ nɔɔryinne kanɛ Tema nɛ Royal Borough of Greenwich mɔr ka tɛɛns ayi la sʋŋid taaba gbaʋŋ zamisʋg ni, ninwisigir ni, nɛ gɔmena tʋʋma ni.
english: The visit was part of a twinning link partnership between the city of Tema and the Royal Borough of Greenwich involving co-operation between the two communities in areas of Education, Sports and Governance.

kusaal: Odamtten anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Odamtten is a Christian.

kusaal: O da anɛ gbaʋŋ zamisid nɛ foreign minister, People's National Party (PNP) na'adɔɔg la ni, Ghana Third Republic la ni.
english: Dr.Isaac K. Chinebuah (7 October 1929 – 8 June 2006) was an academic and the foreign minister in the People's National Party (PNP) government of the Third Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Chinebuah da anɛ headmaster kʋdʋgʋ tis Achimota School din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan (1963) ni paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (1966) ni ka da lɛn an pa'an (lecturer) tis Institute of African Studies bɛ University of Ghana, Legon.
english: Dr. Chinebuah was a former headmaster of Achimota School from 1963 to 1966 and also a former lecturer at the Institute of African Studies of the University of Ghana, Legon.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah's Convention People's Party gɔmena la da bɛ Ghana First Republic la ni.
english: He was a Minister for Education and Information in Dr. Kwame Nkrumah's Convention People's Party government in the First Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Chinebuah da lieb wadmaani tisi Nzema East (ka ba yʋ'ʋm buon ye Ellembelle) constituency yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1979) vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Dr. Chinebuah became the Member of Parliament for Nzema East (now Ellembelle) constituency after the 1979 elections.

kusaal: Hilla Limann da an tuon gat Ghana Third Republic la ni din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1979) hali ti paaeban da yis o coup d'état ni yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne nwadis piinɛ ayi dabpistan nɛ yinne daar (December 31, 1981) la.
english: He was appointed Minister of Foreign Affairs in the PNP government by Dr. Hilla Limann in the Third Republic from 1979 until its overthrow in a coup d'état on December 31, 1981.

kusaal: O pʋ'a da anɛ Jane Chinebuah.
english: He was married to Jane Chinebuah.

kusaal: Isaac K. Chinebuah (ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisi nɛ awai nwadis piiga la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 October 1929) ka o maal ka'alim yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ nwaida ayuobʋ daba anii daar (8 June 2006).
english: Dr.Isaac K. Chinebuah (7 October 1929 – 8 June 2006) was an academic and the foreign minister in the People's National Party (PNP) government of the Third Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ Minister for Education and Information Dr.
english: He was a Minister for Education and Information in Dr. Kwame Nkrumah's Convention People's Party government in the First Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye an Minister of Foreign Affairsi bɛ PNP gɔmena dinɛ ka Dr.
english: He was appointed Minister of Foreign Affairs in the PNP government by Dr. Hilla Limann in the Third Republic from 1979 until its overthrow in a coup d'état on December 31, 1981.

kusaal: O da mɔrnɛ yʋma pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (78 years) ka maal ka'alim yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ nwadisa ayuobʋ la daba anii daar (June 8, 2006).
english: He died at the age of 78 on June 8, 2006.

kusaal: O da mɔr biisa anii.
english: He had eight children.

kusaal: Ba du'a Isaac Kwame Asiamah nɛ Burnya nwarig la ni li dabisim pisi nɛ anaasi daar yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbisiwai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu la ni O anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Isaac Kwame Asiamah (born 24 December 1975) is a Ghanaian politician of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Isaac Asiamah n bɛnɛ Mampong ti Ghana sυ'υlυm Burnya nwarig la ni li dabisim pisi nɛ anaasi daar yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbisiwai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu la ni ka ba da du'a o.
english: Isaac Asiamah was born in Mampong, Ghana on 24 December 1975.

kusaal: Yυυm tusa ayi' la ni ka o da keŋ University of Ghana sakur la ni naae ka di'e o Digirii kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Geography nɛ Political Science la.
english: He attended the University of Ghana, Legon where he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Geography and Political Science, in 2000.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o tɔlis Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration maal o mastɛs Digirii linɛ an Governance and Leadership n naae yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ anii la ni.
english: He proceeded to the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration for his master's degree in Governance and Leadership, graduating in 2008.

kusaal: onɛ an Bipɔl wadmaan n bɛ wadmaanib yir la nannanna anɛ Francisca Oteng-Mensah on ka ba da vɔɔt ka o di yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni, o da mɔri yυma pisi nɛ atan' ka lieb wadmaan la.
english: The current holder of the title of the youngest parliamentarian is Francisca Oteng-Mensah, who, in 2016, was elected at age 23.

kusaal: O sυ'υlυm la da paas Wabυg Na'adɔɔg wadmaanib bam pistan' nɛ ayuobʋ (36) nɛ yi wadmaanib la kanl wυsa linɛ da an pistan' nɛ awai ( 39) la ni la n bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: His constituency was a part of the 36 parliamentary seats out of 39 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Ban da vɔt la o da paamnɛ vɔt bam 30,012 n yi' vɔt la kanl wυsa linɛ da an 44,217 la ni, kɔbiga pυυginɛ, o da mɔri 67.9%.
english: He was elected with 30,012 votes out of 44,217 total valid votes cast equivalent to 67.9% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Onɛ John Macitse Oduro H. onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la nɛ Stephen Osei Bossman onɛ mɛ da an Convention People's Party ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over John Macitse Oduro H. of the National Democratic Congress and Stephen Osei Bossman of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Vɔɔt kanɛ ka o da paam anɛ 25,350 n yi vɔɔt la kanl wυsa linɛ da an 44,948 la ni, ka kɔbʋg pυυgin ka o mɔr 56.4%.
english: He was elected with 25,350 votes out of 44,948 total valid votes cast equivalent to 56.4% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Onɛ Amoah Sarpong onɛ an People's National Convention nid la nɛ Ali Yeboah onɛ da an Ma'asim Tiig nid nɛ Kofi Takyi onɛ da an Democratic People's Party nid nɛ Appiahhene Peter onɛ an Convention People's Party la da nyi'ad ka o di ka basi ba, kɔbiga pυυginɛ ba wυsa da mɔri 0.68%, 32.01%, 0.42%, 1.12% and 9.37% n dɔl nɛ ba yυda la si'iŋi buoli kena naae si'em la.
english: He was elected over Amoah Sarpong of the People's National Convention, Ali Yeboah of the National Democratic Congress, Kofi Takyi of the Democratic People's Party, Appiahhene Peter of the Convention People's Party and Raphael Baffour Awuah an independent candidate.

kusaal: Onɛ Kwaku Agyemang-Mensah Ma'asim Tiig nid la nɛ Frank Tachie Mensah onɛ da an Convention People's Party da nya'and ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over Kwaku Agyemang-Mensah of the National Democratic Congress and Frank Tachie Mensah of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pυυginɛ Ma'asim Tiig nid la da mɔri 41.94% ka Convention People's Party nid la mɛ mɔr 0.79% vɔt.
english: These obtained 41.94% and 0.79% respectively of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Atwima Mponua sυ'υlυm la.
english: He is the Member of Parliament of Atwima Mponua constituency.

kusaal: O si'iŋi an wadmaan n bɛ wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anaasi, anu, ayuobʋ, ayɔpɔi hali ti paae anii ti Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: He has been the member of parliament for the constituency in the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th and the 8th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Asiamah mɔr tυυma mi'ilim hali bɛdigʋ, Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la da nɔk o ye o an onɛ gɔsidi ba wada maalυg yɛla n bɛ ba Headquarters Ankara sυ'υlυm.
english: Asiamah has had a varied professional background, including being employed as a Policy Analyst at the New Patriotic Party Headquarters in Accra.

kusaal: Asiamah si'iŋi o pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb ka an bipɔl ka da zi'en Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la zugu nyi'a di Atwima Mponua sυ'υlυm wadmaanib kυk la yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni.
english: Asiamah entered Ghanaian politics at an early age when he contested and won the Atwima Mponua constituency elections on the ticket of the NPP in 2005.

kusaal: On da di'e kυk la ka anɛ yυma pisi nɛ awai, onɛ an bipɔl yiiga n bɛ Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni.
english: In January 2017, President Nana Akuffo-Addo nominated him for the position of Minister of Youth and Sports in Ghana.

kusaal: Burnya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni ka Ghana Gɔmina Nana Akuffo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an na'akim nɛ pu'asada nɛ ninwisigir Minista n bɛ ti Ghana sυ'υlυm kpɛla.
english: In January 2017, President Nana Akuffo-Addo nominated him for the position of Minister of Youth and Sports in Ghana.

kusaal: Ban da vɛɛnsidi o ye ba gɔs la, o da yɛl ye on ya'a kena, o na gɔs Ghana ninwisigir di'ema yɛla ka li nɔbig.
english: During the vetting, he articulated his views on how to improve sports in Ghana.

kusaal: Yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la vɔɔt la ni ka ba da vɔɔt ka Asiamah di Atwima Mponua kυk la linɛ bɛ Ghana Kumasi sυ'υlυm la.
english: Asiamah was elected as the member of parliament for the Atwima Mponua constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana for the first time in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pυυginɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la da mɔri 30.5% ka CPP nid la mɛ mɔr 1.7% vɔt la wυsa pυυgin.
english: These obtained 30.5% and 1.7% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O sυ'υlυm la da paas Wabυg Na'adɔɔg wadmaanib bam pistan' nɛ anaasi (34) n yi wadmaanib la kanl wυsa linɛ da an pistan' nɛ awai ( 39) Wabυg na'adɔɔg nidib banɛ da di Ashanti Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: His constituency was part of the 34 parliamentary seats out of 39 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O da paamnɛ vɔt bam 33,961 n yi vɔt la kanl wυsa linɛ da an 59,300 la ni kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 57.27% vɔt.
english: He was elected with 33,961 votes out of 59,300 total valid votes cast equivalent to 57.27% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yuobu la ni nɛ yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi la ni ka ba da lɛn vɔti gaŋ o ya'as ye o an wadmaan n bɛ wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi nɛ anii la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: He was re-elected in the 2016 and 2020 general election to represent in both the 7th and 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Asiamah di pu'a mɔr biis atan'.
english: Asiamah is married with three children.

kusaal: Onɛ Kristo biig, Anglican karimbiig.
english: He identifies as a Christian and is a member of the Anglican Church of Ghana.

kusaal: Yυυm kan Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la da mɔri wadmaanib bam kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ anii (128) n yi wadmaanib la kanl wʋsa linɛ da an tusa ayi' nɛ pistan' la ni (230).
english: The New Patriotic Party won a majority total of 128 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Na'akim nɛ pu'asada nɛ ninwisigir di'ema Minista lin da yi Burnya nya'aŋ nwaris ayi' yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi n ti paae Burnya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne, yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne la ni.
english: From February 2017 to January 2021, he served as the Minister of Youth and Sports.

kusaal: Isaac Yaw Opoku anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tisi Offinso South constituency bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Isaac Yaw Opoku is a Ghanaian politician and member of parliament for the Offinso South constituency in the Ashanti region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27 August 1957) o yinɛ Offinso bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: He was born on 27 August 1957 and hails from Offinso in the Ashanti region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr PhD in Mycology yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan la ni (1993).
english: He holds a PhD in mycology in 1993.

kusaal: O da anɛ executive director tis Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana dinɛ bɛ Cocobod ni la.
english: He was the executive director of the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana under Cocobod.

kusaal: O paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni (NPP) ka an Wadmaani, MP tis Offinso South Constituency.
english: He is a member of the NPP and currently the MP for Offinso South Constituency.

kusaal: O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid banɛ mɔr ɔfis banɛ mɔr nyɔɔd la (Holding Offices of Profit Committe) ka lɛm paas la'askanɛ gɔsid kpikpiŋ, girima nɛ vɛnlim zin'is (Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee).
english: He is a member of the Members Holding Offices of Profit Committee and also a member of the Trade, Industry, and Tourism Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Gaana vɔɔtʋg la, o da dii o sʋ'ʋlim kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ awai, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne (39,971) ka Yussif Haruna paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ awai, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi (19,952).
english: In the 2020 General Elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 39,971 votes, whilst Yussif Haruna had 19,952 votes.

kusaal: Opoku anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Opoku is a Christian.

kusaal: Isaac Zion Dogboe (Ba dʋ'a o nɛ 26 September 1994) ka o an Ghana nɛ British professional boxer onɛ da zanl WBO junior-featherweight kpɛŋ la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la ni.
english: Isaac Zion Dogboe ( DOG-bay; born 26 September 1994) is a Ghanaian-British professional boxer who held the WBO junior-featherweight title in 2018.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Dogboe nɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana, amaa ka o da tɔɔm keŋ Londoni bɛ England la.
english: Dogboe was born in Accra, Ghana, but moved to London, England.

kusaal: Dogboe da di 2013 Amateur Boxing Association British lightweight title la, on da zabid zin'ikanɛ ka' Territorial Army London BC.
english: Dogboe won the 2013 Amateur Boxing Association British lightweight title, when boxing out of the Territorial Army London BC.

kusaal: O da paam suori nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) Olympics ka da di Amzurifa (silver medal) bɛ African Olympic Qualifying Event, o da nyaŋi bʋ' Mohamed Bedir (EGY), Emilian Polino (TAN), Ayabonga Sonjica (RSA) ka da gʋ'ʋŋ countback 6:6 draw nya'aŋi tis Aboubakr Lbida (MAR) naar zaba (final) la ni.
english: He qualified for the 2012 Olympics by winning a silver medal at the African Olympic Qualifying Event, beating Mohamed Bedir (EGY), Emilian Polino (TAN), Ayabonga Sonjica (RSA) and only losing on countback after a 6:6 draw in the final to Aboubakr Lbida (MAR).

kusaal: Yiiga round la ni 2012 Olympics la, o da zab nɛ Satoshi Shimizu onɛ yi Japan la.
english: In the first round of the 2012 Olympics he faced Satoshi Shimizu of Japan.

kusaal: On da yʋ'ʋm mi' tʋʋma yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013), o da la'asi o record ka di paae 17–0 ka o naan zab nɛ Cesar Juarez ye o di'e WBO interim junior-featherweight title, ka da di nɛ fifth-round stoppage.
english: After turning professional in 2013, he compiled a record of 17–0 before challenging Cesar Juarez for the vacant WBO interim junior-featherweight title, winning via fifth-round stoppage.

kusaal: Zabkanɛ tuon la, Dogboe na zab nɛ ka nyaŋi bʋ' Jessie Magdaleno ka naan nyaŋi di'e WBO junior-featherweight title la mummi.
english: In his next fight Dogboe would face and beat Jessie Magdaleno to capture the full WBO junior-featherweight title.

kusaal: O da nyaŋi gu' o WBO title da nwɛ' first-round knockout nɛ Hidenori Otake yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadisa anii dabpisi nɛ anu daar (25 August 2018) Gila River Arena bɛ Glendale, US.
english: He successfully defending his WBO title with a first-round knockout against Hidenori Otake on 25 August 2018 at the Gila River Arena in Glendale, US.

kusaal: Dogboe da bʋ' Otake onɛ kʋdʋgid la digil nɔɔra ayi ka zab pansid la (referee) Patrick Morley kpɛn' sʋʋgin gu' ka Otake da di'e namisʋg bɛdegʋ.
english: Dogboe knocked the ageing Otake down twice before referee Patrick Morley stepped in to prevent Otake from taking further punishment.

kusaal: O da kɔ'ɔŋi o WBO title tis Emanuel Navarrete, Hulu Theater bɛ New York City's Madison Square Garden la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii la nwadis piinɛ ayi la daba anii daar (8 December 2018).
english: He lost his WBO title to Emanuel Navarrete at the Hulu Theater in New York City's Madison Square Garden on 8 December 2018.

kusaal: 11 May 2019, bayi' la da zabya ya'as, ka Dogboe lɛn gʋ'ʋŋ ya'as, sankaŋa da anɛ rounds piinɛ ayi ni (twelfth round) technical knockout.
english: On 11 May 2019, the pair fought a rematch, and Dogboe lost once again, this time by twelfth-round technical knockout.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai nwadisa awai daba anu daar (5 September 2019), ba da mɔɔl ye Dogboe na zab nɛ Carl Frampton kabkanɛ an o featherweight debut zaba.
english: On 5 September 2019, it was announced that Dogboe would be facing Carl Frampton in his featherweight debut.

kusaal: Bob Arum Top Rank kɛ ka o paam tuon ken.
english: He is promoted by Bob Arum's Top Rank.

kusaal: O da lɛn fɛndigi lɛbna zab nɛ Mexican American Chris Avalos, July 2020, on da nyaŋi gu'oe o naar (final) round kanɛ ka ba da zabid featherweight bout bɛ MGM Grand la.
english: He made a comeback against Mexican American Chris Avalos in July 2020, after stopping him in the final round of their featherweight bout at the MGM Grand.

kusaal: June 2021, o da zab nɛ Adam Lopez featherweight bout ni Las Vegas ka nyaŋ o dɔlisid Saria katib atan la da tis diib kanɛ pa'al ye o diya la.
english: In June 2021, he defeated Adam Lopez in a featherweight bout in Las Vegas with two out of the three judges scoring the fight in his favor.

kusaal: November 2021, o da zabi nyaŋ Christopher Diaz Terence Crawford nɛ Shawn Porter bout, Las Vegas.
english: In November 2021, he defeated Christopher Diaz on the undercard of the Terence Crawford and Shawn Porter bout in Las Vegas.

kusaal: Round nam ayi banɛ gaad tuon la o da bɛ tuon ka mɔr (4:3, 3:2) amaa, ka da kɔ'ɔŋ roundkanɛ da paasi atan la saria katib la da ti Shimizu diib la 5:2, ka di tiak Dogboe pa'a bɛ tuon la.
english: Ahead on points in the first two rounds (4:3, 3:2) he lost the bout after the judges scored round three 5:2 in favour of Shimizu, overturning Dogboe's lead.

kusaal: ban da kad saria la si'em la da mɔr nyɔlʋgʋ ken' banɛ gɔsid la san'an ka ba da ye di anɛ "contentious" ka labaya dim mɛ ye di anɛ "mystery decision".
english: The verdict was met with vocal displeasure from ringside spectators and was later described as "contentious" and a "mystery decision" by media outlets.

kusaal: Ye nɛ' na sʋŋ o ka o tʋgʋsi zamisi di'e o bachelor's degree, dinɛ ka o da sɔs suori ye o keŋ tʋmi o tʋʋma on an zabzabid la.
english: This would make it possible for him to continue to study for his bachelor's degree, which he had to defer due to the demanding nature of his career as a boxer.

kusaal: Dinɛ aan o yiiga zaba ka on nɛ Barry Hunter onɛ pa'al o zaba la zab.
english: That was the first time he fought with Barry Hunter as his trainer.

kusaal: Islamic University College, Ghana anɛ asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ universities bɛ Ghana.
english: The Islamic University College, Ghana is one of the private universities in Ghana.

kusaal: Lin bɛ zin'ig si'a anɛ East Legon linɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region la.
english: It is located at East Legon, Adjringanor in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Lʋgir kanɛ da sʋŋi pin'ili li anɛ Ahlul Bait Foundation, lʋgir kanɛ yi mɔɔm tɛŋ kanɛ an Iran la.
english: This was under the sponsorship of the Ahlul Bait Foundation of the Islamic Republic of Iran.

kusaal: Lin da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi la ni, ka onɛ da pin'ili li an Dr.
english: It was established in 2000 by Dr. Abdolmajid Hakimollahi.

kusaal: Issifu Pangabu Mohammed (ba dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi nwadisa atan la daba ayuobʋ, 6 March 1962) ka o an onɛ tʋm kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl tʋʋma (agriculturist) nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd bɛ Ghana.
english: Issifu Pangabu Mohammed (born 6 March 1962) is an agriculturist and a politician from Ghana.

kusaal: O da zi'en National Democratic Congress nɔba zugʋ nya' ka di zi'eni tis Ejura-Sekyedumase constituency bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim Ghana la, 4th nɛ 5th parliaments la ni Ghana 4th republic la ni.
english: He was a member of parliament on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress party, representing the Ejura-Sekyedumase constituency in the Ashanti Region of Ghana in the 4th and 5th parliaments of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Bawku, tenkanɛ bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Bawku, a town in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paami o GCE O Level secondary education yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai la ni (1979).
english: He obtained his GCE O Level secondary education qualification in 1979.

kusaal: Mohammed sʋ'oe ka an managing director tis Pee Farms dinɛ bɛ Ejura la.
english: Mohammed is the owner and managing director of Pee Farms in Ejura.

kusaal: O da lieb wadmaan yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 2005) on da di vɔɔtkanɛ ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni la (December 2004).
english: He became a member of parliament from January 2005 after emerging winner in the General Election in December 2004.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka o lieb wadmaan constituency kaŋa ni fourth nɛ fifth parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.
english: He was elected as the member of parliament for this constituency in the fourth and fifth parliament of the fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt Mohammed ka o an wadmaani tis Ejura-Sekyedumase constituency bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la yiiga nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni.O da zi'enɛ National Democratic Congress nɔba zugʋ nya' ka di.
english: Mohammed was elected as the member of parliament for the Ejura-Sekyedumase constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana for the first time in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: National Democratic Congress da di kʋgʋs bi'ela nwɛnɛ kʋgʋs piswai nɛ anaasi (94) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan' pʋʋgin (230 seats).
english: The National Democratic Congress won a minority total of 94 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ anii (17,058) yi vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ atan, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anii (33,448) pʋʋgin.
english: He was elected with 17,058 votes out of 33,448 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas Raymond Abuska onɛ bɛ Peoples' National Convention, Richard Ofori Dwamena onɛ bɛ New Patriotic Party, Mathias N. G. Naala onɛ bɛ Convention People's Party nɛ Dominic Kwabena Anomah B. independent candidate.
english: He was elected over Raymond Abuska of the Peoples' National Convention, Richard Ofori Dwamena of the New Patriotic Party, Mathias N. G. Naala of the Convention People's Party and Dominic Kwabena Anomah B. an independent candidate.

kusaal: Dinɛ ka ba da paam la zɛmnɛ nɛ vɔɔt yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1%), vɔɔt pisnaasi du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (40.7%), nɛɛm du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.7%) nɛ ayuobʋ du'ali ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (6.6%) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: These were equivalent to 1%, 40.7%, 0.7% and 6.6% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008), o da zi'en National Democratic Congress nɔba zugʋ lɛn di constituency kʋk la.
english: In 2008, he won the general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress for the same constituency.

kusaal: National Democratic Congress da di kʋgʋs bi'ela nwɛnɛ kʋgʋs kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ atan (113) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan' pʋʋgin (230 seats).
english: The National Democratic Congress won a majority total of 113 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi, nɛ pistan nɛ anii (20,038) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa an tusa pistan' nɛ anii, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piinɛ anii (38,618) dinɛ zɛm nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne du'al pisnii nɛ awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.89%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He was elected with 20,038 votes out of 38,618 total valid votes cast equivalent to 51.89% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Josuah Ayarkwa onɛ bɛ New Patriotic Party, Patrick K. Konadu onɛ bɛ People's National Convention, K.K. Nti Oliver onɛ bɛ Democratic Freedom Party, Joseph Snwok Lambon onɛ bɛ Convention People's Party nɛ Yusif Mohammed Kpajal onɛ an independent candidate.
english: He was elected over Dr. Josuah Ayarkwa of the New Patriotic Party, Patrick K. Konadu of the People's National Convention, K.K. Nti Oliver of the Democratic Freedom Party, Joseph Snwok Lambon of the Convention People's Party and Yusif Mohammed Kpajal an independent candidate.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔt la kanl kɔbiga pʋʋgin zɛmnɛ nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anaasi du'al pisnii nɛ atan (44.83%), nɛɛm du'al pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (0.56%), nɛɛm du'al pistan' nɛ anu (0.35%), nɛɛm du'al piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (0.97%) nɛ yinne du'al pistan' nɛ awai (1.39%) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la tun' taaba si'em la.

kusaal: Nɛ' da zɛmnɛ nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.

english: These obtained 324, 13,608,240 and 2,218 votes respectively of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ivor Kobina Greenstreet, dʋ'am dabisir anɛ yʋʋm tusa kɔbis wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu, nwadisa anu la ni, dabisa pistan' nɛ yinne (31 May 1966).
english: Ivor Kobina Greenstreet (born 31 May 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and lawyer.

kusaal: Dennis Greenstreet nɛ Miranda Greenstreet, O da anɛ pa'an-pa'an University of Ghana,ka kɛŋ tuoni da lɛn an kpɛɛm yinne tis nɛ Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO).
english: Ivor is the third of four siblings born on 31 May 1966 in Accra at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital to Prof. Dennis Greenstreet and Miranda Greenstreet, formerly a professor at the University of Ghana and co-chair of the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers.

kusaal: O pʋ'a anɛ Ghana zugraan kʋdʋg nya'andɔl kanɛ dig o nʋ'ʋg zug ka ba buon o Vice President kʋdʋg Kow Arkaah, onɛ mɛ da an kɔɔtɔ tʋntʋn.
english: He is married to the daughter of late former Vice President Kow Arkaah, who is also a lawyer with three children, a son and two daughters.

kusaal: O yitnɛ Ga-Mashie Accra sʋ'ʋlim.
english: He is a native of Ga-Mashie in Accra.

kusaal: On da naae o zamisʋk la, o da nyɛ tʋʋma Middle Temple nɛ Ghana Bar kɔɔtɔ tʋʋma.
english: On completion, he was called to the Middle Temple and Ghana Bar respectively.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1997) la ni, o da paam sapʋ'ad bɛ sour kanɛ an Tema Motorway, ka li pɔn'ɔlim o ti paae zina ka o nan zin'i pɔn'ɔr kɛ'kɛ ni la.
english: In 1997, he was involved in an accident on the Tema Motorway, which resulted in him using a wheelchair till date.

kusaal: O nyɛ kɔɔtɔ ni tʋʋma linɛ an Ghana Bar nɛ English Bar (Inner Temple).
english: He was called to the Ghana Bar and the English Bar (Inner Temple).

kusaal: O da anɛ niŋkpi'eŋi paas People's Convention Party (PCP) na'adɔɔg la ni nɛ o na'adɔɔg la daa ti nɔki ba mɛŋi la'as nɛ na'adɔɔg kanɛ an NCP yʋ'ʋn kilim CPP yʋm tusa kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobu la ni (1996).
english: He was an active member of the People's Convention Party (PCP) before the party merged with NCP to form the CPP in 1996.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la ni (2004), o na'adɔɔg dim da gaŋʋ o ye o an wada maan tis Ayawaso West Wuogon constituency nya'a na'am yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la ni votʋʋg la (2004 Ghanaian general election) linɛ ka o da kɔ'ɔŋ ka Akosua Frema Osei-Opare onɛ da an NPP na'adɔɔg nid, da di' la.
english: In 2004 he was selected by the party as its parliamentary candidate for Ayawaso West Wuogon constituency to contest in the 2004 Ghanaian general election, which he lost to Akosua Frema Osei-Opare of the NPP.

kusaal: Onɛ da an na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon CPP la nii da di na'am, an ba gbaʋŋ sɔbid nɔɔr ayi' yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la, nɛ tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ yinne la ni (2007 and 2011).
english: He was the first General Secretary to be re-elected twice for the CPP in 2007 and also in 2011.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ mɔr pɛbisim la'adi lubid kuom wʋʋ ziŋ nɛ (Scuba diver), onɛ da an yiiga daani an ninsabilis tɛŋ nidi da paasi nya'a nɛ dunia dim diem kanɛ an a-iank nɛ pɛbisim naani agɔli signa yiiga diema la (parachuting event), o mɛ lɛn anɛ banɛ gɔsid malifʋ nam yɛla Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka ba buoni ba ye Ghana National Rifle Association la (GNRA).
english: He is an enthusiastic Scuba diver, the first African to participate in an international parachuting event, and a member of the Ghana National Rifle Association (GNRA).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu, pin'ilig nwadig la (January 2016), o da nya'a na'am nɛ o taaba na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon CPP la zugraan ka da di ya'an, bozugo banɛ da vɔɔti tis o la da anɛ nidib tusa kɔbʋsyi' nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1,288 votes), ka lin da anɛ pisyuobu nɛ anaasi nɛ pʋdigir ayi' (64.2%), kɔbʋga pʋʋgin, ka onɛ daa nya'a nɛ o ka o yʋʋr buon Samia Nkrumah, onɛ an Ghana yiiga zugraan kudug ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Kwame Nkrumah po'ayua, da nyɛ nidib biela ka ba tɔn' tis o, nidib kɔbʋs nu nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai ma'a (579 votes).
english: In January 2016, he contested for the Presidential Nomination to represent the CPP and won with a total vote of 1,288 votes, representing 64.2% of valid votes cast, while his closest contender, Samia Nkrumah, daughter of Ghana's first President Kwame Nkrumah, managed only 579 votes.

kusaal: Onɛ da an na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon (CPP) la kpɛɛm nya' na'am yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu (2016 Ghanaian general election).
english: He was the 2016 Ghanaian general election flagbearer for the (CPP).

kusaal: O da kɔ'ɔŋ na'am la, bɔzugo, nidib tusa pisinɛ anu nɛ kɔbʋsnu nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi' (25,552 votes), ka lin anɛ kɔbʋga pʋʋgin anɛ zaalim nɛ pʋdigir pisi nɛ anaasi (0.24%) ka Nana Akufo-Addo da di' ya'an.
english: At the end of the election he lost with 25,552 votes representing 0.24 with Nana Akufo-Addo emerging as winner.

kusaal: O anɛ na'am nya'ad Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka lɛn an kɔɔtɔ tʋmtʋm (lawyer).
english: Ivor Kobina Greenstreet (born 31 May 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and lawyer.

kusaal: Onɛ da lieb na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon Convention People's Party (CPP) la tuongat, da nya'a na'am yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi na'am,nya'ab saŋa la ni (2020 Ghanaian general election)
english: He was the Presidential candidate for the Convention People's Party (CPP) in the 2020 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Ivor da paas nɛ o saam biis anaasi ni, abʋatan' ni, ka o dʋ'am dabisir anɛ yʋʋm tusa, kɔbis wai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu, nwadis anu la ni, dabisa pistan' nɛ yinne (31 May 1966), asibiti kanɛ ka ba buon ye Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital, Accra sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Ivor is the third of four siblings born on 31 May 1966 in Accra at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital to Prof. Dennis Greenstreet and Miranda Greenstreet, formerly a professor at the University of Ghana and co-chair of the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers.

kusaal: O da pin'il o sakur kɛnnɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, O mɛ lɛn anɛ onɛ mɔr pɛbisim la'adi lugid ku'om wʋʋ ziŋ nɛ (Scuba diver), onɛ da an yiiga daani an ninsabilis tɛŋ nidi da paasi nya'a nɛ dunia dim diem kanɛ an a-iank nɛ pɛbisim naani agɔli signa yiiga diema la (parachuting event), o mɛ lɛn anɛ banɛ gɔsid malifʋ nam yɛla Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka ba buoni ba ye Ghana National Rifle Association la.
english: He had his early education in Ghana and is an enthusiastic Scuba diver, the first African to participate in an international parachuting event, and a member of the Ghana National Rifle Association.

kusaal: Ivor tʋmnɛ lawyer tʋʋma ka lɛn an onɛ sɔbid gbana.
english: Ivor is a lawyer by profession and a publisher.

kusaal: O da tʋm tʋʋma bɛdɛgʋ CPP ni.
english: He continued to play various roles in the CPP.

kusaal: O ya'an la da kɛ ka o an yiiga sɔb Ghana sʋ'ʋlim nya'a gɔmena zugraan na'am ka mɔr wintadimis.
english: This victory made him the first physically challenged person to contest for a Presidential election in Ghana.

kusaal: Na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon Convention People's Party (CPP) da len gaŋ o ye o an ba tuongat yʋʋm tusa sayi' nɛ pisi la ni na'am nya'ab saŋa la (2020 general elections).
english: He was re-elected as the flagbearer for the Convention People's Party (CPP) for the 2020 general elections.

kusaal: O anɛ na'a,nya'ad kanɛ mɔr bɔɔdim kati waae nidib yɔlisim nɛ ba nyali' yɛla li kaskas anɛ dasam nɛ pʋ'asada nɛ pʋ'ab nɛ banɛ pʋ,mɔraa bɛɛ nɔŋ dim.
english: He is a political militant with the vision of augmenting the rights, freedom and opportunities of the youth, women, and the less privileged.

kusaal: Jacob Iddriss Abdulai (Da dʋ'a nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadisa ayi la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar, 24 February 1957) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka bɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress ni.
english: Jacob Iddriss Abdulai (born 24 February 1957) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Savelegu Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Northern Region la.
english: He is the member of parliament for Savelugu Constituency, Northern Region.

english: Geodetic Engineering and Msc.

english: Jacob was born on February 24, 1957, and hails from Savelugu.
