english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Jambaidu Awuni da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd Ghana first republic la ni.
english: Jambaidu Awuni was a Ghanaian politician in the first republic.

kusaal: O da paasnɛ Legislative Assembly zi'eni tis Northern territories Northern People's Party (NPP) nɔba zug di yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne la ni (1951) paae yʋʋm yusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ naasi (1954).
english: He was a member of the Legislative Assembly representing the Northern territories on the ticket of the Northern People's Party (NPP) from 1951 to 1954.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn gaŋ o ya'as yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yuobʋ (1956) ka o zi'eni tis Kusasi Central constituency dim yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yuobʋ (1956) kem paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ nu (1965).
english: He was re-elected into the legislative in 1956 to represent the Kusasi Central constituency from 1956 until 1965.

kusaal: Awuni da zɛrig Mumuni Bawumia nɛ on gʋ'ʋŋ la ka ye o kʋ lɛn nyaŋi an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid ya'asɛ Mumuni Bawumia nan bɛ Na'adɔkan ni la.
english: Awuni blamed Mumuni Bawumia for the failure and felt he could no longer remain a member of the NPP as long as Mumuni Bawumia remained a member of the party.

kusaal: O da sɔb gbaʋŋʋ tis ka yi Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, NPP tiaki keŋ naal Convention People's Party (CPP) banɛ zin'i nya'aŋ Parliament nya'aŋ la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yɔpɔi lnwadisa anii la ni (August 1957).
english: He then resigned from the NPP and crossed carpets to join the Convention People's Party (CPP) backbenchers in parliament in August 1957.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu la ni (1965) o da lieb wadmaani tis Garu constituency.
english: In 1965 he became the member of parliament for the Garu constituency.

kusaal: O da kpɛlim ani hali ti paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ nwadisa ayi la ni (February 1966) ban da yisi Nkrumah government na'amin la.
english: He remained in parliament until February 1966 when the Nkrumah government was overthrown.

kusaal: James Agalga anɛ Ghana nwa pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paas ayɔpɔi Ghana republic kanɛ paas anaasi nwa ni la,o zi'inɛ tis Builsa North Constituency bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlum , o zi'enɛ tis ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la.
english: James Agalga is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Builsa North Constituency in the Upper East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Agalga da anɛ Deputy Minister for Interior bɛ John Mahama saŋa la.
english: Agalga was the Deputy Minister for Interior under the John Mahama Administration.

kusaal: Nannana o anɛ Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament's Defense nɛ Interior Committee.
english: He is currently the Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament's Defense and Interior Committee.

kusaal: Ba da du'a James nɛ bɛ Chuchuliga kanɛ bɛ Upper East Region, Ghana nwa ni, nwadis ayuobʋ li dabisim piiga daar, yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbisawai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai la ni.
english: James was born in Chuchuliga in the Upper East Region of Ghana on 10 June 1979.

kusaal: O da keŋ University of Ghana, ka o yina nɛ kasɛtta gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka ti buon ye, LLB Hons bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayi' la ni.
english: He attended University of Ghana where he graduated with LLB Hons in 2002.

kusaal: Ka o da lɛn di'e o kasɛtta gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka ti buon ye, B.L bɛ Ghana School of Law bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la ni.
english: He also obtained his B.L from the Ghana School of Law in 2004.

kusaal: O da anɛ Managing Partner of Law Temple yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' la ni.
english: He was the Managing Partner of Law Temple from 2008 to 2013.

kusaal: O da anɛ Associate bɛ Center for Public Interest Law.
english: He was an Associate at the Center for Public Interest Law.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ tu'as tu'asid bɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ti buon ye, NDEZEB Law Consult.
english: He was also the Barrister at NDEZEB Law Consult.

kusaal: O pʋ'ʋsid I Catholic pʋ'ʋsʋm .
english: He is a Catholic.

kusaal: O da lɛn yina nɛ kasɛtta gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka ti buon ye, M.A in Conflict, Peace and Security bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anii.
english: He also graduated with an M.A in Conflict, Peace and Security in 2018.

kusaal: O da paas la'asʋg kanɛ ka ti buon ye, Members Holding Offices of Profit la'asʋg, Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Committee ka lɛn paas Appointments la'asʋg.
english: He was part of the Members Holding Offices of Profit Committee, Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Committee and also Appointments Committee under the 6th Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: James Gyakye Quayson (ba da dʋ'a o nɛ 9 October 1952) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tis Assin North constituency.
english: James Gyakye Quayson (born 9 October 1952) is a Ghanaian politician who is currently serving as the member of Parliament (MP) for Assin North.

kusaal: Daʋŋ: o da gɛsig Ghana wada gbaʋŋ la article 92 2a, dinɛ yɛl ye sɔ pʋ nar ye o lieb wadmaan na o ya'a an tensi'a nidi paas ka ka' Gaana ma'aanɛ.
english: Quayson, who was a citizen of Canada, was found in violation of Article 92, Clause 2a of Ghana's constitution, when he ran for MP for Assin North during the 2020 parliamentary election, which states "a person shall not be qualified to be a member of parliament if he owes allegiance to a country other than Ghana".

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Quayson nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi Nwadis piiga la daba awai daar (9 October 1952) ka o yi Assin Bereku bɛ Central Region, Ghana.
english: James Gyakye Quayson hails from Assin Bereku in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔnrɛ bachelor's degree in Social Sciences nɛ master's degree in Urban Planning and Community Development.
english: He also obtained a master's degree in Urban Planning and Community Development as well.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ lieb Wadmaan la o da anɛ District Manager tis City of Toronto Employment and Social services.
english: Prior to being in parliament, he worked as a District Manager for the City of Toronto Employment and Social services from 2020.

kusaal: Quayson anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid ka an Wadmaani tis Assin North Constituency bɛ Central Region, Ghana.
english: Gyakye Quayson is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and was the member of parliament for Assin North Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi la nii (December 2020), onɛ bɛ Assin Bereku ka o yʋ'ʋr an Michael Ankomah-Nimfah da keŋ Cape Coast High Court ye Quayson pʋ mɔr suor ye o an Wadmaani tisi Assin North bɔzugɔ o mɔr gbaʋnkanɛ pa'al ye o anɛ Canada nɛ Ghana nid sankanɛ ka o da' gbaʋŋ la ye o bɔɔd ye o lieb Wadmaan banɛ gɔsid vɔɔtʋg yɛla, Electoral Commission, nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la.
english: Michael Ankomah-Nimfah, the plaintiff/applicant who filed an election petition against Mr. Quayson has initiated another action at The Supreme Court of Ghana requesting that, the court allows the Cape Coast High Court judgement to take effect as well as prevent further breach of the 1992 Constitution of Ghana by restraining him as member of parliament (MP) since he continued to sit in parliament as MP and this was challenged within the house as well.

kusaal: Quayson paas Privileges Committee ka lɛn paas Local Government and Rural Development Committee.
english: Quayson was a member of the House Committee and also a member of the Local Government and Rural Development Committee.

kusaal: Ghana wada gbaʋŋ la pa'al ye sɔ ya'a bɛ tɛɛnsa ayi on sɔb pʋ nar ye o mɔr gɔmina ɔfisɛ bɛɛ o an Wadmaana.
english: In a unanimous decision by The Supreme Court of Ghana consisting of Justices Jones Dotse, Nene Amegatcher, Mariama Owusu, Gertrude Torkonoo, Henrietta Mensah-Bonsu, Emmanuel Kulendi and Barbara Ackah Ayensu, presiding Judge Justice Jones Dotse on 17 May 2023 ruled that the Electoral Commission of Ghana acted unconstitutionally by accepting the nomination of Mr. Quayson without proof of citizenship renunciation before contesting the 2020 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: James Klutse Avedzi anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la tis Ketu North Constituency bɛ Volta Region la.
english: James Klutse Avedzi (born 14 July 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ketu North Constituency in the Volta Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Xipe bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Xipe in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ University of Liverpool ka naae ani nɛ master's digirii in Finance and Accounting kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016).
english: He attended University of Liverpool and graduated with a master's degree in Finance and Accounting in 2016.

kusaal: O da lɛn maal Fcfia yi Chartered Institute of Financial and Investment Analysis Ghana ya'as.
english: He also had his Fcfia from the Chartered Institute of Financial and Investment Analysis in Ghana.

kusaal: O pu'a da kpinɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la dabpistan' daar (30 yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2020) ban'as bi'ela da nya'aŋ o bɛ Ketu South District Sibiti la ni.
english: He is a Christian who worships in the Global Evangelical Church His wife died on 30 January 2020 after being unwell for some time at the Ketu South District Hospital.

kusaal: James Klutse Avedzi da anɛ principal accountant bɛ Controller and Accountant Generals Department Accra yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la ni (1995) ka naan kpɛn' pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi (2004).
english: James Klutse Avedzi worked as the principal accountant at the Controller and Accountant Generals Department in Accra from 1995 before seeking political office in 2004.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ kʋkdaan tis Public Accounts Committee.
english: He was also the chairman of the Public Accounts Committee of parliament.

kusaal: James anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg (NDC) nid, o da nyi'a ya ka di Ketu North constituency sʋ'ʋlim wadmaan kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: James is a member of the National Democratic congress (NDC), He contested and won the parliamentary seat for the Ketu North constituency in 2005.

kusaal: Din yi sankan la onɛ an wadmaani tis Ketu North Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim la Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anu (5th), ayuobʋ (6th) nɛ ayɔpɔi la (7th) Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He has since then represented the Ketu North Constituency in the 5th, 6th and 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a James Klutse Avedzi nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi Nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpii nɛ anaasi daar (14 sɛnlʋŋ nwadig 1964).
english: James Klutse Avedzi was born on 14 July 1964.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ maal doctorate in International and Political Finance in Business university of Costa Rica.
english: He further pursued a doctorate in International and Political Finance in Business at the university of Costa Rica. He also had his ICA-G from the Institute of Chartered Accountant in Ghana and also his MCIT from Ghana Chartered Institute of Taxation.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr ICA-G kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Institute of Chartered Accountant bɛ Ghana la ka lɛn maal o MCIT Ghana Chartered Institute of Taxation.
english: He further pursued a doctorate in International and Political Finance in Business at the university of Costa Rica. He also had his ICA-G from the Institute of Chartered Accountant in Ghana and also his MCIT from Ghana Chartered Institute of Taxation.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Global Evangelical pʋ'ʋsʋm.
english: He is a Christian who worships in the Global Evangelical Church His wife died on 30 January 2020 after being unwell for some time at the Ketu South District Hospital.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Deputy Minority Leader tis Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC Wadmaanib yin la.
english: In 2023, he was removed from office as the Deputy Minority Leader for the NDC and was replaced by Kofi Armah Buah together with some other leaders.

kusaal: O da anɛ kʋkdaan kʋdʋgʋ tis la'askanɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla Wadmaanib yin la.
english: He was also the chairman of the Public Accounts Committee of parliament.

kusaal: Nimbanɛ bɛ Jeju, di kas kas anɛ banɛ bɛ Gwideok, Geumnyeong, nɛ Aewol zin'isin la nɔkid 12 postnami niŋid wief zugin nɛ gum fuugkanɛ ka ba nɔg gumma kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔbi ʋgi li ye ba kɛ ka teŋgbanpʋ'a la Yeongdeung Halmang mɔr sumalisim, onɛ ka ba niŋ yadda ye o kaae ba sʋ'ʋlim la Korean shamanism saŋa.
english: The people of Jeju, especially those in the Gwideok, Geumnyeong, and Aewol areas put up 12 posts in the shape of horse heads and colorful silk fabrics to cheer up the goddess Yeongdeung Halmang, who is believed to have visited their place in Korean shamanism.

kusaal: Malʋŋ kaŋa anɛ dinɛ ka ba gu'ud bɔzugɔ di anɛ Important Intangible Cultural Properties of Korea.
english: This celebration is protected as an Important Intangible Cultural Properties of Korea.

kusaal: Ya'asa, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni, Jeju Chilmeoridang yeondeunggut da paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists la ni.
english: Furthermore, in 2009, Jeju Chilmeoridang yeondeunggut was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists.

kusaal: Nananna, gut kaŋa pʋ lɛm nyɛt na'ana bɔzugɔ shaman kanɛ tʋmi li la pʋ nyɛt na'ana.
english: Now, this gut is very rare because the shaman who practices it is rare.

kusaal: Ya'a dɔlis mu'a zin'a gʋʋra Egypt teŋin nɛ Sudan nɛ Beja buudinam la sʋʋgin, ba bɔɔddɛ Arabic dishdash la kpaadibi yɛɛdi li la yɛla.
english: Along the Red Sea coast in Egypt, and Sudan and among Beja tribesmen, the Arabic dishdash is preferred due to the jalabeya's relation to farming.

kusaal: Yiiga din la bɛ Middle Upper Egypt, lin zaŋ Beni Suef keŋ paae Assiut, ka yuolʋŋ din la bɛ Delta.
english: The former is common in Middle Upper Egypt from Beni Suef to Assiut, and the latter is common in the Delta.

kusaal: Ba mɛ yɛɛd fuug la Sudan teŋin, amaa li mɔr saalim sieba, ka si'im la kpɛn anɛ pielig, la'am nɛ teŋ sieba Eritrea nɛ Ethiopia sʋ'ʋlim namin.
english: A full male dress in Sudan usually consists of three pieces, the jibba, the kaftan, and the sederi.

kusaal: Jellabiya fuyɛɛdiŋ la bɛɛ li kɔn' nɛ Arabic thawb la, ka lin nwaar la yalim nɛ, lin pʋ mɔr si'im si'a ( ka sieba nii, ga'adis pʋ bɛɛ), ka wa'am, ka funu'us la yalim.
english: The Jellabiya, also Jalabiya, Galabeya or Dalabiya (Standard Arabic: جَلَّابِيَّة / ALA-LC: Jallābīyah, Sudanese Arabic: Jilabīyah, Egyptian Arabic: Galabiya, Saʽidi Arabic: Dalabiya, Egyptian Arabic: [ɡæ.læ.ˈbej.jæ-]; is a loose-fitting, traditional garment from Egypt.

kusaal: Egypt teŋi nɛ, pu'ab galabeya bɛ gʋn-gʋn sʋ'ʋlim nam la ni.
english: Deep Upper Egypt has both, distributed along ethnic lines.The galabeya bi wist has a bodice and separate skirt.

kusaal: Ba bɛdigʋ niŋgɔɔnr kibigir ye anɛ nwa nam, V neck, square, open nɛ collared, ba mɛ lɛn tun'e gʋli pɛ'ɛs.
english: The popular necklines are V neck, square, open, and collared, and may be combined in design.

kusaal: Jenny Morris,ka nidib mɛ lɛm buon on ye "The Giggling Gourmet" anɛ niŋkanɛ di'e yʋ'ʋr diib dʋgʋb nɛ li kuosʋg pʋʋgʋn ka lɛn an onɛ pian'ad walisin bɛ South Africa.
english: Jenny Morris, also known as "The Giggling Gourmet", is a celebrity chef and radio personality from South Africa. Having run a cooking school since 1997, and appearing on television and radio in South Africa, she has signed to appear on the Food Network, becoming the first South African to host her own show on the channel.

kusaal: O da sɔb gbana atan' sieba ka ba anɛ "Rude Food, Nude Food, Good Food" in 2004, "More Rude Food" in 2006 nɛ "Cooking with Jenny Morris" in 2012, ka mɛ la'am sʋŋ labaya dim gbana sɔbʋgin, hali ka la'am sɔbid bakɔi wʋsa tis lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid di'ema nɛ duorum yɛla bɛ South Africa.
english: She has written three cookbooks, "Rude Food, Nude Food, Good Food" in 2004, "More Rude Food" in 2006 and "Cooking with Jenny Morris" in 2012, as well as contributing to magazines and writing a weekly column for an entertainment guide in South Africa. She is also a presenter on radio station Cape Talk, where she discusses both food and romance.

kusaal: O da yi yiŋ na sɔnsi o diib dʋgʋb sɔnsʋg tiivi ni dinɛ ka o da pʋd yɛ, Jenny Morris Cooks Morocco, on da sɔs paam sour tiivi ni August 2011.
english: She has appeared in a show for the Food Network entitled Jenny Morris Cooks Morocco, having signed for the network in August 2011.

kusaal: On nɛ o yidim da bɛnɛ Cape Town.
english: She lives with her family in Cape Town.

kusaal: Morris da yɔ'ɔg didʋgʋdib di'ema zin'ig 1997, maali di ka an diib dʋgʋb sakur nɛ diib kuosʋg zin'ig.
english: Morris opened "Cook's Playground" in 1997, operating it as a cooking school and catering company.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛm anɛ pian'a walisin Cape Talk, Ani ka o ɛnnti sɔnsid diib dʋgʋb yɛla la'am nɛ Nɔŋilim sɔnsʋg.
english: She has written three cookbooks, "Rude Food, Nude Food, Good Food" in 2004, "More Rude Food" in 2006 and "Cooking with Jenny Morris" in 2012, as well as contributing to magazines and writing a weekly column for an entertainment guide in South Africa. She is also a presenter on radio station Cape Talk, where she discusses both food and romance.

kusaal: Jirapa an tempʋtita'ari tis Jirapa Municipali bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Jirapa is the capital town of the Jirapa Municipal in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Bipumis sakur yimmir kanɛ bɛ region la ni, Saint Francis of Assisi Girls' Secondary School, bɛnɛ tempʋʋg la ni.
english: The only girls' secondary school in the region, St. Francis Girls' Secondary School, is situated in the town.

kusaal: Jirapa Senior Secondary School.
english: Jirapa Senior High School.

kusaal: Joseph's Hospital dinɛ bɛ Jirapa la an district la sibiti.
english: St. Joseph's Hospital in Jirapa is the district hospital.

kusaal: Di tʋʋma la Franciscan Missionaries of Mary da pinili di yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai (1949) la ni ye ba kennɛ pi'esid fɛn'ɛd, ka ba da tiaki di ka di kilim sibiti ka Catholic Mission of Tamale dim da di'e di yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ atan (1953).
english: The Franciscan Missionaries of Mary started the work in 1949 as a wound-dressing centre.

kusaal: Pa'alʋg Sakuya ayi da naal nɛ sibiti la ka yʋ'ʋn zi'e ba nyadi Jirapa Nurses' Training College nɛ Jirapa Midwifery Training College.
english: Two training schools originally attached to the hospital are now the autonomous Jirapa Nursing Training College and Jirapa Midwifery Training College.

kusaal: Joseph Orphanage mɛ da tiaki yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la n iyi kpiibʋg kanɛ yʋ'ʋn bɛ Italy.
english: The St. Joseph Orphanage was renovated in about 2004 by an orphan who is now resident in Italy.

kusaal: Joseph Catholic Church an Catholic Church kanɛ kʋdʋg hali Upper West Region.
english: St. Joseph Catholic Church is the oldest Catholic Church in the Upper West Region.

kusaal: Roman Catholic malima bɛ Jirapa-Lambussie district.
english: There is a very strong Roman Catholic tradition in the Jirapa-Lambussie district.

kusaal: White Fathers da yɔ'ɔg mission station yiiga Navrongo yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ ayuobʋ (1906), ani ka ba da tʋm dapa atan ye ba tʋm Jirapa yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisi nɛ awai (1929) la ni.
english: The White Fathers opened a mission station first in Navrongo in 1906, from which three men were delegated to work in Jirapa in 1929.

kusaal: Gɔmena gbana ni, kɔbiga pʋʋgin, pisnaasi nɛ ayi du'al anu (42.5%) yi nimbanɛ bɛ district la ni yʋ'ʋn anɛ Kristo biis, ka piswai nɛ ayuobʋ du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (96.1%) anɛ Catholic dim, ka banɛ kpɛlim la an mɔɔm bɛɛ ba'amaannib.
english: According to government statistics, 42.5% of the population in the district now claim to be Christian, 96.1% of which are Catholic, the remainder being affiliated to either Islam or traditional religion.

kusaal: Jirapa na'abi an Paramount Chief tis Jirapa traditional area, ka nananna anɛ Peter Nanfuri, Naa Ansoleh Ganaa II.
english: The Chief of Jirapa is the Paramount Chief of the Jirapa traditional area, and is at present Peter Nanfuri, Naa Ansoleh Ganaa II.

kusaal: Ba mɔr yʋʋm-yʋʋm malʋŋ kanɛ an Bong-Ngo bɛ Jirapa tis na'ab la nɛ nidib la.
english: There is an annual festival called Bong-Ngo in Jirapa for the chiefs and people of the area.

kusaal: Nimbanɛ bɛ ani la anɛ Dagaaba, ka ba pian'ad la an Dagaare, dinɛ paas Gur buudi dinɛ bɛ Niger–Congo buudi pian'ad zakin la.
english: The local people are called Dagaaba, and speak Dagaare, which is a Gur branch of the Niger–Congo language family.

kusaal: Police Station nɛ district magistrate court bɛ sʋ'ʋlim la ni.
english: There is a police station and a district magistrate court.

kusaal: La'an nɛ zaba da bɛ banɛ da paam faangir yiiga la nɛ teŋ la na'anam, nɛ ban da pʋ siak ye ba di'e British District Commissioner of Lawra, ba da kɛ satita'ar ni ni ʋʋn hali Lawra district, Jirapa ma'aa, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan nɛ ayi (1932) la ni.
english: Despite early conflicts between converts and the local chiefs, and even the resulting disapproval of the British District Commissioner of Lawra, the work was given great impetus by the locally famous 'rain event' of 1932 in which rain fell during a severe drought in the Lawra district, only in Jirapa and in nearby villages following prayer for each case.

kusaal: Ba sɔbid teŋ la yʋ'ʋr Dagaare nɛ Gyerebaa, ka ba lɛɛ buoni li ye jira-'baa, ka di gbin anɛ kɔlkɛɛna bɔn'ɔg.
english: The name of the town, written in Dagaare as Gyerebaa, is pronounced roughly as jira-'baa, and means 'reed-stream', i.e. a stream of reeds.

kusaal: Onɛ da an ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la (Speaker of Parliament) kpɛɛm nya'andɔl onɛ paas ayi' lin da yi yʋʋm 2013 ti paae yʋʋm 2017 ka lɛn an Railways and Development Minista lin yi yʋʋm 2017 ti paae yʋʋm 2021 la ni.
english: He is a former Attorney-General of Ghana (2006–2009), Second Deputy Speaker of Parliament (2013–2017) and Railways Development Minister (2017–2021).

kusaal: O ma da anɛ pa'an ka o yυ'υr buon ye, Lauraine Ghartey (née Daniels), ka o saam mɛ da anɛ Gɔmina tυmtυm ka o yυ'υr buon Joseph Ghartey.
english: Joe Ghartey was born in Accra, Ghana, to a teacher, Lauraine Ghartey (née Daniels), and a public servant, Joseph Ghartey, on 15 June 1961.

kusaal: O si'iŋi o biilimin sakur kennɛ Ridge Church School linɛ bɛ Ankara sυ'υlυmin la, ka lin nya'aŋ ka o tɔlisi keŋ SHS Mfantsipim Sakur linɛ bɛ Cape Coast la ni.
english: He started his early education at the Ridge Church School in Accra and later moved to the secondary boarding school, Mfantsipim School, in Cape Coast.

kusaal: Ghartey da naae Mfantsipim Sakurin ka tɔlisi keŋ University of Ghana yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1986).
english: After Mfantsipim, Ghartey enrolled to study law and obtained his LLB (Hons) degree in 1986 from the University of Ghana, and BL from the Ghana School of Law in 1988.

kusaal: Ghartey n da naae o sakur ka ye o tʋm yυυm yinne tis Gɔmina la, o da tυmnɛ n bɛ Komenda Eguafo Abirem linɛ bɛ ti Ghana Cape coast Sυ'υlυm la n bɛ wada tυυma dɔɔgin tυm.
english: Ghartey undertook his National Service duty as Legal Officer to the Komenda Eguafo Abirem District Assembly in the Central Region of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o paam tυυma linɛ an Chambers of Lawyer Gwira n bɛ Sekondi.
english: He also took up a job as an Associate at the Chambers of Lawyer Gwira in Sekondi.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ya'as, ka o paas Akufo-Addo, Prempeh nɛ ninsieba banɛ da yɔ'ɔg wada tυυma ti Ghana sυ'υlυm kpɛla la, lin ka John Kufuor Nana Akufo-Addo da mɔri kena la.
english: Later, he would join the firm of Akufo-Addo, Prempeh & Co., a leading law firm in Ghana, which was co-founded by his future colleague parliamentarian and Cabinet Minister in the John Kufuor administration, Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Yυma ayɔpɔi ka Ghartey da tυm ani ka yʋʋm 1994 la ni ka Ghartey bas wada tυυma kanna ka tɔɔm yɔ'ɔgi o mɛŋ wada tυυma linɛ buon ye, Ghartey & Ghartey onɛ o pu'a Efua Ghartey onɛ da an lawyer kanɛ ka ba tisidi o girima hali.
english: Ghartey left this firm after seven years and in 1994 co-founded the law firm, Ghartey & Ghartey with his wife Efua Ghartey, who is also a lawyer.

kusaal: Girima daan Ghartey da mɔr zamisυg nam kɔn'ɔ-kɔn'ɔb linɛ an Human Rights, Civil Rights nɛ zamisυg linɛ nami pa'an teŋim bii n nar ye o tυm si'em.
english: As a co-founder of the Ghana Committee on Human and Peoples Rights, Ghartey has provided education on Human Rights, Civil Rights and Obligations to various citizen groups.

kusaal: Onɛ da lɛn an kυk daan n tis Inter African Network of Human Rights Organizations n bɛ Zambia.
english: He was chair of the Inter African Network of Human Rights Organizations based in Zambia.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'an n bɛ the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).
english: He has been a lecturer in Corporate Governance and Executive MBA at the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'an n bɛ Ghana Stock Exchange.
english: He was an instructor at the Ghana Stock Exchange.

kusaal: Yuuma 2004 la ni ka o da yɔ'ɔg Doing Business and Investing in Ghana – Legal and Institutional Framework".
english: In 2004, he wrote Doing Business and Investing in Ghana – Legal and Institutional Framework.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn pa'an linɛ an Company Law n bɛ Ghana School of Law nɛ Mountcrest University la ni n bɛ Ankara.
english: He also taught Company Law at the Ghana School of Law and Mountcrest University in Accra.

kusaal: O da paas nimbanɛ da sɔb gbaυŋ linɛ buon ye "Stolen Verdict", la yυυm 1993 la ni, li da anɛ gbaυŋ linɛ pa'an wa'adim linɛ da bɛ vɔt kanɛ da maal yuma 1992 la ni.
english: He was part of the team that wrote the "Stolen Verdict", in 1993, which was a detailed account of the widespread electoral malpractices that occurred during the 1992 general election in Ghana.

kusaal: Lin nɔk tembanɛ kpi'e atɛok nɔorin Gaana sυ'υlυm la, Ghartey sυŋ sυ'υlυm nam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb banɛ sieba anɛ; Ho, Sakondi, Shama, Takoradi, Tarkwa, Effie Kwasimintsim, Tarkwa, Prestea, Amenfi, Korle Klottey, La-Dade Kotopon nɛ Hohoe.
english: Along the coastal belt of Ghana, Ghartey has supported constituencies in the Western, Central, Greater Accra and Volta Regions, including Shama, Sekondi, Takoradi, Effie Kwasimintsim, Tarkwa, Prestea, Amenfi, Korle Klottey, La-Dade Kotopon and Hohoe.

kusaal: Nannanna Ghartey an wadmaan n zi'enɛ tis Essikado/Ketan sυ'υlυm ti Gaana Republic la ni.
english: Ghartey is the NPP Member of Parliament for Essikado/Ketan Constituency in the Western Region of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ti Gaana Gɔmina John Agyekum Kufuor win la, ba da gaŋi Ghartey ye o an Deputy Attorney General nɛ Minista of Justice nya'andɔl Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris atan' yuma tusa yi nɛ anu la pυυgin.
english: During the administration of President John Agyekum Kufuor, Ghartey was appointed Deputy Attorney General and Deputy Minister of Justice in March 2005.

kusaal: O da an Attorney-General la, li anɛ Ghartey n da yɔ'ɔg pian'azug linɛ an ye tiakir la Ministry of Justice la ni.
english: As Attorney-General, Ghartey launched an Agenda for Change in the Ministry of Justice.

kusaal: Nannanna one an Members Holding Offices of Profit la kpɛɛm.
english: He chairs the Committee of Members Holding Offices of Profit.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris anu la, yuma tusa yi nɛ piina yɔpɔi ni, ka ti Gaana Gɔmid Akufo-Addo da yɔ'ɔg linɛ an Ministry of Railways Development ka gaŋ Minista kanɛ na gɔsi li yɛla.
english: In May 2017, President Akufo-Addo created the Ministry of Railways Development as a cabinet position and named Ghartey as the sector Minister.

kusaal: Efua Ghartey n da an Bible Society of Ghana la kpɛɛm ka lɛn an United Bible Societies la kpɛɛm, la'asυg nwa tυmnɛ nɛ tɛmis kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb wυυ kɔbis yi'.
english: Efua Ghartey is the Chairperson of the Bible Society of Ghana and the Chairperson of the International Board of the United Bible Societies (UBS), which operates in more than 200 countries.

kusaal: Joe Ghartey anɛ lɔya nɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Joe Ghartey was born in Accra, Ghana, to a teacher, Lauraine Ghartey (née Daniels), and a public servant, Joseph Ghartey, on 15 June 1961.

kusaal: Onɛ da aan ti Ghana Attorney-General lin yi yʋʋm 2006 ti paae yʋʋm 2009 la ni.
english: He is a former Attorney-General of Ghana (2006–2009), Second Deputy Speaker of Parliament (2013–2017) and Railways Development Minister (2017–2021).

kusaal: O yinɛ Shama linɛ bɛ Ghana Sekondi Sυ'υlυm la.
english: Along the coastal belt of Ghana, Ghartey has supported constituencies in the Western, Central, Greater Accra and Volta Regions, including Shama, Sekondi, Takoradi, Effie Kwasimintsim, Tarkwa, Prestea, Amenfi, Korle Klottey, La-Dade Kotopon and Hohoe.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Joe Ghartey Ankara sυ'υlυm linɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlimin.
english: Joe Ghartey was born in Accra, Ghana, to a teacher, Lauraine Ghartey (née Daniels), and a public servant, Joseph Ghartey, on 15 June 1961.

kusaal: O da naae ani ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ bigis ye o zamis nɛ wada yɛla linɛ an LLB.
english: After Mfantsipim, Ghartey enrolled to study law and obtained his LLB (Hons) degree in 1986 from the University of Ghana, and BL from the Ghana School of Law in 1988.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o lɛn tɔlisi zamis wada yɛla linɛ bɛ Ghana School of Law yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii la ni (1988) naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an BL, yʋʋm kan la pυυgin yim ka ba da buol o ye o paas banɛ zamis wada yɛla la pυυgin.
english: After Mfantsipim, Ghartey enrolled to study law and obtained his LLB (Hons) degree in 1986 from the University of Ghana, and BL from the Ghana School of Law in 1988.

kusaal: Nannana onɛ an kpɛɛm n tis Ghartey & Ghartey wada tυυma la ka lɛn an lɔya kanɛ ka ba tisidi o girima hali, o anɛ banɛ gɔsid wada yɛla n bɛ Labone Ankara Sυ'υlυm.
english: He is the senior partner of a Labone-based law firm.

kusaal: O mi'ilim linɛ ka o mɔr n kati wa'ae wada yɛla la, Ghartey nyaŋi sυŋ ka ti Ghana ligidi nɛ ti diib nɛ tυυma nam bɛllim nɔbig sʋ'υŋa.
english: Ghartey was an adjunct lecturer of Investment Law at the University of Ghana Business School.

kusaal: O nɔki o mi'ilim linɛ an wada tυυma la kɛ ka o tυm tis tυυma dim kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb banɛ bɛ Ghana kpɛla hali nɛ tembanɛ ka' Ghana.
english: He was an instructor at the Ghana Stock Exchange.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2009) la ni la, o da lɛn mɔr kasɛta gbauŋ tita'ar kanɛ an kpikpiŋ nɛ nu'ug tʋʋma maalʋg nɛ li gɔsʋg yɛla (kati wa'ae ligidi tʋʋma yɛla) yir GIMPA lʋgir dimin.
english: In the year 2009, he was awarded an MBA (Finance) from GIMPA.

kusaal: O mɛ da mɔr kpikpiŋ tʋʋma nɛ li pin'ilʋg zamisʋg kasɛta gbauŋ n yi Nobel tɛɛns la'asʋg kpikpiŋ tʋʋma sakur la ni yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ awai (2019) la ni.
english: He also had his Post Graduate Diploma in Applied Business Research from the Nobel International Business School in 2019.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi la, li nwadis piig nɛ yinnɛ la ni (November 2020), o da di'e kpikpiŋ tʋʋma nɛ li tɛndigir kasɛta gbauŋ n yi swiss kpikpiŋ tʋʋma sakur kanɛ bɛ Switzerland sʋ'ʋlimin la.
english: In November 2020, Kumah received a Doctorate in Business Innovation from the Swiss Business School in Switzerland.

kusaal: Ba da nɔk o ka o tʋm ka an wada tʋmtʋm onɛ sa'an nidib wada yɛla nɛ kpɛɛm n bɛ Gaana kɔɔtʋ tita'ar dɔɔg la ni yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ atan' (2013) la ni.
english: He was called to the Ghana Bar as a solicitor and legal practitioner for the Supreme Court of Ghana in 2013.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Aduaprokye kɔɔtʋ linɛ bɛ Adabrakra sʋ'ʋlimin la kpɛɛm yinnɛ.
english: He was a founding member and Managing Partner of Aduaprokye Chambers; a Law Firm located at Adabraka.

kusaal: Ba da anɛ Peter mensa nɛ Moses Addai.
english: They were Peter Mensah and Moses Addai.

kusaal: O yinɛ Ejisu teŋ tita'ar kanɛ ka ba kuod ka gʋ'ʋn ka li bɛ kumasi sʋ'ʋlimin la.
english: He hailed from Ejisu Odaho, a farming community in the Ejisu Municipal in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Joon Ampontuah Kumah mɔr tʋʋma baŋir nɛ li ya'am hali yʋʋma piin anu n bɛ tuongaadʋg ni nɛ nu'ug la'ad maalʋg ni nɛ tʋʋma yɔ'ɔsʋg ni, ka lɛn sʋŋid dasam nɛ pu'asada tʋʋma nɔbigir pʋʋgin.
english: John Ampontuah Kumah had over fifteen years of experience in leadership, creativity, innovation and resourcefulness in creating jobs, and supporting youth development.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn gaŋ o ka o paas Gaana gɔmma zugdaan Akufo Addo nidib piisi banɛ mɔr na'asi nɛ kpi'euŋ la ni yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ awai la ni (2019).
english: John Kumah was judged the most efficient, prominent appointee for 2018 and was also listed among President Akufo Addo's top 20 Most Humble and respectful Appointees In 2019.

kusaal: Ala mɛn ka o lɛn mɔr wada zamisυg kasɛta gbauŋ ya'as n yi Gaana sakur tita'arin la.
english: He also had a Degree in Law (LLB) from the University of Ghana and a Professional Law Degree (BL) from the Ghana School of Law.

kusaal: Ba du'anɛ biisa ayuobʋ nɛ bisieba banɛ ka ba du'adib kae ka ba ugus ba la.
english: They had six children.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ ayi' la ni li nwadis anii (February 2022) la ni, Joon kuma da sʋŋ nɛ ligidi bɛdegʋ ye ba da' niŋgbiŋ luas la'adnam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb anu ka ba nɔki sʋŋ banɛ paam sapu'ad suoya zug ka ba niŋgbiŋ luas mɔr gbɛlʋŋ la.
english: In August 2022, John Kumah made payments for five different sets of prostheses for some victims of road accidents.

kusaal: Ka lɛn mɔr wada zamisυg kasɛta gbaun tita'ar kanɛ paas ayi' n yi Gaana wada zamisυg sakur tita'ar la ni.
english: He also had a Degree in Law (LLB) from the University of Ghana and a Professional Law Degree (BL) from the Ghana School of Law.

kusaal: John Oti Bless (du'anɛ sawa'ar nwadig 19, 1979) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni, zi'eni tis Nkwanta North Constituency kanɛ bɛ Oti Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: John Oti Bless (born Friday, October 19, 1979) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Nkwanta North Constituency in the Oti Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Saboba, tenkanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Saboba, a town in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ University of Ghana ka naae ka di'e Diploma in Youth Development kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayi' la ni (2002).
english: He entered the University of Ghana and obtained his Diploma in Youth Development in 2002.

kusaal: · Wadmaan (January 7, 2013 – present; 2nd term).
english: Member of Parliament (January 7, 2013 – present; 3rd term)

kusaal: Ba da du'a Bless nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai Nwadis piiga la dabpii nɛ awai daar (sawa'ar nwadig 19, 1979).
english: John Oti Bless (born Friday, October 19, 1979) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Nkwanta North Constituency in the Oti Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni (2012), o da zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg nɔba zugʋ nyi'a Nkwanta North kʋk la ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Nkwanta North seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: O anɛ Ma'asim tiig paati nid, ka da an Mp tis Bole Bamboi bɛ 1997 ti paae 2009 ka lɛm an Deputy Minister for Communication dinɛ yi 1997 ti paae 1998 la ni ka naam substantive Minister for Communications bɛ 1998 yʋʋm la ni.
english: Mahama served as a Member of Parliament for Bole/Bamboi from 1997 to 2009 and served as Deputy Minister for Communication between 1997 and 1998 before becoming the substantive Minister for Communications in 1998.

kusaal: Mahama du'am teŋ bɛnɛ Damongo dinɛ bɛ Damango-Daboya sʋ'ʋlʋm kani bɛ Northern region.
english: He was born on 29 November 1958 in Damongo, an area in the present-day West Gonja District of the Northern Region.

kusaal: O saam, Emmanuel Adama Mahama onɛ da an mui arizak daan nɛ pa'an, ka da yiiga Mp tis West Gonja sʋ'ʋlʋm nɛ yiiga Regional Commissioner tis Northern Region bɛ yiiga Ghana Republic, Kwame Nkrumah saŋa.
english: His father, Emmanuel Adama Mahama, a wealthy rice farmer and teacher, was the first Member of Parliament for the West Gonja constituency and the first Regional Commissioner of the Northern Region during the First Republic under Ghana's first president, Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Mahama saam la da lɛm senior presidential advisor bɛ Ghana's Third Republic bɛ Hilla Limann onɛ ka Jerry Rawlings da lubʋ 1981 la ni.
english: Mahama's father also served as a senior presidential advisor during Ghana's Third Republic under Hilla Limann who was overthrown in 1981 by Jerry John Rawlings.

kusaal: O da dɛŋin anɛ zugdaan nya'andɔl bɛ Ghana dinɛ yi January 2009 ti paae July 2012 la ni, ka yʋ'ʋn da an zugdaan bɛ 24 July 2012 ka di dɔlisi o tuogat, John Evans Fiifi Attah Mills.
english: In line with Ghana's constitution, Mahama became president on 24 July 2012 on the death of his predecessor, John Atta Mills.

kusaal: Mahama anɛ onɛ an pian'a-pian'ad, onɛ sɔbid gbana nɛ onɛ min' labakʋda.
english: After completing his undergraduate education, Mahama became a secondary school teacher for a few years.

kusaal: Mahama an yiiga zugdaan nya'adɔl kani di'e na'am yi tuon sɔb onɛ kpi kuk la zug, John Evans Atta Mills nɛ onɛ an yiiga zugdaan kani ka ba da du'au Ghana sʋ'ʋmɛŋ yʋʋm nya'aŋ.
english: On 7 January 2009, Mahama was sworn into office as the Vice-President of Ghana with John Atta Mills as President.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o December 2012 vɔɔtʋg la ni ka o an zugdaan.
english: Mahama won the December 2012 general election with 50.70% of the total valid votes cast and a 3% winning margin beating his nearest rival, Nana Akufo-Addo of the main opposition New Patriotic Party, who polled a close 47.74%.

kusaal: O da lɛm zi'en ye ba vɔɔt o pɛ'ɛs ayi' 2016 vɔɔtʋg la ni, ka Nana Akufo-Addo nɔk wabʋg paati la lʋbʋ bɛ 2016 la ni.
english: In February 2019, Mahama was confirmed as the candidate of the opposition NDC to contest in the 2020 elections, against incumbent president Nana Akufo-Addo, who unseated Mahama in 2016, capitalizing on an economy that was slowing due to falling prices for gold, oil and cocoa exports.

kusaal: O da zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug nya' yʋʋm Tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi Ghana Wadmaanib nɛ zugraan nam vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: The General Council of Assemblies of God, Ghana honored Mahama with its Daniel Award.

kusaal: John Majisi (du'am; 11 dawalig nwadig 1956) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an politis wɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: John Majisi (born 11 March 1956) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Krachi Nchumuru constituency in the Volta Region, on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Majisi anɛ karimbiig ka pʋ'ʋsid Seventh-day Adventist pʋ'ʋsʋm .
english: Majisi is a Christian (Seventh-day Adventist).

kusaal: o yinɛ Boafri, tempʋʋg kanɛ bɛ Volta Region, Ghana nwa la.
english: He hails from Boafri, a town in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: o daa keŋɛ University of Education, Winneba ka yina nɛ o MPhil kanɛ an Special Education la kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm 2007 la ni.
english: He entered the University of Education, Winneba and obtained his MPhil in Special Education in 2007.

kusaal: O ane wadmaan (7 yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2013 – present; 2nd term)
english: Member of Parliament (7 January 2013 – present; 2nd term)

kusaal: Ka an wadmaan tis Krachi Nchumuru Constituency n bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim , o anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid.
english: John Majisi (born 11 March 1956) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Krachi Nchumuru constituency in the Volta Region, on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Majisi anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid (NDC).yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni, o daa nyi'ad ye o lieb wadmaan tis Krachi Nchumuru ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg kanɛ paas wadmaaanib yikanɛ passi ayuobʋ bɛ Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ka nɛ o di.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Krachi Nchumuru seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: O mɔr pu'a nɛ biis ayɔpɔi.
english: He is married (with seven children).

kusaal: Ba du'a o nɛ Obuasi dinɛ bɛ Ashanti la, Mensah yinɛ scouting system bɛ Ghana, dinɛ gɔsid ninpaalis banɛ mɔr si'el min'ilim sa ka naam kpɛn' anina paam dɛmisʋg ka tʋsiba tis Europe.
english: Born in Obuasi, Ashanti, Mensah is a product of the scouting system in Ghana.

kusaal: O bɛ 2009–10 nɛ 2010–11 yʋʋm la, nɛ lɔɔn bɛ English club Sunderland bɛ Premier League ni.
english: He spent the 2009–10 and 2010–11 seasons on loan at English club Sunderland in the Premier League.

kusaal: Banɛ da du'a o Obuasi dinɛ bɛ Ashanti, Mensah da pin'ili nwɛ'ɛd o biilimin sa, dinɛ ka o pɛ'ɛs MBC Accra.
english: Born in Obuasi, Ashanti, Mensah began playing at a young age, which saw him join MBC Accra.

kusaal: Onɛ da an biig la, Mensah da keŋ Italy ye pɛ'ɛs Bologna ka da you nɔɔr ayi' bɛ zi'ikana bɛ Coppa Italia ni.
english: As a teenager, Mensah then moved to Italy to join Bologna and went on to make two appearances for the side, both coming from Coppa Italia.

kusaal: 2001–02 yʋʋm la tuonɛ, Mensah lɛb Italy ye o saen bɛ Serie B side Genoa.
english: Ahead of the 2001–02 season, Mensah returned to Italy to sign for Serie B side Genoa.

kusaal: O da mwɛ' o nwɛ'ɛb tita'ar yinne Genoa bɛ Copa Italia nwɛ'ɛb kani tʋ'ʋsid Treviso bɛ Group Stage bɛ August 20, 2001, dinɛ da paae ka ba kpɛn'ɛs o, bɛ 2–1 dii ni.
english: He made his Genoa debut in the Copa Italia match against Treviso in the Group Stage on August 20, 2001, coming on as a second-half substitute, in a 2–1 win.

kusaal: Wandig yinne pʋʋgʋnɛ, September 23, 2001 nii, Mensah da sʋŋa tisi o kilab la banɛ da kpɛ'ɛs o miti 86 la ni , banɛ da di 3–0 dɔl Messina.
english: A month later, on September 23, 2001, Mensah made his league debut for the club, coming on as an 86th-minute substitute, in a 3–0 win against Messina.

kusaal: Mensah da di o yiiga gɔɔl tis kilab la, bɛ 2–1 dɔl Cosenza bɛ November 11, 2001 ni.
english: Mensah then scored his first goal for the club, in a 2–1 loss against Cosenza on November 11, 2001.

kusaal: O zi'esim zugɔ ba tis o nɛ yʋ'ʋr ye "Rock of Gibraltar", ka Mensah yʋ'ʋri da gaad tuon bɛ Ghana's squad for the 2006 FIFA World Cup la ni.
english: Mensah was named to Ghana's squad for the 2006 and 2010 FIFA World Cup.

kusaal: Mensah da bɛ Swiss yʋʋma ayi' nɛ Bellinzona, dinɛ ka o da nwɛ' sʋm nɛ o minilim la, ka la'ani onɛ da pʋ tɔn'ɔn zɔd tɔn'ɔtɔn' la nidib da pʋ gɔti nyɛt o min'ilim la.
english: Mensah then spent two years at Swiss side Bellinzona, where he honed his talents, and despite his lack of speed, many scouts have overlooked his talent.

kusaal: Reverend John Ntim Fordjour anɛ Ghana pɔlits nwɛ'ɛd ka paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Reverend John Ntim Fordjour is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Assin South Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Nannana, o anɛ minista onɛ gɔsid gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yɛla la nya'andɔl, dɔlisidi Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ka wadmaanib la siaki tis o.
english: He served as the Deputy Minister of Education in H.E Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo's administration.

kusaal: Onɛ an Ghana nɛ Canada Wadmaannib nɔɔr yinne la'asʋg la kʋkdaan.
english: He is also the Chairman of the Ghana-Canada Parliamentary Friendship Association, Vice Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on Members Holding Offices of Profit as well as a Member of Parliament Select Committee on Foreign Affairs.

kusaal: O anɛ karim saam kpɛɛm tis VBCI Higher Heights Sanctuary n bɛ East Legon la.
english: He is the Senior Pastor of Victory Bible Church International (VBCI) Higher Heights Sanctuary in East Legon.

kusaal: O yinɛ Assin Kruwa n bɛ Central Region Ghana la.
english: Fordjour was born on 28th May 1986 and hails from Assin Kruwa in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ Assin Manso Senior High School.
english: He attended Assin Manso Senior High School.

kusaal: Ntim Fordjour yʋ'ʋn maan nɛ PhD Department of Political Sciencen bɛ University of Ghana.
english: Rev. Ntim Fordjour is currently a PhD Candidate in the Department of Political Science at the University of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o bachelor's degree linɛ anɛ sanlimnam tʋʋb yɛla yit University of Mines and Technology (UMaT), n bɛ Tarkwa la yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007), din nya'aŋ ka University of Ghana piinl o Master of Arts Degree in Economic Policy Management yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi la ni (2014).
english: He graduated with a bachelor's degree in Mineral Engineering from the University of Mines and Technology (UMaT), Tarkwa in 2007, and subsequently was awarded a Master of Arts Degree in Economic Policy Management by University of Ghana in 2014.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la, o da paam vɔɔtnam tusa pisi nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbistan' nɛ anii (23,308) yi vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ awai nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi (39,887) pʋʋgin.
english: In the 2016 elections, he obtained 23,308 votes out of the 39,887 valid votes cast, representing of 58.99% votes to become the member of parliament for Assin South Constituency.

kusaal: John Ntim Fordjour paas nɛ Governing Board of Ghana Integrated Iron & Steel Development Corporation (GIISDEC) ka lɛn an kʋkdaan tis Investments and Strategy Committee of the Board.
english: John Ntim Fordjour is a Member of the Governing Board of Ghana Integrated Iron & Steel Development Corporation (GIISDEC) and also serves as the Chair of the Investments and Strategy Committee of the Board.

kusaal: O anɛ Assin South kanɛ bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim la dim wadmaan.
english: Reverend John Ntim Fordjour is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Assin South Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O anɛ minista onɛ gɔsid gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la nya'andɔl, ka lɛn an wadmaani tis Assin South sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: He is the Member of Parliament for Assin South Constituency of the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ka li an pisnu nɛ anii du'al piswai nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (58.99%) ka lieb wadmaani tis Assin South sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: In the 2016 elections, he obtained 23,308 votes out of the 39,887 valid votes cast, representing of 58.99% votes to become the member of parliament for Assin South Constituency.

kusaal: Fordjour mɔr pu'a nɛ biisi anaasi, ba wʋsa anɛ bipumis.
english: Fordjour is married to Tracy Fordjour and has three children, all girls.

kusaal: Ba da du'a John-Peter Amewu nɛ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ ayi la ni n bɛ Wli-Todzi linɛ bɛ Hohoe Volta Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: John-Peter Amewu was born in 1968 in Wli-Todzi in the Hohoe Municipality of the Volta Region.

kusaal: Ka lɛn tɔlisi keŋ Lolobi and Adisadel Kɔligi linɛ bɛ Cape Coast la.
english: He attended Hohoe E. P. Senior High School, St. Mary's Seminary/Senior High School, Lolobi and Adisadel College, Cape Coast for his high school education.

kusaal: O da yii anina keŋ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology n naae ka di'e o digirɛɛ kasɛta gbaυŋ.
english: John-Peter Amewu obtained his bachelor's degree in Construction Technology from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology.

kusaal: O da lɛn tɔlis University of Ghana, Legon n naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an MBA na'asaalin la, ani ka o lɛn tɔlisi maaali o mastɛs n bɛ University of Dundee (UK) sakurin la.
english: He furthered his education and obtained an MBA in finance from University of Ghana, Legon, and proceeded to obtain a postgraduate degree in international energy industry management and a master's degree in petroleum law and policy from University of Dundee (UK).

kusaal: Onɛ da yɔ'ɔg Africa Centre for Energy Policy (ACEP) la, ani ka o da an tυυma la tuongat onɛ sa'an Gɔmina nɛ A-su'oemɛŋ nam tυυma la.
english: He is a co-founder of Africa Centre for Energy Policy (ACEP), where he worked as the director of policy and research, and provided policy advice to support a variety of government and private sector projects.

kusaal: John Agyekum Kufour da gaŋ o ye o an minista banɛ gɔsid na'am yɛla n bɛ Hohoe sυ'υlυm la.
english: He was appointed by His Excellency John Agyekum Kufour as the municipal chief executive for Hohoe Municipal Assembly.

kusaal: John-Peter Amewu anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka aan ti Gaana Minista tis banɛ gɔsid ziriga suoya yɛla la, o anɛ wadmaan n tis Hohoe.
english: John-Peter Amewu (born 16 March 1968) is a Ghanaian politician and current Minister for Railways Development and Member of Parliament (MP) for Hohoe Constituency in the Volta Region .

kusaal: Onɛ da an Minister of Energy nɛ Minista banɛ gɔsidi ti tam nam la'ad yɛla la yυυm banɛ gaad la.
english: He was Minister of Energy and Minister for Lands and Natural Resources.

kusaal: O da keŋi o sakur bɛ Hohoe E. P. Senior High Sakur linɛ yυ'υri buon St.
english: He attended Hohoe E. P. Senior High School, St. Mary's Seminary/Senior High School, Lolobi and Adisadel College, Cape Coast for his high school education.

kusaal: Mary's Seminary/Senior High sakur la ni.
english: He attended Hohoe E. P. Senior High School, St. Mary's Seminary/Senior High School, Lolobi and Adisadel College, Cape Coast for his high school education.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris anu la yuma tusa yi nɛ piina yɔpɔi la ni ka Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ John-Peter Amewu ye o an Minista banɛ gɔsidi ti tam nɛ ti tam la'ad yɛla.
english: In August 2018, following the sacking of Boakye Agyarko as Energy Minister, President Nana Addo-Danquah Akufo-Addo moved Amewu's to the Energy Ministry.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris anii la yυma tusa yi nɛ piina nii la ni ka ti Gɔmina Nana Addo-Danquah Akufo-Addo tiak o ye o aan ti Gaana Energy Minista, ka o da tυm tituaa hali n tis Gaana dim.
english: In August 2018, following the sacking of Boakye Agyarko as Energy Minister, President Nana Addo-Danquah Akufo-Addo moved Amewu's to the Energy Ministry.

kusaal: Vɔt kanɛ da maal Buniya nwarig la li dabisim ayɔpɔi yuma tusa yi nɛ piisi la nya'aŋ la, ka John-Peter Amewu zi'en Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la zugu nya'a di Hohoe dim wadmaanib kυk la hali lin da yi yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ ayi n ti paae saŋ kanna la.
english: John-Peter Amewu was born in 1968 in Wli-Todzi in the Hohoe Municipality of the Volta Region.

kusaal: Di pu'a du'a biis anaasi.
english: He is married with four children.

kusaal: Ba dʋa John Paul Arabome dabispiiga nɛ yinnɛ yiiga wadig la yʋʋm tʋsir kɔbʋswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi la Uromi, ka li bɛ Edo State ka o yidim kin pʋ'ʋs kanɛ an catholic, ba mɔr biis awai ka ɔn an kpa'anr.
english: JohnPaul Arabome was born on 11 January 1982 in Uromi, Edo State into a catholic family as the last born in a family of nine.

kusaal: o dad keŋnɛ Lumen Christi Secondary School o kɔligi sakʋr saŋa ka ba d nɔk o University kanɛ bɛ Benin la yʋʋm tʋsir Kɔbʋswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai ye o zamis ligidi kanl yɛla.
english: He attended Lumen Christi Secondary School for his secondary education and was admitted at the University of Benin in 1999 to study accounting.

kusaal: O da tɔɔm kɛŋ na'asaatɛŋ yʋma tʋsa ayinɛ nɛ yʋʋm yinnɛ ye o tɔlisi o sakʋr zamisʋg Saint Benedict College nɛ Saint John University linɛ bɛ Minnesota ka da di'ɛ gbaŋ ye o mi economics ka yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi kiŋ paaɛ yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ awai ka o da di'ɛ gbaŋ kanɛ pa'al yɛ o mɔya nɛ business administration na'asaasɔɔg labaya ni nɛ California Lutheran University.
english: He migrated to the United States in 2001 to further his education at the College of Saint Benedict and Saint John's University, Minnesota where he earned a bachelor's degree in economics and from 2007 to 2009, a master's degree in business administration in information technology and entrepreneurship from California Lutheran University.

kusaal: Arabome da tʋm nɛ tis America banki yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ anʋ kiŋ paaɛ yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la'am nɛ tɛŋwʋsa.
english: Arabome worked as a consultant from 2005 to 2013 for Bank of America and Countrywide Insurance.

kusaal: O da yii anɛ ka yɔ'ɔgi o mɛŋ tʋʋma zin'ig Chatsworth, kɛ li bɛ Los Angeles anɛ ka o da sin'iŋi ɔ bʋŋɔsida la tʋʋma.
english: Afterwards, he established his production warehouse in Chatsworth, Los Angeles where he started his film production and directing career.

kusaal: Arabome da sin'iŋi o diib dʋgib tʋʋma COVID-19 saŋa, o da yɔ'ɔgnɛ The Pepper Goat ka li mɔr zin'ig kanɛ ka fʋ na kiŋ da' bɛɛ fʋ bʋɔl kaba mɔri fʋ diib na tisif.
english: Arabome started his culinary career during the COVID-19 pandemic by establishing The Pepper Goat which started up as pick-up and delivery.

kusaal: Ban da mi' yɛ The Goat Daddy anɛ onɛ dʋgid diib ka yit Nigeria la, o da la'as nɛ ninsieba ka ba maa adʋgigaadtaaba Los Angeles linɛ bɛ California, yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi ka da di ka bas banɛ yit Ghana, Liberia, Senegal, nɛ tɛŋsiɛba banɛ bɛ west Africa.
english: Known as The Goat Daddy as a chef, Arabome, who represented Nigerian in a jollof cook-off championship in Los Angeles, California, in 2022 beat contestants from Ghana, Liberia, Senegal, and other West African countries.

kusaal: Nidib na'asid Arabome "nɛ on tɔ'ɔn ɛar sʋɔya bɛdigɔ yaŋi kɛ ka linɛ ka o gba'ɛ ye o maal sid niŋ amɛŋa".
english: Arabome has been lauded for "his ability to navigate multiple artistic mediums and bring his unique vision to life." His movies include, Bootivity which was his debut production in 2013, Touchdown X (2014) and The Queen's Fiction.

kusaal: John Paul yʋ'ʋm yʋ'ma yʋ'ʋr Pepp Digital da sin'iŋ yiiga yʋ'ʋma, Ma OI Shiii Vol.
english: JohnPaul singing as PeppDigital has released his debut album, Ma Ol Shiii Vol. 1 which comprises 13 songs, in 2021, two extended plays, The Goat Daddy Project (2023), which comprises 7 songs, and Goat Daddy, which comprises 6 songs.

kusaal: Johnson Kwaku Adu (du'am; 10 mɔtul nwadig 1969) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi nɛ anii la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Ahafo Ano South West Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region la Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg zug.
english: He represented the Ahafo Ano South West Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adu nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai Nwadisa anii la dab piiga daar (10 mɔtul nwadig 1969) Akrokerri n bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: Adu was born on 10 August 1969 in Akrokerri in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O maali o Diploma in Chemistry/Biology yʋʋm tusa ayi' la ni (2000).
english: He had his Diploma in Chemistry/Biology in 2000.

kusaal: O da lɛn maali o BEd kasɛta gbaʋŋ (Science) yit University of Education, Winneba yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ yinne la ni (2001).
english: He earned his BEd (Science) at University of Education, Winneba in 2001.

kusaal: Adu anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Pentecost pʋ'ʋsʋm .
english: Adu is a Christian and fellowships at Church of Pentecost.

kusaal: Adu da anɛ NADMO District Coordinator tis Ahafo Ano South District din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayi' la ni (2002) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2009), ka lɛn tʋm gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni (kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsidi li yɛla) bɛ Ahafo Ano District Office yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga la ni (2010) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012).
english: Adu was a NADMO District Coordinator for Ahafo Ano South District from 2002 to 2009, and Ghana Education Service (Circuit Supervisor) Ahafo Ano District Office from 2010 to 2012.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'an Akrokeri College of Education.
english: He was also a Science tutor at Akrokeri College of Education.

kusaal: Adu anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg NPP nid.
english: Adu is a member of NPP.

kusaal: O da anɛ Presiding Member tis Ahafo Ano South District Assembly, Mankraso, din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai Nwadisa anaasi la (April 2009) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la (January 2011); ka an wadmaan, MP din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la (January 2013) paae zina; o ken kanɛ paasi ayi' daan.
english: He was the Presiding Member of Ahafo Ano South District Assembly, Mankraso, from April 2009 to January 2011; and MP from January 2013 to date; it is his second term.

kusaal: O da diya nɛ vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ anu nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne (15,761) ka li an pisnu nɛ anaasi du'al pisnu nɛ yinne kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (54.51%) ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC nid Sadik Abubakar paam vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ atan nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' (13,153) ka li an pisnaasi nɛ anu du'al pisnaasi nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (45.49%) ka onɛ pʋ mɔr Na'adɔɔg la ka zi'e o nyadi la kanɛ aan Adom Douglas Kwakye la mɛ paam vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ yinne nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi' (11,052).
english: He won with 15,761 votes making 54.51% of the total votes whiles the NDC parliamentary candidate Sadik Abubakar had 13,153 votes making 45.49% of the total votes and an Independent candidate Adom Douglas Kwakye had 11,052 votes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne 2021 la mi, Adu nɛ Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin nɛ Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah nɛ Laadi Ayii Ayamba nɛ Emmanuel Kwasi Bedzrah pan'alim ya Extraordinary Session yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne la ni (2021) ka paas ECOWAS Wadmaanibin dinɛ da naam Freetown bɛ Sierra Leone.
english: In 2021, Adu together with Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin, Abdul-Aziz Ayaba Musah, Laadi Ayii Ayamba and Emmanuel Kwasi Bedzrah were sworn in during the Extraordinary Session 2021 of the Parliament of the ECOWAS which happened in Freetown in Sierra Leone.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadisa anaasi (vaala nwadig 2017), British High Commission dinɛ bɛ Ghana la da zɛrigɛ Adu nɛ George Boakye nɛ Richard Acheampong, nɛ Joseph Benhazin Dahah ye ba sʋŋi ba buudi ka ba keŋ UK ka pʋ dɔl suokanɛ nar ye ba dɔl laa.
english: In April 2017, the British High Commission in Ghana allegedly accused Adu, George Boakye, Richard Acheampong, and Joseph Benhazin Dahah of helping their relatives enter the UK illegally using their diplomatic passports.

kusaal: Adu da nwien keŋ London nɛ o pu'a nɛ o pu'ayua ka ba da yɛl ye o su'aa basi ba Britain.
english: Adu traveled to London with his spouse and daughter and was suspected to have left them behind in Britain.

kusaal: O da paas wadmaanib banɛ da zu'ie gad wadmaan yikanɛ paasi ayuobʋ la ni Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He was a majority member of the 6th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da nyi'a yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) kanɛ da an Ghana vɔɔtʋg yʋʋm la, Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, nɔba zug ka di keŋ paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He contested in the 2020 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party and won to represent in the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Adu anɛ kʋkdaani tis pu'asada nɛ dasam, nɛ ninwisigir nɛ buudi malima nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid nimma'asim yɛla la.
english: Adu is the Chairperson of the Youth, Sports and Culture Committee and a member of the Health Committee.

kusaal: O mɔr pu'a nɛ biisa ayi'.
english: He is married with two children.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlʋm kanɛ ka ba da buon Jolof bɛɛ Wolof Empire da anɛ tɛŋ kanɛ da sʋ'ʋg West Africa zin'ig si'eba wan wʋʋ zin'is banɛ ka ti buon zina ye Senegal, Mali, Gambia nɛ Mauritania hali 12th century saŋa sa ka ba da pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr nya'aŋ ye Jolof na'am sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: The Jolof or Wolof Empire was a confederacy state that ruled parts of West Africa situated in modern-day Senegal, Mali, The Gambia and Mauritania from around the 12th century and was later known as the Jolof Kingdom.

kusaal: Ninkanɛ gɔsid African kʋdʋmin diib yela ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Fran Osseo-Asare, pa'al ye jollof rice pin'ilig da bɛ nɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka mui da bɛ; ka ban da pin'ili buoni li si'em an thieboudienne bɛɛ thiebou djeun, ka ban mɔr si'elnami maan an mui, zimi, nɛ vaand bɛɛ bʋnbʋta lʋ'as si'eba.
english: According to African food historian Fran Osseo-Asare, the origins of jollof rice can be traced to the area, where rice was grown; the original dish was known as thieboudienne or thiebou djeun, and contains rice, fish, shellfish and vegetables.

kusaal: Ninkanɛ gɔsid diib, kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl yela ka ba buon o James C. McCann pa'al ye diib la da na pin'il nɛ yi Senegal paae lin bɛ zin'ig si'eba zina nwa la, bɔzugɔ ba pʋ nyɛ ka buudi pian'ad, kʋdʋmin tʋʋma wala buudi ka li da di'e tɛŋa.
english: Food and agriculture historian James C. McCann argued that it was unlikely that the dish could have naturally spread from Senegal to its current range since a similar cultural diffusion is not seen in "linguistic, historical or political patterns".

kusaal: Amaa o pa'al ye diib la yadigi di'e tɛŋ wʋsa la yinɛ Mali empire, li kaskas anɛ Djula buudi banɛ da an kpikpinib la banɛ da zamisi li mɔri li kɛŋ tɛɛns kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb da'a diib, ba da lɛn mɔr kʋnt kʋndʋb, da'a diib nɛ mui kuob paae tɛɛns bɛdigʋ, nɛ mɔɔm pʋ'ʋsʋg.
english: Instead, he proposed that the dish spread with the Mali empire, especially the Djula tradespeople who dispersed widely to the regional commercial and urban centers, taking with them economic arts of "blacksmithing, small-scale marketing, and rice agronomy" as well as the religion of Islam.

kusaal: Marc Dufumier, Ninkanɛ yit an Emeritus ka zamis bʋnbʋtta yela, yis pian'ak na pa'al diib la yi si'el na, o ye diib la dɔlis nɛ ban da kuod sʋnma Senegal tisid French dim ka ba maan kpaam, ka ki nɛ sɔɔgum nam kuobi da si'e la ka ba mɔr mui yi Southeast Asia kpɛn'ɛ na.
english: Marc Dufumier, an emeritus professor of agronomy, proposes a more recent origin for the dish, which may only have appeared as a consequence of the colonial promotion of intensive peanut cropping in central Senegal for the French oil industry, and where commensurate reduction in the planted area of traditional millet and sorghum staples was compensated for by imports of broken rice from Southeast Asia.

kusaal: Tamantoos kanɛ yʋ'ʋn bɛ, tomato gan'alig, nanzʋ'ʋs, Indian dim nanzʋ'ʋs nɛ Asia dim mui kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb banɛ bɛ zina, kɛ ka ba gɔs ka yel ye diib la kɛna pʋ gaad 19th century, amaa ba pʋ mɔr kasɛta kanɛ ka ba na nyaŋi pa'al ye ba da kuod bʋnbʋta kaŋa mɔri dʋgʋdi li bɛɛ ba da mɔr laʋk kaŋa yit katɛŋi mɔri kɛn na dʋgʋdi li.
english: The use of New World tomatoes, tomato paste, capsicum peppers (bell, chili, paprika), Indian curry powder, Mediterranean thyme, and Asian rice varieties, may limit the origin of the current dish to no earlier than the 19th century, there being no evidence of the ingredients being locally cultivated or imported before this period.

kusaal: Senegal tɛŋin, ba mɔr sɔlima pʋʋgin ka ba na'asid Penda Mbaye, o da anɛ onɛ dʋgʋd diib tisid na'asaanam banɛ da sʋ'ʋg tɛŋ la bɛ Saint-Louis, Senegal, ba yɛt ye onɛ da pin'il dikaŋa yit nɛ ki da kae ka o nɔk mui dʋg la.
english: In Senegal, oral histories credit Penda Mbaye, a cook at the residence of one of the colonial rulers in Saint-Louis, Senegal, as having created the dish when she ran out of barley and substituted rice.

kusaal: Ban nyɛ yʋ'ʋr la ye jollof ka sɔ' wʋsa mi' la yinɛ Nidib banɛ bɛ Wolof, ka Senegal, Mauritania nɛ Gambia ka ba buoni li nɛ Wolof pian'ad ni ye ceebu jën bɛɛ benachin.
english: The dish's most common name of jollof derives from the name of the Wolof people, though in Senegal, Mauritania and The Gambia the dish is referred to in Wolof as ceebu jën or benachin.

kusaal: Coconut-jollof rice anɛ diib kanɛ ka banɛ dit tita'am an Igbo buudi banɛ bɛ Nigerians.
english: Coconut-jollof rice is particularly often eaten by riverine and some Igbo Nigerians.

kusaal: UNESCO si'ak ye Senegal jollof la, ka ba buon ye thieboudienne, ye li paas buudi malima pʋʋgin.
english: UNESCO recognized Senegal's version of jollof, thieboudienne, as an intangible cultural heritage dish.

kusaal: Banɛ buoni li ala anɛ West Africa tɛɛns banɛ pian'ad Fariŋ buudi pian'ad, ka si'eba an Beninese, Burkinabé, Guinean, Ivorian, Nigerien, nɛ Togolese diib dʋgʋdib ni, ba mɛ mɔri li buudi yinnɛ ka ba buon ye riz gras bɛɛ riz au gras, linɛ gbini an "mui kanɛ mɔr kpaam", lin anɛ mui ginma banɛ ka ba mɔri dʋgʋd la la.
english: In French-speaking West Africa, including Beninese, Burkinabé, Guinean, Ivorian, Nigerien, and Togolese cuisines, there is a variant called riz gras or riz au gras, which translates to "fat rice", a reference to the short-grain rice usually used in the dish.

kusaal: Linɛ paas ya'as, Guinea-Bissauan diib pʋʋgin, tɛɛns banɛ mɛ pian'ad Portuguese mɛ mɔr.
english: This also exists in Guinea-Bissauan cuisine.

kusaal: Nigeria tɛŋin ba pian'akpɛŋ, "Gɔsim jollof" gbin anɛ ye "gɔsim malisim kanɛ ka li mɔr na" nwa dɔlis nɛ ninkanɛ an Nigeria nid ka an onɛ gɔsidi ba kʋdʋmin diib yela ka o yʋ'ʋr an Ozoz Sokoh.
english: In Nigeria the phrase "see jollof" means "see how much fun is being had", according to Nigerian food historian Ozoz Sokoh.

kusaal: Di'ema kanɛ ka ba buon Jollof malima la ka di'emidi bɛ Washington, DC, nɛ Toronto.
english: Jollof food festivals have been held in Washington, DC, and Toronto.

kusaal: Tɛŋ banɛ ka ba pia'ad French ka ba bɛ West Africa ni, ba buon diib la yʋ'ʋr nɛ ye riz au gras.
english: In French-speaking West Africa, a variation of the dish is known as riz au gras.

kusaal: Senegal dim din la, thieboudienne, anɛ bʋnlinɛ ka lʋgir kanɛ buon UNESCO si'ak ye li paas ninsaalib diib pʋʋgin.
english: UNESCO recognized Senegal's version of jollof, thieboudienne, as an intangible cultural heritage dish.

kusaal: Ba ya'a nɔk ni'im m maal, ba buoni li ye ceebu yapp.
english: If made with meat, it is called ceebu yapp. The fishing communities of Saint-Louis are considered the birthplace of thieboudienne.

kusaal: Jollof rice anɛ dikanɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr yi hali bɛ West Africa.
english: Jollof rice is one of the most common dishes in West Africa. There are several regional variations in name and ingredients; for example, in Mali it is called zaamè in Bamanankan.

kusaal: Zin'is banɛ ka ba pian'ad Fariŋ pian'ad, ba buoni li ye riz au gras.
english: In French-speaking areas, it is called riz au gras.

kusaal: Baa lin bɛ kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb la, diib la yʋ'ʋr yi ya hali bɛ tɛɛns bɛdigʋ Africa sʋ'ʋlʋm nɛ li sʋ'ʋlʋm nya'aŋ.
english: Jollof rice is one of the most common dishes in West Africa. There are several regional variations in name and ingredients; for example, in Mali it is called zaamè in Bamanankan.

kusaal: Jollof rice anɛ linɛ ka ba mɔr mui, kpaam, tamantoos, gabʋ, yaarim, nanzʋ'ʋs, nɛ la'abanɛ ka ba la'as si'eba maal wan wʋʋ tamantoos gan'alig, nanzʋ'ʋs, garlic, kakaduro: la'ad banɛ ka ba mɔri dʋgʋd la bɛ kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb tɛŋ wʋsa nɛ ban dʋgʋd si'em.
english: Jollof rice traditionally consists of rice, cooking oil, tomato puree, onion, salt, chilies, and often some combination of other ingredients such as tomato paste, bell pepper, garlic, ginger, thyme, curry powder, bay leaves, grains of selim, and bouillon cubes or stock; recipes vary from country to country and cook to cook.

kusaal: Tɛɛns banɛ bɛ West Africa dʋgʋd diib la buudi yinnɛ, ka Ghana, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Liberia nɛ Cameroon nya'ad banɛ dʋgʋ li gaadi ba taaba yela.
english: West African countries typically have at least one variant form of the dish, with Ghana, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Liberia and Cameroon particularly competitive as to which country makes the best jollof.

kusaal: Zabir nwa' kpɛlim bɛ Nigeria nɛ Ghana, ka li kɛ ka ba maal nya'ab si'eba, wan wʋʋ diib dʋgʋb nya'ab nɛ na'asaasɔɔng ni nɛ malima pʋʋgin.
english: The gastronationalism rivalry is especially prominent between Nigeria and Ghana, and has led to various events, including cooking competitions and social media campaigns, fostering cultural pride.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ ni, Sister Deborah da yis yʋda yis yʋʋma paalig ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye "Ghana Jollof", ka li da pa'al ye Nigerian dim din la bɛ nya'aŋ.
english: In 2016, Sister Deborah released the song "Ghana Jollof", which denigrated the Nigerian version and Nigerians for being proud of their version.

kusaal: Ghana jollof rice anɛ linɛ ka ba nɔk kpaam, gabʋ, kakaduro, garlic, nanzʋ'ʋs, tamantoos, naaf ni'im bɛɛ bʋʋg ni'im bɛɛ nua ni'im, mui kanɛ ka ba nɛɛm, ka ba nɔki la'asi dʋgi li.
english: Ghanaian jollof rice is made of vegetable oil, onion, ginger, pressed garlic cloves, chillies, tomato paste, beef or goat meat or chicken (sometimes alternated with mixed vegetables), local or refined rice, typically jasmine rice and black pepper.

kusaal: Ban pin'ini dʋgʋd Ghana jollof si'em anɛ ba ɛɛti maal nɛ naaf ni'im bɛɛ nua ni'im la yiiga dʋgʋ li waae nɛ kakaduro, gabʋ, nɛ garlic, ba na kiimi li nɛ lin ti si'al.
english: The method of cooking Ghanaian jollof begins with first preparing the beef or chicken by seasoning and steaming it with a pureé of ginger, onions and garlic and frying it until it is well-cooked.

kusaal: Ban dit Ghana jollof la nɛ si'el anɛ bɔɔdiɛ nɛ naaf ni'im, nua ni'im, zi'iŋ ki'ima, bɛɛ ban gɛndig zɛnvaand.
english: Jollof in Ghana is often served alongside shito (a popular type of pepper sauce which originates from Ghana) and salad during parties and other ceremonies.

kusaal: Ba dit Jollof bɛ Ghana nɛ shito ka paasid salad bɛ tigir nɛ di'ema nam ni.
english: Jollof in Ghana is often served alongside shito (a popular type of pepper sauce which originates from Ghana) and salad during parties and other ceremonies.

kusaal: Ba mɔr buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb bɛɛ anina, ban mɔr si'el nami dʋgʋd Nigerian jollof mui ka ba dʋgʋd la anɛ mui kanɛ wa'am, tamantoos ma'asa nɛ tomato gan'alig, gabʋ, nanzʋ'ʋs (nanzʋ'ʋs baanlig nɛ bʋʋ nanzʋ'ʋs), kpaam, ni'im ka paas la'asi'eba nam wan wʋʋ vaand, nanzʋ'ʋs pi'elig bi'ela, nɛ maagi.
english: Although considerable variation exists, the basic profile for Nigerian jollof rice includes long-grain rice (including golden sella basmati rice), tomatoes puree and/or tomato paste, onions, pepper (scotch bonnets and/or habanero peppers; poblanos and/or bell peppers), vegetable oil, meat broth/stock and a various mixture of additional ingredients, including thyme, bay leaves, curry powder, white pepper, (small amounts of) nutmeg and stock cubes.

kusaal: Mui kanɛ ka ba mɔri dʋgʋd Nigeria tɛŋin maan jollof rice tita'am anɛ mui kanɛ ka ba waae yiiga ka nyaan nɛɛm.
english: In Nigeria the phrase "see jollof" means "see how much fun is being had", according to Nigerian food historian Ozoz Sokoh.

kusaal: Fʋn na gban'ae gban'ar ye fʋ gaŋ mui buudi sia dʋg, banɛ an muma wa'ama la anɛ ba dʋgʋbʋ na pʋ tɔe ya bɛɛ ban an wa'ama la yela (buudi si'eba anɛ, Tolly Boy, Mama Gold, Dangote Rice, Veetee, Village Pride, Tropical Sun, Mama Pride, Mama Africa, Cap Rice, Uncle Ben's, Royal Stallion, Carolina Gold) bɛɛ Golden Sella basmati-mui kanɛ ka ba ɛɛti waae mɛn (ka mɛ su bɔtɔ ni li kɔn'ɔ wʋʋ Asli, Tilda) linɛ na kɛ ka fʋ gaŋ mui bama nwa anɛ ban na bɛ, li dʋgʋbʋ na pʋ tɔe ya nɛ ninsaal la mɛŋ bɔɔdim.
english: The decision whether to use any of the numerous brands of conventional long-grain parboiled/easy-cook rice (e.g., Tolly Boy, Mama Gold, Dangote Rice, Veetee, Village Pride, Tropical Sun, Mama Pride, Mama Africa, Cap Rice, Uncle Ben's, Royal Stallion, Carolina Gold) or Golden Sella basmati-parboiled rice (further sub-branded, e.g., Asli, Tilda) is merely a matter of availability, convenience and/or personal preference and the sub-status of one or the other grain-group being conventional long-grain or basmati long-grain completely irrelevant.

kusaal: Sella basmati mui, anɛ buudi kanɛ ka nidib gɔs ka li vɛnli tisi ba.
english: Sella basmati rice, however, is considered more aesthetically pleasing to some.

kusaal: Ba dit diib nwa nɛ disi'eba (wʋʋ naaf ni'im, kolokolo ni'im, nua ni'im zimi; ka si'eba banɛ ka ba pʋ taa paasid mɛ an pɛog, kurkur ni'im, nɛ banɛ kpɛlim) ba mɛ diti li nɛ bɔɔdiɛ ki'ima, moi-moi (bɛŋa diib), vaand, salad, etc.
english: The dish is then served with the protein of choice (which in theory may be any meat but often beef, turkey, chicken or croaker-fish; much less commonly lamb, pork, etc.) and very often with fried plantains, moi-moi (bean pudding), steamed vegetables, coleslaw, salad, etc.

kusaal: Ba dʋgʋd diib bɛdigʋ ka li wan Nigerian jollof rice, ka si'ebas an coconut-jollof rice.
english: Several variations of prototypal Nigerian jollof rice exist, including coconut-jollof rice.

kusaal: Thieboudienne anɛ linɛ ka ba mɔr mui banɛ kʋ'ʋsi maan.
english: Thieboudienne typically uses broken rice.

kusaal: Nidib banɛ bɛ Sierra Leone tɛŋin mi' diib la yela, ban pʋ mɔr abɛkpaam maana, ka lɛɛ mɔr tamantoos gan'alig.
english: The dish is known in Sierra Leone, where it may not call for red palm oil but instead tomato paste.

kusaal: Jollof anɛ dikanɛ paas malima pʋʋgin hali bɛ West Africa ka ba mɔr yelisim tisi li ye, "Tigir ya'a bɛ ka jollof kae li kʋdim anɛ la'as zaalig".
english: Jollof is culturally important in much of West Africa to the point there is a common saying, "A party without jollof is just a meeting".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga nam saŋa la, banɛ bɛ West African mɔr nɔŋilim hali tisi dunia zin'is si'eba diib.
english: Since the 2010s, there has been increasing interest in West African foods in the western world.

kusaal: Ba pin'il "Dunia Jollof Dabisir" di'ema hali yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anu, Mɔtul nwadig, dabpisi nɛ ayi daar sa, ka li nyɛ yʋ'ʋr hali bɛ na'asaasɔɔng di'ema zin'isin ni ka dunia wʋsa wʋm jollof rice yela.
english: "World Jollof Day" has been celebrated since 2015 on 22 August, gaining traction on social media, and has helped increased the global recognition of jollof rice.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi, Sapal nwadig, daba atan' daar, na'asaasɔɔng zin'ig kanɛ ka ba buon Google da tis diib nwa zuonr.
english: On 3 November 2022, the dish was honoured with a Google Doodle.

kusaal: · Di'ema ni jollof bɛɛ di'ema mui anɛ diib kanɛ ka ba dʋgʋd nɛ daad bugum pi'elim, ka li kɛt ka li mɔr nyɔ'ɔs malisim nyʋʋg ka dʋg la gbinin tɔ'ɔn kanp, ban la'asid la'asi'eba maan anɛ tamantoos ma'asa nɛ nanzʋ'ʋs, tamantoos gan'alig, gabʋ, kpaam, bʋnyʋbisasi'ebas, ni'im ku'om, etc.
english: Party jollof or party rice is traditionally cooked outdoors over a wood fire, which gives it a smoky flavor and a crusty "bottom pot" similar to tahdig or socarrat, it is prepared with fresh tomato and pepper mix, tomato paste, onions, vegetable oil, spices like thyme, rosemary, curry, meat stock, etc.

kusaal: · Ba ya'a dʋgʋd tɛŋkpɛŋ mui, ba mɔri abɛkpaam nɛ zimi kanɛ ka ba ɔnl ka li kʋdʋk ka zʋn'ʋni paas (ka ba mɛ buon ye kpalʋg bɛɛ dawa-dawa), uziza biili nɛ vaand banɛ ka ba nyʋʋg malis, (ka ba buoni ba ye nchuanwu, arimu nɛ ahuji bɛ Igbo buudi pian'ad ni; ntong bɛ Efik-Ibibio buudi ni; efirin bɛ Yoruba pian'ad ni, añyeba bɛ Igala buudi ni, aramogbo bɛ Edo; etc.), ka saŋsi'eba ka ba nɔkid bʋnyʋbisa zuasidi li.
english: Native rice, also called concoction rice, uses red palm oil and smoked, dried fish and is seasoned with locust beans (also known as iru or dawa-dawa), uziza seeds and/or scent leaf, (respectively known as nchuanwu, arimu and ahuji in Igbo; ntong in Efik-Ibibio; efirin in Yoruba, añyeba in Igala, aramogbo in Edo; etc.), occasionally sprinkled with cut olili (local mint).

kusaal: Nua, kolokolo, naaf ni'im, kɔnbʋg ni'im bɛɛ zimi ka ba mɔri dʋgʋd ka paasidi diti li.
english: Chicken, turkey, beef, lamb or fish are often cooked with or served with the dish.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana captain kʋdʋg Abedi Pele ka o ba'abiis kani mɛn nwɛ'ɛd bɔɔl André nɛ Ibrahim Ayew.
english: The son of former Ghana national football captain Abedi Pele, and the brother of fellow players André and Ibrahim Ayew, Ayew began his professional career with Marseille, scoring on his senior debut in 2009.

kusaal: Banɛ du'a o France laa, Ayew nwɛ' o nwɛ'ɛb tita'ar tis Ghana national team la yʋʋm 2010 ka paam kabnam 90.
english: Born in France, Ayew made his senior debut for Ghana in 2010, and has served as captain since 2025.

kusaal: O nwɛ' tis FIFA World Cups nam ayi' (2014 nɛ 2022), nɛ Africa Cup of Nations nam anu (2012, 2015, 2017, 2019 nɛ 2021), ka sʋŋid ka ba naad runners-up yʋʋm 2015 la ni.
english: Ayew played for the national team at three FIFA World Cups (2014, 2022 and 2026), as well as six Africa Cup of Nations (2012, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2023), helping them finish runners-up in 2015.

kusaal: Ayew di o gɔɔl dinɛ pɛ'ɛs ayi' bɛ Nice bɛ Stade Vélodrome yʋʋm 27 April 2011 bɛ nwɛ'ɛb ni ka o bier André Ayew mɛn nwɛ' nimmua ka di gɔɔl.
english: Ayew scored his second goal against Nice at the Stade Vélodrome on 27 April 2011 in a match which saw his elder brother André Ayew score a hat-trick.

kusaal: 1 November 2011 nii, Jordan and André wʋsa da pin'ili bɛ UEFA Champions League match ba yiiga daani nwɛ' kpa' nɛ Premier League giants Arsenal.
english: On 1 November 2011, Jordan and André both started a UEFA Champions League match for the first time against Premier League giants Arsenal.

kusaal: 6 January 2014, o pɛ'ɛs Ligue 1 rivals Sochaux bɛ lɔɔn ni ka 2013–14 yʋʋm la naam naae.
english: On 6 January 2014, he joined Ligue 1 rivals Sochaux on a loan deal until the end of the 2013–14 season.

kusaal: 28 July 2014, Ayew tik yʋma anaasi kɔntirak nɛ Lorient Ayew da bigis suor nɛ sʋm kani ka Lorient bɔɔd la da an dinɛ yɛla ka di da naam.
english: On 28 July 2014, Ayew signed a four-year contract with Lorient.

kusaal: O di o yiiga gɔɔl tis kilab la bɛ 24 October 2015 nɛ bier kilab la, Swansea City bɛ 62nd minute ni.
english: He scored his first goal for the club on 24 October 2015 against his elder brother's club, Swansea City, in the 62nd minute.

kusaal: 31 January 2017, Jordan Ayew pɛ'ɛd Swansea City ti paae 2019–20 yʋʋm la naar, ba tiaknɛ Welsh International defender Neil Taylor, pɛ'ɛs nɛ yɔɔbi yit Swansea dinɛ na an £5 million di ya'a an dinɛ ka ba vɛɛnsi baŋi la.
english: On 31 January 2017, Jordan Ayew joined Premier League Swansea City until the end of the 2019–20 season in exchange for Welsh International defender Neil Taylor, plus add-on fees from Swansea rising to £5 million if undisclosed future conditions were met.

kusaal: 12 February 2017, o nwɛ' o nwɛ'ɛb tita'ar bɛ 2–0 nya'an ka bas Leicester City onɛ da kpɛ' 72nd minute tis Fernando Llorente.
english: On 12 February 2017, he made his debut in a 2–0 victory over Leicester City after coming on in the 72nd minute for Fernando Llorente.

kusaal: Nwɛ'ɛb la naar bɛ yʋʋm la pʋʋgʋnɛ, Ayew di o yiiga gɔɔl tis Swansea onɛ da di yiiga gɔɔl, dinɛ an an 2–1 comeback nya'an ka bas West Bromwich Albion.
english: In the final match of the season, Ayew scored his debut goal for Swansea by scoring the first goal, an equaliser which led to a their 2–1 comeback victory over West Bromwich Albion.

kusaal: 22 August 2017 ni Ayew da di 20-yard strike gɔɔl ka paam man of the match ka lɛm sʋŋ Tammy Abraham ka o di o gɔɔl bɛ Swansea EFL Cup nwɛ'ɛb nɛ MK Dons.
english: On 22 August 2017, Ayew put up a man of the match performance by scoring a 20-yard strike goal and assisting another for Tammy Abraham's debut goal in Swansea's EFL Cup match against MK Dons.

kusaal: O 20-yard mukkir gɔɔl la ka ba da pian'a BBC labaar ni ye di anɛ sitiraik tita'ar.
