english: His goal 20-yard effort was described by news outlet BBC as a tremendous strike.

kusaal: Ayew di o yiiga gɔɔl bɛ 2017–18 yʋʋm la ni, ka 26 August 2017 ye o sʋŋ Swans ka ba di 2–0 ya'an nɛ o bɛog kilab Crystal Palace.
english: Ayew scored his first goal in the 2017–18 season, on 26 August 2017, to help The Swans to a 2–0 victory over his future club Crystal Palace.

kusaal: 17 January 2018, o di yiiga gɔɔl bɛ Swans' 2–1 FA Cup alɛmnwɛ'ɛ-ya'as nɛ Wolverhampton Wanderers.
english: On 17 January 2018, he scored the opening goal in the Swans' 2–1 FA Cup replay match against Wolverhampton Wanderers.

kusaal: O yʋʋma ayi' nwɛ'ɛb la naarɛ, onɛ bɛnɛ kilab la yʋʋm la ni wʋsa, o nwɛ' nwɛ'ɛb 44 bɛ yigilim-yigilim la ni ka di gɔɔlnam 11 nɛ 7 lik la ni.
english: At the end of his second season, his only full season with the club, he played 44 matches in all competition and scored 11 goals with 7 coming in the league.

kusaal: August 2018 Ayew pɛ'ɛs Crystal Palace bɛ lɔɔn pʋʋgʋn yʋʋm 2018–19 la ni.
english: On transfer deadline day in August 2018, Ayew joined Crystal Palace on loan for the 2018–19 season.

kusaal: 15 September, o digil nwɛ' sʋŋ tis ban nɛ Huddersfield ni, nɛ onɛ sʋŋ ka Wilfried Zaha di gɔɔl ka Palace an 1–0 ya'an diib la.
english: On 15 September, he put on an impressive performance against Huddersfield, providing the assist to Wilfried Zaha's goal to earn Palace a 1–0 victory.

kusaal: Di daba atan' daar, Ayew kpɛn' 68th minute ka Jairo Riedewald di naar ya'an gɔɔl ( 86th minute ni) nɛ Grimsby Town bɛ FA Cup la ni.
english: Three days after, Ayew came on in the 68th minute for Jairo Riedewald to score a late winner (in the 86th minute) against Grimsby Town in the FA Cup.

kusaal: Ba du'a o nɛ Marseille, Ayew da nɔbignɛ was France ka pin'ili o nwɛ'ɛb la nɛ Lyon Duchère ka naam kɛŋi pɛ'ɛs Marseille academy yʋʋm 2006 la ni.
english: Ayew joined Marseille as a trainee in 2006.

kusaal: Ayew pɛ'ɛs Marseille an onɛ zamisid bɛ 2006 ni.
english: Ayew joined Marseille as a trainee in 2006.

kusaal: O tik yʋma atan' professional kɔntirak nɛ Marseille yʋʋm 2009.
english: He signed a three-year professional contract with Marseille in 2009.

kusaal: Jordan Ayew nwɛ' o nwɛ'ɛb tita'ar tis senior team la bɛ 16 December 2009 bɛ league nwɛ'ɛb ni, o da di gɔɔl ka di lieb alira nɛ Lorient.
english: Jordan Ayew made his debut for the senior team on 16 December 2009 in a league match, scoring the equaliser against Lorient.

kusaal: Marseille kɛŋ tuoni di nwɛ'ɛb la 2–1.
english: Marseille went on to win the match 2–1.

kusaal: 27 July 2015, Ayew da pɛ'ɛs Aston Villa yʋma anu gba'ar kani ka sɔ' zi ligidi la bɛnɛ, ba yʋ'ʋn da yɛl ye di anɛ £8 million.
english: On 27 July 2015, Ayew joined Aston Villa on a five-year deal for an undisclosed fee, reported to be in the region of £8 million.

kusaal: Aston Villa da yi 2015–16 yʋʋm la naarin, kaɔr 17 points ma'aa, amaa Ayew da paae nwɛ'ɛb la naarin an onɛ di gɔɔli gaadi ba zan', dinɛ an gɔɔlnam ayɔpɔi.
english: Aston Villa were relegated at the end of the 2015–16 season, winning only 17 points, but Ayew did end the season as their top scorer, albeit with just seven goals.

kusaal: Jordan bier la da anɛ Swansea City nwɛ'ɛd bɛ 2015–16 yʋʋm la ka pɛ'ɛs o bɛ winter transfer window of 2018.
english: Jordan's elder brother was a Swansea City player during the 2015–16 season and later joined him in the winter transfer window of 2018.

kusaal: O nwɛ'ɛ an ninkani sʋŋ ka league la vʋ'ʋg ka pʋ ya'as, bani da nwɛ' nwɛ'ɛb 14 la, o pin'ili nwɛ'ɛdi yi nwɛ'ɛb awai ni, ka di gɔɔl yinne ka sʋŋ ka ba di gɔɔlnam atan'.
english: He played a key role in helping them survive the league and avoid relegation by playing 14 matches, starting nine of those, scoring a goal and assisting three goals.

kusaal: O naar yʋʋm la ka an onɛ di gɔɔlnami gaad sɔ' wʋsa kilab la ni ka ba gaŋ o Players' Player yʋʋm kana ni.
english: At the end of the season, Ayew was the highest goalscorer for Crystal Palace with 9 goals, and won the Crystal Palace Player of the season, Players' Player of the season and Goal of the season awards.

kusaal: O kɔn'ɔkɔn' gɔɔl kani ka o di banɛ da nwɛ'ɛd nɛ Wolverhampton Wanderers bɛnɛ 17 January 2018 bɛ FA Cup di kilab la gɔɔl bɛ nyʋʋm kan la ni.
english: His solo goal against Wolverhampton Wanderers scored on 17 January 2018 in the FA Cup won the club's goal of the season award.

kusaal: La'am nɛ onɛ da mʋk si'em la wʋsa, Swansea da yinɛ bɛ championship la ni.
english: Despite his performance over the season, Swansea was relegated to the championship.

kusaal: O pin'ili o nwɛ'ɛbi bɛ 1 September 2018, pin'in nɛ Palace's 2–0 liib tis Southampton.
english: He made his debut on 1 September 2018, starting in Palace's 2–0 loss to Southampton.

kusaal: 2 January 2019, o di o yiiga gɔɔl tis Palace ka di an yiiga gɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb la ni dinɛ an 2–0 ya'an ka bas Wolverhampton Wanderers.
english: On 2 January 2019, he scored his first league goal for Palace by scoring the opening goal in their 2–0 victory over Wolverhampton Wanderers.

kusaal: Ba du'a Quarm nɛ nwadis anu la ni li daba ayɔpɔi daar yʋʋma 1975, o yinɛ Manso Nsiana linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la Ghana nwa.
english: Quarm was born on 7 May 1975 and hails from Manso Nsiana in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an BSc nɛ Mphi nɛ PhD Digirii n bɛ Biological Science n yi Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, KNUST sakurin la.
english: He holds BSc, MPhil and PhD degrees in Biological Sciences from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, KNUST.

kusaal: Quarm da anɛ pa'an n bɛ Vicande Sakurin la lin da yi yʋʋm 1996 ti paae yʋʋm 1998 la ni.
english: Quarm was a tutor in Vicande School from 1996 to 1998.

kusaal: O da lɛn tʋm n bɛ Central Gold African Ghana Limited la ni an kpɛɛm yʋʋm 2007 la ni.
english: He also worked at Central Gold African Ghana Limited as a part-time Environmental Officer in 2007.

kusaal: Quarm Hospital Complex lin da yi yʋʋm 2012 la ni ti paae yʋʋm 2016, ka lɛn sʋ'oe Prof.
english: He was also the CEO of Prof Quarm Publications Limited from 1995 to 2016 as well as the CEO of Prof Quarm Hospital Complex from 2012 to 2016, CEO of Prof Quarm Football Club and CEO of Prof Quarm Construction Limited.

kusaal: Nwadis ayɔpɔi la daba ayɔpɔi la ni yʋʋm 2020, Ka ba da gaŋ o ye o an kʋk daan n tis Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) sakur la ni ye o tʋm yʋma ayi' ka kpɛɛmnam la da tis o.
english: On 7 July 2020, he was appointed as the new Chairman of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) Foundation by the University Council for a tenure of 2 years.

kusaal: Quarm anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid ka an wadmaan kʋdʋg n tis Manso Nkwanta Sʋ'ʋlʋm.linɛ bɛ Nwadis ayuobʋ la yʋʋm 2015 la ni, ka o da di Wadmaan Na'adɔɔg la ni ye o zi'enɛ nyi'a kʋk la, Quarm da di kʋk la nɛ vɔtnam bam 32140 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da mɔri 83.26% vɔɔt la kanl wusa ni, Ka Ma'asim Tiid nid Alex Kwame Bonsu mɛ Mɔr vɔɔt kal 5503 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 14.26% vɔɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.(13)
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general election, Quarm won the parliamentary seat with 32,140 votes making 83.26% of the total votes cast, whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Alex Kwame Bonsu had 5,503 votes making 14.26% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Quarm la anɛ Ghana Pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n tis Manso-Nkwanta Sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Joseph Albert Quarm popularly known as Prof. Quarm is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Manso-Nkwanta Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Quarm Publications Limited la lin da yi yʋʋm 1995 ti paae yʋʋm 2016 la mi la, on la mɛ da lɛn sʋ'oe Prof.
english: He was also the CEO of Prof Quarm Publications Limited from 1995 to 2016 as well as the CEO of Prof Quarm Hospital Complex from 2012 to 2016, CEO of Prof Quarm Football Club and CEO of Prof Quarm Construction Limited.

kusaal: Atilati daar, nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la dabisim yinnɛ la yʋʋm 2020 la ni ka ti Ghana Republic gɔmina Nana Addo Darkwa Akufo-Addo da tis Prof.
english: On Tuesday, 1 December 2020, the President of the Republic of Ghana, H. E. Nana Addo Darkwa Akufo-Addo commissioned a 100-bed Prof. Quarm hospital facility in Manso Nsiana in the Amansie West District of the Ashanti region.

kusaal: Quarm Sibiti la gat bam kubiga 100 n bɛ Manso Nsiana linɛ bɛ Amansie West Sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: On Tuesday, 1 December 2020, the President of the Republic of Ghana, H. E. Nana Addo Darkwa Akufo-Addo commissioned a 100-bed Prof. Quarm hospital facility in Manso Nsiana in the Amansie West District of the Ashanti region.

kusaal: Joseph Betino ( 27 August 1966) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas Gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Suaman Constituency bɛ Western North Region la.
english: Joseph Betino (born 27 August 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and a member Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing Suaman Constituency in the Western North Region.

kusaal: O anɛ Ma'asi tiig Na'adɔɔg (National Democratic Congress) nid.
english: He became a member of parliament on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Nandom ka ba da du'a o yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ, Nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (l27th of August 1966).
english: He comes from Nandom and was born on the 27th of August 1966.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai (1990) la ni ka o da maali o A level education.
english: In 1990, Betino had his A level education.

kusaal: Betino anɛ Diisi (District Chief Executive) kʋdʋgʋ tis Suaman Constituency.
english: Betino was formerly the District Chief Executive for the Suaman Constituency.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa anii nɛ kɔbiswai (8,900) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (51.2%)
english: He pulled 8900 votes representing 51.2% of the total vote to win.

kusaal: O da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Wadmaanib la yin suoya dɔlʋsʋg la (standing Order Committee) nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid diib, kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl nɛ Kooko yɛla la (Food, Agriculture and Cocoa affairs).
english: He serves as a member of the standing Order Committee of parliament and the Food, Agriculture and Cocoa affairs Committee.

kusaal: O da nya' nɛ o Na'adɔɔg nidib ka dii zi'en Ma'asim tiig nɔbir zugʋ nya' Suaman Constituency kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi (December 2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: He contested and won the NDC Parliamentary Primaries at Suaman Constituency to become the party's candidate for the December 2020 election.

kusaal: Joseph Bipoba Naabu (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar, (24 mɔtul nwadig 1964) o anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana n zi'eni tis Yunyoo Constituency dinɛ bɛ Northern Region la ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nɔba zug.
english: Joseph Bipoba Naabu (born 24 August 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Yunyoo Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Naabu nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar, (24 mɔtul nwadig 1964) bɛ Namong, Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Naabu was born on 24 August 1964 in Namong, in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Naabu da maali o bachelor of art digirii in political science yi University of Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayuobʋ (2006) la ni.
english: Naabu earned a bachelor of art degree in political science from the University of Ghana in 2006.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da keŋ Ghana wada sakur zamis Bachelor of Law ka din nya'aŋ o lɛn keŋ university of London zamis Literally Legum Baccalaureus, yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: He then went to Ghana School of Law to study for a Bachelor of Law degree and later went to the University of London to study Literally Legum Baccalaureus, 2009.

kusaal: Onɛ da an managing director tis J.B. Naabu Farms and Company Limited on da nam pʋ kpɛn' pɔlitis la.
english: Naabu is a farmer and was the managing director of J.B. Naabu Farms and Company Limited prior to entering politics.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt tis Naabu ka o zi'eni tis Yunyoo constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) kanɛ da an Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, nɔba zug.
english: Naabu contested the Yunyoo constituency parliamentary seat on the ticket of National Democratic Congress during the 2012 Ghanaian general election and won the election with 9,591 votes representing 65.32% of the total votes.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt tis o yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) kanɛ da an Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni ka o keŋi o ken kanɛ paasi ayi' la.
english: Naabu was re-elected as a member parliament for Yunyoo constituency on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) during the 2016 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Cudjoe nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi nwadis piiga la daba ayi' daar (2 sawa'ar nwadig 1964).
english: Cudjoe was born on 2 October 1964.

kusaal: O da maali o Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics (gɛligir) yinɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi nɛ o MBA in Finance University of Ghana ni.
english: He received his Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi and his MBA in Finance from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Cudjoe pin'ili pa'al gɛligir Archbishop Porter Girls Secondary School din yi yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la yʋʋmpaal nwadig (yʋʋmpaal nwadig 1995) ken paa nwadis piiga la ni yʋʋmkan nɔɔ (sawa'ar nwadig 1995).
english: Joseph Cudjoe started his career as a Mathematics Teacher at the Archbishop Porter Girls Secondary School from January 1995 to October 1995.

kusaal: Cudjoe da lɛn an pa'an bɛ Takoradi Technical University din yi yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu (1995) ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' la ni (2000).
english: Cudjoe worked as a lecturer at the Takoradi Technical University from 1995 to 2000.

kusaal: Di nya'aŋ ka o keŋ naal nɛ Eno International, LLC ani ka o da tʋm Financial Analysis & Planning Manager tʋʋma yʋʋm tusa ayi' (2000) paae (2001).
english: He later joined Eno International, LLC where he worked as a Financial Analysis & Planning Manager from 2000 to 2001.

kusaal: Cudjoe da kpɛn' wadmaanib yin la nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' la yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2013) zi'eni tis Effia constituency dim.
english: Cudjoe entered parliament on 7 January 2013 representing the Effia constituency on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Joseph Cudjoe anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Ghana wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Joseph Cudjoe is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Effia Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tisi Effia Effia Constituency bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Joseph Cudjoe is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Effia Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Effia n bɛ Western Region, Ghana la.
english: He hails from Effia a town in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋn da kilim Senior Consultant SEM International Associatesyʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayi' nwadisa anaasi la ni (vaala nwadig 2002) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ atan' nwadis piiga la ni (sawa'ar nwadig 2003) din nya'aŋ ka o kilim general manager SEM International LTD din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la nwadis pii nɛ yinne la ni (sapal nwadig 2003) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la nwadis atan' la ni (dawalig nwadig 2004).
english: He became a Senior Consultant at SEM International Associates in April 2002 to October 2003 and then later the general manager at SEM International LTD from November 2003 to March 2004.From April 2004 until December 2012, Cudjoe was the Investment Manager for Ghana Cocoa Board.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi nwadisa anaasi la ni (vaala nwadig 2004) hali ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la ni (samanpiid nwadig 2012), Cudjoe da anɛ Investment Manager tis Ghana Cocoa Board.
english: He became a Senior Consultant at SEM International Associates in April 2002 to October 2003 and then later the general manager at SEM International LTD from November 2003 to March 2004.From April 2004 until December 2012, Cudjoe was the Investment Manager for Ghana Cocoa Board.

kusaal: Cudjoe mɔr pu'a nɛ biis atan'.
english: Cudjoe is married with three children.

kusaal: Joseph Dindiok Kpemka anɛ Ghana Pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Gbana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n tis Tempane linɛ bɛ Upper East Region Sʋ'ʋlʋm la, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Joseph Dindiok Kpemka (born 13 August 1973) is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Tempane constituency in the Upper East Region, on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O mɔr kasɛta gbaʋŋ digirii linɛ an LLB yi University of Gbana n bɛ Ghana School of Law la ni.
english: Born on 13 August 1973, Kpemka holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in English and Bacher of law from the University of Ghana and Barrister at law from the Ghana School of Law.

kusaal: O da anɛ onɛ an na'asaal pa'an n bɛ Ghana gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni li da yi yʋʋm 2002 ti paae yʋʋm 2005 la ni.
english: He taught English at the Ghana Education Service from 2002 to 2005.

kusaal: Ka lin da yi yʋʋm 2008 la ti paae yʋʋma 2009 la ni ka ba da gaŋ o ye o an D.E.C. O da kena an lɔya ka lɛn an pa'an n bɛ Bolgatanga Technical University sakur lin da yi yʋʋm 2009 ti paae yʋʋma 2016.
english: He became a lawyer and lectured at the Bolgatanga Technical University from 2009 to 2016.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2020 la ni ka ba da vɔt ka o kɔŋ kʋk la ka Lydia Akanvariba Lamisi onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la di ka bas o.
english: During the 2020 Ghanaian general election, he failed to retain his seat against the opposition party parliamentary candidate Miss Lydia Akanvariba Lamisi of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Joseph Frempong anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Gaana wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Joseph Frimpong is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Nkawkaw Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Obo Kwahu n bɛ Easthern Region la.
english: Frempong was born on 16 July 1969 and hails from Obo Kwahu in the Eastern Region.

kusaal: O da maali o GCE O level nɛ yʋʋmtusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai (1990) nɛ o GCE A level yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992).
english: He completed his GCE O level in 1990 and his GCE A level in 1992.

kusaal: O da tɔlis tuoni maal bachelor's degree in Social Studies yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni (2004).
english: He later obtained his bachelor's degree in Social Studies in 2004.

kusaal: Ka keŋ tuoni maal master's degree in Public Affairs yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011).
english: He further had his master's degree in Public Affairs in 2011.

kusaal: Frempong da anɛ pa'ani bɛ Adosu Islamic School.
english: Frempong was a teacher in Adosu Islamic School.

kusaal: O da lɛn pa'an Geography Sandema Senior High Technical School.
english: He was also the Geography teacher at the Sendema Senior High Technical School.

kusaal: O da lɛm pa'al Geography Nkawkaw Senior High School.
english: He was also the Geography teacher in Nkawkaw Senior High School.

kusaal: Ka da lɛn an pa'an nya'andɔl University of Education, Winneba.
english: He was also the Assistant Lecturer at the University of Education, Winneba.

kusaal: Frempong paasnɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg (NPP) la ni.
english: Frempong is a member of NPP and currently the MP for the Nkawkaw Constituency in the Eastern region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋgin laa, o da paam vɔɔtnam tusa pisnaasi nɛ anaasi nɛ pisyuobʋ nnɛ ayɔpɔi (44, 067) ka ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid la Oppong Francis paam tusa piinɛ annasi, kɔbisyi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi (14, 272).
english: In the 2020 Ghana general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 44,067 votes whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Oppong Francis had 14,272 votes.

kusaal: O zi'enɛ tisi Nkawkaw bɛ Easthern Region sʋ'ʋlim la dim.
english: Joseph Frimpong is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Nkawkaw Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Nannanna onɛ an wadmaani tisi Nkawkaw bɛ Easthern Region sʋ'ʋlim la dim.
english: Joseph Frimpong is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Nkawkaw Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Frempong anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Frempong is a Christian.

kusaal: Joseph Kofi Kowe Adda da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd, o da anɛ wadmaan tʋm bɛ wadmaanib yir la ka mɛ tʋm linɛ an Minista Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg gɔmina saŋa Akufo-Addo win ti nwadig yinne la ni yʋʋm 2021 la ni.
english: Joseph Kofi Kowe Adda (22 April 1956 – 14 October 2021) was a Ghanaian politician, who served as a Member of Parliament and also the Minister for Aviation in the New Patriotic Party government under President Akufo-Addo until January 2021.

kusaal: Ba du'a Joseph Adda nɛ n bɛ Navrongo, tempʋʋg tita'ar linɛ bɛ Kassena-Nankana sʋ'ʋlʋm Upper East Region Ghana la.O da keŋi o secondary sakʋr nɛ St.
english: Joseph Adda was born at Navrongo, the capital of the Kassena-Nankana District in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: John's School, Sekondi ka di'e digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an pɔlitis nɛ economics la n yi Indiana Wesleyan University, linɛ bɛ Marion, Indiana, United States la, lin da yi yʋʋm 1979 ti paae yʋʋm 1982 la ni la.
english: He had his secondary education at St. John's School, Sekondi and obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in politics and economics from the Indiana Wesleyan University, Marion, Indiana, United States, which he attended between 1979 and 1982.

kusaal: Ka yʋʋm 1982 ti paae yʋʋm 1984 la ni, ka o da bɛ Columbia University, linɛ bɛ New York, ani ka o maal o mastɛs digirii zamisʋg linɛ an International Affairs, ka o zamisʋg nwa zug da anɛ ligidi mɔrim nɛ Banking yɛla.O da tɔlisi ya ya'as n di'e kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an African Studies n bɛ Nyunivɛsiti kan nɔɔ ni.
english: Between 1982 and 1984, he was at Columbia University, New York, where he studied for a Master's degree in International Affairs, specialising in Finance and Banking.

kusaal: Ka yʋʋm 1989 la ni, ka o di'e kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ ye o zamis French pian'ad la ka lɛn zamis linɛ ka ba buon ye civilization la yi Sorbonne University, Paris, France ni.
english: In 1989, he obtained a certificate in French language and civilization from the Sorbonne University, Paris, France.

kusaal: O da tʋmnɛ an kpɛɛm n bɛ Ministry of Trade and Industry Ghana yʋʋm 1983 la ni.
english: He worked as an executive officer at the Ministry of Trade and Industry, Ghana in 1979.

kusaal: Ka yʋʋm 1983 nɛ yʋʋm 1984 la ni, ka o tʋm an onɛ an gbaʋŋ zamisʋg vɛɛns-vɛɛns n bɛ Third World Trade Institute, New York, USA.
english: Between 1983 and 1984, he worked as a Research Analyst intern at the Third World Trade Institute, New York, USA.

kusaal: Ka yʋma ayi' nya'aŋ,ka o tʋm an kpɛɛm kanɛ an Darɛta n tis Equitable Financial Service, Inc., in New Jersey, USA.
english: Over the next two years, he was an account Executive and Management trainee at the Equitable Financial Service, Inc., in New Jersey, USA.

kusaal: Adda da lɛn tʋm n bɛ Essex County College, Newark, New Jersey, USA yʋʋm (1986 – 1988) la ni, ka tʋm bɛ Thomson McKinnon Securities Inc., New York (1989 – 1991) la ni ka tʋm nɛ Deloitte and Touche Consulting, (West Africa), n bɛ Ankara yʋʋma (1991 – 1994) la ni.
english: Mr. Adda has also worked at Essex County College, Newark, New Jersey, USA (1986 – 1988), Thomson McKinnon Securities Inc., New York (1989 – 1991) and with Deloitte and Touche Consulting, (West Africa), Accra (1991 – 1994).

kusaal: Lin yi wʋʋ yʋʋma 1994 la ni sa, Joseph Adda n an Darɛta tis Omni Consulting International (Ghana) Ltd tʋʋma la.Ka lin da yi yʋʋma 1996 ti paae yʋʋma 2000 la ni, ka o tʋm n bɛ tʋʋmnamin zi'is kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ka li kas-kas anɛ Minista banɛ gɔsid Ghana ligidi yɛla la.
english: Since 1994, Joseph Adda has been the director of Omni Consulting International (Ghana) Ltd. Between 1996 and 2000, he worked in various capacities at the Ministry of Finance, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da maali alɛm maligim vɔt vɔtʋg ka ba da vɔt ka o di n tis Navrongo Central linɛ bɛ Upper East Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm la John Achuliwor onɛ da wadmaan la kʋm la nya'aŋ la.O da lɛn di'e kʋk la ya'as yʋʋma 2004 vɔt la ni.
english: He won the by-election for the Navrongo Central constituency of the Upper East Region of Ghana after the death of the incumbent, John Achuliwor.

kusaal: Onɛ Gabriel Pwamang onɛ da PNC nid la, Andema Emmanuel onɛ da Ma'asim Tiig nid, Azantinlwo Anemana Jennifer Grace onɛ da CPP nid la, Bagonia Grace DPP nid la, Donald Amuah, Otito Werseh nɛ Achuliwor A. banɛ da zi'enɛ ba mɛŋ nyari, ba wʋsa da paamnɛ vɔt bam 6,512, 6,201, 140, 83, 2,262 nɛ 4,015 wʋʋ ba yʋda la tʋʋnl taaba si'em la yi vɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: He was elected over Gabriel Pwamang of the Peoples' National Convention, Andema Emmanuel of the National Democratic Congress, Azantinlwo Anemana Jennifer Grace of the Convention People's Party, Bagonia Grace of the Democratic People's Party, Donald Amuah and Achuliwor A. Otito Werseh both independent candidates.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ ba wʋsa da mɔri 20.6%, 19.6%, 0.4%, 0.3%, 7.1% and 12.7% wʋʋ ba yʋda la tʋʋnl taaba si'em la vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: These were equivalent to 20.6%, 19.6%, 0.4%, 0.3%, 7.1% and 12.7% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Gɔmina John Kufuor da gaŋi Adda ye o an minista kanɛ gɔsid saalib paŋ nɔbigir nɛ tʋʋma nɔgusʋg yɛla yʋʋm 2005 la ni.
english: Adda was appointed the Minister for Manpower Development and Employment by President John Kufuor in 2005.

kusaal: Ka yʋʋm 2006 ani ka o si'iŋi o minista tʋʋma la.Lin nya'aŋ ka Gɔmina Kuffuor tiak o tʋʋma la tis Felix Owusu-Adjapong ye o an minista la.
english: He was later replaced by Felix Owusu-Adjapong as Minister of Energy by President Kuffuor.

kusaal: Joe Adda da lɛn di'e kʋk la Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la li vɔɔdʋg linɛ da maal yʋʋm 2008 ni la.
english: Joe Adda retained his seat when the NPP lost the general elections in 2008.

kusaal: O da anɛ Catholic karim biig.
english: He was a Catholic.

kusaal: Adda yiiga kpɛn'em wadmaanib yir la da anɛ yʋʋma 2003 la ni.
english: Adda first became a Member of Parliament in 2003.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 39.3% vɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 39.3% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Adda da kpinɛ nwadis piiga la ni dabisim pii nɛ anaasi Alamis daar, yʋʋm 2021 la ni n bɛ Legon Sibiti linɛ bɛ Ankara sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni.
english: Adda died in the early hours of Thursday, 14 October 2021, at the Legon Hospital in Accra.

kusaal: Joseph Kwame Kumah (24 January 1974) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd onɛ an Wadmaani bɛ Gaana Wadmaanib yin la zi'eni tis Kintampo North constituency sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Joseph Kwame Kumah (born 24 January 1974) is a Ghanaian politician who currently serves as the Member of the Parliament of Ghana for the Kintampo North constituency.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Kumah nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar (24 January 1974), o yinɛ Sugliboi bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Kumah was born on 24 January 1974 and is Sugliboi in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o bachelor's degree in educationnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nyʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999).
english: He achieved a bachelor's degree in education in 1999.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa atyi nɛ piiga la (2010), ka o da naae sakur nɛ postgraduate kasɛtta gbaʋŋ in Public Administration.
english: In 2010, he graduated with a postgraduate certificate in Public Administration.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ ka o maal Master of Arts degree in Local Government Administration and Organization Institute of Local Government Studies.
english: He later received a Master of Arts degree in Local Government Administration and Organization from the Institute of Local Government Studies.

kusaal: Kumah paasnɛ ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress ni.
english: Kumah is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pistana nɛ atan, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyuobʋ (33,460) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi du'al piswai nɛ anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (62.98%).
english: He won with 33,460 votes (62.98% of the votes cast).

kusaal: Wabʋg nid la, Micheal Sarkodie Baffoe, da ti'ali ayi nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayuobʋ, kɔbisnaasi nɛ piswai nɛ awai (16,499) dinɛ an pistan' nɛ yinne du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (31.05%).
english: The NPP candidate, Micheal Sarkodie Baffoe, came second with 16,499 (31.05%).

kusaal: Kumah paasnɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid wada tʋʋma yɛla la (Judiciary Committee) ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yɛla (Education Committee).
english: Kumah is a member of the Judiciary Committee and also a member of the Education Committee.

kusaal: Kumah da anɛ kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid sakur biis gbɛɛnsa yɛla Gaana gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni.
english: Kumah was a house master at the Ghana Education Service.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni ka ba vɔɔt o ye o an Wadmaani tis Kintampo North sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: He was elected as the Member of Parliament for Kintampo North in the 2020 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Kumah anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Kumah is a Christian.

kusaal: Joseph Kwasi Mensah (ba da du'a o nɛ 18 November 1962) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd onɛ an Wadmaani Nkoranza North Constituency bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah (born 18 November 1962) is a Ghanaian politician who currently serves as the Member of Parliament for the Nkoranza North Constituency in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Joseph Kwasi Mensah nɛ Manso ka o yi Manso n bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim,Ghana.
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah was born and hails from Manso in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Kwasi Mensah da naae o Basic Education nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswainɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (1975) dinɛ da sʋŋi oka o maali o Middle School Leaving Certificate(MSLC) yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1979), Ordinary Level (GCE O-Level) yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (1989) ka maali o Advanced Level (GCE O-Level) yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai (1990).
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah had and passed his Basic Education in 1975 which enabled him to obtain his Middle School Leaving Certificate(MSLC) in 1979, Ordinary Level (GCE O-Level) in 1989 and Advanced Level (GCE O-Level) in 1990.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ maali o pa'anib zamisʋg (Teacher Training) yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1984), Diploma in Business Education (Accounting & Mathematics) yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998), Bachelor of Education(B.Ed.) - (Accounting & Mathematics) yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2000).
english: He then proceeded to have his Teacher Training in 1984, Diploma in Business Education (Accounting & Mathematics) in 1998, Bachelor of Education(B.Ed.) - (Accounting & Mathematics) in 2000.

kusaal: Joseph Kwasi Mensah da anɛ Municipal Internal Auditor tis gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr, Ghana Education Service, Nkoranza North Constituency bɛ Bono East Region, Ghana.
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah works as the Municipal Internal Auditor of Ghana Education Service in Nkoranza North Constituency in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Kwasi Mensah da nya' nɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg NDC la nidb, Nkoranza North Constituency bɛ Bono East Region, Ghana la.
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Nkoranza North Constituency in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress zug ka di nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anu, kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi (15,124) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi du'ali awai (57.9%) ka keŋ paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii, Eighth (8th) Parliament, Fourth Republic of Ghana ka bas Derrick Oduro (Major Rtd.) onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid onɛ da paam vɔɔt tusa piiga, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (10,978) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayi du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋg (42.1%).
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah won again in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress with 15,124 votes (57.9%) to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana against Derrick Oduro (Major Rtd.) of the New Patriotic Party who had 10,978 votes (42.1%).

kusaal: Joseph Kwasi Mensah paas la'askanɛ gɔsid banɛ mɔr ɔfis banɛ mɔr nyɔɔd la o lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid wada gbana yɛla, wada yɛla, nɛ Wadmannib yir suoya dɔlisʋg (Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs) Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah is a committee member of the Members Holding Offices of Profit Committee and also a member of Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Committee of the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Kwasi Mensah nɔk kʋgʋs, furniture banɛ ligidi na an wʋʋ Ghana siidi tusa pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (GHC75,000) tis biis sakuya o sʋ'ʋlim la ni, (Nkoranza North Constituency) bɛ Bono East Region, Ghana.
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah donated furniture worth GHC75,000 to basic schools in his constituency (Nkoranza North Constituency) in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn nɔk nimma'asim tʋʋma la'ad bɛdigʋ tis nimmaa'asim lʋgʋr la o sʋ'ʋlim la ni, District's Health Directorate, (Nkoranza North Constituency) bɛ Bono East Region, Ghana.
english: He again donated large quantity of medical equipment to District's Health Directorate in his constituency (Nkoranza North Constituency) in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Kwasi Mensah da nɔk samɛt bɔtɔ pisnu (50 bags) tis Dromankese ye ba nɔki sʋŋi mɛ community's technical school o sʋ'ʋlimin (Nkoranza North Constituency) bɛ Bono East Region, Ghana la.
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah presented 50 bags of cement to Dromankese to be used for the construction of community's technical school in his constituency (Nkoranza North Constituency) in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Mensah lɛn anɛ Wadmaani, Member of Parliament (MP) tis Nkoranza North Constituency bɛ Bono East Region, Ghana la.
english: Joseph Mensah is also working as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Nkoranza North Constituency in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Kwasi Mensah o da lɛn di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisa (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la.
english: Joseph Kwasi Mensah won again in the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress with 15,124 votes (57.9%) to join the Eighth (8th) Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana against Derrick Oduro (Major Rtd.) of the New Patriotic Party who had 10,978 votes (42.1%).

kusaal: Joseph Mensah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n tis Kwesimintsim sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg ni, ba du'a o nɛ nwadis anii la dabisim pisi nɛ ayi' la yʋʋm 1957 la ni.
english: Joseph Mensah (born 22 August 1957) is a Ghanaian politician and former member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Kwesimintsim Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da paamɛ o diploma kasɛta gbaʋŋ ka paam B.A linɛ an Social Sciences zamisʋg n yi University of Cape Coast sakurin la, ka maali o Mastɛs digirii n bɛ University of Antwerp, Belgium sakurin la, ka an kpɛɛm n paas Chartered Institute of Logistics Transport tʋʋma la ni.
english: He got a diploma in education and a B.A in Social Sciences from the University of Cape Coast, his Master's degree from the University of Antwerp, Belgium, and a member of the Chartered Institute of Logistics Transport.

kusaal: Joseph Mensah da mɔr zi'esim bama n bɛ Ghana Ports and Harbours ni; o da anɛ operations manager lin da yi yʋʋma 2013 ti paae yʋʋm 2016 la ni, ka da lɛn an human resource manager kpɛɛm lin da yi yʋʋma 2005 ti paae yʋʋm 2016 la ni, o da lɛn anɛ training manager lin da yi yʋʋma 1998 ti paae yʋʋma 2013 la ni, ka an accounts supervisor lin da yi yʋʋma 2013 ti paae yʋʋm 2016 la ni.
english: Joseph Mensah held the following positions at the Ghana Ports and Harbours; operations manager from 2013 to 2016, human resource manager from 2005 to 2016, training manager from 1998 to 2013, and accounts supervisor from 2013 to 2016.

kusaal: Joseph Nii Laryea Afotey-Agbo (ka ba du'a o Mɔraug Nwadig 31, 1967) la anɛ Ghana Pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an Greater Accra Regional Minista Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Joseph Nii Laryea Afotey-Agbo (born July 31, 1967) is a Ghanaian politician and was the Greater Accra Regional Minister of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Yesu Kristo pʋ'ʋsʋm nid ka pʋ'ʋsid Presbyterian.
english: He is a Christian (Presbyterian) who is married with seven children.

kusaal: Afotey-Agbo anɛ Ma'asim Tiig (NDC) la nid.
english: Afotey-Agbo is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: O da anɛ kpeem zi'ig bama ni; Environment, Science nɛ Technology kpeem, nɛ Youth, Sports nɛ Malima (culture) kpeem, nɛ Privileges kpeem.[7] O da anɛ States minista yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai(2009) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piina ayi (2012).
english: Serving as a committee member on committees on Environment, Science and Technology Committee, Youth, Sports and Culture Committee, and Privileges Committee.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Afotey-Agbo nɛ Mɔraug Nwadig la dabisim pistan' nɛ yinne (31) yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi (1967).[4] Ba du'a o nɛ Katamanso-Nungua, tɛŋkanɛ bɛ Ankara sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Afotey-Agbo was born on July 31, 1967.

kusaal: O anɛ Parliament nidi tis Kpone-Katamanso vootʋg sʋ'ʋlim bama ni; anaasi, anu, anii si'ig nɛ ayɔpɔi zi'ig Parliament linɛ an Ghana Republic anaasi zi'ig la.
english: He is a member of Parliament representing Kpone-Katamanso Constituency in the 4th, 5th, 8th, and the current and 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Osei-Owusu anɛ lɔya ka an pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd n bɛ Ghana.
english: Joseph Osei-Owusu (born 22 January 1962, in Bekwai) is a Ghanaian lawyer, and politician.

kusaal: O keŋi o O-level sakuri n bɛnɛ Juaben Secondary Sakur la ni linɛ bɛ Juaben Kumasi sυ'υlυm la yυυm 1981 pυυgin.
english: He had his O-level secondary school education at Juaben Secondary School in Juaben in the Ashanti Region in 1981.

kusaal: Yυυm 1983 la ni ka o tɔlis A-level n bɛ Wenchi Secondary sakurin la.
english: In 1983, he also had his A-level in Wenchi Secondary School.

kusaal: Ya'asɛ, o lɛn keŋ Ghana wada sakur naae ka mɔr Barrister of Law (BL) yuum 1989, ka' lin ma'aanɛ o da lɛn tɔlis Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration sakur la ni naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ (GIMPA) yυυm 2007 la pυυgin.
english: He then went on to have a Bachelor of Arts (BA) Classics and Law from the University of Ghana in 1987, a Barrister of Law (BL) from the Ghana School of Law in 1989 and an Executive master's degree in Governance and Leadership from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) in 2007.

kusaal: Osei-Owusu tυm lɔya tυυma wυυ yυυm 29 pυυgin ban da buol o paas Ghana lɔya nam tυυma pυυgin yυυm 1990 la ni la.
english: Osei-Owusu has worked as a lawyer for 29 years in Ghana after being called to the bar in 1990.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ya'as ka John Agyekum Kufour da gaŋ o ye o an Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) kpɛɛm n gɔti li.
english: He later became chief executive officer (CEO) of the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA), a political appointment he got during the tenure of John Agyekum Kufour.

kusaal: O yiiga saŋa linɛ ka o da kena an wadmaan la anɛ yuum 2009 la ni ban da vɔɔt ka di la, kɔbiga pυυgin o da nyɛnɛ 86.06%.
english: He first became an MP in 2009, after being elected with 86.06% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Onɛ an Privileges Committee la kpɛɛm nannanna ka mɛ paas nimbanɛ gɔsid ka gaansid nidib wadmaanib yir la ni.
english: He is currently the chairperson for Privileges Committee and also the Appointments Committee in parliament.

kusaal: O da si'iŋi o sakuri ba teŋin la linɛ an Bekwai la.
english: Osei-Owusu was born on 22 January 1962 had his basic education in his hometown, Bekwai.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o tɔlis University of Ghana naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Bachelor of Arts nɛ Law yυυm 1987 la pυυgin.
english: He then went on to have a Bachelor of Arts (BA) Classics and Law from the University of Ghana in 1987, a Barrister of Law (BL) from the Ghana School of Law in 1989 and an Executive master's degree in Governance and Leadership from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) in 2007.

kusaal: O da si'iŋi wada tυυma nwa nɛ Yaw Barimah nɛ sieba ka lin nya'aŋ ka o bas ka keŋ paas George Sarpong wada tυυma la ni, ani ka ba da ti gaŋ o ye o an kpɛɛm la nya'andɔl.
english: He started his career in the chambers of Yaw Barimah & Co and later joined George Sarpong Legal Services where he rose to become Assistant Head of Chambers.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o an wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la kpɛɛm yiiga nya'andɔl Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni ka wadmaan yir linɛ paas anii la ni ka ba da lɛn lɛbis o ye o tυm paas.
english: He was elected the First Deputy Speaker of the 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic and re-elected to that position for the 8th Parliament.

kusaal: Otsiman da maal sini dinɛ an Kojo Bonzu The Burial of Kojo, Blitz the Ambassador da an onɛ da gɔs sini kan maalʋg yɛla.
english: Otsiman played the title character, Kojo Bonsu in The Burial of Kojo, directed by Blitz the Ambassador.

kusaal: awai(2019) Africa Movie Academy Awards.
english: He was nominated for Best Actor in a Supporting Role at the 2016 AMA Awards and Best actor in a Leading Role at the 2019 Africa Movie Academy Awards.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ da di ya'an nɔɔr ayi bɛ Africa Movie Academy Awards la ni.
english: He is a two-time Africa Movie Academy Awards nominee.

kusaal: Joseph Akuerteh Tettey (5 mɔtul nwadig 1974) anɛ Ghana politis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Joseph Tetteh is a Ghanaian politician and a member of parliament of the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Kpone Katamanso Constituency bɛ Kpone Katamanso Municipal,Greater Accra Region, Ghana la.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the deputy regional minister of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani paas Ghana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la ni, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the deputy regional minister of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔri Degree Masters in Business Administration yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ yinne la ni (2011) yi Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) nɛ Bachelor of Arts Degree in Economics yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayi' la ni (2002) yi University of Ghana.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the deputy regional minister of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid tam nɛ tiis yɛla la Ghana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la, Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He was vetted by the Appointments Committee of the Parliament of Ghana in the same month.

kusaal: O tʋmi bɛ 4th, 5th, 6th nɛ 7th parliament bɛ 4th Republic of Ghana ni.
english: He served as the Member for Parliament for Wa West Constituency in the 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Parliaments of the 4th Republic of Ghana from January 2005 to January 2021.

kusaal: Chireh ka ba da du'a o Lassia Tuolu dinɛ bɛ Upper West Region of Ghana la.
english: Chireh was born in the Lassia-Tuolu, a village in Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O kɛŋi o secondary sakur zamisʋg bɛnɛ Navrongo Secondary School dinɛ bɛ Upper East Region dinɛ ka o zamis GCE Ordinary nɛ Advanced bɛn kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: He attended the Navrongo Secondary School in the Upper East Region from 1968 to 1975 where obtained both Ordinary and Advanced Level West African Examination Council School certificates.

kusaal: O kɛŋ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology din yi yʋʋm1975 la ni ka paam Bachelor of Pharmacy digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm 1979 la ni.
english: He studied at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology from 1975 and obtained a Bachelor of Pharmacy degree in 1979.

kusaal: O kɛŋ tuon bɛ Ghana wada sakur bɛ yʋʋm 2001 ka paam suori an barrister yʋʋm 2006 la ni.
english: He proceeded to the Ghana School of Law in 2001 and qualified as a lawyer in 2006.

kusaal: Yieleh Chireh tʋmi anɛ Chairman tis Procurement Taskforce dinɛ ka PNDC Gɔmma la da zi'eli bɛ yʋʋm 1991 ni.
english: In 1991, PNDC chairman Jerry John Rawlings appointed Chireh chairman of the Procurement Taskforce.

kusaal: Onɛ an kpɛɛm la ba kɛnɛ ka o kpanbi gɔsid ka kpansid itʋma bɛ'ɛd bɛ Ministries Departments and Agencies (MDAs) dinɛ ka ti mi' anɛ Ministry of Health, Volta River Authority, Electricity Corporation of Ghana nɛ former Post & Telecommunications Corporation.
english: As chairman he is credited with spearheading the investigations of procurement malpractices in selected Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs); notable among them is the Ministry of Health, the Volta River Authority, Electricity Corporation of Ghana and the Post and Telecommunications Corporation.

kusaal: Chireh paas ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg ninbanɛ da zi'eli di yʋʋm 1992 la ni ye di anɛ pɔlitis paati bɛ Ghana.
english: Chireh joined the National Democratic Congress when it was formed in 1992 on the resumption of party politics in Ghana.

kusaal: Di da anɛ Jerry Rawlings da gaŋ o ye o an Upper West Regional Minister onɛ da an gɔmma la bɛ yʋʋm 1993 la ni.
english: He was appointed by President Jerry John Rawlings as Upper West Regional minister in his government in February 1993.

kusaal: Ba kɛ ka o an Ambassador Extraordinary nɛ Plenipotentiary tis Algeria nɛ Tunisia saŋa yinne, Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic and Mauritania yʋʋm 1997 nɛ yʋʋm 2001 pʋʋgʋn.
english: President Jerry John Rawlings appointed Chireh to serve as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to Algeria with concurrent accreditation to Tunisia, Mauritania and the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic from July 1997 to March 2001 and minister for the Upper West Region from March 1993 to March 1997.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan kʋdʋg tis Wa West.
english: He served as the Member for Parliament for Wa West Constituency in the 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Parliaments of the 4th Republic of Ghana from January 2005 to January 2021.

kusaal: O anɛ Pan-African wadmaanib yir nid mɛn.
english: He also served as a member of the Pan-African Parliament between May 2017 to January 2021.

kusaal: O tʋm bɛ zi'es bɛdigʋ dinɛ yi Regional minister, Ambassador, mp tis Minister of Local Government nɛ Rural development nɛ Minister of health.
english: In the 7th parliament of the 4th republic, he served on the Subsidiary Legislation Committee, Local Government and Rural Development Committee and Appointments Committee.

kusaal: Joyce Adeline Bamford-Addo, JSC, CV (ba du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan nɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa atan la dabpisi nɛ ayuobʋ daar, 26 March 1937) ka o an Ghana lɔya nɛ piyam ka da an yiiga pʋ'akanɛ da an Speaker of Parliament tis Ghana din yi yʋʋm tusa ay nɛ awai (2009) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013).
english: Joyce Adeline Bamford-Addo, (born 26 March 1937) is a Ghanaian barrister and judge who served as the first female Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana from 2009 to 2013.

kusaal: Mary's Boarding School nɛ Our Lady of Apostles (OLA) Boarding School, on nɛ o taʋn Cynthia, Cape Coast ka o da maali basic education.
english: Joyce Bamford-Addo attended the Government Girls' School, Accra, St. Mary's Boarding School and Our Lady of Apostles (OLA) Boarding School, along with her sister Cynthia, in Cape Coast for her basic education.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da keŋ Holy Child School, dinɛ mɛ bɛ Cape Coast la maali o secondary education.
english: She subsequently attended Holy Child School, also in Cape Coast, for her secondary education.

kusaal: O da naal Inner Temple ye o zamis tʋʋmkanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Inns of court ka da lieb lɔya tis English Bar la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiwai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne la ni (1961).
english: She joined the Inner Temple to train under the apprenticeship system known as Inns of Court and was called to the English Bar in 1961.

kusaal: O da lieb lɔya Ghana kpɛla yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi la ni (1962).
english: She was called to the Ghana Bar in 1962.

kusaal: O da pin'il tʋmnɛ Assistant State Attorney tʋʋma yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan la ni (1963) ka da paam tuon kennɛ lieb State Attorney, din nya'aŋ ka o da paam kpɛŋʋ tɔlis tuoni lieb Senior State Attorney ka yʋ'ʋn naan kilim Principal State Attorney.
english: She started working as an Assistant State Attorney in 1963 and promoted to State Attorney, then subsequently promoted to become a Senior State Attorney before becoming a Principal State Attorney.

kusaal: O da nɔbʋgʋ kena kilim Chief State Attorney yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan la ni (1973).
english: She became Chief State Attorney in 1973.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o an Director of Public Prosecutions yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1976), da bɛ kpɛŋkan ni yʋʋm piiga.
english: She was appointed Director of Public Prosecutions in 1976, a position she held for 10 years.

kusaal: erry Rawlings da lɛn gaŋ o ye an Supreme Court piayam yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne la ni (1991), ka an yiiga pʋ'akanɛ an kilim Piyam tis Supreme Court of Ghana.
english: She was appointed by Jerry Rawlings as a Supreme Court Judge in 1991, becoming the first female Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: On da tʋm gɔmena tʋʋma yʋma bɛdigʋ la, o mɛŋ da siaki yi ka bas tʋʋma la Supreme Court ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi nwadis piiga la ni (October 2004).
english: After working in the public service for several years, she retired voluntarily from the Supreme Court in October 2004.

kusaal: Nidib da yɛl ye o yi tʋʋma la ninɛ ban gaŋ o gaadi nɔk onɛ bɛɛ o nya'aŋ, Justice George Kingsley Acquah, ye o an Chief Justice la.
english: It was allegedly reported that she retired over being bypassed by her junior, Justice George Kingsley Acquah, in the appointment of Chief Justice.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne la ni (1991), Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC) saŋa, Bamford-Addo da lieb Second Deputy Speaker tis Ghana's Consultative Assembly, ka da paas banɛ da sɔb gbaʋŋkanɛ da yuolim lieb Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi wada gbaʋŋ la (1992 constitution).
english: In 1991, during the late Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC) era, Bamford-Addo became the Second Deputy Speaker of Ghana's Consultative Assembly, set up to draft what became the 1992 constitution.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) zuraan nɛ wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la nya'aŋ ba da vɔɔt o ka sɔ' pʋ nya' nɛ o ka kilim Speaker tis Fourth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana o da di'e yinɛ Ebenezer Sekyi-Hughes ni, ka da an yiiga pʋ'akanɛ mɔr kpɛŋkan, ka an pʋ'akanɛ paasi ayi an zuraan tis gɔmena lʋgʋr, ban da gaŋ Georgina Theodora Wood ka o da an Chief Justice tis Supreme Court of Ghana.
english: Following the 2008 presidential and parliamentary elections, she was elected unopposed as the Speaker of the Fourth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, taking over from Ebenezer Sekyi-Hughes, serving as the first female to take up that position, and second female to head an arm of government after Georgina Theodora Wood was appointed Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: Vɔɔtʋg la keya ka o an pʋ'akanɛ bɛ tuon Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb ni, hali gaad Georgina Theodora Woods.
english: The election also made her the highest ranked female in Ghana's political history surpassing Georgina Theodora Woods.

kusaal: O yɛla yʋ'ʋn da tiig Africa nɛ dunia wʋsa ka o yʋ'ʋn naali o pʋ'a taab banɛ an speaker nam nwɛnɛ Betty Boothroyd onɛ bɛ United Kingdom nɛ Nancy Pelosi onɛ bɛ United States of America ka ba an yiiga pʋ'abanɛ an speaker nami ba tɛɛnsin.
english: She became known across Africa and across the globe joining other female speakers like Betty Boothroyd in the United Kingdom and Nancy Pelosi of the United States of America as first female speakers of their respective countries.

kusaal: Bamford-Addo paas Ghana Bar Association, Catholic Lawyers Guild, International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) nɛ Commonwealth Lawyers Association.
english: Bamford-Addo is a member of the Ghana Bar Association, Catholic Lawyers Guild, International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) and the Commonwealth Lawyers Association.

kusaal: On da tʋm gɔmena tʋʋma la ka an Supreme Court Piyam la, o da paas Legal Aid Board nɛ Judicial Council (General Legal Council) pʋʋgin.
english: Whilst working in the public service as a Supreme Court Judge, she also served as a member of the Legal Aid Board and the Judicial Council (General Legal Council).

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ onɛ zi'en Ghana nɔba zug UN Commission on the Status of women international conferences nam bɛdegʋ ni.
english: She served as the representative from Ghana at several UN Commission on the Status of women international conferences.

kusaal: American Biographical Institute da tis Bamford-Addo ya'an piini ye onɛ an pʋ'akanɛ mɔ gaadi o taaba yʋʋm yusa ayi la ni (2000) on da mɔɔd pʋ'ab yɛla nɛ ba tuon ken yɛla la.
english: Bamford-Addo was awarded the best woman of the year by the American Biographical Institute in 2000 due to her zeal and unfettered efforts towards women issues and women empowerment.

kusaal: Ghana Association of Women Entrepreneurs (GAWE) da zun'oe o bɛ Global Women Entrepreneur Trade Fair and Investment Forum bɛ Accra dinner and awards night yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne la ni (2011) on nɛ Justice Georgina Theodora Wood, pʋ'akanɛ an yiiga Chief Justice, Anna Bossman, pʋ'akanɛ da an yiiga zi'en Commissioner for the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ) nɔba zug nɛ Elizabeth Mills-Robertson, pʋ'akanɛ da an yiiga zi'en Inspector General of Police (IGP) nɔba zug.
english: She was honored by Ghana Association of Women Entrepreneurs (GAWE) at their Global Women Entrepreneur Trade Fair and Investment Forum in Accra dinner and awards night in 2011 along with other Ghana's first women top office holders Justice Georgina Theodora Wood, first woman Chief Justice, Anna Bossman, first woman Acting Commissioner for the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ) and Elizabeth Mills-Robertson, first woman Acting Inspector General of Police (IGP).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne nwadis piiga la ni (October 2011), Zuraan John Evans Atta Mills da piinl o nɛ Companion of the Order of the Volta, dinɛ gad Order of Volta piininam la wʋsa, pa'an tʋʋmsʋŋkanɛ ka o tʋmmi tisid Ghana la.
english: In October 2011, she was honored by President John Evans Atta Mills with the Companion of the Order of the Volta, highest in the Order of Volta awards, in recognition of her outstanding service to Ghana.

kusaal: Bamford-Addo anɛ Kristo biig onɛ pɛsigi o mɛŋ ka an Roman Catholic pʋ'ʋsim nid.
english: Bamford-Addo is a devout Christian and worships as a Roman Catholic.

kusaal: Onɛ an pʋ'akanɛ ka ba da gaŋi o tis kpɛŋkan ni West African sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.
english: She was the first woman to be elected to that position in the West African sub-region.

kusaal: Bamford-Addo da lɛn anɛ yga pʋ'a lieb Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana.
english: Bamford-Addo also was the first female Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: O da tʋm ani din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiwai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne la ni (1991) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni (2004) ka o tʋʋma naae.
english: She served in that role from 1991 until 2004, when she retired.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1937).
english: Born in 1937 in Accra to an English father and a Ghanaian mother from Aburi.

kusaal: O saam da anɛ na'asaara ka o ma an Ghana ninkanɛ yi Aburi, Joyce Bamford-Addo dakɛŋnɛ St.
english: Born in 1937 in Accra to an English father and a Ghanaian mother from Aburi.

kusaal: Ka tɔlisi keŋ United Kingdom paami legal training.
english: She proceeded to the United Kingdom for legal training.

kusaal: Bamford-Addo da fɛndigi lɛb Ghana on da tʋm tis United Kingdom yʋma bi'ela la nya'aŋ.
english: Bamford-Addo returned to Ghana after working in the United Kingdom for a year.

kusaal: O lɛn anɛ pʋ'akanɛ yɔ'ɔg suor law nɛ legislation ni Ghana ka lɛn an zanbin tis Ghana pʋ'ab.
english: She is considered as a female pacesetter in law and legislation in Ghana and an inspiration and role model generally to Ghanaian women.

kusaal: Ba da dua Joyce Adwoa Akoh Dei nɛ yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu la li nwadis piiga la dabisim pii nɛ ayi' daar (12th sawa'ar nwadig 1965) O anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka a wabʋg na'adɔɔg la (NPP) nid yinne.
english: Joyce Adwoa Akoh Dei was born on 12 October 1965 in Asiwa, Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Joyce Adwoa Akoh Dei anɛ pu'a kanɛ kpimisid ka lɛn an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd paas wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nid (NPP) la.
english: Joyce Adwoa Akoh Dei (born 12 October 1964) ) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O di'e o level 3 Adult nɛ further sakur pa'an-pa'an gbaʋŋ.
english: She holds a level 3/Adult and further Education Teachers Certificate.

kusaal: Akoh Dei da nyi'a wadmaanib kʋk bɛ Bosome-Freho constituency kanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la dɔlisidnɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg la ni yʋʋm tʋsa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ kanɛ da an Ghana wʋsa vɔɔdʋg tita'ar la ka nidib tusa pii nɛ anu nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (15,497) vɔɔt tis o ka o di pa'al ye o di ya nɛ vɔɔt kal 62.17%.
english: Akoh Dei contested the Bosome-Freho constituency parliamentary seat in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party in the 2016 Ghanaian general election and won with 15,497 votes, representing 62.17% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da di ya ka kɛ Nana Yaw Ofori-Kuragu, IND onɛ ka nidib tusa anaasi nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnu nɛ anu (4,655) vɔɔt tis o ka o mɔr 18.68% ka Kwame Adarkwa onɛ dɔlisid ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la da paam vɔɔt nam nidib tusa anaasi nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnu (4,550) ka li an vɔɔt pii nɛ anii du'al pisi nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (18.25%), ka Bright Baffour Asare kanɛ da dɔli PPP dim dɔɔg la mɛ mɔr vɔɔt nam nidib kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ atan' ka din an nɛɛm du'al pisnaasi nɛ awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.49%) ka Yeboah Samuel onɛ mɛ da an Anɔraʋg na'adɔɔg nid ka mɛ da paam vɔɔt nam kɔbiga ka li mɛ an nɛɛm du'al pisnaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.40%).
english: She won the election over Nana Yaw Ofori-Kuragu (Independent) who polled 4,655 votes, equivalent to 18.68%, while parliamentary candidate for the National Democratic Congress Kwame Adarkwa had 4,550 votes, representing 18.25%, Bright Baffour Asare of the PPP polled 123 votes, representing 0.49% and the parliamentary candidate for the Convention People's Party Yeboah Samuel had 100 votes, equivalent to 0.40% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadamaan tis Bosome -Freho constituency bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: She was the member of parliament for Bosome-Freho constituency in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dua Akoh Dei nɛ yʋm tʋsir, kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuob nɛ anu nwadis piiga la dabis piinɛ ayi daar Asiwa, bɛ Ashanti Region.
english: Joyce Adwoa Akoh Dei was born on 12 October 1965 in Asiwa, Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Akoh Dei anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg la (NPP) nid yinne ka an wadmaan tis Bosome -Freho constituency kanɛ bɛ seventh parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana ni la.
english: Akoh Dei is a member of the New Patriotic Party and was the member of Parliament for Bosome-Freho constituency in the seventh parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔri biisa atan ka on nɛ o sid lɛm kai.
english: She is divorced, with three children.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Tetteh nɛ Tsyome-Sabadu, Volta Region.
english: Tetteh was born in Tsyome-Sabadu, Volta Region.

kusaal: O da keŋ nɛ Lɔyanam sakurin zamis Lɔɔ nɛ BEd in Management Studies University of Cape Coast.
english: She studied Law and BEd in Management Studies at the University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ awai la Nwadisa anii la ni, North Dayi Constituency Na'anam nɛ nidib la nif da tigi o tʋʋma yɛla ka ba tis o piini ka lɛn diis o Na'am kanɛ ka di yʋ'ʋr an; Mama Edzeame.
english: She was honoured in August 2019 by the Chiefs and people of the North Dayi Constituency, who conferred on her the title: Mama Edzeame.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana Wadmaan tis North Dayi sʋ'ʋlim ka an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la NDC nid.
english: In 2016, she contested and won the NDC parliamentary seat for the North Dayi Constituency in the Volta Region.

kusaal: O paas nɛ pu'ab pistan' nɛ ayuobʋ (36) banɛ bɛ Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: She was one of the 36 female parliamentarians of the seventh parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Joycelin anɛ onɛ zabid nidib kuosʋg bɛɛ banɛ mɔr nidibi tʋm tʋʋmkpi'ema yɛla Ghana kpɛla la.
english: Tetteh is also currently the ambassador for human trafficking in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da nwaae dinɛ yi Ejisu-Juaben Constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi' (2012) vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: It was created out of the Ejisu-Juaben Constituency in 2012.

kusaal: Juaben constituency bɛnɛ Ejisu-Juaben Municipal District dinɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Juaben is located in the Ejisu-Juaben Municipal District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ama Pomaa Andoh an wadmaan nananna tis Constituency la.
english: It was created out of the Ejisu-Juaben Constituency in 2012.

kusaal: Di da paasnɛ Juaboso-Bodi District dinɛ da dɛŋim bɛ la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi nwasdisa anii (August 2004) la ni, k aba da nwaae di yi Sefwi-Bibiani District Council la ni, ti paae sankanɛ k aka ba da pʋdigi di Ya-dagɔbʋg-nya'aŋ la yis ka di lieb Bodi District yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa ayuobʋ la dabpisi nɛ anii daar la ( 28 June 2012); ka yʋ'ʋn tiak zin'ikanɛ kpɛlim la yʋ'ʋri buon ye Juaboso District.
english: Originally it was formerly part of the then-larger Juaboso-Bodi District in August 2004, which was created from the former Sefwi-Bibiani District Council, until the southeast part of the district was split off to create Bodi District on 28 June 2012; thus the remaining part has been renamed as Juaboso District.

kusaal: Distirik assembly la bɛ Western North Region Ya-dagɔbʋg tuon baba ka Juaboso aan di tempʋtita'ar.
english: The district assembly is located in the northwest part of Western North Region and has Juaboso as its capital town.

kusaal: Di na nwɛnɛ 65 kilometers yi ya-datiʋŋ lɛbid tuon baba tɔnd nɛ distirik tempʋtita'ar la, Wiawso.
english: It is about 65 kilometers northwest of the district capital Wiawso.

kusaal: Di mɛ lɛn anɛ kilomita nam kɔbistan nɛ pisyuobʋ (360 kilometers) yi ya-datiʋŋ lɛbid tuon baba tɔnd nɛ Takoradi dinɛ bɛ Atlantic Ocean baba ka an kilomita nam kɔbisyi' nɛ pisi nɛ anu (225 kilometres)Ya-datiʋŋ lɛbid tuon baba tɔnd nɛ Kumasi, dinɛ aan Ashanti Region tempʋtita'ar la.
english: It is also 360 kilometers northwest of Takoradi on the Atlantic Ocean coast and 225 kilometres south west of Kumasi, capital of the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Tembanɛ kpi'e di lɛbid ya-nya'aŋ baba anɛ Asunafo South nɛ Bodi Distirik nam.
english: Its eastern neighbours are the Asunafo South and Bodi Districts.

kusaal: Suaman Distirik bɛ di dagɔbʋg ka La Cote d'Ivoire bɛɛ di tuon baba.
english: The Suaman District lies south and the La Cote d'Ivoire is to the west.

kusaal: Juaboso District mɔr sʋ'ʋlʋm nam anaasi: Ba anɛ Kofikrom-Proso, Asempaneye, Benchema-Nkatieso nɛ Boinzan.
english: Juaboso District has four area councils: Kofikrom-Proso, Asempaneye, Benchema-Nkatieso and Boinzan.

kusaal: Juaboso District bɛnɛ latitude 6° 6'N nɛ 7°N, nɛ longitude 2°40'W nɛ 3°15'W sʋʋgʋn.
english: Juaboso District lies between latitude 6° 6'N and 7°N, and longitude 2°40'W and 3°15'W. To the north are the Bia East, Bia West and Asunafo North Municipal Districts.

kusaal: Di tɔndnɛ Bia East lɛbid, Bia West nɛ Asunafo North Municipal District nam lɛbid Ya-datiʋŋ baba.
english: Juaboso District lies between latitude 6° 6'N and 7°N, and longitude 2°40'W and 3°15'W. To the north are the Bia East, Bia West and Asunafo North Municipal Districts.

kusaal: Juliet Yaa Asantewa Asante anɛ Ghana sini di'ema sɔb, ka maan sini, ka len an one sʋŋid tadimnam.
english: Juliet Yaa Asantewa Asante is a Ghanaian film actress, producer and director, and philanthropist.

kusaal: One an Chief Executive Officer (CEO) tis National Film Authority (NFA).
english: She is a former Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the National Film Authority (NFA).

kusaal: Sini kanɛ ka o maal ka li pʋ yuugɛ, Silver Rain, ba da gaŋi li paas banɛ nar piini di'er pʋʋgin bɛ "Best Film in West Africa" nɛ "Best costume" yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu (2015) bɛ Africa Magic viewer's choice awards (AMVCA) nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu (2015) "Best Overall Film In Africa".
english: Her latest film, Silver Rain, was nominated for "Best Film in West Africa" and "Best costume" for 2015 in the Africa Magic viewer's choice awards (AMVCA) and also 2015 "Best Overall Film In Africa".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ wai la (1999), Asante da pin'il sini maalig zin'ig kanɛ ka o buol ye Eagle House Productions.
english: In 1999, Asante started the production house Eagle House Productions.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan ni ka o pin'il "Save Our Women International", asʋ-ʋmmɛŋ lʋgir kanɛ gɔsid pʋ'ab pʋ'alim yela zamisig ka pin'il pʋtɛn'ɛr kanɛ ka ba maan sini ginma gɔsid fon nam ni Africa sʋ'ʋlim yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ naasi (2014) ka li yʋ'ʋr an Mobile Flicks.
english: That same year she also started "Save Our Women International", a non-profit entity focusing on female sexual education and launched an innovation that makes short movies for the mobile phone in Africa in 2014 called Mobile Flicks.

kusaal: One pin'il ka mɛ len an executive director tis Black Star International Film Festival.
english: She is also the Founder and executive director of Black Star International Film Festival.

kusaal: Eagle Productions sʋŋ hali zamis sini maanib Ghana sʋ'ʋlim dɔlisidi li zamisig lʋgir kanɛ an Eagle Drama Workshop la.
english: Eagle Productions has helped train some actors and actresses in Ghana through its training arm, the Eagle Drama Workshop.

kusaal: O mɔr gbaŋ kanɛ an master's degree in Public Administration (MPA) nɛ Master's in Public Policy (MPP) yit Harvard Kennedy School of Government.
english: She holds a master's degree in Public Administration (MPA) and a Master's in Public Policy (MPP) from Harvard Kennedy School of Government.

kusaal: O da naae nɛ University of Cape Coast, ka mɛ len naae National Film and Television Institute.
english: She graduated from University of Cape Coast, and also graduated from National Film and Television Institute.

kusaal: Asante anɛ CEO tis National film Authority of Ghana, ka an board chair tis National Film and Television Institute (NAFTI) nɛ Founding President of the Black Star International Film Institute, banɛ maan di'em kanɛ ka ba buon Black Star International Film Festival (BSIFF) la.
english: Asante is the former CEO of the National film Authority of Ghana, the board chair of the National Film and Television Institute (NAFTI) and the Founding President of the Black Star International Film Institute, organizers of the Black Star International Film Festival (BSIFF).

kusaal: One an kpɛɛm tis Curriculum committee of the Creative Arts School, zamisig lʋgir kanɛ bɛ Ministry of Education, Ghana.
english: She chairs the Curriculum committee of the Creative Arts School, a revolutionary educational concept by the Ministry of Education, Ghana.

kusaal: One da pin'il Yaa Asantewa Library project, mɛɛd libraries nam ka pɛ'ɛni ba nɛ gbana.
english: She is the founder of the Yaa Asantewa Library project, building and stocking libraries in Ghanaian communities.

kusaal: Asante da paam ya'an piini kanɛ an 'Best Actress' Ghana sʋ'ʋlim yʋʋm tusayi nɛ yinne (2001).
english: Asante was awarded 'Best Actress' in Ghana in 2001.

kusaal: Li ya'aŋ ka o kɛŋ National Film and Television institute of Ghana, anina ka o zamis gbaŋi gaad o taaba bɛ Film Directing zamisig pʋʋgin.
english: She later went to the National Film and Television institute of Ghana, where she got her first class honors in Film Directing.

kusaal: On paas sini di'em si'eba ni nwana: Twin Lovers, Fresh Blood, Tears of Blood, Ripples, and Thread of Ananse.
english: Some of the films in which she has acted are Twin Lovers, Fresh Blood, Tears of Blood, Ripples, and Thread of Ananse.

kusaal: O da paasi maal sini kanɛ buon Deadly Voyage yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayʋobʋ (1996) an Albert Mensah pʋ'a.
english: She appeared in the 1996 film Deadly Voyage as Albert Mensah's wife.

kusaal: O sɔb di'ema suoya gbana, gaad tuoni maan di'ema Ghana sini pʋʋgin ka ba si'eba an Obaby, din anɛ pʋ'aliak zin'ig, nɛ Secrets, di'ema kanɛ ka o paas kpɛɛm banɛ maan la pʋʋgin.
english: She has written, directed and produced shows on Ghana television, such as Obaby, a dating show, and Secrets, a drama series for which she is also executive producer.

kusaal: On an kpikpiŋ nɛ sini maan la, Asante da pin'il Eagle Productions Limited yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999), ka gaad lʋgir nwa' tuoni maan sini nam bɛdigʋ Ghana TV pʋʋgin lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ yinne paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga la ( 2001 paae 2010).
english: As an Entrepreneur and Filmmaker, Asante founded Eagle Productions Limited in 1999, creatively leading the company to produce some of the most successful shows on Ghana Television between 2001 and 2010.

kusaal: O tʋʋma yʋ'ʋr la, Mobile fliks da tʋm nɛ MTN ka maal sini ginma banɛ ka ba gɔsid fon nam ni.
english: Her company, Mobilefliks successfully worked with MTN to make short films available to audiences through the mobile phone.

kusaal: O anɛ gbansɔbidi tis The Huffington Post ka an sa'an-sa'an ni bɛ da'a diib pʋʋgin bɛ Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Sloan school of business lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piine tan' paae zina nwa', ka mɛ pa'an Mass Communication bɛ Webster University, Ghana yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi (2017).
english: She is a regular writer and blogger for The Huffington Post and has served as a Mentor on Entrepreneurship at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Sloan school of business from 2013 to date, also lecturing Mass Communication at the Webster University, Ghana campus in 2017.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Asante nɛ Ghana ka o paas nɛ o dʋ'adib biis ayi' ni, baba nu pʋʋgin.
english: Asante was born in Ghana and is the second of five children.

kusaal: O len mɔr bachelor's degrees kasɛta gbana ayi'.
english: She also holds two bachelor's degrees.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o sini kanɛ ka o maal ka li pʋ yuugɛ, Silver Rain,piin kanɛ an "Best Film in West Africa" nɛ "Best costume" ni yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu (2015) piin kanɛ buon Africa Magic viewer's choice awards (AMVCA) la, ka yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu (2015) ka ba lɛn gaŋ o bɛ "Best Overall Film In Africa".
english: Her latest film, Silver Rain, was nominated for "Best Film in West Africa" and "Best costume" for 2015 in the Africa Magic viewer's choice awards (AMVCA) and also 2015 "Best Overall Film In Africa".

kusaal: Ba da lɛm buon o nɛ yee West African dim onɛ vɛnni gat sɔ' wʋsa, ka di anɛ A-listers Magazine da yɛl wala.
english: She has been referred to as the "Most Beautiful West African Woman" according to A-listers Magazine.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ o sakur dinɛ ka buoni li Ghana Institute of Languages, anima ka o zamis English, French nɛɛ Spanish.
english: She studied at the Ghana Institute of Languages, where she studied English, French, and Spanish.

kusaal: O da lɛm zamis dinɛ anɛ Marketing, Advertising and Public Relations bɛ Ghana Institute of Journalism.
english: She also studied marketing, Advertising, and Public Relations at the Ghana Institute of Journalism.

kusaal: Ibrahim da yɛl yee, on ya'a bɛ Africa, nidib pʋ gɔs ka on an pua manɛ an ninsabilɛ ka li anɛ o niŋgnin la zʋg, amaa on ya'a yi Africa naae, ba gɔsid onɛ ka on an ninvusabilig.
english: Ibrahim has commented that in Africa, she is not regarded as a black woman because of her skin tone, but outside Africa, she is recognized as being black.

kusaal: Ibrahim da maali o sini a nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni film crime paae Christ starring Majid Michel.
english: Ibrahim made her acting debut in the 2005 film Crime to Christ starring Majid Michel.

kusaal: O Nollowood sini la da anɛ Yankee Boys ka din nya'aŋ ka o maal sininam pɛɛs ka li tʋʋg wʋʋ pisnu(50) yɛla.
english: Her first Nollywood film was Yankee Boys, and she has featured in more than 50 films afterwards.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsa ayi, piiga nɛ anaasi (2014) la ni, o da maali o yiiga sini dinɛ an, Number One Fan, ani ka o sin'iŋi tʋm sini tʋʋma ka sɔ' pian'ad o sini la ni.
english: In 2014, she produced her first film, Number One Fan, in which she stars as an actress being stalked by a fan in the film.

kusaal: O sini kanɛ da pɛɛsi ayi anɛ Shattered Romance dinɛ ka Ghana nɛ Nigeria dim sini tumtumidib da pɛɛsi o zug ka o zʋŋ sini kannɛ bɛ amidst fanfare Accra pʋʋgin, Ghana, yʋʋm tʋsir nɛ piiga nɛ anaasi, Sampiid nwadig la dabisa anu la ni (5th December, 2014).
english: Her second movie, Shattered Romance, which features Nigerian and Ghanaian actors, launched amidst fanfare in Accra, Ghana, on 5 December 2014.

kusaal: O TV paal sini sia bɛ ka li pian'a zug an (Every Woman Has a Story) ani ka o da bigisi o pa'alʋg ya'am, ka ba da mɔri yisid Terrestrial TV ni, ka o sini paal kanɛ an, The Perfect Assistant la, di kʋ yʋʋgɛ ka o yisi li paalʋ.
english: Her new TV series; Every Woman Has a Story, where she debuted her directorial skills, is airing on terrestrial TV.

kusaal: O maal Twi sininam, Yoruba sininam, nɛɛ Ladan Sure dinɛ anɛ Hausa pian'ad sininam.
english: She has featured in Twi movies, in Yoruba language films, and also in Ladan Aure, a Hausa Language film.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ni, onɛ da di sininam malʋg la ya'an yiiga bɛ 4 Play.
english: She won the Best Actress in a Leading Role award at the 2010 Ghana Movie Awards for her role in 4 Play.

kusaal: Ba da dua juliet Ibrahim nɛ yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan' la, Dɔnwalig nwadig la dabisa atan' la (3rd March, 983) ni.
english: Juliet Ibrahim was born on 3 March 1986 to a Lebanese father and a Ghanaian-Liberian mother in Accra.

kusaal: O saam da anɛ Lebanese dim nid ka o ma lɛɛ da an Ghana nɛɛ Liberia nid ka bɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Juliet Ibrahim was born on 3 March 1986 to a Lebanese father and a Ghanaian-Liberian mother in Accra.

kusaal: Onɛ da an bi kpɛɛm ka mɔr pitib ayi'iŋa pɛsi o zug, nɛɛ Sonia Ibrahim onɛ mɛ sini maan maan, nɛ o taʋ.
english: She is the oldest child and has two sisters, including the actress Sonia Ibrahim, and a brother.

kusaal: Juliet nɛ o pitib la da bɛ nɛ Lebanon nɛ Ivory Coast dinsin'iŋi ba biilimin sa, ka li anɛ tapnam zabanam yɛla.
english: Ibrahim and her siblings spent the longest part of their childhood in Lebanon and Ivory Coast due to civil wars.

kusaal: O da sin'iŋi piramili sakur la nɛ Lebanon teŋin ka tɔlis tʋoni keŋi o Sekondei sakur la nɛ Ivory Coast, ka nɛ nɛ o duadib.
english: Ibrahim and her siblings spent the longest part of their childhood in Lebanon and Ivory Coast due to civil wars.

kusaal: O a tun'e pian'a English nɛ French.
english: She studied at the Ghana Institute of Languages, where she studied English, French, and Spanish.

kusaal: O pin'ili o dasanʋgnɛ bɛ Sheffield Alarib daar yʋʋm 1995, ka tɔlisi keŋ kpɛmnam senior squad yʋʋm 1997 la ni.
english: He began his youth career at Sheffield Wednesday in 1995, moving up to the senior squad in 1997.

kusaal: Zi'ikani ka o nwɛ' yʋʋg anɛ Bristol Rovers (2003–2006), dinɛ ka o yi nɔɔr 140 ka di gɔɔlnam 40 ka naam tɔlis Nottingham Forest.
english: His longest spell was at Bristol Rovers (2003–2006), where he made 140 appearances and scored over 40 goals before moving to Nottingham Forest.

kusaal: Agogo dinɛ gɔɔlnam 143 bɛ o bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb wʋsa ni.
english: Agogo scored a total of 143 goals during his professional football career.

kusaal: Junior Agogo du'am yʋʋm anɛ 1 August 1979 bɛ Accra, Ghana pɛ'ɛs yinne o mabiis 11 la ni.
english: Junior Agogo was born on 1 August 1979 in Accra, Ghana as one of 11 siblings.

kusaal: O keŋnɛ Ridge Church School dinɛ bɛ Accra, amaa o da pʋ naae primary school, ka o du'adib zii o keŋ UK.
english: He attended the Ridge Church School in Accra, but before completing primary school, he moved with his family to the UK.

kusaal: Augustine College, di anɛ dasam-wʋsa bɔɔdin secondary school dinɛ bɛ Cape Coast.
english: He subsequently returned to Ghana for three years, attending St. Augustine's College, an all-boys Catholic boarding secondary school in Cape Coast.

kusaal: Agogo saam, Mr Emmanuel Agogo, onɛ an kpikpinkpin la, yɛl o ye o zamisim ka bas bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb.
english: Agogo's father, Mr Emmanuel Agogo, a businessman, encouraged him to study instead of playing sports.

kusaal: Ba du'a o nɛ Ghana amaa o biilimɛn wʋsa o bɛnɛ UK.
english: He then moved back to Ghana during his years in secondary school.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋn da lɛb Ghana saŋkani ka o bɛ secondary school la.
english: He then moved back to Ghana during his years in secondary school.

kusaal: O nwɛ' gaad kilabnam piinɛ anu yʋma piinɛ anu ni, ka naam gɛ' nɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb yʋʋm 2012.
english: He played for fifteen different clubs over the next fifteen years, before retiring from professional football in 2012.

kusaal: O nwɛ' o nwɛ'ɛb la wʋsa ni nɛ bɛ England, pɛ'ɛs nɛ nwɛ'ɛb bi'ela bɛ US, Egypt, Cyprus nɛ Scotland.
english: He spent most of his playing career in England, with additional spells in the US, Egypt, Cyprus and Scotland.

kusaal: Agogo nwɛ' tis Ghana national team la yʋʋm 2006 nɛ 2009 pʋʋgʋn.
english: Agogo played for the Ghana national team between 2006 and 2009.

kusaal: O naae gɔɔlnam atan' da bɛ naae nwɛ'ɛb yʋʋm 2008 Africa Cup of Nations sʋŋ Ghana ka ba mɔr nɔɔr atan' naae, pɛ'ɛs kilabnam atan' piini kani ka o paam bɛ o nwɛ'ɛb wʋsa ni.
english: Agogo was called up to the Ghana squad for the 2008 Africa Cup of Nations.

kusaal: O da pʋ nwɛ' bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb tiim ni bɛ St Augustine's College, amaa ka zi'eni wa' tis sakur la yigilim-yigilim ni.
english: He did not play on the football team at St Augustine's College, but instead represented the school in dancing competitions.

kusaal: Agogo ansib an JJ Rawlings.
english: Agogo was the nephew of JJ Rawlings.

kusaal: Bani da buos o bɛ yʋʋm 2008, Agogo bigis ye o gba'anɛ ye o yʋ'ʋg diib zi'ig yi o bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb la ni amaa, Agogo o pin'ili o mɛŋ niŋgbina wisigir tʋʋma.
