english: During an interview in 2008, Agogo revealed that he planned to open his own restaurant after his football career.

kusaal: Di da anɛ on nɛ o duadibi keŋ UK la ka o baŋ ye o mɔr bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb baŋir onɛ da nwɛ'ɛd nɛ o yidim nɛ o zuanam la.
english: It was not until his family moved to the UK that he discovered his love and talent for football while playing with his siblings and friends.

kusaal: Justin Bonello (dʋ'am 21 Sigir 1971) anɛ Nidkanɛ yit South African ka an onɛ dʋgʋd diib, pian'ad T.V ni, ka maan sini, ka lɛn an gbaŋ sɔbid.
english: Justin Bonello (born 21 June 1971) is a South African cook, television personality, producer, and writer.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Bonello nɛ Durban ka o nɔbigi bɛ Cape Town.
english: Bonello was born in Durban and grew up in the Gardens suburb of Cape Town.

kusaal: O biilim saŋa o da zin'ini kpi'e Breede kɔlʋg nɛ Wild Coast.
english: He also spent some of his childhood on the Breede River and the Wild Coast.

kusaal: O yaab pʋ'a sa'an ka o zamis diib dʋgʋb, onɛ sa'al o ya'am sʋŋ, ka zamis sini maaligi yi o ma kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Jeanne sa'an.
english: He learned to cook through his grandmother, who gave him his first pan, and about filmmaking through his mother Jeanne.

kusaal: O naae o na'asaasɔɔng zamisigi bɛnɛ Cape Peninsula University of Technology.
english: He graduated with a degree in Information Systems, Analysis and Design from Cape Peninsula University of Technology.

kusaal: Bonello da paas diib dʋgʋb nya'ab pʋʋgin yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ ni bɛ BBC diib ni ka li nya'aŋ ka o lɛn paas BBC nidib tʋʋma ni.
english: Bonello's first cooking series Cooked first premiered in 2006 on BBC Food and later BBC Lifestyle.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayi ni, o da pin'il ka sin'iŋi gaad tuoni gɔsid nya'ab kanɛ ka o da maal ka buoli li ye The Ultimate Braai Master la, li nya'aŋ ka "Okuhle Media" sʋ'ʋgʋ li ka nannanna ba buoni li nɛ "Trace Studios".
english: In 2012, he created and began hosting the competition The Ultimate Braai Master, which was later acquired by "Okuhle Media" now "Trace Studios".

kusaal: Bonello gbɛɛnsig zin'ig bɛnɛ Noordhoek on nɛ o pʋ'a Eugenie (née Tancred nɛ ba biis atan'.
english: Bonello lives in Noordhoek with his wife Eugenie (née Tancred) and their three children.

kusaal: On nɛ Peter Gird la'a'si pin'il sini maalig tʋʋma zin'ig yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ, anina ka o an kpɛɛm maal sini nam la ka gaad tuoni gɔs diema si'eba nam mɛn T.V ni, ka ba si'eba an suor kanɛ kpɛn'ɛd Africa, Mɔɔd banɛ tɛɛnd yela, nɛ ti mɔr kpɛmisigi kpɛn'ɛd Iceland tɛŋin.
english: Together with Peter Gird, Bonello co-founded the production company Cooked in Africa Films in 2011, through which he has executive produced and hosted a number of food and travel shows, such as Getaway to Africa, Exploring the Vine, and Around Iceland on Inspiration.

kusaal: Linɛ lɛn paas ya'as, Bonello da pin'il asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ lʋgir kanɛ gɔsid gɔsid kpaadib, o gban'ar da anɛ ye li nyaŋi tis nidib tʋʋma ka sʋŋ ka diib bɛ, ka mɔr tɛŋpʋʋgin dim kuob baŋiri lɛb tɛŋkpɛmisin nɛ sakur nam ni bɛ Cape Town.
english: In addition, Bonello founded the non-profit organisation Neighbourhood Farm, which aims to create jobs and improve food security by bringing urban farming into communities and schools in Cape Town.

kusaal: · Justin Bonello Cooks...
english: Justin Bonello (born 21 June 1971) is a South African cook, television personality, producer, and writer.

kusaal: Kaaseman F.C. anɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb lʋgʋr bɛ Sefwi-kaase linɛ bɛ Ghana kpɛla.
english: Kaaseman F.C. is a Ghanaian football club based in Sefwi-Kaase, Ghana.

kusaal: Asare Lartey onɛ an Prempeh College kpɛɛm, nɛ Owarean bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib linɛ bɛ Orlando kpɛɛm la, nɛ Florida onɛ bɛ United States, ka mɛ tʋm bɛ Kaaseman F.C linɛ Kumasi, Ghana kpɛla la.
english: The club is run by Prempeh College's Mr. Asare Lartey, and the Owarean sports master in Orlando, Florida, United States, which also operates Kaaseman F.C. in Kumasi, Ghana.

kusaal: Kade Constituency bɛnɛ Eastern region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The Kade constituency is in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) nɔba zug yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) during the 2016 election.

kusaal: Ba wadmaan anɛ Kwabena Ohemeng-Tinyase.
english: The member of Parliament for the constituency in 2016 was Kwabena Ohemeng-Tinyase.

kusaal: Ka da di constituency la wadmaan yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: The member of Parliament for the constituency in 2016 was Kwabena Ohemeng-Tinyase.

kusaal: Ofosu Asamoah da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug 4th Republic parliament la.
english: The member of Parliament for the constituency in 2016 was Kwabena Ohemeng-Tinyase.

kusaal: Kalbelia nam anɛ Sage Kanifnath nya'andɔlib, onɛ da nu tibɛ'ɛd nɛ diib laa pɛ'ɛli ka da paam barikir ye o mɔr iku kanɛ na sʋ'ʋg wa'abɛ'ɛd nam nɛ bʋnkɔnbid, venomous snake and animals.
english: Kalbelias belong to the Nath Shaiva sect and are followers of Sage Kanifnath, who according to a legend, drank a bowl of poison and was blessed with control over venomous snakes and animals.

kusaal: Kalbelia nam pʋdig nɛ zin'is buudi ayi, Daliwal nam la nɛ Mewara.
english: Kalbelias are divided into two main groups, the Daliwal and Mewara.

kusaal: Ba mɛ buoni ba ye Sapera nɛ Jogira, Gattiwala nɛ Poogiwara.
english: They are also called Sapera and Jogira, Gattiwala and Poogiwara.

kusaal: Kalbelia nam la bɛdigʋ bɛnɛ Pali district, ka banɛ dɔl ban nya'aŋ bɛ Ajmer, Chittorgarh nɛ Udaipur district.
english: The largest cluster of the Kalbelias is in Pali district, followed by significant other groups in Ajmer, Chittorgarh and Udaipur district.

kusaal: Ban da tiaki maal Wildlife Act of 1972 la, li da yis Kalbelia nam la ba wiigi tʋʋma la ni.
english: Since the enactment of the Wildlife Act of 1972, the Kalbelias have been pushed out of their traditional profession of snake handling.

kusaal: Ba wa'anam nɛ yʋʋma nam la anɛ linɛ ma'adi ba sunf ka an Kalbelias nam la zanbin, banɛ an teŋ la wiigi vɛnlim nɛ ti'asig teŋ la malima ni, nɛ ba tʋʋma Rajasthani nidibin.
english: Their dances and songs are a matter of pride and a marker of identity for the Kalbelias, as they represent the creative adaptation of this community of snake charmers to changing socio-economic conditions and their own role in rural Rajasthani society.

kusaal: Kalbelia yʋʋma anɛ linɛ yit sɔlima kanɛ pa'ani ba buudi malima nɛ Holi saŋa wa'a.
english: Kalbelia songs are based on stories taken from folklore and mythology and special dances are performed during Holi.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga 2010 la ni, UNESCO da kpɛn'ɛs Kalbelia yʋʋma nɛ Rajasthan wa'a la Intangible Heritage List gbaʋŋin.
english: In 2010, the Kalbelia folk songs and dances of Rajasthan were declared a part of its Intangible Heritage List by the UNESCO.

kusaal: Wiigi gban'ab nɛ snake venom kpikpiŋi da aan ba tʋʋm kpɛŋ.
english: Their traditional occupation is catching snakes and trading snake venom.

kusaal: Ba bɛnɛ normadic bɛllim ka an scheduled tribes.
english: They live a nomadic life and belong to the scheduled tribes.

kusaal: Ba na'asid dunduug, cobra la ka pian'adi pa'an ye ba da kʋʋd wa'aban buudii.
english: They revere the cobra and advocate the non-killing of such reptiles.

kusaal: Saŋa wʋsa ni, Kalbelia nam la paam yam si'a local flora nɛ fauna ni, ka mi' sʋŋa ye tivaand anɛ ban'as bɛdigʋ tiim, herbal remedies ka lɛn an linɛ ka ba nigid ka li titti ba ligidi.
english: Over the generations, the Kalbelias acquired a unique understanding of the local flora and fauna, and are aware of herbal remedies for various diseases which, in turn, is an alternative source of income for them.

kusaal: Nananna nwa, performing art, nidib sʋʋgin di'ema aan ba tʋʋm kpɛŋ ka nidib mi' li yɛla India teŋ wʋsa pʋʋgin la'am nɛ katensin.
english: Now performing arts are a major source of income for them and these have received widespread recognition within and outside India.

kusaal: Kalbelias nam la anɛ Cultural Hindus ka pʋ'ʋsid wiigi, snake worship; ba pʋ'ʋsidi Nāga nɛ Manasa, ka ba kassi dabisir an Naga Panchami.
english: This deep-rooted connection to serpents is expressed through the worship of deities like Manasa and the observance of Naga Panchami, a day dedicated to honoring the cobra as a divine entity.

kusaal: Kalbelias nam la mɔri buudi malima gʋngʋn yi Hindus la bɛdigʋ ni.
english: The Kalbelias are Hindus and dedicated followers of the Nath (a Shaiva sub-tradition) tradition, and the Kalbelias center their spiritual life around Lord Shiva and the sacred Nāgas.

kusaal: Kalbelias nam pindi ba kum nɛ yaʋgin ka ka' a yɔn'ɔdi ba (woo Hindus banɛ kpɛlim teŋin la).
english: The Kalbelias are Hindus and dedicated followers of the Nath (a Shaiva sub-tradition) tradition, and the Kalbelias center their spiritual life around Lord Shiva and the sacred Nāgas.

kusaal: Kalbelia wa'a la, rajasthan buudi wa'a ka ba wa'adi linɛ woo buudi malima nɛ, li paasɛ Kalbelia malʋŋin.
english: The Kalbelia dance, folk dance of rajasthan performed as a celebration, is an integral part of Kalbelia culture.

kusaal: ba yɛɛd fuug ka li yʋ'ʋr an angrakhi ka gir bɔbig ka li yʋ'ʋr an adhani, fuug kan ka ba sɔn tingir la buon nɛ lehenga.
english: They wear an upper body cloth called an angrakhi and a headcloth known as the odhani; the lower body cloth is called a lehenga.

kusaal: Dap la nwɛn'ɛdi bʋn-nwɛn'ɛda, woo pungi, ba zaŋi daagi maal ka piebid pɛbisim niŋidi la ka li buon wiigi, dufli la, been, khanjari la – a percussion instrument, yʋʋma lak kanɛ ka ba zanl ka dammid, morchang, khuralio nɛ dholak ka li maan yʋʋma la ka wa-wa'adib la wa'ad.
english: The male participants play musical instruments, such as the pungi, a woodwind instrument traditionally played to capture snakes, the dufli, been, the khanjari - a percussion instrument, morchang, khuralio and the dholak to create the rhythm on which the dancers perform.

kusaal: Ban bɛ di'ema la pʋʋgin la, yʋʋma yʋʋn kennɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ al aka wa'a, dance la mɛ yʋʋn ken tɔ'ɔtɔ.
english: As the performance progresses, the rhythm becomes faster and faster and so does the dance.

kusaal: Dinzug ba teŋ wa'a la nɛ wa'a la fuud la mɔri nwɛnim nɛ wiigi la din.
english: Hence, the dance movements and the costumes of their community bear a resemblance to those of the serpents.

kusaal: Kamini Panther (ka ba dʋa o dabis'pisi da'ar wadisa anaasi yʋʋm tusir kɔbuswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan la) anɛ South Africa onɛ dʋgid diib, ka ki'ad diib niŋid fɔɔtɔ ni pa'an nidib, ka lɛm piand TV nɛ wa'lis ni.
english: Kamini Pather (born 20 April 1983) is a South African chef, food blogger, and television and radio personality.

kusaal: Tʋŋtʋŋ nam piinɛ anu South Africa da si'iŋ India tɛŋdatiʋŋ, ba da dʋa Panther nɛ Mobeni Heights, tɛŋkpiŋkpɛŋ kanɛ bɛ Durban, o dʋadib da an Rajen nɛ Anitha ka ba da nɔbignɛ Glenwood.
english: A fifth-generation South African of South Indian origin, Pather was born in Mobeni Heights, a suburb of Durban to parents Rajen and Anitha and grew up in Glenwood.

kusaal: O mɔr pitʋ ka o yʋʋr an Neelan.
english: She has a younger brother, Neelan.

kusaal: O da kiŋnɛ Durban Girls college ka da kɛŋ tʋɔn lɛm na'ae KwaZulu-Natal University ka di'e gbaŋ kanɛ pa'al ye o mɔya commerce nɛ fʋn na kʋos kʋosidim si'ɛm.
english: She attended Durban Girls' College and went on to graduate with a Bachelor of Commerce in Marketing and Management from the University of KwaZulu-Natal.

kusaal: Panther walis da mɔr 2oceansvibe Radio, Good Hope FM, nɛ Heart 104.9 FM.
english: Pather's radio gigs have included 2oceansvibe Radio, Good Hope FM, and Heart 104.9 FM.

kusaal: On naae sakʋr si'a yiiga la anɛ wiiʋg nɛ dobʋʋlum tolʋŋ sakur ka mɔ' yoga zamisug ni.
english: She holds a diploma from the Red and Yellow Creative School of Business and has a qualification in yoga.

kusaal: On da sɔb Aficionado naae la, Panther da si'iŋi o mɛŋ diib tʋʋma, ka pʋt li yʋ'ʋr Deelishuss, yʋma tusa ayi nɛ anii.
english: After writing for Aficionado, Pather started her own food blog, then titled Deelishuss, in 2008.

kusaal: Yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii, O da la'asi nɛ UCOOK South Africa dim ye ba sʋŋ o diib nam yela, ka da yo'og Füdy, o mɛŋ diib da'aŋ ka nidib na buɔl ka ba mɔr diib kɛŋ tisiba nɛ lo'or.
english: In 2018, she collaborated with South African meal kit service UCOOK and went on to launch Füdy, her own plant-based dark kitchen via UberEats SA.

kusaal: Karatsu Kunchi (唐津くんち; "kunchi" gbin anɛ malʋŋ) anɛ Japanese malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba maan yʋʋm-yʋʋm tempʋkanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Karatsu, Saga Prefecture, bɛ Japan island of Kyūshū.
english: Karatsu Kunchi (唐津くんち; the suffix "kunchi" simply meaning festival) is a Japanese matsuri that takes place annually in November in the city of Karatsu, Saga Prefecture, on Japan's island of Kyūshū.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii (1980) la ni, ba da zaŋ malʋŋ la paas "Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property".
english: In 1980, the festival was designated an "Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property".

english: The event takes place on 2-4 November, when the 3rd is a national holiday in Japan called Culture Day.

kusaal: Dinɛ an malʋŋ tita'ari bɛ Karatsu dabisa kal ni, ka di ɛɛnti kɛ ka nidib yi zin'is kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb nwɛnɛ nidib tusa kɔbiga nɛ pisnu (150,000) keŋ paae nidib tusa kɔbisnu (500,000) tembanɛ gilig la ni ka nɛ' zug ba ɛɛnti tisi bad aba atan ye ba vʋ'ʋs-daba atan vʋ'ʋsim dabisa.
english: It is the major event of the Karatsu calendar, regularly drawing crowds of anywhere between 150,000 and 500,000 people from the surrounding area over the course of the event.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la, dinɛ ka teŋin la Shinto shrine (kpi'e nɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ba su'ad la'ad la gur yʋʋm ya'as la), ka ba maali li ka di yuug yʋma bɛdegʋ nwa; la'abanɛ ka ba mɔri maan nananna la da maalnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piinɛ awai (1819) nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (1876) tensʋk.
english: The event, which is coordinated by the local Shinto shrine (near which the floats are stored during the rest of the year), has been held for several centuries now; the current incarnations of the floats were constructed between 1819 and 1876.

kusaal: Karen Dudley (ba dʋa o nɛ daba anʋ daar yiiga wadig la yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii) South Africa diib dʋgib sɔb, ka sɔbid diib nam yɛla, ka mɔr zin'ig kanɛ ka ba kennɛ dit, O daʋŋ la yʋ'ʋr anɛ Woodstock ka bɛ Cape Town zin'ig kanɛ ka zugdaan kʋdig pʋ'a Michelle Obama da ka'ai wadisa ayʋobɔ la yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne.
english: She is best known for her restaurant, The Kitchen in Woodstock, Cape Town, which was visited by former First Lady Michelle Obama in June 2011.

kusaal: O yʋʋr nam'mi yi CNN nɛ TEDx ka New York Times dim nɛ Guardian dim da buol o bu'os bu'osa.
english: Karen has appeared on CNN and TEDx and has been interviewed by The New York Times and The Guardian.

kusaal: South Africa onɛ sɔbid diib yɛla Andy Fennerl yɛl ye Dudley anɛ "onɛ mɔr baŋir nɛ zɛnvaand dʋgib ka nyaŋidi kɛt ka malisim bɛ lini pʋ malis ni".
english: South African food blogger Andy Fenner has described Dudley as "a genius with vegetables and teasing flavour out of simple things".

kusaal: Yolisa Qunta bɛ Daily Maverick ye o tʋʋma la "teŋ mi li yela" ka di banɛ ka o tid nidib la "pa'al ye li anɛ di paalig ka o paasid linɛ ket ka li an sʋm ka malis hali"
english: Yolisa Qunta of Daily Maverick noted that her work is "driven by community" and that the recipes which she shares with the public "emphasise the texture and flavour of fresh produce and finding the perfect condiments and relishes to compliment."

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaan adʋgigaadtaaba linɛ ka ba bʋon ye mdaʋŋ wada South Africa ka ba ɛnti buoli ba sɔns TV ni la.
english: She has been a guest judge on the reality cooking show My Kitchen Rules South Africa and is often interviewed on national TV.

kusaal: Pin'ilʋgin di da pɛ'ɛsnɛ sankan Kassena-Nankana District yʋʋm 1988 la ni, ka ba yʋ'ʋn pʋdʋg di ya-tuona la zi'el Kassena-Nankana West District bɛ 29 February 2008 yʋʋm ni; ka zi'ikani kpɛlim la an Kassena-Nankana East District, dinɛ ka ba yʋolim kɛ ka di yʋ'ʋn an municipal assembly bɛ yʋʋm 28 June 2012 ka di an Kassena-Nankana Municipal District.
english: Originally it was formerly part of the then-larger Kassena-Nankana District in 1988, until the western part of the district was split off to create Kassena-Nankana West District on 29 February 2008; thus the remaining part has been renamed as Kassena-Nankana East District, which it was later elevated to municipal assembly status on 28 June 2012 to become Kassena-Nankana Municipal District.

kusaal: Municipality la bɛnɛ Upper East Region ya-tuona ka Navrongo an di teoŋpʋtita'ar.
english: The municipality is located in the western part of Upper East Region and has Navrongo as its capital town.

kusaal: Municipality zigisim bɛnɛ wʋʋ 11°10' nɛ 10°3' North pʋʋgʋn nɛ longitude 10°1' West.
english: The municipality lies approximately between latitude 11°10' and 10°3' North and longitude 10°1' West.

kusaal: Municipality la'asɛ nɛ distric nam ayɔpɔi bɛ teŋ yinne ni; ya-datiʋŋ ni anɛ Kassena Nankana West District nɛ Burkina Faso, ka ya-tuon an Kassena Nankana West District, Bolgatanga Municipality, Talensi District nɛ Bongo District, ya-tuon mɛn anɛ Builsa South nɛ Builsa North Districts ma ya-dagɔbʋg an West Mamprusi Municipality (dinɛ bɛ Northern Region)
english: The Municipality is bounded by seven (7) districts and one country; on the North by Kassena Nankana West District and Burkina Faso, on the East by Kassena Nankana West District, Bolgatanga Municipality, Talensi District and Bongo District, on the West by the Builsa South and Builsa North Districts and on the South by West Mamprusi Municipality (in the Northern Region).

kusaal: Kassena Nankana Municipality mɔri bɛllimnam ayi' sɛɛung nɛ ʋʋn, dinɛ mɔr air masses ayi' – North-East Trade winds nɛ South-Westerly's (Tropical Maritime).
english: The climatic conditions of the Kassena Nankana Municipality is characterized by the dry and wet seasons, which are influenced mainly by two (2) air masses – the North-East Trade winds and the South-Westerly's (Tropical Maritime).

kusaal: Harmattan air mass (North-East Trade Winds) yiti anɛ kpi'emis ka an ʋʋnsʋg nwennɛ di yitnɛ Sahara Desert.
english: The harmattan air mass (North-East Trade Winds) is usually dry and dusty as it originates from the Sahara Desert.

kusaal: Dabisir wina tʋdi an wʋʋ 42 °C (kas-kas February nɛ March) ka yʋ'ʋg wina mɛn bɛ tɛŋin wʋʋ 18 °C. Municipality paamid tropical maritime air mass bɛ May nɛ October tensʋk.
english: Day temperatures are high recording 42 °C (especially between February and March) and night temperatures could be as low as 18 °C. The Municipality experiences the tropical maritime air mass between May and October.

kusaal: Zi'ig la mɔri kʋnkʋna bani zi'e ba kɔn' ka ba wa'alim an wʋʋ 300 metres gaad mu'anr bɛn dinɛ bɛ municipal la ya-tuona.
english: The landscape is generally undulating with isolated hills rising up to about 300 metres above sea level in the western parts of the municipality.

kusaal: Kʋnkʋna bama yʋ'ʋra anɛ Fie (280 metres), Busono (350 metres) nɛ Zambao (360 metres) gat mu'anr bɛn.
english: Notably among these hills include Fie (280 metres), Busono (350 metres) and Zambao (360 metres) above sea level.

kusaal: Municipality la teŋ fɛɛgir yiti anɛ ye ku'obibis la yiti pʋbi kpɛn' Sissili River – Asibelika, Afumbeli, Bukpegi nɛ Beeyi.
english: The drainage system of the municipality is constituted mainly around the tributaries of the Sissili River – Asibelika, Afumbeli, Bukpegi and Beeyi.

kusaal: Asibelika River (Tono River) ka ba la'asi di ka ba mɔri ku'od zʋʋd.

kusaal: Yʋʋm pʋʋgʋn saa anɛ wʋʋ 950mm.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusur yinne, kɔbus yuobʋ nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi, 1687 la ni France nid Louis xiv da tʋm Simon de la Loubere Siamese teŋin ye o sɔbi digil linɛ wʋsa k'o nyɛ teŋin la.
english: In 1687, King Louis XIV of France sent a diplomat Simon de la Loubère to record all that he saw in the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

kusaal: Siamese la mɔrɛ di'ema buudi atan': Ka ba buonnɛ ba ye Cone [ ] li anɛ a'a kanɛ ka ba wa'ad ka violin nwɛn'ɛd, la'am nɛ bʋnnwɛn'ɛd sieba vuud.
english: The Siamese have three sorts of Stage Plays: That which they call Cone [khôn] is a figure dance, to the sound of the violin and some other instruments.

kusaal: Di'ema la ka ba buon ye Lacone la anɛ sɛnlʋŋ kanɛ paas nɛ di'ema, li zaŋid nɛ daba atan', ka pin'in bɛkɛɛng kɛrifa anii ti paae yʋ'ʋŋ kɛrifa ayɔpɔi.
english: The Show which they call Lacone is a poem intermix with Epic and Dramatic, which lasts three days, from eight in the morning till seven at night.

kusaal: Siamese Khon wa'wa'adib la fuud, La Loubere da sɔbi digil ye, "[T]hose, banɛ wa'ad Rabam, nɛ Cone, la pid nɛ ba zut, ka lusi ba tiengʋ'or nɛ bʋnlinɛ an woo pepe ka ba zaŋ sanlima maal nɛ,gilded wood, ka lɛɛ yuli ba lɛma baba ka li aan nwɛn woo kuga ka ba zaŋi maal nɛ, ka tisid vɛnlim.
english: Of the attire of Siamese Khôn dancers, La Loubère recorded that, "[T]hose that dance in Rabam, and Cone, have gilded paper-bonnets, high and pointed, like the Mandarins caps of ceremony, but which hang down at the sides below their ears, which are adorned with counterfeit stones, and with two pendants of gilded wood."

kusaal: Yiiga, "Khon" Benguela Kalinin ni anɛ woo pian'ad "Kora" bɛɛ "Khon" kanɛ an bʋn-nwɛn'ɛdir yʋ'ʋr ka ba zaŋ Hindi gbaʋŋi maal nɛ.
english: First, "Khon" in Benguela Kalinin appears in the words "kora" or "Khon" which is the name of a musical instrument made of Hindi leather.

kusaal: Tamil buudi pian'ad la ni, Tamil language "Khon" yinɛ "koli" piank la linɛ pʋ lal nɛ "goli" bɛɛ "golumn" Tamil nii.
english: In the Tamil language "Khon" derives from the word "koll" which is close to "goll" or "golumn" in Tamil.

kusaal: "Khon" Iran ni da yinɛ "zurat khan" pian'adin ka li gbin an ye bʋn linɛ kʋ tun'oe vurigi li tu'orɛ, ka ba mɔri li maan nɛ ba di'ema malima.
english: "Khon" in Iran was derived from the words "zurat khan" which means 'handed-doll' or 'puppet', used in local performances.

kusaal: Khon di'ema la sɔlim nɛ nintiris, epic Ramakien (Thai adaptation of Hindu epic Ramayana), woo Thai literature nɛ di'ema, drama paamid kpɛmisig Indian arts nɛ legend naming la.
english: Khon is based on the tales of the epic Ramakien (Thai adaptation of Indian Hindu epic Ramayana), as Thai literature and drama draws great inspiration from Indian arts and legend.

kusaal: Khon ( )anɛ Thailand dim wa'a buudi.
english: Khon (Thai: โขน, pronounced [kʰǒːn]) is a dance drama genre from Thailand.

kusaal: Pu'ab la'am wa'adi li ka ba buon ye khon phu ying ( )
english: A variation of this genre with female performers is called khon phu ying (โขนผู้หญิง).

kusaal: Khon anɛ Thai dim buudi wa'a kanɛ ka banɛ wa'ad nɛ di'ema dim la'asidi maan.
english: Khon is a Thai traditional dance which combines many arts like dance and drama.

kusaal: Gbana kasɛttʋg pa'al ye Thai di'ema la da na si'iŋ nɛ 17th century la ni.
english: Historical evidence shows that the Thai art of stage plays must have already been highly evolved by the 17th century.

kusaal: Ba yɛl ye Khon wa'a la si'iŋ si'em la yinɛ "Khon piank la ni na.
english: First, "Khon" in Benguela Kalinin appears in the words "kora" or "Khon" which is the name of a musical instrument made of Hindi leather.

kusaal: Tamil pian' bama nwa yɛttɛ fuud ka ba pin'ini yɛɛd zugin nɛ ti paae nɔbbibisin woo lin an si'em nɛ khon malima fuud nɛ li la'ad yɛɛbin.
english: These Tamil words relate to dressing or decorating the body from head to toe as in the use of Khon costumes.

kusaal: Dap ma'aa da tun'oe di'em Khon Ramakien, originally could be performen by men only Pu'ab da anɛ maliaknam nɛ teŋgbana.
english: Khon Ramakien originally could be performed by men only.

kusaal: La'abanɛ ka ba zaŋi lusi ba nindaas la bɛdigʋ ye pʋ vɛnl nɛ baa bi'elaa saa ka kɛt ka ba nwɛn nɛ bʋngba'ada bɛɛ sibɛ'ɛdnam bɛɛ nimbɛ'ɛdnam.
english: Most of their masks are hideous, and represent either monstrous Beasts, or kinds of Devils.

kusaal: Panicoideae pʋʋgin la, soogum (great millet) paas nɛ Andropogoneae buudi ni, amaa ka pearl millet, proso, foxtail, fonio, little millet, sawa, Japanese barnyard millet nɛ kodo paas Paniceae buudi ni.
english: Proso millet is a relative of foxtail millet, pearl millet, maize, and sorghum within the grass subfamily Panicoideae.

kusaal: wʋʋ dinɛ ka ba buon ye Finger millet, proso millet, nɛ foxtail millet la mɛ anɛ ki banɛ an' nimʋa .
english: Proso millet is a relative of foxtail millet, pearl millet, maize, and sorghum within the grass subfamily Panicoideae.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' ni (1753), Carl Linnaeus da pʋd ki kanɛ buon foxtail millet la ye Panicum italicum.
english: Panicum miliaceum is a grain crop with many common names, including proso millet, broomcorn millet, common millet, hog millet, Kashfi millet, red millet, and white millet.

english: Panicum miliaceum is a grain crop with many common names, including proso millet, broomcorn millet, common millet, hog millet, Kashfi millet, red millet, and white millet.

kusaal: Banɛ sʋ'ʋe li anɛ Kumasi Muslim community ka ba nɔki li pʋdi dɔlis King Faisal of Saudi Arabia, Ba nya'adi bɛ Division One League, football league kanɛ paas ayi Ghana.
english: Owned by Kumasi's Muslim community and named after King Faisal of Saudi Arabia, the Babes compete in Division One League, the second tier football league in Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ da zi'eni ba nɔba zug 2006 FIFA World Cup da anɛ Habib Mohamed.
english: They were represented at the 2006 FIFA World Cup by left-back Habib Mohamed.

kusaal: King Solomon F.C. anɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib tiim kanɛ bɛ Nkawkaw ka nwɛ'ɛdi bɛ 3B Zone dinɛ bɛ Ghana Division One League ni la.
english: King Solomon F.C. is a Ghanaian professional football team based in Nkawkaw that plays in the 3B Zone of the Ghana Division One League.

kusaal: Zone 3B mɔrnɛ tiimnam ayɔpɔi ka ba nya'ad, ba bɛnɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlʋm zin'isieba nɛ Volta Region dinɛ bɛ Ghana.
english: Zone 3B has seven competing teams from the part of the Greater Accra Region and the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kingsley Aboagye Gyedu (ba da du'a o nɛ sapal nwadig 29, 1969) anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an politis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan kʋdʋg.O anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nid, ka mɛ lɛn an minista nya'andɔl kʋdʋg bɛ alaafi lʋgir la nɛ regional minista nya'andɔl kʋdʋg bɛ Western North Region Ghana.
english: Kingsley Aboagye Gyedu (born November 29, 1969) is a Ghanaian politician and a former Member of Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ teŋpʋʋg kanɛ bɛ Sefwi Anhiawuso n bɛ western region Ghana nwa la.
english: He hails from the town of Sefwi Anhiawuso in the western region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr MBA bɛ finance n yit University of Leister kanɛ bɛ UK la, nɛ o CA bɛ Ghana nɛ o BA bɛ economics bɛ University of Ghana, Legon.
english: He holds an MBA in finance from the University of Leister in the UK, and earned his CA in Ghana and his BA in economics at University of Ghana, Legon.

kusaal: Gyedu da anɛ financial analyst bɛ USAID nɛ yʋʋm 2005, nɛ Finance Manager bɛ Bat West Africa Area yit yʋʋm 2005 ti paae yʋʋm 2007 nɛ kɛɛm bɛ Kingsag Associates Limited yit yʋʋm 2007 ti paae yʋʋm 2012 la mi.
english: Gyedu was a financial analyst at USAID in 2005, the Finance Manager at Bat West Africa Area from 2005 to 2007 and the executive director at Kingsag Associates Limited from 2007 to 2012.

kusaal: Gyedu anɛ kristo biig ka an Methodist.
english: Gyedu identifies as a Christian and a Methodist.

kusaal: Gyedu da mɔri vɔɔt kal 33,145 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 51.80% yi nidib banɛ vɔɔt la ni, nɛ o di lieb wadmaan tis ai Bibiani-Anwiaso-Bekwai constituency n bɛ Western Region Ghana nwa .
english: Gyedu obtained 33,145 votes which represents 51.80% of the total valid votes cast, and thus won the seat of Bibiani-Anwiaso-Bekwai constituency of the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba du'a Gyedu nɛ sapal nwadig 29, 1969.
english: Gyedu was born on November 29, 1969.

kusaal: Ba daa gaŋ o paas land nɛ forestry committee nɛ public accounts committee.
english: He was appointed to join the land and forestry committee and public accounts committee.

kusaal: O mɔr pu'a nɛ biis anaasi.
english: He is married with five children.

kusaal: Du'ata Kingsley Nyarko anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tis Kwadaso constituency bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: Dr. Kingsley Nyarko is a Ghanaian politician and a member of Eighth parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing Kwadaso constituency within the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ gbansɔbidi tis National Accreditation Board (NAB) of Ghana.
english: He is also the secretary of the National Accreditation Board (Ghana).

kusaal: Ba da du'a Nyarko nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan Nwadisa ayuobʋ dabpiiga daar (10 June 1973) o yinɛ Obo Kwahu bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Nyarko was born on 10 June 1973 and hails from Obo Kwahu in the Eastern Region, (Ghana).

kusaal: O da maali o Common entrance yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1986) la ni, ka maali o Ordinary level yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) la ni, o Advance level yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1997) ka maali o Teacher Certificate yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la ni (1995).
english: He had his Common entrance in 1986, his Ordinary level in 1992, his Advance level in 1997 and his Teacher Certificate in 1995.

kusaal: O da tɔlis tuoni maal o Bachelors in Education in Psychology yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2000), ka maali o Masters in Educational psychology/ Differential psychology yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005) nɛ Ph D in Educational psychology yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008).
english: He gained his Bachelor in Education in Psychology in 2000, his Masters in Educational Psychology/ Differential Psychology in 2005, and his Ph D in Educational Psychology in 2008.

kusaal: Nyarko da anɛ zugdaan (headmaster) tis Mile 18 Junior High School.
english: Nyarko was the headmaster for the Mile 18 Junior High School.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'ani Ejisuman Senior High School.
english: He was also a tutor at the Ejisuman Senior High School.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ African Representative and Marketing specialist tis Voicecash, ka an Executive Director tis Danquah Institute.
english: He also was the African Representative and Marketing Specialist for Voicecash.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Senior Lecturer University of Ghana.
english: He was a Senior Lecturer at the University of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn an Executive Secretary tis National Accreditation Board.
english: He was also the Executive Secretary for the National Accreditation Board.

kusaal: Nyarko paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Kwadaso Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: Nyarko is a member of the 8th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana representing the Kwadaso Constituency.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi (61,772) dinɛ an pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (87.51%).
english: He won the seat after getting 61,772 votes making 87.51% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Nyarko paas la'askanɛ gɔsid nɔŋ sier suoya yɛla (Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee) ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la (Education Committee).
english: Nyarko is member of the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee and also the member of the Education Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, Nwadis piiga la nii, October 2021, Nyarko da nɔk sakur fuud tusir yinne (1,000 pieces of school uniforms) tis Nwamase M/A, Denkyemuoso M/A, Asuoyeboah M/A, Kwadaso M/A, Beposo M/A Block A, and B, Prempeh Experimental M/A Block A, B, and C nɛ Central Agric Station Primary bɛ Kwadaso Constituency la.
english: In October 2021, Nyarko donated about 1,000 pieces of school uniforms to Nwamase M/A, Denkyemuoso M/A, Asuoyeboah M/A, Kwadaso M/A, Beposo M/A Block A, and B, Prempeh Experimental M/A Block A, B, and C and also Central Agric Station Primary in the Kwadaso Constituency.

kusaal: O paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party ni.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O pɔlitiks yɛla pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni (2020) on da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg zug nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la.
english: His political career began in 2020 when he contested the 2020 Ghanaian general elections on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ye o an Wadmaani tis Kwadaso constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: He was elected as a member of parliament for the Kwadaso constituency in the 2020 December parliamentary elections.

kusaal: Nyarko anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Nyarko is a Christian.

kusaal: Kintampo yʋ'ʋn anɛ municipal lɛbid ya-tuon 2004 la.
english: It became the capital of Kintampo North Municipal in 2004.

kusaal: Teŋ la mɛ mɔr " Senior High School" dinɛ bɛ Kyeremankoma la.
english: Kintampo also has Senior High Schools (KINSS) which is located at Kyeremankoma, has participated in the National Science Quiz on numerous occasions.

kusaal: Alaafi koligi dinɛ ka ba buol ye " College of Health and Well - being (COHW )" la bɛ teŋin la.
english: There is a College of Health, The Kintampo College of Health and Well-being (CoHK) in the town, which is proposed to become a full fledge University.

kusaal: Bono nɛ Mo anɛ buudbanɛ ya'ad bɛɛ tʋn' taaba.
english: The main ethnicity of Kintampo are the Bono people.

kusaal: Kintampo United anɛ Ghanaian professional football team linɛ bɛ Bono East Region ka ba nwɛn'ɛdi bɛ nɛ 1B Zone Ghana Division One League ni.
english: Kintampo United is a Ghanaian professional football team based in the Bono East Region that plays in the 1B Zone of the Ghana Division One League.

kusaal: Zone 1A mɔr teams ayɔpɔi ka ba nya'ad onɛ na di ya'an, ba si'eba yitnɛ Ashanti Region, Bono Region, Ahafo Region nɛ Northern Regions nam atan' banɛ bɛ Ghana la.
english: Zone 1A has seven competing teams from the part of the Ashanti Region, Bono Region, Ahafo Region and the three Northern Regions of Ghana.

kusaal: Kiran Jethwa anɛ onɛ ka ba da dʋ'a bɛ August 22, 1976, bɛ Nairobi, ka o an Kenya nid kanɛ tʋm sinni tʋʋma, kuosid diib ka lɛn kpiisid ya'as.
english: Kiran Jethwa born August 22, 1976, in Nairobi, is a Kenyan-born celebrity chef, restaurateur, and entrepreneur.

kusaal: Onɛ da gɔsid sɔnskanɛ ka ba maan bɛ tiivi ni ka ba buoni di ye, Tales From The Bush Larder dinɛ sɔnsid diib banɛ ka ba maan ka di pa'an Africa sʋ'ʋlʋm dim malima amn si'em.
english: He is the host and presenter of the TV show, Tales From The Bush Larder which focuses on the culinary culture of Africa. Since 2016, Jethwa has co-presented Food Unwrapped on Channel 4.

kusaal: Jethwa's saam, Batuk, yinɛ Hindu Indian (Gujarati) buudi, ka o ma, Clare, lɛɛ yi British buudi ni.
english: Jethwa's father, Batuk, is of Hindu Indian (Gujarati) ethnic origin, while his mother, Clare, has British ancestry.

kusaal: O da bɛnɛ Kenya saŋa pamm, ka dinzug ka o da naae sakur bɛ Manchester, United Kingdom zamis tʋʋmsʋma nɛ diib kuosʋg yɛla.
english: Having lived most of his life in Kenya, he completed his education in Manchester, United Kingdom in the arena of hospitality management.

kusaal: On da naae sakur la, o da nyaŋi gilig dunia wʋsa; Europe, USA, Africa, Southeast Asia, South & Central America, nɛ Australia maligim paam baŋir bɛdigʋ.
english: Following the completion of his education, he travelled globally in Europe, the USA, Africa, Southeast Asia, South & Central America, and Australia for further experience.

kusaal: Jethwa's dʋgʋt disieba da anɛ dibanɛ bɛ Africa, Europe, nɛ India, ka ba da lɛn buon o ye Afro-Mediterranean fusion din da dɛndig nɛ Indian diib la zug.
english: Jethwa's cooking influences include African, European, and Indian, and has been described as Afro-Mediterranean fusion with an Indian influence.

kusaal: Jethwa anɛ onɛ gɔsid ka ba sɔnsid tiivi ni, onɛ mɔɔn labaya bɛ tiivi ni, ka lɛn an onɛ da di ya'an piini yi diib dʋgʋb ni, Tales from the Bush Larder, ka da lɛm pin'ili sɔns saaŋ kanɛ an Fearless Chef.
english: Jethwa is the producer, presenter, and host of the award-winning cooking series, Tales from the Bush Larder, and also started a new show Fearless Chef.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011), Jethwa mɛ lɛn anɛ onɛ sʋ'ʋe diib kuosʋg zin'ikanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Seven Restaurants, diib kuosʋg zin'itita'akanɛ bɛ Nairobi.
english: Since 2011, Jethwa has also been the chef and owner of Seven Restaurants, a premier Nairobi restaurant company.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la saŋa, o da paas Jimmy Doherty, Kate Quilton, nɛ Matt Tebbutt ka ba sɔnsid bɛ Food Unwrapped bɛ Channel 4 tiivi ni.
english: Since 2016, he has co-presented Food Unwrapped on Channel 4 alongside Jimmy Doherty, Kate Quilton, and Matt Tebbutt.

kusaal: Jethwa anɛ nimbanɛ kad saria la yinne bɛ The Great Kenyan Bake Off, Kenya dim da maan dinɛ yʋ'ʋri buon ye The Great British Bake Off bɛ KTN Home.
english: Jethwa is one of the judges on The Great Kenyan Bake Off, the Kenyan version of The Great British Bake Off on KTN Home.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi (2022) la saŋa, Jethwa ɛɛnti gɔsid ka ba sɔnsid Chefs vs.
english: Since 2022, Jethwa has been the host of Chefs vs. Wild on Hulu.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) keŋ paae nananna, Jethwa paasi sɔnsid Food Unwrapped bɛ Channel 4 ni.
english: He is the host and presenter of the TV show, Tales From The Bush Larder which focuses on the culinary culture of Africa. Since 2016, Jethwa has co-presented Food Unwrapped on Channel 4.

kusaal: Klapa anɛ yʋʋma buudi kanɛ ka ba pʋ nwɛn'ɛd bʋn-nwɛn'ɛda,a cappella yʋʋma ka yinɛ Dalmatia.
english: Klapa music is a form of traditional a cappella singing with origins in Dalmatia, Croatia.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi, 2012 la ni, klapa da kpɛn'ɛ UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity gbaʋŋin.
english: In 2012 klapa was inscribed in UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Thes fetival of the Dalmatian Klapas Omiš ni anɛ malima kanɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr yi hali ka li bɛllim yʋʋg klapa yʋʋma, music ni.
english: The Festival of the Dalmatian Klapas in Omiš is the best known music festival and has a long tradition in Klapa music.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan' 2013 la ni,Croatia da gaŋ klapa la'asg yinne ka li zi'en teŋ la nɔba zug, represent the country Eurovision Song Contest 2013 ni..
english: In 2013, Croatia chose a klapa group to represent the country at the Eurovision Song Contest 2013.

kusaal: klapa la'asig la yʋ'ʋr da buon nɛ Klapa s Mora, ka kpɛn'ɛb an "Mižerja".
english: The klapa group was called Klapa s Mora, with the entry "Mižerja".

kusaal: Klapa s Mora anɛ " super klapa ensemble" nɛ banɛ di'emid la, nidiba ayuobʋ ka Maestro mojmir Čačija gaŋi yi klapa la'asig nama anu ni, ayi na yi Kampanel, ka yin-yin na yi Sinj, Crikvenika, Šibenik nɛ Grdelin.
english: Klapa s Mora is a "super klapa ensemble" of six performers chosen by Maestro Mojmir Čačija from five existing klapa groups, namely two from Kampanel, and one each from Sinj, Crikvenica, Šibenik and Grdelin.

kusaal: klapa pian'ak la gbin anɛ "zuanam la'asʋg" ka si'iŋ nɛ littoral pʋ'ʋsim yir yʋʋma ni, littoral church singing.
english: The word klapa translates as "a group of friends" and traces its roots to littoral church singing.

kusaal: Motifs la malima anɛ nɔŋilim wɔ'ɔgir, wine (grapes), teŋgbaʋŋ, (teŋdu'adir) nɛ atɛʋk.
english: The motifs in general celebrate love, wine (grapes), country (homeland) and sea.

kusaal: Klpa la'asig la anɛ yiiga tenor, tenor kanɛ paas ayi, baritone, nɛ bass kʋkɔyanam.
english: A klapa group consists of a first tenor, a second tenor, a baritone, and a bass.

kusaal: Lin an cappella yʋʋma laa, malima tita'ar ni, bʋn-nwɛn'ɛda woo guiter nɛ mandolin (instruments similar in appearance and sound to tamburitzas).
english: Although klapa is a cappella music, on occasion it is possible to add a gentle guitar and a mandolin (instrument similar in appearance and sound to tamburitzas).

kusaal: Klapa malima la nan kpɛm bɛ hali, ka ba maan nɛ li yʋʋm paala ka maan nɛ li malima, with new songs composed and festivals held.
english: The klapa tradition is still very much alive, with new songs composed and festivals held.

kusaal: Kobla Mensah Wisdom Woyome anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani bɛ Ghana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni an Wadmaani tis South Tongu bɛ Volta Region la.
english: Kobla Mensah Wisdom Woyome (born 21 September 1971) is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the South Tongu in the Volta Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Dabala tembil kanɛ bɛ South Tongu District Volta Region, Ghana la.
english: He hails from Dabala a town in the South Tongu District of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Woyome da naae nɛ Presbyterian Boys' Secondary School ka naae o Sixth Form Science College, Legon.
english: Woyome is a graduate of the Presbyterian Boys' Secondary School and Sixth Form Science College, Legon.

kusaal: Woyome da maali o Bachelors of Science degree in Computer Science and Statistics nɛ University of Ghana, Legon yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1997) la ni.
english: Woyome completed his Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science and Statistics at the University of Ghana, Legon, in 1997.

kusaal: O da lɛn maali o postgraduate diploma in business administration, Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).
english: He also had his postgraduate diploma in business administration at the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).

kusaal: O da lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid tɛɛns kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb yɛla, (Foreign Affairs Committee) nɛ Wadmaanib yin suoya dɔlisʋg.
english: He was also a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee and Standing Order committee.

kusaal: Kobla Mensah Wisdom Woyome anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Action Chapel International.
english: Woyome identifies as a Christian and is a member of Action Chapel International.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Woyome nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne Nwadisa awai la dabpisi nɛ yinne daar (21 senlʋŋ nwadig 1971).
english: Woyome was born on 21 September 1971.

kusaal: Kobla Mensah da anɛ chief executive officer tis Stewise group of companies din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2009) ken paae on da lieb Wadmaani (MP) tis South Tongu sʋ'ʋlim dim la.
english: Woyome was the chief executive officer of the Stewise group of companies from 2009 until he became the MP for South Tongu.

kusaal: O mɔr pu'a nɛ biisa atan'.
english: He is married with three children.

kusaal: Kobina Tahir Hammond anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Kobina Tahir Hammond (born 16 June 1960), known as K.T. Hammond, is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Hammond pin'li o sakuri n bɛ Adisadel College la ni.
english: Hammond had his high school education at Adisadel College.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ University of Ghana naae ka di'e digirii kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Law nɛ Political Science la.
english: He holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in Law and Political Science from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ da keŋ Gray's Inn sakur la ni linɛ bɛ London UK la n zamis wada (Law) yɛla yυma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ yinne la ni.
english: He is also a product of Holborn Law School, London, UK.

kusaal: O da paam Vɔt wυυ bam 10,306 n yi kanl la wυsa ni linɛ da an 19,407 la.
english: He was elected with 10,306 votes out of 19,407 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 54.4%.
english: This was equivalent to 54.4% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Onɛ Theresa Mensah Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid, Nana Yaw Frimpong anɛ an People's National Convention la nid, Kwame Amoh onɛ an Convention People's Party la nid, Peter Kofi Essilfie onɛ an National Reformed Party nɛ Prince Lawrence United Ghana Movement onɛ banɛ da nya'a ka o di ka basi ba, ba da mɔri 7,230, 1,001, 241, 92 nɛ 61 kɔbiga pυυginɛ ba paamnɛ 38.2%, 5.3%, 1.3%, 0.5% and 0.3% vɔt.
english: He was elected over Theresa Mensah of the National Democratic Congress, Nana Yaw Frimpong of the People's National Convention, Kwame Amoh of the Convention People's Party, Peter Kofi Essilfie of the National Reformed Party and Prince Lawrence of the United Ghana Movement.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 62.9% vɔt Seidu S. Adams onɛ an Peoples' National Convention nidi da nya'and ka o di ka bas o.
english: He was elected over Seidu S. Adams of the Peoples' National Convention and Reverend Evans Amankwa of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pυυgin ban da paam vɔt si'a anɛ 37.59%, 5.43% and 1.28%.
english: These obtained 37.59%, 5.43% and 1.28% respectively of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas atan', anaasi, anu, ayuobʋ, ayɔpɔi, nɛ anii la ti Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni n tis Adansi-Asokwa linɛ bɛ Gaana Ashanti Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: In the year 2000, Hammond won the general elections as the member of parliament for the Adansi-Asokwa constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Asokwa tempʋʋg linɛ bɛ Ghana Kumasi sυ'υlυm la.
english: He hails from Asokwa, a town in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Hammond anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Hammond was a member of the Finance Committee, Mines and Energy Committee as well as the Local Government and Rural Development Committee of the eighth Parliament of the 4th Republic.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Adansi-Asokwa sυ'υlυm la.
english: In the year 2000, Hammond won the general elections as the member of parliament for the Adansi-Asokwa constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa la ni ka ba da vɔt ka Hammond di Adansi-Asokwa linɛ bɛ Gaana Ashanti Region sυ'υlυm wadmaanib kuk la.
english: Hammond was elected as the member of parliament for the Adansi-Asokwa constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana for the second time in the 2004 elections.

kusaal: Hammond da di Adansi-Asokwa linɛ bɛ Gaana wadmaanib kυk la nɔɔra yi Ashanti Region sυ'υlυm la yυυma tusa yi nɛ anaasi vɔt kanɛ da maal la.
english: Hammond was elected as the member of parliament for the Adansi-Asokwa constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana for the second time in the 2004 elections.

kusaal: O sυ'υlυm da paas Wabυg wadmaanid bam piistan' nɛ anaasi n yi kanl la wυsa linɛ da an piistan' nɛ awai n bɛ Ashanti Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: His constituency was part of the 34 parliamentary seats out of 39 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Onɛ Alhaji Abdul-Lateef Madjoub onɛ da an.
english: He was elected over Alhaji Abdul-Lateef Madjoub of the National Democratic Congress, Amoako Anaafi of Democratic Freedom Party and Owusu-Boamah Francis of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la nid nɛ Amoako Anaafi onɛ an Democratic Freedom Party nid la ka on nɛ ban da nya'a ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over Alhaji Abdul-Lateef Madjoub of the National Democratic Congress, Amoako Anaafi of Democratic Freedom Party and Owusu-Boamah Francis of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Hammond anɛ mor.
english: Hammond is an Ahmadiya Muslim.

kusaal: O anɛ Ahmadiya moom la nid.
english: Hammond is an Ahmadiya Muslim.

kusaal: O da paamɛ vɔt bam 15,176 n yi vɔt la kanl wυsa linɛ da 24,112.
english: He was elected with 15,176 votes out of 24,112 total valid votes cast equivalent to 62.9% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Kofi Iddie Adams (dʋ'anɛ 2 May 1975) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: Kofi Iddie Adams (born 2 May 1975) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Buem Constituency bɛ Oti region la sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: He was elected a member of Parliament for the Buem Constituency in the Oti region in 2020, and re-elected for the same constituency in 2024.

kusaal: O anɛ National Organizer kʋdʋg tis Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress.
english: He is a former National Organizer for the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Teteman, tenkanɛ bɛ Jasikan District bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: He comes from Teteman, a town in the Jasikan District in the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr Bachelor of Science degree in Zoology with emphasis on Epidemiology of Parasitic Diseases.
english: He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Zoology with emphasis on Epidemiology of Parasitic Diseases from the University of Ghana in 2001.

kusaal: Adams da anɛ pa'ani bɛ Adisadel College.
english: Adams served as a tutor at Adisadel College.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da lɛn an Spokesperson And Director Of Public Affairs tis Flt Lt.
english: He later served as the Spokesperson And Director Of Public Affairs for Flt Lt. Jerry John Rawlings (Rtd), a former President Of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi Nwadis piinɛ ayi la nii (December 2014), ba da vɔɔt o ye o lieb National Organizer tis Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Executive elections.
english: In December 2014, he was elected as National Organizer for the party in the National Executive elections.

kusaal: Wa'ae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la, ba da gaŋ o ye o an tuon gat tis nidib piinɛ anu (15) banɛ ka ba da gaansi ba ye ba gɔs pɔlitiks la yɛla, nɛ ninsieba nwɛnɛ Joyce Bawah Mogtari, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Daniel Ohene Agyekum, Dan Abodakpi, Samuel Ofosu-Ampofo wʋsa da paas la'asʋg la ni ka Johnson Asiedu Nketia an ba kʋkdaan.
english: In the run off to the 2016 elections, he was selected as the campaign coordinator of the NDC's 15-member national campaign team, along with others such Joyce Bawah Mogtari, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Daniel Ohene Agyekum, Dan Abodakpi, Samuel Ofosu-Ampofo all serving as members and Johnson Asiedu Nketia as chairman.

kusaal: Adams da paam vɔɔt kɔbistan nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (388) ka yis onɛ pʋn zin'i kʋk la zug la, Daniel Kosi Ashaimah onɛ da paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnii (280).
english: Adams secured 388 votes to unseat incumbent member of parliament Daniel Kosi Ashaimah who polled 280 votes.

kusaal: Banɛ kpɛlim la Ibrahim Adams Muniru nɛ Daniel Adeapena da paam piswai (95) nɛ awai (9).
english: The others Ibrahim Adams Muniru and Daniel Adeapena polled 95 and nine votes respectively.

kusaal: O da nyɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anii, kɔbisnu nɛ pisi nɛ anii (18,528) dinɛ an pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne du'al pisnii nɛ anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (71.84%) ka onɛ ti'al o la, Lawrence Kwami Aziale ka an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la paam vɔɔt tusa ayuobʋ, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnaasi nɛ atan (6,843) dinɛ an pisi nɛ ayuobʋ du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (26.5%).
english: In December 2020, Adams won the Buem Constituency, by getting 18,528 votes representing 71.84% against his closest contender Lawrence Kwami Aziale of the New Patriotic Party who had 6,843 votes representing 26.5%.

kusaal: O paas la'asbanɛ gɔsid Public Accounts Committee nɛ Defence and Interior Committee bɛ Wadmaanib yin la.
english: During his first term as MP Adams served as a member on the Public Accounts Committee and the Defence and Interior Committee of Parliament.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Kofi Iddie Adams nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu Nwadisa anu la daba ayi daar (2 May 1975).
english: Kofi Iddie Adams was born on 2 May 1975.

kusaal: Jerry John Rawlings (Rtd), Pirɛsidɛn kʋdʋgʋ tis Ghana.
english: He later served as the Spokesperson And Director Of Public Affairs for Flt Lt. Jerry John Rawlings (Rtd), a former President Of Ghana.

kusaal: Adams da anɛ gbansɔbid nya'adɔli tis Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress.
english: Adams has served as deputy General Secretary in the past for the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Adams da di Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress vɔɔtʋg la Buem Constituency ni gur yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020).
english: Adams won the parliamentary bid to represent the National Democratic Congress for the Buem Constituency ahead of the 2020 elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi (December 2020), Adams da di Buem Constituency kʋk la.
english: In December 2020, Adams won the Buem Constituency, by getting 18,528 votes representing 71.84% against his closest contender Lawrence Kwami Aziale of the New Patriotic Party who had 6,843 votes representing 26.5%.

kusaal: Adams da paam suori kpɛn' Wadmaan yin la tis Buem Constituency bɛ Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la ni Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2021).
english: In December 2020, Adams won the Buem Constituency, by getting 18,528 votes representing 71.84% against his closest contender Lawrence Kwami Aziale of the New Patriotic Party who had 6,843 votes representing 26.5%.

kusaal: Adams anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Adams is a Christian.

kusaal: Kofi Ahenkorah Marfo anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paasi Gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la, Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Kofi Ahenkorah Marfo is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Achiase Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Onɛ an kʋkdaani tis Metro Mass Transit Limited.
english: He is currently the Board Chairman for the Metro Mass Transit Limited.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Marfo nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyubʋ nɛ anii Nwadisa anaasi la dabpisinɛ ayuobʋ daar, 26 April 1968.
english: Marfo was born on 26 April 1968 and hails from Akim Bieni in the Eastern region.

kusaal: O da naae o Junior Secondary School Certificate nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981) la ni ka naae o GCE O level yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1986) la ni.
english: He completed his Junior Secondary School Certificate in 1981 and his GCE O level in 1986.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ ka o maal Proficiency Certificate in custom house agency yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2000) ka maali o Executive certificate yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) la ni.
english: He later had his Proficiency Certificate in custom house agency in 2000 and his Executive certificate in 2013.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ maali o Executive Masters yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014) la ni.
english: He further had his Executive Masters in 2014.

kusaal: Marfo da anɛ kpɛɛm tita'ar (Managing Director) tis KAM-G Services Limited nɛ KAMPHA Logistics Limited.
english: Marfo was the Managing Director of KAM-G Services Limited and KAMPHA Logistics Limited.

kusaal: Marfo anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (NPP) la nid ka an Wadmaani tis Achiase Constituency bɛ Eastern region.
english: Marfo is a member of NPP and currently the MP for the Achiase Constituency in the Eastern region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la nii, o da di kʋk la ka di yinɛ on da paam vɔɔtnam tusa piinɛ anaasi, kɔbis yɔpɔi nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ (14,796) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne du'al piinɛ ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (61.16%) ka Ma'asim tiig NDC nid la Kwasi Akyem Apea-Kubi paam vɔɔtnam tusa awai, kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi (9,154) dinɛ anpistan nɛ ayɔpʋi du'al pisnii nɛ anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (37.84%) ka GUM nid la, Christiana Yeboah paam vɔɔtnam kɔbisyi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ atan (243) dinɛ an yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1%) la.
english: In the 2020 Ghana general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 14,796 votes making 61.16% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Kwasi Akyem Apea-Kubi had 9,154 votes making 37.84% of the total votes cast and the GUM parliamentary candidate Christiana Yeboah had 243 votes making 1% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Marfo paas la'askanɛ an Privileges committee ka lɛm paas la'askanɛ gɔsid suor nɛ lɔbanɛ ziid la'ad la yɛla.
english: Marfo is a member of the Privileges committee and also a member of Roads and Transport Committee.

kusaal: Marfo da nɔk masinbanɛ ka ti buon ye hair dryer la ban piinɛ ayuobʋ, lɔpaala ayi (2 new buses), teelanam pisyɔpɔi (70 new sewing machines) nɛ ligidi Gaana siidi tusa piiga (10,000 Ghana cedis) sʋŋ sakur biis pisi (20 students) banɛ bɛ sakur titada ni Achiase sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Marfo presented 16 hair dryers, 2 new buses, 70 new sewing machines and an amount of 10,000 Ghana cedis as a form of scholarship to 20 students at the tertiary level in Achiase.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Achiase Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Easthern Region la.
english: Kofi Ahenkorah Marfo is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Achiase Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Akim Bieni bɛ Eastern Region la.
english: Marfo was born on 26 April 1968 and hails from Akim Bieni in the Eastern region.

kusaal: Kofi Amankwa-Manu anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) la ni.
english: Kofi Amankwa-Manu (born 11 April 1969) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Atwima-Kwanwoma Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Gaana.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Atwima-Kwanwoma Constituency in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Amankwa-Manu nɛyʋʋm tusir, kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai Nwadisa anaasi la dabpiinɛ yinne daar (11 April 1969), o yinɛ Atwima Foase bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlim, Gaana la.
english: Amankwa-Manu was born on 11 April 1969 and hails from Atwima Foase in the Ashanti region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o Ordinary Level nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (1989) ka maali o Advanced level yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswa nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991).
english: He gained his Ordinary-level qualifications in 1989 and his Advanced levels in 1991.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maal BSci in Banking and Finance yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) ni nɛ o LLB yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu la ni (2015).
english: He further had his BSci in Banking and Finance in 2012 and his LLB in 2015.

kusaal: Amankwa-Manu da anɛ Head of Impact Assessment Unit pirɛsidɛn Nana Akufo-Addo ɔfisin on da nan kpɛn'ɛ o yiiga yʋma anaasi an Gaana pirɛsidɛn la.
english: Amankwa-Manu served in the office of the president as the Head of Impact Assessment Unit during the first term of President Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: O da anɛ research assistant Fonaa Institute.
english: He was the research assistant Fonaa Institute.

kusaal: Ka lɛn an CEO tis Waltons Limited.
english: He was also the CEO of the Waltons Limited.

kusaal: On da ti'ebidi gur yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la, Amankwa-Manu da nya' nɛ o Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nidib taaba (NPP) Atwima-Kwanwoma Constituency sʋ'ʋlimin.
english: Ahead of the 2020 Ghanaian general election, Amankwa-Manu entered the race for the parliamentary candidate in the NPP primaries in the Atwima-Kwanwoma Constituency.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayuobʋ la nii (June 2020) o da diya ka basi o Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg banɛ nya' nɛ o la n bɛ Atwima-Kwanwoma Constituency sʋ'ʋlim la, on da di ka bas onɛ pʋn dɛŋim an Wadmaan nɔɔr atan la, Kojo Appiah Kubi, da da bɛ Wadmaanib yin la din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai la yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la.
english: In June 2020, he won the primaries for the Atwima-Kwanwoma constituency after defeating incumbent member of parliament (MP) Kojo Appiah-Kubi, who had served as MP for three terms and had been in parliament since January 2009.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tisi Amankwa-Manu ka o lieb Wadmaani tis Atwima-Kwanwoma yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Nwadis piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋgin la.ba da yina yɛl nyain ye onɛ di ka di yinɛ on da paam vɔɔtnam tusa pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii, kɔbisyi' nɛ awai (78,209) dinɛ an pisnii nɛ atan du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (83.78%) ka onɛ da dɔl o nya'aŋ, Ma'asim tiig National Democratic Congress' nid la, Grace Agyemang Asamoah da paam vɔɔtnam tusa piinɛ anaasi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pistan (14,730) dinɛ an piinɛ anu du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (15.78%).
english: He was declared winner in the parliamentary elections after obtaining 78,209 votes representing 83.78% against his closest contender the National Democratic Congress' candidate Grace Agyemang Asamoah of who had 14,730 votes representing 15.78%.

kusaal: Amankwa-Manu paas la'askanɛ gɔsid pʋ'abnɛ dap nɛ biis yɛla (Gender and Children) ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid diib, kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl nɛ Kooko yɛla (Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs).
english: Amankwa-Manu is a member of the Gender and Children Committee and also the Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs Committee.

kusaal: O da diya nɛ vɔɔt kɔbisnaasii nɛ piinɛ anu (415) ka onɛ zin'i kʋk la zug la paam vɔɔt pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (69).
english: He won by securing 415 votes, while the incumbent had 69 votes.

kusaal: Amankwa-Manu anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Amankwa-Manu is a Christian.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Kofi Amoakohene nɛ dabisim piiga nɛ yinnɛ la daar nwadisa anaasi la ni 1969 ka o yit Atebubu bɛ Bono East Sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana.
english: Amoakohene was born on 11 April 1969 and hails from Atebubu in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Central University Accra 2005.
english: He had his Bachelor of Science degree in administration from the Central University in Accra in 2005.

kusaal: Amoakohene da anɛ Chief executive Officer tis Customer Company Limited bɛ Accra.
english: Amoakohene was the chief executive officer for Customer Company Limited in Accra.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2020 kanɛ da an Ghana dim vɔɔtʋg tita'ar la ni la, o da lʋ ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid Sanja Nanja di.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he lost to the NDC parliamentary candidate Sanja Nanja.

english: The Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC) is a training centre based in Ghana which provides training and research in peacekeeping and peaceoperations.

en_article: Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre

kusaal: · Ye ba sʋŋ ka azin'in baanlim yela zamisig kanɛ bɛ Koulikoro linɛ bɛ Mali tɛŋin ka banɛ sʋŋidi li tʋʋma an French dim la nɛ koligi kanɛ gɔsid zaba yela ka ba Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim la nyaŋi la'as taaba ka li mɔr sʋŋir.
english: To provide the operational focus that will link the basic tactical Peace Operations training provided at Koulikoro in Mali under French sponsorship with the high level strategic training provided at the War College in Nigeria.
kus_article: Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre
en_article: Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre

kusaal: KAIPTC la'asi ba mɛŋ nɛ zin'is banɛ ka ba pa'an azin'in baanlim yela bɛdigʋ dunia nwa ni nɛ vɛɛnsa lʋga bɛdigʋ, ka zin'ig yinnɛ an Pearson Peacekeeping Centre linɛ bɛ Canada tɛŋin la.
english: The KAIPTC is engaged in partnerships with several research and training facilities in the world, including Canada's Pearson Peacekeeping Centre.

en_article: Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre

english: KAIPTC commenced its first full annual training and education cycle in March 2004, and has since expanded its curriculum to more than twenty different courses.

kusaal: Kofi Arko Nokoe anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress ni.
english: Kofi Arko Nokoe is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira Constituency bɛ Western region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He is the member of Parliament for the Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira Constituency in the Western region.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Nokoe nɛyʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan Nwadisa anu la dabpiinɛ atan daar (13 May 1983) o yinɛ Axim n bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Nokoe was born on 13 May 1983 and hails from Axim in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋi o tertiary educationɛ Komenda College of Education.
english: He started his tertiary education at the Komenda College of Education.

kusaal: Ka tɔlisi keŋ University of Ghana, maal Bachelor of Arts degree in Political studies.
english: He attended the University of Ghana, where he completed with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political studies.

kusaal: Nokoe lɛn mɔr master's degree in Development Studies yi Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology.
english: Nokoe also holds a master's degree in Development Studies from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology.

kusaal: Nokoe da anɛ Senior Superintendent gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni, Ghana Education Service.
english: Nokoe was the Senior Superintendent at the Ghana Education Service.

kusaal: O da lɛn an Assistant Director tis Ministry of Local Government.
english: He was also the Assistant Director at the Ministry of Local Government.

kusaal: Nokoe da nya' Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira Constituency gur yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai Nwadisa awai la dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 September 2019) ka di nɛ vɔɔt kɔbisnu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (546) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (64.2%) ka onɛ ti'al o la, Herbert Kua Dickson paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi nɛpiswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (297) dinɛ an pistan nɛ anaasi du'ali awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (34.9%).
english: Nokoe won the parliamentary bid to represent the National Democratic Congress for the Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira Constituency ahead of the 2020 elections on 28 September 2019 after polling 546 votes representing 64.2% beating his main contender, Herbert Kua Dickson who had 297 votes representing 34.9%.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi , (December 2020) la nii, o da di Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira Constituency kʋk la ka yis onɛ pʋn dɛŋim zin'i kʋk la zug la, Catherine Ablema Afeku onɛ an Minista kʋdʋgʋ tis Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts.
english: In December 2020, He won the Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira Constituency in the parliamentary elections unseating the incumbent member of parliament Catherine Ablema Afeku who is a former Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ awai, kɔbisnii nɛ pistan (19,830) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ atan du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (53.4%) ka onɛ dɔli o nya'aŋka an onɛ da pʋn dɛŋim zin'i kʋ la zug, Catherine Ablema Afeku onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi (17,287) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ du'ali ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (46.6%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He won by polling 19,830 votes representing 53.4% against his closest opponent the incumbent member of parliament, Catherine Ablema Afeku of the New Patriotic Party who obtained 17,287 votes representing 46.6% of the votes cast.

kusaal: Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira kʋk la da paasnɛ kʋgʋsbanɛ ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress kʋkbanɛ ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party da di'e yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋgin la ama aba da pʋ nyaŋi di yʋma anaasi banɛ dɔl la ya'asa.
english: The Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira seat was one of the seats that was taken away from the National Democratic Congress by the New Patriotic Party in the 2016 Parliamentary Elections but the party couldn't retain it for an extra 4 years.

kusaal: Nokoe paasnɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid Special Budget Committee ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Foreign Affairs.
english: Nokoe is a member of the Special Budget Committee and also a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee.

kusaal: Nokoe anɛ Kristo biig ka o keŋ Methodist.
english: Nokoe is a Christian and worships as a Methodist.

kusaal: Kofi Brako anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Tema Central Constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Kofi Brako (born 11 September 1959) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Tema Central Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Akyem Bieni bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Akyem Bieni in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o Diploma in Freight Forwarding yi Zurich, Switzerland yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013).
english: He obtained his Diploma in Freight Forwarding from Zürich, Switzerland in 2013.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ kpɛn' pɔlitis la, Brako da anɛ chief executive officer tis Teamwork Freight Services bɛ Tema.
english: Prior to entering politics, Brako was the chief executive officer of Teamwork Freight Services in Tema.

kusaal: Brako da kpɛn' wadmaannib yin nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2013) wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug tis Tema Central Constituency.
english: Brako entered parliament on 7 January 2013 on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party representing the Tema Central Constituency.

kusaal: Din yi vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ yinne, kɔbisnu nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (41,581), o da paam da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anii, kɔbistan nɛ pistan nɛ anaasi (28,334) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisyuobʋ nɛ anii du'al pistan nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (68.31%) di kʋk la.
english: Out of the 41,581 valid votes cast, he polled 28,334 votes (68.31%%) to win the seat.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig ka keŋ Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints pʋ'ʋsim.
english: He identifies as a Christian and a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Brako nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai nwadis awai dabpiinɛ yinne daar (11 September 1959).
english: Brako was born on 11 September 1959.

kusaal: Wadmaannib yin la, o da tʋm la'asʋg nam kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb nib a sieba anɛ; Roads and Transport, Gender and Children, nɛ Youth, Sports and Culture.
english: In parliament, he has served on various committees, some of which include; the Roads and Transport Committee, the Gender and Children Committee, and the Youth, Sports and Culture Committee.

kusaal: Brako is mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa anaasi.
english: Brako is married with four children.

english: Kofi Okyere-Agyekum (born 8 March 1958) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Fanteakwa South Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

english: He hails from Osino, a town in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

english: In 2012, he contested for the Fanteakwa South seat on the ticket of the NPP sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

english: Kojo Appiah-Kubi (born 15 June 1956) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Atwima Kwawoma Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Appiah-Kubi anɛ wadmaan tis Atwima Kwanwoma constituency ka paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anu bɛ Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: Appiah-Kubi represented the Atwima Kwanwoma constituency as the Member of Parliament in the 5th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.
