english: Asemanyi was the Deputy Chairman of Parliamentary Select Committee on Sports.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaan kʋdʋg tis Gomoa East bɛ Central Region Sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana.
english: Kojo Asemanyi is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Gomoa East Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Kojo Vincent Oppong Nkrumah (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 5 Vaala/Nwadisanu 1982) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an lɔya, ba da du'a nɛ Burnya nya'aŋ nwaris anaasi la li daba anu yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi' la ni la.
english: Kojo Vincent Oppong Nkrumah (born 5 April 1982) is a Ghanaian politician and lawyer.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Nkrumah bɛnɛ Koforidua, linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.O du'adib anɛ Kwame Oppong Nkrumah nɛ Felicia Oppong Nkrumah.
english: His parents are Kwame Oppong Nkrumah and Felicia Oppong Nkrumah.

kusaal: O yinɛ Akim Anyinase sʋ'ʋlʋm na.
english: He hails from Akim Anyinase.

kusaal: O da naae ani ka tɔlis Pope John Senior High School and Minor Seminary sakur linɛ bɛ Koforidua la, ka lin nya'aŋ ka o tɔlis University of Cape Coast n zamisi naae ka di'e digirɛɛ kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Commerce.
english: Nkrumah had his basic school education at St. Bernadette Soubirous School in Dansoman, continued to Pope John Senior High School and Minor Seminary in Koforidua for his senior high education, and later studied at the University of Cape Coast, where he received a bachelor's degree in Commerce.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni ka o da lɛn tɔlis University of Ghana, linɛ bɛ Legon la naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an MBA linɛ an Kpikpiυŋ zamisυg la.
english: In 2012, he graduated with an MBA in Marketing from the University of Ghana, Legon.

kusaal: Nkrumah da pin'ili tυm nɛ British American Tobacco dim n gɔsidi ba ligidi yɛla yυυma tusa aayi' nɛ ayuobʋ la pυυgin.
english: Nkrumah started his career as a Treasury Analyst at British American Tobacco in 2006.

kusaal: O da yii ani n keŋ tʋm nɛ Joy FM dim n an labaya mɔɔl-mɔɔl, onɛ da ɛɛnti su'oe bɛkɛung saŋa Komla Dumor da kae la.
english: He moved on to Joy FM as a broadcast journalist, hosting the Super Morning Show after the departure of host Komla Dumor.

kusaal: Kojo anɛ Kristo biig ka mɔr pu'a ka o yυ'υr buon Akua.
english: Kojo is married to Akua, and they are both devoted Christians.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Ofoase-Ayirebi sυ'υlυm la.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Ofoase-Ayirebi constituency.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi la ni ka o da naae GIMPA sakurin la ka di'e wada kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an wada zamisυg yɛla la yυυma ayi' pυυgin ka o da zamisi li.
english: In 2014, he was awarded a bachelor's degree in law (LLB) at the GIMPA Faculty of Law after two years of studies.

kusaal: Yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni ka ba da buol o paas Ghana lɔya nam la kanlin.
english: In 2016, he was called to the Bar as a barrister and solicitor of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: Yυυma tυsa ayi' nɛ pisi la ka World Economic Forum dim da gaŋ o ye o an dunia wυsa dasam baanlυg kpɛɛm.
english: He was selected as one of the world's 115 Young Global Leaders for 2020 by the World Economic Forum.

kusaal: Yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anu la ni ka Wabυg Na'adɔɔg dim da ye bavɔɔt gaans ba kpɛɛmnam la ka o di Ofoase-Ayirebi linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: In 2015, he contested and won the NPP parliamentary primaries for Ofoase-Ayirebi constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Da anɛ ti Ghana Minista kanɛ gɔsid labaya yɛla la.
english: He additionally served as a member of the Finance and Constitutional committees of the 7th and 8th Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn paasi tυm nɛ kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Ghana ligidi nɛ wada nam yɛla la wadmaanib yir linɛ da paas ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: In January 2024, he was maintained as the parliamentary candidate of the New Patriotic Party for the Ofoase-Ayirebi (Ghana parliament constituency).

kusaal: Kwaku nɛ Afua nɛ Kofi.
english: They have four children so far, Kwaku, Afua, Araba and Kofi.

kusaal: O ma da anɛ pa'an ka o saam mɛ an pa'an ka bas ka tɔɔm tυm bankin.
english: His mother was a teacher and his father was initially a teacher before becoming a banker.

kusaal: Ghana teŋgbaŋin laa, banɛ taa dit kokonte anɛ buud bama.Ga, Akan, Hausa dim wʋsa.
english: In Ghana, kokonte is eaten by most of the ethnic groups like the Ga, Akan, Hausa, Kokonte usually is brown, grey and deep green depending on the type of ethnic group that prepares the dish.

kusaal: Kokonte, ka tita'am buon ye "face the wall", la anɛ dikanɛ ka nidib banɛ bɛ ninsabilis sʋ'ʋlʋm la dit.
english: Kokonte, also known as abeti3, lapiiwa, lapelawa or "face the wall", is a staple swallow food eaten in some parts of Africa including Togo, Ghana and others.

kusaal: Konkonte anɛ Ghana dim diib kanɛ ka ba mɔr banki zɔm maan ka ba dit nɛ suma nɛ abɛ zɛɛn'ɛd.
english: Konkonte is a Ghanaian dish made from cassava flour usually eaten with soups made from palm nut or groundnuts.

kusaal: Di ka' disaaŋ West Africa sʋ'ʋlʋmin wʋʋ Nigeria.
english: It is popular in West African countries such as Nigeria and is also eaten in the Caribbean.

kusaal: Na'asaanam buon dikaŋa nɛ ye "brown fufu".
english: The English name for the dish is "brown fufu".

kusaal: Di ye di nwa'asi nɛ Brazil dim diib kanɛ ka ba buon ye tapioca la.
english: It is similar to tapioca, a popular Brazilian dish that is also popular in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana teŋin Akan buudi la taa maan ka di yʋ'ʋr la yinɛ buudi banɛ kwa pian'ad la ni na.
english: In Ghana, kokonte is eaten by most of the ethnic groups like the Ga, Akan, Hausa, Kokonte usually is brown, grey and deep green depending on the type of ethnic group that prepares the dish.

kusaal: Kolo (Serbian Cyrillic: Коло) anɛ South Slavic circle dance, ka ba da maali li yʋ'ʋkaŋa tɛɛns bam ani Bosnia nɛ Herzegovina, Croatia nɛ Serbia.
english: Kolo (Serbian Cyrillic: Коло) is a South Slavic circle dance, found under this name in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia.

kusaal: Di paasnɛ UNESCO List of Intagible Cultural Heritage la ni tis Serbia.
english: It is inscribed on the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage for Serbia.

kusaal: Antonín Dvořák da nɔk yʋʋma la maali o Slavonic Dances –Serbia kolo an wa'akanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi din yi opus 72.
english: The dance was used by Antonín Dvořák in his Slavonic Dances – the Serbian kolo is the seventh dance from opus 72.

kusaal: South Slavic tensieba ni, ba mɔr horo (Bulgarian: хоро) bɛ Bulgaria ka oro (Macedonian: оро) mɛ bɛ North Macedonia nɛ Montenegro.
english: Elsewhere in South Slavic countries, there is horo (Bulgarian: хоро) in Bulgaria and oro (Macedonian: оро) in North Macedonia and Montenegro.

kusaal: Region wʋsa mɔr kolo wa'ab yinne bɛɛ babʋg ka di/ba bɛɛ di kɔn' nɛ regon sieba.
english: Each region has at least one unique kolo.

kusaal: Region banɛ kpi'e taaba la'adi nwɛn taaba bi'ela.
english: Bordering regions are mostly more similar to each other.

kusaal: Tiig la wal, ka ba buon kookoo wal la anɛ gbilig, 15–30 cm (6–12 in) wa'alim ka li bɛdigm an 8–10 cm (3–4 in), ka li ya'a bi'ig, li pak la anɛ dɔnbʋʋlim, ka li wa'alim an 500 g (1 lb) li bi'igir saŋa.
english: The fruit, called a cacao pod, is ovoid, 15–30 cm (6–12 in) long and 8–10 cm (3–4 in) wide, ripening yellow to orange, and weighs about 500 g (1 lb) when ripe.

kusaal: Buudi yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba pʋd kookoo na'asaalin ye Theobroma la yinɛ Greek ni ka li gbin an "Wina diib"; yinɛ θεός (theos), ka li gbin an 'Win' bɛɛ 'paŋ daan', nɛ βρῶμα (broma), ka lin gbin mɛ an 'diib'.
english: The generic name Theobroma is derived from the Greek for "food of the gods"; from θεός (theós), meaning 'god' or 'divine', and βρῶμα (brôma), meaning 'food'.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka ba buon cacao la yinɛ Spain dim buudi pian'ad ni ka ba pʋdi ba kʋdʋmin bʋnbʋta si'eba ka ba si'eba an kakaw bɛ Tzeltal, K'iche' nɛ Classic Maya; kagaw bɛ Sayula Popoluca; nɛ cacahuatl bɛ Nahuatl ka lin gbin an "kookoo tiig biilif".
english: The specific name cacao is the Hispanization of the name given to the plant in indigenous Mesoamerican languages such as kakaw in Tzeltal, K'iche' and Classic Maya; kagaw in Sayula Popoluca; and cacahuatl in Nahuatl meaning "bean of the cocoa-tree".

kusaal: Kookoo (Theobroma cacao) paas nɛ buudi banɛ an pisi nɛ ayuobʋ ka bɛ Theobroma buudi ni ka Byttnerioideae banɛ an mallow dɔɔg buudi ka ba buoni ba Malvaceae mɛ paasi ba buudi la ni.
english: Cacao (Theobroma cacao) is one of 26 species belonging to the genus Theobroma classified under the subfamily Byttnerioideae of the mallow family Malvaceae.

kusaal: Buudi bama anɛ: Amelonado, Criollo, Nacional, Contamana, Curaray, Cacao guiana, Iquitos, Marañon, Nanay, nɛ Purús.
english: These groups are: Amelonado, Criollo, Nacional, Contamana, Curaray, Cacao guiana, Iquitos, Marañon, Nanay, and Purús.

kusaal: Banɛ gɔsid tɛngbaŋ yela pa'al ye sankanɛ ka dunia da an ma'asig ma'a yʋʋm tusa pisi nɛ yinnɛ (21,000) linɛ gaad saŋa la, saŋkan ka kookoo da pʋ maal titua nɛ, amaa zin'ig kaŋa da la'an wan kookoo ka linɛ kɛ ka li buud si'eba nan kpɛlim bɛ.
english: Climate models indicate that at the peak of the last ice age 21,000 years ago, when habitat suitable for cacao was at its most reduced, this area was still suitable, and so provided a refugium for species.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan' ni (2023), ba da kua kookoo dunia wʋsa nɛ 11,650,000 hectares (28,800,000 acres).
english: In 2023, cocoa beans were cultivated on roughly 11,650,000 hectares (28,800,000 acres) worldwide.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmin sa, banɛ maa chocolate mi' nɛ buudi atan' banɛ ka ba mɔri maan chocolate: Forastero, Criollo nɛ Trinitario.
english: Historically, chocolate makers have recognized three main cultivar groups of cacao beans used to make cocoa and chocolate: Forastero, Criollo and Trinitario.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, sapal nwadig la ni (November 2000), kookoo banɛ da yit Chuao la da nyɛ yʋ'ʋr paal ye Cacao de Chuao (lin yinɛ Spanish: 'kookoo linɛ yit Chuao').
english: In November 2000, the cacao beans coming from Chuao were awarded an appellation of origin under the title Cacao de Chuao (from Spanish: 'cacao of Chuao').

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan' ni (2023), dunia wʋsa kookoo da maali anɛ 5.6 million tonnes, ka tɛŋkanɛ ka li da maalig gaad o taaba an Ivory Coast, ban da mɔr pisnaasi nɛ ayi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (42.5%) dunia wʋsa kookoo.
english: In 2023, world production of cocoa beans was 5.6 million tonnes, led by Ivory Coast with 42.5% of the total (table).

kusaal: Tɛŋbanɛ mɛ da ti'al da anɛ Ghana (11.7%) nɛ Indonesia (11.5%).
english: Other major producers were Ghana (11.7%) and Indonesia (11.5%).

kusaal: · Cocoa mirids bɛɛ capsids dunia wʋsa (li kaskas Sahlbergella singularis nɛ Distantiella theobroma bɛ West Africa nɛ Helopeltis spp.
english: Cocoa mirids or capsids worldwide (but especially Sahlbergella singularis and Distantiella theobroma in West Africa and Helopeltis spp. in Southeast Asia)

kusaal: · Conopomorpha cramerella (cocoa pod borer – bɛ Southeast Asia)
english: Conopomorpha cramerella (cocoa pod borer – in Southeast Asia)

kusaal: · Moniliophthora roreri (frosty pod rot)
english: Moniliophthora roreri (frosty pod rot)

kusaal: · Moniliophthora perniciosa (witches' broom)
english: Moniliophthora perniciosa (witches' broom)

kusaal: · Ceratocystis cacaofunesta (mal de machete) or (Ceratocystis wilt)
english: Ceratocystis cacaofunesta (mal de machete) or (Ceratocystis wilt)

kusaal: · Oncobasidium theobromae (vascular streak dieback)
english: Oncobasidium theobromae (vascular streak dieback)

kusaal: Ti mɔr Kooko biili la maan chocolate ,Kooko kpaam, milo, nɛ si'elnam bɛdigʋ.
english: Its seeds—cocoa beans when dried and fermented—are used to make chocolate liquor, cocoa powder, cocoa butter and chocolate.

kusaal: Puum la anɛ ban'alig, 1–2 cm (3⁄8–13⁄16 in) wa'alim, ka linɛ lus puum la an wiig.
english: The flowers are small, 1–2 cm (3⁄8–13⁄16 in) diameter, with pink calyx.

kusaal: Puum bɛdigʋ dunia ni anɛ siinsi diti li ka maan diib (Hymenoptera) bɛɛ pimpiŋ nɛ bʋnvʋya si'eba, kookoo puum maan diibi dɔlisid nɛ bʋndʋmma banɛ ka ba buoni ba na'asaalin ye Forcipomyia midges.
english: While many of the world's flowers are pollinated by bees (Hymenoptera) or butterflies/moths (Lepidoptera), cacao flowers are pollinated by tiny flies, Forcipomyia biting midges.

kusaal: Bʋnvʋya banɛ dʋm ka ba buon Forcipomyia midges la kɛt ka kookoo maan wala bɛdigʋ gaad suobanɛ kpɛlim wʋsa.
english: Using the natural pollinator Forcipomyia midges produced more fruit than using artificial pollinators.

kusaal: Biili la ka ba mɔri maan chocolate, ka linɛ lus biila la pʋʋgin la tɛŋ si'eba mɔri maan juice, smoothies, jelly, nɛ cream.
english: The seeds are the main ingredient of chocolate, while the pulp is used in some countries to prepare juice, smoothies, jelly, and cream.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a di dinɛ lus biilif la, li malisim wan wʋʋ lychee bɛɛ tropical melon.
english: The pulp tastes like lychee or tropical melon.

kusaal: Biilif yinnɛ wʋsa mɔr kpaam bɛdigʋ (40–50%) ka ba buon cocoa butter.
english: Each seed contains a significant amount of fat (40–50%) as cocoa butter.

kusaal: Bʋnlinɛ bɛ li pʋʋgin anɛ theobromine, linɛ wan caffeine.
english: The fruit's active constituent is the stimulant theobromine, a compound similar to caffeine.

kusaal: Kookoo yadigi paae zin'ig yinɛ yadagɔbʋg-yanya'aŋ Mexico tɛŋin paae Amazon basin.
english: T. cacao is widely distributed from southeastern Mexico to the Amazon basin.

kusaal: Banɛ vɛɛns la pa'al ye ninsaalib nyaŋi ti'aki li zi kpɛn'ɛ yaan dɔlis nɛ suoya ayi; yinnɛ da bɛ nɛ Lacandon mɔɔgin zin'ig kan bɛnɛ Mexico ka yinnɛ mɛ da bɛ South America.
english: There were originally two hypotheses about its domestication; one said that there were two foci for domestication, one in the Lacandon Jungle area of Mexico and another in lowland South America. More recent studies of patterns of DNA diversity, however, suggest that this is not the case.

kusaal: Vɛɛnsig la mɛ nyaŋi baŋ zin'ig la, wan wʋʋ Iquitos linɛ an Peru nɛ Ecuador, anina ka buudi bɛdigʋ da yi na yʋʋma tusanu banɛ gaad la saŋa, ka li da dɔlis anina ka buud kanɛ ka ba buon Nacional cocoa bean yina.
english: This study also identified areas, for example around Iquitos in modern Peru and Ecuador, where representatives of several genetic clusters originated more than 5000 years ago, leding to development of the variety, Nacional cocoa bean.

kusaal: Ban gɔs DNA la ka nɔki mak nɛ tɛŋ vʋ'ʋsim ka bʋ nyaŋi baŋ lin nar ye tɛŋ an si'em ka li nyaŋi maal titua la, vɛɛnsig yinnɛ yinɛ maligim ti'aki li kuob yela, ka pa'al ye kookoo bɛ kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb la yinɛ zinɛ zin'ig kanɛ an gbilig wan wʋʋ bɛŋa gilig Ecuador, titɔndig kanɛ bɛ Brazil nɛ Peru nɛ Colombian–Brazilian ni la.
english: Using the DNA sequences and comparing them with data derived from climate models and the known conditions suitable for cacao, one study refined the view of domestication, linking the area of greatest cacao genetic diversity to a bean-shaped area that encompasses Ecuador, the border between Brazil and Peru and the southern part of the Colombian–Brazilian border.

kusaal: Banɛ ka ba paamig tɔe, ka ba ligidi kpi'em anɛ buudi kanɛ buon Criollo, kookoo buudi kanɛ ka Maya dim da mɔr la.
english: The most prized, rare, and expensive is the Criollo group, the cocoa bean used by the Maya.

kusaal: Ba mɔr Criollo maan chocolate nɛ piiga, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (10%), lin mɔr malisim ka nyʋʋsidi malisi gat banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa.
english: Only 10% of chocolate is made from Criollo, which is arguably less bitter and more aromatic than any other bean.

kusaal: Banɛ gɔsid kuob yela su'ad bʋnbʋta buudi-buudi bɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka ba buon na'asaalin ye genebanks, anina ka ba digin ka li la'asidi li taaba kilimid buud paala, amaa kookoo biila la yela tɔi galisi kɛ ka ba kʋ nyaŋi nɔki li niŋ genebank ni ka li maal buud paalaa.
english: Breeders rely on the genetic diversity conserved in field genebanks to create new varieties, because cacao has recalcitrant seeds that cannot be stored in a conventional genebank.

kusaal: · Dayuus nɛ vertebrate pests (squirrels, woodpeckers, etc.)
english: Rats and other vertebrate pests (squirrels, woodpeckers, etc.)

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ anii ni (2008), vɛɛn-vɛɛnsidib da yinɛ nɛ suor kanɛ ka ba na nyaŋi la'as kookoo buudinam kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb dɔlisidi ba zin'ig kanɛ nyɛt paalʋ, lin bɛ zin'ig si'a, nɛ ba tʋŋ: ba pʋdʋgi ba piiga dɔlisid nɛ ban yi zin'ig si'eba bɛɛ tɛŋ la dimi kuod buud si'a ka pʋdi li si'em.
english: In 2008, researchers proposed a new classification based upon morphological, geographic, and genomic criteria: 10 groups have been named according to their geographic origin or the traditional cultivar name.

kusaal: Vɛɛnsig yinnɛ da nɔk nɛ tiis ban tusir, kɔbisyi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yinnɛ (1241) ka la'asi ba ka ba an buudi piiga.
english: One study sampled 1241 trees and classified them into 10 distinct genetic clusters.

kusaal: Sɛɛ ka fʋ la'as biili tusir nɛ kɔbisyi yel (1,200) lin anɛ wala pisnaasi yel li la ka fʋ na la'as ka nyaan paami li gan'alig la tɛbisim 1 kg (2.2 lb).
english: About 1,200 seeds (40 pods) are required to produce 1 kg (2.2 lb) of cocoa paste.

kusaal: Ban'abɛ'ɛdnam nɛ bʋnvʋya si'eba bɛ san'amid kookoo tʋʋma ka li pʋ nyaŋidi maan titua nɛ.
english: Various plant pests and diseases can cause serious problems for cacao production.

kusaal: Koose (Dagbani: buon [ˈKooshe]) ka lɛn an bɛŋa diib anɛ diib kanɛ mɔr kpaam ka nidib banɛ diti di tita'am an banɛ bɛ ninsabilis ya'tuona sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Koose (Dagbani: [ˈKooshe]) also known as Bean Cake is a spicy black-eyed pea fritter that is commonly eaten in West Africa as a snack.

kusaal: Sansi'eba, ba pɔnbini di nɛ bodobodo pʋʋgin, ka ba buon din ye "Koose Bodobodo" bɛɛ "Paanu Kooshe".
english: Sometimes it is sandwiched in bread, and called "Koose Bread" or "Paanu Kooshe".

kusaal: Ba ye li yinԑ Yorubas buudi banԑ bԑ Nigeria zina la nina ka ba buoni li akara.
english: The food is said to have spread from the Yorubas of present day Nigeria who call it akara.

kusaal: Koose anԑ dikanԑ nyԑ yʋ'ʋr West Africa bԑnԑ Hausa buudi banԑ bԑ Northern Nigeria, Dagomba nԑ Hausa banԑ bԑ Ghana, nԑ West Africa sʋ'ʋlim tԑŋ si'eba wan wʋʋ Sierra Leone nԑ Cameroon.
english: Koose is common in West Africa among the Hausa people of Northern Nigeria, the Dagomba and Hausa people of Ghana, and other parts of West Africa, including Sierra Leone and Cameroon.

kusaal: Koose mԑ bԑ Caribbean tԑԑns ni wʋʋ Cuba nԑ South America tԑԑns ni wʋʋ Brazil.
english: Koose can also be found in Caribbean countries such as Cuba and in South American countries such as Brazil.

kusaal: In Nigeria, it is known as "akara", in Brazil as "acaraje" and in Cuba as "bollitos de carita".[citation needed] To the Dagbamba of Ghana it is known as "Kooshe", the Ewe call it "agawu", and to some in the Zongo community as "koose tankuwa".
english: To the Dagbamba of Ghana it is known as "Kooshe", the Ewe call it "agawu", and to some in the Zongo community as "koose tankuwa".

kusaal: It is known in Ghana as "koose", "kooshe" or "koosay"[citation needed].
english: It is known in Ghana as "koose", "kooshe" or "koosay".

kusaal: Koose nyɛ yʋ'ʋr ya'tuona ninsabilis sʋ'ʋlim ka di kaskas an Hausa dim banɛ bɛ ya'datiʋŋ Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim la, Dagomba nidib banɛ bɛ Ghana, nɛ ninsabilis ya'tuona sʋ'ʋlim tɛɛns, ka ba si'eba an Sierra Leone nɛ Cameroon.
english: Koose is common in West Africa among the Hausa people of Northern Nigeria, the Dagomba and Hausa people of Ghana, and other parts of West Africa, including Sierra Leone and Cameroon.

kusaal: Koose mɛ bɛ na'asaatɛɛnsin wan wʋʋ Cuba nɛ America ya'dagɔbʋg tɛnsi'eba wʋʋ Brazil.
english: Koose can also be found in Caribbean countries such as Cuba and in South American countries such as Brazil.

kusaal: Ghana dim buoni di ye "koose", "kooshe" bɛɛ "koosay".
english: It is known in Ghana as "koose", "kooshe" or "koosay".

kusaal: Nigeria dim, buoni di ye "akara", Brazil dim buoni di ye "acaraje" ka Cuba dim mɛ buon ye "bollitos de carita".
english: In Nigeria, it is known as "akara", in Brazil as "acaraje" and in Cuba as "bollitos de carita".

kusaal: Dagbamba banɛ bɛ Ghana buoni di ye "Kooshe", Ewe dim buoni di ye "agawu" ka si'eba banɛ bɛ Zongo community buoni di ye "koose tankuwa".
english: To the Dagbamba of Ghana it is known as "Kooshe", the Ewe call it "agawu", and to some in the Zongo community as "koose tankuwa".

kusaal: Ba taa diti di nɛ kooko.
english: It is often taken with porridge.

kusaal: Kotoku Royals F.C. (ka ba da buon ye Kotoku Royals Academy) anɛ professional football team kanɛ yi Akim Oda, Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana, ka nwɛ'ɛd Ghana Division One ni.
english: Kotoku Royals F.C. (previously known as Kotoku Royals Academy) is a professional football team from Akim Oda, Eastern Region in Ghana, currently playing in Ghana Division One.

kusaal: Di da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan la ni (2003) ka paam suor ye ba nwɛ' professional maknam yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005), kilab la paam tɔlisi keŋ tuon ka yʋ'ʋn nwɛ'ɛd Ghana League system Division One ni.
english: Founded in 2003 and given permission to play professional matches in 2005, the club made successive promotions through the Ghana League system to their current place in Division One.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa atan la ni (March, 2017) Englishman Matt Ward ka ba da gaŋ ye o an Head Coach yʋma ayi (two years).
english: In March, 2017 Englishman Matt Ward was appointed Head Coach for two years.

kusaal: Kpabia anɛ tempʋbili bɛ Yendi Municipal district, district kanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana Ya-dagɔbʋg baba.
english: Kpabia is a small town in the Yendi Municipal district, a district in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kpalbe bɛɛ Palbe anɛ tenkanɛ bɛ Savannah Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Kpalbe or Palbe is a town in the Savannah Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di anɛ tempʋtita'ari tis North East Gonja District.
english: It is the capital of the North East Gonja District.

kusaal: Kpalbe bɛnɛ Ya-dagɔbʋg-Nya'aŋ tis Tamale dinɛ an tempʋtita'ari tis Northern Region.
english: Kpalbe lies south east to Tamale the capital of the Northern Region.

kusaal: Tembanɛ bɛ Ya-datiʋŋ anɛ Bung (Gbung) nɛ Chanbulugu.
english: Towns to the north are Bung (Gbung) and Chanbulugu.

kusaal: Kwisini nɛ Chandayili bɛ di Ya-nya'aŋ baba.
english: Kwisini and Chandayili are found to the east.

kusaal: Di Ya-dagɔbʋg baba anɛ JIdanyile, Palbusi nɛ Wala.
english: Towards the south are JIdanyile, Palbusi and Wala.

kusaal: Tembanɛ bɛ di Ya-nya'aŋ anɛ Vano, Deboko, Panshiaw nɛ Changburi.
english: Its western neighbours are Vano, Deboko, Panshiaw and Changburi.

kusaal: Damongo, tempʋtita'ari tis Savannah Region anɛ 172 kilometres dɔl suor wa'alim lɛbid Kpalbe Ya-tuona.
english: Damongo, the capital of the Savannah Region is 172 kilometres by road to the west of Kpalbe.

kusaal: Kpini Chugu, ka li gbin an kpa'aŋ malʋŋ bԑ Dagban buudi pian'ad ni la, anԑ malʋŋ kanԑ ka ba maan nwadis anaasi la ni Damba di'ema la nya'aŋ bԑ Northern region Ghana.
english: Kpini Chugu, which means Guineafowl Festival in Dagbani, is a minor festival celebrated on the fourth month after Damba in Northern region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba maan malʋŋ la bԑ Dagbon, Mamprugu nԑ Nanung buudi pian'ad dim zin'is ni.
english: It is observed in the Dagbon, Mamprugu and Nanung traditional areas.

kusaal: Sͻlima pʋʋgin pa'al ye Naa Zangina da mͻr Islam pʋ'ʋsʋm kԑn Dagbon na.
english: Naa Zangina according to oral history was the one who brought Islam to Dagbon.

kusaal: Kpa'aŋ anԑ bʋnvʋl kanԑ ka ba gͻs ka o bԑ o kͻn' bԑ Northern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The guineafowl is more than just a bird in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Malʋŋ nwa' da pin'il nԑ sankanԑ ka Naa Zangina da an na'ab.
english: This festival as stated earlier was initiated during the reign of Naa Zangina.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmin labaar bԑ ye Prophet Mohammed saŋa la, o da tu suor ka paae mͻͻgin ka o kuom naae ka kuonuud kʋʋd o.
english: The ancient folklore states that during the time of the Prophet Mohammed, he was on a journey in the desert and along the way he ran out of water and he was virtually dying with thirst.

kusaal: Krachi East Constituency anɛ Ghana Parliament constituency nam la yinne.
english: Krachi East is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Krachi East bɛ nɛ Krachi East district bɛ Oti Region, Ghana la.
english: Krachi East is located in the Krachi East district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Electoral Commission of Ghana da sin'iŋ constituency la yiiga nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni paas nɛ pisinɛ anaasi sieba, ba yʋ'ʋn da paas constituency nam la ban kɔbisyi (200) kɛŋ paae ban kɔbisyi nɛ pistan (230).
english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Constituency la da sin'iŋɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi Ghana wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la ni, ka Krachi constituency da pudiga ayi an Krachi East nɛ Krachi West.
english: This seat was created prior to the Ghanaian parliamentary election in 2004 when the Krachi constituency was split into the Krachi East and the Krachi West constituencies respectively.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Krachi East district bɛ Volta Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Krachi East District of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la da bɛnɛ Volta Region ka ba naam pʋdig Region paala dɔlisid yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ay (2012) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: The constituency was originally located within the Volta Region of Ghana until new Regions were created following the December 2018 referendum.

kusaal: Krachi Nchumuru Constituency anɛ Ghana Parliament constituency nam la yinne.
english: Krachi Nchumuru is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Krachi Nchumuru bɛ nɛ Krachi Nchumuru district bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: Krachi Nchumuru is located in the Krachi Nchumuru district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la da bɛ nɛ Volta Region ka ba naam pʋdig Region paala dɔlisid yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: The constituency was originally located within the Volta Region of Ghana until new Regions were created following the December 2018 referendum.

kusaal: Krachi West Constituency anɛ Ghana Parliament constituency nam la yinne.
english: Krachi West is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidi ba Member of Parliament (MP) dolisidnɛ onɛ vɔɔti zuoe gat.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Ban nɛ Nkwanta South mɔr titɔndig ka li bɛɛ li North East.
english: It also shares a short border with the Nkwanta South to the north east.

kusaal: Li kpies banɛ bɛ ba ya-tuona anɛ Sene constituency bɛ Sene District Brong Ahafo Region la.
english: Its western neighbour is the Sene constituency in the Sene District of the Brong Ahafo Region.

kusaal: Ba kpies banɛ bɛ ya-dagobuk anɛ East Gonja District bɛ Northern Region.
english: Its northern neighbour is the East Gonja District in the Northern Region.

kusaal: Krachi West bɛ nɛ Krachi district bɛ Oti Region, Ghana la.
english: Krachi West is located in the Krachi district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba kuk la bɛ nɛ Krachi West district bɛ Volta Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Krachi West district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li lʋs Krachi West district paal la wusa.
english: The seat is located within the Krachi West district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li ya-yaʋŋ anɛ Krachi East constituency bɛ Krachi East District la.
english: To the east is the Krachi East constituency in the Krachi East District.

kusaal: Ba da tias titɔndis la dolisidnɛ yʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi Ghana wadmaannib vɔɔtugin ka Krachi constituency da pudigi an Krachi West nɛ Krachi East constituency ban da yis Krachi East District li kɔ Krachi district la.
english: The boundaries of this constituency were changed prior to the Ghanaian parliamentary election in 2004 when the Krachi constituency was split into the Krachi West and the Krachi East constituencies respectively due to the creation of the new Krachi East District from the Krachi district.

kusaal: Li anɛ linɛ pa'an Greece kʋdʋmin nidib bɛdegʋ da pʋ'ʋsid ka dɔli li nɛ yadda si'em, ka li lɛbid nyaŋi pa'an Bronze yʋma ni sa hali la'am nɛ kʋdʋmin Greece dim yɛla.
english: It is one of the basic religious acts that define piety in ancient Greece, dating back to the Bronze Age and even prehistoric Greece.

kusaal: Ku'om kpa'ar bɛnɛ saŋa kanɛ ka ba ye ba nu daam, ba da maan tʋʋm kaŋa nɛ Homeric epics pin'ilʋgʋn sa.
english: A libation is poured any time wine is to be drunk, a practice that is recorded as early as the Homeric epics.

kusaal: Dap di'e Ku'om kpa'ar yi ayi' krater kanɛ ka ba maal la, nɛ Zeús Téleios (Ζεύς Tέλειος, ni.
english: Heroes received a libation from the second krater served, and Zeús Téleios (Ζεύς Tέλειος, lit.

kusaal: Suor daa lɛm bɛ ye ba kpa'ae Ku'om yi yiiga nwam la ni tis Agathos Daimon ba'ad la ka kpa'ae Ku'om mɛ yi nwam kanɛ paas atan' la ni tis Hermes.
english: An alternative was to offer a libation from the first bowl to the Agathos Daimon and from the third bowl to Hermes.

kusaal: Kum gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka Odyssey, nɛ Odysseus da sɔb la, li yɛl ye o tunɛ maan bʋmbɔg ka kpa'ad o siind nɛ daam nɛ Ku'om banɛ ka o yiti tʋm ka ba mɔda la.
english: In the Book of the Dead in the Odyssey, Odysseus digs an offering pit around which he pours in order honey, wine, and water.

kusaal: Rome ba'ar kanɛ ka ba buon ye Liber Pater la ("Father Liber"), nya'aŋ ka Greek dap ayi' banɛ ka ba yʋda an Dionysus bɛɛ Bacchus la, baŋ ka pʋdi li Greek pian'adin ye libamina, ka li gbin pa'al ye "Ku'om kpa'ar," nɛ banɛ ka ba buon ye liba, ka li an maan ma'asir linɛ ka ba nɔk siind maali li la.
english: The Roman god Liber Pater ("Father Liber"), later identified with the Greek Dionysus or Bacchus, was the divinity of libamina, "libations", and liba, sacrificial cakes drizzled with honey.

kusaal: Ba da kpa'ad ku'om ka li anɛ malʋŋ kanɛ pa'an ban tɛnr kpi'imnam yɛla si'em (gɔslim labakaŋa bɛ Parentalia nɛCaristia ni), ka ba yɔ'ɔg vɔɔnr bɛɛ paib nam kpɛn' yɔsieba ni lin na niŋ si'em ka kaanbʋg maan la dɔli sig paae banɛ kpi ka ba mumi ba la ni.
english: Libations were poured in rituals of caring for the dead (see Parentalia and Caristia), and some tombs were equipped with tubes through which the offerings could be directed to the underground dead.

kusaal: Ba da mɛ nɔki li tis Mercurius Sobrius (onɛ pʋ nuud Mercury), ka ba mi'i o ba'ar la sʋ'ʋŋa bɛ Roman Africa sʋ'ʋlʋm ka Africa teŋ dim mɔri li keŋ Rome tempʋʋgin.
english: It was offered also to Mercurius Sobrius (the "sober" Mercury), whose cult is well attested in Roman Africa and may have been imported to the city of Rome by an African community.

kusaal: Ba da mɔr daam kaanbid ba'ar bɛ Jerusalem karindɔɔgin la, ka kaanb ba'ar nɛ daam Ku'om nɔɔr ayi' jew dim yʋʋm wʋsa malʋŋ saŋa la, li kas-kas anɛ saa niib maan.
english: Libations of wine were offered at the Jerusalem temple, and a double libation of wine and water was offered during Sukkot, possibly as a rain making ritual.

kusaal: Buudi malima di'ema wʋʋ Asafotu nɛ Homowo banɛ an Ga Adangbe buudi banɛ bɛ Ghana nwa' ni nɛ Togo la.
english: Traditional Festivals like Asafotu and Homowo of the Ga-Adangbe people of Ghana and Togo.

kusaal: IQuechua nɛ Aymara buudi malima linɛ bɛ America ya-tuona sʋ'ʋlʋm ni la, ba yiti bu'oe nɛ Ku'om bi'ela bas teŋin ka nyaan nu ka li an kaanbʋg maan tis Pachamama ba'ar, bɛɛ teŋ ma gbin la.
english: In the Quechua and Aymara cultures of the South American Andes, it is common to pour a small amount of one's beverage on the ground before drinking as an offering to the Pachamama, or Mother Earth.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛŋa an sida ba ya'a ti nuud Chicha daam kanɛ bugud ka ba nuudi li bɛdegʋ dunia nwa ni la.
english: This especially holds true when drinking Chicha, an alcoholic beverage unique to this part of the world.

kusaal: Hinduism pʋ'ʋsʋm ni ku'om kpa'ar pɛ'ɛsi Tarpan ka ba mɛ maannɛ li Pitru Paksha (kpi'imnam yʋ'ʋŋ) malʋŋ saŋa kanɛ dɔl Hindu Bhadrapada nwadig la, (mɔtul nwadig-sawa'ar nwadig).
english: Libations are part of Tarpan and also performed during Pitru Paksha (Fortnight of the ancestors) following the Bhadrapada month of the Hindu calendar, (September–October).

kusaal: India nɛ Nepal tɛɛnsin la, win kanɛ ka ba buon Shiva la (ka li yʋ'ʋr lɛn an Vishnu nɛ bada banɛ bɛ la) ka banɛ siak nɛ ba suunr wʋsa ka yi pʋ'ʋsʋm dɔɔdin kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ni na ye ba tʋm la, tisid win kaŋa abhisheka nɛ ku'om saŋa kanɛ wʋsa ka ba keŋ ye kaae pʋ'ʋsʋm yir la, nɛ la'aʋŋ sieba ni, ba kennɛ ka mɔr ku'om nɛ iilim nɛ yogurt, ghee, siind nɛ sigir.
english: In India and Nepal, Lord Shiva (also Vishnu and other deities) is offered abhisheka with water by devotees at many temples when they go visit the temple, and on special occasions elaborately with water, milk, yogurt, ghee, honey, and sugar.

kusaal: Burmese Buddhism dim pʋ'ʋsʋm ni, ba buon ku'om kpa'ar malʋŋ ye yay zet cha (ရေစက်ချ), ka li anɛ malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba kabigid ku'om yit zin'ikanɛ ka ku'om bunni yit niŋid nwamin, la'am nɛ Buddhist malima banɛ an la'aʋŋ kanɛ an sʋŋir yɛla, nɛ shinbyu malima nɛ di'ema bɛdegʋ ni.
english: In Burmese Buddhism, the water libation ceremony, called yay zet cha (ရေစက်ချ), which involves the ceremonial pouring of water from a vessel of water into a vase, drop by drop, concludes most Buddhist ceremonies, including donation celebrations, shinbyu, and feasts.

kusaal: Ku'om linɛ ka ba da mɔri kaanbid Vasudhara ba'ar la tʋn'e mɔr Buddhist malima nya'ar, ba tis sida ye na'ab Bimbisara da pin'ili li.
english: Although the offering of water to Vasudhara may have pre-Buddhist roots, this ceremony is believed to have been started by King Bimbisara, who poured the libation of water, to share his merit with his ancestors who had become pretas.

kusaal: Malʋŋ zi'ela bɛɛ wada banɛ ka ba la'as gban'e la yɛl ye, yiiga nwam kanɛ ka daam la bɛ la ya'a zi'elɛ, li pa'al ye ba kaanb Zeus bɛɛ Olympian bada la nɛ.
english: The etiquette of the symposium required that when the first bowl (krater) of wine was served, a libation was made to Zeus and the Olympian gods.

kusaal: "Zeus kanɛ naar") yit linɛ paas atan' ni la, ka daa nar ye li an kpi'i bʋn la.
english: "Zeus who Finishes") from the third, which was supposed to be the last.

kusaal: Zin'ikanɛ ka ba maan nwa' bɛnɛ Greek bada ya'abʋg ni, ka an linɛ mɛ lɛm pa'an banɛ kaanbid si'em bɛɛ bada la mɛŋi zanl nwam la si'em.
english: This scene is commonly depicted in Greek art, which also often shows sacrificers or the gods themselves holding the phiale.

kusaal: Greek itʋg pian'ʋk kanɛ buon ye spéndō (σπένδω), ka li gbin pa'al ye "kaanb ba'ad", ka lɛn an "zaŋ nɔɔr siakir paas", ka yi Indo-European pian'ʋk kaŋa *spend-, ka li gbin pa'al ye "maal maan tis, maal malima rite, zaŋim mɛŋ kpɛn'ɛs malʋŋ tʋʋmin".
english: The Greek verb spéndō (σπένδω), "pour a libation", also "conclude a pact", derives from the Indo-European root *spend-, "make an offering, perform a rite, engage oneself by a ritual act".

kusaal: Pian'ad kanɛ ka ba da pian' ye "tinam pʋlis nwa' kpa'anɛ Ku'om" la da anɛ sunbʋgʋsʋm nɔzi'elʋg bɛɛ "Wina'am sunbʋgʋsʋm", dinzug ba da gɔsid nɔzi'elʋg kaŋa nɛ Saŋkanɛ wʋsa ka tempʋʋgin nidib la kena la'as taaba ye ba di'em Panhellenic di'ema la, nɛ bʋnwɛ'ɛda di'ema, bɛɛ Eleusinian kʋdʋmin malima di'ema la: Ku'om kpa'ar kaŋa buudi pʋ gɛndig ziim, ka an baanlim, ka daʋŋ pʋ bɛɛ li nii, nɛ naar.
english: The formula "We the polis have made libation" was a declaration of peace or the "Truce of God", which was observed also when the various city-states came together for the Panhellenic Games, the Olympic Games, or the festivals of the Eleusinian Mysteries: this form of libation is "bloodless, gentle, irrevocable, and final".

kusaal: Ku'om kpa'ar kanɛ buon ye choē (Ancient Greek: χεῦμα, cheuma, ka li gbin pa'al ye "bʋn linɛ ka ba kpa'ae la"; ka li yi IE *gheu- ni), ka yɔ'ɔg vɔɔsim keŋi kpɛn' bʋmbɔk zin'ikanɛ ka chthonic bada bɛ la ni, ala ka bada la mɛ tʋn'e lɛn di'e spondai.
english: For the form of libation called choē (Ancient Greek: χεῦμα, cheuma, "that which is poured"; from Proto-Indo-European *gʰeu-), a larger vessel is tipped over and emptied onto the ground for the chthonic gods, who may also receive spondai.

kusaal: Banɛ maan ku'om kpa'ar la anɛ na'asayʋ'ʋr linɛ an sunsan'aŋ yi Orestes Trilogy of Aeschylus ni na, ka li pa'an Electra n mɔr maan ken tisid o saam kanɛ kpi ka o yʋ'ʋr buon ye Agamemnon la.
english: The Libation Bearers is the English title of the center tragedy from the Orestes Trilogy of Aeschylus, in reference to the offerings Electra brings to the tomb of her dead father Agamemnon.

kusaal: Yiiga, ba kabigid ku'om yiti ku'osuor kanɛ zɔt; yɔya banɛ zi'e kasi zin'igin la anɛ kɔnbʋlʋg nɛ bʋnvɛnla ka ba nɔki maali ba ka ku'om nɛ siind bɛ ba pʋʋgin; ka li zi'e kpa' ya-dagɔbʋg ka maanmaan la na zaŋ paib nam la kpa' ya-datiʋŋ baba; ka o na nɔk olive vaanr banɛ ka o zanli o nu'ugin la digil teŋin zin'ikanɛ tans fɔɔne kaanbʋg la; ka sɔs o suunfin baanlim ka keŋ ka kʋ gɔs nya'aŋa.
english: First, water is fetched from a freshly flowing spring; cauldrons which stand in the sanctuary are garlanded with wool and filled with water and honey; turning towards the east, the sacrificer tips the vessels towards the west; the olive branches which he has been holding in his hand he now strews on the ground at the place where the earth has drunk in the libation; and with a silent prayer he departs, not looking back.

kusaal: Alexandria pa'al suokanɛ ka ba na dɔlisi maal maan nwa' ka li anɛ ban na nɔk maan bimbim bugum n muki nyɛlig kpaam linɛ bɛ nwama ayi' ni la.
english: Hero of Alexandria described a mechanism for automating the process by using altar fires to force oil from the cups of two statues.

kusaal: Room dim la'ad maalʋg ni, ba maan Ku'om kpa'ar bɛnɛ mensa (maan diib teebul), bɛɛ linɛ mɔr nɔba atan' zi'e.
english: In Roman art, the libation is shown performed at a mensa (sacrificial meal table), or tripod.

kusaal: Ba da pʋ mɔr mɛlk kaanbid wʋʋ Ku'om kpa'ar an si'em bɛ Rome teŋin laa, amaa teŋgban sieba ni ma'a ka ba da maannɛ li kas-kas anɛ Abby banɛ ka ba nɔk nu'usi maal la, bɛɛ banɛ ka ba da pʋn dɛŋim yɛli ba yɛla la, nwɛnnɛ Rumina, ba'ad kanɛ an du'am nɛ biig ugub ba'ar kanɛ kɛ ka bin'isim nɛ cunina pʋbid, ka ti'en bɛɛ an suak zin'igi tis biis.
english: Milk was unusual as a libation at Rome, but was regularly offered to a few deities, particularly those of an archaic nature or those for whom it was a natural complement, such as Rumina, a goddess of birth and childrearing who promoted the flow of breast milk, and Cunina, a tutelary of the cradle.

kusaal: Article la mɛŋ: ku'om kpa'ar maana da pɛ'ɛsi Judaism kʋdʋmin malʋŋ ni ka pʋdigi li yʋ'ʋr bɛ Wina'am gbaʋŋ la ni: ka Jacob mɛ maan bimbim zi'el zin'ibanɛ ka o pian' nɛ zugsɔb la, o da nɔki kuga mɛ bimbim la; ka kpa'ae bɛɛ bu'oe daam nɛ kpaam niŋi li zug.
english: And Jacob set up a Pillar in the place where he had spoken with him, a Pillar of Stone; and he poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.

kusaal: Azaya gbaʋŋin 53:12 , Azaya zaŋi ku'om kpa'ar maal zanbin pa'al sankpan'as kanɛ namisid ka "zaŋ o vʋm bas kum nu'usin".
english: In Isaiah 53:12, Isaiah uses libation as a metaphor when describing the end of the Suffering Servant figure who "poured out his life unto death".

kusaal: Li pa'al ba'ar kaanbʋg yinɛ upper Nile bɔn'ɔfaligin na ka yʋ'ʋn yadigi paae Africa sʋ'ʋlʋm nɛ dunia wʋsa ni.
english: It is suggested that libation originated somewhere in the upper Nile Valley and spread out to other regions of Africa and the world.

kusaal: Kat wa'ae nɛ Ayi Kwei Armah n yɛl si'el la, "[daʋ kanɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ mi'i o yɛla la pa'al malima banɛ bɛ African sʋ'ʋlʋm wʋsa: ba'ar kaanbʋg anɛ linɛ ka ba mɔr pataase bɛɛ daam buudi banɛ bɛ ka li an maan tis kpi'imnam nɛ wina.
english: According to Ayi Kwei Armah, "[t]his legend explains the rise of a propitiatory custom found everywhere on the African continent: libation, the pouring of alcohol or other drinks as offerings to ancestors and divinities."

kusaal: Nwɛnnɛ 1920s yʋma ni na la, li da anɛ malʋŋ bɛ Lower Nubia teŋin n tis pu'ab ka ba ti'eb ka keŋi ba buudi yaadin Adazum daar wʋsa ka kpa'ae kaanbʋg ku'om niŋ lazɛn'ɛʋg ni n bɛ yaʋg la zugin.
english: As recently as the 1920s, it was a custom in Lower Nubia for women to go to the graves of relatives every Friday and pour a libation of water into a red bowl at the head of the grave.

kusaal: Ala mɛn nɔɔ li da anɛ pʋ'ʋsʋm malʋŋ tis pu'ab ye ba keŋ kaae ba sidib yaad banɛ bɛ lallin nɛ yamma, dabisim pisnaasi kum la nya'aŋ, nɛ di'ema wʋʋ Nayrouz.
english: Similarly, it has been Coptic tradition for women to visit graves and make water libations, both in intervals during the first 40 days after a death, and during a few annual occasions, such as Nayrouz.

kusaal: Ban da kpa'ad Ku'om si'emi nwa': ba ya'a nu octli daam naae, ba na lɛm octli danpaalig gɔs, sɔ' ya'a maal octli daam o na la'as nidib bɛdegʋ.

kusaal: Kwabena Appiah-Pinkrah (du'am; nwadisa anii la ni dabisim pisi nɛ atan' daar 1947 ) anɛ consultant nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd Ghana Republic.
english: Kwabena Appiah-Pinkrah (born August 23, 1947) is a consultant and Ghanaian politician of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr diploma gbaʋŋ tita'ar yi University of Bremen West Germany sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: He acquired a diploma (higher level degree) from the University of Bremen West Germany.

kusaal: O da kilim wadmaan lin yi yiiga nwadig 2005 kati waae on da di vɔɔtʋg la nwadis piiga nɛ ayi' 2004 vɔɔtʋg la ni la.
english: He became a member of parliament from January 2005 after emerging winner in the General Election in December 2004.

kusaal: Onɛ an wadmaan tis Akrofoum Constituency kanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana nwa, o fa zi'en nɛ anaasi nɛ anu nɛ ayʋobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi wadmaanib yir linɛ pass Ghana Republic anaasi la.
english: He is the Member of Parliament representing Akrofoum constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana in the 4th,5th,6th and 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Kwabena Appiah-Pinkrah nɛ nwadisa anii la ni dabisim pisi nɛ atan' daar 1947.O yinɛ Akrofoum Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana.
english: Kwabena Appiah-Pinkrah (born August 23, 1947) is a consultant and Ghanaian politician of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ naae Sakur tita'ar kanɛ anFairleigh Dickson University linɛ bɛ United States of America naasateŋ sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: He is a product of the Fairleigh Dickson University in the United States of America. He holds a Master of Arts in International Studies from the university.

kusaal: Kwabena Appiah-Pinkrah anɛ management nɛ development consultant.Onɛ an zugdaan tis Global Linkages company limited bɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: He is the CEO of Global Linkages Company Limited in Accra.

kusaal: Kwabena Appiah-Pinkrah anɛ Wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Kwabena Appiah-Pinkrah (born August 23, 1947) is a consultant and Ghanaian politician of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔtʋg la ka lieb wadmaan tis Constituency keŋ wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas anaasi nɛ, anu nɛ ayʋobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi linɛ paas Ghana Republic anaasi la ni.
english: He was a member of the Local Government and Rural Development Committee and Government Assurance Committee in the 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Kwabena Appiah-Pinkrah anɛ Kristo pʋ'ʋsʋm nid, o pʋ'ʋsidi Methodist pʋ'ʋsʋm ka.
english: He fellowships with the Methodist Church.

kusaal: Kwabena Donkor (ba da du'a o nɛ 5 fuluŋfuk nwadig 1958) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an minista kʋdʋg kanɛ da gɔsid bugum yɛla.
english: Kwabena Donkor (born February 5, 1958) is a Ghanaian politician and a former Minister for Power.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Donkor nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔsiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii nwadis anu la daba anu daa 05-02-1958, Lonto n bɛ Yeji la, Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Donkor was born on February 5, 1958, in Lonto via Yeji in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr PhD nɛ master's degree dinɛ ka paam yi University of Bristol, nɛ master of business administration, Lancaster University.
english: He holds a PhD and master's degree from the University of Bristol, and a Master of Business Administration from Lancaster University.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2013-2014), Donkor da anɛ minista kanɛ gɔsid labaya yɛla la nya'andɔl.
english: Donkor served as the deputy minister of information from 2013 to 2014.

kusaal: O paas banɛ da pin'il Petroleum Commission ka da aan di tuon gat yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi (2014).
english: He is a founding member of Petroleum Commission and he served as its chief executive officer in 2014.

kusaal: Donkor da nyi'a Pru East kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la ka di.
english: Donkor contested for the seat of the Pru East constituency in the 2016 general elections and won.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Pru East n bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim Ghana nwa.
english: He is a former Member of Parliament for the Pru East constituency, in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Nannanna, o anɛ wadmaani tis Pru-East n bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: He represented the Pru East Constituency in the Bono East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress until 7 January 2021.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔtnam tusa pii nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (13,512) ka li an 56.19% kɔbʋg pʋʋgin.
english: He garnered 13,512 votes which represents 56.19% of the total votes cast and therefore defeated the other contestants including David Amoah, Danjumah Desmond, Noah Ken Boadai and Zevor Mattew Tsiditsey.

kusaal: Donkor anɛ kpɛɛm tis la'askanɛ gɔsid tʋʋma, nidib bɛlim, nɛ gɔmena tʋʋma zin'is, ya'asa, o lɛm paas la'asbanɛ gɔsid wadmaanib yir la suoya dɔlisʋg, o lɛm bɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid sanlimanam nɛ bugum yɛla.
english: Donkor is the Ranking Member of the Employment, Social Welfare and State Enterprises Committee; also a member of the Standing Orders Committee; and also a member of the Mines and Energy Committee.

kusaal: Donkor anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Donkor is a Christian.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan ni ka o lɛn lieb Cabinet minista tis Gaana gɔmena.
english: In that same year, he became a cabinet minister of the Government of Ghana.

kusaal: Kwabena Mintah Akandoh anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd, o anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la nid ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi ti Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni n tis Juaboso linɛ bɛ Western Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Kwabena Mintah Akandoh (born 19 June 1980) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Juaboso Constituency in the Western North Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Sefwi Antobia tempυυg linɛ bɛ Ghana Western Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: He hails from Sefwi Antobia a town in the Western North Region of Ghana.

kusaal: On anɛɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd la zugɔ, ba da gaŋ Akandoh ye o an banɛ gɔsid National Voluntary Programme la kpɛɛm nya'andɔl n bɛ Ankara.
english: Prior to entering politics, Akandoh was assistant director in charge of National Voluntary Programme of the National Service Scheme at its Head Office in Accra.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig kanɛ pʋ'ʋsid Anglican pʋ'ʋsʋm la.
english: He identifies as a Christian and belongs to the Anglican denomination.

kusaal: O da keŋi o sakur n bɛ University of Cape Coast naae ka di'e o digirii kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Kaanlυg nɛ Gɛligir yɛla yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: He obtained his Bachelor of Science in Statistics and Mathematics from the University of Cape Coast in 2007.

kusaal: Akandoh di pu'a mɔr biis anu.
english: Akandoh is married with five children.

kusaal: Kwabena Ohemeng-Tinyase anɛ Ghana pɔlitis wɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la bɛ Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: Kwabena Ohemeng-Tinyase (born 6 April 1952) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Kade Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O mɔr bachelor of Arts degree in Economics nɛ Political Science n yit University of Ghana bɛ yʋʋm 1978.
english: He earned his bachelor of Arts degree in Economics and Political Science from the University of Ghana in 1978.

kusaal: O da lɛn di'e certificate in Charted Accountancy yi Institute of Chartered Accountants Ghana bɛ yʋʋm 2004, nɛ master's digirii in Business Administration yit Warwick University.
english: In 2004, he obtained his certificate in Charted Accountancy from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Ghana, and a master's degree in Business Administration from the University of Warwick.

kusaal: Pɔi ka Ohemeng-Tinyase lieb wadmaan la, o da anɛ chartered Accountant/ country consultant bɛ dunia wʋsa Bank ( Rural and private sector development project, Freetown, Sierra Leone yi yʋʋm 2010 ti paae yʋʋm 2015, consultant with international fund for agricultural development, Freetown, Sierra Leone yi 2015 ti paae 2016.
english: Before Ohemeng-Tinyase was elected as a member of parliament, he was a chartered Accountant/ country consultant with the World Bank Rural and private sector development project, Freetown, Sierra Leone from 2010 to 2015, consultant with international fund for agricultural development, Freetown, Sierra Leone, from 2015 to 2016.

kusaal: Ohemeng-Tinyasa da nyi'ad ye o lieb wadmaan tis Kade constituency n bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid, bɛ yʋʋm 2016 Ghana dim vɔɔdʋg tita'ar la ni ka di, o da paam nɛ vɔɔt kal 33, 442 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o paam vɔɔt kal 69.92% yi vɔɔtnam la ni, ninbanɛ vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: Ohemeng-Tinyasa contested the Kade constituency parliamentary seat in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party during the 2016 Ghanaian general election and won with 33,442 votes, representing 69.92% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da di ka basid George Agyemang Duah onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la mɛ mɔr 14, 088 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋginɛ o paami 29.46% nɛ nɔraug paati la nid Frank Eshun paam 296 vɔɔts 0.62% yi nidib banɛ vɔɔt la ni.
english: He was elected over George Agyemang Duah of the National Democratic Congress, who polled 14,088 votes, which is equivalent to 29.46%, while the parliamentary candidate for the Convention People's Party Frank Eshun had 296 votes, representing 0.62% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Kade Constituency n bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim,o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Kwabena Ohemeng-Tinyase (born 6 April 1952) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Kade Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ohemeng-Tinyase nɛ 6 vaala nwadig 1962 bɛ Kade n bɛ Eastern Region Ghana nwa.
english: Ohemeng-Tinyase was born on 6 April 1952 at Kade in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ohemeng-Tinyase anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nid, ka an wadmaan tis Kade constituency n bɛ Eastern Region Ghana nwa,o paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la bɛ Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi.
english: Ohemeng-Tinyase is a member of the New Patriotic Party and was the member of parliament for Kade constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana in the Seventh Parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ o secondary sakur nɛ Mfantsipim Sakurin.
english: He had his secondary education at the Mfantsipim School.

kusaal: O anɛ Nwabʋg Paati la nid (NPP) ka an Deputy minista tis Aviation Ghana ni.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and the Deputy Minister for Aviation in Ghana.

kusaal: O da paami o Bachelor of Science digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ biochemistry ni yʋʋm 2000 la ni yit Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and technology la ni.
english: He obtained his Bachelor of Science degree in biochemistry in 2000 from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology.

kusaal: O da lɛn paam postgraduate degree democracy nɛ Government nɛ Law nɛ Development yi Cape Coast University la ni na yʋʋm 2006 la ni.
english: He later pursued a postgraduate degree in Democracy, Governance, Law and Development from the University of Cape Coast in 2006.

kusaal: O mɛ da paam kasɛta gbaʋŋi n yit Sangonet, South Africa, nɛ Empretec Ghana.
english: He has also received certificates from Sangonet, South Africa, and EMPRETEC, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Darko-Mensah nɛ 18 sigir nwadig 1974 n bɛ Takoradi teŋin.
english: Darko-Mensah was born on 18 June 1974 in Takoradi.

kusaal: O yinɛ Anwhiankwanta, tenpʋʋg la ni.
english: He hails from Anwhia-Nkwanta in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Aduomi nɛ 17 September 1960 bɛ Ejisu-Besease, Ashanti Region Ghana nwa.
english: Aduomi was born on 17 September 1960 in Ejisu-Besease, Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Aduomi anɛ kristo biig ka an Assemblies of God Ghana pʋ'ʋsʋm nid .O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis ayuobʋ.
english: Aduomi identifies as a Christian and a member of the Assemblies of God Church.

kusaal: O mɔr bachelors of science digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ civil engineering yit Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology yʋʋm 1985.
english: He earned his bachelor of science degree in civil engineering at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology in 1985.

kusaal: Aduomi da anɛ kpɛɛm bɛ maintenance engineer n bɛ highway authority bɛ Temale yi yʋʋm 1987 ti paae yʋʋm 1994, ka tɔlis ti an projects manager bɛ highway authorities n bɛ western region sʋ'ʋlim yi yʋʋm 1994 ti paae yʋʋm 2002.
english: Aduomi became a maintenance engineer at the highway authority in Tamale in 1987–1994, then proceeded to be a projects manager at highway authorities in the western region in 1994–2002.

kusaal: O da mɛ lɛn anɛ kpɛɛm bɛ highways n bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlim yʋʋm 2002 ti paae yʋʋm 2008 la ni.
english: He became the regional director for highways in the Ashanti region in 2002–2008.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt ka o di lieb wadmaan tis Ejisu Constituency n bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana nwa yʋʋm 2009 la ni.
english: He was elected as MP for Ejisu Constituency in the Ashanti Region of Ghana in 2009.

kusaal: O daa gaan o paas subsidiary legislation committee nɛ Local Government and Rural Development Committee.
english: He was selected to join the subsidiary legislation committee and the Local Government and Rural Development Committee.

kusaal: Aduomi da nyi'ad nɛ ye o lieb wadmaan tis Ejisu constituency n bɛ Ashanti Region Ghana nwa, o da zi'enɛ tis wabʋg paati la yʋʋm 2012 Ghana dim vɔɔtʋg tita'ar la ni ka nɛ o di, o da paam nɛ vɔɔt kal 51, 976 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 80.52% yi vɔɔtnam la ni.
english: Aduomi contested for Ejisu constituency parliamentary seat in the Ashanti Region of Ghana on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party in the 2012 Ghanaian general election and won with 51,976 votes representing 80.52% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da di ka basi Augustus Andrew onɛ an ma'asim paati la nid nɛ Isaac Prah onɛ an PPP nɛ Richard Nana Asare onɛ an UFP nɛ Rita Nti-Adjei onɛ an nɔraug paati nid la mɛ Lucy Kazapoe onɛ an PNC la nɛ Kwaku Adusei onɛ an DPP nɛ Lasisi Fatao onɛ an NDP.
english: He was elected over Augustus Andrew of the National Democratic Congress, Isaac Prah of the PPP, Richard Nana Asare of the UFP, Rita Nti-Adjei of the Convention People's Party, Lucy Kazapoe of the PNC, Kwaku Adusei of the DPP and Lasisi Fatao of the NDP.

kusaal: Ba wʋsa da mɔri vɔɔtnam kal 11, 788 vɔɔts, 632 vɔɔts, 155 vɔɔts, 0 vɔɔts, 0 vɔɔts, 0 vɔɔts nɛ 0 vɔɔts.
english: They obtained 11, 788 votes, 632 votes, 155 votes, 0 votes, 0 votes, 0 votes and 0 votes respectively, equivalent to 18.26%, 0.98%, 0.24%, 0.00%, 0.00%, 0.00% and 0.00% of the total votes respectively.

kusaal: Aduomi da lɛn nyi'a ya'as ye o an wadmaan tis Ejisu constituency teŋkanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim la, o da zi'enɛ tis wabʋg paati la, yʋʋm 2016 kanɛ da an Ghana dim vɔɔtʋg tita'ar la ni, o da di ya nɛ vɔɔt kal 54, 508 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 83.79% yi vɔɔtnam la ni.
english: Aduomi again contested for Ejisu constituency parliamentary seat in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party during the 2016 Ghanaian general election and won with 54,508 votes representing 83.79% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da di ka basi Gloria Korshar Huze onɛ da zi'enɛ tis Ma'asim tiig paati la paam vɔɔt kal 9, 485 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋguinvka o mɔr 14.58%, ka PPP na'anyi'adi Isaac Prah mɛ paam vɔɔt kal 859 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 1.32% nɛ Alex Appiah Koree onɛ zi'enɛ tis nɔraug paati paam 200 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o paam 0.31% yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋdin.
english: He won the election over Gloria Korshar Huze of the National Democratic Congress, who polled 9, 485 votes which is equivalent to 14.58%, PPP parliamentary candidate Isaac Prah had 859 votes representing 1.32% and Alex Appiah Koree of the Convention People's Party had 200 votes representing 0.31% of the total votes.

kusaal: Kwabena Owusu Aduomi (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ, nwadisa awai la dabpiinɛ ayɔpɔi daar, (17 senlʋŋ nwadig 1960) ka o an Ghana nid kanɛ an politis wɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan Ghana nwa .O anɛ wabʋg paati la nid (NPP) ka lɛn an Roads and Highways minista nya'andɔl Ghana nwa.
english: Kwabena Owusu Aduomi (born 17 September 1960) is a Ghanaian politician and a Member of Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: O daa yʋ'ʋn liebi wadmaan pass wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayuobʋ bɛ Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi.
english: He then became a member of the 6th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la nid ka lɛn an incumbent Member of Parliament n tis Berekum East.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the incumbent Member of Parliament for Berekum East.

kusaal: O da kɛŋɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, ani ka o da di'e Bachelor of Science in Human Biology kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusa ayi' la ni kɛŋ paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la ni (2000-2003) nɛ Commonwealth Executive Masters in Business Administration (CEMBA), general management lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni ka len an MSc Public Health lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ yinnɛ ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni.
english: He studied at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology where he obtained a Bachelor of Science in Human Biology (2000–2003), a Commonwealth Executive Masters in Business Administration (CEMBA) General Management (2009–2012) and an MSc Public Health (2011–2012).

kusaal: Kwabena twum-Nuamah anɛ kʋkdaan tis Parliament Select Committee of the 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic bɛ Ghana.
english: Twum-Nuamah is the Chairman of the Parliamentary Select Committee of the 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic in Ghana.

kusaal: O da zi'eni tis parliament yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ tan' la ni parliament vɔɔtug linɛ bɛ Berekum West constituency linɛ ka ba da nan maalidi paalimin la.
english: He stood for parliament in the 2013 parliamentary election in the newly formed Berekum West constituency.

kusaal: O da lɛn di o kʋk bɛ Ghanaian parliamentary vɔɔtug la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayobʋ la ni.
english: He retained his seat in the Ghanaian parliamentary election of 2016.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo nid(Methodist).
english: He is a Christian (Methodist).
