english: He is the current member of parliament for the Sene West Constituency (from 2012 to date).

kusaal: Kwamena Minta Nyarku anɛ Gaana pɔlittiks nwɛ'ɛd ba da du'anɛ Buniya nwarig la ni li daba yɔpɔi yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi la ni, o anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Kwamena Minta Nyarku (born 7 December 1974) is a Ghanaian academic and politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Cape Coast North linɛ bɛ Gaana Central Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Cape Coast North Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Apewosika, linɛ bɛ Gaana Cape Coast sυ'υlυm Central Region la.
english: He hails from Apewosika, Cape Coast in Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da naae o sakur linɛ an GCE Ordinary level nɛ GCE Advanced level la nɛ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ ayi n naae li yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ ayuobu la ni n bɛ Adisadel College sakur, linɛ bɛ Cape Coast la.
english: He completed his GCE Ordinary level and GCE Advanced level certificate in Business in 1992 and 1996 respectively at Adisadel College, Cape Coast.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi Komenda Training College naae ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ pa'alυg gbaυŋ linɛ an yυυma tan' Post Sec Teacher Cert yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ anu la ni.
english: He further moved to the Komenda Training College completing with a Teacher Certificate A (3 year Post Sec Teacher Cert A) in 1995.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' la ni, ka o da naae bachelor's digirɛɛ zamisυg linɛ an Business Education n bɛ University of Cape Coast sakurin la.
english: In 2000, he completed a bachelor's degree in education with emphasis on Business Education at the University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: O da lɛn keŋ University of Ghana Business Sakur la ni n naae mɔr Masters of Business Administration (MBA) zamisυg linɛ an da' diib yɛla la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ atan' la ni.
english: He went on to the University of Ghana Business School, graduating with a Master of Business Administration (MBA) in Marketing in 2003.

kusaal: O da lɛn keŋ University of Leicester ya'as, ani ka o maal Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) zamisυg kpazɛɛri linɛ an da' diib yɛla yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina wai la ni ka mɛ lɛn maal Chartered Institute of Marketing n bɛ United Kingdom.
english: He is also a graduate of the University of Leicester, where he completed with a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Marketing in 2019 and the Chartered Institute of Marketing in the United Kingdom.

kusaal: Nyarku anɛ pa'an-pa'an kpɛɛm n bɛ Chain Management, School of Business, University of Cape Coast,Ghana n pa'an kati wa'ae linɛ tɔlυŋ nɛ da' diib yɛla.
english: Nyarku is a Senior Lecturer at the Department of Marketing and Supply Chain Management, School of Business, University of Cape Coast, Ghana.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ yinne ka ba da wa'al Nyarku ka o kpɛn' wadmaanib yir la ni n zi'enɛ tis Cape Coast North kυk la wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anii la ti Gaana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la.
english: Nyarku was sworn into office as the Member of Parliament representing the Cape Coast North Constituency in the 8th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana on 7 January 2021.

kusaal: Onɛ an Poverty Reduction Strategy kpɛɛmnam yinne.
english: He serves as a member on the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee.

kusaal: Ba du'a Nyarku nɛ Buniya nwarig la ni li daba yɔpɔi yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi la ni.
english: Nyarku was born on 7 December 1974.

kusaal: Nyarku anɛ Kristo biig Nidib wυsa mi' o nɛ ye Ragga.
english: He is popularly known referred to by his nickname Ragga.

kusaal: Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh (du'am; samanpiid nwadig 6, 1966) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tis Sunyani East sʋ'ʋlim dim, ka paas Ghana wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anu la, Republic kanɛ aan anaasi la ni.
english: Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh (born November 6, 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and was the member of parliament for the Sunyani East constituency in the 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th parliament of the 4th republic.

kusaal: O yinɛ Jinijini, tenkanɛ bɛ Brong Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Jinijini, a town in the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ University of Ghana ka di'e o Master of Philosophy degree in Public Administration yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii la ni (2008).
english: He entered the University of Ghana and obtained his Master of Philosophy degree in public administration in 2008.

kusaal: O da lɛn keŋ Lɔyanam sakur (Ghana wada sakur) ka di'e o Bachelor of Laws kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la ni (1995).
english: He also attended Ghana School of Law and obtained his Bachelor of Laws in 1995.

kusaal: O da lɛn keŋ Galilee College bɛ Israel la, ka naae anina yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii la ni (2008).
english: He has also attended the Galilee College in Israel and graduated with the 2008 class.

kusaal: Ameyaw-Cheremeh anɛ kʋkdaan (Board Chairman) tis Bui Power Authority.
english: Ameyaw-Cheremeh is currently serving as the board chairman of Bui Power Authority.

kusaal: O da anɛ gbansɔbidi tis National Association of Local Authorities of Ghana (NALAG).
english: He served as the general secretary at the National Association of Local Authorities of Ghana (NALAG).

kusaal: O da mɔri vɔɔtnam tusa pistan' nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu (33,765) yit vɔɔtnam tusa pisnu nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anaasi (53,844), ka li an pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi' du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (62.71%).
english: He obtained 33,765 votes of 53,844 total valid votes cast, equivalent to 62.71% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt tis o ka bas Alanyina Sampana Sampson onɛ an People's National Convention, nɛ Justice Samuel Adjei onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la, nɛ Peter Kwaw Alibah onɛ an Democratic Freedom Party nɛ Kwakye Kofi onɛ bɛ Anɔraʋg na'adɔɔg la.
english: He was elected over Alanyina Sampana Sampson of the People's National Convention, Justice Samuel Adjei of the National Democratic Congress, Peter Kwaw Alibah of the Democratic Freedom Party and Kwakye Kofi of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Bama wʋsa kɔbʋg pʋʋgin kal da anɛ yinne du'al pisi nɛ anu (1.25%), piatan' nɛ anaasi du'al piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (34.97%), nɛɛm du'al pisi nɛ awai (0.29%) nɛ nɛɛm du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (0.78%) vɔɔtnam la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: These obtained 1.25%, 34.97%, 0.29% and 0.78% respectively of all total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la pʋʋgin, (2012), o da lɛn zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zugʋ nyi'a Sunyani East constituency kʋk la ka ba vɔɔt tis o ka o keŋ paas Ghana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayuobʋ la tis Sunyani East constituency.
english: In 2012, he contested again for the Sunyani East constituency seat on the ticket of the NPP for the sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: On da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug la, (NPP) o da paam vɔɔtnam tusa pisnaasi nɛ ayi' nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (42,478) yit vɔɔtnam tusa pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pii nɛ anii (71,918) ka li an pisnu nɛ awai du'al ayuobʋ kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (59.06%) yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la.
english: As a New Patriotic Party (NPP) member, he obtained 42,478 votes out of the 71,918 valid votes cast representing 59.06% of the total votes cast in the 2012 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Ameyaw-Cheremeh anɛ kʋkdaani tis la'askanɛ gɔsid wada tʋʋma yɛla (Judiciary Committee); o paas banɛ gɔsid Wadmaanib yinsuor dɔlisʋg (Standing Orders Committee); o lɛn paas banɛ gɔsid wada gbana nɛ wada tʋʋma nɛ Wadmaanib yir bɛlim yɛla (Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Committee); ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yɛla (Education Committee la ni.
english: Ameyaw-Cheremeh was the chairperson for the Judiciary Committee; a member of the Standing Orders Committee; a member of the Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Committee; and a member of the Education Committee.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ameyaw-Cheremeh nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ la nwadis pii nɛ yinne la daba ayuobʋ daar (sapal nwadig 6, 1966).
english: Ameyaw-Cheremeh was born on November 6, 1966.

kusaal: Ameyaw-Cheremeh paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (NPP) la ni.
english: Ameyaw-Cheremeh is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii 2008 Ghana gil vɔɔtʋg la ye o lieb Wadmaani tis Sunyani East Constituency Ghana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anu la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi Anaasi la ni.
english: The 2024 parliamentary election in the Sunyani East Constituency marked a significant political shift as the incumbent New Patriotic Party (NPP) Member of Parliament (MP), Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh, lost his seat to Seid Mubarak of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ majority chief whip ya'as.
english: He served in the Parliament of Ghana for Sunyani East constituency and as the house majority chief whip.

kusaal: Ameyaw-Cheremeh anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Ameyaw-Cheremeh is a Christian.

kusaal: O mɔr pu'a nɛ biis anaasi.
english: He is married, and has four children.

kusaal: Kwasi Anin-Yeboah JSC da nyɛ dunia nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ atan', nwadis anu, dabisa pisi' nɛ anaaasi daar (born 24 May 1953) ka o anɛ piiyam (judge) Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, one da an piiyamnam kpɛɛm (Chief Justice of Ghana).
english: Kwasi Anin-Yeboah (born 24 May 1953) is a Ghanaian judge and a former Chief Justice of Ghana.

kusaal: Anin Yeboah tɛŋ dʋadʋg anɛ Toase linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnu nɛ atan', nwadis anu, dabisa pisi' nɛ anaaasi daar (24 May 1953).
english: Anin-Yeboah was born in Toase in Ashanti Region of Ghana on 24 May 1953.

kusaal: O da pin'il sakur kɛnnɛ Amaniampong Secondary School nɛ Apam Secondary School lin da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi ne ayuobʋ la ni (1968 to 1976).
english: He attended Amaniampong Secondary School and Apam Secondary School from 1968 to 1976.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi kɛŋ University of Ghana ka lin nya'aŋ ka o kɛŋ wada zamisʋg sakur kanɛ an Ghana School of Law, naae lin yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne la (1981).
english: He then continued his education at the University of Ghana and later the Ghana School of Law, graduating in 1981.

kusaal: On da naae wada zamisʋg sakur la, o da an Assistant state Attorney bɛ Attorney General tʋʋma nii bɛ Koforidua sʋ'ʋlim.
english: After graduating from law school he served as an assistant state attorney at the Attorney General's Office in Koforidua.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ tuoni anɛ onɛ paas Koforidua kɔɔtɔ tʋʋma linɛ an Afisem Chambers.
english: He proceeded to work as a partner at the Koforidua branch of Afisem Chambers.

kusaal: O da tʋm kɔɔtɔ tʋʋma linɛ an Justice of the High Court lin da yi yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ ayi' kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ atan' (2002 to 2003) nɛ kɔɔtɔ kanɛ buon Court of Appeal lin yi yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ atan' kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ anii (2003 to 2008) Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: He served as a Justice of the High Court from 2002 to 2003 and the Court of Appeal from 2003 to 2008 in Ghana.

kusaal: Justice Anin Yeboah da nɔk ya'am kanɛ da o mɔr wada pʋʋgin la paae nɔba diema dim sa'an, o tɛŋin, bozugo o da an ba tuongat tɛŋkpɛmisin nɛ Ghana wʋsa ni, o da an banɛ tɛɛgid nɔba diema dim tʋba linɛe an Disciplinary Committee tis nɛ Eastern Region Football Association (FA) nɛ Appeal Committee bɛnɛ Ghana Football Association lin da yi yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ anaasi kɛŋ paae tusayi' nɛ anii (2004 to 2008).
english: Anin-Yeboah has also provided his legal experience to football in his country, serving as chairman both locally and nationally, as the Disciplinary Committee for the Eastern Region Football Association (FA) and Appeal Committee at the Ghana Football Association from 2004 to 2008.

kusaal: Nannanna onɛ an chairman of the Legal Aid Board nɛ Chairman of the Disciplinary Committee of The General Legal Council of Ghana.
english: He is currently the chairman of the Legal Aid Board and Chairman of the Disciplinary Committee of the General Legal Council of Ghana.

kusaal: President John Kufuor da gaŋ Anin-Yeboah ye o kɛŋ kɔɔtɔ kanɛ gat kɔɔtɔnam wʋsa ka ti buon Supreme Court of Ghana nɛ yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ anii, nwadis ayuobu la ni (June 2008).
english: Anin-Yeboah was appointed to the Supreme Court of Ghana by President John Kufuor in June 2008.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ awai, naar nwadig la ni (December 2019), zugraan Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Justice Anin-Yeboah ye o die Sophia Akuffo nobir an piiyam nam kpɛɛm bɛ Supreme Court of Ghana.
english: In December 2019, President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo nominated Justice Anin-Yeboah to replace Sophia Akuffo as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: Saŋkanɛ ka ba daa vɛn'ɛsid ye ba gɔs ye o na nyaŋi tʋm tʋʋma la bɛɛ o kʋ nyaŋ bɛ la, onɛ an Executive Director for the Alliance for Social Equity and Public Accountability (ASEPA), Mensah Thompson da pʋ siakɛ, o da bɔɔd ye Ghana wada maanib gʋ'ʋm Justice Anin Yeboah vɛn'ɛsʋg nwa' ka lʋgʋr kanɛ buon CHRAJ la nyaŋi naae ba vɛn'ɛsʋg o yelaa naae.
english: His vetting was opposed by the Executive Director for the Alliance for Social Equity and Public Accountability (ASEPA), Mensah Thompson who wanted Parliament to put on hold, the vetting of Justice Anin Yeboah to allow for CHRAJ to complete investigations on a petition against the nominee.

kusaal: O vɛɛnsʋg la da naae la, CHRAJ dim da gɔs ka o da dɔl Ghana wada pʋʋgin, wada kɔbʋsyi' nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (article 286), da tʋas o mɔrim wʋsa tis nɛ auditor general.
english: At the end of the preliminary investigations the commission finds as a fact that the respondent has complied with article 286 of the constitution by declaring his assets and liabilities to the auditor general.

kusaal: Akuffo-Addo da nwɛ' suora nɛ the Council of State ka gaŋ Anin Yeboah wɛnnɛ Ghana wada linɛ an Constitution of Ghana siak siem la, ye o an piiyam nam kpɛɛm Ghana sʋ'ʋlim dɔlis wada maanib Parliament of Ghana da vɛn'ɛs o yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ awai, naar nwadig la ni (December 2019).
english: Anin Yeboah whose appointment by Akuffo-Addo was in consultation with the Council of State as stipulated by the Constitution of Ghana was approved as the Chief Justice of the Republic of Ghana by the Parliament of Ghana after vetting in December 2019.

kusaal: Justice Anin Yeboah da an one paas piiga nɛ anaasi nii die ya'an kan (14th Chief Justice) bɛ Supreme Court of Ghana yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ pisi, pin'ilig nwadig, daba ayɔpɔii daar la (7 January 2020).
english: Justice Anin Yeboah was sworn in as the 14th Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana on 7 January 2020.

kusaal: Linɛ lɛn paas o tʋʋma on an piiyamnam kpɛɛm tis nɛ Supreme Court la anɛ ye o lɛn anɛ pa'anpa'an saŋ sieba (Part-Time) bɛnɛ Ghana School of Law anina ka o pa'an Ghana wada yɛla nɛ nidib bellim an siem.
english: In addition to his work as a Justice of the Supreme Court he also serves as a Part-Time lecturer at the Ghana School of Law where he teaches Civil procedure and Ghana Legal System.

kusaal: FIFA anɛ tɛns bɛdɛgɔ nɔba diema la'asʋg kpɛɛmanam banɛ mɔr diema bedego li yinne an dunia wʋsa nɔba kikiid diema (World up).
english: FIFA is an international soccer's governing body and organizer of global tournaments including the World up.

kusaal: Li da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ anaasi la ni (1904).
english: It was founded in 1904.

kusaal: La'asʋg kpɛɛm tisnɛ FIFA Ethics Committee, lʋgʋr kanɛe gɔsid FIFA wada gɛsigir yɛla.
english: Chairman of the FIFA Ethics Committee, a body primarily responsible for investigating possible infringements of the FIFA Code of Ethics.

kusaal: Anin Yeboah tʋm tis ninsabilis nɔba diema linɛ an all Confederation of African Footb(CAF).
english: Anin Yeboah has also served in the Confederation of African Football (CAF)

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ awai, nwadis awai la ni (September 2019), ba da gaŋ o ye o an CAF/FIFA Reform Implementation Taskforce team tis ninsabilis sʋ'ʋlim nɔba diema.
english: In September 2019, he was named onto the CAF/FIFA Reform Implementation Taskforce team for African football.

kusaal: Ghana Bar Association, daa mɔr diema tis o linɛ buon ye ti pʋ'ʋs ya la, zugraan Nana Akufo-Addo daa pian'a o yɛla ye o anɛ ka o tʋʋma saŋa daa mɔr girima tisid banɛ tʋm Ghana wada tʋʋma wʋsa.
english: During a farewell party organised by the Ghana Bar Association, the president, Nana Akufo-Addo described him as one whose tenure brought honour to the Judiciary.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ awai la, naar nwadig la (December 2019), ka Ghana zugraan Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Justice Anin-Yeboah ye o an piiyamnam kpɛɛm Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: In December 2019, President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo nominated Justice Anin-Yeboah as the Chief Justice of Ghana.

kusaal: Justice Anin Yeboah anɛ one paas anaasi piiyam banɛ tʋm kɔɔtɔ kanɛ gat kɔɔtɔ nam wʋsa Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la ka li yʋʋgi gaadi ba taaba.
english: In December 2019, President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo nominated Justice Anin-Yeboah to replace Sophia Akuffo as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: John Mahama da bu siak vɔɔtʋg la da naae siem la, bozugo o da yɛl ye on nya'ad na'am la nɛ Nana Akufo-Addo nɛ o taaba ba banɛ kpɛlim anii la wʋsa baa yinne pʋ nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋ kɔbʋga pʋʋgin pʋsʋk ka mɔr pa'alʋg yinne (50%+1), Ghana wada yel siem ye ba paae siem bɛn ka yaan di' ya'an la.
english: John Mahama was challenging the election on the basis that his contender Nana Akufo-Addo and the other eight presidential candidates did not attain the mandatory 50%+1 vote constitutional threshold to be declared the winner of the polls.

kusaal: Justice Anin-Yeboah's Legal baŋir paae nɛ on na kat saria dɔlis wada pʋʋgin nɛ nidib bellimin nɛ tʋʋmbɛɛd yɛla nam ni.
english: Justice Anin-Yeboah's Legal experience includes writing judgement in constitutional matters, civil and criminal cases.

kusaal: O da anɛ kɔɔtɔ tʋmtʋm tis Adjudicatory chamber of FIFA ka li nya'aŋ ka ba gaŋ o yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi, nwadis anu la ni (May 2017), ka o an kpɛɛm tis nɛ la'asʋg kanɛ buon Disciplinary Committee linɛ paas pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi la (67th) FIFA Congress bɛ Bahrain.
english: He is currently the chairman of the Legal Aid Board and Chairman of the Disciplinary Committee of the General Legal Council of Ghana.

kusaal: One an la'asʋg kpɛɛm nannanna tis Legal aid board.
english: He is also the current Chairman of the Legal aid board.

kusaal: Anin Yeboah officially daa paae o tʋʋma bɛn ka kul ye o vʋ'ʋs nɛ o duam dabisir linɛ an yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ pisi nɛ atan', nwadis anu, dabisa pisi' nɛ anaasi la (24 May 2023).
english: Anin Yeboah officially retired from Judiciary service on his birthday 24 May 2023.

kusaal: O nɔɔr pian'ak la nwa; "Chief Justice Anin-Yeboah anɛ tuongat kanɛ bɛɛ o kɔn' tis banɛ tʋm wada tʋʋma wʋsa.
english: According to him; "Chief Justice Anin-Yeboah has been an exceptional leader to the judiciary.

kusaal: Li mɔr tɛn'ɛs kɔbʋsyi' nɛ piiga nɛ yinnɛ (211).
english: It has a membership of 211.

kusaal: Ka an wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yir linɛ paas Ayɔpɔi ti Ghana Republic kanɛ aan anaasi la ni n tis New Juaben north linɛ bɛ Eastern Region, O anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Kwasi Boateng Adjei (born August 29, 1954) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the New Juaben North Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Onɛ da an Minista for Local Government nɛ onɛ gɔsid tenkpikpɛmis maalʋg la kpɛɛm nya'andɔl yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: A Deputy Minister for Local Government and Rural Development from 2017 to Date.

kusaal: O yinɛ Asokore – New Juaben tempυυg linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: He hails from Asokore – New Juaben, a town in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ University of Ghana naae ka di'e o kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Bachelor of Science degree in business administration yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii la ni.
english: He entered University of Ghana and obtained his Bachelor of Science degree in business administration in 1980.

kusaal: Yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni ka o da zi'en Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zugu nyi'a di New Juaben North wadmaanib kυk la n bɛ wadmaanib yir linɛ da paas ayuobʋ republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: In 2012, he contested for the New Juaben North seat on the ticket of the NPP sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: Onɛ da anɛ New Juaben College of Commerce la tuongat, n bɛ Koforidua sʋ'ʋlʋm .
english: He had his secondary education at Ghana Senior High School, Koforidua.

kusaal: Adjei anɛ Kristo biig, Methodist karimbiig.
english: Adjei is a Christian (Methodist).

kusaal: Kwasi Boateng Adjei anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Kwasi Boateng Adjei (born August 29, 1954) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the New Juaben North Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Adjei anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Adjei is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O di pu'a mɔr biis atan'.
english: He is married, and has three children.

kusaal: Kwasi Etu-Bonde anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi tis Kintampo North linɛ bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la o anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Kwasi Etu-Bonde is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Kintampo North Constituency in the Bono East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2019 la ni, ka ba da gaŋ o ye wadmaanib la ni wʋsa, onɛ an onɛ paas ayi' ka o tʋʋma an sʋm galis n bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni.
english: In 2019, he was ranked the 2nd Best Performing Member of Parliament in the Bono East Region.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Etu-Bonde bɛnɛ Vume linɛ bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana la.
english: Kwasi Etu-Bonde born in Vume in the Volta Region of Ghana on October 13, 1968 is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Kintampo North Constituency in the Brong-Ahafo Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Etu-Bonde da zamis linɛ an GIMPA linɛ an (SME, Nɔbigir nɛ Zanlim sʋŋ yɛla la) ani ka ba tis o kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an EMBA yʋʋma 2004 la ni.
english: Etu-Bonde studied at the GIMPA (SME, Development and Management) where he received an EMBA in 2004.

kusaal: Etu-Bonde tʋmnɛ an entrepreneur ka an onɛ su'oe SKY-3 Investments Limited and Sustenance Agro Ventures linɛ bɛ Kintampo la.
english: Etu-Bonde is an entrepreneur and CEO of SKY-3 Investments Limited and Sustenance Agro Ventures located in Kintampo.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 2015 la ka o da zi'enɛ nya'a nɛ o taaba banɛ bɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la ni ka di n bɛ Kintampo North linɛ bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana la.
english: In 2015 he contested and won the NDC parliamentary primaries for Kintampo North constituency in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Joseph Kwame Kumah onɛ da an Ma'asim Tiig nid onɛ da an wadmaan bɛ Kintampo North ka da bas ka tʋʋm la ka o da di'e o nɔbir.
english: He was succeeded by Joseph Kwame Kumah during the National Democratic Congress primaries in the Kintampo North Constituency after he declined to contest.

kusaal: Ka yʋʋma 2016 vɔt kanɛ ka Ghana dim da maal la ka o nya'a di.
english: He won this parliamentary seat during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O da paamnɛ vɔt bam 22,407 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 53.89% n yi vɔt kanl wʋsa ni ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid Nkangmah Mateerl Charles mɔr vɔt bam 17,610 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 42.36% vɔt kanl wʋsa ni.
english: He won with 22,407 votes making 53.89% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Nkangmah Mateerl Charles had 17,610 votes making 42.36% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Etu-Bonde di pu'a mɔr biis anu.
english: Etu-Bonde is married with five children.

kusaal: Etu-Bonde anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Etu-Bonde is a Christian.

kusaal: Kweku George Ricketts-Hagan anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Ghana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni zi'eni tis Cape Coast South Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Central Region la dim ka bɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔgin la (NDC).
english: Kweku George Ricketts-Hagan (born 1963) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Cape Coast South Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ricketts-Hagan nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan', Nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ yinne daar (21 mɔtul nwadig 1963) Cape Coast bɛ Central Region, Ghana la.
english: Ricketts-Hagan was born on 21 August 1963 in Cape Coast in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr MBA kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit University of Chicago Business School nɛ master's degree in Financial Economics kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit University of London.
english: He holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Business School and a master's degree in Financial Economics from the University of London.

kusaal: Ricketts-Hagan da anɛ kpɛɛmtita'ar (managing director) tis SAS Finance Group.
english: Ricketts-Hagan was the managing director of SAS Finance Group.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) kanɛ da an Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la, o da di Cape Coast South Constituency Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔtnam tusa pisi nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (20,456) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ awai du'ali anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (49.8%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin, ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (NPP) nid Michael Arthur Dadzie mɛ paam vɔɔtnam tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pii nɛ anii (19,718) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (48.0% ), ka PPP nid Bright Edem Droefenu da paam vɔɔtnam kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (606) dinɛ an yinne du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.5%), ka Mr.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, he won the Cape Coast South Constituency parliamentary seat with 20,456 votes making 49.8% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Michael Arthur Dadzie had 19,718 votes making 48.0% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Bright Edem Droefenu had 606 votes making 1.5% of the total votes cast, an Independent parliamentary candidate Mr. Albert Isaac Kofi Cobbinah had 203 votes making 0.5% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Ato Aidoo-Nyanor had 78 votes making 0.2% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ(2016) kanɛ da an Ghana wʋsa vɔɔdʋg la, o da di Cape Coast South Constituency Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pii nɛ anii ((21,118) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.7%) vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka, ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid Ernest Arthur da paam vɔɔt tʋsa pii nɛ awai nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (19,714) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ anii du'ali atan' kɔbiga pʋʋgin (48.3%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he again won the Cape Coast South Constituency parliamentary seat with 21,118 votes making 51.7% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Ernest Arthur had 19,714 votes making 48.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O da lɛn an minista kanɛ gɔsid Ghana ligidi yɛla nya'andɔl di yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' la ni (2013) ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (2014) ka lɛn an Trade and Industries minista nya'andɔl yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (2014) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: He served in the Government of Ghana ministry as the deputy minister for Finance from 2013 to 2014 and the deputy minister for Trade and Industries from 2014 to 2016.

kusaal: Ricketts-Hagan anɛ kpɛɛm bɛ la'akanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Privileges Committee la, o lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid dap, pʋ'ab nɛ biis bɛlim yɛla ka lɛn bɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid kpikpiŋ nɛ duorim / zin'ivɛnla yɛla la.
english: Ricketts-Hagan is a Ranking Member of the Privileges Committee, also a member of the Gender and Children Committee and also a member of the Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee.

kusaal: Ernest Arthur onɛ da an Diisi (Metropolitan Chief Executive) tis Cape Coast la da mɔr Ricketts-Hagani keŋ kɔɔtʋ ye o san'ami o yʋ'ʋr.
english: In October 2021, Ricketts-Hagan was sued by Mr. Ernest Arthur who was the Metropolitan Chief Executive for Cape Coast for his defamatory comments made against him.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn kɛ ka Ricketts-Hagan yɔ Gaana siidi tusa kɔbiga (GH¢100,000).
english: Ricketts-Hagan was also charged GH¢100,000.

kusaal: Ricketts-Hagan anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Ricketts-Hagan is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Nannanna o anɛ Wadmaani tis Cape Coast South Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: He is currently the member of parliament representative for the Cape Coast South Constituency.

kusaal: Albert Isaac Kofi Cobbinah onɛ da pʋ mɔr Na'adɔɔg la da paam vɔɔtnam kɔbisyi nɛ atan' (203) dinɛ an nɛɛm du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.5%), ka Anɔraʋg Na'adɔɔg nid Ato Aidoo-Nyanor da paam vɔɔt pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (78) dinɛ an nɛɛm du'ali ayi' kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (0.2%).
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, he won the Cape Coast South Constituency parliamentary seat with 20,456 votes making 49.8% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Michael Arthur Dadzie had 19,718 votes making 48.0% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate Bright Edem Droefenu had 606 votes making 1.5% of the total votes cast, an Independent parliamentary candidate Mr. Albert Isaac Kofi Cobbinah had 203 votes making 0.5% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Ato Aidoo-Nyanor had 78 votes making 0.2% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuonʋ (2016) la ni la, Ricketts-Hagan da lieb Central Region sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa minista.
english: In 2016, Ricketts-Hagan became the minister of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ricketts-Hagan anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Ricketts-Hagan is a Ranking Member of the Privileges Committee, also a member of the Gender and Children Committee and also a member of the Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee.

kusaal: Cape Coast High Court da yɛl Ricketts-Hagan ye o yisim pian'akanɛ ka o pian'a la ka nwɛ' Mr.
english: Ricketts-Hagan was asked by the Cape Coast High Court to retract and apologize to Mr. Arthur.

kusaal: Kwasi Amoako-Attah anɛ lɔya n bɛ Ghana, o anɛ management consultant ka mɛ an pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd, ba da du'a o nɛ Burya nya'aŋ nwaris anii la li daba anu daar yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnu nɛ yinne la ni.
english: Kwasi Amoako-Attah (born 5 August 1951) is a Ghanaian lawyer, management consultant and politician.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Atiwa West linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: He is the Member of Parliament of the Atiwa West constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Kwesi Amoako Atta nɛ Burnya nya'aŋ nwaris anii la li daba anu daar yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnu nɛ yinne la ni n bɛ Akyem-Awenare teŋ linɛ bɛ ti Ghana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Kwesi Amoako Atta was born on 5 August 1951 at Akyem-Awenare in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ o sakur bɛnɛ Abuakwa State College la ni naae ka di'e o kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an GCE Ordinary Level , ka tɔlisi Tarkwa Senior High Sakur la ni naae ka di'e o kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an GCE Advanced Level.
english: He attended Abuakwa State College where he received his GCE Ordinary Level certificate and continued to Tarkwa Senior High School for his GCE Advanced Level certificate.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maali o Bachelor of science Digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit University of Ghana Legon.
english: He obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Administration from the University of Ghana, Legon.

kusaal: Ka lin nya'aŋ ka o tɔlis n keŋ Ghana School of Law, Makola n zamis wada yɛla ka yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ ayi' la ni ka ba buol o paas ti Ghana wada mi'ilim lυgυr dim la ni.
english: He then proceeded to the Ghana School of Law, Makola and was called to the Ghana Bar in 2002.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Executive Master of Business Administration n yit University of Ghana sakur la ni.
english: He obtained an Executive Master of Business Administration from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Atta n da naae University of Ghana la, ka Meat Marketing Board da nɔk o ye o an regional manager lin da yi yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai n ti paae yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu la ni.
english: After graduation from the University of Ghana, Atta was employed from 1979 to 1985 at the now defunct Meat Marketing Board as a regional manager.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o kena tυm nɛ Unilever Ghana dim ani ka ba nɔk o ye o an manager nɛ zugdaan of logistics and marketing tυυma la ni.
english: He then joined Unilever Ghana, where he was first made the brands manager then head of logistics and marketing.

kusaal: Ban da buol o paas wada mi'ilim lυgυr dim la ni la, o da bɛnɛ gɔsid wada yɛla tυυma dɔɔgin, li pυ yυυgɛ ka ba gaŋ o ye o an banɛ gɔsid wada yɛla la wυsa sa'an-sa'an n tis Vlisco Ghana Group la.
english: When he was called to the Ghana Bar, he joined the legal department, where he rose to Group Legal Advisor of Vlisco Ghana Group.

kusaal: On nɛ nidiba atan' da nyi'ad, ba yυda anɛ, Emmanuel Atta Twum onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid nɛ George Padmore Apreku onɛ an New Vision Party nid nɛ Kasum Abdul-Karim onɛ mɛ da an People's National Convention la ni, ban da maligim ye ba vɔɔt gaŋ wadmman la, vɔɔt la da maali Burnya nya'aŋ nwadis anii la li dabisim pistan' nɛ yinne daar yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ piiga la ni.
english: Three other candidates, namely Emmanuel Atta Twum of the National Democratic Congress, George Padmore Apreku of the New Vision Party, and Kasum Abdul-Karim of the People's National Convention also contested in the 2010 by-election of Atiwa held on 31 August 2010.

kusaal: Ban da vɔɔt naae la ka Atta di, o da mɔri vɔɔt kal 20,282 n yit vɔɔt la kanl wυsa linɛ da an 27,540 la ni, ka kɔbʋg pυυgin, o da mɔri 75.0% .
english: Atta won the election by obtaining 20,282 votes out of 27,540 cast, representing 75.0 percent of total valid votes.

kusaal: Burnya nya'aŋ nwadig yinne la yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ka ti Ghana Gɔmena Nana Akuffo-Addo da gaŋ Atta ye o an Minista kanɛ na gɔsidi ti suoya nam yɛla.
english: In January 2017, President Nana Akuffo-Addo nominated Atta for the position of Minister of Roads and Highways in Ghana.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris ayuobu la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yɔpɔi la ni ka o da yɔ'ɔg tadim nam tυυma linɛ da buon ye Disability Road Toll Initiative.
english: In July 2017 he launched the Persons with Disability Road Toll Initiative.

kusaal: O anɛ Presbyterian karimbiig.
english: He is a member of the Presbyterian Church of Ghana.

kusaal: Nannana, onɛ an ti Ghana Minista kanɛ gɔsidi ti suoya yɛla la.
english: He is a former Ghana's Minister for Roads and Highways.

kusaal: Atta kpɛn' pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb nɛ Yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga la ni ka o da zi'enɛ nyi'a Atiwa West sυ'υlυm wadmaanib kυk la.
english: Atta entered the Ghanaian political scene in 2010 when he contested the Atiwa West seat.

kusaal: Ba yɛl Atta ye o gɔsim ka tempυυgin suoya la wυsa maal ka li kas-kas anɛ suobanɛ ka ti Ghana kpaarib dɔl.
english: Atta was tasked with improving urban and feeder roads in the country, especially those in Ghana's agricultural belt.

kusaal: Wadmaanib yir kpɛɛmnam la da buoli Atta nɛ Burnya nya'aŋ nwadis ayi' li daba ayi' daar yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni vɛɛns o yɛla n gɔsi gaŋ o ye tυm o Minista tυυma la.
english: The Appointments Committee of Parliament met Atta on 2 February 2017 and vetted him on his vision for the ministry.

kusaal: Akuffo-Addo da wa'alim Minista nam la wυsa Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris ayi' la li dabisim piiaga yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yɔpɔi la ni ye ba paas wadmaanib yir la ni.
english: Akuffo-Addo swore in all the ministers who had been approved by Parliament on 10 February 2017.

kusaal: Atta mɛn da paas Minista nam ban piiga banɛ ka ba da gaŋ ye ba si'iŋ tυυma la ni.
english: Atta was among ten other ministers who received their ministerial charters to begin work in their various ministries.

kusaal: Atta di pu'a du'a biis anaasi.
english: Atta is married with four children.

kusaal: Atta da yina yɛl ye ba na nɔk tadim bam tusa yi' (200) ya'as ka ba tυm.
english: Atta reiterated the fact that a total of 200 persons with disabilities would be employed under the initiative.

kusaal: Nannanna o anɛ Minista kanɛ gɔsidi ti suoya yɛla la.
english: He is currently the Minister for Roads and Highways.

kusaal: O anɛ ninkanɛ ka ba mi'i o pamm ka buon o ye, Darwin kʋkɔr, Gumball zua sunf nɛ Cartoon Newyork animated TV series linɛ ka ba buon ye Amazing World of Gumball la tʋm-tʋm yinne.
english: He is best known as the original voice of Darwin, Gumball's best friend and adoptive brother on the Cartoon Network animated TV series The Amazing World of Gumball.

kusaal: Onɛ da an biig o saam biis atan' la wʋsa ni; ba da anɛ Kwame Boateng, nɛ Kofi Siriboe.
english: Kwesi Nii-Lante Boakye is the youngest of three brothers who are also actors; Kwame Boateng, and Kofi Siriboe.

kusaal: Boakye's buudi bɛɛ o yidim da yinɛ Ghana na.
english: Boakye's family is originally from Ghana.

kusaal: Boakye da pin'il sini maalig ka an yʋma yuobʋ, o da paasi maal sini banɛ an television di'ema ka ba buon Strong Medicine nɛ Inconceivable.
english: Boakye began his acting career at the age of six, making one-episode appearances on the television shows Strong Medicine and Inconceivable.

kusaal: O da paasi maal sininam ban piinɛ nii bɛ NBC soap opera series linɛ buon Days of Our Lives.
english: He then appeared in eighteen episodes of the NBC soap opera series Days of Our Lives.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ la (2006), o da paasi maal sini kanɛ buon Day Break la nɔɔr ayuobʋ ka ba buon o anina ye James Mathis.
english: In 2006, he appeared in five episodes of Day Break as James Mathis.

kusaal: O da pin'ili paasid o kʋkɔr sini pʋʋgin on da an yʋma ayɔpɔi la, anina ka o nɔk o kʋkɔri paas sini kanɛ ka' nidibi maalɛ ni ka ba buon Happy Feet.
english: He then began his voice acting career at the age of seven, where he provided several voices to the animated film Happy Feet.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan nɔɔ ni, o da paas sini kanɛ buon If I Had Known I Was a Genius la nii an biig.
english: In the same year, he appeared as a little boy in the film If I Had Known I Was a Genius.

kusaal: O da lɛn paas sini maalig ni ka ba buon o ye Turnip bɛ wada yela di'em kanɛ buon Boston Legal la ni.
english: He then appeared on an episode as Turnip in the legal drama series Boston Legal.

kusaal: Ba da nɔk o kʋkɔri maal Newspaper Boy ka li bɛ Disney sini banɛ ka saalib pʋ paasi li pʋʋginɛ ka buon yinne The Princess and the Frog ka lɛn paas TV ni sini kanɛ an Men of a Certain Age la ni ka ba buon o Jamie Thoreau.
english: He voiced Newspaper Boy on the Disney animated film The Princess and the Frog and starred on the TV series Men of a Certain Age as Jamie Thoreau.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga ni (2010), o da yi NBC television series Community nina ka ba buon o ye Elijah Bennett ka lɛn paas sini di'ema kanɛ an Valentine's Day nii an bikanɛ nwɛ'ɛd nɔba kikiid.
english: In 2010, he appeared on the NBC television series Community as Elijah Bennett and the romantic comedy film Valentine's Day as a soccer kid.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn buon o Andrew bɛ Playhouse Disney television series ka ba buoni li Special Agent Oso ba da buon o William Glass nɛ bɛ TNT TV sini di'ema kanɛ buon Hawthorne.
english: He also appeared as Andrew on an episode of the Playhouse Disney television series Special Agent Oso and William Glass in the TNT TV series Hawthorne.

kusaal: Lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011) paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piine anaasi ni (2014), o da paas o kʋkɔri maal Darwin Watterson linɛ bɛ Cartoon Network ka ba buon The Amazing World of Gumball la.
english: From 2011 to 2014, he voiced Darwin Watterson on Cartoon Network's The Amazing World of Gumball.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi saŋa la (2014), Terrell Ransom Jr.
english: During 2014, he was replaced by Terrell Ransom Jr. due to puberty.

kusaal: O da paas Southland di'ema ni ka ba buon o Richard, Hawaii Five-0 ni ka ba da buon o Kevin ka The Mentalist ni ka ba da buon o Anthony Rome.
english: He appeared on an episode of Southland as Richard, Hawaii Five-0 as Kevin and The Mentalist as Anthony Rome.

kusaal: Lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011) paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan' (2013) saŋa, Boakye da paas o kʋkɔr Gossamer di'em kanɛ bɛ television ni ka ba buon The Looney Tunes Show la, ka ba mɛ da yisi li bɛ Cartoon Network.
english: From 2011 to 2013, Boakye provided the voice of Gossamer on the television cartoon The Looney Tunes Show, which also aired on Cartoon Network.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛyi ni (2012), o da paas Touch di'ema ni ka ba buon o ye Farai ka lɛn paas ini kanɛ an Unconditional la ni ka ba buon o Macon.
english: In 2012, he appeared on an episode of Touch as Farai and the biographical drama film Unconditional as Macon.

kusaal: O kʋkɔr ka ba nɔki maal one kpɛn'ɛ lɔr kʋkɔr ka li bɛ YouTube/VRV sini di'ema kanɛ buon Bravest Warriors la.

kusaal: Daar wʋsa zi bʋnvʋya bɛnɛ an zɛn'ɛs la nwɛnɛ banɛ gaad biliyɔŋ ayi' nɛ pʋsʋg (2.5 billion) nɛ 50–100 billion granulocytes.

kusaal: Kɔnb-banɛ ka na'asaanam buon ye matrix anɛ din yi piswai paae piswai nɛ anu kɔbʋga pʋʋgʋn (90-95%) an dinɛ ka ba buon ye ossein, ka dinɛ kpɛlim la anɛ titan.

english: Two doors over 5,000 years old have been found by archaeologists near Zürich, Switzerland.

kusaal: Kʋlʋŋ kanɛ bɛ Balawat vɔnya la ba da nɔk nɛ bronze n bʋligi li (nananna di bɛ British Museum).
english: The tenons of the gates at Balawat were sheathed with bronze (now in the British Museum).

kusaal: Kʋlʋs bama ya'ae nɛ vaad ayi'yi', ka yinne wʋsa an 2.54 m (100 in) yaliŋ nɛ 8.2 m (27 ft) wa'alim; ka ba nɔk bronze bands la bʋlʋgi di, 25.4 cm (10.0 in) wa'alim, ka ba nɔk repoussé niŋi di ye di vɛn.
english: These doors or gates were hung in two leaves, each about 2.54 m (100 in) wide and 8.2 m (27 ft) high; they were encased with bronze bands or strips, 25.4 cm (10.0 in) high, covered with repoussé decoration of figures.

kusaal: Hauran linɛ bɛ Syria ka daad kae la, ba da mɔri kuga maan kʋlʋmis, ka yinne wʋsa an wʋʋ 1.63 by 0.79 m (64 by 31 in) ka li bɛ British Museum.
english: In the Hauran in Syria, where timber is scarce, the doors were made of stone, and one measuring 1.63 by 0.79 m (64 by 31 in) is in the British Museum; the band on the meeting stile shows that it was one of the leaves of a double door.

kusaal: Kuffeir dinɛ pʋ lal nɛ Bostra bɛ Syria la, Burckhardt da nyɛ kuga kʋlʋs, 2.74 to 3.048 m (8.99 to 10.00 ft) wa'alim, dinɛ bɛ za'anɔɔr kanɛ dɔli kpɛn'ɛd tɛnpʋʋg la ni.
english: At Kuffeir, near Bostra in Syria, Burckhardt found stone doors, 2.74 to 3.048 m (8.99 to 10.00 ft) high, being the entrance doors of the town.

kusaal: Ancient Greek nɛ Roman kʋlʋs da mɔr daag yinne, daad ayi', daad atan', sliding doors bɛɛ folding doors.
english: Ancient Greek and Roman doors were either single doors, double doors, triple doors, sliding doors, or folding doors.

kusaal: Theron yaʋk linɛ bɛ Agrigentum ba nɔk kuguri kpi'a za'anɔɔr dinɛ pʋdig zin'is anaasi.
english: In the tomb of Theron at Agrigentum, there is a single four-panel door carved in stone.

kusaal: Cosmas and Damiano, Rome tɛŋin la, an sankani ka Roman dim kʋntnam tʋʋma da an tituaa; di da mɔr van'ad ayi, yinne wʋsa mɔr panels ayi, ka di tabidis an bronze.
english: Cosmas and Damiano in Rome are important examples of Roman metal work of the best period; they are in two leaves, each with two panels, and are framed in bronze.

kusaal: Bronze kʋlʋs banɛ da bɛ Roman period la bɛ Lateran Basilica.
english: Two other bronze doors of the Roman period are in the Lateran Basilica.

kusaal: Greek nid one zamis gbaŋ Heron of Alexandria da maal yiiga kʋlʋŋ ka di tʋmi di tuor first century AD Roman Egypt saŋa.
english: The Greek scholar Heron of Alexandria created the earliest known automatic door in the first century AD during the era of Roman Egypt.

english: 604–618), who had one installed for his royal library.

english: Stiles – Vertical boards that run the full height of a door and compose its right and left edges.

kusaal: Dɔkʋda banɛ da bɛ la kʋlʋŋ la da anɛ daad ka ba nɔki maal, wʋʋ din sɔb wina'am gbaŋin na'ab Solomon ni da ye o mɛ wina'am pʋ'ʋsim yin ka da nɔk olive wood (yiiga na'anam vi.
english: The most ancient doors were made of timber, such as those referred to in the Biblical depiction of King Solomon's temple being in olive wood (I Kings vi.

english: The doors that Homer mentions appear to have been cased in silver or brass.

english: Besides olive wood, elm, cedar, oak and cypress were used.

kusaal: Sankanɛ gaad la kʋlʋmis daa ɛɛnti tɔ'ɔŋ nɛ pintles di zugun nɛ tɛŋin kʋnkpɛmis zin'is banɛ ka bamaal vɔnbibis la, ka ba da maal nɛ vɔnya anina tis lintel nɛ sill, ka sill la bɛ kugkpi'em wan wʋʋ basalt bɛɛ granite.
english: Ancient doors were hung by pintles at the top and bottom of the hanging stile, which worked in sockets in the lintel and sill, the latter in some hard stone such as basalt or granite.

kusaal: Daad kʋlʋmis la da wan wʋʋ 7.62 cm (3.00 in) labisim, ka dinɛ ya'an la gat 360 millimetres (14 in) labisim.
english: The wood doors would seem to have been about 7.62 cm (3.00 in) thick, but the hanging stile was over 360 millimetres (14 in) diameter.

english: Doors of the mosques in Cairo were of two kinds: those externally cased with sheets of bronze or iron, cut in decorative patterns, and incised or inlaid, with bosses in relief; and those of wood-framed with interlaced square and diamond designs.

kusaal: Etruria tɛŋin, kuga kʋlʋmis bɛdigʋ da bɛ anina ka Dennis nyɛɛba.

english: The first foot-sensor-activated automatic door was made in China during the reign of Emperor Yang of Sui (r.

kusaal: Kʋlʋmis banɛ ka ba paŋ bɛ kuomin ka Arab inventor Al-Jazari da maali li.
english: Gates powered by water featured in illustrations of the automatons of the Arab inventor Al-Jazari.

kusaal: Kʋlʋŋ anɛ dinɛ mɔr tabidis bɛɛ dinɛ gu'ud za'anɔɔr ka di an suor ka ba dɔlli kpɛn'ɛd k yit zin'ig kanɛ lusi lɛbis.
english: A door is a hinged or otherwise movable barrier that allows ingress (entry) into and egress (exit) from an enclosure.

english: A door's essential and primary purpose is to provide security by controlling access to the doorway (portal).

english: Door furniture or hardware refers to any of the items that are attached to a door or a drawer to enhance its functionality or appearance.
