kusaal: Ba da pin'ili ba nwɛn'ɛb yiiga bɛ nɛ Poly Tank Division One League, ka ba tɔlisi ba tuoni kɛŋ Ghana Telecom Premier League ba yʋʋm kanɛ paas ayi, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998).
english: The club started their first season in the Poly Tank Division One League, but were promoted to the Ghana Telecom Premier League within their second season in 1998.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ, Mɔraʋg nwadig la ni (July 2021), club la nwɛn'ɛb da lɛb nya'aŋ ka ba lɛbisi ba Ghana Division One League 2020–21 season la ni, ban da nwɛn'ɛ Ghana Premier League yʋma pisi nɛ ayi nya'aŋ, ban da tɔlisi ba yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii saŋa la sa .
english: In July 2021, the club was relegated to the Ghana Division One League at the end of the 2020–21 season, after 22 years in the Ghana Premier League since gaining promotion in 1998.

kusaal: Ban di'emidi ba yin di'ema zin'ig si'a anɛ Carl Reindorf Park linɛ ka nidib tusayi (2,000) na nyaŋi kpɛn'ɛ.
english: Their home stadium is Carl Reindorf Park which can seat up to 2,000 people.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ, vaala nwadig la ni (April 2021), 2020–21 season naar saŋa la, ba da lɛb nɛ WAFA (West African Football Academy) Stadium linɛ bɛ Sogakope la.
english: In April 2021, during the latter part of the 2020–21 season they switched to WAFA (West African Football Academy) Stadium in Sogakope.

kusaal: Liberty Professionals mɔr bibaanlig zamisig zin'ig ka li bɛ zin'is atan' Kenya, Togo nɛ Ghana.
english: Liberty Professionals have three youth academies in Kenya, Togo and Ghana.

kusaal: Michael Essien da nwɛn'ɛ tis Ghana Academy 1998–99 season la.
english: Michael Essien played for the Ghana Academy for the 1998–99 season.

kusaal: Mubarak Alhassan, da naae o zamisig ka kɛŋ la'as nɛ Granada CF yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi la ni (2020).
english: Mubarak Alhassan, an academy graduate joined Granada CF in 2020.

kusaal: Abraham Wayo onɛ da zamisi naae anina la da nwɛn'ɛ 2020–21 season la ka an onɛ di goal nami gaad o taaba, anina ka o da paam suori kɛŋ Tunisian Ligue Professionnelle 1 club Étoile Sportive du Sahel.
english: Abraham Wayo an academy graduate ended the 2020–21 season as the club's top goal scorer and later secured a deal to Tunisian Ligue Professionnelle 1 club Étoile Sportive du Sahel.

kusaal: Li paas club banɛ pin'il yiiga Ghana sʋ'ʋlim zamisid football club baŋir.
english: The club was one of the earliest in Ghana to adopt a professional approach to the management of a football club.

kusaal: Lin yi sankan sa, club la kpɛn kɛn tuoni nwɛn'ɛ titua.
english: Since then, the club has consistently maintained respectable league match performances.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga la ni, UNESCO da paas Gingerbread craft linɛ yit Northern Croatia la "Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage" bɛnɛ Croatian malima pʋʋgin.
english: In 2010, UNESCO added the Gingerbread craft from Northern Croatia to the "Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage" for Croatian culture.

kusaal: Banɛ maan Licitar, ka ba buoni ba ye Medičari, da nyɛt na'asi hali ba tɛŋin la, ka nidib mɛ bɔɔd Licitars la hali (licitars tisib da mɔr girima gat tiig puum tisib).
english: Licitar makers, known as Medičari, were highly regarded in society, and their licitars were very much sought after (gifting licitars was considered more sentimental than gifting roses).

kusaal: Licitars nyɛ yʋ'ʋr ban kuosidi li bɛ Marian teŋgbanin la, linɛ bɛ Marija Bistrica (pʋ lal Zagreb la) anina ka suor kennib kaad St Mary of Bistrica ditnɛ linɛ an Assumption bɛɛ St Margaret's Day dabisir la.
english: Licitars became famous due to their being sold at the Marian shrine of Marija Bistrica (near Zagreb), which pilgrims visited for the Assumption or St Margaret's Day.

kusaal: Li anɛ zanbin linɛ bɛ tis Croatian tɛmpʋʋg tita'ar kanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Zagreb la.
english: They are a traditional symbol of the Croatian capital Zagreb.

kusaal: Li anɛ piini linɛ an bʋnyʋbisa, ka ba nidib tisid taaba malima banɛ nwɛnɛ pʋ'adiir bɛɛ Valentine's Day.
english: They are used as an ornamental gift, often given at celebrations of love such as weddings and Valentine's Day.

kusaal: Li ka' winpʋ'ʋs si'a diti lii, amaa nidib da da'ad licitars mɔri kʋn yin ka li anɛ zanbin ye ba wien' keŋ suowɔk hali paae Zagorje.
english: Although not a religious symbol, licitars were often bought to take home as a reminder of the long and sometimes arduous journey to Zagorje.

kusaal: Ninsieba buon Licitars ye gingerbread, ba zi'ilim la zug, baa ban pʋ mɔr kakaduru maani li la.
english: Licitars are often erroneously referred to as gingerbread, although they do not actually contain ginger.

kusaal: Saŋa nwa, Licitars anɛ Croatia nɛ Slovenia dim din (ka li bɛ Croatian nɛ Slovenian na'asaa silig zin'isin nɛ zin'is banɛ ka ba da'ad piini la'ad wʋsa), buninya tiig maalʋg, pu'adiir piini nam, tʋmtʋmnibi piin taaba, nɛ li vɛnlim yɛla, ka nidib nan mɔri li tisid banɛ ka ba nɔŋi.
english: Licitars (pronounced [lǐtsitaːr]; Croatian: licitarska srca; Slovene: lectova srca) are colorfully decorated biscuits made of sweet honey dough that are part of Croatia and Slovenia's cultural heritage.

kusaal: Pʋʋginɛ, bakir la ɛɛnti yinɛ pounds kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (168 pounds) dinɛ zɛm nɛ (76 kg) ka paae 175 pounds dinɛ zɛm nɛ (79 kg), ka di zi'esim an super middleweight nɛ cruiserweight.
english: In professional boxing, the division is above 168 pounds (76 kg) and up to 175 pounds (79 kg), falling between super middleweight and cruiserweight.

kusaal: Ba sieba anɛ: Bernard Hopkins (onɛ da di dunia wʋsa kpɛŋ (world title), Tommy Loughran, Billy Conn, Joey Maxim, Archie Moore, Michael Moorer, Bob Foster, Ann Wolfe, Michael Spinks, Dariusz Michalczewski, Roy Jones Jr., Sergey Kovalev nɛ Zsolt Erdei.
english: The light heavyweight class has produced some of boxing's greatest champions: Bernard Hopkins (who, upon becoming champion, broke the record for oldest man to win a world title), Tommy Loughran, Billy Conn, Joey Maxim, Archie Moore, Michael Moorer, Bob Foster, Ann Wolfe, Michael Spinks, Dariusz Michalczewski, Roy Jones Jr., Joe Calzaghe, Sergey Kovalev, Zsolt Erdei, Dmitry Bivol, & Artur Beterbiev.

kusaal: Light heavyweight champion nam bɛdegʋ pʋ nyaŋi nya' heavyweight crown ti paae sankanɛ ka Michael Spinks lieb yiiga light heavyweight champion di heavyweight championship.
english: Many light heavyweight champions unsuccessfully challenged for the heavyweight crown until Michael Spinks became the first reigning light heavyweight champion to win the heavyweight championship.

kusaal: Bob Fitzsimmons da di light-heavyweight championship on da kɔ'ɔŋi o heavyweight championship la.
english: Bob Fitzsimmons captured the light heavyweight championship after losing his heavyweight championship.

kusaal: Great heavyweight champion nam, Ezzard Charles nɛ Floyd Patterson, da pin'ilnɛ an light heavyweight.
english: Two all-time great heavyweight champions, Ezzard Charles and Floyd Patterson, started out as light heavyweights.

kusaal: Charles da nyaŋ Archie Moore nɛ Joey Maximnɔɔrim babiga non-title bouts ni ka naan lieb heavyweight champion ka Patterson mɛ da kɔ'ɔŋ eight-round tis Joey Maxim ka naan lieb heavyweight champion.
english: Charles defeated Archie Moore and Joey Maxim several times in non-title bouts before becoming heavyweight champion and Patterson lost an eight-round decision to Joey Maxim before becoming heavyweight champion himself.

kusaal: Evander Holyfield da naan light-heavyweight division dʋ' ruiserweight division ka tɔlisi paae heavyweight division ka sɔ' pʋ nya' nɛ o ka o an heavyweight champion ya'as.
english: Evander Holyfield successfully moved up from the light heavyweight division to the cruiserweight division and eventually the heavyweight division and became undisputed champion of the latter two.

kusaal: Amateur boxing, light heavyweight anɛ weight division kanɛ gaad 165 pounds (75 kg) ka mɛ paae 178 pounds (81 kg), ka bɛ middleweight nɛ heavyweight sʋʋgʋn.
english: In amateur boxing, light heavyweight is a weight division above 165 pounds (75 kg) and up to 178 pounds (81 kg), falling between middleweight and heavyweight.

kusaal: Light heavyweight, ka ba buon ye junior cruiserweight bɛɛ light cruiserweight, anɛ tɛbisim zi'esim ninwisigir di'ema ni.
english: Light heavyweight is a weight class in combat sports.

kusaal: Light-heavyweight zi'esim la paam boxing greatest champion nam bɛdegʋ.
english: The light heavyweight class has produced some of boxing's greatest champions: Bernard Hopkins (who, upon becoming champion, broke the record for oldest man to win a world title), Tommy Loughran, Billy Conn, Joey Maxim, Archie Moore, Michael Moorer, Bob Foster, Ann Wolfe, Michael Spinks, Dariusz Michalczewski, Roy Jones Jr., Joe Calzaghe, Sergey Kovalev, Zsolt Erdei, Dmitry Bivol, & Artur Beterbiev.

kusaal: Lillian Elidah anɛ Zambia ninkanɛ dʋgʋt diibi kuosid, ka da naae sakur bɛ Cesar Ritz Culinary Arts Academy dinɛ bɛ Switzerland la ka nananna ka o yʋ'ʋn an onɛ sʋ'ʋe o mɛŋ diib kuosʋg zin'igi bɛ Twaala, dinɛ bɛ Lusaka, Zambia.
english: Lillian Elidah is a Zambian chef, who is a graduate of the Cesar Ritz Culinary Arts Academy in Switzerland and now owns and runs her restaurant Twaala, in Lusaka, Zambia.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Lillian Elidah bɛnɛ Lusaka, Zambia, amaa, o biilim saŋa wʋsa o da bɛnɛ ka nɔbʋg Sweden, zin'ikanɛ ka o da naae o koligi.
english: Lillian Elidah was born in Lusaka, Zambia, but most of her childhood was spent in Sweden, where she graduated from college.

kusaal: O da gban'e ye o lieb onɛ dʋgʋt diibi kuosid, ka da keŋi di sakuri zamisi di yɛla bɛ Cesar Ritz Culinary Arts Academy dinɛ bɛ Switzerland zin'ikanɛ ka o da paami o yiiga Foundation Degree bɛ Culinary Arts.
english: She decided to become a professional chef, and trained at Cesar Ritz Culinary Arts Academy in Switzerland where she achieved a Foundation Degree in Culinary Arts.

kusaal: On da zamis bɛ Switzerland la nya'aŋ, o da tʋm bɛ France an onɛ dʋgʋt diib ka da maligim zamis diib dʋgʋb yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa yi Anthony Leboube san'an.
english: After training in Switzerland, she worked in France as a chef where she was mentored by Anthony Leboube.

kusaal: On da an yʋʋm piinɛ awai (19) la, o da lieb onɛ sɔbid diib yɛla tis Zambian labaya zɔŋ kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon ye The Post, onɛ da an biig banɛ sɔbid la wʋsa sʋʋgʋn.
english: At the age of 19, she became the food writer for the Zambian national newspaper The Post, the youngest writer they had on staff.

kusaal: O da pin'ili o mɛŋ diib dʋgʋb tʋʋma zin'ig bɛ, Twaala Catering, ka lɛn yɔ'ɔg diib kuosʋg zin'ig bɛ Twaala Restaurant.
english: She started her own catering company, Twaala Catering, and opened a restaurant named the Twaala Restaurant.

kusaal: O tʋʋma yʋ'ʋn da yi paalʋ hali bɛnɛ ban ninsieba da di kasɛtta bɛ Nyamuka Zambia, dinɛ ka UK Department for International Development da yɔɔ di sam la.
english: Her entrepreneurial work was highlighted in a report by the private enterprise programme Nyamuka Zambia, funded by the UK Department for International Development.

kusaal: Linda Obenewaa Akweley Ocloo anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaani paas partliment kanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana fourth Republic la ni.
english: Linda Obenewaa Akweley Ocloo, born on 21 February 1979 at Ayinaa Abasa, is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh, eighth and ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Shai-Osudoku constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Yuum tusa ayi' la ni la, Linda da di'e o kasɛtta gbaʋg kanɛ ka ti buon ye, Diploma bɛ Banking yit Cambridge Academy kanɛ bɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlʋm la, nɛ Business Administration kasɛta gbaʋŋ (BA) yit University of Cape Coast, Ghana nwa.
english: In 2000, Ocloo obtained her Diploma in Banking from the Cambridge Academy in Accra and a Business Administration (BA) from the University of Cape Coast, Ghana.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr kasɛta gbaʋg kanɛ an diploma in Insurance ka o di'e yiti National Insurance College bɛ Airport Accra bɛ yuum tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la ni.
english: She holds a diploma in insurance from the National Insurance College at Airport-Accra, which she achieved in 2004.

kusaal: O tʋmnɛ linɛ ka ti buon ye, Client Service Consultant bɛ Old Mutual Assurance, linɛ ka ba boun ye, Provident Life Insurance la.
english: She served as a Client Service Consultant at Old Mutual Assurance, formerly Provident Life Insurance.

kusaal: O sid Desmond William Ocloo, da anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg na'anya'ad bɛ Shai-Osudoku constituency amaa, ka da kpi nɛ sapu'at ni, bɛ nwdis anu la, yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni.
english: Her husband, Desmond William Ocloo, was the original NDC parliamentary candidate for the Shai-Osudoku constituency but died prior to the election following a road traffic collision in May 2016.

kusaal: O anɛ kristo biig (Mission of God Church, Dodowa)
english: She is a Christian (Mission of God Church, Dodowa)

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Shai-Osudoku Constituency kanɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlum la.
english: Linda Obenewaa Akweley Ocloo, born on 21 February 1979 at Ayinaa Abasa, is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh, eighth and ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Shai-Osudoku constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Linda Obenewaa Akweley Ocloo anɛ on ka ti boun ye, Economist la, Banker nɛ Insurer..
english: Linda Obenewaa Akweley Ocloo, born on 21 February 1979 at Ayinaa Abasa, is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh, eighth and ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Shai-Osudoku constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Ocloo anɛ pʋkɔɔnr, ka mɔr biisa anu.
english: Her husband, Desmond William Ocloo, was the original NDC parliamentary candidate for the Shai-Osudoku constituency but died prior to the election following a road traffic collision in May 2016.

kusaal: O anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd tita'ar yinne kani bɛ dunia nwa ni, Messi di Ballon d'Or piini nɔɔr anii [baŋim 2] ka lɛm di European Golden Shoes nɔɔr ayuobʋ, ka yʋʋm 2020 la ni ba pʋd o nɛ Ballon d'Or Dream Team la.
english: After completing his growth hormone therapy at age 14, Messi became an integral part of the "Baby Dream Team", which has been lauded as Barcelona's greatest-ever youth team.

kusaal: Onɛ da yi ka bas kilab la yʋʋm 2021 la ni, o nɔki o bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb bɛllim la wʋsa tis Barcelona, dinɛ ka o di kabnam 34 tis kilab la, pɛ'ɛsnɛ piininam piiga bɛ La Liga titles, Copa del Rey piinnɛm ayɔpɔi nɛ UEFA Champions League nɔɔr anaasi.[baŋim 3] O mɛŋ teŋin la, o di yʋʋm 2021 Copa América nɛ yʋʋm 2022 FIFA World Cup.
english: However, his subsequent victories in the 2021 Copa América and the 2022 FIFA World Cup resulted in him finally winning every top tier trophy at both the club and country levels, an achievement that many pundits felt cemented Messi's legacy.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ mɔr gɔɔl ya'am nɛ onɛ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛri kɛt ka nwɛ'ɛb la an sʋm, Messi mɔr yʋ'ʋr pʋdʋgʋr gɔɔlnam bɛdigʋ yɛla bɛ La Liga (474), hat-tricks nam bɛdigʋ bɛ La Liga (36) ni nɛ UEFA Champions League (anii), pɛ'ɛsnɛ asʋŋ ka ba di bɛ La Liga (192) nɛ Copa América (17).
english: The next year, Messi contributed one goal and one assist at the 2019 Copa América. Argentina finished the tournament in third place after defeating Chile, a victory which marked the start of a 36-game winning streak for the team that lasted for more than three years.

kusaal: Messi di gaad gɔɔlnam 800 o bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb ni tis kilabnam nɛ o mɛŋ teŋ, ka mɔr gɔɔlam bɛdigʋ nwɛ'ɛb yinne kilab ni (672).
english: His records include most goals in a calendar year (91), most goals for a single club (672 for Barcelona), most goals in La Liga (474), most assists in the FIFA World Cup (12), and most assists in international football (65).

kusaal: Lionheart anԑ yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai America sini kanԑ maan zaba, ka onԑ gaad tuoni gͻsi li yela an Sheldon Lettich, banԑ paasi maal sini la si'eba anԑ Jean-Claude Van Damme, Deborah Rennard, Harrison Page, Lisa Pelikan nԑ Brian Thompson.
english: Lionheart is a 1990 American martial arts film directed by Sheldon Lettich, starring Jean-Claude Van Damme, Deborah Rennard, Harrison Page, Lisa Pelikan and Brian Thompson.

kusaal: Van Damme maal o mԑŋ sini la ni nԑ an Fariŋ dim ninkanԑ bԑ Africa, onԑ bas ka kԑŋ United States, nͻk o mԑŋi paas banԑ zabid ka ba yͻͻdi ba ni, lin na niŋ si'em ka o paam ligidi gͻs o ba'abiig kanԑ ka ba kʋ o pʋ'a nԑo biis.
english: Van Damme plays a French Foreign Legionnaire stationed in Africa, who must desert to the United States and enter the underground fighting circuit to raise money for his murdered brother's family.

kusaal: Ba da pin'il sini la gͻsig France nԑ Mͻtul nwadig pin'ilig daar, yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai la ni, ka United States tԑŋin da an Yʋʋmpaal nwadig dabpiinԑ yinnԑ daar, yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ yinnԑ la ni.
english: The film premiered in France on August 1, 1990, and opened in the United States on January 11, 1991.

kusaal: Ba da yisi li United Kingdom ka pʋdi li ye A.W.O.L: Absent Without Leave, ka Oceania mԑ da an Wrong Bet, banԑ da gͻsi li yela anina da pʋdi li yʋda ayi' si'eba pin'iligin si'em la.
english: It received lackluster reviews, but marked Van Damme's breakthrough as a theatrical leading man in North America. It was released in the United Kingdom as A.W.O.L: Absent Without Leave, and in Oceania as Wrong Bet, two early titles considered by the producers.

kusaal: Lyon Gaultier anԑ tԑnzʋŋ dim zabzabidi bԑ Djibouti, East Africa.
english: Lyon Gaultier is in the French Foreign Legion stationed in Djibouti, East Africa. After his brother, who lives in Los Angeles, is set on fire during a drug deal gone bad, Lyon receives a letter from his sister-in-law Hélène begging him to come see his dying brother, who has been calling his name in agony.

kusaal: On da paae New York City ka ligidi kae o nu'ug ni ka o na nͻki lͻ'ͻŋi kul Los Angeles la zug, Lyon da nͻk o mԑŋi kԑŋ paas nԑ banԑ zabid ka ba yͻͻdi ba zin'ig, ba kpԑԑm yʋ'ʋri buon Joshua Eldridge.
english: Arriving in New York City with no money to cross the country to Los Angeles, Lyon is attracted to an illegal street fight being run by a tramp named Joshua Eldridge.

kusaal: O zu'a Sheldon Lettich da sͻbid gbaʋŋ ye o tis Sylvester Stallone ka ba maal sini kanԑ buon Rambo III.
english: Meanwhile, his friend Sheldon Lettich was working on a script about the French Foreign Legion intended for Sylvester Stallone, for whom he had already written Rambo III.

kusaal: Bʋnlinԑ da tisi ba kpԑmisig da anԑ sini kanԑ ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ pisyͻpͻi nԑ anu saŋa ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr Hard Times la, Van Damme nԑ Lettich da nͻŋ sini kan yela hali.
english: A significant inspiration for the film was 1975's Hard Times, a favorite of both Van Damme and Lettich.

kusaal: The Wrong Bet mԑ da dͻl nya'aŋ, onԑ mukud nԑ tʋʋma da la'as nԑ onԑ gͻsid sini maalig titua k aba maali li (banԑ da maal an Charles Bronson nԑ James Coburn).
english: The Wrong Bet followed a similar template, pairing a somber hero with a shifty yet endearing manager (respectively played by Charles Bronson and James Coburn in the classic film).

kusaal: Sunil Shah kanԑ da bԑ Imperial Entertainment da tʋm nԑ Van Damme kʋdʋm ka da maal Black Eagle, nidib da da'a li hali.
english: Sunil Shah of Imperial Entertainment, who had already worked with Van Damme on Black Eagle, was sold on the pitch.

kusaal: Angel Town sini maan kanԑ buon Olivier Gruner da anԑ French dim soogia kʋdʋg.
english: Incidentally, Angel Town actor and Imperial contract player Olivier Gruner was a former French marine commando in real life.

kusaal: Onԑ da gͻs ka gaans sini maanib Lionheart sini la ni anԑ James Tarzia, onԑ da tʋm hali gaad o taaba o saŋa.
english: Lionheart was cast by James Tarzia, who had worked on Best of the Best, and became the leading casting agent for fight films of the era.

kusaal: Jeff Speakman da di'e Jean-Claude Van Damme zin'ig sini maanib la gaansig saŋa, amaa on da muk o mԑŋ sini la maalig zaba ni la, o da yi sini la pʋʋg na ka pʋ paas zaba la nii.
english: Jeff Speakman served as line reader, substituting for Jean-Claude Van Damme during the film's casting sessions but, as he was trying to make his mark in acting without flaunting his martial arts skills, he only appeared in a non-fighting bit part.

kusaal: Jean Dry Lake, da zi'en nԑ Nevada ka ba ki'e o foto ka nͻki maal ye Djibouti tԑŋin.
english: Jean Dry Lake, in the Nevada desert, stood in for Djibouti in the film's escape scene.

kusaal: Lin da an o yiiga sini ka o da gͻsidi li maalig yela la zug, Lettich da nyԑ yela hali bԑ nidib la ni, li kaskas da anԑ Robert C. New, li da kpԑlim bi'ela ka o yis on tʋʋma la ni.
english: As a first time director, Lettich felt challenged by some members of his crew, and had an especially contentious relationship with cinematographer Robert C. New, whom he came close to firing.

kusaal: Van Damme, Michel Qissi nԑ Frank Dux da la'asi gͻsid ka ba maan zin'ig la ka li sid wan wʋʋ ba zabid nԑ zabmԑŋir nԑ.
english: Fight choreography was a joint effort between Van Damme, Michel Qissi and Frank Dux.

kusaal: Zaba kanԑ bԑ sini la ni on nԑ Jeff Langton ka ba da zabid lͻrnam zin'igin la da tigid nini hali, amaa Van Damme da bͻͻd ye li naae tͻ'ͻ ka banԑ gͻsid la sʋnf ma'ae.
english: The tussle with Jeff Langton in the underground car park was originally one of the film's athletic showpieces, but Van Damme wanted to surprise the audience and suggested ending it quickly with a hit to the groin.

kusaal: Amaa, Imperial brass dim da nyԑ sini la ka li an sʋ'ʋm k aba si'ak ye ba na gͻsi li bʋnwԑn'ԑda yela, ka onԑ da gͻsi li yela an British nid John Scott.
english: However, Imperial brass saw the film's potential and extended the budget to give it a full orchestral score by British veteran John Scott.

kusaal: Sini la da yina bԑ Cannes Film Market yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai, Sigsaa nwadig dapiinԑ anii daar, da ba pʋdi li ye A.W.O.L. Yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai Mͻtul nwadig, daba ayi' daar ka li da kpԑn'ԑ Universal Studios banԑ bԑ U.S nu'ugin.
english: The film was screened at the Cannes Film Market on May 18, 1990, under the title A.W.O.L. On August 2, 1990, it was reported that the film had been picked up by Universal Studios in the U.S. It was Van Damme's first film to be released by a major studio in the territory.

kusaal: Ba da pʋdi li anina ye Full Contact linԑ da an o sini kanԑ an yiiga daani paam nidib ka ba tʋʋg million yinnԑ gͻsili, nidib la da anԑ 1,226,025 admissions.
english: Released there as Full Contact, it became his first film to cross the symbolic one-million-spectator threshold in the country, finishing with 1,226,025 admissions.

kusaal: Li da pʋ yʋʋgԑ ka li da'a lu, sini la da paam ligidi sia anina anԑ $24,078,196, o da paam ligidi saŋkan sini la ni gaad o sini nam la wʋsa ti paae zina.
english: Although it fell down the charts rather quickly, the film finished its domestic run with a tally of $24,078,196, by far the best of Van Damme's career up to that point.

kusaal: Sini la da pin'ili yit yaani bԑ VHS ni yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ yinnԑ, Sigir nwadig dapisi nԑ anu daar dͻlisid MCA/Universal Home Video.
english: The film made its domestic home video debut on VHS on June 25, 1991, through MCA/Universal Home Video.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ anii, Sigir nwadig dapiinԑ ayi' daar, sini la da nyԑ suori bԑ Blu-ray yit MVD Entertainment Group ni, anina ka Van Damme nԑ Lettich da gͻsi li yela.
english: On June 12, 2018, the film received a special edition Blu-ray from MVD Entertainment Group as part of their "MVD Rewind" line, to which Van Damme and Lettich have personally collaborated.

kusaal: Michael Wilmington kanԑ da bԑ Los Angeles Times da buoli li ye sini kanԑ mͻr zaba ka vԑnli gaad yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ pisnii saŋa sininam wʋsa." Richard Harrington onԑ da bԑ The Washington Post da pa'ali li yela ye "ba nyaŋi tiasi li ka fʋ kʋ nyaŋi baŋ ban zi'en lͻsia maali li." Owen Gleiberman onԑ da bԑ Entertainment Weekly da pa'al ye li anԑ linԑ ka ba ki'e li pԑsi maali li ka li pʋ wan wʋʋ sinii ka lԑԑ wan wʋʋ li maal nԑ fʋ tuon."
english: Michael Wilmington of the Los Angeles Times called it "a sub-Schwarzenegger thriller" that "has that grotesquely off-scale exaggeration of many post-'80s action movies." Richard Harrington of The Washington Post described it as "really little more than a change of costume and locations for an overly familiar plot." Owen Gleiberman of Entertainment Weekly had a slightly more favorable opinion of the film, saying that it "is nicely shot and edited, and it comes about as close to being a real movie as you get in this genre."

kusaal: Onԑ da pa'al Lionheart yela giŋa nwa' anԑ John Scott, ka vuud la yi Munich Symphony Orchestra.
english: Lionheart's score was composed and produced by John Scott, and recorded by the Munich Symphony Orchestra.

kusaal: Li nya'aŋ ka German label Digi Dreams dim mԑ paas yʋʋma kanԑ buon "No Mercy" ka onԑ yʋʋmi li buon Bill Wray la, ba yis yʋʋma la ka li pʋ paas sini la zin'is si'ebaa.
english: Subsequent reissues by German label DigiDreams include the licensed song "No Mercy" by Bill Wray, which features in the film but was omitted from the Intrada version.

kusaal: Van Damme da kԑŋ tuoni maal sini banԑ mͻr ligidi si'eba, banԑ gͻsid o sini la si'eba mͻr o sini la foto ka yet ye, "nidib la nͻŋ Lionheart gͻsig bͻzugͻ, li pa'an nidi na bԑ nԑ o zua, nͻŋir, bԑԑ o ba'abiig si'em." Knock Off da buosid o buosa ka Van Damme lԑbis ye Timecop nԑ Lionheart anԑ o sini nama ayi' banԑ ka nidib nar ye ba gͻs.
english: While Van Damme went on to appear in bigger and more lucrative films, he has acknowledged the picture's enduring popularity with his fans, saying, "The audience loves Lionheart because it's sincere with the relationships, brotherhood, friendship, love, betrayal." During a promotional interview for Knock Off, Van Damme mentioned Timecop and Lionheart as the two films of his that people should see.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayuobʋ ni, ba da kaanl sini la paas banԑ bͻͻd maaligi bԑ Moonstone Entertainment, banԑ sʋ'ʋe Imperial library hali yʋʋm tusayi nԑ pisi nԑ atan' saŋa sa, amaa li pʋ tʋmm.
english: By 2016, the film was listed in the production slate of Moonstone Entertainment, owner of the Imperial library since 2013, but it did not happen.

kusaal: Ka mԑ paas sini maan Ashley Johnson.
english: It also features the acting debut of Ashley Johnson.

kusaal: O da mͻr ba'abiig ka o bԑ Los Angeles, ka ninsi'eba yʋ'oe o nԑ bugum on da kԑŋ ye o kuos ti'kpi'ema ka pʋ nyaŋ la, Lyon da di'e gbaʋŋi yi o ba'abiig la pʋ'a kanԑ yʋ'ʋri buon Hélène sa'an ka o bԑlim o ye o kulim na gͻs o ba'abiig la ka o wa'a nԑ kum, ka namisid ka buon o yʋ'ʋr.
english: Lyon Gaultier is in the French Foreign Legion stationed in Djibouti, East Africa. After his brother, who lives in Los Angeles, is set on fire during a drug deal gone bad, Lyon receives a letter from his sister-in-law Hélène begging him to come see his dying brother, who has been calling his name in agony.

kusaal: Lyon da sʋ'a zͻ' ka bas o zabzabid taaba la ye o kul yin, o da nyԑ ka anrʋŋ lͻ'ͻŋid wa'ae United States.
english: Lyon escapes the Legion in a daring breakout and sets off across the desert, until he reaches a dockyard on the coast, where he finds work aboard a tramp steamer headed for the United States.

kusaal: Joshua sunf da ma'ae nԑ ka o dͻl Lyon kԑŋ ye o sial Cynthia Caldera, on da anԑ onԑ gͻsid banԑ an kpan'anam zaba.
english: Impressed, Joshua takes Lyon to meet Cynthia Caldera, an unscrupulous organizer of underground fights for the rich elite.

kusaal: Cynthia da siak ye o na sʋŋ Lyon, anina ka o da pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye "Lionheart" ka da ye o zab nԑ zabzabid kanԑ yʋ'ʋri buon Sonny, on anԑ zabzabid kanԑ mͻr o taaba zamisid hali zaba pʋʋgin.
english: Cynthia agrees to sponsor Lyon, dubbing him "Lionheart" and setting him up in a no-holds-barred fight against Sonny, a fighter known for heavily taunting his opponents.

kusaal: Lyon da zabi nyaŋ Sonny na'ana', ka dͻl Joshua kԑŋ lͻkanԑ ka baŋwiins bԑ ye o buol Hélène, tԑŋin la ninyaalis si'eba da kԑna ye ba zab nԑ o.
english: Lyon defeats Sonny easily, then leaves with Joshua to find a phone booth to call Hélène, fending off an attack by a local street gang of punks.

kusaal: Ka Joshua buol Cynthia ka o sʋŋi mͻri ba lͻ'ͻŋi paae Los Angeles.
english: Joshua calls in a favor from Cynthia, who gets them both across the States to Los Angeles.

kusaal: Ba da gban'ae banԑ tʋm tʋʋmkan la, amaa Hélène da pʋ lԑn mͻr ligidi o san'an ya'asԑ, ka sibiti ni sama nan digi ka pʋ yͻͻ, ka mԑ lԑn mͻr o pʋ'ayʋabil ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Nicole ka li nar ye o gͻs o.
english: Lyon decides to help Hélène and Nicole without their knowledge.

kusaal: Lyon nԑ Joshua da nyaŋi vԑԑnsi baŋ Hélène gbԑԑnsig zin'ig, amaa, Lyon da ye o pian'a nԑ Hélène, ka o pʋ siakida ka ye Lyon bas ye ka o sid kpi, ye onԑ lԑn kԑ ka o sid kpԑn'ԑ tikpi'ema kuosʋg.
english: Lyon and Joshua track down Hélène's address, but as Lyon tries to speak to Hélène, she angrily rejects his offers for much needed financial help, admonishing Lyon for deserting his brother and unjustly blaming him for her late husband's involvement in the drug business.

kusaal: Lyon da gban'a o sʋn'ʋrin ye o na dͻlis sʋosia sʋŋ Hélène nԑ Nicole ka ba kʋ baŋ ye onԑ sʋŋidi baa.
english: Lyon decides to help Hélène and Nicole without their knowledge.

kusaal: O da dͻlis Cynthia ni paas zabzabid ni ka o ya'a zab zaba nyaŋ wʋsa, o yͻͻd wa'ae nԑ Hélène n, ka o kԑ ka Joshua ma' pʋ'a la ye o sid da digil nԑ ligidi lͻsia ka nyaan kpi.
english: Through Cynthia, he joins the local street fighting circuit and has the profits delivered to Hélène in the form of checks, with Joshua claiming that her husband subscribed to life insurance prior to his death.

kusaal: Lyon da zabi nyaŋ zabzabid kpi'ema, ka ba si'eba an, dau kanԑ da zabid hali yit Scotland, zabzabid kanԑ da bԑ squash court, ka zabzabid kanԑ zabid kuom pʋʋgin.
english: Lyon defeats a number of high-profile fighters, including a dirty-fighting Scotsman, a wrestler in a squash court, and a martial artist in a shallow swimming pool.

kusaal: Lyon da mͻr o ligidi wʋsa tisid yin la da kԑ ka li fʋfʋm gban'a Cynthia nԑ Lyon n tisid Hélène o ligidi wʋsa la, li da kԑ ka o tʋm o tʋmtʋm Russell ye o dͻlisim gͻs Lyon yela.
english: Seeing as Lyon is not keeping his winnings, and spurns her advances, Cynthia grows suspicious of Lyon and jealous towards Hélène and puts her assistant Russell on Lyon's trail.

kusaal: Zabzabidib ayi' banԑ ka ba kpԑԑm tʋmi ba ye ba kԑna gban'e Lyon la da paae Hélène yin la na da mͻͻd ye ba gban'e: Russell da faae o, amaa ka o sapirig kͻnbir da damm.
english: Similarly, the two Legionnaires sent after Lyon stake out Hélène's apartment and eventually try to capture Lyon: he is saved by Russell but suffers a broken rib.

kusaal: Hélène da nyԑ ban da kԑna ye ba gban'e o la, ka mԑ baŋ sida ye o sid da pʋ bas ligidi zin'ig si'aa, anina ka o yʋ'ʋn da siak ye Lyon anԑ Nicole saambil.
english: Hélène, who has witnessed the attack, learns the truth about the nonexistent insurance policy, whereupon she finally acknowledges Lyon as Nicole's uncle.

kusaal: Cynthia da ti'eb ye Lyon zab nԑ Attila, zabzabid kanԑ ka ba pʋ zabidi nyaŋid o, o ԑԑnti maal o mԑŋ wan wʋʋ tadim nԑ, ka ti kpԑlim ti'ebi zab nԑ o paŋ wʋsa nyaŋi ba.
english: Cynthia arranges for Lyon to fight with Attila, an undefeated combatant whose style includes giving his opponents the illusion of a fighting chance, only to permanently disable them with callous finishing moves.

kusaal: Cynthia da siak ye Lyon ya'a zab zabkaŋa naae o na nͻk o tis banԑ kԑna ye ba gban'e o la.
english: Cynthia agrees to hand Lyon over to the Legionnaires after the fight.

kusaal: Saŋa da kԑna ka Attila nwԑn'ԑ o digil nͻͻr babig ka ba tԑn'ԑs ye o nyaŋ zaba la naae, anina ka Joshua maligim bԑlim Lyon ye o basim zaba la ka on waae loto ye o kʋ nyaŋ zaba laa, o na di'e ligidi la ka ba pʋdig abʋyi'.
english: When Attila appears to have won after repeatedly knocking down his opponent, Joshua begs Lyon to give up the fight and offers to split the winnings from his own bet against Lyon.

kusaal: Banԑ da ied o la da gban'e Lyon, ban da mͻr o gat la, ba da wʋm ka bibil la kaasid Lyon yela, li nimbaanlig da kpԑn'ԑ ka ba mͻr o kԑŋ bi'ela ka bas o ye o kpԑlim America.
english: The Legionnaires capture Lyon, but with remorse listening to his niece's cry at the farewell to Lyon, they release him a couple of blocks away and wish him luck with his new life in America. The film ends with Lyon reunited with his family and Joshua.

kusaal: Sini la naar ni, Lyon yʋ'ʋn la'as nԑ o yir-dim nԑ Joshua.
english: The Legionnaires capture Lyon, but with remorse listening to his niece's cry at the farewell to Lyon, they release him a couple of blocks away and wish him luck with his new life in America. The film ends with Lyon reunited with his family and Joshua.

kusaal: Lionheart da yinԑ sini ayi' ni na.
english: Lionheart has its roots in two different projects.

kusaal: Van Damme da sͻb gbaʋŋ ye o maal sini kanԑ maan zaba ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr The Wrong Bet.
english: Van Damme had written an outline for an underground fighting film, called The Wrong Bet.

kusaal: Ban da pʋ maal sini kan la zug, ba da la'asi li nԑ The Wrong Bet.
english: The Wrong Bet followed a similar template, pairing a somber hero with a shifty yet endearing manager (respectively played by Charles Bronson and James Coburn in the classic film).

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ on ye o sa'ali ba The Wrong Bet maalig kati wa'ae soogianam tʋʋma yela.
english: Looking to promote their in-house star, Imperial suggested him as a military advisor on The Wrong Bet, although his contributions were minimal.

kusaal: Van Damme da bas suor ka Lettich maligim sͻb gbaʋŋ la, ka ba da nͻk o ka o gͻsi li maalig yela.
english: At the insistence of Van Damme, Lettich was allowed to step in for a rewrite, and was eventually hired to direct.

kusaal: Lettich pa'al ye sʋŋir kanԑ da kpԑlim an Warren tʋʋma da anԑ yʋ'ʋr kanԑ ka ba da pʋd ye "Lionheart" la ma'a.
english: According to Lettich, the only contribution left from Warren's screenplay was the hero's nickname, "Lionheart".

kusaal: Ligidi kanԑ ka ba da pin'il nԑ $3 million, nԑ lin ti dʋ ala paae $6 million.
english: The film's budget projections started at a mere $3 million, and went up to $6 million.

kusaal: Zabzabidib gaansig da maali bԑ nԑ Frank Dux gym ka nidib banԑ da bͻͻd ye ba gaansi ba da paae ban tʋsir yela.
english: Fighters' auditions took place at Frank Dux's gym and drew close to one thousand candidates.

kusaal: Brian Thompson da anԑ Lettich zua, ka ba da gaŋ o ye o banԑ zabid yͻͻg yͻͻg la zug bԑ sini la ni.
english: Brian Thompson, a good friend of Lettich's, was immediately hired as the main antagonist's right-hand man.

kusaal: Ashley Johnson da paas sini la ni an Lyon pitʋ biig.
english: Ashley Johnson, who plays Lyon's young niece, made her acting debut in this film.

kusaal: Zin'ig kanԑ ka ba ki'a sini la bԑdigʋ anԑ Los Angeles baba nԑ New York City.
english: The majority of the film was shot in the Los Angeles area, including scenes set in New York City.

kusaal: Van Damme mԑŋi da bas suor ka ba yԑԑs o fuud sini la ni.
english: The tussle with Jeff Langton in the underground car park was originally one of the film's athletic showpieces, but Van Damme wanted to surprise the audience and suggested ending it quickly with a hit to the groin.

kusaal: Stephen "Steve" Edwards an onԑ da maal yʋʋma nԑ bʋnwԑn'ԑda tis sini la.
english: Stephen "Steve" Edwards, who would later become a martial arts film staple, produced a synthesizer demo for the film's score.

kusaal: Lini da an yiiga sini kanԑ ka Van Damme maal ka di'ema zin'is bԑda yisi li ka nidib gͻs.
english: The film was screened at the Cannes Film Market on May 18, 1990, under the title A.W.O.L. On August 2, 1990, it was reported that the film had been picked up by Universal Studios in the U.S. It was Van Damme's first film to be released by a major studio in the territory.

kusaal: Lionheart da yi paalʋ France tԑŋin nԑ yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai, Mͻtul nwadig pin'ilig daar, anina ka nidib bԑdigʋ di'e o nԑ nu'us ayi' on kpin nԑ Fariŋ dim la yela.
english: Lionheart debuted on August 1, 1990, in France, where the star had accrued an early following thanks to his francophone background.

kusaal: United States tԑŋin, sini la da yi paalʋ nԑ yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ yinnԑ, yʋʋmpaal nwadig dapiinԑ yinnԑ daar.
english: In the United States, the film opened on January 11, 1991.

kusaal: Wan wʋʋ di'ema zin'isin la, U.K. din linԑ ka ba da gͻsidi yit Guild Home Video la ba da pʋ tiak si'eli li pʋʋginԑ, ka li da paae anina yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai, Samanpiid nwadig, daba atan' daar.
english: Like the theatrical version, the U.K. version from Guild Home Video was uncut, and arrived on December 3, 1990.

kusaal: Australia dim da di'e linԑ ka ba pʋ ti'ak mԑn la yi Palace Entertainment nԑ Roadshow ni.
english: In addition to a trimmed M-rated VHS that matched the country's theatrical cut, Australia received an uncut R18+ reissue from Palace Entertainment and Roadshow.

kusaal: Rotten Tomatoes zin'igin la, nidib pisnaasi nԑ ayi' kͻbiga pʋʋgin da di'e sini la ka nidib piinԑ awai mԑ sͻbi li yela sʋ'ʋŋa.
english: On Rotten Tomatoes, the film has a 40% rating based on 20 reviews.

kusaal: Metacritic ni, nidib pisnaasi nԑ yinnԑ kͻbiga pʋʋgin di'e li ka nidib piiga sͻbi li yela ban tԑn'ԑs ka li an si'em.
english: On Metacritic it has a score of 41% based on reviews from 10 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.

kusaal: Intrada Records dimi yis sini la yʋʋma bԑ kaset ni yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai ni.
english: Intrada Records released the film's soundtrack album on CD in 1990.

kusaal: Lettich da paas ya ye "Nidib banԑ nͻŋ Van Damme ka an pʋ'ab la nͻŋ sini la hali bͻzugͻ, o pa'al nͻŋilim anina hali.
english: Lettich added that "Van Damme's female fans seem especially enamored of this film because it was the first (and possibly the best) to showcase JCVD's softer, more compassionate side.

kusaal: Ba tԑn'ԑsi gͻs ye ba maal sini tͻlis Lionheart n naae si'em bԑn la.
english: A follow-up to Lionheart has been considered on several occasions.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ anaasi ni, sini kpԑԑm Albert Pyun da yel ye ba kԑn na yel on ye o gͻs ka maal sini la ya'as.
english: In 2014, director Albert Pyun said that he had been approached to direct a remake of the film.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ anii, Fulumfug nwadig la ni, Van Damme da yis labaar na ye ba na maal Lionheart 2 yʋʋmkan ni, amaa o da lԑn tiak o pʋtԑn'ԑr.
english: In February 2018, Van Damme announced on social media that an actual sequel—simply called Lionheart 2—would enter production later that year, but it was quickly called off.

kusaal: Nidib da tͻn' tis sini la bԑ Cinema Score ka nidib da tisi li "B+" ba da ye ba gaŋim lin yi A+ kԑŋ paae F.
english: Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.

kusaal: Di kal da paas yi 260 bɛ vɔtʋg kanɛ da gat la n bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi' li nwadis piinɛ ayiwadmaanib vɔtʋg.constituency wʋsa mɔr wadmaan yinne ka o zi'eni tisi ba.
english: The number of constituencies has increased from 260 at the previous election held in December 2012 parliamentary election.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Saŋkanɛ ka Ghana da di'e o mɛŋ na'asa nam nuusi, wadmaanib 104 bɛ wadwaanib yir.
english: At the time Ghana became an independent country, there were 104 seats in parliament.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Nɛ' kal paas 198 bɛ 1965 saŋkanɛ Ghana da aan paaati yinne state.
english: This increased to 198 after 1965, when Ghana became a one-party state.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Second Republic kanɛ paasi ayi bɛ1969, wadmaanib kal da paasi aan 140.
english: With the start of the Second Republic in 1969, the number of seats was increased to 140.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Nɛ' da pʋ tiak ya'asɛ ti paae republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la sin'iŋi, linɛ da paasi yi 140 ti paae 200.
english: This did not change further until the start of the Fourth Republic when it was increased from 140 to 200.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: 2000 population census nya'aŋ la, ka distriks nam kal da paas yi 110 paas 138.
english: After the 2000 population census, the number of districts increased from 110 to 138.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Electoral Commission of Ghana pʋdig lina kɛ ka constituencies nam la kal paas yi 200 paasi 230.
english: Subsequently, the Electoral Commission of Ghana conducted a demarcation exercise which increased the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Nɛ' da yinɛ Electoral Commission of Ghana banɛ nyɛ final results of the 2010 population census nya'aŋ la.
english: This was done by the Electoral Commission of Ghana after the final results of the 2010 population census became available.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim la anɛ regions nam yinne ka ba pʋdig paala ayi' yis Brong Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The Bono East Region is one of the two new regions carved out of the Brong Ahafo Region.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Constituencies nam bɛ region kaŋa kal paasi yi 33 ka paasi 39 bɛ 2004 nɛ 48 lin da yɔe yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi Ghana dim vɔtʋg.
english: The number of constituencies in this region increased from 33 to 39 in 2004 and to 48 in 2012 before the 2012 Ghanaian general election.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Ba da pʋdig distriks paala sieba bɛ 2008 ka lin da'am constituencies nam sieba.
english: Some new districts were created in 2008, affecting the location of certain constituencies.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Constituencies nam region sʋ'ʋlim da paasi yi 17 ka paasi 19 bɛ 2004 nɛ 23 lin yɔe yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi Ghana dim vɔtug.
english: The number of constituencies in the region increased from 17 to 19 in 2004 and to 23 in 2012 before the 2012 Ghanaian general election.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Constituencies nam da paasi yi 26 paasi 28 bɛ 2004 nɛ 33 lin yɔe yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi' Ghana dim vɔtʋg.
english: The number of constituencies was increased from 26 to 28 in 2004 and to 33 in 2012 before the 2012 Ghanaian general election.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: constituencies nam kal da paas yi 22 paasi 27 bɛ 2004 nɛ 34 lin da yɔe yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi Ghana dim vɔtʋg.
english: The number of constituencies increased/spread from 22 to 27 in 2004 and to 34 before the 2012 Ghanaian general election.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Constituencies nam kal da paasi yi 23 paasi 26 bɛ 2004 nɛ 31 linɛ yɔe yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛayi' Ghana diim vɔtʋg .
english: The number of constituencies increased from 23 to 26 in 2004 and to 31 in 2012 before the 2012 Ghanaian general election.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka ba pʋdig sʋ'ʋlim , Northern nɛ North Eastern regions sʋ'ʋlim nam , region su'ʋlim la nannana mɔr 18 constituencies nam.
english: After the division of the region into Northern and Northeastern regions, the region now has 18 constituencies.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Oti Region sʋ'ʋlim la pʋdig dɔlis December 2018 referendum.
english: The Oti Region was created following the December 2018 referendum.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Savannah Region sʋ'ʋlim la pʋdig dɔlis December 2018 referendum.
english: The Savannah Region was created following the December 2018 referendum.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Constituencies nam da paasi yi 12 paasi aan 13 bɛ 2004 nɛ 15 bɛ 2012 linɛ da yɔe yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi Ghana dim vɔtʋg.
english: The number of constituencies increased from 12 to 13 in 2004 and to 15 in 2012 before the 2012 Ghanaian general election.
en_article: List of parliamentary constituencies of Ghana

kusaal: Constituencies nam kal da paasi yi 8 paasi aan 10 nɛ 11 bɛ 2012 linɛ da ti yɔe tʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi, Ghana vɔtʋg la.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Mahama Ayariga nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (12 dawalig nwadig 1974) Bawku bɛ Upper East Region, Ghana la.
english: Mahama Ayariga was born on 12 May 1974 in Bawku in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋ Barewa College bɛ Zaria teŋkanɛ bɛ Kaduna State, Nigeria la.
english: He was educated in Ghana and Nigeria and the United States of America. He attended the Barewa College in Zaria in Kaduna State, Nigeria.

kusaal: O mɔr Master of Law (LLM) degree yit Harvard Law School bɛ United States of America nɛ Bachelor of Law (LLB) Degree yit University of Ghana, Legon.
english: He holds a Master of Law (LLM) degree from the Harvard Law School in the United States of America and a Bachelor of Law (LLB) Degree from University of Ghana, Legon.

kusaal: O da anɛ executive director tis Legal Resource Centre bɛ Accra la.
english: He was the executive director of Legal Resource Centre in Accra.

kusaal: Ayariga bierkpɛɛm Ayariga Hassan da zi'en ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la zugʋ nya' Ghana yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayi' (2012) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: Ayariga's older brother Hassan Ayariga was the presidential candidate of the People's National Convention (Ghana) for the 2012 General Elections in Ghana.

kusaal: O da pin'ili o tʋʋma la nɛ an pa'an nya'adɔl (teaching assistant) bɛ natural resources law nɛ international law n bɛ Faculty of Law, University of Ghana.
english: He started his career as a teaching assistant in natural resources law and international law at the Faculty of Law, University of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛn paas ka ba pin'il ka lɛn an executive director tis Legal Resources Centre, la'askanɛ da zabid nidib nyadi yɛla, teŋ maalʋg yɛla nɛ bɛllim sʋŋ yɛla la.
english: He also co-founded and was the executive director of the Legal Resources Centre, an organization aimed at promoting human rights, community development and social justice.

kusaal: Ayariga da anɛ Ghana Wadmaannɛ tis Bawku Central constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anu (2005) la ni, amaa ka da lu yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anii (2008) vɔɔtʋg la ka tis ka Adamu Dramani Sakande onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP nid la di.
english: Ayariga was the member of Ghana's parliament for the Bawku Central constituency from 2005 but lost his seat in the 2008 Elections to Adamu Dramani Sakande of the NPP.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni, (2009) John Evans Atta Mills da di vɔɔt la, Ayariga da lieb onɛ pian'adi tisid o ka din nya'aŋ ka o gaŋ o ye o an Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry.
english: In 2009, when Prof John Evans Atta Mills won the elections, Ayariga became the Presidential Spokesman before he was subsequently appointed Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da lɛn gaŋ o ye o an minista kanɛ gɔsid gbaʋŋ zamisʋg nya'adɔl (Deputy Minister of Education).
english: He was subsequently appointed Deputy Minister of Education.

kusaal: John Dramani Mahama da gaŋɛ Mahama Ayariga ye o an Minista onɛ gɔsid labaya yɛla (Information) yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la ni, (yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2013).
english: Mahama Ayariga was nominated for appointment as Minister for Information by President John Dramani Mahama in January 2013.

kusaal: Mahama Ayariga da tʋm la'askanɛ gɔsid tʋʋma tisib yɛla la (Appointments Committee) Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Mahama Ayariga serves on the Appointments Committee of the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti gaŋ Ayariga ye o an Wadmaannɛ tis Bawku constituency bɛ Upper East Region, Ghana vɔɔtʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni la.
english: Ayariga was elected as the Member of Parliament for Bawku constituency of the Upper East Region of Ghana in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress da pʋ zu'oe, ba da paamɛ kʋgʋs piswai nɛ anaasi ma'aa (94) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan' (230) ni.
english: The National Democratic Congress won a minority total of 94 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ anii nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pii nɛ anii (18,518) yit vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ anii nɛ kɔbiga nɛ anii (38,108) pʋʋgin.
english: He was elected with 18,518 votes out of 38,108 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔti tis o ka bas Amidu Mamudu Sisala onɛ an Peoples' National Convention nid la nɛ Hawa Yakubu onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la nɛ Yussif Taiban Kundima onɛ an Convention People's Party nid nɛ Sadat Amadu nɛ Abubakar Jibreel Ustarz banɛ pʋ zi'en Na'adɔsi'a zugɔ, independent candidates.
english: He was elected over Amidu Mamudu Sisala of the Peoples' National Convention, Hawa Yakubu of the New Patriotic Party, Yussif Taiban Kundima of the Convention People's Party, Sadat Amadu and Abubakar Jibreel Ustarz both independent candidates.

kusaal: Ka ba kal pʋdigir kɔbiga pʋʋgin da anɛ; 0.9%, 26.7%, 0.9%, 0.4% nɛ 22.5% nwɛnnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: These were equivalent to 0.9%, 26.7%, 0.9%, 0.4% and 22.5% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt kal tusa pisi nɛ anaasi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne (24,071) yi vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (43,876).
english: He was elected with 24,071 votes out of 43,876 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o ka bas Awuni Aguuda Joseph onɛ an Peoples' National Convention nid la nɛ Alhassan Haruna onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la nɛ Iddrisu Mubarak onɛ an Progressive People's Party nid la nɛ Ibrahim Zaliya onɛ an Convention People's Party nid la.
english: He was elected over Awuni Aguuda Joseph of the Peoples' National Convention, Alhassan Haruna of the New Patriotic Party, Iddrisu Mubarak of the Progressive People's Party and Ibrahim Zaliya of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Ba kɔbiga pʋʋgin anɛ vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (0.69%), vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ atan' du'al pisnaasi nɛ awai (43.49%), vɔɔt nɛɛm du'ali ayuobʋ (0.61%) nɛ vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pistan' nɛ anaasi (0.34%) nwɛnnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: These were equivalent to 0.69%, 43.49%, 0.61% and 0.34% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayuobʋ, June 2020 Wadmaannib yikpɛɛm la (Speaker of Parliament) da zan'as Mahama Ayariga ka pʋ siak ye Electoral Commission nɔk Ghana card nɛ passports ma'aa maal vɔɔdʋg gbaʋŋ paala la vɔɔt yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: In June 2020, the Speaker of Parliament rejected Mahama Ayariga's challenging the Electoral Commission's decision to make the Ghana card and passports the sole valid identification for registering to vote in the 2020 elections.

kusaal: o saam, Frank Abdulai Ayariga, mɛ da anɛ Wadmaannɛ tis Bawku Constituency Republic kanɛ paasi atan la ni, Hilla Liman saŋa.
english: His father, Frank Abdulai Ayariga, also served as member of parliament for the Bawku Constituency during the third republic administration of Hilla Limann.

kusaal: Mahama Ayariga (Ba da du'a o nɛ 12 May 1974) o anɛ lɔya nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd Ghana kpɛla.
english: Mahama Ayariga (born 12 May 1974) is a lawyer and politician in Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: He belongs to the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da anɛ Minista kanɛ gɔsid labaya nɛ labadi'esidib tʋʋma yɛla nɛ minista onɛ gɔsid pu'asada nɛ dasam nɛ niŋwisigir yɛla John Dramani Mahama saŋa la.
english: He was the Minister of Information and Media Relations and the Minister of Youth and Sports under the John Dramani Mahama administration.

kusaal: o da keŋ o sakur nɛ Ghana nɛ Nigeria nɛ United States of America.
english: He was educated in Ghana and Nigeria and the United States of America. He attended the Barewa College in Zaria in Kaduna State, Nigeria.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaannɛ paas Wadmaanib yibanɛ paasi anaasi (4th) nɛ ayuobʋ (6th) nɛ ayɔpɔi (7th) la Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.
english: He is currently the Member of Parliament representing Bawku Central constituency of the Upper East Region of Ghana in the 4th, 6th, 7th and 8th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress.
english: He won on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlim la paas nɛ sʋ'ʋlim nama awai (9) banɛ ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la da dii yi sʋ'ʋlim nam pii nɛ atan' (13) banɛ bɛ Upper East Region la.
english: His constituency was a part of the 9 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election for the Upper East Region.

kusaal: nɛ' da anɛ pisnaasi nɛ anii du'ali ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin 48.6%.
english: This was equivalent to 48.6% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la (2012), ba da lɛn vɔɔti tis o ya'as ka o an Wadmaannɛ tis o sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: In 2012, he was elected as the member of parliament for the same constituency.

kusaal: O da zɛrig Girimadaan Boakye Agyarko onɛ ka ba da gaŋ ye o tʋm Energy Ministry la ye o yɔ ligidi tis Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg ninsieba ye ba sʋŋ ka vɔɔti tis o.
english: He accused Hon. Boakye Agyarko, a nominee for the Energy Ministry of paying the minority caucus on the committee bribes for his approval.

kusaal: Ba kpɛɛm la da gaans ninsieba (AD-HOC committee) ye ba vɛɛns yɛl la gɔs ka mɔri ba vɛɛnsʋg labaari ken wadmanib yin yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi Nwadisa atan' dabpisi nɛ awai la daar (dawalig nwadig 29, 2017) na.
english: An AD-HOC committee set up by the speaker investigated and submitted its report to parliament on 29 March 2017.

kusaal: Aaron Michael Oquaye da bas nɔɔr yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ awai Nwadisa Ayuobʋ daba anaasi daar (sigir nwadig 4, 2019), ye ba tisim onɛ an Wadmaannɛ tis Bawku Central, Mahama Ayariga, suor ka o keŋ ka kɔɔtʋ (High Court) vɛɛnsi gɔs ligidi la yɛla (Financial Court).
english: In 2019, there have been controversies about him facing a court trial as it is perceived he has done some wrong to be litigated in the High Court though there has been some resistance, the Speaker of Parliament, Prof. Aaron Michael Oquaye on 4 June 2019, ruled that, the Member of Parliament for Bawku Central, Mahama Ayariga, be released to stand trial at the High Court (Financial Court) to begin the necessary proceedings against him.

kusaal: Bama da paamnɛ kɔbistan' nɛ pistan' nɛ atan' (333), tusa piiga nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (10,169), kɔbistan' nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' (353), kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne (161), nɛ tusa anii nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (8,574) ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em.
english: These obtained 333, 10,169, 353, 161 and 8,574 votes respectively of total votes cast.

kusaal: nɛ' anɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi du'al pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (54.86%).
english: This was equivalent to 54.86% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O lɛm zi'eni an zugdaan-nya'andɔl tis NPP bɛ 2012 vɔɔtʋg ka ba gaat o tuon maal partition bɛ 2012/2013 Zugdaan vɔɔtʋg Petition dinɛ mak John Mahama ka o di vɔɔtʋg laO dinɛ Samira Ramadan dinɛ ka ba mɔr biis anaasi.
english: He also ran as the NPP vice-presidential candidate in the 2012 general elections and was the lead witness for the petitioners in the 2012/2013 Presidential Election Petition, which challenged the declaration of John Mahama as winner of the election.

kusaal: Mahamudu Bawumia kɛŋnɛ Sakasaka Primary school bɛ Tamale la, ka paam suori kpɛn' Tamale Secondary School bɛ 1975.
english: Mahamudu Bawumia attended the Sakasaka primary school in Tamale and gained admission to Tamale Secondary School in 1975.

kusaal: Onɛ da naae Tamale Secondary School la, o kɛŋ United Kingdom dinɛ ka o zamis banking ka paam Chartered Institute of Bankers Diploma (ACIB).
english: After graduating from Tamale Secondary School, he went to the United Kingdom, where he studied banking and obtained the Chartered Institute of Bankers Diploma (ACIB).

kusaal: Onɛ da an Zugdaan tis Ghana United Nations Students' Association (GUNSA) bɛ 1981 ni.
english: He was the president of the Ghana United Nations Students' Association (GUNSA) in 1981.

kusaal: O da paam First Class Honours Degree bɛ Economics ni bɛ Buckingham University bɛ 1987 ni.
english: He took a First Class Honours Degree in Economics at Buckingham University in 1987.

kusaal: O da paam master's degree bɛ Economics bɛ Lincoln College, Oxford, ka paama Ph.D. bɛ Economics bɛ Simon Fraser University, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada bɛ 1995.
english: He then obtained a master's degree in economics at Lincoln College, Oxford, and obtained a PhD in economics at the Simon Fraser University, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada in 1995.

kusaal: Deputy Governor Bawumia tʋmnɛ an Boards bɛ Bank of Ghana, Ghana International Bank (UK), Ghana Telecom, Revenue Agencies Governing Board, Social Security nɛ National Insurance Trust.
english: As deputy governor, Bawumia served on the Boards of the Bank of Ghana, Ghana International Bank (UK), Ghana Telecom, Revenue Agencies Governing Board, Social Security and National Insurance Trust.

kusaal: Wabig paati (NPP) da paam vɔɔtʋg gaad 2004 vɔɔtʋg la ni dinɛ nɔk Northern Regions nam atan' la, yiiga nɛ ayi' din la.
english: The NPP increased its share of the vote compared to 2004 in all the three Northern Regions, in both the first and second round.

kusaal: Bawumia tʋm an consultant tis Economic Commission of Africa dinɛ yi February nɛ March 2009 ni.
english: Bawumia served as a consultant to the Economic Commission of Africa between February and March 2009.

kusaal: Dinɛ yi April nɛ October 2009, o da anɛ visiting scholar bɛ University of British Columbia Liu Centre bɛ Global Studies nɛ UBC Fisheries Centre.
english: Between April and October 2009, he was a visiting scholar at the University of British Columbia Liu Centre for Global Studies and UBC Fisheries Centre.

kusaal: October 2009 nii, o da paam gaŋir bɛ pɛ'ɛs International Growth Centre (IGC), research institute dim pɛ'ɛsi bɛ London School of Economics nɛ Political Science nɛ Oxford University dinɛ ka mɔr sa'alʋg tisid economic nɔbigir tis governments of developing countries, tʋmi an IGC Team Member tisid Sierra Leone.
english: In October 2009, he was appointed as a Fellow of the International Growth Centre (IGC), a research institute based jointly at the London School of Economics and Political Science and Oxford University that provides advice on economic growth to governments of developing countries, specifically serving as an IGC Team Member for Sierra Leone.

kusaal: O da lɛm tʋm an advisor tis Central Bank of Sierra Leone bɛ bank la zi'esim diakir nɛ di monetary policy framework.
english: He also served as an advisor to the Central Bank of Sierra Leone on the redesigning of the organizational structure of the bank and its monetary policy framework.

kusaal: Dinɛ yi October 2009 ti paae October 2010, o da anɛ Senior Research Associate bɛ Centre for the Study of African Economies bɛ Department of Economics, University of Oxford.
english: Between October 2009 and October 2010, he was a senior research associate at the Centre for the Study of African Economies at the Department of Economics, University of Oxford.

kusaal: January 2011 nii, Bawumia ka ba da gaŋ o an Resident Representative of the African Development Bank tis Zimbabwe bɛ African Development Bank.
english: In January 2011, Bawumia was appointed resident representative of the African Development Bank for Zimbabwe by the African Development Bank.

kusaal: O da bɛ kuk kaŋa ni laa ti paae saŋkani ka ba naam lɛm gaŋ o ye o an Vice-Presidential Candidate tis Nana Akufo-Addo bɛ New Patriotic Party tis Ghana's 2012 Zugdaan vɔɔtʋg ni.
english: Bawumia was re-nominated as the Vice-Presidential Candidate to Nana Akufo-Addo for the 2012 General Elections in March 2012.

kusaal: O da kpɛn' kuk la zug bɛ 7 January 2017 an Zugdaan-nya'andɔl tis Ghana.
english: Mahamudu Bawumia (born 7 October 1963) is a Ghanaian politician and former central banker who served as the seventh vice president of Ghana from 7 January 2017 to 7 January 2025 under President Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Bawumia da anɛ Deputy Governor tis Bank of Ghana, banɛ da gaŋ o an zugdaan-nya'andɔl ye o zi'en vɔɔtʋg bɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) bɛ 2008, nɛ o zugdaan Nana Akufo-Addo.
english: Mahamudu Bawumia was running mate to the New Patriotic Party candidate in the 2008 elections, Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: 2008 vɔɔtʋg la nya'aŋ giŋa, Bawumia sig ka bas Deputy Governor bɛ Bank of Ghana.
english: Shortly before the 2008 election, Bawumia resigned as deputy governor at the Bank of Ghana.

kusaal: Mahamudu Bawumia da anɛ running mate tis New Patriotic Party candidate bɛ 2008 vɔɔtʋg la ni, Nana Akufo-Addo.
english: Mahamudu Bawumia was running mate to the New Patriotic Party candidate in the 2008 elections, Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Maloya anɛ bun saaŋ kani yit African nɛ Malagasy nɛ saŋpkan'asnam bani bɛ Indian indentured workers m bɛ island zugiŋ sa, nɛ yʋma zin'is zin' sieba Réunion, séga pʋʋgiŋ.
english: Maloya is a new form that has origins in the music of African and Malagasy slaves and Indian indentured workers on the island, as has the other folk music of Reunion, séga.

kusaal: Dunia wʋsa yʋma lava mɔɔn nɛ banɛ pʋ zanmis yʋma labaya tisib la ɛnti duoe saŋsiebamamissi pa'al maloya tnɛ American yʋma, nɛ blues, ka ba mɔri nwanim sieba bi'ela.
english: World music journalists and non-specialist scholars sometimes compare maloya to the American music, the blues, though they have little in common.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 1970s la French dim da gɔs Maloya anɛ bʋnkani an namisʋgʋ tisi ba pamm.
english: Maloya was considered such a threat to the French state that it was banned in the 1970s.

kusaal: Maloya yʋma nɛ ba wa'ab la dɔlisid si'em la nwɛnii African dim yʋma nɛ ba wa'ab him kiapi dɔlisid faar kani yit Africa dim malima ("service Kaf" nɛ Madagascar ("servis kabaré"), nɛ faar linɛ ka ba la'am yi yamis banɛ da dɛŋim bɛ tɛɛns banɛ da bɛ saŋkan la.
english: The indigenous music and dance form of maloya was often presented as a style of purely African origin, linked ancestral rituals from Africa ("service Kaf" and Madagascar (the "servis kabaré"), and as such a musical inheritance of the early slave population of the island.

kusaal: Françoise Vergès pian'a pa'al yɛ Firmin Viry in 1959 da ɔnɛ da yyiiga sɔbi mɔr maloya tʋʋma yi paalʋ na, Communist Party la da mɔri ba party la kɛn paalim na la.
english: According to Françoise Vergès, the first public performance of maloya was by Firmin Viry in 1959 at the founding of the Communist Party.

kusaal: Maloya da zienɛ tis political nɛ social protest by Creole poets bani an Waro, ka yʋ'ʋn ta bɛɛbɛɛ tiaki an Ziskakan.1980s li nɛ da an maloya sin'igidin la, ba da pʋ nɛ zin'is-zin'is ka ba nɛ an Ziskakan, Baster, Firmin Viry, Granmoun Baba, Rwa Kaff nɛ Ti Fock, ka sieba la'as nɛ maloya, banɛ an séga, zouk, reggae, samba, afrobeat, jazz and rock ka li kɛ ka ba yʋr yi pamm tɛɛns bɛdigʋ ni.
english: Since the start of the 1980s, maloya groups, such as Ziskakan, Baster, Firmin Viry, Granmoun Baba, Rwa Kaff and Ti Fock, some mixing maloya with other genres such as séga, zouk, reggae, samba, afrobeat, jazz and rock, have had recognition outside the island.

kusaal: Maloya da nieɛ paalʋ nɛ 2009 yʋ'ʋm la ka ba yʋma da pɛɛs Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity of UNESCO tis France.
english: Maloya was inscribed in 2009 on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity of UNESCO for France.

kusaal: Maloya anɛ dinɛ an bun yinnɛ dinɛ pɛɛs Réunion yʋma la'ad dinɛ pak pamm, Réunion Creole ni ka ba ɛɛnti yʋm nɛ ba buudi ni dɔli nɛ ba yʋma lak kani pɔnd la.
english: Maloya is a musical genre of Reunion island, usually sung in Reunionese Creole, and traditionally accompanied by percussion and a musical bow.

kusaal: Saansa biela ni, Tamil malima nɛ ba nwɛ'ɛb da anɛ linɛ ka Danyèl Waro pa'ala nɛ o yʋma nwɛ'ɛb dɔlisʋg da kpɛ' li pʋʋgin paam ka li kɛ ka ba yʋma la bigis nyai yɛ li yini African, Malagasy nɛ Indian bɛdigʋ ni na.
english: More recently, however, the possible influence of the sacred drumming of the Tamil religious rituals has been introduced by Danyèl Waro, which makes Maloya' heterogeneous African Malagasy and Indian influences more explicit.

kusaal: Ba da kat Maloya nwɛnɛɛ yʋma pisyuobu nam baba, bɔzugɔ ba da kɛŋɛ maal nɔɔr yinɛ nɛ creole culture.
english: Maloya was banned until the sixties because of its strong association with creole culture.

kusaal: Yʋm bama nwa', Jean Paul Roig, da sɔbnɛ digil 1994 saŋa, ka tisid li yʋ'ʋr yɛ Maloya Dousman.
english: This musical form was the subject of a 1994 documentary film by Jean Paul Roig, entitled Maloya Dousman.

kusaal: Kwaku Ampratwum-sarpong an wadmaan tis teŋ la lin pin'il yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni sa (2016).
english: Kwaku Ampratwum-Sarpong has been the Member of Parliament for the constituency since 2016.

kusaal: Onɛ da di'e Francis Addai Nimoh kanɛ da mɔr wadmaan kʋk la wadmaanib yir kanɛ da paas anaasi la ni la.
english: He succeeded Francis Addai Nimoh who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament.

kusaal: Nicknamed the Red Devils, ba da pin'ilnɛ Newton Heath LYR 1878 la, amaa ka tiaki ba yʋ'ʋr keŋ Manchester United 1900.
english: Nicknamed the Red Devils, they were founded as Newton Heath LYR Football Club in 1878, but changed their name to Manchester United in 1902.

kusaal: Ba sieba yʋda anɛ George Best, Denis Law nɛ Bobby Charlton ka ba buon ye – United Trinity la.
english: Eight players were killed in the Munich air disaster, but Busby rebuilt the team around star players George Best, Denis Law and Bobby Charlton (known as the United Trinity).

kusaal: Manchester united da pin'ilɛ yʋʋm 1878 nwɛnnɛ Newton nimma'asim LYR bɔɔl nwɛɛb dɔɔg, ka li da anɛ Carriage nɛ Wagon lʋgʋr linɛ bɛ Lancashire and Railway (LyR) la'as Newton Health ni.
english: Manchester United were formed in 1878 as Newton Heath LYR Football Club by the Carriage and Wagon department of the Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway (LYR) depot at Newton Heath.

kusaal: Banɛ bɛ Cameraton, Manchester la nya'aŋ ka tis banɛ di'em la keŋ ba zin'ig kanɛ bɛ ba nananna la, Anld Trafford 1910.
english: Mangnall was considered a significant influence behind the team's move to Old Trafford in 1910, and Manchester United won the First Division for the second time in 1911.

kusaal: Mankessim anɛ tɛmpʋ'ʋg bɛ Central Region dinɛ bɛ Ghana, West Africa.
english: Mankessim is a town in the Central Region of Ghana, West Africa. It is approximately 75 km west of Accra, on the main road to Sekondi-Takoradi.

kusaal: Mankessim pin'ilʋg da ta'alɛ nɛ zabzabidib atan' banɛ ka nidib bɛdigʋ mi' ba ; Obrumankoma, Odapagyan nɛ Oson, banɛ da sʋŋ Fante dim la ka ba duoe yi Techiman dinɛ ka ba yʋn buon ye Bono Region kɛŋ Adoagyir bɛ Central Region.
english: Mankessim's history is linked to three famed warriors: Obrumankoma, Odapagyan and Oson, who helped the Fante people migrate from Techiman in the current Bono Region to Adoagyir in the Central Region.

kusaal: Tɛmpʋ'ʋg la da bɛnɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu 75 meters linɛ tʋʋg mu'ar lalim ka li nidib kanl da an 38,313 fʋ ya'a gɔs 2010 nidib kaanlug la ni.
english: The town is located at an elevation of 75 meters above sea level and its population according to the 2010 Census was 38,313.

kusaal: Mankessim tɛŋ la an tɛbisim zin'ig tis nidib banɛ pian'ad Fante pian'ad buudi wʋsa ka li da bɛ Sacred Nananom Pow linɛ kpi'e nɛ Obidan.
english: Mankessim is the traditional paramountcy for all Fante-speaking people and was the location of the sacred Nananom Pow (sacred grove) which is also near Obidan.

kusaal: Wɛnnɛ da' banɛ Fante dim tɛŋ titada an si'em la,Makessim mɔr Asafo kompeni nam, ka mɛ mɔr soogia nam banɛ pʋ lɛn zabid zaba amaa ba tisidi ba girima nɛ ban tʋm si'el tis tɛŋ la ka tɛŋ maalʋg kɛŋ tuon tɛŋ la pin'iligin la.
english: Just as in other prominent Fante towns, Mankessim has Asafo companies, traditional military groups which no longer fight wars but are acknowledged for their role in the history and development of the town.

kusaal: Augustine Arhinful; o nwɛn'ɛdne bɔɔl – ba da dua o nɛ 1994.

kusaal: Ba da ti'as biis nwa yʋda buol ye Marcus nɛ Linda Samuelsson.

english: After becoming interested in cooking through his maternal grandmother in Sweden, Samuelsson studied at the Culinary Institute in Göteborg (Gothenburg) where he was raised.

kusaal: O da zamis tʋʋma Switzerland nɛ Austria ka naam keŋ Restaurant Aquavit United State 1994 an tʋʋmzamis.
