english: This tradition is an important part of the Culture of Bulgaria and there is a similar tradition in North Macedonia, as well as in Greece, Albania (known as verorja), and Romania and Moldova, where is known as Mărțișor.

kusaal: Ethnographers sieba yɛl ye ba tun'oe dɔlis malʋŋ la keŋ Eleusinian Mysteries.
english: Some ethnographers claim that the custom can be traced in the Eleusinian Mysteries.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kʋdʋg malʋŋ kanɛ an zina Greek "martis" ba tɛn'ɛsid ye li anɛ kroke (κρόκη).
english: The ancient equivalent of the modern Greek "martis" is thought to be the kroke (κρόκη).

kusaal: 20th century pin'iligin Bulgarian sɔlima yɛl ye yiiga Martenitsi da bɛ 7th century Battle of Ongal kanɛ bɛ Bulgar Khan Asparuh nɛ Byzantine sʋʋgin, kɛ ka ba gban'ae Bulgar victory.battle, zaba la nya'aŋ, Asparuch la tʋmi danwana banɛ zanl gum piel ye ba mɔɔli ba ya'an diib.
english: An early 20th-century Bulgarian story relates the first Martenitsi to the 7th-century Battle of Ongal between the Bulgar Khan Asparuh and the Byzantines, which resulted in a decisive Bulgar victory.

kusaal: Ba yɛɛd martenitsa nɛ Baba Marta Day (Donwalig nwadig 1) ka onɛ yɛ la nyaan ti nyɛ stork, swallow, bɛɛ Blosoming tree (bɛɛ Donwalig nwadig la ya' ti kpi (Vaala nwagid 1))Bulgarian nɛ Macedonian dim ni, holiday (dabiszaal) la yʋ'ʋr la gbin anɛ "Grandma March", "Yaabpu'a Donwalig nwadig" , dabiszaal la nɛ Martenitsa yɛɛb la anɛ Bulgarian nɛ Macedonian buudi malima kanɛ ka ba maan ka li pa'an ye spring saŋa paae ya ka ba tʋ'ʋsidi di'edi li.
english: Martenitsi are worn from Baba Marta Day (March 1) until the wearer first sees a stork, swallow, or blossoming tree (or until the end of March (April 1)).

kusaal: Bulgarian nɛ Macedonian dim nii, folklore malima pin'inɛ Donwalig, March.
english: The name of the holiday means "Grandma March" in Bulgarian and Macedonian, the holiday and the wearing of Martenitsi are a Bulgarian and Macedonian tradition related to welcoming the spring, which according to Bulgarian and Macedonian folklore begins in March, and very similar to Mărțișor tradition in Romania and Moldova.

kusaal: Martenitsa ye anɛ ban na sɛn yaadi ka zaŋ gummi su ka ba nwɛni biisa ayi nɛ pizho nɛ penda (Bulgarian Пижο и Πeндa).
english: A typical Martenitsa consists of two small wool dolls, Pizho and Penda (Bulgarian: Пижо и Пенда).

kusaal: Ba anɛ heralds banɛ kɛ ka spring kenna nɛ vʋm paalig la.
english: They are the heralds of the coming of spring and of new life.

kusaal: Martenitsa la mɛ anɛ ma sʋŋ zanbin bɛlimin, piel la an snow, (mɛligim) nyɛligir nyain zanbin la, nɛ nintaŋ an zin'a la, linɛ ka li paŋ la paasid nɛ, progresses ma'aa spring saŋa la pʋʋgin.
english: The Martenitsa is also a stylized symbol of Mother Nature, the white symbolizing the purity of the melting white snow and the red setting of the sun, which becomes more and more intense as spring progresses.

kusaal: Ka li pin'inɛ Donwalig nwadig la yiiga daar la, ba zangidi yinne bɛɛ bɛdigʋ tabil nɛ fuud banɛ ka ba yɛ, bɛɛ nu'ugin bɛɛ ningɔɔnrin, ka onɛ yɛ nyaan ti nyɛ stork bɛɛ swallow yi kateŋi kunna, bɛɛ blossoming tree, tiig kanɛ pu hali ka yʋʋn yis Martenitsa la.
english: Beginning on the first of March, one or more are worn pinned to clothing, or around the wrist or neck, until the wearer sees a stork or swallow returning from migration, or a blossoming tree, and then removes the Martenitsa.

kusaal: ba pʋtɛn'ɛr anɛ ye ba ya' yɛ Martenitsa si'im zin'a nɛ si'im piela la, nidib la sɔsidi nimbaanlzɔɔr Baba Marta ni.
english: The common belief is that by wearing the red and white colors of the Martenitsa, people ask Baba Marta for mercy.

kusaal: Ba ti'ir anɛ winter gaad tɔ'ɔtɔ ka spring kena.
english: They hope that it will make winter pass faster and bring spring.

kusaal: Yiiga stork bɛɛ swallow kanɛ lɛn na la anɛ spring harbinger ka kasetʋg ye Baba Marta pʋtɛn'ɛr an sʋm ka li kpɛlim nɛ ye o vʋ'ʋs.
english: The first returning stork or swallow is taken as a harbinger of spring and as evidence that Baba Marta is in a good mood and is about to retire.

kusaal: Ninsieba lɔɔdi Martenitsa la ta'al tiig puum wil, ka li an laafi nɛ zugsʋŋi tit tiig la, kanɛ ka nid kanɛ yɛ Martenitsa la wʋmi li malisim ban daa yɛ li, wearing it sansi'a la.
english: Some people tie the Martenitsa on a branch of a fruit tree, thus giving the tree health and luck, which the person wearing the Martenitsa has enjoyed themselves while wearing it.

kusaal: Sieba lakidi kugir ka zaŋi li niŋi li lɛgin ka ba ya'amin an ye bʋnkɔnbʋg kan buudi (li ye anɛ bʋniandir) kpi'el nɛ token la dabsis kanɛ dɔl la na pa'al nida laafi yʋʋm la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Others put it under a stone with the idea that the kind of creature (usually an insect) closest to the token the next day will determine the person's health for the rest of the year.

kusaal: Bʋniandir la ya'a anɛ larva bɛɛ worm, yʋʋm kanɛ na kena la na mɔri nima'asim nɛ yɛlʋma.
english: If the creature is a larva or a worm, the coming year will be healthy and full of success.

kusaal: Bʋniandir kanɛ kpi'e nɛ token la ya'a an sisipaanlʋŋ, spider, … alaa nid da bɛnɛ yɛllin ka kʋ di zugsʋŋ malisim, laafi, bɛɛ yɛlsʋm mɛ.
english: If the creature nearest the token is a spider, then the person is in trouble and may not enjoy luck, health, or personal success.

kusaal: Martenitsa yinne bɛɛ bɛdigʋ yɛɛb anɛ bʋn linɛ ka Bulgarian nɛ Macedonian dim bɛdigʋ niŋid ka li an malʋŋ la.
english: A Martenitsa (Bulgarian: мартеница, pronounced [ˈmartɛnit͡sa]; Macedonian: мартинка, romanized: martinka; Greek: μάρτης, romanized: mártis [ˈmaɾ.tis]; Romanian: mărțișor [mər.t͡siˈʃor] ; Albanian: verore; Turkish: marteniçka [marteˈnit͡ʃka]) is a small piece of adornment, made of white and red yarn and usually in the form of two dolls, a white male and a red female.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la dɔlisig sieba, kas kas, a lɔɔd gum piel nɛ gum zin'a kanɛ ka ba nwiig la, anɛ yʋʋm kʋda ni malʋŋ ka yɛt ye Thracian (paleo-Balkan) bɛɛ tun'oe an Hellenic bɛɛ Roman origins.
english: Some specific features of the ritual, especially tying the twisted white and red woolen threads, are a result of centuries-old tradition and suggest Thracian (paleo-Balkan) or possibly Hellenic or Roman origins.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la yʋ'ʋr pʋdigi Photios' Lexicon ni.
english: The custom is mentioned in Photios' Lexicon.

kusaal: Ba yɛl ye maanmaanib la […] lɔɔdi ba datiʋŋ nu'ud nɛ datiʋŋ nɔbir foot nɛ gum zin'a [κρόκη].
english: It is said that the priests [μύσται] wrap a red thread [κρόκη] around their right hand and foot.

kusaal: Saŋkan la gum zin'a bɛɛ li tun'oe an si'im sieba gum dɔri gu'udi biis nɛ bipɔla sibɛ'ɛdnam nɛ sɔɔnb, witchcraft nu'usin.
english: At that time red or otherwise colored threads were used to protect children and youths from evil spirits and witchcraft.

kusaal: Ba tisidi nidib banɛ ka ba nɔŋ, zuanam, nɛ ban kpin nɛ ninsieba.
english: They are given to loved ones, friends, and those people to whom one feels close.

kusaal: Martin Gyarko Oti anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n tis Techiman North linɛ bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la, o anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Martin Gyarko Oti is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Techiman North Constituency in the Bono East Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Oti nɛ nwadis anaasi daba atan' la yʋma1980 la ni, o yinɛ Aworowa linɛ bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana la.
english: Oti was born on 3 April 1980 and hails from Aworowa in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o digirii zamisʋg linɛ an Social Science yi University of Cape Coast sakurin yʋma 2008 la ni.
english: He had his Bachelor's degree in Social Science from the University of Cape Coast in 2008.

kusaal: Oti da anɛ pa'an n bɛ Ayeasu-Atrensu District Assembly Junior High Sakur la ni.
english: Oti was a tutor at Ayeasu-Atrensu District Assembly Junior High School.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaanɛ tis Techiman North sʋ'ʋlʋm la lin da yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la 2017 ti paae yʋma 2021 la ni.[5] Yʋma 2020 la ka Ghana dim da maal vɔɔt la, ka o kɔ'ɔŋ kʋk ka Elizabeth Ofosu-Agyare onɛ da an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la da di ka bas o.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he lost the parliamentary seat to the NDC parliamentary candidate Elizabeth Ofosu-Agyare.

kusaal: O da mɔri vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne nɛ anii (21,008) ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin anɛ vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al anu (47.5%) vɔɔt la kanl wʋsa ni ka o tiraan Elizabeth mɔr vɔɔt kal 23,252 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin anɛ pisnu nɛ ayi' du'ali anu (52.5%) vɔɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: He had 21,008 votes making 47.5% of the total votes cast whilst Elizabeth had 23,252 votes making 52.5% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Onɛ da an Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la Minista nya'andɔl.
english: He was the former Deputy Minister for Bono East Region.

kusaal: Oti anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Oti is a member of New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Oti anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Oti is a Christian.

kusaal: Martin Kwaku Adjei-Mensah Korsah anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas Gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la tis Techiman South Constituency bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Martin Kwaku Adjei-Mensah Korsah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Techiman South Constituency in the Bono East Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Nannanna, o anɛ Deputy Minister for Local Government, Decentralization and Rural Development.
english: He is currently the Deputy Minister for Local Government, Decentralization and Rural Development.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Korsah nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii, Nwadisa anaasi la dabpiinɛ ayi daar (12 April 1978) o yinɛ Techiman bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Korsah was born on 12 April 1978 and hails from Techiman in the Bono East Region.

kusaal: O da maalnɛ Government, History and Christian Religious Studies.
english: He completed his SSSCE in 1998 where he studied Government, History and Christian Religious Studies.

kusaal: O da maali o Bachelors of Arts in Political Science yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005), University of Ghana, ka lɛn maali o master's degree in Politics and International Relations yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2007).
english: He received his Bachelors of Arts in Political Science in 2005 from the University of Ghana, and his master's degree in Politics and International Relations in 2007.

kusaal: Korsah da anɛ basic school coordinator gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni, GES.
english: Korsah was a basic school coordinator of GES.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ presiding member of the Techiman Municipal Assembly.
english: He was also the presiding member of the Techiman Municipal Assembly.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Director of Elections and Research tis Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party.
english: He was also the Director of Elections and Research for the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Korsah anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg NPP nid, ka an Wadmaani, tis Techiman South Constituency bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim la dim.
english: Korsah is a member of NPP and currently the MP for the Techiman South Constituency in the Bono East Region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, o da di Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ awai, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi (49,682) dinɛ an pisnu du'al pisi nɛ anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.24%) ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC nid la, Christopher Beyere Baasongti paam vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ awai, kɔbisyi' nɛ anu (49,205) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ awai du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (49.76%).
english: In the 2020 Ghana general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 49,682 votes making 50.24% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Christopher Beyere Baasongti had 49,205 votes making 49.76% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Korsah paas la'askanɛ gɔsid ya yɛla la (House committee) ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Foreign Affairs.
english: Korsah is a member of the House committee and also a member of Employment, Social Welfare and State Enterprises Committee.

kusaal: O da naae o SSSCE nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii (1998) la ni.
english: He completed his SSSCE in 1998 where he studied Government, History and Christian Religious Studies.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o an minista nya'adɔli tis Local Government, Decentralization and Rural Development.
english: He was appointed as the deputy minister for Local Government, Decentralization and Rural Development.

kusaal: Mary Grant vʋm bɛllim lin yi (6 Motul 1928 – 18 Senlʋŋ 2016) O da anɛ ti Ghana du'ata nɛ pɔliitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Mary Grant (6 August 1928 – 18 September 2016) was a Ghanaian physician and politician.

kusaal: Onɛ da an yiiga Ghana Council of State nid nɛ onɛ an yiiga sɔb onɛ paam zamisʋg linɛ an medical doctor n yi Wesley Girls High Sakurin la.
english: She was Ghana's first Council of State member and also the first Wesley Girls High School alumna to be a medical doctor.

kusaal: Grant n da an Ghana pu'a onɛ paasi atan' ka ba siak ye o mɔr mi'ilim kati wa'ae du'ata tima ni Susan Ofori-Atta (1947) nɛ Matilda J. Clerk da yi la nya'aŋ (1949).
english: Grant was the third Ghanaian woman to qualify in medicine after Susan Ofori-Atta (1947) and Matilda J. Clerk (1949).

kusaal: O da kpin nɛ Paa Grant, onɛ ka ba da buon o ye "Gold Coast pɔlitis saam la".
english: She was a relation of Paa Grant, who has been called "the father of Gold Coast politics".

kusaal: Mary Grant da keŋi o pin'ilʋg sakuri bɛ Obuasi Methodist Sakurin la.
english: Mary Grant had her basic education at Obuasi Methodist School.

kusaal: Ka o tɔlisʋg sakur mɛnɛ o da keŋnɛ Wesley Girls High Sakur linɛ bɛ Cape Coast sʋ'ʋlʋm la, Onɛ da an yiiga sakur bil kanɛ da mɔr mi'ilim sakurin la linɛ da tis o suor ye o keŋ United Kingdom keŋi medical doctor.
english: She had her secondary education from the Wesley Girls High School in Cape Coast, and went on to become the school's first alumna to qualify as a medical doctor after completing her training in the United Kingdom.

kusaal: On da tʋm n an laafi lʋgʋr du'ata kpɛɛm la nya'aŋ, Mary Grant da kena liebnɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd saŋkan la ka ba mɛ da gaŋ o ye o an nimma'asim lʋgʋr gbansɔbid yʋʋma 1985 la ni.
english: After working in the government health service as a medical officer, Mary Grant began her political career when she was appointed Secretary of Health in 1985.

kusaal: Grant da mɔr tʋʋma zi'esim nam sieba wʋʋ, onɛ da an nimma'asim lʋgʋr minista la nya'andɔl ka paas Provisional National Defense Council (PNDC) la ni.
english: Grant held many positions, including Deputy Minister of Health and Member of the Provisional National Defense Council (PNDC).

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ ti Ghana nɔba zug la'asʋg nam bɛdigʋ ni dunia zi'is bɛdigʋ ni, sieba wʋʋ World Health Organisation (WHO), General Assemblies bɛ Geneva nɛ Regional Conferences bɛ Africa, World Bank Meeting linɛ bɛ Africa Nimma'asim lʋgʋr, Cairo Conference linɛ Nidib kanl nɛ ba nɔbigir yɛla la, on mɛ da lɛn paas kpɛɛm banɛ da keŋ World Conference la'asʋg linɛ da an pu'ab held in Beijing in 1995.
english: She led Ghana's delegation to many international conferences, including World Health Organisation (WHO) General Assemblies in Geneva and Regional Conferences in Africa, World Bank Meeting in Africa Health, Cairo Conference on Population and Development, and she was among Ghana's delegation to the World Conference on Women held in Beijing in 1995.

kusaal: O da mɔri yʋʋma pisnii nɛ anii (88) ka kpi, niŋtaŋ win Sɛnlʋŋ dabisim 18, 2016 n bɛ 37 soogianam sibiti la ni linɛ bɛ Ankara, Ghana dim n da maal o kum malima la.
english: She died aged 88, on the afternoon of 18 September 2016 at the 37 Military Hospital in Accra, and was given a state funeral.

kusaal: Masawud Mohammed anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi n tis Pru West linɛ bɛ Brong-Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la, ba da du'a o nɛ nwadis anaasi la dabisim yinne daar la yʋma 1971.
english: Masawud Mohammed (born 1 April 1971) is a Ghanaian politician and was the member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Pru West Constituency in the Brong-Ahafo Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Mohammed nɛ nwadis anaasi la dabisim yinne daar la yʋma 1971 la ni n bɛ Prang linɛ bɛ Brong-Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Mohammed was born on 1 April 1971 at Prang in the Brong-Ahafo Region.

kusaal: O da keŋi University of Cape Coast ka naae ka di'e o kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an yiiga digirii nɛ o mastɛs digirii, li wʋsa bɛ gbaʋŋ zamisʋg ni.
english: He attended the University of Cape Coast and graduated with a bachelor's degree and master's degree, both in Education.

kusaal: O da anɛ pa'an n bɛ Atebubu College of Education sakurin la ka tʋm an D.E.C n tis Pru sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni.
english: Prior to this he worked as a teacher at Atebubu College of Education and served as the District Chief Executive of the Pru District.

kusaal: O da paam vɔt bam 10,740 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da paamnɛ vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ awai du'al pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu (49.66%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa ni, banɛ ka o da di ka basi ba la da anɛ Stephen Pambiin Jalulah, Eric Kwabena Asamoah nɛ Akurugu Zakarai Atiah.
english: He garnered 10,740 votes which represents 49.66% of the total votes cast and therefore defeated the other contestants including Stephen Pambiin Jalulah, Eric Kwabena Asamoah and Akurugu Zakarai Atiah.

kusaal: Mohammed da anɛ Pru West sʋ'ʋlʋm la wadmaan kʋdʋg.
english: Mohammed was the member of parliament for Pru West Constituency.

kusaal: Mohammed anɛ Mɔɔr.
english: Mohammed is a Muslim.

kusaal: O di pu'a mɔr biis anaasi.
english: He is married with four children.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobu (2016) la ni ya'as, ka o da lɛn zi'enɛ nya'a ka ba vɔt ka o di.
english: In 2016, he contested for the seat again in the 2016 general elections and won.

kusaal: O mɔr pu'a ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Victoria Sam, ba mɔr biis ayuobʋ.
english: He is married to Mrs. Victoria Sam (with six children).

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ntow bɛnɛ Nkwanta No.
english: Hon. Ntow was born in Nkwanta No. 2 on Monday, 11 November 1957.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ sakur bɛnɛ University of Education Winneba naae ka di'e o digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ zamisʋg linɛ an Social Studies la.
english: He attended the University of Winneba and had a Bachelor of Education Degree in Social Studies.

kusaal: Ntow da naae o zamisʋg bɛ University of Education Winneba sakur la ni ka di'e o Masters of Art in Human Rights kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋma 2007 la ni.
english: Ntow graduated from University of Education Winneba with a Masters of Art in Human Rights in 2007.

kusaal: Ghana gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr dim da nɔk o ye o tʋm nɛ ba an (Principal Supt and Social Science Tutor, Enchi College of Education).
english: He was also employed by GES (Principal Supt and Social Science Tutor, Enchi College of Education).

kusaal: Ntow da zi'enɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la zugu nya'a Aowin linɛ bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana kpɛla la yʋʋma 2008 ka Ghana dim da maal vɔt la ka o di kʋk nɛ vɔt nam bam 19, 291 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 54.09% n yi vɔt kanl wʋsa.
english: Ntow contested for Aowin constituency in the Western Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress in the 2008 Ghanaian general election and won the parliamentary seat with 19,291 votes representing 54.09% of the total votes.

kusaal: Onɛ Samuel Adu Gyamfi Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid o vɔt da anɛ 15, 393 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 43.16%, ka PNC nid Ebenezer Ebbi Kwaw Dankwa mɛ da mɔr vɔt bam 631 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 1.77% ka PP nid Martin Boadu la mɛ da mɔr 347 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 0.97% vɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: He won the election over Samuel Adu Gyamfi of the New Patriotic Party who polled 15,393 votes representing 43.16%, parliamentary candidate for PNC Ebenezer Ebbi Kwaw Dankwa had 631 votes which is equivalent to 1.77% and parliamentary candidate for the Convention People's Party Martin Boadu had 347 votes representing 0.97% of the total votes.

kusaal: Ntow anɛ onɛ ka ba da lɛn vɔɔt ka o di ya'as n an wadmaanɛ tis Aowin linɛ bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana la, Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug yʋma 2012 vɔɔt la ni.
english: Ntow was re-elected as a member of parliament for Aowin constituency in the Western Region of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress during the 2012 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: O da mɔri vɔɔt kal 035 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 56.67% yit vɔɔt la kanl wʋsa ni.
english: He was elected with 30,035 votes representing 56.67% of the total votes.

kusaal: 2008 the art meddah da pɛɛs nɛ Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
english: In 2008 the art of the meddahs was relisted in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Meddah da dɛŋim sin'iŋɛ sɔbʋdnɛ pʋ'ʋsʋmnam labaya, Turkish oral literature bʋʋdi Malina yɛla ka mɛ lɛm kpɛm zi'e kiŋ-kiŋ sɔbid ka pian'ad ka li dɔlisidi Turkish nomadic nɛ shamanist buudi malima yɛla dinɛ ka ba mɔri yi Central Asia na ka li ka' yɛ yɛl sia maalɛ, din yi 11th-13th centuries Turkish story-telling la, di pian'andɛ Arabic nɛ Persian buudi malima yɛla bɛdigʋ ka li yʋ'ʋn da nwɛnii nid yinnɛ ma'aa yɛla nɛ.
english: Whilst strongly based on Turkish nomadic and shamanist traditions brought from Central Asia rather than external influences, Turkish story-telling was influenced by the Arabic and Persian traditions by the 11th-13th centuries to become a form of one-man theatre.

kusaal: kıssahan la da pʋm bɛnɛ Seljuq saŋa sa la ɛɛnti pian'ad Arabic nɛ Persian epics yɛla, nɛɛ sɔlima dinɛ pa'an Ali and Hamza nɛ tales dinɛ yit One Thousand and One Nights ni na.
english: Such kıssahan existed during the Seljuq period and usually told Arabic and Persian epics, stories of Ali and Hamza, as well as tales from One Thousand and One Nights.

kusaal: Kıssahan labakʋda gbaʋŋin tiesidi pa'an ba buudi malima la da kɛn tuonɛ lɛm paae Ottoman saŋa la ba tʋmid Mustafa na'ayin, Mehmed II ɔnɛ da zin' I o na'am kʋkzug.
english: The tradition of kıssahan continued into the Ottoman period, as evidenced by the documentation of a kıssahan working in the royal palace named Mustafa during the reign of Mehmed II.

kusaal: 16th nɛ 18th centuries la sʋʋgiŋ, ka meddah nɔbʋg hali ka nidib bani li yɛla bɛdigʋ pamm.
english: Between the 16th and the 18th centuries, the meddah increased their influence in the society.

kusaal: Meddah anɛ yʋ'ʋri tis Turkey dim ninkanɛ pian'adi ba buudi malima yɛlkuda yɛla onɛ da zi'en nidib tuoni bɛ coffeehouse la'asʋg zin'igin la.
english: Meddah is the name given to a traditional Turkish storyteller, who played in front of a small group of viewers, such as a coffeehouse audience.

kusaal: Saŋa bɛdegʋ nii, ba da ɛɛnti ma Ottoman Empire 16th century saŋa mɔri wa'ae sa.
english: This form of performance was especially popular in the Ottoman Empire from the 16th century onwards.

kusaal: Meddah ɛɛnti mɔri ma'asim tiig, bɛɛ aŋkitif, bɛɛ bɔbʋg mɔri maan zanbina pa'an ye o bɔɔdi o tiaknɛ di'ema, ka o lɛm mɔr kʋkɔya tiasʋg ya'am ka I nyaŋidi dɔlisid buudi pian'ad kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb.
english: Meddah is the name given to a traditional Turkish storyteller, who played in front of a small group of viewers, such as a coffeehouse audience.

kusaal: nimbama da pian'dii epik tales yɛla tita'am di na ti lɛm buon yɛ kıssahan, dinɛ pɛ'ɛl nɛ Islamic yɛla bɛdigʋ, ka li koɛmisid Muslim Nam la yada niŋir ka mɛ sʋŋidi tiakid banɛ ka' Muslims la ka ba lieb Muslim nidib.
english: These narrators of mainly epic tales were known as kıssahan, with their stories containing strong Islamic elements that reinforced the faith of the Muslims in the audience and attempting to convert the non-Muslims.

kusaal: Saansa biela ni ka sɔlimbama yʋ'ʋm da nɔbigi pɛɛs Battal Gazi yɛla.
english: These stories expanded over time to include stories such as Battal Gazi.

kusaal: A la zug ka meddah dim la yu'on da di'emidi ba die'ma la nɛ ka li dɔl satire: ka ba si'em zug dɔl nɛ heroic tales ma'a nɛ bʋmbani naamid ninsaal vʋm pʋʋgin.
english: As such, the performances by the meddah became theatrical acts based on satire: their themes included heroic tales as well as occurrences of daily life; humorous anecdotes, mimicry of stereotypes and familiar people, "mockery of social mores" and criticism of officials, at times even the sultan, became the quintessence of their plays.

kusaal: Ba Nam kpɛm kɛnnɛ tuon hali pae 20th century.
english: They remained popular into the 20th century.

kusaal: Ba da buoni li yiiga ye Kessben F.C. ka nyaan ti'aki li yʋ'ʋr la lɛb Medeama Sporting Club yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ, yʋʋm paal nwadig la ni (January 2011).
english: It was formerly known as Kessben F.C. before changing its name to Medeama Sporting Club in January 2011.

kusaal: Medeama Football Club da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anii la ni (2008) ka nwɛn'ɛdi bɛ Ghana Division Three League.
english: Medeama Football Club was established in 2008 and began playing in the Ghana Division Three League.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga ni (2010), club da pʋ nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋ nwɛn'ɛ Ghana Premier League nii.
english: In 2010, the club failed in its initial attempt to qualify for the Ghana Premier League.

kusaal: Gbaŋ kanɛ pa'al ye ba an club la da yina yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga, samanpiid nwadig ni (December 2010) ka ba ti'aki li yʋ'ʋr la lɛb Medeama Sporting Club yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ, yʋʋmpaal nwadig ni (January 2011).
english: The licensing of the club was fully completed in December 2010, and the club was renamed Medeama Sporting Club in January 2011.

kusaal: Ba di'ema zin'ig la da ti'aki yi Abrankese linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la lɛb Tarkwa linɛ bɛ Western Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: The base of the Kessben club was moved from Abrankese in the Ashanti Region of Ghana to Tarkwa in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Zin'igkan kpɛn'ɛd nidib tusa piiga (10,000).
english: The stadium, commissioned in August 2024, has a seating capacity of just over 10,000.

kusaal: Lin zug ka yʋʋmkan na, ka ba da da' Kessben FC yʋʋmkan.
english: This led to the purchasing of the defunct Kessben FC the same year.

kusaal: Medeama SC nwɛn'ɛdi ba yin di'ema nɛ Akoon Park linɛ bɛ Tarkwa, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Medeama SC play their home matches at the T&A Stadium located in Tarkwa, Ghana.

kusaal: Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) anɛ a-sʋ'o-m-mɛŋ lʋgʋr kanɛ bɛ Accra, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, ka ba da pin'ili di yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1997).
english: The Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) is an international non-governmental organisation based in Accra, Ghana, and was founded in 1997.

kusaal: Kwame Karikari da an kʋkdaan kʋdʋg tis la'asʋg la.
english: It campaigns against violations and attacks on freedom of expression and promotes freedom of the press in West Africa. Kwame Karikari is the founder of the organization.

kusaal: Ba da zuŋi dinɛ Accra.Ghana gɔmena da yɛl ye ba kpɛmisid pʋ'ab ye ba la'am paasi zamis ICT.
english: The Government of Ghana was claimed to have committed to encouraging the mentorship and interaction of women to ICT issues.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016), MFWA da la'as nɛ nimbanɛ yi UNDP bɛ Ghana la ye ba pa'al labamɔɔnib SDGs yɛla nɛ pɔɔtim dinɛ ka di nyaŋi tʋm.
english: In 2016, MFWA collaborated with the rep of UNDP in Ghana to train journalists on SDGs and how they can report on the achievement of the goals.

kusaal: pʋ'ab banɛ yi Greater Accra, Volta, Eastern, Ashanti, Bono, nɛ Northern regions, Ghana da paam pa'al kaŋa.
english: Ladies from Greater Accra, Volta, Eastern, Ashanti, Bono, and Northern regions in Ghana benefited from the training.

kusaal: Labamɔɔn ban da yinɛ Radio Peace bɛ Winneba la, Citi FM bɛ Accra la, nɛ TV3 Network dinɛ bɛ Accra.
english: The journalists were Abdul Hameed Amponsah of Radio Peace in Winneba, Umaru Sanda Amadu of Citi FM in Accra, and Nina Abena Antwi-Kusi of TV3 Network also in Accra.

kusaal: Di mɔɔnnɛ gɛɛsid banɛ nimbanɛ daamid bɛɛ gu'ud ka labaya tʋntʋnnib pʋ nyaŋidi pian' ka dabiem kae la West Africa sʋ'ʋlim.
english: It is the biggest and most influential media development, and freedom of expression advocacy organisation in West Africa with national partner organisations in all 16 countries of the region.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2017), MFWA da zuŋi ba ligidi ieb suor ye di sʋŋ ka ba paam ligidi sʋŋ ka labamɔɔnib banɛ bɛ Ghana ka ba nyaŋi ka ba paam labayab ka pɔɔtim tis SDGS.
english: In 2017, MFWA launched a funding project to assist journalists in Ghana in accessing information and generating reports on SDGs.

kusaal: UNDP da sʋŋ la'ʋg la ba na niŋ si'em ka Labamɔɔnib nyaŋi tʋmi ba tʋʋma din nar ka di yin ɛ ban na zamis nidib la si'em.
english: The UNDP supported the scheme in the aim of the journalists playing their role in achieving the goals by educating citizens.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni (2020), MFWA da lɛn la'as nɛ Embassy of Netherlands dinɛ bɛ Ghana, la'as pʋ'abi pa'ali ba ye ba baŋ pʋ'ab nyad an si'em na'asaasɔɔngin Ghana kpɛla ni.Ba da pa'al pʋ'ab nwɛnɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisi ye ba baŋi ba nyadi Ghana kpɛla.
english: In 2020, MFWA in collaboration with the Embassy of Netherlands in Ghana, organized a workshop for female individuals to improve the rights of women online in the country.

kusaal: La'asʋg la da lɛn zuŋ ban na dɔl suokanɛ ka ba na dɔl ka nɔɔryinne ken' Ghana Police Service nɛ labaya mɔɔlʋg zin'is Ghana.
english: The organization also launched a framework to improve the relations between the Ghana Police Service and the media in Ghana.

kusaal: Gbana la anɛ siakiri yi daʋŋ kanɛ da naam police service nɛ media dim zaŋi ken ban da daam labamɔɔn sieba la yɛla.
english: The document was said to be in response to the 'frosty' relationship that occurred between the police service and the media concerning attacks on some journalists.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016), MFWA da tis labamɔɔnib sieba piini nɛ ban mɔɔl SDGs yɛla la.
english: In 2016, MFWA rewarded some journalists for reporting on SDGs.

kusaal: Mercy Adu Gyamfi (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋma tusir mɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne nwadis anu la yiiga daar (1 sigisaa nwadig 1971) o da anɛ Ghana wadmaan ka bɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party, wadmaanib banɛ da zu'oe gati ba wadmaan taaba banɛ da Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.
english: Mercy Adu Gyamfi (born 1 May 1971) is a Ghanaian Parliamentarian, a member of the New Patriotic Party, the majority group in parliament, and a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Mercy Adu-Gyamfi yinɛ Akwatia, bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana ka ba da du'a o nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne nwadis anu la yiiga daar (1 sigisaa nwadig 1971)
english: Mercy Adu-Gyamfi comes from Akwatia, in the Eastern Region, of Ghana, and was born on 1 May 1971.

kusaal: Mercy Adu-Gyamfi da keŋɛ Presby Middle School bɛ Akwatia ka yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) la ni ka o da di'e o Middle School Leaving kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: Mrs. Mercy Adu-Gyamfi attended Presby Middle School in Akwatia and in the year 1988, she obtained the Middle School Leaving Certificate.

kusaal: O anɛ kpipinkpin ka lɛn an onɛ maan zut ka da lieb wadmaan Ghana kpɛla yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ nwadis pii nɛ ayi' (samanpiid nwadig 2016) on da di Akwatia constituency bɛ Eastern Region kʋk la.
english: She became a member of Ghana's parliament in December 2016, when she won the seat of Akwatia constituency in the Eastern Region.

kusaal: O da anɛ managing director, tis Amasey Pharmacy, bɛ Kade sʋ'ʋlim, bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana.
english: She was a managing director, of Amasey Pharmacy, in Kade, in the Eastern Region.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pistan' nɛ atan' (21,433) yit vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (37,716) yit vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin, dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al pisi nɛ yinne kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (57,21%) ka bas o taaba Baba Jamal Mohammed Ahmed nɛ Joice Sakei.
english: She obtained 21,433 votes out of the 37,716 valid votes cast, equivalent to 57,21% over her opponents Baba Jamal Mohammed Ahmed and Joice Sakei.

kusaal: Mercy Adu Gyamfi mɔr sid nɛ biisa ayuobʋ.
english: Mercy Adu Gyamfi is married and has six children.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Church of Pentecost.
english: She is a Christian and a member of the Church Of Pentecost.

kusaal: O mɔr sid nɛ biisa ayuobʋ.
english: She is married with six kids.

kusaal: Mexico nye dukɔ si le Dziehe Amerika ƒe dzigbe gome, eye United States do liƒo le eƒe dziehe gome, Mexico-ƒuta kple Caribbean Ƒua le eƒe ɣedzeƒe gome, Belize kple Guatemala le eƒe dzigbeɣedzeƒe gome, eye le ɣetoɖoƒe kple dzigbe gome Atsiaƒu si me Ŋutifafa le.
english: Mexico, officially the United Mexican States, is a country in North America. It is the northernmost country in Latin America, bordering the United States of America to the north and Guatemala and Belize to the southeast, while having maritime boundaries with the Pacific Ocean to the west, the Caribbean Sea to the southeast, and the Gulf of Mexico to the east.

kusaal: Mexico nye dukɔ evelia si ƒe ganyawo le sesẽm wu le Latin Amerika eye wònye dukɔ si le ŋgɔ yim eye wòle ŋgɔ yim.
english: Mexico has one nuclear power plant, the Laguna Verde Nuclear Power Station located in the state of Veracruz and numerous wind farms, with the largest wind farm in Latin America located in Oaxaca.

kusaal: Tsaɖiɖi nye Mexico ƒe ganyawo ƒe akpa vevi aɖe, eye teƒe siwo amewo lɔ̃a yiyi abe Cancun, Riviera Maya, Los Cabos, Mexico City, kple dutanyigbawo abe Oaxaca kple San Miguel de Allende ene le afima.
english: To the south of Cancun is the coastal strip called Riviera Maya which includes the beach town of Playa del Carmen and the ecological parks of Xcaret and Xel-Há.

kusaal: Mexicotɔwo ƒe dekɔnuwo nye anyigbadzitɔwo, Spaintɔwo, eye le mɔ sue aɖe nu la, Afrikatɔwo kple Asiatɔwo ƒe ŋusẽkpɔɖeamedziwo ƒe tsakatsaka.
english: Mexican culture reflects a long and complex history of interactions between various peoples through migration, conquest, and trade.

kusaal: Ba maali dinɛ ka di paas Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Japan ka lɛn paas UNESCO Representative List of Human Intangible Cultural Heritage ye di gu' Intangible Cultural Heritage.
english: It has been designated as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Japan and is listed in the Representative List of Human Intangible Cultural Heritage of the UNESCO Convention for the Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

kusaal: Di anɛ kuob malʋŋʋ ye ba zun'oe Sanbai (Ta-no-Kami) ka sɔs Wina'am ye tisi ba zʋʋd bɛdegʋ ka ba bʋn, di mɛ lɛn anɛ suokanɛ ka nidib la dplli tʋm tʋʋmtitada.
english: It is a farming ritual to worship Sanbai (Ta-no-Kami) and pray for a good harvest and good harvest, and it is also a device to enjoy the hard labor of rice planting.

kusaal: Nidib yɛl ye di paami di yʋ'ʋr kanɛ an Hanada Ue ka li yinɛ din an si'em la zug.
english: It is said that it got the name of Hanada Ue because of its gorgeous appearance.

kusaal: Mibu no Hana Tadashi an zin'ikanɛ ka ba kuod mui bɛdegʋ western Japan wʋsa, ka "Kawatoda Orchestra" nɛ "Mibu no Hana Tadashi" maan malima la.
english: Mibu no Hana Tadashi is the largest rice planting in western Japan, and the "Kawatoda Orchestra" and "Mibu no Hana Tadashi" convey the tradition.

kusaal: Ya'asa, din bɛllim yuug si'em la zug, Ba da zaŋi li paas important intangible folk cultural property tis Japan yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayupobʋ (1976) la ni, ka lɛn zaŋi li paas UNESCO intangible cultural heritage yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne nwadis piinɛ yinne la ni.
english: In addition, due to its depth of history, it was designated as an important intangible folk cultural property of Japan in 1976, and was registered as a UNESCO intangible cultural heritage in November 2011.

kusaal: Din yi Kamakura saŋa, di anɛ malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba maan bɛ western Japan ye Saotome yʋʋm mui sɛɛb yʋʋma, ka ba ya'a yʋʋm mui sɛɛb yʋʋma laka vʋʋn nɛ bʋnnwɛ'ɛda, bʋnnwɛ'ɛdbil, wiig, bɛɛ kane kanɛ ka ba nɔk nu'ugi maaldɔlisid sankanɛ ka Sasara tik nu'ug ka ba maali li.
english: Since the Kamakura period, it has been customary in western Japan for a Saotome to sing a rice planting song while singing a rice planting song, whispering with a large drum, a small drum, a flute, or a hand-made kane, in accordance with the time signature of Sasara.

kusaal: O mɛn da an kabitin bɛ Ghana national team la ni bɛ wʋʋ nɔɔrin 50.
english: He also played for the Ghana national team, earning more than 50 caps.

kusaal: Ka 2000 nii, o du'oe keŋ France pɛ'ɛs Bastia, dinɛ ka o bɛ anina yʋma atan' ka nwɛ' gaad nwɛ'ɛb 60 ka naam pɛ'ɛs Ligue 1 title holders Lyon bɛ 2003 ni.
english: In 2000, he moved to France to join Bastia, where he would spend three seasons and appear in over 60 matches before joining Ligue 1 title holders Lyon in 2003.

kusaal: Lyon nii, Essien di back-to-back league titles bɛ 2003–04 nɛ 2004–05 ni, ka di Ligue 1 Player tita'ar bɛ yʋum kana ni 2005.
english: At Lyon, Essien won back-to-back league titles in 2003–04 and 2004–05, and won Ligue 1 Player of the Year in 2005.

kusaal: O di UEFA Champions League bɛ 2011–12 ni, ka ba nɔk o ni'iŋ runner-up bɛ 2007–08 UEFA Champions League ni.
english: He won the UEFA Champions League in 2011–12, while also placing as runner-up in the 2007–08 UEFA Champions League.

kusaal: Ba du'au nɛ Accra tis Aba Gyandoh nɛ James Essien, Essien keŋnɛ Gomoa Nyanyano DC Primary nɛ JSS.
english: Essien attended Gomoa Nyanyano DC Primary and JSS.

kusaal: O da nwɛ' bɛ kilab under-17 tiim ni ka di tis Derby Teŋ la.
english: He played in the club's under-17 team's defeat to Derby County.

kusaal: O nwɛ'ɛb saŋa laa, Essien da anɛ midfilda tita'ar yinne dunia la wʋsa.
english: Essien broke through when he played in the 1999 FIFA U-17 World Championship in New Zealand.

kusaal: Essien da ka'nɛ ye onɛ tɔn'ɔn takid la zug ma'aanɛ, amaa onɛ mɛn da tɔn'ɔn zi'enid lalli ka yaŋidi dit gɔɔlnam la.
english: On 12 January 2002, Essien scored the equalising goal against Marseille at the Stade Vélodrome to even the match at 2–2.

kusaal: Essien da pin'ili o nwɛ'ɛb lanɛ Liberty Professionals bɛ Ghana la.
english: A midfielder, Essien started his career playing for Liberty Professionals in Ghana.

kusaal: Ka 2005 nii, Essien keŋ Premier League ni bɛ Chelsea ka ba yɔɔd o £24.4 million transfer fee, onɛ da an Africa bɔɔlnwɛ'ɛd kanɛ ligidi kpi'em bɛ bɔɔl pin'ilʋg wʋsa.
english: The same year, Essien signed with Premier League side Chelsea for a £24.4 million transfer fee.

kusaal: Chelsea nii, Essien da sʋŋ kilab la ka ba di'e Premier League bɛ 2006 nɛ 2010 ni, pɛ'ɛs nɛ three FA kapnam atan' nɛ League kab yinne.
english: At Chelsea, Essien helped the club win the Premier League in 2006 and 2010, as well as three FA Cups and one League Cup.

kusaal: O di Chelsea Goal bɛ yʋʋmkana ni nɔɔr ayi', bɛ 2006–07 nɛ 2008–09 yʋʋm la ni.
english: He has won the Chelsea Goal of the Season award twice, in the 2006–07 and 2008–09 seasons.

kusaal: Augustine's College bɛ Cape Coast, nwɛ'ɛdi bɛ Liberty Professionals.
english: He began his football career after graduating from St. Augustine's College in Cape Coast, playing at a local club, Liberty Professionals.

kusaal: Essien suor da yɔ'ɔg ya onɛ da nwɛ' 1999 FIFA U-17 World Championship bɛ New Zealand la.
english: Essien's international career started with the Ghana under-17 national team, the Black Starlets when he played in the 1999 FIFA U-17 World Championship in New Zealand and won the bronze medal.

kusaal: Ka Europeandim pin'ili kpans o, ka Essien paam kpansib bɛ Manchester United bɛ April 2000 ni.
english: European scouts began to take notice, prompting a trial at Manchester United in April 2000.

kusaal: Michael Yaw Gyato anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da lɛn an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Krachi East Constituency bɛ Volta Region la wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba Zug.
english: Michael Yaw Gyato (born 2 April 1970) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Krachi East Constituency in the Volta Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Michael Gyato nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nwadisa anaasi la li daba ayi' daar (vaala nwadig 2, 1970), Dambai, bɛ Volta Region la.
english: Michael Gyato was born on 2 April 1970, in Dambai, in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o HND kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛnɛ Accra Polytechnic ka maal o Master's kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit Ghana Institute of Management.
english: He acquired his HND from Accra Polytechnic and his Master's degree from the Ghana Institute of Management.

kusaal: Onɛ pin'il, ka an Board Member ka lɛn an Executive Director tis Smiling Heart Foundation.Asʋ'oe-m-mɛŋ lʋgʋr kanɛ bɛ Krachi East Municipality bɛ Oti Region la ka di tʋʋm an ye di sʋŋ nɔŋ dim nɛ tadimnam.
english: He is the founder, Board Member and Executive Director of Smiling Heart Foundation.

kusaal: Girimadaan Gyato da anɛ Minista for Sanitation and Water Resources nya'andɔl Akuffo-Addo gɔmena yiiga la ni din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021).
english: Gyato again contested the Krachi East Parliamentary seat on the New Patriotic Party ticket during the 2020 Ghanaian general election but lost the election to Wisdom Gidisu of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba mi'i o nɛ ye o ɛnti maan sini la ka gbɛɛni bɛ E4 sitcom Chewing Gum yʋma tusa ayi, nɛ piiga nɛ anu paae yʋma tusa ayi, nɛ piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi (2015–2017) la ni ka o da di ya'an bɛ BAFTA Award for Best Female Comedy Performance; nɛ the BBC One/HBO comedy-drama series I May Destroy You yʋma tusa ayi, nɛ pisyi (2020) la ni ka o da di dinɛ anɛ British Academy Television Award for Best Actress yʋma tusa ayi, nɛ pisyi nɛ ayinne (2021)la ni.
english: She is known for creating and starring in the E4 television sitcom Chewing Gum (2015–2017), for which she won the BAFTA Award for Best Female Comedy Performance; and the BBC One / HBO comedy-drama series I May Destroy You (2020), for which she won the British Academy Television Award for Best Actress in 2021.

kusaal: O di'ema dinɛ yʋʋri buon yee I May Destroy You, Coel da anɛ yiiga ninsabil kanɛ an pua da nyaŋi di ya'aŋ bɛ Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Limited series sini nam bi'ela nwa, Movie, bɛɛ Dramatic Special.
english: For her work on I May Destroy You, Coel was the first black woman to win the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Limited Series, Movie, or Dramatic Special.

kusaal: Michaela Ewuraba Boakye-Collinsonba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm kɔbiswai pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi (1987) bɛ East London.
english: Michaela Ewuraba Boakye-Collinson was born on 1 October 1987 in East London, England.

kusaal: O da kenne Catholic schools bɛ East London, ka ba ye on da nam ken biis sakur la o da bugusidi nidib biis, k aba pa'al ye on an da ninsabil o kɔn'ɔkɔn'ɔ bɛ sakurin la yɛla.
english: She attended Catholic schools in East London, and has said that, during primary school, she bullied other pupils.

kusaal: Din yi yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi yʋma tusa ayi(2007) la keŋi paae yʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni Coel da kenɛ University of Birmingham, zamisid English Literature nɛ Theology.
english: From 2007 to 2009, Coel attended the University of Birmingham, studying English Literature and Theology.

kusaal: O da di yiiga bɛ Laurence Olivier Bursary Award ka li da sʋŋɔ ka o nyaŋi gɔsidi o sakur yɛla.
english: She won the Laurence Olivier Bursary Award, which helped her fund her schooling.

kusaal: Saŋa kanɛ ka o da bɛ Guildhall la, Coel kenɛ Mark Proulx zamisʋg zin'ig bɛ Prima del Teatro zamis dinɛ an Kat Francois Poetry zamisʋg dinɛ bɛ Theatre Royal Stratford East.
english: During her time at Guildhall, Coel attended the Mark Proulx workshop at Prima del Teatro and took the Kat Francois Poetry Course at the Theatre Royal Stratford East.

kusaal: O da zamis yʋma nɛ d'ema sakur (Guildhall School of Music and Drama) bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayi (2012) la ni.
english: She graduated from the Guildhall School of Music and Drama in 2012.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobu (2006) la ni Coel da yi palʋ na maan sɛnlʋŋ bɛ Ealing.
english: In 2006, Coel began performing at poetry open mics in Ealing.

kusaal: Coel onɛ maan sɛnldʋŋ di'ema la da di'em di'ema nam zin'isnam bɛdigʋ la'am pɛɛs Wembley Arena, Bush Theatre, Nuyorican Poets Cafe nɛ De Doelen, Rotterdam.
english: As a poet, Coel performed on many stages, including Wembley Arena, Bush Theatre, Nuyorican Poets Cafe and De Doelen, Rotterdam.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋr da anɛ Michaela The Poet.
english: She went by the name Michaela The Poet.

kusaal: Coel da tʋm nɛ Talawa Theatre Company summer school program TYPT bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai(2009) la ni.
english: Coel joined the Talawa Theatre Company summer school program TYPT in 2009.

kusaal: O saŋa ka o da bɛ Talawa la, Coel o da pɛɛs TYPT yʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) Krunch sini maalʋg la ni, dinɛ ka Amani Naphtali da gɔsidi li yɛla.
english: During her time at Talawa, Coel was in the TYPT 2009 production of Krunch, directed by Amani Naphtali.

kusaal: Di'ema mɔri kɛŋ Bush Theatre yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayi (2012) la ni, Royal Theatre Holland yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayi (2012) la ni, Royal Exchange Theatre yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ atan' (2013) la ni, nɛ National Theatre yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anaasi (2014) la ni.
english: The play was next produced by the Bush Theatre (2012), Royal Theatre Holland (2012), Royal Exchange Theatre (2013) and the National Theatre (2014).

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi ne piiga atan' (2013) la ni Coel yi Channel 4 drama Top Boy ni na ka da onɛ gaad tuoni bɛ National Theatre, ka lɛm pɛɛs ban ɛ da di yiiga yin la ka Media da pian'a o yɛla.
english: In 2013, Coel appeared in the Channel 4 drama Top Boy.

kusaal: Channel 4 da pi'an pa'al ye Coel n sɔb galima sini dinɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr buon ye Chewing Gum, kpɛmisidi o di'ema nɛ Chewing Gum Dreams be Mɔtul Nwadig yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anaasi (August 2014) la ni.
english: Channel 4 announced in August 2014 that Coel would write and star in a new sitcom called Chewing Gum, inspired by her play Chewing Gum Dreams.

kusaal: O da yi sini kanɛ an "C4 Comedy Blaps" na an ninla'as Sɛnlʋŋ Nwadig yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anaasi(2014) la ni, di'ema la da sin'iŋi E4 bɛ Mɔtul Nwadig yʋma tusa ayi piiga nɛ anu(October 2015).
english: "C4 Comedy Blaps" were released as teasers in September 2014, and the series began on E4 in October 2015.

kusaal: On da di'em sʋ'dŋa la zug ka o da d'e British Academy Television Award an pua kanɛ an Best Female Comedy Performance bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu (2016) la ni.
english: Her performance earned her the British Academy Television Award for Best Female Comedy Performance in 2016.

kusaal: O da di BAFTA ya'an dinɛ anɛ Breakthrough Talent nɛ on da nyaŋi sɔb yʋma la titua la.
english: She also won a BAFTA for Breakthrough Talent for writing the show.

kusaal: yʋʋma banɛ da dɔl wʋsa o da di'em dinɛ an Lilyhot be E4 sci-fi comedy-drama The Aliens, ka di yi Bulgaria na.
english: The following year, she played Lilyhot in the E4 sci-fi comedy-drama The Aliens, which was filmed in Bulgaria.

kusaal: O da lɛm yi dinɛ an Nosedive" nɛ "USS Callister" episodes an Charlie Brooker's series Black Mirror.
english: She also appeared in both the "Nosedive" and "USS Callister" episodes of Charlie Brooker's series Black Mirror.

kusaal: Coel da lɛm mɔr tʋʋma bi'ela bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi(2017) sini kanɛ an Star Wars: The Last Jedi.
english: Coel also had a small role in the 2017 film Star Wars: The Last Jedi.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anii(2018) la ni, Coel da pɛɛsi bɛ Black Earth Rising, a co-production nɛ BBC Two tɛŋsʋg nɛ Netflix, anina ka o di'em di'em kanɛ an kate, ani ka o an diem-di'em kpɛɛm.
english: In 2018, Coel starred in Black Earth Rising, a co-production between BBC Two and Netflix, where she played Kate, the main character.

kusaal: O da lɛm pɛɛs nɛ Simone yʋma di'ema sini dinɛ an Been So Long, ka Che Walker gɔsi li yɛla, on mɛŋ di'ema an si'em dinɛ ka o da yi li bɛ Netflix ni k aba pian'a di yɛla sʋm yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anii(2018) la ni.
english: She also starred as Simone in the musical-drama film Been So Long, by Che Walker, based on his own stage play, which was released on Netflix to positive reviews in October 2018.

kusaal: Di'em kan da maalnɛ bɛ BBC One bɛ UK nɛ HBO bɛ US yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi Sigir nwadig (June 2020) la ni, dinɛ da gilig babir bɛdigʋ.
english: The show launched on BBC One in the UK and HBO in the US in June 2020 to widespread acclaim.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi (2022) la ni, Coel da pɛɛsi kɔbiga ni nimbanɛ mɔr ya'am na nyaŋi pan'a tiak ninsaal ya'am(Time's 100 Most Influential People).
english: In 2020, Coel was included in Time's 100 Most Influential People.

kusaal: Coel da lɛm yinɛ British Vogue's yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi (2020) ni n aka di pa'al ye onɛ an puakanɛ mɔr mi'ilim, ya'am ka mi'i pian'ad.
english: Coel also appeared in British Vogue's 2020 list of influential women.

kusaal: Dinɛ lɛm pɛ'ɛs ya'as anɛ 15th annual Powerlist dinɛ da pa'an banɛ mɔr ya'am African bɛɛ African-Caribbean heritage bɛ United Kingdom, Coel da dinɛ zi'isim anaasi daan (ranked fourth) nɛ on da tʋm sʋm sʋŋ dinɛ anɛ I May Destroy You.
english: Furthermore, in the 15th annual Powerlist of the most influential people of African or African-Caribbean heritage in the United Kingdom, Coel was ranked fourth for the impact of her work I May Destroy You.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi ayinne, Mɔraug Nwadig (July 2021) Coel da pɛɛs Black Panther: Wakanda Forever dinɛ ka o da yisi li Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi ayi, Sapal Nwadig (November 11, 2022) la ni.
english: In July 2021, Coel was cast in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever which was released on November 11, 2022.

kusaal: O da lɛm di'em dinɛ an Aneka o da lɛm pɛɛsi tʋm nɛ Dora Milaje.
english: She plays the role of Aneka, a member of the Dora Milaje.

kusaal: Coel yiiga gbaʋŋ, dinɛ an Misfits: a Personal Manifesto la, o da zaŋii li pa'al UK nɛ USA yimmʋ, Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi ayinne (7 September 2021) ka li anɛ Ebury Press da gbaʋŋ la pa'alʋg yɛla.
english: Coel's first book, Misfits: a Personal Manifesto, was published simultaneously in the UK and the USA on 7 September 2021 by Ebury Press.

kusaal: On mɛŋi zamis si'el nɛ MacTaggart bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi anii (2018) la ni, bɛ Edinburgh Festival, dinɛ da si'isi Coel mi'ilim dinɛ anɛ si'el kanɛ ninvʋsaal pʋʋgin pa'an dinɛ ka o na nyaŋ, onɛ da zaŋ gbaʋŋ la pa'al la pian'a di yɛla ye di an sʋm, ka di pia'adi sida dinɛ na nyaŋi tiak ninsaal bɛlim.
english: Based on her MacTaggart lecture at 2018's Edinburgh Festival, which touches on Coel's experiences with racism and misogyny, her publisher described the book as "a powerful manifesto on how speaking your truth and owning your differences can transform your life".

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ coel ka o pɛɛs banɛ gɔsid pdtɛn'ɛr pian'ad yɛla, yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi ayi (Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature in 2022) la ni.
english: Coel was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature in 2022.

kusaal: O da lɛm di ya'an bɛ David Lowery's Mother Mary.
english: In 2026, she starred in David Lowery's Mother Mary.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu 2016 British Academy Television Awards, Coel da yɛtnɛ fʋ ti ta'ar dinɛ ka o ma maal, o da maal nɛ Kente cloth (fʋʋg).
english: At the 2016 British Academy Television Awards, Coel wore a gown designed by her mother, made of Kente cloth.

kusaal: o da yɛli ala, wʋʋ o di'ema kanɛ an Chewing Gum di'em- di'em Tracey, o da kena yʋ'ʋm pʋ'ʋsid hali bɛ Pentecostal Christian ka pʋ bɔɔd ye o ɛllɛ.
english: She has said that, like her Chewing Gum character Tracey, she became very religious as a Pentecostal Christian and embraced celibacy.

kusaal: O yaaŋi da an raaper ka an author Guvna B.
english: Her cousin is the rapper and author Guvna B.

kusaal: O du'adib la wʋsa anɛ Ghanaian.
english: Her parents are Ghanaian.

kusaal: O ma la da gɔs on nɛ o pitʋ yinne bɛ ka ba nɔbig kpɛɛmnam bɛ East London, bɛ Hackney sakur la ni nɛ Tower Hamlets.
english: She and her sister were raised by their mother in East London, primarily Hackney and Tower Hamlets.

kusaal: O da nɔk Ché Walker masterclass ba da nyɛ Walker di'ema zin'igin yʋ'ʋŋ la.
english: She took a Ché Walker masterclass after meeting Walker at open mic nights.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai(2009) o da yi o sakur kudʋg la ni lɛb Guildhall Schoɔol of Music and Drama, onɛ da an yiiga nin sabil da maan yʋma anu la zamisʋg bɛ sakur la ni.
english: In 2009, she transferred to the Guildhall School of Music and Drama, where she was the first black woman enrolled in five years.

kusaal: On da kpɛm kɛn tuon ni maan la Ché Walker kanɛ an d'em-di'em ka lɛm gɔsi di'ema yɛla la da kpɛmis o, on da nyɛ ka o bɛ Hackney Empire ka ti maal ala nɔɔ bɛ Guildhall la.
english: As she continued to do open mics, she was encouraged to apply to Guildhall by director and actor Ché Walker, who saw her perform at the Hackney Empire.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan nɔɔ, coel da yis sɛlʋŋ paal dinɛ ka li yʋ'dr buon ye Fixing Barbie, ka di pa'al on maan sɛnlʋŋ nɛ yʋma zi'em.
english: That same year, Coel released an album entitled Fixing Barbie, which featured her work as a poet and musician.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ yinne (2011) la ni, Coel da yis dinɛ anɛ We're the Losers.
english: In 2011, Coel released the record We're the Losers.

kusaal: Coel di'ema kanɛ da an Chewing Gum Dreams anɛ on da bɛ sakurin la ka maali di bɛ Guildhall yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga.
english: Coel's play Chewing Gum Dreams was her senior graduation project at Guildhall in 2012.

kusaal: O da dɛsim yis yʋma la nɛ bɛ The Yard Theatre in Hackney Wick di'ema la ni Coel da anɛ pua yinne pa'an di'ema sɔlima dinɛ pian'adi pa'an yʋma piiga nɛ anaasi bipuŋɔ (a 14-year-old girl) ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Tracey.
english: The play was first produced at The Yard Theatre in Hackney Wick.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anu(2015) la ni, coel da yi bɛ BBC One drama London Spydi'ema ni na.
english: In 2015, Coel appeared in BBC One drama London Spy.

kusaal: Coel maal, sɔb, yis, ka gts di'ema yɛla dinɛ an I May Destroy You, ka di anɛ o mɛŋ mi'ilim da kpɛmis o dinɛ ka o da zamisi yi dinɛ anɛ puasan'aʋŋ yɛla la.
english: Coel created, wrote, produced, co-directed and starred in the comedy-drama series I May Destroy You, inspired by her own experience of sexual assault.

kusaal: TV ni di'ema dinɛ kena la Coel na sɔbi d'em dinɛ anɛ, nwad bil o yiiga daar dunia ni (First Day On Earth).
english: She will write, star in and executive produce First Day On Earth, a 10-part series for the BBC, which is in production as of 2026.

kusaal: Coel da kɛŋ Guildhall ya'aŋ la o da bas Pentecost pʋ'dsim la nɛ.
english: Coel stopped practising Pentecostalism after attending Guildhall.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anii (August 2018) la ni Coel da pian'a yis paalʋ ye da ayi da mʋk o ye ba digin nɛ o (sexually assaulted) saŋa kanɛ ka o da sɔbidi o di'ema dinɛ an Chewing Gum.
english: In August 2018, Coel disclosed that she was drugged and sexually assaulted by two unnamed men during the writing of her sitcom Chewing Gum.

kusaal: Ban da mʋk o la ya'aŋ ka di kpɛmis o ka o maal TV ni di'ema dinɛ an I May Destroy You la.
english: The attack would later inspire her to create the TV drama I May Destroy You.

kusaal: Misfits: A Personal Manifesto (UK ed.).
english: Coel's first book, Misfits: a Personal Manifesto, was published simultaneously in the UK and the USA on 7 September 2021 by Ebury Press.

kusaal: Ba nwɛ'ɛdi ba yaan bɔɔl bɛnɛ Jos International bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb zin'ig kanɛ mɔr yalʋŋ wʋʋ 45,000 la ni.
english: They play their home games at the Jos International Stadium, which has a capacity of 45,000.

kusaal: Ministry for Foreign Affairs anɛ Ghana gɔmena tʋʋma lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid teŋ la nɛ tensieba bɛllim an si'em nɛ international diplomacy.
english: The Minister for Foreign Affairs is a government official responsible for overseeing the foreign policy and international diplomacy of Ghana.

kusaal: Soogianami da faand na'am Ghana la, ba da tiak minister yʋ'ʋm buon ye commissioner bɛɛ secretary.
english: Under pre-1992 military regimes in Ghana, the title minister has been replaced by commissioner or secretary.

kusaal: Ministry yʋ'ʋ la'asnɛ nɛ lʋgʋr sieba ka di yʋ'ʋr an Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration ka di yinɛ Nana Akufo-Addo onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid la gban'ar.
english: During the government rule of Nana Akufo-Addo of the New Patriotic Party between January 2017 and January 2025, the ministry was combined with other portfolios to form the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration under Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey.

kusaal: Foreign minister ɛɛnti an kpɛɛm Cabinet la ni.
english: Currently Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, the minister is usually one of the most senior members of Cabinet.

kusaal: Minister for Foreign Affairs di yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi yʋʋmpaal nwadig la (January 2017) anɛ Honorable Shirley Ayorkor Botchway.
english: During the government rule of Nana Akufo-Addo of the New Patriotic Party between January 2017 and January 2025, the ministry was combined with other portfolios to form the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration under Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey.

kusaal: Ministry of Justice da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne la ni (1951) ban da maal Lidbury Commission ye di maal vɛɛnsʋg ka mɔri di pʋtɛn'ɛr na ka ba tiak Gold Coast Civil Service.
english: The Ministry of Justice was created in 1951 after the Lidbury Commission reviewed the administration of the Gold Coast Civil Service and recommended a structure modelled on the British Home Office.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Ministry of Justice da yɔ'ɔgya ka P. F. Branigan, onɛ an English expatriate la da aan di tuon gat.
english: The first head of the ministry was P. F. Branigan, an English expatriate.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ naasi la ni (1954) All African government da maal Gold Coast la, Ministry of Justice da nan kae.
english: In 1954, the Ministry of Justice was merged with the Ministry of Interior in the first all-African government.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnu nɛ yuobʋ la ni (1956), gɔmena paali da di la dɔlisid ban da lɛn vɔɔti Kwame Nkrumah ye o an Prime Minister, Ministry of Interior yʋ'ʋn da tiaki an Ministry of Interior and Justice, ka Ebenezer Ako-Adjei da an lʋgʋr la kpɛɛm, onɛ da an yiiga Ghana ninkanɛ da gɔsid ministry Ghana da paami asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yɔpɔi nwadisa atan la ni (March 1957).
english: It re-emerged in 1956 as the Ministry of Interior and Justice under Ebenezer Ako-Adjei.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Sankaŋa, Ministry of Justice da pʋ lɛn gɔsid Attorney General department ya'as nwɛnɛ Ministry for the Attorney General da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yɔpɔi nwadisa anii daba ayɔpɔi daar la (7 August 1957) ka Geoffrey Bing aan di zuraan.
english: Following Ghana's independence in 1957, the ministry was again split, creating a separate Ministry of Justice and an independent Ministry for the Attorney General, led by Geoffrey Bing.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii la ni (1958), ministry da paasnɛ Ministry of Local Government ka Kofi Asante Ofori-Atta da an onɛ aan di tuon.
english: Between 1958 and 1961, the ministry was merged with Local Government under Kofi Asante Ofori-Atta.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Judicial service da gaŋ Mrs Regina Ayerko Apotsi ye o an yiiga pʋ'a tʋm Judicial Secretary tʋʋma (13th).
english: In 2004, Mrs Regina Ayerko Apotsi became the first woman to serve as Judicial Secretary, the 13th person to hold the post.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Attorney Generali gɔsid civil cases ka vɔlisid nidib ka ba pʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛd Ghana.
english: It drafts legislation, advises the executive, oversees state prosecutions, and represents the Government of Ghana in civil cases.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Ministry of Justice da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne la ni (1951) dɔlisid Lidbury Commission da pian' di yɛla sʋm si'em la ka Attorney General mɛ pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yɔpɔi la ni (1877).
english: The modern Ministry of Justice was created in 1951 following recommendations of the Lidbury Commission.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Attorney Generali gɔsid Ministry of Justice.
english: The Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office of Ghana is the government ministry responsible for the legal affairs of the Republic of Ghana.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Ministry la da paasnɛ Attorney General ka da gɔsid Attorney General department tʋʋma.
english: The Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office of Ghana is the government ministry responsible for the legal affairs of the Republic of Ghana.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Di da la'asnɛ nɛ Ministry of Interior, ka ministry yʋ'ʋr da an; Ministry of Interior.
english: In 1954, the Ministry of Justice was merged with the Ministry of Interior in the first all-African government.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Ghana da paami asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yɔpɔi nwadisa atan la ni (March 1957) la, Ministry of Interior and Justice da buaki ayi kilim Ministry of Justice (yʋ'ʋn liebi di mɛŋ ministry) nɛ Ministry Interior.
english: Following Ghana's independence in 1957, the ministry was again split, creating a separate Ministry of Justice and an independent Ministry for the Attorney General, led by Geoffrey Bing.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Ako-Adjei yʋ'ʋn da kilim yiiga Minister of Justice tis Ghana din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1957) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii la ni (1958).
english: It re-emerged in 1956 as the Ministry of Interior and Justice under Ebenezer Ako-Adjei.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Ministry da yuolim buak yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nwadoisa awai la ni (September 1961) yʋ'ʋn kilimi di mɛŋ Ministry, Ministry of Local Government da la'asnɛ nɛ Ministry of Interior ka Kwaku Boateng an zuraan.
english: Between 1958 and 1961, the ministry was merged with Local Government under Kofi Asante Ofori-Atta.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Ministry of Justice da lɛn la'asnɛ nɛ ministry for Attorney General.
english: Following Ghana's independence in 1957, the ministry was again split, creating a separate Ministry of Justice and an independent Ministry for the Attorney General, led by Geoffrey Bing.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Attorney General da tiaki kilim Minister of Justice and Attorney General.
english: It became a standalone ministry again in September 1961 and was reunited with the Attorney-General's Ministry in 1965, forming the combined portfolio of Minister of Justice and Attorney General under Bashiru Kwaw-Swanzy.
en_article: Ministry of Justice and Attorney-General's Office

kusaal: Ministry of Attorney General kpɛɛm da anɛ B. E. Kwaw-Swanzy.
english: It became a standalone ministry again in September 1961 and was reunited with the Attorney-General's Ministry in 1965, forming the combined portfolio of Minister of Justice and Attorney General under Bashiru Kwaw-Swanzy.

kusaal: Din yi sankani paae zina Ministry of the Attorney General yʋ'ʋn la'asnɛ nɛ Ministry of Justice.
english: It became a standalone ministry again in September 1961 and was reunited with the Attorney-General's Ministry in 1965, forming the combined portfolio of Minister of Justice and Attorney General under Bashiru Kwaw-Swanzy.

kusaal: Ban dɔl Civil Service Law of 1993 (PNDCL 327) Sections 11 nɛ 13, Ministry of Youth and Sports mɔr tʋʋma dɔlisid Executive Instrument (EI) 28 yi 2017, ba maan ka duosid gbɛlima zaŋi ke dasam nɛ pʋ'asada nɛ ninwisigir yɛla.
english: Adhering to the provisions outlined in Sections 11 and 13 of the Civil Service Law of 1993 (PNDCL 327), the Ministry of Youth and Sports has been entrusted, under Executive Instrument (EI) 28 of 2017, with the responsibility of instigating and shaping policies related to Youth and Sports.

kusaal: Li da pin'il tʋʋma nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (1976).
english: It was formed in 1976.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi, nwadis ayɔpɔi, dabisa piiga nɛ awai (July 19, 1997), Ghana gɔmena da pin'il "Sports for All" gba'ar ka li anɛ ye li kɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa paas ninwisigir di'em ani, ka li sʋŋi ba niŋgbina nɛ ba pʋtɛnda nɛ ba siis nɛ ba bɛllim nɛ ba malima nam pʋʋgin.
english: On July 19, 1997, the Ghanaian government introduced the "Sports For All" policy to encourage widespread public involvement in sports, aiming to promote holistic physical, mental, spiritual, social, and cultural development among citizens.

kusaal: Honorius Akpeere da nyɛ gba'ar kaŋa yinɛ Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) ka mɔri li ken Ghana na yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1977).
english: Dr. Honorius Akpeere imported this concept from the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) and introduced it to Ghana in 1977.

kusaal: Li da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (1974) yinɛ wada NRDC 241, National Youth Authority (NYA) anɛ gɔmena lʋgʋr kanɛ ka ba tʋʋma an ye ba maal pu'asada nɛ dasam sʋŋir suoya Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka dasam nɛ pu'asada nɔbigir yɛla an ba bɔɔdim.
english: Established in 1974 through NRDC 241, the National Youth Authority (NYA) is a Statutory Public Organization tasked with coordinating and facilitating youth empowerment initiatives in Ghana to foster holistic youth development.

kusaal: Pin'ilig la li daa anɛ National Youth Council (NYC), ka nyɛ tiakir.
english: Originally known as the National Youth Council (NYC), the Authority underwent transformations.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981), ka li da tiaki an "National Youth Organizing Commission" ka li gban'ar an ye li maal "Democratic Youth League of Ghana (DYLG)".
english: In 1981, it became the "National Youth Organizing Commission" with a focus on creating the "Democratic Youth League of Ghana (DYLG)." Following the advent of constitutional rule in 1992, it reverted to being the "Council."

kusaal: Wada la da nyɛ tiakir laws of Ghana (Revised Edition) Act, 1998 (Act 562) ni, ka li da kɛ ka yʋ'ʋr kanɛ bɛ zina nwa an "National Youth Authority" la kena.
english: A statutory law revision under the laws of Ghana (Revised Edition) Act, 1998 (Act 562) resulted in the current name, the "National Youth Authority." Its role is to promote and oversee activities for empowering Ghanaian youth for comprehensive development.

kusaal: National Sports College la ba da mɛɛ li nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1984) bɛ Winneba mɛ bɛ Central region la.
english: The National Sports College was built in 1984 in Winneba in the Central region.

kusaal: College la da pin'il nɛ Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC) gɔmena na'adɔɔg na'am diib saŋa, ye li sʋŋ ka ninwisigir di'emanam nɔbigi paae dunia wʋsa.
english: The college was established by the Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC) government to promote various sporting disciplines to international levels.

kusaal: Harrison K. Sasu - DIRECTOR, FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION (F&A)
english: Mr. Harrison K. Sasu - DIRECTOR, FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION (F&A)

kusaal: Ministry of Youth and Sports dinɛ bɛ Ghana la anɛ gɔmena lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid dasam nɛ pʋ'asada tuon ken nɛ ba ninwisigir di'ema nɔbʋgir yɛla.
english: Adhering to the provisions outlined in Sections 11 and 13 of the Civil Service Law of 1993 (PNDCL 327), the Ministry of Youth and Sports has been entrusted, under Executive Instrument (EI) 28 of 2017, with the responsibility of instigating and shaping policies related to Youth and Sports.

kusaal: Ya'asa, ministry la tʋʋma an ye di gɔs ka la'as taaba, ka baŋi ba tʋʋma la kɛŋ tuoni paae siem bɛn ka mɛ lɛn kpɛmis taaba ka tʋʋma la nyaŋi kɛŋ tuon.
english: Moreover, the ministry is charged with the task of overseeing the coordination, assessment of operational efficacy, and appraisal of the sector's effectiveness.

kusaal: Yelkpan kanɛ ka Ministry of Youth and Sports mɔr anɛ ba sa'al gɔmena kati wa'ae suobanɛ na nyaŋi sʋŋ ka ba maal wada, ka gɔs ka li tʋm, ka baŋ lin tʋm paae si'em bɛni na nyaŋi sʋŋ dasam nɛ pu'asada tuon ken nɛ ba ninwisigir di'ema nɔbʋgir yɛla.
english: The core purpose of the Ministry of Youth and Sports is to offer proficient guidance in the creation, coordination, execution, surveillance, and assessment of policies concerning the development of Youth and Sports.

kusaal: National Sports Council tʋmmi ba tʋʋma an zug tis ninwisigir lʋga banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa.
english: Previously known as National Sports Council.

kusaal: National Youth Council anɛ gɔmena lʋgʋr kanɛ da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (1974) ye li mɔr sʋŋir nɛ nɔbigir ken pu'asada nɛ dasam nɔbigir pʋʋgin, dɔlisid la'asʋg sieba nam ni.
english: Established in 1974 through NRDC 241, the National Youth Authority (NYA) is a Statutory Public Organization tasked with coordinating and facilitating youth empowerment initiatives in Ghana to foster holistic youth development.

kusaal: Ninwisigir di'emanam da bɛnɛ Sporting Clubs, Cooperatives, nɛ Trade Unions nu'usin.
english: While various sporting disciplines were traditionally managed by Sporting Clubs, Cooperatives, and Trade Unions, the "Sports For All" discipline aimed to engage all segments of society, with a focus on development rather than competitive excellence.

kusaal: "Sports For All" da gba'a ye li la'as teŋgbaŋ wʋsa, ka li bɔɔdim anɛ teŋ maalig yɛla ka,ka' ya'an diib la ma'a ne.
english: While various sporting disciplines were traditionally managed by Sporting Clubs, Cooperatives, and Trade Unions, the "Sports For All" discipline aimed to engage all segments of society, with a focus on development rather than competitive excellence.

kusaal: Di'ema sieba bɔɔdim an ye ba di' ya'an la, "Sports for All" yelkpan ka' ye anɔ'ɔn gaad tuon bɛɛ kpɛlim nyaŋa.
english: Unlike disciplines striving for Olympic-level excellence, "Sports For All" doesn't emphasize rankings.

kusaal: Li yelkpan anɛ ye li sʋŋ ka mɔr tʋʋm sieb na ka Ghana pu'asada nɛ dasam nɔbigi keŋ tuon.
english: A statutory law revision under the laws of Ghana (Revised Edition) Act, 1998 (Act 562) resulted in the current name, the "National Youth Authority." Its role is to promote and oversee activities for empowering Ghanaian youth for comprehensive development.

kusaal: Li tʋʋma da anɛ ye li zamis Ghana dim ninwisigir di'emanam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb, ka tɛnrig banɛ tam di'em sieba nam.
english: A statutory law revision under the laws of Ghana (Revised Edition) Act, 1998 (Act 562) resulted in the current name, the "National Youth Authority." Its role is to promote and oversee activities for empowering Ghanaian youth for comprehensive development.

kusaal: John Kufour saga, administration k'o da la'as nɛ lʋg kʋda ayi, suoken lʋgʋr, Ministry of Roads and Highways la nɛ suoken nɛ labaya tisib lʋgʋr la nɛ 2001.
english: The ministry was formed from former agencies of two government ministries namely the Ministries of Roads and Highways and the Ministry of Transport and Communication in 2001 by the John Kufuor administration.

kusaal: 2009 yʋʋm la ni John Atta Mills da ti'aki lii pʋd Mimistry of Transport o saŋa la ni.
english: This name was changed in 2009 to the Ministry of Transport by the John Atta Mills administration.

kusaal: Ghana kateŋ kpikpiʋŋ, international trade, linɛ dɔlisid kuomin gat piswai kɔbʋga pʋʋgin, Tema Harbour bɛ Greater Accra Rrgion la n Takoradi Harbour bɛ Western Region la.
english: Over ninety percent of Ghana's international trade depends on the country's sea ports namely the Tema Harbour in the Greater Accra Region and the Takoradi harbour in the Western region.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr la kpɛɛm anɛ Minister of Transport la.
english: The head of the Ministry of Transport is the Minister of Transport.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr la tʋʋm anɛ ye li gɔs maal suoya la sʋ'ʋŋa ka kɛ ka sour duor mɛ an sʋm ti Ghana suokennib lʋgʋrin la, transport industry.
english: The ministry is responsible for the infrastructural development and service delivery in Ghana's transport industry.

kusaal: Ban da la'as lʋga ayi la, ba da pʋdi linɛ Ministry of Roads and Transport.
english: After the merger, it was known as the Ministry of Roads and Transport.

kusaal: Ghana gɔbina zugraan, President of Ghana sʋ'oe lʋgʋr la kpɛɛm gaŋir ka li lɛɛ anɛ Ghana wadmaannib, Parliament of Ghana na siak ka li nyaan zi'en.
english: It is a political appointment made by the President of Ghana subject to approval from the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: lʋgʋr kpɛɛm nananna anɛ Kwaku Ofori Asiamah, 2013 yʋʋm la ni k'o di'e kpɛŋ la yi Dzifa Attivor ni.
english: The sector minister during Nana Akufo-Addo's tenure was Kwaku Ofori Asiamah.

kusaal: Mohammed Abdul Aziz anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Mohammed Abdul Aziz is a Ghanaian politician who was the Member of Parliament for Mion constituency in the Northern Region of Ghana which he won in the 2016 Ghanaian parliamentary election.

kusaal: Onɛ da an wadmaan n tis Mion linɛ bɛ Ghana Northern Region sυ'υlυm la, yʋma tυsa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ vɔɔt la ni ka ba da vɔɔt ka o di.
english: Mohammed Abdul Aziz is a Ghanaian politician who was the Member of Parliament for Mion constituency in the Northern Region of Ghana which he won in the 2016 Ghanaian parliamentary election.

kusaal: Mohammed Adams Sukparu (6 January 1985) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la nid, National Democratic Congress.
english: Mohammed Adams Sukparu (born 6 January 1985) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Sissala West Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Upper West Region la dim.
english: He is the member of Parliament for the Sissala West Constituency in the Upper West Region.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Sukparu nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayuobʋ daar la, 6 January 1985, o yinɛ Bouti bɛ Sissala West District Upper West Regionsʋ'ʋlim, Gaana la.
english: Sukparu was born on 6 January 1985, he hails from Bouti in the Sissala West District in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da naaenɛ University of Professional Studies Accra (UPSA).
english: He attended the University of Professional Studies Accra (UPSA).

kusaal: O da anɛ pirɛsidɛni tis Asʋoe-m-mɛŋ Yunivɛsitinam sakur biis Gaana kpɛla (Private Universities Students' Association) of Ghana (PUSAG).
english: He was a student leader and served as the president of the Private Universities Students' Association of Ghana (PUSAG).

kusaal: O da lɛn zi'en Gaana sakur bis nɔba zug bɛ ninsabilis Yunivɛsitinam sakur biis la'askanɛ yʋ'ʋri an All-Africa Students Union (ASSU).
english: He also served as Ghana's representative to the All-Africa Students Union (ASSU).

kusaal: Sukparu da kpɛn' o Na'am nya'ab la nɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg (NDC) la bɛ Sissala West Constituency gur yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋg (2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: Sukparu entered the race for the parliamentary candidate in the NDC primaries in the Sissala West Constituency ahead of the 2020 elections.

kusaal: Sukparu da zi'en nya' nɛ o Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la (National Democratic Congress) nidib gur yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋg la (2020) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai Nwadisa anii la ni (August 2019) ka di yinɛ on da paam vɔɔt kɔbistan nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anu (345) gaad nidib ayi banɛ nya'ad nɛ o la, Mumuni Hakeem Duwiejuah nɛ Mary Hagbana Abu banɛ da paam kɔbis yi nɛ pistan nɛ anu (235) nɛ vɔɔt pistan nɛ anu (35).
english: Sukparu won the parliamentary bid to represent the National Democratic Congress for the Constituency ahead of the 2020 elections in August 2019 after securing 345 votes to beat his two other opponents Mumuni Hakeem Duwiejuah and Mary Hagbana Abu who had 235 votes and 35 votes respectively.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi la (December 2020), Sukparu da di Sissala West Constituency kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pistan nɛ yinne (17,731) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ ayi du'al pisnu nɛ anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (52.54%) ka onɛ ti'al o la , Naliwie Baluwie Salifu onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (New Patriotic Party) nid lan, Diisi kʋdʋg tis Sissala West District, da paam tusa piinɛ atan, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (13,994) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ atan du'al pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (43.87%).
english: In December 2020, Sukparu won the seat for Sissala West Constituency in the parliamentary elections after polling 17,731 votes representing 52.54% against his closest opponent, Naliwie Baluwie Salifu of the New Patriotic Party, a former District Chief Executive for the Sissala West District, who had 13,994 votes representing 43.87%.

kusaal: O yinɛ Ashalley Botwe bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He hails from Ashalley Botwe in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: O mɔr bachelor's degree of Business Administration, master's degree in Business Administration dinɛ ka zamis ligidi yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa.
english: He holds a bachelor's degree of Business Administration, a master's degree in Business Administration with specialization in Finance.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr Master of Arts in Economic Policy Management.
english: He also holds a Master of Arts in Economic Policy Management.

kusaal: Ramadan da anɛ onɛ sʋŋid (Special Assistant) nɛ presidential staffer bɛ Flagstaff House sankanɛ ka John Mahama da an pirɛsidɛn la.
english: Ramadan was a Special Assistant and presidential staffer at the Flagstaff House during the Presidency of John Mahama.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la, Ramadan da zi'en Ma'asim tiig National Democratic Congress zugʋ nya' Adenta Constituency ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party's nid la, Yaw Buaben Asamoa.
english: In the 2016 Parliamentary elections Ramadan stood for the National Democratic Congress in the Adenta Constituency and lost to the New Patriotic Party's Yaw Buaben Asamoa.

kusaal: Asamoa di ka bas o nɛ vas o nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistsn nɛ atan, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi (33,952) dinɛ an pisnu du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.64%) ka Ramadan paam vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ ayi,kɔbisnu nɛ pisnii nɛ anii, (32,588) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ anii du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (48.61%).
english: Asamoa polled 33,952 votes representing 50.64% as against Ramadan's 32,588 votes which was 48.61%.

kusaal: O da lɛn zi'eni nya' Ma'asim tiig NDC ninsieba ka dii lɛn nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: He once again stood for the primaries for the NDC and won to represent them in the 2020 Elections.

kusaal: O da diya ka bas Minista kʋdʋg kanɛ da gɔsid dap nɛ pʋ'ab nɛ biis bɛlim yɛla (Gender, Children and Social Protection), Nana Oye Lithur.
