english: He won against a former Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Nana Oye Lithur.

kusaal: O da diya nɛ vɔɔt kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pistan (730) ka pʋ'a la paam vɔɔt kɔbisnu nɛ pisnu nɛ anii (558) ka ba yɛl nyain ye onɛ di.
english: He won by polling 730 votes against her 558 votes to be declared winner.

kusaal: O ken kanɛ da paasi ayi la ka o da bɔɔd ye o di Adenta Constituency kʋk la, o da diya ka bas onɛ zin'i kʋk la, Yaw Buaben Asamoah onɛ da nya' nɛ o yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la, o da paam vɔɔt tusa pisyuobʋ nɛ atan, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pistan nɛ ayuobʋ 63,436 dinɛ an pisnu nɛ anu du'al awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (55.9%) ka o tiraan la paam tusa pisnaasi nɛ awai, kɔbisyi nɛ pisnu nɛ anu (49,255) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ atan du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (43.4%).
english: In his second bid to win the Adenta Constituency seat, he won against the incumbent member of parliament Yaw Buaben Asamoah who he contested against in the 2016 elections, He managed to poll 63,436 votes representing 55.9% as against 49,255 votes representing 43.4% by him.

kusaal: Mohammed Adamu Ramadan da kpɛn' Wadmaan yin la zi'eni tisi Adenta Constituency sʋ'ʋlim Gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba anii daar.
english: Mohammed Adamu Ramadan was sworn in as Member of Parliament representing the Adenta Constituency in the 8th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana on 7 January 2021.

kusaal: Onɛ aan Ahmed Ramadan People's National Convention (PNC) kʋkdaan kʋdʋg la dakɔnkpɛɛm ka aan Samira Bawumia, onɛ an pirɛsidɛn nya'adɔl pʋ'a la, taun kpɛɛm.
english: He is the first child of Ahmed Ramadan former chairman of People's National Convention (PNC) and the elder brother of Ghana's Second Lady Samira Bawumia.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ kpɛn pɔlitiks la o da tʋm nɛ Ghana Airways nɛ Ghana International Airlines.
english: Prior to entering politics, he worked with the former national airlines Ghana Airways and Ghana International Airlines.

kusaal: Mohammed Adamu Ramadan (da du'anɛ 3 May 1975) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Mohammed Adamu Ramadan (born 3 May 1975) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: Paasnɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la National Democratic Congress la ni.
english: He is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tisi Adenta Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Adenta Constituency for the 8th parliament of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd Ahmed Ramadan dakɔɔnr ka aan Samira Bawumia, onɛ an pirɛsidɛn nya'adɔl pʋ'a la, taun kpɛɛm.
english: He is the son of politician Ahmed Ramadan and the elder brother of Samira Bawumia, who served as the Second Lady of Ghana from 2017 to 2025.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Mohammed Adamu Ramadan nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu Nwadisa anu la daba atan daar, (3 May 1975).
english: Mohammed Adamu Ramadan was born on 3 May 1975.

kusaal: Mohammed Gargo (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ n 19 June 1975) ka o an Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd onɛ nwɛ'ɛd nya'aŋ (defender).
english: Mohammed Gargo (born 19 June 1975) is a Ghanaian former professional footballer who played as a defender.

kusaal: Gargo's da tʋm si'el 1991 FIFA U-17 World Championship da kɛ ka o nie paalʋ ka European clubs' scouts dim nyɛ' o.
english: Gargo's performances at the 1991 FIFA U-17 World Championship brought him to the notice of European clubs' scouts.

kusaal: O da siak ye o na keŋ nwɛ' tis Bayer 04 Leverkusen on nɛ o tiraan onɛ ka ba la'an nwɛ'ɛdi tisid Ghana national under-17 football team ka o yʋ'ʋr aan Sebastian Barnes.
english: He had initially agreed to join Bayer 04 Leverkusen alongside fellow Ghana national under-17 football team member Sebastian Barnes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne nwadis piiga la ni, October 1991 Italian lira da yɔ ligidi nɛwɛ miliyɔŋ kɔbiga (100,000,000) tis Gargo's dʋ'adib ye o paam suor yi keŋ Turin, ani ka o taaba banɛ ka on nɛ ban nwɛ'ɛd national under-17 team la, Samuel Kuffour nɛ Emmanuel Duah yʋ'ʋn da keŋ paas o.
english: In October 1991 a payment of 100,000,000 Italian lira to Gargo's parents secured his move to Turin, where he was joined by his national under-17 team colleagues Samuel Kuffour and Emmanuel Duah.

kusaal: Torino's Zuraan Gian Mauro Borsano da gban'e ka pan'as ye o tisi ba nɛ tʋʋma ye ba an "messengers" o kompin mɛɛbin hali nɛ ban na ti paae yʋʋm piinɛ nii ka paam suor sɔbi ba yʋda ka naan nyaŋi lieb bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib.
english: Torino's president Gian Mauro Borsano planned fake employment for the three players as "messengers" in his construction company until they were 18 years old and eligible to be registered as professional footballers.

kusaal: O gban'ar la da mɔr daʋŋ na ka Italian Football Federation (FIGC) da zan'as ye ba kʋ bas suor ka Ghana nidib la an amateurs bɛɛ professionals.
english: The plan was controversial and the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) refused to register the Ghanaian players as either amateurs or professionals.

kusaal: FIGC zuraan Antonio Matarrese da mamis yɛl la nɛ biis zuub (trafficking of children).
english: FIGC president Antonio Matarrese compared the situation to the trafficking of children.

kusaal: Torino nɛ Gargo da bɛllim Confederation of African Football (CAF) ka ba lɔb bɛllʋŋ la bas yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la nwadis piiga la ni (October 1992), sankaŋa win la ka Kuffour nɛ Duah pʋm bas kilab la sa.
english: An appeal by Torino and Gargo to Confederation of African Football (CAF) was thrown out in October 1992, by which time Kuffour and Duah had already left the club.

kusaal: CAF zuraan Issa Hayatou sunf da duoe hali nɛ Dominico Ricci, onɛ African Football Management agency kanɛ maal suoya ye bay ii keŋi ani la.
english: CAF president Issa Hayatou was particularly hostile to Dominico Ricci, whose African Football Management agency had brokered the transfers.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 1993–94 siizin la, Gargo da bɛ Borussia Dortmund saŋa bi'ela, ka o saam bil, Ibrahim Tanko bɛ nwɛ'ɛd sa.
english: During the 1993–94 season, Gargo spent time at Borussia Dortmund, where his cousin Ibrahim Tanko already played.

kusaal: Ba da nɔk o niŋnɛ kilab la biis team dinɛ yʋ'ʋri an Oberliga Westfalen, ka Dortmund da mɔɔd ye ba da' o la, Torino da zan'as ligidkanɛ ka ba ye ba yɔ la nyain.
english: He was restricted to the club's Amateure team in the Oberliga Westfalen, and when Dortmund tried to buy him outright Torino declined the transfer fee on offer.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi nwadis piinɛ yinne la ni (November 1994) Giovanni Trapattoni da nɔk Gargo keŋ Bayern Munich.
english: In November 1994 Giovanni Trapattoni took Gargo to Bayern Munich.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi nwadisa anu la ni (May 1994) Gargo da nwɛ'ɛ tis Torino ban nɛ Juventus da nwɛ'ɛdi di'em la.
english: In May 1994 Gargo had appeared for Torino in a non-competitive game against rivals Juventus.

kusaal: "Memorial Giorgio Calleri" da nwɛ bɛnɛ Novara ka nidib da pʋ yi bɛdegʋ naa nɛ daʋŋ yɛla (hooliganism).
english: The "Memorial Giorgio Calleri" fixture was staged in Novara and was marred by poor attendance and hooliganism.

kusaal: Gargo da keŋ Stoke City ka iizin nam pʋ paae 1995–96 campaign.
english: Gargo joined Stoke City as a pre-season trialist ahead of their 1995–96 campaign.

kusaal: Ban da kpɛn'ɛs o ka o nwɛ' friendly match nɛ Stockport County, Stoke's manager Lou Macari sʋnf da ma'ae nɛ Gargo tʋm si'em la.
english: After fielding him in a friendly match with Stockport County, Stoke's manager Lou Macari was impressed with Gargo's potential.

kusaal: Gargo suunri da pʋ malis nɛ on pʋ nyɛt bɔɔl sʋma nwɛ'ɛd la, o da yuolim keŋ naal Italian team Udinese yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu nwadis piiga la ni (October 1995).
english: Increasingly unhappy at his lack of competitive football, Gargo then joined Italian team Udinese in October 1995.

kusaal: Real Tamale United nan kpɛn zi'enɛ ba zi'esimin kuosʋgin la ka Gargo tisi po kilab kʋdʋg la gbaʋŋ ye o na tisi ba Dollar tusa pisi ($20,000) ka ba da pʋ lɛn mɔr daʋŋ nɛ on na keŋ Udinese.
english: Real Tamale United remained entitled to a sell-on fee and Gargo gave his former club a promissory note for $20,000 so they did not dispute his transfer to Udinese.

kusaal: Gargo da paas men's national team la banɛ di di bronze medal yʋʋm tuisr, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) Summer Olympics bɛ Barcelona, Spain, nɛ gold 1991 FIFA U-17 World Championship bɛ Italy.
english: Gargo was a member of the men's national team that won the bronze medal at the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona, Spain, and gold in the 1991 FIFA U-17 World Championship in Italy.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la ni (2013) Gargo da yel ye ba buol o ye o nwɛ' tis Ghana yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ, ayuobʋ, 2006 FIFA World Cup, dinɛ an yiiga ka teŋ la paam suori ye ba nwɛ', ban da ye ba yɔɔm wa'adim ligidi la (bribe).
english: In 2013 Gargo claimed that he had refused an approach to play for Ghana at the 2006 FIFA World Cup, the first time the nation had qualified, after being asked to pay a bribe.

kusaal: Gargo da pin'ili o coach tʋʋma nɛ o bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛbi da naae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga nwadisa ayi la ni (February 2010) ka o da an coach tis New Edubiase United.
english: Gargo started after his retirement the job as coach in February 2010 by New Edubiase United.

kusaal: O da pa'al kilab la da bɛ Poly Tank Division One League kem paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) summer.
english: He trained the club of the Poly Tank Division One League until summer 2010.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga nwadis anii la daba ayuobʋ daar (6 August 2010), ba da ye onɛ an manager paali tis Poly Tank Division One League dataas Real Tamale United.
english: On 6 August 2010, he was named as the new manager of Poly Tank Division One League rival Real Tamale United.

kusaal: O da coach RTU kem paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayin wadis piinɛ yinne la ni (November 2012) ka ye o kʋ lɛn nyaŋi tʋm ya'asa ban da lɛbisi ba nya'aŋ Ghana Premier League ni la.
english: He coached the club RTU until November 2012 and resigned after the relegation from the Ghana Premier League his contract.

kusaal: Gargo da lɛn an manager tis Ghana Premier League kilab BA United yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu nwadisa atan la ni (March 2015), amaa ka ba da kad o yis on da zɛrigi o nwɛ'ɛd nwɛ'ɛdib la ye ba betitnɛ gɛɛsidi ba mɛŋ la.
english: Gargo was appointed manager of Ghana Premier League club BA United in March 2015, but was sacked after one match when he accused his players of betting against themselves.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadisa awai la ni (September 2018) Namibian Premier League kilab Tura Magic F.C. da nɔk Gargo ye o aan ba head coach.
english: In September 2018 Namibian Premier League club Tura Magic F.C. signed a contract with Gargo as their head coach.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Gargo nɛ Burma Camp bɛ Accra la, o saam da anɛ Physical training instructor tis Ghana Army.
english: Gargo was born in the Burma Camp in Accra, where his father was a Physical training instructor in the Ghana Army.

kusaal: Ba yinɛ Bawku, paas Busaans buudi, Mandé ethnicity.
english: The family hailed from Bawku, part of the Busanga tribe of Mandé ethnicity.

kusaal: Amaa ka Leverkusen lɛb nya'aŋ ka bas Gargo ma'aa din da pa'al nyain ye ba kʋ nyaŋi yɔ ligidi bɛdigʋ kanɛ ka di nar ye ba yɔ tis Torino.
english: However Leverkusen withdrew from the Gargo transfer when it became evident that they could not compete financially with a much larger offer from Torino.

kusaal: La'anɛ Gargo nɛ on saami yɛl ye on gban'e si'em Turin la paae ba ya'am la, bɔɔl nwɛɛdib ka kpɛn zi'enɛ ba zi'esimin.
english: Although Gargo and his father emphasised that they were happy with the arrangements in Turin, the football authorities retained their opposition.

kusaal: Ba da maal o nɛ Dortmund dim da maal o si'em la ka o pʋ nyaŋi yii.
english: He suffered the same fate he had at Dortmund and was unable to conclude a transfer.

kusaal: Ba da tʋ'ʋd Gargo on an ninsabil la yɛla ka banɛ sʋŋid Torino Andrea Fortunato onɛ maal ka'alim ka di pʋ yuug la.
english: Gargo was subjected to racist chanting, while Torino supporters mocked the recent death of Andrea Fortunato.

kusaal: Gargo da di 2–2 draw ka ba naan di Torino penalty nwɛ'ɛbin.
english: Gargo scored in a 2–2 draw before Torino lost the penalty shootout.

kusaal: La'anɛ on da bɛ yʋma atan ka pʋ tʋm si'el la, Gargo da la'an sin ka bɔɔd ye o nwɛ' tis Torino.
english: Despite his three years of inactivity, Gargo maintained ambitions of playing competitively for Torino.

kusaal: Amaa o da pʋ mɔr zusʋŋ nɛ kilab la zuraan paal kanɛ kenna la Gianmarco Calleri.
english: However he was not favoured by the club's incoming president Gianmarco Calleri.

kusaal: Amaa, Macari sunf da pʋ ma'ae nɛ Gargo, nidib bɛdegʋ pʋ yina la nɛ nidib la widig si'em tɔ'ɔtɔ' ban naae bɔɔl la.
english: However, Macari was less impressed with Gargo's poor attendance record and sudden unexplained departure, which took place shortly afterwards.

kusaal: On da bɛ ani yʋʋm yinne ka pʋ tʋm la, ba da bas Gargo suor ka o register nɛ Udinese ka ba siizin naam paae.
english: After a further year of inactivity, Gargo was allowed to register with Udinese before their 1996–97 season.

kusaal: O da lɛb Udinese nɛɛm ka ba pʋ yɔ si'ela (free transfer), o yʋʋma anu tʋʋma saŋa da paae nɛ Torino la.
english: He transferred to Udinese on a free transfer, on the expiry of his five-year contract with Torino.

kusaal: Mohammed Hardi Tufeiru anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la n tis Nanton linɛ bɛ Northern Region sυ'υlυm la, o anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Mohammed Hardi Tufeiru (born July 16, 1969) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Nanton Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O mɔr kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an MBA linɛ an Accounting n yi University of Ghana ka mɛ maal o Bachelor of Commerce digirii n yi University of Cape Coast sakurin la.
english: He is an academician and accountant, from the Institute of Chartered Accountant (ICAG) and holds MBA in Accounting from the University of Ghana and a Bachelor of Commerce degree from University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: O da di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an GCE yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobυ la ni ka tɔlis University of Cape Coast n maal B.Comm (Accounting) yυυma tusa ayi' la ni.
english: He obtained GCE in 1996 and proceeded to University of Cape Coast to obtain B.Comm (Accounting) in the year 2000.

kusaal: O anɛ IIA (Auditing) dim la nid yinne yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobυ.
english: He is a member of IIA ( Auditing) 2016.

kusaal: Girima daan Mohamed Hardi Tuferu da anɛ pa'an n bɛ Tamale Technical University sakurin la lin da yi yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ yinne ti paae yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ ayuobυ la ni, ka mɛ da lɛn an Audit tυυm zugdaan lin da yi yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ ayuobυ la ni ti paae yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobυ la ni.
english: Hon. Mohamed Hardi Tuferu was a lecturer from 2001 to 2006 at the Tamale Technical University and the Head of Audit from 2006 to 2016.

kusaal: O bɛ Audit Reports Implementation tυυma la ni post-secondary institutions lin da yi yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ anii la nɛ yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobυ la ni, hali University for Development Studies nɛ Tamale Technical University da paasi o tυυma la ni.
english: He sat on the Audit Reports Implementation Committees of a number of post secondary institutions between 2008 and 2016, including the University for Development Studies and Tamale Technical University.

kusaal: Lin da yi yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la nɛ yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobυ la ni, onɛ da an Tamale Technical University's Internal Audit Department la zugdaan.
english: From 2007 to 2016, he was the Head of the Tamale Technical University's Internal Audit Department.

kusaal: N bɛ Tamale Technical University nɛ Institutes for Distance Learning sakurin la, pa'al lυga kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb wυυ accounting, Taxation, Cost & Management Accounting, Auditing, MIS, Public Sector Accounting, nɛ Quantitative Methods n bɛ (University of Cape Coast, University of Ghana nɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology).
english: At Tamale Technical University and the Institutes for Distance Learning, he taught accounting, Taxation, Cost & Management Accounting, Auditing, MIS, Public Sector Accounting, and Quantitative Methods (University of Cape Coast, University of Ghana and Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology).

kusaal: Wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la ni, onɛ da an Ranking Member of the Public Accounts kpɛɛm nya'andɔl (PAC) ka mɛ lɛn paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Environment, Science nɛ Technology la ni.
english: During the 7th parliament, he was a Deputy Ranking Member of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and a member of the Committee on Environment, Science and Technology.

kusaal: O da zi'en Ghana nɔba zug African Parliamentary Union la ni.
english: He was also an African Parliamentary Union delegate.

kusaal: O da paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Petroleum Commission Ghana Board of Directors la ni din da yi yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi ti paae yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, ani ka o da an kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Finance nɛ Local Content kυkdaan.
english: He was a member of the Petroleum Commission Ghana Board of Directors from 2017 to 2021, where he chaired the Finance and Local Content Committees.

kusaal: din da yi yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi ti paae yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, O paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Public Accounts la ni(PAC) nɛ Local Government, Rural Development, and Decentralization n bɛ wadmaanib yir la ni .
english: He is a member of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and the Committee on Local Government, Rural Development, and Decentralization in the current parliament.

kusaal: O anɛ astute academic nɛ accomplished accountant, n bɛ Institute of Chartered Accountant (ICAG) tυυma la ni.
english: He is an academician and accountant, from the Institute of Chartered Accountant (ICAG) and holds MBA in Accounting from the University of Ghana and a Bachelor of Commerce degree from University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: Nannanna onɛ an ti Ghana Minista kanɛ gɔsid kuob yɛla nya'andɔl.
english: He also obtained an M.B.A in accounting from the University of Ghana in the year 2006.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn maal M.B.A in accounting yi University of Ghana yυυma tusa ayi' nɛ ayuobυ.
english: He also obtained an M.B.A in accounting from the University of Ghana in the year 2006.

kusaal: O da paas Institute of Chartered Accountant (Accounting) dim tυυma la ni yυυm tusa ayi' nɛ awai.
english: He became a member of Institute of Chartered Accountant ( Accounting) in 2009.

kusaal: Mohammed Kudus (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nwadisa anii la daba ayi daar, 2 August 2000) ka o an Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdkanɛ zamis ka nwɛ'ɛd attacking midfielder bɛɛ right winger tisid Premier League kilab kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon West Ham United ka lɛn bɛ Ghana national team la ni.
english: Mohammed Kudus (born 2 August 2000) is a Ghanaian professional footballer who plays as a winger or attacking midfielder for Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur and the Ghana national team.

kusaal: Kudus da naan Ghanaian Right to Dream Academy paae Danish kilab kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Nordsjælland naali ba ka anɛ yʋma piiga (10years) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ nii yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 2018) on nɛ o taaba yi, Ibrahim Sadiq nɛ Gideon Mensah.
english: In January 2018, Kudus arrived at Danish club Nordsjælland from the Ghanaian Right to Dream Academy together with two teammates, Ibrahim Sadiq and Gideon Mensah.

kusaal: Kudus da pa'ali o nɔŋilim tis Nordsjælland nɛ o yʋʋmpiinɛ nii du'am dabisir tienri da gaad la daba atan daar ban da di Brøndby IF 2–0.
english: Kudus made his official debut for Nordsjælland only three days after his 18th birthday, in a 2–0 defeat against Brøndby.

kusaal: O da nwɛ' o yiiga bɔɔli tis kilab la 20 September league match kanɛ ka ba da nwɛ' gɛɛs RKC Waalwik.
english: He made his official debut for the club on 20 September in a league match against RKC Waalwijk.

kusaal: Head coach Erik Hag da keŋ tuoni buol Kudus ye o anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdkanɛ mɔr baŋir pamm.
english: Head coach Erik ten Hag subsequently called Kudus as a player with "incredible potential".

kusaal: On da pin'il UEFA Champions League la nwɛ' home match gɛɛs nɛ Liverpool yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadis piiga la dabpisi nɛ yinne daar la (21 October 2020), di da pʋ maal o sʋ'ʋŋaa.
english: He debuted in the UEFA Champions League for the home match against Liverpool on 21 October 2020, though was substituted out after only six minutes as he suffered a meniscus injury, keeping him out for several months.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne nwadisa ayi la dabpisi nɛ yinne daar (21 February 2021), o da lɛbi Ajax yʋ'ʋn nwɛ'ɛd banɛ pin'in piinɛ yinne la ni din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadis piiga la ni (October 2020), ka da di gool mitpisnu saŋa tisi Ajax ka ba yʋ'ʋm paam 4–0 gɛɛs Sparta Rotterdam.
english: On 21 February 2021, he returned to Ajax's starting eleven for the first time since October 2020, and scored a goal in the 50th minute of a 4–0 win over Sparta Rotterdam.

kusaal: On da lɛbna la nya'aŋ, o da nwɛ'ɛ geemnam piinɛ atan (13) yi Ajax fanal gemnam piinɛ naasi la (14) pʋʋgin, ka lɛn nwɛ' mitpistan nɛ yinne (31 minutes) ban da nwɛ' KNVB Cup semi-fanali gɛɛs nɛ Heerenveen ka Ajax da di ayi yiiga siizin la naarin la.
english: After his return from injury, Kudus played in 13 of Ajax's final 14 league games, as well as 31 minutes of their KNVB Cup semi-final match against Heerenveen as Ajax clinched the domestic double at the end of his first season.

kusaal: O da dii o yiiga tʋʋma ya'an (career trophy) 2020–21 KNVB Cup nɛ Ajax yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne nwadisa naasi la dabpiinɛ anii daar (18 April 2021) ban da nwɛ' mitpiswai nɛ yinne la nya'aŋ ka David Neres da di gooli tisi ba.
english: He won his first career trophy, the 2020–21 KNVB Cup on 18 April 2021, after David Neres scored in additional time to secure a 2–1 victory over Vitesse.

kusaal: O da nwɛ' kʋdʋm tis Nordsjælland nɛ Ajax.
english: In January 2018, Kudus arrived at Danish club Nordsjælland from the Ghanaian Right to Dream Academy together with two teammates, Ibrahim Sadiq and Gideon Mensah.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpiinɛ ayuobʋ daar (16 July 2020), Kudus da tik Eredivisie kilab la, Ajax ye o di'e dɔlanam miliyɔŋ awai (€9 million), ye o tʋm yʋma anu tisi ba.
english: On 16 July 2020, Kudus signed for Eredivisie club Ajax for €9 million, on a five-year contract.

kusaal: O da paam laafi ka lɛbnɛ yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 2021), ka da yuolim kpɛn'ɛna nwɛ' mit piiga ma'a ka ba da duoe 2–2 gɛɛs nɛ PSV.
english: He returned from injury in January 2021, enjoying a 10-minutes in a 2–2 draw against PSV.

kusaal: Moutya bɛɛ Moutia, anɛ Africa buudi malʋŋ kanɛ an wa'ab ka nwɛnɛ Sega, amaa saŋa bɛdegʋ di ɛɛnti an dinɛ kaanbid.
english: Moutia or Moutya, is a traditional African dance similar to the Sega, but with often more pronounced suggestive movements.

kusaal: Hali keŋ paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi (1970) la naarin, Moutya da anɛ risqué dance ka nidib da pʋ lɛm bɔɔdi di wa'abɔ.
english: Until the late 1970s, the Moutya was considered more of a risqué dance and generally shunned.

kusaal: Moses Anim anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da lɛn an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Trobu Constituency bɛ Greater Accra Region, Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Moses Anim is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Trobu Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Adukrom bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Adukrom in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ University of Ghana, ani ka o da maal Bachelor of Science degree Biochemistry kasɛta gbaʋŋ ka lɛn maal Master of Business Administration degree in Project Management yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991), nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu (2005) la ni nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: He studied at the University of Ghana where he obtained his Bachelor of Science degree Biochemistry and his Master of Business Administration degree in Project Management in 1991 and 2005 respectively.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ kpɛn' pɔlitis la, Anim da an Project Manager tis Wilhelm Construction Company Limited bɛ Accra.
english: Prior to entering politics, Anim was the Project Manager of Wilhelm Construction Company Limited in Accra.

kusaal: Anim da kpɛn' wadmaannib yin la nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 yʋʋmpaal nwadig 2013) Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug tis Trobu Constituency.
english: Anim entered parliament on 7 January 2013 on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party representing the Trobu Constituency.

kusaal: Vɔɔt la wʋsa da anɛ tusa pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi' la (76,782), o da mɔri vɔɔt kal tusa pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (46,446) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ anii du'al piswai nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (58.96%), ka di kʋk la.
english: Out of the 76,782 valid votes cast, he polled 46,446 votes (58.96%) to win the seat.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Anim nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu nwadisa anaasi dabpisi nɛ anu daar (25 vaala nwadig 1965).
english: Anim was born on 25 April 1965.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔti tis o yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la ni ka o lɛn zi'eni tisi ba yʋma anaasi ya'as.
english: He was re-elected in 2016 to remain in parliament for another four (4)-year term.He was re-elected once again in 2020 after a tough battle when an independent candidate known as Vida Oppong challenged him for the seat.

kusaal: Mpraeso Constituency bɛnɛ Eastern region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The Mpraeso constituency is in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ yʋ'ʋn an wadmaani tis constituency la anɛ Davis Ansah Opoku.
english: The current member of Parliament for the constituency is Davis Ansah Opoku.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) nɔba zug, ka o da di nɛ vɔɔt pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan du'al pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (73.56%), tusa pisi nɛ anu, pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi gaadi o tiran kanɛ ti'al o la, ka da kilim constituency la wadmaan.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and won a majority of 73.56%, 25,064 votes more than the candidate closest in the race, to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: O da di'e kʋk lanɛ Seth Kwame Acheampong onɛ da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisinɛ yinne (2021) 4th Republic parliament la dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP).
english: He succeeded Seth Kwame Acheampong who had represented the constituency from 2009 to 2021 in the 4th Republican parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Alhaji Muhammad Bawah Braimah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaannib paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Ejura-Sekyedumase Constituency teŋ kanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la Ma'asim tig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: Alhaji Muhammad Bawah Braimah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ejura-Sekyedumase Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Braimah nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai, Nwadis pii nɛ yinne la dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 sapal nwadig 1959) ka o yi Kulungugu bɛ Upper East Region, Ghana.
english: Braimah was born on 28 November 1959 and hails from Kulungugu in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Tamale Secondary School ti maali o GCE 'O' Level.
english: He attended Tamale Secondary School where he had his GCE 'O' Level June, 1979.

kusaal: O mɔri o MBA in Management, Almond Institute.
english: He had his MBA in Management at Almond Institute.

kusaal: Braimah da anɛ Municipal Coordinator tis NADMO yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2009) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' (2013) ka din nya'aŋ ka o lieb Municipal Chief Executive tis Ejura-Sekyedumase Municipal Assembly yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' (2013) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: Braimah was the Municipal Coordinator for NADMO from 2009 to 2013 and later became the Municipal Chief Executive for Ejura-Sekyedumase Municipal Assembly from 2013 to 2016.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Managing Director tis Mubabra Company Limited in Ejura.
english: He is also the Managing Director for Mubabra Company Limited in Ejura.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana vɔɔtʋg la ni, Braimah da di wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ atan, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (23,277) ka NPP nid la, Mohammed Salisu Bamba paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piswai nɛ anu (21,795).
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, Braimah won the parliamentary seat with 23,277 votes whilst the NPP parliamentary aspirant Mohammed Salisu Bamba had 21,795 votes.

kusaal: CPP's sɔb la, Abdalla Mahawan Sani mɛ da paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ pistan nɛayi (132) ka onɛ bɛ PNC la, Laari Samuel paam vɔɔt pisnii nɛ atan (83).
english: CPP's aspirant Abdalla Mahawan Sani also had 132 votes whiles PNC's aspirant Laari Samuel had 83 votes.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana vɔɔtʋg la nii, o da lɛn di Wadmaan kʋk la ya'as nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (30,056) ka NPP nid la, Mohammed Salisu Bamba paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ anu nɛ awai (25,009).
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, he again won the parliamentary seat with 30,056 votes whilst the NPP parliamentary aspirant Mohammed Salisu Bamba had 25,009 votes.

kusaal: CPP nid la, Adams Hussein paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ awai (119) ka onɛ bɛ PNC la, Laari Samuel paam vɔɔt pisnu nɛ atan (53).
english: CPP's aspirant Adams Hussein also had 119 votes whiles PNC's aspirant Laari Samuel had 53 votes.

kusaal: Braimah paas Public Accounts Committee la ni ka lɛn paas Defense and Interior Committee.
english: Braimah is a member of the Public Accounts Committee and also a member of the Defense and Interior Committee.

kusaal: Concerned Youth of Ejura da na'as Braimah nɛ on kɛ ka gbaʋŋ zamisʋg keŋ tuon sʋ'ʋlimin la.
english: Braimah was honored by the Concerned Youth of Ejura for his efforts in the improvement of education in the community.

kusaal: Braimah anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid ka an wadmaani tis Ejura-Sekyedumase Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: Braimah is a member of the National Democratic Congress and the member of parliament for Ejura-Sekyedumase Constituency in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Braimah anɛ Mɔr.
english: Braimah is a Muslim.

kusaal: Asian mui da kpɛn'ɛ yin China tɛŋin din yi yʋʋm tusa piinɛtan' nɛ kɔbisnu' kɛŋ paae yʋʋm tusanii, nɛ kɔbisyi (13,500 to 8,200) banɛ gaad la; African mui la da kpɛn'ɛ yin Africa sʋ'ʋlim mɛ yʋʋm tusatan' (3,000) banɛ gaad la.
english: Asian rice was domesticated in China some 13,500 to 8,200 years ago; African rice was domesticated independently in West Africa about 3,000 years ago.

kusaal: Mui anɛ mɔɔg kanɛ buudi buon Oryza sativa la bi'elim (Asian mui)—bɛɛ, buud banɛ pʋ zuoe wala, Oryza glaberrima (African mui).
english: Rice is the seed of the grass species Oryza sativa (Asian rice)—or, less commonly, Oryza glaberrima (African rice).

kusaal: Mui yʋ'ʋn anɛ dikanɛ bɛ buudi bɛdigʋ ni dunia wʋsa; yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) la, ba da bʋn mui 787 million tons, ka di da paas diib anaasi, dɔl kikan'asiind, kawɛnna, nɛ wheat nya'aŋ.
english: Rice has become commonplace in many cultures worldwide; in 2023, 800 million tons were produced, placing it third after sugarcane and maize.

kusaal: Mui mɔɔg la nɔbigid nɛ wa'alim paad tʋʋgid 1 m (3 ft); di ya'a bɛ kuom zin'ig, di wa'alim tɔn'e paae 5 m (16 ft).
english: The rice plant can grow to over 1 m (3 ft) tall; if in deep water, it can reach a length of 5 m (16 ft).

kusaal: Mumuni keŋi University of Education, Winneba sakur la ni, ka naae nɛ o Bachelor of Education degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: Mumuni attended the University of Education, Winneba, and graduated with a Bachelor of Education degree.

kusaal: Yʋma 2012 kanɛ da gaad la, o da nya' Salaga North wadmaan kʋk la n bɛ NDC wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas ayuobʋ ka an Ghana Republic kanɛ paas anaasi la nɔba zug ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested the Salaga North seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔdʋg la ka bas Adam Mahammed Kamarudeen onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid (NPP) ka mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa atan' nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi' (3,462) ka li an pistan' nɛ yinne nɛ du'alʋg pisnii nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (31.81%) la, nɛ Abdul-Fataw Abdul-Wahab onɛ an IND na'adɔɔg nid ka mɔr vɔɔt kal kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisi nɛ yinne ka li an anu nɛ du'alʋg pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin la (5.72%).
english: He won the election over Adam Mohammed Kamarudeen of the New Patriotic Party who polled 3,462 votes representing 31.89%, and IND parliamentary candidate Abdul-Fataw Abdul-Wahab who had 621 votes representing 5.72% of the total votes.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2016 la ni la, ba da lɛn vɔɔt tis Mumuni onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid la ka o an Salaga North sʋ'ʋlʋm wadmaan.
english: Mumuni was re-elected in the 2016 Ghanaian general election as a member of parliament for Salaga North constituency on the ticket of National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔt la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbistan' nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' (6,363) ka li an pisnu nɛ ayi' nɛ du'alʋg pisi nɛ ayi' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (52.22%) vɔɔt la wʋsa ya'a la'as taaba.
english: He won the election with 6,363 votes representing 52.22% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da di wadmaan kʋk la ka bas Lucas Alhassan Abilla onɛ an wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid ka mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa atan' nɛ pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi (3,037) ka li an pisi nɛ anaasi nɛ du'alʋg piswai nɛ ayi' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (24.92%) la, nɛ Abdul-Fataw Abdul-Wahab onɛ an PPP na'adɔɔg nid la ka mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa ayi' nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pistan' nɛ atan ' (2,733) ka li an pisi nɛ ayi' nɛ du'alʋg pisnaasi nɛ atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (22.43%) la, nɛ CPP na'adɔɔg nid kanɛ da nyi'ad na'am la ka mɔr vɔɔt kal pisnu nɛ ayi' (52) ka li an du'alʋg pisnaasi nɛ atan' kɔbiga pʋʋgin(0.43%) la.
english: He won the parliamentary seat over Lucas Alhassan Abilla of the New Patriotic Party who polled 3,037 votes which is equivalent to 24.92%, Abdul-Fataw Abdul-Wahab of PPP who had 2,733 votes representing 22.43% and the parliamentary candidate for convention people's party polled 52 votes representing 0.43% of the total votes.

kusaal: Mumuni onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la da lɛn zi'en nyi'a Salaga North wadmaan kʋk la Ghana vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2020 la ni la, amaa ka kɔ'ɔŋ ka Alhassan Abdul Iddi onɛ an wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid la di ka bas o.
english: Mumuni again contested the 2020 Ghanaian general election for the Salaga North constituency on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress but lost the election to Alhassan Abdallah Iddi of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Mumuni nɛ sɛɛʋng nwadig la li dabisim pisi nɛ atan' daar yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (23 September 1967) n bɛ Gbung teŋ kanɛ bɛ Northern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm nwa ni la.
english: Alhassan Mumuni (born 23 September 1967) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Salaga North Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Mumuni anɛ maalim daan, ka di pu'a du'a biisa ayuobʋ.
english: Mumuni attended the University of Education, Winneba, and graduated with a Bachelor of Education degree.

kusaal: Mumuni anɛ Ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Mumuni is a Muslim, and is married with six children.

kusaal: Mumuni onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid la da zi'en nyi'a Salaga North teŋ kanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la wadmaan kʋk ka dii li nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' (6,772) ka li an pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi' nɛ du'alʋg pistan' nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (62.39%).
english: Mumuni contested the 2012 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress for the Salaga North parliamentary seat in the Northern Region of Ghana and won the election with 6,772 votes which is equivalent to 62.39% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da anɛ kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid Ghana sakur ken tʋʋma nɛ Rural North 'B' Circuit dim lʋgir kanɛ bɛ Salaga sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: Ghana Education Service (Circuit Supervisor, Rural North "B" Circuit Salaga)

kusaal: Alhaji Mohammed Mubarak Muntaka anɛ Wadmaan tis Asawase teŋ kanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anaasi (4th), anu (5th), ayuobʋ (6th), ayɔpɔi (7th) nɛ anii (8th) Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Alhaji Mohammed Mubarak Muntaka is the Member of Parliament for Asawase in the Ashanti Region of Ghana of the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th and the 8th parliaments of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Nannanna, o anɛ Minority Chief Whip n bɛ Ghana Wadmaanib yin la.
english: He was the Minority Chief Whip in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Akuse linɛ bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana teŋgbaʋŋin, amaa o du'adib yinɛ Kumbungu linɛ bɛ Northern Ghana la.
english: Muntaka was born on 17 October 1971 and hails from Akuse in the Ashanti Region of Ghana but his parents originally came from the northern part of Ghana in a town called Kumbungu.

kusaal: O da anɛ tuongat yinne lʋgir kanɛ an (RME) banɛ da'ad kooko ka ba buon ye Adwumapa Buyers Limited.
english: Muntaka was the head of research at one of the units (RME) of Adwumapa Buyers Limited, a cocoa buying company.

kusaal: Ban da vɔɔt Ghana wʋsa vɔɔdʋg la, o da di Asawase constituency la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbʋg nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayi' (11,142) O da di'enɛ Dr Gibril Adamu Mohammed, onɛ da an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg (NDC) nid ka da maal ka'alim la.
english: Muntaka first entered the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress in 2005 when he won a by-election in the Asawase constituency with a majority of 11,142, replacing the late Dr Gibril Adamu Mohammed also of the NDC who had won the seat in December 2004 with a majority of 4,474.

kusaal: Muntaka da anɛ Majority Chief Whip m bɛ Wadmaanib yin la tis Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg dim (NDC caucus), banɛ da zu'oe gati ba taaba la.
english: Muntaka was the Chief Majority Whip in parliament for the NDC caucus, the majority in Government.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai yʋʋmpaal Nwadig (yʋʋmpaal 2009), John Evans Atta Mills da gaŋ Mubarak Minister-designate tis pu'asada nɛ dasam nɛ Bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb tʋʋma .
english: In January 2009, Mubarak was appointed as Minister-designate for the Youth and Sports Ministry by President John Evans Atta Mills.

kusaal: Mohammed Abdul-Kabir onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg/ New Patriotic Party nid la nɛ Elyasu Mohammed onɛ an People's National Convention nid la, nɛ Mohammed Bashir Tijani onɛ an Democratic Freedom Party nid nɛ Alhaji Baba Musah onɛ an Convention People's Party nid la.
english: He was elected over Dr. Mohammed Abdul-Kabir of the New Patriotic Party, Elyasu Mohammed of the People's National Convention, Mohammed Bashir Tijani of the Democratic Freedom Party and Alhaji Baba Musah of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt kal tusa pisnaasi nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi (43,917) yi vɔɔt tusa pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ pistan' nɛ anaasi (77,034).
english: He was elected with 43,917 votes out of 77,034 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Nɛ' pa'al ye kɔbʋg pʋʋgin, o da paam nɛ vaar pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi' nɛ fiin (57.01%).
english: This was equivalent to 57.01% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt tis o ka bas Nana Okyere-Tawiah Antwi, New Patriotic Party nid nɛ Jerry Joseph Quayson onɛ an Progressive People's Party nid nɛ Abdulai Umaru onɛ an People's National Convention nid nɛ Elias Mohammed onɛ an Convention People's Party nid nɛ Yakubu Adams Zakaria onɛ an National Democratic Party nid nɛ Alhassan Abdul Majeed onɛ da pʋ zi'en paati sɔ' zugɔ.
english: He was elected over Nana Okyere-Tawiah Antwi of the New Patriotic Party, Jerry Joseph Quayson of the Progressive People's Party, Abdulai Umaru of the People's National Convention, Elias Mohammed of the Convention People's Party, Yakubu Adams Zakaria of the National Democratic Party and Alhassan Abdul Majeed an independent candidate.

kusaal: Muntaka da lɛn di o sʋ'ʋlim kʋk la ya'as yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔdʋg dinɛ an Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Muntaka retained the parliamentary seat in the 2020 general election to represent in the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic.

kusaal: O da diya nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pisnu nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnu nɛ awai (51,659) ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP nid la paam tusa pistan' nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisyi nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (31,256).
english: He won with 51,659 votes while the NPP parliamentary candidate polled 31,256.

kusaal: Muntaka daa di nɛ vɔɔtnam tusir nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' (1,063) ka Masawudu paam vɔɔtnam kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pistan' nɛ anu (735).
english: He won with 1,063 votes against Masawudu who polled 735 votes.

kusaal: O da maali o Masters of Science degree in Development Policy and Planning University la ni ka naae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004).
english: He acquired a Master of Science degree in development policy and planning from the university in the year 2004.

kusaal: Muntaka anɛ development planner.
english: Muntaka wrote his common entrance exam in 1987.and continued to gain his BSc agric (agriculture economist) in 2000 and MSc development policy and planning (development planner) in 2004.

kusaal: Muntaka da kpɛn' o yiiga Wadmaanib yin la nɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg linɛ ka ba buon ye National Democratic Congress nɔbir zug yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: Muntaka first entered the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress in 2005 when he won a by-election in the Asawase constituency with a majority of 11,142, replacing the late Dr Gibril Adamu Mohammed also of the NDC who had won the seat in December 2004 with a majority of 4,474.

kusaal: The Ghana Center for Democratic Development da yɛl ye vɔɔdʋg la anɛ nyain nɛ sida, amaa dabiem zɔtim da bɛ.
english: The Ghana Center for Democratic Development deemed this by-election as "fair and transparent, but not free from fear." He retained his seat in the Ghanaian parliamentary election held in December 2008.

kusaal: Di nya'aŋ o da di kʋk la Ghana Wadmaanib vɔɔdʋg kanɛ da bɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anii Nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la ni la, (samanpiid 2008).
english: The Ghana Center for Democratic Development deemed this by-election as "fair and transparent, but not free from fear." He retained his seat in the Ghanaian parliamentary election held in December 2008.

kusaal: O da lɛn di yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' vɔɔdʋg la (2012).
english: He also won the next election in 2012.

kusaal: O da anɛ Minista tis pu'asada nɛ dasam nɛ Bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb lʋgir Ghana government ni.
english: He was the Minister for Youth and Sports in the Ghana government.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid kpikpiŋ yɛla nɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid gaansʋg yɛla (Committee of Selection Committee).
english: Muntaka holds membership in multiple committees, including the House Committee, the Appointments Committee, the Standing Orders Committee, the Health Committee, the Mines and Energy Committee, the Business Committee, and the Committee of Selection Committee.

kusaal: Muntaka da kpɛn' o yiiga Wadmaanib yin la nɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg linɛ ka ba buon National Democratic Congress nɔbir zug yʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: Muntaka first entered the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress in 2005 when he won a by-election in the Asawase constituency with a majority of 11,142, replacing the late Dr Gibril Adamu Mohammed also of the NDC who had won the seat in December 2004 with a majority of 4,474.

kusaal: O da dii amaligim vɔɔt la nɛ Asawase constituency nɛ vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayi' (11,142).
english: Muntaka first entered the Parliament of Ghana on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress in 2005 when he won a by-election in the Asawase constituency with a majority of 11,142, replacing the late Dr Gibril Adamu Mohammed also of the NDC who had won the seat in December 2004 with a majority of 4,474.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anii la ni (2008), o gaŋir la da mɔr summalisim bɛdigʋ tis National Youth Council, on da an dasaŋ la zug.
english: His appointment was applauded by the National Youth Council due to his youthfulness and youthful exuberance as by the time of his appointment, he was 39 years.

kusaal: Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg linɛ ka ba buon ye National Democratic Congress la da di wadmaanib kʋgʋs bɛdigʋ wadmaanib yin la.
english: The National Democratic Congress won a majority total of 113 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Bama wʋsa ya'a la'as kɔbiga pʋʋgin li duonɛ vaar pisnaasi ka du'al pisi nɛ ayuobʋ (40.26%), nɛɛm du'al pisnu nɛ awai (0.59%), nɛɛm du'al pistan' nɛ anu (0.35%), nɛɛm du'al pistan' nɛ atan' (0.33%), nɛɛm du'al pisi nɛ anaasi (0.24%) nɛ yinne du'al pisi nɛ atan (1.23%).
english: These were equivalent to 40.26%, 0.59%, 0.35%, 0.33%, 0.24% and 1.23% respectively of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Asibit daar, yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ atan' Nwadisa ayuobʋ la dabpiinɛ atan' daar la, Muntaka nɛ Masawudu Mubarick daa nyi'a onɛ na zi'enɛ tis Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg vɔɔt la Asawase Constituency sʋ'ʋlimin.
english: Muntaka on Saturday, 13 May 2023, was retained as National Democratic Congress parliamentary representative for the Member of Parliament for Asawase Constituency by beating Masawudu Mubarick in the NDC 2023 primaries for a chance to represent the party in the 2024 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: La'anɛ Muntaka Mubarak nya'andɔlib nɛ Masawudu Mubarick daa paam nɔŋgbannwa'ar la, fuud dim Ghana Police Service daa kena guoe di baanlimm.
english: Although supporters of Muntaka Mubarak and his contender, Masawudu Mubarick got into a scuffle that was swiftly curtailed by personnel of the Ghana Police Service.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋgin la, ba da zɛrig Muntaka ye o kɛya ka o yʋma ayuobʋ biig tik vɔɔt gbaʋŋ la tis o, dinɛ ka nidib bɛdigʋ da zɛrig o hali bɔzugɔ Ghana wada la bas suor ye yʋʋm pii nɛ anii bɛn ma'aa na nyaŋi vɔɔt.
english: During the 2020 general election, Muntaka was said to have allowed his 6-year-old daughter to thumbprint his ballot on his behalf, an act that attracted wide condemnation as the Ghana electoral laws only permit people above 18 years to participate in elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2021 Yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni, ba da zɛrig o ye o yɛl ye Supreme Court piyam da tis Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, (NDC) Wadmaan onɛ an pu'a si'el ye o bɛlis o ka o vɔɔti tis Mike Oquaye ka o lieb Wadmaanib yir kpɛɛm.
english: In January 2021, he allegedly said a Supreme Court judge offered an inducement to a female member of parliament of the NDC in an attempt to persuade her to cast a vote for Mike Oquaye during the Speaker of parliament election.

kusaal: Muntaka mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis anu (5).
english: Muntaka is married to Meimuna Ezideen Adul Wahab and has five (5) children.

kusaal: Kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan' (230) la ni, ba da dinɛ kʋgʋs kɔbiga nɛ pii nɛ atan' (113).
english: The National Democratic Congress won a majority total of 113 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: O da paam nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pistan' nɛ ayuobʋ, nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (36,557) yi vɔɔt tusa pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ atan' (64,443).
english: He was elected with 36,557 votes out of 64,443 total valid votes cast equivalent to 56.73% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Banɛ da zi'en paati banɛ ka ti pʋdi ba yʋda la da paamnɛ: tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (27,168), kɔbistan nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne (371), pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (86) nɛ kɔbisyi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne (261).
english: These obtained 27,168, 371, 86 and 261 votes respectively of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da paamnɛ tusa pistan' nɛ yinne nɛ pii nɛ atan' (31,013), kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnu nɛ anii (458), kɔbisyi' nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi (267), kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne (251), kɔbiga nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi' (182) nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ (946).
english: These obtained 31,013, 458, 267, 251, 182 and 946 votes respectively of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Mustapha Ussif (16 August 1979) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Mustapha Ussif (born 16 August 1979) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O zi'ennɛ tis Yagaba-Kubori bɛ North East Sʋ'ʋlim, Gaana.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party(NPP) and a member of the 8th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana representing the Yagaba-Kubori Constituency in the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Tantaala n bɛ Tamar sʋ'ʋlim, Gaana.
english: He hails from Tantaala in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋ Bagabaga Teacher Training College nɛ Anglia Ruskin University ani ka da di'e Bachelor of Arts degree in International Business and Management yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga la ni (2010).
english: He studied at Bagabaga Teacher Training College(BATCO) and Anglia Ruskin University where he obtained his Bachelor of Arts degree in International Business and Management in 2010.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ University of Gloucestershire ka naae ani yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛyinne (2011) nɛ master's degree ligidi nɛ ligidsu'ab yɛla (Finance and Investment).
english: He continued at the University of Gloucestershire where he graduated in 2011 with a master's degree in Finance and Investment.

kusaal: Ussif da tʋmnɛ ligidsu'ad tʋʋma Ray and Associates, UK yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010).
english: Ussif worked as an Investment Analyst at Ray and Associates, UK in 2010.

kusaal: Yʋʋmkan ni ka o lɛn tʋm Freelance Consultant tis Action Aid UK.
english: That same year, he joined Action Aid UK where he worked as a Freelance Consultant.

kusaal: Anɛ Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nid ka paas Gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party(NPP) and a member of the 8th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana representing the Yagaba-Kubori Constituency in the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne la yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni ka Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an minista tis pu'asada nɛ dasam nɛ ninwisigir yɛla.
english: On 21 January 2021, he was nominated by Nana Akufo-Addo to serve as Minister of Youth and Sports.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ussifnɛ yʋʋmtusir kɔbiswai nɛ piyɔpɔi nɛ awai la nwadisa anii la dabpiinɛ ayuobʋ daar (16-08-1979).
english: Ussif was born on 16 August 1979.

kusaal: Ussif da kpɛn' Wadmaannam yin la yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la yʋʋmpaal nwadig daba ayɔpɔi daar on da nyaŋi o tiraan Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim la.
english: Ussif entered parliament on 7 January 2013 on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party after defeating the incumbent member of parliament Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim.

kusaal: O anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg (NPP) la nid.
english: He stood for the NPP's parliamentary primaries unopposed and was declared the person to represent the party in the 2020 December elections.

kusaal: O da an wadmaani tis Yagba-kubori lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan' keŋ paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la Gaana Wadmaannib yikanɛ paasi ayuobʋ la, ka din nya'aŋ ka o tiraan, Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim, ma'asim tiig nid la da di ka bas o yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ vɔɔtʋg yʋʋm la.
english: He represented the Yagaba-Kubori Constituency from 2013 to 2017 in the 6th parliament but subsequently lost in his bid to be reelected into the 7th parliament to his previous opponent Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim of the National Democratic Congress during the 2016 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: O da diya ka bas onɛ nya'ad nɛ o nɔɔri ayi' la, Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim.
english: He beat the incumbent member of parliament Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim who he had faced on two occasions in the past elections.

kusaal: On da di Yagaba-kubori kʋk la yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋgin la, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal nwadig la dabpisi nɛ yinne daar, Pirɛsidɛn Nana Akufo-Addo da lɛn di pirɛsidɛn la, da gaŋ o ye o an pʋ'asada nɛ dasam nɛ ninwisigir yɛla minista.
english: After winning back the Yagaba-Kubori Constituency seat in 2020, Ussif was nominated on 21 January 2021 by President Nana Akufo-Addo to serve as Minister of Youth and Sports during his second term.

kusaal: Ussif mɔr pu'a nɛ biisi ayi.
english: Ussif is married with two children.

kusaal: O anɛ pʋ'ʋsidnɛ mɔɔm pʋ'ʋsim.
english: He identifies as a Muslim.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana nid, onɛ tʋm nɛ ligidi zanlim yɛla tʋʋma ni (Ghanaian accountant) ka lɛn an pɔlitis nwɛn'ɛd, onɛ an Damango Constituency bɛ Savanna Region la National Democratic Congress (NDC) wadmaan Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana la ni.
english: Mutawakilu Adam (born 2 March 1974) is a Ghanaian accountant and politician who is member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Damango Constituency in the Savanna Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: O mɔri pa'annib kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Bagabaga Training College la ni.
english: He holds a teacher's certificate A from Bagabaga Training College.

kusaal: O mɔri bachelor's degree in Administration kasɛta gbaʋŋ n yi University of Ghana ni yʋma 2002 la ni nɛ Commonwealth Executive Master of Business Administration kasɛta gbaʋŋ (CEMBA) n yi Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, 2010 yʋʋm la ni.
english: He earned a bachelor's degree in Administration from University of Ghana in 2002, and Commonwealth Executive Master of Business Administration (CEMBA) from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology in 2010.

kusaal: Ka o nyaan da niŋ DCE la, Mutawakilu da anɛ Chief Cashier and Head of Tresury 2004 ti paae 2009, University for Development Studies, Central Administration Tamale.
english: Prior to being appointed as DCE, Adam worked as a chief cashier and head of treasury from 2004 to 2009 at University for Development Studies, at the Central Administration in Tamale.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ sakur dɔɔpʋʋg pa'anɛ da tʋm nɛ Ghana Education Service 1996 ti paae 2003 yʋʋm la ni.
english: He also worked as class tutor from 1996 to 2003 at Ghana Education Service.

kusaal: 2012 yʋʋm la ni, o da nya' vɔɔtʋg nɛ National Democratic Congress ka di ya'an nɛ 9,518 vɔtnamɛ an 56.79% ka lɔbi o tiraan Albert Kassim Diwura da zi'en nɛ New Patrotic Party, ka da paam vɔtnam 7,041 n an 42.01%.
english: Adam contested for the Damango constituency seat in 2012 on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress, and won by getting 9,518 votes, representing 56.79% against Albert Kassim Diwura, his closest contender and the New Patriotic Party's candidate, who got 7,041 votes representing 42.01%.

kusaal: o da tʋm nɛ nɛ wadmaanid banɛ da zu'oe la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) o party da dɔlis John Dramani Mahama da lɛn di ya'an ka mɔr wadmaannib bɛdigʋ parliament la.
english: Adam served on the majority bench from 2013 to 2017 since his party had retained power in the elections through President John Dramani Mahama and had maintained their majority seats in parliament.

kusaal: 2016 yʋʋm la nii, Mutawalilu da lɛ zi'enɛ nya' party la vɔɔtʋgʋn, Damango Constituency.
english: In 2016, Adam contested for reelection for the Damango Constituency.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔtnam 10,2663 linɛ an 55.22% ka Albert Kassim Diwura, on nɛ onɛ da la'am zi'enɛ nya' 2012 yʋʋm la vɔɔtʋgʋn la mɛ nyɛ vɔɔtnam 8,139 linɛ an 43.79%.
english: He won the parliamentary elections by getting 10,263 votes, which represented 55.22%, against Albert Kassim Diwura, the same candidate from the 2012 elections, who this time had 8,139 votes representing 43.79%.

kusaal: Mutaakilu paasnɛ Minority Bench la bɛ 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.
english: Adam is a member of the Minority Bench of the 7th Parliament of the 4th Republic in Ghana.

kusaal: O lɛn tʋm nɛ Members Holding Offices of profit Committee.on da tʋm n Mines and Energy la, o da muki paam ligidi Ghana National Petroleom Corporation (GNPC) n sʋŋid tenmaalʋg la o teŋ yɛla.
english: Serving as the ranking member on Mines and Energy, Adam pushed to secure funding from the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) foundation for projects within his constituency.

kusaal: Linɛ ka ba na tʋm anɛ bama, a zi'el ku'om zin'isa anaasi (mechnised boreholes), pɔmpinam piinɛ ayi (12 hand pump boreholes) nɛ dʋ'ʋnim dɔɔd (2 seater KVIPs o sʋ'ʋlimin la teŋ sieba, woo West Gonja District n pa'al si'em la.
english: The projects included drilling of four mechanized boreholes, 12 hand pump boreholes and two 12 seater KVIPs in some selected communities as reported by the West Gonja District.

kusaal: 2020 yʋʋm la nwadisa awai la ni, o da lɛn tis Busunu Health Centre ban'adnam lɔr kanɛ da an o nɔdigilʋg pin'ak la,ye li sʋŋi zi ban'adnam sibiti bibisin keŋ sʋ'ʋlim la sibiti tita'ar (hospital) la ni.
english: In September 2020, he presented an ambulance to the Busunu Health Centre in fulfillment of a promise he made to the chiefs and people, to help in the transportation of patients from the health care to the district hospital.

kusaal: Mutawakilu da an ranking member mines nɛ energy ni la, o da buol ye da gban'e Prof Frimpong-Boateng, Minister of Science and Technology nɛ Minister for Lands and Natural Resources zaŋi ken zam linɛ excavators nam 500 linɛ ka Galamstop daa faain galamsey dimin la.
english: Adam, in his capacity as ranking member on mines and energy, called for the arrest of both Prof. Frimpong-Boateng, Minister of Science and Technology, and the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, regarding the scandal of about 500 missing excavators which were seized from illegal miners by the task force Galamstop.

kusaal: Mutawakilu Adam anɛ onɛ ka ba da du'a o nɛ dawalig nwadig la daba ayi' daar yʋma 1974 la ni.
english: Mutawakilu Adam (born 2 March 1974) is a Ghanaian accountant and politician who is member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Damango Constituency in the Savanna Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Mutawakilu Adam yinɛ Damango bɛ Savanna Region la.
english: Mutawakilu Adam comes from Damango in the Savanna Region.

kusaal: John Evans Atta mills da gaŋ Mutawakilu ye o an Gonja West District, ka li tempʋtita'ari an Damango la an o teŋ teŋdu'adir District Chief Executive (DCE).
english: Adam was nominated by John Evans Atta Mills to serve as district chief executive for West Gonja District, whose capital is Damango, his hometown.

kusaal: On da an DCE la o da tʋm dɔlis gbaʋŋ zamisig lʋgʋrin, ku'om, a bɛ nyain nɛ ninma'asim.
english: Prior to being appointed as DCE, Adam worked as a chief cashier and head of treasury from 2004 to 2009 at University for Development Studies, at the Central Administration in Tamale.

kusaal: o party la da kɔ'ɔŋ zugraan vɔɔtʋg la tis nɛ New Patrotic Party ka kɔ'ɔŋi ba wadmaanib zin'isa la da an bɛdigʋ la.
english: His party lost the general presidential elections to the New Patriotic Party, and had lost their majority seats.

kusaal: O tʋmnɛ nɛ ligidi zanlim yɛla tʋʋma ni.
english: He is an accountant and financial officer.

kusaal: O anɛ mɔr pʋ'ʋsim nid ka mɔr pu'a nɛ biisa 5.
english: He is married, with five children.

kusaal: O yinɛ Gomoa Lome bɛ Central Region, Gaana la.
english: Naana Eyiah was born on 14 February 1963 and hails from Gomoa Lome in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ Gaana gil vɔɔtʋgin la, o da di Gomoa Central kʋk la nɛ vɔtnam tusa piinɛ anaasi, kɔbiga nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (14,178), dinɛ an pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ du'al ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.6%) ka ma'asim tiig nid la Rachel Florence Appoh paam tusa piinɛ ayi, kɔbisnii nɛpisnu nɛ anii (12,858) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ du'al anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (46.8%), ka Nɔraʋg na'adɔɔg la nid Emmanuel Appoh Mensah paam vɔɔtnam kɔbisyi nɛ pisnii (280) dinɛ an yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.0%), ka PPP nid la, Grace Ignophia Appiah paam vɔɔtnam kɔbiga nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (174).
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general elections, she won the Gomoa Central Constituency parliamentary seat with 14,178 votes making 51.6% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Rachel Florence Appoh had 12,858 votes making 46.8% of the total votes cast, the CPP parliamentary candidate Emmanuel Appoh Mensah had 280 votes making 1.0% of the total votes cast and the PPP parliamentary candidate Grace Ignophia Appiah had 174 votes making 0.6% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ pisi Gaana vɔɔtʋgin la, o da lɛn di Gomoa Central kʋk la nɛ vɔtnam tusa pisi kɔbisnu nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (20, 527) dinɛ an Pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ du'al pisnii nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (56.81%), ma'asim tiig nid la Jonamoah Moses Jehu-Appiah da paam vɔɔtnam tusa piinɛ anaasi, kɔbisnu nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (12, 568) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayi du'al pistan nɛ ayi (42.32%).
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, she again won the Gomoa Central Constituency parliamentary seat with 20,527 votes making 56.81% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Jonamoah Moses Jehu-Appiah had 14,568 votes making 42.32% of the total votes cast, the GUM parliamentary candidate Hannah Chrissam had 561 votes making 1.6% of the total votes cast and the NDP parliamentary candidate Frank Otchere Painstil had 476 votes making 1.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Quansah paas la'skanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Government Assurance Committee la ni, ka lɛn bɛ la'askanɛ gɔsid nimma'asim yɛla la ni.
english: Quansah is a member of the Government Assurance Committee and also a member of the Health Committee.

kusaal: Naana Eyiah Quansah anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la ni.
english: Naana Eyiah is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Nannanna onɛ a Wadmaani tis Gomoa Central n bɛ Central Region la dim.
english: She is the former member of parliament for Gomoa Central Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o diploma in Project Management yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: She had a diploma in Project Management in 2017.

kusaal: Quansah da anɛ kpɛɛmtita'ar (Executive Officer) Naaba Company Limited.
english: Eyiah was the chief executive officer for Naaba Company Limited.

kusaal: Quansah paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni.
english: Quansah is a member of the Government Assurance Committee and also a member of the Health Committee.

kusaal: GUM nid la, Hannah Chrissam mɛ da paam vɔɔtnam kɔbisnu nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne (561) dinɛ an yinne du'al ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (1.6%) ka NDP nid la, Frank Otchere Painstil mɛ paam vɔɔtnam kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ dinɛ an yinne du'al atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.3%).
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, she again won the Gomoa Central Constituency parliamentary seat with 20,527 votes making 56.81% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Jonamoah Moses Jehu-Appiah had 14,568 votes making 42.32% of the total votes cast, the GUM parliamentary candidate Hannah Chrissam had 561 votes making 1.6% of the total votes cast and the NDP parliamentary candidate Frank Otchere Painstil had 476 votes making 1.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Quansah anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Quansah is a member of the Government Assurance Committee and also a member of the Health Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi la nwads anaasi la ni, o da piinl nidib nwɛnɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisi (120) banɛ da paam suor ye ba keŋ Senior High School la sakur la'adnam kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb.
english: In April 2022, she donated some school materials to about 120 graduates in her constituency who had admissions to senior high schools.

kusaal: Onɛ an interior minista nya'adɔl.
english: She was a Deputy Minister for Interior.

kusaal: Nadowli anɛ tempʋbil ka an tempʋtita'ari tis Nadowli district, district kanɛ bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana Ya-datiʋŋ.
english: Nadowli is a small town and is the capital of Nadowli district, a district in the Upper West Region of north Ghana.

kusaal: Tembanɛ ka nidib mi' ka ba kpi'e nɛ Nadowli anɛ Tangasia, tenkanɛ mɔr da'akanɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa mi' district la ni, Cherekpong.
english: Other well-known cities around Nadowli are Tangasia, which has the most popular market in the district and Cherekpong.

kusaal: Nadowli East bɛni Nadowli district n bɛ Upper West Region Ghana nwa.
english: Nadowli East is located in the Nadowli district of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Na'am kʋk la bɛni Nadowli District n bɛ Upper West Region, Ghana nwa.
english: The seat is located within the Nadowli District of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li dɔlisnɛ ban daa tiak Nadawli North nɛ Nadawli South constituency nam tis Nadawli East nɛ Nadowli West constituency nam.
english: This followed the altering of the Nadawli North and Nadawli South constituencies to the Nadawli East and Nadowli West constituencies respectively.

kusaal: Nadowli East anɛ constituency nam la yinne ka mɔr wadmaan ka o zi'el tis ba bɛ wadmaanib yir la Ghana nwa.
english: Nadowli East is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba daa paam na'am kʋk la nɛ saŋkanɛ ka Ghana dim vɔtʋg tita'ar la bɛ 2004.
english: This seat came into being prior to the Ghanaian parliamentary election in 2004.

kusaal: Nadowli West bɛni Nadowli district, Upper West Region Ghana nwa.
english: Nadowli West is located in the Nadowli district of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Na'am la bɛni Nadawli District,Upper West Region of Ghana nwa .Ba kpi'ɛs banɛ ya-tuon anɛ Côte d'Ivoire.
english: The seat was located within the Nadawli District of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ka ya-datiuŋ an Jirapa/Lambussie District, ka ya-nya'aŋ an Nadowli East constituency ka ya- dagɔbʋg mɛ Wa Municipal District nɛ ya-dagɔbʋg an Wa West District.
english: To the north was the Jirapa/Lambussie District, to the east the Nadowli East constituency and to the south east the Wa Municipal District and to the south the Wa West District.

kusaal: Nadowli west Constituency da tiak nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la, Ghana vɔtʋg la lʋgir da ti tiak la yiiga Nadowli North tis Nadawli West nɛ Nadwoli South ka yʋ'ʋŋ an Nadowli East constituency.
english: The constituency changed in 2004 when the Electoral Commission of Ghana changed the initial Nadowli North to Nadawli West and the Nadwoli South to Nadowli East constituency.

kusaal: Nadowli West anɛ constituencies nam la yinne ka mɔr wadmaan ka o zi'el tis ba bɛ wadmaanib yir la Ghana nwan.
english: Nadowli West was one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Najat Kaanache anɛ onɛ ka ba da dʋ'a yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii la Nwadis piinɛ yinne dabpisi nɛ anii daa (28 November 1980) ka o an onɛ sʋ'ʋe/gɔsid AMC Networks' dʋgʋb sɔnsʋg "Cocina Marroquí" dinɛ ka ba sɔnsid Walis kanɛ bɛ Canal Cocina dinɛ bɛ Spain la nɛ El Gourmet yi tɛmis pisi (20) banɛ bɛ Latin America.
english: Najat Kaanache (born 28 November 1980) is the host of AMC Networks' cooking series "Cocina Marroquí" which airs on Canal Cocina in Spain and El Gourmet throughout 20 countries in Latin America.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Kaanache San Sebastián dinɛ bɛ Spain's Basque Country la ka o nɔbʋg ani.
english: Kaanache was born and raised in San Sebastián of Spain's Basque Country.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋr da yiya ka di yinɛ on da gaad tuonɛ di'em sini kanɛ ka ba da maal bɛ Spanish daytime television series ni la nɛ on da nwie keŋ bɛɛ gilig Middle East nɛ South America tʋm tʋʋmsʋma sʋŋ pʋ'ab nɛ biis kpi'eʋŋ yɛla.
english: She gained fame as a lead actress on Spanish daytime television series and then traveled throughout the Middle East and South America working in philanthropy to empower women and street kids.

kusaal: O da yuolim nya'aŋi keŋ diib maalʋg ka o yʋ'ʋr lɛn yi ya'as on da lieb "The Pilgrim Chef" ka di yinɛ on da naae o yʋma anaasi la nɛ dunia wʋsa banɛ dʋgʋd diibi gati ba taaba la zug: Ferran Adrià, René Redzepi, Thomas Keller, Grant Achatz, Heston Blumenthal nɛ Martín Berasategui.
english: She later attended culinary school and gained fame as "The Pilgrim Chef" by blogging throughout her four years training with the world's top chefs: Ferran Adrià, René Redzepi, Thomas Keller, Grant Achatz, Heston Blumenthal and Martín Berasategui.

kusaal: On da tʋm yʋma ayi diib kuosʋg zamisʋg zin'igin bɛ Chicago's Alinea, Napa's The French Laundry, New York's Per Se (restaurant), nɛ Copenhagen's Noma Kaanache nya'aŋ o da keŋ lieb Executive nɛ Creative Haute Cuisine Certification on da naae yʋma ayi la bɛ Spain's El Bulli.
english: After spending two years working as an apprentice in the kitchens at Chicago's Alinea, Napa's The French Laundry, New York's Per Se (restaurant), and Copenhagen's Noma Kaanache went on to achieve the auspicious Executive and Creative Haute Cuisine Certification after completing her apprenticeship during the final two seasons at Spain's El Bulli.

kusaal: Ferran Adrià yɛl Maghreb Arabe Presse ye "Najat Kaanache da zi'eni tis Morocco dɔlisid buudi pian'ad dan'aŋin.
english: Ferran Adrià stated to the Maghreb Arabe Presse that "Najat Kaanache represents the soul of Morocco through the language of the kitchen.

kusaal: El Bulli's yɔɔb nya'aŋ, Kaanache da gɔɔn kaae di-dʋgʋdib banɛ bɛ dunia wʋsa la'anɛ White House Executive Pastry Chef, Bill Yosses onɛ bɛ banɛ zamisid dʋgʋb yɛla bɛ Harvard University, New York University nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) Beijing Science Festival dinɛ da bɛ China.
english: Her passion for creativity and innovation should be a reference for the country." After El Bulli's historic closure, Kaanache traveled extensively to instruct chefs across the globe in the latest gastronomic techniques and taught and lectured alongside White House Executive Pastry Chef, Bill Yosses on the science of cooking at Harvard University (pictured), New York University and at the 2013 World Science Festival in NYC (pictured) and 2013 Beijing Science Festival in China.

kusaal: O da la'as nɛ sɔ' ka ba yɔ'ɔg diib kuisʋg zin'igi bɛ Souk Restaurant dinɛ bɛ Dallas, TX.
english: She was the opening chef partner of Souk Restaurant in Dallas, TX.

kusaal: O da lɛbn la'as nɛ sieba ka ba yɔ'ɔg Piripi Restaurant bɛ Village of Merrick Park dinɛ bɛ Coral Gables, FL; Onɛ an dikuos ka lɛn sʋ'ʋe Nur Restaurant, dinɛ bɛ Medina of Fez, Morocco.
english: She was the opening chef partner of Piripi Restaurant in the Village of Merrick Park in Coral Gables, FL; She is the chef and owner of Nur Restaurant, in the Medina of Fez, Morocco.

kusaal: Sini la paami li dunia wusa zuŋir nɛ Berlin 66th International Film Festival la nɛ Panorama zin'ig kanɛ bɛ Na'asarteŋ, Germany la ka North America premiere dim da lɛn buoli ba New Director/New film Festival n bɛ New York la.
english: The film had its world premiere at the 66th Berlin International Film Festival in the Panorama section and was invited to have its North American premiere at the New Directors/New Films Festival in New York.

kusaal: Sini la bigisidnɛ Northern Ghana sʋ'ʋlim sɔlʋŋ, Nakom anɛ linɛ pian'ad Iddrisu onɛ mɔr duata gbauŋzamisʋg piini onɛ ka li an tilas ye o bas sakur ka lɛbi kʋl o teŋin, o saam kum nya'aŋ n sʋŋ o yir dim ka ba da namisɛ.
english: An intimate narrative from Northern Ghana, Nakom follows Iddrisu, a talented medical student who must return to his home village after his father's sudden death and fight for his family's survival.

kusaal: Nakom sini da paam piini bɛɛ di Audience Choice Award 37th Durban International Film Festival la ni Ba da gaŋi li ka li an sini wɔk kanɛ an yiiga Ghana sini linɛ gaad tuon n di ya'an 66th Berlin International Film Festival la.
english: Nakom won the Audience Choice Award at the 37th Durban International Film Festival.

kusaal: Ya'asɛ, bɛnɛ Hong Kong International Sini la'asʋg zin'ig la, ba da gaŋi li ya'as yɔɔd kanɛ ni an FIPRESCI Prize la, Golden Firebird Award la, nɛ SIGNIS Award la.
english: At the Hong Kong International Film Festival, it was nominated for the FIPRESCI Prize, the Golden Firebird Award, and the SIGNIS Award.

kusaal: Li da lɛn paam gaŋir yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piina ayuobo Independent Spirit John Cassettes Award la.
english: It has been nominated for the 2016 Independent Spirit John Cassavetes Award.

kusaal: Nɛ Seattle International Sini la'asʋg zin'ig.
english: At the Seattle International Film Festival, it was nominated for the New Directors Competition.

kusaal: Di bɛnɛ North East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: It is located in the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ yʋ'ʋn an wadmaani zi'eni tis constituency la anɛ Alhaji Seidu Issifu Baba.
english: He succeeded Alhaji Seidu Issifu Baba.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni ka ba da vɔɔti tis o, o paasnɛ wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nidib ni ka da paam vɔɔt pisnu nɛ atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (53%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: In 2016, he was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and won with over 53% of the votes.

kusaal: Miss Malaika di'ema linɛ da naam yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan (2003) ni la, o da di ya'an tia'al ayi daan.
english: She was the second runner-up in Miss Malaika 2003 and the winner of Miss Ghana-Germany in 2005.

kusaal: o da di'e yɔɔd bɛdegʋ, la'am nɛ di'ema linɛ buon Glitze Style nɛ City People Entertainment Awards yɔɔd bɛdigʋ.
english: She has received awards, including the Glitz Style Awards and City People Entertainment Awards.

kusaal: Alamɛn ka di'ema line buon Miss Ghana-German ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) la ni, o da di ya'an yiiga.
english: She was the second runner-up in Miss Malaika 2003 and the winner of Miss Ghana-Germany in 2005.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2017 ni la, o da zamis siini di'ema ɛntʋg ye lin na niŋ si'em ka o paas New York siini zamisʋg lʋgʋr linɛ bɛ nasaateŋ sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni.
english: As of 2017, she was studying acting at the New York Film Academy in the United States.

kusaal: Addo si'iŋi o tʋʋma nɛ siini di'ema ni, o da naam siini di'emanam bɛdegʋ wʋʋ bikanɛ mɔr bɛʋg, ziim yɛla, saa, di kae pian'adɛ, di kʋ naam ya'asa nɛ ninta'am.
english: From the early 2020s onward, Addo built a reputation as one of Ghana's most prominent fashion figures, known for avant-garde, architecturally inspired red-carpet looks.

kusaal: O mɔrnɛ biis ayi'.
english: She is a mother of two children.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Nana Akua Owusu Afriyie nɛ 3 Selʋŋ nwadig daba atan daar, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (1969) la ni ka o an Ghana nid kanɛ an pɔlitis wɛ'ɛd ka an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Nana Akua Owusu Afriyieh (born 3 September 1969) is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Owusu Afriyie bɛnɛ 3 Selʋŋ nwadig 1969 bɛ Saltpond, Central Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Owusu Afriyieh was born on 3 September 1969 in Saltpond, Central Region.

kusaal: O mɔr diploma bɛ Management Studies n yit University of Cape Coast.
english: She holds a diploma in Management Studies from the University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: Lin yi yʋma 2015, O da di lieb wadmaan tis Ablekuma North Constituency n bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: In 2015, she contested and won the NPP parliamentary seat for the Ablekuma North Constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: O daa di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg tita'ar la ni.Nidiba atan' da nya' nɛ o, ba yʋda anɛ; Sally Amaki Darko onɛ zi'enɛ tis Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la, nɛ Akwasi Asiama Adade onɛ zi'enɛ tis nɔraʋg paati daa mɛ la'am nyi'ad yʋma 2016 by-election bɛ Ablekuma North linɛ da an 7 samanpiid nwadig 2016.
english: Three other candidates, namely Sally Amaki Darko of the National Democratic Congress, and Akwasi Asiama Adade of the Conventions People's Party also contested in the 2016 by-election of Ablekuma North held on 7 December 2016.

kusaal: Owusu Afriyie daa di vɔɔdʋg la ka paam vɔɔt kal tusa pisnu nɛ anaasi, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piswai nɛ anii (54,698) yit vɔɔt tusa pisnii nɛ ayi, nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (82,091) pʋʋgin, ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o paam vɔɔt pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ du'al pisnii nɛ anaasi (66.84) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Owusu Afriyie won the election by obtaining 54,698 votes out of the 82,091 cast, representing 66.84 percent of total valid votes.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Ablekuma North Constituency.
english: In 2015, she contested and won the NPP parliamentary seat for the Ablekuma North Constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: O da anɛ Attorney General dinɛ yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne (2001) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan (2003) la in, ka lɛn an Foreign Affairs minista din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan (2003) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la in, bɛ Kufuor gɔmina la ni.
english: He previously served as Attorney General from 2001 to 2003 and as Minister for Foreign Affairs from 2003 to 2007 under the administration of then-president John Kufuor.

kusaal: O da pʋ paam ka Ma'asim-tiig paati la ka John Evans Atta Mills di bɛ 2008 ka John Dramani Mahama lɛm di bɛ 2012 ni.
english: He lost on both occasions to National Democratic Congress' candidates: John Evans Atta Mills in 2008 and John Dramani Mahama in 2012.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o zi'en zugdaan tis Wabig paati la nɔɔr atan' bɛ 2016 vɔɔtʋg la ni, ka nanna nwa Mahama onɛ da bɛ kuk la zug la (nɛ 53.85% bɛ vɔɔtʋg la wʋsa), dinɛ da an yiiga yɛlʋg ka onɛ ka'e kuk la zugɔ nyaŋi lʋb onɛ bɛ kuk la zug.
english: He was chosen as the presidential candidate of the New Patriotic Party for a third time for the 2016 general elections, and this time he defeated incumbent John Dramani Mahama in the first round, winning with 53.85% of the votes.This marked the first time in a Ghanaian presidential history that an opposition candidate won an outright majority in the first round.

kusaal: Nana Addo Dankwa Akuffo-Addo ka ba da du'au bɛ Swalaba, teŋbil kani nɛ Accra, Ghana bɛ 29 March 1944, tis Edward Akuffo-Addo onɛ da an Ghana zugdaa la.
english: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo was born in Accra, Ghana, on March 29, 1944, to Adeline Ofori-Atta and Edward Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: O saam Edward Akufo-Addo anɛ Akropong-Akuapem nid la da anɛ Ghana Chief Justice onɛ paasi atan daan din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (1966) ti paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi (1970) la ni, chairman bɛ 1967–68 Constitutional Commission nɛ non-executive president of Ghana bɛ 1970 ti paae 1972 ni.
english: His father, Edward Akufo-Addo, from Akropong-Akuapem was Ghana's third Chief Justice from 1966 to 1970, chairman of the 1967–68 Constitutional Commission and the non-executive president of Ghana from 1970 till 1972.

kusaal: Akufo-Addo madir yaadaʋ anɛ Nana Sir Ofori Atta, Akyem Abuakwadim Na'ab, onɛ da pɛ'ɛs executive council gɔmma ni saŋkanɛ da an Gold Coast ka naan tiaki yʋ'ʋn an Ghana la.
english: Akufo-Addo's maternal grandfather was Nana Sir Ofori Atta, King of Akyem Abuakwa, who was a member of the Executive Council of the Gold Coast before Ghana's independence.

kusaal: O anɛ Kofi Asante Ofori-Atta nɛ William Ofori Atta ansig.
english: He is a nephew of ex-Speaker of Parliament Kofi Asante Ofori-Atta and the Big Six member William Ofori Atta.
