kusaal: O yaadaʋ da an J. B. Danquah, onɛ pɛ'ɛs Big Six la ni.
english: J. B. Danquah, another member of The Big Six, was a granduncle of his.

kusaal: O pin'ili o primary education bɛ Government Boys School, Adabraka, ka yʋolim keŋ Rowe Road School, nɛ' wʋsa bɛnɛ Accra Central.
english: He started his primary education at the Government Boys School and Rowe Road School (now Kinbu), both in Accra Central.

kusaal: O da keŋ England ye zamis O-Level nɛ A-Level kpansib sɔb bɛ Lancing College, Sussex, zin'ikanɛ ka ba da pʋdʋ ye "Billy" ka pɛ'ɛs Anglican faith la.
english: He went to England and continued his education at Holmewood House Preparatory School before studying for his O-Level and A-Level examinations at Lancing College, Sussex, where he was nicknamed "Billy" and joined the Anglican faith.

kusaal: O da pin'ili o Philosophy, Politics nɛ Economics course bɛ New College, Oxford bɛ 1962 ni, ka bas da lɛm zaŋi bas.
english: He began the Philosophy, Politics and Economics course at New College, Oxford, in 1962, but left soon afterwards.

kusaal: O da lɛb Ghana nɛ nɛ 1962 ye o pa'al bɛ Accra Academy, ka naam keŋ ye o zamis economics bɛ University of Ghana ni, Legon bɛ 1964, ka paam BSc (Econ) degree 1967 yʋʋm la ni.
english: He returned to Ghana in 1962 to teach at the Accra Academy, before going to read economics at the University of Ghana, Legon, in 1964, earning a BSc (Econ) degree in 1967.

kusaal: O da keŋ tuoni pɛ'ɛs Middle Temple ka zamisi an lawyer bɛ dinɛ ka ba ye Inns of Court la, dinɛ ka formal law degree pʋ tʋmma.
english: He subsequently joined the Middle Temple and trained as a lawyer under the apprenticeship system known as the Inns of Court, where no formal law degree was required.

kusaal: Ba da buol o yit English Bar (Middle Temple) bɛJuly 1971.
english: He was called to the English Bar (Middle Temple) in July 1971.

kusaal: Ghanaian bar dim mɛn da buol o bɛ July 1975.
english: He was called to the Ghanaian bar in July 1975.

kusaal: Akufo-Addo tʋmi bɛ Paris office of the U.S. law firm Coudert Brothers ni.
english: Akufo-Addo worked with the Paris office of the U.S. law firm Coudert Brothers.

kusaal: Ka 1979 nii, o pin'il law firm Prempeh and Co nɛ sɔ'.
english: In 1979, he co-founded the law firm Akufo-Addo, Prempeh and Co.

kusaal: Akufo-Addo pin'ili o pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛbnɛ 1970s naar dinɛ ka o da pɛ'ɛs People's Movement for Freedom and Justice (PMFJ), lʋgʋr kani la'as ye di ki'is General Acheampong-led Supreme Military Council's Union Government proposals.
english: Akufo-Addo's participation in politics formally began in the late 1970s when he joined the People's Movement for Freedom and Justice (PMFJ), an organization formed to oppose the General Acheampong-led Supreme Military Council's Union Government proposals.

kusaal: Ka May 1995 nii, o da pɛ'ɛs lʋgʋr da na'am paalʋ ye ba bɔɔdnɛ tiakir, ki'isʋg lʋgʋr kani ki'isid Neo-liberal gban'ar nwɛnnɛ gban'ar kani an ye ba pi'il Value Added Tax nɛ human rights violations kani ka Rawlings mɛn da mɔr na la.
english: In May 1995, he was among a broad group of elites who formed Alliance for Change, an alliance that organized demonstrations against Neo-liberal policies such as the introduction of Value Added Tax and human rights violations of the Rawlings presidency.

kusaal: Banɛ da bɛ tuoni maan mɛ' anɛ o mɛŋ, Abdul Malik ,Kwaku Baako nɛ Saifullah Senior minister Victor Newman, Kwasi Pratt Jnr, Dr.
english: At the forefront of this demonstration were himself, Abdul Malik, Kwaku Baako and Saifullah Senior minister Victor Newman, Kwasi Pratt Jnr, Dr. Charles Wereko Brobbey among others.

kusaal: O da anɛ 2nd, 3rd and 4th Mp bɛ 4th republic bɛ Abuakwa Constituency la ni.
english: He was a member of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th parliament of the 4th republic representing the Abuakwa constituency.

kusaal: 1996 vɔɔtʋg la ni, o da paam vɔɔtnam 28,526 bɛ 50,263 vɔɔtnam ka mɔr 56.75% gaad Owuraku Amofa onɛ da paam vɔɔtnam 20,173, Adoo-Aikins onɛ mɛn da paam vɔɔtnam 705, Ahmadu Rufai mɛn da paam vɔɔtnam 682 ka Emmanuel Kofi Tamakloe onɛ mɛn da paam vɔɔtnam 177.
english: In the 1996 elections, he polled 28,526 votes out of the 50,263 valid votes cast representing 56.75% over Owuraku Amofah who polled 20,173 votes, Adoo-Aikins who polled 705 votes, Ahmadu Rufai who polled 682 votes and Emmanuel Kofi Tamakloe who polled 177 votes.

kusaal: O lɛm di bɛ 2000 General Elections nɛ vɔɔtnam 28,633 yit 45,795 vɔɔtnamin ka bɛ 62.50% gaad Christiana Annor onɛ paam vɔɔtnam14,486, Addo-Aikins onɛ paam vɔɔtnam 1.088, Theresa Stella Amakye onɛ paam vɔɔtnam 593, Kofi Opoku-Gyamera onɛ paam vɔɔtnam 519 ka Isaac Duodu Awah mɛn paam vɔɔtam 506.
english: He won again in the 2000 General Elections with 28,633 votes out of the 45,795 valid votes cast representing 62.50% over Christiana Annor who polled 14,486 votes, Addo-Aikins who polled 1,088 votes, Theresa Stella Amakye who polled 593 votes, Kofi Opoku-Gyamera who polled 519 votes and Isaac Duodu Awah who also polled 506 votes.

kusaal: Akufo-Addo da pin'ili nya'ad na'am la nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) vɔɔtʋg la ni nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) la ni ya'as, nɔɔr ayi' la o da bɛnɛ Wabig paati la ni (NPP).
english: Akufo-Addo first ran for president in the year 2008 and again in 2012, both times as the presidential candidate of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Ka 2012 vɔɔtʋg la nii, o da pʋ basɛ ka mɔri keŋ kooto ni, amaa ka Supreme Court of Ghana siak ye Mahama diya.
english: After the 2012 general elections, he refused to concede and proceeded to court to challenge the electoral results, but the Supreme Court of Ghana affirmed Mahama's victory.

kusaal: Ka nidib wʋʋ 100,000 pɛ'ɛsi ba.
english: They were joined by about 100,000 other people.

kusaal: Oheneba Nana Ama Dokua Asiamah-Adjei anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n tis Akropong linɛ bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la, ba da du'a o nɛ nwadis ayɔpɔi dabisim pisi nɛ anaasi daar yʋma 1982 la ni.O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid onɛ an minista kanɛ an Trade & Industry nya'andɔl nannanna.
english: Oheneba Nana Ama Dokua Asiamah-Adjei (born 24 July 1982) is a Ghanaian politician and was the member of parliament for Akropong Constituency in the Eastern Region.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Adjei nɛ nwadis ayɔpɔi dabasim pisi nɛ anaasi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi (1982) la ni, o saam anɛ Nana Osae Nyampong IV, ka o ma an Aforo Asiamah-Adjei bɛ Akropong, linɛ bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm, Ghana.
english: Adjei was born on 24 July 1982 to Nana Osae Nyampong IV and Mrs. Aforo Asiamah-Adjei in Akropong, Eastern Region.

kusaal: O da sin'iŋi o sakur nɛ biis sakur la nɛ tɔlisʋg zamisʋg la nɛ bɛ Alsyd Academy nɛ St Roses Senior High school la ni.
english: She had her basic and senior school education at Alsyd Academy and St Roses Senior High school respectively.

kusaal: O mɔr digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ zamisʋgu an pʋtɛn'ɛr yɛla la (psychology) bɛ University of Ghana ka maali o mastɛs digirii zamisʋg linɛ an Logistics nɛ Supply Chain la yi Exter University linɛ United Kingdom la O da tɔlis mastɛs digirii zamisʋg linɛ an sunbugusum nɛ Gu'u mɛŋ yɛla bɛ Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC) sakurin la.
english: She holds a bachelor's degree in psychology from the University of Ghana and a master's degree in Logistics and Supply Chain from the Exter University in United Kingdom She further had her master's degree in Peace and Security at the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC).

kusaal: Adjei da an darɛta gɔsid Bekleen Limited tʋʋma lin da yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la ni ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la ni, ka lɛn an Pongas Limited tʋʋma kpɛɛm lin da yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la ni ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015) la ni.
english: Adjei was the managing director for Bekleen Limited from 2007 to 2016 and also Pongas Limited from 2007 to 2015.

kusaal: Yʋma 2016 la ni ka Ghana dim da maal vɔt la ka o di, Akropong/Akuapem North sʋ'ʋlʋm wadmaanib kʋk nɛ vɔt bam 26,655 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 62.3% vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni ala ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid Yaw Appiah-Kubi mɛ da mɔr 6,949 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 16.8% vɔt la wʋsa ni, ka Asiedu Ofei onɛ da zi'en o mɛŋ nyari la mɛ da mɔr vɔt bam 9,092 kɔbiga pʋʋgin o da mɔri 21.2% vɔt la kanl wʋsa ni ka CPP nid la Gifty Mercy Anakwa mɛ da mɔr 102 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 0.2% n yi vɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general election, she won the Akropong/Akuapem North Constituency parliamentary seat with 26,655 votes making 62.3% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Yaw Appiah-Kubi had 6,949 votes making 16.8% of the total votes cast, an Independent parliamentary candidate Asiedu Ofei had 9,092 votes making 21.2% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Gifty Mercy Anakwa had 102 votes making 0.2% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋma 2020la ni ka Ghana dim da maal vɔt la ka o lɛn di, Akropong/Akuapem North sʋ'ʋlʋm wadmaanib kʋk nɛ vɔɔt bam 26,646 kɔbiga pʋʋginɛ o da mɔri 55.3% vɔɔt la kanl wʋsa ni ala ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid, Justice Kotey Amasah mɔr vɔt ban10,505 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 21.8% vɔt la wʋsa ni.Ka Adjei Twumasi William Kwabena onɛ da zi'enɛ o nyari la mɛ da mɔr 10,444 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 21.7% vɔɔt la wʋsa ni, PNC nid Desmond Twumasi Ntow da mɔr vɔɔt bam 421 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 0.9% vɔɔt la kanl wʋsa ni, ka CPP nid Gifty Mercy Anakwa mɔr vɔɔt bam 146 ka kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 0.3% yi vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general election, she again won the Akropong/Akuapem North Constituency parliamentary seat with 26,646 votes making 55.3% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Justice Kotey Amasah had 10,505 votes making 21.8% of the total votes cast, an Independent parliamentary candidate Adjei Twumasi William Kwabena had 10,444 votes making 21.7% of the total votes cast, the PNC parliamentary candidate Desmond Twumasi Ntow had 421 votes making 0.9% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Gifty Mercy Anakwa had 146 votes making 0.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Adjei anɛ Defence nɛ Interior kpɛɛmnam la yinne.
english: Adjei was a member of the Defence and Interior Committee.

kusaal: Nwadis pii nɛ yinne yʋma 2021 la ni, o da da' kɔmpuuta nam n tis Mangoase Methodist Sakur linɛ bɛ Akuapim North sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: In November 2021, she presented computers and accessories to Mangoase Methodist School in the Akuapim North Constituency.

kusaal: Adjei anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.Onɛ an wadmaan n tis Akropong linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: She was the Member of Parliament for the Akropong Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana from 2017 to 2025.

kusaal: Adjei mɔr pu'a ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Charles Cromwell Nanabanyin Bissue ka ba mɔr biribiŋ nɛ bipumis ayi'.
english: Adjei has two sons and two daughters.

kusaal: Nwadis anu la yʋma 2022 la ni, Adjei da nɔk ligidi linɛ an wʋʋ GHc30,000 ye ba mɛ' na'am sʋg n bɛ Adawso la.Ka nwadis ayɔpɔi la yʋma 2022 la ni, ka o da sʋŋ Akropong Daakye Sibiti bil la.
english: In May 2022, Adjei donated an amount of GHc30,000 for the construction of the chief palace at Adawso.

kusaal: Nana Amaniampong Marfo (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa atan' la daba ayuobʋ daar, 6 March 1957) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas 6th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.
english: Nana Amaniampong Marfo (born 6 March 1957) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the 6th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Marfo da maali o GCE O level certificate nɛ Tetrem School ka maali o GCE A level bɛ St.
english: Marfo obtained his GCE O-level certificate from Tetrem School and his GCE A-level from St. Augustine's College, Cape Coast.

kusaal: O da maal BSc Admin in Finance and Management nɛ MBA in Marketing bɛ University of Ghana.
english: He earned a BSc Admin in Finance and Management and MBA in Marketing at the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Marfo yinɛ Tetrem-Afigya bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Marfo hails from Tetrem-Afigya in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Marfo anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Afigya-Kwabre North Constituency bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlim Ghana la wabʋg na'adɔɔg (New Patriotic Party) nɔba zug.
english: Marfo is a Ghanaian politician and a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Afigya-Kwabre North Constituency in the Ashanti region of Ghana on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Marfo da nyi'a yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔdʋgin la wabʋg na'adɔɔg, (New Patriotic Party) nɔba zugʋ tis Afighya-Kwabre North bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la ka da di nɛ vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (17, 597) dinɛ an vɔɔt pisyuobʋ nɛ awai du'al pistan' nɛ anaasi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (69.34%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Marfo first contested in the 2012 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party for Afighya-Kwabre North in the Ashanti region of Ghana and won the election with 17,597 votes, representing 69.34% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔt la ka bas Alex Yaw-Poku onɛ bɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, (National Democratic Congress), ka Daniel Atta Asenso Preprah onɛ bɛ PPP ni nɛ Duah Hubert onɛ bɛ CPP ni nɛ Francis Boadu onɛ bɛ NDP ni nɛ Joyce Oduro onɛ bɛ PNC ni.
english: He won the election over Alex Yaw-Poku of the National Democratic Congress, Daniel Atta Asenso Preprah of the PPP, Duah Hubert of the Convention People's Party, Francis Boadu of the NDP and Joyce Oduro of the PNC.

kusaal: Marfo da nya' Afighya-Kwabre North wadmaannib kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug ka di nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (17, 978) dinɛ an vɔɔt pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne du'al pisnu nɛ ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (71.52%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Marfo contested for Afighya-Kwabre North parliamentary seat in the 2016 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of New Patriotic Party and won the election with 17, 978 votes representing 71.52% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔt la ka bas Kwaku Agyekum Asare onɛ bɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress onɛ da paam vɔɔt tusa ayuobʋ, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (6, 689) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisi nɛ ayuobʋ du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (26.61%), Convention people's party wadmaan na'anya'ad Frank Opoku da paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi nɛ anaasi (204) dinɛ zi'eni tis vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pisnii nɛ yinne (0.81%), PPP wadmaan na'anya'ad, Francis Boadu da paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (197) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.78%) ka PNC wadmaan na'aya'ad, Joyce Oduro paam vɔɔt pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (68) dinɛ zɛm nɛ vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.27%).
english: He won the election over Kwaku Agyekum Asare of the National Democratic Congress who polled 6,689 which is equivalent to 26.61%, the Convention people's party parliamentary candidate Frank Opoku had 204 votes representing 0.81%, the parliamentary candidate of the PPP Francis Boadu had 197 votes representing 0.78% and PNC parliamentary candidate Joyce Oduro polled 68 votes which is equivalent to 0.27% of the total votes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) NPP wadmaannib gaansigin la, Marfo da liya ka Collins Adomako Mensah da di zi'eni tis Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: During the 2020 NPP primaries, Marfo lost the election to Collins Adomako Mensah to represent the New Patriotic Party in 2020 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: On da naae University of Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (1989), Marfo da maali national service nɛ National Mobilization.
english: After completing his studies at the University of Ghana in 1989, Marfo worked as a national service personnel at National Mobilization.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994) o da anɛ Senior Superintendent bɛ Ghana Education Service (GES).
english: From 1991 to 1994 he was a Senior Superintendent at the Ghana Education Service (GES).

kusaal: On da bas GES la yʋʋm yinne nya'aŋ, ba da gaŋ o ye o an senior manager tis Ghana Commercial Bank ka o da an SME kpɛɛm tis Northern Sʋ'ʋlim.
english: A year after leaving GES, he was appointed senior manager of the Ghana Commercial Bank working as the SME head of the Northern Sector.

kusaal: O da tʋm din yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu (1995) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012).
english: He served in that capacity from 1995 to 2012.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) o da anɛ pa'an (lecturer) tis University College of Education.
english: From 2009 to 2012 he doubled as a lecturer at the University College of Education.

kusaal: Augustine's College, Cape Coast.
english: Marfo obtained his GCE O-level certificate from Tetrem School and his GCE A-level from St. Augustine's College, Cape Coast.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔt la da zɛm nɛ vɔɔt pisi nɛ anaasi du'al pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (24.46%), vɔɔt anaasi du'al pisi nɛ atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (4.23%), vɔɔt nɛɛm pisnii nɛ yinne kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (0.81%), vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (0.69%), nɛ vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (0.47%) nwɛnnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: They obtained 6,207 votes, 1,073 votes, 205 votes, 175 votes and 120 votes respectively out of the total votes, equivalent to 24.46%, 4.23%, 0.81%, 0.69%, and 0.47% respectively.

kusaal: O mor pʋ'a nɛ biisa ayi'.
english: He is married with two children.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Amoakoh nɛ dabisim piiga nɛ anu daar nwadisa atan' la ni 1958 ka o yit Denkyira - Apkropong teŋ kanɛ bɛ Central Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm nwa ni na.
english: Amoakoh was born on 15 March 1958 and hails from Denkyira-Akropong in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ York College n yina nɛ o bachelor's degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ psychology zamisʋgin.
english: He attended the York College and graduated with a bachelor's degree in psychology.

kusaal: Amoakoh anɛ Psychologist nɛ kpikpiʋŋ tʋʋma sɔb.
english: Amoakoh is a Psychologist and a businessman.

kusaal: 2020 Npp primaries la ni ka o da lʋ tis Festus Awuah Kwofie ka pʋ nyaŋi nyi'a na'am la bɛ Upper Denkyira East ya'asa.
english: In 2020 during the NPP primaries, he lost his bid to represent the Upper Denkyira East in parliament to Festus Awuah Kwofie in the 2020 general election.

kusaal: O da pin'ili o Kɔligi Sakur ken nɛ Boa Amposem Senior High School.
english: He had his secondary education at the Boa Amponsem Senior High School.

kusaal: O da lieb wadmaan bɛ Ghana kpɛla ni nɛ yʋma 2005 la ni.
english: In 2005, he became a member of the parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Amoakoh anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid (NPP).O da lieb Wadmaan bɛ Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni nɛ yʋma 2005.
english: In 2020 during the NPP primaries, he lost his bid to represent the Upper Denkyira East in parliament to Festus Awuah Kwofie in the 2020 general election.

kusaal: yʋmyʋmnib banɛ ka o mi' nɔkiba o tʋʋma ni la ba sieba anɛ Shatta Wale, Stonebwoy, nɛ Becca, nɛ Kumi Guitar, nɛ Joyce Blessing.
english: In 2016, He founded Zylofon Media, a multimedia company which he used to recruit notable musicians like Shatta Wale, Stonebwoy, Becca, Kumi Guitar, and Joyce Blessing.

kusaal: Zylofon Media nɔbigi ba tʋʋma paae sini maanib (film industry) kɛ ka banɛ ka nidib mi' ba ka ba an sini maanib wʋʋ Benedicta Gafah, nɛ Toosweet Annan, nɛ Nana Appiah mɛŋ paasi li pʋʋgin.
english: Zylofon Media also extended its reach to the film industry, signing popular actors like Benedicta Gafah, and Toosweet Annan.

kusaal: Nwa' da kɛ ka banɛ gɔsid tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nam ka ba yʋ'ʋr buon Criminal Investigations Department bɛ Ghana Police Service tʋʋma ni la ka ba tis nɔɔr linɛ buon ye Interpol red alert.
english: On 9 January 2019, a circuit court issued a warrant to arrest Mensah for money laundering and fraud causing the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service to trigger an Interpol red alert.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi, nɛ piiga nɛ anii la, nwadis awai la ni (September 2018), Menzgold da mɔr Securities and Exchange Commission, Ghana (SEC) nɛ Bank of Ghana (BOG) kɛŋ kɔɔtɔ ni' banɛ daa die o tʋʋma gbaʋŋ la yela.
english: In September 2018, Menzgold took the Securities and Exchange Commission, Ghana (SEC) and the Bank of Ghana (BOG) to court after its license was revoked by the SEC.

kusaal: Mensah da lɛb Ghana na yʋʋm tusa ayi, nɛ piiga, nɛ awai la, nwadis ayɔpɔi la ni (July 2019), ye wada pʋ gban'e o Dubai tɛŋine ka o na gɔs ka yɔ' Menzgold sama' la wʋsa.
english: Mensah returned to Ghana in July 2019, claiming he had been acquitted in Dubai and would assist authorities in paying back Menzgold customers.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ atan', dabisa piiga, nɛ anii la daar (18 August 2023), Nana Appiah Mensah, daa gban'e ye o lɛn paam ligidi yi banɛ ka o mori ba sama la ni linɛ daa an Digital Verification Access Card ka li yɔɔd an million ayʋobu, tusa ayi' nɛ kɔbʋs nu' (GHC650) O daa mudugud ye yɔɔd la an suor kanɛ ka banɛ ka o mori ba sam la na pa'ali ba mɛŋ ka o nyaan yɔɔ ba.
english: On 18 August 2023, Nana Appiah Mensah, attempted to further raise more money from his victims through a purported Digital Verification Access Card priced at GHC650.

kusaal: 4syte Music Video ya'an piini yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2017) – ya'an piini tita'ar.
english: 4syte Music Video Awards 2017 - Lifetime Achievement Award.

kusaal: Ya'an piini linɛ bɛɛ li kɔn' – yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii (2018) Radio and Television Personality (RTP) Awards ka nyaan paas ayi' daani bɛ Most Influential Entertainment Personality Ghana sʋ'ʋlim yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii (2018), da tial ne one an chief executive officer tis EiB Network, Kwabena Adisi onɛ ka ba buon ye 'Bola Ray' la.
english: Special Award - 2018 Radio and Television Personality (RTP) Awards before popping up second on a list of the Most Influential Entertainment Personality in Ghana for 2018 behind the chief executive officer of EiB Network, Kwabena Adisi known as 'Bola Ray'.

kusaal: O da paas dasam nɛ pʋ'asada ban kɔbʋga banɛ nyaŋi tʋm tʋʋma ninsabilis sʋ'ʋlim gatti ba taaba, ka ba da die yi nɛ Confederation of West African Youth (CWAY), yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii, nwadis ayɔpɔi (July 2018) la ni.
english: 100 Most Influential Young Persons in Africa by the Confederation of West African Youth (CWAY) in July 2018.

kusaal: O da die ya'an piini an onɛ paas anii 8th Ghana Entrepreneur and Corporate Executive Awards yʋʋm tusa sayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii, nwadis anaasi (April 2018) - Best Business Executive yʋʋm kan la.
english: 8th Ghana Entrepreneur and Corporate Executive Awards in April 2018 - Best Business Executive of the Year.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii, nwadis awai (November 2018) – O da die ya'an piini kanɛ bɛɛ li kɔn' bɛ Ghana Music Awards South Africa.
english: November 2018 - Special Award at the Ghana Music Awards South Africa.

kusaal: NAM 1 da paam linɛ buon lower-tier Star Madrid FC, ka li yinɛ o tʋʋm kanɛ buon ye Zylofon Cash la, ka li da anɛ yʋma nu' ka ligidi kanɛ bɛɛ li pʋʋgin an na'asaatɛŋ ligidi million piiga ($10 million) anina kʋ da kilim one sʋŋid Ghana Premier League yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii, nwadis anu (May 2018) la ni.
english: Acquiring lower-tier Star Madrid FC, NAM 1 through one of his companies Zylofon Cash signing a five-year deal worth $10 million to become the headline sponsors of the Ghana Premier League in May 2018.

kusaal: Piini kane an Special Recognition Award for Business Innovation bene the Exclusive Men Of The Year Africa Awards (EMY AFRICA) League yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi, nwadis ayuobu (June 2017) la ni.
english: Special Recognition Award for Business Innovation at the Exclusive Men Of The Year Africa Awards (EMY AFRICA) in June 2017.

kusaal: O pʋ'a yʋ'ʋri buon Rose Mensah, onɛ sʋ'ʋe Rozzy's Collection, ka dʋ'a biribiŋ yinne.
english: He is married to Rose Mensah, who was charged by the state as a coconspirator.

kusaal: Nana Appiah Mensah da pin'il o sʋ'ʋm-mɛŋ tʋʋma ka mɔr gban'ar ye o tiak di'ema yela (entertainment industry) Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Nana Appiah Mensah had his secondary school education at Adisadel College in the Cape Coast.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu la ni, o da pin'il Zylofon Media, linɛ nyaŋi sʋŋ Ghana nidib banɛ mɔr ya'am kati wae diema pʋʋgin ka kɛ ka yʋʋma nam nɛ diema yela nyaŋi kɛŋ tuon.
english: In 2016, He founded Zylofon Media, a multimedia company which he used to recruit notable musicians like Shatta Wale, Stonebwoy, Becca, Kumi Guitar, and Joyce Blessing.

kusaal: Linɛ paas on tʋm tʋʋm si'eba di'ema pʋʋgin anɛ ye, Nana Appiah Mensah da tumtʋʋmsia, li si'eba anɛ sanlima kuosug ne ya' kuosug.
english: Nana Appiah Mensah had his secondary school education at Adisadel College in the Cape Coast.

kusaal: Banɛ gɔsid lʋgir nwa tʋʋma ka ti buon ye Ghana Securities and Exchange Commission la da gu'oe ba tʋʋma yʋʋm tusa ayi', nɛ piiga nɛ anii la, nwadis awai la ni (September 2018).
english: In September 2018, Menzgold took the Securities and Exchange Commission, Ghana (SEC) and the Bank of Ghana (BOG) to court after its license was revoked by the SEC.

kusaal: Li da dɔlisnɛ Zylofon Arts Fund ligidi, ka o da suŋ banɛ an yʋmyʋmnib nɛ banɛ nan duod di'ema tʋʋma ni, nɛ sini maanib nɛ ligidi ye ba nyaŋi nɔbig.
english: Zylofon Media also extended its reach to the film industry, signing popular actors like Benedicta Gafah, and Toosweet Annan.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piiga nɛ awai la, pin'ilig nwadig la, daba awai daar (9 January 2019), kootu da tis o gbaʋŋ ye ba gban'e Mensah ka yɛ o mɔri ligidi tʋm lin pʋ nar si'em ka mɛ len ma'a nidib ye o fan'e ba.
english: On 9 January 2019, a circuit court issued a warrant to arrest Mensah for money laundering and fraud causing the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service to trigger an Interpol red alert.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ atan' (2023), ka A-G daa tis nɔɔr ye o na gɔs Menzgold tubur tɛɛgir yela, ka nwe' o nɛ yela pistan' nɛ awai (39).
english: In the fall of 2023, the A-G announced that he would take over the prosecution of the Menzgold case, slapping him with 39 counts of various charges.

kusaal: Nana Appiah Mensah daa paae Ghana naan nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabisa piiga nɛ yinne daar (11 July) ye banɛ ka ba buon ye Criminal Investigation Department ka li bɛ Ghana Police Service tʋʋma ni la, vɛɛnsi gɔs.
english: On 9 January 2019, a circuit court issued a warrant to arrest Mensah for money laundering and fraud causing the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service to trigger an Interpol red alert.

kusaal: One an Attorney General nɛ Minister of Justice daa tis nidib ti'ir ye banɛ ligidi bɛ Menzgold Ghana Limited dim ni la na paami ba ligidi dies, bɔzugɔ gɔmena pin'il ye ba tɛ'ɛg tʋʋma nwa' tubir, nɛ one sʋ'ʋe li, Nana Appiah Mensah.
english: Nana Appiah Mensah and his companies were charged with 39 counts of various offences on August 30, 2023 including unlicensed gold sales, unauthorized deposit-taking, investment inducement, defrauding by false pretences, fraudulent breach of trust, and money laundering involving over GH₵340 million.

kusaal: O da paam ya'an piini ka li anɛ o tʋʋma yela benɛ Exclusive Men of the Year Africa Awards 2017.
english: Special Recognition Award for Business Innovation at the Exclusive Men Of The Year Africa Awards 2017.

kusaal: O da die ya'an piini kane an one paas ayi' one nyaŋidi sʋŋid diema yela ka ba buon 2nd Most Influential Entertainment Personality bɛ Ghana yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii (2018).
english: Special Award - 2018 Radio and Television Personality (RTP) Awards before popping up second on a list of the Most Influential Entertainment Personality in Ghana for 2018 behind the chief executive officer of EiB Network, Kwabena Adisi known as 'Bola Ray'.

kusaal: Dua'ata Nana Ayew Afriye anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Effiduase-Asokore Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region la New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Dr. Nana Ayew Afriye is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Effiduase-Asokore Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Afriye nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la dabpisi nɛ ayi' daar ((22 January 1978), ka o yi Effiduase n bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Afriye was born on 22 January 1978 and hails from Effiduase in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋma 2004 la ni la, o da maali o Bachelor of Medicine nɛ Bachelor of Surgery kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit University of Ghana ka lɛn maali o Post Graduate Certificate in Health Economics Oxford University ni.
english: In 2004, he had his Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery from the University of Ghana and also a Post Graduate Certificate in Health Economics from the Oxford University.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009), o da tɔlisi maali o MA in Economics Policy Management yit University of Ghana.
english: In 2009, he further had his MA in Economics Policy Management from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Ka yʋma 2011 la ni la, ka maal o MPH in Health Economics University of Leeds in UK.
english: In 2011, he had his MPH in Health Economics from the University of Leeds in UK.

kusaal: Johns Hospital and Fertility kanɛ bɛ Tantra Hills, Accra la.
english: Afriye was the CEO of St. Johns Hospital and Fertility located at Tantra Hills in Accra.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid Institutional Public Health bɛ Ridge Hospital.
english: He was also the Head Institutional Public Health at the Ridge Hospital.

kusaal: Afriye da anɛ CEO tis St.
english: Afriye was the CEO of St. Johns Hospital and Fertility located at Tantra Hills in Accra.

kusaal: Afriye anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nid (New Patriotic Party) ka an wadmaani tis Effiduase-Asokore Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Ashanti Region la dim.
english: Afriye is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the member of parliament for Effiduase-Asokore Constituency in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Afriye anɛ kʋkdaani tis la'askanɛ gɔsid nimma'asim yɛla ka lɛm paas la'askanɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla ya'as.
english: Afriye is the Chairperson for the Health Committee and also a member of the Finance Committee.

kusaal: Afriye anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Afriye is a Christian.

kusaal: O mɔr biis atan'.
english: He has four children.

kusaal: Nandom an tempʋtita'ari tis Nandom Municipal bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Nandom is the capital town of the Nandom Municipal District of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Nimbanɛ bɛ Nandom la pian'adnɛ Lobr buudi pian'ad, ka Dagaaba banɛ bɛ Ya-dagɔbʋg la pian'ad Ngmere (bɛɛ Central Dàgááre).
english: The people of Nandom speak the Lobr dialect, and the Dagaaba to the south speak Ngmere (or Central Dàgááre).

kusaal: Nambanɛ bɛ Nandom la mɔrnɛ 'Dagara' pa'an pian'ad la, ka nimbanɛ mɛ bɛ Ya-datiʋŋ la mɛ mɔr 'Dagaaba' pa'an nidib la ka mɔr Dagaare pa'an pian'ad piana'ad la.
english: People in Nandom use the label 'Dagara' for the language and the people while southern speakers in areas like Jirapa, Nadowli, Kaleo and Daffiama use the label 'Dagaaba' for the people and Dagaare for the language.

kusaal: Nandom bɛnɛ Lawra-Nandom District zin'isieba.
english: Nandom used to be part of the Lawra-Nandom District.

kusaal: Di da liebi di mɛŋ district nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni ka di lieb municipal, ka ba buon ye Nandom Municipal, ka mɔr wadmaan ka o zi'eni tisi ba Parliament of Ghana bɛ Accra.
english: It became a district by itself in 2012 and in 2020 it became a municipality, called the Nandom Municipal, with a parliamentary representative in the Parliament of Ghana in the capital city of Accra.

kusaal: Nandom tempʋʋg la anɛ mɛɛla anu lɛbid Volta River Ya-nya'aŋ baba dinɛ an Ghana nɛ Burkina Faso titɔdig.
english: Nandom town is eight kilometres (five miles) east of the Volta River which is the natural border between Ghana and neighbouring Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Suoraʋg bɛ yi Nandom ken River Volta la ni ka naad tembil kanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Dabagteng.
english: There is a road running west of Nandom to the River Volta ending at the village of Dabagteng.

kusaal: Mɛɛla piiga (10 mi) lɛbid Nandom dagɔbʋg baba anɛ tenkanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Hamile zin'ikanɛ ka Ghana nɛ Burkina Faso titɔdig bɛ ka customs nɛ immigration ɔfisnam bɛ.
english: Sixteen kilometres (10 mi) north of Nandom is a town called Hamile where there is a formal border between Ghana and Burkina Faso with customs and immigration offices.

kusaal: pian'asieba nwɛnɛ Wiile nɛ Ule mɛ bɛ Burkina Faso.
english: Wiile or Ule) and Malba Birifor are also spoken in Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Ba bɛdegʋ anɛ Mossi banɛ yi Burkina Faso ka da kena zin'in teŋin la yʋma kɔbisbanɛ gaad la.
english: Most of them are Mossi people from Burkina Faso who settled in the town several decades ago.

kusaal: Nandom anɛ zin'ikanɛ ka Nandom Senior High School, sakur kanɛ an Catholic school ka FIC Brothers da maal.
english: Nandom is the home of Nandom Senior High School, a Catholic school established by the FIC Brothers.

kusaal: Teŋ kan ni ka Nandom Technical School mɛ bɛ, ka FIC Brothers da pin'il.
english: The town is also home to the Nandom Technical School, also established by the FIC Brothers.

kusaal: Anne's Vocational School for girls, ka Catholic church dim da pin'il.
english: St. Anne's Vocational School for girls was established by the Catholic church.

kusaal: Andrew School, nɛ St.
english: There are also elementary schools: St. Andrew School, and St. Paul School.

kusaal: Nandom tempʋʋg nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi di dagɔbʋg, datiʋŋ, nya'aŋ nɛ tuon wʋsa anɛ Dagara nami sʋ'oe.
english: Nandom town and the multiple villages that surround it to the north, south, east, and west are inhabited by the Dagara people.

kusaal: Dagara banɛ bɛ Nandom municipal sʋ'ʋlim la ka Dagaaba bɛ Nandom ya-dagɔbʋg la yinne ethnic group yinne, la'an nɛ ban pian'ad buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔba ayi la, ba wʋsa anɛ yinne.
english: The Dagara of the Nandom municipal area and the Dagaaba to the south of Nandom are the same ethnic group, though they speak two different dialects or varieties of the same language.

kusaal: Tempʋʋs nɛ tembibis banɛ lɔ'ɔŋ southern Burkina Faso la mɛ pian'adnɛ Dagara nwɛnɛ banɛ bɛ Nandom la.
english: Many of the towns and villages across the border in southern Burkina Faso also speak the same dialect of Dagara as the people of Nandom.

kusaal: Catholic Basilica dinɛ bɛ Nandom la ba da mɛɛ dinɛ nɛ kuga ka da an pʋ'ʋskanɛ yalimi gat Kristo biis pʋ'ʋsim West Africa.
english: The Catholic Basilica in Nandom is built of stone and was once the largest Christian church in West Africa. Christian missionary activities in the area were introduced by the Catholic Missionaries of Africa (also called the White Fathers) in the 1930s.

kusaal: Catholic Missionaries of Africa (ka ba buoni ba ye White Fathers la) da pin'il Christian Mission tʋʋma yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan la ni.
english: The Catholic Basilica in Nandom is built of stone and was once the largest Christian church in West Africa. Christian missionary activities in the area were introduced by the Catholic Missionaries of Africa (also called the White Fathers) in the 1930s.

kusaal: Ba da mɛ Catholic church la nɛ kuga ka nimbanɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlimin la da sʋŋi ba mɛŋ.
english: The Catholic church was built of stone through labour provided by the native people themselves.

kusaal: Mɔɔm la bɛdegʋ yinɛ Ghana zin'is kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb bɛɛ tembanɛ kpi'e nwɛnɛ Burkina Faso.
english: The majority of Muslims are from other parts of Ghana or neighboring Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Tembibis banɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlimin la mɔri ba primary nɛ/ bɛɛ middle schools.
english: Most of the villages in the area have primary or middle schools.

kusaal: Michael's Secondary School.
english: It was formerly called St. Michael's Secondary School.

kusaal: Sakur la da pin'ilɛ yʋʋm 1968 la ni, ka di yitnɛ Friars of Immaculate conception dinɛ ka di giŋa an (FIC) la, dinɛ ka sakur biis la da an 38 ka yʋʋn nɔbigi an biis 858 nanna.
english: The school was founded in 1968 by the Friars of Immaculate conception (FIC) brothers, with an initial number of 38 students.

kusaal: Nandom Senior High School, dinɛ mɛn an NANSEC la, da paam yʋ'ʋr sʋŋ kas-kas anɛ General Certificate of Education (GCE) Ordinary and Advanced saŋa la.
english: The Nandom Senior High is a Catholic secondary school for boys, located in Nandom, in the Nandom district of the Upper West Region in Ghana.

kusaal: Sakur la yʋ'ʋr da dɛŋin buonɛ yɛ St.
english: It was formerly called St. Michael's Secondary School.

kusaal: Nania FC bɛnɛ Legon kologi tita'ar la, ka zamisidi ba bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb lammɛ ban maan lɔya maalʋg zin'ikanɛ li'el nɛ rugby bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb zin'igin la, ba buon zin'ikan ye Legon lɔya maalʋg zin'ig, ka li bɛ Accra Ghana kpɛla.
english: Nania FC is located at the Legon University ground, the club trains near the Legon car maintenance which is adjacent to the rugby stadium, the field is known as Legon Maintenance Park Accra Ghana.

kusaal: Maha Ayew onɛ an Abedi Pele kanɛ an Nania FC kpɛɛm la da gban'e Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb lʋgʋr la nɛ Kwesi Nyantakyi onɛ aan ba tuongat la, nɛ Amadu Tanko nɛ Justice Anim Yeboah banɛ an FA kpɛɛmnam kanɛ gɔsid wada nɛ tʋbtɛɛgir nu'ug-nwɛ'ɛb yɛla la tuongatib la, ye kootʋ gu'um FA ka ba da wʋm bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb yɛlkanɛ bɛ on bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib la nɛ Okwawu United dim laa.
english: Maha Ayew, wife of Abedi Pele, who is a director and a shareholder of Nania FC sued the Ghana Football Association as well as its President, Kwesi Nyantakyi, the chairmen of the Disciplinary and Appeals Committee of the FA – Amadu Tanko and Justice Anim Yeboah respectively, asking the court to restrain the FA from rehearing the alleged match of convenience case between her club and Okwawu United.

kusaal: Ba nya'adnɛ Division One League bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb la.
english: They are competing in the Division One League.

kusaal: Tuogatib yɛl ye nidib atan' nwa; Kwesi Nyantakyi, Amadu Tanko nɛ Justice Anim Yeboah da tʋmmi ba tʋʋma ka li pʋ nar ye ba saminɛ ba bɛ ba mɛŋ tʋʋma nii.
english: The ruling stated that the three persons – Kwesi Nyantakyi, Amadu Tanko and Justice Anim Yeboah acted in their official capacity and that they couldn't have been sued in their private capacities.

kusaal: Ba da tis nidib atan' nwa sɔ' mɛkama nɛ miliyɔn anii-nii Maha Ayew n maal dama'am zɛrigi ba la, ka nɔk miliyɔŋ yinne tis Nania FC.
english: A cost of 800 GH cedis each was awarded against Maha Ayew for the three correspondents while a 1,000 GH cedi cost was slapped on Nania FC.

kusaal: Amaa saria kat kanɛ da gɔsid yɛlkan la da yɛl ye a-maligim vɛɛns gɔs wada kʋ tʋm bɛ FA nii, bɔzugɔ vɛɛnsʋg kan tʋmmɛ gɔmma tʋʋmlʋga ni kae a-sʋ'oe-m-mɛŋ tʋʋma ni wʋʋ FA laa.
english: But the sitting judge in dismissing the suit explained that an application for judicial review cannot apply to the FA, stating that such applications are applicable to public bodies and not private bodies like FA.

kusaal: Ba da nye wala bama buudi yʋ'ʋr Capsicum yit na'asaanam pian'ʋk kanɛ buon Greek bɛ Latin sɔbʋg capto dinɛ pa'an "to grasp,seize "nɛ li pa'an li wala la tɔi siem ,la mɛ lɛn pa'al ye yʋ'ʋr la yitnɛ Latin sɔbʋg capsa "box" pa'an wala la an siem ba buudi la ni.
english: The genus name Capsicum derives from a Greek-based derivative of the Latin word capto, meaning 'to grasp, to seize', in reference to the heat or pungency of the species' fruit, although it has also been speculated to derive from the Latin word capsa, 'box', referring to the shape of the fruit in forms of the typical species.

kusaal: Nɛ wɛla Nanzʋ'ʋs kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb yʋ'ʋr annuum gbin anɛ "annual" (bɛ Latin annus , "yʋʋm"), tiig la ka'a nɛ lin bɛ saŋa si'a amaa ma'asuŋ zin'ig ni.
english: Although the species name annuum means 'annual' (from the Latin annus, 'year'), the plant is not an annual but is frost tender.

kusaal: Tituunli yinne anɛ mɔɔgʋn chiltepin, dinɛ pɛ'ɛl Northern Peru hali ka widigi paae Southwestern United States.
english: One example of this is the wild chiltepin, which has a massive range of habitat from Northern Peru to Southwestern United States.

kusaal: Nanzʋ'ʋbanɛ ka ba bʋd zin'ig la vɛnlim zug sieba anɛ U.S. National Arboretum's "Black Pearl" nɛ "Bolivian Rainbow".
english: Some cultivars grown specifically for their aesthetic value include the U.S. National Arboretum's "Black Pearl".

kusaal: Ba da fasigi tɛ'ɛns ye spicy fruits anɛ buudi yine nɛ black pepper plant , kanɛ mɛ mɔr spicy fruit.
english: They mistakenly thought the spicy fruits were a variety of the black pepper plant, which also has spicy fruit.

kusaal: Amaa tiig wala pʋ mɔr kpɛnim biɛla.Yʋ'ʋr banɛ ka ti mɔr buon Capsicum annuum wala bɛ na'asaalin bɛnɛ kɔ'ɔnb-kɔn'ɔnb dɔlisid yit zi'isi'a nɛ li buudi.
english: Commonly used names for the fruit of Capsicum annuum in English vary by location and cultivar.

kusaal: Ba bɛdim, masim kɔ'ɔb -kɔ'ɔb bɛ Australia nɛ New Zealand.
english: The larger, sweeter cultivars are called "capsicum" in Australia and New Zealand.

kusaal: Great Britain nɛ Ireland, tiwala ba ma kuodib la'asid sɔnsid bɛ la'aŋ nam ni ye ba baŋ wala la "malisim " bɛɛ "tɔi/chilli" peppers, li pʋ taa tisid ba yʋ'ʋr kim nɛ.Canada nɛ United States an zi'ig kanɛ ka ba kuodi ba buudi buudi wɛn wuu "bell", "jalapeño", "cayenne", or "bird's eye" peppers, ka li mɔr giŋgaŋ bɛ fʋ ya'a lɛm di bʋn malisima nɛ dinɛ tɔi.
english: In Canada and the United States it is commonplace to provide the cultivar in most instances, for example "bell", "jalapeño", "cayenne", or "bird's eye" peppers, to convey differences in taste including sweetness or pungency.

kusaal: Nanzʋ'ʋs puum ɛɛnti mɔr petal nɛ sepal nam ayuobʋ bɛɛ ayɔpɔi, Stamen nam ayɔpɔi, ka mɔr ovary kanɛ ya'ae style yinne zugin, ka di mɔr.
english: Flowers of Capsicum annuum generally consist of 6–7 petals and sepals, have 7 stamens, and contain an ovary that is superior to a single style consisting of 2–3 carpels and a single stamen.

kusaal: Pʋʋm la nii, luos bɛdegʋ bɛ gɔsid wiakir (du'am) yɛla, ka dɔl pollination nɛ fertilization, banɛ kpin taaba ayi' la anɛ anther nam nɛ ovary.
english: Within the flowers there are several reproductive structures that are used in pollination and fertilization, the two relative include the anthers and the ovary.

kusaal: Anther nam anɛ daʋ luakanɛ yisid microgametes dinɛ na la'as nɛ megagamete dinɛ bɛ pʋ'a la ovary ni la, ka ba ya'a la'as taaba di na kilim propagule (wal).
english: Anthers are the male organ producing the microgametes (pollen) that will disperse to fertilize the megagamete that is located in the ovary of the female reproductive organ, leading to the development of the propagule (fruit).

kusaal: Ba sieba anɛ Whiteflies nɛ aphids.
english: Some can harbor viruses deadly to the species, these include whiteflies and aphids.

kusaal: Bʋn-ian'ad banɛ daamid nanzʋ'ʋs tiig la sieba anɛ tobacco budworms nɛ thrips.
english: Other pests that can cause damage to the plants are the tobacco budworms and thrips.

kusaal: Ban'as banɛ gban'ad nanzʋ'ʋs anɛ bama bi'ela phytophthora blight, anthracnose, phytophthora root nɛ gbin la na pun'od.
english: Diseases include phytophthora blight, anthracnose, phytophthora root and basal rot.

kusaal: Bʋn-ian'ad kanɛ mɛ mɔr la'asan'aŋ bɛdegʋ anɛ weevil, di bʋmbibis ɛɛnti daam nanzʋ'ʋs la sankanɛ ka ba maan puum bɛɛ ba pin'in wala maalʋg, ka na nyaŋi kɛ ka di sie din naan dʋ'an si'em la yi kɔbiga pʋʋgʋn lɛbis piswai (90%).
english: Another pest which is quite vicious is a weevil (Anthonomus eugenii Cano) which the larva of this pest affects the plants during the flowering and fruiting stages of its life, and can reduce its production rate by up to 90%.

kusaal: Wal la na nɔbʋgʋ paae o bɛn ka yʋ'ʋn ti'ebi gur ye pak la pik ka biili la yina widig.
english: The fruit grows to maturity, then is ready for dispersal of its seeds.

kusaal: Naser Toure Mahama (March 17, 1965) anɛ Ghana ninkanɛ nwɛ'ɛd pɔlitis ka an wadmaani paas Ghana wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la ka zi'eni tis Ayawaso East n bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Naser Toure Mahama (17 March 1965 – 4 January 2026) was a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Ayawaso East Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Nima-Ankara, tenkanɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region, Ghana.
english: He hailed from Nima, a town in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ West Africa Senior High School.
english: He went to the West Africa Senior High School.

kusaal: Ka tɔlisi keŋ Central University College n bɛ Ghana ka di'e o Bachelor of Science degree in marketing kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi (1987).
english: He entered Central University College, Ghana and obtained his Bachelor of Science degree in marketing in 1987.

kusaal: Mahama anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid (NDC).
english: Mahama was a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: O anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid (NDC).
english: Mahama was a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Ba da du'a Mahama nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu nwadis atan' la ni dabpiinɛ ayɔpɔi daar (March 17, 1965).
english: Mahama was born on 17 March 1965.

kusaal: O da lɛn tʋm OTA Forex Bureau, n bɛ Ankara (2001-2003)
english: OTA Forex Bureau, Accra (2001–2003)

kusaal: Nathaniel Azarco Welbeck yʋʋma pin'ilʋg lin yʋʋma (1915–1972) O da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka mɛ da lɛn an onɛ zi'e ti Ghana nɔba zug teŋ sieba ni.
english: Nathaniel Azarco Welbeck (1915–1972) was a Ghanaian politician and a diplomat.

kusaal: O da anɛ Convention People's Party la na'adɔɔg nid ka da an minister of state n da bɛ yiiga republic la ni.
english: He was a member of the Convention People's Party and minister of state in the first republic.

kusaal: Onɛ da an resident minister tis Ghana n bɛ Guinea nɛ resident minister ya'as tis Ghana bɛ Congo.
english: He was briefly resident minister of Ghana in Guinea and also resident minister of Ghana in the Republic of the Congo (Léopoldville).

kusaal: Ba da du'a Welbeck nɛ bɛ Cape Coast Senlʋŋ nwadig la dabisim piisi nɛ anu la yʋʋma 1915 la ni, o du'adib anɛ Madam Adwoa Twi nɛ Nomo Welbeck banɛ da yii lɛb Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire teŋin la.
english: Welbeck was born at Cape Coast on 25 September 1915 to Madam Adwoa Twi and Nomo Welbeck who migrated to Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.

kusaal: O saam da anɛ Ewe nid ka o tʋŋ lɛɛ yi Ga dim buudi ni ka o ma mɛ da anɛ Fanti, dinzugɔ, Welbeck da anɛ Fanti, Ga ka lɛn an Ewe dim ya'as, wʋʋ Fanti an Akan dim buudi ka ba malima sieba an ma faar diib la ka fʋ ma yidim mɛ su'oe fʋ la, Welbeck da anɛ Fanti yi Cape Coast.
english: His father was of Ewe and Ga descent and his mother was Fanti, Welbeck identified as a Fanti, a Ga and also an Ewe however, due to Akan (of which Fantis constitute) customs and tradition which places more emphasis on one's maternal background, Welbeck was a Fanti from Cape Coast.

kusaal: French pian'ad da an pian'akanɛ ka ba mɔri zamisidi bɛ sakurin sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni, li da ti kena ka Welbeck mi'i French pian'ad la hali tituaa.
english: The French language being the medium of communication in schools in the area, Welbeck became well versed in the French language.

kusaal: O da keŋ sakur nam bɛdigʋ naae ka di'e kasɛta gbana yʋʋma 1932 la ni ka kpɛn' Wesley College la ni yʋʋma 1933 la ni zamis linɛ an pa'an zamisʋg.
english: He sat for his standard seven school leaving certificate in 1932 and entered Wesley College in 1933 to train as a teacher.

kusaal: O da anɛ pa'an yʋʋma 1936 la ni.
english: He qualified as a teacher in 1936.

kusaal: O da pa'an n bɛ zi'is kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb, sakur kanɛ ni ka o da pa'al ka pʋ lɛn pa'al ya'as la da anɛ Takoradi Methodist Sakur la ni.
english: He taught in many institutions, the last school he was posted to before he brought his teaching career to a close was Takoradi Methodist School.

kusaal: O da nɔki o mɛŋi paas nɛ na'adɔɔg linɛ da yɔ'ɔg paalim ka li yʋ'ʋr buon United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC); na'adɔɔg nwa mɛŋim da yɔ'ɔgi sʋŋ mɔr Gold Coast keŋi afaae mɛŋ ni na la.Yʋʋma 1949 la ni ka ba da gaŋ o ye o an gbaʋŋ sɔbid n tis Local Education kpɛɛmnam la.
english: In 1949 he was appointed the secretary to the Local Education Committee.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da bas UGCC ka keŋ yɔ'ɔg na'adɔɔg linɛ an Convention People's Party (CPP) Sigir nwadig dabisim piina ayi la yʋʋma 1949 la ni ka Welbeck da la'al na'adɔɔg la daa kan noo n an nid yinne banɛ si'iŋi li.
english: Kwame Nkrumah left the UGCC to form the Convention People's Party(CPP) on 12 June 1949 and Welbeck joined the party that same day as one of its founding members.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 1951 la ni ka CPP na'adɔɔg la da gaŋ o ye o aan ba gbaʋŋ sɔbid.
english: In 1951 he was appointed the national propaganda secretary for the CPP.

kusaal: Kwesi Plange kum la nya'aŋ yʋʋma 1953 la ni ka o na'adɔɔg CPP la da gaŋ o ye o an ye o zi'enɛ nya'a na'am ba teŋin linɛ an Cape Coast municipal n zi'enɛ an legislative assembul la.
english: After the death of Kwesi Plange in 1953 he was selected by his party the CPP to stand elections in his home town Cape Coast as a municipal member of the legislative assembly.

kusaal: On nɛ Amponsah Dadzie onɛ da an United Party na'adɔɔg nid la da la'asi nya Cape Coast kʋk la.
english: He contested for the Cape Coast seat with Amponsah Dadzie of the United Party.

kusaal: Cape Coast Vɔt la ba da lɛm maligim gban'e dabisir n vɔt yʋʋma 1954 ni la ka ban da lɛn vɔt la ka Welbeck di ka pian'ad la pʋ lɛn keŋ Kɔtɔ ni ya'asɛ.
english: The general elections for Cape Coast was rescheduled for 1954 and this time Welbeck was elected and he kept the seat without any court proceedings.

kusaal: O da kpɛn' tʋʋma dɔɔgin la nɛ yʋʋma 1956 la ni ka yʋʋma 1958 la ni ka ba da gaŋ o ye o an minista n zi'en Ghana nɔba zug n bɛ Guinea la.
english: He was elected in office in 1956 and in 1958 he was appointed a resident minister to Guinea.

kusaal: Yʋʋma 1960 la ni ka ba da lɛn vɔt ka o di kʋk la n kpɛn bɛ wadmaanib yir la ka ba da lɛn gaŋ o ye o an minister of state for Defence.
english: In 1960 he was retained in parliament and appointed minister of state for Defence.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan mɛŋim ni ya'as ka ba da gaŋ o Minister Plenipotentiary nɛ minista kanɛ na zi'en ti Ghana nɔba zug n bɛ Congo.
english: That same year he was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary and Ambassador Extraordinary posted to Congo as resident minister representing Ghana.

kusaal: O da yii anina lɛb Ghana na yʋʋma 1960 Sapal nwadig la ni dɔlis nɛ zaba nam banɛ da naam Congo la sogianam Patrice Lumumba da duoe zabid nɛ gɔmina la Mobutu win la.
english: He was returned to Ghana in November 1960 after his residence was besieged by the Congo military for allegedly plotting with the then deposed Patrice Lumumba against Mobutu's regime.

kusaal: Senlʋŋ nwadig la ni yʋʋma 1962 la ni, ka o da an gbaʋŋ sɔbidi tis CPP na'adɔɔg ka li yinɛ ban da yis Hugh Horatio Coffie Crabbe la.
english: In September 1962, he became acting executive secretary of the CPP due to Hugh Horatio Coffie Crabbe's detention.

kusaal: O da anɛ Philip Quaque linɛ bɛ Cape Coast la yaaŋ.
english: He was the great grandson of Philip Quaque of Cape Coast.

kusaal: Yiiga o di pu'a ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Sarah Andrews ka ba du'a bipʋŋ yinne.
english: He first married Ms. Sarah Andrews and they had a daughter together.

kusaal: Ba da zi'ini lin da yi yʋʋma 1942 ti 1950 la ni ka bas taaba.
english: The marriage lasted from 1942 to 1950.

kusaal: Ka o tɔɔm di Esther Quarm yʋʋma 1954 la ni.
english: He married Ms. Esther Quarm in 1954.

kusaal: Bugum da laŋ yir ka li ta'asi o saam kum n bɛ Abidjan zi'ikanɛ ka buudi da bɛ la.
english: His father died in a house fire at Abidjan where the family resided.

kusaal: Welbeck da pɔɔdnɛ hali nɛ on da na baŋ o saam.
english: Welbeck was too young to know his father.

kusaal: Welbeck da pin'ili o sakuri bɛ Abidjan.
english: Welbeck had his early education at a school in Abidjan.

kusaal: Ka Welbeck ma da ti gban'e ye o na kɛ ka Welbeck kuli o teŋin linɛ an Gold Coast la n kuli bɛ nɛ o saam nam buudi la o saam yinne; Mr.
english: Welbeck's mother decided to send Welbeck to his native Gold Coast to stay with his paternal uncle; Mr. Joseph Mensah Attabrah.

kusaal: Onɛ o buudi la da la'asi bɛnɛ Swedru zi'ikanɛ ka o da tɔlisi kennɛ o sakur la, amaa saŋkan yu'un da anɛ na'asaal zamisʋg.
english: He lived with his family in Swedru where he continued schooling, this time in the English Language.

kusaal: Yʋʋma sieba nya'aŋ, ka ba da gban'a o n dɔl nɛ Nkrumah da pian'a si'el ye "ba na duoe tawai linɛ dɔl suor ka ziim ka' li pʋʋgin la." Ba da gban'a o nwɛ'ɛd o sam ka yɔ o wʋʋ nwadis piina ayi pʋʋgin.
english: A year later, he was arrested during an unrest which followed Nkrumah's declaration of "Positive Action Without Violence." He was tried and charged with sedition leading to his 12-month incarceration.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o an gbaʋŋ sɔbid n tis na'adɔɔg la nɛ yʋʋma 1963 la ni amaa ka Nkrumah lɛɛ aan wʋsa-wʋsawas gbaʋŋ sɔbid.
english: He was appointed Executive Secretary of the party in 1963 while Nkrumah was the general secretary.

kusaal: Welbeck da nɔŋ si'el anɛ lawn tennis nɛ stamps.
english: Welbeck's hobbies included lawn tennis and stamps collection.

kusaal: Welbeck da kpinɛ yʋʋma 1972 la ni wiim n da daam o hali pamm la nya'aŋ.
english: Welbeck died in 1972 after a protracted illness.

kusaal: O da kpɛn' pɔlitis ni naae ka naan bas pa'alʋg la.
english: He entered politics before quitting the teaching profession.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan noo ni ka ba da gaŋ o ye o an minista gɔsid tʋʋma nam yɛla.
english: That same year he was appointed minister for works.

kusaal: Ka o lɛn lɛbi kpɛn' bugum la ni ye o yis biig yinne ya'as, ka o yis biig la tud takɔrɔ ni ka o yi amaa on naae la ka bugum la nyaŋi o ka o ia suor ye o yii gʋ'ʋŋ ka kpi.
english: He then went back to the flaming house to rescue another child by throwing it out of the window into safety but he was overcome by the flames and could not find the door to get out of the burning house.

kusaal: Ban da maal Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC), dinɛ da bɛ Ghana ka sooginam da maal coup d'état yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne nwadis piinɛ yi' la dabpistan nɛ yinne daar (31 December 1981), mugusʋg da bɛ na'asaanamin ye ba mɔr wada suori lɛb Ghana na.
english: Following the formation of the Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC), which ruled Ghana following the military coup d'état on 31 December 1981, there was pressure from the international community to restore democracy.

kusaal: NDC paasnɛ Progressive Alliance nɛ Socialist International.
english: The party colors are red, white, green, and black, with the party slogan or motto as "Unity, stability, and development." Internationally, the NDC is a member of the Progressive Alliance and Socialist International.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadis piinɛ ayi daba awai daar, (9 December 2012), ka Electoral Commission of Ghana da yɛl ye NDC na'anya'ad John Dramani Mahama an onɛ di zuraan na'anya'ab la nɛ vɔɔt pisnu du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.7%).
english: On 9 December 2012, the Electoral Commission of Ghana declared NDC candidate John Mahama to be president-elect after a hotly contested race in which he won 50.7% of the votes cast.

kusaal: John Atta Mills da an zuraan na'anya'adi tis National Democratic Congress ban da gaans nidib ka ba vɔɔt Ho bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: John Atta Mills became the presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress at a special delegate congress held in Ho in the Volta Region.

kusaal: Zuraan nya'andɔl John Atta Mills da li yʋʋm tusa ayi (2000) vɔɔt la tis Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid, John Kufour ban da vɔɔt nɔɔr ayi la.
english: Vice-president John Atta Mills lost in 2000 to the New Patriotic Party's John Kufuor after two rounds of voting.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi vʋʋtʋg la ni (2004 elections) na'adɔɔg la nɔɔr ku'om dinɛ da an "A Better Ghana".
english: In the 2004 elections, the party's manifesto called for "A Better Ghana".

kusaal: John Atta Mills da lɛn nya' ya'as yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi vɔɔtʋgin la (2004) ka Alhaji Muhammad Mumuni da an o nya'andɔl.
english: John Atta Mills ran again for the NDC in the 2004 presidential elections with his running mate Muhammad Mumuni.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt pisnaasi nɛ naasi du'ali ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (44.6%) vɔɔt la wʋsa ni, amaa o da lii tis New Patriotic Party.
english: He won 44.6% of the vote, but lost to the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yuobʋ nwadis piinɛ yi' dabpisi nɛ yinne daar (21 December 2006), ba da vɔɔt Mills ye zi'en ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nɔba zugʋ nya' 2008 presidential election nɛ vɔɔt pisnii nɛ yinne du'ali anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (81.4%), bɛɛt vɔɔt tusir yinne, kɔbistan' nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yi' (1,362).
english: On 21 December 2006, Mills was overwhelmingly elected by the NDC as its candidate for the 2008 presidential election with a majority of 81.4%, or 1,362 votes.

kusaal: Ekwow Spio-Garbrah da ti'al ayi nɛ vɔɔt anii du'al ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (8.7%) (dinɛ an vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yuobʋ (146), Alhaji Mahama Iddrisu da paasi atan' daan nɛ vɔɔt anii du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (8.2%) (vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ pistan' nɛ yɔpɔi(137)), nɛ Eddie Annan onɛ da paasi anaasi nɛ vɔɔt yinne du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.7%) (vɔɔt pisi nɛ nii (28)).
english: Ekwow Spio-Garbrah was second with 8.7% (146 votes), Mahama Iddrisu was third with 8.2% (137 votes), and Edward Annan was fourth with 1.7% (28 votes).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii nwadisa anaasi la ni (April 2008), ba da gaŋ John Mahama ye o an zuraan nya'adɔli tis na'adɔɔg la.
english: In April 2008, John Mahama was chosen as the party's vice-presidential candidate.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba atan' daar, (3 January 2009), ba da tis nɔɔr ye Mills di ban da lɛm maligim vɔɔt yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi dabpisi nɛ anii daar la (28 December 2008) ka o da lieb Ghana Zuraan.
english: On 3 January 2009, Mills was certified as the victor of the 28 December 2008 run-off election and became the next president of Ghana.

kusaal: Zuraan John Atta Mills da lu ban'a ka maal ka'alim, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar nintaŋ (24 July 2012) on da bɛ o ɔfisin la.
english: President John Atta Mills died, after a short illness, in the afternoon of 24 July 2012 while still in office.

kusaal: NDC dim da nɔk John Dramani Mahama ye o aan ba Zuraan na'anya'ad nɛ Paa Kwesi Amissah-Arthur ye o aan o Zuraan nya'andɔl yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yi' vɔɔtʋgin (2012 elections) la.
english: The NDC picked Mahama for their presidential candidate and sitting vice president Paa Kwesi Amissah-Arthur as their vice-presidential candidate for the 2012 elections.

kusaal: Katti wa'ae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋg la (2020 elections), February 2019, ba da siak ye John Dramani Mahama na an National Democratic Congress zuraan na'anya'ad ye o nya' 2020 vɔɔtʋg la, Nana Akufo-Addo onɛ da dɛŋim zin'i kʋk la zug da diya ka bas Mahama 2016 vɔɔtʋgin la, dɔlisid on da yɛl ye teŋ la lɛbidnɛ nya'aŋ ka di yinɛ sanlima, kooko nɛ kpaam ligidi sied la.
english: In February 2019, John Mahama was confirmed as the candidate of the opposition National Democratic Congress to contest in the 2020 elections, the incumbent president Nana Akufo-Addo who unseated Mahama in a 2016 election, capitalizing on an economy that was slowing due to falling prices for gold, oil and cocoa exports.

kusaal: O da di National Democratic Congress primaries la nɛ vɔɔt tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnii nɛ yɔpɔi (213,487) dinɛ zi'eni tis vɔɔt piswai nɛ anu du'al pisi nɛ tan' kɔbiga pʋʋgi (95.23%) ka basi o taaba ayuobʋ banɛ kpɛlim la ka ba nɔk vɔɔt anaasi kɔbiga pʋʋgin la pʋdʋg.
english: He won the National Democratic Congress primaries by securing an overwhelming 213,487 votes representing 95.23 percent of the total valid votes cast with the other six contenders managing with about 4 percent of the votes.

kusaal: 25 June 2020 NDC ka Asiedu Nketiah onɛ aan di gbaʋŋ sɔbid la, da keŋ Supreme Court of Ghana na'anɔɔg la yɛla ka pʋ di bʋʋdɛ on da mɔɔd ye o kɛ ka ba vɔɔt gbaʋŋ kʋda paas Electoral Commission da maan Vɔɔt gbampaala la.
english: On 25 June 2020 the NDC led by its General Secretary Asiedu Nketiah, lost a case in the Supreme Court of Ghana in which the party had sought to achieve the inclusion of old Voter ID cards in the Electoral Commission's compilation of a New Voter's Register, among other reliefs.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋgin la (2020 elections), nidib piinɛ anii (18 members) da mɔɔd ye ba zi'eni ba kɔn'ɔ kɔn' nya' ka bay is na'adɔɔgin la.
english: In the 2020 elections, 18 members of the party who sought to run as independent candidates lost their membership.

kusaal: · Mills government (2009–2012)
english: Mills government (2009–2012)

kusaal: National Democratic Congress da maali ba national delegates conference nɛ 17–19 November Ghana International Trade Fair Centre, La, Accra.
english: The National Democratic Congress held its national delegates conference on 17–19 November at the Ghana International Trade Fair Centre, La, Accra.

kusaal: NDC gban'e ye ba nɔk yʋ'ʋŋ yinne tien J J Rawlings yɛla, onɛ da pin'il na'adɔɔg la da maal ka'ailnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadis piinɛ yinne la dabpiinɛ yi' daar (12 November 2020) Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital.
english: The NDC decided to hold a vigil in memory of JJ Rawlings, the founder of the party who died on 12 November 2020 at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital.

kusaal: National Democratic Congress (NDC) anɛ na'adɔɔg kanɛ bɛ Ghana ka ti buon ye Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg ka Jerry Rawlings da pin'ili di, ka da lieb Zuraani tis Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne la ni (1981) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ tan' (1993) ka da lɛn an Zuraani tis Ghana din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ tan la ni (1993) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne la ni (2001).
english: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) is a social democratic political party in Ghana, founded by Jerry Rawlings, who was Head of State from 1981 to 1993.

kusaal: Ba da maal NDC ka di an na'adɔkanɛ bɛ kʋk zug yʋʋm tuir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) vɔɔtʋg la, ka ba da vɔɔti Rawlings ka o lieb Zuraan ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1996) ba da lɛn vɔɔt Rawlings ka o an Ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, NDC na'anya'ad.
english: The NDC was formed as the ruling party ahead of elections in 1992, in which Rawlings was elected president, and in 1996 Rawlings was re-elected as the NDC candidate.

kusaal: Ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la, NDC da li yʋʋm tusir vɔɔtʋgin la (2000 election) ka pʋ lɛm paam ya'asɛ ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii vɔɔtʋgin la (2008 election), ka ba da lɛn di'e kpɛŋ la ka John Atta Mills ka an ba na'anya'ad.
english: The NDC lost the presidency in the 2000 election, and it was not until the 2008 election, that they regained it with John Atta Mills as its candidate.

kusaal: Jerry Rawlings onɛ da an zuraan 1981 soogianami da an zuraan nam la, da pin'il National Democratic Congress.
english: The National Democratic Congress was founded by Jerry Rawlings, who had been the military leader of Ghana since 1981.

kusaal: NDC da di yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ (1996) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: The NDC won the 1992 and 1996 elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir vɔɔtʋg la (2000 election) da an yiiga zuraannam vɔɔtʋg din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la (1992) ka na'akanɛ zin'i kʋk la zug pʋ lɛn yi vɔɔt gbaʋŋʋnɛ.
english: The 2000 election was the first presidential election since 1992 that an incumbent president was not on the ballot.

kusaal: Jerry Rawlings' yʋʋma anii kʋk la zug naaeya nwɛnɛ Ghana wada gbaʋŋ la yɛl si'em la.
english: Jerry Rawlings' eight-year tenure had expired as per the Constitution of Ghana.

kusaal: Vɔɔtkanɛ ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi nwadis piinɛ ayi' daba yɔpɔi daar la (7 December 2004), na'adɔɔg la da di kʋgʋs piswai nɛ anaasi (94) ma'aa yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan (230) pʋʋgin.
english: In the general elections held on 7 December 2004, the party won only 94 of the 230 seats.

kusaal: Ba da zuŋ Zuraan nya'andɔl John Dramani Mahama onɛ bɛ NDC la daakan zaam ye o lieb Zuraan.
english: Vice President John Mahama of the NDC was sworn in as president that evening.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu nwadis piinɛ yi' la (November 2015) on da paam vɔɔt miliyɔŋ yinne, tusa kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ wai, kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ nii (1,199 118) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa an miliyɔŋ yinne, tusa kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnii nɛ yuobʋ, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisi nɛ nii (1, 286, 728) dinɛ zɛmnɛ piswai nɛ nu du'al piiga kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (95.10%) o na'adɔɔg zuraan nya'abin la.
english: In November 2015 after securing an overwhelming 1,199,118 out of a total of 1,286,728 votes representing 95.10% party members in the presidential primaries, President John Mahama was endorsed to lead the NDC in the 2016 general elections.

kusaal: Ba da bas Zuraan John Dramani Mahama suor ye o gaad NDC tuon yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ vɔɔtʋg la ni (2016 general elections).
english: In November 2015 after securing an overwhelming 1,199,118 out of a total of 1,286,728 votes representing 95.10% party members in the presidential primaries, President John Mahama was endorsed to lead the NDC in the 2016 general elections.

kusaal: NDC da pin'ili paae zina, di mɔr gɔmena nam atan, ayi la dɔlisnɛ vɔɔtʋg ka yinne la mɛ dɔlis Zuraan Mills kum la yɛla.
english: Since the NDC was formed, it has formed two governments following elections, and a third following the death of President Mills.

kusaal: · Rawlings government (1993–2001)
english: Rawlings government (1993–2001)

kusaal: · Mahama government (2012–2017)
english: Mills government (2009–2012)

kusaal: National Democratic Congress gaansidi ba tuongatibnɛ yʋma anaasi wʋsa.
english: The National Democratic Congress holds elections every four years to elect its national executives.

kusaal: University of Media, Arts and Communication- Institute of Film and Television (UniMAC-IFT) (ka ba da buon National Film and Television Institute (NAFTI)) anɛ sakur kanɛ bɛ Accra, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The University of Media, Arts and Communication- Institute of Film and Television (UniMAC-IFT) (formerly the National Film and Television Institute (NAFTI)) is an educational institution in Accra, Ghana.
en_article: University of Media, Arts and Communication- Institute of Film and Television

kusaal: Ghana gɔmɛna da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (yʋʋma pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi banɛ gaad) ka li an kpɛɛmnam sakur ka pa'an sini maalig nɛ TV ni pian'ad.
english: It was established in 1978 (1978) by the Government of Ghana as a public institution of higher education in film and television production.
en_article: University of Media, Arts and Communication- Institute of Film and Television

kusaal: Lin da pin'il sa, sakur la kpɛlim pa'an sini maalig zamisig nɛ TV pian'ad zamisig, ka la'asi ba mɛŋ nɛ University of Ghana.
english: Since its inception, the institute has offered professional and academic education in film and television education, in affiliation with the University of Ghana.
en_article: University of Media, Arts and Communication- Institute of Film and Television

kusaal: Ba da yis labaar yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, Vaala nwadig la ni, ye ba na ti'ak sakur la ka li lieb media and creative arts university college.
english: It was announced in April 2016 that in the next few years, the institute will be converted into a media and creative arts university college.
en_article: University of Media, Arts and Communication- Institute of Film and Television

kusaal: National House of Chiefs anɛ gɔmena lʋgʋr kanɛ mɔr paŋ Ghana kpɛla ka la'asid banɛ an buudi kpɛɛmnam, na'anam nɛ na'atitada.
english: The National House of Chiefs is the highest body in Ghana that unites all traditional rulers, chiefs and kings.

kusaal: African-American pʋ'ʋsim tuon gat Ra Un Nefer Amen,da zi'en U.S. na'anam nɔba zug ban da maal la'asʋg.
english: The African-American religious leader Ra Un Nefer Amen, for example, serves as the U.S. representative of the chiefs in congress assembled.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr la mɔr kpi'eŋʋ yi Ghana wada gbaʋŋ la ni tʋmmi di tʋʋma.
english: The institution has backing from the Constitution of Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana buudinam kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb nɛ buudi tuongatib la'asi paas regional houses of chiefs kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb.
english: The various rulers of Ghana's numerous tribes and clans automatically become members of a number of regional houses of chiefs.

kusaal: Ban paas regional houses of chiefs ni la tisi ba suor ka ba paas national house of chiefs ni.
english: The various rulers of Ghana's numerous tribes and clans automatically become members of a number of regional houses of chiefs.

kusaal: Banɛ paas na'abama anɛ, pʋ'ana'nam banɛ ka national house la gaans ye ba paasi la'asi tʋm.
english: In addition to these chiefs, a number of queen mothers are also appointed to the national house as associate members.

kusaal: La'anɛ national nɛ regional houses an Ghana nidib gad la, ba mɔr kpininim nɛ tensieba dim.
english: Although the national and regional houses are dominated by citizens of Ghana, they are affiliated with a number of foreign nationals.

kusaal: Tʋʋmkaŋa sin'iŋnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (1969) la ni.
english: The practice first started in 1969.

kusaal: Ba gaansid kpɛɛmbama ka ba tʋmnɛ yʋma anaasi bɛn ka mɔr suor ye ba lɛn gaŋi ba yʋma anaasi la nya'aŋ.
english: These titleholders are appointed for four-year terms, and are eligible for re-appointment thereafter.

kusaal: National Reform Party anɛ pɔlitis na'adɔɔg Ghana.
english: The National Reform Party is a political party in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili dinɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999) la ni dɔlisid nimbanɛ da buaki yi Ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) ni.
english: It was founded in 1999 by a splinter group from the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Onɛ da aan di zuraan na'anya'ad, Augustus Obuadum Tanoh ("Goosie" Tanoh) da paam vɔɔt yinne du'al yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.1%) yi zuraan vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: Its presidential candidate Augustus Obuadum Tanoh ("Goosie" Tanoh) had 1.1% of the presidential vote.

kusaal: Onɛ da aan o nya'adɔl anɛ Fetus Kosiba.
english: His running mate was Fetus Kosiba.

kusaal: Onɛ an kʋkdaan nɛ na'adɔɔ la kpɛɛm anɛ Peter Kpordugbe, onɛ an head of the National Service Secretariat kʋdʋg ka da bɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg, NDC ni.
english: The chairman and leader of the party is Peter Kpordugbe, former head of the National Service Secretariat and a former member of the NDC.

kusaal: Na'adɔɔg la pian'akpan anɛ "Ghana first", Ghana yiiga.
english: The party's motto is "Ghana first".

kusaal: Di gbaʋŋ sɔbid, gbaʋŋ sɔbid anɛ Kyeretwie Opoku.
english: The general secretary is Kyeretwie Opoku.

kusaal: National Sports College Winneba anɛ gbaʋŋ zamisʋg zin'ikanɛ zamisid ninwisigir yɛla Ghana.
english: National Sports College Winneba is an educational institution for sports in Ghana.

kusaal: Di bɛnɛ Winneba bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: It is located at Winneba in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: National Sports College Winneba da pin'inɛ yʋʋmtusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1984) dɔlisid yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (1976) SMC Decree number 54, ka PNDC Law da tiaki di.
english: The National Sports College Winneba was established in 1984 by the 1976 SMC Decree number 54, and amended by the PNDC Law.

kusaal: Dinɛ mɔr Navrongo Solar Power Station, Ghana yiiga solar plant.
english: It houses the Navrongo Solar Power Station, Ghana's first solar plant.

kusaal: Navrongo bɛnɛ 10°53'5″N 1°5'25″W. Navrongo nidib kanli bɛ 2005 da anɛ wʋʋ 25,470 ka 2012 nidib kanl mɛn an wʋʋ 27,306.
english: Navrongo's population in 2005 was estimated to be 25,470, and in 2012 was estimated to be 27,306.

kusaal: Onɛ da pin'il teŋ la yʋ'ʋr anɛ Butu yʋʋm 1740 la ni, o pian'adnɛ Nankane pian'ad la ka an tɔn'ɔsi yit Zecco (nanna yʋ'ʋn bɛnɛ Burkina Faso ya-tuona), onɛ da dɛŋin zi'in Pungu (di anɛ Kasem buudi pian'ad teŋ yinne dinɛ bɛ Zecco ya-tuona).
english: The town was founded around 1740 by Butu, a Nankane speaking hunter from Zecco (present day southern Burkina Faso), who initially settled in Pungu (a Kasem speaking community further south of Zecco).

kusaal: 19th century saŋa laa, teŋ la da anɛ zi'isʋŋ kani bɛ Sahel caravan suorin.
english: During the 19th century, the town became an important staging post on the Sahel caravan route.

kusaal: 20th century pin'ilʋg ni British dim da maali ba zi'isʋg Navrongo.
english: At the beginning of the 20th century the British established a base at Navrongo.

kusaal: Catholic mission da zi'el yʋʋm 1906 lla ni - Fathers pielis la ("Pères Blancs"), French dim banɛ an French Canadians.
english: A Catholic mission was established in 1906 - the White Fathers ("Pères Blancs"), a French group made up of French Canadians.

kusaal: Ba da naamnɛ Upper Volta (nanna yʋ'ʋn an Burkina Faso) na bɛ Upper East region ka di yitnɛ French anti-clerical wada ni (Faadanam la da tis sida ye ba na du'oe ba yis Upper Volta).
english: They came to Upper East region from Upper Volta (now Burkina Faso) due to French anti-clerical laws (the Fathers believed they would be expelled from Upper Volta).

kusaal: Ka British la basi ba suor ka tisi ba yɛl yinne ba ya'a ma siak kaa naam zi'in Navrongo, ba da ye ba kʋ nya'aŋi pian'a buud sia ya'a ka'e English ma'aa nɛɛ.
english: The British allowed them to set up in Navrongo on the condition that the school that they were to establish used English only.

kusaal: La'amnɛ dinɛ da mɔr tɔɔg pin'ilʋg la ni ( Faadanam la zamisnɛ pian'abil kani ka ba da pʋ pian'ada ka nyɛ sakur biis 5 ma'aa bɛ nwadis 18), sakur la da naaenɛ yɔlim – British dim nid yinne yʋʋʋm 1927 la ni ye dinɛ da an sakur sʋŋ tita'ar (yit 5 anu ma'aa bɛn ni) bɛ Ghana ya-datiʋŋ ni.
english: Despite a rocky beginning (the Fathers had learnt the wrong local language and only attracted 5 students in the first 18 months), the school eventually became a success – a British official in 1927 said that it was the best school (of only 5) in the north of Ghana.

kusaal: Banɛ dɔlisid Ghana 1957 suo-mɛŋ yit British colonial sʋ'ʋlʋm ni, Navrongo da lieb teŋ tita'ar tis Kassena/Nankani district.
english: Following Ghana's 1957 liberation from British colonial authority, Navrongo was designated as the district capital of the Kassena/Nankani district.

kusaal: Navrongo mɔri tropical savanna sawina (di dɔlisnɛ Köppen sawina yɛlisim) teŋ la mɔr tʋʋlʋgi gilig yʋʋm la wʋsa laa, la'amnɛ sɛɛung nɛ ʋʋni bɛ la.
english: Navrongo has a tropical savanna climate (Aw according to the Köppen climate classification) with the temperature being hot year-round, although there is a wet season and a dry season.

kusaal: 26 March 2017 nii, Navrongo da mɔri a teŋtʋʋlʋg 43.8 °C (110.8 °F), dinɛ da an teŋtʋʋlʋg kani zu'oe ka Ghana teŋ sia nan zi' paamɛ.
english: On 26 March 2017, Navrongo recorded a temperature of 43.8 °C (110.8 °F), which the highest temperature to have ever been recorded in Ghana.

kusaal: Navrongo mɔri Economy kani nɔbigid tɔ'ɔtɔ.
english: Navrongo has a fast-developing Economy.

kusaal: Tono Irrigation Project bɛ anina la, Naara Bank, GCB Bank, ADB Bank, Hospitals, Navrongo Health Research Centre, radio stations nɛ PIO TV station nɛ asuo-mɛŋ tʋʋmanam, nidib bɛdigʋ an pa'anib, neesnam nɛ kpaadib bani ku'od ka gʋ'ʋn (bʋʋs, pɛn'ɛs, niigi, nɔɔr bɛɛ kpin'ini).
english: Coupled with the existence of The Tono Irrigation Project, Naara Bank, GCB Bank, ADB Bank, Hospitals, Navrongo Health Research Centre, radio stations and PIO TV station, and several other companies, there is a lot of the population who are teachers, nurses and subsistence level farmers in crops and rearing (goats, sheep, cattle, poultry).

kusaal: Navrongo Cathedral, nanna ka yʋ'ʋn baŋ, ka ba da mɛ' was yʋʋm 1906 ka yalig yʋʋm 1920.
english: Navrongo Cathedral, as it is now known, was built in 1906 and expanded in 1920.

kusaal: Navrongo anɛ teŋpʋtita'ar tis Kassena-Nankana District – dinɛ bɛ is Upper East Region bɛ northern Ghana.
english: Navrongo is a town and the capital of Kassena-Nankana Municipal District in the Upper East Region of northern Ghana, adjacent to the border with Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Navrongo ka 2012 nidib kanl la an 27,306.
english: Navrongo's population in 2005 was estimated to be 25,470, and in 2012 was estimated to be 27,306.

kusaal: Navrongo anɛ teŋpʋʋg kani mɔr sʋŋir, ka ba mi' di cathedral nɛ di grotto la yɛla.
english: Navrongo is an important market town, known for its cathedral and its grotto.

kusaal: Sakuya mɛn zu'oya wʋʋ, C.K Tedam University, St John Bosco teacher training college, Nursing training college, Navrongo SHS (NAVASCO), Notre Dame SHS, OLL Girls SHS nɛ bɛdigʋ.
english: There are also several institutions including, the C.K Tedam University, St John Bosco teacher training college, Nursing training college, Navrongo SHS (NAVASCO), Notre Dame SHS, Our Lady of Lourdes Girls SHS etc.

kusaal: Di yʋ'ʋr da anɛ "Di pʋ'a kani mɔr faranam ayɔpɔi", di da anɛ White Fathers kpɛmnam la da yɛl.
english: Originally called "Our Lady of Seven Sorrows", the construction was overseen by the White Fathers.

kusaal: Di pʋʋgʋn laa, zamguoma la mɔri bʋnkɔnbid fotonam ani, daar wʋsa tʋʋma, nɛ Christian pian'azut nwennɛ Zugsɔb diib la nɛ Bethlehem tʋʋma bɛ za'anɔɔrin la.
english: On the inside, the walls are decorated with animal forms, scenes of everyday life, and Christian themes such as the Last Supper and the Bethlehem scene in the entrance area.

kusaal: Zi'ig la 'ɛn lɛm mɔri grotto nɛ gbɛɛnsa bɛdigʋ.
english: The site also contains a grotto and accommodation facilities.

kusaal: Nya'aŋɔ, di yʋ'ʋr da anɛ Navrongo School (NAVASCO).
english: Later, it was simply called Navrongo School (NAVASCO).

kusaal: Sakur la pian'azug anɛ "LUX BOREALIS" Latin pian'ad.
english: The school's motto is "LUX BOREALIS" in Latin.

kusaal: Di anɛ sakur kʋdʋg yinne nɛ secondary schools dinɛ bɛ Upper East Region kani mɔr yʋ'ʋr ka lɛm pɛ'ɛs sakuya anii kani bɛ Ghana Ya-datiʋŋi mɔr yʋ'ʋr bɛda.
english: It is the Upper East's oldest and arguably most prestigious public secondary school and among about six elite schools in northern Ghana.

kusaal: Di mɔr Kasadjan Sports Stadium dinɛ ka ba na di'emid ani.
english: There is the Kasadjan Sports Stadium for recreation.

kusaal: Ba anɛ Kwegyir Aggrey, John F. Kennedy, Livingtone, Abatey, Ferguson, Garvey, Guggisberg, Nkrumah, Volta, nɛ Abavana dɔɔd anɛ dab ma'aa.
english: They are Kwegyir Aggrey, John F. Kennedy, Livingtone, Abatey, Ferguson, Garvey, Guggisberg, Nkrumah, Volta, and Abavana halls all for gentlemen.

kusaal: Sakur la maanɛ Agricultural Science, General Science, General Business, General Arts, Visual Arts nɛ Home Economics.
english: NAVASCO offers programmes in Agricultural Science, General Science, General Business, General Arts, Visual Arts and Home Economics.

kusaal: Yiiga pa'an kpɛɛm da anɛ J.K Fiegbor.
english: The first headmaster was J.K Fiegbor.
