kusaal: Alosius Alexis Abem mɛn da an bani ka nidib mi' ye ba na pa'an kpɛmnam bɛ yʋʋm 1980s ka Madam Katumi mɛn pin'il tʋʋma yʋʋm 1990 la ni.
english: Mr. Adenze Kangah and Mr. Alosius Alexis Abem were also two well-known headmasters of the school in the 1980s before Madam Katumi assumed responsibility in the 1990s.

kusaal: Patrick Tangonyire mɛn di'e yʋʋm 2000 la ni.
english: Mr. Patrick Tangonyire took over in the 2000s.

kusaal: NAVASCO anɛ sakur yinne kani bɛ Ghana ya-datiʋŋ ka mɔr mɛɛsa bɛdigʋ, yɛlkpan kani anɛ dinɛ nyaŋi yisid sakur biis bɛdigʋ la.
english: NAVASCO is one of few schools in northern Ghana with a wealth of physical infrastructure, a major reason for its ability to educate many people.

kusaal: MacDonald saŋa la, onɛ da an British nid onɛ mɔr baŋir.
english: In the 1970s, it became known for its agricultural activities under Mr. MacDonald, a veteran British educator.

kusaal: MacDonald Hall dinɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa mi' la tʋmir anɛ di'ema nɛ la'asʋg zi'ig.
english: The famous MacDonald Hall serves assembly and entertainment purposes.

kusaal: Slessor, Tono, Independence, and Luther King dɔɔd mɛn anɛ pʋ'ab din.
english: Slessor, Tono, Independence, and Luther King halls serve ladies.

kusaal: Ba mɔr Science Laboratory kani pɛ'ɛl nɛ la'ad nɛ sakur pɔɔg dinɛ ka bani zamisid science la na nyaŋi paam paalʋ zamisʋg.
english: The campus offers a well-equipped Science Laboratory and a School Farm, both of which offer practical training to science students.

kusaal: C.G MacDonald, onɛ an pa'an kpɛɛm kani ka nidib mi' o dinɛ yi sakur la pin'ilʋg.
english: He was followed by Agyemang Dickson, Crawford, and then Mr. C.G MacDonald, probably the famous headmaster in the school's history.

kusaal: O nɔknɛ sakur biisi mɛ' MacDonald Hall, dinɛ an sakur biis la'asʋg zin'ig.
english: He used students to construct MacDonald Hall, the assembly place for students.

kusaal: Ba sieba mɛn yit Ya-dagɔbʋg Ghana ni kpɛla mɛn.
english: Others come from the southern parts of Ghana.

kusaal: Zugdaan la da bigisi o gba'ae kati wa'ae sakur la ye sakur la naati an sakur tita'ar Ya-datiʋŋ ni ka paas ye o na gɔsi di nɛ sʋŋa.
english: The president indicated his dream that this school will become a great centre of learning in the north and that he will watch its progress with keen interest.

kusaal: Sakur la gbana bʋʋr la tʋmi tis sakur la nɛ teŋ la yʋma bɛdigʋ.
english: The school library served the school and the community for years.

kusaal: Nelson Kyeremeh anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Nelson Kyeremeh is a Ghanaian politician and an administrator.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Berekum East Constituency bɛ Bono Region hali yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal Nwadig daba ayɔpɔi daar, 7 January 2021.
english: He has been the member of parliament for the Berekum East Constituency in the Bono Region since 7 January 2021.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Kyeremeh nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu Nwadisa atan la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar, 27 March 1985.
english: Kyeremeh was born on 27 March 1985 and hails from Berekum in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da naae o Basic Education Certificate yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni, 2000 ka naae o secondary school yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan la ni, 2003.
english: He obtained his basic education certificate in 2000 and his secondary school certificate in 2003.

kusaal: O da di'e o Bachelor of Science degree in Management Studies (Administration/Management) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni, 2012 paasi o Diploma in Basic Education dinɛ ka da paam yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai ni la, 2009.
english: He was awarded his Bachelor of Science degree in Management Studies (Administration/Management) in 2012 succeeding a Diploma in Basic Education in 2009.

kusaal: Kyeremeh da anɛ Assistant Headteacher tʋm nɛ gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la, Ghana Education Service ka da lɛn an Administrator Agyengoplus Transport and Logistical Service Limited.
english: Kyeremeh was an Assistant Headteacher with the Ghana Education Service and subsequently an Administrator at Agyengoplus Transport and Logistical Service Limited.

kusaal: Kyeremeh da nya'anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, NPP nidib ka dii nya' Berekum East Constituency nɛ Kwabena Twum-Nuamah.
english: Kyeremeh won to contest as the NPP Parliamentary candidate for the Berekum East Constituency against the incumbent MP Kwabena Twum-Nuamah.

kusaal: O da keŋ tuoni di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi, 2020 vɔɔtʋg la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pistan nɛ yinne (27,731) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne kɔbiga pʋʋgin (61.3%) ka Ma'asim tiig, NDC nid la, Simon Ampaabeng Kyeremeh paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbistan nɛ anu (17,305) dinɛ an pistan nɛ anii du'al ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (38.2%) ka onɛ pʋ zi'en Na'adɔsia, Francis Manu-Gyan paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi, 217 dinɛ an nɛɛm du'ali anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.5%).
english: He further won the 2020 general elections by 27,731 votes making 61.3% of total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Simon Ampaabeng Kyeremeh had 17,305 votes making 38.2% of the total votes cast and an Independent candidate Francis Manu-Gyan had 217 votes making 0.5% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Kyeremeh paas la'askanɛ gɔsid banɛ mɔr ɔfis kanɛ mɔr nyɔɔd la (Holding Offices of Profit) ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid tʋʋma nɛ ya yɛla la.
english: Kyeremeh is a member of Members Holding Offices of Profit Committee and a member of Works and Housing Committee.

kusaal: O yinɛ Berekum bɛ Bono Region, Ghana.
english: Kyeremeh was born on 27 March 1985 and hails from Berekum in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kyeremeh anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Kyeremeh is a Christian.

kusaal: Mandela du'anɛ bɛ Thembu royal family bɛ Mvezo la, South Africa.
english: A Xhosa, Mandela was born in Mvezo to the Thembu royal family.

kusaal: O da keŋ sakur zamis law bɛ University of Fort Hare nɛ University of Witwatersrand ka da naam tʋmi an lawyer la bɛ Johannesburg.
english: He studied law at the University of Fort Hare and the University of the Witwatersrand before working as a lawyer in Johannesburg.

kusaal: Anina ka o nɔki o mɛŋi pɛ'ɛs anti-colonial nɛ African nationalist politics, pɛ'ɛsid ANC bɛ 1943 ka mɛn sin'igid nɔɔr yinne nɛ Youth League bɛ 1944.
english: There he became involved in anti-colonial and African nationalist politics, joining the ANC in 1943 and co-founding its Youth League in 1944.

kusaal: Ka Marxism da sʋŋ o laa, o da sua pɛ'ɛs South African Communist Party (SACP).
english: Influenced by Marxism, he secretly joined the South African Communist Party (SACP).

kusaal: Mandela du'am yʋʋm anɛ 18 July 1918 bɛ teŋkpɛŋ Mvezo bɛ Umtata la, ka South Africa's Cape Province.
english: Mandela was born on 18 July 1918, in the village of Mvezo in Umtata, then part of South Africa's Cape Province.

kusaal: Banɛ da nɔk yʋ'ʋr Rolihlahla tis o la, di amɛ Xhosa pian'ʋk dinɛ bigis ye yɛl-iɛɛt (troublemaker) ka dina yan'aŋɔ ba da buon o nɛ o buudi la yʋ'ʋr kani an Madiba.
english: He was given the forename Rolihlahla, a Xhosa term colloquially meaning "troublemaker", and in later years became known by his clan name, Madiba.

kusaal: O saam yir yaadaʋ onɛ yʋ'ʋri an Ngubengcuka, da anɛ Thembu Kingdom la na'atita'ar bɛ Transkeian Territories of South Africa's modern Eastern Cape province.
english: His patrilineal great-grandfather, Ngubengcuka, was ruler of the Thembu Kingdom in the Transkeian Territories of South Africa's modern Eastern Cape province.

kusaal: Ngubengcuka biig yinne onɛ yʋ'ʋri an Mandela, Nelson yaadaʋ nɛ onɛ ni ka o paam yʋ'ʋkan.
english: One of Ngubengcuka's sons, named Mandela, was Nelson's grandfather and the source of his surname.

kusaal: O da teŋkan ninsabilik zugdaan nɛ yiiga zugdaan democratic vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: He was the country's first black head of state and the first elected in a fully representative democratic election.

kusaal: Di da ka'enɛ o mɛŋ teŋin ma'aa nɛɛ, amaa Africa wʋsa, onɛ da an zugdaan tis African National Congress (ANC) parti la dinɛ yi 1991 ti paae 1997 ni.
english: Ideologically an African nationalist and socialist, he served as President of the African National Congress (ANC) party from 1991 to 1997.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye o an zugdaan tis ANC's Transvaal branch, ye nɛ onɛ pɛ'ɛsid nɛ 1952 Defiance Campaign nɛ 1955 Congress of the People.
english: Mandela was appointed President of the ANC's Transvaal branch, rising to prominence for his involvement in the 1952 Defiance Campaign and the 1955 Congress of the People.

kusaal: Ba da yɔ'ɔ nɔɔrin babʋg ye mɔri nidibi kpɛ'ɛd mɔɔg amaa, di da pʋ nyaŋi bɛ 1956 Treason Trial laa.
english: He was repeatedly arrested for seditious activities and was unsuccessfully prosecuted in the 1956 Treason Trial.

kusaal: Mandela da bɛ sarika ni yʋma 27, bɛ Robben Island, Pollsmoor Prison nɛ Victor Verster Prison.
english: Mandela served 27 years in prison, initially on Robben Island, and later in Pollsmoor Prison and Victor Verster Prison.

kusaal: Nɛ' nam wʋsa ni ka domestic and international pressure pɛ'ɛsnɛ ya'am iansir bɛ teens tanb, Zugdaan F. W. de Klerk yis o 1990.
english: Amid growing domestic and international pressure, and with fears of a racial civil war, President F. W. de Klerk released him in 1990.

kusaal: Mandela nɛ de Klerk pɛ'ɛs paŋ ye ba maal suguru nɛ nidib nɛ'ɛsʋg bɛɛ gaans, dinɛ naae nɛ 1994 multiracial general election dinɛ ka Mandela gaad ANC tuon an zugdaan ka da di ya'ani an zugdaan.
english: Mandela and de Klerk negotiated an end to apartheid and organised the 1994 multiracial general election in which Mandela led the ANC to victory and became President.

kusaal: New Edubease bɛ nɛ Adansi South district bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: New Edubease is located in the Adansi South district of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kuk la bɛ nɛ Adansi South District bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Adansi South District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ yʋ'ʋn an wadmaan constituency la ni anɛ Michael Okyere Baafi onɛ bɛ New Patriotic Party.
english: The current member of Parliament for the constituency is Michael Okyere Baafi of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da di'e kuk la yinɛ Mark Assibey-Yeboah onɛ da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug 4th Republic dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) la san'an.
english: He succeeded Mark Assibey-Yeboah who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republican parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti gaŋ o yiiga nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: He was the former head of Free Zone Ghana.

kusaal: Michael Okyere Baafi da yinɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) ni ka da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la, ani ka o da mɔr vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi.
english: The current member of Parliament for the constituency is Michael Okyere Baafi of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: John Kufuor onɛ paas NPP ni la da an Zugraan tis Ghana din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ yinne (2001) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awa (2009).
english: John Kufuor of the NPP was president of Ghana from 2001 to 2009.

kusaal: Vɔɔtkanɛ ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi nwadis piinɛ ayi la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 December 2004), Na'adɔɔg la da di Wadmaannib kʋgʋs kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ awai (129) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi nɛ pistan pʋʋgin (230).
english: At the elections held on 7 December 2004, the party won 129 out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt NPP na'anya'ad, Kufuor, ye o an Zugraan nɛ vɔɔt pisnu nɛ ayi du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (52.75%).
english: The NPP candidate was Kufuor, who was re-elected as president with 52.75% of the vote.

kusaal: New Patriotic Party wada gbauŋ la, Article 10(2) & (3) tis suor ye National Annual Delegates na la'asi zin'in ba ya'a maal Regional Annual Delegates Conference gaad bakɔi anaasi.
english: According to the New Patriotic Party's constitution, Article 10(2) & (3) mandates that the National Annual Delegates shall meet at least four weeks after the last Regional Annual Delegates Conference.

kusaal: NPP National Delegates Congress da bɛnɛ 12 April 2014 Tamale Sports Stadium la ni.
english: The National Delegates Congress was slated for 12 April 2014 in Tamale Sports Stadium.

kusaal: Nidib nwɛnɛ 5,265 da nary a ba keŋ vɔɔt.
english: About 5,265 delegates were expected to partake in the internal elections of the party.

kusaal: NPP da maali ba national delegates congress nɛ Eastern region din yi 15 June 2018 paae 17 June 2018.
english: The NPP organised the national delegates congress in Eastern region from 15 June 2018 to 17 June 2018.

kusaal: National Organiser; Sammi Awuku.
english: Three people contested in the National Organiser position; Sammi Awuku, Suleiman Sadik, and Emmanuel Kodua.

kusaal: National executives banɛ ka ba da vɔɔt 2022 17th of July Accra Sports Stadium la nwa.
english: The national executives elections for 2022 was held on 17 July at the Accra Sports Stadium.

kusaal: New Patriotic Party (NPP) anɛ pɔlitis na'adɔɔgʋ bɛ Ghana.
english: The New Patriotic Party (NPP; Twi: Ahofama Foforo Kuw) is a centre-right and liberal-conservative political party in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba dataa paa tuon nɛ nya'aŋ anɛ National Democratic Congress (NDC).
english: Since the democratisation of Ghana in 1992, it has been one of the two dominant parties in Ghanaian politics, with its leading rival being the centre-left National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: New Patriotic Party (NPP) vɔɔtidi ba national executive nam nɛ yuma anaasi wusa.
english: In alignment with the party constitutional provisions,the leadership of the New Patriotic Party scheduled its National Delegates Conference for September 19 to elect a new cohort of national executive officers to steer the party's administrative and political strategies.

kusaal: National Youth Organiser; Henry Nana Boakye.
english: The National Youth Organiser had four persons; Henry Nana Boakye, Dominic Eduah, Kamal-Deen Abdulai, and Emmanuel Nana Appiah.

kusaal: National Women's Organiser: Kate Gyamfua.
english: The National Women's Organiser role had three people contesting; Kate Gyamfua—620, Ellen Ama Daaku—9, Hajia Sawadatu Saeed—32.

kusaal: Nhyiaeso constituency bɛnɛ Kumasi Metropolitan district linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Nhyiaeso is located in the Kumasi Metropolitan district of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: One an wadmaani tis Nhyiaeso Constituency anɛ Stephen Amoah lin pin'il yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) sa'.
english: The Member of Parliament for the Nhyiaeso Constituency is Stephen Amoah since 2017.

kusaal: Constituency la da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi (2004) yitnɛ Ghana vɔɔtug lʋgʋr la ni, ka li da paasnɛ constituency nam paala pisi nɛ awai banɛ ka ba da maal la zug, li da kɛ ka constituency nam la nɔbigi yi kɔbʋsyi keŋ kɔbʋsyi nɛ pistan'.
english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Ninsaalib kuud bʋŋkɔnb sieba ka gʋ'ʋn sieba ni'im yɛla dunia sin'iŋirin sa.
english: Humans have hunted and farmed other animals for meat since prehistory.

kusaal: O anɛ Parliament kpɛɛm yinne tis Amenfi East Constituency dinɛ bɛ Western Region la.
english: He is the member of Parliament for the Amenfi East Constituency in the Western region.

kusaal: Amankwah da dɛŋi anɛ DCE tis Wassa Amenfi East teŋin n da an district ka yʋʋn an municipal la lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piina ayuobo to paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piina ayɔpɔi.
english: Amankwah served as District Chief Executive (DCE) for the Wassa Amenfi East District Assembly now Wassa Amenfi East Municipal Assembly from 2016 to 2017.

kusaal: Ba da vooti ngaŋ o, August Nwadig la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piina awai tis NDC an maasim tiig paati la Amenfi East teŋin.
english: He was acclaimed in August 2019 after he went opposed in the National Democratic Congress primaries making him the NDC's candidate for the Amenfi East constituency.

kusaal: Amankwah n kpe Parliament tʋʋma yɛla tis NDC paati la tit Amenfi East constituency zaŋi ken yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi vɔɔtʋg la.
english: He was acclaimed in August 2019 after he went opposed in the National Democratic Congress primaries making him the NDC's candidate for the Amenfi East constituency.

kusaal: O da paam vootʋg kanl ban tus pistan' nɛ kɔbisyi ni piina anu linɛ an pisnu nɛ atan' li nya'aŋ awai, zaalim kɔbiga pʋʋgin n gaad o tiraan onɛ ann Edward Amo-Acquah tis NDC paati la onɛ da paam vɔɔtʋg kanl la tusa pisi nɛ awai nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisbu na anaasi linɛ an pisnaasi na anaasi li nya'aŋ anu, nɛ anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin.
english: He was acclaimed in August 2019 after he went opposed in the National Democratic Congress primaries making him the NDC's candidate for the Amenfi East constituency.

kusaal: Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus Glover (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm rusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ nwadisa anii dabpisi nɛ anii daar, 28 August 1966) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani tis Tema East constituency.
english: Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus Glover (born 28 August 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and the Member of Parliament of Tema East constituency.

kusaal: O paasnɛ Wabʋd Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party ni ka an Minister of Transport nya'andɔl, Ghana.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the Deputy Minister of Transport in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Glover nɛ yʋʋm rusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ nwadisa anii dabpisi nɛ anii daar, 28 August 1966) Asere-Ga Mashie bɛ Greater Accra Region la.
english: Glover was born on 28 August 1966 in Asere-Ga Mashie in the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Glover da keŋɛ o secondary education nɛ Nungua Presbyterian Secondary School yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981).
english: Glover had a year of secondary education at the Nungua Presbyterian Secondary School in 1981.

kusaal: O da zamisya ka di'e o ordinary level kasɛta bɛ Presbyterian Boy's Senior High School, Legon yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi (1982) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1986).
english: He studied for and obtained his ordinary level certificate at the Presbyterian Boy's Senior High School, Legon between 1982 and 1986.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ Accra Academy privately din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi (1987) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) ka da di'e o Advanced Level kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: He continued at the Accra Academy privately from 1987 to 1988 and obtained his Advanced Level Certificate.

kusaal: Glover mɔrnɛ master's degree dinɛ ka o di'e yi Warwick University, Coventry.
english: Glover holds a master's degree from Warwick University, Coventry.

kusaal: O lɛm mɔr certificate of higher education yi Ruskin College, Oxford, ka lɛm mɔr certificate in labour studies yi University of Cape Coast.
english: He also has a certificate of higher education from Ruskin College, Oxford, and a certificate in labour studies from University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: O kennɛ Miracle Life Gospel Church.
english: He is a member of the Miracle Life Gospel Church.

kusaal: Glover paasnɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔ, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nidib ni.
english: Glover is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) la ni, o da di Tema East kʋk la Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP nɔba zug keŋ paas sixth parliament of the fourth republic.
english: In 2012, he won the Tema East seat on the NPP ticket for the sixth parliament of the fourth republic.

kusaal: O da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ka an wadmaan na'anya'adi tis Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party la.
english: He contested in the 2020 Ghanaian general election as the parliamentary candidate for the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da anɛ human resources manager tis Ken City Media Ltd.
english: He works as a human resources manager for Ken City Media Ltd.

kusaal: O da anɛ manager/administrator/HR practitioner.
english: He works as a human resources manager for Ken City Media Ltd.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a ye fʋ gɔ zamisidibi mamis siem, nananna niimis la (Neornithes) da bɛnɛ Late Cretaceous kudimin la bɛ pin'iligʋn nɛ kudimin Cretaceous (100 Ma) la teŋsʋk ka ba da kɛna nabi nab bɛ Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event saŋa la yʋma miliyɔn pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (66 million), dinɛ da kʋ pterosaurs nɛ banɛ kaae-ornithuran dinosaurs la wʋsa.
english: According to some estimates, modern birds (Neornithes) evolved in the Late Cretaceous or between the Early and Late Cretaceous (100 Ma) and diversified dramatically around the time of the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event 66 million years ago, which killed off the pterosaurs and all non-ornithuran dinosaurs.

kusaal: Aves nɛ banɛ wɛn taaba buudi , dɔlisid Crocodilia an siem, mɔri bʋŋvʋr kanɛ zieni tis dinɛ anɛ clade Archosauria la.
english: Aves and a sister group, the order Crocodilia, contain the only living representatives of the reptile clade Archosauria.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir kɔbis wai nɛ piswai (1990s), Aves niimis buudi la da anɛ dinɛ ka sɔ' wʋsʋ da pa'al ye ba anɛ niim banɛ an nananna niimis la buudi (phylogenetically as all descendants of the most recent common ancestor of modern birds nɛ Archaeopteryx lithographica).
english: During the late 1990s, Aves was most commonly defined phylogenetically as all descendants of the most recent common ancestor of modern birds and Archaeopteryx lithographica. However, an earlier definition proposed by Jacques Gauthier gained wide currency in the 21st century, and is used by many scientists including adherents to the PhyloCode.

kusaal: Gauthier nɛ de Queiroz da pa'al dinɛ biological yʋ'ʋr "Aves" la pa'alʋg nami anaasi dinɛ an yɛla.
english: Gauthier and de Queiroz identified four different definitions for the same biological name "Aves", which is a problem.

kusaal: Aves tun'e pa'al ye archosaurs nam wʋsa banɛ niimisi gat banɛ wɛnɛ crocodiles (bɛɛ Avemetatarsalia).
english: Aves can mean all archosaurs closer to birds than to crocodiles (alternately Avemetatarsalia)

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi saŋa la mi'ilim di banɛ bɛ Liaoning Province, northeast China la, banɛ da p'al ye theropod feathered dinosaurs la sʋ'ʋoe ka bi'esim-bi'esim kaŋa bɛ.
english: By the 2000s, discoveries in the Liaoning Province of northeast China, which demonstrated many small theropod feathered dinosaurs, contributed to this ambiguity.

kusaal: Banɛ mɔr nananna niimis la itima la anɛ wɛnii 40% kɔbiga pʋʋgin da bɛ yʋma miliyɔn pisyuobu (60) la saŋa yiiga niimis banɛ da dɛŋim bɛ an bird-line archosaurs tis yiiga maniraptoromorphs, dinɛ an, yiiga dinosaurs wɛnɛ niimbanɛ vʋoe la gat Tyrannosaurus rex.
english: Over 40% of key traits found in modern birds evolved during the 60 million year transition from the earliest bird-line archosaurs to the first maniraptoromorphs, i.e. the first dinosaurs closer to living birds than to Tyrannosaurus rex.

kusaal: Maniraptoromorpha da yi saŋa sia na la nyaŋ, wɛnɛ yʋma miliyɔn pisnaasi saŋa (40 million) na ti kena ya'aŋ la, di da kpɛ pin'ilnɛ anina ka ba niŋgbina sin'iŋi sied ka ba neotenic (juvenile-like) itima la lɛɛ nɔbigid.
english: After the appearance of Maniraptoromorpha, the next 40 million years marked a continuous reduction of body size and the accumulation of neotenic (juvenile-like) characteristics.

kusaal: Yʋma anu wʋsa Bird Life International dimi makidi pa'an niimis kanl dunia wʋsa.Yinne niimis buudi ayi la ni ɛɛnti sienɛ "in decline".
english: Many bird populations are declining worldwide, with 1,227 species listed as threatened by BirdLife International and the IUCN in 2009.

kusaal: Ba yinɛ dinosaurs.
english: Birds evolved from earlier theropods, and thus constitute the only known living dinosaurs.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a gɔs tituaa nɛ niimis anɛ dinosaurs.
english: Birds evolved from earlier theropods, and thus constitute the only known living dinosaurs.

kusaal: Ba yinnɛ anɛ peacock onɛ na nyaŋi widig o kɔnbilig la ka li lusi ba zuur ka wan wʋʋ fan.
english: Birds have evolved a variety of mating behaviours, with the peacock tail being perhaps the most famous example of sexual selection and the Fisherian runaway.

kusaal: Saŋa kan ba competitors banɛ kpi'e nɛ ba la, pterosaurs, ka li ke ka ba kanl sie nɛ ba buudi kena bɔdig nyain bɛ Mesozoic la.
english: While they were the dominant group of avialans during the Cretaceous period, Enantiornithes became extinct along with many other dinosaur groups at the end of the Mesozoic era.

kusaal: Taxonomists nɔk niimis nɛ ye ba anɛ 'Aves' (Avialae).
english: Avialae, initially proposed to replace the traditional fossil content of Aves, is often used synonymously with the vernacular term "bird" by these researchers.

kusaal: Niimis nɛ Crocodilia ma'aa an bʋnvʋya banɛ pʋ mɔr paŋa bɛ Archosaur reptiles buudi la ni.
english: Aves and a sister group, the order Crocodilia, contain the only living representatives of the reptile clade Archosauria.

kusaal: Gauthier da pa'al ye Aves yɛla la'am pɛɛs nɛ the only crown group la ka ba mi'i ba ka an fossils, ka maali ba, ka ban naanɛ aan Avialae bɛdigʋ buudi la, dinɛ pa'al ye clade la anɛ banɛ an extent spicies la nar ye li mɔr bɛn nɛ banɛ kpi'ie nɛ taaba la.
english: This was done by excluding most groups known only from fossils, and assigning them, instead, to the broader group Avialae, on the principle that a clade based on extant species should be limited to those extant species and their closest extinct relatives.

kusaal: Aves mɛ tun'e lɛm pa'al ye archosaurs banɛ mɔr kpamkpam bɛda (bɛɛ Avifilopluma).
english: Aves can mean those advanced archosaurs with feathers (alternately Avifilopluma)

kusaal: Aves tun'e pa'al ye dinosaurs banɛ mɔr kpamkpam iand la (bɛɛ Avialae).
english: Aves can mean those feathered dinosaurs that fly (alternately Avialae)

kusaal: Aves tun'e pa'al ban yi zin'i sia na nɛ niimis banɛ wʋsa vʋe la, nɛ banɛ wʋsa yit "crown group", nɛ Neornithes (a "crown group", in this sense synonymous with Neornithes).
english: Aves can mean the last common ancestor of all the currently living birds and all of its descendants (a "crown group", in this sense synonymous with Neornithes)

kusaal: Di ya'a an fossil nɛ biological nyɛ siel la vikki la, scientists dim siakya ye niimis la lɛm pɛɛs theropod dinosaurs nɛ kas-kas anɛ yit Maniraptora gniin la dinɛ an theropods pɛɛs dromaeosaurids and oviraptorosaurs, nɛ banɛ bɛ.
english: Based on fossil and biological evidence, most scientists accept that birds are a specialised subgroup of theropod dinosaurs and, more specifically, members of Maniraptora, a group of theropods which includes dromaeosaurids and oviraptorosaurs, among others.

kusaal: Kanlʋg saŋa bɛ contemporary palaeontology la anɛ banɛ theropods, bɛɛ avialans la da anɛ banɛ iand da anɛ banɛ pʋ lal nɛ deinonychosaurs, banɛ an dromaeosaurids nɛ troodontids.
english: The consensus view in contemporary palaeontology is that the flying theropods, or avialans, are the closest relatives of the deinonychosaurs, which include dromaeosaurids and troodontids.

kusaal: Pɛɛs nɛ buud banɛ ka ba buon ye Paraves.
english: Together, these form a group called Paraves.

kusaal: Basal buudi sieba banɛ an Deinonychosauria, banɛ an Microraptor, mɔr kpamkpama dinɛ sʋŋidi ba ka ba nyaŋidi iand.
english: Some basal members of Deinonychosauria, such as Microraptor, have features which may have enabled them to glide or fly.

kusaal: Banɛ an basal deinonychosaur la pɔɔdnɛ pamm.
english: The most basal deinonychosaurs were very small.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛŋa pa'al ye di anɛ na'ana ka sɔ' na nyaŋi pa'al ye ba yiti paravians buudi la ni na ka tun'e yi arboreal buudi la ni na ka na nyaŋi iank.
english: This evidence raises the possibility that the ancestor of all paravians may have been arboreal, have been able to glide, or both.

kusaal: Pʋ wɛnɛ Archaeopteryx nɛ banɛ kaae avialan dinosaurs kpamakpama la, ka dit ni'im la, zamisʋg pa'al ye yiiga avialans nam la da anɛ omnivores.
english: Unlike Archaeopteryx and the non-avialan feathered dinosaurs, who primarily ate meat, studies suggest that the first avialans were omnivores.

kusaal: Late Jurassic Archaeopteryx la da anɛ banɛ ka wʋsa da mi'i ye ba yiiga traditional fossils banɛ ka ba nyɛɛ ba ka ba da nyɛ ka li sʋŋ dinɛ an theory of evolution bɛ19th centuries la ni.
english: The Late Jurassic Archaeopteryx is well known as one of the first transitional fossils to be found, and it provided support for the theory of evolution in the late 19th century.

kusaal: Archaeopteryx da an yiiga fossil kanɛ ka ba da mɔri yina pa'al nyain ka li an traditional reptilian characteristics—yina, ka ba nɔba mɔr nu'ug ɛɛns, ka wa'am, ka ba zʋʋr wɛni abaŋgya zʋʋrnɛ - ka mɛ lɛm mɔr kpʋkpam banɛ ia'and ka li wɛni nananna niimis la nɛ.
english: Archaeopteryx was the first fossil to display both clearly traditional reptilian characteristics—teeth, clawed fingers, and a long, lizard-like tail—as well as wings with flight feathers similar to those of modern birds.

kusaal: Ka osteoderms banɛ da an nana'a bɛ archosaurs nɛ acquisition ka ba kpamkpama la wɛn taaba bɛ yiiga phase la.
english: The loss of osteoderms otherwise common in archosaurs and acquisition of primitive feathers might have occurred early during this phase.

kusaal: Hypercarnivory la da yʋ'ʋm kpɛm nɔbigidnɛ bɛ zin'ig wʋsa ka ba zug waʋŋ la an bɛridi ka ba tuon nɔba la mɛ wa'ama - wa'ama.
english: Hypercarnivory became increasingly less common while braincases enlarged and forelimbs became longer.

kusaal: Niimis banɛ bɛ nananna la buudi wusa yinɛ Aves buudi la ni, di pʋnɛ zin'isa ayi: Palaeognathae nɛ Neognathae, banɛ mɔr niimis buudi wusa.
english: All modern birds lie within the crown group Aves (alternately Neornithes), which has two subdivisions: the Palaeognathae, which includes the flightless ratites (such as the ostriches) and the weak-flying tinamous, and the extremely diverse Neognathae, containing all other birds.

kusaal: Buudi ayi bama wusa mɔr yʋ'ʋbanɛ an superorder, cohort, bɛɛ infraclass.
english: These two subdivisions have variously been given the rank of superorder, cohort, or infraclass.

kusaal: Niimis mɔr kpamkpama.
english: There are several types of feathers, each serving its own set of purposes.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o dɔlisidnɛ New Patriotic Party yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋg tita'ar la ni, ka o da di constituency la ni ka da kilim wadmaan.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party in the 2024 General election to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: Onɛ yʋn an wadmaan tis constituency la anɛ Hon Kwakye Daffour.
english: He succeeded Kwakye Darfour who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republican parliament on the ticket as an Independent candidate.

kusaal: Nkoranza North Constituency anɛ constituency banɛ bɛ Ghana la yinne ka mɔr sɔ' ka o zi'e ba nɔba zug Parliament of Ghana.
english: Nkoranza North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Nkoranza North Constituency bɛnɛ Nkoranza district dinɛ bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Nkoranza North is located in the Nkoranza district of the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la da pin'ilnɛ ka Ghana Wadmaannib dinɛ da bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la nyaan paae, ka din yi sankan paae zina, na'adɔkanɛ zanl na'am constituency ni anɛ New Patriotic Party.
english: This seat was created prior to the Ghanaian parliamentary election in 2004 and has been held by the New Patriotic Party since then.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi , nwadis atan' la, dabpiinɛ atan' daar (13 March 2007), tenkan vɔɔtʋgin la, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nid, Derek Oduro, da di na'am.
english: At the by-election held on 13 March 2007, the New Patriotic Party (NPP) candidate, Derek Oduro, won the seat with an increased majority.

kusaal: Di dagɔbʋg anɛ Nkoranza South constituency.
english: To the south is the Nkoranza South constituency.

kusaal: Li tuon anɛ Techiman North constituency linɛ bɛ Techiman Municipal District.
english: Its western boundary is the Techiman North constituency in the Techiman Municipal District.

kusaal: Di datiʋŋ anɛ Kintampo South constituency bɛ Kintampo South District ka Pru constituency linɛ bɛ Pru District la an li nya'aŋ-datiŋ.
english: To the north is Kintampo South constituency in the Kintampo South District and the Pru constituency in the Pru District is north east.

kusaal: Li nya'aŋ titɔdig anɛ Atebubu Amantin constituency linɛ bɛ Atebubu-Amantin District.
english: The eastern boundary is formed by the Atebubu Amantin constituency in the Atebubu-Amantin District.

kusaal: Li Ya-dagɔbʋg-nya'aŋ titɔdig anɛ Ejura Sekyedumase constituency linɛ bɛ Ejura/Sekyedumase District, Ashanti Region.
english: The south eastern boundary is formed by the Ejura Sekyedumase constituency in the Ejura/Sekyedumase District of the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Constituency la da pin'il yiiga nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni, ka banɛ da maali li an Electoral Commission of Ghana nɛ constituency sieba pisi nɛ awai, ka li da kɛ ka constituency nam la kal da paasi yi kɔbis ayi (200) keŋ kɔbisyi nɛ pistan' (230).
english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Nkoranza districti bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Nkoranza district of the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Nkwanta North Constituency anɛ Ghana Parliament constituency nam la yinne.
english: Nkwanta North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba kuk la bɛ nɛ Nkwanta North District bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Nkwanta North District of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di dagɔbug anɛ Nkwanta South District ka li nya'aŋ an Republic of Togo.
english: It is bounded to the south by the Nkwanta South District and to the east by the Republic of Togo.

kusaal: Li datiʋŋ anɛ Northern Region ka tuon an Northern Region nɛ Volta Kɔdaʋg la.
english: To the north is the Northern Region and to the west, the Northern Region and the Volta River.

kusaal: Li da sin'iŋe yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) nwadis piinɛ ayi zugraan nɛ wadmaan vɔɔtʋg kanɛ ka ba da pʋdigi Nkwanta kudʋg la yʋ'ʋm maali Nkwanta North paal nɛ Nkwanta South constituency la.
english: It was formed prior to the 2004 December presidential and parliamentary elections by the division of the old Nkwanta constituency into the new Nkwanta North and Nkwanta South constituencies.

kusaal: Nkwanta North Constituency bɛnɛ Nkwanta districti bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: Nkwanta North is located in the Nkwanta district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Nkwanta South Constituency anɛ Ghana Parliament constituency nam la yinne.
english: Nkwanta South is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Nkwanta South bɛnɛ Nkwanta South districti bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: Nkwanta South is located in the Nkwanta South district of the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba kuk la bɛ nɛ Nkwanta District bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Nkwanta District of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li da sin'iŋnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi nwadis piinɛ ayi zugraan nɛ wadmaannib vɔɔtʋgin la ka ba da pʋdig Nkwanta kudig la yʋ'ʋm maal Nkwanta North paal nɛ Nkwanta South constituency la.
english: It was formed prior to the 2004 December presidential and parliamentary elections by the division of the old Nkwanta constituency into the new Nkwanta South and Nkwanta South constituencies.

kusaal: Trasacco teŋkanɛ bɛ Ghana kpɛla ka ligidi tʋʋma yiti ani la bɛnɛ teŋkan ni.
english: Trasacco Estate, a high income gated community in Ghana is located at the periphery of the town.

kusaal: Ani ba mɔr nyɔ'ɔg nwɛ'ɛb nɛ sakurnam yɛla, lin yi Junior High bɛɛn ti paae kologinam sakur bɛɛn, ka li pin'inɛ Nii Sowah Din Primary school nɛ li junior Secondary school.
english: This settlement boast of educational facilities from the junior level up to the tertiary level starting with the Nii Sowah Din Primary and Junior Secondary School.

kusaal: Galaxy International secondary school mɛ pʋ lal nɛ Nmai Dzorn ka sɔ' ya'a wa'ae ani li anɛ wʋʋ mit anu bɛɛn.
english: Galaxy International School's secondary facility is located within five minutes from Nmai Dzorn.

kusaal: Ka Canadian International School la mɛ bɛnɛ tembanɛ bɛ Nmai Dzorn sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: The Canadian International School is also located within the environs.

kusaal: Ghana lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid tɛɛns nyain bɛllim yɛla, ka an banɛ sid tʋm hali ka ba yʋ'ʋr yi Africa wʋsa la, ba zuglʋgʋr zin'ig bɛnɛ Nmai Dzorn teŋin.
english: Zoomlion Ghana Limited, a giant in waste management and environmental sanitation in Ghana and across Africa is headquartered in Nmai Dzorn.

kusaal: Teŋ la nidib kal nɔbignɛ hali yʋma piig linɛ gaad la, ka li anɛ nidibi yi Accra sʋ'ʋlʋm ken zin'is kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ni la zug.
english: The population of the area has increased over the past ten years mainly due to the expanding settlement outside Accra Metropolis.

kusaal: Nompumelelo Mqwebu (ba dʋa o yʋma tusir kobʋswai ne pisyopɔi ne ayɔpoi) yitnɛ Africa ya dagobʋg ka dʋgid diib ka lɛm a onɛ sobid ya'as.
english: Nompumelelo Mqwebu (born 1977) is a South African chef and author.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi ne piiga ne anii la, o gbaŋ kane an ye yitnɛ Africa dukdugid nini'ni, ka ba da pʋdi li ye dʋnia wusa diib dugib gbaŋ kane yaŋi kʋosi li mɛŋ be Gourmand Dunia wusa Dʋgib gbaŋ piini ka ba da maal China la.
english: In 2018, her book, Through the Eyes of an African Chef, was named the world's best self-published cookbook at the Gourmand World Cookbook Awards which took place in China.

kusaal: Ba da dʋa Mqwebu ne KwaZulu-Natal ya-datiʋŋ naarin amaa o nobignɛ Umlazi.
english: Mqwebu was born on the North coast in KwaZulu-Natal, but grew up in Umlazi.

kusaal: O da zamis ne tolimtolim da'asin yela Centec College, ka da di'e diib dugib gbaŋ City and Guilds of London Institute, ka zamisi dugid diib be diib ne daam dugib dim sakurin Morningside, Durban, ne Ballymaloe Cookery School be Ireland.
english: She studied Marketing Management at Centec College, acquired a Culinary Diploma from City and Guilds of London Institute, and trained as a cook at the Chef School of Food and Wine in Morningside, Durban, and Ballymaloe Cookery School in Ireland.

kusaal: One sɔe' Mzansi International Culinary Festival (MICF) ne Africa ne Europe la'as taaba diib dugib yela, on da nan pu si'iŋ ne Africa ne Europe la'as taaba diib dugib la, o da tʋmne Janet's Restaurant be Kloof ne Zimbali Lodge.
english: Prior to establishing Africa Meets Europe Cuisine, she worked at Janet's Restaurant in Kloof and Zimbali Lodge.

kusaal: Gourmand Dunia wusa Dʋgib gbaŋ piini anɛ tɛŋgbaŋ wusa ny'ab ka ba piin diib bee daam dugib gbaŋ kanɛ gaad so wusa.
english: The Gourmand World Cook Awards is an international competition that honours the best food and wine books.

kusaal: O ane pʋa ka mɔr biribis ayi.
english: She is a mother of two sons.

kusaal: Region la maalig la da anɛ nɔɔr zi'elʋg kanɛ ka na'adɔɔg kanɛ buon New Patriotic Party da zieli kati waae yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piinɛ ayuobu (2016) vɔɔtug la.
english: The creation of this new region was in fulfillment of a promise made by the New Patriotic Party prior to the 2016 Ghana general election.

kusaal: Solomon Namliit Boar one an Mp tis Bunkpurugu Constituency ka lɛn an Northern Regional Minister nya'andɔl kudug ka o da gaŋ ye o an yiiga Regional Minister tis region paal, North East Region.
english: Upon winning the elections, the President, Nana Akuffo Addo created the Ministry of Regional Reorganization to oversee policy formulation and implementation, and Hon. Solomon Namliit Boar, Mp for Bunkpurugu Constituency and former Deputy Northern Regional Minister was appointed as the first Regional Minister for the newly created North East Region.

kusaal: Regions banɛ daa kpɛlim la anɛ Western North, Bono, Bono East, Ahafo, Savannah nɛ Oti regions.
english: The other regions are Western North, Bono, Bono East, Ahafo, Savannah and Oti regions.

kusaal: Ba da maal vɔɔtug yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piinɛ anii, naar nwadig la dabisa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (December 27, 2018) ka li da an titʋaa ka nidib kɔbiga pʋʋgin pisnii nɛ ayinne da vɔɔt (81% vɔɔter turnout) region la ni ka piswai nɛ awai nɛ pʋdʋgir anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (99.8%) da siak ye ba maalim North East Region.
english: A referendum vote held on December 27, 2018 was successful with 81% voter turnout in the proposed region voting 99.8% in favor of the creation of the North East Region.

kusaal: Region la tɛŋpʋtita'ari an Nalerigu bɛ East Mamprusi Municipal Assembly la.
english: The region's proposed capital is the town of Nalerigu in the East Mamprusi Municipal Assembly.

kusaal: North East Region datiʋŋ anɛ Upper East region, ka li ya'ya'aŋ an eastern Ghana-Togo international border, ka li ya'dagɔbʋg an Northern region, ka li ya'tuona an Upper West region.
english: The North East Region is bordered on the north by the Upper East region, on the east by the eastern Ghana-Togo international border, on the south by the Northern region, and on the west by the Upper West region.

kusaal: The North East Region mɔr kpi'emisi gat Northern Ghana sʋ'ʋlim nam la wʋsa, lin kpi'e nɛ Sahel nɛ Sahara la yɛla.
english: The North East Region is much drier than southern areas of Ghana, due to its proximity to the Sahel, and the Sahara.

kusaal: Li tʋligir nɛ li ma'ar nɛ an wʋʋ 17 °C (63 °F) yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ 47 °C (117 °F) nintaŋ.
english: The temperatures can vary between 17 °C (63 °F) at night and 47 °C (117 °F) during the day.

kusaal: Nayiri an zugraani sʋ'oe Mamprugu traditional area kanɛ ka region la wʋsa paasi li pʋʋgin la.
english: The Nayiri is the King (overlord) of Mamprugu traditional area of which the entire region is a part.

kusaal: Mamprusi bʋʋdi la zu'oe Municipality kan ni.
english: Mamprusi people are the major ethnic group in the Municipality.

kusaal: Amaa, Dagombas, Bimobas, Konkombas, Talensis, Tampulma, Bissa, Mossis, Chakosis mɛ kɛŋi zin'in zin'ikan.
english: However, there are also Dagombas, Bimobas, Konkombas, Talensis, Tampulma, Bissa, Mossis, Chakosis and Hausas who have settled in the area.

kusaal: Bʋʋdi malimanam ayi' ka ba maan yʋʋm pʋʋgin, Damba Festival, nɛ Bugum Festival.
english: Two traditional festivals are celebrated annually, Damba Festival, Bugum (Fire) Festival.

kusaal: Nidib wʋʋ pisnii nɛ anu kɔbiga pʋʋgin (85%) anɛ kpaadib.
english: More than 85% of the economically active population are agricultural.

kusaal: North East Region nidib pʋ zu'oe wala, ka bʋʋdi pian'ad banɛ ka ba pian'adi paas na'asaal anɛ Gur linɛ paas nɛ Niger–Congo language family, ka ba sieba an Mampruli, Tampulma, Bimoba, Kusaal, Dagbani, bɛɛ Konkomba.
english: The North East Region has a low population density, and, along with the official language of English, most inhabitants speak a language of the Gur subfamily in the Niger–Congo language family, such as Mampruli, Tampulma, Bimoba, Kusaal, Dagbani, or Konkomba.

kusaal: Ka li anɛ ye, region la pʋdʋgi mɔr MMDA's nam ayuobu (ka li la'as nɛ an Metropolitan kai, Municipal nam ayi' nɛ Assembly nam anaasi).
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into six MMDA's (made up of 0 Metropolitan, 2 Municipal and 4 Ordinary Assemblies).

kusaal: District, Municipal bɛɛ Metropolitan Assembly, mɔri ba kpɛɛm ka onɛ an Chief Executive, zi'e gɔmena nɔba zug, ka nyɛ paŋi yi Assembly, linɛ ka li kpɛɛm an presiding member kanɛ ka Assembly man nam la mɛŋ gaŋ.
english: Each District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly, is administered by a Chief Executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an Assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Li bɛ nɛ Ghana datiʋŋ ka ba da pin'ili li yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piinɛ anii, samanpiid nwadig (December 2018), ban da vɔɔt ye ba waae li yis Northern region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: It is located in the north of the country and was created in December 2018 after a referendum was voted upon to break it off of the Northern region.

kusaal: li tɛŋpʋtita'ari an Nalerigu.
english: The region's capital is Nalerigu.

kusaal: North East Region bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la da waae nɛ yis Northern Region of Ghana kanɛ da bɛ la.
english: The North East Region of Ghana was a proposed new region to be carved out of the existing Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: On da di' na'am la nya'aŋ, Zugraan, Nana Akuffo Addo da pin'il Ministry of Regional Reorganization ye li gɔsi gba'ae gba'asa ka tʋm tʋʋma.
english: Upon winning the elections, the President, Nana Akuffo Addo created the Ministry of Regional Reorganization to oversee policy formulation and implementation, and Hon. Solomon Namliit Boar, Mp for Bunkpurugu Constituency and former Deputy Northern Regional Minister was appointed as the first Regional Minister for the newly created North East Region.

kusaal: North East region mɔr district nam ayuobʋ (6 districts).
english: North East region is made up of 6 districts.

kusaal: Tɛŋ la siakid mɔɔg tita'am ka li kas-kas anɛ savanna ka mɔr tiis banɛ tun'e sawak ka ba sieba an tɛ'ɛs bɛɛ acacia nam.
english: The vegetation consists predominantly of grassland, especially savanna with clusters of drought-resistant trees such as baobabs or acacias.

kusaal: Li sɛɛʋng anɛ nwadisa ayuobʋ nɛ nwadis piinɛ yinne la tɛnsʋk ka li saa niib an wʋʋ 750 to 1050 mm (30 to 40 inches).
english: The wet season is between about June and November with an average annual rainfall of 750 to 1050 mm (30 to 40 inches).

kusaal: Nayiri mɔr na'akpɛɛmnam nɛ na'abibis banɛ ka o sʋ'oe ba.
english: The Nayiri is supported by paramount chiefs, divisional and other sub-chiefs under him.

kusaal: O na'am sʋ'ʋlim la zu'oe gaad North East Region nɛ tɛŋ la wʋsa.
english: His paramountcy extend beyond the boundaries of the North East Region and even the nation.

kusaal: O na'abibis sieba an Wulugu Naaba, Wungu Naaba, Soo Naaba, Kulgu Naaba, Yunyoorana nɛ Bunkpurugu Naaba nɛ Zuarungu Naaba, Tongu Naaba, Sakuti.
english: Notable among the chiefs are the Wulugu Naaba, Wungu Naaba, Soo Naaba, Kulgu Naaba, Yunyoorana and Bunkpurugu Naaba, Gbankoni Naaba, and Zuarungu Naaba, Tongu Naaba, Sakuti (all in Upper East Region).

kusaal: Mamprusi sʋ'ʋlim bɛnɛ Region nwa' pʋʋg.
english: The Mamprusi Kingdom is located in the region.

kusaal: Nidib banɛ bɛ North East region la bɛdegʋ pʋ'ʋsʋdi Kristo biis pʋ''ʋsim, mɔɔm pʋ'ʋsim nɛ bɛɛ Ba'amaannib pʋ'ʋsim.
english: Most residents in the North East region are affiliated with Christianity, Islam, and/or Traditional African Religion.

kusaal: Region la tʋmmi ba tʋʋma nɛ dɔlisid local government system.
english: The political administration of the region is through the local government system.

kusaal: O mɔr na'ayikpɛɛmnam banɛ sa'an o.
english: He has a traditional council of elders who advise him.

kusaal: North Tongu sʋ'ʋlʋm bɛnɛ North Tongu district linɛ bɛ Ghana Volta Region la ni.
english: North Tongu is located in the North Tongu district of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kʋk la bɛnɛ North Tongu District linɛ bɛ Ghana Volta Region sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: The seat is located within the North Tongu District of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da yɔ'ɔgi sʋ'ʋlʋm nɛ Samanpiid nwadig la ni yʋʋma 2004 ti Ghana vɔt la ni ka wadmaanib la da maal vɔt n pʋdʋg zi'ig la n yi North Tongu constituency kʋdʋg la ni n liebi li ka li yu'un tiaki an North Tongu paal nɛ Central Tongu constituencies nam la.
english: It was formed before the 2004 December presidential and parliamentary elections by the division of the old North Tongu constituency into the new North Tongu and Central Tongu constituencies.

kusaal: North Tongu anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ paas sʋ'ʋlʋm banɛ bɛ ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni.
english: North Tongu is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: North Tongu constituency saŋa la anɛ yʋʋma 2004.
english: The boundaries of the present constituency thus differs from the North Tongu constituency of elections prior to 2004.

kusaal: North Tongu District anɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ paas sʋ'ʋlʋm nam bam piina anii linɛ bɛ Ghana, Volta Region.
english: North Tongu District is one of the eighteen districts in Volta Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba district assembul kpi'enɛ nɛ Addidome, linɛ kpi'e nɛ Adidome Senior High Sakur la baba linɛ an (Adisec) la, li lɛbnɛ Southwest baba linɛ bɛ Volta Region ka ba Battor Dugame linɛ aan ba temputita'ar.
english: The district assembly is located in Addidome, near Adidome Senior High School (Adisec) the southwest part of Volta Region and has Battor Dugame as its capital town.

kusaal: · Adaklu District n lɛb ya-datiʋŋ.
english: Adaklu District to the north.

kusaal: Sansi'an la sa li da paasnɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm tita'ar la ni lin da an North Tongu District nwadis atan' dabisim piiga la yʋʋma1989 la ni, Adidome aan ba temputita'ar, linɛ ka ba da yɔ'ɔgi li yi Tongu District Council ni la, hali ti paae saŋkanɛ ka ba da bɛŋ western district la ka yɔ'ɔg North Tongu District la nwadis ayuobʋ la dabisim piisi nɛ anii yʋʋma 2012 la ni, lin ka Battor Dugame aan ba temputita'ar la, ba da dɔlisnɛ ti Ghana wada gbaʋŋ lakir linɛ an Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 2081 la ni yɔ'ɔgi li; ala ka zi'ig linɛ da kpɛlim la ka ba pʋdi li ye Central Tongu District, ka Adidome aan ba temputita'ar, ba da dɔlisnɛ ti Ghana wada gbaʋŋ lakir linɛ an Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 2077 la ni yɔ'ɔgi li.
english: Originally it was created as part of the then-larger North Tongu District on 10 March 1989, with Adidome as its capital town, which was created from the former Tongu District Council, until the western part of the district was split off to create a new North Tongu District on 28 June 2012, with Battor Dugame as its capital town, which was established by Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 2081; thus the remaining part has been renamed as Central Tongu District, with Adidome as its capital town, which was established by Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 2077.The district has a male population of 43,990(47.1%) and female population of 49,370 which constitutes (52.9%) The total population is 93,360.

kusaal: Volta mu'ar la giligi li nɛ yi ya-datiʋŋ ti tɔn ya-dagɔbʋg.
english: The Volta River cuts the district into two halves from north to south.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi' nɛ piinɛ anii, nwadis piinɛ ayi (December 2018) la ni, ka ba da nwaae Savannah Region nɛ North East Region yi Northern region ni.
english: In December 2018, the Savannah Region and North East Region were created from it.

kusaal: Northern Region titɔndig kanɛ lɛb datiʋŋ anɛ North East region, ka li ya'ya'aŋ an eastern Ghana-Togo international border; ka li dagɔbʋg an Oti region; ka li Ya-tuona an Savannah Region.
english: It shares borders with the North East Region and Savannah Region to the north and Oti Region to the south, and neighbouring countries, including the Republic of Togo to the east and La Côte d'Ivoire to the west.

kusaal: Guinea Savanna ɛɛnti madigi gaad savanna ecological zones nam atan' la wʋsa.
english: The Guinea Savanna is the wettest of the three savanna ecological zones.

kusaal: Li tɛŋ tʋʋlim bɛ ma'asim anɛ wʋʋ 14 °C (59 °F) yʋ'ʋŋ ka nintaŋ mɛ an 40 °C (104 °F).
english: During this time, temperatures can vary between 14 °C (59 °F) at night and 40 °C (104 °F) during the day.

kusaal: Northern Region sʋ'ʋlimnam wʋʋ Kingdom of Dagbon nɛ Dagbani.
english: The Northern Region contains much of the territories of the Kingdom of Dagbon, and Dagbani is the most widely spoken language, along with English.

kusaal: Dagbani paasnɛ Oti–Volta pian'ad bʋʋdi linɛ bɛ Niger–Congo buudi dɔɔgin la.
english: Dagbani belongs to the Oti–Volta subfamily in the Niger–Congo language family.

kusaal: Bʋʋdi pian'ad banɛ bɛ region la ni sieba an Likpakpaanl nɛ Nawuri.
english: Other languages spoken within the region include Likpakpaln and Nawuri.

kusaal: Region la bɛ zin'ig sia la pʋ lal nɛ Europe nɛ North Africa,fʋ ya'a mak anina nɛ Accra, ka li kɛ ka da' diib kɛn tuon anina.
english: The region's location and greater proximity to both Europe and North Africa, compared to Accra, make it an increasingly attractive destination for investors.

kusaal: · Sabali (River Oti)
english: Sabali (River Oti)

kusaal: · Nawuni River (White Volta)
english: Nawuni River (White Volta)

kusaal: Li bɛnɛ tɛŋ la datiʋŋ ka mɛ paas ayi' daan, regions piinɛ ayuobu la zu'oe gaad o taaba.
english: It is situated in the northern part of the country and ranks as the second largest of the sixteen regions.

kusaal: Lin daa nan pʋ pʋdʋg la, li daa mɔr tɛŋgbaʋŋ wʋʋ 70,384 square kilometres bɛɛ pʋdʋgir pistan' nɛ yinnɛ (31%) Ghana sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.
english: Before its division, it covered an area of 25,000 square kilometres, representing 10 percent of Ghana's area.

kusaal: Northern Region mɔrnɛ districts piinɛ anaasi.
english: The Northern Region is divided into 16 districts.

kusaal: Li tɛmpʋʋgtita'ar anɛ Tamale, Ghana tɛŋ kanɛ paas atan' zu'or pʋʋgin.
english: The region's capital is Tamale, Ghana's third-largest city.

kusaal: Northern Region anɛ Guinea Savanna grassland.
english: The Guinea Savanna is the wettest of the three savanna ecological zones.

kusaal: Li sɛɛʋng bɛnɛ nwadis anu nɛ nwadis piiga la tɛnsug, ka saa kanɛ niid an wʋʋ 750 to 1050 mm (30 to 40 inches).
english: There is an average annual rainfall of 750 to 1050 mm (30 to 40 inches).

kusaal: Wɛn wʋʋ Ghana zin'is wʋsa an siem la, nidib tʋʋg pʋsʋg ka ba tʋʋma an kuob nɛ gʋ'ʋl.
english: Like all parts of Ghana, more than half of the economically active population are agricultural.

kusaal: Region la anɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka da' diib kɛn tuon Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, ka Tamale da anɛ ya'tuona ninsabilis tɛŋpʋʋg kanɛ nɔbʋgid tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ; ka da kpɛlim nɔbigid tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ, fʋ ya'a mak anina nɛ Ghana tɛŋpʋʋs banɛ kpɛlim la.
english: The region is a hotspot for investment in Ghana, with Tamale previously being ranked as the fastest-growing city in West Africa, experiencing tremendous growth compared to other cities in Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana's iron ore reserves, ka na nwɛn wʋʋ three billion tons, kɛ ka region la an zin'ig sʋŋ kanɛ ka ba did da' steel nɛ iron.
english: Ghana's largest iron ore reserves, estimated to be more than three billion tons, make the region an ideal destination for investments in steel and iron.

kusaal: Nidib atan', babanu' pʋʋgin banɛ bɛ Northern region pʋ'ʋsidi mɔɔm (60.0%).
english: Around three out of five residents in the Northern region were affiliated with Islam (60.0%).

kusaal: Northern Region of Ghana mɔr districts piinɛ ayuobu.
english: The Northern Region of Ghana contains 16 districts.

kusaal: Piinɛ yinne anɛ districts, ka yinne an metropolitan ka anaasi an municipal districts: municipality, metropoly nɛ districts la wʋsa mɔr tɛŋ bibis nɛ tɛŋ kpɛmis.
english: 11 are ordinary districts in addition to 1 metropolitan and 4 municipal districts.

kusaal: Tamale Teaching Hospital, Ghana sibiti kanɛ paasi atan bɛdim pʋʋgin.
english: The region is a hotspot for investment in Ghana, with Tamale previously being ranked as the fastest-growing city in West Africa, experiencing tremendous growth compared to other cities in Ghana.

kusaal: Lʋgir kaŋa da paas 2019 CFU CHIMP bɔɔlwɛ'ɛb la ni bɛ first elimination stage of the Preliminary phase(ka di'emid yiiga zin'ikanɛ ka ba dɔl nɔɔr la).
english: The club participated in the 2011 CFU Club Championship, playing in the first elimination stage of the Preliminary phase.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛŋa, Northern United da dɔlnɛ Surinamese Hooldcasse zɔtzɔtib la, dinɛ an Walking Bout Company la.
english: There, Northern United took on the Surinamese Hoofdklasse runners-up, Walking Bout Company.

kusaal: Bɔɔlwɛ'ɛb la'asʋg ni ba da yisi ba nɛ 6-1 ka gʋ'ʋŋ 3-0 bɛ yin wɛ'ɛb dinɛ an WBC, nɛ 3-1 bɛ WBC la ni.
english: In the tournament, they were eliminated 6–1 on aggregate, losing 3–0 at home to WBC, and 3–1 at WBC.

kusaal: Nsawam Adoagyiri anɛ constituency paal kani yi Aburi- Nsawam constituency bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana.
english: Nsawam Adoagyiri is one of the constituencies created from the now defunct Aburi-Nsawam constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kʋk la bɛ nɛ Akuapem South Municipal Assembly bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana.
english: The seat is located entirely within the Akuapem South Municipal Assembly of the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaani zi'eni tisi ba, onɛ paam vɔɔti gaadi o taaba.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Nsoatreman Football Club anɛ Ghanaian professional football club linɛ bɛ Nsoatre, Bono Region banɛ nwɛn'ɛdi bɛ Ghana Premier League, di'amkanɛ gat o taaba bɛ Ghana football ni.
english: Nsoatreman Football Club is a Ghanaian professional football club based at Nsoatre, Bono Region that competes in the Ghana Premier League, the top-flight of Ghanaian football.

kusaal: Ba nwɛn'ɛdi ba yin di'ema bɛnɛ Nana Konamansah Park astroturf.
english: It plays its home matches at the Nana Konamansah Park astroturf.

kusaal: Li da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ (2021), ba da di Ghana Division One league yʋʋm kanɛ ka ba da pin'ili li di'ema la ka ba tɔlisi ba Ghana Premier League ye ba nwɛn'ɛ 2021–22 season.
english: Founded in 2021, they won the Ghana Division One league title in their maiden season and got promoted to the Ghana Premier League for the 2021–22 season.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi ni (2024), Nsoatreman da di'e ba yiiga ya'ani bɛ Ghana FA Cup, ba da nyaŋ Bofoakwa Tano 5–4 dɔlis penalties pʋʋgin.
english: In 2024, Nsoatreman won their first ever trophy as winners of the Ghana FA Cup, defeating Bofoakwa Tano 5–4 on penalties.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi, sɛnlʋŋ nwadig, daba wai daar (9 September 2022) Nsoatreman F.C. da yisi ba kpɛɛmnam yʋda paalʋ na, lin na niŋ si'em ka ba nyaŋi di ya'an Ghana Premier League.
english: On 9 September 2022 Nsoatreman F.C. unveiled their board members and technical staff to see the smooth running of the team and achieve success as a debutant in the Ghana Premier League.

kusaal: Ba kpɛɛmnam la si'eba anɛ wadmaanib, tɛŋ sʋ'ʋdib, nɛ kpikpiŋ dim.
english: Their board members comprise legislators, traditional leaders and business executives.

kusaal: Adelaide Ntim an wadmaani tis constituency la nananna.
english: Adelaide Ntim is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: O da diya nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ atan', kɔbis yuobʋ nɛ pisi nɛ ayi (23,622) dinɛ an kɔbiga pʋʋgin, vɔɔt pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne (71.71%) nyaŋi gaad onɛ ti'al o la, Newman Dapaah onɛ da zi'en Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug la, on da paam vɔɔt tusa awai, kɔbistan' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (9,321) dinɛ an vɔɔt pisi nɛ anii dʋ'al pisi nɛ awai, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (28.29%), vɔɔt la wʋsa da la'asnɛ tusa pistan' nɛ ayi, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ atan' (32,943).
english: She won with 23,622 (71.71%) votes over her competitor, Newman Dapaah of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), who got 9,321 votes (28.29%), this makes a total of 32,943 votes.

kusaal: Nannana ba nya'ad nɛ ba nwɛ'ɛdib taaba ayi' kat wa'anɛ Division One League linɛ an nwɛ'ɛkpɛŋ kanɛ paas ayi ka lɛn an MTN FA Cup la.
english: The club currently competes in Zone Two of the Division One League which is the second tier of the football league system in Ghana, and the MTN FA Cup.

kusaal: Bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb kaŋa da pin'ili 2013, ka nannana ka ba nwɛ'ɛd bɛ Ghana Division One League la ni.
english: The club was founded in 2013 and currently plays in the Ghana Division One League.

kusaal: yʋʋm 2020 ni la, ba bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd kanɛ nwɛ' di kal gaadi ba wʋsa ka o yʋ'ʋr buon ye Agyenim Boateng Mensah la, ba da tɔlis o keŋ Dreams.
english: In 2020, the club's top goal scorer, Agyenim Boateng Mensah was transferred to Dreams.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2021 la ni li nwadis ayi la ni, bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib la'aʋŋ kaŋa da pin'ili nwɛ'ɛd yin nwɛ'ɛb bɛ Akoon Park linɛ bɛ Tarkwa, ka an linɛ ye li pin'il sʋŋi ba gur Ghana Premier League linɛ ken Medeama na la.
english: In February 2021, the club started playing the home matches at Akoon Park in Tarkwa, the home grounds of Ghana Premier League side Medeama.

kusaal: La'am nɛ ban bɛ Western Region la, ba kpi'es da anɛ Karela United (nannana ba bɛnɛ Ghana Premier league linɛ me bɛ Nzema zone la).
english: Due being located in the Western Region of Ghana, the club's rivals is their neighbours Karela United (currently in the Ghana Premier League) which is also within the Nzema zone.

kusaal: Ban nɛ Karela United dim banɛ aan ba kpi'es la.
english: They are rivals with city neighbours Karela United.

kusaal: Nōgaku (能楽) anɛ Japanese buudi malima nam zin'is la yinne.
english: Nōgaku (能楽; Japanese pronunciation: [noː.ɡa.kɯ, -ŋa-]) is one of the traditional styles of Japanese theater.

kusaal: Di mɔr daʋŋ bɛdegʋ bɛ Bunraku, bɛɛ Japanese puppet theatre kanɛ ka ba buon ye Kabuki la.
english: It has influenced the Bunraku, or Japanese puppet theatre as well as Kabuki.

kusaal: Nōgaku theatre da paas UNESCO List of Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity ninɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni.
english: Nōgaku theatre was inscribed in 2008 by UNESCO on the List of Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Dinɛ bɛ di pʋʋgin anɛ di'ema yʋʋma dinɛ ka ba buon ye noh, nɛ comic theater dinɛ yʋ'ʋri an kyōgen (狂言).
english: It is composed of the lyric drama noh, and the comic theater kyōgen (狂言).

kusaal: Malima pʋʋgin, theatre buudi ayi la la'asidnɛ tʋm saŋa yinne, kyōgen ka ba nɔki gɛndig noh ni di maalʋg saŋa.
english: Traditionally, both types of theatre are performed together, the kyōgen being interposed between the pieces of noh during a day of performances.

kusaal: Labaar kaŋa "poultry" yi nɛ Middle English pultry or pultrie, kanɛ ka ba mɔri yi Old French/Norman nɔɔr sɛ'asiŋ.
english: The word chicken comes from Old English ċicen (pronounced essentially the same as in Modern English).

kusaal: Ka banɛ dɔl la'ad ni vɛɛnsid saalib tʋʋma yɛla la zaŋ kasɛt linɛ sid pa'an ye yin nɔɔs da bɛ Asia ya-tuona tɛɛnsin ka yʋma 6000 BC nyaan paae, ka bɛ China sʋ'ʋlʋm wʋʋ 6000 BC saŋa nɛ, nɛ India teŋin wʋʋ 2000 BC saŋa nɛ.
english: Archaeological evidence appeared to support domestic chickens in Southeast Asia well before 6000 BC, China by 6000 BC and India by 2000 BC.

kusaal: Ba gʋ'ʋn yin nɔbama ka li yalig yʋ'ʋn paae Asia ya-tuona nɛ Asia ya-tuonɛ ya-nya'aŋ dim tensʋk ni, ka ba la'am gʋ'ʋn mɔɔgin bʋnkɔnbid sieba ka ba gɛndig nɛ banɛ bɛ kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb wʋsa.
english: These domesticated chickens spread across Southeast and South Asia where they interbred with local wild species of junglefowl, forming genetically and geographically distinct groups.

kusaal: Ka ba vɛɛns nɔɔs buudi banɛ ka ba gʋ'ʋn bɛdegʋ ka li pa'al ye nɔrapielig buudir la mɔr nwɛnnɛm bɛɛ kɔnbʋlʋg si'im kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb linɛ yi yaab nam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb bani yi junglefowl zian buudir la ni na.
english: Analysis of the most popular commercial breed shows that the White Leghorn breed possesses a mosaic of divergent ancestries inherited from different subspecies of red junglefowl.

kusaal: Ka ban da ieed ma'ad tɛɛns paalʋ yɛla yʋʋm 2020 saŋa la, ba zamis nɔɔs 863 yɛla gilig dunia pamm ka yɛl ye, yin nɔɔs wʋsa yinɛ yin gʋ'ʋlʋg saŋa yinne linɛ an junglefowl zian kanɛ ka ba gʋ'ʋn zina ka li da yi China ya-tuona nɛ ya-nya'aŋ tɛɛns tensʋkin, nɛ Thailand nɛ Myanmar ya-nya'aŋ tɛɛnsin ni na la.
english: A 2020 Nature study that fully sequenced 863 chickens across the world suggests that all domestic chickens originate from a single domestication event of red junglefowl (Gallus gallus) whose present-day distribution is predominantly in Southeast Asia.

kusaal: Patrick Boakye yiadom an wadmaan tis constituency la.
english: Patrick Boakye-Yiadom is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: Obuasi East Constituency bɛnɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana nwa ni.
english: Obuasi East is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Nannana Na'adɔɔg bɛɛ paati kanɛ mɔr wadmaan kʋk la bɛ Obuasi East sʋ'ʋlʋmin la anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg paati la.
english: Obuasi East is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋid wadmaan ka o bɛ wadmmanib yin la n zi'eni tis teŋ la lin pin'il yiiga vɔɔtʋg kanɛ gaad la ni sa.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Sakur la bɛnɛ Gausu nɛ Koffikrom tensʋg.
english: The school is located in between the two towns, Gausu and Koffikrom.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da pin'il sakur la yʋʋm 1965 ka di anɛ gɔmma sɛkɛndiri nɛ tɛknikal sakur, dinɛ da biribis ma'aa sakur ka pa'an Science nɛ Technical Pa'ala ma'aa, dinɛ buudi mɛn bɛ ya-dagɔbʋg Ghana ni.
english: It was established by Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah in 1965 as Government Secondary Technical School, which was an all-boys institution offering science and technical programmes only, the first of its kind in the northern sector of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 1990 la ni ka Obuasi Secondary Technical School yʋ'ʋn da tiaki pɛ'ɛsid bipʋmis ye di sʋŋi ba science zamisʋg ni.
english: In 1990, Obuasi Secondary Technical School was converted into a mixed-sex school to aid the "more girls in science" campaign by the government of Ghana.

kusaal: Sakur la da mʋkki paae kɔtta faenal banɛ da maan National Science and Maths Quiz Competition yʋʋm 2019 banɛ da yaŋi di ka bas St Francis Xavier Minor Seminary nɛ Krobo Girls SHS la.
english: The school in 2019 reached the quarter-finals of the National Science and Maths Quiz Competition after beating St Francis Xavier Minor Seminary and Krobo Girls SHS.

kusaal: Sakur la da di yiiga ka mɔr diib 44 dɔl St Francis banɛ mɛn da mɔr diib 18 nɛ Krobo mɛn da mɔr diib 16.
english: The school came up first with 44pts followed by St Francis with 18 pts and Krobo with 16pts.

kusaal: Banɛ zi'eni maali paam yiiga la anɛ Kojo Daniel Eshun nɛ Lawrence Adjei.
english: Masters Kojo Daniel Eshun and Lawrence Adjei were the proud contestants for that day.

kusaal: Obuasi Senior High Technical School di Ashanti regional Milo nɔba kikiʋg nwɛ'ɛb yʋʋm 2005 nɛ 2015 ni.
english: Obuasi Senior High Technical School won the Ashanti regional Milo soccer competition in 2005 and 2015.

kusaal: Kweku Kwarteng an wadmaan nananna tis constituency la.
english: Kweku Kwarteng is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug ka di' na'am la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan' nɛ yinne, kɔbiga nɛ yinne (31,101) yit vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi nɛ anii, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnu' nɛ anaasi (48,254) ka da lieb wadmaan.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) won a majority of 31,101 votes out of 48,254 to become the MP.

kusaal: Odambea Festival anԑ malʋŋ kanԑ ka na'anam nԑ nidib banԑ bԑ Nkusukum Traditional Area linԑ bԑ Saltpond Central Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la maan.
english: Odambea Festival is an annual festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of Nkusukum Traditional Area in Saltpond in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba maan malʋŋ kaŋa ka li anԑ zanbini pa'an Nkusukum nidibi da yi Techiman zin'ig kanԑ da bԑ Brong Ahafo region sʋ'ʋlim kԑŋ zin'ini ba zin'igin nannanna la.
english: This festival is celebrated to commemorate the migration of the Nkusukum people from Techiman in formally Brong Ahafo region to their present settlement.

kusaal: Nidib banԑ mԑ lԑn maani li anԑ Anomabo dim.
english: It is also celebrated by the people of Anomabo.

kusaal: "Odambea" gbin anԑ "tͻ'ͻŋir kanԑ kpiem".
english: "Odambea" means "fortified link" in the local language.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔtnɛ tis o dolisidnɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni ka da di vɔɔt nam tusa piinɛ awai, kɔbusyɔpoi nɛ pisyuobu nɛ anii.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) in 2024.

kusaal: Onɛ da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug 4th Republic parliament la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni.
english: He had also represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament in 2004.

kusaal: Emmanuel Akwasi Gyamfi yʋ'ʋn an wadmaani tis constituency la ni.
english: Anthony Mmieh is the current member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: Odwira festival anԑ malʋŋ kanԑ ka na'anam nԑ nidib banԑ bԑ Fanteakwa District nԑ Akuapem linԑ bԑ Eastern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la maan.
english: The Odwira festival is celebrated by the chiefs and peoples of Fanteakwa District and Akuapem in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Banԑ maan Odwira Festival anԑ nidib banԑ bԑ Akropong-Akuapim, Aburi, Larteh, nԑ Mamfe sʋ'ʋlim nam ni.
english: The Odwira Festival is celebrated by the people of Akropong-Akuapim, Aburi, Larteh, and Mamfe.

kusaal: Ba maan malʋŋ la ka li anԑ zanbini pa'an ban da nyaŋ Ashanti nidib zaba pʋʋgin yʋʋm tusir, kͻbisnii nԑ pisi nԑ ayuobʋ ni la zug.
english: The festival celebrates a historic victory over the Ashanti's in 1826.

kusaal: Nwa' da anԑ saŋkanԑ ka Okuapimhene kanԑ da an na'abi tis paas piinԑ awai daani tis Akropong da zin' I na'am kʋg zug la, o yʋ'ʋri da an Nana Addo Dankwa (I) yinԑ yʋʋm tusir, kͻbisnii nԑ piinԑ yinnԑ paae yʋʋm tusir, kͻbisnii nԑ pistan' nԑ anu saŋa.
english: This was during the reign of the 19th Okuapimhene of Akropong, Nana Addo Dankwa (I) from 1811 to 1835.

kusaal: Nidib banԑ bԑ Jamestown Accra sʋ'ʋlim la mԑ maan malʋŋ la.
english: It is also celebrated by the people of Jamestown in Accra.

kusaal: Li wa'ae nԑ yʋʋma kͻbisyi' wana ka nidib banԑ bԑ Akropong, Amanokrom nԑ Aburi sʋ'ʋlim maan Odwira festival malʋŋ kanԑ ka na'ab kanԑ da pin'ili li an Nana Addo Dankwa 1 (1811 - 1835), na'ab kanԑ da paae piinԑ awai daan.
english: For nearly 200 years, generations of Akropong, Amanokrom and Aburi have annually celebrated the Odwira festival which was initiated by Nana Addo Dankwa 1 (1811 - 1835), the 19th Okuapehene of Akuapem.

kusaal: Ba maan malʋŋ la tiend nԑ nyaŋir kanԑ ka Okuapeman nidib da paam ban nԑ Asante zaba la pʋʋgin, zaba la da buon Katamansu ka ba da zabi kpi'e Dodowa yʋʋm tusir, kͻbisnii nԑ pisi nԑ ayuobʋ ni la.
english: The celebration is linked to the victory of the people of Okuapeman over the then-powerful Asante army during the historic battle of Katamansu near Dodowa in 1826.

kusaal: Akan buudi pʋʋgin, ba si'ak ye na'ab pʋ kpiida.
english: In the Akan dispensation, there's the belief that a chief never dies.

kusaal: Ban maan si'el daar kan anԑ ba piis malima suor la yi Akropong, zin'ig kanԑ an tԑnpʋʋgi tis Okuapeman kԑŋ paae Royal Mausoleum zin'ig kanԑ ka ba lԑn buon ye Amanprobi.
english: This sacred private event involves the clearing of the ceremonial path from the centre of Akropong, the capital of Okuapeman, to the Royal Mausoleum also known as Amanprobi.

kusaal: Dabiskaŋa daar, onԑ ka ba buon Gyaasehene ka o an Divisional Chiefs anu la yinnԑ bԑ Akuapem Traditional Area ka lԑn gͻsid banԑ suad na'am la'ad la wʋsa la buon onԑ ka ba buon Banmuhene (onԑ an na'abi tis Royal Mausoleum ka lԑn gͻsidi ba yaanam malima yela).
english: On this day, the Gyaasehene – one of the five Divisional Chiefs of the Akuapem Traditional Area and Administrator of all royal courtiers, summons the Banmuhene (Chief of the Royal Mausoleum and custodian of the Ancestors).

kusaal: Onԑ ka ba buon Okuapehene kaad na'am kʋgʋs ayͻpͻi banԑ bԑ Akropong la wʋsa – Aboasa, Asona, Twafo, Benkum, Kyeame nԑ Akrahene ye o kԑŋ maal sʋnsa'aŋ nԑ ba.
english: The Okuapehene visits each of the seven stool houses in Akropong – Aboasa, Asona, Twafo, Benkum, Kyeame and Akrahene to sympathise with them.

kusaal: Na'anam, na'ayir kpԑԑmnam nԑ nidib la wʋsa la'asidi bԑ Mpeniase – (tiig kanԑ ka ba da sԑ' yiiga daar kanԑ ka Akropong da lieb Okuapeman tԑnpʋʋg la.
english: The chiefs, elders and people of Okuapeman congregate at Mpeniase – (the first tree planted on the first day that Akropong became the capital of Okuapeman.

kusaal: Mpeniase, anԑ anԑ tiig kanԑ mͻr zanbin hali tis Akuapem Traditional Area) ye ba tis na'asi paalʋ ni.
english: The Mpeniase, hence remains a living symbol of the spirit of the Akuapem Traditional Area) to publicly pay homage.

kusaal: Zaba kaŋa da buon nԑ Katamansu ka ba da zabi kpie Dodowa.
english: This was the battle of Katamansu near Dodowa.

kusaal: Dabisa pisnaasi ka Odwira festival nyaan paae la, nidib pʋ maan kʋya bԑԑ tʋkpiidig ya'asi bԑ Akuapem sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.
english: For forty days preceding the Odwira festival, there is a ban on all forms of noisemaking and funerals across Akuapem.

kusaal: Odwira anԑ malʋŋ kanԑ ka ba sak ye li anԑ piini kanԑ ka ba yaanam tisiba ye ba maal.
english: The ancestors (Nananom), for whom the path has been ceremonially cleared for, are considered to spiritually join the Odwira.

kusaal: Dabisir kaŋa daar, nidib banԑ bԑ Akropong wʋsa la'asid taaba kumm.
english: Beginning at dawn, the memory of all Ancestors (Nananom) and all citizens from every household in Akropong who have died over the preceding year are honoured.

kusaal: Okuapeman nidib la si'ak ye Wina'am tita'ar bԑ ka tisid o pʋ'ʋsʋm bԑdigʋ, ba mԑ pa'an ye ba si'ak ka dͻl li ba na'ab kanԑ zin'i Ofori Kuma na'am kʋk zug la.
english: Okuapeman practically believes in the supreme God and while they offer thanksgiving to him, they also affirm their loyalty to the Omanhene – occupant of the Ofori Kuma stool.

kusaal: Alasid daar la, onԑ an 'Krontihene' tis Akuapem na la'as na'anam la ka li pa'al ye Odwira Festival naar bԑn ni lal.
english: On Sunday, the 'Krontihene' of Akuapem holds a special durbar as part of the Odwira Festival and to climax the festival.

kusaal: Dabisir kaŋa an dabisir kanԑ ka malima wʋsa naad.
english: This day essentially climaxes the rites and traditions of the celebration.

kusaal: Augustine Collins Ntim an wadmaani tis constituency la.
english: He succeeded Augustine Collins Ntim who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament.

kusaal: Kofi Konadu Apraku nɔbir zi'eni tis constituency la 4th Republic parliament la ni.
english: He succeeded Augustine Collins Ntim who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament.

kusaal: Offinso South constituency bɛnɛ Offinso districti bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Offinso South is located in the Offinso district of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: By-election kanɛ ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ nwadis piiga la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar la ni, Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) na'anya'ad, Owusu Achaw Duah, da di gaadi o taaba la nɛ vɔɔt tusa piiga nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (10,097) ka lieb wadmaan.
english: At the by-election held on 24 October 2006, the New Patriotic Party (NPP) candidate, Owusu Achaw Duah, won the seat with a majority of 10,097.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk bɛnɛ Offinso district linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim pʋʋgin, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Offinso district of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah an wadmaan tis constituency la.
english: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti o dɔlisid New Patriotic Party (NPP) ni.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug 7th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana daba ayopɔi yiiga nwadis piinɛ ayi' la ni yʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni.
english: He had represented the constituency in the 7th parliament of the 4th Republic held on the 7th of December 2016.

kusaal: Emmanuel Marfo an wadmaani tis Oforikrom Constituency linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Oforikrom is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ohenɛ Djan da an Ghana nid yiiga minister of sports bɛ Central Organisation of Sports (COS) ka da lɛm anɛ vice president tis Confederation of African Football.
english: He was the First Director (Minister) of Sports of Ghana at the Central Organisation of Sports (COS) and was also vice-president of the Confederation of African Football.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ Yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisinɛ anaasi la ni yiiga nwadig la dab pisinɛ awai daar, o duadib da anɛ Mankrado Kwafo Kraba onɛ paasa ayi la nɛ Aberewatia Juliana Yaa Amponsah Otoo alias Yaa Gyinae.
english: Ohene Djan was born on 29 January 1924 as one of the children of Mankrado Kwafo Kraba II and Aberewatia Juliana Yaa Amponsah Otoo alias Yaa Gyinae both from Aburi, Eastern Region.

kusaal: O da pinli keŋ sakur nɛ Aburi Presbyterian Primary School nɛ Aburi Methodist Boardiŋ School.
english: His education begun at the Aburi Presbyterian Primary School and Aburi Methodist Boarding School.

kusaal: On da naae anina la ka keŋ Accra Academy ya'as ka da naae anina yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ atan la ni.
english: He later continued to the Accra Academy where he obtained his secondary education, completing in 1943.

kusaal: Yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinnɛ vɔɔtʋg saŋa ka o da zi'en CPP ni ka ba da gaŋi o yɛ o an Member of Legislative Assembly ntis Akuapem-Nɛw Juaben on da nyaŋi gaad Edward Akufo Addo vɔt ban pinnɛ ayi yit vɔt ban piswai nɛ ayɔpoi la.
english: In the 1951 general elections he stood on the ticket of the CPP and was elected as Member of the Legislative Assembly for the Akuapem-New Juaben beating Edward Akufo-Addo by 97 to 12 votes.

kusaal: Yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpoi nwadisa awai la ka ba da vɔɔt Djan yɛ o an Genɛral Secretary tis nɛ Ghana Amateur Football Association (GAFA).
english: In September 1957, Djan was elected General Secretary of a new Ghana Amateur Football Association (GAFA).

kusaal: O tʋʋm kaŋa nwa saŋa da gat Richard Akwei naasi sɔb onɛ an council nidib Accra ka da an kpɛɛm Football ni sankani ka Ghana da nam an Gold Coast la yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayi hali nɛ yʋʋm bani gaad.
english: He had led a revolution that had toppled the administration of Richard Akwei, a respected councillor of Accra, who had ruled football in Ghana, then known as Gold Coast officially since 1952 and unofficially for some years before then.

kusaal: Djan da sin'iŋ Ghana Nation Team kani an Black Stars, ka da nɔki li la'as nɛ FIFA yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii nɛ CAF yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobʋ.
english: Djan founded the Black Stars, Ghana's famous national team, and he strategically affiliated the Association with FIFA in 1958 and the CAF in 1960.

kusaal: O da mukidnɛ yɛ o nyɛ sʋŋiri tis Ghana FA Cup yiiga dim la Merrs R.R. Hardiŋ ni, nɛ company si'eba.
english: He was instrumental in securing sponsorship for the first Ghanaian FA Cup competition from a pharmaceutical firm, Merrs R.R. Harding and Company.

kusaal: O da nyaŋi mɔr Coach George Ainsley nyi zin'siana yɛ o bɛ national team la ni yuum kan.
english: He succeeded in securing the services of an expatriate Coach, George Ainsley, for the National Team in that same year.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da dʋ'ʋs Djan yɛ o an Director of Sports, bɔɔl wʋsa kpɛɛm Ghana teŋbaŋ.
english: In July 1960, Ghana's first President, Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, elevated Djan to the ministerial portfolio of 'Director of Sports', the overall boss of sports administration in Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ da an kpɛɛm Central Organisation of Sports (COS) paal kani ka di yʋ'ʋr yʋn an Ministry of Youth and Sports (Ghana) la.
english: He was in charge of the newly created Central Organisation of Sports (COS) (now the Ministry of Youth and Sports (Ghana)), a sports ministry-like organization.

kusaal: O da muki suŋ ka Ghana paam suor yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ atan African Cup of Nations dinni ka Black Stars da di (hali ka Black Stars da lɛm keŋ tuoni di cup la Tunisia yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ anu Djan saŋa).
