english: Djan's reputation grew on the continent, his lobbying helped Ghana gain the hosting rights for the 1963 African Cup of Nations which the Black Stars won (the Black Stars went on to defend the trophy in Tunisia in 1965 under his tenure of leadership).

kusaal: O da yɛli Nkrumah yɛ o tis cup bani ka ba buon yɛ CAF Champions League la.
english: He also suggested to Nkrumah to donate a trophy for a tournament that is now known as the CAF Champions League.

kusaal: Ba da keŋ CAF di'ema la'asig Addis Ababa ka o di'e onɛ paasa ayi nyaŋi gɔsi bɔɔl yɛla ka ba da gaŋ o yɛ CAF president Ydnekatchew Tessema Ethiopia yaa kai onɛ bɛ, yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ atan la ni yiiga nwadig la yiiga dabisir.
english: At a CAF extraordinary assembly in Addis Ababa he became second in command of the continent's highest football administrative body, emerging as CAF vice president alongside Ethiopia's Ydnekatchew Tessema in January, 1963.

kusaal: Babayi nwa da tʋmidnɛ ka CAF president bɛ Egypt ka o yʋ'ʋr an Abdel Aziz Moustafa gɔsi li wʋsa.
english: They both served under Egyptian Abdel Aziz Moustafa, the CAF president.

kusaal: Sir Stanley Rous da an FIFA president sankan ka da nyɛ Djan ka o an onɛ mi bɔɔll nwɛ'ɛb zin'ig wʋsa.
english: Sir Stanley Rous, FIFA's president then, described Djan as a 'valued' player at the World football governing body.

kusaal: Ghana da maal nɛ silver medal yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu summer Olympics kati'waanɛ Clement Quartey onɛ da Africa wusa yiiga da die Olympic medalist.
english: Ghana produced a silver medalist at the 1960 Summer Olympics in the name of Clement Quartey he became the first black African olympic medalist.

kusaal: Ghana mɛ da an teŋ kani di medals nam bedigu yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayi British Empire and Commonwealth Games ni.
english: Ghana was also the African country that won the most medals in the 1962 British Empire and Commonwealth Games.

kusaal: Yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ anaasi FIFA da gba'e nɛ yɛ team nam piinɛ ayuobu la na an Europe team nam piiga lam nɛ Eŋland lokani ka ba da yɛ ba nwe' la , Latin American nama anaasi (South America) team nɛ team yinni Central America nɛ Caribbean soolim.
english: In January 1964, FIFA decided that the 16-team finals would consist of 10 European teams, including hosts England, four South American teams, and one team from the Central American and Caribbean region, thus leaving only one place for three continents: Africa, Asia and Oceania.

kusaal: Portugal Eusebio onɛ ka ba da dua o Mozambique da an onɛ da di goal nami gaad so wusa.
english: Moreover, Portugal's Eusébio, who was actually born in Mozambique (a Portuguese colony at the time), finished as top scorer.

kusaal: Ban da naae la FIFA da gbaenɛ yɛ Africa na nwe noor ayinni ba yaa ti lem mor World Cup Mexico.
english: In 1968, FIFA unianimously decided that Africa would have one place for the next World Cup in Mexico.

kusaal: Ghana zin'ig kani ka ba nwɛ'ɛd ball Accra Sports Stadium la da putnɛ o yuurin yɛ li tenr on maal siel teŋ nwa ball yɛla la.
english: Ghana's national stadium the Accra Sports Stadium is named after him in recognition of his contribution to sports in the country.

kusaal: Ohene Djan Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisinɛ anaasi la ni yiiga nwadig la dab pisinɛ awai daar ka o da kpi Yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni nwadisa atan la ni dab pisinɛ ayuobu.
english: Ohene Djan (29 January 1924 – 26 March 1987) was a Ghanaian sports administrator and politician.

kusaal: O da anɛ kpɛɛm Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdiben.
english: He was the First Director (Minister) of Sports of Ghana at the Central Organisation of Sports (COS) and was also vice-president of the Confederation of African Football.

kusaal: On da naae secondary school la ka dɔli o saami tumid cocoa tʋʋma.
english: After his secondary school education, he joined his father in his cocoa business.

kusaal: O da tʋmnɛ o saam nɛ yʋʋm yinnɛ ka bas ka keŋ civil service an second division clerk.
english: He worked with his father for a year and joined the civil service as a second division clerk.

kusaal: Yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu ka o da kilim CPP nid, party kani ka Kwame Nkrumah da an gɔmina yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinni la kɛŋi paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayuobu da maal.
english: In 1950, Djan became an active member of the CPP; the political party founded by Kwame Nkrumah, the Ghanaian government head from 1951 to 1966.

kusaal: Parliament ni, ba da gaŋ Djan yɛ o an Deputy Minister of Finance.
english: In parliament, Djan was appointed Ministerial Secretary (deputy minister) to the Ministry of Finance.

kusaal: O da bɛ office kan nii keŋ paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi on da bas parliament nɛ ligidi fiin pian.ad ka ba da pian'a ziili o.
english: He held that office until 1954 when he left Parliament due to corruption charges that were levelled against him.

kusaal: Yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii o da lɛm nyaŋi organize yiiga national league ka Ghana naan kilim di mɛŋ teŋ gʋn yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu yiiiga dabisir nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: In 1958, he succeeded again in organizing the first national league, before Ghana became a republic on 1 July 1960.

kusaal: Yuma tusir nɛ kɔbuswai nɛ pisyuobu nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni ka Ghana yiiga gɔmina Dr.
english: In 1958, he succeeded again in organizing the first national league, before Ghana became a republic on 1 July 1960.

kusaal: Djan da bas GAFA ban da dʋ'ʋsʋ agɔla la yɛla amaa o da nan kpɛn tumnɛ di Genɛral Secretary tʋʋma.
english: Although Djan left his GAFA chairmanship post due to this promotion, he continued to play a key role as General Secretary.

kusaal: Li yʋʋm kani gaad la ka ba da gaŋ Djan paas FIFA Executive Committee kani yʋn an FIFA Executive Council la.
english: A year earlier, Djan had been voted unto the powerful FIFA Executive Committee (now known as the FIFA Executive Council).

kusaal: Djan da moor yam kani na naŋi ti'as sienam Nkrumah gomena saŋa la ka National Liberation Council da kadu nidibin laasig.
english: Due to the influential role he played in Nkrumah's government, Djan was banned from public activities by the National Liberation Council, the military junta that undertook the coup of 1966, thus resulting in a loss of his place on the FIFA Executive Committee and subsequently, at CAF too.

kusaal: Ohenɛ Djan da yɛl FIFA yɛ ba maligim gba'e gbaar la ka di pu nar ka Afro-Asia dim namisi zamisi ba ball nwe'eb ka mi nwe'eb kaba yɛt yɛ ba moor slot ayinni.
english: Within a month, Djan, a member of the FIFA executive committee, sent a telegram to FIFA condemning the decision and calling it "pathetic", also challenging FIFA to reconsider the decision on the grounds that arranging a play-off between the best teams from Asia, Oceania and Africa for one place would be onerously expensive and fraught with logistical difficulties.

kusaal: Tessema da dol Djan ka ba moor yɛlig nwa yi Africa kiŋ tis FIFA, ka yɛti ba yɛ ball Africa nwa ni nobigidnɛ yuum wusa, dinzuk ban mukid yɛ ba maal dinni na suŋi ba meŋ la na niŋ zaalim.
english: Tessema then joined Djan to present Africa's case to FIFA, also arguing that the standard of football in Africa had significantly improved over the years.

kusaal: Zina Africa team nam la yun nwɛ'ɛd nɛ nɛ World Cup slot nama anu.
english: In 1968, FIFA unianimously decided that Africa would have one place for the next World Cup in Mexico.

kusaal: Okaikwei South constituency anɛ constituency nam la yinne bɛ Ghana wadmaanib yin la.Ba vɔɔdir gaŋir nid yinne ka o an wadmaan ka li dɔlisid vɔɔdʋg wada.Okaikwei South bɛnɛ Accra Metropolitan Assembly linɛ bɛ Accra Region titaˈar sʋˈʋlʋmin la.
english: Okaikwei South is located in the Accra Metropolitan Assembly of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di'e nɛ Brandford Kwame Daniel Adu onɛ da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug 4th Republic parliament dɔlisidnɛ New Patriotic Party la san'an.
english: He succeeded Dan Botwe who had represented the constituency in the 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th Republic parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Daniel Botwe an wadmaan tis constituency la ka lɛm an Minister for Local Government nɛ Rural Development.
english: He succeeded Dan Botwe who had represented the constituency in the 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th Republic parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o dɔlisidnɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ka o da di vɔɔt nam tusa piinɛ yinne, nɛ kɔbʋswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi ka di pa,al ye o mɔr 60.83% vɔɔt la ka o da kilim wadmaan.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) in 2024 and won with a total number of 9,080 votes representing 68.43% of the vote cast to become the MP.

kusaal: Ba nya'adnɛ Access Division One Bank League la.
english: They are competing in the Division One League.

kusaal: Ba mɛŋ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb zin'ig anɛ Nkawkaw bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb zin'igin la.
english: Okwawu United is a Ghanaian professional football club based in Nkawkaw, Eastern Region.

kusaal: Nwɛnɛ nidib la'aʋŋ kanɛ pʋ nyaŋ sɔbi li du'am nɛ li nɔbigir yɛla niŋ gbaʋŋʋn ka ba zi' ba yɛla si'em la, ala mɛn ka ba zi' Okwawu United labaar nwa vikkiinɛ kat wa'anɛ din si'iŋ si'em.
english: Okwawu United is a Ghanaian professional football club based in Nkawkaw, Eastern Region.

kusaal: Pʋtɛn'ɛkanɛ paasi ayi la anɛ ye Okwawu United nɔbʋgʋ yinɛ fourth division tiim kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon ye YOUNG AFRICANS.
english: Okwawu United is a Ghanaian professional football club based in Nkawkaw, Eastern Region.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (1974) la ni, ba da zin'in naalʋg la'asʋg tis Executives of Okwahu Stores, Super Obuoma nɛ Young Africans bɛ Nkawkaw topway ye di sʋŋi bu'oe sam kanɛ ka kilab banɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm kan la wʋsa nwɛ'ɛd la.
english: Okwawu United is a Ghanaian professional football club based in Nkawkaw, Eastern Region.

kusaal: Alhaji Osei da siakya ka lieb kilab la kʋkdaan ka di yinnɛ Eastern Regional sports organizer H.A. Asamoah, da tik nu'ug la, ka ba yʋ'ʋn tiak Young Africans yʋ'ʋri siki di KWAHU UNITED bɛ 15 Sigir 1975 ka mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr ye ba na paam sʋŋir yi nimbanɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni.
english: Okwawu United is a Ghanaian professional football club based in Nkawkaw, Eastern Region.

kusaal: Vincent Ekow Assafuah an wadmaani tis constituency la nananna.
english: Vincent Ekow Assafuah is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: O da zi'ennɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug ka di' na'am la yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nwadis piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋg la ni tis Old Tafo Constituency.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and won the 2020 December parliamentary elections for the Old Tafo Constituency.

kusaal: O da diya' nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisnaasi, kɔbis yuobʋ nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (42,616) ka da gaadi o taaba la, o vɔɔt la da zɛm nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi, du'al pisnu nɛ anu, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (74.55%) ka onɛ da ti'al o la, Sahmudeen Mohammed Kamil onɛ da zi'en Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug la mɛ da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anaasi, kɔbisnaasi nɛ anu (14,405), din anɛ vɔɔt pisi nɛ anu du'al pisi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (25.20%).
english: He was declared the winner with 42,616 votes representing 74.55% against his closest contender Sahmudeen Mohammed Kamil of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) who had 14,405 votes representing 25.20%.

kusaal: Omo tuo (Twi: ɛmo tuo; "mui gbila") anԑ Ghana diib kanԑ ka ba nͻk mui maal.
english: Omo tuo (Twi: ɛmo tuo; "rice balls") is a Ghanaian staple food made with rice.

kusaal: Nigeria dim Hausa buudi buoni li ye Tuwon Shinkafa, anina ka ba paam "Tuwo" linԑ ka ba mͻri buon "Tuwo Zaafi", linԑ an Ghana dim diib yinnԑ ya'as linԑ yi Hausa buudi ni.
english: It is a Ghanaian version of the Nigerian Hausa staple Tuwon Shinkafa, which provides the name "Tuwo" used in this dish and in "Tuwo Zaafi", another popular Ghanaian dish with Hausa origins.

kusaal: Opemso Festival anԑ malʋŋ kanԑ ka ba maan yʋʋma ayi' wʋsa bԑ Ghana ye ba zanbil Otumfuo Osei Tutu I, Ashantis na'ab kanԑ da an yiiga daan la dʋ'am.
english: The Opemso Festival is a biennial festival held in Ghana to commemorate the iconic birth of Otumfuo Osei Tutu I, the first king of the Ashantis.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la saŋa, nidib la maan di'ema dͻlisid bʋnlinԑ da maal ka ba nyaan dʋ'a Tutu la yiiga ka nyaan kԑŋ kԑŋ paae zin'ig kanԑ ka tiis la'as ka ba buon Teneabasaso bԑԑ Kwantakese zin'ig kanԑ ka ba da dʋ'a o ka ba buon ye Kokofu-Anyinam kali bԑ Ashanti Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: During the festival, events that led to Tutu's birth are mimicked until the final rites are performed in the Teneabasaso or Kwantakese sacred grove where he was born at Kokofu-Anyinam in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Biig la dʋ'am saŋa da paad la, Osei Tutu ma da kԑŋ o yaab pʋ'a san'ani bԑ Esiase linԑ bԑ Ashanti Region.
english: When his birth was due, Osei Tutu's mother journeyed to his grandmother's hometown at Esiase in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Li da anԑ Arizum daar, lin ka ba da pʋd o Kofi.
english: It was on a Friday, hence his name Kofi.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la an nimmua hali tis Ashanti nidib la bͻzugͻ na'ab la da tis Asante nidib ti'ir ka ba nyԑ yͻlisim yi Gyamans nԑ Denkyiras nu'usin.
english: The festival is very important to the Ashanti people because the birth of the king gave the Asante people hope of freedom from the Gyamans and Denkyiras.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la maalig saŋa, Ashantis nidib la tusa-tusa nԑ ba na'anam wʋsa la'asid taaba ka onԑ gati ba tuon an Asantehene bԑԑ onԑ ka o gaŋ ye o di'e o nͻbiri gaad tuon, ba dͻlisid suori kԑn wala ti paad zin'ig kanԑ ka ba da dʋ'a ba yiiga na'ab la.
english: During the festival commemoration, thousands of Ashantis and their kings led by the Asantehene or his representative walks via the street to the sacred grove where their first king was born.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr kanԑ ka ba da tis Otumfuo Osei Tutu I yiiga ye Opemso la anԑ yʋ'ʋr kanԑ ka ba tisid Ashanti na'anam ka li pa'al ye ba mͻr paŋ ka pʋ zͻt dabi'em.
english: The title Opemso, first given to Otumfuo Osei Tutu I, is given to Ashanti kings to indicate a fearless and persistent nature in executing plans without giving in to any obstacles.

kusaal: Tiis zin'igin la ba buon ye Teneabasaso bͻzugͻ, ba si'ak ye Otumfuo Osei Tutu I ma da gban'a nԑ kikaŋ tili zanl ka ʋnsi dʋa o.
english: The sacred grove is called Teneabasaso because it is said that the mother of Otumfuo Osei Tutu I held the branches of the Ceiba tree in pushing hard to deliver him.

kusaal: Ba lԑn buon tiis zin'igin la sansi'eba nԑ ye Kwantakese bͻzugͻ, Ashanti nidib la si'ak ye suor kanԑ dͻlididi wa'ae zin'ig kanԑ ka ba da dʋa ba na'ab la anԑ suor kanԑ mͻr paŋ.
english: The sacred grove is sometimes also called Kwantakese because the Ashanti people assert that the road to where their monarch was delivered is a great path.

kusaal: Ba maan Opemso festival malʋŋ la ye ba zanbil nԑ ba na'ab tita'ar kanԑ da an yiiga daan ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Otumfuo Osei Tutu I la dʋ'am dabisir ba tisid o girima bͻzugͻ, ba siak ye onԑ da la'as Akan buudi ayͻpͻi ka ba kilim na'am sʋ'ʋm Asante Kingdom.
english: The Opemso festival is celebrated to mark the events that led to the birth of the first king of the Ashanti people, Otumfuo Osei Tutu I who is credited to have united the seven Akan clans to form the Asante Kingdom.Oral tradition has it that Nana Gyamfua Manu Kutusi, the mother of Otumfuo Osei Tutu I, desperately needed a child but her efforts proved futile after experiencing several miscarriages.

kusaal: Sͻlima pʋʋgin, ba pa'al ye Nana Gyamfua Manu Kutusi, onԑ da an Otumfuo Osei Tutu I ma da pʋ paam biiga ka muk hali gʋ'ʋŋ, o pʋʋg da ԑԑnti kpa'ae nԑ.
english: The Opemso festival is celebrated to mark the events that led to the birth of the first king of the Ashanti people, Otumfuo Osei Tutu I who is credited to have united the seven Akan clans to form the Asante Kingdom.Oral tradition has it that Nana Gyamfua Manu Kutusi, the mother of Otumfuo Osei Tutu I, desperately needed a child but her efforts proved futile after experiencing several miscarriages.

kusaal: Tiim daan sͻ' da bԑ Awukugua linԑ bԑ Akuapim district linԑ bԑ Eastern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka da an ba'akͻlig daani bԑ Tutu bada ni la da sʋŋ o siig pʋʋgin ye o paam dasaŋ.
english: Finally, a traditional priest at Awukugua in the Akuapim district in Eastern Region of Ghana who serves the Tutu deity helped her spiritually to conceive a male child.

kusaal: Ba da mͻr o kԑŋ paae onԑ da an pʋ'ana'ab tis Kokofu-Anyinam ka o da mͻr o kԑŋ zin'ig kanԑ an sʋ'ʋŋa guŋ tiig tita'ar gbinin.
english: They took her to the then queenmother of Kokofu-Anyinam who took her to a safe spot under a big Ceiba or Onyina tree that is now called Onyina Sei.

kusaal: Nidib la nԑ saam banԑ bԑ malʋŋ la ni wʋsa zienԑ yi'iŋi gur ka maanmaanib la nԑ na'anam banԑ bԑ Anyinam-Kokofu na'am sʋ'ʋlim la paae zin'igin la maal malima banԑ bԑ la ka lԑb na, bͻzugͻ li anԑ kisig nԑ banԑ pʋ paas na'am tʋ'ʋŋin la na yaki ba nͻbiri kpԑn'ԑ zin'igin la.
english: The jubilant crowd of residents and visitors then wait at the entrance of the sacred grove for the traditional priests, chiefs and elders in the traditional council of Anyinam-Kokofu to perform the required rituals in the sacred grove since it is a taboo for non-royals to enter the grove.

kusaal: Ba mͻr di'em sia ka ba buon "Miss Opemso" ka mͻr yʋʋma nԑ wa'a nya'ab, dʋgʋb, buudi fuud yԑԑb nya'ab nԑ malima baŋir nya'ab kati wa'ae ba si'ilima pʋʋgin, ba maan di'ema bama wʋsa.
english: A beauty pageant dubbed "Miss Opemso" as well as singing and dancing competitions, cooking, traditional cloth wearing competition and a cultural knowledge quiz on proverbs are carried out as part of the event.

kusaal: Ba mͻr malima bama ka li maligim tԑndigidi ba Ashantis nidib la ba malima yela ka ba biis mԑ zamisid.
english: These performances are used as a means of reviving the cultural values of the Ashantis while teaching children and visitors the rich cultural heritage of the Ashanti people.

kusaal: Ba maan malʋŋ nԑ yʋʋma ayi' wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: The festival is observed once every two years.

kusaal: Malima la ya'a maali naae, linԑ kpԑlim anԑ ye ba la'as taaba nwԑ'ԑd bʋnwԑ'ԑda ka wa'ad ka maan sʋmmalisim.
english: After a successful performance, drumming, dancing, merry making continues.

kusaal: Open University of West Africa (OUWA) anɛ John Roberts nɛ Patrick Steele da bɔɔ li zi'el Ghana, Sapal nwadig la, 2011 yʋʋm la ni.
english: Open University of West Africa (OUWA) was founded in Ghana in November 2011 by John Roberts and Patrick Steele.

kusaal: John Roberts nɛ o tiraan la da paam kpɛmsʋg nɛ yɛl bama nwa ni: saŋkan la, sakur titada ken zin'igin Africa da pɔɔd nɛ hali, university sʋma banɛ bɛɛ gilig dunia wʋsa la da pin'in ye ba zaŋi ba zamisa namɛ dɔlis pɛbisimin woo Coursera, edX, Udacity, nɛ sieba ya'as.
english: With the goal to break the poverty cycle in West Africa through online education, John Roberts and his co-founder were inspired by a simple but contradictory observation: at the moment, higher education penetration in Africa was very low, many of the best universities around the world were beginning to put their courses online through platforms like Coursera, edX, Udacity etc.

kusaal: Pʋtɛn'ɛr nwa da kɛ ka nidiba ayi banɛ zi'el sakur la da maal Open Education Resources (OER), kɛ ka mobile technology paamʋg an na'anaa, ka mukʋd hali ye nidib ken sakuri laligid West Africa teŋgbaʋŋ pʋʋgin.
english: The two founders became driven by the idea of harnessing this "perfect storm" of free Open Educational Resources (OER), cheaper access to mobile technology, and the profound need to spur development through higher-ed in West African countries.

kusaal: Ban da yɔ'ɔg 'internet café of education' Accra pʋʋgin, Ghana la nya'aŋ, OUWA da pin'ili nɛ sakur bibis 40 nɛ nya'aŋ, banɛ da ken zamisa.
english: After opening an 'internet café of education' in Accra, Ghana, OUWA began with more than 40 students attending the courses.

kusaal: Yʋʋm nɛ pʋsʋk pʋʋgin ban da yɔ'ɔgi li la, OUWA da mɔr woo sakur bibis 200.
english: A year and a half into launch, OUWA had around 200 students.

kusaal: Nɛŋa pa'al ye Sub-Saharan Africa teŋgbaʋŋ da mɔr sakur bibis bɛdigʋ banɛ da kpɛn'ɛd MOOCs sankan la.
english: This represented the largest concentration of students accessing MOOCs in Sub-Saharan African.

kusaal: Entrepreneurship zamisa da bɛ, Computer Science zamisa, General Education, ka li wʋsa yit nɛ Coursera nɛ Udacity ni.
english: There were courses on Entrepreneurship, Computer Science, General education all drawn from Coursera and Udacity.

kusaal: Kpimsig: Ba dɔlis nɛ malima nam wʋʋ Startup West Africa (SWA), ka gaŋ kpikpiʋŋ banɛ an sʋm ka na nyaŋi zi'en.
english: Invest: Through events like Startup West Africa (SWA), talented judging panels selected the business ideas with the most potential.

kusaal: Li na an teŋgbauŋ la kpikpiʋŋ paala la yigilʋŋ titada la yinne, Apps for Africa, ba da gaŋi ba ka tisi ba ligiid $10,000 ka ba keŋ New York ye ba yɔ'ɔg NYSE.
english: One of the largest start-up competitions on the continent, Apps for Africa, selected them to be given $10,000 funding and travel to New York for the opening of NYSE.

kusaal: Si'ir kanɛ ka ya'am paala dim da mɔri tʋm la, Open University of West Africa la'am nɛ Slice Bis, da pin'il ya maal HUB Accra, banɛ na tʋm nɛ ba ka li na sʋŋi kɛ ka kpikpiuŋ kanɛ ka Africa nidib sʋ'oe la bɔbig.
english: With the momentum created by these early innovators, Open University of West Africa, along with SliceBiz, spearheaded the creation of HUB Accra, a co-working space devoted solely to helping African-led businesses flourish.

kusaal: "innovation hub" kanɛ bɛ zin'ig wʋsa la, Impact HUB da di'e li tɔ'ɔtɔ "Impact Hub Accra" ka li an suor kanɛ ba na la'as ka dɔlisi sʋŋ ka kpikpiuŋ paala la bɛ Accra La keŋ tuon.
english: A worldwide network of "innovation hubs", Impact Hub quickly adopted "Impact Hub Accra" as its way to partner in the accelerating startup ecosystem in Accra.

kusaal: Gambia pʋʋginɛɛ, OUWA da mɔr zamisʋg kanɛ ka ba zanl primary sakur pa'annib banɛ da gaad 20.
english: In Gambia, OUWA ran a successful teacher training program with over 20 primary school teachers.

kusaal: Linɛ pɛ'ɛs EFL zamisʋg la ni, ba da maan suoya ye ba pin'il Physician Assistant Program zamisʋg.
english: In addition to the EFL curriculum program, headways were made in the conception of a physician Assistant program.

kusaal: Li da naamɛ refugees nam zin'is la ayi' ni, Western sʋ'ʋlim Ghana pʋʋgin: Ampain nɛ Krisan.
english: It was carried out in two refugee camps in the Western region of Ghana: Ampain and Krisan.

kusaal: Pa'alʋg nwa ni, OUWA da la'am tʋmmɛ nɛ École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) Swiss teŋgbauŋ dakur kanɛ nyɛ na'asi kpikpiuŋ yɛla tʋʋma zin'igin.
english: For this pilot, OUWA partnered with École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) a Swiss federal institute revered in entrepreneurship.

kusaal: Open University of West Africa bɛ Ghana (OUWA) pʋʋgin la, ka zamisʋg la yɔɔb zin'igin anɛ na'anaa hali (US$10/yʋʋma), ka lɛn kpɛmisid sakur bibis la yinne yinne ye ba lieb banɛ na zi tiakiri kena ba mɔɔr nwa pʋʋgin.
english: Located in Ghana, Open University of West Africa (OUWA) provided extremely low-cost education (US$10/year), while also encouraging each student to become an agent of change in this fight.

kusaal: West Africa pʋʋginɛɛ, sakur bibis banɛ laligi kpɛn' sakur titada an 10%, ka nɔŋ daamid nidib bɛdigʋ bɛlim.
english: In West Africa, less than 10% of students are enrolled in an institution of higher education, and extreme poverty is a life-threatening reality for many.

kusaal: La'am nɛ West Africa gɔbna namɛ mɔɔ maal suoya ye sakur ken an na'anaa la, tiakir kae pa'an ye zamisʋg zin'igin la ken sʋ'ʋŋa Africa teŋgbaʋŋ pʋʋginɛ.
english: Despite some efforts by West African governments to expand educational opportunities, there are no tangible improvements in the field of education in this region of Africa. Simple efforts to increase the number of people enrolled in schools have not solved the problem.

kusaal: Bɛdigʋ banɛ da bɔɔd sakur ken yam da gban'ae Open University of West Africa.
english: Open University of West Africa attracted numerous potential students.

kusaal: Yam kaŋa ka sakur bibids la da zaŋ la, da lieb nɛ yɛlkpanɛ tis banɛ la'am da pɛ'ɛsi sʋ'oe sakur la zi'elʋg la da zaŋ "Educate-Incubate-Invest" kpikpiŋ tʋʋma kanɛ da ye la lieb yɔ'ɔgir la yɛlkpan zamisʋg kanɛ na pɛ'ɛsa ayi la "sakur paal" nwa ni.
english: This very natural student-led idea became an essential pivot-point for the co-founders leading to the "Educate– Incubate– Invest" business model that was to become the launching point for the next phase of this pioneering "new school".

kusaal: OUWA unib zin'igin la pʋtɛn'ɛr da gban'ae ya zi'el West African setup ecosystem.
english: The incubation component of OUWA's vision consisted of building the West African startup ecosystem.

kusaal: Ka na zaŋ ligidi sʋŋi li yɔ'ɔgir ka li ya'a zi'eni naae, pʋdigir 10% na keŋ tis OUWA.
english: Then, seed funding would help launch the startups in exchange for around 10% equity stake to OUWA.

kusaal: Banɛ da sʋŋi zi'el OUWA la da gɔsi nyɛ ka Slice Biz n da an kpikpiʋŋ paala la yinne, kanɛ ka ba na yɔ'ɔg.
english: SliceBiz became one of the most visible start-ups to be launched by OUWA co-founders.

kusaal: ban an banɛ ye ba sʋŋ kpikpiuŋ paala kpikpiuŋ zin'igin la, Impact Hub Accra Impact Hub Accra mɛ da gɔsid malim bɛda tisid kpikpinnib buudi buudi.
english: As a convener in the startup ecosystem, Impact Hub Accra also curates special events and experiences for and with different stakeholders.

kusaal: Hub nwa anɛ yiiga tʋʋm kanɛ ka Open University of West Africa da dɛŋi tʋm la.
english: As a convener in the startup ecosystem, Impact Hub Accra also curates special events and experiences for and with different stakeholders.

kusaal: Ba da mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr sʋŋ kanɛ na siei ka ka sa'am nɔŋ baŋ kanɛ lɔbi gɛɛl, cycle of poverty, OUWA da tʋm ya ka li sʋŋ ka sakur nɛ da an yɔn ka an sʋ'ʋm la nyɛ paŋ, ka li ka'ae nɛ Accra an Ghana tempʋ tita'ar la ma'aa nii.
english: With a clear vision to reduce and break the cycle of poverty, OUWA contributed to the flourishing of affordable access to quality education not only in the capital city Accra in Ghana.

kusaal: Zamisa zin'is da bɛ Kumasi, ka ba da maan suoya nɛ nimmua ye li widigi kpɛn Gambia, nɛ mali, nɛ Burkina.
english: There were learning places in Kumasi and serious attempts to scale to Gambia, Mali, and Burkina.

kusaal: Burkina nɛ Mali, sakur la da la'am tʋmmɛ zaŋ nasaal (EFL) paas zamisa la ni, ba da maal zamisʋg la nɛ ka li na nyaŋi kɛ ka na sʋŋ banɛ zamisid nasaal ye li sʋŋi ba zamisʋg zin'igin la nyɛ sʋŋir.
english: In Burkina and Mali, the university elaborated an English as a Foreign Language (EFL) curriculum.

kusaal: Ban da dɔlisidi maan Open IDEO Challege ̶̶ ka banɛ da maali li bɛnɛ Califonia ̶ OUWA da paam tiakir kanɛ da bɛɛ li kɔn' ka da yinɛ ba da kɛ ka zamisʋg la paae refugees nam, ka kɛ ka ba paamid zamisa la ban bɛ zin'isieba la.
english: While pursuing an OpenIDEO Challenge—an international design and consulting firm based in California—OUWA's next evolution came in the unique form of how to provide education to refugees and improve learning opportunities in refugee camps.

kusaal: Open University of West Africa da pʋdig smartphone nam banɛ da mɔr kpikpiuŋ yɛla zamisʋg la'adi tis nidib banɛ da bɛ zin'i bama ni.
english: Open University of West Africa distributed smartphones pre-loaded with entrepreneurship courses and educational tools tailored to people living in these camps.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛga nwa da kɛ ka ban da giligidi pa'an sʋ'ʋlim banɛ ka nɔŋ da bɛ hali la, da bɔ nyɛdigir tis Open University of West Africa.
english: This pivot to mobile education in poorer regions turned out to be a major turning point for Open University of West Africa.

kusaal: OUWA da nyɛ yʋma anaasi gaad la, John Roberts da kena baŋ ye "linɛ na kɛ ka zʋmauŋ la paam paŋ anɛ fʋ ya'a na nyaŋi sʋŋ banɛ kuosid gabʋ suor kpʋkɛŋ ka ba paas kuosim sieba ya'as, bɛɛ ba nyaŋi baŋ linɛ na paasi ba kuosim la paŋ, ba tun'e paam ka ba ligiid na pɛ'ɛsa abʋ naasa nɛ abʋ nu yɛla.
english: After 4 years of leading OUWA, John Roberts understood that "what's going to empower the masses is if you can help the person who is selling onions on the side of the road to diversify their products or figure out a value add, they potentially start earning four to five times as much income.

kusaal: Tɛn'ɛsim gɔs onɛ kuosidi paamid dollar dabsir yinne pʋʋgin, ka yʋʋn nyaŋidi kuosidi paamid dollar anaasi dabsir yinne pʋʋginc, ala la ba tun'e keŋ sibiti ie laafi." Ba ya'a dɔlisid suor kanɛ na kɛ ka kpikpiuŋ yɛla keŋ tuon, ba na nyɛɛ li sʋ'ʋm anii ni nɔɔ.
english: Imagine someone earning a dollar a day suddenly able to earn 4 dollars a day, then they can go to a clinic and access services." There is immediate benefit when improving the naturally occurring climate of entrepreneurship.

kusaal: ka OUWA tʋʋm kpan da anɛ ba kɛ ka zamisʋg an yɔn, Invest ED na gɔs pa'alʋg kanɛ pʋ paam suorɛ, ka kɛ ka ba na zamisid ba vʋm saŋa wʋsa.
english: Invest: Through events like Startup West Africa (SWA), talented judging panels selected the business ideas with the most potential.

kusaal: OUWA bɛlim da anɛ li kɛ ka zamisʋg paae zin'i kana ka ba pʋ paamid la , ka sʋŋi kɛ ka baŋir kanɛ kpi'ilim la na yinɛ open educational resources .
english: OUWA existed with a mission to bring great education to those who lacked access and leveraged technology by being the last mile delivery system for open educational resources.

kusaal: La'amnɛ OUWA pʋ lɛn tʋm laa, ya'am kanɛ ka ba nyɛɛ yi yʋʋm anaasi kanɛ ka ba da tʋm la kɛ ya ka Invest ED paam paŋ: app kanɛ mɔr android "na mɔri pa'an banɛ zamisid kpikpiuŋ yɛla ka pʋ tun'e la, ka ba na nyaŋi kɛ ka ba ligiid yɛla zi'en sʋŋa, la ya'a dɔlis cutting-edge mobile technology".
english: Although OUWA has recently ceased operations, what was learned during the four years of blazing new trails has fueled the founding of InvestED: an android-based app "to educate struggling entrepreneurs towards financial stability via cutting-edge mobile technology."

kusaal: Ba mɔr zin'i na tis kpikpiuŋ paala, freelancer nam, maker nam, creative nam bɛɛ kpikpiuŋ kʋda dim banɛ bɔɔd zin'i sʋŋ Ye ba tʋm.
english: They have a space for startups, freelancers, makers, creatives or established businesses looking for a flexible and inspiring space.

kusaal: Tʋʋm bama nɛ teŋin kpɛm ya' kae, maalʋg kʋ bɛ.
english: Without these industry and community leaders, economic development is almost impossible.

kusaal: Ophelia Mensah Hayford anɛ Gaana Pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Ophelia Mensah Hayford is a Ghanaian Politician.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Hayford nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisuɔpɔi nɛ atan Nwadis piiga la ni dabpisi nɛ awai daar (29 October 1973), o yinɛ Akwapim-Akropong bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim,Ghana la.
english: Hayford was born on 29 October 1973 and hails from Akwapim-Akropong in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o Bachelor's degree in Political Science and Linguistics nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012).
english: She had her Bachelor's degree in Political Science and Linguistics in 2012.

kusaal: in Criminal Law; International Human Rights Law and Administrative Law yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018).
english: in Criminal Law; International Human Rights Law and Administrative Law in 2018.

kusaal: Ophelia was da anɛ Assistant superintendent of Police (ASP).
english: Ophelia was an Assistant superintendent of Police(ASP).

kusaal: O da lɛn an chief Inspector tis Ghana Police Service.
english: She was the chief Inspector with the Ghana Police Service.

kusaal: Ophelia Hayford da lɛn tʋm nɛ Interpol Unit at the CID Headquarters.
english: Ophelia Hayford also worked with Interpol Unit at the CID Headquarters.

kusaal: O sid kanɛ da kpi la, Ekow Hayford da anɛ Wadmaani, tisi Mfantsiman Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: Her late husband, Ekow Hayford was the Member of parliament for Mfantsiman Constituency.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi (December 2020) vɔɔtʋgin laa, ba da vɔɔt o ye lieb Wadmaani tis Mfantsiman Constituency on da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg zugʋ, New Patriotic Party nya' la ka di.
english: In December 2020, she was elected member of Parliament for Mfantsiman Constituency after she competed in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election under the ticket of the New Patriotic Party and won.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ anii nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (36,091) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'al pisnii nɛ atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.83%).
english: She polled 36,091 votes which represents 51.83% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ka bas, James Essuon onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid la nɛ Alijatu Ibrahim onɛ an Ghana Union Movement nid la.
english: She was elected over James Essuon of the National Democratic Congress and Alijatu Ibrahim of the Ghana Union Movement.

kusaal: Bama da paamnɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ ayi, kɔbistan nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (32,379) nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piinɛ yinne (911).
english: These obtained 32,379 and 911 votes respectively out of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Hayford anɛ kʋkdaan nya'andɔli tis la'askanɛ gɔsid Defense and Interior la ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid ya yɛla la.
english: Hayford is the Vice chairperson for the Defense and Interior Committee and also a member of the House Committee.

kusaal: O da nya' la ka 2020 Gaana Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg ka di Mfantsiman Constituency sʋ'ʋlim kʋk la.
english: She contested in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election and won the parliamentary seat for the Mfantsiman Constituency.

kusaal: O tʋmi o pʋlis tʋʋmnɛ yʋʋma pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (27 years).
english: And since then, she has served in the service for 27 years.

kusaal: Hayford anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party nid.
english: Hayford is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O sid la kum nya'aŋ, on da nan an pʋliŋ la, o da gban'eya ye o na di'e o sid nɔbir lieb Wadmaani tis Mfantsiman Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: After the death of her husband while serving in office, she decided to replace him as the Member of parliament for the Mfantsiman Constituency.

kusaal: On da aan Assistant Superintendent Gaana Pʋlis tʋʋma zin'igin la, ka o sɔb gbaʋŋʋ tisi ba ye o kʋ lɛn nyaŋi tʋm ya'asa nwɛnɛ Gaana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi wada gbaʋŋ (1992 Constitution) la yɛl si'em la ka yʋ'ʋn nyaŋi nya' vɔɔtʋg la.
english: As Assistant Superintendent in the Ghana Police Service, she tendered her resignation as required by the 1992 Constitution to enable her contest the elections.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pʋʋgin ba da paamnɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ du'al pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (46.76%), nɛ yinne du'al pistan nɛ yinne (1.31%).
english: These were equivalent to 46.76%, and 1.31% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ Ekow Hayford, onɛ da kpi la pʋ'a.
english: She is the wife of the late Ekow Hayford.

kusaal: O mɔr biis ayi.
english: She has two children.

kusaal: Oscar Liwaal anɛ onɛ ka ba da dʋ'a 1 May 1978) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Oscar Liwaal (born 1 May 1978) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Yunyoo Constituency bɛ Yunyoo-Nasuan Districti bɛ North East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He is a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Yunyoo Constituency in the Yunyoo-Nasuan District in the North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ Chief Executive Officer kʋdʋg tis Bunkpurugu Yunyoo nɛ Yunyoo-Nasuan district.
english: He was a former chief executive officer for Bunkpurugu Yunyoo and Yunyoo-Nasuan district respectively.

kusaal: O yinɛ Jimbale.
english: He hails from Jimbale.

kusaal: Ka mɔr Degree in education (2013).
english: He holds a degree in education (2013).

kusaal: Liwaal anɛ New patriotic Party nid.
english: Liwaal is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (In 2017), Pirɛsidɛn Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ka o lieb District chief executive tis Bunkpurugu Yunyoo dinɛ da an Northern region la.
english: In 2017, he was nominated by President Nana Akufo-Addo and confirmed as the District chief executive for Bunkpurugu Yunyoo in the then Northern region.

kusaal: O da nya' Yunyoo Constituency kʋk la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) ka lu tis onɛ pʋn dɛŋim zin'i kʋk la zug la, Naabu Joseph Bipoba.
english: He contested the Yunyoo Constituency seat in 2016 but lost to the incumbent Naabu Joseph Bipoba.

kusaal: Di nya'aŋ ka ba lɛn gaŋ o ye o zi'eni o Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug nadɔɔg la nɔba zug nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi (December 2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: He was again chosen as the party's candidate for the December 2020 election.

kusaal: O da di Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt Tusa piinɛ ayi kɔbiga nɛ atan (12,103) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ dua'ali atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (56.3%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin nyaŋ ka bas onɛ pʋn zin'i kʋk la zug la, Naabu Joseph Bipoba onɛ bɛ NDC la ka paam vɔɔt Tusa awai kɔbiga nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (9,177) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayi dua'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (42.7%).
english: He won the parliamentary election with 12,103 votes representing 56.3% of the total votes cast, beating his main opponent and incumbent member of parliament Naabu Joseph Bipoba of the NDC who obtained 9177 votes representing 42.7% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O da anɛ kʋkdaan nya'adɔli tis holding Office of Profit Committee ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid nimma'asim yɛla (Health Committee) Wadmaanib yikanɛ paas anii la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He serves as the vice chairperson and member of the Members holding Office of Profit Committee and Health Committee respectively in the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Liwaal nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii Nwadisa anu la yiiga daar (1 May 1978).
english: Liwaal was born on 1 May 1978.

kusaal: o da yii anina keŋ Yunyoo-Nasuan district.
english: He was later moved to head the newly formed Yunyoo-Nasuan district.

kusaal: Oscar Ofori Larbi (Ba dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa awai la dabpiinɛ anaasi daar, 14 September 1966) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress ni.
english: Oscar Ofori Larbi (born 14 September 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Aowin Constituency, bɛ Western North Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la dim.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Aowin Constituency, in the Western North Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr Public administration kasɛtta gbaʋŋ.
english: He holds a certificate in Public administration.

kusaal: Osei Bonsu Amoah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd, o anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid n bɛ wadmaanib yikanɛ paas ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la.
english: Osei Bonsu Amoah (born August 15, 1961) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and represents the people of Akwapim South Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana under the flag of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Aburi, tempυυg kanɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: He hails from Aburi, a town in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O si'iŋi o secondary school n bɛ Prempeh College sakur la ni ka tɔlisi maal o Digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ an Bachelor of Science linɛ an wada zamisυg n bɛ University of Ghana yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ anu.
english: He spent his secondary school years in the prestigious Prempeh College and he earned his Bachelor of Science degree in law from University of Ghana in 1985.

kusaal: O da lɛn tɔlisi keŋ Ghana wada sakur n di'e Bachelor of Law digirii kasɛta gbaυŋ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la ni.
english: At Ghana School of Law he obtained a Bachelor of Law degree in 1995.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la vɔɔt la ni la, ka ba da vɔɔt ka o di Akwapim South wadmaanib kυk la ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 49.73% ka o tiraan kanɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid ka o yʋ'ʋr buon William Ntow Boahene la mɛ da mɔri vɔɔt kal 8,694 kɔbiga pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 33.99%, ka CPP nid Isaac Opare Addo mɛ da mɔr vɔɔt kal 3,713 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da mɔri 14.52%, ka ala mɛn ka PPP nid Micheal Asante mɛ da paam vɔɔt kal kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da mɔri 1.76% vɔɔt la wʋsa pυυgin.
english: In the 2012 Ghanaian general election, he won the Akwapim South Constituency parliamentary seat with 12,720 votes making 49.73% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate William Ntow Boahene had 8,694 votes making 33.99% of the total votes cast the CPP parliamentary candidate Isaac Opare Addo had 3,713 votes making 14.52% of the total votes cast and the PPP parliamentary candidate Micheal Asante had 450 votes making 1.76% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yυma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ vɔɔt la ni ya'as ka ba vɔɔt ka o di Akwapim South sυ'υlυm wadmaanib kυk la, o da mɔri vɔɔt kal 14,049 kɔbʋg pυυgin bigis ye o da mɔri 52.8% ka o tiraan onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Lawrencia Dziwornu la mɛn da paam vɔɔt kal 8,417, ka kɔbʋga pυυgin bigis ye o da paamɛ 31.6% ka CPP nid Isaac Opare Addo mɛ da paam vɔɔt kal 4,153 kɔbiga pυυgin o da mɔri 15.6% vɔɔt la wυsa pυυgin.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general election, he again won the Akwapim South Constituency parliamentary seat with 14,049 votes making 52.8% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Lawrencia Dziwornu had 8,417 votes making 31.6% of the total votes cast and the CPP parliamentary candidate Isaac Opare Addo had 4,153 votes making 15.6% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yυma tusa ayi' nɛ piisi la vɔɔt la ni ka ba lɛn vɔɔt ka o di nɛ vɔɔt kal 21,247 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin bigis ye o da paamnɛ 65.41% vɔɔt la wυsa pυυgin, ka o tiraan onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid Winston Kwadwo Afari-Djan da paam vɔɔt kal 11,237 ka kɔbʋg pυυgin bigis ye o da paamnɛ 34.59% vɔɔt la wυsa pυυgin.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general election, he again won the Akwapim South Constituency parliamentary seat with 21,247 votes making 65.41% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Winston Kwadwo Afari-Djan had 11,237 votes making 34.59% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yυma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la ni, ka ba da gaŋ o ye o an kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Subsidiary Legislative n bɛ ti Ghana wadmaanib yir la kυkdaan.
english: In 2016, he was the Chairman of the Subsidiary Legislative Committee of Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: O paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Standing Orders la ni, ka mɛn paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Subsidiary Legislation la ni, o mɛ lɛn paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid ka ba gaansid kpɛɛmnam wadmaanib yir la ni mɛn.
english: He is a member of the Standing Orders Committee, a member of the Subsidiary Legislation Committee and also a member of the Appointments Committee.

kusaal: Nannana, onɛ an Minista kanɛ gɔsid Local Government yɛla la nya'andɔl, nɛ Decentralization and Rural Development.
english: He is currently the Deputy Minister for Local Government, Decentralization and Rural Development.

kusaal: Poi ka o naan kena an wadmaan la, Amoah da tυmnɛ n an kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid lampɔ di'esʋg yɛla nɛ kpɛɛm kanɛ da gɔsidi ti Ghana lampɔ di'esυg yɛla, yii ani n tυm nɛ IRS lin da yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ anii la n ti paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ ayuobʋ la ni.
english: Prior to his appointment into parliament, Amoah worked as the Inspector of Taxes, IRS between 1988 and 1996.

kusaal: Ba nɔk o ye o tυm n bɛ Gɔmina tυυma dɔɔgin ye o an Special Assistance lin da yi yυma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ti paae yυma tusa ayi' nɛ anii la ni.
english: He was appointed as the Special Assistance, Office of the President, and served from 2001 to 2005.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Akwapim South linɛ bɛ Ghana Eastern Region sυ'υlυm la, ba da du'a o nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyuobʋ nɛ yinne, Burnya nya'aŋ nwaris anii la li dabisim pii nɛ anu daar.
english: Osei Bonsu Amoah (born August 15, 1961) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and represents the people of Akwapim South Constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana under the flag of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Amoah nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyuobʋ nɛ yinne, Burnya nya'aŋ nwaris anii la li dabisim pii nɛ anu daar.
english: Amoah was born on August 15, 1961.

kusaal: O di pu'a onɛ da aan ti Ghana lɔya tita'ar amɛŋa, ka mɔr biis atan'.
english: In 2016, he was the Chairman of the Subsidiary Legislative Committee of Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Osei Kyei Mensah Bonsu (Onɛ ka ba da mi'i o ye Lawrence Addae la Ba da du'a o nɛ nwadis ayi' la daba 3, yʋma 1957) O anɛ onɛ gban'asa kat wa'ae nɛ tempʋʋg nɔbigir yɛla, o mɛ lɛn anɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Osei Kyei Mensah Bonsu (previously known as Lawrence Addae and born on February 3, 1957) is a Ghanaian urban planner and politician.

kusaal: O Bremang-Afrancho, bɛ tempʋʋg linɛ bɛ Kumasi, Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: He hails from Bremang-Afrancho, a town in Kumasi, Ashanti Region.

kusaal: yʋma 1982 la ni, ka o da naae Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology ka di'e digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ n bɛ zamisʋg linɛ an Urban Planning yɛla.
english: In 1982, he graduated from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology with a Bachelor of Science degree in Urban Planning.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ mɔr mi'ilim kati wa'ae nɛ nɔbigir gban'asa/Architect/Quantity Surveyor yɛla.
english: He is a Development Planner/Architect/Quantity Surveyor.

kusaal: Nwadig yinne la yʋma 1997 la ni da aan o yiiga saŋa linɛ ka o da kpɛn' wadmaanib yir la n zi'enɛ tis Old Tafo, Suame linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: He first became a member of the Parliament in January 1997, representing the people of Old Tafo, in the Suame Constituency of the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: o si'iŋi an wadmaan bɛ o sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni n paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayi' nɛ atan' nɛ anaasi nɛ anu nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi la n bɛ ti Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: He has kept his seat since then, representing his constituency in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th Parliaments of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ an kʋkdaan n tis Special Budget nɛ House nɛ kpikpinnib kpɛɛmnam la.
english: He was the chairperson for the Special Budget, House, and Business Committees.

kusaal: Yʋma 1996 la ni ka Ghana dim da maal vɔɔt la ka o da zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la zugu nyi'a di ka lin da aan o yiiga kpɛn'ɛb bɛ wadmaanib yir la n zi'enɛ tis Suame teŋkanɛ bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana nwa ni la.
english: Osei was first elected to Parliament during the 1996 Ghanaian General Elections on the Ticket of the New Patriotic Party representing the Suame Constituency in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da mɔri vɔɔt kal 47,455 yit vɔɔt kanl wʋsa linɛ da an 64,394 la ni, ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o da mɔr 57.40%,ka Paul Yeboah onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig nid la da mɔri vɔɔt kal 10,828, ka Azong Alhassan onɛ an PNC nid la mɛ da mɔr vɔɔt kal 3,219, ka Habiba Atta onɛ an CPP nid la mɛ da mɔr vɔɔt kal 2,892 ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He polled 47,455 votes out of the 64,394 valid votes cast representing 57.40% against Paul Yeboah an NDC member who polled 10,828 votes, Azong Alhassan a PNC member who polled 3,219 votes and Habiba Atta a CPP member who polled 2,892 votes.

kusaal: Ghana dim da lɛn maal vɔɔdʋg yʋma 2004 la ni ka Osei lɛn di Suame linɛ bɛ Ghana Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la kʋk la.
english: Osei was elected as the member of parliament for the Suame constituency of the Ashanti Region of Ghana in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: Ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da mɔri 82.1% yit vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 82.1% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kanna Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la da mɔri wadmaanib bam 109 n yi wadmaanib kanl wʋsa linɛ an 230 la ni pa'al ye banɛ da pɔɔd.
english: The New Patriotic Party won a minority total of 109 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da mɔri 78.31% vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 78.31% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ba da mɔri 37.59%, 5.43% nɛ 1.28% wʋʋ ba yʋda la tʋʋnl taab si'em.
english: These were equivalent to 37.59%, 5.43% and 1.28% respectively of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o da mɔri 79.15% vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 79.15% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: On nɛ Alidu Baba Dambasea kanɛ an Ma'asim Tiig nid la nɛ Solomon Nkrumah Appia Kubi onɛ an PPP na'adɔɔg nid nɛ Mavis Afriyie onɛ an DPP nid nɛ Abena Nyarko onɛ an NDP nid nɛ Osei-Bempah Hayford nɛ Paul Richard Kofi Yeboah banɛ da zi'enɛ ba nyari la da zi'en ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over Alidu Baba Dambasea of the National Democratic Congress, Solomon Nkrumah Appia Kubi of the Progressive People's Party, Adam Mohammed of the People's National Convention, Frederick Antwi-Nsiah of the Convention People's Party, Mavis Afriyie of the Democratic People's Party, Abena Nyarko of the National Democratic Party, Osei-Bempah Hayford and Paul Richard Kofi Yeboah both independent candidates.

kusaal: Osei Kyei Mensah Bonsu nɛ nidib anaasi da la'asi nyi'ad ka ba yʋda da anɛ Dodoovi Francis onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig na'adɔɔg la nid nɛ Sulemana Mohammed onɛ an CPP nid nɛ Mohammed Mubarak onɛ an APC nid nɛ onɛ da zi'enɛ o nyari la.
english: Hon. Osei Kyei Mensah Bonsu contested with four other candidates, which include Dodoovi Francis of the National Democratic Congress, Sulemana Mohammed of the Convention People's Party, Mohammed Mubarak of the All People Congress and the Independent candidate.

kusaal: Ka Dodoovi Francis onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig nid mɔr 9,312, ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 10.6% ka Sulemana Mohammed onɛ an CPP nid la mɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal 299 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 0.3%, APC mɛ da mɔr 213 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin 0.2%, George Prempeh mɛ da mɔr 11,217 ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka o mɔr 12.7%.
english: Finally the Independent candidate George Prempeh also came second with 11,217 votes making 12.7%of the total vote cast.

kusaal: Commonwealth Parliamentary of Association (CPA) kpɛɛmnam la da vɔti gaŋ Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu ye o an kʋkdaan nya'andɔl.
english: Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu was elected by the Executive Committee of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) as its new acting Vice-Chairperson.

kusaal: O da lɛn mɛɛbi ayi banɛ bɛ Job 600 nya'aŋ la ka ba nɔki Peter Ala Adjetey yʋ'ʋri n pʋdi li, onɛ da di'e Justice Annan zi'esim la.
english: He also proposed that one of the two new blocks built behind the main Job 600 be named after Peter Ala Adjetey, who succeeded Justice Annan.

kusaal: Amaa ka Convention People's Party na'adɔɔg nidib duoe pʋ siakɛ, ka ye ba ya'a tiak Job 600 yʋ'ʋr la li na ɛɛns tʋʋm kanɛ ka Kwame Nkrumah tʋm tis Ghana li bɛ labakʋda la ni la bas.
english: Opposition to these naming issues was led by members of the Convention People's Party, who believed renaming Job 600 would erase the contributions of Kwame Nkrumah from Ghanaian history.

kusaal: Osei mɔr pu'a ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Irene Kyei-Mensah Bonsu ka ba mɔr biis anii.
english: Osei is married to Mrs. Irene Kyei-Mensah Bonsu and has eight children.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig onɛ an Assemblies of God Karimbiig.
english: He is a Christian and fellowships with the Assemblies of God Church.

kusaal: Nannanna onɛ an wadmaanib banɛ zu'oe la kpɛɛm n bɛ wadmaanib yir la Ghana nwa ni ka an Minista onɛ gɔsid wadmaanib yir la yɛla bɛ Ghana kpɛla.
english: He was the majority leader in the Ghanaian Parliament until he stepped down on 21 February 2024 and is the Minister for Parliamentary Affairs in Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ tʋm wada tʋʋma yʋʋg hali Ghana kpɛla.
english: He is the longest serving lawmaker in Ghana.

kusaal: Osei Kyei Mensah anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Osei Kyei Mensah is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla la nɛ Salima tuub nɛ Energy Standing Orders nɛ banɛ gɔsidi gaansid kpɛɛmnam la ni.
english: He was also a member of the Finance, Mines and Energy Standing Orders and Selection Committees.

kusaal: Nwadis anii la yʋma 2023, ka o pian'a nɛɛr pa'alʋg ye ba ya'a ti ye ba vɔɔt gaans nidib Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni ka ba keŋi nya'a gɔmina na'am la, ye kɔbʋg pʋʋgin Gɔmina nya'andɔl Bawumia na mɔr wʋʋ 70% vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: In August 2023, he provided a prediction that 70% of the NPP voters who will vote in the flagbearer super delegate congress will be in favor of the Vice President Bawumia After the election was over, Bawumia took the lead with 68% which was nearly 70% as predicted.

kusaal: Ban daa ti vɔɔt naae ka, Bawumia mɔr 68% ka li kpɛlim nɛ 70% wʋʋ on da pian'a si'em la.
english: In August 2023, he provided a prediction that 70% of the NPP voters who will vote in the flagbearer super delegate congress will be in favor of the Vice President Bawumia After the election was over, Bawumia took the lead with 68% which was nearly 70% as predicted.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlʋm da paas wadmaanib bam 36 banɛ ka Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la da paam sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni n yi kʋkʋs la wʋsa kanl sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni linɛ da an 39 linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: His constituency was a part of the 36 parliamentary seats out of 39 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: On nɛ Agonno Sampson Young onɛ an CNP nid nɛ Paul Richard Kofi onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid nɛ Frederick Antwi onɛ an CPP nid da zi'en ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over Agonno Sampson Young of the People's National Convention, Paul Richard Kofi Yeboah of the National Democratic Congress and Frederick Antwi of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Ka kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ba da mɔri 1.6%, 14.3% nɛ 2% wʋʋ ba yʋda la tuunl taab si'em.
english: These were equivalent to 1.6%, 14.3% and 2% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O sʋ'ʋlʋm da paas wadmaanib bam 34 banɛ ka Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la da paam sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni n yi kʋkʋs la wʋsa kanl sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni linɛ da an 39 linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: His constituency was part of the 34 parliamentary seats out of 39 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: On nɛ David Osei Manu Ma'asim Tiig nid nɛ Ameyaw Aboagye Peter onɛ DPP nid nɛ Frederick Antwi-Nsiah CPP nid da zi'en ka o di ka basi ba.
english: He was elected over David Osei Manu of the National Democratic Congress, Ameyaw Aboagye Peter of Democratic People's Party and Frederick Antwi-Nsiah of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: Ghana dim da lɛn maal vɔɔdʋg yʋma 2020 la ni ka Osei lɛn di Suame linɛ bɛ Ghana Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlʋm kʋk la.
english: He again contested the 2020 Ghanaian general election as the parliamentary candidate for the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: On naae o wadmanib yir tʋʋma wʋʋ mɛɛb nam bam Job 600 la, Mensah Bonsu pa'ali o ya'am ye li sum ka ba nɔk onɔ da dɛŋim an pian'adi'es wadmaanib yir la pʋt yir la ka li an wɔ'ɔgir n tis o on maal si'eli tis teŋ la nɔbigir nɛ ti Ghana nimma'asim yɛla la.
english: Prior to the completion of the Parliament's Job 600 building, Mensah Bonsu proposed the renaming of the main Job 600 building.

kusaal: yʋʋm kanna la Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la da mɔri wadmaanib bam 128 n yi wadmaanib kanl wʋsa linɛ an 230 la ni pa'al ye banɛ zu'oe gat .
english: The New Patriotic Party won a majority total of 128 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Osman Bukari (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpiinɛ atan daar, 13 December 1998) ka o an Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdi nwɛ'ɛd right winger tisid Serbian kilab kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Red Star Belgrade nɛ Ghana national team.
english: Osman Bukari (born 13 December 1998) is a Ghanaian professional footballer who plays as a right winger for Serbian SuperLiga club Red Star Belgrade, on loan from Ekstraklasa club Widzew Łódź, and the Ghana national team.

kusaal: Yiiga European kilab kanɛ ka Osman Bukari sin'iŋi o tʋʋma anɛ Slovakian ʋ ya'a yis AS Trenčin.
english: The first European club in Osman Bukari's professional career was Slovak side AS Trenčín.

kusaal: Bukari da paasi ba yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ nii nwadis ayɔpɔi la ni (July 2018) on da yi Accra Lions dinɛ bɛ o teŋin la.
english: Bukari joined them in July 2018 from Accra Lions in his homeland.

kusaal: O yʋma ayi banɛ ka o da bɛ Slovakian football la, Bukari da anɛ banɛ mi' bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb pamm la yinne, o da nwɛ' maknam pisyuobʋ nɛ yuobʋ (66 matches) ka di goolnam piinɛ yuobʋ (16 goals) ka sʋŋ pisi nɛ nu (25 assists).
english: In his two years in Slovak football, Bukari was one of the best players in his team, playing 66 matches and recording 16 goals and 25 assists.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2019–20 siizin la ni, onɛ da an Trenčin's ninkanɛ mi' nwɛ'ɛbi gati ba wʋsa ka ba da paas o league best XI la pʋʋgin.
english: In the 2019–20 season, he was officially Trenčin's best player and was inducted in the league's best XI.

kusaal: Serbian gɔmena da tis o suor yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisinɛ atan nwadisa yuobʋ la ni, (June 2023).
english: He was granted Serbian citizenship by the Serbian government in June 2023.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ vɔɔtʋgin la, Nana Akufo-Addo da yɛl ye o ya'a di na'am la, o na maal region paala yi region banɛ dɛŋim bɛ la ni ka nyaŋɛ mɔr Gɔmena li'el teŋin nidib la wusa.
english: This followed the campaign promise of Nana Akufo-Addo to create new regions in order to bring governance closer to the people.

kusaal: Li tempʋtita'ar anɛ Dambai.
english: The region was inaugurated on May 14, 2019 with Dambai as its capital.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr paal kanɛ an Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development, ka Hon.
english: The execution of plans for the creation of the regions was ceded to the newly created Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development which is under the leadership of Hon. Dan Botwe.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa atan (March 2017) la ni, ministry la da maal suoya ye ba pin'il region nam la la'as nɛ Council of State.
english: In March 2017, the ministry sent the blue print for the creation of the region along with others to the Council of State.

kusaal: Region nam la maalʋg wʋsa naar da anɛ vɔɔtʋg kanɛ ka ba da kɛ ka nimbanɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlimin la vɔɔt ye ba maal region paal la 27 December 2018 ka ba da siak nwaae Oti Region.
english: A referendum on 27 December 2018 approved the creation of Oti Region.

kusaal: Vɔɔtʋg la daar, nidib tusa kɔbistan nɛ pisi nɛ atan, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ anii (323, 708) da vɔɔt ka li nar ye ba an nidib tusa kɔbistan nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (366,481) kɔbiga pʋʋgin nidib pisnii nɛ anii du'al pistan nɛ atan (88.33%) da yi vɔɔt.
english: On election day, 323,708 out of 366,481 (88.33% voter turnout) registered voters cast their votes.

kusaal: Kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid Municipal nɛ District Assembly la, anɛ onɛ zi'e gɔmena nɔba zug ka lɛɛ di'ed paŋ yit Assembly la kpɛɛm (presiding member) kanɛ ka ba mɛŋ gaŋ la ni.
english: Each Municipal and District Assembly, is administered by a Chief Executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an Assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Oti Region gilignɛ nɛ Northern region dagɔbʋg ka Volta Region bɛ li datiuŋ ka Volta Lake la bɛ li tʋɔn.
english: The Oti Region is bordered on the north by the Northern region, to the south by the Volta Region, and to the west by the Volta Lake.

kusaal: Ghana Geological Survey Authority dim nye ya ka Iron bɛdigɔ bɛ Akokrowa, kpaadib tɛŋ kani bɛ Oti Region, Ghana.
english: The Ghana Geological Survey Authority has discovered large quantities of Iron ore deposits in Akokrowa, a farming community in the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba gɔsya ka ye iron la tɛbisim anɛ 55.22 percent (Fe) ka mɛ an bʋnsʋŋ.
english: The iron ore, according to the geological investigation, is 55.22 weight percent (Fe) and of a higher grade.

kusaal: Kyabobo National Park: Bɛ nɛ Nkwanta, tɛŋ la dagɔbʋg, li bɛnɛ Savannah nɛ tropical rain forest tɛŋsʋk.
english: Kyabobo National Park: The reserve is situated in Nkwanta, in the Nkwanta South District of the area, between the Savannah and tropical rain forest.

kusaal: Di da sin'iŋnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan (1993) la ni ye ba gur siarin bʋnkɔnbid nɛ bʋnkɔnb banɛ kpɛn' yɛlin yisi ba yɛl la ni nɛ nidibin.
english: The reserve was established in 1993 with the intention of safeguarding wildlife and other endangered animal species while also giving them a comfortable place to live away from danger and human activity.

kusaal: Di paae yʋma pisyuobʋ nwa ka nidib banɛ bɛ Oti region la da pʋm bɔɔd ye ba an regioni ba kɔn' ka pʋ paam amaa ka yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la ni, ka Zuraan Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo da maal region paala o na'am saŋa yʋʋm tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni.
english: This followed the campaign promise of Nana Akufo-Addo to create new regions in order to bring governance closer to the people.

kusaal: (Municipal nama anaasi nɛ District Assembly nama anu).
english: Each Municipal and District Assembly, is administered by a Chief Executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an Assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Oti Region zin'ig la kudigi gaad tɛŋ bani bɛ Ghana south la din liel nɛ north la zug.
english: The Oti Region is bordered on the north by the Northern region, to the south by the Volta Region, and to the west by the Volta Lake.

kusaal: Amaa Hamattan sapɛbis tʋʋlig kani yit Sahara la da'andɛ saŋa wusa din nɔk bʋnia nwadik la kiŋ paae nwadisa ayi la ni.
english: However, the hot Harmattan wind from the Sahara blows frequently between December and the beginning of February.

kusaal: Iron tʋʋma na nyaŋi yɔ'ɔg tʋʋma nɛ ligidi tis nidib banɛ bɛ Oti la nɛ Ghana nidib wusa.
english: The Ghana Geological Survey Authority has discovered large quantities of Iron ore deposits in Akokrowa, a farming community in the Oti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di mɔri distric nama awai.
english: It has 9 districts.

kusaal: Nidib tʋsa kɔbistan nɛ piinɛ awai, kɔbisyi nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ (319,296) da vɔɔt ɛɛn ka nidib tusa ayi, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii da vɔɔti ayei ka vɔɔt banɛ da san'am da an kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne.
english: A total of 319,296 (98.64 per cent) voted Yes and 2,878 voted No (0.89 per cent) while the number of rejected ballots was 951 (0.24 per cent).

kusaal: sɛ'ɛʋg sin'ingidnɛ nwadisa anu la ni kiŋ paae nwadis piinɛ yinne la ka saa niib makir an 750 to 1050 mm.
english: The wet season is between about May and November with an average annual rainfall of 750 to 1050 mm (30 to 40 inches).

kusaal: 1757 – after 1791), onɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr lɛm buon ye John Stuart, da anɛ onɛ ka ba karʋ yis, political activist, nɛ natural rights philosopher n yit West Africa ka da kpi'im hali n bɛ Great Britain 18th century pʋsʋg la saŋa.
english: 1791), also known as John Stuart, was a British abolitionist and activist who was born in the Gold Coast (modern-day Ghana).

kusaal: O yʋma piiga nɛ atan' saŋa ka ba da gban o Gold Coast n kuos o tis sankpansib, ka ba mɔr o lɔ'ɔŋ kuo tita'ar la kɛŋ Grenada tɛŋin linɛ bɛ West Indies la.
english: He was sold into slavery at the age of thirteen and shipped to Grenada in the West Indies.

kusaal: Ba dua Quobna Ottobah Cugoano nɛ 1757 Agimaque (Ajumako) dinɛ bɛ Gold Coast (modern-day Ghana).
english: He was born Quobna Ottobah Cugoano in 1757 in Agimaque (Ajumako) in the Gold Coast (modern-day Ghana).

kusaal: O yʋʋm piiga nɛ ata' (13) saŋa la, ba da zu o nɛ biis sieba pɛɛs o zug ka kuosi ba tis saŋkpan'asib ka mori ba yi Cape Coast tɛŋin la kɛŋ kpɛn'ɛsiba saŋkpan'asnam arʋŋ la ni kɛŋ Grenada tɛŋin.
english: At the age of 13, Cugoano was kidnapped with a group of children, sold into slavery and transported from Cape Coast on a slave ship to Grenada.

kusaal: Ba da kɛ nɛ ka o tʋm pɔɔgin tʋʋma bɛ Lesser Antilles tɛŋin hali nɛ Scottish dim tɛŋ nid onɛ sʋoe pɔtnam ka o yʋ'ʋr buon ye Alexander Campbell, ti kɛna da o 1772 mor o kuli o yin.
english: He worked on a plantation in the Lesser Antilles until he was purchased in 1772 by Alexander Campbell, a Scottish plantation owner, who took him into his household.

kusaal: 1772 saŋa sia ka Campbell da nɔk o mor kɛŋ kaae England, anina ka Cugoano yʋ'ʋm da paam yɔlisim.
english: Late in 1772, Campbell took Cugoano with him on a visit to England, where Cugoano was able to secure his freedom.

kusaal: Ka ba da suu o wina'am kuom 20 August 1773, bɛ St James's Church, Piccadilly, ka pudi o yʋ'ʋr ye "John Stuart – a Black, saŋkan na la ka o mor yʋʋm piiga nɛ ayuobu (16).
english: On 20 August 1773, Cugoano was baptised at St James's Church, Piccadilly, as "John Stuart – a Black, aged 16 Years".

kusaal: Saŋkan la, di da dɔlisnɛ Cosways la ni ka British politisdim buudi la baŋɔ, la'am nɛ William Blake nɛ Prince of Wales.
english: Through the Cosways, he came to the attention of leading British political and cultural figures of the time, including the poet William Blake and the Prince of Wales.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobu(1786) la ni ka o da tʋm tʋʋm tirin Henry Demane yɛla la ni, ninsabil kanɛ an saŋkpan'as ka ba da bɔɔd yɛ ba zuu o lɛb West Indies la.
english: In 1786, he played a key role in the case of Henry Demane, a kidnapped black man who was to be shipped back to the West Indies.

kusaal: Cugoano da yɛl saŋkpan'asnam onɛ ka ba mi o hali ka ba buon o yɛ Granville Sharp la, onɛ da yaŋi kɛŋi yis Demane anriŋ la pʋʋgin ka ba pʋ yaŋi mɔr o kɛŋɛɛ.
english: Cugoano contacted Granville Sharp, a well-known abolitionist, who was able to have Demane removed from the ship before it sailed.

kusaal: O da nɔk labaar la kɛŋi tis King George III, onɛ da an Prince of Wales nɛ Edmund Burke onɛ da an politis kpɛɛm la.
english: The work was sent to prominent British political figures such as George III, the Prince of Wales and Edmund Burke.

kusaal: Di pʋʋginɛɛ, o da pian'a pa'annɛ Britist dim la da pʋ yaŋi sʋ'ʋg Sierra Leone tis London's "Poor Blacks" kas-kas anɛ banɛ da paam yɔlisim yi Africa-America yamis banɛ ka ba da nɔki ba American Revolutionary War nya'aŋ la tɔɔm kɛŋ London la.
english: In the shortened work, addressed to the "Sons of Africa", Cugoano expressed qualified support for the efforts to establish a colony in Sierra Leone for London's "Poor Blacks" (mostly freed African-American slaves who had been relocated to London after the American Revolutionary War.

kusaal: Banɛ da dɛŋim bɛɛ teŋin la da anɛ Nova Scotian Settlers banɛ da an black Loyalists, la'am nɛ American yamis banɛ da an niŋkʋda ka da yit Nova Scotia, ka da duoe tɔɔm kɛŋi zin'in Sierra Leone la.
english: Other early settlers were the Nova Scotian Settlers, that is Black Loyalists, also former American slaves, from Nova Scotia, who chose to move to Sierra Leone).

kusaal: Cugoano da bɔɔd nɛ ye o nwiɛe kɛŋ Nova Scotia tɛŋin la nɔk nidib ka ba tʋm sʋŋ ka bam banɛ an African Britons dim la paam yɔlisim yi Sierra Leone amaa ti pʋ nyaŋi baŋ ye o da nyaŋi maal bɛɛ o pʋ nyaŋi maalɛ.
english: Cugoano wished to travel to Nova Scotia to recruit settlers for the proposed free colony of African Britons in Sierra Leone but it is not known if he did so.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsa ayi, nɛ pisyi 2020 dinɛ an Sapal Nwadig dabis pisyi la ni ka English Heritage blue plaque da nie pa'al nyain ban da zu'od Cugoano siem bɛ Schomberg House bɛ Pall Mall, London, zin'ikanɛ ka o da bɛ ka tʋmmid nɛ Cosways din yi Yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi paae yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ piswai nɛ yinne la ni 1784 paae 1791.
english: In November 2020, an English Heritage blue plaque honouring Cugoano was unveiled on Schomberg House in Pall Mall, London, where he had lived and worked with the Cosways from 1784 to 1791.

kusaal: yʋʋm tʋsa ayi, nɛ pisyi nɛ atan' 2023 dinɛ an Mɔtul Nwadig dabisim pisyi la ni 20/08/2023 la St James's Church, da nɔk dabisir kaŋa ye di'em di dinɛ anɛ Cugoano's ku'om sʋʋb dabisir dinɛ paas kɔbiga nɛ pisnu (250 Anniversary) ku'om sʋʋb dabisa banɛ ka o di'ɛm gaad la yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' 1773 , o da di'eɛɛ ku'om sʋʋb la nɛ yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' 1773 la ni, nɛ'ɛŋa ma'aa an dabisir kannɛ ka ba sɔbi digili o pʋgin wʋsa ni.
english: On 20 August 2023, St James's Church, Piccadilly, dedicated a new plaque to honour the 250th anniversary of Cugoano's baptism there in 1773, the only recorded date in his life.

kusaal: Lɛm pɛɛs ya'asaa, St James da kɛ ka Trinidad-based artist Che Lovelace maal siel bʋmpaal ka ba nɔki maal Cugoano ku'om sʋʋb tier yɛla.
english: St James's additionally commissioned Trinidad-based artist Che Lovelace to create a new artwork in commemoration of Cugoano's baptismal anniversary, to be installed in the church entrance on 20 September 2023 – the first permanent artwork commissioned by St James's Church, as well as the first anywhere in the world to commemorate Cugoano.

kusaal: Sɔ' da da o 1772 yʋma saŋa la m mɔr o kɛŋ England, anina ka Cugoano yʋ'ʋm da zamis karʋŋ nɛ sɔb ka ba da bas o.
english: In 1772, he was purchased by a merchant who took him to England, where Cugoano learned to read and write, and was emancipated.

kusaal: din nya'aŋ la, o yʋ'ʋm da tʋmiɛ nɛ tisit artists Richard nɛ Maria Cosway, Cugoano da kena yʋ'ʋm mi Bristist dim gomenam nɛ buudi malima nimbeda la.
english: In 1784, Cugoano was employed as a servant by the artists Richard Cosway and his wife, Maria.

kusaal: O da nɔki o mɛŋi pɛɛs nɛ Sons of Africa, la'as kanɛ an African nim banɛ ka ba kari yis ka ba bɛ Britain sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He joined the Sons of Africa, a group of Black abolitionists in Britain, and died at some point after 1791.

kusaal: Richard nɛ Maria Cosway, nɛ Ottobah Cugoano (1784), Richard Cosway da an onɛ da sʋŋi ba.
english: In 1784, Cugoano was employed as a servant by the artists Richard Cosway and his wife, Maria.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsir, kobis yɔpɔi nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1784), artists Richard Cosway nɛ o pua, Maria da nɔk Cugoano ka o lɛbigi tʋm-tʋm ba yin ka ba yɔɔd o.
english: In 1784, Cugoano was employed as a servant by the artists Richard Cosway and his wife, Maria.

kusaal: Prince of Wales nɛ Africans gbami'idib banɛ da bɛ Britain la, Cugoano da anɛ onɛ da kpi'ɛm nɛ Africa dim yʋma la ni bam banɛ ka ba da kari baa bas la, o da mɛ lɛm pɛɛs banɛ da sɔbid daar wʋsa gbana gesid saŋkpan'asnam tʋʋma yɛla la.
english: Together with Olaudah Equiano and other educated Africans living in Britain, Cugoano became active in the Sons of Africa, an abolitionist group whose members wrote frequently to the newspapers of the day, condemning the practice of enslavement.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ pisnii nɛ ayɔpoi (1787) la ni ka o zua Olaudah Equiano, da sʋŋ Cugoano ka o zaŋ o gbaʋŋ dinɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr an yɛ Pʋtɛnra nɛ Sʋŋsa'aŋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nɛ zukpi'ʋŋ tʋʋma dinɛ ka ba mɔri maan saŋkpan'snam la yɛla nɛ Commerce of the Human Species (1787) la.
english: In 1787, possibly with the help of his friend Olaudah Equiano, Cugoano published an abolitionist work entitled Thoughts and Sentiments on the Evil and Wicked Traffic of the Slavery and Commerce of the Human Species (1787).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ piswai nɛ yinne 1791 dinɛ an yʋma anaasi saŋa sa la ka o da nɔki o gbaʋŋ la zaŋi pa'al sɔ' wʋsa ka li pa'al ye o sɔb gbaʋŋ, dinɛ da bɛ gbaʋŋ la pʋʋgin da anɛ pian'ad kanɛ tisid dinɛ anɛ Africa biis la "Sons of Africa".
english: He joined the Sons of Africa, a group of Black abolitionists in Britain, and died at some point after 1791.

kusaal: Cugoano da buol ka sɔs sour ye ba sʋŋ ka ke ka ba kɛna mɛ' sakuya tis Britain dim kas-kas anɛ sakubiis banɛ bɛ African.Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ piswai nɛ yinne 1791 la ni ka Cugoano da kɛn nɛ Cosways paae 12 Queen Street dinɛ bɛ Mayfair la.
english: In 1791, Cugoano moved with the Cosways to 12 Queen Street in Mayfair.

kusaal: O naar gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka o da sɔb Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ piswai nɛ yinne 1791 la, o da pian'a o sour nwiɛer yɛla kɛn "upwards of fifty places" din na niŋ siem ka o gbaʋŋ la yʋ'ʋr kɛŋ tuon ka nidib nyaŋi baŋi li amaa o da pʋ nyaŋi tʋm nwɛnɛ on tɛns siem la.
english: His last known letter, written in 1791, mentions travelling to "upwards of fifty places" to promote the book and that he found that "complexion is a predominant prejudice".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ piswai nɛ yinne 1791 la nya'aŋ ka ba pʋ lem nyɛ o labaar ka li bɛ yɛlkʋda gbana la nii ya'ase, ka li pa'al yee, daa sierɛ o tʋn'ʋm da kpi nɛ yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ piswai nɛ yinne 1791 la ni bɛɛ yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbisyɔpoi nɛ piswai nɛ ayi 1792 la ni.
english: After 1791, Cugoano disappears from the historical record, and it is likely that he died in 1791 or 1792.

kusaal: Ba da ye ba nɔk dinɛ ka artist Che Lovelace da maal la nɛ ziel St James's Church la za'anɔɔrin dinɛ anɛ yʋʋm tʋsa ayi, nɛ pisyi nɛ atan'(2023) la ni.
english: St James's additionally commissioned Trinidad-based artist Che Lovelace to create a new artwork in commemoration of Cugoano's baptismal anniversary, to be installed in the church entrance on 20 September 2023 – the first permanent artwork commissioned by St James's Church, as well as the first anywhere in the world to commemorate Cugoano.

kusaal: Nɛ' an dinɛ an yiiga dunia ni ka St James's Church da maali nɔki tier Cugoano ku'om sʋʋb.
english: St James's additionally commissioned Trinidad-based artist Che Lovelace to create a new artwork in commemoration of Cugoano's baptismal anniversary, to be installed in the church entrance on 20 September 2023 – the first permanent artwork commissioned by St James's Church, as well as the first anywhere in the world to commemorate Cugoano.

kusaal: O da anɛ Fanti ka o buudi da kpi'ɛ nɛ teŋ la naab.
english: He was born into a Fante family and his family was close to the local chief.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Sow bɛnɛ Dakar linɛ bɛ Senegal sʋ'ʋlʋm la, 10 Sawa'ar 1935.: 39.
english: Sow was born in Dakar, Senegal, on 10 October 1935.

kusaal: O saam nɛ da kpi yʋʋm 1956 nya'aŋ la, o da yi Dakar teŋin keŋ France, ti zamis gbaʋŋ, ani ka o di'e Diploma in physiotherapy kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: After the death of his father in 1956, he left Dakar to study in France, where he obtained a diploma in physiotherapy.

kusaal: Senegal n da faaɛn ba mɛŋ yi nasanam nu'usin bɛ 1960 yʋʋm saŋa la, o da lɛb anina n pin'il o nima'asim tʋʋma.
english: He returned to Senegal after it became independent in 1960 and started a practice in physiotherapy.

kusaal: Di nya'aŋ, o da lɛb France teŋin ti tʋm o nimma'asim tʋʋma ani, amaa o da lɛn lɛb Senegal teŋin na 1978.
english: He later went back to France and practised there, but returned to Senegal in 1978.

kusaal: O da mɔri yʋma pisnii (81) ka kpi linɛ an Dakar teŋin,1 Samanpiid Nwadig la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piina ayuobʋ (2016).
english: He died in Dakar on 1 December 2016 at the age of 81.

kusaal: Sow da anɛ onɛ ka Nuba dim banɛ bɛ Sudan ya-tuona nid yinne kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon ye Leni Riefenstahl ka maan nidib fotonam la, da zamis o li tʋʋma, ka din yi 1984 saŋa la, o da pin'ili tʋmmɛ fotonam tʋʋma, ka mɔr la'ad kpi'ed ya'abid Nuba zabzab la.
english: Sow was inspired by photographs by Leni Riefenstahl of the Nuba peoples of southern Sudan, and from 1984 began to work on a series of larger-than-life sculptures of muscular Nuba wrestlers.

kusaal: O da nɔk ya'abid dinɛ ka o ya'ab la zi'el Centre Cultural Francaise de Dakar bɛ 1987 yʋʋm la ni.
english: They were shown at the Centre Culturel Français de Dakar in 1987.

kusaal: 2008 yʋʋm la ni ka ba da tisid Prince Claus Yɔɔd dinɛ pa'an buudi malʋŋ nɛ ninsaal niŋgbiŋ tʋʋma ni la, o da paasnɛ nimbanɛ di piig nɛ yinne yɔɔd la ni.
english: In the 2008 Prince Claus Awards, on the theme of Culture and the human body, he was one of the eleven laureates.

kusaal: 11 dawalig 2012 ni la, ba da vɔɔt gaŋi Sow ka o an Membre Associé Etranger ("foreign associate member") dinɛ an Académie des Beaux-Arts linɛ an Institu de France, ka di'e Andrew Wyeth nɔbir.
english: On 11 April 2012 Sow was elected a Membre Associé Etranger ("foreign associate member") of the Académie des Beaux-Arts of the Institut de France, replacing Andrew Wyeth.

kusaal: Di nya'aŋ o da ya'ab Maasai dim, Zulu dim, Peul dim, bɛɛ Fulani dim, ka 1990s saŋa ka o da ya'ab Native Americans.
english: Sow later made series of sculptures of Maasai people, of Zulu people, of Peul or Fulani people, and, in the late 1990s, of Native Americans.

kusaal: Onɛ da an ninsabilig yiiga daan kanɛ ka ba vɔɔt gaŋ o ka paas tʋʋm kan ni.
english: He was the first black person to have been elected to membership.

kusaal: Owari Tsushima Tenno Matsuri (天王祭り) anɛ malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba maan yʋʋm-yʋʋm, nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni, bɛ Tsushima bɛ Aichi sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Tenno Matsuri (天王祭り) is a festival held annually, in July, in Tsushima, Aichi.

kusaal: Daba ayi malʋŋ la naar anɛ zaamnɔɔr malʋŋ kanɛ ka ba maan ka aarʋma bɛdegʋ bɛ, ka ba dɛrɛsi ba wʋsa nɛ kanianam banɛ ka ba nɔk gbana maali ba nwɛnɛ ban kɔbisnaasi, ka ba gilig Tenno River la wʋsa.
english: The highlight of the two-day event is the evening festival in which a dozen boats, each decorated with nearly 400 paper lanterns, float down the Tenno River.

kusaal: Malʋŋ la maanɛ ye ba zun'oe ba'akanɛ an Gozu Tenno.
english: The festival honors the deity Gozu Tenno.

kusaal: Ba mɛ maan malʋŋ kaŋa Tokyo teŋin.
english: This festival also takes place in Tokyo.

kusaal: Paa Grant Soccer Academy anɛ Ghanaian association football kilab ka lɛn zamisid bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb yɛla ya'as bɛ Sekondi-Takoradi, Ghana.
english: Paa Grant Soccer Academy is a Ghanaian association football club and academy based in Sekondi-Takoradi, Ghana.

kusaal: Kim Tyrone Grant onɛ an o yaaŋ la da pin'il tiim la bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni ye di tien George Alfred (Paa) Grant yɛla, o da anɛ Black Stars nidib yinne ka lɛn an England legionnaire.
english: The team was founded in 2009 in honour of George Alfred (Paa) Grant, by his grandson Kim Tyrone Grant, a former Black Stars member and England legionnaire.

kusaal: Ba nya'adi bɛ GAFCOA.
english: They are a competing in the GAFCOA.

kusaal: Paa Grant Soccer Academy anɛ vʋ'ʋsʋg zin'ig ka lɛn an dasm nɛ pʋ'asada tiim tis F.C. Takoradi.
english: Paa Grant Soccer Academy is the reserve and youth team of F.C. Takoradi.

kusaal: Benjamin Paapa Kofi Yankson, ka si'eba buon o Paapa Yankson (22 June 1944 – 21 July 2017) da anԑ Ghana nid kanԑ yʋʋm yʋʋma, sͻbid yʋʋma gbana, ka lԑn gͻsid yʋʋma maalig.
english: Benjamin Paapa Kofi Yankson, known as Paapa Yankson (22 June 1944 – 21 July 2017) was a Ghanaian highlife singer, songwriter, and producer.

kusaal: O da di'e ya'an piini bԑdigʋ, ka yinnԑ da anԑ o yʋʋma "Yaaba" da tis o ya'an la bԑ yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ ayͻpͻi Konkomba Awards ni.
english: He won multiple awards, including Best Composition for his song "Yaaba" at the 1997 Konkomba Awards.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Benjamin Paapa Kofi Yankson nԑ yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ pisnaasi nԑ anaasi, Sigir nwadig dabpisi nԑ ayi' daar bԑ Winneba linԑ bԑ Central Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Benjamin Paapa Kofi Yankson was born on 22 June 1944 at Winneba in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O dʋ'adib da anԑ banԑ mi' yʋʋma yela, o saam Benjamin Akono Yankson da anԑ onԑ pi'ebid na'atani bԑ Apam Brass Band, ka o ma Akua Doma mԑ an yʋʋmyʋʋmi bԑ Christ Little Band linԑ bԑ Methodist Church la.
english: He was born into a musical family with his father, Benjamin Akono Yankson, being a trumpeter with the Apam Brass Band, and his mother Akua Doma, a singer in the Christ Little Band of the Methodist Church.
