kusaal: O da kԑŋ sakur nԑ Takoradi Methodist School o biilimin ka tͻlis tuoni kԑŋ Ahantaman Secondary Commercial School.
english: He attended Takoradi Methodist School for his primary education and proceeded to Ahantaman Secondary Commercial School, from which he graduated with a certificate in stenography.

kusaal: On da naae sakur la, Yankson da nyԑ tʋʋma bԑ Kingsway Chemist ye o sͻgid pian'ad gbana ni.
english: After graduating from commercial school, Yankson was employed at Kingsway Chemist as a stenographer.

kusaal: Li yʋma anu saŋa ka o tʋm tʋʋma bԑ African Timber and Plywood Company, lʋgir kanԑ paas United African Company (UAC), ka bԑ Samreboi.
english: Five years later he became a stenographer for the African Timber and Plywood Company, a subsidiary of the United African Company (UAC), at Samreboi.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ pisyͻpͻi saŋa, C. K. Mann, onԑ da an tuongati bԑ The Carousel Seven, da bԑlis o tuongat kanԑ sʋ'ʋe ba ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Anis Mubarak, ye o nͻk Yankson paasi ba.
english: In the 1970s, C. K. Mann, the leader of the regional band The Carousel Seven, impressed upon the band's owner, Anis Mubarak, to sign Yankson to his band.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ pisyͻpͻi nԑ anu ni, o da tͻlisi kԑŋ sakur kanԑ buon National Academy of Music bԑ Winneba ka da paam o gbaʋŋi bԑ yʋʋma pʋʋgin.
english: In 1975 he enrolled at the National Academy of Music at Winneba and graduated with a diploma in music.

kusaal: Lin da yi yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ pisni nԑ ayi' paae yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ yinnԑ ni, o tʋʋma da anԑ ye o gͻsid yʋʋma tʋʋma bԑ Garrisons Education Unit linԑ bԑ Burma Camp Accra.
english: From 1982 to 1991 he worked as a music organizer at the Garrisons Education Unit of Burma Camp in Accra.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ yinnԑ ni, kpikpiŋ daan kanԑ buon Ebo Coker da nͻk Yankson tʋʋma ye o paas o yʋʋmyʋʋmidib Western Diamonds ni, lin nya'aŋ ka o da kԑŋ Takoradi bͻzugͻ, anina ka tʋʋma la da bԑ.
english: In 1991, businessman Ebo Coker signed Yankson to his band Western Diamonds, after which he relocated to Takoradi where the band was based.

kusaal: Yankson da bas tʋʋm kaŋa bԑ yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ atan' ni, o da kԑŋi tʋmmԑ nԑ Obuasi Golden Nuggets.
english: Yankson left the band in 1993 after a successful stint and joined the Obuasi-based band Golden Nuggets.

kusaal: Onԑ da kԑ ka o kԑŋ Obuasi da anԑ CEO tis Ashanti Goldfields Corporation,ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Sam Jonah.
english: His move to Obuasi was influenced by the then-CEO of Ashanti Goldfields Corporation, Sam Jonah.

kusaal: O yʋʋma banԑ da nyԑ yʋ'ʋr si'eba anԑ "Wiase Mu Nsem", "Show Your Love", "Wo Yere Anaa Wo Maame", nԑ "Tena Menkyen", nԑ yʋʋmkanԑ ka o da maal nya'aŋ nԑ Paulina Oduro la.
english: His hit songs included "Wiase Mu Nsem", "Show Your Love", "Wo Yere Anaa Wo Maame", and "Tena Menkyen", the latter recorded with Paulina Oduro.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kͻbiswai nԑ piswai nԑ ayͻpͻi ni, o da yʋʋm yʋʋma kanԑ buon "Yaaba", li da dͻlisnԑ yʋʋmkan ni ka o di'e ya'an piini bԑ Komkomba Awards.
english: In 1997 he composed "Yaaba", which won Best Composition at the Komkomba Awards.

kusaal: Yankson zamis nidib ka mԑ yʋʋm yʋʋma bԑ tԑԑn bԑdigʋ ni, ka tԑԑns la si'eba an United States, Canada, Belgium, United Kingdom, Germany, nԑ Holland.
english: Yankson taught and performed in many countries across the world, including the United States, Canada, Belgium, United Kingdom, Germany, and Holland.

kusaal: Yankson da di'e piini kanԑ an Grand Medal bԑ Ghana yʋʋm tusayi nԑ ayuobʋ Girima tisib nԑ ya'an piini malima ni, onԑ da an gͻmԑna zugraan sankan anԑ John Agyekum Kufour, ba da tis o piinkan on sʋŋ Ghana yʋʋma pʋʋgin la zug.
english: Yankson was awarded the Grand Medal of Ghana during the 2006 National Honours and Awards Ceremony by President John Agyekum Kufour, in recognition of his contribution to Ghanaian music.

kusaal: O da di'e piinkanԑ buon Lifetime Achievement Award bԑ yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayͻpͻi Vodafone Ghana Music Awards ni.
english: He also won the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2017 Vodafone Ghana Music Awards.

kusaal: Labaar da pa'al ye o da gbis nԑ tͻl Arizum daar bԑ o yin Dansoman linԑ bԑ Accra.
english: It was reported that he had died in his sleep on Friday at his home in Dansoman in Accra.

kusaal: O yʋʋma si'eba banԑ da nyԑ yʋ'ʋr anԑ "Wiase Mu Nsem", "Show Your Love", "Wo Yere Anaa Wo Maame", nԑ "Tena Menkyen".
english: He recorded two dozen albums during his career; his hit songs included "Wiase Mu Nsem", "Show Your Love", "Wo Yere Anaa Wo Maame", and "Tena Menkyen".

kusaal: O da di'e ya'an piini Ghana kati wa'ae o tʋʋm kanԑ ka o da tʋm bԑ Ghana yʋʋma pʋʋgin la.
english: He was a recipient of the Grand Medal of Ghana for his contribution to Ghanaian music.

kusaal: Tʋʋma zin'igin la da mͻr banԑ maan yʋʋma ka ba buoni ba Big Sound Band ka ba da yʋʋm saŋa wʋsa tʋʋma zin'igin la.
english: The company had a workers' band — the Big Sound Band — which performed regularly after work.

kusaal: Yankson da anԑ onԑ gaadi ba tuoni yʋʋm, o yʋma anaasi banԑ ka o da bԑ tʋʋma zin'igin la wʋsa.
english: Yankson was the lead singer of the band during his four years with the company.

kusaal: Mann da nyԑ ka Yankson da yʋ'ʋm bԑ Yankson ma kʋʋrin ka li da ma'ae o sʋnf hali.
english: Mann had seen Yankson perform during Yankson's mother's funeral and was impressed by his talent.

kusaal: Yankson da siak ye o tʋm nԑ ba.
english: Yankson accepted the offer.

kusaal: Yʋʋmyʋʋmidib ban da yi lԑb Accra, ka yʋʋm tusir, kͻiswai nԑ piswai nԑ anu ni ka Yankson yi kԑŋ bԑ o kͻn'.
english: After a while the band was moved to Accra, and in 1995 Yankson broke away and went solo.

kusaal: Paapa Yankson da maal album nam pisi nԑ anaasi.
english: Paapa Yankson recorded two dozen albums during his career.

kusaal: O da zin'in pͻn'ͻr kԑԑkԑ ni yʋʋm yʋʋma bԑ Exclusive Men of The Year Awards Sigir nwadig la ni, ka lԑn maal ala bԑ Bottles & Bands Festival yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayuobʋ, Sapal nwadig la ni.
english: He performed in a wheelchair at the Exclusive Men of The Year Awards in June and at the Bottles & Bands Festival 2016 in November.

kusaal: Paapa Yankson da mͻr yʋma pisyͻpͻi nԑ atan' ka nyaan kpi, o yidim pa'al ye o da bԑn'ԑ ya ka li yuug.
english: Paapa Yankson has died at the age of 73, after a prolonged illness, family sources have disclosed.

kusaal: O dʋ'adib lԑԑ da bͻͻd ye o maal kpikpiŋ.
english: His parents, though, wanted him to go into business.

kusaal: Pascal Aka (ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm anɛ mɔraʋg 17, 1985 bɛ Ivory Coast sʋ'ʋlʋm) anɛ Ivorian dim siini kpɛɛm, nɛ siini di'e nɛ yʋ'ʋma siini kpɛɛm nɛ onɛ lɛn maannɛ li ya'as, o mi'i o tʋʋma sʋ'ʋŋa bɛ "Jamie nɛ Eddie" linɛ ka ba buon ye souls of strife la (2007) ni, nɛ "Evol (2010)" di'ema linɛ ka ba gaans nidib bɛdegʋ kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb bɛ Ghana siini yɔɔd 2014 saŋa la.
english: Pascal Aka (born in Ivory Coast, July 17, 1985) is an Ivorian film director, actor, music video director and producer, very well known for his work on "Jamie and Eddie: Souls of Strife (2007)", "Evol (2010)",Double-Cross which got several nominations at the Ghana Movies Award 2014.

kusaal: ba da du'a Pascal Aka nɛ Abidjan linɛ bɛ Ivory Coast sʋ'ʋlʋm, amaa nɔbig bɛ Ghana.
english: Born in Abidjan, Ivory Coast, Pascal Aka grew up in Ghana.

kusaal: o da keŋ o sakur bɛnɛ Ontario based university of Carleton, n zamis siini zamisʋg, ka lɛn an zamis-zamis bɛ a-sʋ'ʋ-m-mɛŋ siini lʋgʋr la linɛ bɛ Ottawa sʋ'ʋlʋm la, anina o da anɛ tungatib kpɛɛm nɛ, kɔmitii kpɛɛm nɛ ba tuongat la nya'andɔl.
english: He attended Ontario based University of Carleton where he studied " film studies program" and a former trainee at the Independent Filmmaker's Cooperative of Ottawa, at which he served as the Director's General, Chairman of the Diversity Committee and Vice President.

kusaal: on da mɔr yʋma 21 la ka maal o siini linɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr buon, "Jamie nɛ Eddie: sunpɛɛn siis" .
english: He produced his debut movie "Jamie and Eddie: Souls of Strife" which he produced, directed and co-starred at age 21.

kusaal: on da bɛ Canada teŋin, li yʋma awai nya'aŋ, Pascal da lɛb Ghana si'iŋi o mɛŋ tʋʋma kanɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr buon ye, "suor yɔ'ɔgir media tʋʋma".
english: After 9 years in Canada, Pascal returned to Ghana and started his own production company called "Breakthrough Media Productions".

kusaal: O da lɛm maal sininam la bɛ Nollywood films la ni.
english: She has also acted in a number of Nollywood films.

kusaal: Ninanna, o maanɛ sininam la ka mɛ lɛm sʋŋid nidib ka ba maani ba sininam, nɛ sini msslʋg sakur, sininami maan si'em-si'em, nɛ nnwisigir zin'ig kanɛ an yiiga bɛ Ghana, GeoDan Health and Fitness Centre.
english: Currently, she combines her career as an actress with managing her film acting training school, Film Techniques, and a fitness gym in Ghana, GeoDan Health and Fitness Centre.

kusaal: Ban da du'a o bɛ Lomé, Togo yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi (1970) la ni, Pascaline Edwards da kenɛ Ghana na bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobu (1986) la ni na kpɛ' Ghanatta Senior High School la.
english: Born in Lomé, Togo in 1970, Pascaline Edwards came to Ghana in 1986 and attended Ghanatta Senior High School.

kusaal: On da namɔr yʋma piiga nɛ nya'aŋ la, o da keŋ pa'ali o mi'ilim an si'em be yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai (1990s) la ni ka tʋm nɛ Ghana nidib banɛ banɛ mi' I sini tʋʋma hali la dinɛ an Talent Drama Group.
english: Barely out of her teens, she honed her stage skills in the early 1990s as a member of Ghanaian acting group Talent Drama Group.

kusaal: O da anɛ sini di'em-di'em tuongati bɛ The Leopard's Choice yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi (1992) la saŋa.
english: She was the lead actress in The Leopard's Choice (1992).

kusaal: O da lɛb nyaŋi maligim zamis ka lɛb na ka o di'ema la an sʋm hali, on da ye la'asʋg di'ema dinɛ anɛ Emancipation Day ye ba tiɛe dinɛ anɛ saŋkpansim tʋʋma dinɛ k aba da kadi bas Ghana kpala yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu (1995) la ni.
english: She went back to stage acting and her major break came with a series of classic performances when Emancipation Day celebrations to commemorate the abolition of slavery were introduced in Ghana in 1995.

kusaal: O da gi'em kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon ye Fathia Nkrumah, Ghana yiiga zugraan pua, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, di'ema la ni o maali o mɛŋ nwɛni onɛ da an saŋkpan'as kudim pua nɛ, ka da kpi'im hali ye ba kad saŋkpan'asim da' diibʋ bas di'ema la ni yʋʋm tusir,kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu(1995) la ni.
english: She played the role of Fathia Nkrumah, wife of Ghana's first President Dr Kwame Nkrumah in a drama staged during the celebrations and played the role of the wife of former slave trader who was active in abolition of the slave trade in the drama Abolition (1995).

kusaal: O da di'em sininsm la bɛdigʋ bɛ Ghana kpala, on da tʋm nɛ Nollywood (Nigerian) sini dim la, di da sʋŋɔ ka o tʋʋma kɛŋ tuon, di'em kanɛ da an Journey of the Dead yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayinne (2001) la ni.
english: After a series of Ghanaian productions, her career took another major boost when she began acting major roles in Nollywood (Nigerian) movies with Journey of the Dead (2001).

kusaal: Edward da mɛ' sini maalʋg sakur, dinɛ anɛ Film Techniques bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la ni ka li sʋŋ ka o ya'ŋi pa'al nimbani duod n aka bɔɔd ye ba pɛɛs sini maalʋg di'ema la ni.
english: Edwards set up a film acting institute, Film Techniques in 2007, to share her experience with young actors and actresses, who have the flair and passion to act.

kusaal: O sini banɛ yʋ'ʋri da yip aa anɛ A Stab in the Dark, Forbidden Fruit (2000), The Mask, House Arrest, My Father's Wife (1998), Messages, Deadline for Asante, Without Her Consent, and Jewels.
english: Some of the popular movies she starred in include A Stab in the Dark, Forbidden Fruit (2000), The Mask, House Arrest, My Father's Wife (1998), Messages, Deadline for Asante, Without Her Consent, and Jewels.

kusaal: Edward da ɛlnɛ Dan Badu, onɛ da an Commissioner for TV3's Ghana's Strongest IV.
english: Edwards is married to Dan Badu, Commissioner for TV3's Ghana's Strongest IV.

kusaal: O dgin an vɛnl hali ka maali o mɛŋ nwɛni niŋsʋŋ nɛ,ka dɔlisi ani paam suori dɛgin nɛ o zua kanɛ nɔki o yada wʋsa tis o saam, ka san'am sumalisim kanɛ bɛ buudi la ni, bɛ o sini kanɛ an Stab in the Dark yʋʋm yusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai (1999) la ni, di anɛ di'em kasa da ke ka o yʋ'ʋr dʋ hali.
english: It was her portrayal of a student, who took advantage of a friend's trust to seduce her friend's father and destabilise a happy family, in Stab in the Dark (1999) that took her film career to a new level and projected her into stardom.

kusaal: Patricia Appiagyei (du'anɛ 28 November 1956) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd, o da anɛ tʋm an Deputy Ashanti Regional Minister ka an pʋ'a kanɛ an yiiga daan lieb Mayor of Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly.
english: Patricia Appiagyei (born 28 November 1956) is a Ghanaian politician, one-time Deputy Ashanti Regional Minister and the first female mayor of Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la na Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la tis Asokwa Constituency sʋ'ʋlim .
english: She is the Member of Parliament (MP) in the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing Asokwa Constituency.

kusaal: O yinɛ Konongo/Asawase-Kumasi kanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Appiagyei was born on 28 November 1956 in Kumasi and hails from Konongo/Asawase-Kumasi, in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋi o secondary education nɛ St Louis Senior Secondary bɛ Kumasi la ka tɔlisi keŋ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, ani ka o da maal BA Social Science Economics/Law kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii (1980).
english: She had her secondary education at the St Louis Senior Secondary in Kumasi and proceeded to Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, where she studied BA Social Science Economics/Law Archived 25 April 2023 at the Wayback Machine in 1980.She further did her Post graduate diploma- Development Economics in 1988.

kusaal: Appiagyei da tʋmnɛ City Investments Company Limited ni ka aan ba executive director of Marketing din yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la ni (1995) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piiga (2010).
english: Appiagyei previously worked with City Investments Company Limited as the executive director of marketing from 1995 to 2010.

kusaal: Appiagyei da anɛ Deputy Minista tis Ashanti region yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ yinne (2001) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu (2005) di da pʋ yuugɛ ka ba gaŋ o ye o an Deputy Ashanti Regional Minista yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni 2(005).
english: Appiagyei was a Deputy Minister for Ashanti region from 2001 to 2005 and was shortly appointed a Deputy Ashanti Regional Minister in 2005.

kusaal: Din da yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu (2005) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni la (2009) o da anɛ Municipal Chief Executive tis Kumasi.
english: From 2005 to 2009 she served as the Municipal Chief Executive for Kumasi.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Asokwa Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim, on da di ka bas deputy Local Government minista kʋdʋg, Maxwell Kofi Jumah, ka di Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, (New Patriotic Party) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: She is currently the Member of Parliament (MP) for Asokwa Constituency after beating former deputy Local Government minister, Maxwell Kofi Jumah, to win the New Patriotic Party (NPP) primary election and subsequently won the parliamentary seat during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O da lɛn di yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la lieb Wadmaani tis o sʋ'ʋlim dim ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaas la ni.
english: She won the 2020 general election to represent her constituents in the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la nii (2017), Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ka Wadmaanib siaki tis o ye o lieb deputy minista tis Environment, Science and Technology and Innovation.
english: In 2017, she was appointed by Nana Akufo-Addo and approved by parliament to serve as the deputy minister for Environment, Science and Technology and Innovation.

kusaal: O paas banɛ gɔsid Nuclear Power Ghana kpɛla la ni.
english: She is a board member for the Nuclear Power Ghana.

kusaal: Appiagyei da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid tam nɛ tiis yɛla (Lands and Forestry) o lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid nidib banɛ gaansid nidib tisidi ba tʋʋma yɛla (Appointments Committe).
english: Appiagyei is a member of the Lands and Forestry Committee and also a member of the Appointments Committee.

kusaal: Appiagyei Dr K. K. Sarpong da anɛ CEO kʋdʋg tis Kotoko FC nɛ Ghana National Petroleum Corporation pʋ'a kanɛ paasi ayi', o mɔr biisa atan'.
english: Appiagyei is the second wife of Dr K. K. Sarpong, a former CEO of Kotoko FC and Ghana National Petroleum Corporation, and has three children.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni, (July 2021) o da gilig sʋ'ʋlim sieba bɛ Kumas; Old Asokwa nɛ Kaase nɛ Asokwa Extension nɛ Atonsu nɛ Agogo zin'ibanɛ ka satita'ar da ni daba ayi' ka ku'om di'e zin'ig la ka pʋ gat la.
english: In July 2021, she paid visits to some areas in Kumasi including Old Asokwa, Kaase, Asokwa Extension, Atonsu and Agogo which got flooded after a two-day downpour.

kusaal: O mɛ da kaae New Bethel Presbyterian Primary nɛ JHS la.
english: She also visited the New Bethel Presbyterian Primary and JHS.

kusaal: O paas nɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, (New Patriotic Party) ni, Ghana kpɛla.
english: She is a member of the New Patriotic Party in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Appiagyei nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ Nwadis pii nɛ yinne la dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 November 1956) Kumasi.
english: Appiagyei was born on 28 November 1956 in Kumasi and hails from Konongo/Asawase-Kumasi, in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi maali o Post graduate diploma- Development Economics kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) la ni.
english: She had her secondary education at the St Louis Senior Secondary in Kumasi and proceeded to Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, where she studied BA Social Science Economics/Law Archived 25 April 2023 at the Wayback Machine in 1980.She further did her Post graduate diploma- Development Economics in 1988.

kusaal: O anɛ Kumasi Mayor kʋdʋg.
english: From 2005 to 2009 she served as the Municipal Chief Executive for Kumasi.

kusaal: Patrick Al-Hassan Adamah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Sissala West Constituency bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim la wabʋg na'adɔɔg, (New Patriotic Party) nɔba zug.
english: Patrick Al-Hassan Adamah (born 23 November 1948) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Sissala West Constituency in the Upper West Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O mɔri Associate degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi University of London's Royal School of Mines nɛ BSC in English kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Imperial College.
english: He earned an Associate degree from the University of London's Royal School of Mines and a BSC in English from Imperial College.

kusaal: Din yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' la ni (1972) keŋ paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) la ni la, Patrick Al-Hassan da tʋm tis British Coal n an research mining engineer.
english: From 1972 until 1988, Adamah worked for British Coal as a research mining engineer.

kusaal: Din yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) la ni, o da anɛ regional manager tis Kolon Limited, U.K. Africa.
english: From 1988 to 2007, he served as the regional manager of Kolon Limited, U.K. Africa.

kusaal: Ba du'a Banor nɛ nwadis ayuobʋ la li dabisim piinɛ atan' daar yʋʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu la ni n bɛ kernyasi sʋ'ʋlim zin'ikanɛ ka ba buon ye 'kal ayi'' la ni (13th june 1975).
english: Banor was born on Friday 13 June 1975 at Kenyasi No.2.

kusaal: O da naae ka mɔri o pin'ilʋg sakur kasɛta gbauŋ nɛ yʋʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi la ni (1994).
english: He obtained his Basic Education Certificate in 1991, and his Secondary School Certificate in 1994.

kusaal: Gaana tuogatib wʋsa gaansʋg saŋa kanɛ da bɛ yʋʋma tusa pisi nɛ pisi la ni la (2020), o da lɛn zi'en nya'a wadmaanib kυk la nɛ Ebenezer kwaku Addo onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la nɛ Ka nya'a nɛ kofi anani o an GUM dim na'adɔɔg nid la n di ka basi ba.
english: During the 2020 Ghanaian general election, Banor contested for the Asutifi North seat with Ebenezer Kwaku Addo of the NDC, and Kofi Annan of GUM.

kusaal: Ka Addo mɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa piinɛ ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayuobʋ(16546) ka li an kal pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ du'alʋg anu(47.05%) kɔbʋg pʋʋgin.
english: He polled 18505 votes representing 52.62% of the total valid votes cast against Addo's 16546 votes and Anane's 116 votes, representing 47.05% and 0.33% of the total valid votes cast respectively.

kusaal: Patrik Banor anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd nɛ kpɛɛmnam la yinne.
english: Patrick Banor is a Ghanaian politician and an administrator.

kusaal: O mɔr ninsaalib kpinim nɛ bɛllim tʋʋma zamisʋg kasɛta gbauŋ yʋʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: He was awarded his Bachelor of Arts degree in Sociology and Social Work in 2009.

kusaal: O da mɔri vɔɔt kanl tusa piinɛ anii nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ anu(18505) ka li an kanl pisnu nɛ ayi' nɛ du'alʋg pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi'(52.62%) kɔbʋg pʋʋgin, ba ya'a la'as vɔɔtnam la wʋsa.
english: He polled 18505 votes representing 52.62% of the total valid votes cast against Addo's 16546 votes and Anane's 116 votes, representing 47.05% and 0.33% of the total valid votes cast respectively.

kusaal: Ka an onɛ mɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ(116) ka li an du'alʋg pistan' nɛ atan(0.33%) kɔbʋg pʋʋgin.
english: He polled 18505 votes representing 52.62% of the total valid votes cast against Addo's 16546 votes and Anane's 116 votes, representing 47.05% and 0.33% of the total valid votes cast respectively.

kusaal: Ka nwadis anii la ni ka o lɛn sʋŋ tis pu'asada sakur kanɛ bɛ o sʋ'ʋlimin la kʋkʋs kɔbisnaasi (400 desks).
english: In August 2021, he presented about 400 desks to Ola Girls' SHS.

kusaal: Patrick Boakye-Yiadom anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Ghana wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi nɛ anii la pʋʋg, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: Patrick Boakye-Yiadom is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Obuasi East Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Patrick nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1976).
english: Patrick was born on 2 November 1976 and hails from Obuasi in the Ashanti region.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ ka o keŋ maal MBChB, General Medical Practitioner yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la ni (2003).
english: He obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in human biology in 2000 and a MBChB in General Medical Practitioner in 2003.

kusaal: O anɛ sakur biigi bɛ KNUST ka o paas yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' (2003) sakur biis banɛ zamisid nimma'asim yɛla la (Class of the School of Medical Science).
english: He is a student of KNUST in the 2003 Class of the School of Medical Science.

kusaal: Patrick da anɛ Medical Director nya'andɔli tis Bryant Mission Hospitali bɛ Obuasi.
english: Patrick was the Deputy Medical Director for the Bryant Mission Hospital in Obuasi.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔdʋgʋn la, o da di kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbis yɔpɔi nɛ pii nɛ anu (27,715), ka ma'asim tiig (NDC) Richard Ofori-Agyeman Boadi paam vɔɔt kal tusa piiga nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi (10,604), ka PPP Patrick Aboagye Danyansah mɛ paam vɔɔt kal tusir yinne nɛ kɔbistan' nɛ pii nɛ anii (1,318), ka CPP Emmanual Oduro Fosu paam vɔɔt kal piswai nɛ anii (98), ka Akubɛ, PNC sɔb la, Shaibu Fuseini paam vɔɔt pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (66).
english: In the 2016 Ghana general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 27,715 votes whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Richard Ofori-Agyeman Boadi had 10,604 votes and the PPP parliamentary aspirant Patrick Aboagye Danyansah also had 1,318 votes whiles the CPP parliamentary aspirant Emmanual Oduro Fosu had 98 votes and the PNC parliamentary Shaibu Fuseini had 66 votes.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔdʋgʋn la, o da lɛn di kʋk la ya'as nɛ vɔɔtnam tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnii nɛ atan' (27,583), ka ma'asim tiig (NDC) Samuel Aboagye da paam vɔɔtnam tusa pii nɛ anaasi nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (14,786).
english: In the 2020 Ghana general elections, he again won the parliamentary seat with 27,583 votes whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Samuel Aboagye had 14,786 votes.

kusaal: Patrick da anɛ kʋkdaan nya'andɔli tis la'askanɛ gɔsid nimma'asim yɛla, o da lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Government Assurance ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid tʋʋma nɛ ya yɛla la.
english: Patrick is the Vice chairperson of the Health Committee, a member of the Government Assurance Committee and also a member of the Works and Housing Committee.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) la ni, Patrick da da' gadis pisi (20 beds) tis Sibitinam anaasi Obuasi East sʋ'ʋlim.
english: In 2020, Patrick provided about 20 beds to four hospitals in the Obuasi East Constituency.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi la nwadis ayuobʋ la ni (August 2022), o da nɔk masinkanɛ maan popcorn, firik zuluma (deep freezers), masin banɛ tuod sa'ab la nɛ saana bɔtʋnami tis tadimnam (PWDs ) banɛ bɛ Obuasi East District.
english: In August 2022, he presented popcorn machines, deep freezers, fufu pounding machines and some bags of charcoal to PWDs in the Obuasi East District.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Obuasi East sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Kumasi la.
english: Patrick Boakye-Yiadom is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Obuasi East Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Obuasi bɛ Kumasi sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Patrick was born on 2 November 1976 and hails from Obuasi in the Ashanti region.

kusaal: O da tɔlis naae o SSSCE nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994).
english: He completed his basic in 1988, his BECE in 1991, and his SSSCE in 1994.

kusaal: Ka tɔlis tuoni maal bachelor's in science degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ in Human Biology yʋma tusa ayi' la ni (2000).
english: He obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in human biology in 2000 and a MBChB in General Medical Practitioner in 2003.

kusaal: Ka an wadmaani tis Obuasi East bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Patrick is a member of NPP and currently the MP for the Obuasi East Constituency in the Ashanti region.

kusaal: Patrick Bogyako-Siaime anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka bɛ Seventh Parliament dinɛ bɛ Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Amenfi East Constituency bɛ Western Region bɛ wabʋg paati la ni.
english: Patrick Bogyako-Siaime is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Amenfi East Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: September 24, 1964 ka ba da du'a o.
english: On September 24, 1964, he was born.

kusaal: O mɔr MBA kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit KNUST nɛ Bachelor of Commerce kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit University of Cape Coast nɛ Post Graduate Diploma in purchasing and supply kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply ni mɛn .
english: He earned an MBA from KNUST, a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Cape Coast, and a Post Graduate Diploma in purchasing and supply from the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply.

kusaal: Din yi yʋma 1993 ti paae yʋma 1998, Patrick Bogyako-Saime da tʋmnɛ anregional marketing officer bɛ Electricity Company of Ghana ni.
english: From 1993 to 1998, Patrick Bogyako-Saime served as the regional marketing officer for the Electricity Company of Ghana.

kusaal: Ka lin yi yʋma 1998 ti paae yʋma 2003 la ni la, o da anɛ transport manager, ka lin yi yʋma 2003 ti paae nwɛ'ɛd yʋma 2006 ni la o da anɛ internal audit manager tis Ghana Oil Palm Plantation, ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2006) la ni, ka o da tʋm an group internal auditor.
english: From 1998 to 2003, he served as the transport manager, from 2003 to 2006 as the internal audit manager for the Ghana Oil Palm Plantation, and in 2006, he worked for Golden Star Resources as a group internal auditor.

kusaal: ŋPatrick Yaw Boamah (dʋ'anɛ 1974) anɛ politis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Okaikwei Central Constituency teŋkanɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region la ni, Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (New Patriotic Party) nɔba zug.
english: Patrick Yaw Boamah (born 1974) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Okaikwei Central Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Boamah nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi Nwadisa awai la dabpii nɛ awai daar (19 mɔtul nwadig 1974).
english: Boamah was born on 19 September 1974.

kusaal: O yinɛ Mourso-Effiduase teŋkanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana la.
english: He hails from Mourso-Effiduase, in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maal o bachelor of laws nɛ master's degree kasɛta gbana in International Affairs yit University of Ghana yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la ni (2004) nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu (2005).
english: He obtained his bachelor of laws and master's degree in international affairs from the University of Ghana in 2004 and 2005 respectively.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ ka o tɔlis tuoni keŋ Ghana School of Law maali o barrister-at-law degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: He later proceeded to the Ghana School of Law where he received his barrister-at-law degree in 2009.

kusaal: Boamah da kpɛn' Wadmaanib yin la nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2013) Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (New Patriotic Party) nɔba zug zi'eni tis Okaikwei Central Constituency.
english: Boamah entered parliament on 7 January 2013 on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party representing the Okaikwei Central Constituency.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt tis o yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana dim wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la ye o lɛn zi'eni tisi ba ya'as, ken kanɛ paasi ayi' .
english: He was re-elected in the 2016 ,2020 and 2024 Ghanaian General Election to represent the constituency for a second consecutive term.

kusaal: Wadmaanib yin la, o tʋm la'asʋg nam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ni ka ba sieba anɛ; the Subsidiary Legislation Committee, the Judiciary Committee, and the Foreign Affairs Committee.
english: In parliament, he has served on various committees, some of which include; the Subsidiary Legislation Committee, the Judiciary Committee, and the Foreign Affairs Committee.

kusaal: O da nya' yʋm tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana dim wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la la ni, Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, (New Patriotic Party) nɔba zug ka di.
english: He contested in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election as the parliamentary candidate for the New Patriotic Party and he won.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Methodist pʋ'ʋsʋm Ghana.
english: He identifies as a Christian and a member of the Methodist Church of Ghana.

kusaal: Boamah mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa ayi'.
english: Boamah is married with two children.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) la ni, UNESCO da yɛl ye di anɛ Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008), ka zaŋi li paasi di Representative List ni.
english: In 2005, UNESCO declared it one of the Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity and, in 2008, inscribed it on its Representative List.

kusaal: Documented since 1628.
english: They have been documented since 1628.

kusaal: Els Turcs i Cavallets (Turks and Little Knights).
english: The Trucs/Turcs i Cavallets (Turks and Knights) are a representation of four Turk soldiers, wearing turbans and carrying scimitars, and four Christian knights with wooden horses at their waists.

kusaal: Els Nans Vells (The Old Dwarfs).
english: The Nans/Nanos Vells (Old Dwarfs).

kusaal: "La Patum" da pin'ilnɛ pre-Christian da maan Summer solstice, dinɛ ka Catholic Church da tiaki tisidi di yʋ'ʋpaal nɛ zanbin paal ka di paasi ba Corpus celebration.
english: "La Patum" has its origins in pre-Christian celebrations of the summer solstice, which were recycled and given new symbolism by the Catholic Church as part of its Corpus celebrations.

kusaal: Anthropologists nɛ mi'ilim dim banɛ bɛ folklore la mɔr bɔɔdim tis La Patum.
english: Anthropologists and specialists in folklore have been interested in La Patum.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ay nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) la ni, ka ba da ye ba maali ba malʋŋkanɛ paas kɔbiga nɛ piisnu la (150th anniversary kanɛ ka "old giants" (Gegants vells) nɛ yʋʋm kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ anu tienr malʋŋ tis "new giants" (Gegants nous), Bruce Springsteen yʋʋmkanɛ an "If I should fall behind", ka Sergi Cuenca la'asi li la, both couples of giants da la'asi wa'a di.
english: In 2016, to celebrate the 150th anniversary of the "old giants" (Gegants vells) and the 125th anniversary of the "new giants" (Gegants nous), the Bruce Springsteen song If I should fall behind, arranged by Sergi Cuenca, was danced by both couples of giants.

kusaal: Els Nans Nous (The New Dwarfs).
english: The Nans/Nanos Nous (New Dwarfs).

kusaal: Berga pʋʋgin, ba da pin'ili maal Corpus procession nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi, nwadisa anu la dabpisi daar (May 20, 1454).
english: In Berga, the earliest conserved reference to a Corpus procession is May 20, 1454.[1] The origins of the festival come from the figures in this procession, destined to educate the people on Christian values.

kusaal: La'an nɛ Corpus Christi mɔr nyɔɔd si'em tis pʋ'ʋsimnam nɛ malima suoya la, nɛ Patum yi "eucharistic tʋʋmanamin la, din an si'em nananna la an sʋ'ʋm gaad ban na bɔɔd ye ba ʋki ba mɛŋ bɛdegʋ.
english: Despite the religious significance of Corpus Christi and the Patum's descent from "eucharistic performances," in its present form it is rather a show of popular theater.

kusaal: Paul Apreku Twum-Barimah anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani tis Dormaa East constituency n bɛ Bono region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Paul Apreku Twum-Barimah is a Ghanaian politician and member of parliament for the Dormaa East constituency in the Bono region of Ghana .

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Paul nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi Nwadisa anu la dabpisi nɛ atan daar (23 May 1982) ka o yi Kobedia-Asupra n bɛ Bono region, Ghana.
english: Barimah was born on 23 May 1982 and hails from Kobedia-Asupra in the Bono region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da sɔbi o SSSCE yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2000).
english: He had his SSSCE in 2000.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ maal o MSc in Communications and Public Affairs yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni (2012).
english: He further had his MSc in Communications and Public Affairs in 2012.

kusaal: Ka maali o LLB in General Law yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018).
english: He had his LLB in General Law in 2018.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr certificate in Oil, Gas & Petroleum Management yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2020).
english: He also had his certificate in Oil, Gas & Petroleum Management in 2020.

kusaal: Paul da dnɛ Head of Event and Production tis Radio Universe.
english: Barimah was the Head of Event and Production at Radio Universe.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Station Manager tis RGU radio.
english: He was also the Station Manager at RGU radio.

kusaal: O da an Media mechanical and engineering manager tis EXP Ghana ka lɛn an Assistant Communication Officer tis British High Commission.
english: He was also the Assistant Communication Officer at the British High Commission.

kusaal: O da lɛn an Corporate Affairs and Sustainability Manager tis Zen Petroleum.
english: He was also the Corporate Affairs and Sustainability Manager for Zen Petroleum.

kusaal: O da lɛn an Development Communication Coordinator tis SADA.
english: He was also the Development Communication Coordinator for SADA.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Government Relations and Regulatory Affairs tis ENI Ghana Exploration & Production Limited.
english: He was also the Government Relations and Regulatory Affairs for ENI Ghana Exploration & Production Limited.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP nid ka an Wadmaani, tis Dormaa East Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: He is a member of NPP and currently the MP for Dormaa East Constituency.

kusaal: O da di Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayuobʋ, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pidyɔpɔi nɛ awai (16,679) ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC nid la, Racheal Owusuah paam vɔɔt Tusa piinɛ yinne, kɔbistan nɛ pisnii nɛ atan (11,383).
english: He won the parliamentary seat with 16,679 votes whilst the NDC aspirant Racheal Owusuah had 11,383 votes.

kusaal: O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid Special Budget, ka lɛm paas banɛ gɔsid Foreign Affairs nɛ banɛ gɔsid Poverty Reduction Strategy.
english: He is a member of the Special Budget Committee, a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, Privileges Committee, Roads and Transport Committee, Mines and Energy committee and also a member of the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee.

kusaal: O da lɛn tis Sibiti gat nɛ nimma'asim tʋʋma la'ad sieba tis Wamfie District Hospital.
english: He also gave hospital beds and medical equipment to the Wamfie District Hospital.

kusaal: O da maali o bachelor's degree in Sociology & Information Studies in Social Science yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ ni (2006).
english: He is lawyer, had his bachelor's degree in Sociology & Information Studies in Social Science in 2006.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni, (December 2021), o da nɔk diib nɛ la'asieba piinl pʋkɔnya nwɛnɛ kɔbisyi' Dormaa East constituency sʋ'ʋlim.
english: In December 2021, he donated food and other assorted items to about 200 widows in the Dormaa East constituency.

kusaal: Ka lɛn nɔk tʋʋma la'ad tis nidib nwɛnɛ kɔbisnaasi (400) banɛ zamisid tʋʋma Wamanafo nɛ Wamfie.
english: He also donated working equipment and tools to about 400 apprentices and workers in Wamanafo and Wamfie.

kusaal: Da ba du'a o nɛ pʋdi o yʋ'ʋr ye Joseph Paul Walcott bɛ London, England, anina ka o nɔbig.
english: He was born Joseph Paul Walcott in London, England, where he grew up.

kusaal: O ma yʋ'ʋr anɛ Bertha May Walcott, o da anɛ naasara, ka o saam yʋ'ʋr an Joseph Boakye "J.B." Danquah o da anɛ Ghanaian politician ka lɛm an traditional aristocrat; Paul li da an bi kpɛɛm o puab ayi la wʋsa ni.
english: His mother, Bertha May Walcott, was English, and his father Joseph Boakye "J.B." Danquah was a Ghanaian politician and traditional aristocrat; Paul was the eldest of his many children from two marriages and various relationships.

kusaal: Danquah da zamisnɛ wada(law) ka ba buol o ka kena pɛɛs wadmaanib (call to the bar) la bɛ Inner Temple o da tʋmnɛ Ghana ka mɛ lɛm tʋm bɛ Washington, D.C. o da lɛm ken tʋmnɛ bankuŋ bɛ World Bank hali ti kɛm paae o saŋa bɛn yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuonu(1989) la ni ka ka bɛ Washington befriended African-American arts practitioners pɛɛs nɛ Maya Angelou, James Baldwin, Roberta Flack and Nina Simone.
english: Danquah studied law and was called to the bar at the Inner Temple, as well as in Ghana and in Washington, D.C. He subsequently worked as a consultant with the World Bank until his retirement in 1986, and while living in Washington befriended African-American arts practitioners including Maya Angelou, James Baldwin, Roberta Flack and Nina Simone.

kusaal: Danquah da nam an sakur biig la ka maal sini bɛ British sini ni dinɛ anɛ A Taste of Honey yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ ayinne(1961), la ni ka o tʋʋm da an Jimmy.
english: While still a student, Danquah made his acting debut in the British film A Taste of Honey (1961), featuring in the role of Jimmy.

kusaal: New York Times dim mɛ da pian'a di yɛla: "Paul Danquah da di'em wʋʋ Negro sailor nɛ an baanlim ka mɔr ya'am kani ka ba bɔɔdi o yɛla.
english: A review in The New York Times noted: "Paul Danquah in his movie debut as the Negro sailor, is gentle and subtle in a small but demanding role".

kusaal: O da keŋ pian nɛ BBC Two television series Play School ni bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ anu (1965) la ni k aba pian'a pa'al ye on ma'aa an ninsabil kanɛ kena pian'a biis la'asʋg di'ema bɛ UK.
english: He presented the BBC Two television series Play School in 1965 and is reported to have been the first black presenter of a children's programme in the UK.

kusaal: Painter Francis Bacon da gbɛɛndnɛ nɛ Danquah ka Danquah da tʋm nɛ Peter Pollock yʋʋm tusir, wain ɛ piiga nɛ awi Sapal nwadig la dabisim piiga nɛ awai paae yʋʋma tusa ayi, nɛ ayinne Mɔraʋg nwadig la ni.
english: Painter Francis Bacon lived with Danquah and Danquah's partner Peter Pollock (19 November 1919 – 18 July 2001) in their Battersea flat from 1956 to 1961.

kusaal: Saŋ kaŋa bɛ yʋʋmtusir nɛ kɔbis wain ɛ pisyuobu naar la ka Danquah da ti'ebid nɛ Don Bachardy ye on yaŋ Bacon.
english: During this period, in late 1961, Danquah arranged for Don Bachardy to draw Bacon.

kusaal: Danquah kennɛ nɛ Pollock paae Tangier, Morocco, dinɛ bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi (1970s) la naarin.
english: Danquah moved with Pollock to Tangier, Morocco, in the late 1970s.

kusaal: Danquah da kpinɛ bɛ Tangier bɛ yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anu Mʋtul nwadig la dabisim piiga nɛ atan' (13 August 2015) la ni, ka o mɔr yʋma piswai (90yrs); nwɛnɛ o yaaŋ Meri Nana-Ama Danquah da yɛli ba si'em la, ba da mʋm o nɛ bɛ Boubana kum yaadin la kpi'eɛ nɛ Peter Pollock nwɛnɛ o mɛŋi da yɛl si'em la.
english: Danquah died in Tangier on 13 August 2015 at the age of 90; according to his niece Meri Nana-Ama Danquah, he was buried in Boubana Cemetery, beside Peter Pollock, as he had requested in his will.

kusaal: O da anɛ British dim sini tʋm-tʋm ka nidib mi' o pamm yee o da tʋmnɛ nɛ A Taste of Honey yʋʋm tʋsir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobu nɛ yinne(1961) la ni, o da tʋm nɛ Shelagh Delaney ka o da sɔbnɛ o yʋ'ʋ kan nɔɔ, yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai pisnu nɛ anii(1958) la ni.
english: Paul Danquah, born Joseph Paul Walcott (25 May 1925 – 13 August 2015), was a British film actor, known particularly for his role in the film A Taste of Honey (1961), adapted from the 1958 play of the same name written by Shelagh Delaney.

kusaal: O da mʋ'asidi o tʋm-tʋm tiraan Rita Tushingham, ka o da pian'a pa'al dinɛ an yiiga mʋ'asʋg dinɛ ka on mʋ'as sɔ nɔɔr sini pʋʋgin.
english: He shared a kiss with his co-star Rita Tushingham, which she claims was the first interracial kiss on screen.

kusaal: bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ piswaii (1990s) la naarin, Danquah nɛ Pallock da nyɛ gʋlisim ka di sɔbi bɛ siel pʋʋgin ka Baton da sɔbi li; gʋlisim bama da anɛ dinɛ ka Tate bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis wai nɛ piswai nɛ ayoubu(1996) ka ba pa'al li di bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ(1999) la ni.
english: In the late 1990s, Danquah and Pollock discovered a suitcase containing drawings by Bacon; these drawings were acquired by the Tate in 1996 and exhibited in 1999.

kusaal: O da kɛna anɛ wadmaan ka lɛm an onɛ gɔsid ligidi yɛla.
english: He later became a barrister and a bank consultant.

kusaal: Paul Essien anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Jomoro Constituency bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlʋm, wabʋg na'adɔɔg (New Patriotic Party) nɔba zug.
english: Paul Essien is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Jomoro Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ Nass Senior High School ti maali o Ordinary level certificate ka da tɔlisi keŋ maali o Advanced Level bɛ Nsein Senior High School.
english: He attended Nass Senior High School for his Ordinary level certificate and for his Advanced Level he moved to Nsein Senior High School.

kusaal: O mɔri Bachelor Science degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ in Statistics yit University of Cape Coast.
english: He also has a Bachelor Science degree in Statistics from the University of Cape Coast.

kusaal: Fassi ka o maal dinna, Essien,da maali o Higher National Diploma (HND) kasɛta gbaʋŋ yinɛ Takoradi polytechnic kanɛy yʋ'ʋn an Takoradi Technical University la.
english: Prior to that Essien, had obtained a Higher National Diploma (HND) from Takoradi polytechnic now Takoradi Technical University.

kusaal: O da maali o tʋmma tis gɔmena nɛ national service Nɛ GRA (VAT) Din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2007) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anii (2008).
english: He did his mandatory national service at GRA (VAT) from 2007 to 2008.

kusaal: O da pa'al gɛligir (mathematics) Zamisʋg ka da lɛn an form master nɛ pa'an kanɛ gɔsid ninwisigir yɛla (sports teacher) tis Annor Adjaye Senior High School din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anii la ni (2008) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: He taught as a mathematics teacher whilst serving as a form master and sports teacher at Annor Adjaye Senior High School from 2008 to 2016.

kusaal: O da anɛ District kpɛɛm kanɛ gɔsid Bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb yɛla yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii la ni (1998) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la ni (2003).
english: He was the District Sports Chairman from 1998 to 2003.

kusaal: O da paas nɛ 7th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana la ni, ka zi'eni tis Jomoro Constituency.
english: He is a member of the 7th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana representing the Jomoro Constituency.

kusaal: O da di kʋk la ka bas Thomas Elleamo Yankey onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid la, (National Democratic Congress), nɛ Samia Yaaba Christina Nkrumah onɛ an Nɔraʋg na'adɔɔg nid la (Convention People's Party) ka an wadmaan kʋdʋg yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' (2013), ka da lɛn an Ghana yiiga Zugraan kʋdʋg Kwame Nkrumah pu'ayua.
english: He won in a fiercely contested election against most notably Thomas Elleamo Yankey of the National Democratic Congress and Samia Yaaba Christina Nkrumah of the Convention People's Party who is a former member of parliament (2009-2013) and happens to be the daughter of Ghana's first president Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: O da paam nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ anii nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (18,694) yit vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin ka li an vɔɔt pistan' nɛ awai du'al pisnaasi nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (39.49%), ka Thomas Yankey nɛ Samia Nkrumah da paam vɔɔt tusa pii nɛ anaasi nɛ kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yinne (14,241) ka li an vɔɔt pistan' du'ali anii kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (30.08%), nɛ vɔɔt tusa awai nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (9,714) ka li an vɔɔt pisi du'al pisnu nɛ ayi' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (20.52%), nwɛnnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: He won after obtaining 18,694 votes representing 39.49%, whilst Thomas Yankey and Samia Nkrumah had 14,241 votes representing 30.08% and 9,714 votes representing 20.52% respectively.

kusaal: Essien da tʋm bɛ kpikpiʋŋ tʋʋma ni nɛ Industry nɛ Tourism Committee nɛ Judiciary Committee bɛ 7th parliament la ni.
english: Essien serves on the Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee and the Judiciary Committee in the 7th parliament.

kusaal: Essien anɛ pa'an.
english: Essien is a teacher by profession.

kusaal: Essien paas nɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg (New Patriotic Party) ni.
english: Essien is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da di jomoro constituency sʋ'ʋlʋmwadmaan kʋk la yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016) Ghana vɔɔdʋg tita'ar.
english: He won the bid to represent the constituency after winning in the 2016 parliamentary and presidential elections.

kusaal: O da kɛŋne Uganda College zamis da'ab ne kʋosʋg, Nakawa zi'ig kane ka zina ka ba bʋon ye Makerere University Business School, o da naae ne yʋʋm tusir kobuswai ne piswai ne ayi, ka die gbaŋ Hotel ne diib gosʋg yela.
english: She studied at the Uganda College of Commerce, in Nakawa, which today is the Makerere University Business School, graduating in 1992, with a Diploma in Hotel Management and Catering.

kusaal: Yʋma tusir ne kobuswai ne piswai ne atan la, o da tʋmne so' sa'an wadisa atan Nile Hotel be Kampala.
english: In 1993, she worked as an apprentice for three months, at the Nile Hotel in Kampala.

kusaal: O me da dʋg diibʋ tis zʋgran Bill Clinton ne o yir'dim.
english: She has also, in the past, prepared meals for President Bill Clinton and his family.

kusaal: Peace Butera da kʋl sid Vincent Butera ka ba la'asi dʋa biis anaasi, Kylie, Kelly, Lillian, ne Laban, ayi da ane ba mɛŋ biis ka ba da nɔk ayi zin'sia mɛn.
english: Peace Butera is married to Vincent Butera and together are the parents of four children Kylie, Kelly, Lillian and Laban, two natural ones and two adopted ones.

kusaal: Hotel kaŋa anɛ zin'ig tita'ari bɛ Uganda tenmpʋtita'ar kanɛ an' Kampala la.
english: Peace Nankunda Butera is a Ugandan culinary artist, who works as the Executive Sous Chef (second-in-command) at the Kampala Serena Hotel, a five-star establishment in Kampala, Uganda's capital and largest city.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi ne anaasi la, Hotel la da tiak yʋʋr la ne lɛbis Kampala Serena Hotel.
english: In 2004, the hotel changed ownership and was renamed Kampala Serena Hotel Archived 2017-12-18 at the Wayback Machine.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ Peace Butera ye o zamis dʋgʋb Serena Hotel dim ni.
english: Peace Nankunda Butera is a Ugandan culinary artist, who works as the Executive Sous Chef (second-in-command) at the Kampala Serena Hotel, a five-star establishment in Kampala, Uganda's capital and largest city.

kusaal: On da lɛb Kampala la, ba da gaŋ o ne ka o an kpɛɛm daʋŋin Kampala Serena yʋma tusa ayi ne anu.
english: On her return to Kampala, she was appointed Sous chef at the Kampala Serena in 2005.

kusaal: Saŋa kane ka tens' zʋgran'nam gomena nam da la'as yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayopɔi la, li da ane Kampala ka si'iŋ dabis pisinɛ atan paae dabis pisinɛ anu wadis piinɛ yine yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayopɔi, pʋana'ab Elezabeth one paasa ayi la da gbɛ' Kampala Serena daba anaasi.
english: During the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 2007, which was held in Kampala, from 23 to 25 November 2007, Queen Elizabeth II stayed at the Kampala Serena for four days.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ Peace Butera ye o dʋg diibʋ tis pʋana'ab la saŋkan.
english: Chef Peace Butera was selected to prepare some of the Queen's menu items during that period.

kusaal: Ba dʋa o ne yir kanɛ mɔr biis piiga.
english: She was born in a family of ten siblings.

kusaal: Pentecost University anɛ asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ university kanɛ bɛ Sowutuom, Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim linɛ bɛ Ghana.
english: Pentecost University is a private university located at Sowutuom, in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Church of Pentecost (COP) dimi da pin'ili li ka li da pin'ili yinɛe Pentecost Bible College, zin'ig kanɛ ka ba da pa'an Wina'am tʋmtʋmnib ye ba tʋm Wina'am tʋʋma bɛ Pentecost Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔgin.
english: It was founded by The Church of Pentecost (COP) and evolved from the Pentecost Bible College, which initially trained only Lay Leaders and full-time Ministers for the COP.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ atan', sigsaa nwadig la ni, dabpisi nɛ ayi' daar la, Ghana gɔmɛna zugraan kʋdʋg J. A. Kufuor da zʋŋ sakur la bɛ Sowutuom zamisig zin'igin la.
english: On May 22, 2003, former President of Ghana J. A. Kufuor officially inaugurated PUC at the Sowutuom campus.

kusaal: University la da nɔki ba mɛŋi la'as nɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, University of Cape Coast, nɛ University of Ghana.
english: Prior to receiving a Presidential Charter, the university was affiliated to the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, University of Cape Coast, and University of Ghana.

kusaal: Kwabena Agyapong-Kodua, ye o di'e Apostle Daniel Okyere Walker nɔbiri an Vice-Chancellor kanɛ an yiiga, sakur la zi'eni ba mɛŋ nyali saŋa.
english: On June 1, 2020, the university announced the appointment of Rev. Prof. Kwabena Agyapong-Kodua, who replaces Apostle Daniel Okyere Walker, as the first Vice-Chancellor since the university became fully-fledged.

kusaal: Banɛ da an sakur kpɛɛmnam yiiga tis PUC da pin'ili bɛ nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi, sigsaa nwadig la, daba ayuobʋ daar.
english: The first PUC Council was inducted on May 6, 2004.

kusaal: Pentecost University paam paŋ kanɛ ka ba na tis kasɛta gbana nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi, Sapal nwadig la ni, ka Gɔmɛna zugraan mɛ tik nu'ugi bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, Sigsaa nwadig la ni, dabpisi nɛ anii daar, onɛ da an gɔmɛna zugraan tik nu'ug sankan la da anɛ Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo.
english: Pentecost University received accreditation from the National Accreditation Board (NAB) of Ghana in November 2004 and awarded its Presidential Charter on May 28, 2020, by Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, then President of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, sigir nwadig la pin'ilig daar, university la da yis mɔɔlig na ye ba gaŋ Rev.
english: On June 1, 2020, the university announced the appointment of Rev. Prof. Kwabena Agyapong-Kodua, who replaces Apostle Daniel Okyere Walker, as the first Vice-Chancellor since the university became fully-fledged.

kusaal: People's National Convention anɛ Na'adɔɔgʋ bɛ Ghana.
english: The People's National Convention is a political party in Ghana.

kusaal: Wada dɔlʋsʋgʋ da lɛb Ghana na yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛyi' (1992) ka Hilla Limann onɛ da an Ghana Zuraan la da pin'il Na'adɔɔg la dɔlisid baŋi kanɛ ka o paam yi People's National Party dinɛ ka o da aan di tuon gat yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ wai (1979) vɔɔtʋgin ka da di la.
english: After constitutional rule was restored back in Ghana in 1992 the party was formed by former President Hilla Limann based on ideals from the People's National Party which he led in the 1979 elections and won.

kusaal: PNC da nya' vɔɔtʋgnam kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb din yii di pin'ilʋg saŋa fourth republic la ni yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yi' wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la (1992 parliamentary election), kanɛ ka ban nɛ Na'adɔsieba da zan'as ye ba kʋ nya' la ma'aa.
english: The PNC has contested all national elections since the inception of the fourth republic apart from the 1992 parliamentary election, which was boycotted along with other opposition parties.

kusaal: Vɔɔtʋg kanɛ da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi Nwadis piinɛ yi' daba ayɔpɔi daar la (7 December 2004), Na'adɔɔg la da paas Grand Coalition, dinɛ da di kʋgʋs anaasi yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan' pʋʋgin la (230 seats).
english: At the elections held on 7 December 2004, the party was part of the Grand Coalition, which won four out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Edward Mahama, onɛ da an Na'anya'adi tis Grand Coalition, da paam vɔɔt yinne du'ali awai kɔbiga pʋʋgin (1.9%) Zuraanam vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Edward Mahama, candidate of the Grand Coalition, won 1.9% of the vote at the presidential elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii nwadis piinɛ yi' vɔɔtʋgin la (December 2008 elections), na'adɔɔg la da di wadmaannib kʋgʋs ayi keŋ wadmaannib yin la.
english: At the December 2008 elections, the party won two seats in Parliament.

kusaal: Hassan Ayariga da yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011) na'adɔɔg la vɔɔtʋgin ka da zi'eni nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yi' Zuraannam vɔɔtʋg la (2012 presidential election).
english: Hassan Ayariga was elected in 2011 by the party to stand in the 2012 presidential election.

kusaal: Hassan Ayariga onɛ da gaad na'adɔɔg la tuon yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yi' vɔɔtʋgin la (2012 elections) da yiya ka bas na'adɔɔg la on da nya' nɛ Edward Mahama ka pʋ di la, ka keŋ pin'ili o mɛŋ na'adɔɔg dinɛ yʋ'ʋri an All People's Congress.
english: Hassan Ayariga who led the party in the 2012 elections quit the party after losing to Edward Mahama and decided to start his own party All People's Congress.

kusaal: Paas nɔɔr anaasi tuunl ka Edward Mahama da an na'adɔɔg la Zuraan na'anya'ad.
english: For the fourth time in a row, Edward Mahama was the presidential candidate.

kusaal: Ayariga da paam vɔɔt nɛɛm du'al pisi nɛ yi' kɔbiga pʋʋgin.
english: Ayariga received 0.22% of the vote.

kusaal: Na'adɔɔg la da gaans tuon gatib paala yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu la ni (2015), Edward Mahama da aan di Zuraan na'anya'ad ka gbaʋŋ sɔbid Bernard Mornah lieb na'adɔɔg la kʋkdaan.
english: The party elected new officials in 2015, with Edward Mahama becoming its presidential candidate and General Secretary Bernard Mornah becoming the chairman.

kusaal: Ba Ghana wʋsa ligidsu'ad yʋ'ʋn anɛ Akane Adams onɛ di'e yi David Apasera san'an, onɛ an wadmaan kʋdʋgʋ tis Bolga Central.
english: The new National Treasurer is now Akane Adams who is taken over from his predecessor David Apasera, a former member of Parliament for Bolga Central.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt nɛɛm du'ali anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin.
english: He received 0.8% of the vote.

kusaal: Peter Ala Adjetey (Ba du'a o nɛ 11 August 1931 – ka o maal ka'alim 15 July 2008) da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ lɔya.
english: Peter Ala Adjetey (11 August 1931 – 15 July 2008) was a Ghanaian politician and lawyer.

kusaal: O da anɛ Speaker of the 3rd Parliament, Ghana Fourth Republic la ni din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ (2001) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: He served as Speaker of the 3rd Parliament of Ghana's Fourth Republic from 2001 to 2005.

kusaal: O da anɛ wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party, o da anɛ na'adɔɔg la National Chairman din yi yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu la ni (1995) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piwai nɛ anii (1998).
english: A member of the New Patriotic Party, he was the party's National Chairman from 1995 to 1998.

kusaal: Adjetey da anɛ Member of Parliament tis Kpeshie din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (1979) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (1981) Third Republic la ni ka an zuraani tis Ghana Bar Association din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu (1985) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai (1989).
english: Adjetey previously served as Member of Parliament for Kpeshie from 1979 to 1981 in the Third Republic and as president of the Ghana Bar Association from 1985 to 1989.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Peter Ala Adjetey nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan nɛ yinne nwadisa anii dabpiinɛ yinne (11 August 1931) La, Accra sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Peter Ala Adjetey was born on 11 August 1931 at La, a suburb of Accra.

kusaal: Paul's School bɛ La nɛ Accra Bishop Boys' School.
english: Adjetey had his basic education at St. Paul's School at La and at Accra Bishop Boys' School.

kusaal: Accra Academy ni, o da anɛ editor of the school's journal ka lɛn an prefect bɛ boarding house ka naan naae sakur yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne la ni (1951).
english: At Accra Academy, where he had his high school education, he was the editor of the school's journal and a prefect in the boarding house before his completion in 1951.

kusaal: Adjetey da keŋ University of London maal intermediate bachelor's degree, on da keŋ University College of the Gold Coast yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi la (1954) nya'aŋ.
english: Adjetey obtained the University of London's intermediate bachelor's degree after studies at the University College of the Gold Coast in 1954.

kusaal: Adjetey da tɔlisi keŋ United Kingdom, ka da naae ani nɛ bachelor's degree in law yi University of Nottingham yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anii la ni (1958).
english: Adjetey proceeded to the United Kingdom, where he graduated with a bachelor's degree in law from University of Nottingham in 1958.

kusaal: Adjetey da kilim lɔya bɛ Middle Temple bɛ London la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai la ni (1959).
english: Adjetey was called to the Bar at Middle Temple in London in 1959.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai (1959) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayai la ni (1962), Adjetey da anɛ Law Officer tʋm nɛ Attorney General's department.
english: From 1959 to 1962, Adjetey worked as a Law Officer with the Attorney General's department.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'an (part-time lecturer) tis Institute of Adult Education, University of Ghana din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ la ni (1960) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi la ni (1962).
english: He was a part-time lecturer at the Institute of Adult Education, University of Ghana between 1960 and 1962.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'an (part-time lecturer) tis Ghana School of Law din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi (1964) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii la ni (1968).
english: He was also a part-time lecturer at the Ghana School of Law between 1964 and 1968.

kusaal: Adjetey da anɛ gbansɔbid tis Ghana Bar Association din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ wai (1969) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne la ni (1971).
english: Adjetey served as secretary of the Ghana Bar Association from 1969 to 1971.

kusaal: O da tʋm boardsnam bɛdigʋ ni nwɛnɛ o da paas Judicial Council of Ghana din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1984) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ wai (1989).
english: He also served on numerous boards at various times including membership of the Judicial Council of Ghana from 1984 to 1989.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ o ye an zuraani tis African Bar Association yʋʋm tusa ayi la ni (2000).
english: He was appointed the President of the African Bar Association in 2000.

kusaal: Adjetey da anɛ kʋkdaani tis board of governors bɛ Accra Academy din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ nii (1988) ken paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii la ni (1998) on da an kʋkdaani tis sakur la Parent-Teacher Association (P. T. A.) din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yuobʋ la ni (1986) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii la ni (1988).
english: Adjetey was chairman of the board of governors of Accra Academy from 1988 to 1998 after previously being chairman of the school's Parent-Teacher Association (P. T. A.) from 1986 to 1988.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ tuon gati tis United National Convention Parliamentary group sankan ni.
english: He was also the leader of the United National Convention Parliamentary group during the same period.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛnu la ni (1995), o da lieb kʋkdaani tis New Patriotic Party (NPP), o da mɔr kpɛŋkaŋa paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii la ni (1998).
english: In 1995, he became Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), a position he held until 1998.

kusaal: Adjetey da paam national honour bɛ Order of the Volta yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008).
english: Adjetey was awarded the national honour of the Order of the Volta in 2008.

kusaal: Adjetey da paami o basic education bɛ St.
english: Adjetey had his basic education at St. Paul's School at La and at Accra Bishop Boys' School.

kusaal: O da fɛndigi lɛb Ghana yʋʋmkan ni ka ba buol o ka o paas Ghana lɔyanam.
english: He returned to Ghana in the same year where he was also called to the bar.

kusaal: O da anɛ zuraani tis Ghana Bar Association din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ nu (1985) paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛwai la ni (1989).
english: He was the President of the Ghana Bar Association between 1985 and 1989.

kusaal: Adjetey da anɛ Member of Parliament tis Kpeshie Third Republic of Ghana ni.
english: Adjetey was the Member of Parliament for Kpeshie in the Third Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋmkan nii, o da di'e honorary doctorate yi University of Ghana.
english: In that same year, he received an honorary doctorate from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Adjetey da maal ka'alim nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpiinɛ anu daar (15 July 2008) ban'a bi'ela nya'aŋ.
english: Adjetey died on 15 July 2008 after a short illness.

kusaal: O yinɛ Jirapa bɛ Upper West sʋ'ʋlim la, Gaana.
english: He hails from Jirapa in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋi o sakurnɛ Lawra secondary School n bɛ Lawra Upper west sʋ'ʋlim la, Gaana.
english: He has his secondary school education at Lawra Secondary School in Lawra in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋ Ghana Police Academy an pʋlis zamisʋg sakur la zamisi lieb pʋliŋ.
english: He was trained as Police Officer at the Ghana Police Academy.

kusaal: O lɛn keŋ Kofi Annan International Peace Keeping Training Centre lɛn zamis ka di'e kasɛtta gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka ti buon ye Masters of Arts degree in Leadership.
english: He holds a Master of Arts degree in Leadership from the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre.

kusaal: Onɛ da an gbaʋŋ sɔbidi tis pʋlis la wʋsa kpɛɛm kʋdʋg (IGP) David Asante Apeatu lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ Piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) keŋ paae sankanɛ ka o da sig ye o pʋ lɛ bɔɔd tʋʋma la ya'asa, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019).
english: He served as the Executive Secretary to the former Inspector General of Police (IGP) David Asante Apeatu from 2017 until he resigned and retired from the service to go into Politics in 2019.

kusaal: O da pa'al faandibi tʋm si'em o sʋ'ʋlim la, Wa West nɛ tɛɛnsbanɛ giligi di nɛ din yi Sisaala West keŋ paae Bawku West.
english: He pointed out armed robbery cases in his constituency, Wa West and surrounding areas from Sissala East to Bawku West.

kusaal: Peter Lanchene Toobu da du'anɛ nwadis Ayuobʋ la daba Anii daar, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ Anii.
english: Peter Lanchene Toobu (born 8 June 1968) is a Ghanaian retired police officer and politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wa West dinɛ bɛ Upper West sʋ'ʋlim la wadmaan.
english: He is the member of Parliament for the Wa West Constituency in the Upper West region.

kusaal: Toobu daa tʋm o pʋlis tʋʋma la ka duoe hali ti kena di'e kpɛŋkanɛ ka ti buon ye Supirintɛndɛn la ka naan naae o tʋʋma ka yʋ'ʋŋ kuli vʋ'ʋsid.
english: Toobu served in the Ghana Police Service and rose to the rank of Superintendent of Police before retiring.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadis piinɛ ayi la Burunya nwadig la ni, Toobu da di Wa West kʋk la vɔɔt la pʋʋgin.
english: In December 2020, Toobu won the Wa West Constituency seat in the parliamentary elections.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar, Toobu daa da paam suori kpɛn' wadmaanib yin la yʋ'ʋn an wadmaani ts Wa West dim.
english: On 7 January 2021, Toobu was sworn in as Member of Parliament representing the Wa West Constituency in the 8th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, nwadis ayuobʋ daba ayuobʋ daar, o da sɔb gbaʋŋʋ tis wadmaanib kpɛɛm, Alban Bagbin ye o kɛ ka gɔmena baŋ yɛlsieba ka maali ba duos ka Gaana da an wʋʋ wada kae laa.
english: On 6 April 2021, he petitioned the Speaker of Parliament, Alban Bagbin to draw the President's attention to issues relating to security and address the growing insecurity within Ghana.

kusaal: Toobu anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Toobu is a Christian.

kusaal: Peter Mensah (o dʋ'am dabisir an yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai, nwadis anii, dabpisi nɛ yɔpɔi, 27 August 1959) anɛ one maan sini di'ema Ghana-British tɛn'ɛsin, ka taa bɛ Canada.
english: Peter Mensah (born 27 August 1959) is a Ghanaian-British actor, based in Canada.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋr yi ya nɛ sini di'em kani ka o da maal ka ba pʋd o Oenomaus ka ba da gɔsidi li Starz television series Spartacus (2010–2013).
english: He is best known for his role as Oenomaus on the Starz television series Spartacus (2010–2013).

kusaal: O paas sini si'eba ni wan wʋʋ Tears of the Sun, Hidalgo, The Incredible Hulk, 300, Avatar, nɛ Gladiator II.
english: He has also appeared in such films as Tears of the Sun, Hidalgo, The Incredible Hulk, 300, Avatar, and Gladiator II.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Mensah nɛ Chiraa, Ghana, ka o dʋ'adib anɛ gbaŋmi'idib.
english: Mensah was born in Chiraa, Ghana, and comes from an academic family.

kusaal: O dʋ'adib yitnɛ Brong Ahafo Region, ka o da kɛŋ zin'in Hertfordshire, England tɛŋin, nɛ o saam, Peter Osei Mensah, anɛ architect engineer, o ma anɛ gbansɔbid, nɛ o tanp ayi'.
english: He was born to parents from the Brong Ahafo Region, and moved to Hertfordshire, England, with his father, Peter Osei Mensah, an architect engineer, his mother, a writer, and two younger sisters at a young age.

kusaal: O sakur zamisig ni, o zamis di'ema yela zamisig, amaa Mensah da zamis nɛ engineering yiiga, o da kɛŋ Canada tɛŋin anɛ engineer tis British Gas, gɔsid gas yela bɛ Morecambe Bay.
english: Though he had done drama in school, Mensah originally studied engineering, and arrived in Canada as an engineer for British Gas, developing gas fields at Morecambe Bay.

kusaal: Mensah sini di'ema pʋʋgin si'eba anɛ Avatar, 300, Hidalgo, Tears of the Sun, Jason X, Harvard Man, Bless the Child nɛ The Incredible Hulk.
english: Mensah's film credits include Avatar, 300, Hidalgo, Tears of the Sun, Jason X, Harvard Man, Bless the Child and The Incredible Hulk.

kusaal: O mɛ len paas sini kanɛ buon The Seed, linɛ ka Linkin Park's DJ Joe Hahn da aan li tuongat la.
english: He also stars in the short film The Seed, produced and directed by Linkin Park's DJ Joe Hahn.

kusaal: O len yi sini pʋʋgin TV ni wʋʋ Star Trek: Enterprise, Tracker, Witchblade, Blue Murder, Relic Hunter, Earth: Final Conflict, Highlander: The Raven, nɛ La Femme Nikita.
english: He has made television appearances in Star Trek: Enterprise, Tracker, Witchblade, Blue Murder, Relic Hunter, Earth: Final Conflict, Highlander: The Raven, and La Femme Nikita.

kusaal: O da paas sini kanɛ yi A&E Network series A Nero Wolfe Mystery nɛ Terminator: The Sarah Connor Chronicles.
english: He was a member of the repertory cast of the A&E Network series A Nero Wolfe Mystery and Terminator: The Sarah Connor Chronicles.

kusaal: Zach Hammond si'em bɛ EA's video game Dead Space.
english: He voiced and provided his likeness for Sgt. Zach Hammond in EA's video game Dead Space.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋr da anɛ Oenomaus sini kanɛ buon Spartacus la ni ka paas Spartacus Panel pʋʋgin bɛ Comic Con yʋʋm tusayi nɛ awai (2009) nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinne (2011).
english: Mensah played the character Oenomaus in Spartacus and was on the Spartacus Panel at Comic Con 2009 and 2011.

kusaal: O da yi bɛdigʋ bɛ fifth season of True Blood sini ni.
english: He had a recurring role in the fifth season of True Blood.

kusaal: Peter Tenganabang Nanfuri (Ba da du'a o nɛ 12 October 1942 – ka o maal ka'alim 17 February 2023) da anɛ Inspector General tis Ghana Police Service kʋdʋg onɛ da kilim Paramount Chief tis Jirapa Traditional Area ka o Na'ayʋ'ʋr aan Naa Ansoleh Ganaa II on da naae o tʋʋma la.
english: Peter Tenganabang Nanfuri (12 October 1942 – 17 February 2023) was a former Inspector General of Ghana Police Service who became the Paramount Chief of the Jirapa Traditional Area with the title Naa Ansoleh Ganaa II upon retirement.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Peter Nanfuri nɛ Jirapa, tenkanɛ bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Peter Nanfuri was born at Jirapa, a town in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Nanfuri da keŋnɛ University of Ghana, Legon, ka da zamis B.A. degree in political science nɛ law degree.
english: Nanfuri studied at the University of Ghana, Legon, where he obtained B.A. degree in political science and a law degree.

kusaal: O da an Director of the Bureau of National Investigation (BNI) yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1986) dinɛ gɔsid teŋ la zi'esim yɛla.
english: He was once the Director of the Bureau of National Investigation (BNI) 1986 that deals with state security related issues.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1996), ba da gaŋi o ye o an Inspector General of Police.
english: In 1996, he was appointed the Inspector General of Police.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpisi nɛ tan daar (23 July 2005), Peter Nanfuri da dii o Na'am la paas 4th Paramount chief tis Jirapa Traditional Area.
english: On 23 July 2005, Peter Nanfuri was enskinned as the 4th Paramount chief of the Jirapa Traditional Area.

kusaal: Ba da tisi o kpɛŋ la paalʋ zin'ikanɛ yʋ'ʋr buon ye Naa Yelpoe Park bɛ Jirapa la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa anaasi la dabpisi nɛ anaii daar (28 April 2007).
english: He was publicly presented in his new capacity at the Naa Yelpoe Park at Jirapa on 28 April 2007.

kusaal: Onɛ da an yiiga la Naa Ansoleh Ganaa, British dimi da gaŋ o ka tis o yʋ'ʋr la ye Naa Ansoleh Ganaa I. Nanfuri da anɛ o yaaŋ.
english: The first Naa Ansoleh Ganaa, was appointed by the British colonial administration with the stool name of Naa Ansoleh Ganaa I. Nanfuri was his great-grandson.

kusaal: Paramount Chief kanɛ da bɛ la, Bapereyiri Yelpore, da kpinɛ yʋma ayɔpɔi nwana.
english: The previous Paramount Chief, Bapereyiri Yelpore, died seven years earlier.

kusaal: Nanfuri da maal ka'alimnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan nwadisa ayi la dabpiinɛ yɔpɔi daar (17 February 2023), o da anɛ yʋma pisnii (80 years).
english: Nanfuri died on 17 February 2023, at the age of 80.

kusaal: o da anɛ Inspector General of Police (IGP) bɛ Ghana.
english: He served as Inspector General of Police (IGP) in Ghana.

kusaal: Nanfuri tʋm zin'is kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb Ghana Police Service ni.
english: Nanfuri worked in various capacities within the Ghana Police Service.

kusaal: O da tʋmmi o tʋʋma bɔɔd naar la on da an IGP la, di da muk o hali nɛ ban da kʋʋd pʋ'asieba Ghana la.
english: Towards the end of his service as IGP, he came under severe pressure due to the serial murder of some women in Ghana.

kusaal: O Na'ayʋ'ʋr anɛ Naa Ansoleh Ganaa II.
english: His official or royal name or title was Naa Ansoleh Ganaa II.

kusaal: La'anɛ Nanfuri's saami da an Na'ab la, o da nya' kpɛŋ la nɛ o saam bibis.
english: Although Nanfuri's father was a chief, he had to contest this position with some cousins.

kusaal: Peter Kwasi Nortsu-Kotoe (6 May 1956) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas Gaana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la, o anɛ Wadmaani tisi Akatsi North Constituency bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim la ka an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Peter Kwasi Nortsu-Kotoe (born 6 May 1956) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Akatsi North Constituency in the Volta Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Kpeduhoe teŋkanɛ bɛ Volta Region Ghana la.
english: He hails from Kpeduhoe in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Nortsu-Kotoe da naae nɛ University of Ghana ka di'e bachelor of degree in English kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: Nortsu-Kotoe is a graduate of the University of Ghana with a bachelor of degree in English.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr master of development management kasɛta gbaʋŋ, Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration.
english: He holds a master of development management from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration.

kusaal: O da anɛ pa'an bɛ Accra Academy ka nɔbʋg hali ti kena aan assistant director gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni (Ghana Education Service).
english: He was a tutor at Accra Academy and an assistant director of the Ghana Education Service by rank.

kusaal: Nortsu-Kotoe da anɛ Diisi tisi Akatsi District nɛ Akatsi South District la ni yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la Nwadisa anaasi la hali nɛ on ti kpɛn' Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la niyʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar.
english: Nortsu-Kotoe was the District Chief Executive of the Akatsi District and the Akatsi South District from April 2009 until entering parliament on 7 January 2013.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ye o zi'eni tis Akatsi North Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni 2012 Gaana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni, o da zi'enɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug, National Democratic Congress.
english: He was elected to represent the Akatsi North Constituency on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress during the 2012 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) nii, ba da lɛn vɔɔti tis o ye o lɛn zi'eni tisi ba yʋma anaasi la ya'as.
english: In 2016, he was elected again to represent the constituency for the next four years in parliament.

kusaal: O anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Evangelical Presbyterian Church, Ghana.
english: He identifies as a Christian and a member of the Evangelical Presbyterian Church, Ghana.

kusaal: Wadmaan January 7,– present; 2nd term)
english: MP (January 7, 2013 – present; 4th term)

kusaal: Ba da du'a Nortsu-Kotoe nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa anu la daba ayuobʋ daar (6 May 1956).
english: Nortsu-Kotoe was born on 6 May 1956.

kusaal: Nortsu-Kotoe tʋmnɛ gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋrin la.
english: Nortsu-Kotoe is an educationist by profession.

kusaal: Peter Yaw Kwakye-Ackah (dʋ'anɛ 15 June 1957) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Gaana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Amenfi Central Constituency bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim la Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug.
english: Peter Yaw Kwakye-Ackah (born 15 June 1957) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Amenfi Central Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Kwakye-Ackah yinɛ Manso-Amenfi.
english: Kwakye-Ackah hails from Manso-Amenfi.

kusaal: O mɔr MBA in Marine Engineering yi Leicester University, UK nɛ 1st Class Marine Engineering yi South Glamoorgan Institute of Higher Education, Cardiff bɛ Wales la.
english: He holds an MBA in Marine Engineering from the Leicester University, UK and 1st Class Marine Engineering South Glamoorgan Institute of Higher Education, Cardiff, Wales (1990).

kusaal: Petroleum Commission (Ghana) anɛ Ghana State agency tʋm nɛ lugir kani an Ministry of Energy and Petroleum ka ba tʋʋm anɛ yee ba gɔsid tʋʋmaam dinɛ bɛ kpaam maalʋg zin'igin nɛ nyɔɔd kanɛ bɛɛ li ni ka na sʋŋ Ghana dim nimma'asim yɛla.
english: The Petroleum Commission is a Ghanaian state agency under the Ministry of Energy and Petroleum responsible for the regulation, management and coordination of all activities in the upstream petroleum industry for the benefit and welfare of Ghanaians.

kusaal: Ba mɛ tʋm tʋʋma la ye ba mɔr suor ka Ghana nidib kpɛn' kpaam tʋʋma la ni nwɛnɛ ban pa'al si'em bɛ Petroleum Exploration and Production law of 1981 (PNDCL 54), nɛ wada sieba zaŋi keŋ temmaalʋg yɛla la.
english: The commission is also tasked with the promotion of local content and Ghanaian participation in the petroleum industry as stated by the Petroleum Exploration and Production Law of 1984 (PNDCL 84), and other laws and regulations for national development.

kusaal: Lʋgir kaŋa da sin'iŋ nɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ yinne(2011) la ni, ka soe o mɛŋ tʋmi o kɔ'ɔkɔ' ka gɔsid siel wʋsa kpaam la maaalʋg bzbir la bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The commission was established in 2011 as an independent regulator in the petroleum sector of Ghana.

kusaal: Lʋgir la tʋʋma anɛ ye ba gɔsid, ka vɛɛns kpaam tʋʋma wʋsa dinɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The commission is responsible for monitoring, supervising, inspecting and auditing all petroleum activities in Ghana.

kusaal: Lʋgir la kpɛɛmnam la mɛ pa'al lʋgir la wada nɛ tʋʋm banɛ bɛ lʋgir la ni tis Minister of Energy la.
english: The commission also recommends national policies connected to petroleum activities to the Minister of Energy.

kusaal: O da zamis dʋgʋbʋ yinɛ on da tʋmi bɛ Marco Pierre White tuoni bɛ Harveys sʋ'ʋlim nɛ on da bɛ Simon Hopkinson sa'ani bɛ Bibendum la.
english: He gained cooking skills while working under Marco Pierre White at Harveys and Simon Hopkinson at Bibendum.
