kusaal: Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig la ni, on nɛ sɔ' da la'asi maal kpikpiŋ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Rebecca Mascarenhas ka ba yɔ'ɔg tʋʋma zin'ig kanɛ buon Elystan Street, zin'ig kan da dɛŋin anɛ diib kuosʋg zin'igi tis Tom Aikens ka bɛ Chelsea sʋ'ʋlim.
english: That September, he and another business partner Rebecca Mascarenhas opened Elystan Street, a former site of one of Tom Aikens's eponymous restaurants in Chelsea.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Philip Howard nɛ Johannesburg, South Africa, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ ni.
english: Philip Howard was born in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1966.

kusaal: On da kɛŋ Australia bɛ saŋa bi'ela la, Howard da anɛ onɛ zanl diibi kɛn ni tisid nidib ka da kuosid diibi bɛ Volkswagen Kombi.
english: During his brief stint in Australia, Howard was a waiter and cooked and sold food from a 1969 Volkswagen Kombi.

kusaal: On da lɛb England tɛŋin la, o da pin'ili tʋmi tisid diiib kuosʋg zin'ig kanɛ buon Roux Restaurants Ltd, zin'ig kan an nid nɛ o pitu Albert nɛ Michel Roux da sʋ'ʋe.
english: After his return to England, he started working under a contract for the catering division of Roux Restaurants Ltd, a restaurant group led by brothers Albert and Michel Roux.

kusaal: Howard nɛ Platts-Martin da kuos The Square yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, Dɔnwalig nwadig la ni tis Marlon Abela diib kuosʋg tʋʋma kanɛ buon Marlon Abela Restaurant Corporation (MARC), la ligidi US$4 million.
english: Howard and Platts-Martin sold The Square in March 2016 to Marlon Abela's eponymous restaurant group, Marlon Abela Restaurant Corporation (MARC), for US$4 million.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋ kpɛɛm kanɛ da bɛ The Square ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Brett Graham ye o an kpɛɛm tis The Ledbury.
english: The Square's former sous chef Brett Graham was appointed head chef and later became chef patron of The Ledbury.

kusaal: Onɛ da an banɛ dʋgʋd diib kpɛɛm kʋdʋgi bɛ The Square ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Mark Kempson ka ba da gaŋ o ye o an banɛ dʋgʋd diib kpɛɛm bɛ diib zin'ig la yɔ'ɔgir daar.
english: The Square's former sous-chef Mark Kempson was appointed head chef upon the restauarnt's opening.

kusaal: Howard nɛ Mascarenhas da la'asi sʋ'ʋg Sonny's Kitchen lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayi saŋa sa, ka ba da ti'aki li lɛb Church Road yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ awai la ni.
english: Howard and Mascarenhas have also co-owned Sonny's Kitchen since 2012, later reopened as Church Road in 2019.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, Sɛnlʋŋ nwadig, dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔ daar, Howard nɛ Mascarenhas da yɔ'ɔg diib kuosʋg zin'ig paalig ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Elystan Street, zin'ig kan da anɛ onɛ dʋgʋd diib ka ba buon Tom Aikens da kuosid diib anina, ka li bɛ 43 Elystan Street, Chelsea sʋ'ʋlim.
english: On 27 September 2016, Howard and Mascarenhas opened a new London restaurant Elystan Street, the former site of chef Tom Aikens's eponymous restaurant (out of Aikens's restaurants), located at 43 Elystan Street, Chelsea.

kusaal: Onɛ da an banɛ dʋgʋd diib kpɛɛm bɛ Gezellig anɛ Graham Long.
english: The head chef of Gezellig was Graham Long.

kusaal: Howard mɛ da lɛn sʋ'ʋe diib kuosʋg zin'igi Union linɛ bɛ La Plagne (France).
english: Howard also owned and operated another restaurant Union, located at the ski resort Montalbert of La Plagne (France).

kusaal: O mɛ sʋ'ʋe yir bil kanɛ ka on nɛ o yidim kɛna anina vʋ'ʋsid, o da da'a li nɛ €500,000 yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ ka lɛn san'am ligidi €900,000 ya'as ye o maligim maal yir la.
english: He also owns a chalet there for family vacations and ski trips, having purchased it for €500,000 in 2006 and spending an additional €900,000 for home transformation.

kusaal: Martin Cuchet anɛ onɛ ka on nɛ Howard la'asi yɔ'ɔg Union.
english: Martin Cuchet is Howard's business partner for Union.

kusaal: Ba da ti'ak yʋ'ʋr la yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi ka li yʋ'ʋn an Notto ban da kpɛn'ɛ wada pʋʋgin nɛ tʋʋma zin'ig kanɛ yʋ'ʋri mɛ buon Otto la yela.
english: The name was changed in 2022 to Notto after a legal dispute with another business also called Otto.

kusaal: O da paas banɛ da kat saria bɛ banɛ dʋgʋd diib piini 2010 Catey Awards, ka onɛ da di'e piinkan da an Mark Hix; nɛ diib kuosig zin'ig kanɛ gaad o taaba bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ ya'an piini ni.
english: He was also one of judges for the Chef Award of the 2010 Catey Awards, which went to Mark Hix; and for the Restaurateur of the Year (Independent) of the 2016 Catey Awards.

kusaal: Baa on da pʋ bɔɔd ye o yi T.V ni la, Howard da yi T.V ni bɛ Master Chef: The Professionals (yiiga bɛ Sawaar 2009), Market Kitchen, nɛ Saturday Kitchen (yiiga bɛ Samanpiid nwadig daba atan' 2011).
english: Despite mostly avoiding television appearances, Howard made guest appearances in MasterChef: The Professionals (first in October 2009), Market Kitchen (Good Food), and Saturday Kitchen (first on 3 December 2011).

kusaal: Di'ema kanɛ da paas piinɛ yinnɛ ni da an Great British Menu la, on nɛ o taaba banɛ dʋg diibi di ya'an (Colin McGurran, Daniel Clifford, nɛ Simon Rogan), o da gbɛn'ɛs o dikanɛ da kɛ ka o di ya'an la tis nidib ka ba di bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayi zɔtzɔtib nɛ banɛ di'emidi bɛ Old Royal Naval College linɛ bɛ Greenwich, bakwai nam bi'ela ka yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayi di'ema la nyaan paae.
english: In the seventh series of Great British Menu, alongside three other winning chefs (Colin McGurran, Daniel Clifford, and Simon Rogan), he served his winning dish (Cornish mackerel with oysters, mussels, winkles and samphire) as the fish course of the 2012 Olympians' banquet at the Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich, weeks before the 2012 Summer Olympics.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anii, Mɔraug nwadig, dabpisi daar, bɛ Canterbury Cathedral ni, University of Kent da tis Howard kanɛ da naae anina la kasɛta gbaŋ linɛ an Doctor of Arts on "nyaŋi ti'ak nidib vʋm ka mɛ sʋŋ diib yela si'em la".
english: On 20 July 2018 at Canterbury Cathedral, the University of Kent gave its alumni, Howard an honorary Doctor of Arts degree for his "inspirational life and outstanding contribution to hospitality and food".

kusaal: Phil n da paam laafi la nwadis awai nya'aŋ, o ba'abiig Greg da kpi nɛ on da nu tikpi'ema tʋʋg o paŋ la zug yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ ni.
english: Nine months after Phil's recovery, his brother Greg died of drug overdose in 1996.

kusaal: Howard mɔr pʋa ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Jennie ka o da di o yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai saŋa paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi ni ti paae o pʋa pʋʋgi da san'am bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai la ni.
english: Howard has been married to Jennie from the early 1990s to 1997 and since their remarriage in 1999.

kusaal: Ba da gbɛɛndi bɛ nɛ Barnes, London hali yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai bɛɛ yʋʋm tusayi ni.
english: They have resided in Barnes, London since 1999 or 2000.

kusaal: Philip Howard (dʋam 1966) anɛ onɛ dʋgʋd diibi bɛ South Africa ka lɛɛ yit British, ka an banɛ dʋgʋd diib kpɛɛm ka lɛn an onɛ sʋ'ʋe diib kuosig zin'ig.
english: Philip Howard was born in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1966.

kusaal: Howard nɛ White da anɛ banɛ la'asi maan kpikpiŋ nɛ Nigel Platts-Martin ka yɔ'ɔg diib kuosʋg zin'igi bɛ London ka pʋdʋ li yʋ'ʋr ye The Square bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinnɛ, naar nwadig la ni, baa ban da pʋ mɔr diib kuosʋg baŋir saŋkan la.
english: Howard and White's then-business partner Nigel Platts-Martin opened London restaurant The Square in December 1991, despite both of their inexperience in operating a restaurant at the time.

kusaal: Ban da bɛ ba tʋʋma zin'ig kanɛ buon The Square, linɛ ka ba da yisi li zin'igi yi St James's tɔɔm kɛŋ Mayfair yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi ni, nidib da noŋ Howard hali ka vɔɔti tis o lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi ni paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ ni.
english: While operating The Square, which moved from St James's to Mayfair in 1997, Howard had held Michelin stars from 1994 to 2016.

kusaal: On nɛ Platts-Martin da kuos The Square ka bas zin'ig kan nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ, Dɔnwalig nwadig la ni.
english: He and Platts-Martin sold and left The Square in March 2016.

kusaal: Howard mɔr diib kuosʋg zin'is si'eba ya'as ka li kɛ ka o di ya'ani bɛ tʋʋma zin'is si'eba ni wan wʋʋ The Caterer, The AA, nɛ GQ.
english: Howard owns a few other restaurants and has won accolades from companies such as The Caterer, The AA, and GQ.

kusaal: O da an saan kanɛ an kpɛɛm ka ba buol o ye o kɛna gɔs diib dʋgʋb di'ema kanɛ buon Sibit daar da'aŋ ka mɛ da paasi nya'a diib dʋgʋb ya'ani bɛ Great British diib ni, nya'aŋ ka o da an sariakiti tisi ba ya'as.
english: He appeared in Saturday Kitchen as a guest and Great British Menu as one of its contestants, then one of its veteran chef judges.

kusaal: On da an yʋma ayɔpɔi la, on nɛ o dʋ'adib da yi kɛŋ zin'in England.
english: At the age of seven, he and his family moved to England.

kusaal: Howard da kɛŋ sakur ka mɔr gbaŋi bɛ bʋnkɔnbid gʋ'ʋlʋg ni University of Kent.
english: Howard earned a bachelor's degree in microbiology at the University of Kent.

kusaal: Howard da gɔs ka o nɔŋ diib dʋgʋb hali on da bɛ university la ka da pin'il o diib dʋgʋb tʋʋma bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii ni on da naae sakur la nya'aŋ, ka lɛɛ bas o zamisig kanɛ ka o zamis bʋnvuya yela la.
english: Howard discovered his passion for cooking during university and then began a cooking career in 1988 after graduating, rather than pursuing a career in microbiology.

kusaal: O da tʋm waad win ni tis bɛ Dordogne chateau.
english: He worked one summer for a Dordogne chateau.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋŋ yinnɛ, Howard kɛŋi di bɛ Harveys ka o ya'am da kpɛn'ɛ dikanɛ ka Marco Pierre White da dʋg la.
english: One night, Howard had dinner at Harveys and was impressed by the food made by its chef Marco Pierre White.

kusaal: Howard da kilim banɛ dʋgʋd kpɛɛm bɛ o zin'igin bɛ Harveys yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai ni, anina ka Howard da zamis Fariŋ diib dʋgʋb.
english: Then Howard became a chef de partie of Harveys in 1989, where Howard learned to appreciate modernised French cooking.

kusaal: On da tʋm Harveys ni paae nwadis awai la, White da kad Howard yis tʋʋma ni on da dʋg White "potato diib kanɛ ka li yʋ'ʋr da yi la" yela.
english: After working at Harveys for nine months, Howard was sacked by White for boiling White's "then-famous creamed potato" (pomme purée).

kusaal: Li pʋ yʋʋgɛ, o da tʋm bɛ Bibendum ka da an kpɛɛm bɛɛ o zin'igin ka lɛɛ bɛ onɛ an ba wʋsa kpɛɛm Simon Hopkinson nu'usin, anina ka li da malis Howard nɛ ban da dʋgʋd ka li an titua ka mɔr nyʋʋg sʋ'ʋŋa ka lɛn an na'ana'a la yela.
english: Shortly afterwards, he worked at Bibendum as chef de partie under Simon Hopkinson, from where Howard was inspired by the emphasis on the quality and flavour of the cooking and its simplicity.

kusaal: On da tʋm Bibendum ni la, Howard nɛ White da nan kpɛlim mɔr sɔnsig nɛ taaba.
english: While working at Bibendum, Howard and White had stayed in touch with each other.

kusaal: White da ɛɛti buol Howard ye o kɛn Harveys na lɛm o disaʋŋ wʋsa.
english: White frequently invited Howard to Harveys to test out White's new dishes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai la ni, Marco Pierre White da lɛn nɔk Howard tʋʋma ya'asi bɛ Harveys, anina ka o da zamis o mɛŋ lin na niŋ si'em ka o kilimi ba kpɛɛm bɛʋg sa tis White nɛ o kpikpiŋ tiraan kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Nigel Platts-Martin diib zin'ig kanɛ ka ba da bɔɔd ye ba yɔ'ɔg.
english: In 1990, Howard was rehired by Marco Pierre White to work at Harveys, he would then be trained as a future head chef for White and White's then-business partner Nigel Platts-Martin's upcoming restaurant.

kusaal: Nigel Platts-Martin nɛ White nɔnaalig la da naae ya.
english: Nigel Platts-Martin and White's partnership of the restaurant project ended.

kusaal: Howard nɛ o tʋmtʋm tiraan kanɛ ka ba la'as Platts-Martin, ba baba yi' la da pʋ mɔr baŋir kanɛ ka ba na nɔki yɔ'ɔgi ba mɛŋ diib kuosʋg zin'igɔ, ka o da yɔ'ɔg o kʋkɔn' ka bas White, diib kuosʋg zin'ig kanɛ buon The Square ka li bɛ King Street, St James's yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinnɛ, naar nwadig, dabpiinɛ atan' daar.
english: Howard and his business partner Platts-Martin, both inexperienced in operating a restaurant at the time, and without White, opened what became the fine dining restaurant The Square at King Street, St James's on 13 December 1991.

kusaal: Ban da gaŋ Howard ka o an banɛ dʋgʋd kpɛɛm la nɛ on da mi' Fariŋ diib dʋgʋb la da kɛ ka nidib da nɔŋ The Square yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi, naar nwadig la ni.
english: With Howard appointed as head chef and his emphasis on simple yet elegant and contemporary French cuisine, The Square earned its first Michelin star in December 1994.

kusaal: Howard da tʋm anina nɛ o tʋmtʋm tiraan (on nɛ Platts-Martin) ka an kpɛɛm anina on da bɛ anina la wʋsa.
english: Howard had also been the restaurant's co-owner (alongside Platts-Martin) and chef patron throughout most of his tenure.

kusaal: Ba da ti'ak The Square zin'ig la lɛbis Mayfair yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi, Fulumfug nwadig la ni ka nidib lɛn nɔŋi li ya'as bɛdigʋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii, yʋʋm paal nwadig la ni.
english: The Square moved to Mayfair in February 1997 and then earned its second Michelin star in January 1998.

kusaal: The Square da nyɛ nɔŋir hali yi nidib sa'an nɔɔra anaasi bɛ AA plc ni lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ ni ka anii yi piiga pʋʋgin si'aki ba bɛ Good Food Guide lin da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ ni.
english: The Square also earned four Rosettes by AA plc from 2007 to 2016 and eight out of ten by the Good Food Guide from 1999 to 2016.

kusaal: Howard da yɔ'ɔg diib kuosʋg zin'ig ka li yʋ'ʋr buon The Ledbury on nɛ onɛ da paasi sʋ'ʋe The Square ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Nigel Platts-Martin la bɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu, Mɔraʋg nwadig la ni.
english: Howard opened Michelin-starred restaurant The Ledbury as its co-owner alongside The Square co-owner Nigel Platts-Martin in July 2005.

kusaal: Baa on da an sʋ'ʋd la, Howard da pʋ tʋm The Ledbury ni wan wʋʋ Platts-Martin da tʋm anina si'em la.
english: Despite ownership, Howard never operated The Ledbury as much as Platts-Martin did.

kusaal: Ba da yɔ' The Ledbury yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi ni, Sigir nwadig la ni sa, ye ba da pʋ bat taaba faalʋ COVID-19 ban'as la saŋa ban da nar ye ba niŋ si'em la.
english: The Ledbury had been indefinitely closed since June 2020, citing social distancing measures amid the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic as impractical for the restaurant.

kusaal: Howard mɛ da paasi sʋ'ʋe diib kuosʋg zin'ig si'eba banɛ pʋ zuoe wan wʋʋ Square kanɛ ka ba da yɔ' zi'el la.
english: Howard also co-owns other restaurants that are less formal and "more casual" than the (now closed) Square.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛn paasi sʋ'ʋe Kensington diib kuosʋg zin'ig Kitchen W8 yʋʋm tusayi nɛ awai, Sawaar nwadig, dabpisi nɛ anii daar, o da pin'il lin nɛ o kpikpiŋ tiraan Rebecca Mascarenhas.
english: He has co-owned Kensington restaurant Kitchen W8 since 28 October 2009, opening it with his other business partner Rebecca Mascarenhas, who owned the site under previous names Abingdon Road and then Bistro Eleven.

kusaal: Kitchen W8 da paam nɔŋir nidib ni yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinnɛ ni ka nidib nan kpɛlim pa'an nɔŋilim yʋʋm kan ni sa.
english: Kitchen W8 earned its first Michelin star in 2011 and has retained it every year since.

kusaal: Sonny's Kitchen da anɛ Sonny da sʋ'ʋe lin da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ ni paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayi ni ka li da anɛ Mascarenhas ma'a da sʋ'ʋe li.
english: Sonny's Kitchen was originally Sonny's from 1986 to 2012 under Mascarenhas's sole ownership.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a mak nɛ The Square, Elystan Street da pʋ zuoe wala.
english: In contrast to The Square, Elystan Street is less formal and more casual.

kusaal: Howard da an li kpɛɛm la, Elystan Street da paam nɔŋir hali yit nidib sa'an yiiga nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔopɔi ni, ka li kpɛlim kɛn tuon ka nidib nɔŋi li paae zina.
english: Under Howard as its current chef patron, Elystan Street earned its first Michelin star in 2017, which has been retained every year since.

kusaal: Howard nɛ Mascarenhas da la'asi sʋ'ʋe diib dʋgʋb zin'ig kanɛ buon Gezellig lin da yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ awai, Sigsaa nwadig la ni, lin da yɔ'ɔg la ti paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, yʋʋm paal nwadig, dabpistan' nɛ yinnɛ daar, lin da yɔ' la.
english: Howard and Mascarenhas also co-owned a London wine-focused restaurant Gezellig from May 2019, when it opened to 31 January 2020, when it closed.

kusaal: Howard da pin'il tʋʋma zin'igi tɔlim diibi tisid banɛ bɔɔd yaan ka li yʋ'ʋr buon Otto ka li bɛ London yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ, Sigsaa nwadig, dabpiiga daar.
english: Howard launched a London-based pasta delivery service Otto on 10 May 2021.

kusaal: O da lɛn yɔ'ɔg yinnɛ ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Notto bɛ Piccadilly suorin yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi, Sapal nwadig la ni on nɛ o tiraan Julian Dyer.
english: He opened a pasta restaurant also called Notto at the Piccadilly road in November 2022 with co-partner Julian Dyer.

kusaal: Ba da digil Howard nɔɔra ayi ye ba ti'eb o ka o bas tikpi'ema si'eba nub yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu, on da nuud wii hali yʋma atan' pʋʋgin ye o nyaŋi tʋm tʋʋma bɛ The Square ni la.
english: Howard was admitted twice to drug rehabilitation in 1995 after a three-year addiction to primarily crack cocaine, which he used to compensate his excessive workload at The Square.

kusaal: O saam da anɛ onɛ tʋm ligidi kaanlig tʋʋma ka lɛn an kpikpiŋ daan; o ma da anɛ yi'pʋ'a.
english: His father was an accountant and a businessman; his mother was a housewife.

kusaal: Ba mɔr biis ayi.
english: They have two children.

kusaal: Philip Atta Basoah da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni zi'eni tis Kumawu Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim la dim.
english: Philip Atta Basoah (18 November 1969 – 27 March 2023) was a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Kumawu Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Philip nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai Nwadis pii nɛ yinne la li dabpiinɛ anii daar (November 18, 1969), ka da kpi Atini daar, Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ atan' la Nwadisa atan' la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (Monday, 27th March, 2023).
english: Philip was born on 18 November 1969, and died on Monday, 27 March 2023.

kusaal: O da maali o master's degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ nɛ Paris graduate school of management yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) ka maali o Bachelor of Arts kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ University of Cape Coast yʋma tusa ayi' la ni (2000).
english: He had master's degree at the Paris graduate school of management in 2012 and also had Bachelor of Arts at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana in 2000.

kusaal: O da lɛn maali o GCE A level nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994), nɛ o GCE O level yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991) ka maali o MLSC kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1986) la ni.
english: He also had his GCE A level in 1994 and his GCE O level in 1991 and his MLSC in 1986.

kusaal: O da anɛ projects coordinator tis gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la (Ghana Education Service), kanɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: He was the projects coordinator for Ghana Education Service in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Diisi (District Chief Executive) bɛ Ministry of Local Government n tis Sekyere East District din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu Nwadisa ayuobʋ la (June 2005) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai yʋʋmpaal Nwadig (January 2009).
english: He was also the District Chief Executive at the Ministry of Local Government for the Sekyere East District from June 2005 to January 2009.

kusaal: O da anɛ pa'an-pa'an bɛ Agogo Senior High School.
english: He was a tutor at the Agogo Senior High School.

kusaal: O da paas nɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni, (NPP) ka an Wadmaani tis Kumawu Constituency teŋ sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ bɛ Ashanti region la.
english: He was a member of NPP and the MP for the Kumawu Constituency in the Ashanti region.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) kanɛ da an Ghana wʋsa vɔɔdʋg tita'ar la ni la, o da di Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pisi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (21,794) ka li an pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii du'ali ayi' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (78.2%), ka Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg (NDC) nid Emmanuel William Amoako da paam vɔɔt kal tusa anu nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ awai (5,899) ka li an pisi nɛ yinne du'ali ayi' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (21.2%), ka CPP nid Opoku Kyei Clifford paam vɔɔt kal kɔbiga nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (188) ka li an nɛɛm du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (0.7%).
english: In the 2016 Ghana general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 21,794 votes making 78.2% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Emmanuel William Amoako had 5,899 votes making 21.2% of the total votes cast while the CPP parliament aspirant Opoku Kyei Clifford had 188 votes making 0.7% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi la nii (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la nii, o da di Wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ anaasi nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ (14,960) ka li an pisnu nɛ yinnɛ du'al yinne kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (51.1%), ka Ma'asim tiig (NDC) nid Bernard Opoku Marfo mɛ da mɔri vɔɔt kal tusa ayi' nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pistan' nɛ awai (2,439) ka li an anii du'al atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (8.3%), ka onɛ pʋ zi'en Na'adɔsi'a bɛɛ pʋ dɔl paati si'a la (Independent parliament), Duah Kwaku mɛ da paam nɛ tusa pii nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piswai nɛ anii (11,698) ka li an pisnaasi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (40%), ka GUM nid Nana Amoako mɔr vɔɔt kal kɔbiga nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi (174) ka li an nɛɛm du'ali ayuobʋ kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (0.6%).
english: In 2020 Ghana general elections, he won the parliamentary seat with 14,960 votes making 51.1% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary aspirant Bernard Opoku Marfo had 2,439 votes making 8.3% of the total votes cast while the Independent parliament aspirant Duah Kwaku had 11,698 votes making 40% of the total votes cast and the GUM parliament aspirant Nana Amoako had 174 votes making 0.6% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O yinɛ Kumawu teŋkanɛ bɛ Ashanti region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana nwa ni la.
english: He hails from Kumawu in the Ashanti region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da anɛ kʋkdaani tis la'askanɛ gɔsid Employment, Social Welfare and State Enterprises la.
english: He was the Chairperson for Employment, Social Welfare and State Enterprises Committee and also a member of Lands and Forestry Committee and also a member of the Selection Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadisa anaasi la ni, April 2021, o da nɔk la'adi tis Kumawu Constituency sʋ'ʋlim ye ba di'e zamis pʋ'asada nɛ Dasam nu'ug tʋʋma.
english: In April 2021, he presented training equipment to artisans in the Kumawu Constituency to aid the youth acquire employable skills.

kusaal: Basoah da kpinɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan Nwadisa atan la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27th March, 2023).
english: Basoah died on 27 March 2023, at the age of 54.

kusaal: California ni, Thiam da pin'il ka su'e Pierre Thiam Group, dinɛ la'am kpabi su'e Teranga diib zi'igi bɛ New York City nɛ Yolélé Foods.
english: Based in California, Thiam is the founder of Pierre Thiam Group, which owns Teranga restaurants in New York City and Yolélé Foods.

kusaal: Dinɛ lɛm pɛ'ɛs dinɛ yi yʋʋm 2015 laa, Thiam an dʋgib la kpɛɛm tis Nok bani paam piini yit Alara bɛ Lagos, Nigeria, nɛ Pullman Hotel dinɛ bɛ Dakar, Senegal la dʋgib kpɛɛm nu'ug tigir.
english: In addition, since 2015, Thiam has served as Executive Chef of the award-winning restaurant Nok by Alara in Lagos, Nigeria, and the Signature Chef of the Pullman Hotel in Dakar, Senegal.

kusaal: Yolélé, dinɛ yʋʋm pin'ilʋgi bɛ 2017 la, anɛ diib lʋgʋr dinɛ ka ba dʋgid mui ma'aa, dinɛ an African dikpɛŋ yinne.
english: Yolélé, founded in 2017, is a food company centered on fonio, an ancient African super-grain.

kusaal: Pirekua mɔr kpinnim nɛ son nɛ waltz, ka Henrietta Yurchenco pa'al ye babayi' la son nɛ pirekua anɛ triple meter banɛ an baanlim, ka ba maani ba nwɛnɛ duets, naan nɛ rhythmic sequence la'asid nɛ nwiinsa ayi bɛɛ atan gitaai (I-IV-V) bɛdegʋ bɛɛ bi'ela ka ba gɔsidi li yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa.
english: Pirekua is related to the son and the waltz, and Henrietta Yurchenco points out that both the son and pirekua are in a slow triple meter, performed as duets, feature rhythmic sequence against fixed patterns in the accompaniment, and use two to three chords (I-IV-V) in major or minor with little modulation.

kusaal: Pirériechas anɛ dinɛ an nu'unwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn pa'an daʋŋkanɛ bɛ ka mɔɔn labaya tisid Purépecha sʋ'ʋlim nam.
english: Pirériechas act as social mediators and "express sentiments and communicate events of importance to the Purépecha communities."

kusaal: Planners Athletic Club, ka ba da buon ye Okyeman Planners Football Club, anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib kilab kanɛ bɛ Tafo, Eastern Region, Ghana, ka nya'ad division one (zone three), second-tier bɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb ni.
english: Planners Athletic Club, formerly Okyeman Planners Football Club, is a professional football club based in Tafo, Eastern Region, Ghana, that competes in division one (zone three), the second-tier of Ghanaian football.

kusaal: Kilab la da nwɛ' ba yiiga bɔɔl bɛnɛ first division la ni ka da tia'ali ayi, dɔl Great Olympics bɛ 2015–16 league season la ni.
english: The club's maiden season in the first division saw them placed second to leaders Great Olympics of the 2015–16 league season.

kusaal: George Afriyie an onɛ sʋ'oe ka lɛn an zugraan tis Planners Athletic Club.
english: George Afriyie is the owner and President of Planners Athletic Club.

kusaal: Onɛ sʋ'oe Okyeman Planners F.C. da yɛl yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai la ni ye on da pin'il kilab la nɛ yʋʋm to=usa ayi (2000) la ni, amaa hali ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) saŋa kilab la mɔrnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015) ka di bɛ di zanbin ni.
english: The owner of Okyeman Planners F.C. in 2019 stated that he founded the club in 2000, but as at 2020 the club has the year 2015 on its badge.

kusaal: Okyeman Planners F.C. zanbin zabyʋ'ur anɛ Yen Nhwe Ma Ensei.
english: The badge of Okyeman Planners F.C. included the motto Yen Nhwe Ma Ensei.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa ayi la ni, February 2017, kilab la nwɛ'ɛdi ba bɔɔl zin'isi'a la, Club Licensing Board dinɛ bɛ Ghana Football Association la da faaen ba tʋʋma gbaʋŋ.
english: In February 2017, the club's match venue was decertified by the Club Licensing Board of the Ghana Football Association.

kusaal: Kilab la yʋ'ʋn da nar ye ba keŋ ia zin'ipaal kanɛ ka ba na nwɛ'ɛdi ba bɔɔl, nananna, ba yʋ'ʋm bɛnɛ CRIA Park dinɛ bɛ New Tafo.
english: The club needed to find another venue for upcoming home games, and are now based at the CRIA Park, New Tafo.

kusaal: Ban da tiak kilb la yʋ'ʋr yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadisa ayi, February 2020 la ni la yi Okyeman Planners F.C. keŋ Planners Athletic Club, ba zabyʋ'ʋr mɛ da tiaki yi The Planners keŋ The Executioners.
english: On changing the name of the club in February 2020 from Okyeman Planners F.C. to Planners Athletic Club, the nickname was changed from The Planners to The Executioners.

kusaal: William Opoku da pin'ili o bɔɔn nwɛ'ɛbnɛ Okyeman Planners F.C., nɛ Prosper Avor da nwɛ' tis kilab la bɛ 2015 and 2016.
english: William Opoku began his career with Okyeman Planners F.C., and Prosper Avor played for the club in 2015 and 2016.

kusaal: Bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb kaŋa dim nya'adnɛ Ghana Division Two League la.
english: The club is competing in the Ghana Division Two League.

kusaal: Yiiga club la da tólis Ghana Premier League la ni 1997-1998.
english: The club was first promoted to the Ghana Premier League in 1997–98.

kusaal: Yiiga, ba da paam tɔlʋsʋg n tɔlis Ghana premier league bɛ 1997-1998 ni.
english: The club was first promoted to the Ghana Premier League in 1997–98.

kusaal: Ba da naae nɔɔr atan' tuon ken linɛ da naam 2000 ni la, Adansiman Obuasi dim da di ka kɛɛ ba, ka ba lɛbisi ba nya'aŋ ya'as.
english: They finished third from bottom in 2000, and were relegated after losing to Adansiman Obuasi in a play-off.

kusaal: Ka ban da lɛn di ya'an nɔɔr atan' naae la, ba da di Mysterious Dwarfs dim la nɛ 1-0.
english: After finishing third from bottom again, they retained their place in the top flight after beating Mysterious Dwarfs 1–0.

kusaal: Amaa la'am nɛ wala wʋsa ba da lɛn nyaŋ duoe zi'enɛ banɔba zug ka lɛn lɛb Division One ni na.
english: However, they were promoted back to the Ghana Premier League in their first season back in Division One after beating Ghaphoa Readers 3–2 in a promotion playoff match.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn nwɛ' nɛ Mysterious Dwarf dim ka nyaŋi ba, ani ka ba lɛn paami ba kpi'euŋ zin'ig bɛɛ agɔl ya'as yʋʋm 2006-2007 la ni.
english: After finishing third from bottom again, they retained their place in the top flight after beating Mysterious Dwarfs 1–0.

kusaal: Presbyterian University, Ghana (ka ba da buon ye Presbyterian University College, Ghana) anɛ university kanɛ ka fan an asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ dim bʋn, ka fan mɛ an gɔmɛna bʋn, ka ba zamisig zin'is bɛ zin'is kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb, ka li dɔtita'ar bɛ Abetifi-Kwahu linɛ bɛ Eastern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋim.
english: The Presbyterian University, Ghana (formerly Presbyterian University College, Ghana) is a partially private & public university with multi- campuses and its headquarters located at Abetifi-Kwahu in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Presbyterian Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg dim banɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la da yɔ'ɔgi li yʋʋm tusayi nɛ atan', Sapal nwadig dabpisi nɛ atan' daar ka Ghana zugraan kʋdʋg John Agyekum Kufuor da zʋŋi li yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi, Dɔnwalig nwadig, dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar.
english: It was established by the Presbyterian Church of Ghana (PCG) on 23 November 2003 and inaugurated on 27 March 2004 by the former president of Ghana in that republic, John Agyekum Kufuor.

kusaal: Ba gɔs ka ye linɛ an asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ university kanɛ gaad o taaba Ghana sʋ'ʋlim, ka mɛ paas nɛ atan' daan, fʋ ya'a yis University of Ghana nɛ KNUST ka banɛ vɛɛn vɛɛnsig kaŋa anɛ dunia wʋsa lʋgir kanɛ mamisid university nami gɔsid ka ba buon webometrics la.
english: It has been ranked the best private university in Ghana and third best after the University of Ghana and KNUST by world university ranking website webometrics.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anii la ni, sakur la da mɔr zin'ig kanɛ ka ba pa'an Wina'am tʋmtʋmnib ka ba buon ye teacher-catechist seminary, bɛɛ Basel Mission Seminary, lin nya'aŋ ka ba tiaki buon Presbyterian Training College ka li bɛ Akropong, linɛ da paas ayi' daani an sakur tita'ari bɛ West Africa, ka yiiga daan la da an Fourah Bay College linɛ bɛ Sierra Leone tɛŋin la.
english: In 1848, the church founded a teacher-catechist seminary, the Basel Mission Seminary, later known as the Presbyterian Training College (PTC) at Akropong as the second higher educational institution in West Africa after Fourah Bay College in Sierra Leone.

kusaal: University la mɔr zamisig zin'is anu ka ba bɛ Abetifi-Kwahu, Akropong-Akuapem linɛ bɛ Eastern Region, Agogo – Asante Akyem linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region, tɛmpʋʋgin Tema linɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region la nɛ Kumasi Santasi linɛ bɛ Ashanti Region la.
english: The university has five campuses at Abetifi-Kwahu, Akropong-Akuapem in the Eastern Region, Agogo – Asante Akyem in the Ashanti Region, the city campus at Tema in the Greater Accra Region and Kumasi Santasi Ashanti Region.

kusaal: · Bachelor of Law (LLB)
english: Bachelor of Law (LLB)

kusaal: · Master of Public Health (MPH)
english: Master of Public Health (MPH)

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi', motul nwadig, dabpistan' daar, dabiskanɛ da lut Atalata daar la, university la nɛ o taaba ayi', da paam paŋ ye ba zi'eni ba mɛŋ nyali yi Ghana gɔmɛna zugraan kʋdʋg Akufo Addo ni, tigir kanɛ ka ba da la'asi maal Accra sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: On Tuesday, 30 August 2022, the university, with two others, was granted a Presidential Charter by President Akufo Addo, in a small ceremony in Accra.

kusaal: Li paas university banɛ an paala bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka lʋgir kanɛ gɔsid kpɛɛmnam sakur bɛda nam la tisi ba suor ye ba tʋmi ba tʋʋma.
english: The Presbyterian University, Ghana (formerly Presbyterian University College, Ghana) is a partially private & public university with multi- campuses and its headquarters located at Abetifi-Kwahu in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmin gbana pa'al ye ye Presbyterian Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg dim banɛ bɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim da mɛ' biban'alig sakur yiiga Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnaasi nɛ atan' la ni, ka li dɔlis anina ka gbaŋ zamisig nɔbigi kɛŋ tuon.
english: Per historical accounts, the Presbyterian Church of Ghana established Ghana's first elementary school in the country in 1843 which resulted in the institutionalization of formal education in the country.

kusaal: Nwa da kɛ ka ba la'as nɛ Ghana gɔmɛna ka ba mɛ' primary nɛ secondary sakur nam nɛ koliginam; ba da anɛ sakurnam tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ, ka kɔbisnaasi nɛ piswai an kindergartens, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' an primary sakur nam, kɔbistan' nɛ pisnii nɛ anii an JSS, pisi nɛ nu an senior secondary school nam, anu an vocational institutes ka anu mɛ an colleges of education.
english: This development led to the establishment of several primary and secondary schools and colleges of education through a strategic partnership with the Ghanaian government; specifically, 1,886 schools made up of 490 kindergartens, 973 primary school, 388 junior secondary schools, 25 senior secondary schools, five vocational institutes and five colleges of education.

kusaal: Ban da gban'ae si'em da anɛ ye ba kɛ ka Presbyterian Training College linɛ da bɛ Akropong la kilim university wan wʋʋ Fourah Bay College zi'esim paae si'em bɛn la, amaa, gban'a kan da pʋ zi'enɛ.
english: The initial plan was to upgrade the Presbyterian Training College at Akropong to a full-fledged university like Fourah Bay College but that did no come into fruition.

kusaal: Yʋʋma kɔbiga nɛ pisnu nya'aŋ, ka Presbyterian Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔg kpɛɛmnam da la'as taaba yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ la'asig la ni ye ba dɔlis ban na niŋ siem ka sakur la nɔbigi paae university bɛn, ba da yis kpɛɛmnam ye ba gɔsi li yela yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii la ni.
english: More than a century and a half later, the Synod of the Presbyterian Church during its 1996 conference voted to establish an actual university culminating in the setting up of an Implementation Committee in 1998.

kusaal: La'an nɛ lin an Winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔgi sʋ'ʋe la, university di'esid nidib ka ba ba' kae nɛ ba dima yit zin'ig si'a bɛɛ ban an buud si'a.
english: Despite its religious affiliation, the university college welcome students of all backgrounds, ethnicity, religion and geography.

kusaal: Nwa' da tis university la paŋ ye ba tis degree nɛ diploma kasɛta gbana linɛ pa'al ye nidib zamis anina naae.
english: The charter granted the university gives it a legal authorization to award its own degree or diploma certificates.

kusaal: · Ye ba zamis nidib banɛ gban'adi ba mɛŋ, ka na nyaŋi muku ba mɛŋ ka mɛ na lɛn nyaŋi an tuongatib ka an ninsʋma Wina'am, nidib, nɛ tɛngbaŋ wʋsa tuon."
english: To produce disciplined, self-motivated individuals and leaders with moral and intellectual values in the realization of their responsibilities to God, fellow citizens and the state."

kusaal: Sakur la mɛ zamisid na'asaasɔɔng zamisig nam ka ba si'eba kati wa'ae nɛ laafi yela, tima yela, nɛ nɛɛsnam zamisig.
english: The school also offers programs in science and technology including health sciences, medicine, dentistry and nursing.

kusaal: Prince Hamid Armah anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid ba da du'anɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris piiga la li daba yuobυ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ yinne, onɛ wadmaan n tis Kwesimintsim linɛ bɛ Gaana Western Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Prince Hamid Armah (born 6 October 1981) is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the Member of Parliament for Kwesimintsim Constituency in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da dɛgim tυmnɛ an Director General n tis National Council for Curriculum and Assessment.
english: He previously served as the Director General of the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment.

kusaal: Armah nɛ bɛ Kwesimintsim linɛ bɛ Gaana Western Region sυ'υlυm, ani ka o da pin'ili o sakur ken ka naan tɔlis St John's Secondary Sakur linɛ bɛ Sekondi la.
english: Dr. Armah was born in Kwesimintsim in the Western Region of Ghana, where he had his basic education before proceeding to St John's Secondary School in Sekondi.

kusaal: O da yii ani keŋ University of Education, Winneba, ani ka o maal o Bachelor's nɛ Mastɛs digirɛɛ linɛ Gɛligir zamisυg la.
english: From there, he went to the University of Education, Winneba, where he obtained both his Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Mathematics Education.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o maal Doctor of Philosophy n bɛ Gɛligir pυυgin, o zamisυg la zug anɛ Curriculum, Pedagogy and Education Policy zamisυg.
english: He later earned a Doctor of Philosophy in Mathematics Education, with specialization in Curriculum, Pedagogy and Education Policy at the University of Aberdeen, UK.

kusaal: O da lɛn di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Quantitative Methods n yi Doctoral Training Centres linɛ bɛ University of Edinburgh, University of Manchester, nɛ University of Nottingham.
english: Also, Armah holds certificates in Quantitative Methods from the Doctoral Training Centres of the University of Edinburgh, the University of Manchester, and the University of Nottingham.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina wai la, ba gaŋ o ye o an Executive Secretary n tis National Council for Curriculum nɛ Assessment.
english: In January 2019, he was appointed as the Executive Secretary of the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn gaŋ o ye o an yiiga (acting) Director General n tis curriculum tυυma.
english: Following the passing of the Education Regulatory Bodies Act 2019, he was appointed as the first (acting) Director General of the curriculum body.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris ayuobυ la li dabisim piisi yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi la ni ka ba vɔt ka o di, ka bas Mr Joe Mensah, o da paamnɛ vɔt 222 ka o tiraan la mɔr 167.
english: On June 20, 2020, he defeated then incumbent Member of Parliament, Mr Joe Mensah in the party's parliamentary primary, polling 222 votes against his opponent's 167.

kusaal: Processional giants and dragons (French: Géants et dragons processionnels) dinɛ yi Belgium nɛ France la anɛ folkloric pa'alʋg banɛ mɔr processional giants, dinɛ ka UNESCO zaŋi paas lists of Intangible Cultural Heritage yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) la ni, ka ba da dɛŋinm pian' di yɛla yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu nwadis piinɛ yinne la ni.
english: The processional giants and dragons (French: Géants et dragons processionnels) of Belgium and France are a set of folkloric manifestations involving processional giants, which have been inscribed by UNESCO on the lists of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2008, originally proclaimed in November 2005.

en_article: Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a gɔs Belgium dim, bam alima anɛ festivities of Dendermonde (Ommegang van Dendermonde), Mechelen (Ommegang van Mechelen), Mons ( Ducasse de Mons, nɛ the fight dinɛ ka ba pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr "Lumeçon"), Ath (Ducasse d'Ath) nɛ Brussels (Meyboom).
english: In the case of Belgium, these are the festivities of Dendermonde (Ommegang van Dendermonde), Mechelen (Ommegang van Mechelen), Mons (the Ducasse de Mons, and the fight which is named the "Lumeçon"), Ath (the Ducasse d'Ath) and Brussels (the Meyboom).

en_article: Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France

kusaal: Amaa France, bama aan ba malima bɛ Douai (feasts of Gayant) nɛ Cassel (carnival) nɛ totemic animals nɛ ban maani ba si'em bɛ Tarascon nɛ Pézenas (Mardi Gras, ka ba zuŋidi li Mirondela dels Arts Alasid daar kanɛ an yiiga nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni).
english: For France, these are the feasts at Douai (feasts of Gayant) and Cassel (carnival) and the totemic animals and their celebrations in Tarascon and Pézenas (Mardi Gras, inauguration of the Mirondela dels Arts on the first Sunday in July).

en_article: Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France

english: Belgium has nearly 1500 giants on its soil.
kus_article: Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France
en_article: Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France

kusaal: Ba an si'em anɛ wʋʋ din da an si'em 15th century ni la; Goliath of Nivelles, dinɛ ka ba da pʋdigidi li kʋdʋmin sa yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (1457) la ni, ka an dinɛ kʋdʋgi gaad Belgium giant nam la wʋsa.
english: Their appearance dates back to the 15th century; Goliath of Nivelles, which is mentioned as early as 1457, is the oldest known Belgian giant.

en_article: Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France

kusaal: Belgium mɛ lɛm mɔr giant tita'ar Europe; Jean Turpin onɛ bɛ Nieuwpoort, dinɛ gaad 11 metres (36 ft).
english: Belgium also has the largest giant in Europe; Jean Turpin of Nieuwpoort, which exceeds 11 metres (36 ft).

kusaal: Si'igirinɛ, li da pɛ'ɛsɛ nɛ Bawku Municipal sʋ'ʋlʋm 1988; yʋ'ʋn da ti paae saŋa kanɛ ka ba pʋdʋgi nyɛ Binduri sʋ'ʋlʋm (yi Ya-tuon) nɛ Pusʋg sʋ'ʋlʋm (yi Ya-nya'aŋ) bɛ 28 June 2012.

kusaal: Pütchipü'ü, bɛɛ pütche'ejachi (bɛ Wayuu, "Onɛ ka labaar la tʋmmid"; Spanish: palabrero), an laʋk kanɛ yɛla pak hali bɛ ban dɔloisid malima maan pian'ad nɛ sida si'em tis nimbanɛ bɛ Wayuu.
english: A pütchipü'ü, or pütche'ejachi (in Wayuu, "messenger of the word"; Spanish: palabrero), is a mediator and the central element in the traditional administration justice system of the Wayuu people.

kusaal: Nɛ' tʋn'e an zaba gɛɛsid buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb bɛɛ zak yinne dim banɛ bɛ Wayuu sʋ'ʋlimin bɛɛ ninsieba bɛɛ la'asʋg banɛ pʋ bɛ Wayuu nidib sʋʋginɛ.
english: This can include conflicts between different members or clans of the Wayuu community or with people or organizations outside the Wayuu people.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ni, UNESCO da nyɛ sɔnskaŋa ka di nar ka ba zaŋi li paas Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
english: In 2010, this mediation system was recognized by UNESCO as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Venezuela nɛ Colombia gɔmenanam n gɔmenanam nyɛ yʋʋmpʋkʋdʋgin wada kaŋa ka di an sʋm ka mɔr sʋŋir hali tisi ba.
english: This indigenous law system has been recognized by governments of Venezuela and Colombia.

kusaal: Ba da la'as pütchipü'ui lanɛ dɔlisid Major Autonomous Board of Palabreros.
english: The pütchipü'ui are organized by the Major Autonomous Board of Palabreros; as of 2010, there were 37 pütchipü'ui serving the council, as well as a further 20 young Wayuu professionals, both from Venezuela and Colombia.

kusaal: Pütchipü'ü tʋʋm anɛ di mɔr naalʋgʋ kɛn' banɛ mɔr nɔŋgbannwa'ar sʋʋgin dɔlisid ban na nwɛ' nu'ug nɛ sɔnsʋg.
english: The role of a pütchipü'ü is to solve conflicts through mediation and negotiation.

kusaal: Nwɛn wʋʋ bʋnkɔbid wʋsaa, pɛ'ɛs yinɛ Artiodactyla buudi ni.
english: Like all ruminants, sheep are members of the order Artiodactyla, the even-toed ungulates.

kusaal: Pɛ'og anɛ bʋnkɔnbig kanɛ ka ninsaalib da mɔr o kpɛn'ɛ yin yiiga (baa ban da mɔr baa kpɛn'ɛ yin wan wʋʋ yʋma tusa piiga bɛɛ tusa pisi banɛ gaad la); ban da mɔr o kpɛn'ɛ yin da anɛ yʋʋm 11,000 nɛ 9000 BC tɛnsʋki bɛ Mesopotamia ka Mehrgarh tɛŋin an wʋʋ yʋʋm 7000 bɛ Indus Valley.
english: Sheep were among the earliest animals to be domesticated by humankind (along with dogs, which were domesticated 10 to 20 thousand years earlier); the date of domestication is estimated to fall between 11,000 and 9000 BC in Mesopotamia, from which it spread to Mehrgarh in the Indus Valley around 7000 BC.

kusaal: Banɛ vɛɛnsid kʋdʋmin dim yela pa'al ye ba nyɛ zin'ig si'a Iran pa'al ye ba da gaans pɛ'ɛs banɛ mɔr kɔnbilig nɛ 6000 BC, ka li yʋʋm tusayi paae tusatan' ni ka ba mɔr kɔnbilig la fuudi yɛɛd.
english: Archaeological evidence from statuary found at sites in Iran suggests that selection for woolly sheep may have begun around 6000 BC, while the earliest woven wool garments have been dated to around 4000 BC, two thousand years later.

kusaal: "Shipping fever" (pneʋmonic mannheimiosis, formerly called pasteurellosis) anɛ wi'im yitnɛ gɛnlis ni, kas kas anɛ fʋn na mɔrʋ waɛ zin'isia bɛɛ fʋn na zanl ɔ.
english: "Shipping fever" (pneumonic mannheimiosis, formerly called pasteurellosis) is a disease of particular concern, that can occur as a result of stress, notably during transport and (or) handling.

kusaal: Zʋn'zʋya la anɛ bot fly nɛ blow-fly, wɔɔ Lucilia sericata bɛ li ti'ran L. cuprina.
english: Maggots are those of the bot fly and the blow-fly, commonly Lucilia sericata or its relative L. cuprina.

kusaal: Nose bots anɛ bʋn iiada banɛ nanpʋ kpɛ'iŋɛ ka bɛ pɛ'og yɔ'ya ni ka kɛ ka pɛ'og la pʋ tɔ'ɔn vʋ'ʋsida.
english: Nose bots are fly larvae that inhabit a sheep's sinuses, causing breathing difficulties and discomfort.

kusaal: "Mutton" linɛ an pɛ'og ni'im na'asaalin la yina Old French moton, linɛ da an yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka Anglo-Norman tuongatib da pʋd pɛ'og, banɛ da yit British Isles Middle Ages saŋa.
english: "Mutton" is derived from the Old French moton, which was the word for sheep used by the Anglo-Norman rulers of much of the British Isles in the Middle Ages.

kusaal: 21st century saŋa, tɛɛns banɛ ka ba da ɔnbid pɛ'og ni'im hali da anɛ Arab states of the Persian Gulf, New Zealand, Australia, Greece, Uruguay, United Kingdom nɛ Ireland.
english: In the 21st century, the nations with the highest consumption of sheep meat are the Arab states of the Persian Gulf, New Zealand, Australia, Greece, Uruguay, the United Kingdom and Ireland.

kusaal: Tɛɛns bama ɔnbid 14–40 lbs (3–18 kg) pɛ'og ni'im yʋʋm wʋsa.
english: These countries eat 14–40 lbs (3–18 kg) of sheep meat per capita, per annum.

kusaal: Pɛ'og ni'im yʋ'ʋr mɛ yi France, Africa (li kaskas Arab tɛɛnsin), Caribbean, banɛ kpɛlim Middle East, India, nɛ China zin'is si'eba.
english: Sheep meat is also popular in France, Africa (especially the Arab world), the Caribbean, the rest of the Middle East, India, and parts of China.

kusaal: Linɛ ka ba mɔr pɛ'og ni'imi maan ka li bɛ li kɔn' anɛ Scottish haggis, lin anɛ pɛ'og puʋgin la'ad ka ba dʋg nɛ oatmeal ka sɛ gabʋ gɛndig nɛ pʋʋr la.
english: An unusual dish of sheep meat is the Scottish haggis, composed of various sheep innards cooked along with oatmeal and chopped onions inside its stomach.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a ye fʋ mamisi gɔs, tɛɛns wan wʋʋ U.S. ɔnbid ni'im la wan wʋʋ pound bɛɛ li gaad ala (pʋ paae 0.5 kg), ka America nidib ɔnbid kurkur ni'im 50 pounds (22 kg) nɛ naaf ni'im 65 pounds (29 kg).
english: In comparison, countries such as the U.S. consume only a pound or less (under 0.5 kg), with Americans eating 50 pounds (22 kg) of pork and 65 pounds (29 kg) of beef.

kusaal: Ban nɔk pɛ'og bin'isim maal bin'isim diib si'eba an feta linɛ bɛ Bulgaria nɛ Greece, Roquefort linɛ bɛ France, Manchego yit Spain, pecorino romano (Itali dim buon pɛ'og ye pecore) nɛ ricotta Italy tɛŋin nɔɔ.
english: Well-known cheeses made from sheep milk include the feta of Bulgaria and Greece, Roquefort of France, Manchego from Spain, the pecorino romano (the Italian word for "sheep" is pecore) and ricotta of Italy.

kusaal: Yogurts, si'eba maali yinɛ pɛ'og bin'isim ni.
english: Yogurts, especially some forms of strained yogurt, may also be made from sheep milk.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛyi ni (2012), pɛ'og kanɛ da mɔr buudi kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb ka ba buon "Peng Peng" da yi paalʋ na dɔlis Chinese scientists, onɛ da vɛɛns ka ye o buudi anɛ samɛrid buudi ka li da dɔlis anina ka li nyaŋi maal kpaam kanɛ pʋ mɔr daʋŋi tis ninsaal ningbiŋɔ.
english: In 2012, a transgenic sheep named "Peng Peng" was cloned by Chinese scientists, who spliced his genes with that of a roundworm (C. elegans) in order to increase production of fats healthier for human consumption.

kusaal: Pɛ'og anɛ zanbina tis banɛ yʋm yʋʋma wan wʋʋ The Wolf in Sheep's Clothing, Little Bo Peep, Baa, Baa, Black Sheep, nɛ Mary Had a Little Lamb; gbana wan wʋʋ George Orwell gbaŋ kanɛ buon Animal Farm nɛ Haruki Murakami gbaŋ kanɛ an A Wild Sheep Chase; yʋʋma banɛ ka ba si'eba an Bach's Sheep may safely graze (Schafe können sicher weiden) nɛ Pink Floyd yʋʋma ka o buol ye "Sheep", nɛ yʋm si'eba wan ni William Blake din linɛ ka o pʋd "The Lamb".
english: Sheep are symbols in fables and nursery rhymes like The Wolf in Sheep's Clothing, Little Bo Peep, Baa, Baa, Black Sheep, and Mary Had a Little Lamb; novels such as George Orwell's Animal Farm and Haruki Murakami's A Wild Sheep Chase; songs such as Bach's Sheep may safely graze (Schafe können sicher weiden) and Pink Floyd's "Sheep", and poems like William Blake's "The Lamb".

kusaal: Saŋkanɛ gaad sa la, ba da mɔr pɛ'og zanbina winpʋ'ʋsʋm zin'isi bɛ ancient Near East, Mideast, nɛ Mediterranean zin'is: Çatalhöyük, Egyptian winpʋ'ʋs kʋdʋg, Cana'anite nɛ Phoenician malima ni, Judaism, Greek winpʋ'ʋsʋm, nɛ si'eba banɛ kpɛlim.
english: In antiquity, symbolism involving sheep cropped up in religions in the ancient Near East, the Mideast, and the Mediterranean area: Çatalhöyük, ancient Egyptian religion, the Cana'anite and Phoenician tradition, Judaism, Greek religion, and others.

kusaal: Winpʋ'ʋsʋm zanbina nɛ malima da pin'il nɛ yiiga yadda niŋidib la sa'an: pɛ'ɛs zu'wana (nɛ niigi) ka ba da mɔri bɛ badanam ni bɛ Çatalhöyük zin'is ni 8,000 BCE.
english: Religious symbolism and ritual involving sheep began with some of the first known faiths: Skulls of rams (along with bulls) occupied central placement in shrines at the Çatalhöyük settlement around 6,000 BCE.

kusaal: Madagascar tɛŋin, ba da pʋ ɔnbid pɛ'og ni'imɛ bɔzugɔ ba da si'ak ye pɛ'og anɛ ba yaanam la ti'aki lɛb na.
english: In Madagascar, sheep were not eaten as they were believed to be incarnations of the souls of ancestors.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmin Greek dim pian'a pɛ'og yela bɛdigʋ: ka ba buon Chrysomallos, ka o kɔnbilig la an dɔnbʋʋlim wan wʋʋ sanlim nɛ, ka ba pa'an o yela kʋdʋmin sa ti paae zina nwa'.
english: There are many ancient Greek references to sheep: that of Chrysomallos, the golden-fleeced ram, continuing to be told through into the modern era.

kusaal: Greeks and Romans dim da mɔr pɛ'ɛsi maan maana ka li an ba malima, ka banɛ ka win kanɛ ka ba pʋ'ʋsid an Judaism mɛ kuud pɛ'ɛs ka ba buoni li Korban, malima la si'eba anɛ Wina'am kum maliak gaadʋg maliŋ ka ba kuud pɛ'ɛs.
english: Greeks and Romans sacrificed sheep regularly in religious practice, and Judaism once sacrificed sheep as a Korban (sacrifice), such as the Passover lamb.

kusaal: Wina'am gbaŋ mɛ pa'al ye Kristo anɛ maan pɛ'og kanɛ yi Wina'am sa'an na ka Easter di'ema nam ka ba maani bɛ Greece nɛ Romania tɛɛnsin la ba kuud Paschal pɛ'ɛs anina.
english: Christ is also portrayed as the Sacrificial lamb of God (Agnus Dei) and Easter celebrations in Greece and Romania traditionally feature a meal of Paschal lamb.

kusaal: Yin pɛ'ɛs la an' pɛ'ɛs banɛ zu'oe.Na'asaanam buon pɛ' nya'aŋ la nɛ ye ewe (/juː/ yoo), ka buon pɛ'raug la ye ram, saŋa bɛdigʋ, ba buon ban fuoe pɛ'raad sieba la ye wether, ka pɛ'bibis la ye lamb.
english: An adult female is referred to as a ewe ( yoo); an intact male as a ram, occasionally a tup; a castrated male as a wether; and a young sheep as a lamb.

kusaal: Vɛɛnsig pa'al ye Ovis aries yinɛ Asiatic (O. gmelini) buudi kanɛ buon mouflon ni; Mɔɔgin pɛ'og kanɛ bɛ Europe ka ba buon European mouflon (Ovis aries musimon) dɔlis nɛ buudi kaŋa ni kɛna.
english: The most common hypothesis states that Ovis aries is descended from the Asiatic (O. gmelini) species of mouflon; the European mouflon (Ovis aries musimon) is a direct descendant of this population.

kusaal: zabir, dabiɛm, nɛ siɛnam bɛdigʋ tɔ'ɔn kɛ ka ɔ paam ɛpinephrine (adrenaline).
english: Pain, fear and several other stressors can cause secretion of epinephrine (adrenaline).

kusaal: Oral anti-parasitic medicine ka ba bʋɔn drenches ka ba mɔrɛ tisid bʋnkɔn'bid la ka li ti'ɛbid wɔrms ba ya'a ti nɔbigid yɛ li sin'iŋ tʋʋma.
english: Oral anti-parasitic medicines, known as drenches, are given to a flock to treat worms, sometimes after worm eggs in the feces has been counted to assess infestation levels.

kusaal: Bʋnvʋya banɛ da'amid pɛ'og niŋbiŋ la anɛ: karigis (li bɛ nɛ ɔ niŋbiŋ lʋas kɔn'bkɔn'b), sheep keds, nose bots, sheep itch mites, nɛ zʋn'zʋr.
english: External sheep parasites include lice, sheep keds, nose bot flies, sheep itch mites, and maggots.

kusaal: Keds la anɛ bʋnvʋr banɛ nʋʋd ziim ka kɛt ka pɛ'og la pʋ tɔ'ɔn di'ta ka lɛɛ kaɛ sapʋadɛ.
english: Keds are blood-sucking parasites that cause general malnutrition and decreased productivity, but are not fatal.

kusaal: China, Australia, India, nɛ Iran mɔr pɛ'ɛs bɛdigʋ, anina ka ba tɛŋin dim paamid ni'im nɛ gbana, ka mɛ lɛn mɔri laligid tɛŋ si'eba.
english: China, Australia, India, Nigeria, and Iran have the largest modern flocks, and serve both local and exportation needs for wool and mutton.

kusaal: Amaa, banɛ gʋ'ʋn bi'ela, ka mɔr bʋn-nya'as wan wʋʋ piiga paae pisnu (10 to 50 ewes), pʋ mɔr nyɔɔdɛ bɔzugɔ ba pʋ gɔsidi ba titua nɛ.
english: However, small flocks, from 10 to 50 ewes, often are not profitable because they tend to be poorly managed.

kusaal: Ba buon pɛ'og ni'im ye pɛ'og ni'im, ka yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin ba kuud pɛ'ɛs wan wʋʋ 540 million maan ni'im dunia wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: Sheep meat prepared for food is known as either mutton or lamb, and approximately 540 million sheep are slaughtered each year for meat worldwide.

kusaal: Nwa' da kilim pɛ'og ni'im na'asaalin, ka yʋ'ʋr kanɛ yi Old English ni ka ba buon sceap la ka ba lɛɛ da nɔki pʋd bʋnvʋr la yʋ'ʋr.
english: This became the name for sheep meat in English, while the Old English word sceap was kept for the live animal.

kusaal: Pɛ'og lana—ka ba buon animelles bɛɛ lamb fries—anɛ dikpɛŋi tis tɛɛns bɛdigʋ dunia ni.
english: Sheep testicles—called animelles or lamb fries—are considered a delicacy in many parts of the world.

kusaal: zin'ig kanɛ ka ba buon Roslin Institute of Edinburgh, Scotland tɛŋin la mɔr pɛ'ɛs buudi kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔbi maan vɛɛnsig ye ba gɔs yelsi'eba.
english: In particular, the Roslin Institute of Edinburgh, Scotland used sheep for genetics research that produced groundbreaking results.

kusaal: Egyptian winpʋ'ʋsʋm ni, pɛ'og da anɛ zanbini tis wina bɛdigʋ: Khnum, Heryshaf nɛ Amun (on da anɛ winkanɛ tisid biis).
english: In Ancient Egyptian religion, the ram was the symbol of several gods: Khnum, Heryshaf and Amun (in his incarnation as a god of fertility).

kusaal: Bada banɛ mɛ da pa'an pɛ'og zanbina da anɛ winpʋ'ak Ishtar, Phoenician winkanɛ ka ba buon Baal-Hamon, Babylonian dim winkanɛ ka ba buon Ea-Oannes.
english: Other deities occasionally shown with ram features include the goddess Ishtar, the Phoenician god Baal-Hamon, and the Babylonian god Ea-Oannes.

kusaal: Banɛ gɔsid kudʋmin yela pa'al ye ba zanbina pʋʋgin, pɛ'og anɛ yiiga zanbin bɛ Greek zodiac zanbina nam ni, ka mɛ paas bʋnkɔnbid anii banɛ ka ba mɔri kaan yʋʋma paad yʋʋm piinɛyi bɛn la, ka li an bʋnlinɛ ka ba nɔki pʋd nwadis la yʋda yʋʋm pʋʋgin.
english: Astrologically, Aries, the ram, is the first sign of the classical Greek zodiac, and the sheep is the eighth of the twelve animals associated with the 12-year cycle of the Chinese zodiac, related to the Chinese calendar.

kusaal: Pɛ'og da paas Abraham nam saŋa ka li pa'an ban da mɔr yadda si'em; Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, nɛ King David nam da anɛ kɔnbkimnib.
english: Sheep play an important role in all the Abrahamic faiths; Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, and King David were all shepherds.

kusaal: Wina'am gbaŋ la pa'al ban da lɔ Isaac la, ba da kʋ nɛ pɛ'og ka o di'e Isaac maliak la da gban'e Abraham nu'ug la (mɔɔm pʋ'ʋsim pʋʋgin, Abraham da ti'eb nɛ ye o ku Ishmael li maal maan).
english: According to the Biblical story of the Binding of Isaac, a ram is sacrificed as a substitute for Isaac after an angel stays Abraham's hand (in the Islamic tradition, Abraham was about to sacrifice Ishmael).

kusaal: Ba buon karindɔɔg kpɛɛm nɛ ye pastor, ka lin yinɛ latin buudi pian'ad ni linɛ gbin ni an kɔnbkim.
english: A church leader is often called the pastor, which is derived from the Latin word for shepherd.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a buol nid ye o anɛ pɛ'og, li pa'al ye ba zɔt nɛ dabi'em ka ka'a gba'arɛ.
english: In the English language, to call someone a sheep or ovine may allude that they are timid and easily led.

kusaal: Ba la'asi buon banɛ an Kristo biis ye pɛ'ɛs ka Kristo mɛŋ an kɔnbkim sʋŋ, ka pɛ'ɛs mɛ paas Yesu dʋ'am saŋa sa.
english: Collectively, followers of Christianity are often referred to as a flock, with Christ as the Good Shepherd, and sheep are an element in the Christian iconography of the birth of Jesus.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a gɔs bʋnbama nɛ pɛ'og ligidi mɛ pʋ zuoe wala, nwa' wʋsa pa'al ye banɛ gʋ'ʋn pɛ'ɛs la mɔr nyɔɔd, baa o kɔnbid la ya'a pʋ zuoe.
english: Some farmers who keep sheep also make a profit from live sheep.

kusaal: Pɛ'og ni'im nɛ o bin'isim da anɛ diib hali tis dʋdʋmin dim ka ba da dit ka li maani ba ningbina ban da pin'ili tɔn'ɔsid ka la'asid kuod nɛ gʋ'ʋl la'ad la.
english: Sheep meat and milk were one of the earliest staple proteins consumed by human civilization after the transition from hunting and gathering to agriculture.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a buol nid ye pɛ'og sabil, li pa'al ye o anɛ ninkanɛ pʋ dɔlisid la'asig la wadaa.
english: To call an individual a black sheep implies that they are an odd or disreputable member of a group.

kusaal: Salla anɛ maliŋ kanɛ ka mɔɔm maan, sankan ka ba mɔr pɛ'ɛs (bɛɛ bʋnkɔnb si'eba) kuud ka li pa'an ye ba ti'en nɛ bʋnlinɛ da maal la.
english: Sheep are occasionally sacrificed to commemorate important secular events in Islamic cultures.

kusaal: O da anɛ MP tis Agona East Constituency yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) la ni.
english: She has been the member of parliament of the Agona East Constituency since 2013.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Sawyerr nɛ Nasaar nwadig ayɔpɔi dabisim yinne daar (1 July 1964) bɛ Agona Kwanyako teŋkanɛ bɛ Central Region, Ghana.
english: Sawyerr was born on 1 July 1964 and hails from Agona Kwanyako in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ Accra Polytechnic sakurin la naae ka paam Diploma kasɛta gbaʋŋ nɛ Degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ zaŋi ken Kpikpinnib Lʋgir la nɛ Public Administration yi Atlantic International University.
english: She received her higher national diploma from Accra Polytechnic and received a bachelor's degree in Business Administration and master's in Public Administration from Atlantic International University.

kusaal: O da anɛ CEO tis Queenstar Real Estates Company Limited yiiga ka nyaan kpɛn' wada maalʋg yin.
english: She was CEO of Queenstar Real Estates Company Limited before assuming her position as a member of parliament.

kusaal: Nimbanɛ da vɔɔt tis o la kanl da anɛ tusa pisi nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbisyi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi (23,247) ka li an pisnu nɛ li du'alʋg ayuobʋ vɔɔdʋg la kanl wusa ni, ka NPP nid la da on paam bi'ela linɛ an 22,292 ka li an 48.5% vɔɔdʋg kanl wusa ni, ka LPG wadmaanib yir nid, Samuel Aryeequaye mɛ da paam vɔɔt kal 204 ka li an 0.4%.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general elections, Sawyerr won the Agona East parliamentary seat with 23,247 votes making 50.6% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Kwesi Yankah had 22,292 votes making 48.5% of the total votes cast and the LPG parliamentary candidate Samuel Aryeequaye had 204 votes making 0.4% of the total votes cast, the CPP parliamentary candidate Appiah Kubi Sharfiu had 139 votes making 0.3% of the total votes cast and an Independent parliamentary candidate Anthony Adjetey Adjei had 97 votes making 0.2% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Nwɛnnɛ yʋma piiga (10) banɛ gaad la, Sawyerr da dɔlisnɛ Maame Pokua ligipɛmisa Scheme (MPLS) la n pʋr ligidi sʋŋ pu'ab banɛ kpɛmisidi o sʋ'ʋlim la ni.
english: For over 10 years, Sawyerr developed the Maame Pokua Loan Scheme (MPLS) to distribute money and support women traders in her constituency.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (2014) la ni, o da tis Mathematics set nam sakur banɛ da sɔbid BECE o sʋ'ʋlimin la.
english: In 2014, she presented mathematical sets to over 1400 students in her constituency who wrote the BECE.

kusaal: October Nwadig la yʋma 2020 la, Nana Kojo Amuakwa V (Agona Duakwa Na'ab) da kad Sawyerr ye o da nwɛ' Pɔlitis Agonaa.
english: In October 2020, Sawyerr was banned from campaigning on the land of Agona by Nana Kojo Amuakwa V (the Chief of Agona Duakwa).

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana nid onɛ nwɛ'ɛd Pɔlitis ka an minista nya'aŋdɔl tis Voltal Region, Ghana.
english: Sawyerr was born on 1 July 1964 and hails from Agona Kwanyako in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Sawyerr anɛ kpikpiʋŋ puak.
english: Sawyerr is a business woman.

kusaal: Nannana o anɛ Wadmaani tis Agona East Sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Central Region, Ghana la.
english: She is currently the Member of parliament for Agona East Constituency in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Sawyerr anɛ committee nid onɛ gɔt Na'akim Bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb nɛ malima yɛla nɛ Public Account committee nid; nɛ Sakur ken yɛla committee nid ya'as.
english: Sawyerr is a member of the Youth, Sports and Culture Committee; a member of the Public Accounts Committee; and also, a member of the Education Committee.

kusaal: Sawyerr mɔr sid nɛ biis anaasi.
english: Sawyerr is married with four children.

kusaal: O kennɛ Yesu Pʋ'ʋsʋm, Anglican Windɔɔgin.
english: She is a Christian and worships as an Anglican.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) la ni ya'asɛ, o da pʋdig diibi tis mɔɔm banɛ bɛ Agona East sʋ'ʋlim ba nɔlɔr saŋa la.
english: In 2017, she presented food items to Muslims in Agona East Constituency during the month of Ramadan.

kusaal: Sini la da yi paalʋ bԑ Un Certain Regard ni bԑ yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ anii Cannes Film Festival; Linԑ da an yiiga sini kanԑ ka ba maal Kenya ka yisi li di'ema la ni.
english: The film had its international premiere in the Un Certain Regard section at the 2018 Cannes Film Festival; it was the first Kenyan film to be screened at the festival.

kusaal: Kena sʋŋid o saam John Mwaura ka o kuosid sitͻͻ bԑ Nairobi ka o saam la lԑԑ nya'a tԑŋin la vootʋg na'am.
english: Kena helps her father John Mwaura run a small convenience store in Nairobi as he campaigns for a local election.

kusaal: Kena da nͻk o mԑŋi la'as nԑ Ziki, pʋ'asadir kanԑ an ba kpi'a, on anԑ onԑ nya'ad na'am nԑ Kena saam ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Peter Okemi.
english: Kena starts flirting with Ziki, a neighbourhood girl with colourful hair, who also happens to be the daughter of Peter Okemi, John's political rival.

kusaal: Ban da nyԑ kpԑmisig zin'ig sia maal sini la anԑ Uganda Monica Arac de Nyeko 2007 Caine Prize-sini giŋ kanԑ da buon "Jambula Tree" la ni.
english: The film is inspired by Ugandan Monica Arac de Nyeko's 2007 Caine Prize-winning short story "Jambula Tree".

kusaal: Sini la da yi paalʋ Dutch bԑ International Film Festival Rotterdam yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ awai ni, linԑ da paasid pisnaasi nԑ anii daan la.
english: The film made its Dutch premiere at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in 2019, during its 48th edition.

kusaal: Ba da yisi li paalʋ bԑ Dublin International Film Festival yʋʋm kan ni.
english: It also got screened at the Dublin International Film Festival in the same year.

kusaal: Mugatsia da di ya'an piini kanԑ an pʋakanԑ mͻr sini baŋiri gaad o taaba bԑ 2019 FESPACO bԑ Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso on da maal sini pa'al nidib bԑilim Kena tԑŋin la yela.
english: Mugatsia won the Best Actress award at the 2019 FESPACO in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso for her portrayal of Kena.

kusaal: Sini la da lԑn kԑ ka ba di ya'ani bԑ Seattle Queer Film Festival yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ awai ni.
english: The film won the Best Narrative feature at the Seattle Queer Film Festival in 2019.

kusaal: Li da lԑn kԑ ka ba di'e ya'an piini kanԑ buon Silver Hugo award bԑ Chicago International Film Festival.
english: It also won the Silver Hugo award at the Chicago International Film Festival.

kusaal: Rafiki anԑ yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ anii Kenya dim sini kanԑ ka onԑ gaad tuoni maal an Wanuri Kahiu.
english: Rafiki (Swahili for 'friend') is a 2018 Kenyan drama film directed by Wanuri Kahiu.

kusaal: Rafiki anԑ nͻŋilim sini kanԑ pa'an pʋ'ab ayi' banԑ buon Kena nԑ Ziki, la'an nԑ wada pʋʋgin pʋ bas suor ye pʋ'ab dim taaba bԑ Kenya la.
english: Rafiki is the story of romance that grows between two young women, Kena and Ziki, amidst family and political pressures around LGBTQ rights in Kenya.

kusaal: Kena nԑ Ziki kԑn zin'is si'eba wan wʋʋ nid nԑ o pʋ'a nԑ, ka miilim taaba hali, ka lԑԑ kʋ nyaŋi pa'ali ba nͻŋilim la paalʋ nii, bͻzugͻ, wada pʋ siak ye pʋ'ab di pʋ'ab bԑ Kenya tԑŋinԑ.
english: Kena and Ziki have a number of romantic dates, and quickly become very close, but there are tensions about displaying their affection in public because homosexuality is illegal in Kenya.

kusaal: Sini la ka ba pʋd "Rafiki" (li gbin anԑ "zua" anԑ Swahili buudi pian'ad) la yinԑ ban pʋ siakid ye pʋ'a kʋl o pʋ'a tiraan bԑԑ daʋ dii o daʋ tiraan la zug, ka li tͻi nԑ sͻ' na yel o sabua nwana ka ba babayi' la wʋsa an pʋ'ab bԑԑ dab, linzug ka ba yet nidib ye ba zua.
english: The film's title "Rafiki" (meaning "friend" in Swahili) was chosen, because due to homophobia in society, partners in a same-sex relationship often need to introduce their partner as a "friend", even if they are more than a friend.

kusaal: Ban nyԑ taaba ka maan sʋmmalisim la ka sini la naae: yʋma si'em nya'aŋ ka ba nan kpԑlim nͻŋ taaba.
english: The film ends just as they are reunited: after all these years their love has not died.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ras Mubarak bɛnɛ tamal teŋ kanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlʋmin la amaa ka o yit Satani linɛ bɛ kumbungu distrik teŋ kanɛ ka o saam yaaŋ da an na'atita'ar la ni na.
english: Ras Mubarak was born in Tamale, in the Northern Region of Ghana but hails from Satani, in the Kumbungu district where his great-grandfather was the Paramount Chief.

kusaal: O mɔr labaya tʋʋma Diploma kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit London labaya sakur la ni yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni, nɛ International Development Studies Post Graduate Diploma kasɛta gbaʋŋ (NIBS) yit Uniersity of Oslo Norway School la ni yʋma 2010 ni, nɛ Business Administration Post Graduate kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit Nobel International Business School kanɛ bɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: He holds a Diploma in Journalism from the London School of Journalism in the year 2009 and Post Graduate Diploma(NIBS) in International Development Studies from the University of Oslo Norway in the year 2010, and a Post Graduate Certificate in Business Administration from the Nobel International Business School in Accra.

kusaal: Ras Mubarak da zi'en ma'asim tiig nɔba zug nyi'a ye ba gaŋ o ka o na nyaŋi mɔr suor nyi'a Alekuma North wadmaan kʋk la yʋma 2011 la ni.
english: Ras Mubarak contested for the National Democratic Congress (Ghana) parliamentary nomination for Ablekuma North in 2011.

kusaal: Ka o lɛn keŋ tuon nyi'a ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nidib banɛ ye ba zi'en nyi'a kʋk na'am la vɔɔdʋg bɛ kumbungu yʋma 2015 la ni.
english: He then proceeded to contest for the NDC Parliamentary slot in Kumbungu in 2015.

kusaal: O da lɛn di ya'as ka zi'en nyi'a kumbungu kanɛ bɛ Northern Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm nwa ni la wadmaan kʋk la yʋma 2016 vɔɔdʋg tita'ar la ni.
english: He again won and contested for the Member of Parliament of Kumbungu (Ghana parliament constituency) in the Northern Region of Ghana for the 2016 Ghanaian general Election.

kusaal: O da di kumbungu linɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlʋmin la wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ anii nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi (18,777 votes) ka li an pisnu nɛ anu nɛ du'alʋg atan' kɔbʋg pʋdʋgir pʋʋgin (55.03%).
english: He won the parliamentary seat of Kumbungu constituency in the Northern Region of Ghana with 18, 777 votes of the total votes representing 55.

kusaal: Ras Mubarak da nyi'a ma'asim tiig coŋgerɛs kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2019 la amaa ka kɔ'ɔŋ vɔɔtʋg la ka Hamza Adam di.
english: Ras Mubarak contested for the 2019 National Democratic Congress primaries but lost the election to Hamza Adam.

kusaal: Ras Mubarak Anɛ mɔr, o mɔr nɛ biis atan'
english: Ras Mubarak is a Muslim.

kusaal: Tigir la daa maal banɛ bɛ national team la, the Black Steads, onɛ an teŋ la yiiga yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi.
english: The club formed the core of the national team, the Black Stars, in its early years.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da mɔr bɔɔdim ye o la'as Africa ka da gɔs ka o na nyaŋi dɔl football di'ema ni.
english: Kwame Nkrumah had an ambition to unite Africa and believed football could be used as a tool.

kusaal: O da gaŋ Ohene Djan yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisyuobʋ, Mɔraʋg nwadig, pin'ilig dabisir (1 July 1960) ka o an Director of Sports.
english: He appointed Ohene Djan on 1 July 1960 as the Director of Sports.

kusaal: O da kpɛmis Ohene Djan ye o maalim football club linɛ ka di yʋ'ʋr da buon Osagyefo's Own Club.
english: He encouraged Ohene Djan to form the football club which was also known as Osagyefo's Own Club.

kusaal: Ba si'eba da anɛ Baba Yara nɛ Dogo Moro banɛ da bɛ Asante Kotoko, Addo Odametey nɛ Doddo Ankrah banɛ da yit Hearts of Oak.
english: Notable among them was Baba Yara and Dogo Moro from Asante Kotoko, Addo Odametey and Doddo Ankrah from Hearts of Oak.

kusaal: Ba da di ba Ghana Premier League ya'an nɔɔr yinnɛ bɛ 1962/63 season.
english: The team won its only Ghana Premier League title in the 1962/63 season.

kusaal: Ba da nwɛn'ɛ tituaa bɛ Ghanaian FA Cup ni gaad league la ni, ka da di ya'an nɔɔra anaasi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nam saŋa la (1960s), lin pa'al ye yʋʋm piiga kan pʋʋgin ba da nyɛ zugsʋŋ.
english: The team were more successful in the Ghanaian FA Cup than the league, winning four consecutive tournaments in the 1960s, which proved to be a great decade for the club.

kusaal: Republikan da di FA Cup yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu ni la (1965) da an sankanɛ ka ba da nwɛn'ɛ ba naar di'ema, bɔzugɔ, FA Cup da kae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ la nii (1966), yʋʋmkan ka club la yi di'ema pʋʋgin.
english: Republikan's last FA Cup win in 1965 was also their last participation in the tournament, as there was no FA Cup in 1966, the year the club dissolved.

kusaal: Edward Jonah Aggrey-Fynn, onɛ ka ba da gaŋ o ka o an captain tis Real Republikans da paas team la ni 1950s/early 1960s la, da kɛŋ tuoni kilim captain tis Ghana national football team on da pa'al o baŋir club la ni la.
english: Edward Jonah Aggrey-Fynn, who was appointed captain of Real Republikans upon signing for the team in the late 1950s/early 1960s, went on to captain the Ghana national football team after showing great ability and leadership skills at club level.

kusaal: Ba mɛ da mɔ bɛ CAF Champions League, ban da nyaŋi paae semi-final di'ema la pʋʋgin yʋʋm 1964/65 ni la.
english: The club also found success in the CAF Champions League, reaching the semi-final of the competition in 1964/65.

kusaal: Amaa ba da nyaŋi ba 2–1, ka banɛ da di ba la an Oryx Douala banɛ yit Cameroon yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu, yʋʋmpaal nwadig, dabpistan' nɛ yinnɛ daar (31 January 1965) nidib tusa pisnu (50,000) tuoni bɛ Accra Stadium ka linzug ka ba da pʋ nyaŋi paas di'ema la pʋʋgin paae naarɛ.
english: However, they were beaten 2–1 by opponents Oryx Douala from Cameroon on 31 January 1965 in front of 50,000 at the Accra Stadium and therefore did not reach the final.

kusaal: Oryx Douala went da kɛŋ tuoni di ya'an ban da nwɛn'ɛ nɛ Stade Malien banɛ yit Mali la.
english: Oryx Douala went on to win the final against Stade Malien of Mali.

kusaal: Real Republikans da nwɛn'ɛ gɛɛs nɛ Real Madrid Kwame Nkrumah da kaanbi buoli ba dɔlis Ohene Djan sa'an Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Real Republikans played against Real Madrid after they were invited by Kwame Nkrumah through Ohene Djan in Ghana.

kusaal: Di'ema la da naae nɛ 3–3 zinzɛma bɛ Accra Sports Stadium.
english: The game ended with a 3–3 draw at the Accra Sports Stadium.

kusaal: Ba da di Great Ashanti nɛ goals nam atan' bɛ Kumasi ka da nyaŋi di Ghana FA Cup.
english: They defeated Great Ashanti by 3 goals to nil in Kumasi to win the Ghana FA Cup.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' , Dɔnwalig nwadig, daba naasi daar (4 March 1963), team la da paam sapʋ'at nɛ motor bɛ Kpeve, ban da lɛbid Accra la, ban da nwɛn'ɛ league match ban nɛ Volta Heroes n Kpandu la.
english: On 4 March 1963, the team had a motor accident which occurred at Kpeve, when they returning to Accra after playing a league match against Volta Heroes at Kpandu.

kusaal: Ba da kad team la President Kwame Nkrumah da yi na'am kug zugi dɔlis sooginam nu'usin la.
english: The team was disbanded after President Kwame Nkrumah and his government were overthrown by coup d'état.

kusaal: Di mɔr Ghana gbauŋ sɔb bɛdegʋ ka Fa Cup di ya'an la, nɛ anaasi.
english: It holds Ghana's record for the most consecutive FA Cup wins, four.

kusaal: Bɔɔdim nɛ gban'ar kanɛ ka Nkrumah da mɔri tis football la zug ka o da pin'il football club la.
english: The passion and belief Nkrumah had in football led to the formation of the football club.

kusaal: Ba da ye team la nidib anɛ tɛŋ la nidibi da la'as taaba.
english: It was claimed the team was made up of talented local boys who were assembled together.

kusaal: Nwa' an club la da di ya'an si'a ti paae zina, nɛ ban da kɛna gaad yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1966) yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ ka ba da di ya'an la.
english: This remains the club's only title to date, as they were dissolved in 1966 at the height of their success.

kusaal: Real Republikans da anɛ club yinnɛ kanɛ ka Ghana football dim da mi' li yela ban da pin'il sankanɛ ka league la mɛ da pin'il Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka zabir si'a da kɛna ka teams nama ayuobʋ yi anii la pʋʋgin da zan'as ye ba pa'ali ba sʋnfi san'am si'em nɛ di'ema la kpɛɛm la.
english: Real Republikans were once seen as a model club for the rest of Ghanaian football as they were established at a time when the first edition of a league system in Ghana resulted in chaos and ended with 6 of the 8 teams in the league boycotting in protest at the federation's leader.

kusaal: Baba Yara kanɛ ka ba da ye onɛ an nwɛn'ɛ-nwɛn'ɛd baŋir sɔb Ghana la, da paam sapʋ'at ka li da sa'am o tʋʋma o dasamnim on da an yʋma pisi nɛ ayuobʋ saŋa.
english: Baba Yara who was claimed to be one of the glamorous footballer of all times in Ghana, got seriously injured which led to his career curtailed in his prime at the age of 26.

kusaal: Sooginam gɔmɛna kanɛ da kɛna la da kad Real Republikans ka Ghanaian football di'ema da lɛb nya'aŋ.
english: The new military regime disbanded Real Republikans and Ghanaian football went into a relative period of decline.

kusaal: Di'emkaŋa da bɛnɛ Mɔtul nwadig la dabpiinɛ wai daar (19 August).
english: The game was played on 19 August.

kusaal: Real Tamale United, RTU giŋa,anɛ football club kanɛ bɛ Tamale, Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Real Tamale United, often abbreviated as RTU, is a football club based in Tamale, Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da lɛbis team la second tier Division One League yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan la ni (2013).
english: The team was relegated to the second tier Division One League in 2013.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) la ni, RTU da paam tuon keni lɛn lɛb first tier Ghana Premier League ban da di Unity FC 2 - 0 Division One League Season la naar daar la.
english: In 2021, RTU sealed promotion back to the first tier Ghana Premier League after beating Unity FC 2 - 0 on the last day of the Division One League Season.

kusaal: Ba yin stadium anɛ dinɛ nɔkid nidib tusa pisi nɛ yinne (21,000-Seater Capacity) Aliu Mahama Sports Stadium bɛ Tamale.
english: Their home stadium is 21,000 Seater Capacity Aliu Mahama Sports Stadium in Tamale.

kusaal: Ba da tiaki yi zin'ikanɛ ka ba da bɛ la, Kaladan Park yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) African Cup of Nations la nya'aŋ.
english: They relocated to their current grounds from the Kaladan Park after the 2008 African Cup of Nations.

kusaal: Yiiga kʋkdaan Alhaji Adam.H (Progress) da pin'il kilab la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (1976) la ni.
english: The club was founded in 1976 by the first chairman Alhaji Adam.H (Progress).

kusaal: Real Tamale United mɔr dataadʋg nɛ Steadfast FC, Tamale City FC.
english: Real Tamale United has rivalries with Steadfast FC and Tamale City FC.

kusaal: Kilab nama atan la wʋsa bɛnɛ Tamale, Ghana, dinzug ka ba mɔr nyɛlʋg nɛ dataadʋg dinɛ kpi'em hali nɛ taaba.
english: All three clubs are located in Tamale, Ghana, causing rivalries amongst one another.

kusaal: Yʋʋm 2019 ni la, labaar da yina ye Red Bull Music Academy nɛ Red Bull Radio la wʋsa ba gu'onɛ bas nwadis piig la ni li dapistan' daar, Red Bull dimi da naal nɔɔr nɛ Yadastar company kanɛ gɔsidi ba wʋsa la.
english: In August 2014 Red Bull closed the academy and the club and it was merged with Feyenoord Academy to West African Football Academy.

english: The Regent University College of Science and Technology (often referred to as Regent-Ghana) is located in Accra, Ghana.
