kusaal: Reggie Tsiboe (ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu, nwadis awai dabisa ayɔpɔi daar, 7 September 1950) o anɛ Ghanaian-British di'ema sɔb, wa'awa'ad, ka len an yʋʋm-yʋʋmi tis disco group Boney M. Lin yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yi paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayʋobʋ (1982 nɛ1986 tɛnsʋk) ka len yʋɔlim nya'aŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai nɛ tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai tɛnsʋk (1989 nɛ 1990 tɛnsʋk).
english: Reggie Tsiboe (born 7 September 1950) is a Ghanaian-British entertainer, dancer and one of the singers of the disco group Boney M. between 1982 and 1986 and later between 1989 and 1990.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi saŋa la (1970s), Tsiboe da paas la'asig kanɛ an Sugarcane la ka o yʋ'ʋr da yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ nii (1978) nɛ Bobby Bloom's "Montego Bay" la.
english: During the 1970s, Tsiboe was a member of the group Sugarcane who had a 1978 hit with Bobby Bloom's "Montego Bay".

kusaal: La'asig nwa' da paas Linda Taylor ba sʋʋgin.
english: The group also included Linda Taylor in its line up.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinnɛ (1981), on da la'as o mɛŋ nɛ Boney M la, Tsiboe da di'e nɛ wa'awa'ad Bobby Farrell nɔbir, amaa, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi ni (1984), Farrell da lɛb na ka ba yʋ'ʋn an bababa yiŋa.
english: In 1981, having joined Boney M., Tsiboe originally replaced the dancer Bobby Farrell, but in 1984 Farrell rejoined the group and they became a quintet.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii ne ayuobʋ (1986), yʋma piiga nya'aŋ ka ba bak nɛ taaba, amaa yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai la (1989), Boney M., Liz Mitchell nɛ Tsiboe da la'as taaba ya'as la, ba da pʋdi ba tʋʋma yʋ'ʋr ye Boney M. Ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai ni (1990) ka Frank Farian da gaad tuon ka ba yis yʋʋma paalig na ka li buon "Stories", nwadis bi'ela nya'aŋ ka ba len bak taaba ya'as.
english: In 1986, the original band split after 10 successful years, but in 1989 after an unexpected reunion of Boney M., Liz Mitchell and Tsiboe formed a new version of Boney M. and in 1990 released with the help of the producer Frank Farian the single "Stories" as Farian's response to another Boney M. lineup consisting of Bobby Farrell, Marcia Barrett, Maizie Williams, and Madeline Davis releasing the single "Everybody Wants To Dance Like Josephine Baker" which was an unauthorized release and legally withdrawn by Farian.

kusaal: Tsiboe da paasi maal Boney M. Albums nam atan' ni: Ten Thousand Lightyears (1984), Kalimba de Luna - 16 Happy Songs (1984) nɛ Eye Dance (1985) ka yʋm buninya yʋʋma nɛ o taaba, ka ba bakir nya'aŋ la ka yʋʋm kan nyaan yina Boney M. Christmas album zʋŋir saŋa, The 20 Greatest Christmas Songs da anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ ni (1986).
english: Tsiboe appeared on the last three Boney M. albums: Ten Thousand Lightyears (1984), Kalimba de Luna - 16 Happy Songs (1984) and Eye Dance (1985) and also recorded Christmas songs with the group, which were internationally released only after the split of the band on the new Boney M. Christmas album, The 20 Greatest Christmas Songs in 1986.

kusaal: Reggie da gaad tuoni yʋʋm yʋʋma bɛdigʋ Boney M. yʋʋma nam ni, ka ba si'eba an: "Kalimba de Luna", "Happy Song", "Going Back West", "My Chérie Amour", "Young, Free and Single", "Bang Bang Lulu", "Dreadlock Holiday", "Barbarella Fortuneteller", "Mother and Child Reunion" nɛ burinya yʋʋma kanɛ an "Joy to the World", "Oh Christmas Tree", "The First Noël" nɛ "Auld Lang Syne".
english: Reggie sang the main vocals on a number of Boney M. songs, including "Kalimba de Luna", "Happy Song", "Going Back West", "My Chérie Amour", "Young, Free and Single", "Bang Bang Lulu", "Dreadlock Holiday", "Barbarella Fortuneteller", "Mother and Child Reunion" and the Christmas songs "Joy to the World", "Oh Christmas Tree", "The First Noël" and "Auld Lang Syne".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ, nwadis awai, dabpisi nɛ yinne daar (21 September 2006), Tsiboe nɛ o taaba banɛ yʋmmidi gat tuon, Boney M., Liz Mitchell nɛ Marcia Barrett, da anɛ saam banɛ an girima dimi bɛ London ban da zʋŋid yʋʋma, Daddy Cool, linɛ da paasi ba la'asig la pʋʋgin la.
english: On 21 September 2006, Tsiboe and the two other lead singers of Boney M., Liz Mitchell and Marcia Barrett, were guests in London at the premiere of the musical Daddy Cool, which is based on the music of the group.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ la'as nɛ nimbama la, o da anɛ one an sini maan baŋir sɔb Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Before he joined the group he was a movie star in Ghana.

kusaal: Sini yinne kanɛ da kɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr yi anɛ Love Brewed in an African Pot.
english: One of the movies that gained him popularity was the film Love Brewed in the African Pot.

kusaal: O da lɛb sini maalig ni, o da paasi maal sini UK sini maanib ni, ka sini yinne an Doctor Who.
english: He has also starred in a few UK TV productions including Doctor Who.

kusaal: Reginald Yates (ba dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ tan', nwadis anu, dabpistan' nɛ yinne, 31 May 1983) anɛ labadi'ei bɛ British television ni, ka len an walis DJ, one sɔbid gbana, nɛ one maan sini, o tʋm tʋʋm kaŋa ka da paae yʋʋm pistan'.
english: Reginald Yates (born 31 May 1983) is a British television presenter, actor, writer and director with a career spanning three decades on screen as an actor, television presenter and radio DJ.

kusaal: Yates di'em Leo Jones di'ema bɛ sini kanɛ buon Doctor Who la mɛ tʋm BBC walis nɛ TV ni–o maal di'ema bɛdigʋ BBC Radio 1 ka li wa'ae nɛ yʋʋm piiga nwana, ka mɛ len gɔs di'ema kanɛ an yʋʋma an BBC One singing show The Voice UK, o paas banɛ pin'ili li ka tʋmi li tʋʋma yʋʋma yi nɛ Holly Willoughby.
english: Yates played Leo Jones in Doctor Who and has worked at the BBC in radio and television–presenting various shows for BBC Radio 1 for a decade as well as hosting the BBC One singing show The Voice UK, hosting the first two series with Holly Willoughby.

kusaal: Yates da paasi gɔs nintaŋ di'em kanɛ buon prime-time BBC One game show Prized Apart, on nɛ Emma Willis, ka lɛn paas ITV2 reality show ka ba buon Release the Hounds la, lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan' paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi (2013 paae 2017) ka mɛ lɛn paas di'em kanɛ an BBC Three documentary series, ka ba buon Reggie Yates' Extreme Russia, Extreme South Africa nɛ Extreme UK ka ba nɔk o kʋkɔri maal CBeebies animated cartoon series linɛ ka ba buon Rastamouse la.
english: Yates co-presented the prime-time BBC One game show Prized Apart, alongside Emma Willis, the ITV2 reality show Release the Hounds from 2013 until 2017 and was also the presenter of the BBC Three documentary series Reggie Yates' Extreme Russia, Extreme South Africa and Extreme UK as well as featuring as lead voice actor for the CBeebies animated cartoon series Rastamouse.

kusaal: Yates' dʋ'adib, Felicia Asante nɛ Reginald "Jojo" Yates, ba da dʋ'a ba nɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim; Amaa, o yaab, o saam saam one buon Harry da anɛ English accountant, George Yates biig, one tʋm salima tʋʋma.
english: Yates' parents, Felicia Asante and Reginald "Jojo" Yates, were both born in Ghana; however, his paternal grandfather Harry was the son of an English accountant, George Yates, who worked in the gold mining industry.

kusaal: Harry Yates' ma Dorothy mɛ da paas nɛ Ghana's Euro-African community: o saam da anɛ British sankpan'asnam gɔmɛna, Augustus George Lloyd, ka o ma Sarah da an Fante buudi, one da an kpaad nɛ kpikpinkpiŋi bɛ Dixcove, Ghana.
english: Harry Yates' mother Dorothy was also a member of Ghana's Euro-African community: her father was a British colonial administrator, Augustus George Lloyd, while her mother Sarah was an ethnic Fante, who worked as a farmer and trader in Dixcove, Ghana.

kusaal: Yates nɔbig nɛ North London, ka kɛŋ sakuri bɛ Central Foundation Boys' School linɛ bɛ Cowper Street, Islington.
english: Yates grew up in North London, where he attended Central Foundation Boys' School in Cowper Street, Islington.

kusaal: Yates da yi television ni yiiga nɛ Desmond's on da an yʋma nii la.
english: Yates made his first television appearance in Desmond's at the age of eight.

kusaal: O da yi Disney Club, an Robbie.
english: He also appeared in Disney Club, as Robbie.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ nii (1998), Yates da anɛ labadi'es kanɛ ka ba da kaanbi buol o bɛ Diggit nɛ CITV ka ba buon o anina ye Robbie.
english: In 1998, Yates appeared as a guest presenter on Diggit on CITV also under the name Robbie.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayi (2002), o da pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Carl Fenton di'em biis di'ema dinɛ buon Grange Hill la.
english: In 2002, he played Carl Fenton in the popular children's series Grange Hill.

kusaal: Lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayi paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anaasi (2002 to 2004), one da tisid lasid daar labaya dinɛ ka ba da pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Smile la, ka mɛ paasi maal Top of the Pops on nɛ o tiraan kanɛ maal Smile ka ba buon o Fearne Cotton la, nɛ ban ti yisi li paalʋ BBC Two ni yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ, nwadis ayɔpɔi, dabis pistan' daar (30 July 2006).
english: From 2002 to 2004, he presented the Sunday morning programme Smile, and then went on to present Top of the Pops with former Smile co-host Fearne Cotton before the final episode broadcast on BBC Two on 30 July 2006.

kusaal: O mɛ paasi maal The Crust nɛ Dance Factory nɛ o BBC Radio 1 di'ema.
english: He also created and starred in the series The Crust and presented Dance Factory and his own radio show on BBC Radio 1.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ anu (2005) la ni, Yates da paas BBC yʋʋma nya'ab Comic Relief Does Fame Academy paas nɛ Comic Relief, anina ka o da naae nidib anaasi zin'igin.
english: In 2005, Yates appeared in the BBC singing contest Comic Relief Does Fame Academy in aid of Comic Relief, finishing in fourth place.

kusaal: Di'ema la pʋʋgin, yʋʋma banɛ ka o da yʋʋm si'eba anɛ "Boombastic", "You're The First, The Last, My Everything", "It Ain't Over Til It's Over", "U Can't Touch This" nɛ "This Old Heart of Mine (Is Weak for You)".
english: On the show, his songs included "Boombastic", "You're The First, The Last, My Everything", "It Ain't Over Til It's Over", "U Can't Touch This" and "This Old Heart of Mine (Is Weak for You)".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ, nwadis ata', dabpiiga daar (10 March 2006) la, Yates da yi Stars in Fast Cars di'ema ni na nyaŋi nyan'a paae di'ema la laar, ka di ya'an ka bas Elton Welsby nɛ Ben Fogle.
english: On 10 March 2006, Yates appeared on Stars in Fast Cars and won his heat to get into the final, beating Elton Welsby and Ben Fogle in the last round.

kusaal: Yates da an labadi'esi tis Mighty Truck of Stuff nɛ Only in America on nɛ Fearne Cotton bɛ CBBC nɛ di'ema yinne kanɛ bɛ BBC Radio 1.
english: Yates presented Mighty Truck of Stuff and Only in America with Fearne Cotton on CBBC as well as a programme on BBC Radio 1.

kusaal: Banɛ da gɔsid bɛʋgin di'ema asibid daar nɛ alasid daar, da di'ed nɛ yit JK and Joel.
english: They presented a breakfast show on Saturday and Sunday mornings, taking over from JK and Joel.

kusaal: Ba da gaad tuonɛ maal The Radio 1 Chart Show lin da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi, nwadis piiga, dabpiinɛ naasi ti paae alasid daar, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ awai, nwadis awai la, dabpisi (14 October 2007 paae Sunday 20 September 2009).
english: The duo then went on to present The Radio 1 Chart Show starting on 14 October 2007 until Sunday 20 September 2009.

kusaal: Linɛ lɛn paas chart show la, Yates da gaad tuoni gɔs di'em kanɛ an asibid daar di'ema, ka ba buon The Radio 1 Request Show, anina ka banɛ kɛlisid na nyaŋi sɔb labaari tɔlim bɛ buol nɛ fooni pa'al ye ba nwɛ'ɛ yʋ'ʋm kanɛ ka ba bɔɔd.
english: In addition to the chart show, Yates also presented a request show on Saturday afternoons, known as The Radio 1 Request Show, where listeners could send in a text or phone in to request a song.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yi, nwadis anaasi la (April 2012), ba da tis labaar ye Yates na naae di'em kan ka gaad tuoni gɔs The Official Chart.
english: In April 2012, it was announced that Yates would finish the request show and continue with only The Official Chart.

kusaal: O da tis labaar yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yi, nwadis piinɛ yinne (November 2012) ye o na yi BBC Radio 1, ka di'em kanɛ ka o da di'em naarin anɛ yʋʋm kan, naar nwadig la, dabpisi ne atan' (23 December).
english: He announced in November 2012 that he would leave BBC Radio 1, and his last show aired on 23 December that year.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2006), Yates da yi Reality TV Special di'em kane an The Weakest Link ka vootʋ yis nɔɔr anaasi ni.
english: In 2006, Yates appeared on a Reality TV Special of The Weakest Link and was voted off in the fourth round.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007), Yates da paas science-fiction series linɛ paas atan', Doctor Who, ka ba buon o Leo Jones anina, Tenth Doctor dɔlim taa Martha.
english: In 2007, Yates appeared in the third series of revived science-fiction series Doctor Who as Leo Jones, brother of the Tenth Doctor's companion Martha.

kusaal: Yates da paasi di'em series 1 of Escape from Scorpion Island, on nɛ o labadi'es tiraan Caroline Flack bɛ BBC 1 dabisa tan' kɛŋ paae pisi nɛ yinne, nwadis awai la ni, yʋʋm tusay nɛ ayɔpɔi la (3 and 21 September 2007).
english: Yates also presented series 1 of Escape from Scorpion Island with co-presenter Caroline Flack on BBC 1 between 3 and 21 September 2007.

kusaal: O da yina bɛ Dizzee Rascal yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi (2007) nɛ "Flex" ka paasi an sariakati bɛ parody TV show linɛ buon "Flex Factor" la.
english: He also appeared on Dizzee Rascal's 2007 single "Flex" music video as one of the judges in a parody TV show called "Flex Factor".

kusaal: Yates da paasi gɔs MOBO Awards yʋʋm tusayi nɛ wai (2009) la on nɛ Keri Hilson bɛ SECC, Glasgow.
english: Yates co-hosted the MOBO Awards 2009 with Keri Hilson at the SECC, Glasgow.

kusaal: O mɛ maal di'em banɛ an Glastonbury, Reading nɛ T in the Park la sini tis BBC Three, ka buos nimbanɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋr yi wʋʋ Estelle nɛ 50 Cent buosa tis MTV specials.
english: He has also presented live coverage of the Glastonbury, Reading and T in the Park music festivals for BBC Three, and interviewed stars such as Estelle and 50 Cent for MTV specials.

kusaal: Yates da yi sini kanɛ buon Jack Osbourne's Celebrity Adrenaline Junkie la ni na bi'ela.
english: Yates made a cameo appearance in Jack Osbourne's Celebrity Adrenaline Junkie.

kusaal: Yates da paas Family Guy di'ema kanɛ bɛ BBC Three ni la, ka paas nɛ banɛ maal di'ema kan la nidib pisi ni.
english: Yates appeared in a special Family Guy episode on BBC Three, counting down the top 20 characters of the show as part of a special Family Guy weekend.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinne la (2011), Yates da dɔl one gaad sini la tuon, Rastamouse, bɛ CBeebies di'em kanɛ buon Rastamouse la.
english: In 2011, Yates voiced the main character, Rastamouse, in the CBeebies television show Rastamouse.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yinne, nwadis atan' ni (March 2011), o da paaas nɛ Lenny Henry, Angela Rippon, nɛ Samantha Womack ka ba maal sini ieed sʋŋiri bɛ BBC ye ba tis Comic Relief kanɛ buon Rich, Famous and in the Slums, sankan ka ba da tʋm nimbanɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋr yi anaasi ka ba kɛŋ Kibera linɛ Kenya, Africa sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: In March 2011, he appeared with Lenny Henry, Angela Rippon, and Samantha Womack in the BBC fundraising documentary for Comic Relief called Rich, Famous and in the Slums, where the four celebrities were sent to Kibera in Kenya, Africa's largest slum.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi ne piinɛ yinne, nwadis piiga ni (October 2011), Yates da paas sini kanɛ ka Arjun Rose maal, UK sʋ'ʋlim ka ba buon Demons Never Die la ni, ka ba da buon o anina ye Officer Mason.
english: In October 2011, Yates starred in Arjun Rose's UK slasher Demons Never Die as Officer Mason.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛyi la (2012), BBC Three dim di'em kanɛ an Criminal Britain Season la ni, Yates da wɛlisi pa'al dinɛ an dabi'em, sʋnpɛɛn nɛ zaba kanɛ bɛ dasam nɛ pʋ'asada la'asidi maan.
english: In 2012, as part of BBC Three's Criminal Britain Season, Yates explored the culture of fear, anger and violence that drives the dangerous world of teen gangs.

kusaal: Di'ema la yʋ'ʋr anɛ, Reggie Yates: Teen Gangs, da kɛ ka o da sɔnsid nɛ dasam nɛ pʋ'asada la'asig kpɛɛmnam lin niŋ si'em ka ba paasid la'as ban ni.
english: The show, Reggie Yates: Teen Gangs, involved him speaking to current and former gang members to find out why and how teens get into gangs.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛyi la ni (2012) nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan' la ni (2013), Yates da gaad tuonɛ gɔs BBC One yʋʋma di'ema kanɛ buon The Voice UK, on nɛ one da gaad tuon yʋʋma ayi pʋʋgin anɛ Holly Willoughby.
english: In 2012 and 2013, Yates hosted the BBC One singing show The Voice UK, hosting the first two series with Holly Willoughby.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan' la (2013), Yates da tʋ' sur nɛ kɛŋ South Africa ye o maal sini kanɛ buon Reggie Yates' Extreme South Africa: White Slums, ka nidib da kɛlisi li yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ naasi la (2014) bɛ BBC Three.
english: 2013 saw Yates travel to South Africa to shoot a series, Reggie Yates' Extreme South Africa: White Slums, which aired in Spring 2014 on BBC Three.

kusaal: Li da an sʋm ka linzug ka o da lɛm maal linɛ buon Reggie Yates' Extreme Russia yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu, nwadis anaasi ni la (April 2015) tis BBC Three.
english: It was successful enough for Yates to return with Reggie Yates' Extreme Russia in April 2015 for BBC Three.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan' (2013), o sini kanɛ ka o da maal yiiga ka li yʋ'ʋr buon Patriarch la da yi Channel 4 na ka li anɛ ban gban'e ye ba maal sini ginma la, ka len maal sini kanɛ ti'al ayi la ka li yʋ'ʋr buon Date Night, ka banɛ paas an Daniel Kaluuya nɛ Tony Way, linɛ da di ya'an piini kanɛ buon "Best UK Short Film" linɛ bɛ London Independent Film Festival ni la.
english: In 2013, his first short film Patriarch aired on Channel 4 as part of their "Random Acts" season and he has just completed his second short called Date Night, starring Daniel Kaluuya and Tony Way, which won "Best UK Short Film" at the London Independent Film Festival.

kusaal: Matt Edmondson da di'e o nɔbir yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piine yɔpɔi ni (2017).
english: He was replaced by Matt Edmondson in 2017.

kusaal: Yates da paas di'em kanɛ an Who Do You Think You Are?, ka ba da wʋmi li yela yiiga yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piine naasi, nwadis awai, dabpisi nɛ anu daar la (25 September 2014), anina ka o da kɛŋ Ghana ye o baŋ o zak dim.
english: Yates appeared in an episode of Who Do You Think You Are?, first aired on 25 September 2014, for which he travelled to Ghana to trace his family history.

kusaal: Yates nɛ Emma Willis da gaad di'em kanɛ an sibid daar di'ema, Saturday-night game show Prized Apart bɛ BBC One yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piine nu la (2015).
english: Yates, along with Emma Willis presented the Saturday-night game show Prized Apart on BBC One in 2015.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayuobʋ la (2016), Yates da di'e piini ye one an labadi'es kanɛ gaad o taaba on gaad tuoni gɔs di'em kanɛ an Extreme Russia la yela, bɛ Royal Television Society Awards ka len di'e piini kanɛ an Best Multi-channel Programme bɛ Broadcast Awards.
english: In 2016, Yates was awarded Best Presenter for his critically acclaimed series Extreme Russia at the Royal Television Society Awards and Best Multi-channel Programme at the Broadcast Awards.

kusaal: On da kɛn tuoni maan o sini la, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ ni la (2016) Yates di'em kanɛ bɛ BBC ka ba buon The Insider la da kɛ ka o kpɛn' pʋlʋs nʋ'ʋsin bɛ Texas ka mɛ lɛn paas Unit 27 of the 56th Infantry Battalion linɛ bɛ Acapulco ni la ye o an soogia kanɛ zabidi tisid o tɛŋ.
english: Continuing his documentarian journey, in 2016 Yates's BBC Three series The Insider saw the presenter spend time behind bars in Texas and join Unit 27 of the 56th Infantry Battalion in Acapulco to live the life of an ordinary soldier fighting on the front line of the brutal war against the country's powerful and violent drug cartels.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nii (2018) ni, ba da maal Yates nɛ sariakati tis Koestler Trust di'em kanɛ an I'm Still Here, bɛ Southbank Centre, London, ka lin anɛ banɛ bɛ sarɛga ni, nɛ banɛ naani anina yi, ye ba pa'ali ba nu'ug tʋʋma.
english: In 2018, Yates was the themed category judge for Koestler Trust's I'm Still Here at the Southbank Centre, London, an exhibition of art works by prisoners, detainees and ex-offenders.

kusaal: Yates yʋ'ʋr paas Powerlist, ka li pa'al ye o paas nimbanɛ nyaŋi ti'aki ba taaba bɛ UK ka yinɛ African/African-Caribbean sʋ'ʋlim, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ wai (2019), yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi (2020) nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) kanl.
english: Yates has also been listed in the Powerlist, as one of the most influential people in the UK from African/African-Caribbean descent, most recently making the 2019, 2020 and 2021 editions.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi (2020), Yates television sini kanɛ buon Make Me Famous da yi BBC Three ni na.
english: In 2020, Yates' television film Make Me Famous premiered on BBC Three.

kusaal: Sini la anɛ siya ka ba maan la'ad ka ba da maali li yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai saŋa (1990s) bɛ London, ka nidib da pian'a li yela sʋ'ʋŋa.
english: The film, a comedy-drama set in 1990s London, received largely favourable reviews from critics.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi ni (2017), BBC da mugusi ba mɛŋi nwɛ'ɛ nu'ug tis Yates (nɛ tʋmtʋmnib banɛ maan sini, Sundog Pictures) sini kanɛ ka ba maal Australia tɛŋin ka ba buon Hidden Australia: Black in the Outback la yela, Ba da maali li nɛ Wilcannia, New South Wales.
english: In 2017, the BBC was forced to apologise for a Yates (and independent production company, Sundog Pictures) piece on Australia's Indigenous communities called Hidden Australia: Black in the Outback, filmed in Wilcannia, New South Wales.

kusaal: Ba mɔri ba mɛŋ nyali, ba pʋ nɔki ba mɛŋi kɛŋ kɛ ka Jewish nid kanɛ yit west London an ba tuongatɛ, ba tɛŋ dim nɔɔ an ba tuongatib".
english: They're independent, they're not managed by some random fat Jewish guy from north west London, they're managed by their brethren".

kusaal: Community Security Trust dim nid, Dave Rich ka ye on pian' si'em la ka' sʋm, ka mɛ yel ye: "lababɛ'ɛd kae paae Yates pian'a tis nidib si'em ka li mɔr barigaŋ la".
english: His remarks were condemned by the Community Security Trust's Dave Rich who said: "Even worse than any offence is the message Yates gives his audience by reinforcing an anti-Semitic stereotype".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛwai (2019) la, on da bɛ anina maan o MTV television di'ema kanɛ buon Reggie Yates vs The World bɛ Derry, Northern Ireland la, ba da pa'al ye zaba bɛdigʋ da duoe bɛ tɛnpʋʋgin la ka li da dɔlis nɛ anina ka ba da ku Lyra McKee.
english: In 2019, when filming for his MTV television series Reggie Yates vs The World in Derry, Northern Ireland, it was claimed that tensions on the street were stoked by dissident Republicans "for the benefit of the film crew", resulting in a riot during which Lyra McKee was murdered.

kusaal: Detective Superintendent Jason Murphy one bɛ Police Service of Northern Ireland da yel ye nidib la yel si'el la ka' sidaa.
english: Detective Superintendent Jason Murphy of the Police Service of Northern Ireland said that those claims were untrue.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne la (2021), Yates da yis o yiiga sini kanɛ ka o da gaad tuoni gɔsi li yela ka mɛ lɛn sɔbi li yela ka ba buon Pirates la.
english: In 2021, Yates released his first feature film as writer/director, Pirates.

kusaal: O da yʋʋm "It Takes Two", on nɛ Edith Bowman, one da di ya'an di'ema nwa' pʋʋgin la.
english: He also sang a duet, "It Takes Two", with Edith Bowman, the eventual winner of the show.

kusaal: O da nɔk nɛ galʋʋrʋ wiigi niŋ o zug ka nyaan di'em "Dancing on the Ceiling".
english: He dyed his hair red for his performance of "Dancing on the Ceiling".

kusaal: Cotton da bas ya, ban da tis o kpɛŋ ka o yʋ'ʋn tʋm bɛkɛʋg Radio 1 lin yi 10:00 a.m.
english: Cotton left following her promotion to weekday mornings on Radio 1 from 10:00 a.m. to 12:45 pm, leaving Yates to present on his own.

kusaal: Banɛ da kɛna di'e ba nɔba anɛ Emma Willis nɛ Marvin Humes yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan' la (2013).
english: They were replaced by Emma Willis and Marvin Humes in 2013.

kusaal: Yates da gaad tuoni gɔsid ITV2 di'em kanɛ buon Release the Hounds la, lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ tan' (2013) paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi (2017).
english: Yates hosted the ITV2 programme Release the Hounds from 2013 until 2017.

kusaal: Li pian'azug da anɛ 'connections'.
english: The theme was 'connections'.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) la, Yates da paasi maal sini kanɛ buon Pirates, ka yisi li paalʋ yʋ'ʋs.
english: In 2021, Yates's debut directorial feature film, Pirates, was released.

kusaal: O pian'ak kan zug, o da pʋ paasi maal yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi (2017) di'ema dinɛ da buon Top of the Pops la.
english: Following his comments, he stood down from presenting the 2017 festive special editions of Top of the Pops.

kusaal: · MOBO Awards (BBC; 2009)
english: Yates co-hosted the MOBO Awards 2009 with Keri Hilson at the SECC, Glasgow.

kusaal: · The Fearne & Reggie Saturday request show (BBC Radio 1)
english: In addition to the chart show, Yates also presented a request show on Saturday afternoons, known as The Radio 1 Request Show, where listeners could send in a text or phone in to request a song.

kusaal: · The Request Show with Reggie Yates (BBC Radio 1)
english: In addition to the chart show, Yates also presented a request show on Saturday afternoons, known as The Radio 1 Request Show, where listeners could send in a text or phone in to request a song.

kusaal: · Grange Hill (BBC)
english: In 2002, he played Carl Fenton in the popular children's series Grange Hill.

kusaal: · Doctor Who (BBC) (as Leo Jones)
english: In 2007, Yates appeared in the third series of revived science-fiction series Doctor Who as Leo Jones, brother of the Tenth Doctor's companion Martha.

kusaal: · Make Me Famous (2020)
english: In 2020, Yates' television film Make Me Famous premiered on BBC Three.

kusaal: Regions of Ghana an yiiga bu'ami bɛ gɔmena zanlim ni Republic of Ghana.
english: The regions of Ghana are the first level of subnational government administration within the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: La'anɛ zuŋir la da bɛ 1987, Upper West Region da pʋm bɛnɛ di kɔn' ka tʋm ban da buak Upper Region la December 1982 la, ka 1984 Ghana wʋsa nidib nɛ ya kaalʋg la naam paae.
english: The ten former regions were officially established in 1987, when the Upper West Region was inaugurated as the state's newest administrative region, although it had already functioned as an administrative unit since the break-up of the Upper Region in December 1982, prior to the 1984 national census.

kusaal: Vɔɔtkanɛ ka ba da maal ye ba gɔs ye ba siak ye ba maal region paala ayuobʋ la da bɛnɛ 27 December 2018 – ba da siakya ka ba yɔ'ɔg region paala la wʋsa.
english: A referendum on the creation of six new regions was held on 27 December 2018, where all proposed new regions were approved.

kusaal: Asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ ni March 1957, Northern Sʋ'ʋlim, Trans-Volta Togoland nɛ Gold Coast da kena la'as taaba lieb Ghana.
english: At independence in March 1957, the Northern Territories, Ashanti, Trans-Volta Togoland and the Gold Coast came together to form Ghana.

kusaal: Trans-Volta Togoland da la'asnɛ nɛ Eastern Region zin'isieba nɛ Northern Sʋ'ʋlim ka din mɛ an Volta Region.
english: The Trans-Volta Togoland was combined with part of the Eastern Region and Northern Territories to form the Volta Region.

kusaal: 4 April 1959, Ashanti Region da buaki kilim Ashanti nɛ Brong-Ahafo Region nam.
english: On 4 April 1959, the Ashanti Region was split into the Ashanti and Brong-Ahafo regions as a result of the Brong Ahafo Region Act No. 18 of 1959.

kusaal: Di da dɔlnɛ Brong Kyempem movement da mɔɔd ye ba maal si'el la, dinɛ ka Bono dim da gɔs ka di an ye ba buaki ba mɛŋi yi Ashantis ni ka mɔri ba mɛŋ region.
english: This was in line with what the Brong Kyempem movement had been campaigning for, which was the recognition of the Bono people as a separate ethnic group from the Ashantis with their own region.

kusaal: Daakan ka Ghana da lieb republic, 1 July 1960, Northern Region mɛ da buaki lieb Northern nɛ Upper region nam raising ka region nam la kal yʋ'ʋn an ayɔpɔi.
english: On the day Ghana became a republic, 1 July 1960, the Northern Region got split into the Northern and Upper regions raising the number of regions to seven.

kusaal: Repɔbilik kanɛ paas ayi la nii, Western Region da buaki lieb Western nɛ Central Region nam, ka region nam la yʋ'ʋn aan anii.
english: During the Second Republic, the Western Region was split into the Western and Central regions, making eight regions in total.

kusaal: Nɛ' da naamnɛ ka 1970 nidib kaalʋg la naam paae.
english: This was done ahead of the 1970 census.

kusaal: 1971 ni, Sekondi nɛ Takoradi da la'as taaba lieb Sekondi-Takoradi, dinɛ da an tempʋtita'ari tis Western Region.
english: In 1971, Sekondi and Takoradi were merged to form Sekondi-Takoradi, the new capital of the Western Region.

kusaal: Provisional National Defence Council dinɛ da an soogianam faand paŋ la da bɛnɛ 31 December 1981 nɛ January 1993 ka da an Greater Accra Law (PNDCL 26), 23 July 1982 ka Greater Accra Region mɛ da pin'il.
english: The Provisional National Defence Council, which was the military government in power between 1981 and 1993, promulgated the Greater Accra Law (PNDCL 26) of 23 July 1982 which created the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: Nɛ' da kɛ ka Accra an Capital District, ka national capital, Accra nɛ Ada Local Council, da bɛ Eastern Region yʋ'ʋm paas Greater Accra Region paal la.
english: The new region consisted of the Accra Capital District and the Ada Local Council, which were split off from the Eastern Region.

kusaal: Yʋʋmkanɛ ka dɔl la 1983, Upper Region da buaki lieb Upper East Region nɛ Upper West Region, ka region nam la kal yʋ'ʋn an piiga.
english: In the following year 1983, the Upper Region was divided into the Upper East Region and Upper West Region, bringing the total number of regions to ten.

kusaal: Din yi 2020 la ni, Ghana mɔrnɛ region nam piinɛ ayuobʋ, ka ban mɛ bu'as zanlim yɛla keŋ 260.
english: As of 2020, there are 16 regions, which are further divided for administrative purposes into 260 local metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies (or MMDA's).

kusaal: Bu'asban anɛ metropolitan, municipal nɛ district assembly nam (MMDA's).
english: As of 2020, there are 16 regions, which are further divided for administrative purposes into 260 local metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies (or MMDA's).

kusaal: Region kʋda banɛ da an piiga la da pin'ilnɛ 1987, sankan ka ba da zuŋ Upper West Region ka di lieb region paali paas region nam la zug.
english: The ten former regions were officially established in 1987, when the Upper West Region was inaugurated as the state's newest administrative region, although it had already functioned as an administrative unit since the break-up of the Upper Region in December 1982, prior to the 1984 national census.

kusaal: Nɛ' da ta'as ka ba da maal Brong Ahafo Region Act No.
english: On 4 April 1959, the Ashanti Region was split into the Ashanti and Brong-Ahafo regions as a result of the Brong Ahafo Region Act No. 18 of 1959.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Reuben Riffel nɛ Franschhoek, Cape Province, South Africa, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi, samanpiid nwadig, dabpisi nɛ atan' daar.
english: Reuben Riffel was born in Franschhoek, Cape Province, South Africa, on 23 December 1974.

kusaal: O paas nɛ o dʋ'adib biisa atan' la yinnɛ, ka on nɔbig tɛŋ sia la yʋ'ʋr buon Groendal, Franschhoek kʋkʋna ni.
english: He is one of three siblings, and grew up in an area called Groendal, a valley in Franschhoek.

kusaal: Riffel da kɛŋ sakur nɛ Paarl.
english: Riffel attended high school in Paarl.

kusaal: Riffel da tʋm bi'ela bɛ mɛɛb nam tʋʋma ni, ka li pʋ yʋʋgɛ ka o bas ka lɛb diib kuosig ni, ka o yiiga tʋʋma da anɛ on da di'esid diib nɛ daam tisid nidibi bɛ Chamonix Restaurant ni.
english: Riffel worked briefly in the building trade, but soon migrated to the hospitality industry, where his first job was that of a waiter at Chamonix Restaurant.

kusaal: O ma da paas nɛ diib kuosig tʋʋma ni ka o saam an onɛ gɔsid mɛɛb yela.
english: His mother was intermittently involved in the restaurant industry and his father was involved in the building and construction industry.

kusaal: Richard Acheampong (May 18, 1970) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la pʋʋgin.
english: Richard Acheampong (born May 18, 1970) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Bia East Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Adabokrom tenkanɛ bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Adabokrom, a town in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ University College of Management Studies, Kumasi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ yinne (2011) ka di'e bachelor's degree in Human Resource kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: He entered University College of Management Studies, Kumasi in 2011 and obtained his bachelor's degree in Human Resource.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ Mountcrest University College, n bɛ Kanda- Accra la nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) ka di'e o lɔya kasɛtta gbaʋŋ (bachelor's degree in law).
english: He also attended the Mountcrest University College, Kanda- Accra in 2016 and obtained his bachelor's degree in law.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Banki kpɛɛm nya'andɔl Nfana Rural Bank dinɛ bɛ Sampa la.
english: He also worked as an assistant manager at Nfana Rural Bank Sampa.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) ni la, o da zi'en Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la zugʋ nya' Bia East Constituency kʋk la ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Bia East seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la nwadis anaasi la ni, (April 2017) Britain dim kpɛɛmbanɛ bɛ Ghana kpɛla la da zɛrigi Achempong nɛ George Boakye nɛ Johnson Kwaku Adu nɛ Joseph Benhazin Dahah ye ba sʋŋi ba buudi ka ba mɔr gbanbanɛ pʋ nara kpɛn' UK.
english: In April 2017, the British High Commission in Ghana allegedly accused Acheampong, George Boakye, Johnson Kwaku Adu, and Joseph Benhazin Dahah of helping their relatives enter the UK illegally using their diplomatic passports.

kusaal: O paasnɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg (NDC) la dim.
english: Acheampong is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Ba da du'a Acheampong nɛ yʋma tusir awai kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyɔpɔi la nwadisa anu la dabpiinɛ anii daar (May 18, 1970).
english: Acheampong was born on May 18, 1970.

kusaal: Achempong anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Acheampong is a Christian (Assemblies of God Church).

kusaal: Achempong anɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid.
english: Acheampong is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisi anu.
english: He is married (with five children).

kusaal: O da nɔk o gbankanɛ ka o mɔr nwɛɛd la dɔlis ka o pu'a keŋ UK bakɔya ayi', ka kpɛlimi ani hali tʋʋg yʋʋm.
english: He used his diplomatic passport to secure a holiday visa for his spouse for a two-week holiday, continued to stay in the UK for more than a year.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Gyan nɛ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ ayi la, Buniya nya'aŋ nwairs ayuobυ la li dabisim piisi daar, o yinɛ Gomoa Assin Brofoyedur linɛ bɛ Gaana Central Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Gyan was born on 20 June 1982 and hails from Gomoa Assin Brofoyedur in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O keŋi o sakur linɛ an SSSCE la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ yinne ani ka o da zamis linɛ an kpikpiuŋ yɛla.
english: He had his SSSCE in 2001 where he studied business.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ pa'an n bɛ City Business College.
english: He was also a part time tutor at City Business College.
