kusaal: O pin'li nɔbig ka li yitne o zamisig Ghana nɛ on da keŋ naasaateng zamis la.
english: He rose through the ranks after attending courses in Ghana and the United Kingdom.

kusaal: Colonel Roger Felli da paas dapa ayuobu banɛ da an soogia kpeem nam bani da dɛŋim tum tis gɔmɛna la.
english: Colonel Roger Felli was one of six senior military officers who had previously served in government, executed by firing squad at the Teshie Military Range at Teshie, at the outskirts of Accra.

kusaal: Ba da piinl o Goldman Environmental Prize bɛ yʋma 2004 la ni, nɛ o mɔkir kanɛ ka o sʋŋ ka ku'om an na'ana tis nidib ka kɛ pian'adi tisid nidib ye ku'om da an suak bʋni bɛ Ghana nii.
english: He was awarded the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2004, for his efforts in keeping water supplies affordable for the population and campaigning against the privatization of water in Ghana.

kusaal: World Bank nɛ IMF da sʋŋid o laa, Ghana gɔmma da ti'ebidi ba ku'om lʋgʋr tisid a-sʋ'oe-mɛŋ dim.
english: Backed by the World Bank, and the IMF, Ghana's government was readying its water system for privatization.

kusaal: O paam Bachelor of Arts kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit University of Ghana nɛ EMGL yit Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration nɛ Barrister of Law kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit Ghana School of Law ni na.
english: He obtained a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Ghana, an EMGL from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration, and a Barrister at Law from the Ghana School of Law.

kusaal: Onɛ an zugdaan tisid Globalization Response Program bɛ Integrated Social Development Centre, Amenga integrity, warmth nɛ o piinkanɛ bɛ di kɔn' ka o mɔri ken dunia wʋsa la, ka sʋŋ nɔŋ dim ka a-sʋ'oe-mɛŋ ku'om pʋ lɛn tɔya dinɛ an pɔlitis nɛ bɛdegʋ laafi yɛla.
english: As the head of the Globalization Response Program for the Integrated Social Development Centre, Amenga integrity, warmth, and his unique ability to move between the worlds of the powerful, and the poor helped elevate water privatization as an important political and public health issue.

kusaal: Di anɛ World Bank nɛ International Monetary Fund sʋŋid nɛ ligipɛmisa tisid Ghana gɔmma ye ba sʋŋ ku'om yɛla teŋ la ni.
english: The main opposition is the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund who are offering loans to the Ghanaian government to improve the water infrastructure across the country.

kusaal: Ba da tis o Goldman Environmental Prize piini bɛ yʋma 2004, nɛ o mʋkir kanɛ ka o kɛt ka ku'om paad nidib bɛdigʋ la nɛ on pian'adi tisid nidib ye ku'om pʋ nar ye nidib sʋ'oe ka kati ba taaba di yɛla bɛ Ghana ni.
english: He was awarded the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2004, for his efforts in keeping water supplies affordable for the population and campaigning against the privatization of water in Ghana.

kusaal: Ka World Bank nɛ International Monetary Fund da an banɛ pʋ siak alaa, din ka ba tisid ligipɛmisa ye ba kɛ ka ku'om yɛla an na'ana teŋ la ni.
english: The main opposition is the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, which are offering loans to the Ghanaian government to improve the water infrastructure across the country.

kusaal: O di Goldman environmental prize piini la nɛ yʋma 2004 la ni .
english: He won 2004 Goldman environmental prize.

kusaal: Onɛ da an lɔyabil la, o nyɛ ka o sʋŋid nɔŋ dim banɛ pʋ nyaŋidi yɔɔdi ba ku'om sama bɛɛ banɛ ka ba gban'adi ba ye ba zu ku'om ye ba nu ka vʋe.
english: As a young lawyer, he found himself defending poor people who had not paid their water bills and those who were being persecuted for tapping into illegal water sources to survive.

kusaal: Sportiva Calcio Adelaide dinɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa buoni li yee Adelaide bɛɛ giŋa S.C. Adelaide la anɛ Ghanaian lʋgir kani nwɛn'ɛd bool ka bɛ Tema, Greater Accra, banɛ da nwɛn'edi nya'ad nɛdinɛ anɛ Ghana Division Three League la.
english: Sportiva Calcio Adelaide commonly referred to as Adelaide or the abbreviation S.C. Adelaide, is a Ghanaian professional football club based in Tema, Greater Accra, who are competing in the Ghana Division Three League.

kusaal: Clab la da nɔk saŋa bɛdigʋ tisi ba dasam bool nwɛn'ɛb la'asʋg la yɛla, amaa bam yʋ'ʋm tiak nana an kpɛɛmnam bool nwɛ'ɛb la'asʋg k aba pɛɛs ayi bɛ Ghana Football Leagues.
english: The club has spent most of their history as a youth football team, but recently converted into a senior team in second tier of the Ghana Football Leagues.

kusaal: Ba yɛlisim anɛ Deo Juvante (Latin) ka li gbin anɛɛ nɛ Wina'am Sʋŋir la.
english: Their motto is Deo Juvante (Latin) meaning with God's Help.

kusaal: Ba da pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye li an after St Adelaide Italy (si'em ka Italian tuon Gatib Callicio Adelaide).
english: It was named after St Adelaide of Italy (thus the Italian connection Sportiva Calcio Adelaide).

kusaal: Ba gɛrima yʋ'ʋr klap la daa nam kpɛm mɔr Italian yʋ'ʋr kanɛ an Sportiva Calcio Adelaide Sporting Club, ka S.C la bɛ Adelaide tuon ka ye di ya'aŋa, dinɛ ke ka saŋa sieba ka yidigir bɛ niŋwisgir diema la bɛdigʋ ka ba nɔk la yɛla.
english: "The opening of the club is with an aim to developing talents and to raise up a generation who will be brave enough to face the world practically and make the nation and the continent as a whole proud." In honor of its origins, the club has retained the Italian name as Sportiva Calcio Adelaide, instead of changing it to the Adelaide Sporting Club, the S.C. is in front of the Adelaide and not after, which is sometimes confused since more sporting activities are being taken.

kusaal: Dinɛ pɛɛs ayi anɛ di lɛm mɔrnɛ naalʋg nɛ Italian, Azzurro pa'al ye saŋgbaʋŋ), light blue anɛ Italy dim teŋ la si'im nwɛnii Adelaide's blue jersey, ka ba baa yʋ'ʋr an Azzurri.
english: Secondly with its Italian connection, Azzurro (meaning sky), a light blue, is the national colour of Italy as such Adelaide's blue jersey, they have gained the nickname Azzurri.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋnɛ piɛlig (white) bɔzugɔ di da anɛ zanbini tis Catholics dim la, piɛlig la gbin pa'al yee kassi.
english: White was chosen because White was the symbol of Catholics, white means purity.

kusaal: Ba da zin klap la yɛla da mɛ lɛm paam baa yʋ'ʋr yit Tema Municipality la ni na dinɛ ka ba da ɛɛɛnti buon yeenwama teŋ (land of calabashes) la (Tema teŋ la yʋ'ʋr la yini Ga dim pian'adin dinɛ an ' Tor-man ' 'pa'al yee nwam teŋ' (calabash-town)).
english: The nickname also comes from the municipality Tema which used to be a land of calabashes (Tema originated from ' Tor-man ' in Ga meaning calabash-town).

kusaal: Team kaŋa nwɛn'ɛdi ba bɔɔl zin'isia la yalʋŋ anɛ wʋʋ nɔba makir tusa piiga (10,000) bɛ Christ Church, dinɛ bɛ Ningo Prampram distict la.
english: The team's current home grounds is a 10,000 capacity park – Christ Church, in the district of Ningo Prampram where it's located.

kusaal: Ka sieba mɛ pa'al bam nwɛn'ɛdi ba bool siem la ye Total football ka di anɛ ba Dutch coach la baa yʋ'ʋr la yɛla "Dutchmaster".Fʋ ya'a bɔɔd yee fʋ gɔsnɛ Total football la dinɛ an Netherlands national football team bɛɛ Arsenal F.C. nɛ fʋ mɛŋ nini nyain ka kae yee TV nii, da lɛm iieedi gɛɛnda, kʋdim gɔsim .C. Adelaide bam maani li siem" Kulusha, onɛ enti piadi bɛ Peace FM Ghana kpala ni la.
english: Others interpret their style as Total football due to their Dutch coach nicknamed the "Dutchmaster".

kusaal: S.C. Adelaide dim la da anɛ banɛ nya'ŋid sasa wʋsa bɔzugo ba na'ab kanɛ ka ɛɛnti tʋmʋ la Seth Hoffmann da bɛnɛ boolwɛ'ɛdib banɛ an yʋma piiga nɛ ayi(under 12) nɛ yʋma piiga nɛ ayɔpoi(17) sourthern sector la ni tis Ghana Football Association la, banɛ nwɛ'ɛd bool la sʋ'ʋŋa la tita'am bɛnɛ banɛ an yʋma piiga nɛ ayi(12) la ni.
english: At the youth level, S.C. Adelaide's talent recruitment is aided by chief scout Seth Hoffmann, who also serves as the under–12 and under–17 southern sector scout for the Ghana Football Association.

kusaal: Tituli anɛ Ransford Osei kanɛ ka FIFA.com da pa'ali o yɛla yee o anɛ onɛ k aba paam zugsʋŋ ka o an onɛ did goolnam hali, ka lɛm tuoe mɔr bool la nwɛdigidi o mɛŋ sʋŋa, biribiŋ paalig kanɛ did boolnam hali ka da ken tuon tituaa, Osei ka World Soccer Magazine da pa'ali o yɛla yee o pɛɛs biribis paalis banɛ pisnu(50) la banɛ k aba nɔŋi ba yɛla dunia ni wʋsa bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpoi la sapal nwadig(November 2007) la ni yɛla.
english: Striker Ransford Osei was described by FIFA.com as an "opportunistic goal machine" with strong pace and movement, and was included in World Soccer Magazine's November 2007 list of the "50 Most Exciting Teenagers on the Planet".

kusaal: Ba da Opare yɛla sʋm hali nɛ on da yaŋi nɔki o paŋ nɛ o yam sʋŋ ka Ghana's U-17 Team, dinɛ an The Black Starlets bɛ 2007 U-17 World Cup.
english: Fullback Daniel Opare was also featured in the same World Soccer Magazine issue following his performances for Ghana's U-17 team, the Black Starlets, at the 2007 U-17 World Cup.

kusaal: Ba da vood David Addy ka o an biribiŋ paalig boolwɛ'ɛd kanɛ bɛ Ghana kpala yʋma tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) la ni.
english: Additionally, David Addy was named the 2008 Young Player of the Year in Ghana.

kusaal: Adelaide anɛ boolnwɛ'ɛdib lʋgir yinnɛ kanɛ pɛɛs banɛ ken tuon hali bɛ dasam paalis klaps banɛ bɛ Ghana kpala ni, nɛ bam nyaŋi mɔr European-based players bɛ Ghana kpala dinɛ an dasam paalis teamnam la wʋsa la.
english: Adelaide is one of the most successful youth clubs in Ghana, having produced the most number of European-based players by any youth team in Ghana.

kusaal: Eric Bekoe anɛ ba klab la boolnwɛ'ɛd ka di goal nam la hali ka mɔr goals banɛ ka o di ka li an kɔbiga nɛ ayuobu (106) ba nwɛ'ɛb saŋa la wʋsa dinyi yʋma tusa ayi nɛ yinnɛ (2001) la nɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la teŋsʋk tis banɛ an yʋma piiga nɛ ayɔpoi (17) la dim (under -17) ka onɛ dɔl anɛ Ransford Osei, o goals nam anɛ pisyɔpoi nɛ awai bɛ yʋma tusa ayi (2000) la nɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayi la teŋsʋk tis yʋʋm piiga nɛ ayi (12) boolnwɛ'ɛdib la (under-12).
english: Eric Bekoe is the club's top goalscorer with 106 goals in all competitions between 2001 and 2004 for the under – 17's followed by Ransford Osei's total of 79 between 2000 and 2002 for the under – 12's.

kusaal: Jimmy Addo ma'aa an onɛ ka o yʋma pɔɔd paam ka da nwɛ' gees nɛ kpɛɛmnam team o yʋma piiga nɛ anaasi nɛ nwadisa ayi saŋa (at 14 years 2 months).
english: Jimmy Addo is the youngest player to ever play against a senior team at 14 years 2 months.

kusaal: Adelaide da an onɛ mɔr goals nam bɛdigʋ saŋa yinne ni, nɛ'ɛna anɛ youth league, national youth cup nɛ colts cup nya'ab la ni, ka ba goals nam wʋsa da an kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi (124 goals) bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayinne (2001) la paae yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2002) la saŋa.
english: Adelaide holds the record for the most goals in a single season, this includes youth league, national youth cup and colts cup competition, with a total of 124 goals in the 2001–02 season.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayinne (2001) la ken paae yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayi (2002) la saŋa, Eric Bekoe da nwɛ' boolnam nɛ la'as bam pistan' nɛ anaasi (39) ka di goals nam pisnaasi nɛ ayi (42), nɛ'ɛŋa da ke ka o di'eɛ yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka sɔ' nan zi di'eɛ kʋdim saŋa yinne bɛ Ghana kpala ni.
english: In the 2001–02 season, Eric Bekoe scored 42 goals in 34 appearances, setting the Ghanaian record in a single season.

kusaal: Dinɛ mɛ lɛm pɛɛs anɛ goals banɛ ka ba di bedigʋ bɛ nwɛ'ɛb yinne ni ma'aa anɛ ayɔpoi (7), ka li anɛ Saddick Adams da di goals ban wʋsa, nɛ' buudi mɛ nam zi naam Ghana sʋ'ʋlim kudimm, goals banɛ zuoe hali nwɛ'ɛb yinne ma'aa ni da anɛ piiga nɛ anaasi (14), nɛ'ɛnam wʋsa sɔbnɛ digil ban da nwɛ' yin nwɛ'ɛbi gees Hamilton Youth F.C. bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ atan' kem paae yʋma tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2003-2004) la ni saŋa.
english: The most goals scored by a player in a single match is 7 by Saddick Adams, which is also a Ghanaian record, the highest number of goals in a single match was 14 both records in a home match against Hamilton Youth F.C. in the 2003–04 season.

kusaal: Adelaide dim la da gʋri ba goal la zin'ig siem la ti nwɛ' bool la nwɛni nɔɔrim pisyi nɛ ayi (22) ka ba pʋ dii ba baa bielaa bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpoi paae tusa ayi nɛ anii (2007-2008) la ni wʋsa, saŋa kan la.
english: The Adelaide defense set a new record after going 22 consecutive games without conceding a goal and went unbeaten the whole of the 2007/08 season.

kusaal: Ba da di ya'an kanɛ pa'al yee ba tuoe an wild card tis Zone 1 la Playoffs, ban da da di ya'ani bɛ dasam boolnwɛ'ɛbin dinɛ an (Colts Football) league la, ba da pɛɛs playoff nam la'asʋg dinɛ da an team nam atan' banɛ na nwɛ' bɛ pʋdigir dinɛ pɛɛsiri ayi la - Palma F.C. nɛ ayi yiiga ka dinɛ dɔl atan' sɔb la ka ba nɔki pɛɛs third division la ni - Great African United nɛ Techiman Universal Stars dɔli ala buudi.
english: They qualified as a wild card for the Zone 1 playoffs after winning the youth (Colts Football) league, they were included in one of three playoffs groups which consisted of one of three relegated teams from the second division – Palma F.C. and two first and second placed teams from the third division – Great African United and Techiman Universal Stars respectively.

kusaal: Ba da pin'il Adelaide la'asʋg, ka di anɛ banɛ gɔsid niŋwisigir bɛdegʋ.
english: Adelaide was initially started as a football club, as a club oriented to multiple sports.

kusaal: Adelaide mɔr la'asʋg tis niŋwisigir di'emanam dinɛ anɛ for athletics, basketball, football, handball, swimming, volleyball nɛ sieba.
english: Adelaide has departments for athletics, basketball, football, handball, swimming, volleyball, and others.

kusaal: Klap la labakʋda saŋa la wʋsa, ba da ɛɛnti mɔri ba fʋʋd si'sm kanɛ kanɛ an blue nɛ white.
english: Throughout the entire history of the club, they have been represented by the colour blue and white.

kusaal: Nimbanɛ mɔr blue aura la taa nɛ nɔŋ babigin tʋʋma dinɛ anɛ sa'alʋg, pa'alʋg, sɔbʋg nɛ psychologist ka di anɛ lʋgir la bɔdɔ siella zug.
english: People with blue auras are said to be interested in social service work and to be in occupations such as social worker, counsellor, teacher, writer, and psychologist.

kusaal: Ba da mɔri blue jerseys nam la nɛ nwɛn'ɛd yin ka mɔr jerseys piɛlis la mɔri nwɛn'ed nyiŋ bɔɔlnam.
english: Blue jerseys are used for home matches and white jerseys for away matches.

kusaal: Ya'am burimis daa bɛnɛ nɛ yʋ'ʋr la yi zin'isia na, catholic Catedrals nam la bɛdigʋ da mɔri li yʋ'ʋr la kena, ba mɛ da lɛm niŋ yada yee yʋ'ʋr la anɛ dinɛ tisiba sʋor yee ba keŋ zin'isia paam sʋmalisim.
english: There is ambiguity with the origin of the name, it was named after the many catholic cathedrals, it is also believed the name was given as a place for rejoicing for the fans where they will go and enjoy themselves from the football.

kusaal: Ba da pa'al yee S.C. Adelaide anɛ banɛ na mɔr sumalisim kena bɛɛ daaʋŋ, ba bool nwɛn'ɛp nwɛni Arsenal F. C. nɛ, nwɛ'ɛdi mɔri tisid taab tɔ'ɔtɔ, ka tisid taaba bool la nɛ lali-lali sa.
english: S.C. Adelaide has been described as a team which has a desire to entertain and attack, their style of play has been likened to Arsenal F.C. style of playing, quick one two passes, through passes and the odd one or two long passes.

kusaal: Daniel Opare ka World Soccer Magazine da pa'al yee o anɛ onɛ pɛɛs biribis paalis pisnu(50) banɛ ka ba nɔŋi ba hali yʋma tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpoi Sapal Nwadig(November 2007) dunia wʋsa ni.
english: Fullback Daniel Opare was also featured in the same World Soccer Magazine issue following his performances for Ghana's U-17 team, the Black Starlets, at the 2007 U-17 World Cup.

kusaal: Boolwɛ'ɛdib da kpɛm ken klap la ni na 2006 la ya'aŋ keŋi paae 2007 biribis paalis saŋa la, boolwe'ɛdib banɛ da dɛŋim kɛnna tis banɛ bɛ tuon la, biribis paalis klap nwɛnii Hearts of Oak ne Kotoko.
english: Following the 2006–07 youth season, the entire first-team squad was transferred to prominent Ghana Premier League clubs, including Hearts of Oak and Kotoko.

kusaal: Pa'alʋg bɛ yee ba boolnwɛɛdib la ayuobu; banɛ nya'aŋi ken tuon hali gaad nidib bɛdigʋ la bɛ klab yinne ni bɛ under-17 hali klab la sin'iŋirin sa.
english: A total of 17 players have been produced for the under-17 since the club's inception.

kusaal: Bool pian'ad-pian'ad la da yee " ba (Adelaide) gʋri ba goal la zin'ig la nwɛni daa sierɛ bool la ya'a si'isi ba goal daad la ba wʋsa ya'a ye ba kpini nɛ, ka keti banɛ naa na dii baa goal lɛɛ".
english: A commentator said "they (Adelaide) are protecting their goal like they will all die if the ball hit the post let alone if they conceded a goal".

kusaal: S.C. Adelaide da paam suori na nwɛ' second division bool yʋma tusa ayi nɛ anii nɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai (2008/2009) la ni.
english: S.C. Adelaide has qualified for the 2008/09 second division but is yet to register the club for the season.

kusaal: Ba gaans dasam paalis la yi banɛ an yʋma piiga nɛ ayuobu (16) bɛɛ gaad wala pɛɛs nɛ yʋma piiga nɛ anaasi la (14-year-old) ka ba nwɛ'ɛdi adagɔbʋg baba sensation Jimmy Addo da sʋŋ Ryan Giggs paalimin la, boolnwɛ'ɛdib la wʋsa sɔ'ɔsɔ da kaae ka o yʋma tʋʋg piiga nɛ ayɔpoi (17 years).
english: The fielded the youngest team with an average age of a little over 16, including 14-year-old left midfield sensation Jimmy Addo touted the new Ryan Giggs, none of the players was over 17 years.

kusaal: Sagre Bambangi (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ nwadisa anu la daba ayi daar (May 2, 1966) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Walewale Constituency bɛ Northern Region la wabʋg na'adɔɔg (New Patriotic Party) nɔba zug.
english: Sagre Bambangi (born May 2, 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Walewale Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Wungu, tenkanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Wungu, a town in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ Navrongo Senior High School maal SC/GCEO O level nɛ GCE A level.
english: He attended Navrongo Senior High School and obtained SC/GCE O level and GCE A level.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ University of Ghana ti maali o Doctor of Philosophy degree in Agricultural Economics yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009).
english: He entered University of Ghana and obtained his Doctor of Philosophy degree in Agricultural Economics in 2009.

kusaal: O da anɛ pa'an-pa'an bɛ University for Development Studies din yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (1997) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016).
english: He was a lecturer at the University for Development Studies from 1997 to 2016.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' (2012) la ni, o da nyi'a Walewale wadmaan kʋk la wabʋg na'adɔɔg (NPP) nɔba zug sixth parliament of the fourth republic of Ghana la ni ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Walewale seat on the ticket of the NPP sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: O anɛ pa'an (lecturer in economics) tis University for Development Studies - Wa Campus.
english: Bambangi is a lecturer in economics at the University for Development Studies - Wa Campus.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi (January 7, 2013); o yʋ'ʋm bɛnɛ o ken kanɛ paasi ayi daani la.
english: He has been a member of the Parliament since January 7, 2013; he is in his second term.

kusaal: Ba a dʋ'a Bambangi nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ nwadisa anu la daba ayi' daar, (May 2, 1966).
english: Bambangi was born on May 2, 1966.

kusaal: Bambangi paas nɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg (New Patriotic Party) nidib ni.
english: Bambangi is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa ayuobʋ.
english: He is married, with six children.

kusaal: Kindergarten bɛɛ preschool anɛ zin'is banɛ ka ba pa'an bibibis paa la (banɛ mɔr yʋʋma atan' paae anu).
english: Kindergarten or preschool provide some schooling to very young children (typically ages 3–5).

kusaal: University, vocational school, college bɛɛ seminary mɛ bɛɛ tis banɛ naae secondary school.
english: University, vocational school, college, or seminary may be available after secondary school.

kusaal: sʋ-Aʋm-mɛŋ sakurnam la si'eba anɛ winpʋ'ʋs nami sʋ'ʋe, wʋʋ kiristo biis sakurnam, gurukula (Hindu winpʋ'ʋsnam sakur), madrasa (Arabic sakurnam), hawzas (Shi'i Mɔɔm sakurnam), yeshivas (Jewish dim sakurnam), nɛ si'eba banɛ bɛ; bɛɛ sakurnam banɛ ka ba zamisig bɛɛ di kɔn' bɛɛ ba pa'anɛ tʋʋm si'eba pa'alig anina.
english: Other private schools can also be religious, such as Christian schools, gurukula (Hindu schools), madrasa (Arabic schools), hawzas (Shi'i Muslim schools), yeshivas (Jewish schools), and others; or schools that have a higher standard of education or seek to foster other personal achievements.

kusaal: Sakur ka ba buon na'asaalin ye school la yinɛ Greek sɔb kanɛ an σχολή (scholē), di gbin da pin'ili anɛ "vʋ'ʋsʋm" bɛɛ "dinɛ ka azin'ini-vʋ'ʋs bɛɛ di pʋʋgin", ka di ya'aŋ ka di yʋ'ʋn ti'aki an "nidib banɛ la'as taaba ka pa'an-pa'an zamisidi ba".
english: The word school derives from Greek σχολή (scholē), originally meaning "leisure" and also "that in which leisure is employed", but later "a group to whom lectures were given, school".

kusaal: sakurnam yʋda bɛ kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb tɛns bɛdigʋ ni, amaa, bɛdigʋ ni, si'eba an primary school ka din anɛ bibibis sakurnam nɛ secondary school, din anɛ bikpɛɛmnam banɛ naae primary education la tɔlisid anina.
english: The names for these schools vary by country (discussed in the Regional terms section below) but generally include primary school for young children and secondary school for teenagers who have completed primary education.

kusaal: Banɛ lɛn paas sakur bama ni, sakur biis banɛ bɛ tɛnsi'eba ni mɔr sakurnam ka ba kɛn ka nyaan paad primary (U.S. dim buon ye elementary) ka primary school nya'aŋ an secondary (U.S. dim buon ye middle school) education.
english: In North America, the term school can refer to any educational institution at any level and covers all of the following: preschool (for toddlers), kindergarten, elementary school, middle school (also called intermediate school or junior high school, depending on specific age groups and geographic region), high school (or in some cases senior high school), college, university, and graduate school.

kusaal: Sakurnam pʋdis nɛ bɛ kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔbi bɛ sakur la mɛŋ pʋʋgin, ka ba si'eb an departmental, nidib bi'ela zamisig zin'is, gbaŋ zamisig zin'is, zamisig bɛdigʋ zin'is, nɛ sakur bibis, sakur titada pʋʋgin.
english: Schools are organized in several different organizational models, including departmental, small learning communities, academies, integrated, and schools-within-a-school.

kusaal: Sakur anɛ zamisig zin'ig bɛɛ dɔɔd banɛ ka ba mɛ ye paalʋ bɛ ka pa'an-pa'anib pa'an nidib anina ka guri ba.
english: A school is an educational institution (and, in the case of in-person learning, the building) designed to provide learning environments for the teaching of students, usually under the direction of teachers.

kusaal: zin'is bama ni, sakurnam kɛn tuon, ka gɔmɛna sakurnam bɛ ka asʋ-ʋm-mɛŋ sakurnam mɛ bɛ.
english: In addition to these core schools, students in a given country may also attend schools before and after primary and secondary education.

kusaal: Sakurnam banɛ ka' gɔmɛna sʋ'ʋe ya, ka ba buoni ba asʋ-ʋm-mɛŋ sakurnam, bɛ tɛŋ si'eba, gɔmɛna sakurnam la ya'a pʋ nyaŋi paae nidib la wʋsa bɛɛ zamisid tutua nɛ.
english: Non-government schools, also known as private schools, may be required when the government does not supply adequate or specific educational needs.

kusaal: Salaga anɛ tempʋʋgi di mɛŋ ka an tempʋtita'ari tis East Gonja district, district kanɛ bɛ Savannah Region sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Ghana Ya-datiʋŋ.
english: Salaga is a town and is the capital of East Gonja district, a district in the Savannah Region of north Ghana.

kusaal: Salaga da lieb zin'ikanɛ ka ba kuosid, da'ad bɛɛ kpiisid nidib bɛɛ ti'asidi ba nɛ bʋnkɔnbid gaad zin'ig wʋsa din yi 18th nɛ 19th century nam la ni.
english: Salaga was the largest slave market in the 18th and 19th centuries.

kusaal: Di yʋ'ʋr la, Salaga yinɛ Dagomba pian'ad "salgi" dinɛ gbinni an ye "Amiilim zin'ikanɛ ka fʋ bɛ".
english: The name Salaga comes from the Dagomba word "salgi" which means "To get used to a place of abode".

kusaal: Din da bɛ Sahel Ya-dagɔbʋg la, ba da buon Salaga ye "Timbuktu of the south" ban da kpiisid zʋʋd kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔbi ani la zug.
english: Situated in the southernmost reaches of the Sahel, Salaga was referred to as "the Timbuktu of the south" for its cosmopolitan population and varied trade.

kusaal: Nɛ wala, din an tenkanɛ zu'oe la, nimbanɛ da bɛ Salaga anɛ Hausas, Wangaras, Dagombas, Gurmas, nɛ buudi sieba region la ni ka Gonja nam lɛɛ an teŋimbiis.
english: However, being a cosmopolitan town, Salaga was inhabited by Hausas, Wangaras, Dagombas, Gurmas, and other groups from the region as well as the indigenous Gonja.

kusaal: Salaga da an la'asʋg zin'igi tis Zabarima nam (emirate) la ka paŋ la da bɛ zin'ikanɛ yʋ'ʋn an northern Ghana, gbam-mi'id Alfa Hano nɛ zabzabid Gazari da yinɛ Niamey Ya-dagɔbʋg-Nya'aŋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ nam la ni.
english: Salaga was central to the emergence of the Zabarima (emirate) as a power in the area that is now northern Ghana, when the scholar Alfa Hano and the warrior Gazari migrated here from their former homes south-east of Niamey in the 1860s.

kusaal: Salaga da' la da an zin'ikanɛ ka ba du'odi ken northern Sahel nɛ southernmost coast of the 'Sahel', ka dɔl Dagomba tempʋʋsin, Kpabia nɛ Yendi.
english: The Salaga market served as a transit point through the northern Sahel and the southernmost coast of the 'Sahel', as well as through the Dagomba towns of Kpabia and Yendi.

kusaal: Di mɛ lɛn anɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ba ziid gʋʋri yit Ghana ken Nigeria Ya-datiʋŋ baba.
english: It also was the transit point through which kola was transported from modern day Ghana to northern Nigeria.

kusaal: Trans-Atlantic slave trade la saŋa, Salaga da lɛn anɛ da'a sʋŋ kanɛ ka ba da la'asid nimbanɛ ka ba da' la lʋʋri zii keŋ zin'ikanɛ ka ba na mɔri ba gaad.
english: During the Trans-Atlantic slave trade, Salaga also served as an important market from where slaves were transported to the coast for export.

kusaal: Nɛ' zug ka da' si'a bɛ Jamestown ka ba buon ye "Salaga da' la": ba ya'a da ɛɛnti lʋʋr yi Salaga slave market ani ka ba da kuosid ba.
english: This is why a market in Jamestown is called the "Salaga Market": slaves originally shipped from the Salaga slave market were sold there.

kusaal: 18th nɛ 19th centurynam la ni, Salaga da anɛ tempʋkanɛ an da', ka ba da kpiisid gʋʋr region la ni ka Salaga da kɛ ka kpiisʋg Ya-dagɔbʋg nɛ Ya-datiʋŋ an na'ana.
english: Salaga was the largest slave market in the 18th and 19th centuries.

kusaal: Gonja la, zabzabid kanɛ mɔr paŋ hali, da zanl Salaga nɛ tensieba bɛdegʋ.
english: Gonja, a powerful warrior kingdom, ruled Salaga and several other towns.

kusaal: Nɛ' da kɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋm ziid niigi nɛ suma yit Yendi dɔl Salaga da' la.
english: This gave rise to the transport of cattle and groundnuts from Yendi via the Salaga market.

kusaal: Salaga pʋʋgin, kɔlbil bɛ ani ka ba buoni di ye "Wonkan bawa", dinɛ an Huasa pian'atɔŋgiŋ kanɛ gbinni an ye saŋkpan'asnam sʋʋb zin'ig.
english: In Salaga, there is a pond named "Wonkan bawa," which is a Huasa phrase that means "the bathing spot of slaves." There is also a young Baobab tree in the area that was formerly the Slave Market.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ ayi la ni, zaba da duoe Salaga, ka di da kɛ ka nimbanɛ bɛ Zongo la bɛdegʋ zɔ ka bas zin'ig la.
english: In 1892, civil war broke out in Salaga, resulting in a mass exodus of mostly Zongo peoples out of the area.

kusaal: Salaga da mɔrnɛ nidib kal tusa pisi nɛ anu, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi (25,472) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi kaalʋg la ni.
english: Salaga had a 2012 settlement population of 25,472 people.

kusaal: Salaga anɛ constituencies nam layinne ka mɔr wadmaan ka o zi'el tis ba bɛ wadmaanib yir la Ghana nwa.Ba vɔtʋg gaŋ wadmaan yinne ka an linɛ ka nidib la vɔɔt gaŋ nid yinne ma'a.
english: Salaga is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Li bɛni Northern Region Ghana nwa.On an wadmaan nannana tis constituency kaŋa anɛ Ibrahim Bey Abubakari.
english: The current member of Parliament for the constituency is Ibrahim Bey Abubakari.

kusaal: O anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid (NDC) ka o di, ka paam 3,046 vɔɔts gaŋi o na'anya'ad tiraan onɛ daa nya'adi o la, ka di nɛ o lieb wadmaan MP.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and won a majority of 3,046 votes more than the candidate closest in the race, to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: O daa Boniface Abubakar Saddique nɔba zug , ka zi'enɛ tis constituency n bɛ Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la, o anɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg nid(NPP).
english: He succeeded Boniface Abubakar Saddique who had represented the constituency in the 4th Republican parliament on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Salaga North Constituency anɛ constituency banɛ mɔr sɔ' ka o zi'e di nɔba zug bɛ Parliament of Ghana.
english: Salaga North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Salaga North constituency bɛnɛ East Gonja district linɛ bɛ Savannah Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The Salaga North constituency is located in the East Gonja district of the Savannah Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ East Gonja District pʋʋgin linɛ bɛ Savannah region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The seat is located entirely within the East Gonja District of the Savannah region of Ghana.

kusaal: Alhassan Mumuni an wadmaan nannanna tis Salaga North constituency.
english: Alhassan Mumuni is the current MP for the Salaga North constituency.

kusaal: Salaga South Constituency anɛ constituency banɛ mɔr sɔ' ka o zi'e di nɔba zug bɛ Parliament of Ghana.
english: Salaga South is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Salaga South constituency bɛnɛ East Gonja district linɛ bɛ Savannah Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The Salaga South constituency is located in the East Gonja district of the Savannah Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Salifu Adam Braimah an wadmaan nannanna tis Salaga North constituency.
english: Zuwela Mohammed Ibrahimah is the current MP for the Salaga South constituency.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaan dɔlisid onɛ vɔɔti gaadi o taaba.
english: It elects one member of parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan (MP) tis Salaga South Constituency dinɛ bɛ Northern Region.
english: Salifu Adam Braimah (25 September 1965 – 12 April 2026) was a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Salaga South Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Salifu Adam Braimah mɔr CA Part 2 yit Institute of Professional Studies nɛ GCE O Level nɛ A-Level yit Tamale Secondary School, B.S.C.
english: Salifu Adam Braimah (25 September 1965 – 12 April 2026) was a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Salaga South Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ka din yi yʋma 1991 ti paae yʋma 2000 la ni, Salifu Adam Braimah da anɛ onɛ kaan ligidi bɛ Ghana Cotton Company nɛ Deputy Finance Minister tis Tamale Polytechnic yʋma 2000 ti paae yʋma 2001 la ni.
english: Salifu Adam Braimah (25 September 1965 – 12 April 2026) was a Ghanaian politician who was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Salaga South Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Samia Nkrumah (ba da du'a o nɛ 23 naadʋʋnr nwadig 1960) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Nɔraʋg na'adɔɔg la kpɛɛm ( CPP).
english: Honourable Samia Yaba Christina Nkrumah (born 23 June 1960) is a Ghanaian politician and former chairperson of the Convention People's Party (CPP) making her the first woman to ever head a major political party in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a samia bɛnɛ Aburi teŋ kanɛ bɛ Eastern Region Ghana nwa ni la nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ (1960) la ni.
english: Samia was born at Aburi in the Eastern Region of Ghana in 1960.

kusaal: Ka on nɛ o yidim la da lɛb Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm na nɛ yʋma 1975 kanɛ ni ka General Acheampong National Redemption Council da buol o la, o keŋ Achimota sakur bɛ anina.
english: She returned with her family in the year 1975 at the invitation of General Acheampong's National Redemption Council government and attended Achimota School.

kusaal: Samia da tɔlis keŋ London sʋ'ʋlʋm ti keŋ university of London sakur kanɛ an school of oriental and African studies yʋma 1991 la ni.
english: Samia proceeded to London, later completing her studies at the School of Oriental and African Studies of the University of London in the United Kingdom, where she obtained the degree of Bachelor Arabic Studies in the year 1991.

kusaal: O da lɛn naae o mastɛs digirii kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ sakur kan ni nɔɔ yʋma 1993 la ni.
english: She also completed a Master's degree at the same institution in the year 1993.

kusaal: Samia Nkrumah pin'ili o tʋʋma bɛnɛ London bank kanɛ da bɛ India sʋ'ʋlʋm yʋma 1989 la ni n an onɛ gɔsid nidib ligidi digilʋg nɛ yiisʋg yɛla nɛ ɔfis tʋʋma sieba paas.
english: Honourable Samia Nkrumah started work as a bank clerk with the London branch of the Bank of India in 1984.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ labaya tʋmtʋn n tʋm nɛ Al-Ahram zin'is kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ni yʋma 1989 la ni.
english: She then worked with Al-Ahram as a journalist in various capacities starting from the year 1989.

kusaal: Huffington post da pa'al ka pian'a o yɛlasʋma banɛ sʋŋ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛdib si'em.
english: In an article about her, entitled "The new Mandela is a woman", the Huffington Post described and analyzed her impact on Ghanaian and African politics.

kusaal: O anɛ ninbanɛ da sʋ'oe Africa must unit kanɛ ka li yɛlkpan an ye li sʋŋ nɔbig Kwame Nkrumah nyɛɛb (pʋtɛn'ɛr baŋir) nɛ pɔlitikal malima yɛla la nid yinne.
english: She is one of the founders of Africa Must Unite, which aims to promote Kwame Nkrumah's vision and political culture.

kusaal: Vɔɔdʋg kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2008 la ni la, o da zi'en nyi'a Jomoro teŋ kanɛ bɛ western region sʋ'ʋlʋm la wadmaan na'am kʋk la ka dii li nɛ vɔɔt kal 6,571 ka bas Lee ocran onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid la, ka li an pisnu kɔbʋga pʋʋgin (50%) vɔɔtnam la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: In December 2008, she contested the Jomoro constituency seat in the Western Region of Ghana and beat the incumbent MP, Lee Ocran of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) with a majority of 6,571, winning about 50% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ka lin da an on ma'aa da an nɔraʋg na'adɔɔg nid (CPP) bɛ wadmaanib yin la, li da anɛ gaŋir tis o ye o dɔl NDC dim banɛ an ninbabʋg bɛ wadmaanib yin la bɛɛ o dɔl NPP dim banɛ an bi'ela la.
english: Being the only CPP member of parliament, she had to either align with NDC who were the majority in parliament or the minority NPP.

kusaal: Onɛ da an yiiga pu'a kanɛ ka ba vɔɔt gaŋ o ka o an kpɛɛm tis nɔraʋg na'adɔɔg la (CPP) sawa'ad nwadig la dapiiga daar yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ yinne la ni (10th September 2011).
english: She was elected as the first woman chairperson of the Convention People's Party on 10 September 2011.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔt la nɛ vɔɔt kal 1,191, ka onɛ da pʋn dɛŋim bɛ kʋk la zug ka o saŋa paae ka o lɛn nyi'ad nɛ o la mɛ da mɔri vɔɔt kal 353.
english: She won the poll with 1,191 votes, and her nearest contender, the incumbent, polled 353 votes.

kusaal: Samia aan o saam Kwame Nkrumah onɛ da an yiiga Ghana gɔmma zudaan nɛ o ma' Fathia Nkrumah bikanɛ tial ayi' o biis la wʋsa ni.
english: Samia is the second child and only daughter of Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first President and his Copt wife, Fathia Nkrumah.

kusaal: Kwame Nkrumah da an yiiga prim minista nɛ Ghana gɔmma zudaan onɛ da faaen Gold Coast yi nasanam la nu'usin ka mɔr faangir kena yʋma 1957.
english: Nkrumah was the first Prime Minister and President of Ghana, having led the Gold Coast to independence from Britain in 1957.

kusaal: On da an pan-Africanism kpɛɛm kanɛ zi'e li yɛla la, Nkrumah da an onɛ sʋ'oe bɛɛ naam Africa nɔɔr yinnɛ la'asʋg la ka an onɛ di Lenin sunmalisim ligidi la yit soviet union yʋma 1962 la ni.
english: An influential advocate of pan-Africanism, Nkrumah was a founding member of the Organization of African Unity and winner of the Lenin Peace Prize from the Soviet Union in 1962.

kusaal: Sania mɔr tanpa ayi'; ba anɛ Gamal Nkrumah nɛ Sekou Nkrumah.
english: Samia has two brothers, Gamal Nkrumah (born 1958) and Sekou Nkrumah (born 1963).

kusaal: O mɛ lɛn mɔri o taʋn kpɛɛm professor francis Nkrumah onɛ an sakur pa'an-pa'an kanɛ keŋ vʋ'ʋsʋm ka da lɛn an noguchi memorial institute tiima vɛɛnsʋg kpɛɛm bɛ Legon Ghana nwa ni.
english: She also has an older paternal half-brother, Professor Francis Nkrumah (1936–2024), a retired lecturer of medical sciences and consultant pediatrician, who previously worked as director of the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research in Legon, Ghana and the only child of his relationship with a Euro-African woman, Fanny Miller whom he was briefly married prior to furthering studies in the United Kingdom.

kusaal: Ka ban da nyaŋ yiis o saam nɛ Ghana yiiga sɔgianam paŋ zaba kanɛ da bɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ la nwadisa ayi' la li dabisim piiga daar la, samia mɛŋ nɛ o ma' nɛ o tanp la da kpɛn' lɔpit keŋ Cairo kanɛ bɛ Egypt teŋin la ka li anɛ Egypt zudaan Gamal Abel gɔmma la da mɔri ba keŋ anina ye ba ti zin'in ka ba saam la mɛ keŋ Guinea.
english: After her father was overthrown in Ghana's first successful military coup d'état on 24 February 1966, Samia, her mother, and her brothers, had to flee to Cairo, Egypt on a plane sent by Egyptian President, Gamal Abdel Nasser, to stay in the country while her father went into exile in Guinea.

kusaal: O ɛlli Micheal Melega onɛ an Italy Danish dim dau la.
english: She is married to Michele Melega, an Italian-Danish man.

kusaal: Ba mɔr biribiŋ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon kwame Thomas melega.
english: They have a son, Kwame Thomas Melega.

kusaal: Samia mi'i nɛ Arabic nɛ Italy nɛ Danish nɛ na'asaal pian'ad.
english: Samia is fluent in Arabic, Italian, Danish, and English.

kusaal: Wadmaanib vɔɔdʋg kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2008 la ni la, o da di Jomoro wadmaan kʋk la, ka li da anɛ o yiiga nyi'ab ka o da zi'en nyi'a.
english: In the 2008 parliamentary election, she won the Jomoro constituency seat on her first attempt.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana yiiga gɔmena zudaan kʋdʋg Kwame Nkrumah pu'ayua.
english: She is the daughter of Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, the first President of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da mʋgʋs o nɛ o ma' nɛ o tanp la ye ba yi Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm kpala daakanɛ ka mʋgʋsʋg nɛ paŋ zaba da duoe ye ba yiis Kwame Nkrumah kʋk la ni la.
english: She was forced to leave Ghana with her mother and brothers on the day of the 1966 military coup that overthrew Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Ka la'am nɛ lin da an si'em la, o da lɛn bas Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm la ya'as saŋkanɛ ka o ma' da gban'e bɛɛ bɔɔd ye o lɛb EGYIPT sʋ'ʋlʋm yʋma 1980 pin'ilʋgʋn sa la.
english: She was forced to leave Ghana with her mother and brothers on the day of the 1966 military coup that overthrew Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: li nya'aŋ ka o da gban'e o pʋtɛn'ɛr ye o dɔl NPP dim bɛ Ghana republic kanɛ aan anaasi la wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas anu la ni.
english: She decided on the latter, aligning with the NPP in the House of 5th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O paŋ bɛɛ o nyaŋir kanɛ ka o mɔr la la'as nɛ paati la pu'aba atan' yina zi'en nyatir ye ba vʋ'ʋg bɛɛ tɛndig CPP paati la, ka zi'en tis nɔɔr nyain wa'ae kati na'adɔɔg la da mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr ye li sʋŋ nɔbig pu'ab nɛ mɔr suor ka ba naa nyaŋir maan si'el la.
english: Being the only CPP member of parliament, she had to either align with NDC who were the majority in parliament or the minority NPP.

kusaal: Ka on da paam ya'an kaŋa la zug la, o da an pu'a kanɛ an yiiga sɔb lieb paati tita'ar kanɛ bɛ Ghana nwa ni kpɛɛm, tʋm ala hali ti paae yʋma 2015.
english: She served in this role until 2015.

kusaal: O da an labaya tʋmtʋn nɛ media consultant la'am nɛ Egypt media tʋʋma ni yʋma bɛdegʋ banɛ gaad.
english: She has worked many years as a journalist and media consultant, including in the Egyptian media space.

kusaal: Samiu Kwadwo Nuamah anɛ Ghana gbaʋŋ zamisid, engineer, nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Samiu Kwadwo Nuamah is a Ghanaian academic, engineer, and politician.

kusaal: O paas nɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nidib ni ka an wadmaani tis Kwadaso Constituency.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the incumbent Member of Parliament for the Kwadaso Constituency.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpisi nɛ anu daar (25 July), Nuamah yinɛ Tanoso, Kumasi sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Ashanti Region, Ghana.
english: Born on 25 July, Nuamah is from Tanoso, a suburb of Kumasi in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr engineering doctorate kasɛta gbaʋŋ (EngD) nɛ master's degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi University of Nottingham UK nɛ Cranfield University UK nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la, din nya'aŋ o da pa'al University of Ghana ka naan kpɛn' wadmaannib yin la yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2017).
english: He holds an engineering doctorate (EngD) and a master's degree from The University of Nottingham UK and Cranfield University UK respectively in Chemical Engineering, and subsequently lectured at University of Ghana before entering parliament in 2017.

kusaal: Burnya nya'aŋ nwadisa ayuobʋ la yʋma 2015 la ni la, Nuamah da nyi'a constituency wadmaannib gaansʋg la ka mɔr ti'ir ye o na paam vɔɔt ka ti nyaŋi zi'en constituency wadmaannib vɔɔdʋg la ni.
english: In June 2015, Nuamah contested the constituency primary with the hope of securing enough votes to allow him contest the constituency parliamentary election.

kusaal: Nidiba anu ka onɛ pʋn dɛŋim an wadmaan la Owusu Afriyie Akoto nɛ Josephine Hilda Addo, da nyi'a vɔɔdʋg la ni.
english: Five other people including the incumbent Owusu Afriyie Akoto and Josephine Hilda Addo, a former Member of Parliament for the constituency, contested the election.

kusaal: O da diya nɛ vɔɔt kal kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (191) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He won the election with 191 of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ka lin yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin, o da paam vɔɔt kal gaad Monica Buamah onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid la (National Democratic Congress), nɛ David Akwasi Adongo onɛ an PNC ( People's National Convention) nɛ Kwame Boateng Antwi onɛ an Nɔraʋg na'adɔɔg la nid (Convention People's Party) la ka zi'eni tis Kwadaso Constituency, Ghana wadmaanib yir la ni.
english: Out of 68541 votes cast in Ghana's general election, Nuamah won over 90% of the votes, beating his rivals Monica Buamah of the National Democratic Congress, David Akwasi Adongo of the People's National Convention and Kwame Boateng Antwi of the Convention People's Party to represent the Kwadaso Constituency in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Nuamah pʋ'a anɛ Nana Akosua Serwaa Nuamah ka o mɔr biig yinne nɛ o.
english: Nuamah is married to Naana Akosua Serwaa Nuamah and has two children with her.

kusaal: Yi vɔɔt tusa pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (68541) pʋʋgin Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni, Nuamah da paam vɔɔt ka di gaat piswai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (90%).
english: Out of 68541 votes cast in Ghana's general election, Nuamah won over 90% of the votes, beating his rivals Monica Buamah of the National Democratic Congress, David Akwasi Adongo of the People's National Convention and Kwame Boateng Antwi of the Convention People's Party to represent the Kwadaso Constituency in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Sampson Ahi anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas Ghana Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republi kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Bodi constituency teŋkanɛ bɛ Western region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Sampson Ahi is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Bodi constituency in the Western region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ahi nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa awai la dabpiinɛ anaasi daar (14 September 1976).
english: Ahi was born on 14 September 1976.

kusaal: O yinɛ Sefwi Bodi tenkanɛ bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Sefwi Bodi a town in the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di'e o Bachelor of Arts degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ nɛ University of Ghana, Legon ka di'e o Executive Masters in Governance and Leadership kasɛta gbaʋŋ (EMGL) yi Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).
english: He received his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Ghana, Legon and his Executive Masters in Governance and Leadership (EMGL) from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA).

kusaal: On da nam pʋ kpɛn' Wadmaanib yin la, Ahi da anɛ manager tis Armar Jaro din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la ni (2003) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la ni (2004).
english: Prior to entering parliament, Ahi worked as a sector manager for Armar Jaro from 2003 to 2004.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Deputy Minista kanɛ gɔsid tʋʋma nɛ ya maalʋg yɛla Mahama saŋa.
english: He was the Deputy Minister of Works and Housing under the Mahama administration.

kusaal: Ahi da kpɛn' Wadmaanib yin la nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la li daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2005) zi'eni tis Juabeso constituency dim.
english: Ahi entered parliament on 7 January 2005 representing the Juabeso constituency on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ tisi ba ala hali nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni kanɛ (2012) ka ba da maal wadmaan kʋk paal kanɛ an Bodi constituency sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He represented the constituency until 2012 when he stood for the seat of the then newly created Bodi constituency.

kusaal: Ahi mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa anu.
english: Ahi is married with five children.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis sʋ'ʋlim la ken paae zina.
english: He has been the member of parliament of the constituency to date.

kusaal: Sampson Tangombu Chiragia (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ Nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar, 24 October 1966) o anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: Sampson Tangombu Chiragia (born 24 October 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Navrongo Central Constituency bɛ Upper East Region, Ghana.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Navrongo Central Constituency in the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Chiragia yinɛ Navrongo.
english: Chiragia hails from Navrongo.

kusaal: O mɔr MBA in Financial management kasɛtta gbaʋŋ.
english: He holds an MBA in Financial management.

kusaal: Samuel Abdulai Jabanyite anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka da an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Chereponi Constituency teŋkanɛ bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim la, ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nɔba zug (National Democratic Congress).
english: Samuel Abdulai Jabanyite is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Chereponi Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yɔpɔi la ni ka ti Gaana Gɔmina Nana Addo Dankwah Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an Mininsta kanɛ an Chief of Staff la nya'andɔl, n gɔsid linɛ ken wυsa bɛ Gɔmina tυυma dɔɔgin la, o da mɔri yυυma piistan' nɛ atan' ka ba gaŋ o la, onɛ da yiiga onɛ an dasanpɔl n zi'en zi'esim kan ni yiiga.Nannanna onɛ an Minista onɛ gɔsid Lands and Natural Resources yɛla.
english: Former President Akufo-Addo nominated him as the Minister responsible for Lands and Natural Resources in his second term government.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Jinapor nɛ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ atan' la ni, saam yυ'υr buonɛ Abudulai Jinapor o da anɛ pulυŋ kpɛɛm n bɛ Buipe linɛ bɛ Gaana Savannah Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Samuel A. Jinapor was born in 1983 to Abdulai Jinapor, a former police officer and Chief of Buipe in the Savannah Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yυυm kanɛ ka o da naae la yim ka ba nɔk o tυυma n bɛ LLB at Ghana School of Law, Makola linɛ bɛ Ankara sυ'υlυm la.
english: That same year, he was admitted to read LLB at Ghana School of Law, Makola, Accra.

kusaal: Ka yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yi' la ni ka ba da buol o paas wada mi'ilim lυgυr dim la ni ye o an Solicitor and Barrister n bɛ ti Gaana Supreme Court la ni.
english: He was called to the Ghana Bar in 2012 as a Solicitor and Barrister of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology sakurin la naae ka di'e o Digirɛɛ kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Bachelor of Science in physics, linɛ ka o da zamisi li pυυgin anɛ Biomedical Physics.
english: He attended the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology and graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree in Physics but specialized in Biomedical Physics in 2006.

kusaal: O zi'en ti Gaana nɔba zug n bɛ temis kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb n pian'a kati wa'ae Solicitor nɛ Legal yɛla, both in.
english: Over the years, he had the rare opportunity of representing major foreign companies in Ghana as a Solicitor and Legal Advocate, both in Ghanaian Courts and Arbitral Tribunals.

kusaal: O yiiga na'asaa teŋ ken la ni ka o mɔri yυυma piisi nɛ atan', o da paam suory hali babυga n dɔl ti Gaana Gɔmina kυdυg John Agyekum Kufour keŋ United Kingdom (UK) nɔɔrim babυg yυυma tusa yi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni n an onɛ pian'adi tisid Gɔmina la hali ka o yɛla da yi na'asaa sɔɔngin na hali ka nidib mɔri gɔsid.
english: His political activism earned him the opportunity at the age of 23 to accompany the then President of the Republic, His Excellency, John Agyekum Kufour, on a State Visit to the United Kingdom (UK) in 2007.

kusaal: Samuel Abu Jinapor anɛ lawyer ka an Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd, ba da du'anɛ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisnii nɛ atan' la ni.
english: In the 2016 general elections, Samuel Abu Jinapor, played a major political advocacy role for the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and candidate, Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid ka an wadmaan n tis Damongo sυ'υlυm la.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and the Member of Parliament for the Damongo Constituency.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' nɛ ayuobu ka o da keŋ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology sakurin la naae ka di'e o Digirɛɛ kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Bachelor of Science in physics.
english: He attended the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology and graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree in Physics but specialized in Biomedical Physics in 2006.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' nɛ anii la ni ka o da lɛn tɔlis University of Ghana sakurin la naae yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piiga la ni ka di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Bachelor of Laws.
english: He proceeded to the University of Ghana in 2008 where he earned a Bachelor of Laws in 2010.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛn mɔr Master of Laws linɛ an Alternative Dispute Resolution n yi Faculty of Law, University Of Ghana sakur la ni.
english: He proceeded to the University of Ghana in 2008 where he earned a Bachelor of Laws in 2010.

kusaal: yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yi' la ni ka ba da buol o paas wada mi'ilim lυgυr dim la ni ye o an Solicitor and Barrister n bɛ ti Gaana Supreme Court la ni.
english: He was called to the Ghana Bar in 2012 as a Solicitor and Barrister of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛn mɔr Master of Laws (LL.M) linɛ an Alternative Dispute Resolution n yi Faculty of Law, University Of Ghana sakur la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yɔpɔi la ni.
english: He proceeded to the University of Ghana in 2008 where he earned a Bachelor of Laws in 2010.

kusaal: O da zamisnɛ yi tutelage onɛ da aan o mɛŋ lawyer nyari la, Yonny Kulendi, onɛ yυ'υn an Justice n bɛ ti Gaana Supreme Court la ni.
english: He was called to the Ghana Bar in 2012 as a Solicitor and Barrister of the Supreme Court of Ghana.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yuobu la vɔt la ni , ka girima daan Jinapor da nwɛ'ɛ pɔlitiks hali tisi Akufo-Addo ka Gaana dim wυsa da wυm o labaar.
english: Having worked, closely, in various capacities with President Akufo-Addo, both in opposition and government, Mr. Jinapor has gained considerable experience in the workings of government.

kusaal: Yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yɔpɔi la ni ka Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an Minista kanɛ an Chief of Staff la nya'andɔl n gɔsid tυυmbanɛ bɛ Gɔmina tυυma dɔɔgin la.
english: In 2017, President Akufo-Addo appointed him as Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Operations at the Office of the President.

kusaal: O da tυm zi'es kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb hali tisi ti Gɔmina Akufo-Addo, o paam tυυma mi'ilim hali n yi Gɔmina ni.
english: In July 2024, he was appointed the Oversight Minister for Energy by President Akufo-Addo following the resignation of Dr. Mathew Opoku-Prempeh, following his nomination as Vice Presidential Candidate for the ruling New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Naada D.B. Jinapor, onɛ an Lawyer ka an head of the Corporate Law tυυma dim la nɛ Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) dim la.
english: He is happily married to Mrs. Naada D. B. Jinapor, a Lawyer and head of the Corporate Law Department of the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) of Ghana and their marriage is blessed with four (4) daughters and a son.

kusaal: O ya'am da bɛ Gaana nɔbig yɛla la zug da kɛ ka o kpɛn' pɔlitiks yυυma tusa yi' nɛ anaasi la ni, ani ka nidib wυsa da pian'a o ye o mɔr mi'ilim hali kati wa'ae pɔlitiks yɛla.
english: His interest in Ghana's public affairs encouraged him to join politics in 2004.

kusaal: O mɔri o mastɛs gbaʋŋ pa'alʋg kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit University of cape coast nɛ o mastɛs of Arts in pedagogy yit university kan ni nɔɔ.
english: He obtained a master's degree in education at the University of Cape Coast and a Master of Arts in pedagogy at the same university.

kusaal: Samuel da pin'il o pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb ka anɛ wadmaanib yir nid yʋma 2005 la ni, ban da pa'al onɛ di ya'an bɛ Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2004 la ni nya'aŋ la.
english: Samuel began his political career as a member of parliament in 2005 after he emerged winner at the 2004 Ghanaian General Elections.

kusaal: O da di ka bas John kwekucher Achah onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid ka mɔr vɔɔt kal 16,358 ka li an 41.70% kɔbʋg pʋʋgin yit vɔɔtnam la wʋsa ni, ka Ebenezer Ebb kweku Bankwa onɛ an PNC nid ka mɔr vɔɔt kal 854 ka li an 2.20% kɔbʋg pʋʋgin yit vɔɔtnam la wʋsa ni.
english: He won with 22,059 representing 56.20% out of the total valid votes, he defeated John Kwekucher Ackah of the National Democratic Congress who gained 16,358 representing 41.70% of the total votes and Ebenezer Ebb Kwaku Bankwa of the People's National Convention with 854 votes representing 2.20% of the total votes.

kusaal: La'am nɛ nɛ'ɛnam wʋsaa, Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2008 la ni la, o da kɔ'ɔŋ kʋk la ka mathias Kwame Ntow onɛ an ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg nid la di.
english: However, during the 2008 Ghanaian general elections he lost the seat to Mathias Kwame Ntow of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ka teŋ la da pin'il ye ba mɔri ba mɛŋ constituency nɛ ba mɛŋ wadmaan yʋma 2004 la ni la, onɛ da an yiiga sɔb di kʋk la.
english: He was the first person to represent his constituency after it was established in 2004.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt gaŋ o ka o paas Ghana republic kanɛ aan anaasi wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas anaasi la ni la, samanpiid nwadig la li daba ayɔpɔi daar yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi la ni (samanpiid nwadig 7, 2004) wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug.
english: He was elected into the 4th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana on 7 December 2004 on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da di vɔɔdʋg la nɛ vɔɔt kal 22,059 ka li an 56.20% kɔbʋg pʋʋgin yit vɔɔtnam la wʋsa ni.
english: He won with 22,059 representing 56.20% out of the total valid votes, he defeated John Kwekucher Ackah of the National Democratic Congress who gained 16,358 representing 41.70% of the total votes and Ebenezer Ebb Kwaku Bankwa of the People's National Convention with 854 votes representing 2.20% of the total votes.

kusaal: Ka yʋma 2019 kanɛ gaad la, pan- Africa dim da mɔr piini bɛdegʋ ka la'am nɛ BORGCA dim ka ba pʋr o yʋ'ʋsʋŋ ye onɛ an municipal chief executive sʋŋ tis o sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: In 2019, awards organised by the Pan- African Heroes of change in collaboration with the Bureau of Research on Governance Commerce and Administration (BORGCA), named Gyamfi as the best Municipal Chief Executive for the Aowin constituency.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ University of Ghana, Legon la ka naae ka paam Bachelor of Arts degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ linɛ anɛ Wada nɛ Philosophy tʋʋma yɛla yʋma 1989 la ni.
english: He attended the University of Ghana, Legon and graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Law and Philosophy in 1989.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ Ghana wada sakurin la n paam o wada kasɛta gbaŋ yʋma 1993 la ni.
english: He proceeded to the Ghana School of Law and obtained his practising license in 1993.

kusaal: O da yuolim keŋ la'as nɛ A-sʋ'oe-mɛŋ wada Lʋgir la, Akufo-Addo Prempeh & Co Accra teŋin.
english: He later joined the private law firm, Akufo-Addo, Prempeh & Co in Accra.

kusaal: Atta Kyea da kpɛn' Pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛb nɛ yʋma 2008 la ni, ba da vɔɔt tis o ka o li'eb wadmaan tis Abuakwa Ya-Tuon.
english: Atta Akyea entered politics in 2008 when he was elected the parliamentarian for the Abuakwa South constituency.

kusaal: Atta Kyea da lɛn zi'en ya'as kʋk kan la ni nɔ'ɔr ayi' bɛ yʋma 2012 la ni nɛ yʋma 2016 vɔɔdʋg la ni.
english: Atta Akyea went on to retain his seat in the 2012, 2016 and 2020 elections.

kusaal: Wadmaanib yir la ni la, o tʋm committee tʋʋma bɛdegʋ la'am paas Finance nɛ Public Accounts Judiciary nɛ Appointments Committee la.
english: In parliament, he has served on various committees including the Finance, Public Accounts, Judiciary and Appointments Committees.

kusaal: O da paam nɛ vɔɔt kanl tusa pisi nɛ anii nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayi' (28,442) ka li an pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii nɛ du'al ayɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbʋg pʋʋgin vɔɔdʋg la wusa ni , Owuraku Amofaha kanɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la, paam vɔɔt kal tusa ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (7,697) ka li an pisi nɛ yinne nɛ du'alʋg atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general election, he won the Abuakwa South Constituency parliamentary seat with 28,442 votes making 78.7.61% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Owuraku Amofah had 7,697 votes making 21.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Sanusi Mohammed da mɔri vɔɔt kanl 7,740 ka li an 19.6% kɔbʋg pʋʋgin, ka Bannieng-Peprah Felix onɛ an GUM wadmaanib yir nid la mɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal 957 ka li an 2.4% kɔbʋg pʋʋgin, ka Marfo Enoch Kwame onɛ nyati ka pʋ dɔl paati si'a la nid mɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal 905 ka li an 2.3% kɔbʋg pʋʋgin.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general election, he again won the Abuakwa South Constituency parliamentary seat with 29,897 votes making 75.7% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Sanusi Mohammed had 7,740 votes making 19.6% of the total votes cast, the GUM parliamentary candidate Banning-Peprah Felix had 957 votes making 2.4% of the total votes cast and an Independent parliamentary candidate Marfo Enock Kwame had 905 votes making 2.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Atta Kyea anɛ Kukdaan tis mines nɛ Energy Kɔmatii, Subsidiary Legislation Kɔmatii nid ka mɛ lɛn a Special Budget Kɔmatii nid.
english: He is also a member of the Subsidiary Legislation and Special Budget Committees.

kusaal: Vaanla Nwadig la yʋma 2022 la ni, nidib da kadi o yiis Abuakwa vɔɔdʋg teŋin la.
english: In March 2022, he was chased out by the people in the Abuakwa South Constituency.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana lɔya yinne ka mɛ nwɛ'ɛd Pɔlitis.
english: He was the Member of Parliament of Akim Abuakwa South constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana between 2009 and 2025.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (NPP) la nid .
english: He was the Member of Parliament of Akim Abuakwa South constituency in the Eastern Region of Ghana between 2009 and 2025.

kusaal: O da anɛ Minista onɛ gɔsid Tʋʋma nɛ Ya' maalʋg yɛla (Minister for Works and Housing) hali ti paae yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la ni yʋma 2021, ka an Wadmaanɛ tis Akim Abuakwa Ya-Tuona sʋ'ʋlim (Member of parliament for Akim Abuakwa Constituency).
english: He was the Minister for Works and Housing from 2017 until January 2021.

kusaal: On ma'aa pa' Nana Akufo-Addo lieb Wadmaan (MP) sʋ'ʋlin kan la Republic kanɛ paas anaasi la.
english: He is the second person aside Nana Akufo-Addo to be elected as MP for that constituency in the 4th republic.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ Kebi teŋkanɛ bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana nwa ni.
english: He was born in Kyebi in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: On da naae Wada sakur la, o da paam tʋʋma an State Attorney n bɛ Attorney General Department la ni.
english: After being called to the Bar in 1994, Atta Akyea was employed as a state attorney at the Attorney General's Department.

kusaal: Yʋma1995 la ni la, o da keŋ la'as A-sʋ'oeg-mɛŋ wada lʋgir si'a ya'as, Zoe Akyea & Co., ani ka ba da maal o ba tʋm-tʋm tiraan yinne ka o tʋm yʋʋm piina anaasi.
english: In 2003, he founded the law firm, Zoe Akyea & Co. He worked there as head of Chamber until 2008 when he left legal practice for politics.

kusaal: O da bas A-sʋ'oe-mɛŋ wada tʋʋma la ni ka keŋ li'a gɔmena na'am vɔɔdʋg kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2008 Abuakwa Ya-Tuon la.
english: Atta Akyea entered politics in 2008 when he was elected the parliamentarian for the Abuakwa South constituency.

kusaal: O da len nyi'a ya'as nɛ nidib ayi' banɛ yʋda an Samuel Osei onɛ an Ma'asim Tiig Na'dɔɔg la nid nɛ Nana Addo Aikins, onɛ da zi'eni an A-sʋ'oe-mɛŋ paati la.
english: He competed against two other aspirants, namely, Sammy Osei of the National Democratic Congress and Nana Addo Aikins, an Independent candidate.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2016 la ni la,saŋa la o da di Abuakwa sʋ'ʋlim wadmaan na'am kʋk la.
english: In the 2016 Ghanaian general election, he won the Abuakwa South Constituency parliamentary seat with 28,442 votes making 78.7.61% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Owuraku Amofah had 7,697 votes making 21.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2020 la ni la, o da lɛn di ya'anɛ nɔk Abuakwa sʋ'ʋlim wadmaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kanl 29,897 ka li an 75.7% vɔɔdʋg la wʋsa ni ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: In the 2020 Ghanaian general election, he again won the Abuakwa South Constituency parliamentary seat with 29,897 votes making 75.7% of the total votes cast whilst the NDC parliamentary candidate Sanusi Mohammed had 7,740 votes making 19.6% of the total votes cast, the GUM parliamentary candidate Banning-Peprah Felix had 957 votes making 2.4% of the total votes cast and an Independent parliamentary candidate Marfo Enock Kwame had 905 votes making 2.3% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Birim Kɔldaaʋg la anɛ linɛ dɔli yit o sʋ'ʋlim la ni n sʋŋid Ghana teŋ la nɛ ku'om.
english: The Birim river which passes through his constituency is a major river body in Ghana and supplies a substantial amount of the constituency's water requirement.

kusaal: Yʋma 2021 la ni la, o da anɛ kɔmatii nid yinne onɛ ka ba da gaŋ o la.
english: In 2021, Atta Akyea was made Chairperson of the Mines and Energy Committee.

kusaal: Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la yʋma 2017 la ni la, Ghana Zugraan Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an Tʋʋma nɛ Ya maalʋg yɛla Minista linɛ paas o nɔɔr ayi' minista zi'esim ni.
english: He was sworn in along with eleven other ministers by President Akufo-Addo on 8 February 2017 at the Jubilee House.

kusaal: Vaala Nwadig yʋma 2020 ni, o da mor la'adbanɛ an a-gu'u ban'a keŋ tis o teŋ Sʋ'ʋlim la ye o zab na'asar dankɔŋ ban'a la.
english: In March 2020, he presented some sanitary products to his constituency in the fight against COVID-19 pandemic.

kusaal: O di pu'a ka mɔr biis atan' ka an karimbiig.
english: He is married with three children and is a Christian.

kusaal: Li da anɛ ye o da pʋ pidis o kaanbʋg la tis nidib la.
english: It was alleged he failed to honor his campaign promises to the people.

kusaal: Samuel Atta Mills (du'am yʋʋm anɛ 26 Vaala/Nwadisanu 1956) anɛ Ghana pɔlits nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni zi'eni tis Komenda Edina Eguafo Abrem Constituency bɛ Central Region la.
english: Samuel Atta Mills is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Komenda Edina Eguafo Abrem Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ Kissi bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Mills was born on Thursday 26 April 1956 and hails from Kissi in the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋi o secondary School nɛ Mfantsipim School, ani ka o da di'e o GCE kasɛtta gbaʋŋ.
english: He had his secondary education at Mfantsipim School, where he obtained his GCE Certificate.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ Komenda College sakur tita'ar la ni ani ka o da di'e pa'an kasɛta gbaʋŋ (Diploma in Education).
english: He proceeded to Komenda College where he obtained a Diploma in Education.

kusaal: On da keŋ Komenda la zugɔ, Mills da paam suori keŋ Belmont University zamis ka ba da tis o BBA in Economics and Accounting kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (1984), nɛ o MBA in Finance and Banking kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1986) la ni.
english: Following his studies at Komenda, Mills enrolled at Belmont University where he was awarded his BBA in Economics and Accounting in 1984, and his MBA in Finance and Banking in 1986.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ lieb Wadmaan la, Mills da tʋmnɛ Ghana Tourism Development Company la ni ka aan ba chief executive officer yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ atan' la ni (2003) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: Prior to entering parliament, Mills worked at the Ghana Tourism Development Company as the chief executive officer from 2003 to 2005.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu kanɛ da gaad la ni (2005), o da naam Panera Bread la ni lieb Regional Manager.
english: In 2005, he joined Panera Bread as a Regional Manager.

kusaal: O da tʋmnɛ ala paae ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni (2009) ka ba gaŋ o ye o an onɛ sʋŋid gɔmma zudaan John Atta Mills.
english: He worked in this capacity until 2009 when he was appointed Presidential Aide to the then president John Atta Mills.

kusaal: O da lɛn tʋm nɛ First American Bank la ni ka an kpɛɛmkanɛ gɔsidi ba ligipɛmisa yɛla.
english: He once worked at First American Bank as a Commercial Loans Manager.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔdʋg la ni la, o da di Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abirem Constituency Wadmaan kʋk la.
english: During the 2016 Ghanaian general election, he won the Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abirem Constituency parliamentary seat.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt kal tusa pisi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi (21,957) ka li an pistan' nɛ anii du'ali anaasi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin la (38.4%), ka Stephen Nana Ato Arthur onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg(NPP) nid la, mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ anu nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ (15,960) ka li an pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi du'ali awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (27.9%), ka John Sterlin onɛ an PPP nid la, mɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ anii nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ (18,860) ka li an pistan' nɛ atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (33.0%), Mrs.
english: He won with 21,957 votes making 38.4% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Stephen Nana Ato Arthur had 15,960 votes making 27.9% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate John Sterlin had 18,860 votes making 33.0% of the total votes cast, and the CPP parliamentary candidate Mrs. Rose Austin Tenadu had 410 votes making 0.7% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: O da paas la'askanɛ gɔsid suoya nɛ la'ad ziib nam yɛla (Roads and Transport Committee), ka lɛn an kʋkdaan nya'adɔli tis la'askanɛ gɔsid nidibi tuunsid ban di gɔmena ligidi si'em (Public Accounts Committee).
english: He is a member of the Roads and Transport Committee, and the vice chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt kal tusa pisi nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (26,886) ka li an pisnaasi nɛ ayi' du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbʋg pʋʋgʋn la (42.7%), ka Samuel Joe Acquah, onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg (NPP) nid la paam vɔɔt kal tusa pisi nɛ atan' nɛ pistan' nɛ awai (23,039) ka li an pistan' nɛ ayuobʋ du'ali ayuobʋ (36.6%), ka GUM nid Abubakr Sadiq Cann mɛ mɔr vɔɔt kal tusir nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ ayi' (1,122) ka li an yinne du'ali anii kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (1.8%), ka John Sterlin onɛ an Anɔraʋg na'adɔɔg nid la (PPP) paam vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi (11,964) ka li an pii nɛ awai kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (19.0%).
english: Mills retained the Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abirem seat during the 2020 Ghanaian general election polling a total of 26,886 votes making 42.7% of the total votes cast against Samuel Joe Acquah, the NPP parliamentary candidate who had 23,039 votes making 36.6% of the total votes cast and the GUM parliamentary candidate Abubakr Sadiq Cann had 1,122 votes making 1.8% of the total votes cast, and the PPP parliamentary candidate John Sterlin had 11,964 votes making 19.0% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Mills anɛ Kristo biig ka ken Methodist pʋ'ʋsʋm, Ghana.
english: Mills is a Christian and a member of the Methodist Church of Ghana.

kusaal: Mills anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg (National Democratic Congress) nid.
english: Mills is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Rose Austin Tenadu onɛ an Anɔraʋg Na'adɔɔg (CPP) nid la paam vɔɔt kal kɔbisnaasi nɛ piiga (410) ka li an nɛɛm du'ali ayɔpɔi (0.7%).
english: He won with 21,957 votes making 38.4% of the total votes cast whilst the NPP parliamentary candidate Stephen Nana Ato Arthur had 15,960 votes making 27.9% of the total votes cast, the PPP parliamentary candidate John Sterlin had 18,860 votes making 33.0% of the total votes cast, and the CPP parliamentary candidate Mrs. Rose Austin Tenadu had 410 votes making 0.7% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt Mills Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abirem yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: Mills retained the Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abirem seat during the 2020 Ghanaian general election polling a total of 26,886 votes making 42.7% of the total votes cast against Samuel Joe Acquah, the NPP parliamentary candidate who had 23,039 votes making 36.6% of the total votes cast and the GUM parliamentary candidate Abubakr Sadiq Cann had 1,122 votes making 1.8% of the total votes cast, and the PPP parliamentary candidate John Sterlin had 11,964 votes making 19.0% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: o ba'abiigi an Ghana gɔmena zudaan kʋdʋg John Atta Mills.
english: He is the brother of the late ex-president John Atta Mills.

kusaal: Samuel Ayeh-Paye anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn an mp tis Seventh Parliament bɛ Fourth Republic of Ghana tisid Ayensuano Constituency bɛ Eastern Region bɛ New Patriotic Party.
english: Samuel Ayeh-Paye is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Ayensuano Constituency in the Eastern Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Samuel du'am yʋʋm anɛ Alamis daar, 17 May 1973 ka yit Aburi, Eastern Region of Ghana.
english: Samuel was born on Thursday, 17 May 1973 and he hails from Aburi, Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Din yi yʋma 1999 ti paae yʋma 2000 la ni la, o da anɛ transport manager bɛ Accra Metropolitan Assembly tʋmi bɛ Waste Management Department, o mɛ da lɛn anɛ workshop manager din yi yʋma 2003 ti paae yʋma 2005 bɛ Metro Mass Transit in Ghana.
english: From 1999 to 2000, He was a transport manager in the Accra Metropolitan Assembly working at Waste Management Department He became a workshop manager from 2003 to 2005 at Metro Mass Transit in Ghana.

kusaal: Din yi sankan la o da anɛ assistant technical manager din yi yʋma 2005 ti paae yʋma 2008 bɛ DVLA in Ghana.
english: From there he became an assistant technical manager from 2005 to 2008 at DVLA in Ghana.

kusaal: O da paas 5th, 6th nɛ 7th parliament bɛ 4th Republic .o da anɛ wadmaan (MP) din da yi yʋma 2009 ti paae yʋma 2021 la ni.
english: He has been a member of the 5th, 6th and 7th parliament of the 4th Republic haven been a member of parliament from 2009 to 2021.

kusaal: Ka dawalʋg nwadig 2017 la ni, o da bɔɔd ye ba vɔɔti bɛ Upper Chamber ye ba lɛbis Council of State la.
english: In March 2017, he called for an elected Upper Chamber to replace the Council of State.

kusaal: O mɔr HND kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ Accra Polytechnic (nannana ka li yʋ'ʋn an Accra Technical University) bɛ Accra, Ghana.
english: He has an HND at Accra Polytechnic located in Accra (now Accra Technical University) located at Accra, Ghana.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr MVM training kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ Accra Technical Training Center (ATTC) Ghana, nɛ kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ Indian Institute of Management Studies India sʋ'ʋlʋm .
english: He also had an MVM training from Accra Technical Training Center (ATTC) located at Accra, Ghana, and a certificate at Indian Institute of Management Studies in India.

kusaal: Onɛ an DVLA officer kʋdʋg laa, o pian'a bɛ wadmaanib yir tis suosʋma yɛla.
english: As a former DVLA officer, he has spoken in Parliament on the need for better road safety measures.

kusaal: Samuel mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis anaasi.
english: Samuel is married with four children.

kusaal: Samuel Erickson Abakah (dʋ'anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai Nwadis piiga la dabpiiga daar (10 October 1959) o anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka paas Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la ni, New Patriotic Party ni.
english: Samuel Erickson Abakah (born 10 October 1959) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Shama Constituency bɛ Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: He was the member of parliament for the Shama Constituency, in the Western Region of Ghana From 7 January 2021 to 6 January 2025.

kusaal: Abakah yinɛ Abuesi.
english: Abakah hails from Abuesi and is a barrister who qualified in 2000.

kusaal: Girimadaan Samuel Nartey George (Ba da du'a o nɛ 22 January 1985) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Samuel Nartey George (born 22 January 1985) is a Ghanaian politician and a lawyer.

kusaal: O yinɛ Ahwiam, bɛ Old Ningo.
english: He is from Ahwiam, Old Ningo.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Sam Nartey George nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anu yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la dabpisi nɛ ayi' daar (22 January 1985) Somanya bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana la.
english: Sam Nartey George was born on 22 January 1985 in Somanya in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o BSc.
english: He obtained a BSc.

kusaal: O mɔr Executive Masters kasɛta gbaʋŋ (Dissertation) (Conflict, Peace, and Security) dinɛ ka o paam yi Kofi Anann International Peacekeeping and Training Centre (KAIPTC).
english: He has an Executive Master (Dissertation) in Conflict, Peace, and Security) from the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping and Training Center (KAIPTC).

kusaal: yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ ayi' Nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la ni la (December 2022), o da maali o MSc in International Strategy and Diplomacy London School of Economics and Political Science.
english: In December 2022, he graduated with an MSc in International Strategy and Diplomacy from the London School of Economics and Political Science.

kusaal: Sam Nartey George da anɛ assistant director bɛ Office of the Head of Civil Service yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piiga (2010) ken paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (2014) ka lɛn an onɛ pian'adi bɛ pirɛsidɛn ɔfisin yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi (2014) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016).
english: Sam Nartey George was an assistant director at the Office of the Head of Civil Service from 2010 to 2014 and a communications specialist at the office of the President from 2014 to 2016.

kusaal: Vɔɔdʋg kanɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anu Nwadis pii nɛ yinne dabpisi nɛ yinne daar la, (21 November 2015) Sam Georg da yis Wadmaan kanɛ zi'eni tis Ningo-Prampram dim la, Girmadaan Enoch Teye Mensah (MP 1996-2015) Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, NDC Na'am li'abin ka zi'eni nyi'a yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Wadmaanib vɔɔdʋg la ni.
english: On 21 November 2015, Sam George defeated the incumbent Member of Parliament for Ningo-Prampram Hon. Enoch Teye Mensah (MP from 1996 to 2015) in the NDC primaries for a chance to represent the party in the 2016 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: O da diya nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa anaasi nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiga (4,910) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ atan' du'ali anaasi (53.4%) ka E. T. Mensah paam vɔɔt kal tusa ayi' nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pistan' nɛ yinne (2,831) dinɛ an pistan' nɛ anii du'ali anu kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (38.5%).
english: He won with 4,910 votes, representing 53.4% of total votes, while E. T. Mensah polled 2,831, representing 38.5%.

kusaal: Sam George da paas nɛ Public Accounts Committee nɛ Communications Committee.
english: Sam George is a member of the Public Accounts Committee and the Communications Committee.

kusaal: O anɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: He is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anu la Nwadis piinɛ yinɛ (November 2015) la ni, o da lub onɛ zin'i kʋk la zug, E. T. Mensah ka zi'en Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la zug nyi'a yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ( 2016 Wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la) Ningo-Prampram Constituency sʋ'ʋlim.
english: On 21 November 2015, Sam George defeated the incumbent Member of Parliament for Ningo-Prampram Hon. Enoch Teye Mensah (MP from 1996 to 2015) in the NDC primaries for a chance to represent the party in the 2016 parliamentary elections.

kusaal: O paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Ningo-Prampram constituency dim.
english: He again won the 2020 Ghanaian general election and the 2024 Ghanaian general election and is currently a member of the ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Ningo-Prampram constituency.

kusaal: in Agricultural Engineering (Soil & Water Engineering) nɛ KNUST, ka maali o L.L.B kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ University of London.
english: in Agricultural Engineering (Soil & Water Engineering) from KNUST and an L.L.B from the University of London (External).

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi vɔɔdʋg la ni la, George da di Ningo-Prampram Constituency Wamaan kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pisi nɛ atan' nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ (23, 860) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (63%) ka Mr.
english: In the 2020 election, George was declared the winner of the Ningo-Prampram Constituency parliamentary Elections by polling 23,860 votes representing 63% to defeat his closest contender, Sylvester Tetteh of the NPP, who polled 13,588 votes.
