english: In the 2020 election, George was declared the winner of the Ningo-Prampram Constituency parliamentary Elections by polling 23,860 votes representing 63% to defeat his closest contender, Sylvester Tetteh of the NPP, who polled 13,588 votes.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) la ni la, on nɛ Wadmaan sieba da yina ye, ba yiisim wada kanɛ na pa'al ye daʋ nɛ daʋ digin taaba ka pʋ'a nɛ pʋ'a digin taaba la bas, LGBTI anɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.
english: In 2021, George threatened to assault Australian High Commissioner Gregory Andrews for his support of the LGBTQI community.

kusaal: Sam George anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Sam George is a Christian and married.

kusaal: Samuel Nsowah-Djan anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd onɛ an Seventh Parliament bɛ Fourth Republic of Ghana tisid Upper Denkyira West Constituency dinɛ bɛ Central Region bɛ Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la nid .
english: Samuel Nsowah-Djan is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Upper Denkyira West Constituency in the Central Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

english: Samuel was born on 26 June 1961.

english: He was also the CEO of Nsowah Mining Company Limited in Dunkwa-On-Offin.

kusaal: Ka yʋma 2015 la ni NPP parliamentary primaries, o da zi'en nyi'a ka lub Benjamin Kofi Ayeh onɛ zi'en nɛ o la .
english: During the 2015 NPP parliamentary primaries, he contested and defeated the Incumbent Benjamin Kofi Ayeh.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2016 la ni la, Samuel di bɛ Upper Denkyira West Constituency wadmaan kʋk la.
english: During the 2016 Ghanaian general election, Samuel won the Upper Denkyira West Constituency parliamentary seat.

kusaal: Samuel da lu bɛ Ghana vɔɔdʋg kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2020 la ni la ka Daniel Ohene Darko onɛ an NDC na'adɔɔg nid la di Upper Denkyira West Constituency wadmaan kʋk la.
english: Samuel lost the Upper Denkyira West Constituency parliamentary seat during the 2020 Ghanaian general election to the NDC parliamentary candidate Daniel Ohene Darko.

kusaal: O da lu nɛ vɔɔt kal 17,925 ka mɔr 49.3% yi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ka Daniel mɔr vɔɔt kal 18,446 ka mɔr 50.7% kɔbʋg pʋʋgin .
english: He lost with 17,925 votes making 49.3% of the total votes cast whilst Daniel had 18,446 votes making 50.7% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: COVID-19 wiim saŋa la Ghana nwa ni la, o da tis la'ad nwɛnnɛ bu'atanam nɛ ku'om laas nɛ thermometer guns nɛ hand sanitizers nɛ PPEs tis Upper Denkyira West District Health Directorate.
english: During the COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana, he presented items such as Veronica buckets, water basins, thermometer guns, hand sanitizers and other PPEs to the Upper Denkyira West District Health Directorate.

kusaal: Samuel anɛ karimbiig .
english: Samuel is a Christian.

english: He built mechanized boreholes in Aburi, Gyaman and Kakyerenyansa.

english: Ablakwa was born on 11 August 1980 in Aveyime-Battor in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da keŋ nɛ Presbyterian Boy's Secondary school –Legon (PRESEC).
english: He attended the Presbyterian Boys' Secondary School, Legon (Presec-Legon), where he served as Vice President of the Scripture Union.

kusaal: O da keŋ nɛ sakur tita'ar linɛ ka ba buon ye University of Ghana la ka di'e kasɛta gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka ba buon ye Bachelor of Arts, zamis kanɛ an Political Science nɛ Philosophy la yʋma 2002 ti paae yʋma 2006 la ni.
english: He studied Political Science and Philosophy at the University of Ghana, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree.

kusaal: O mɛ da keŋ sakur tita'ar linɛ bɛ Nasaa teŋ ka ba buon ye University of Leicester la ka zamis Labaya Tisib yɛla (Communication Media) nɛ A-tu'asi tis Wʋrʋg (Public Relations) ka di'e Master of Arts in Communication kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: He later pursued a Master of Arts in communication, Media and Public Relations at the University of Leicester.

kusaal: Ablakwa mɛ mɔr Tuongaadʋg tʋʋma (Leadership) kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit Harvard Kennedy Sakur linɛ zamisid Gɔmina tʋʋma yɛla USA nɛ Master of Science in Defense and International Politics Ghana Sogianam Sakur kanɛ Zamisid soogia kpɛɛmnam la.
english: He also holds a certificate in leadership from the Harvard Kennedy School of Governance and a Master of Science degree in Defense and International Politics from the Ghana Armed Forces Command and Staff College.

kusaal: On da bɛ Univesiti linɛ bɛ Ghana legon la, o da anɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa Univesti sakurbibis linɛ ka ba buon ye National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) la kpɛɛm din yi yʋma 2005 ti paae yʋma 2006 la ni.
english: While at the University of Ghana, Ablakwa served as President of the National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) from 2005 to 2006.

kusaal: O mɛ da anɛ Committe for Joint Action (CJA) banɛ gɔsid ka gɔmina tʋm linɛ nari tisid Ghana nidib la.
english: He was also involved in drafting youth policies for the NDC's 2008 election manifesto and was a member of the Committee for Joint Action (CJA), a pressure group advocating for economic and social reforms.

kusaal: O mɛ anɛ kpɛɛm Komitii kanɛ gɔsid Ghana tʋʋm nɛ Teŋzʋna yɛla (Ranking Member of Parliament Foreign Affairs).
english: As a Member of Parliament, he has served on the Appointments Committee and is the Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee.

kusaal: Saavi Solutions tʋʋma Kpɛɛm (2007-2009)
english: Managing Director, Savvi Solutions (2007–2009)

kusaal: O pu'a anɛ Nuhela Seidu onɛ saamme an Mumuni Seidu ka o an lɔya.
english: Ablakwa is married to Nuhela Seidu, a lawyer and daughter of the late Mumuni Abudu Seidu.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaan tis North Tongu district linɛ bɛ Volta Region O da anɛ deputy minister saŋa kanɛ ka John Atta Mills nɛ John Dramani Mahama da an Ghana Zugraannam la.
english: He previously served as Deputy Minister for Information and Deputy Minister for Education during the administrations of Presidents John Atta Mills and Mahama.

kusaal: Onɛ da an kpɛɛm kanɛ da gɔsid Karimbiis la'asʋg linɛ buon ye Scripture Union la nya'andɔl.
english: He attended the Presbyterian Boys' Secondary School, Legon (Presec-Legon), where he served as Vice President of the Scripture Union.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg la paati la zi'esim nyi'a North Tongu wadmaan kʋk la yɛla Nasaa yʋʋm 2008 la ni.
english: Ablakwa was first elected to Parliament in 2012, winning the North Tongu seat with 90.5% of valid votes cast.

kusaal: O da lɛn dii o kʋk la yʋma 2016 la ni, amaa o paati zugraan da pʋ dii.
english: He was re-elected in the 2016, 2020, and 2024 general elections.

kusaal: wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas a yuobʋ la ni la ka Ablakwa da paas banɛ vɛɛnsidi gaansid gɔmina tʋmtʋm banɛ ka Ghana Zugraan gaŋ ye ba tʋm tʋʋm sieba la.
english: In 2009, Ablakwa was appointed Deputy Minister for Information at age 28, becoming one of the youngest ministers in Ghana's Fourth Republic.

kusaal: O da tʋm tʋʋm kaŋa nɛ yʋma 2013 la ni ti paae yʋma 2020 la ni.
english: He was re-elected in the 2016, 2020, and 2024 general elections.

kusaal: O da anɛ yʋma pisi nɛ anii ka Atta Mills gɔmina la maal o Deputy Minister of Information.
english: He previously served as Deputy Minister for Information and Deputy Minister for Education during the administrations of Presidents John Atta Mills and Mahama.

kusaal: Ablakwa mɛ da anɛ Education Minister nya'apa'ad gɔsid Sakur Titada saŋa kanɛ ka Prof.
english: He later served as Deputy Minister for Education, focusing on tertiary education, from 2013 to 2016.

kusaal: Jean Naana Opoku Agyemang da an Minister of Education ka John Dramani Mahama an Ghana Gɔmna Zugraan la.
english: He was appointed Minister for Foreign Affairs in 2025 under the government of President John Dramani Mahama.

kusaal: Okudzeto Ablakwa anɛ onɛ ka ba tis o piini kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ka piin banɛ an:TNG Corporate Excellence Piini – Accra 2010, Dasam Tuongat onɛ Kpɛ'ɛŋidi o Mɛŋ West Africa.
english: Outstanding Youth Leader in West Africa by the West Africa Students' Union (2009)

kusaal: West Africa Sakurbibis la'asʋg (WASU) da tis o piini la Kaduna linɛ bɛ Nigeria la yʋma 2009 la ni.
english: Outstanding Youth Leader in West Africa by the West Africa Students' Union (2009)

kusaal: Labaya Gɔsidib Minista nya'anpa'ad, 2009-2013 (Ghana Gɔmna)
english: Deputy Minister for Information (2009–2013)

kusaal: Sakurnam Gɔsib Minista nya'apa'ad, 2013-2016 (Ghana Gɔmna)
english: Deputy Minister for Education (2013–2016)

kusaal: Wada Maan , 2009 – till date (Office of Parliament)
english: Member of Parliament, North Tongu (2013–present)

kusaal: Nasaa nwadig August 2022 la ka o da tis yʋma anii biig ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Samelia Mekporsigbe ka yit Battor DA Primary School ka bɛ dɔɔd atan' la sʋŋir zaŋi kennɛ o sakur zamisʋgin.
english: In 2022, Ablakwa awarded a scholarship to Samelia Mekporsigbe, a pupil from Battor DA Primary School, who had won the Volta Regional USAID Learning Initiative competition.

kusaal: Ba mɔri biis ayi', bipuŋ nɛ bidibiŋ.
english: They have two children.

kusaal: O da kpɛn' University of Gaana, 2005 maal Bachelor of Arts Sociology nɛ History.
english: He entered University of Ghana and obtained his Bachelor of Arts in Sociology and History in 2005.

kusaal: Sanja Nanja da du'anɛ Na'asaanwadis Ayi la ni daba Atan daar, yʋma tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii la ni.
english: Sanja Nanja (born February 3, 1968) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eight Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Atebubu Amantin Constituency in the Bono East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Atebubu Amantim bɛ Bono East sʋ'ʋlim la dim ka paas Gaana wadmaanib yikanɛ paas anii tinamɛ faaen ti mɛŋi yi na'asaanam nu'usin la nya'an.
english: Sanja Nanja (born February 3, 1968) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Eight Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Atebubu Amantin Constituency in the Bono East Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Nanja anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Nanja is a Christian (Assemblies of God).

kusaal: O kɛnnɛ Assemblies of God.
english: Nanja is a Christian (Assemblies of God).

kusaal: Nanja da du'anɛ Na'asaanwadis Ayi la ni daba Atan daar, yʋma tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii la ni, 03-02-1968.
english: Nanja was born on February 3, 1968.

kusaal: O yinɛ Saboba, bɛ Tamar sʋ'ʋlim, Gaana.
english: He hails from Saboba, a town in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Nanja anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Nanja is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Nanja anɛ onɛ paas wadmaanib banɛ gɔsid wada tʋʋma yɛla la.
english: Nanja could not maintain his position as Member of Parliament for Attebubu Amantin during the 2016 elections due to a ban placed on him by members of the traditional council of his constituency.

kusaal: O da aan Atebubu Diisi 2009-2013.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Atebubu Amantin seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: Sankofa (Amharic: ሳንኮፋ) anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' (1993) sini kanɛ ka Ethiopia dim maal, ka one sɔbi li ka gaadi li tuon an Haile Gerima li pa'al nɛ Atlantic slave trade ka ba da kuosid nidib sankpan'asim la.
english: Sankofa (Amharic: ሳንኮፋ) is a 1993 Ethiopian-produced drama film written and directed by Haile Gerima that is centered on the Atlantic slave trade.

kusaal: Banɛ paas sini la ni anɛ Oyafunmike Ogunlano, Kofi Ghanaba, Mutabaruka, Alexandra Duah, nɛ Afemo Omilami.
english: The storyline features Oyafunmike Ogunlano, Kofi Ghanaba, Mutabaruka, Alexandra Duah, and Afemo Omilami.

kusaal: Sankofa yinɛ Akan buudi pian'ad kanɛ bɛ Ghana la, ka li gbin an "lɛm, ieem, ka nyɛ ya'am, paŋ nɛ ti'ir," wan wʋʋ Dr.
english: The word Sankofa is derived from the Akan language of Ghana and means to "go back, look for, and gain wisdom, power and hope," according to Dr. Anna Julia Cooper.

kusaal: Gerima sini nwa' pa'al ye African dim pʋ tammidi ba buudi malima nɛ ban yi si'el naa.
english: Gerima uses the journey of the character Mona to show how the African perception of identity included recognizing one's roots and "returning to one's source" (Gerima).

kusaal: Sarah Adwoa Safo (dʋ'anɛ 28 December 1981) anɛ Ghana lɔya nɛ pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Sarah Adwoa Safo (born 28 December 1981) is a Ghanaian lawyer and politician.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nid (NPP) ka an Wadmaan din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' (2013) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) tis Dome Kwabenya Constituency teŋkanɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana nwa' la.
english: She is a member of the New Patriotic Party and member of Parliament since 2013 for the Dome Kwabenya Constituency of the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da Adwoa Safo nɛ tis Ghana onɛ mɔr tʋʋma zin'is bɛdigʋ (industrialist) ka lɛn an karim saam (pastor), Apostle Kwadwo Safo yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne Nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 December 1981).
english: Adwoa Safo was born to Ghanaian industrialist and pastor, Kwadwo Safo Kantanka on Monday, 28 December 1981.

kusaal: Ba da pa'al o nɛ yin ka o keŋ sɔb GCE A' Level bɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anii la ni (1998) ka di ya'an.
english: She was home-tutored and wrote and passed her GCE A' Level in 1998.

kusaal: On da an yʋma piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ka kpɛn' University of Ghana Faculty of Law zamis ka di'e Bachelor of Law (L.L.B.) degree kasɛtta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ ayi' la ni (2002).
english: At age 17, she entered the University of Ghana Faculty of Law where she obtained Bachelor of Law (L.L.B.) degree in 2002.

kusaal: Safo da anɛ pirɛsidɛn nya'andɔli tis Law Students Union (LSU) on da bɛɛ o naar yʋʋm ni la.
english: Safo was the vice-president of the Law Students Union (LSU) in her final year.

kusaal: Ka lɛn tɔlisi keŋ Ghana School of Law ka da lieb lɔya yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi Nwadis piiga la ni (October 2004) ka an yʋma pisi nɛ ayi' (22 yrs).
english: She then continued to the Ghana School of Law and was called to the Bar in October 2004 at the age of 22.

kusaal: O mɔri o LLM kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit George Washington University.
english: She holds an LLM from George Washington University.

kusaal: yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ ayi' Nwadisa awai la ni (September 2022), o da naae University of Nottingham ka di'e Postgraduate Diploma in Public Procurement law and Policy.
english: In September 2022, she graduated from the University of Nottingham with a Postgraduate Diploma in Public Procurement law and Policy.

kusaal: O da tʋm bi'ela tis Office of the Attorney General bɛ District of Columbia, Washington DC bɛ United States ka din nya'aŋ ka o lɛb Ghana ye o tʋm tisi o ten.
english: She worked briefly with the Office of the Attorney General for the District of Columbia, Washington DC in the United States and thereafter returned to Ghana.

kusaal: On da lɛbi kulna la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu ni la (2005), o da keŋ la'as lɔyanam tʋʋm kanɛ yʋ'ʋri an Kulendu @ law, ka da an Zoe, Akyea & Co, ka di aan asʋ'oe-m-mɛŋ lɔyanam lʋgʋr la ka lɛn tʋm Mediation Committee of the Legal Aid Board of Ghana an Mediator.
english: In 2005, she joined the law firm Kulendi @ law, then Zoe, Akyea & Co, as a private legal practitioner and concurrently served on the Mediation Committee of the Legal Aid Board of Ghana as a Mediator.

kusaal: O da anɛ first legal officer tis Public Procurement Authority (PPA) yʋma ayi (2 years) ka da tʋm hali ka ba sʋnf ma'anɛ on da sɔb gbana hali ka ba da maal Appeals and Complaint Panel, PPA ka lɛn tiak Public Procurement Board tis Public Procurement Authority kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: She worked as the first legal officer of the Public Procurement Authority (PPA) for two (2) years and was very instrumental in the formulation of the proposals that formed the basis for the creation of the Appeals and Complaint Panel of PPA and the change of name of the Public Procurement Board to Public Procurement Authority.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt tis o ya'as bɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ la (2016) nɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi la ni (2020).
english: She was re-elected in the 2016 and 2020 elections.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋi o ye o an Minister of State gɔsid Government Procurement bɛ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2017), ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021); Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo saŋa, pirɛsidɛn kanɛ paasi anu Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: She was appointed Minister of State in charge of Government Procurement in 2017, serving till 2021, under Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, 5th president of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni la, Zuraan Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection ka o tʋm wala ken ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ ayi' Nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 July 2022) ka Nana Akuffo Addo Danquah yis o tʋʋma ni.
english: She was the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection until 28 July 2022 when she was dismissed by President Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋi Adwoa Nobles Forum Award yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni (2012).
english: Adwoa was a nominee for the Nobles Forum Award in 2012.

kusaal: Glitz Africa da girimi o ye ba ya'a kaal pʋ'ab kɔbiga banɛ ken tuon yʋʋm kan pʋʋgin o paasya.
english: She was honored by Glitz Africa as one of the Top 100 Women of the Year.

kusaal: O da anɛ Minista for Gender, Children and Social Protection ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ ayi' Nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 July 2022) ka Nana Akuffo Addo Danquah yis o tʋʋma ni.
english: She was the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection until 28 July 2022 when she was dismissed by President Nana Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o yiiga ka o lieb wadmaani tis Dome Kwabenya yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni (2012).
english: Sarah Adwao Safo contested the Dome Kwabenya constituency parliamentary seat during the 2012 Ghanaian general election on the ticket of New Patriotic Party and won with 63,373 votes representing 63.75% of the total votes.

kusaal: O da anɛ deputy majority leader Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la ni ka lɛn an pʋ'a kanɛ ma'aa nam mi'i an Majority leader nya'andɔl.
english: She was Deputy Majority Leader of the 7th Parliament of the Republic of Ghana and is the only female MP in Ghana to ascend to the number 2 position of the Majority front.

kusaal: Sasadu Festival anԑ yʋʋm-yʋʋm malʋŋ kanԑ ka na'anam nԑ nibid banԑ bԑ Sasadu sʋ'ʋlim banԑ an Alavanyo, Akrofu, Saviefe nԑ Sovie maan.
english: Sasadu Festival is an annual festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of the Sasadu communities of Alavanyo, Akrofu, Saviefe and Sovie.

kusaal: Li bԑnԑ Hohoe Municipality kanԑ bԑ Volta Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la ni.
english: It is located in the Hohoe Municipality in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: SASADU anԑ sͻb giŋi tis Sovie, Alavanyo, Saviefe, Akrofu Development Union linԑ an zanbini pa'an nͻŋilim nԑ ala'astaaba bԑ tԑԑns anaasi bama ni.
english: SASADU is an acronym for Sovie, Alavanyo, Saviefe, Akrofu Development Union which marks the symbol of unity and peace among the four communities.

kusaal: Region la maalʋg da pin'ilnɛ Gonja Traditional Council dimi da sɔb gbaʋŋ, ka onɛ da gaadi ba tuon an Yagbonwura Tumtumba Boresa Jakpa I. Ban da paam lɛbis sʋma yit Northern Region tuongatibin (anina ka li da nwaae yi), Brobbey Commission (Commission kanɛ tʋʋma an ye li maal region paala), sʋ'ʋlim kan dim da vɔɔti siak region nwa' maalʋg yɛla, ka li da anɛ yʋʋm tʋsayi' nɛ piinɛ anii, nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27th December 2018).
english: The creation of the Region follows presentation of a petition by the Gonja Traditional Council, led by the Yagbongwura Tumtumba Boresa Jakpa I. Upon receiving favourable responses from all stakeholders in the Northern Region (the region it was broken off from), the Brobbey Commission (the Commission tasked with the creation of the new regions), a referendum was conducted on the 27th December 2018.

kusaal: Republic of Ghana Zuraan da tikya ka nɔk wada gbaʋŋ nwa' (Constitutional Instrument (CI) 115) paae tis Yagbonwura onɛ bɛ Jubilee House, Accra yʋʋm tʋsayi' nɛ piinɛ awai, nwadis ayi', dabpiinɛ ayi' daar (12 February 2019).
english: The President of the Republic of Ghana signed and presented the Constitutional Instrument (CI) 115 to the Yagbonwura in the Jubilee House, Accra on 12 February 2019.

kusaal: Savannah Region mɔr districts nam ayɔpɔi; Bole, Central Gonja, North Gonja, East Gonja, Sawla/Tuna/Kalba, West Gonja, North East Gonja nɛ Constituencies nam ayɔpɔi; Bole/Bamboi, Damongo, Daboya/Mankarigu, Salaga North, Salaga South, Sawla/Tuna/Kalba nɛ Yapei/Kusawgu.
english: The Savannah Region is divided into 7 districts; Bole, Central Gonja, North Gonja, East Gonja, Sawla/Tuna/Kalba, West Gonja, North East Gonja and 7 Constituencies; Bole/Bamboi, Damongo, Daboya/Mankarigu, Salaga North, Salaga South, Sawla/Tuna/Kalba and Yapei/Kusawgu.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlim kan dim da vot ɛɛn bɛɛ ayei, ka li da anɛ yʋʋm tʋsayi' nɛ piiga nɛ anii, naar nwadig la dabisa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi daar (27 December 2018) da siak ye ba maal Savannah Region, ka nidib tusa kɔbʋsyi' nɛ ayuobu, kɔbʋstan' nɛ pisnu (206,350) piswai nɛ awai, nɛ pʋdʋgir anu nɛ ayi' (99.52%) da siak yi nidib pisnii' nɛ yinne, pudugir ayɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbʋga pʋʋgin (81.77%).
english: A referendum on 27 December 2018 approved the creation of Savannah Region, with 206,350 (99.52%) votes in favour on a turnout of 81.77%.

kusaal: Savannah Region tɔnd nɛ Upper West region li datiŋ, li tuon an Ghana-Côte d'Ivoire international border, ka li dagɔbʋg an Bono nɛ Bono East regions, ka li ya'tuona an North East nɛ Northern regions.
english: The Savannah Region is bordered on the north by the Upper West region, on the west by the Ghana-Côte d'Ivoire international border, on the south by the Bono and Bono East regions, and on the west by the North East and Northern regions.

kusaal: Savannah Region mɔr kpiemisi gat Ghana Ya-dagobug tɛn's la, lin kpie nɛ Sahel, nɛ Sahara la yɛla.
english: The Savannah Region is much drier than southern areas of Ghana, due to its proximity to the Sahel, and the Sahara.

kusaal: Amaa li sisiepiel tʋʋl kanɛ an Harmattan yit Sahara la da'ad lin yi naar nwadig la kɛŋ paae nwadig kanɛ paas ayi' la pin'ilig.
english: However, the hot Harmattan wind from the Sahara blows frequently between December and the beginning of February.

kusaal: Li tʋʋlʋg bɛɛ li waad anɛ wʋʋ 14 °C (59 °F) yʋ'ʋŋ ka nintaŋ an 40 °C (104 °F).
english: The temperatures can vary between 14 °C (59 °F) at night and 40 °C (104 °F) during the day.

kusaal: Region la mɔr wʋʋ 2.69 million hectares of land ka ba mɔri gʋ'ʋn ka kuod mɛn.
english: The Region has about 2.69 million hectares of land under cropping and livestock rearing.

kusaal: Savannah Region nidib pʋ zu'oe wala, official language anɛ Na'asaal, nidib la bedego pian'ad Oti–Volta bʋʋdi pian'ad nam linɛ bɛ Niger–Congo language family, ka ba sieba an Gonja, Vagla, Dagbani, Mamprusi, or Tamprusi.
english: The Savannah Region has a low population density, and along with the official language of English, most inhabitants speak a language of the Central Gur subfamily in the Niger–Congo language family, such as Vagla, Dagbani, Mamprusi or Tampulma, or the Potou-Tano language Gonja.

kusaal: Ka lin an siem an ye, region la pʋdʋgnɛ MMDA nam ayɔpɔi (Metropolitan kai, Municipal nam ayi' nɛ Assemblies nam anu).
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into seven MMDA's (made up of 0 Metropolitan, 2 Municipal and 5 Ordinary Assemblies).

kusaal: District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly nam la wʋsa, tuongat anɛ Chief Executive, one zie gɔmena nɔba zug ka nyɛ paŋi yit presiding member one ka assembly members la mɛŋ gaŋ.
english: Each District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly, is administered by a Chief Executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an Assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Savannah Region anɛ regions of Ghana paala yinne ka la'an nɛ wala linɛ zu'oe gat region nam la wʋsa Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The Savannah Region is one of the newest regions of Ghana and the largest region in the country.

kusaal: Nidib la da vɔɔt ye ɛɛn ka ba siakya nwɛnɛ nidib piswai nɛ awai du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (99.7%).
english: The result was a resounding yes of 99.7%.

kusaal: Li pin'ilig tigir la da ye pʋ'asada nɛ dasam bɛdegʋ banɛ bɛ Gonjaland nɛ wadmaannib, MDCEs banɛ bɛ zina nɛ banɛ gaad wʋsa da bɛ anina, nɛ gɔmena tʋmtʋmnib banɛ yit Gonjaland.
english: The launch was well attended by sons and daughters of Gonjaland including all current and past Mps, MDCEs and all appointees with Gonjaland descent.

kusaal: Damongo ka ba da gaŋ ye li an Savannah Region tɛmpʋʋgtita'ar.
english: The Savannah Region is divided into 7 districts; Bole, Central Gonja, North Gonja, East Gonja, Sawla/Tuna/Kalba, West Gonja, North East Gonja and 7 Constituencies; Bole/Bamboi, Damongo, Daboya/Mankarigu, Salaga North, Salaga South, Sawla/Tuna/Kalba and Yapei/Kusawgu.

english: He was elected on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and won a majority of 10,612 votes more than candidate closest in the race, to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: Schalke anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb banɛ nwɛ'ɛd hali bɛ Germany, hali la'am nɛ kilab la yʋ'ʋri da dʋ 1930s nɛ 1940s saŋa la.

english: Schalke have won seven German championships, five DFB-Pokals, one DFB Ligapokal, one DFL-Supercup, one UEFA Cup and two UEFA Intertoto Cups.

kusaal: senior high sakurbiisi da pin'il Kilab la14 sigisaa1904 la ni ka li yʋ'ʋr da buon ye Westfalia schalke, ka ba da yɛɛdi zɛm'ɛʋg nɛ dɔnbʋʋlʋm.
english: The club was founded on 4 May 1904 as Westfalia Schalke by a group of high school students and first wore the colours red and yellow.

kusaal: Ba da si'iŋ maalʋg kaŋa hali ka li paae 1915 yʋʋm la ni, saŋkanɛ ka sv westfalia schalke dim da maligim maali ba mɛŋ ka yʋ'ʋn aan ba mɛŋ nyari ka sɔ' pʋ lɛn sʋ'ʋe ba ya'as la.
english: This arrangement held up until 1915, when SV Westfalia Schalke was re-established as an independent club.

kusaal: Ba kɔn'ɔn-kɔn'ɔb la da pʋ yuugɛ ka ba la'as taaba 1919 yʋʋm la ni ka ba yʋ'ʋr buon ye Turn-und sportverein Schalke 1877.
english: The separation proved short-lived and the two came together again in 1919 as Turn- und Sportverein Schalke 1877.

kusaal: 1928 yʋʋm la ni la, kilab la da mɛ nwɛ'ɛb zin'ig linɛ buon ye Gluckauf-Kampfbahn, ka tempʋʋg la nidib nɛ sʋŋi bal zug ka ba da pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye FC Gelsenkirchen-Schalke 04.
english: In 1928, the club built a new stadium, the Glückauf-Kampfbahn, and acknowledged the city's support by renaming themselves FC Gelsenkirchen-Schalke 04.

kusaal: Ba da West German ya'an la 1929 yʋʋm la ni, amaa ba da tɛɛgi ba tʋba nɛ ban tʋʋgi ba ligidi yɔɔd linɛ ka League la maal zi'el la bɛɛn gaad la, nɛ ban niŋ ka li pʋ dɔl nwɛ'ɛb kpɛmmir suori an si'em la, ka kadi ba ye ba kʋ lɛn nwɛ'ya'asa hali ka li kpɛlim bi'ela nɛ yʋʋm pʋsʋg.
english: They won their first West German championship in 1929, but the following year were sanctioned for exceeding salary levels set by the league and, in an era that considered professionalism in sport to be anathema, found themselves banned from play for nearly half a year.

kusaal: Dinzug ban da kadi ba ye ba kʋ lɛn nwɛ' la, li da mɔr daʋŋ kɛn ba yʋ'ʋrin na; yiiga nwɛ'ɛb linɛ ka ban nɛ Fortuna Dusseldorf da ye ba nwɛ' bɛ naadɔɔnr 1931 yʋʋm ni la, ba da kɔ'ɔŋi ka ba gɔsidib wʋʋ 70,000.
english: However, the ban had little impact on the team's popularity: in their first match after the ban against Fortuna Düsseldorf, in June 1931, the team drew 70,000 spectators to its home ground.

kusaal: Kilab la suosʋŋ da lɛn pin'il 1931 yʋʋm la ni yɔ'ɔgid, ka ban nɛ Eintracht Frankfurt nwɛ' bɛ 1932 German ya'an nwɛ'ɛb la ni ka ba dii ba gool ayi ka ba an yinne.
english: The club's fortunes begun to rise from 1931 and they made a semi-final appearance in the 1932 German championship, losing 1–2 to Eintracht Frankfurt.

kusaal: Kilab nan zi' nwɛ' ba teŋin nwɛ'ɛb linɛ bɛ Gauliga Westfalen ka kɔ'ɔŋɛ, hali nwɛ'ɛb saŋa nɔɔr piinɛ ayi bama, amaa ka lɛɛ kɔ'ɔŋ yiiŋ nwɛ'ɛbnam ayuobʋ bɛ 1935-36, 1936-37, 1937-38, 1938-39, 19340-41 n 1942-43 yʋma la ni.
english: The club never lost a home match in the Gauliga Westfalen in all these 11 seasons and only lost six away matches, while remaining unbeaten in the 1935–36, 1936–37, 1937–38, 1938–39, 1940–41 and 1942–43 seasons, a sign of the club's dominance.

kusaal: Ba da tis Schalke dim yiiga nwɛ'ɛb yʋ'ʋr nɛ 1934, saŋkanɛ ka ba da nwɛ' nɛ FC Nurnber dim ka dii ba 2-1 la.
english: Schalke's first national title came in 1934 with a 2–1 victory over favourites 1.

kusaal: Kilab la da pʋ nwɛ' kpi'i nya'ab la nii, amaa ba da nwɛ' yʋma ayuobʋ linɛ da an 1937, 1939,1940 nɛ 1942 ni ya'an nwɛ'ɛb la ka da di ya'an.
english: The club missed the 1936 final, but would make appearances in the championship match in each of the next six years, coming away victorious in 1937, 1939, 1940 and 1942.

kusaal: Ba da nwɛ' nwɛ'ɛbnam atan' nɛ Austrian dim nwɛ'ɛdib banɛ an Admira Wien, Rapid wien nɛ Yiiga Vienna bane da nwɛ' bɛ Germany Gauliga Ostmark, Austria dimi da dɔl 1938 Anschluss kpɛn' Reich la nya'aŋ.
english: Three of those national finals were against Austrian teams – Admira Wien, Rapid Wien and First Vienna – which played in Germany's Gauliga Ostmark after Austria's incorporation into the Reich through the 1938 Anschluss.

kusaal: Yʋma bɛdigʋ bane gaad, lin yi 1933 ti paae 1945 saŋa la, Schalke dim da nwɛ' Gauliga nwɛ'ɛbnam 189 ka di 162, ka nyaŋ 21 ka kɔ'ɔŋ 6.
english: Over a dozen seasons, from 1933 to 1945, Schalke won 162 of 189 Gauliga matches, drawing 21 and losing only 6.

kusaal: Ban nɛ Spvgg Herten dim da nwɛ' ka ba di Spvgg Herten dim 20-0 ka li an bʋnsʋŋ gban'e, amaa din da pa'ali ba tadimis bɛ German nwɛ'ɛb la ni gaŋi ba paŋi an si'em.
english: They set a record in a national championship round match with a 20–0 win against SpVgg Herten, but that spoke more to the weakened condition of German football than to the ability of the team.

kusaal: Schalke dim da nwɛ' Oberliga west nwɛ'ɛb line da bɛ 1947 yʋʋm ni la ka lu, ka lɛɛ da nyaŋi nwɛ'ɛnɛ paae ayuobʋ bɛɛn ma'aa.
english: Schalke's play fell off, and they only finished sixth in the new Oberliga West in 1947.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kanɛ da tia'al la ni, DFB-Pokal nwɛ'ɛb da bɛ ka ban nɛ Karlsruher sc da nwɛ' ka Karlsruher dim dii ba 3 ka ba dii 2, ka pa'al ye ba da lunɛ.
english: The following year, they appeared in the DFB-Pokal final, where they lost 2–3 to Karlsruher SC.

kusaal: Ban da nwɛ' League la naae la ba da kpɛn nwɛ'ɛdi ken tuon ka kal la paasid, hali ka ba tuon ken da yʋ'ʋn da pin'il 1971-72, ani ka ba da yʋ'ʋn dʋ paae Bayern Munich n tia'al ayi, ban da gaad league la tuon la nya'aŋ.
english: A number of finishes at the lower end of the league table followed, before a marked improvement in 1971–72, culminating in a second-place finish to Bayern Munich and after having led the league for much of the season.

kusaal: Nidib da ma' ziil nwɛ'ɛdib nɛ tuongatib la ye ba siakɛ ka nidib da'adi ba nɛ ligidi kat wa'anɛ Bundesliga scandal nwɛ'ɛb linɛ da bɛ 1971 yʋʋm ni la.
english: A number of the team's players and officials were accused of accepting bribes as part of the widespread Bundesliga scandal of 1971.

kusaal: 1973 yʋʋm la ni la, kilab la da vuguri keŋ Parkstsdio dinɛ ka ba mɛɛ li paalim tis 1974 FIFA World cup la ni, ka ba nidib banɛ da dɔli ba la da nɔbignɛ an wʋʋ nidib 70,000.
english: In 1973, the club moved to the Parkstadion, newly built for the 1974 FIFA World Cup and having a capacity of 70,000 spectators.

kusaal: Ba da nwɛ' Borussia Monchengladbach nwɛ'ɛb linɛ da bɛ 1976-77 yʋʋm la ni la ka dii tia'al ayi dim.1980s yʋʋm pin'ilʋgʋn sa la, Die knappen da paam yɛl ka lu lɛb Bundesliga second Division la ni lin da pin'il 1981 ti paae 1982 saŋa la, ka li nya'aŋ ka ba da lɛn lɛbi keŋ tuon 1983 ti paae 1984 ni.
english: In the early 1980s, Die Knappen ran into trouble and were relegated to the second division of the Bundesliga for the 1981–82 season and, after promotion, again in 1983–84.

kusaal: Ba da duoe lɛb Bundesliga teŋin 1991-92 ka da bɛɛ ani ka nwɛ'ɛd ka ba yʋ'ʋr bɛɛ agɔla hali ti paae 2012 yʋʋm la ni.
english: They returned to the Bundesliga in the 1991–92 season and stayed in the top flight until 2021.

kusaal: V., ka ba buon ye Schalke 54 ka li sɔbʋg an S04 giŋa la anɛ bɔɔl kilab bɛ Schalk distirick linɛ Gelsenkirchen, Rhine-Westphalia ya-tuona.
english: V., commonly known as Schalke 04 (German: [ˌʃalkə nʊl ˈfiːɐ̯] ), and abbreviated as S04 (German: [ˈɛs nʊl fiːɐ̯] ), is a professional sports club from the Schalke district of Gelsenkirchen, North Rhine-Westphalia.

kusaal: Tʋʋmbanɛ ka Kilab la tʋm paas anɛ zɔɔ nya'ab, basketbaal, nu'us bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb, teebul zugu di'ema, winter sports nɛ esports.

kusaal: Schalke dim nɛ Ruhr kpi'es banɛ ka ba buon ye Borussia Dortmund, ka ba lɛn buonnɛ li ye Revierderby la anɛ kpi'es banɛ nwɛ'ɛd nɛ taaba hali ka li kpi'ueŋ.
english: Schalke hold a long-standing rivalry with Ruhr neighbors Borussia Dortmund, known as the Revierderby.

kusaal: 1912 yʋʋm la ni la, ban da mɔɔ nɔɔr pamm ye ba nyaŋi nwɛ' nwɛ'ɛtita'ar ni ka pʋ nyaŋ la, ba da gʋ'ʋŋ ka la'as nɛ Turn-und sportverein schalke dim 1877 yʋʋm la ni, ye lin na niŋ si'em ka sʋŋi ba ka ba nyaŋi ti paam suori paas.
english: In 1912, after years of failed attempts to join the official league, they merged with the gymnastic club Schalker Turnverein 1877 in order to facilitate their entry.

kusaal: Li da anɛ saŋkan la ka kilab la tisi ba mɛŋ nwɛ'ɛb yʋ'ʋr ye Die knappen, ka li yinɛ German pian'aʋk kʋdʋgin linɛ buon ye "miners" la, bɔzugɔ nwɛ'ɛdib la bɛdigʋ naami ba yda yinɛ Gelsenkirchen tuudibin na.
english: It was around this time that Schalke picked up the nickname Die Knappen, from an old German word for "miners" because the team drew so many of its players and supporters from the coal miners of Gelsenkirchen.

kusaal: 1924 yʋʋm la ni la, bɔɔlnwɛ'ɛdib la da lɛn la'asi ba mɛŋ kpɛn' zamisʋgʋn ya'as, din ni la ba da yʋ'ʋn nɔki ba tuongat la paasnɛ.
english: In 1924, the football team parted ways with the gymnasts again, this time taking the club chairman along with them.

kusaal: Ba da pʋdi ba mɛŋ ye schalke 04 ka yɛɛd fubanɛ an pipɛlig nɛ pielig linɛ ka ba nwɛ'ɛb yʋ'ʋr linɛ buon ye Die konigsblauen kapaas ayi la na yii ani.
english: They took the name FC Schalke 04 and adopted the now familiar blue and white kit from which their second nickname would derive, Die Königsblauen (English: The Royal Blues).

kusaal: Ani ka ba da tɔlis paae Gauliga Ruhr ni, nɛ Cdampions League, ka lɛn mɔri ba tɔlis tɛɛs wʋsa nwɛ'ɛb linɛ an kpi'i la ni.
english: In 1927, it carried them into the top-flight Gauliga Ruhr, onto the league championship, and then into the opening rounds of the national finals.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kan nya'aŋ la, kilab la nwɛ' paae kpi'i nwɛ'ɛb la ni, ka ban nɛ Fortuna Dusseldorf dim sid pa'ali ba tɔn'ɔlim ka di 3-0.
english: They also made failed appearances in the 1936, 1941, and 1942 finals with their only victory coming in 1937 against Fortuna Düsseldorf.

kusaal: Ban da maligim maal German bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb la'asʋg bɛ 1933 yʋʋm ni la, ba da nɔk schalke dim niŋi Gauliga westfalen line da paas nwɛ'ɛdib16 banɛ ka ba pʋdigi ba ye ba mi'i nwɛ'ɛd la ni, ye ba lɛdig banɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm nɛ teŋkpɛŋ nwɛ'ɛdib banɛ dʋ'ʋsidi ba mɛŋ ye mi'i nwɛ'ɛb galis la.
english: With the re-organisation of German football in 1933 under Nazi Germany, Schalke were placed in the Gauliga Westfalen, 1 of 16 top-flight divisions established to replace the innumerable regional and local leagues, all claiming top status.

kusaal: Nwɛ'ɛb kaŋa sid pa'al Schalke dimi mi'i nwɛ'eb si'em; hali lin pin'il 1933-1942, kilab la nyaŋ nwɛ' tɛɛns nwɛ'ɛb 14 yi 18 nwɛ'ɛb ni (piiga an German nya'ab ka anii me an Tschammerpokal linɛ maan zinɛ DFB-Pokal la) ka diti ba ya'an saŋa kanɛ wʋsa ka ba ɛɛnti nwɛ' ba piinɛ ayi saŋa nwɛ'ɛb la yinne.
english: This league saw Schalke's most successful decade in their history: from 1933 to 1942, the club would appear in 14 of 18 national finals (ten in the German championship and eight in the Tschammerpokal, the predecessor of today's DFB-Pokal) and win their league in every one of its eleven seasons.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kanɛ tia'al la ni ba da sid nwɛ' nɛ VTB Stuttgart dim ka dii ba 6-4.
english: It remained Schalke's only victory under Gross, who was sacked as head coach after just eleven matches on 28 February 2021, following losses against rival Borussia Dortmund (0–4) and VFB Stuttgart (1–5).

kusaal: Ban nɛ FC Nurnberg dim da nwɛ' inaugural Tschammerpkal nwɛ'ɛb linɛ da bɛ 1935 yʋʋm la ni la ka ba lu ka FC Nurnberg dim dii ba ayi.
english: They lost the inaugural Tschammerpokal 0–2 to 1.

kusaal: Ala mɛn ka 1936, 1941 nɛ 1942 yʋʋm nwɛ'ɛb ni la, ba lunɛ ka Fortuna Dusseldorf dim ma'a ka ba da di ba bɛ 1937 yʋʋm la ni.
english: They also made failed appearances in the 1936, 1941, and 1942 finals with their only victory coming in 1937 against Fortuna Düsseldorf.

kusaal: Ka din da yi 1935 ti 1939 ni ba da pʋ kɔ'ɔŋ nwɛ'eb baa yinne.
english: From 1935 to 1939, they did not lose a single league match.

kusaal: Kilab la da ken tuon ka ba yʋ'ʋr dʋt agɔla si'em la da kɛnɛ ka Nazi regime nɔki ba yʋ'ʋn pian'adi ba yɛla zin'ig wʋsa ni ye banɛ an "German paal la."
english: The club's dominance throughout this period led them to be held up for propaganda purposes by the Nazi regime as an example of "new Germany".

kusaal: German n da an yɔri-yɔri kat wa'anɛ dunia zaba II naar yɛla la, Schalke dim da nwɛ'ɛnɛ nwɛ'ɛbnam ayi ma'aa bɛ 1945 yʋʋm la ni.
english: With Germany in chaos towards the end of World War II, Schalke played just two matches in 1945.

kusaal: Oberliga zɔɔ linɛ da naam la dabisir kanɛ da an kpi'i la, ba da zɔɔ di tia'al atan' dim, zɔɔ linɛ da paas atan' la.
english: They finished third in a tight three-way race for the 1954 Oberliga West title, decided on the last day of the season.

kusaal: Ka lin yi saŋkan la ti paae zina, kilab la da nwɛ' German ya'an nwɛ'ɛb linɛ da bɛ 1958 la, ban nɛ Hamburger sv dim da nwɛ' ka ba da di ya'an ka kɛ Hamburger sv dim.
english: The club's next, and to date last, German championship came in 1958 with a 3–0 victory over Hamburger SV.

kusaal: Joseph pʋ'ʋsʋm linɛ bɛ Gelsenkirchen la gbana ni.
english: The strong fanbase of the club is as well documented in a local church, St. Joseph, in Gelsenkirchen.

kusaal: Ba da maligim bʋlʋg karimdɔɔg la nɛ, ban da di ya'an bɛ 1958 yʋʋm nya'aŋ la, ani ka ba da sɔb niŋi li galaas yinne ni ye Aloysius Gonzaga, ka buoɛn bɔɔli li ni, nɛ li fuud nɛ li si'im wʋsa.
english: It was renovated shortly after the 1958 victory, where one of the glass windows shows Aloysius Gonzaga with a football and the dress and colours of Schalke.

kusaal: Schalke dim da kpɛn ken tuon nɛ nwɛ'ɛb yim, n nwɛ'ɛd nwɛ'ɛbnam bɛdigʋ ka lin da kɛ ta'as Bundesliga linɛ buon ye West German new federal bɔɔlnwɛ'ɛdib la da naam.
english: Schalke continued to play well, having several top four finishes in the years leading up to the 1963 formation of the Bundesliga, West Germany's new federal, professional league.

kusaal: Lin da pin'il 1964 ti paae 1965 yʋʋm la ni la, ba da yadigi ba bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib la ka ba yʋ'ʋn an nwɛ'ɛdib gum-gum 18, ka ba da pʋ lut ya'asa.
english: Baum's tenure had brought the winless streak up from 18 to 28 Bundesliga games, bringing Schalke to the brink of breaking the all-time record of 31 winless games, set by SC Tasmania 1900 Berlin in the 1965–66 season.

kusaal: Saŋkan nii nɔɔ ka Schalke dim da nwɛ' DFB-Pokal ya'an ka li aan ba ya'an linɛ paas ayi ka ba di DFB-Pokal.
english: DFB-Pokal (German Cup)

kusaal: Linzug shalke kat bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib pamm ye ba nan kʋ nwɛ'ɛ, la'am nɛ ba nidib atan' bama; Klaus Fischer, Stan Libuda nɛ Kaus Fichtel banɛ da nwɛ'ɛdi tisid West German bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib la bɛ saŋkan la.
english: As a result, several Schalke players were banned for life, including three – Klaus Fischer, "Stan" Libuda and Klaus Fichtel – who regularly played for the West Germany national team at the time.

kusaal: Ba da nyaŋ dʋ agɔ 1984 yʋʋm la ni, amaa ba da lɛn lu lɛb nya'aŋ 1988 yʋʋm la ni.
english: They returned to the top flight in 1984 but were relegated once more to the second tier in 1988.

kusaal: Sebastian Ngmenenso Sandaare (Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi yʋʋmpaal nwadig la yiiga dabisid la (1 January 1974) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd onɛ paas Ghana republic kanɛ aan anaasi la wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas ayɔpɔi nid yinne, ka an wadmaan tisi Daffiama-Bussie-Issa Constituency kanɛ bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la wabʋg na'adɔɔg paati la nid .
english: Sebastian Ngmenenso Sandaare (born 1 January 1974) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Daffiama-Bussie-Issa Constituency in the Upper West Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O mɔri bachelor's degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit Kwame Nkrumah Science and Technology nɛ master's degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ Public Health yit University of Ghana ni.
english: He holds a bachelor's degree from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology and a master's degree in Public Health from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Sebastian du'am yʋʋm anɛ yʋʋm paal nwadig 1, 1974, bɛ Daffiama teŋkanɛ bɛ Upper West Region la.
english: Sebastian Ngmenenso Sandaare (born 1 January 1974) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Daffiama-Bussie-Issa Constituency in the Upper West Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Di da paasnɛ Sefwi-Wiawso District kanɛ da zu'oe la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) la ni, ka ba da nwaae li yi ka bas Sefwi-Bibiani District Council, ti paae sankanɛ ka ba da lɛ nwaae Ya-dagɔbʋg tuon baba la ka di lieb Sefwi-Akontombra District yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii nwadisa ayi la dabpisi nɛ awai daar (29 February 2008); dinɛ kpɛlim la yʋ'ʋn da anɛ Sefwi-Wiawso District (dinɛ ka ba da yuolim tiakidi di keŋ municipal zi'esim yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa atan la nni (ka di da pin'il tʋʋma yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa ayuobʋ la dabpisi nɛ anii daar la (28 June 2012) ka an Sefwi-Wiawso Municipal District.
english: Originally it was formerly part of the then-larger Sefwi-Wiawso District in 1988, which was created from the former Sefwi-Bibiani District Council, until the southwest part of the district was split off to create Sefwi-Akontombra District on 29 February 2008; thus the remaining part was retained as Sefwi-Wiawso District (which it was later elevated to municipal district assembly status in March 2012 (effectively 28 June 2012) to become Sefwi-Wiawso Municipal District).

kusaal: Distirict asambile la bɛnɛ Ya-datiʋŋ nya'aŋ baba lɛbid Western North Region ka Akontombra aan di tempʋtita'ar.
english: The district assembly is located in the northeast part of Western North Region and has Akontombra as its capital town.

kusaal: Sefwi-Wiawso Municipal District paasnɛ distirik nam awai banɛ bɛ Western North Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Sefwi-Wiawso Municipal District is one of the nine districts in Western North Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da maali li ka di an distirik assambile nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) la ni ka ba da buoni di ye Sefwi-Wiawso District, ti paae sankanɛ ka ba da nwaae distirik la datiʋŋ lɛbid tuon baba maal Sefwi-Akontombra District bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayiu nɛ anii nwadisa ayi la dabpisi nɛ awai daar (29 February 2008); ka zin'ikanɛ kpɛlim ka an Sefwi-Wiawso District, ka ba da yuolim ʋki di ka di lieb municipal distirik assambile zi'esim bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa atan (March 2012) (ka di da pin'il yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nwadisa ayuobʋ dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 June 2012) ka lieb Sefwsi-Wiawso Municipal District.
english: Originally created as an ordinary district assembly in 1988 when it was known as Sefwi-Wiawso District, until the southwest part of the district was split off to create Sefwi-Akontombra District on 29 February 2008; thus the remaining part has been retained as Sefwi-Wiawso District, which it was later elevated to municipal district assembly status in March 2012 (effectively 28 June 2012) to become Sefwi-Wiawso Municipal District.

kusaal: Munisipal la sʋ'ʋlim bɛnɛ Ya-datiʋŋ nya'aŋ lɛbid Western North Region baba ka Wiawso aan di tɛmpʋtita'ar.
english: The municipality is located in the northeast part of Western North Region and has Wiawso as its capital town.

kusaal: Sega tambour of Rodrigues Island anɛ Sega kanɛ bɛ Mauritius la yʋʋma buudi yinne, ka nidib mi' I ye ba da pin'ili linɛ Rodrigues Island na, island bil kanɛ labisim an nwɛnɛ kilomitanam kɔbiga nɛ anii, 108 square kilometres (42 sq mi).
english: Sega tambour of Rodrigues Island is one of the types of Sega music of Mauritius, with origins in the Rodrigues Island, a small island about 108 square kilometres (42 sq mi) in area.

kusaal: Sega Tambour kanɛ bɛ Rodrigues Island la anɛ dinɛ ka ba maani li ka di an yʋʋma nɛ wa'ab ka li da pin'il zin'ibanɛ ka sankpan'asnam da bɛ.
english: Sega Tambour of Rodrigues Island is a performance of music and dance with its origins in slave communities.

kusaal: la'aʋŋ la da di bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb linɛ buon ye Ghana premier League la bɛ yʋʋm 1977 la ni, ka nannana ba yʋ'ʋn paasnɛ Division one League lin yi Ghana Premier league dinɛ naam 2015 saŋa la.
english: The club won the Ghana Premier League in 1977 and is currently participating in the Division One League following relegation from the 2015-16 Ghana Premier League.

kusaal: Ba buon nwɛ'ɛb la'asʋg kaŋa yee ' West pamis dim', ka li anɛ bam ma'a da an Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib banɛ nyaŋi nwɛ' nɛ Fortuna Dusseldorf dim ka ba di taaba 3-3 West Africa wʋsa bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb saŋa, ka da li'el German baba la yʋʋm 1959 la li nwadis anii la ni.
english: Affectionately referred to as the 'Giants of the West', an accolade it acquired after being the only Ghanaian team to hold Fortuna Düsseldorf to a 3–3 draw during a tour of West Africa by the German side in August 1959.

kusaal: Club la da pin'ilinɛ 1931 la ni, ka mɛ da nan paas Ghana Telecom Premier League la ni.
english: The club was formed in 1931 and was previously a member of the Ghana Telecom Premier League.

kusaal: Club la da bɛ Globacom premier league ni la li yʋma pisi nya'aŋ ka li lɛb nya'aŋ keŋ Poly Tank Division One League ni 2010.
english: After twenty years in the Globacom Premier League, the club was relegated to the Poly Tank Division One League in 2010.

kusaal: Bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib ban ma'a da an tempʋkan bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib banɛ da paas Ghana premiership la ni yʋma 1996-1997, hali ti paae saŋkanɛ ba da lɛb Division One bɛ 2009-2010 league la ni.
english: The team had been the Oil City's only participant in the top flight Ghanaian Premiership for over a decade from the mid 1996–97 football season until its relegation to Division One in the 2009–2010 league season.

kusaal: Sekondi Hasaaccas club la bas labasʋŋ pin'ilʋgʋn, ba da yiis nwɛ'ɛdib anaasi banɛ mi'i nwɛ'ɛb hali ka ba keŋ paas Black Stars dim la ni, ka lɛn nɔki ba bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib anu ka ba paas nwɛ'ɛdib banɛ da di 1982 African cup of Nations la bɛ Tripoli line bɛ Libya sʋ'ʋlʋmin la.
english: The club, Sekondi Hasaacas, has a rich history, producing four captains for the senior national team (the Black Stars) and contributing as many as five players to the squad that won the 1982 African Cup of Nations in Tripoli, Libya.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr kanɛ buon ye Hasaacas la yinɛ ziriga tʋmtʋmnib la ni na, ban da nɔki ba yʋda yiiga sɔbbiela la naami club la yʋ'ʋr bɛ 1931, dinɛ an H.A.S.A.A.C.A.S. ka ba yʋda la anɛ; Hammond, Amua Sakyi, Adotei, Allotey, Cann, Adoey nɛ Sackey.
english: The name Hasaacas came from the railway workers in Sekondi-Takoradi who decided to use the first letters of their names to form the name of the club in 1931, thus H.A.S.A.A.C.A.S.—namely Hammond, Amua Sakyi, Adotei, Allotey, Cann, Adotey and Sackey.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ atan' la ni ka Sekondi Hasaacas Football Club da nɔki yʋri pɛɛs gbana ni yʋ'ʋm an academy ka an yiiga saŋa kan bɛ pin'iligin yɛlkuda ni, dinɛ anɛ puab team, Hasaacas Ladies Football Club la.
english: Sekondi Hasaacas Football Club in June 2003 added to its file an academy and, for the first time in history, a ladies' team, the Hasaacas Ladies Football Club.

kusaal: Ba da gɔsidnɛ nwɛ'ɛdib la yʋma ka pʋʋgini pʋdig academy la kɔ'ɔb-kɔ'ɔb under -12, -14 nɛ -17 yʋma, ka ba sʋŋ ka pa'al dasam paalis banɛ duod na nɛ ya'am la.
english: The academy was divided by age into division for under-12, -14 and -17 years, to help nurture young talents.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai la nya'aŋ la, banɛ mɔr ya'am ka ba an yʋma piiga nɛ ayɔpoi la (under -17) nwɛ'ɛ-nwɛ'ɛdib la ba da sʋŋi ba ka ba keŋ tuon paae hali Malavands Football Club, ka banɛ da kpɛlim bɛdigʋ na nwɛ' Hasaacas Football Club la bɛ Division Three League la ni.
english: Later in 2009, the talented group of under-17 players was promoted to the Malavands Football Club, the reserve side of the mainstream Hasaacas Football Club to participate in the Division Three League.

kusaal: Malavands team la nyaŋ yʋʋm kan la ni nɔɔ ka nwɛ' bɛ Division Two league bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga(2010 ) la ni saŋa, ka di da pa'al nyain bɛ 2nd division nwɛ'ɛb la ni.
english: The Malavands team qualified that same year to play in the Division Two league for the 2010 season, and have proved to be formidable in the 2nd division.

kusaal: Dinɛ an HASMAL banɛ da tis total Secondi Hasaacas buudi la, team tita'ar la nwɛ'ɛbin, dinɛ an ladies' team, Malavands nɛ Hasaacas Academy la.
english: Thus, HASMAL represents the total Secondi Hasaacas family, the mainstream team, the ladies' team, Malavands and the Hasaacas Academy.

kusaal: Di anɛ bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb kanɛ ka nidib bɛdigʋ nɔŋi li bɛ Western Region linɛ mɔr nidib kal wʋʋ tusa-tusa anaasi la ni.
english: The side is the most followed football club in the Western Region, a region with a population of almost four million, and is nicknamed Hasmal, which comes with the response 'We Go Doo'.

kusaal: Nwɛ'ɛb la'aʋŋ kaŋa naamnɛ 1931, ka da nan an Ghana Telecom premier League la yinne.
english: The club was formed in 1931 and was previously a member of the Ghana Telecom Premier League.

kusaal: ka lin da bɛ Globacom Premier League ni la, li yʋma pisi nya'aŋ, li da tɔlis keŋ Poly Tank Division one League la ni bɛ 2010 la ni.
english: After twenty years in the Globacom Premier League, the club was relegated to the Poly Tank Division One League in 2010.

kusaal: Ba da buon Cluba la nɛ ye pamis dim, bɔzgɔ ban ma'a da Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib banɛ nyaŋi nwɛ' nɛ Fortuna Dusseldorf dim ka ba di taaba azinzima saŋkanɛ ka ba da nwɛ'ɛd giligid Africa datiuŋ tɛɛns linɛ lam Geman wʋsa ni la,yʋʋm 1959 li nwadis anii la ni.
english: Affectionately referred to as the 'Giants of the West', an accolade it acquired after being the only Ghanaian team to hold Fortuna Düsseldorf to a 3–3 draw during a tour of West Africa by the German side in August 1959.

kusaal: Ba pamm da anɛ Accra Haerts of Oak sʋŋidib bɛɛ di'em di'emnam amaa ba tʋʋma la zug ka ba da tɔlisi keŋ Sekondi Takoradi.
english: Most of them were supporters of Accra Hearts of Oak but migrated to Sekondi-Takoradi mainly because of their railway work.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr la da tiak ye Sekondi Hasaacas bɔzugɔ ba da bɛnɛ Sekondi teŋin; ba da nɔki dindɛʋg si'imnam la ka aan ba mɛŋ si'im bɔzugɔ ba nidib la pamm da anɛ banɛ sʋŋid Accra Hearts of Oak.
english: The name later became Sekondi Hasaacas because the team was based in Sekondi; they decided to use rainbow colors as their original colors because most of the founding members were supporters of Accra Hearts of Oak.

kusaal: Diniel Egyin da an ba kpɛɛm bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu 2016 Ghanaian Premier League la saŋa.
english: Daniel Egyin served as club captain in the 2016 Ghanaian Premier League season.

kusaal: daniel egyin - da an ba kpɛɛm bɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu 2016 Ghanaian Premier League la saŋa.
english: Daniel Egyin – served as club captain in 2016 Ghanaian Premier League season.

kusaal: Constituency kaŋa paasnɛ constituency paala banɛ ka ba da maal yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) Ghana vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: This constituency was part of the newly created constituency for 2012 general elections in Ghana.

kusaal: Sekyere Afram Plains Constituency bɛnɛ Sekyere Afram Plains Districti bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Sekyere Afram Plains is located in the Sekyere Afram Plains District in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Sekyere Afram Plains District dinɛ bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Sekyere Afram Plains District of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Semeiskie la anɛ ninkʋda pʋ'ʋsim la'asig, Old Believers banɛ da bɛ Transbaikal la, Catherine the Great saŋa la sa.
english: The Semeiskie are a community of orthodox Old Believers who have lived in the Transbaikal since the reign of Catherine the Great.

kusaal: Ninkʋda la pʋ'ʋsim la malima da pʋ dɔlis nɛ teŋ la pʋ'ʋsim wada la, ka li yinɛ 17th century tiasig kanɛ da naam teŋin la pʋ'ʋsim yɛla, ka ba da buon ye Raskol.
english: The sacred rites and rituals of the Old Believers came to be in opposition to those of the official state church after the introduction of the 17th century religious reforms known as the Raskol.

kusaal: Semeiskie da anɛ ninkʋda pʋ'ʋsim la'asig la da du'oe tɔɔmi keŋ Gomel n bɛ Belarus teŋin (at that time part of Poland).
english: The Semeiskie were a particular group of Old Believers who fled to Gomel in Belarus (at that time part of Poland).

kusaal: Sankan la Catherine the Great da kad la'asig la yis teŋ la ta'asi ba Buryatia, ka o yɛlʋg anɛ ye ba tun'oe lieb Cossack teŋgurnam kpaadid banɛ da gur teŋgbaʋŋ la bɛŋir zin'is la.
english: Catherine the Great then exiled the group to Buryatia, on the pretext that they could there become farmers for the Cossack guards who defended the borders of the empire.

kusaal: Semeiskie malimala da kpɛn'ɛ paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity gbaʋŋin 2001.
english: The cultural space and oral culture of the Semeiskie was placed on the UNESCO List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2001.

kusaal: Banɛ da zan'as tiasid la, ba da buon nɛ ba ye "Old Believers".
english: Those who rejected the reforms became known as "Old Believers" (mostly, the Russian Old-Orthodox Church) and continued to practice their faith despite repression.

kusaal: Ba ye Semeiskie yʋʋma nam mɔr nɛ polyphonic dissonance ba pʋ'ʋsim yɛla ni nɛ yʋʋma banɛ pʋ pian'ad pʋ'ʋsim yɛlaa.
english: The Semeiskie songs are notable for their polyphonic dissonance in both sacred and secular music.

kusaal: Yʋʋma la yɛlzut la kpab nɛ yɛla bɛdigʋ, pʋ'ʋsim yɛla ni nɛ daar wʋsa yʋʋma, everyday songs.
english: The themes of the songs vary widely, from religious texts to everyday songs.

kusaal: Sene East Constituency anɛ constituency banɛ bɛ Ghana ka mɔr sɔ' ka o zi'e ba nɔba zug Parliament of Ghana.
english: Sene East is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Sene Districti bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Sene District of the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Sene East constituency bɛnɛ Sene Districti bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Sene District of the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka aan ba wadmaan ka zi'eni ba nɔba zug.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Sene West Constituency anɛ constituency banɛ bɛ Ghana ka mɔr sɔ' ka o zi'e ba nɔba zug Parliament of Ghana.
english: Sene West is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da nwaae di yinɛ Sene constituency linɛ da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi' (1992) la ni, ka lin mɛ da yi Brong Ahafo Region.
english: It was formed from the Sene constituency which at its inception in 1992, was a constituency in the defunct Brong Ahafo Region.

kusaal: Sene constituency da pʋdʋgnɛ zin'isa ayi' dinɛ an Sene East nɛ Sene West yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayi' (2012) la ni.
english: Sene constituency was split into Sene East and Sene West in 2012.

kusaal: Brong Ahafo Region mɛ da pʋdʋgnɛ zin'is atan', Bono, Ahafo nɛ Bono East region.
english: The Brong Ahafo Region was also spit into three, Bono, Ahafo and Bono East region.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ Sene District linɛ bɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the Sene District of the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di da pin'ilnɛ ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi (2012) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la nyaan paae.
english: It was created before the 2012 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Sene West Constituency bɛnɛ Bono East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Sene West is located in the Bono East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Sene West yʋ'ʋm bɛnɛ Bono East.
english: Sene West is now in Bono East.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋ nid yinne ka aan ba wadmaan zi'eni ba nɔba zug.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Ka yʋma 2020 la ni la, o da pʋ di ye o zi'en New Patriotic Party mp ka Davis Ansah Opokudi.
english: In 2020, he lost the bid to lead the New Patriotic Party going into the parliamentary elections to Davis Ansah Opoku.

kusaal: Acheampong anɛ karimbiig (Presbyterian).
english: Acheampong is a Christian (Presbyterian).

kusaal: O yinɛ Atibie-Kwahu, teŋbil yinne kanɛ bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana nwa .
english: He hails from Atibie-Kwahu, a town in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O kpɛn' Graduate School of Management nɛ France nɛ Paris ka paam postgraduate diploma in Management kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ yʋma 2008 la ni.
english: He entered the Graduate School of Management, France, Paris and obtained his postgraduate diploma in Management in 2008.

kusaal: Acheampong anɛ Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la (NPP) nid.
english: Acheampong is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O paas nɛ 5th, 6th nɛ 7th parliament bɛ 4th Republic of Ghana.
english: He is a member of the 5th, 6th and 7th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O pin'ili an wadmaan nɛ yʋʋm paal nwadig 2009 ka paam vɔɔt kal 17,519 yi 25,468 vɔɔtʋg wʋsa bɛ Constituency.
english: He first came into the parliament in January 2009 obtaining 17,519 votes out of 25,468 valid votes in his Constituency.

kusaal: Yʋma 2012 la ni, o da zi'en nɔ'ɔr ayi' bɛ Mpraeso Constituency wadmaan kʋk la bɛ NPP ye o paas wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas ayuobʋ tis fourth republic la ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested for re-election into the Mpraeso Constituency parliamentary seat on the ticket of the NPP to become a member of the sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: O anɛ minista tis Eastern Region.
english: He is currently serving as the minister of the Eastern Region.

kusaal: Acheampong du'am yʋʋm anɛ Burnya nwadig 18, 1971 la ni.
english: Acheampong was born on December 18, 1971.

kusaal: O nam anɛ wadmaan (MP) tis He Constituency la ti paae zina.
english: He is still representing his Constituency till date.

kusaal: o keŋɛ Leicester Business School, UK ka yina nɛ o Master of Business Administration degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ in finance bɛ yʋma 2001 la ni.
english: He went to Leicester Business School in the United Kingdom, where he obtained his Master of Business Administration degree in finance in 2001.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn keŋ University of Cape Coast ka yina nɛ Bachelor of Commerce nɛ Diploma in Education kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ yʋma 1997 la ni.
english: He also studied at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana, and obtained a Bachelor of Commerce with Diploma in Education in 1997.

kusaal: O da mɛ lɛn keŋ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology nɛ Ghana School of Law, bɛ yʋma 2008 nɛ yʋma 2010 la ni.
english: He also attended Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, and Ghana School of Law, in 2008 and 2010 respectively.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan tis Daboya-Mankarigu Constituency n bɛ Northern Region sʋ'ʋlim, o anɛ ma'asim tiig paati nid.
english: Shaibu Mahama (born 15 October 1970) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Daboya-Mankarigu Constituency in Ghana's Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Mahama nɛ October 15, 1970.
english: Mahama was born on 15 October 1970.

kusaal: O yinɛ Daboya tenpʋkanɛ bɛ Northern Region Ghana nwa ni la.
english: He hails from Daboya, a town in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Mahama anɛ Ma'asim tiig paati nid (NDC).
english: Mahama is a member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

kusaal: Yʋma 2012 la ni, O da nyi'ad ye o lieb wadmaan tis Daboya-Mankarigu n paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la, bɛ Ghana kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: Legal Office, Savanna Accelerated Development Authority (SADA), Accra Office Mahama worked at Ghana Breweries Limited from 1999 to 2000 as the Brewery Accountant, Purchase To Pay Manager at Guinness Ghana Breweries Limited from 2003 to 2007, an Associate at Just Kings & Associate from 2010 to 2012.

kusaal: Mahama anɛ mɔr, ka mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis anu.
english: Mahama is Muslim, and is married with five children.

kusaal: Bartels anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party la nid.
english: Bartels is a member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi (December 2020), o anɛ Wadmaani tis Ablekuma North Constituency.
english: In December 2020, she was elected member of Parliament for Ablekuma North Constituency after she competed in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election and won.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisnu nɛ anaasi, kɔbisnii nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (54,821) dinɛ an pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi du'al pisi nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin la (64.26%).
english: She polled 54,821 votes which represents 64.26% of the total votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas Ashley Mensah Winifred onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid la nɛ Princess Agyemang Awuku onɛ an Ghana Union Movement nid la.
english: She was elected over Ashley Mensah Winifred of the National Democratic Congress and Princess Agyemang Awuku of the Ghana Union Movement.

kusaal: Nɛ' da anɛ pistan nɛ anaasi du'alpiswai (34.90%) nɛ nɛɛm du'al pisnii nɛ anaasi (0.84%) kɔbiga pʋʋgin.
english: These were equivalent to 34.90%, and 0.84% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O anɛ Kwamena Bartels onɛ da an Wadmaani tis Ablekuma North yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la (January 1997) ken paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la (January 2009).
english: She is the daughter of Kwamena Bartels who was also member of parliament of Ablekuma North from January 1997 to January 2009.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu Nwadisa atan la daba awai daar (9 March 1975).
english: She was born on 3 September 1975.

kusaal: O yinɛ Gomoa Assin n bɛ Central Region sʋ'ʋlim, Gaana.
english: She is from Gomoa Assin in the Central Region in Ghana.

kusaal: Sheila Bartels anɛ Gaana kpikpin nɛ pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Sheila Penelope Bartels is a Ghanaian entrepreneur and politician.

kusaal: O da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020 Gaana dim vɔɔtʋg la) ka di Ablekuma North Constituency kʋk la.
english: She contested in the 2020 Ghanaian General Election and won the parliamentary seat for Ablekuma North Constituency.

kusaal: Ban da paamnɛ tusa pisi nɛ awai, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi (29,772), nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (716).
english: These obtained 29,772, and 716 votes respectively out of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Shiraz carpet (Persian: قالی شیراز) anɛ Persian rug yinne banɛ ka ba maali ba tɛŋkpɛmis banɛ bɛ Shiraz tɛnpʋʋgin linɛ bɛ Fars, Iran sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: A Shiraz carpet (Persian: قالی شیراز) is a type of Persian rug made in the villages around the city of Shiraz, in the Iranian province of Fars.

kusaal: Ba maan fʋʋd nwa yitnɛ dɔɔg nidib banɛ ʋgʋd fʋʋd la ni, linzug ka ba tʋasid Qashqai, Khamseh (Basseri nɛ Khamseh Arabs), Afshar, Abadeh nɛ Luri ʋgʋb.
english: Designs tend to come from settled tribal weavers so they mimic Qashqai, Khamseh (Basseri and Khamseh Arabs), Afshar, Abadeh and Luri designs.

kusaal: Fuud banɛ yi Basseri buudi dɔɔg nidibin, Persian dɔɔd la yinne bɛ Fars sʋ'ʋlim la nyɛ yʋ'ʋr nɛ ba fuud la vɛnlim yɛla.
english: The rugs of the Basseri tribe, one of the Persian tribes of the Fars province, are famous for their colorful designs.

kusaal: Shiraz rugs ʋgʋd nɛ baanlʋg, ka Qashqai nɛ Abadeh ʋgʋd baanlʋg.
english: Shiraz rugs are not often very finely knotted, with both Qashqai and Abadeh both having a finer knot.

kusaal: Shiraz dɔlnɛ Persia dim ʋgʋb buudi an si'em la.
english: Shiraz utilizes the Persian (asymmetrical) knot.

kusaal: Fuud la gima sieba yinɛ Cyrus' wief piela ni na.
english: Some pieces feature Cyrus' white horse.

kusaal: Shiraz carpet anɛ fʋʋg kanɛ ka ba maal ka li nwɛnɛ niis (nightingales).
english: The Shiraz carpet is the only rug to depict nightingales, which are shown as angular-shaped birds.

kusaal: Niis bama pa'al nɛ pʋʋg tigir nɛ summalisim.
english: These birds are said to symbolise contentment and happiness.

kusaal: Ghana zudaan Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an Minister of Foreign Affairs bɛ 10 yʋʋm paal nwadig 2017.
english: She was appointed foreign minister by Ghanaian president Nana Akufo-Addo on 10 January 2017.

kusaal: Ka mɛ an Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs nɛ Minister of State bɛ ku'om sʋŋir tʋʋma nɛ tʋʋma nɛ ya maalʋg sʋŋir tʋʋma ni, John Kufuor na'am yʋʋm saŋa la ni.
english: Previously, she was a Member of Parliament for Anyaa-Sowutuom from 2013 to 2021 and had served as Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and a Minister of State at the Ministry of Water Resources, Works and Housing under John Kufuor.

kusaal: O anɛ sakur biig kʋdʋg tis University of Ghana Business School (UGBS) nɛ Ghana Institute of Journalism (GIJ) nɛ Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) nɛ Pitman's Central College nɛ University of London nɛ University of Westminster wʋsa bɛnɛ United Kingdom (UK).
english: She studied at the University of Ghana Business School, the Ghana Institute of Journalism (GIJ), Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA), the Pitman's Central College, University of London and University of Westminster.

kusaal: Minister la mɔr Executive MBA, (Project Management option) nɛ MA bɛ Public Communication nɛ Bachelor of Laws Degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ (LLB) nɛ Diploma in Public Relations and Advertising nɛ kasɛta gbana bɛ Marketing Management ni.
english: She holds an Executive MBA (Project Management option), MA in Public Communication, Bachelor of Law Degree (LLB), a Diploma in Public Relations and Advertising as well as a certificate in Marketing Management.

kusaal: Saŋkan la ni la, o da anɛ Ranking Member tis Parliamentary Select Committee bɛ Foreign Affairs ka nannanna o anɛ Appointments nɛ Defence and Interior Committees bɛ wadmaanib yir la ni.
english: During the same period, she was Ranking Member for the Parliamentary Select Committee on Foreign Affairs and later, the Appointments, Defence and Interior Committees of Parliament.

kusaal: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey tʋm nɛ o taaba ye ba sʋŋ Community Parliament nɛ suoya banɛ kɛt ka ba gɔsid yɛl banɛ nar ka bɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm la ni kat wa'ae nɛ ninsaal sʋ'oe-mɛŋ nɛ ba yɔlisim, ka tisid labasʋma kati wa'ae ECOWAS lʋgʋr la yɛla.
english: A member of the ECOWAS Parliament from 2013 – 2017, she worked with her colleagues to assist the Community Parliament in its advisory role in considering matters concerning the region particularly on issues relating to fundamental human rights and freedom, while making recommendations to institutions and organs of ECOWAS.

kusaal: Hon Minister la lɛn an kʋk zudaan onɛ tial ayi' bɛ NEPAD & APRM Committees.
english: She also served as Vice Chair on the NEPAD & APRM Committees.

kusaal: Nannana o bɛnɛ Communication nɛ Gender and Children Committees bɛ wadmaanib yir la ni dinɛ ka o tʋmid nɛ o taaba ye ba gɔs yɛla ni kati wa'ae pian'ad wʋsa ka lɛn kpansid ninsaal buudi wʋsa nɛ biis nɛ ba bɛllim wʋsa.
english: Before she called time on her sixteen years career as member of parliament, Shirley was a member of the Communications as well as the Gender and Children Committees of Parliament where she worked with colleague members to look into matters relating to communications and examined all gender and children focused issues to ensure their inclusion in all appropriate legislation.

kusaal: Yʋda bani nɔki tis wadmaanib yir ka ba gɔs ka di'e di la da bɛnɛ 21 January 2021, ka Ghana Zugdaan Nana Akuffo-Addo da ye o gɔs, Madam Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey ka ba da gaŋ ye o an minister for Foreign Affairs nɛ Regional Integration.
english: On 21 January 2021, she was nominated as the minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration by the president of Ghana, Nana Akuffo-Addo.

kusaal: Yiiga ka o kpɛn' pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛbin, Shirley da anɛ Marketing and Communications Company kpɛɛm ka naam kpɛn' pɔlitis wʋsa ni, din ka o da an consultant tis Ministry of Tourism.
english: Before entering into frontline politics, Botchwey ran a marketing and communications company where she was a consultant for the Ministry of Tourism.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ managing director bɛ Dynacom Limited.
english: She was also the managing director of Dynacom Limited.

kusaal: Onɛ an public administration, o tʋm lʋgʋr kɔn'ɔ-kɔn'ɔb nwɛnnɛ Worldspace Ghana nɛ Divestiture Implementation Committee nɛ Glaxo Group Research nɛ Hodge Recruitment.
english: As a practitioner of public administration, she worked with various organizations such as Worldspace Ghana, the Divestiture Implementation Committee, Glaxo Group Research and Hodge Recruitment.

kusaal: Shirley anɛ Chairperson of ECOWAS Council of Ministers nɛ Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration of Ghana nannanna.
english: Botchwey was the Chairperson of ECOWAS Council of Ministers and the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ karimbiig ka pʋ'ʋsid Anglican pʋ'ʋsʋm la.
english: She is an Anglican.

kusaal: O da anɛ wadmaan (MP) tis Anyaa-Sowutuom teŋ sʋ'ʋlʋm din yi yʋma 2013 ti paae yʋma 2021 la ni.
english: Previously, she was a Member of Parliament for Anyaa-Sowutuom from 2013 to 2021 and had served as Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and a Minister of State at the Ministry of Water Resources, Works and Housing under John Kufuor.

kusaal: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey anɛ onɛ ka ba da du'a o 8 fʋlʋnfʋk nwadig 1963 la ni bɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlʋmin.
english: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey (born 8 February 1963) is a Ghanaian politician, diplomat and lawyer who has served as the seventh secretary-general of the Commonwealth of Nations since 1 April 2025.

kusaal: Zugdaan John Agyekum Kufuor onɛ an NPP nid la na'am yʋʋm naar la ni la, Hon Ayorkor Botchwey tʋmnɛ an Deputy Minister tis Foreign Affairs nɛ Iabaya tʋʋma nɛ Trade and Industry ministries.
english: Previously, she was a Member of Parliament for Anyaa-Sowutuom from 2013 to 2021 and had served as Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and a Minister of State at the Ministry of Water Resources, Works and Housing under John Kufuor.

kusaal: O anɛ legislator kanɛ paas nɔ'ɔr anaasi daan ka bɛ tis Weija constituency kanɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa mi' li yɛla la, li nɔ'ɔr anaasi ka teŋ la naam pʋdʋgɛ.
english: She was a member of parliament for four terms, first representing Ghana's most populous constituency, Weija, and later, Anyaa/Sowutuom which was carved out of Weija before the 2012 elections.

kusaal: O anɛ mp nɔ'ɔr ayi', ka nannana o tʋmidi tisid Anyaa/Sowutuom.
english: She was a member of parliament for four terms, first representing Ghana's most populous constituency, Weija, and later, Anyaa/Sowutuom which was carved out of Weija before the 2012 elections.

kusaal: O kʋ lɛn nyaŋi zi'eni bɛ yʋma 2020 vɔɔtʋg la ni n lieb wadmaan ya'asa.
english: Botchwey chose not to run for a fifth term in Parliament in the 2020 Election.

kusaal: Minister tʋmnɛ an pian'a pian'ad tis Foreign Affairs din yi yʋma 2009 la ni ti paae yʋma 2013 la ni.
english: At the party level, she served as spokesperson on foreign affairs between the year 2009 and 2013.

kusaal: O anɛ onɛ paas ECOWAS wadmaanib yir la ni din yi yʋma 2013 la ni ti paae yʋma 2017 la ni, Hon.
english: A member of the ECOWAS Parliament from 2013 – 2017, she worked with her colleagues to assist the Community Parliament in its advisory role in considering matters concerning the region particularly on issues relating to fundamental human rights and freedom, while making recommendations to institutions and organs of ECOWAS.

kusaal: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey ka' sidaa ka mɔr biis ayi'.
english: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey is a single mother of two.

kusaal: Sibahle Mtongana (/siˈbaːɬɛ əmˈtɔŋana/, dʋ'am 10 Samanpiid 1984) anɛ South Africa nid kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr yi ye o anɛ ninkanɛ dʋgʋd diib, ka pian'ad T.V zug, ka lɛn an gbansɔbid.
english: Sibahle Mtongana (/siˈbaːɬɛ əmˈtɔŋana/, born 10 December 1984) is a South African celebrity chef, restaurateur, television presenter, and author.

kusaal: Nidib lɛn mi' o nɛ ka o an gbaŋ sɔbidi tis labaya zin'ig kanɛ buon Drum Magazine, nɛ Cooking Channel nɛ Food Network T. V nam zug bɛɛ Siba's Table.
english: She is best known for her freelance work at Drum Magazine, and the Cooking Channel and Food Network television series, Siba's Table.

kusaal: Mtongana da nɔbigi bɛ nɛ tɛŋpʋʋg kanɛ ka ba buon Mdantsane ka li kpi'e nɛ East London, South Africa sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Mtongana grew up in the township of Mdantsane near East London, South Africa. She is the daughter of Noliza, a retired teacher and Mncedisi Mnwana, a retired supervisor of a leather goods manufacturer.

kusaal: On nɛ o sid mɔr biis anaasi: Lonwabo, Linamandla, Buhlebenkosi nɛ Ntandoyenkosi.
english: She and Brian have 4 kids: Lonwabo, Linamandla, Buhlebenkosi & Ntandoyenkosi.

kusaal: Siba sid yʋ'ʋri buon Brian Mtongana.
english: Siba is married to Executive Creative Director for Woolworths, Brian Mtongana.

kusaal: O anɛ kpaanr ka paas nɛ o dʋ'adib biisa ayuobʋ ni.
english: She is the youngest in a family of six children.

kusaal: siing banɛ maan kpaam, la'am nɛ Africanized honeybee la, ba bɛnɛ genus Apis la ni.
english: There are 29 subspecies of one of these species, Apis mellifera, native to Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Africanized bees are a hybrid strain of A. mellifera that escaped from experiments involving crossing European and African subspecies; they are extremely defensive.

kusaal: Di pʋ yuugɛ ka ba tis labaar zaŋidi wa'ae siind kpaam yɛla (bee fossil) yit genus Melittosphex la ni, anɛ dinɛ ka ba siak yɛ ba anɛ "an extinct lineage of pollen-collecting Apoidea, sister-group to the modern bees", nɛ saŋa bɛ Lower Cretaceous (~100 mya).
english: A fossil from the early Cretaceous (~100 mya), Melittosphex burmensis, was initially considered "an extinct lineage of pollen-collecting Apoidea sister to the modern bees", but subsequent research has rejected the claim that Melittosphex is a bee, or even a member of the superfamily Apoidea to which bees belong, instead treating the lineage as incertae sedis within the Aculeata.

kusaal: Fʋn na gʋ'ʋn siins ba siind la yɛla anɛ beekeeping, bɛɛ apiculture.
english: Human beekeeping or apiculture (meliponiculture for stingless bees) has been practiced as a discipline of animal husbandry for millennia, since at least the times of Ancient Egypt and Ancient Greece.

kusaal: On an siem la ke ka ba tis sida ye kat adaptive radiation dinɛ bɛ angiosperms la ni, nɛ siins la mɛŋ.
english: The appearance of these structures drove the adaptive radiation of the angiosperms, and, in turn, bees themselves.

kusaal: Evolutionary scenario kaŋa nɔɔ da naam bɛ vespoid siins la ni, bud kaŋa ka ba da buon ye "tangbɛɛnlam puum la" "pollen wasps" ka mɛ lɛm pɛɛs ba yaanam banɛ da kuud la.
english: This same evolutionary scenario may have occurred within the vespoid wasps, where the pollen wasps evolved from predatory ancestors.

kusaal: Wɛnɛ bʋnvʋya bɛdigʋ an siem la, siing niŋgbiŋ la pʋdignɛ zin'is atan': zug la, thorax (o teŋsʋk), nɛ o zʋʋr bɛɛ gbin(o nya'a).
english: The thorax has three segments, each with a pair of robust legs, and a pair of membranous wings on the hind two segments.

kusaal: Monogamy (queens mating singly) anɛ ba kʋdimin tʋʋma ka ba mi dinzugɔ di tun'e an ye haplodiploidy la ta'asid siins anɛ evolution bɛ eusociality.
english: However, since single mating appears to be the ancestral condition in all eusocial lineages studied so far, haplodiploidy may still have played an important role in the early evolution of eusocial behaviour in bees.

kusaal: Dunia wʋsa da kua kikan'asiid yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi ni (2020) ka li zɛm si'em da anɛ 1.9 billion tonnes, ka Brazil kua pisnaai, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (40%) dunia wʋsa kuob pʋʋgin ka India mɛ kua pisi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (20%) dunia wʋsa maalig la pʋʋgin.
english: Global production of sugarcane in 2022 was 1.9 billion tonnes, with Brazil producing 38% of the world total and India 23% (table).

kusaal: Ba kuodi ba bɛnɛ tʋʋlig zin'isi bɛ Indian nɛ Southeast Asia yʋʋm kɔbis si'em yela banɛ gaad la linɛ buon sucrose ka mɔr malisim bɛɛ li bʋʋlim la pʋʋg la yela.
english: They have been cultivated in tropical climates in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia over centuries for the sucrose found in their stems.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi ni (2020), dunia wʋsa da kuo sugar beets ka li maal si'em anɛ 253 million tonnes, ka Russia da gaad tuoni kua linɛ ka ba la'as dunia wʋsa piinɛ atan' kɔbiga pʋʋgin (13%).
english: In 2022 global production of sugar beets was 260 million tonnes, led by Russia with 18.8% of the world total (table).

kusaal: Bɛdigʋ mi'i li ye sucrose, lactose, bɛɛ fructose.
english: Compound sugars, also called disaccharides or double sugars, are molecules made of two bonded monosaccharides; common examples are sucrose (glucose + fructose), lactose (glucose + galactose) and maltose (two molecules of glucose).

kusaal: Sikir sʋŋ bɛɛ sucrose, li yi nɛ kiŋka'ansiin ni bɛɛ sikir beet.
english: Raw sugar is sucrose which is extracted from sugarcane or sugar beet.

kusaal: Brazil an teŋkanɛ maan sikir gat ka India's an teŋkanɛ dit sikir gat teŋ wʋsa.
english: Global production of sugarcane in 2022 was 1.9 billion tonnes, with Brazil producing 38% of the world total and India 23% (table).

kusaal: Fructose anɛ sikir kanɛ bɛ tiig wala niis.
english: Fructose, galactose and glucose are all simple sugars, monosaccharides, with the general formula C6H12O6.

kusaal: Sucrose nɛ fructose anɛ banɛ ka ba maal ka di an sikir bibis.
english: Sucrose is used in prepared foods (e.g., cookies and cakes), is added to commercially available ultra-processed food and beverages, and is used as a sweetener for foods (e.g., toast and cereal) and beverages (e.g., coffee and tea).

kusaal: Glucose an dinɛ an bʋnbil paa bɛ sikir baanlʋg la ni.
english: Glucose has the molecular formula C6H12O6.

kusaal: Sikir tɔn'ɔn an simple carbohydrates bɛɛ complex carbohydrates.
english: Fructose, galactose and glucose are all simple sugars, monosaccharides, with the general formula C6H12O6.

kusaal: Simple carbohydrates yinɛ bʋnmalisiŋ yinnɛ bɛɛ bi'ela ma'a ni.
english: Simple sugars, also called monosaccharides, include glucose, fructose and galactose.

kusaal: Complex carbohydrates yinɛ bʋnmalisima la'as bɛdigʋ maal.
english: Sugar is a class of sweet-tasting, soluble carbohydrates, many of which are used in food.
