kusaal: Fʋ ya'a gɔs brown sugar ba mɔr ku'om sabiligi li pʋʋgin, ka ba mɔri tʋm la'ad sɛn'ɛb zin'igin.
english: The crystals of raw sugar have a sticky brown coating and either can be used as they are, can be bleached by sulfur dioxide, or can be treated in a carbonatation process to produce a whiter product.

kusaal: Sikir gbila la ba paasid sulfur dioxide, bɛɛ ba dʋgʋ li yis bʋnsi'eba li pʋʋgin ka li li'eb pi'elig.
english: The crystals of raw sugar have a sticky brown coating and either can be used as they are, can be bleached by sulfur dioxide, or can be treated in a carbonatation process to produce a whiter product.

kusaal: Ku'om 2,500 litres (660 US galam) nar ye ba paas kilogram yinnɛ wʋsa pʋʋgin (2.2 pounds) sikir kanɛ ka ba maan la ni.
english: About 2,500 litres (660 US gal) of irrigation water is needed for every one kilogram (2.2 pounds) of sugar produced.

kusaal: Sikir bɛ diib si'eba ni, bɛɛ li ye ti nɔkir pa'as diib zug ka li malis.
english: Sugar is a class of sweet-tasting, soluble carbohydrates, many of which are used in food.

kusaal: Din yi yʋma 1996 ti paae yʋma 2002 la ni la, Simon da anɛ surveyor bɛ Nulux Plantation Limited dim lʋgirin la ka lɛn an sakur pa'an-pa'an bɛ Nakpalu-Borle Primary School din yi yʋma 2005 ti paae yʋma 2016 la ni.
english: Between 1996 and 2002, Tampi was a surveyor at Nulux Plantation Limited and also a teacher at Nakpalu-Borle Primary School between 2005 and 2016.

kusaal: O mɔr advanced B.S. kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit Sunyani Polytechnic nɛ kasɛta gbaʋŋ kanɛ bɛ vocational and technical education yit University of Education,Winneba ni la nɛ B.S kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ Construction Education.
english: He has an advanced B.S. certificate from Sunyani Polytechnic, a certificate in vocational and technical education from the University of Education, Winneba and a B.S certificate in Construction Education.

kusaal: O du'am yʋʋm anɛ sigsaa nwadig 24, 1975.
english: He was born on 14 April 1975.

kusaal: Simon Atingban Akunye (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ 2 February 1954) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Simon Atingban Akunye (born 2 February 1954) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O da paasnɛ Wadmaannib yikanɛ paasi anu la Fifth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, zi'eni tis Pusiga constituency bɛ Upper east region sʋ'ʋlim Ghana la.
english: He was a member of the Fifth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Pusiga constituency in the Upper east region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di'e o nɛɛs kasɛta gbaʋŋʋ yinɛ Nigeria.
english: He obtained his nursing certificate in Nigeria.

kusaal: Nɛ' da naamnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi la ni (1984).
english: This was in 1984.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛm mɔr Executive master's degree in Governance and Leadership dinɛ ka o di'e yi Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration.
english: He also holds an Executive master's degree in Governance and Leadership from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration.

kusaal: Akunye anɛ senior nursing officer bɛ Akunye Memorial Clinic.
english: Akunye is a senior nursing officer at Akunye Memorial Clinic.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti Akunye yiga ka o keŋ wadmaannib yin lanɛ ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress nɔba zug yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: Akunye was first voted into parliament on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress during the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: On da li la ka gban'e ye o keŋi o kɔn'ɔ kɔn' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ (2016) Ghana wadmaanib vɔɔtʋg la, amaa ka da pʋ di Pusiga kʋk la ka Laadi Ayii Ayamba onɛ bɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress di.
english: However, he lost the National Democratic Congress primaries in 2016.Thereafter, he decided to go Independent during the 2016 Ghanaian parliamentary elections, but lost the Pusiga seat to Laadi Ayii Ayamba of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O constituency da paasnɛ sʋ'ʋlimnam awai (9) yi kʋgʋs piinɛ atan (13) banɛ ka Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress da di vɔɔtkan ni Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: His constituency was a part of the 9 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election for the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress da dinɛ kʋgda dinɛ kʋgʋs piswai nɛ anaasi (94) yi kʋgʋs kɔbisyi' nɛ pistan pʋʋgin (230).
english: The National Democratic Congress won a minority total of 94 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayi, kɔbiga nɛ piinɛ ayi (12,112) yi vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anii nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi (18,700) pʋʋgin.
english: He was elected with 12,112 votes out of 18,700 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Nɛ' da zɛmnɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi du'ali anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (64.8%) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: This was equivalent to 64.8% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka bas Yahaya Seidu Awinaba onɛ an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nid.
english: He was elected over Yahaya Seidu Awinaba of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: On da paamnɛ vɔɔt tusa ayuobʋ, kɔbisnu nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (6,588) yi vɔɔt la wʋsa pʋʋgin.
english: He obtained 6,588 votes of total votes cast.

kusaal: Nɛ' da zɛmnɛ pistan nɛ anu du'ali ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (35.2%) vɔɔt la wʋsa ni.
english: This was equivalent to 35.2% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa anii, kɔbisnii nɛ atan (8,803) yi vɔɔt tusa piinɛ anu, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi (15,684) pʋʋgin.
english: He was elected with 8,803 votes out of 15,684 total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o ka basi Azongo Peter Tasiri onɛ bɛ Peoples' National Convention, Mohammed Imoro Asoko onɛ bɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɛ Abugbila Daniel onɛ bɛ Anɔraʋg paati, Convention People's Party.
english: He was elected over Azongo Peter Tasiri of the Peoples' National Convention, Mohammed Imoro Asoko of the New Patriotic Party and Abugbila Daniel of the Convention People's Party.

kusaal: O anɛ Catholic pʋ'ʋsim nid ka mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis anii.
english: He is a Catholic and married with eight children.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Akunye nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi nwadisa ayi la daba ayi daar (February 2, 1954).
english: Akunye was born on February 2, 1954.

kusaal: O yinɛ Pusiga bɛ Upper East Region, Ghana.
english: He is a hails from Pusiga in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di'e kasɛta gbaʋŋkaŋa nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la ni (2008).
english: He acquired the certificate in 2008.

kusaal: O da lɛn di nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) la ka di.
english: He run for a second term in office in 2008 in which he won.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ, o da li Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress vɔɔtʋg la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni (2016).
english: However, he lost the National Democratic Congress primaries in 2016.Thereafter, he decided to go Independent during the 2016 Ghanaian parliamentary elections, but lost the Pusiga seat to Laadi Ayii Ayamba of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii la nii (2008), ba da lɛn gaŋ o ye o an wadmaani tis constituency kan ya'as.O da dinɛ Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg National Democratic Congress nɔba zug di.
english: His constituency was a part of the 9 parliamentary seats out of 13 seats won by the National Democratic Congress in that election for the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Nɛ' anɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ du'al piinɛ atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (56.13%).
english: This was equivalent to 56.13% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛnam da zɛmnɛ ayi du'al pisnaasi nɛ awa kɔbiga pal pisnaasi nɛ awa kɔbiga pʋʋgin (2.49%), pistan nɛ ayi du'al yiine kɔbiga pʋʋgin (32.01%) nɛ awai du'al pistan nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (9.37%) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: These were equivalent to 2.49%, 32.01% and 9.37% respectively of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Bama da paamnɛ kɔbistan nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (391), tusa anu nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (5,021) nɛ tusir yinne, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ awai (1,469) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: These obtained 391, 5,021 and 1,469 votes respectively of total votes cast.

kusaal: o pinnate vaand la kaae alaa din wa'alim anɛ 20-40cm (8-16in), ka mɔr 20-30 vaan banɛ bɛ an sabil dɛnɛ'm la, ka o vaand walim na an 3-8cm (1+1⁄4–3+1⁄4 in) wa'alim.
english: The opposite, pinnate leaves are 20–40 cm (8–16 in) long, with 20 to 30 medium to dark green leaflets about 3–8 cm (1+1⁄4–3+1⁄4 in) long.

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋr kanɛ an Azadirachta indica la Adrien-Henri de Jussieu da sɔbi li zaŋi pa'al sɔ' wʋsa bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis nii nɛ pistan' (1830).
english: The name Azadirachta indica was first published by Adrien-Henri de Jussieu in 1830.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir kɔbis yɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' (1753), Carl Linnaeus da pa'al bʋnami ayi, Melia azedarach nɛ Melia azadirachta.
english: In 1753, Carl Linnaeus had described two species, Melia azedarach and Melia azadirachta.

kusaal: De Jussieu on da gɔs ka Melia azadirachta anɛ dinɛ bɛɛ li kɔn' nɛ Melia azedarach nɛ ban na nɔki digil new genus.
english: De Jussieu considered Melia azadirachta to be sufficiently different from Melia azedarach to be placed in a new genus.

kusaal: On da pian'a bʋn sieba yɛla, Linnaeus da ye li yʋ'ʋr anɛ 'azedarach' dinɛ yit French pian'ad yʋ'ʋrin na an 'azédarac', dinɛ da an Persian 'āzād dirakht' (ازادرخت), dinɛ pa'al 'free or noble tree Persian tii la yʋ'ʋr la anɛ azad darakhat-e-hind, ka di pa'al ye 'India dim ti kanɛ mɔr yɔlisim'('the free tree of India,) ka di pa'al yee tii la mtr yɔlisim yi ban'as nɛ bʋnvʋya ni.
english: For both his species, Linnaeus referred to the name 'azedarach', which is derived from the French 'azédarac', which in turn is from the Persian 'āzād dirakht' (ازادرخت), meaning 'free or noble tree'.

kusaal: Sisibig yinɛ Assam region, Pakistan nɛ Bangladesh linɛ bɛ Indian tɛŋin paae Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand nɛ Vietnam linɛ bɛ Indochina.
english: Azadirachta indica is considered to be native to the Assam region, Pakistan and Bangladesh in the Indian subcontinent and to Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam in Indochina.

kusaal: Li paae zin'is si'eba yinɛ South America paae Indonesia.
english: It has been widely introduced elsewhere in tropical and subtropical regions, from South America, West Africa to Indonesia.

kusaal: Li maan sʋ'ʋŋa zin'is banɛ ka tʋʋlig bɛ ka lɛɛ kʋ nyaŋi bɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka tʋʋlig pʋ paae 5 °C (41 °F).
english: It can tolerate high to very high temperatures and does not tolerate temperature below 5 °C (41 °F).

kusaal: Ba da sɛɛ li maki li nɔbigir yela gɔs nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nam saŋa (1960s) nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii saŋa (1980s) tɛnsʋk bɛ Darwin, Queensland, nɛ Western Australia, amaa Australian sisibig pɔɔg la da pʋ nyaŋi zi'enɛ.
english: Trial plantations were established between the 1960s and 1980s in Darwin, Queensland, and Western Australia, but the Australian neem industry did not prove viable.

kusaal: Di anɛ buudi yinnɛ kanɛ pɛ'ɛs Azadirachta buudi ni.
english: It is one of the two species in the genus Azadirachta.

kusaal: Di kae saan India teŋin nɛ Southeast Asia teŋ siebaa.
english: It is native to the Indian subcontinent and to parts of Southeast Asia, but is naturalized and grown around the world in tropical and subtropical areas.

kusaal: Vaan piela banɛ mɔr nyuug la tuu nɛ taaba ka bɛdigʋ bɛɛ bi'ela axilliary panicles nwa lit teŋin ka li wa'alim tun'e paa 25cm (10in).
english: White and fragrant flowers are arranged in more-or-less drooping axillary panicles which are up to 25 cm (10 in) long.

kusaal: o inflorescences la wa'alim an atan' mʋm pʋʋgi la, mɔr puum ka li paae 250 - 300.
english: The inflorescences, which branch up to the third degree, bear from 250 to 300 flowers.

kusaal: Wɛl la gʋʋgin waŋ kanɛ an pielii kpi'im la (endocarp) gurnɛ biilif yinne, ka saansa bi'ela anɛ ayi bɛɛ atan',biili wa'ali wɛnii (kernels) ka dinɛ giligi li la an wilim-wilim.
english: The white, hard inner shell (endocarp) of the fruit encloses one, rarely two, or three, elongated seeds (kernels) having a brown seed coat.

kusaal: Margosa tiig la nɛ nɛ'ɛŋ wɛnɛ taaba, chinaberry bɛɛ bakain, Melia azedarach la baŋir tɔi.
english: The neem tree is similar in appearance to its relative, the chinaberry or bakain, Melia azedarach, with which it may be confused.

kusaal: Li nyaŋidi zi'enid zin'is banɛ ka pɛbisig bɛ bɛɛ tʋʋlʋg bi'ela bɛ, zin'is banɛ ka saa niib bɛn an wan wʋʋ 400–1,200 mm (16–47 in).
english: Normally, it thrives in areas with sub-arid to sub-humid conditions, with an annual rainfall of 400–1,200 mm (16–47 in).

kusaal: Li bɛnɛ zin'is banɛ ka tʋʋlig bɛ ka lin na nyaŋi bɛ zin'ig si'a tʋʋlig bɛn anɛ 21–32 °C (70–90 °F).
english: It is a typical tropical to subtropical tree and exists at annual mean temperatures of 21–32 °C (70–90 °F).

kusaal: India tɛŋin nɛ zin'is banɛ ka Indian nidib paae, li anɛ na'ana'a nɛ fʋ na nyɛ Sisibig tiig la suoya nɔya ni anina, Winpʋ'ʋsʋm zin'is, sakurnamin nɛ zin'is banɛ ka nidib la'asid bɛɛ nidib yampɔna.
english: In India and tropical countries where the Indian diaspora has reached, it is very common to see neem trees used for shade lining streets, around temples, schools and other such public buildings or in most people's backyards.

kusaal: Ba gɔs ka sisibig anɛ mɔɔg zin'ig si'eba, wan wʋʋ Middle East, li kaskas anɛ Sub-Saharan Africa tɛɛns wan wʋʋ West Africa nɛ Indian Ocean tɛɛns, nɛ zin'ig si'eba Australia tɛŋin.
english: Neem is considered a weed in many areas, including some parts of the Middle East, most of Sub-Saharan Africa including West Africa and Indian Ocean states, and some parts of Australia.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛnu, Vaala nwadig ni (April 2015), ba da nɔk sisibig ka li paas nɛ class B nɛ C mɔɔd ni bɛ Northern Territory, Australia sʋ'ʋlim, ka li pa'al ye sɛɛ ka ba gɔsi li ka li da yadig tɛŋa bɛɛ ba da mɔri li kpɛn'ɛ tɛŋ la ni na.
english: In April 2015, A. indica was declared a class B and C weed in the Northern Territory, Australia, meaning its growth and spread must be controlled and plants or propagules are not allowed to be brought into the territory.

kusaal: Lin da kɛŋ Australia tɛŋin, yʋʋm tusir, nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nam saŋa la (1940s), ba da sɛ sisibig yiiga bɛ nɛ Northern Territory ye li maal ma'asim tis bʋnkɔnbid.
english: After being introduced into Australia, possibly in the 1940s, A. indica was originally planted in the Northern Territory to provide shade for cattle.

kusaal: Dinɛ paasi azadirachtin ka mɔr kpinnim anɛ limonoids, biili la kpaam mɔr glycerides, polyphenols kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb, nimbolide, triterpenes, nɛ beta-sitosterol.
english: In addition to the triterpenoid azadirachtin and related limonoids, the seed oil contains glycerides, diverse polyphenols, nimbolide, triterpenes, and beta-sitosterol.

kusaal: Kpakanɛ an dɔnbʋʋlʋm ka mi'is la mɔr nyuug kanɛ nwɛnɛ gabpiel ka mɛ mɔr limonoid compounds dinɛ an 2%.
english: The yellow, bitter oil has a garlic-like odor and contains about 2% of limonoid compounds.

kusaal: Vaand la mɔr quercetin, catechins, carotenes, nɛ vitamin C.
english: The leaves contain quercetin, catechins, carotenes, and vitamin C.

kusaal: Tiig: Margosa tiig la anɛ dinɛ yɛla pak hali di anti-desertification nwaasim la zug nɛ din an sʋ'ʋm nwɛnɛ carbon dioxide sink la zug.
english: Tree: the neem tree is of great importance for its anti-desertification properties and possibly as a good carbon dioxide sink.

kusaal: Margosa genome nɛ transcriptomes banɛ yi lʋga kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb la anɛ dinɛ tuun dɔl taaba.
english: The neem genome and transcriptomes from various organs have been sequenced.

kusaal: Expressed sequence tags anɛ dinɛ ka ba nyɛ ka di dɔl generation of subtractive hybridization libraries dinɛ bɛ margosa wala bʋʋlʋm, vaand, wala pa'ad nam.
english: Expressed sequence tags were identified by generation of subtractive hybridization libraries of neem fruit, leaf, fruit mesocarp, and fruit endocarp.

kusaal: Sissala East bɛni Sissala East Municipal n bɛ Upper West Region Ghana nwa.
english: Sissala East is located in the Sissala East Municipal of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Na'am kʋk la bɛni Sissala East District n bɛ Upper West Region Ghanan nwa.
english: The seat is located within the Sissala East District of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba ya-tiuŋ la kpi'enɛ Burkina Faso.
english: Its northern neighbour is Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Ka lin yi ya-datiuŋ ti paae ya -dagɔbʋg n bɛ ya-nya'aŋ bɛn la, anɛ Chiana-Paga constituency n bɛ Kassena/Nankana District nɛ Builsa North nɛ Builsa South constituencies n bɛ Builsa District, li wʋsa bɛni Upper East Region sʋʋlim.
english: From north to south along the eastern border lie the Chiana-Paga constituency in the Kassena/Nankana District and the Builsa North and Builsa South constituencies in the Builsa District, all within the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Sissala East onɛ constituencies nam la yinne ka mɔr wadmaan ka o zi'el tis ba bɛ wadmaanib yir la Ghana nwa.Ba vɔtʋg gaŋ wadmaan yinne ka an linɛ ka nidib la vɔɔt gaŋ nid yinne ma'a .
english: Sissala East is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Ka ba ya-tuon an Sissala West constituency ka Wa East mɛ bɛ ba ya-dagɔbʋŋg.
english: To the north west is the Sissala West constituency and the Wa East is to the south west.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la, Ghana vɔtʋg lʋgir la daa ti yis Sissala West yi constituency kaŋa ni.
english: In 2004, the Sissala West was carved out of this constituency by the Electoral Commission of Ghana.

kusaal: wadmaan la nɛ vɔtʋg kal la kanɛ bɛ digin nwa, n bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la, anɛ Sissala constituency kʋdʋg la din.
english: The MPs and results listed here prior to 2004 are for the old Sissala constituency.

kusaal: Sissala West bɛni Sissala West district n bɛ Upper West Region Ghana nwa.
english: Sissala West is located in the Sissala West district of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Na'am kʋk la bɛni Sissala West District n bɛ Upper West Region Ghana nwa.
english: The seat is located within the Sissala West District of the Upper West Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ka li ya-datiuŋ an Burkina Faso.Ka ya-toun an kpi'enɛ Jirapa, Lambussie nɛ Nadowli East constituencies nam.
english: Its western neighbours are the Jirapa, Lambussie and Nadowli East constituencies.

kusaal: ka Nadowli East constituency kpɛlim gilig nɛ ya-dagɔbʋg ka ya-nya'aŋ an Sissala East constituency.
english: The Nadowli East constituency continues round the south and to the east is the Sissala East constituency.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi la ni, ka Ghana vɔtʋg lʋgir la daa na naami constituency la yiiga nɛ 29 paala sieba ka other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies nam la kal paas yi 200 ti paae 230.
english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Sissala West anɛ constituencies nam la yinne ka mɔr wadmaan ka o zi'el tis ba bɛ wadmaanib yir la Ghana nwa.Ba vɔtʋg gaŋ wadmaan yinne ka an linɛ ka nidib la vɔɔt gaŋ nid yinne ma'a.
english: Sissala West is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Na'am kʋk la, bad aa paam linɛ saŋkanɛ ka Ghana dim vɔtʋg tita'ar bɛ 2004 la.
english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Lina da naami yi ban daa pʋdig Sissala constituency ayi la, Sissala East nɛ Sissala West constituencies nam.
english: This was done by splitting the previous Sissala constituency into the Sissala East and Sissala West constituencies respectively.

kusaal: O yinɛ Chinderi.
english: He hails from Chinderi.

kusaal: O mɔnrɛ Masters Degree in Democracy, Governance, Law and Development (2016), Bachelor of Art Degree in Political Science and Adult Education (2014) nɛ Diploma in Youth in Development Work.
english: He holds a master's degree in Democracy, Governance, Law and Development (2016), a Bachelor of Art Degree in Political Science and Adult Education (2014) and a Diploma in Youth in Development Work.

kusaal: O da anɛ Stevedore Supervisor tis Golden Gate Services.
english: He was a Stevedore Supervisor at Golden Gate Services.

kusaal: Kuyon anɛ National Democratic Congress nid.
english: Kuyon is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la Nwadisa awai la nii (September 2012), Pirɛsidɛn John Dramani Mahama da gaŋ o ka ba siak ye o an Diisi (District chief executive) tis Krachi Nchumuru District Assemble.
english: In September 2012, he was nominated by President John Dramani Mahama and confirmed as the District chief executive for Krachi Nchumuru District Assemble.

kusaal: O da zi'eni o Na'adɔɔg nɔba zugʋ nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la ka di nɛ vɔɔt Tusa piinɛ atan, kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (13,488) dinɛ zi'eni tis pisnaasi nɛ anaasi dʋ'ali atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (44.3%) gaad onɛ tia'al o la, Kakateche Innocent Tache onɛ bɛ New patriotic Party ka paam vɔɔt Tusa piinɛ ayi, kɔbianaasi nɛ anaasi (12,404) dinɛ an pisnaasi dua'ali anii kɔbiga pʋʋgin (40.8%).
english: He won the parliamentary election with 13,488 votes representing 44.3% of the total votes cast, beating his main opponent Kakateche Innocent Tache of the New patriotic Party who obtained 12,404 votes representing 40.8% of the total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid pʋ'asada nɛ dasam nɛ buudi malima yɛla (Youth, Sports and Culture) ka lɛn paas la'askanɛ gɔsid holding Office of Profit Committee Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la Gaana Fourth Republic la ni.
english: He serves as a member of Youth, Sports and Culture Committee and Members holding Office of Profit Committee respectively in the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Kuyon nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu Nwadisa anii dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 August 1975).
english: Solomon Kuyon (born 28 August 1975) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: Solomon Namliit Boar Bugirbiig (talk) 16:51, 15 June 2023 (UTC) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd, ba da du'anɛ yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyuobυ nɛ anii, nwadis ayɔpɔi la li dabisim piina nu, o anɛ wadmaan n paas ti Gaana wadmaanib la ni.
english: Solomon Namliit Boar (born 15 July 1968) is a Ghanaian politician who served as a Member of Parliament for Bunkpurugu from 2017 to 2021.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg nid ka an Regional Minista kυdυg n tis North East Region linɛ bɛ Gaana la.
english: He is a member of the New Patriotic Party and served as the first Regional Minister of the newly-created North East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Yυυma tusayi' nɛ piina yɔpɔi la li nwadis atan' la ni ka ti Gaana Gɔmina Zugraan Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Boar ye o paas Regional Minista nam nya'andɔlib piiga la ni zi'enɛ tis o Gɔmina la.
english: In March 2017, President Nana Akufo-Addo named Boar one of the ten deputy regional ministers who would form part of his government.

kusaal: Kpɛɛmnam la da gaŋ o ka nɔk o yυ'υre tis Speaker of Parliament wadmaanib yizuk daan la ka wadmaanib yidim la di'e zian'am gɔs ka mɛ siak o.
english: The committee approved him and his name was forwarded to Speaker of Parliament for further approval by the general house of parliament.

kusaal: Boar anɛ Kristo biig, o anɛ Baptist karimbiig.
english: Boar is a Christian (Baptist).

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ University of Cape Coast, linɛ bɛɛ ti Gaana sυ'υlυm la maal o Bachelor of Arts degree linɛ an management studies yυυma tusa yi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: He studied at the University of Cape Coast, and obtained his Bachelor of Arts degree in management studies in 2007.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn keŋ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology maal linɛ an Executive Master of Business Administration (CEMBA) digirii la ani yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yi' la ni.
english: He also attended the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, where he obtained his Executive Master of Business Administration (CEMBA) degree in 2012.

kusaal: O di pυ'a mɔr biis anu.
english: He is married (with five children).

kusaal: Sophia Abena Boafoa Akuffo JSC (du'a nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai li nwadis piinɛ ayi la, li dabisim pisi daar) ka da aan Chief Justice Ghana nwa li da yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi li nwadis ayuobʋ la li daisim piinɛ awai daar ti paae ar ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai li nwadis piinɛ ayi li dabisim pisi daar.
english: Sophia Abena Boafoa Akuffo (born 20 December 1949) is the former chief justice of Ghana from 19 June 2017 to 20 December 2019.

kusaal: O da anɛ Presbyterian karimsaam bipʋŋ , o da keŋ secondary sakur nɛ Parliament Hill School, Hampstead, London nɛ Wesley Girls' High School, Cape Coast ka nɛ o paam Bachelor of law degree n yi University of Ghana.
english: She had her secondary education at Parliament Hill School, Hampstead, London and Wesley Girls' High School, Cape Coast and obtained her Bachelor of law degree from the University of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr Master's degree bɛ Law yi Harvard University in USA.
english: She has a master's degree in law from Harvard.

kusaal: Sophia Akuffo da tʋʋmɛ bɛ private practice ka Jerry Rawlings da nɔki o ka o tʋʋm Supreme Court bɛ yʋʋm tʋsir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai la, li nwadis piinɛ yinne la.
english: Sophia Akuffo worked about 20 years in private practice before being was raised to the Supreme Court bench by Jerry Rawlings in November 1995.

kusaal: O da paasi Governing Committee of the Commonwealth Judicial Education Institute nidib la, ka aan kʋk daan n bɛ Alternative Dispute Resolution Task Force bɛ yʋma bɛdegʋ.Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ li nwadig yinne la, ba da vɔt tis o ka o aan piyam nam la yinne bɛ African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights: Ba da vɔt tis o ka o bɛ yʋma ayi ka ba da lɛm vɔt tis o ya'as ti paae 2014 ka o aan kʋk daan nya'adɔl nɛ kʋk daan bɛ Court.
english: She has been a member of the Governing Committee of the Commonwealth Judicial Education Institute, and the chairperson of the Alternative Dispute Resolution Task Force for several years.

kusaal: Akuffo da sɔb Application of Information & Communication Technology n bɛ Judicial Process – Ghana dim la Experience, a presentation to the African Judicial Network Ghana (2002).
english: Akuffo wrote The Application of Information & Communication Technology in the Judicial Process – the Ghanaian Experience, a presentation to the African Judicial Network Ghana (2002).

kusaal: Ba yiine anɛ John Atta Mills onɛ da o pa'anɛ o bɛ Taxation at the Ghana Law School ka ba mɛ lem gaŋ o n bɛ African Court of Human and Peoples' Rights bɛ Ethiopia.O mɛ lɛm da pʋ'ʋsi Jerry Rawlings onɛ gaŋ o ka o tʋm n bɛ Supreme Court bɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu nɛ John Kufuor onɛ gaŋ o ka o tʋm n bɛ African Court of Human and Peoples' Rights bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ.
english: She also spoke of her gratitude to some former Presidents of Ghana, these included John Atta Mills who was her lecturer on Taxation at the Ghana Law School and also nominated her for the African Court of Human and Peoples' Rights in Ethiopia.

kusaal: o da yʋ'ʋn lieb kʋk daan tis court yi ti John Mahama sʋŋi ka Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ka o an piyam naam kpɛɛm.
english: She became president of this court with the support of John Mahama and was nominated by Nana Akufo-Addo as chief justice.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi li nwadis atan' li dabisim pisi nɛ anii, Nana Akufo-Addo da ti gaŋ appointed Akuffo ka o aan kʋk daan tis gɔmma lʋgir paal ka aan COVID-19 National Trust Fund kanɛ zʋgʋ bɛ COVID-19 pandemic saŋa.
english: On 28 March 2020, Nana Akufo-Addo appointed Akuffo to chair a newly formed COVID-19 National Trust Fund inaugurated during the COVID-19 pandemic.

kusaal: O mɔr bipʋg ka o yʋ'ʋr aan Violet Padi nɛ yaas ayi , Samuel Osei nɛ Cara Nyame.
english: Sophia Akuffo has a daughter, Violet Padi, and two grand children Samuel Osei and Cara Nyame.

kusaal: O da aan piyam bɛ Supreme Court of Ghana li yi yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu.
english: She had been a judge in the Supreme Court of Ghana since 1995.

kusaal: O da dɔlisi o sakur nɛ Ghana School of Law ani ka o paam suor aan barrister.
english: She furthered her education at the Ghana School of Law where she qualified as a barrister in 1975.

kusaal: Akuffo zamis lɔy bɛ Nana Akufo-Addo.
english: Akuffo trained as a lawyer under Nana Akufo-Addo, who would later become the president of Ghana in 2017.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la li nwadis anu li dabisim piinɛ ayinne, ba da ti gaŋ Akuffo ka o aan highest ranking piyam n bɛ Supreme Court of Ghana Nana Akuffo-Addo saŋa,ka wadmaanib yir dim da siak.Akuffo-Addo da zʋgʋ o nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ li nwadis ayuobʋ la li dabisim piinɛ awai , o da paasi Piyam nam kpɛɛm nam piinɛ atan' nam Ghana Republic.
english: On 11 May 2017, Akuffo was nominated as the highest ranking Judge of the Supreme Court of Ghana by Nana Akuffo-Addo, subject to approval by Parliament.

kusaal: Saria kad kanɛ ka o da paas kpi'ilim bɛni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai li nwadis piinɛ ayi' li dabisim piinɛ anii daar, ka Supreme Court da siak ye courts nɛ nya'aŋi zin' bakɔi naar nɛ bank vʋ'osim dabisa nɛ ba tu'a antu'a kpana.
english: The last judgment she was involved in was on 18 December 2019 when the Supreme Court passed a unanimous ruling that courts could sit at weekends and on bank holidays to deal with urgent legal cases.

kusaal: O mɛ da pʋ'ʋs Ghana gɔmma zuraan kʋda si'eba.
english: She was sworn in by President Akuffo-Addo on 19 June 2017 as the thirteenth Chief Justice of the Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da lɛm aan kʋk daan bɛ board of the University of Ghana ka mɛ boards of directors bɛ organizations bɛdegʋ nid yinne.
english: She also serves as the chairperson of the board of the University of Ghana and holds membership on several boards of directors of various organizations.

kusaal: Sophia Karen Edem Ackuaku anɛ Ghana Politis nwɛ'ɛd ka mɛ an Ghana republic kanɛ aan anaasi wadmaanib yir kanɛ paas ayɔpɔi la nid yinne, ka zi'e tis Domeabra-Obom Constituency kanɛ bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlʋm la Ma'asim Tiig na'adɔɔg la (NDC).
english: Sophia Karen Edzem Ackuaku is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Domeabra-Obom Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ackuaku nɛ Sapal Nwadig la (October) daba ayɔpɔi daar yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi' (7th October 1972) la ni.
english: Ackuaku was born on 7 January 1972.

kusaal: O yinɛ Anyako teŋ kanɛ bɛ Volta Region Ghana la.
english: She hails from Anyarko in the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ackuaku anɛ onɛ dɔlis zamisa buudi bɛdegʋ ni paam linɛ anɛ Public Relation nɛ Labaya Mɔɔlʋg tʋʋma nɛ Da' Diib tʋʋma kasɛta gbana Ghana Institute of Journalism.
english: Ackuaku earned her Bachelor of Laws from MountCrest University College and a certificate in public relation, advertisement and marketing from the Ghana Institute of Journalism.

kusaal: O mɛ lɛn mɔr linɛ anɛ Diploma in Social Work kasɛta gbaʋŋ yit Social work Sakurin la bɛ Osu-Accra nɛ Proficiency Dutch Pian'ad yit Zadkine College n bɛ Rotterdam, Holland la.
english: She also has a diploma in social work from the School of Social Work in Osu-Accra and a proficiency in Dutch Language from Zadkine College in Rotterdam, Holland.

kusaal: Ackuaku mɛ mɔr Tuongaadʋg nɛ Human Rights nɛ HIV/AIDS kasɛta gbana yit The Ark Foundation n bɛ Ghana la.
english: Ackuaku also has a certificate in leadership, human rights and HIV/AIDS from the Ark Foundation in Ghana.

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2016 la ni la, Sophia da zi'en Ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la nɔba zug nyi'a Domeabra teŋ sʋ'ʋlʋm wadmaan kʋk la ka paam di.
english: Sophia contested and won the parliamentary seat for the Domeabra-Obom Constituency in the 2016 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O da nyi'anɛ nɛ nidib anaasi banɛ an; Darison Barba Mohammed onɛ da an NPP nid nɛ Ekow Jones Mensah onɛ da an CPP na'adɔɔg la nid nɛ Gideon Dudu onɛ da an PPP na'adɔɔg la nid nɛ Pius Kwame Fiakuna onɛ da an A-sʋ-oe-mɛŋ paati la.
english: She contested against four others namely Darison Barba Mohammed of the New Patriotic Party, Ekow Jones Mensah of the Conventions People's Party, Gideon Dudu of the Progressive People's Party and Pius Kwame Fiakuna an independent candidate.

kusaal: Yiiga ka o lieb wadmaanib yir la nid, o da dɛŋi anɛ Deputy executive director onɛ n sʋ'oe Operations zin'ig kanɛ an Ghana National Service Scheme la, lin yi yʋma 2013 ti paae yʋma 2016 la ni.
english: Before her status as a member of the Ghanaian parliament, she has worked as the deputy executive director in charge of operations at the Ghana National Service Scheme, from 2013 to 2016.

kusaal: Lin yi yʋma 2004 ti paae yʋma 2013 la ni la, o da anɛ Managing director linɛ bɛ Eligreen/Amsos Ghana Limited lʋgir la ni.
english: From 2004 to 2013 she worked as a managing director at Eligreen/Amsos Ghana Limited.

kusaal: Yiiga ka o lieb kpɛɛm kaŋa la, o da dɛŋi anɛ Deputy manager bɛ Golden Souvenir Lotto ni, Northern Region Ghana nwa' ni, lin yi yʋma 1995 ti paae yʋma 2000 la ni ka an FBWE local nid tit Federation linɛ an Business Women Entrepreneur lin yi yʋma 2001 ti paae yʋma 2010 la ni.
english: Before this she has worked previously as the FBWE focal person for the Federation of Business Women Entrepreneurs from 2001 to 2010.

kusaal: Nananna, o anɛ Food, Agriculture nɛ cocoa Affairs Committee nɛ Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee nid.
english: As a parliamentarian in the Ghanaian parliament, she has served on the Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs Committee and the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee of parliament.

kusaal: O da anɛ Ghana wadmaanib yir la nid kanɛ da sʋŋi n gɔt diib yɛla nɛ Agriculture nɛ cocoa tʋʋma Committee nɛ Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee bɛ wadmaanib yir la ni.
english: As a parliamentarian in the Ghanaian parliament, she has served on the Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs Committee and the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee of parliament.

kusaal: Nidib mi' o nɛ pamm ka li anɛ on da zi'eni pian'a tis Usha Gupta saŋa pamm ni bɛ BBC Radio 4 serial The Archers nɛ sini kanɛ ka o da an pʋana'ab Dosh Khaleem bipuŋ la ba sixth season (sini nami ayuobu) saŋa dinɛ an HBO series Game of Thrones la.
english: She is best known for her portrayal of the solicitor Usha Gupta, in the long-running BBC Radio 4 serial The Archers and for her role as the High Priestess of the Dosh Khaleen in the sixth season of the HBO series Game of Thrones.

kusaal: O du'adib da anɛ Irish nɛ Syrian dim, ka ba da du'a Faress nɛ Accra sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana, yʋʋm tʋsir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anii(1948) la ni.
english: Faress was born in 1948 in Accra, Ghana, to Irish and Syrian parents.

kusaal: O nɔbignɛ Southport, Lancashire, ka zamis sini di'emanam la Guildhall School of Music and Drama ka bɛ London.
english: She grew up in Southport, Lancashire, studied drama at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama.

kusaal: Faress da naae o sɔbʋg zamisʋg la nɛ City Literary Institute adult education college.
english: Faress completed a writing course at City Literary Institute adult education college.

kusaal: Fares da yinɛ nɔɔr ayi bɛ BBC series I, sini ni, Claudius(1976) an bipʋŋ saŋkpan'as (kied kuŋ yee bugim) ka on da an wa'ad-wa'ad sɔbi bɛ Messalina's ( ayidaan nɛ sidkulʋg) sidkulʋg la'asigin la o da baŋ yee sogianam na kenna gban'a ba.
english: Faress appeared in two episodes of the BBC serial I, Claudius (1976) as a slave girl (shouting fire) and as a dancer who at Messalina's (second and bigamous) marriage party realises troops are coming to arrest them.

kusaal: O da yi bɛɛgin BBC Selma in the Blake's 7 episode 'Horizon'.
english: In another early BBC appearance, she played the character Selma in the Blake's 7 episode 'Horizon'.

kusaal: Din yii anina Faress yʋ'ʋm da maal sininam dinɛ anɛɛ My beautiful Launderette(1985) nɛɛ Sixth Happiness (1997), nɛ nyiŋ di'emanam UK sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Since then, Faress has had substantial roles in films such as My Beautiful Laundrette (1985) and Sixth Happiness (1997), as well as much stage work around the UK.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ yinne, Sawa'ar Nwadig(October 2001) la ni, o da yina bi'ela nwa na bɛ Coronation Street an Dev Alahan's mother Umila la.
english: In October 2001 she appeared briefly in Coronation Street as Dev Alahan's mother Umila.

kusaal: Souad Faress mɛ da lɛm yii o sini ni na an the Old Rani in The Sarah Jane Adventures series The Mad Woman in the Attic yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ awai, Sawa'ar Nwadig(October 2009) la ni.
english: Souad Faress also appeared as the Old Rani in The Sarah Jane Adventures serial The Mad Woman in the Attic in October 2009.

kusaal: yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anaasi Sawa'ar Nwadig(October 2014) la ni, ba da mʋʋl yee Faress ye o Kenna di'emnɛ dinɛ an Hurried Steps, Sharon Wood's translation of ''Passing Affrettati by Dacia Maraini.
english: In October 2014, it was announced that Faress would perform in Hurried Steps, Sharon Wood's translation of "Passi Affrettati by Dacia Maraini.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛɛ yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga yinne (2010) nɛɛ (2011) teŋsʋk ka o da di'em Jay Faldren's grandmother, Maryam Shakiba, in Casualty.
english: Between 2010 and 2011 she played Jay Faldren's grandmother, Maryam Shakiba, in Casualty.

kusaal: Faress da lɛm Tina di'em nwɛnɛ du'atanɛ dinɛ ka ba buoni ba yee No Angels, Anji Mittel's aunt Di.
english: Faress appeared in an episode of popular nursing drama No Angels as lead character, Anji Mittel's aunt Di.

kusaal: Faress da lɛm di'em nwɛnɛ wʋʋ I anɛ sibiti siani du'ata nɛ, dinɛ an ''The Dead of Jericho'', nɛcɛŋa di ka o da maalibɛ Inspector Morse ni.
english: Faress appeared briefly as a hospital doctor in "The Dead of Jericho", the first episode of Inspector Morse.

kusaal: Yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayuobu(2016) la ni o da kɛŋi tʋm nɛ HBO series Game of Thrones in season 6 ka na'abipʋŋɔ tis Dosh Khaleem.
english: In 2016 she joined the HBO series Game of Thrones in Season 6 as the High Priestess of the Dosh Khaleen.

kusaal: O da lɛm yi ITV sini di'ema dinɛ an Brief Encounters, 'a loose adaptation of Ann Summers CEO Jacqueline Gold's memoirs, Good Vibrations''.
english: Faress also appeared in ITV drama Brief Encounters, "a loose adaptation of Ann Summers CEO Jacqueline Gold's memoirs, Good Vibrations".

kusaal: Yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ anii(2018) la Faress da yina maal sini bɛ Clare Holman's teŋin dinɛ an Only the Lonely.
english: In 2018, Faress appeared in Clare Holman's short film Only the Lonely.

kusaal: Yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ awai(2019) la ni, da onɛ yit ti di'emid saŋa wʋsa bɛ Daisy Haggard nɛ Laura Solon's sitcom Black to Life nɛ as a mother of Eli Cohen bɛ OCS/Netflix ministries The Spy.
english: In 2019, Faress appeared as a recurring character in Daisy Haggard and Laura Solon's sitcom Back to Life and as the mother of Eli Cohen in the OCS/Netflix miniseries The Spy.

kusaal: Ba di,a o nɛ Ghana amaa ka mɛ lɛɛ bɛ Syria nɛɛ Irish dim buud la.
english: Born in Ghana, she also holds Syrian and Irish citizenships.

kusaal: Di'ema la bɛdigʋ da yitnɛ Amnesty International, ka pian'a zug la da an puabibigir, ninkʋʋsim, nyɛbʋg yɛla nɛ puab yɛla Sieba dinɛ geesidi ba.
english: The play's narratives were mainly sourced from Amnesty International, the subject matter including rape, honour killings, sex trafficking and other issues of violence against women.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne, nwadis piinɛ ayi la nii, Haiti da nyɛ yʋ'ʋr nɛ ba zɛɛnd joumou yɛla ka UNESCO dim kaanli li paas saalib malima nɛ ba diib banɛ bɛ dunia nwa pʋʋgin.
english: In December 2021, Haiti obtained official recognition for the knowledge, know-how and practices pertaining to the consumption of soup joumou on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021), joumou zɛn'ɛd da paas UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List kanl ni.
english: In 2021, soup joumou was added to the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List.

kusaal: Ba mɔr nɛ walbanɛ buon squash la dʋgʋd zɛɛnd, li yinne an turban squash.
english: The soup is traditionally cooked with winter squashes such as the turban squash.

kusaal: Ba ɛɛnti wan' walbama dʋgʋl dʋkin nɛ kʋrkʋr niim gbila nɛ kɔnba, potato, nɛ zɛnvaand (vegetables) ka ba sieba an leeks, celery, radishes, carrots, green cabbage, habanero pepper nɛ gabʋ (onions).
english: This pureed squash is then added to the simmering broth and meat mixture along with pieces of beef and soup bones, potato, and vegetables such as malanga, leeks, celery, radishes, carrots, green cabbage, habanero pepper and onions.

kusaal: Ka yʋ'ʋm paas Yaarim (Salt) nɛ gu'ud (seasoning), lime juice, garlic, parsley nɛ vaand sieba nɛ spices.
english: Epis, salt, and seasoning along with lime juice, garlic, parsley and other herbs and spices are then added.

kusaal: Haitian ninsieba paasid pasta biela ka lin sieba anɛ vermicelli, macaroni ka kpaam bɛɛ butter.
english: Some Haitians add thin pasta such as vermicelli and macaroni and a small amount of butter or oil.

kusaal: Soup joumou anɛ zabini pa'al Haiti dimi da nyɛ yɔlisim yi French nu'usin yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs nii nɛ anaasi, yiiga nwadig dabisir yinne daar la (January 1, 1804).
english: 1, 1804, Haitians celebrated by consuming soup joumou all day, relishing the taste of freedom.

kusaal: Yʋʋm paal daar la, Haiti dim banɛ da bɛ ba mɛŋ tɛŋin nɛ banɛ da lɔ'ɔŋ tɛŋ sieba wʋsa da di diib nwa ka li pa'al ban da nyɛ yɔlisim yi yammʋg pʋʋgin yiiga ka ba da sʋ'ʋgi ba mɛŋ teŋ la.
english: In December 2021, Haiti obtained official recognition for the knowledge, know-how and practices pertaining to the consumption of soup joumou on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO.

kusaal: Di ya bɛlim bɛnɛ ya-dagɔbʋg kilo 2,798 (1,739 miles) bɛ kuom babir ka kpi'e nɛ South Atlantic nɛ Indian Ocean; ya-datiʋg babir ka lɛm an kpies nɛ Namibia, Botswana, nɛ Zimbabwe; ya-nya'aŋ nɛ Mozambique nɛ Eswatini ya-datiʋg; ka an Lesotho kpia/yak.
english: South Africa, officially the Republic of South Africa (RSA), is the southernmost country in Africa. The country consists of nine provinces, and is bounded to the south by 2,798 kilometres (1,739 miles) of coastline that stretches along the South Atlantic and Indian Ocean; to the north by the neighbouring countries of Namibia, Botswana, and Zimbabwe; and to the east and northeast by Mozambique and Eswatini.

kusaal: South Tongu Constituency bɛnɛ South Tongu district linɛ bɛ Ghana Volta Region la.
english: South Tongu is located in the South Tongu district of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Constituency la bɛnɛ South Tongu Districti bɛ Volta Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The seat is located within the South Tongu District of the Volta Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Space of gong culture bɛ Vietnam Highland la (Vietnamese: Không gian văn hóa Cồng Chiêng Tây Nguyên) anɛ regioni bɛ Central Vietnam ka buudi malima kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon gong la yɛla paki hali.
english: The space of gong culture in the Vietnam Highlands (Vietnamese: Không gian văn hóa Cồng Chiêng Tây Nguyên) is an intangible cultural heritage of Vietnam's Central Highlands, home to "cultures which value gongs".
kus_article: Space of Gong Culture in the Central Highlands of Vietnam

kusaal: Di widigi paae Tây Nguyên sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk, Đắk Nông, nɛ Lâm Đồng.
english: It spans across the provinces of Quảng Ngãi, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk, and Lâm Đồng — amongst ethnic groups such as the Rade, Jarai, Bahnar, Mạ, and Lạch (Koho).
kus_article: Space of Gong Culture in the Central Highlands of Vietnam

kusaal: UNESCO da nyɛ li ka d nar ka ba zaŋi li paas ye di an Masterpiece of the Intangible Heritage of Humanity nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu nwadis piinɛ yinne dabpisi nɛ anu daar.
english: UNESCO recognized it as a Masterpiece of the Intangible Heritage of Humanity on the 25th of November, 2005.
kus_article: Space of Gong Culture in the Central Highlands of Vietnam

kusaal: Gong buudi la nyɛ gong ka di anɛ ya'ani tisi ba ka naan ninsaalib nɛ Wina'am, ka gong wʋsa mɔr ba'akanɛ paŋi zɛm nɛ gong la an yʋma si'em.
english: The following components make up the space of gong culture: the use of gongs to make music, in certain festivals (e.g. the New Rice Festival, Water Wharf Ceremony, etc.), and the places where such festivals are held (e.g. longhouses, stilt houses / rông houses, gươl houses, a "water source" (bến nước), tombs, "nearby forests", etc.).In the present day, the Gong Culture Festival is held annually across the Central Highlands, and is said to be "significant both as a means of cultural preservation and a popular tourist attraction".
kus_article: Space of Gong Culture in the Central Highlands of Vietnam

kusaal: Onɛ an kpɛɛm nananna, Alban Kingsford Sumana Bagbin, ba da zuŋ o ye o an Speaker tis Ghana wadmaannib yikanɛ paasi anii la (Eight Parliament of Ghana) yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2021).
english: The current speaker, Alban Kingsford Sumana Bagbin, was sworn-in for a second term as Speaker of the Ninth Parliament of Ghana after his reelection on 7 January 2025; having served his first term from 7 January 2021 to January 6, 2025.
en_article: Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana

kusaal: Speaker ɔfis la da yɔ'ɔg yiiga nɛ Gold Coast saŋa, dɔlisid Gold Coast wada gbaʋŋ la (Constitution) Order in Council, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu la ni (1950).
english: The office of the Speaker was first created in the then Gold Coast, under the Gold Coast(Constitution) Order in Council, 1950.
en_article: Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana

kusaal: Onɛ da an yiiga speaker of the Parliament of Ghana da anɛ Sir Emmanuel Charles Quist onɛ da an Speaker of the National Assembly yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne la ni (1951).
english: The first speaker of the Parliament of Ghana was Sir Emmanuel Charles Quist who was Speaker of the National Assembly in 1951.
en_article: Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana

kusaal: O da tʋm ala paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayɔpɔi nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni (December 1957), Ghana da di'e o mɛŋi yi na'asaanam nu'usin la nya'aŋ.
english: He stayed at post till December 1957, a few months after Ghana gained independence.
en_article: Speaker of the Parliament of Ghana
