kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Opoku Ware Sakur linɛ bɛ Kumasi.
english: He completed Opoku Ware School, Kumasi.

kusaal: O naae o Mastɛs zamisυg Digirɛɛ linɛ an Strategic Finance Management la nɛ n bɛ University of Derby, United Kingdom yυυma tusa yi' nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: He holds a Master of Science degree in Strategic Finance Management from University of Derby, United Kingdom in 2007.

kusaal: O mɛ maali o Bachelor of Science Digirɛɛ linɛ an Computer Science la nɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) sakurin la, Gaana sυ'υlυm.
english: He also had his Bachelor of Science Degree in Computer Science from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an Entrepreneurship Mit sakurin la.
english: He also has a Certificate in Entrepreneurship from MIT.

kusaal: O da maali PhD zamisυg la KNUST zamis kaŋa kpazɛɛri da anɛ Actuarial Science.
english: He also holds a PhD in Actuarial Science from KNUST.

kusaal: Amoah da anɛ ti Gaana kpɛla Chief Finance Officer of Kencity ka mɛ da lɛn tυm n an National Coordinator of National Insurance Authority (NHIA) kpɛɛm la nya'andɔl.
english: Amoah was the Chief Finance Officer of Kencity and also served in the past as the Deputy National Coordinator of the National Insurance Authority (NHIA).

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris ayi la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yɔpɔi la ni,ka ti Gaana Gɔmina Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an chief executive officer n gɔs Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) la.
english: In February 2017, He was appointed by President Akufo-Addo as the chief executive officer for the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC).

kusaal: Onɛ an CEO n tis Zintex Portfolio Services Limited la.
english: He is the CEO of Zintex Portfolio Services Limited.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris anii la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ ayi' la ni, ka Amoah da yɔ'ɔg Kumasi FC linɛ an ninwisigir di'ema linɛ bɛ Nhyiaeso Kumasi sυ'υlυm.
english: In August 2022, Amoah established the Kumasi FC which is a football club in Kumasi specifically Nhyiaeso.

kusaal: Ban da vɔt la o da paamnɛ vɔt bam 51,531 kɔbiga pυυginɛ, o da mɔri 81.71% ka o tiraan Richard Kwamina Prah onɛ da an Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg nid la mɛ da mɔr 11,033 vɔt kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 17.49% vɔt.
english: He won the seat after getting 51,531 votes representing 81.71% against his closest contender Richard Kwamina Prah of the National Democratic Congress who had 11,033 votes representing 17.49%.

kusaal: Amoah paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsidi ti ligidi yɛla la ni O mɛ anɛ Privileges kpɛɛmnam la yinne.
english: Amoah is a member of the Finance Committee and also a member of the Privileges Committee.

kusaal: Lin nya'aŋ ka o yυ'υn nɛɛnl o mɛŋ n pa'al GPS naae ka yυ'υn keŋi siak court buolυg la.
english: He later appeared before the court after presenting himself to the GPS.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Nhyiaeso sυ'υlυm la.
english: He is the member of parliament for the Nhyiaeso Constituency.

kusaal: Li liebnɛ ninwisigir di'ema zig ka ba zamisid nidib bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb nɛ zamisυg nam kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb nwɛnnɛ gymnasium, medical center nɛ linɛ kpɛlim.
english: It is a football academy with training center, gymnasium, medical center and other facilities.

kusaal: Yυυma tussah yi' nɛ piisi la vɔt la ni ka ba da vɔt ti Gaana na'am vɔt la ka Amoah Nhyaieso kυk la.
english: Amoah was elected member of parliament for Nhyaieso in the 2020 December parliamentary elections.

kusaal: Amoah anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Amoah is a Christian.

kusaal: Buniya nwarig la yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ yinne, ka ti Gaana La Magistrate Court la da yis gbaυŋ n tis pυlis ye ba gban'am Amoah nɛ Samuel Anim court n da buoli ba ka ba zan'as ye ba kυ keŋ la zug, n dɔl yɛlbanɛ da naamidi ti suoya nam ni la.
english: In December 2021, the La Magistrate Court issued a bench warrants for the arrest of Amoah and Samuel Anim for their refusal to appear before court for road traffic offenses.

kusaal: Ban da vɔt la o da mɔri vɔt bam 332 ka o tiraan la mɛ da mɔr 315 n yi vɔt la kanl wυsa linɛ da an 647 la.
english: He won by garnering 332 votes while the incumbent had 315 votes out of the 647 total vote cast.

kusaal: O nwɛ'ɛb saŋa laa, o da nwɛ' tis Udinese, Parma, Brescia, Juventus nɛ Fenerbahçe.
english: During his career, he played for Udinese, Parma, Brescia, Juventus and Fenerbahçe.

kusaal: Appiah pin'ili o nwɛ'ɛb lanɛ Hearts of Oak bɛ 1995, onɛ da an yʋma 15 la.
english: Appiah began his career at a local club named Hearts of Oak, in 1995, at age 15.

kusaal: Ka 1996 nii, o da bɔɔd ye o keŋ Galatasaray's youth squad, amaa o da pʋ nyaŋi kpɛn' anii, la lɛb Hearts of Oak na.
english: In 1996, he had trials with Galatasaray's youth squad but was not signed and he returned to Hearts of Oak.

kusaal: Ka 1997 pʋʋgʋnɛ, o da keŋ na'asaateŋ ye o nwɛ' Italian Serie A side Udinese, dinɛ ka o da nwɛ'ɛdi an sitiraka.
english: In 1997, he moved abroad to join Italian Serie A side Udinese, where he initially played as a striker.

kusaal: O da yi keŋ Parma 1999 ka wikanɛ ka ba ye viral hepatitis la gba'e o, amaa Appiah da paam laafi 2000 yʋʋm la ni.
english: A transfer to Parma in 1999 was jeopardised by viral hepatitis, but Appiah overcame the illness to move there in the summer of 2000.

kusaal: Ka onɛ nwɛ' yʋma ayi' bɛ Parma laa, Appiah kpɛn' loon bɛ Brescia 2002–03 nwɛ'ɛb la ni.
english: After two seasons at Parma, Appiah went on loan to Brescia for the 2002–03 season.

kusaal: Appiah da di goolnam ayɔpɔi nwɛ'ɛb 31 ni.
english: Appiah became a first-team regular for the Lombardians, and scored seven times in 31 games.

kusaal: Juventus da yɔ' Parma nɛ €2 million 2003 ye a kɛ' ka Appiah ka loon na kpi, ka tɔlisi keŋ tiim sia ni nɛ €6 bɛ 2004 la ni.
english: Juventus paid Parma €2 million in the summer of 2003 to secure Appiah's services on loan, with an option to a permanent €6 million transfer in 2004.

kusaal: Appiah da nwɛ'tis Ghana national team la.
english: Appiah was a member of the Ghana national team, which he represented at youth, Olympic, and senior levels.

kusaal: O da an kabitin tis Ghana ba 2006 nɛ 2010 World Cup la ni.
english: He captained Ghana at the World Cup debut in 2006 and in 2010 World Cup.

kusaal: Appiah da nwɛ'ɛd sʋŋa bɛ Parma dinɛ ka o da sʋŋid Serie A champions Juventus.
english: Appiah's success at Parma alerted defending Serie A champions Juventus to his talents.

kusaal: Ka 2003 la nii, Appiah da bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛd kani pɛ'ʋs 8 bɛ Afirika yʋʋm kana.
english: In 2003, Appiah finished 8th for African Footballer of the Year.

kusaal: Stephen Pambiin Jalulah anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan n tis Pru West linɛ bɛ Bono East region sυ'υlυm la.
english: Stephen Pambiin Jalulah is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of parliament for the Pru West constituency in the Bono East region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a o nɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris piiga la li dabisim piisi nɛ ayi yυυm tυsir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piis yɔpɔi nɛ anaasi la ni n bɛ Saboba linɛ bɛ ti Gaana Northern region su'υlυm la.
english: Jalulah was born on 22 October 1974 and hails from Saboba in the Northern region of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ da aan ba teŋin la DC ka mɛ da lɛn aan ba teŋin la National Health Insurance Authority tυυma la tuongat.
english: He was also the District Manager for the National Health Insurance Authority.

kusaal: Kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri vɔɔt pisnu nɛ ayuobu du'al ayɔpɔi (56.7%) ka o tiraan Masawud Mohammed mɛ da mɔr vɔtnam bam 12,671 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da mɔri 43.3%.
english: He won the parliamentary seat with 16,606 votes making 56.7% of the total votes whilst the incumbent Masawud Mohammed had 12,671 votes making 43.3% of the total votes.

kusaal: Nannanna, ti Ghana Gɔmina Nana Akufo-Addo gaŋ o ye o an Minista banɛ gɔti ti Ghana suoya yɛla la.
english: He was also the Deputy Minister for Roads and Highways after he was sworn in with thirty-nine others by His Excellency the former president Nana Akufo-Addo at the Jubilee House on 25 June 2021.

kusaal: O da naae o sakur linɛ an GCE linɛ ka buon ye Ordinary Level la n zamis Science yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ ayi ka tɔlis n lɛn zamis linɛ kpimisυg yɛla naae yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ anaasi la ni.
english: He had his GCE Ordinary Level in General Science in 1992 and had his GCE Ordinary Level in Business in 1994.

kusaal: Ala ya'as ka o lɛn keŋ tuonɛ naae o GCE Advance Level la zamis linɛ an kpimisυg la yɛla sυ'υŋa yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ ayuobu la ni.
english: He also had his GCE Advance Level in Business in 1996.

kusaal: Stephen anɛ Wabυg Na'adɔɔg la nid ka anɛ mɛ an wadmaan nannanna n tis Pru West sυ'υlυm la.
english: Stephen Pambiin Jalulah is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of parliament for the Pru West constituency in the Bono East region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ka yυυm tusa yi nɛ atan' la ka o tɔlis sakur tita'arin naae ka digirɛɛ linɛ an ligidi nɛ bankin tυυma yɛla, ka lin nya'aŋ ka o lɛn tɔlisi naae ka di'e digirɛɛ linɛ bigis ye o zamisnɛ Law yυυma tusa yi nɛ piina naasi la ni.
english: He further had his Degree in Finance and Banking in 2003 and also had his bachelor's degree in law in 2014.

kusaal: Stephen Michael Essuah Kofi Ackah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaan bɛ Seventh Parliament dinɛ bɛ Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Suaman Constituency dinɛ bɛ Western Region ka an Ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg la nid.
english: Stephen Michael Essuah Kofi Ackah is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Suaman Constituency in the Western Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Ackah yinɛ Suaman-Dadieso teŋ kanɛ bɛ Western region sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: Ackah hails from Suaman-Dadieso in the Western region.

kusaal: O paami o post secondary teacher training bɛ Wesley College, Kumasi ka lɛn keŋ Specialist Training College (STC), Winneba dinɛ ka o paam diploma kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: He had his post secondary teacher training at Wesley College, Kumasi and proceeded to the Specialist Training College (STC), Winneba where he obtained his diploma.

kusaal: O paami o Bachelor of Education (BEd) bɛnɛ Physical Education yit University of Education, Winneba yʋma 2000 la ni, ka paami o Executive Masters dinɛ bɛ Governance and Leadership (EMGL) Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) yʋma 2000 la ni.
english: He earned his Bachelor of Education (BEd) in Physical Education from the University of Education, Winneba in 2000, and had his Executive Masters in Governance and Leadership (EMGL) Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) in 2000.

kusaal: Ackah kɛŋ parliament nɛ yʋʋm paal nwadig la li daba ayɔpɔi daar yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni (7th January 2005) n lieb wadmaan tis Suaman constituency, Wabʋg na'adɔɔg la ni.
english: Ackah entered parliament on 7 January 2005 representing the Suaman constituency on the ticket of the National Democratic Party.

kusaal: Wadmaanib yir la ni, o da tʋm bɛ kɔmitii bɛdigʋ ni, ka ba sieba anɛ Subsidiary Legislation Committee nɛ Local Government and Rural Development Committee nɛ pu'asada nɛ dasam kɔmitii nɛ Bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛb nɛ buudi malima kɔmitii nɛ Special Budget Committee.
english: In parliament, he has served on various committees, including the Subsidiary Legislation Committee, the Local Government and Rural Development Committee, the Youth, Sports and Culture Committee, and the Special Budget Committee.

kusaal: O anɛ karimbiig ka ken Methodist pʋ'ʋsʋm la ni.
english: He is a Christian who fellowships at Methodist.

kusaal: Ackah mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biis atan'.
english: Ackah is married with three children.

kusaal: Stephen Yakubu anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ diplomat.
english: Stephen Mahamudu Yakubu is a Ghanaian politician and diplomat who is a member of the New Patriotic Party of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Stephen Yakubu nɛ yʋʋm tusir yinne, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yuobʋ nwadisa anu la dabpisi nɛ nu daar (May 25, 1966), Gotisaliga-Binduri bɛ Upper East Region.
english: Stephen Mahamudu Yakubu was born on May 25, 1966 at Gotisaliga-Binduri, a farming community in the Upper East Region.

kusaal: O da maali o BSc in Planning yinɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) nɛ o Postgraduate diploma in Information Systems yinɛ Thames Valley University Slough bɛ UK la.
english: He obtained a BSc in Planning from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) and a Postgraduate diploma in Information Systems from Thames Valley University in the UK.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa awai, kɔbiga nɛ atan (9,103) yi vɔɔt tusa piinɛ nii nɛ pisnu (18,050) pʋʋgin dinɛ zi'eni tis pisnu du'al pisnaasi nɛ tan' kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.43%).
english: He won the seat with 50.43% of the vote.

kusaal: Nananna, onɛ an Upper East Regional Minister ka lɛn an kʋkdaani tis Regional Security Council.
english: In 2021, Yakubu was named Upper East Regional Minister; as of 2025, he was Upper West Regional Minister.

kusaal: Yakubu anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nid.
english: During the 2008 general election, Mr. Yakubu contested the Binduri seat which had always been enjoyed by the National Democratic Congress, under the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Stevens Siaka anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana zi'eni tis Jaman North constituency bɛ Bono Region la wabug na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: Stevens Siaka (born 31 December 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Jaman North constituency in the Bono Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Siaka Stevens da anɛ kʋkdaani tis Parliamentary Select Committee on Education ka lɛn an Bono Regional Minister nya'adɔl din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ awai nwadisa atan' dabpisi nɛ ayuobʋ daar (26 March 2019) ken paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 2021).
english: Siaka Stevens was a former chairman of the Parliamentary Select Committee on Education and he was the Deputy Minister for Bono Region from 26 March 2019 till January 2021.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Siaka nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la dabpiinɛ atan' daar (31 December 1964) ka o yi Sampa bɛ Bono Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Siaka was born on 31 December 1964 and hails from Sampa in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o master's degree in Public Administration kasɛta gbaʋŋ nɛ Post Graduate Diploma kasɛta gbaʋŋ yinɛ GIMPA.
english: He had his master's degree in Public Administration and Post Graduate Diploma from GIMPA.

kusaal: O da lɛ maali o bachelor's degree in Management kasɛta gbaʋŋ nɛ Diploma in Accounting and Business Management kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛnɛ University of Education, Winneba.
english: He also had his bachelor's degree in Management and Diploma in Accounting and Business Management from the University of Education, Winneba.

kusaal: O da maal Diploma in Accounting and Business Management Cambridge yinɛ Tutorial College, London ka lɛn di'e Commercial Law kasɛta gbaʋŋ yi Institute of Management Studies.
english: He also earned a Diploma in Accounting and Business Management from the Cambridge Tutorial College in London and obtained a certificate in Commercial Law from the Institute of Management Studies.

kusaal: Siaka paasnɛ wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Partyla ni O da anɛ Bono Regional minista nya'andɔl din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ awai nwadisa atan' dabpisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (27 March 2019) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi nɛ yinne yʋʋmpaal nwadig la ni (January 2021).
english: He was the Deputy Regional Minister for Bono Region from 27 March 2019 to January 2021.

kusaal: Onɛ sʋ'oe Burniton Music Group.
english: He is the CEO of Burniton Music Group.

kusaal: O da di Best international Act: dinɛ bɛ Africa la, 2015 BET Awards nɛ Artist of the yɛar yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu Ghana Music Awards.
english: He won the Best International Act: Africa category at the 2015 BET Awards and Artiste of the Year at the 2015 and 2024 Ghana Music Awards.

kusaal: Stonebwoy di'e Golden Club plaque Boomplay dim san'an on da paae million kɔbiga Boomplay la.
english: Stonebwoy received the Golden Club plaque from Boomplay after surpassing 100 million streams on the platform.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai nwadisa awai ka ba da maal o brand ambassador tis Voltic Natural Mineral Water.
english: In September 2019, he was made the brand ambassador for Voltic Natural Mineral Water.

kusaal: Onɛ an brand ambassador tis Tecno mobile Ghana.
english: He is the brand ambassador of Tecno mobile in Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da dua Stonebwoy ka nidib bʋon yɛ "Stoneboy" la nɛ Ashaiman bɛ Greater Accra sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Etse was born in Ashaiman in the Greater Accra region of Ghana and began making music in his early school days.

kusaal: O da tɔlisi keŋ University of Professional Studies maali o degree in marketing yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan (2013) la ni.
english: He obtained his high school certificate at Tema Methodist Day Secondary School and later enrolled at the University of Professional Studies to pursue a degree in Marketing, in 2013.

kusaal: Satekla di nɛ Louisa Ansong Satekla onɛ an nyina duata la, ka ba mɔr biisa ayi ka ba yʋra an Catherine Jidula Satekla nɛ L Janam Joachim Satekla.
english: Stonebwoy is married to Dr. Louisa, a dental surgeon and ambassador for World Oral Health with two children, Catherine Jidula Satekla and L Janam Joachim Satekla.

kusaal: Stonebwoy yʋʋm raggae Jamaican Patois (Patwa bɛɛ Patwah) ka lɛn an onɛ yʋʋm yʋʋma buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'b.
english: Stonebwoy normally sings in Jamaican Patois (Patwa or Patwah).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anu (2015) la ni o da di'e ya'an piini bɛdigʋ din nɔkid "Artist of the yɛar" keŋ paae "Album of the yɛar".
english: In 2015, he received awards and nominations ranging from "Artist of the Year" to "Album of the Year".

kusaal: O yʋ'ʋm banɛ ka ba bʋon ye "sophomore album" nɛ "Necessary Evil" da kɛ ka o di Ghana Music Awards nama atan, nomination nama ayuobʋ.
english: His sophomore album, Necessary Evil, was the recipient of three Ghana Music Awards from 6 nominations.

kusaal: Nana Appiah Mensah onɛ sʋ'oe Menzgold dinɛ ka ba tɔlim salima la da kpɛmis Stonebwoy o Instagram ni nɛ Stonebwoy.
english: Nana Appiah Mensah, CEO of gold dealership company Menzgold, sent out words of encouragement to Stonebwoy on Instagram for Stonebwoy being supportive.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai nwadisa anu dab piinɛ anii ni ka Nana Appiah Mensah da pa'al Dance hall act Stonebwoy photo ka yɛ o nwɛ' nyɔ'ɔg Bhim Nation kpɛɛm yɛla nɛ on guri o la ka yɛ wina'am na barigu.
english: On 18 April 2019, Nana Appiah Mensah posted a photo of Dance hall act Stonebwoy saying he is proud of the Bhim Nation president for defending him and that God bless him.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi GRAMMY da duus Stonebwoy nɛ on da yʋʋm Grammy award-nominated single "AVRAKEDABRA" Morgan Heritage.
english: In 2020, the Grammy Awards handed a plaque to Stonebwoy in acknowledgment of his role as featured performer on Grammy award-nominated single "AVRAKEDABRA" by Morgan Heritage.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinni ka Stonebwoy yʋʋma zinsa atan ka ba da gaŋ 2022 Grammy Awards.
english: In 2021, three albums on which Stonebwoy featured were nominated for the 2022 Grammy Awards.

kusaal: O yu'uma "Greedy Men" da diɛ pinni nɛ ligiid million kobuga (Ghs 10,000).
english: His song "Greedy Men" received an award and a cash reward of GH¢ 10,000.

kusaal: Stonebwoy da dit o yʋʋm pistan duam dabisir la ka foundation la da nyiis million pisnu ntis accident award Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadisa atan la ni.
english: As part of celebrations for Stonebwoy's 30th birthday, the foundation donated a sum of GH¢5,000 to the accident ward of the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in March 2018.

kusaal: Stonebwoy da lɛm yɔɔg BHIM merch shop Ashaiman.
english: Stonebwoy has also opened the official BHIM merch shop in Ashaiman.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi la ni ka Livingstonɛ Foundation nɛ BHIM Merchandise Shop da laasi ntis sanitizer nam yɛ ba la'asi nzap coronavirus Ghana.
english: In 2020, the Livingstone Foundation in collaboration with the BHIM Merchandise Shop gave out free sanitizers as parts of efforts to combat the coronavirus spread in Ghana.

kusaal: Stonebwoy me da tis sanitizer nam nɛ la'a siɛba ntis Police Department kani bɛ Ashaiman la yɛ ba nyaŋi tumi ba tuuma coronavirus dini mɛ da bɛ Ghana la saŋa.
english: Stonebwoy also donated sanitizers and other items to the Police Department in Ashaiman to aid them in discharging their duties during the coronavirus pandemic in Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisinɛ ayi ka Livingstonɛ Foundation pa'as nɛ Duffour Foundation da maligim maal biis sakur siɛba tɛnsa anaasi siɛba bani kpɛi nɛ Stonebwoy tɛŋin la.
english: In 2022, the Livingstone Foundation together with Duffour Foundation renovated a basic school that serves four towns close to Stonebwoy's hometown.

kusaal: Di pu yuuge ka ba put Stonebwoy Brand Ambassador ntis 'Big Boss' dinni an paŋ dan paalig la (nɛw enɛrgy drink).
english: Stonebwoy is the brand ambassador for Big Boss, an energy drink.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadisa awai la ka ba da put Stonebwoy Tecno Mobile brand ambassador ka da nyis Camon 16 series Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nwadisa piiga la ni.
english: In September 2020, Stonebwoy was named Tecno Mobile brand ambassador and unveiled the Camon 16 Series in October 2020.

kusaal: O kɛŋ Germany, Italy, Spain nɛ Austria nwe yu'uma.
english: He performed in Germany, Italy, Spain and Austria.

kusaal: O Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobu Canada-American tour la o da yu'um Nɛw York City, Ohio, Philadelphia nɛ Ontario.
english: In his 2016 Canada-America tour, he performed in New York City, Ohio, Philadelphia and Ontario.

kusaal: Yuum ka ya'as ka o da lɛm kɛŋ Perth, Melbournɛ, Brisbanɛ nɛ Sidnɛy, bama wusa be nɛ Australia.
english: In the same year, he played in Perth, Melbourne, Brisbane and Sydney.

kusaal: O Euro tour kani da paas ayi la, o da kɛŋnɛ Nordic bani boodi o yɛlla Denmark, Finland nɛ Sweden yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayopoi la naarin.
english: In his second Euro tour, he played in Denmark, Finland and Sweden in the last quarter of 2017.

kusaal: Stonebwoy da yu'um Reggae Sumfest Afro nation festival nda bɛ Portugal la, Rotterdam reggae festival, Uppsala Reggae Festival.
english: Stonebwoy performed at Reggae Sumfest, Afro nation festival in Portugal, Rotterdam reggae festival, Uppsala Reggae Festival.

kusaal: Stonebwoy da yu'um Global Citizen Festival da be Black Star Square, Accra Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisinɛ ayi nwadisa awai la dab pisinɛ anaasi daar.
english: Stonebwoy headlined the 2022 Global Citizen Festival at the Black Star Square, Accra alongside SZA, Usher, Sarkodie, Gyakie, H.E.R, Stormzy and Tems .

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ nwadisa atan la ka o album Anloga Junction daa di Album of the Year Entertainment Achievement Awards ni.
english: In March 2021, his album Anloga Junction won the Album of the Year award in the Entertainment Achievement Awards.

kusaal: O mɛ daa lɛm di Male Artist of the Year Award.
english: He also won the Male Artist of the Year Award.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ nwadisa atan la ka o album Anloga Junction daa di Album of the Year 3Music Awards ni.
english: In March 2021, his album Anloga Junction won the Album of the Year award in the 3Music Awards.

kusaal: O yu'um kani bʋon yɛ Putuu Freestyle (Prayer) la me da di Viral Song of the Year (yu'um kani gilig teng hali).
english: His song Putuu Freestyle (Prayer) won the Viral Song of the Year.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ nwadisa anu la ba da gaŋ o 'Best African Dancehall Entertainer Award'.
english: In May 2021, he was nominated for the 'Best African Dancehall Entertainer Award'.

kusaal: Billboard dim daa naasi o hali nɛ on nyaŋe passi anii sobi Reggae Chart ni la, ka ba ti o gbaŋ.
english: He has been honored by Billboard after securing 8th position on Reggae Chart and received a plaque.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana Afropop, dancehall nɛ reggae yʋʋm yʋʋm (musician).
english: Livingstone Etse Satekla (born 5 March 1988), better known by his stage name Stonebwoy, is a Ghanaian musician from Ashaiman, Accra.

kusaal: O di'e Billboard nama ayi.
english: He is also a recipient of two Billboard plaques.

kusaal: Ba buon o ye reggae na'ab nɛ dance hall Africa pʋʋgin.
english: He has been described as the king of reggae and dance hall in Africa. Stonebwoy is also an actor, having appeared in the movies Happy Death Day and My name is Ramadan.

kusaal: Onɛ an global ambassador for sanitation.
english: He is a global ambassador for sanitation.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi la ka o da la'as nɛ Universal Music Group, Def Jam Recordings ni, nɛ Def Jam Recordings Africa ni.
english: In 2022, he signed to Universal Music Group's Def Jam Recordings, and its flagship Def Jam Recordings Africa, to release his fifth studio album 5Th Dimension (2023), which debuted number eight(8) on Billboard Reggae Albums Charts.

kusaal: O da kɛŋ Methodist Day Secondary School yʋʋm yinne nɛ Sarkodie ka ba da la'asi naae anina ka di'e ba kasɛta gbana.
english: He obtained his high school certificate at Tema Methodist Day Secondary School and later enrolled at the University of Professional Studies to pursue a degree in Marketing, in 2013.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan la nwadisa ayɔpɔi la dab piinɛ ayuobu daar (26 July, 2023) ka faandib da tʋ'ʋs o United States of America on daa keŋi o Fifth Dimension album global tour la.
english: His fifth studio album 5th Dimension, was released on 28 April 2023.

kusaal: YCEO nɛ Avance media dim da gaŋ o paas Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai la ni nidib pisnu bani an CEO nam ka an dasam la.
english: He was listed as part of the 2019 50 (fifty) young CEOs, by YCEO and Avance media.

kusaal: Ba da pin'li nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii la ni ye ba girim dasam bibis bama bɛ ba nkɔ nyaŋidi maan yɛl bibis Ghana la.
english: In 2022, Vodafone Ghana recognized him for using his creativity and music to promote the awareness of environmental and sustainability issues.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinni ka Vodafone Ghana da baŋi o yɛla ka li yitnɛ ban da ŋɔs ka ɔ yu'uma la pa'an nidib siɛlnam yɛla nɛ tɛŋla nɛ ti bellim yɛlla.
english: In 2022, Vodafone Ghana recognized him for using his creativity and music to promote the awareness of environmental and sustainability issues.

kusaal: Stonebwoy da maal 'Livingstone Foundation'.
english: In 2022, the Livingstone Foundation together with Duffour Foundation renovated a basic school that serves four towns close to Stonebwoy's hometown.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayopoi yiiga wadig ka foundation la da sung sakur bibisa anu Tema Methodist Day Senior High School, sakur kani ka o mɛŋ da kɛn.
english: In January 2017 the foundation announced a sponsorship package for five students of the Tema Methodist Day Senior High School, his alma mater.

kusaal: O shop kan ni sungid Livingstone Foundation la tuuma.
english: Proceeds from the shop are used to fund activities of the Livingstone Foundation.

kusaal: Stonebwoy pinli giligid tens nɛ Euro-zonɛ Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi nwadisa anii la ni.
english: Stonebwoy kicked off his world tour in the Euro-zone in August 2014.

kusaal: Buosug ni walisin Asaase Radio Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisinɛ atan la nwadisa ayopoi la ka Stonebwoy daa tuas yɛ o bood nɛ yɛ on nɛ Shatta Wale ti la'as beog daar.
english: Jesse Royal, Stonebwoy & Mutabaruka)

kusaal: Nwadisa anii la dabayi daar ka Stonebwoy daa yɛl tweet ni yɛ oni soe Afrobeats, reggae nɛ dancehall ka paan din an siɛm.
english: Stonebwoy performed at Reggae Sumfest, Afro nation festival in Portugal, Rotterdam reggae festival, Uppsala Reggae Festival.

kusaal: O da anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka lɛn an Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana nid yinnɛ zi'e Karaga Constituency kanɛ bɛ Northern Region la nɔba zʋg dɔlnɛ National Democratic Congress ni.
english: Alhassan Sualihu Dandaawa (born 17 February 1983) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Karaga Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Dandaawa anɛ Mɔr (Muslim) ka mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biig.
english: Dandaawa is a Muslim and is married with a child.

kusaal: O da keŋɛ Islamic University College kanɛ bɛ Accra la, ani ka o da di'e o Bachelor of Business Administration kasɛta gbaʋŋ ka lɛ di'e degree in Banking nɛ Finance kasɛta gbaʋŋ yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai la ni(2009).
english: He entered Islamic University College, Accra and obtained his Bachelor of Business Administration degree in Banking and Finance in 2009.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn keŋ Mouncrest University College, Kanda-Accra ka di'e bachelor of law degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: He also attended Mouncrest University College, Kanda-Accra and obtained a bachelor of law degree.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni(2012) o da nyi'a Karaga kʋk kanɛ an sixth parliament of the fourth republic la dolisnɛ NDC ka di.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Karaga seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Alhassan Sualihu Dandaawa nɛ fʋlʋnfʋk/nwadis ayi' la dadisim pii nɛ ayɔpɔi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ atan' la (February 17, 1983).
english: Alhassan Sualihu Dandaawa (born 17 February 1983) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Karaga Constituency in the Northern Region on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O yinɛ karaga, tɛŋ kanɛ bɛ Northern Region, Ghana nwa.
english: He hails from Karaga, a town in the Northern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Dandawaa anɛ ma'asim tiig na'adɔɔg (NDC) nid yinni.
english: In 2012, he contested for the Karaga seat on the ticket of the NDC sixth parliament of the fourth republic and won.

kusaal: Suaman District paasnɛ distirik nam awai banɛ bɛ Western North Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Suaman District is one of the nine districts in Western North Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da maali li ka di an distirik assambile yinɛ Aowin/Suaman District la nib ɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) la ka ba da buoni di ye Aowin-Amenfi District Council la, ti paae sankanɛ ka ba da nwaae distirik la datiʋŋ lɛbid tuon baba maal Suaman District bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la nwadisa ayuobʋ la dabpisi nɛ anii daar (28 June 2012); ka zin'ikanɛ kpɛlim la tiaki an Aowin District (ka di da pin'il yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa piinɛ yinne dabpii nɛ ayuobʋ daar (16 November 2017) (zuŋir daar da an 15 March 2018) lieb Aowin Municipal District).
english: Originally it was formerly part of the then-larger Aowin/Suaman District in 1988, which was created from the former Aowin-Amenfi District Council, until a small northwest part of the district was split off to create Suaman District on 28 June 2012; thus the remaining part has been renamed as Aowin District (which it was later elevated to municipal district assembly status on 16 November 2017 (effective 15 March 2018) to become Aowin Municipal District).

kusaal: Distirik assambile la bɛnɛ Western North Region Ya-datiʋŋ baba ka Dadieso aan di tɛmpʋtita'ar.
english: The district assembly is located in the southern part of Western North Region and has Dadieso as its capital town.

kusaal: Suame da paasnɛ Kumasi Metropolitan district, amaa di yʋ'ʋn anɛ municipal assembly bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Suame was formerly located in the Kumasi Metropolitan district but now it is a municipal assembly of the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Na'am kʋk la da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi' nɛ anaasi vɔɔtʋg la ni, saŋkan ka Old Tafo-Suame constituency da pʋdigi an Old Tafo nɛ Suame constituency nam.
english: This seat was created prior to the Ghanaian parliamentary election in 2004 when the Old Tafo-Suame constituency was split into the Old Tafo and Suame constituencies respectively.

kusaal: Li na'am kʋk bɛnɛ Kumasi metropolitan assembly pʋʋgin ka li tɔd nɛ Tafo Nhyiaso, Afigya Kwabre South, Bantama.
english: The seat is located within the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly and shares boundaries with Old Tafo (to the north), Afigya Kwabre South (to the east) and Kumasi Metropolis (to the west and south).

kusaal: Constituency la da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni, ka li da kɛ ka constituency nam la kal nɔbigi yi kɔbisyi' paae kɔbʋsyi nɛ pistan'.
english: The constituency was first created in 2004 by the Electoral Commission of Ghana along with 29 other new ones, increasing the number of constituencies from 200 to 230.

kusaal: Eugene Boakye Antwi an wadmaan nananna tis constituency la.
english: He succeeded Eugene Boakye Antwi who had represented the constituency also on the ticket of the NPP.

kusaal: Suhum Constituency bɛ nɛ Eastern region, Ghana ka Suhum an di teŋpʋ'ʋg.
english: The Suhum constituency is in the Eastern region of Ghana with the town Suhum as its capital.

kusaal: Onɛ yʋ'ʋn an constituency la wadmaan anɛ Kwadjo Asante.
english: The constituency has elected six members of parliament since 1992, with Frederick Opare-Ansah being the longest serving MP ever in the constituency, while Immanuel Obeng-Darko, Solomon Kodjoe Akwetey, Ransford Agyapong and Kwadjo Asante have had a single term each.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o dɔlisidnɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) ka o di nɛ vɔɔt nam tusa pistan nɛ anaasi,nɛ pisnaasi nɛ awai ka lin pa'al ye o mɔr 64% gaadi o taaba la, ka da kilim constituency la wadmaan.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Suleman Adamu Sanid (dʋ'anɛ November 13, 1970) anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Ahafo Ano North Constituency sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Ashanti Region la dim, o da zi'enɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party nid.
english: Suleman Adamu Sanid (born 13 November 1970) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Ahafo Ano North Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Suleman yinɛ Worikambo n bɛ Garu-Tempane District kanɛ bɛ Upper East region, Ghana la.
english: Suleman hails from Worikambo in the Garu-Tempane District in the Upper East region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o WAEC Ordinary Level nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii la ni (1988).
english: He had his WAEC Ordinary-Level in 1988.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr MBA kasɛta gbaʋŋ (Marketing) yi Central University kanɛ bɛ Accra la; BA (History), University of Ghana - Legon yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1997).
english: He also holds MBA (Marketing) from the Central University in Accra; BA (History), University of Ghana - Legon in 1997.

kusaal: Suleman da anɛ Manager tis Organizational Development and Management System bɛ Volta River Authority.
english: Suleman was the acting Manager of Organizational Development and Management System at Volta River Authority.

kusaal: Suleman anɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, NPP nid.
english: Suleman is a member of the NPP.

kusaal: Hali nɛ ban da gaŋ o ka o paas Wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni, Suleman da paam vɔɔt kal tusa piinɛ anii nɛ kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ anu (18,895) yi vɔɔt kal tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anii pʋʋgin (37,478) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'al pii nɛ yinne kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (51.11%) gaad onɛ ti'al o ka an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid la, Kwasi Adusei onɛ paam vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ anaasi nɛ kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (14,479) dinɛ an awai du'al piinɛ ayuobʋ kɔbʋg pʋʋgin la (9.16%) yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Until his election into the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, Suleman polled 18,895 votes out of 37,478 representing 51.11%, to beat his main contender of the National Democratic Congress, Kwasi Adusei who polled 14,479 representing 9.16% in the 2016 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Ba da lɛn vɔɔt o ya'as yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔtʋg la ni ka o keŋ paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: He was re-elected in the 2020 Ghanaian general election to represent in the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O da paam vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ yinne nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (21,581) dinɛ an pisnu du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (50.67%) ka Ma'asim tiig, NDC nid la, Kwasi Adusei da paam vɔɔt kal tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ piinɛ atan' (19,013) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ anaasi du'al pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi kɔbʋg pʋʋgin (44.64%).
english: He had 21,581 votes making 50.67% of the total votes, while the NDC parliamentary candidate Kwasi Adusei had 19,013 votes making 44.64% of the total votes.

kusaal: Suleman anɛ kʋkdaan nya'adɔli tis Local Government and Rural Development, O paas la'askanɛ gɔsid nɔŋ sier suoya la (Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee) ka lɛn paas Privileges Committee ya'as.
english: Suleman is the vice-chairperson of the Local Government and Rural Development Committee, a member of the Poverty Reduction Strategy Committee and also a member of the Privileges Committee.

kusaal: O da mɔri baŋir bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛbin hali onɛ da an biig la, Muntari pin'ili o nwɛ'ɛb la nɛ bɛ Ghana onɛ da bɛ Liberty Professionals ka naam pɛ'ɛs Udinese la dinɛ ka o da tɔlis anina yʋ'ʋn an yiiga tiim nwɛ'ɛd.
english: Spoken about as a talented footballer at a young age, Muntari started his youth career in Ghana with Liberty Professionals before joining Udinese where he progressed from their academy into becoming a first team player.

kusaal: O da nwɛ' gaad nwɛ'ɛb 150 tis Udinese ka di gɔɔlnam 9 ka naam kɛŋi pɛ'ɛs English tiim yinne, Portsmouth nɛ English Premier League ni.
english: He featured in over 150 matches for Udinese and scored 9 goals before securing a move to join English team Portsmouth then English Premier League.

kusaal: O naam anina nɛ yʋʋm yinne bɛ Pompey ka mɛn da pɛ'ɛs tiim kani di ya'an bɛ FA Cup dinɛ bɛ 2007–08 ni.
english: He spent only a season with the Pompey and was also part of the team that won the FA Cup in 2007–08.

kusaal: Saŋkani ka o da bɛ Internazionale la, o da sʋŋ tiim la ka ba paam he Champions League bɛ 2009–10 ni nɛ Serie A title dinɛ da bɛ 2008–09 ni nɛ 2009–10 ni nɛ bɛdigʋ sa.
english: During his time with Inter Milan, he helped the team win the Champions League in 2009–10 and the Serie A title in 2008–09 and 2009–10 among other trophies.

kusaal: Onɛ da bɛ international ni bɛ 2002 la, Muntari paami gaad kapnam 80 tis Ghana national team la ka ba da gaŋ o nɔɔr ayi' ye o pɛ'ɛs Africa Cup of Nations nwɛ'ɛb la ni nɛ FIFA World Cups nam atan'.
english: After becoming a full international in 2002, Muntari earned over 80 caps for the Ghana national team and was selected for two Africa Cup of Nations tournaments and three FIFA World Cups.

kusaal: O da pɛ'ɛs Ghana U20 tiim bani ka ba da nɔki ba niŋ ayi' ni bɛ African Youth Championship nɛ FIFA U-20 World Cup wʋsa 2001 ni.
english: He was also a member of the Ghana U20 team that placed second in the African Youth Championship and FIFA U-20 World Cup both in 2001.

kusaal: O pitʋ Sulley Muniru, onɛ nwɛ'ɛd Russian Liga 1 la.
english: His younger brother is Sulley Muniru, who plays in the Russian Liga I.

kusaal: December 2010 nii, Muntari di Ghana kpikpinkpin pʋ'a, Menaye Donkor ka ba mɔri biribʋŋ yinne.
english: In December 2010, Muntari married Ghanaian businesswoman Menaye Donkor and they have a son.

kusaal: 16 September 2020 nii, Donkor da lɛm yɛl ye ba biig kani dɔl la kenna, dinɛ ka GhOne TV da buosi baŋ la.
english: On 16 September 2020, Donkor confirmed the arrival of their second child, in an interview on GhOne TV.

kusaal: Muntari anɛ Muslim amɛŋa.
english: Muntari is a devout Muslim.

kusaal: Scores results list the Ghana's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Muntari goal.
english: Scores and results list the Ghana's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Muntari goal.

kusaal: O da bɛnɛ Italy bɛdigʋ, nwɛ'ɛdi tisid Udinese, Inter Milan, nɛ AC Milan.
english: He spent most of his career in Italy, playing for clubs such as Udinese, Inter Milan, and AC Milan.

kusaal: O nwɛ'ɛb kani ka o da nwɛ' Premier League la ni nɛ FA Cup la ni da tis o suor ka o paam Inter Milan la ni kpɛn' bɛ 2008 ni.
english: His performance in the Premier League and the FA Cup earned him a move to join Inter Milan in 2008.

kusaal: 20 June 2015 nii, ba da yɛl ye Donkor du'a ba bikpɛɛm la.
english: On 20 June 2015, it was reported that Donkor had given birth to the couple's first child.

kusaal: Sunyani East Constituency anɛ wadmaan constituency kanɛ bɛ Bono Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Sunyani East is a parliamentary constituency in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da di'e Henry Mensah, onɛ da zi'e constituency la nɔba zug 4th Republic parliament la tis NPP.
english: He succeeded Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh, who had also represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament on the ticket of the NPP.

kusaal: Onɛ an wadmaani tis constituency la nannanna anɛ Kwasi Ameyaw-Cherimeh.
english: He succeeded Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh, who had also represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament on the ticket of the NPP.

kusaal: Kwasi Ameyaw-Cherimeh an wadmaani tis Sunyani East constituency.
english: He succeeded Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh, who had also represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament on the ticket of the NPP.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nɔba zug ka da di vɔɔtʋg la, nɛ vɔɔt tusa piinɛ ayi', kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ anu (14,935) ka da lieb sʋ'ʋlim la wadmaan.
english: He succeeded Kwasi Ameyaw-Cheremeh, who had also represented the constituency in the 4th Republic parliament on the ticket of the NPP.

kusaal: Sunyani Senior High School (SUSEC) anɛ sɔkɛndiri sakur kani bɛ Sunyani dinɛ bɛ Bono Region Ghana la.
english: Sunyani Senior High School (SUSEC) is a coeducational second cycle institution in Sunyani in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Sunyani Secondary School anɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa buon ye SUSEC la anɛ dinɛ yit Ghana Education Trust la ni na.
english: Sunyani Secondary School popularly known as SUSEC is one of the products of Ghana Education Trust.

kusaal: Di pin'ilʋg yʋʋm anɛ yʋʋm 1960 la ni ka di anɛ Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah da zii li na, onɛ yʋ'ʋm an yiiga Ghana Zugdaan la.
english: It was established in 1960 by Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah, later Ghana's first President.

kusaal: Sakur biis banɛ da pin'il ka ba dieba ye sakur biis anɛ 36, dinɛ ka biribis an 31 ka bipʋmis an 5 bɛ 30 October 1960 la ni.
english: The first batch of 36 students, 31 boys and 5 girls, was admitted on 30 October 1960.

kusaal: Dabisir 13 December 1960 ka Osagyefo Kwame Nkrumah da zʋŋ sakur la nɛ pa'anib atan' nɛ bani pʋ pa'ana mɛn awai.
english: On 13 December 1960, Osagyefo Kwame Nkrumah inaugurated the school, which started with only three(3) teachers and nine non-teaching staff.

kusaal: Sunyani Secondary School da pin'ilɛ an sɛkɛndiri sakur amaa, ba da lɛm tiak ka di an biribis ma'aa ka kɛ ka bipʋmis la keŋ Yaa Asantewaa Girls' School.
english: Sunyani Secondary School started as a co-educational Institution but after a short time, it was decided to make it a boys' school, and the few girls in the school were sent to Yaa Asantewaa Girls' School, but this was reversed the following year and girls were again admitted.

kusaal: Onɛ da an yiiga pa'an kpɛɛm tis sakur la anɛ P.D. Quartey.
english: The first Headmaster of the school was P.D. Quartey from 1960 to 1967 for a period of Seven (7) years.

kusaal: Sunyani Technical University (STU) (ka ba da buon ye Sunyani Polytechnic) anɛ gɔmɛna university sakur kanɛ bɛ Bono Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The Sunyani Technical University (STU) (formally known as Sunyani Polytechnic) is a public tertiary institution in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Li bɛnɛ Asufufu ya'datiŋ-nya'aŋ.
english: It is located northeast of Asufufu.

kusaal: STU da pin'ili anɛ Technical Institute yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi ni (yʋʋma pisnu nɛ anii nwana), li da nan ka' university, ka bɛ Ghana Education Service nu'usin.
english: STU was established as a Technical Institute in 1967 (1967), as a non-tertiary institution, under the Ghana Education Service.

kusaal: Polytechnics wada, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi da tis Polytechnics banɛ bɛ Ghana wʋsa paŋ ye ba tis kasɛta gbana banɛ an Higher National Diploma (HND), Diploma nɛ li gbaŋ bɛda taaba, sakur la kpɛɛmnam ya'a bas suor.
english: The Polytechnics Act, 2007 mandated the Polytechnics in Ghana to run and award Higher National Diploma (HND) Certificates, Diplomas and other higher degrees, subject to the approval of the Polytechnic Councils.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi ni ka Ghana gɔmɛna da ti'aki li lɛbis Polytechnic, ye ba zamis Higher National Diploma (HND) zamisa.
english: It was subsequently upgraded to a Polytechnic in 1997 (1997) by the Government of Ghana, to run Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes.

kusaal: STU gban'e ye ba mɛ' buudi malima la'ad dɔɔg ka nɔk Brong Ahafo Region la'ad kʋda kpɛn'ɛs anina.
english: STU plans to build a cultural museum on the history of the former Brong Ahafo Region.

kusaal: Supa Modo anԑ yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ anii sini kanԑ ka tԑԑns maanmaanib la'asi maal ka onԑ gaad tuoni gͻsi li yela an Likarion Wainaina.
english: Supa Modo is a 2018 internationally co-produced drama film directed by Likarion Wainaina.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋi li ye linԑ an Kenya sini sʋŋi bԑ Best Foreign Language Film bԑ 91st Academy Awards ni.
english: It was selected as the Kenyan entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 91st Academy Awards, but it was not nominated.

kusaal: Supa Modo da paas One Fine Day Films sini nam la pʋʋgin, ba bͻͻdim da an ye ba sʋŋ ka Africa sini maanib ka ba maal sini ka li paae tԑԑns bԑdigʋ.
english: Supa Modo was produced as part of the One Fine Day Films workshop-project, which gives African filmmakers the opportunity to learn from mentors and create their stories for an international audience.

kusaal: Onԑ da pin'il tʋʋm kaŋa anԑ Tom Tykwer nԑ Marie Steinmann.
english: The project was founded by Tom Tykwer and Marie Steinmann.

kusaal: Sini si'eba banԑ ka ba da dͻlis anina maal anԑ Kati Kati, Nairobi Half Life, Something Necessary nԑ Soul Boy.
english: Other movies resulting from this workshop include Kati Kati, Nairobi Half Life, Something Necessary and Soul Boy.

kusaal: Ba da yisi li yiiga nԑ 68th Berlin International Film Festival ni.
english: It first premiered at 68th Berlin International Film Festival.

kusaal: Jo anԑ pʋ'asadir kanԑ bԑ Kenya tԑŋkpԑŋ si'a.
english: Jo is a young girl living in a small village in Kenya.

kusaal: Sini la da yi paalʋ na dunia wʋsa tuon bԑnԑ 68th Berlin International Film Festival da bԑ nԑ "Zʋmaana" zin'igi.
english: The movie had its world premiere at the 68th Berlin International Film Festival in the category "Generations".

kusaal: Ghana yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi wada gbanʋŋ la (Ghana's 1992 constitution) tis suor nɛ paŋ ye Judiciary sʋ'oe di mɛŋ ka zi'e di kɔn' nɛ Legislative nɛ Executive gɔmena lʋga la.
english: Ghana's 1992 constitution guarantees the independence and separation of the Judiciary from the legislative and the executive arms of government.

kusaal: Supreme Court da pin'ilnɛ dɔlisid Supreme Court Ordinance (1876) ye di an kɔɔtʋ kanɛ gat kɔɔtʋ wʋsa Gold Coast (dinɛ yʋ'ʋn an Ghana) sankanɛ ka Ghana da nam pʋ sʋ'oe o mɛŋa.
english: The Supreme Court was established by the Supreme Court Ordinance (1876) as the highest tribunal in the Gold Coast (now Ghana) during the colonial era.

kusaal: Ghana da fuoe o mɛŋi yi WACA ban da paami asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ la nya'aŋka kʋ'ʋg Appeals kanɛ da ken Judicial Committee of the Privy Council London la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ la ni (1960).
english: Until 1960, there was a right of appeal to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London, England.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ atan' nwadisa ayɔpɔi la daba ayi daar (July 2, 2013), Supreme Court da kpɛn'ɛs editor-in-chief tis Daily Searchlight newspaper, Ken Kuranchie, sanrega dabpiiga (10 days) on da buol Piyamnama awai la ye ba anɛ zam dim nɛ barigaŋ dim la.
english: On 2 July 2013, the Supreme Court sentenced the editor of the Daily Searchlight newspaper, Ken Kuranchie, to 10 days in prison for calling the 9 Justices hypocritical and selective.

kusaal: Parliament of Ghana da yis wada zaŋi keŋ wee kuob teŋin la yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi la (2022), Apex Court da yis wada kad cannabis kuob yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ atan nwadisa anu la ni (May 2023) dɔlisid vɔɔtkanɛ ka ba da maal ka paam 5-4 la.
english: After the parliament of Ghana passed a bill allowing the cultivation of weed in the country in 2022, the Supreme Court in May 2023 struck out the cannabis cultivation bill by a 5-4 majority.

kusaal: Ghana Zuraani nwɛ'ɛd Council of State suora ka gaŋid Chief Justice ka Parliament siakid ka basid suor ka ba tʋmmid.
english: The Chief Justice is appointed by the President of Ghana acting in consultation with the Council of State and with the approval of the country's Parliament.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi wada gbaʋŋ la (1992 Constitution) da kpiis public tribunals banɛ ka ba da maal PNDC saŋa la ka maal Regional Tribunal ka ba kʋkdaan zi'esim nwɛnɛ High Court Piyamnam.
english: The 1992 Constitution abolished all the public tribunals established under the Provisional National Defence Council and created the Regional Tribunal, whose chairman was equated with the High Court judges.

kusaal: Onɛ an Chief Justice tis Supreme Court of Ghana nananna anɛ Her ladyship Justice Gertrude Torkornoo.
english: The current Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana is Paul Baffoe-Bonnie, who was appointed following the suspension of Gertrude Torkornoo in April 2025.

kusaal: Ba anɛ Samuel K. Marful-Sau nɛ Agnes M.A Dordzie, ba wʋsa anɛ Appeal Court piyamnam, Nii Ashie Kotey, Dean of the Faculty of Law kʋdʋg tis University of Ghana nɛ Nene A. O. Amegatcher, onɛ an lɔya tʋmmi asʋ'o-m-mɛŋ ni ka da an Ghana Bar Association Zuraan kʋdʋg.
english: In July 2018, President Nana Akufo-Addo appointed four new judges to the Supreme Court: Samuel K. Marful-Sau and Agnes M.A Dordzie, both Justices of the Appeal Court, Nii Ashie Kotey, a former Dean of the Faculty of Law at the University of Ghana, and Nene A. O. Amegatcher, a lawyer in private practice who also a former president of the Ghana Bar Association.

kusaal: Onɛ an piyamkanɛ kʋdʋg hali bɛ Court, William Atuguba da naae o tʋʋma yʋʋmkan ni.
english: One of the longest-serving judges of the Court, William Atuguba, retired in the same month.

kusaal: Jerry Rawlings da gaŋ o yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu nwadis piinɛ yinne la ni (November 1995) kpɛn'ɛs Supreme Court ban da gaŋi o yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni (July 2018).
english: He had been on the Supreme Court after being nominated by Jerry Rawlings in November 1995.

kusaal: Onɛ da an pʋ'akanɛ an nya'aŋ Chief Justice la da anɛ Sophia Akuffo.
english: Sophia Akuffo was appointed Chief Justice by President Akufo-Addo from June 2017 to December 2019.

kusaal: O tʋʋma da naaenɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai nwadis piinɛ ayi la dabpisi daar (20 December 2019) ka Kwasi Anin-Yeboah da di'e o zi'esim yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi yʋʋmpaal nwadig da daba ayɔpɔi la daar (7 January 2020).
english: She retired on 20 December 2019 and was replaced by Kwasi Anin-Yeboah became the Chief Justice on 7 January 2020.

kusaal: Ba da nyɔdignɛ Vida Akoto-Bamfo, Sophia Adinyira, nɛ Sophia Akuffo banɛ tʋʋma da naae ba saŋa paae la zug.
english: They replaced Vida Akoto-Bamfo, Sophia Adinyira, and Sophia Akuffo who had either retired or were due to retire.

kusaal: Din pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ yuobʋ (1876) la ni, Supreme Court mɔrnɛ Chief Justice nam pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (27 Chief Justices)
english: Since its inception in 1876, the Supreme Court has had 27 chief justices.

kusaal: Justice Kwadwo Agyei Agyepong nɛ Major (Rtd) Sam Acquah ka ba da gban'e b aba yaan ka kʋʋ ba Bundase Military Range bɛ Accra Plains la.
english: On 30 June 1982, during the curfew hours, three High Court Judges and a retired Army Officer, Justice Frederick Poku Sarkodee, Justice Cecilia Koranteng-Addow, Justice Kwadwo Agyei Agyepong and Major (Rtd) Sam Acquah, were abducted from their homes and murdered at the Bundase Military Range in the Accra Plains.

kusaal: Ghanaian judicial system zu'odi ba yʋʋm wʋsa Martyrs Day, daakanɛ tiendi b akum la yɛla.
english: The Ghanaian judicial system honours them each year on Martyrs' Day.

kusaal: Zuraan kʋdʋg John Dramani Mahama da zɛrig Registrar of the Supreme Court yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi nwadisa awai la ni (September 2022) nɛ ban pʋ gban'e dabisir ye ba wʋm antua kanɛ ka ba bɔɔd ye ba kɛ ka Electoral Commission gu'oe tʋʋmkanɛ ka ba tʋm la (interlocutory injunction).
english: Former President John Dramani Mahama in September 2022 criticized the Registrar of the Supreme Court for not setting a date to hear an application seeking an interlocutory injunction.

kusaal: Appeals banɛ yi Supreme Court of the Gold Coast da kennɛ West African Court of Appeal (WACA) dinɛ da pin'il yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yuobʋ la ni (1866).
english: The Supreme Court was established by the Supreme Court Ordinance (1876) as the highest tribunal in the Gold Coast (now Ghana) during the colonial era.

kusaal: Military coup d'état kanɛ da naam yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yuobʋ nwadisa ayi dabpisi nɛ anaasi daar la (February 24, 1966), nya'aŋ ka National Liberation Council (NLC), dɔlisid kɔɔtʋ wada, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ la ni (1966) (NLCD.84) ye ba yis Supreme Court ka yʋ'ʋn nɔk paŋi niŋ kɔɔtʋnam ayi ni: Superior Court of Judicature nɛ inferior courts.
english: The 1992 Constitution abolished all the public tribunals established under the Provisional National Defence Council and created the Regional Tribunal, whose chairman was equated with the High Court judges.

kusaal: Ba da tiaki nɔki di tʋʋma la tis Court of Appeal.
english: The Court of Appeal, which includes the chief justice and not fewer than five other judges, has jurisdiction to hear and to determine appeals from any judgment, decree, or High Court of Justice order.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayi wada gbaʋŋ la (1992 constitution) pa'al ye Supreme Court mɔrnɛ Chief Justice of Ghana nɛ piyamnam banɛ ka ba kanl gaadi awai paasi an Piyamnami tis Supreme Court.
english: The 1992 constitution stipulates that the Supreme Court is made up of the Chief Justice of Ghana and not less than nine other Justices of the Supreme Court.

kusaal: Supreme Court Piyambanɛ kpɛlim Zuraani ɛɛnti nwɛ' Judicial Council suora nɛ Council of State ka gaansi ba.
english: The other Supreme Court Justices are appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Judicial Council and in consultation with the Council of State.

kusaal: Asɛɛ ka Parliament tisi ba suor ka ba naan tʋm.
english: This must also be with the approval of Parliament.

kusaal: Court of Appeal, dinɛ mɔr chief justice nɛ piyamnam nwɛnɛ anu la, kɛlisid ka pa'an nimbaanlzɔɔr nɛ saria kadib kanɛ ka kɔɔtʋ si'a maal, High Court of Justice order.
english: The Court of Appeal, which includes the chief justice and not fewer than five other judges, has jurisdiction to hear and to determine appeals from any judgment, decree, or High Court of Justice order.

kusaal: High Court of Justice, dinɛ mɔr chief justice ka mɔr piyamnam nwɛnɛ piinɛ ayi la gɔsid yɛla wʋsa nidib bɛllim nɛ bibi'elim.
english: The High Court of Justice, which consists of the chief justice and not fewer than twelve other justices, has jurisdiction in all matters, civil and criminal, other than those involving treason.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii nwadisa ayɔpɔi la ni (July 2018), Zuraan Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Piyamnama anaasi paas Supreme Court.
english: In July 2018, President Nana Akufo-Addo appointed four new judges to the Supreme Court: Samuel K. Marful-Sau and Agnes M.A Dordzie, both Justices of the Appeal Court, Nii Ashie Kotey, a former Dean of the Faculty of Law at the University of Ghana, and Nene A. O. Amegatcher, a lawyer in private practice who also a former president of the Ghana Bar Association.

kusaal: Onɛ da an onɛ Supreme Court Piyam ka Jerry Rawlings yuolim gaŋ ka o tʋʋma naae.
english: She was the last Supreme Court Judge appointed by Jerry Rawlings to retire.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai la nwadis piinɛ ayi la (December 2019), la ni Zuraaan Akufo-Addo gaŋ Piyam paala atan paas Supreme Court.
english: In December 2019, President Akufo-Addo appointed three new judges to the Supreme Court: Mariama Owusu, Avril Lovelace-Johnson, and Gertrude Tokornoo.

kusaal: Ba da anɛ Mariama Owusu, Avril Lovelace-Johnson, nɛ Gertrude Tokornoo.
english: In December 2019, President Akufo-Addo appointed three new judges to the Supreme Court: Mariama Owusu, Avril Lovelace-Johnson, and Gertrude Tokornoo.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi nwadisa ayuobʋ la dabpistan daar (30 June 1982), din da an curfew saŋa la, High Court Judges titada atan nɛ Army Officer, ka ba yʋda an: Mr.
english: On 30 June 1982, during the curfew hours, three High Court Judges and a retired Army Officer, Justice Frederick Poku Sarkodee, Justice Cecilia Koranteng-Addow, Justice Kwadwo Agyei Agyepong and Major (Rtd) Sam Acquah, were abducted from their homes and murdered at the Bundase Military Range in the Accra Plains.

kusaal: Ba da nɔki ba niŋgbina niŋ gasoline ni ka nyʋ'oe ba nɛ bugum.
english: The victims' bodies were then doused in gasoline and set ablaze.

english: He is a member of the Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro Constituency in the Ga South Municipal District in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana.

english: In the 2020 NPP parliamentary primaries, Tetteh switch from Ningo-Prampram to contest in Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro, where he resides.

english: He is a Christian.

english: Tagalia, also called mullah tagalia or red stew, is a Sudanese and Chadian sauce popular during Ramadan.

english: It is served with bread, kisra (a type of flatbread), gurasa (a heavy Sudanese flatbread), or a dumpling (aseeda/asida) made of wheat, corn, or rice flour.

english: Tain is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

english: Tain is located in the Bono Region of Ghana.

english: The seat is located within the Tain District of the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Takoradi Technical University anɛ university kanɛ bɛ Sekondi-Takoradi, tɛnpʋʋg tita'ar kanɛ bɛ Western Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: Takoradi Technical University is a public tertiary education institution (university) located in Sekondi-Takoradi, the capital of the Western Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Wada kanɛ da an Polytechnic Law of 1992 (PNDCL 321), da gaad ya ka wada paal kanɛ da an Polytechnics Law (Act 745) kɛna di'e li nɔbir yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: Later, after the passage of the Polytechnic Law of 1992 (PNDCL 321), it was replaced by the Polytechnics Law (Act 745) in 2007.

kusaal: Takoradi Technical University anɛ sakur kanɛ ka gɔmɛna da pin'il ka li an nu'ug tʋʋma zamisig zin'ig yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ anaasi ni ka paas tɛŋ la kpɛɛmnam sakur titada kanl ni.
english: In effect, since April 1954, Takoradi Technical University (formerly Takoradi Polytechnic) has existed as a government technical institute under the Ghana Education Service of the Ministry of Education.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ la ni, Ghana wada maanib da tik nu'ugi tis ye polytechnics nam ayuobʋ, piiga pʋʋgin mɔr nyali ka ba yʋ'ʋn an university nam (ka Takoradi Polytechnic da paasi ba kanl pʋʋgin).
english: Takoradi Polytechnic was ranked the first among polytechnics in Ghana for the second time running by the world universities ranking body, Webomatics, the largest public research body known for its scientific methods in web ranking.

kusaal: Tamale bɛnɛ kʋdʋmɛn tɔlʋg suokitta ni; di pin'ili nɔbignɛ an tɔlʋŋ zi'igi tis Northern region yʋma banɛ zulum sa.
english: In 1960, Tamale became the capital of the Northern Region after the region had separated from the rest of the north.

english: There are public transports from Tamale to major cities such as Kumasi, Accra, Mim, Ahafo, Cape Coast, Sunyani, Takoradi, Tema, Ho, Wa, Bolgatanga, Elubo, Aflao, and Techiman.

english: Mohammed Amin Adam, former Deputy Minister for the Northern Region, Former Deputy Minister of State for Finance and Member of parliament for Karaga (2021–)

kusaal: Sakur la anɛ zamisʋg zi'ig kani ka sakur biis na nyaŋi gbɛɛd anina ka di bɛnɛ Education Ridge babir, dinɛ bɛ Sagnarigu Municipality pʋʋgʋn.
english: Tamale Senior High School, formerly Government Secondary School, Tamale, Gbewaa Secondary School, and more recently Tamale Secondary School is a co-educational second cycle boarding school located at Education Ridge, a suburb of the Sagnarigu Municipality.

kusaal: Sakur la anɛ dinɛ bɛ di kɔ' ka tisid suor tisid sakur biis Ghana ka yitnɛ ba kpansib gbana la ni, nɛ sakur biis banɛ ka' Ghana dima, ka di mɛn yitnɛ kpɛ'ɛb kpansib sieba dinɛ ka sakur la tisidi ba.
english: Tamale senior high school is one of the prestigious senior high schools in Ghana and Northern region in particular.

kusaal: Sakur la maan kɔɔs sieba nwa; Tɔlʋŋ yɛla, Bʋnvʋya bɛlim wʋsa yɛla, Ya mɔrim, Si'elnam maalʋg, General Arts, and Visual Arts.
english: Courses offered by the school include; Business, General Science, Home Economics, Technical, General Arts, and Visual Arts.

kusaal: Tamale Senior High School pɛ'ɛsnɛ sakur bɛda sakuya pʋʋgʋn Ghana nwa ni, dinɛ da yʋʋg hali Ghana Asʋ'ʋmɛŋ saŋa la, nɛ nimbɛda banɛ naar anina la Sakur la na nyaŋi kaanl nimbɛda bama; Ghana Zugdaan, Zugdaan nya'andɔlibnam ayi' bɛ anaasi ripubilik tis Ghana, palimɛn pian'a-pian'ad, kɔɔtɔ tita'ar na'anam ayi bɛ Ghana ni, Chiefs of Defence Staff nam ayi', nɛ onɛ di'esid gɔmma tʋntʋnib nɛ mp nam.
english: The school can count amongst its ranks; a head of State, two vice presidents of the fourth republic of Ghana, a speaker of parliament, two Justices of the Supreme Court of Ghana, two Chiefs of Defence Staff, and a host of government ministers and members of parliament.

kusaal: Tamale Senior High School sakur biikʋda banɛ yʋda pʋdʋgʋd anɛ banɛ naae kɛŋi ba tʋʋma zi'igin ka tʋm ka ba yʋda yina.
english: Tamale Senior High School was founded by then British Colonial Administration as Government Secondary School, Tamale in 1951.

kusaal: University la da sin'iŋnɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne(1951) la an kpiiisʋg zamisʋg zin'ig, ka yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' (1963) ka la lɛbig an nu'ug tʋʋma zamisʋg lʋgʋr.
english: The university was founded in 1951 as a trades school and in 1963 as a technical institute.

kusaal: Sakurbiis nwɛn wʋʋ tusa ayɔpɔi (7,000) ka university la nɔk.
english: There are roughly 7,000 varied students enrolled at the university.

kusaal: Ka Commonwealth Association of Technical Universities nɛ Polytechnics bɛ Africa, TaTU pa'as ba ni yinne.
english: The Commonwealth Association of Technical Universities and Polytechnics in Africa counts TaTU as one of its members.

kusaal: Dinɛ lɛn pa'as ya'as, li pa'as nɛ Conference of Vice-Chancellors bɛ Technical Universities nɛ Rectors of Polytechnics bɛ Ghana la'am nɛ Association of Principals bɛ Technical Institutes bɛ Ghana.
english: Additionally, it is a member of the Conference of Vice-Chancellors of Technical Universities and Rectors of Polytechnics in Ghana and the Association of Principals of Technical Institutes in Ghana.

kusaal: Ka bɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka ba tisid yʋ'ʋr ye Education ridge ka pʋridig Tamale sʋ'ʋlim, nɛ Yendi sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The branches are the Tamale main, and the Yendi branch.

kusaal: Bɛdigʋ siak tis ye TaTU's an sum li ya'a ti lɛb applied research nɛ technology Di pa'as nɛ University banɛ bɛ dunia la gilli.
english: Tamale Technical University (TaTU), initially called Tamale Polytechnic(T.poly), is located in the northern part of Ghana.

kusaal: Freda Prempeh an wadmaani tis constituency la.
english: Gideon Boako is a member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: Tano North constituency anɛ constituency banɛ ka Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg ɛɛnti dit na'am ani la yinne.
english: Tano North constituency is one of the constituencies that the New Patriotic Party wins almost every election and a stronghold for the party.

kusaal: Yʋma pisi nwa, constituency la nidib vɔɔtidnɛ gansid Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nidib ka ba an wadmaanibi tis constituency la.
english: In the last two decades, the constituency has consistently elected their representative of parliament from the NPP.

kusaal: Benjamin Yeboah Sekyere an wadmaani tis constituency la.
english: Charles Asiedu is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nɔba zugu nya' na'am la, ka nidib bɛdegʋ da vɔɔti gaŋ o, o da paam vɔɔt tusa atan', kɔbisnii nɛ atan' (3803) ka lieb wadmaani tis constituency la.
english: Charles Asiedu is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: Tariq Hanna da anɛ Executive Pastry Chef ka lɛn paas Sucré dessert diib kuosʋg zin'ikanɛ bɛ New Orleans, Louisiana.
english: Tariq Hanna was Executive Pastry Chef and partner of the Sucré dessert restaurant in New Orleans, Louisiana.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ Nigeria, ka o nɔbʋga anina ka lɛɛ keŋi o sakuri bɛ England, Hanna da tɔɔm teŋi keŋ United States ka tɔlisi o saakur keŋ Lawrence Technological University dinɛ bɛ Detroit, Michigan.
english: He was born and raised in Nigeria, and after attending boarding school in England, Hanna moved to the United States to attend Lawrence Technological University in Detroit, Michigan.

kusaal: Hanna da lɛn keŋ kpɛn' diib maalʋg sakur bɛ Oakland Community College.
english: Hanna enrolled himself in culinary school at Oakland Community College.

kusaal: O yiiga tʋʋmkanɛ ka o da tʋm diib kuosʋg tʋʋma anɛ on da tʋm bɛ sandwich board dinɛ bɛ deli n bɛ Southfield, Michigan named Sol's Deli.
english: His first job in the restaurant industry was working the sandwich board at a deli in Southfield, Michigan named Sol's Deli.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' (1993) la ni, Hanna da yɔ'ɔgi o mɛŋ diib dʋgʋb nɛ kuosʋg zin'ig, bɛ The Northville Gourmet, on da an yʋʋm pisi nɛ anaasi (24) la.
english: In 1993, Hanna opened his own family-operated pastry and catering shop, The Northville Gourmet, at the age of 24.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai Samampiid nwadig la ni, bɛ Motor City Casino da yɔ'ɔg bɛ Detroit.
english: In December 1999, MotorCity Casino opened in Detroit.

kusaal: O tʋʋma saŋa bɛ Motor City, Hanna da paasi nya' diib dʋgʋb nya'abanɛ ka ba da maal bɛ Food Network ni la, la'an nɛ National Bread and Pastry Championship, Chocolate Fantasy Competition, Cereal Bridges and Gingerbread Mansions Competition.
english: During his tenure at MotorCity, Hanna participated in several cooking competitions on the Food Network, including the National Bread and Pastry Championship, Chocolate Fantasy Competition, Cereal Bridges and Gingerbread Mansions Competition.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2004) la ni, onɛ da di ya'an lieb yiiga daan bɛ Central Region Pastry Chef yʋʋmkan ni, ka lɛn an onɛ paasi ayi bɛ National Pastry Chef yʋʋmkan ni bɛ American Culinary Federation.
english: In 2004, he was named the first Central Region Pastry Chef of the Year, and Runner-up National Pastry Chef of the Year by the American Culinary Federation.

kusaal: On da tʋm bɛ Motor City Casino la yʋma ayɔpɔi nya'aŋ, Hanna da naal nɛ New Orleans dim didʋgʋt onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon ye Joel Dondis ka ba maal Dondis' vision dinɛ an Sucré diib kuosʋg zin'ig.
english: After seven years at MotorCity Casino, Hanna joined with New Orleans native restaurateur Joel Dondis to develop Dondis' vision of the Sucré restaurant.

kusaal: Hanna an onɛ da di ya'an lieb Pastry Chef of the Year bɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2007) dinɛ ka New Orleans Magazine da maal la.
english: Hanna was named Pastry Chef of the Year in 2007 by New Orleans Magazine.

kusaal: Hanna da lɛm paas banɛ da paae naar daar bɛ Chef Magazine's yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) la ni, ka ba da yɛl ye onɛ di ya'ani gaadi o taaba la wʋsa yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) nɛ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) New Orleans City Business Culinary Connoisseurs nya'ab la ni.
english: Hanna was also a finalist for Chef Magazine's 2008 Chef of the Year, and was named best pastry chef in both the 2008 and 2009 New Orleans City Business Culinary Connoisseurs issues.

kusaal: O da lɛn nya' bɛ TLC's Ultimate Cake Off yiiga nya'ab la ni ("Shark Summer") nɛ dinɛ paasi anaasi la ni ("Fourth of July"); nɛ Food Network Challenge ("Incredible Edible Mansions").
english: He also competed on TLC's Ultimate Cake Off episode 1 ("Shark Summer") and episode 4 ("Fourth of July"); and the Food Network Challenge ("Incredible Edible Mansions").

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la nii, Hanna da kuosi o pʋʋr dinɛ da bɛ Sucré la ka bas tʋʋma ban da zɛrig o ye mɔ ye digin nɛ sɔ' la zug.
english: In 2018, Hanna sold his shares of Sucré and left the company after sexual misconduct allegations.

kusaal: On da tʋm o mɛŋ tʋʋma la yʋma ayuobʋ nya'aŋ, Hanna da paam suor ye o an yiiga casino pastry dikuos bɛ Detroit.
english: After six years of self-employment, Hanna was offered a position as the first casino pastry chef in Detroit.

kusaal: Wɛlʋŋ 2B dim mɔri nwɛ'ɛdib wɛlʋŋnam ayɔpɔi banɛ yi Ashanti sʋ'ʋlʋm, Western sʋ'ʋlʋm, nɛ Central sʋ'ʋlʋm linɛ bɛ Ghana kpɛla.
english: Zone 2B has seven competing teams from the part of the Ashanti Region, Western Region and the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Techiman North anɛ distrik nam pii nɛ yinne la sʋ'ʋlʋm yinne bɛ Bono East region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana nwa ni.
english: Techiman North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Pin'ilʋgʋn la li da anɛ Techiman Distrik titada nam la yinne dawalig nwadig la 10 yʋma 1989 kanɛ da gaad la ni; hali ti paae saŋa kanɛ ka teŋ la ya-nya'aŋ dim la wɛligi ba kɔn' yiis maali ba mɛŋ distrik kanɛ an Techiman North Districk la n bɛ 28 sigir nwadig la 2012 la ni; ka teŋ kanɛ kpɛlim la an Techiman Distrik ( nya'aŋ ka li da nɔbigi lieb municipal distrik assembly ka ba maligim pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Techiman Municipal Assembly bɛ yʋʋm kan ni nɔɔ).
english: Techiman North is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Teddy Safori Addi (ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anaasi Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig dabpisi nɛ ayuobʋ daar (26 January 1984) anɛ Ghana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nid.
english: Teddy Safori Addi (born Thursday, 26 January 1984) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the National Democratic Congress.

english: He holds a BSc in Project Management.

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Ayensuano Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.

english: Addi hails from Coaltar in the Eastern Region (Ghana).

english: There are also a range of specialized types of tables, such as drafting tables, used for doing architectural drawings, and sewing tables.

english: Tema East is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Sʋ'ʋlimla wadman anɛ Isaac Ashai Odamtten.
english: Isaac Ashai Odamtten is the member of parliament for the constituency.

kusaal: Tempane District anɛ babir yinne dinɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlʋmnam piinɛ anu la ni Upper East Region, Ghana nwa ni.
english: Tempane District is one of the fifteen districts in Upper East Region, Ghana.

kusaal: Yiigin la li da anɛ dinɛ pɛ'ɛsnɛ sʋ'ʋlʋm tita'ar Garu-Tempane District 2004 yʋʋm la ni, ka ba yʋ'ʋn da pʋdʋg Ya-dagɔbʋg la paam Tempane District 15 February 2018 la ni; ka babir kanɛ kpɛlim la an Garu District.
english: Originally it was formerly part of the then-larger Garu-Tempane District in 2004, until the southeast part of the district was split off to create Tempane District on 15 February 2018; thus the remaining part has been renamed as Garu District.

kusaal: Babir la bɛnɛ Ya-dagɔbʋg Upper East Sʋ'ʋlʋm ka Tempane an li tɛŋpʋtita'ar.
english: The district assembly is located in the eastern part of Upper East Region and has Tempane as its capital town.

kusaal: African university college of communications la anɛ asʋ'ʋmmɛŋ sakur tita'ar kanɛ bɛ Adabraka, n bɛ Accra, Ghana teŋgbauŋin, ka ba na zamisid ka pa'an labaya la'asʋŋ nɛ li widigir nɛ labaya baŋir tʋʋma, nɛ kpikpiŋ zin'igin, nɛ Africa malima zamisʋg, kanɛ lina yɔ'ɔg suoya ka zamisʋg keŋ tuon, ka zumaaŋ la na zamis ka tʋm ka Africa paam nɔbigir nɛ tuon ken.
english: The African University College of Communications is a private tertiary institution at Adabraka, Accra, Ghana, for the study and teaching of journalism, communication studies, information technology convergence, business, African Studies, providing opportunities for advanced learning, and practical and professional training for the rapid growth and development of Africa.

english: The African University College of Communications was formerly known as the Africa Institute of Journalism & Communications (AIJC).

english: The institution was a private tertiary institution established in 2002 by Kojo Yankah, former editor of Ghana's widest circulation newspaper, the Daily Graphic, who also served nine years as Director of the Ghana Institute of Journalism, seven years as Minister of State, and eight years as Member of Parliament.

kusaal: 2007 la nii, National Accreditation Board da lɛn tis sakur la suor ye li pa'an Bachelor of Arts degree zamisa, n kɛ ka ba da buon sakur la ye African labaya la'asʋg nɛ li widigir zamisʋg sakur tita'ar (AUCC), ka da niŋ Africa yiiga sakur tita'ar kanɛ zamis labaya la'asʋg nɛ li widigir tʋʋma ka lin an ba zamis kpan 2010 yʋʋm la ni, NAB da lɛn tis AUCC suor ya'as ye ba pa'alim Bachelor of Science degree zamisa tʋʋma zin'isin nɔbigir nɛ ba kligidi zanlim yɛla.
english: In 2007, the institute received another approval from the National Accreditation Board to offer Bachelor of Arts degree courses and became known as the African University College of Communications (AUCC) becoming the first university in Africa to offer journalism and communication studies as its flagship.
