kusaal: The Cursed Ones anɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ nu (2015) British sini ka one da gɔsi li yela an Nana Obiri Yeboah ka one gaad tuon an Nicholas K. Lory.
english: The Cursed Ones is a 2015 British film that was directed by Nana Obiri Yeboah and produced by Nicholas K. Lory.

kusaal: One sɔb sini gbaŋ kanɛ anɛ Maximilian Claussen.
english: The original screenplay was written by Maximilian Claussen.

kusaal: Sini la pa'al nɛ sɔ sɔn'ɔs o tiraan ka Wina'am tʋmtʋm mɛ bɛɛ anina, bɔɔd on na niŋ si'em faan'e one ka ba ye o anɛ sɔn'ela, ye li pa'an West Africa dimi nan maan maliŋ si'eba.
english: The film tells the story of a disillusioned reporter and an idealistic young pastor, who fights to free a girl accused of witchcraft from the clutches of a corrupt system and superstition in the heart of West Africa.

kusaal: Sini la paam ya'an piini abʋtan' yi Africa Movie Academy Awards ni, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ (2016), ka piini la anɛ Best Director, Best Cinematography, nɛ Best Production Design.
english: The film received 3 Africa Movie Academy Awards in 2016 for Best Director, Best Cinematography, and Best Production Design.

kusaal: Ba da gaŋi li nɔɔrim piinɛ tan' bɛ AMAA awards, ka li pa'al ye sini kan ka ba da gaŋi gaad o taaba yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ la (2016).
english: It was nominated for 13 AMAA awards in total, making it the most nominated film of 2016.

kusaal: Sini la zin'is bɛdigʋ da maal nɛ tɛnkpɛŋ yinne kanɛ bɛ Eastern Region, Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The majority of the film was shot in a single village in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba da yis The Cursed Ones sini la Hackney Picturehouse linɛ bɛ London la, England ka li paas ban da gaŋi li ye li paas Royal African Society's Film Africa festival ni la.
english: The Cursed Ones screened at the Hackney Picturehouse in London, England as part of the official selection for the Royal African Society's Film Africa festival.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yuobʋ (2016) sini la da paas o taaba banɛ nya'adi bɛ Pan African Film Festival, Los Angeles sʋ'ʋlim, Atlanta Film Festival, Helsinki African Film Festival, 27th Annual Emden International Film Festival, nɛ New York African Film Festival linɛ bɛ Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts ka banɛ da paasi gɔsi li yela an Human Rights Watch la.
english: In 2016 the film also screened in competition at the Pan African Film Festival in Los Angeles, the Atlanta Film Festival, the Helsinki African Film Festival, the 27th Annual Emden International Film Festival, and the New York African Film Festival at the Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts where it was co-presented by the Human Rights Watch.

kusaal: Ba maal sini la nɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlim.
english: The film was shot entirely on location in Ghana.

kusaal: "Wina'am barikimi ti Ghana teŋgbaʋŋ" la, anɛ Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm la yʋ'ʋmmir kanɛ pa'an faangir nɛ yɔlisim; yʋ'ʋmmir la da naam nɛ yʋʋm 1957 ni, saŋkanɛ ka Ghana dim da faaɛn ba mɛŋ ka nyɛ yɔlisim yi nasanam nu'usin la.
english: "God Bless Our Homeland Ghana" is the national anthem of Ghana; it was adopted in 1957 when Ghana declared its independence from the United Kingdom.

kusaal: Din ka ba sɔb gbaʋŋi li yɛla ka Kwame Gbordzoe, onɛ da an sakur biig bɛ Bishop Herman College saŋkan sa la da mɔr yʋ'ʋmmir linɛ ka ba yʋm ye, "ziankimi Ghana flag la agɔla" ka ba sid da naami li Ghana faangir nya'aŋ la ka nɔki li lieb Ghana faangir yʋ'ʋmmir Nkrumah da an gɔmma zuraan la saŋa kena.
english: A competition was held and Kwame Gbordzoe, who was then a student at Bishop Herman College, presented the current lyrics which were chosen to replace "Lift High The Flag Of Ghana" which had been officially adopted after independence and used as Ghana's national anthem during Nkrumah's presidency.

kusaal: Daʋ kanɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Philip Gbaho la da pin'il naam Ghana yʋ'ʋmmir kanɛ pa'an faangir yɛla la, ka Emmanuel pallor-Thompson yʋm ka sɔbi li niŋ gbaʋŋin.
english: The music for the national anthem was originally composed by Philip Gbeho and sang to lyrics written by Emmanuel Pappoe-Thompson.

kusaal: Michael Kwame Gbordzoe da duoe zi'en ka ye onɛ da tigim yʋ'ʋmmir la sɔbi li Nkrumah onɛ da an gɔmma zuraan la kum nya'aŋ la.
english: Michael Kwame Gbordzoe has made claims to the current lyrics being used saying that it was written by him after the overthrow of President Nkrumah.

kusaal: The Perfect Picture anɛ Ghanaian sini kanɛ ka Shirley Frimpong-Manso da sɔbi li ka ba maali di bɛ yuum tusa ayi nɛ awai (2009) la ni.
english: The Perfect Picture is a Ghanaian movie produced and written by Shirley Frimpong-Manso in 2009.

kusaal: Perfect Picture la kɛ ka ti nyaŋi baŋ dunia kanɛ buudi ka ti bɛ ka li nwɛn wυυ si'el wυsa anɛ sum nyain la hali la'amnɛ ti zuanam.
english: The Perfect Picture offers a colorful and humorous insight into a world where everything is as perfect as your life and that of your friends.

kusaal: UNESCO da bas suor ye di anɛ Masterpiece tis Oral nɛ Intangible Heritage of Humanity bɛ 16 November 2010 la ni.
english: It was declared a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO on 16 November 2010.

kusaal: Nɔdi'esʋg kaŋa da dɛŋin gba'aenɛ digili an sɛnlʋg bɛ Greek pian'ad la, yitnɛ bishop Eusebius of Caesarea ka Sanit Augustine da yʋ'ʋn lɛbigidi ken Latin bɛ The City of God ni.
english: The prophecy was first recorded as an acrostic poem in Greek by bishop Eusebius of Caesarea and later translated into Latin by Saint Augustine in The City of God.

kusaal: Yʋʋma kaŋa da yʋmnɛ bɛ Latin ni ka bɛ Judicii Signum yʋ'ʋr ni, amaa dinɛ yi 13th nwa'ae la, di nwaasim yʋ'ʋn da bɛ Catalan ni.
english: This chant was originally sung in Latin and under the name of Judicii Signum, but from the 13th on, versions in Catalan are found.

kusaal: Di da lɛm yi 10th century ni na bɛ zin'is bɛdigʋ gilig Catalonia, Italy, Castile, nɛ France bɛ labaar kani ki'isid Contra judeos, ka yʋ'olim nɔki kpɛ'ɛs karʋŋ kani pɛ'ɛs ya'am ayuobʋ bɛ ayi daan bɛ nocturn of matins ka di da maalnɛ pɛ'ɛsid pʋ'ʋsʋm yʋma ni.
english: It appeared again in the 10th century in different locations across the Crown of Aragon, Italy, Castile, and France in the sermon Contra judeos, later inserted into the reading of the sixth lesson of the second nocturn of matins and was performed as an integral part of the liturgy.

kusaal: Ba da yisi li paalʋ ni bԑ Canada nԑ yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayuobʋ, Sԑnlʋŋ nwadig, daba anii daar bԑ Toronto International Film Festivald di'ema ni ka mԑ yisi li paalʋ yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayuobʋ, Sapal nwadig la ni dapisi nԑ ayuobʋ daari bԑ Eko Hotel and Suites Lagos sʋ'ʋlim, Nigeria.
english: It premiered on 8 September 2016 at the Toronto International Film Festival in Canada and on 26 November 2016 at Eko Hotel and Suites in Lagos.

kusaal: Ba da yis sini la paalʋ na ye dunia dim wʋsa nyԑ gͻs nԑ yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayuobʋ, Samanpiid nwadig dapiinԑ ayuobʋ daar, ka li da an Nigeria sini kanԑ ka nidib gͻs gaadi li taaba; nԑ lin ti paae yʋʋm tusayi nԑ pisi nԑ yinnԑ ni ka sini kanԑ buon Omo Ghetto: The Saga da kԑna di'e li nͻbir.
english: The film was released worldwide on 16 December 2016, and became the highest grossing Nigerian film; a record which was broken in 2021 by Omo Ghetto: The Saga.

english: In August 2017, the film was made available on Netflix.

kusaal: Onԑ ka ba buon Chidumga Izuzu ka o bԑ Pulse Nigeria la ye, "li anԑ sini kanԑ maan la'ad.
english: According to Chidumga Izuzu of Pulse Nigeria, "It is distinctly a comedy movie that sets out to entertain.

kusaal: Cinema Axis' Courtney Small da yel ye, "The Wedding Party ka'a sini kanԑ ka fʋ tuasi tis sͻ'ͻ ka malisim la wʋsa bԑԑ, amaa li anԑ sini kanԑ ma'ad nidib sʋnya.
english: Cinema Axis' Courtney Small stated, "The Wedding Party may not offer many surprises from a narrative standpoint, but there is no denying that the film is a pure crowd-pleaser.

kusaal: Temitope Adeiye onԑ bԑ thenet.ng da yel ye The Wedding Party anԑ "sini sʋ'ʋŋ yinnԑ kanԑ ka m gͻs yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayuobʋ ni".
english: Temitope Adeiye of thenet.ng stated that The Wedding Party was "one of the best movies I saw in 2016".

kusaal: The Wedding Party anԑ nͻŋilim yela sini kanԑ ka Nigeria dim maal yʋʋm tusayi nԑ piinԑ ayuobʋ ni ka onԑ gaad tuoni gosi li maalig yela an Kemi Adetiba.
english: The Wedding Party is a 2016 Nigerian romantic comedy drama directed by Kemi Adetiba.

kusaal: Tinuade Coker, da maan sid kulug malima nԑ Dozie Onwuka onԑ ka o dʋ'adib an ligidi dim.
english: During the day of the wedding between Dunni Coker a 24-year-old art gallery owner who is the only daughter of Engineer Bamidele and Mrs. Tinuade Coker, and the IT entrepreneur Dozie Onwuka, who comes from a very wealthy family.

kusaal: O ma ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Lady Obianuju Onwuka da gͻs ka o biig la ye o di pʋ'a kanԑ an nͻŋdaan.
english: His mother, Lady Obianuju Onwuka, considers her son to be marrying beneath himself.

kusaal: Pʋ'a la dʋ'adib nԑ o kpi'es sʋnya da pԑlig ya nԑ ban pʋ paas Tinuade Coker yʋ'ʋr di'ema gbaʋŋin la, daʋ la dʋ'adib da dʋk diib kanԑ ka pʋ'a la dʋ'adib pʋ bͻͻda, ka o ma mԑ lԑn pian'a zԑrig pʋ'a la ba'anami tis o zuanam banԑ kԑna la, pʋ'a la nԑ o sid Chief Felix Onwuka da pʋ tʋ'ʋgʋda.
english: Meanwhile, the bride's parents and female relatives are upset by the omission of Tinuade Coker's name in the announcement in the paper, and the groom's parents share an uncomfortable breakfast while the mother talks disparagingly about the Coker family to her friends and is very cold towards her husband, Chief Felix Onwuka.

kusaal: Dunni zuanam la'ad o ye o nan zi' digin nԑ daʋ, ka Dozie zuanam mԑ la'ad o bʋnlinԑ sa naam suos di'ema ni la ela.
english: Dunni is taunted by her female friends about her lack of sexual experience, and Dozie's male friends tease him about the previous night's bachelor's party.

kusaal: Pʋ'adiir la malima saŋa paae la, nidib banԑ kԑna la maal nԑ summalisim, ya'a ka'a Obianuju Onwuka ma'a zin' I anina ka o ya'am kae anina.
english: During the wedding ceremony, guests and family are cheerful, with the exception of Obianuju Onwuka who pointedly refuses to pay any attention, to the embarrassment of Felix.

kusaal: Ban da duoe lͻr yi malima zin'igin la lԑbid diib nԑ di'ema zin'igin la, Dunni da nyԑ pʋ'a pԑtnam ka li bԑ Dozie tuon gԑfa ni ka o sʋnf pԑlig hali.
english: Afterwards, while the cars are going from the ceremony to the party, Dunni finds a pair of women's underpants in the pocket of Dozie's dress jacket, and is upset.

kusaal: Diib zin'igin la mԑ lԑn mͻr la'ad bԑdigʋ, Tinuade Coker da nͻk sͻ' ye o dʋg Yoruba diib ka ba saam la di ka bas diib kanԑ ka Obianuju Onwuka maal la.
english: The dinner had its share of embarrassing incidents, including Tinuade Coker having hired a local Yoruba chef to cook an alternative to the fancy menu set by Obianuju Onwuka.

kusaal: Sola da yis o nͻͻr kuom na ka ye o yis sini giŋ sia ka ba gͻs, o da pʋ baŋԑ ka tiak linԑ ka Dozie ti'eb ye nidib la gͻs la lԑbis bʋnlinԑ mͻr nyan linԑ pa'al wan wʋʋ Dozie anԑ ninkanԑ gaae o pʋ'a la nya'aŋ, linzug ka pʋ'a la zͻ yi.
english: When Sola gives his best man's speech, he accidentally shows video footage from the stag night instead of the video prepared by Dozie for the occasion, and the humiliated Dunni leaves the room after having witnessed what looks like Dozie being unfaithful to her.

kusaal: Sͻ da sial o yi'iŋi an Dozie sabua kʋdʋg ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Rosie, o da ma'a ye on digin nԑ Dozie daar kan nͻͻ - li yelsida anԑ ye Rosie da mͻ ye o digin nԑ o ka lԑԑ gʋ'ʋŋ nԑ.
english: She is met outside the room by one of Dozie's old girlfriends, Rosie, who claims that she had sex with Dozie earlier that day - in reality, Rosie had tried to seduce him but failed.

kusaal: Dozie nԑ o bier Nonso nԑ dʋ'adib la da yii ied Dunni amaa ba da kpԑn'ԑ dͻͻg kanԑ ka ba di'es piini la'asi digil la ka na'ayiig bԑ anina ka nͻk malifʋ kpa' ba ka ba pʋ nyaŋi yii.
english: Dozie, his older brother Nonso, and the two sets of parents set out to look for Dunni but are held up at gunpoint by a thief who has managed to get into the room with the wedding gifts.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili yisidi ba zugun yela tisid taaba, Dozie ma da tuasi pa'al o sid o sʋnfʋ ԑԑnti san'am si'em nԑ on na nyԑ ka o dͻl pʋ'abibis, ka Dunni saam mԑ yel ye o tʋʋma ni la ligidi la wʋsa kpԑn'ԑ mͻͻg.
english: The tense situation causes the couples to open up to each other, with Dozie's mother confessing to her husband how unhappy she had been about his affairs with younger women, and Dunni's father admitting that his company had lost all its money.

kusaal: Dozie da kpԑn'ԑ lͻr ni nԑ Sola ye ba kԑŋ ia Dunni, O da pian'a pa'al o ye on pʋ san'am o mԑŋa bԑԑ ba pʋ'adiir la.
english: Dozie goes off in a car with Sola to find Dunni, and convinces her that he has in fact not broken their mutual promise of chastity.

kusaal: Wilfred Okiche onԑ bԑ ynaija da yel si'eli kati wa'ae Kemi Adetiba nԑ on gaad tuoni gͻsi maal sini la anԑ anwa; "Li ya'a ka'a pian'a bԑdig kanԑ ka sid la saam yina pian'a laa nԑ Sambassa Nzeribe nԑ Hafiz Oyetoro zin'isin la, Adetiba maal si'el wʋsa ka li kԑŋ titua".
english: Wilfred Okiche of ynaija has this to say about Kemi Adetiba and her role as director; "Apart from some red flags, like the overbearing wedding speech by the father of the groom for instance, the haves and haves not sub plot involving Sambassa Nzeribe, and the entire existence of Hafiz Oyetoro's gate crashing character, Adetiba keeps things moving briskly".

kusaal: O da yel o ye li tͻn'ͻ an o zuanam la yinnԑ nͻki niŋ anina, nԑ ban ti paae di'ema zin'igin la.
english: He convinces her that they had been planted there, probably by one of his friends, and they belatedly arrive at the party.

kusaal: Theresa Lardi Awuni (Dʋ'anɛ 2 January 1979) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd onɛ paas Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg la, National Democratic Congress ni.
english: Theresa Lardi Awuni (born 2 January 1979) is a Ghanaian politician who is a member of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Okaikwei North Constituency bɛ Greater Accra region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: She is the member of parliament for the Okaikwei North Constituency in the Greater Accra region of Ghana.

kusaal: O yinɛ Winkongo bɛ Upper East Region la.
english: She hails from Winkongo in the Upper East Region.

kusaal: O da maal o Bachelor of Science degree in Project Management nɛ Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii la ni (2018).
english: She obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Project Management from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration in 2018.

kusaal: O da tʋm nɛ National Disaster Management Organization bɛ Ghana la aan ba principal disaster control officer ka lɛn tʋm Langdi Enterprise (an proprietress).
english: She worked at the National Disaster Management Organization of Ghana as a principal disaster control officer and at Langdi Enterprise (as proprietress).

kusaal: Awuni Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration TEIN pʋ'ab kpɛɛm (Women's Commissioner).
english: Awuni is a former Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration TEIN Women's Commissioner.

english: TEIN (Tertiary Education Institutions Network) is the tertiary wing of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: O da lɛn an onɛ la'asid pʋ'ab nɔɔr atan tisi o sʋ'ʋlim dim (Constituency Women's Organizer of Okaikwei North Constituency).
english: She is also a three-time Constituency Women's Organizer of Okaikwei North Constituency.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai la Nwadisa anii la ni (August 2019), o da nya' National Democratic Congress primaries Okaikwei North Constituency sʋ'ʋlim ka di nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadis piinɛ ayi la (December 2020) vɔɔtʋg la.
english: In August 2019, she contested for the National Democratic Congress primaries for Okaikwei North Constituency and won as the candidate to present the party in the December 2020 Elections.

kusaal: Awuni da diya nɛ vɔɔt kɔbistan nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayi (342) yi vɔɔt kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ (866) ka onɛ tia'al o la, Richard Kwarshie Kudjordjie, Abdul Nasiru Abass nɛ Malik Adama paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi' nɛ pisi (220), kɔbiga nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ awai (179) nɛ piinɛ ayi (12).
english: Awuni won by 342 votes out of a total of 866 ballots cast while her other contenders Richard Kwarshie Kudjordjie, Abdul Nasiru Abass and Malik Adama had 220 votes, 179 votes and 12 votes respectively.

kusaal: On nɛ onɛ da dɛŋim zin'i kʋk la zug la, Fuseini Issah onɛ bɛ Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la, New Patriotic Party ka di nɛ vɔɔt tusa pisi nɛ awai, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnii nɛ yinne (29,281) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ yinne du'ali ayɔpɔi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (51.07%) ka o tiraan la paam tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbisyi' nɛ pisnaasi nɛ ayi (27,242) dinɛ an pisnaasi nɛ ayɔpɔi du'al pisnu nɛ ayi kɔbiga pʋʋgin (47.52%).
english: She was elected member of parliament for the Okaikwei North Constituency in December 2020.She contested against the incumbent member of parliament Fuseini Issah of the New Patriotic Party and won after polling 29,281 votes representing 51.07% against his 27,242 votes representing 47.52%.

kusaal: o paas pʋ'ab pisnaasi (40 women) banɛ zi'eni tisi ba sʋ'ʋlimnam wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii la yʋʋm tusa yi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Yʋʋmpaal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi la daar (7 January 2021).
english: She is one of the 40 women representing their respective constituencies in the 8th Parliament from 7 January 2021.

kusaal: O paasnɛ Subsidiary Legislation Committee nɛ Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee Gaana Wadmaanib yin la.
english: She is a member of the Subsidiary Legislation Committee and the Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee within the Ghanaian Parliament.

english: She was elected member of parliament for the Okaikwei North Constituency in December 2020.She contested against the incumbent member of parliament Fuseini Issah of the New Patriotic Party and won after polling 29,281 votes representing 51.07% against his 27,242 votes representing 47.52%.

kusaal: Awuni anɛ Kristo biig.
english: Awuni is a devout Christian.

kusaal: Tieb buudi si'a buon ye thieboudienne bɛɛ chebu jen (wolof: ceebu jēn; French: thiéboudiénne) dʋgidnɛ nɛ zimi, mui bua'ama nɛ tomatosi ka ba la'asi dʋg dʋk yinne pʋʋgin.
english: The version of tiep called ceebu jën or chebu jen (Wolof: ceebu jën, pronounced [cɛːbu ɟen]) – also known by its Francized name thieboudienne (French: thiéboudiène) – is prepared with fish, broken rice and tomato sauce cooked in one pot.

kusaal: Pulaar ni, li yʋ'ʋr anɛ maaro e liddi ('rice and fish').
english: In Pulaar it is known as maaro e liddi ('rice and fish').

kusaal: Li mɛ anɛ Senegalese terranga (hospitality): zanbin, yidim, zuanam nɛ saam la'asidi dit laa yinne pʋʋgin n (buon ye bolus) kanɛ ka sɔ wʋsa dit nɛ diisʋŋ (couddou pulaar) bɛɛ nɛ bodobodo bi'ela.
english: It is also the symbol of Senegalese terranga (hospitality): family, visiting friends and guests gather around a single dish (called a bolus) from which everyone eats using a spoon (couddou Pulaar) or their hand.

kusaal: Gullah diib, redrice la nwɛni nɛ thieboudienne, ka makid ye creolization of foodways kanɛ yi Africa ka bɛ dunia paal nwa ni ka li anɛ Africa da'aba nɛ ba nya'aŋ dim.
english: The Gullah dish red rice resembles thieboudienne, suggesting a creolization of foodways from West Africa in the New World by enslaved Africans and their descendants.

kusaal: Woo thieboudienne, sʋ'ʋlim nam la Gullah/Geechee Cultural Heritage Corridor wʋsa mɔri red rice, nwi zin'a la nɛ kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb, la'am nɛ Saannah red rice nɛ Charleston red rice.
english: Like thieboudienne, there are regional variations of red rice throughout the Gullah/Geechee Cultural Heritage Corridor, including Savannah red rice and Charleston red rice.

kusaal: Camreroon nɛ Ivory Coast teŋin, diid la yʋ'ʋr anɛ riz gras.
english: In Cameroon, Guinea and Ivory Coast the dish is called riz gras.

kusaal: Li anɛ Senegal teŋ dim dikpɛŋ.
english: It is the national dish in Senegal.

kusaal: Zɛn banɛ paasi li zug anɛ gabʋ, carrots, cabbage, banki vaand, nanzʋ'ʋtɔɔg, leemu-nyaami nɛ suma kpaam, nɛ stock cubes.
english: Additional ingredients often include onions, tomatoes, carrots, cabbage, cassava, hot pepper, lime and peanut oil, and stock cubes.

kusaal: Tieb da anɛ Saint-Louis tempʋtita'ar la diib, 19th century yʋʋma la ni.
english: Historically, tiep is commonly attributed to the city of Saint-Louis, in the nineteenth century.

kusaal: Diib la yʋ'ʋr yinɛ Wolof pian'adin ka li gbin an mui (ceeb) nɛ zimi (jēn).
english: The name of the dish comes from the Wolof words ceeb (meaning 'rice') and jën ('fish').

kusaal: Timket (Geʻez: ጥምቀት T'imk'et) anɛ Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church nɛ Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church malʋŋkanɛ ka ba maani bɛ Epiphany.
english: Timkat (Ge'ez: ጥምቀት T'imk'et) is an Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church celebration of Epiphany.

kusaal: Ba maani linɛ yʋʋmpaal nwadig wʋsa dabpiinɛ awai daar wʋsa bɛɛ dabpisi daar yʋʋm sieba ni dinɛ an yinne nɛ Terr dabpiinɛ yinne daar Ge'ez calendar ni.
english: It is celebrated on 19 January (or 20 in a leap year), corresponding to the 11th day of Terr in the Ge'ez calendar.

kusaal: Nidib mi' malʋŋ la nɛ din zi'eni tisid Wina'am ku'om sʋʋb la (nwɛnɛ Kristo biis bɛdegʋ maan si'em bɛ Holy Land la ba ya'a kaae/ keŋ Jordan).
english: This festival is best known for its ritual reenactment of baptism (similar to such reenactments performed by numerous Christian the Holy Land when they visit the Jordan).

kusaal: Timkat malʋŋ maalʋg saŋa, Tabot, dinɛ an zanbini zi'eni tis Wina'am nɔnaar daka dinɛ bɛ Ethiopian altar nam wʋsa ni la (nwɛnɛ Westhern altar kugir), ba viligi dinɛ nɛ fukanɛ ligiid zu'oe ka maan maan la zii li o zugin.
english: During the ceremonies of Timkat, the Tabot, a model of the Ark of the Covenant, which is present on every Ethiopian altar (somewhat like the Western altar stone), is reverently wrapped in rich cloth and borne in procession on the head of the priest.

kusaal: Tabot, dinɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa pʋ nyɛt na'ana ka di ya'a ka'anɛ maan maanib la, zi'eni tis Kristo tʋm pa'al ye onɛ an Messiah la on da ken' Jordan ye o sʋ Wina'am ku'om la.
english: The Tabot, which is otherwise rarely seen by the laity, represents the manifestation of Jesus as the Messiah when he came to the Jordan for baptism.

kusaal: Malʋŋ kaŋa mɛ da paasi an UNESCO intangible heritage.
english: This celebration is also registered in UNESCO as an intangible heritage.

kusaal: UNESCO da zaŋ Timkat nɛ yʋʋm tusia ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019) la ni paas Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
english: UNESCO inscribed Timkat in 2019 on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Timkat malʋŋ la tiendnɛ Yesu ku'om sʋʋb bɛ River Jordan.
english: Timkat celebrates the baptism of Jesus in the River Jordan.

kusaal: Divine Liturgy malʋŋ la maanɛ kɔlʋg dɛn'ɛr bɛɛ bɛʋgin bɛkɛʋg nwɛnɛ kɛfa ayi.
english: The Divine Liturgy is celebrated near a stream or pool early in the morning (around 2 a.m.).

kusaal: Timqat Daar niŋtaŋ, nidib bɛdegʋ na la'as malʋŋ zin'igin la, ka banɛ kul yin ye bag bis bi'ela la lɛbna, ka ba bi'el Kasi daka la keŋ ka la keŋ karimdɔɔgin nɛ vɛnlim nɛ di'ema.
english: By noon on Timqat Day a large crowd has assembled at the ritual site, those who went home for a little sleep having returned, and the holy ark is escorted back to its church in colorful procession and festivities.

kusaal: O anɛ Wabʋ Na'adɔɔg (NPP) nid; ka Ghana gɔmina Zugdaan Nana Addo da gaŋ o ye, o an kpɛɛm kanɛ dɔli ti laafi lʋgir kpɛɛm la nya'aŋ (Deputy Minister of Health) bɛ nwadis atan' la ni, li dab pii nɛ anu daar, yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni.
english: She is a member of the New Patriotic Party and was appointed into office as deputy Health Minister by Nana Addo on 15 March 2017.

kusaal: Mensah da anɛ onɛ ka ba du'a o bɛ nwadig yinnɛ la ni, li dabisim pisi nɛ atan' daar, yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbis awai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi la ni.Bɛ Jamestown, British Accra bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlum.O daar keŋɛ o secondary education bɛnɛ Accra Girls School la ni.
english: Mensah was born on 23 January 1964 in Jamestown, British Accra of the Greater Accra Region.

kusaal: O mɔri o kasɛtta gbana banɛ ka ti buon ye, bachelor's degree in Public Administration nɛ Masters in international relations nɛ Diplomacy yit Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration.
english: She holds a bachelor's degree in Public Administration and Masters in international relations and Diplomacy from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA)

kusaal: Mensah da mɔri vɔɔt kal 34,216 yit 59,926 kanɛ an vɔɔtnam la wʋsa kal la, yʋma 2016 vɔɔdʋg kanɛ da an wadmaanib na'am nya'dib saŋa la.
english: Mensah secured 34,216 votes out of the 59,926 valid votes cast in the 2016 Ghanaian general election.

kusaal: Obuobia Darko-Opoku nɛ Jessica Adwoa Mannuel da nyi'a na'am la nɛ o.O da ti zi'en wabʋg na'adɔɔg nɔba zug nyi'a wadmaanib kʋk na'am kanɛ da bɛ Ghana yʋʋm vɔɔdʋg tita'ar kanɛ da bɛ yʋma 2020 la ni la ka di lieb wadmaan.
english: She defeated Obuobia Darko-Opoku and Jessica Adwoa Mannuell.

kusaal: O da anɛ kpɛɛm bɛ Gemens Company LTD.
english: She was the managing director of Gemens Company LTD.

kusaal: bɛ Mamprobi, Accra.
english: in Mamprobi, Accra.

kusaal: Nwadis anii la, li daba anaasi daar yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni, o da di'e ya'an piini yiti Ghana-Nigeria Youth Organization yiti on da an kpɛɛm sʋŋ la yɛla .
english: On 4 August 2017, she was awarded by the Ghana-Nigeria Youth Organization for outstanding leadership.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni o da lɛn di'e ya'an piini kanɛ bigis ye o tʋʋma an sʋ'ʋŋa on an laafi lʋgir la kpɛɛm nya'aŋ dɔla, yit FAKS Investigative Services.
english: In 2017 she was adjudged best Deputy Minister by FAKS Investigative Services.

kusaal: O anɛ Ghana politis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan tis Weija-Gbawe constituency.
english: Tina Gifty Mensah is a member of New Patriotic Party and was a member of parliament for Weija-Gbawe constituency in the Greater Accra Region in the Seventh and Eighth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: Tina mɔr sid nɛ biisa atan'.
english: Tina is married with three children.

kusaal: Zin'ig kaŋa anɛ zin'ig kanɛ vɛnl ka an' nidib la'asug zin'ig ka diib nɛ dankpi'ema buudi wʋsa bɛ.O nyaŋidi la'asid ka tɔn'ɔd diibi paad zin'i banɛ bɔɔd sʋŋir wʋʋ Fiesta of Flavours Food Fairs, GTBank Food nɛ Drink Fair, the Mzansi Culinary Festival (SA).
english: She has been involved in planning a number of events in the hospitality space and delivering masterclasses at the Fiesta of Flavours Food Fairs, the GTBank Food and Drink Fair, the Mzansi Culinary Festival (SA).

kusaal: Ba da dʋa Alile bɛnɛ Benin City, o saam anɛ dʋ'ata ka o ma an piiyam.
english: Alile was born in Benin City to a physician father while her mother is a judge.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayi ka o da lɛb sakur kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon L'Academie de Cuisine ni ye o zamis diib dʋgʋb.
english: She went back to school in 2012 to train in the culinary arts at the L'Academie de Cuisine.

kusaal: On da bɛ sakurin la, Alile da mɔr zin'ig kanɛ ka o kuosid diib ka o da pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Tea Time Cupcakes.
english: In high school, Alile had a cupcake store called Tea Time Cupcakes.

kusaal: Yʋma anaasi nya'aŋ, yʋʋm tusayi nɛ atan' ni, o da yɔ'ɔg diib kuosig zin'ig Nigerian ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Mankɛnbiis tʋʋma ka mɛ da an onɛ gɔsid diib yela tis Genevieve Magazine.
english: Four years later, in 2003, she opened up a Nigerian restaurant called Matchsticks Concepts while she was a food columnist for Genevieve Magazine.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anu la ni, Tiyan da zʋŋ o diib kuosig zin'ig ka pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye Tarragon (o da nɔk nɛ dikanɛ ka o nɔŋ yʋ'ʋri pʋd), linɛ ka o da pin'ili yi dinner club ni.
english: In 2015, Tiyan launched her restaurant called Tarragon (named after her favorite spice), which originally started out as a dinner club.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ ayɔpɔi ni, Alile da pin'ili pa'an diib dʋgʋb ka pin'il Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim diib dʋgʋb sakur kanɛ da kɛn yiiga na la yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayi ka li bɛ Lagos, Nigeria.
english: In 2007, Alile began to teach cooking and established Nigeria's first culinary school Culinary Academy in 2012 based in Lagos, Nigeria.

kusaal: Tiyan pa'al kpɛɛmnami ba zamisig zin'igin bɛ Central Johannesburg College sakur ni ka mɛ pa'al o sakur bil yinnɛ kanɛ da paasi nya'a diib dʋgʋb ya'an yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ bɛ India tɛŋin la Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ ayuobʋ di'ema kanɛ ka GTBank da maal ka li an diib dʋgʋb nya'ab la ni, Tiyan nɛ o diib dʋgʋb baŋir dim taaba, da pa'al bipaala banɛ ka ba tʋʋma an diib dʋgʋb.
english: Tiyan has taught master-classes at the Central Johannesburg College and has also trained one of the students at her academy who was invited to participate in the 2016 Young Chef Olympiad in India At the 2016 edition of the GTBank Food and Drink Fair, Tiyan, along with other top chefs, taught young and aspiring chefs new culinary skills.

kusaal: Alile da an zugraani tis Rotary club of Victoria Island East lin yi yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ atan' paae yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi ni.
english: Alile served as the president to the Rotary club of Victoria Island East from 2013 to 2014.

kusaal: Alile di ya'an piini bɛdigʋ, ka li yinnɛ an Luxury Travel Guide piini kanɛ ka ba tisid diib kuosig zin'ig kanɛ gaadi ba taaba, dunia wʋsa diib kuosig zin'ig kanɛ ka diib an sʋ'ʋŋa gaad o taab nɛ dunia wʋsa diib dʋgʋdib la'asig piini nam.
english: Alile has won several awards, including the Luxury Travel Guide Best Restaurant awards, World Luxury Restaurant Award for fine dining and food presentation and the World Chefs Global Connect.

kusaal: O diib dʋgʋb zin'is la si'eba anɛ Ibadan Golf Club nɛ nananana diib zin'is sieba Nigeria teŋin..
english: A few of her former restaurants include a grill at the Ibadan Golf Club and a modernized Nigerian restaurant.

kusaal: Nannaa onɛ an' tuongat didʋgʋdʋb nɛ diib zin'is wʋsa kpeem Nigeria.
english: She is the current president of The Culinary Arts Practitioners Association in Nigeria, the founder and promoter of Culinary Academy and the Executive Chef of Tarragon, a fine dining restaurant and wine club.

kusaal: Onɛ yɔ'ɔg diib dugub zamisig zin'ig ka an' didʋgʋd kpeem bɛ Tarragon.
english: She is the current president of The Culinary Arts Practitioners Association in Nigeria, the founder and promoter of Culinary Academy and the Executive Chef of Tarragon, a fine dining restaurant and wine club.

kusaal: O da pin'il diib dʋgʋb nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai la ni, sankan ka o da pin'ili sɛn'ɛd bʋn'ɔnbida bɛ Ibadan Golf Club ka li yʋ'ʋr an Tees Hot Bites.
english: She officially began working in the culinary arts in 1999 when she started a grill house at Ibadan Golf Club named Tees Hot Bites.

kusaal: Alile sɔb gbaŋ kanɛ ka ba o pʋdi li ye, sɔlima linɛ bɛ bʋnki'ima ni, ka nidib da gɔs ka ye li anɛ "gbaŋ kanɛ pa'an dʋgʋb yela li kɔn' sa".
english: Alile is the author of the book, Tale in a pie, which has been described as "the most scandalous story cook book out there".

kusaal: Diib dʋgʋb zamisig nwa paae li bɛn wan wʋʋ li taaba banɛ bɛ tɛŋ si'eba ni ka ba lɛɛ gɔsid nɛ diib buudi buudi banɛ bɛ Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim ni la yela.
english: She is also the president of Culinary Arts Practitioners Association of Nigeria.

kusaal: Onɛ an zugraani tis lʋgʋr kanɛ la'as banɛ dʋgʋd diibi bɛ Nigeria la.
english: She is also the president of Culinary Arts Practitioners Association of Nigeria.

kusaal: Onɛ dɛŋin an' yiiga sɔbi yɔ'ɔg diib buudi kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb zin'ig sakur Nageria teŋin.
english: She is also the president of Culinary Arts Practitioners Association of Nigeria.

kusaal: Tobata Gion Yamagasa festival (戸畑祇園山笠) anɛ Japanese festival (matsuri) kanɛ nyɛ yʋ'ʋr hali, ka ba maani li yʋʋm wʋsa bɛ Tobata, linɛ bɛ Kitakyushu, Fukuoka prefecture, Kyūshū, Japan.
english: The Tobata Gion Yamagasa festival (戸畑祇園山笠) is a popular local Japanese festival (matsuri) which takes place annually in Tobata, a ward of Kitakyushu in Fukuoka prefecture, Kyūshū, Japan.

kusaal: Region nam anaasi bɛ Tobata paasid malʋŋ la pʋʋgin: Higashi, Nishi, Tenraiji nɛ Nakabaru.
english: There are four regions of Tobata which participate: Higashi, Nishi, Tenraiji and Nakabaru.

kusaal: Ba diti li daba atan' (3 days) Arizum daari paae Alasid daar ka li lut nɛ nwadis ayɔpɔi bakɔi anaasi ni.
english: It is held for three days (Friday–Sunday) before and after the fourth Saturday of July.

kusaal: Yamagasa (bɛɛ Yamakasa) bɛdegʋ anɛ ba kennɛ giligid tɛŋin la, ka lin paas malʋŋ la pʋʋgin.
english: The Yamagasa (or Yamakasa) are very large floats, and are the focal point of the festival.

kusaal: Region wʋsa mɔr Yamagasa tita'ari tis dap ka mɛ mɔri li bʋnbili tis dasam, ka li pa'al ye ba giligid tɛɛns lanɛ zin'is anii.
english: Each region has a large Yamagasa for men and a small one for boys, making eight main floats in total.

kusaal: Ba ya'a ye ba yis Yamagasa la banɛ zanli li la wʋsa na ʋkʋ li.
english: To move the Yamagasa is an art which requires concerted lifting by all the carriers.

kusaal: Ka ba ya'a ye ba maali li titu'aa, ba ɛɛnti tansnɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye "yoitosa, yoitosa" saŋa yinne ka lʋmʋs nɛ dʋʋdis nwɛ'ɛd.
english: To ensure that they do it successfully, they all shout "yoitosa, yoitosa" together in a rhythmic chant with drums and cymbals.

kusaal: Malima nwa da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs nii nɛ ayi la (1802), wiim da gban'e Tobata teŋkpɛŋ kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon ye Chikuzen la, ka ba da sɔs Suga-taijin ye o yis ban'as la, o da wʋmi ba sɔsʋg ka teŋ la nidib wʋsa da paami ba laafi.
english: This festival has its origin in 1802, when people plagued by an epidemic in Tobata Village of Chikuzen prayed to Suga-taijin to disperse the plague, their prayers were answered and all of the villagers with the plague were cured.

kusaal: Linɛ paas anɛ yɛ, ba pin'il Yamagasa malima kanɛ an pu'ab din mɛn.
english: Also, a Yamagasa festival for ladies has been started .

kusaal: Tolani Tayo-Osikoya, ka ba bʋon o ye Chef T, anɛ onɛ dugid diib yit Nigeria ka lɛn maan bʋŋosida, on yʋ'ʋr kanɛ ka o mɔri maan bʋŋosida niŋid YouTube la anɛ Gbaʋŋ kanɛ an onɛ nɔŋ daʋŋ.
english: Tolani Tayo-Osikoya, also known as "Chef T", is a Nigerian chef and YouTuber known for her YouTube channel, Diary of a Kitchen Lover.

kusaal: O anɛ Nigeria nid ka yit Yoruba dim tʋŋ ni.
english: She is Nigerian from the Yoruba ethnicity.

kusaal: Tolani da kiŋɛ Babcock University ti zamis a-kaali-vɛnlig, yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni.
english: in Accounting from Babcock University in 2012.

kusaal: O nam mi zi'ɛn Knorr, nɛ PZ Cussons bekɛʋg ma'asim, nɛ malta Guinness nɛ sieba nobazug bɛ Nigeria.
english: She has been an ambassador for Knorr, PZ Cussons's Morning Fresh, Malta Guinness and other brands in Nigeria.

kusaal: Tolani ɛlne Temitayo Osikoya; ka ba mɔr biig yinne.
english: Tolani is married to Temitayo Osikoya; the couple have one child.

kusaal: Sɔb kanɛ an tomato yinɛ Spanish buudi pian'ad kanɛ ka ba buon tomate, linɛ mɛ yi Nahuatl buudi pian'ad ni ka ba buon tomatl [ˈtomat͡ɬ].
english: The word tomato comes from the Spanish tomate, which in turn comes from the Nahuatl word tomatl [ˈtomat͡ɬ] .

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr la ka ba pʋd lycopersicum, ka li gbin an 'wolf peach', lin yinɛ Galen, ka lin gbin da anɛ bʋnbʋta kanɛ ka ba nan zi'i o yʋ'ʋrɛ.
english: The specific name lycopersicum, meaning 'wolf peach', originated with Galen, who used it to denote a plant that has never been identified.

kusaal: Luigi Anguillara da yis labaar na 16th century ye Galen tɛŋ dim lycopersicum tɔ'ɔn an tomato la, la'anɛ lin tɔi nɛ ban na si'ak ye linɛ la la, lycopersicum kpɛn'ɛ na'asaasɔn'ɔg tʋʋma ni ka anɛ wal yʋ'ʋr.
english: Luigi Anguillara speculated in the 16th century that Galen's lycopersicum might be the tomato, and despite the impossibility of this identification, lycopersicum entered scientific use as a name for the fruit.

kusaal: Ban buon tomato si'em anɛ /təˈmeɪtoʊ/ (bɛ North American English) nɛ /təˈmɑːtoʊ/ (bɛ British English).
english: The usual pronunciations of tomato are (in North American English) and (in British English).

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋr la ka ba buoni li zin'is ayi la da nyɛ yʋ'ʋr ka kpɛlim bɛ Ira nɛ George Gershwin yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔ ni (1937) yi yʋʋma kanɛ da buon "Let's Call the Whole Thing Off" ("fʋ bɔɔd /pəˈteɪtoʊ/ ka mam mɛ bɔɔd /pəˈtɑːtoʊ/ / fʋ bɔɔd /təˈmeɪtoʊ/ ka mam mɛ nɔŋ /təˈmɑːtoʊ/").
english: The word's dual pronunciations were immortalized in Ira and George Gershwin's 1937 song "Let's Call the Whole Thing Off" ("You like and I like / You like and I like ").

kusaal: cerasiforme yʋʋm tusa pisyɔpɔi saŋa kanɛ gaad (78,000), ka tomato kanɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋn da kuod la da pin'il nɛ yʋʋm tusayɔpɔi banɛ gaad la saŋa (5,000 BCE), ka lɛɛ pʋ nyaŋi baŋ nyain wan wʋʋ ninsaalib da paasi ti'aki li bɛ.
english: cerasiforme appeared around 78,000 years ago, while the cultivated tomato originated around 7,000 years ago (5,000 BCE), with substantial uncertainty, making it unclear how humans may have been involved in the process.

kusaal: Aztecs buudi la da gʋ'ʋn tomatos buudi kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb, ka bʋnwiig la ka ba buon xitomatl ka onɛ an kansir la ka ba buon tomatl (tomatillo).
english: The Aztecs raised several varieties of tomato, with red tomatoes called xitomatl.

kusaal: Bernardino de Sahagún ye o nyɛ tomatos kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb Aztec da'an bɛ Tenochtitlán (Mexico tɛnpʋʋgin): "tomato bibis, tomato bɛda, ntoos banɛ mɔr vaand, ntoos banɛ malis, large serpent tomatoes, banɛ wan bin'is nɔnya", nɛ tomato banɛ mɔr kala wʋsa lin yi banɛ muoe wiig paae banɛ an dɔnbʋʋlim.
english: Bernardino de Sahagún reported seeing a great variety of tomatoes in the Aztec market at Tenochtitlán (Mexico City): "large tomatoes, small tomatoes, leaf tomatoes, sweet tomatoes, large serpent tomatoes, nipple-shaped tomatoes", and tomatoes of all colors from the brightest red to the deepest yellow.

kusaal: Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés da gba'ae Tenochtitlan yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnu nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ la (1521) da kɛ ka nidib zamisi ba taaba malima nɛ disi'eba ka ba buon din ye Columbian la'ad ti'asig; ba da kuod tomato Europe tɛŋin ti'asig nwa nya'aŋ.
english: The Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés's capture of Tenochtitlan in 1521 initiated the widespread cultural and biological interchange called the Columbian exchange.

kusaal: Ban da pin'ili pian'ad tomato yela European gbana ni yiiga da anɛ Pietro Andrea Mattioli yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnu nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anaasi (1544) gbaŋ kanɛ ka o da buon herbal la.
english: The earliest mention of the tomato in European literature appeared in Pietro Andrea Mattioli's 1544 herbal.

kusaal: Yʋʋm piiga nya'aŋ ka Mattioli da pʋd wal la yʋ'ʋr ye pomi d'oro, bɛɛ "golden apples".
english: Ten years later, Mattioli named the fruits in print as pomi d'oro, or "golden apples".

kusaal: Ba da mɔri li kɛŋ Philippines, anina ka li yi kɛŋ paae southeast Asia ka yadigi paae Asia sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.
english: After they introduced it to the Philippines, it spread to Southeast Asia and then across Asia.

kusaal: Spanish dim da mɔr tomato kɛŋ Europe, anina ka tɛŋ la ma'asim da an titua ka li da nɔbig sʋ'ʋŋa; ba da pin'il kuob nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnu nɛ pisnaasi nam saŋa (1540s).
english: The tomato was cultivated in Europe only a few years after that event, by the 1540s, and grew easily in the Mediterranean climates.

kusaal: Ba da pin'ili diti li ban da kuodi li la nya'aŋ, ka ba da pin'ili mɔri li maan diib 17th century pin'ilig sa Spain tɛŋin, wan wʋʋ lin sɔbi bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piinɛnii (1618) di'ema kanɛ buon La octava maravilla ka onɛ maali li an Lope de Vega ka labaar kanɛ bɛ li pʋʋgin si'eba an "lovelier than ...
english: It was probably eaten shortly after it was introduced, and tomatoes were used as food by the early 17th century in Spain, as documented in the 1618 play La octava maravilla by Lope de Vega with "lovelier than ...

kusaal: Tomato da paae China sʋ'ʋlim, li tɔn'ɔn da yinɛ Philippines bɛɛ Macau tɛɛnsin, 16th century saŋa.
english: The tomato was introduced to China, likely via the Philippines or Macau, in the 16th century.

kusaal: Ba da pʋdi li yʋ'ʋr ye 番茄 fānqié (tɛŋsi'a wal gbilig), wan wʋʋ Chinese dimi da pʋd diib buudi banɛ da naan tɛŋ si'eba paae ba tɛŋin na la, amaa ka lɛɛ anɛ kʋdʋmn sa bʋnam la.
english: It was given the name 番茄 fānqié (foreign eggplant), as the Chinese named many foodstuffs introduced from abroad, but referring specifically to early introductions.

kusaal: Daʋ kanɛ da an yiiga da bʋd da anɛ John Gerard, ɔ da anɛ barber – surgeon.
english: One of the earliest cultivators was John Gerard, a barber-surgeon.

kusaal: Gerard da tɔn pa'ansid nidib kɛ ka mi yɛ tamantoos pʋ nar nɛ diibɔ Yʋma bɛdigʋ Britain nɛ tɛŋ banɛ bɛ ya datiʋŋ ka America dim da nyaŋ la.
english: Gerard's views were influential, and the tomato was considered unfit for eating for many years in Britain and its North American colonies.

kusaal: Wɛn wɔɔ Elizabeth Blackwell A Curious Herbal, ba bʋɔn ni li nɛ ye "Love Apple (Amoris Pomum)" ban mɔri dit nɛ kpa'am nɛ vinegar Italy tɛŋin, li bʋʋdi wɛn wɔɔ ban dit gɔl UK siɛm la.
english: For example, in Elizabeth Blackwell's A Curious Herbal, it is described under the name "Love Apple (Amoris Pomum)" as being consumed with oil and vinegar in Italy, similar to consumption of cucumbers in the UK.

kusaal: Yʋm tʋsir kɔbʋsyʋɔbʋ nɛ pisyʋɔbʋ nɛ atan la, The New York Times dim da pa'al yʋ'ʋr kani an 'Love Apple' la gbin ka li an ye French dim pʋ yaŋi bʋɔl yʋ'ʋr la sʋm lin nar ye Itali pomo dei Mori ("the Moors' apple") ka ba lɛɛ bʋɔn ye pomme d'amour, ("love apple").
english: In 1963, The New York Times gave an explanation of the name 'Love Apple' as a French misreading of the Italian pomo dei Mori ("the Moors' apple") as pomme d'amour, ("apple of love").

kusaal: 18th century tɛŋsʋk ba da bʋdi li Carolina pɔɔdin nɛ zin'siɛba Southeast.
english: By the mid-18th century, they were cultivated on some Carolina plantations, and probably in other parts of the Southeast.

kusaal: Saŋkanɛ ka Alexander W. Livingston (yʋm tʋsir kɔbʋsnii nɛ pisi nɛ yinnɛ kiŋ paaɛ yʋm tʋsir Kɔbʋsnii nɛ piswai nɛ anii) da pin'li kʋɔd tamatoos bɛdigʋ la, ɔ da bɔɔdnɛ yɛ ɔ bʋd tamantoos ka li venl, ka zɛm, ka lɛm malis.
english: When Alexander W. Livingston (1821–1898) began developing the tomato as a commercial crop, he had aimed to grow tomatoes smooth in contour, uniform in size, and sweet in flavor.

kusaal: University of California, Davis C.M. Rick Tomato Generic Resource Center da mɔr nɛ tamantoos la bʋʋdi yinnɛ.
english: The University of California, Davis's C.M. Rick Tomato Genetics Resource Center maintains a gene bank of wild relatives, monogenic mutants and genetic stocks.

kusaal: Banɛ vɛɛnsid ban maan tamantoos siɛm bɛ California Tomato Research Institute Escalon, California da vɛɛsi li yela.
english: Research on processing tomatoes is also conducted by the California Tomato Research Institute in Escalon, California.

kusaal: California, kpaadib kʋɔdnɛ nɛ ʋʋn kʋɔb li kas kas anɛ linɛ ka ba bʋɔn ye Early Girl tomatoes la.
english: In California, growers have used a method of cultivation called dry-farming, especially with Early Girl tomatoes.

kusaal: Tamantoos la mɔr dɔlnɛ nɔr yinnɛ nɛ arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi wɛn wɔɔ Rhizophagus irregularis.
english: The tomato has a mutualistic relationship with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi such as Rhizophagus irregularis.

kusaal: Cultivar Heinz 1706 genome vʋgiri da sin'iŋnɛ dabis pistan nɛ yinnɛ nwadisa anʋ lani yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi.
english: The complete genome for the cultivar Heinz 1706 was published on 31 May 2012 in Nature.

kusaal: Nan'nan'na genome sin'iŋnɛ yʋma tʋsa ayi nɛ pisinɛ ayi mɔr 799 MB ka protein kanɛ ka ba bʋki baŋ an 34,384 ka li widigi paaɛ chromosome nam piinɛ ayi.
english: The latest reference genome published in 2021 had 799 MB and encodes 34,384 (predicted) proteins, spread over 12 chromosomes.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi ni (2022), tomatos da maal dunia wʋsa nɛ 186 million tonnes, ka linɛ da yi China an pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (37%), ka banɛ dɔl nya'aŋ an India, Turkey, nɛ United States ban mɛ an banɛ ti'ali bɛ tabul la zugin).
english: In 2023, world production of tomatoes was 192 million tonnes, led by China with 36% of the total, followed by India, Turkey, and the United States as secondary producers (table).

kusaal: Bʋnvʋya banɛ san'amid tomato si'eba anɛ tomato bug, stink bugs, cutworms, tomato hornworms nɛ tobacco hornworms, aphids, cabbage loopers, whiteflies, tomato fruitworms, flea beetles, red spider mite, Tuta absoluta (tomato leafminer), slugs, nɛ Colorado potato beetles.
english: Common tomato pests include the tomato bug, stink bugs, cutworms, tomato hornworms and tobacco hornworms, aphids, cabbage loopers, whiteflies, tomato fruitworms, flea beetles, red spider mite, Tuta absoluta (tomato leafminer), slugs, and Colorado potato beetles.

kusaal: Bacterial wilt mɛ anɛ ban'as kanɛ ka o yela pak hali linɛ kɛt ka ba pʋ wan titua nɛ.
english: Bacterial wilt is another common disease impacting yield.

kusaal: Tomatoes, ban malis ka lɛn an tɔlim-tɔlim la, ba mɔri li bɛ Mediterranean zin'is ni paasidi maan pizza nɛ pasta diib.
english: Tomatoes, with their umami flavor, are extensively used in Mediterranean cuisine as a key ingredient in pizza and many pasta sauces.

kusaal: Ba mɔr tomatoes maan si'elnam bɛdigʋ bɛ Spanish gazpacho nɛ Catalan pa amb tomàquet.
english: Tomatoes are used in Spanish gazpacho and Catalan pa amb tomàquet.

kusaal: Tomato anɛ bʋnlinɛ paas Middle East diib zin'is ni, ka ba dit nɛ salads (wan wʋʋ, Arab salad, Israeli salad, Shirazi salad nɛ Turkish salad), ka ba paasi li ni'imini sɛn'ɛd nɛ disi'eba ni.
english: The tomato is a crucial and ubiquitous part of Middle Eastern cuisine, served fresh in salads (e.g., Arab salad, Israeli salad, Shirazi salad and Turkish salad), grilled with kebabs and other dishes, made into sauces, and so on.

kusaal: Tomatoes paas Indian diib dʋgʋb pʋʋgin Europeans dimi da mɔri li kɛna la.
english: Tomatoes were gradually incorporated into Indian curry dishes after Europeans introduced them.

kusaal: Kashmiri diib, rogan josh, mɔr tomato li pʋʋgin; ba da ɛɛti nɔk nɛ nanzʋ'ʋ wiigi gɛndig ka li muoe, ka tomatoes paas Punjabi diib maalig pʋʋgin.
english: A Kashmiri curry, rogan josh, often contains tomato; it may originally have been colored red with chili pepper, and tomatoes may characterize the Punjabi version of the dish.

kusaal: Tomato kanɛ an kansir mɔr kuom piswai nɛ anu, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (95%), paŋ kanɛ bɛ li pʋʋgin an anaasi, kɔbiga pʋʋgin (4%), ka kpaam nɛ linɛ ka ba buon na'asaalin ye protein mɛ an 1%.
english: A raw tomato is 95% water, 4% carbohydrates, and less than 1% each of fat and protein (table).

kusaal: Lʋgir kanɛ gɔsid diib nɛ laafi yela ka ba buoni ba US Food and Drug Administration si'ak ye vɛɛnsig bi'ela bɛ pa'al ye diib banɛ ka ba nɔk tomato maal si'ed dindiig ban'as la.
english: The US Food and Drug Administration has determined there is little credible evidence that tomatoes or tomato-based foods reduce the risk of various types of cancer.

kusaal: Tomato paas nɛ nightshade buudi ni linɛ si'eba an taba, dankal, nɛ nansuos winlis.
english: The tomato is a member of the nightshade family that includes tobacco, potato, and chili peppers.

kusaal: Tomatoes mɔr bʋnvʋya bɛdigʋ nɛ zʋnzʋnya banɛ daamidi ba, ka mɛ mɔr ban'as banɛ yi virus nɛ kpaam-kpaamnam nɛ banɛ ɔnbid vaand la.
english: Tomatoes are also consumed as juice and in beverages such as the Bloody Mary cocktail.

kusaal: Tamantoos da yi tʋŋ si'a na anɛ mɔɔgin din, bʋnlinɛ da wan wiig Solanum pimpinellifolium, anɛ tiig kanɛ yit western South America, da'asi'erɛ anina ka ba mɔri kpɛn'ɛ yaan yiiga.
english: The likely wild ancestor of the tomato, the red-fruited Solanum pimpinellifolium, is native to western South America, namely Chile, Peru, and Ecuador.

kusaal: Spanish dim da mɔr tomatos nɛ kɛŋ Europe yiiga, anina ka ba mɔri maan Spanish diib.
english: The Spanish first introduced tomatoes to Europe, where they became used in Spanish food.

kusaal: Yʋʋm kanɛ ka ba da ti'aki li ka zii kpɛ'ɛ yaani yʋ'ʋn dit, ba pʋ baŋi li an wana vikii; yʋʋm 500 BC, ba da dɛŋin kuodi li bɛ southern Mexico nɛ zin'ig si'eba.
english: By 500 BCE, it was already being cultivated in southern Mexico and probably other areas.

kusaal: Ba bʋn bɛda, banɛ an lʋgalʋga ka pak la an saalig, linɛ ka ba tiig la an fiin la yinɛ America ninkʋda la sa'ana, ka tɔ'ɔn an tomato banɛ ka ba kuod zina la si'eba yaab.
english: The likely wild ancestor of the tomato, the red-fruited Solanum pimpinellifolium, is native to western South America, namely Chile, Peru, and Ecuador.

kusaal: Sahagún pa'al ye Aztecs dim dʋgʋd diib kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔb, ka mɔr ntoos kɔn'ɔbkɔn'ɔbi maan, kuosidi ba tɛnpʋʋgin da'an: "diib nam, di'tʋʋla; ...
english: Sahagún mentioned Aztecs cooking various sauces, some with tomatoes of different sizes, serving them in city markets: "foods sauces, hot sauces; ...

kusaal: Saŋkanɛ ka Spanish dim da sʋ'ʋg America la nya'aŋ, Spanish dim da pʋdʋgi ba tomato tis tɛɛns banɛ ka ba da sʋ'ʋg la wʋsa.
english: It originated from western South America, and may have been domesticated there, in Mexico, or in Central America. The Spanish introduced tomatoes to Eurasia in the Columbian exchange in the 16th century.

kusaal: Tamantɔos da pʋ bʋd England tɛŋ nii ti paaɛ Yʋm tʋsir kɔbʋsnʋ nɛ piswai saŋa.
english: Gerard's Herbal, published in 1597, and largely plagiarized from continental sources, is also one of the earliest discussions of the tomato in England.

kusaal: Gerard da mi yɛ Spain nɛ Italy dim dit tamantoos.
english: Gerard knew the tomato was eaten in Spain and Italy.

kusaal: Saŋa yiiga kanɛ ka ba tʋɔs tamantoos bʋdib yela British North America da anɛ yʋʋm tʋsir kɔbʋsyɔpɔi nɛ piiga, tinya'a dʋata William Salmon da nyɛ linɛ ka zina ka ba bʋɔn ye South Carolina la, Caribbean dimi da pa'ali li.
english: The earliest reference to tomatoes being grown in British North America is from 1710, when herbalist William Salmon saw them in what is today South Carolina, perhaps introduced from the Caribbean.

kusaal: America dim bɛdigʋ gɔs ka tamantoos anɛ yabid saŋkan la, bɛdigʋ da bʋdnɛ ka li maal venlim ka kai diibɔ.
english: Thomas Jefferson, who ate tomatoes in Paris, sent some seeds back to America. After 1860, it was often claimed that Americans believed that tomatoes were poisonous into the 1820s, but the belief was never widespread.

kusaal: Livingston tamantoos yiiga bʋʋdi da anɛ Paragon, li da sin'gnɛ yʋm tʋsir kɔbʋsnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi.
english: Livingston's first breed of tomato, the Paragon, was introduced in 1870.

kusaal: Yʋm tʋsir kɔbʋsnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anʋ la, ɔ da si'iŋ Acme, ka kpaadib bɛdigʋ bʋdi paaɛ yʋm pisinɛ anʋ.
english: In 1875, he introduced the Acme, said to be in the parentage of most cultivars for the next twenty-five years.

kusaal: Tamantoos bʋʋdi banɛ da paas da anɛ Henry Tilden lowa ne Dr.
english: Other early breeders included Henry Tilden in Iowa and a Dr. Hand in Baltimore.

kusaal: California, banɛ bɛ lanbaadin la da kʋɔd tamantoos tisid da'asin nɛ banɛ sʋʋd container namin.
english: In California, growers have used a method of cultivation called dry-farming, especially with Early Girl tomatoes.

kusaal: Tamantoos tɔ'ɔn maali li mɛŋ diib ka siɛl pʋ sʋŋi li la kɛ nɛ ka li bɛɛ li kɔ di ya'a ti paaɛ saŋa kanɛ ka sisi'ɛm naar yɛ li da'aɛ ka tiis mi'im bɛɛ cultured bumblebees.
english: That tomatoes pollinate themselves poorly without outside aid is clearly shown in greenhouse situations, where pollination must be aided by artificial wind, vibration of the plants, or by cultured bumblebees.

kusaal: Flower banɛ yi apical meristem la.
english: The flowers develop on the apical meristem.

kusaal: Li anther la pɔbilnɛ wɔɔ gɔŋnɛ gilig stigma la.
english: The anthers bend into a cone-like structure, surrounding the stigma.

kusaal: Li flower la anɛ 1-2cm (0.4-0.8 in) across, ka an dɔbʋ'ʋlʋg ka mɔr va'ad ka li tɔ zin'sa anʋ corolla la ni; ba bɛ nɛ cyme ka an zin'sa atan kiŋ paaɛ zin's piinɛ ayi la'as taaba.
english: The flowers are 1–2 cm (0.4–0.8 in) across, yellow, with five pointed lobes on the corolla; they are borne in a cyme of three to twelve together.

kusaal: Genetically modified food kanɛ ka ba maal yiiga kʋɔsid anɛ tamantoos ka ba bʋɔn Flavr Savr, ka ba gɔs ka li tɔn diginɛ yʋʋg.
english: The first commercially available genetically modified food was a tomato called Flavr Savr, which was engineered to have a longer shelf life.

kusaal: Dunia wʋsa da nɔk 4.8 million hectares yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yi (2012) tis tomato kuob ka lin da an si'em an 161.8 million tonnes.
english: In 2023, world production of tomatoes was 192 million tonnes, led by China with 36% of the total, followed by India, Turkey, and the United States as secondary producers (table).

kusaal: Tomato buudi bɛ kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb kati wa'ae ban na nyaŋi gu' ban'as yela.
english: Tomato plants can be toxic to dogs if they eat large amounts of the fruit, or chew plant material.

kusaal: Tomato ban'as yinnɛ anɛ tobacco mosaic virus.
english: A common tomato disease is tobacco mosaic virus.

kusaal: Wibɛ'ɛd hali anɛ curly top, ka bʋnlinɛ ziidi li an beet leafhopper, linɛ san'amidi li nɔbigir.
english: A serious disease is curly top, carried by the beet leafhopper, which interrupts the lifecycle.

kusaal: British diib kanɛ ka ba buon tikka masala tita'am mɔr tomato nɛ cream li pʋʋgin.
english: The modern British curry tikka masala often has a tomato and cream sauce.

kusaal: Wang et al., 2019 da nyɛ bʋnlinɛ kʋʋd bʋnvʋya ye li sʋŋi san'am bʋnvʋya la paŋ, sansi'eba anɛ li si'e bʋnvʋya la paŋ ka sansi'eba ka ba nyaŋi gaŋ banɛ tɔn'e wiim ka lɛɛ pʋ nɔbigid tɔ'ɔtɔ'ɔ.
english: Wang et al., 2019 found phage combination therapies to reduce the impact of bacterial wilt, sometimes by reducing bacterial abundance and sometimes by selecting for resistant but slow growing genetics.

kusaal: Ba nɔbigidnɛ ka mɔr ti'la ka lɛm mɔr ti'l tita'ar kanɛ nɔbigid.
english: They grow as a series of branching stems, with a terminal bud at the tip that does the actual growing.

kusaal: Trobu anɛ teŋ yinnɛ kanɛ naa pɛ'ɛs bɛ wada maanɛb zakin Gaana (Ghana) Teŋ la nidib wusa da la'as gaŋi ba wada maan pin'ilʋgʋn la sa.
english: Trobu is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Moses Anim yu'un an ba wada maan kpɛɛm bɛ wada maanɛb Zakin Ghana sɔlʋm.
english: She succeeded Moses Anim.

kusaal: On daa anɛ wabug (NPP) nid ka ba daa vɔɔt gaŋɔ.
english: She was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Trobu Teŋ sɔlʋm.
english: Trobu is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Trobu teŋa da pʋrʋg bɛ 2016.
english: Trobu is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi (1997) la ni ka ba da zaŋi li paas Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.
english: In 1997 it was designated an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.

kusaal: Di yiib zin'ig bɛnɛ Tsuchizaki Station (Ya-datiʋŋ baba kpi'e nɛ Akita Station).
english: The exit station is Tsuchizaki Station (north next of Akita Station).

kusaal: Tubaani, bԑԑ gͻnya anԑ Ghana diib yinnԑ kanԑ ka li yʋ'ʋr yi paalʋ ka ba diti li tita'am bԑ ya'datiʋŋ sʋ'ʋlim nԑ li tԑnkpԑmisin bԑ Ghana.
english: Tubaani, also referred to as steamed black-eyed peas' pudding, is a popular Ghanaian dish that is commonly eaten in the northern regions and Zongo communities of Ghana.

kusaal: Li tisid niŋgbina biim, iron, vitamin B9, nԑ fibre linԑ bԑ bԑŋa ni.
english: It contains proteins, iron, vitamin B9, and soluble fibre as it is made from beans.

kusaal: Tudu Mighty Jets anɛ Ghana bɔɔl nwɛ'ɛdib banɛ bɛ Accra, Greater Accra.
english: Tudu Mighty Jets are a Ghanaian professional football club, based in Accra, Greater Accra.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga nwadis piinɛ yinne daba anu daar, ba da nwɛ'ɛya nɛ Nanja F.C bɛ Poly Tank Division One League Zone III ka nyaŋi dʋ kpɛn' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne nɛ piinɛ ayi Glo Premier League nwɛ'ɛb la ni.
english: On 11 May 2010, the club won the play-offs against Nania F.C. in the Poly Tank Division One League Zone III play-offs and climbed into the 2010–11 season of the Glo Premier League.

kusaal: Ba da nya' yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi nɛ piinɛ atan Poly Tank Division One League ban da lɛbisi ba nya'aŋ yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne nɛ piinɛ ayi Glo Premier League nwɛ'ɛb saŋa la.
english: They are competing in the 2012–13 Poly Tank Division One League after being relegated at the end of the 2011–12 Glo Premier League season.

kusaal: Tumu anɛ tempʋbil ka an tempʋtita'ari tis Sissala East district, a district kanɛ bɛ Upper West Region sʋ'ʋlim Ghana Ya-datiʋŋ, ya'ad nɛ Burkina Faso titɔdig la.
english: Tumu is a small town and is the capital of Sissala East Municipal Assembly, a municipal in the Upper West Region of northern Ghana, adjacent to the border with Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Municipal la mɔr nidib kal nwɛnɛ tusa pisnii, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ piinɛ awai (80,619) ka dap an tusa pistan nɛ awai, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anii (39,868) ka pʋ'ab kal mɛ an tusa pisnaasi, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne (40,751) dɔlisid yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021) nidib nɛ ya kaalʋg la ni.
english: The Municipality has a population of 80,619, with 39,868 males and 40,751 females, according to 2021 population and housing census.

kusaal: Tumu an tempʋkanɛ kpi'e Gbele Resource Centre, dinɛ paasi anaasi labisim pʋʋgin Ghana zin'ivɛnlla pʋʋgin.
english: Tumu is the nearest town to Gbele Resource Centre, the fourth largest reserve in Ghana.

kusaal: Tempʋʋg la mɔrnɛ hotɛl yinne, ka ba buoni di ye Hill Top Hotel, ka mɔr gbɛɛnsa zin'is bɛdegʋ, ba sieba anɛ Gateway Travelers Lodge,nɛ saam gbɛɛnsa zin'is bɛdegʋ mɛn nwɛnɛ, Silti Guest House, nɛ diib zin'is.
english: The town has one hotel, Hill Top Hotel, a number of Lodges, Gateway Travelers Lodge, and a number of guest house, Silti Guest House, and restaurants..

kusaal: Nimbanɛ bɛ teŋin la tita'am anɛ Sissala nam.
english: The town consists mainly of the Sissala by tribe.

kusaal: Suoraʋg tita'ari tɔ'ɔŋ Tumu nɛ Navrongo tɛmpʋʋg.
english: Tumu is connected by road to the town of Navrongo.

kusaal: Tumu tempʋʋg la mɔr zin'ivɛnlla dɔlisid sʋ'ʋlim la nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ tempʋʋgin la, din yi Mu'a nɛ kɔldaad banɛ an zin'ibanɛ ka nidib la nyɛt ku'om ti paae sankanɛ ka Ghana Water Company dim da vɛ'ɛgi ba ku'osuoya paae tempʋʋg la zin'is wʋsa.
english: The Tumu town tourist site is based on the environment and the people within the town, starting from the rivers and dams (only) that serve as the main source of water to the nearby people until the Ghana Water Company Limited (GWC) extended their pipelines to almost all parts of the town.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Tunde Wey nɛ Lagos, Nigeria, ka o dʋ'adib sɔn'ɔe.
english: Tunde Wey was born in Lagos, Nigeria, to middle-class parents.

kusaal: Detroit tɛŋin, o da zamis nɛ community college yʋma ayuobʋ ka nyaan kpɛn'ɛ diib dʋgʋb ni.
english: In Detroit, he studied at a community college for six years before eventually pursuing his interest in cooking.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ atan' ni, Wey da yɔ'ɔg diib kuosig zin'ig, Revolver, zin'ig kanɛ ka o kuosid diib ka nidib kpɛn'ɛd ka yit, banɛ bɛ Detroit sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.
english: In 2013, Wey opened his first restaurant, Revolver, a venue that hosted pop-up dinners with chefs across the metropolitan Detroit area.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ awai la ni, o da kɛŋ United States ye o kɛŋ sakur anina.
english: In 1999, he immigrated to the United States to attend college.

kusaal: Diib kuosig zin'ig la da dʋgʋ li naar diib ka nyaan yɔ nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi, na'asaanwadis atan' ni, ka on nɛ onɛ sʋ'ʋe ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Peter Dalinowski, da yis labaar na ye ba ye ba yɔ' zin'ig la nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi ni, Sawaar nwadig la ni.
english: The restaurant hosted its final dinner in March 2020 and the co-owner, Peter Dalinowski, confirmed its official closure in October 2020.

kusaal: Twifo/Atti-Morkwa constituency bɛni Twifo/Atti-Morkwa District n bɛ Central Region Ghana nwa.
english: The Twifo/Atti-Morkwa constituency is located in the Twifo/Atti-Morkwa District of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Na'am kʋk la ya-datiuŋ gidiginɛ Upper Denkyira East Municipality ka ya-dagɔbʋg an Hemang Lower Denkyira District, ka ya-tuon an Mpohor Wassa East District, ka ya-nya'aŋ an Assin North Municipality nɛ Assin South District n bɛ Central Region Ghana nwa.
english: The seat is bounded on the north by the Upper Denkyira East Municipality on the south by the Hemang Lower Denkyira District, on the west by the Mpohor Wassa East District, and on the east by the Assin North Municipality and Assin South District of the Central Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Twifo-Atti Morkwa anɛ constituencies nam layinne ka mɔr wadmaan ka o zi'el tis ba bɛ wadmaanib yir la Ghana nwa.Ba vɔtʋg gaŋ wadmaan yinne ka an linɛ ka nidib la vɔɔt gaŋ nid yinne ma'a .
english: Twifo-Atti Morkwa is a constituency represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: United Ghana Movement anɛ pɔlitis na'adɔɔgʋ bɛ Ghana.
english: The United Ghana Movement is a political party in Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ pin'il na'adɔɔg la anɛ Charles Wereko-Brobby, onɛ da an Wabʋg na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party tuon gat.
english: The founder is Charles Wereko-Brobby, formerly a leading member of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Na'adɔɔg la da sɔbi di yʋ'ʋr nɛ Electoral Commission of Ghana ye di an pɔlitis na'adɔɔgʋ bɛ Ghana nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi yʋʋmpaal nwadig dabpiiga daar (10 January 1997).
english: The party was officially registered with the Electoral Commission of Ghana as a political party in Ghana on 10 January 1997.

kusaal: Charles Wereko-Brobby da zi'en na'adɔɔg la nɔba zugʋ nya' zuraan vɔɔt la yʋʋm tusa ayi nwadis piinɛ ayi la ni (December 2000) ka da paasi ayɔpɔi daan nɛ vɔɔt nɛɛm du'ali atan kɔbiga pʋʋgin (0.3%).
english: Charles Wereko-Brobby stood for president on the party's ticket in December 2000 and came seventh with 0.3% of the popular vote.

kusaal: · Symbol - A clenched fist of the hand with the index and middle fingers raised together.
english: Symbol - A clenched fist of the hand with the index and middle fingers raised together.

kusaal: Yiiga vɔɔtkanɛ ka na'adɔɔg la nya' zuraannam nɛ wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg ni anɛ vɔɔtkanɛ da maal yʋʋm tusa ayin wadis piinɛ ayi la ni (December 2000).
english: The first general elections the party contested were the presidential and parliamentary elections of December 2000.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayi la (2002) ni, Na'adɔɔg la tuon gat, Wereko-Brobby da mɔɔl ye na'adɔɔg la nan vʋ'ʋsidnɛ.
english: In 2002, the leader of the party, Wereko-Brobby announced that the party is on vacation.

kusaal: · Pian'akpan – Kɛt ka nidib nɔbʋgʋd Ghana maalʋg yɛla.
english: Motto - Growing people for Ghana's development.

kusaal: Ba nyan'adi bɛ nɛ Brong Ahafo Division Two Zone 9.
english: They are competing in the Brong Ahafo Division Two Zone 9.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛtan', Mɔraʋg nwadig la ni (July 2013) club la kpɛɛmnam da voot ya ye ba ti'aki li yʋ'ʋr la lɛbis Wenchi Sporting Club, nwa' da anɛ ye li kɛ ka Nimbanɛ bɛ Wenchi la baŋ ye ba paasi li pʋʋgin.
english: In July 2013 the club executives voted to change the name to Wenchi Sporting Club, a move which was aimed at getting the people to Wenchi to have a sense of belonging to the club.

kusaal: Ernest Anokye-Gyan, o da nyɛ sʋŋiri yi Unity Community & Sport Association nɛ Unity Football Club, linɛ bɛ Reading ka Berkshire, England ye li sʋŋi maal suor ka bibaanlig zamis football baŋir.
english: The club was founded in 2007 by the club's president Mr. Ernest Anokye-Gyan with support from Unity Community & Sport Association and Unity Football Club, of Reading in Berkshire, England to promote safe ground for young athletes to develop their football skills.

kusaal: Ba da nwɛn'ɛ Division Two League "Third tier of Ghana Football Leagues" 2010/2011 nwɛn'ɛb yʋʋŋ la.
english: The club played in the Division Two League "Third tier of Ghana Football Leagues" for the Season 2010/2011.

kusaal: Unity Academy anɛ Centre of Sporting Excellence ka banɛ sʋ'ʋe li an Unity Sporting Club ban nɛ UCSEF.
english: Unity Academy is a Centre of Sporting Excellence run by Unity Sporting Club in association with UCSEF.

kusaal: Sakur la mɔr na'asaasɔɔng zin'ig ka ba buon computer centre, ka banɛ gɔsidi li yela an Enterprise FI Solution.
english: The academy has a computer centre powered by Enterprise FI Solution.

kusaal: Basam kɔbiga nɛ pisnu (150 boys) lin yi yʋma atan' paae pisi nɛ yinnɛ bɛ sakur la ni.
english: 150 boys aged 3–21 years, are currently enrolled.

kusaal: UNITY ACADEMY anɛ suor kanɛ ka ba dɔlisidi paamid biis ka ti'akidi ba ka ba an ban nar ye ba an si'em dɔlisid sʋŋidib banɛ bɛ tɛŋin la nɛ tɛŋ si'eba.
english: UNITY ACADEMY is pioneering in its approach to pastoral care through sport, working collectively with local and international organisations to attain the overall objective of better welfare for local children.

kusaal: Augustine Catholic School nɛ Koase Secondary School.
english: The academy is in partnership with local nursery, primary and secondary schools such as St. Augustine Catholic School and Koase Secondary School.

kusaal: Ba mɛ lɛn mɔri li zamisig sakur ka bibaanlig kɔbiga nɛ pisnu zamisid anina, lin yi yʋʋm piiga paae yʋʋm pisi nɛ yinnɛ pʋʋgin (10 – 21 years), ka ba yelkpan anɛ ban na zamis bibaanlig la ka ba baŋir nɔbig.
english: The club also operates a sports academy which currently has 150 youngsters between the ages of 10 – 21 years, focusing on the education and development of young athletes.

kusaal: Unity Sporting Club nɔknɛ football nwɛn'ɛb ka li an bʋnkanɛ ka ba nyaŋi vaae biisi pa'ani ba, baa bibanɛ nan zi' zamisi li baa bi'elaa.
english: Unity Sporting Club uses football as a tool to engage a large pool of street children on a regular basis who traditionally have little access to sporting activities.

kusaal: Sakur nwa' bɔɔdim anɛ ye ba pa'al biis la ka ba an banɛ ka ba na nyaŋi ti'aki ba, ba football nwɛn'ɛb pʋʋgin, ka dɔlisid zamis banɛ bɛɛ li kɔn' paani ba nɛ di'ema ka kpɛmisidi ba nɛ piini.
english: The academy then aims to develop children's ability to be coached, both on and off the football pitch, with the aim of empowering them through a programme of non-formal education which is complemented by a fun and goal oriented rewards.

kusaal: Ban bɔɔd ye ba kpɛmisi ba la zug, club la paasi ba mɛŋ Ghana Division Two League ni.
english: In other to keep the current players active the club has registered to play in Ghana Division Two League.

kusaal: nwa' na kɛ ka nwɛn'ɛd-nwɛn'ɛd baanlig zamisi bɛ Unity Academy.
english: This will also provide experience for the young players the Unity Academy.

kusaal: Bi'esig kae ye nwa' da kɛ ka Nidib nini nie nya'ab yela bɛ Ghana National League.
english: This in no doubt increased and promoted healthy competition in the Ghana National League.

kusaal: Sakur la bɛnɛ Wenchi linɛ bɛ Brong Ahafo, zin'ig kanɛ bɛ tɛnkpɛŋ ka lɛɛ paas Brong Ahafo region, Ghana.
english: The centre is based in Wenchi in the Brong Ahafo, a deprived area of Brong Ahafo region, Ghana.

kusaal: Sakur la la'asi li mɛŋ nɛ nursery, primary nɛ secondary schools banɛ bɛ tɛŋin la, ka ba si'eba an St.
english: The academy is in partnership with local nursery, primary and secondary schools such as St. Augustine Catholic School and Koase Secondary School.

english: Established in 1992 by the Government of Ghana, its purpose is to accelerate the development of Ghana's north, and the broader nation.

kusaal: Tudu sʋ'ʋlim la anɛ bama, Northern Region, Upper East Region nɛ Upper West Region.
english: These are the Brong Ahafo Region, Northern Region, Upper East Region and the Upper West Region.

kusaal: Wada ka nɛ digi tis sour ye sakur nwa zi'elim la anɛ PNDC Law 279.
english: The legislative instrument that founded the university is PNDC Law 279, which was gazetted on May 15, 1992, but recently repealed to UDS Act, 2025(Act 1134).

kusaal: UDS linɛ paas sakur, university nama anu kanɛ ka Ghana Government zi'el la anɛ ayi, Nyankpala nɛ Dungu, temisin Tamale.
english: The university has two main campuses: Nyankpala and Dungu in Tamale.

kusaal: Sakur la mɔr Central Administration, School of Medicine (SoM), School of Allied Health Sciences (SAHS), School of Nursing and Midwifery (SoNM), School of Public Health (SPH) and Faculty of Education (FoE) nɛ Desert Research Institute (DRI).
english: The campus houses the Central Administration, School of Medicine (SoM), School of Allied Health Sciences (SAHS), School of Nursing and Midwifery (SoNM), School of Public Health (SPH) and Faculty of Education (FoE) and Desert Research Institute (DRI).

kusaal: Nɛ'ɛnamɛ bɛ Nyankpala sakurin la: Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Consumer Sciences (FoAFCS), Faculty of Natural Resources and Environment (FNRE), Faculty of Biosciences (FBO), School of Engineering (FOE), West African Centre for Water,irrigation and Sustainable Agriculture (WACWISA)and West African Centre for Sustainable Rural Transportation (WAC-SRT)
english: The following are located at Nyankpala Campus: Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Consumer Sciences (FoAFCS), Faculty of Natural Resources and Environment (FNRE), Faculty of Biosciences (FoB), School of Engineering (SoE), Faculty of Physical Science (FOPS), Faculty of Communication and Media Studies (FCMS), Faculty of Social Sciences (FOSS), School Economics (SoEc), School of Veterinary Sciences (SoVS), West African Centre for Water, Irrigation and Sustainable Agriculture (WACWISA) and West African Centre for Sustainable Rural Transformation (WAC-SRT).

kusaal: Sakur la anɛ zin' kanɛ k aba pa'an School of Applied Economics and Management Sciences (SAEMS).
english: The Campus is site for School of Applied Economics and Management Sciences (SAEMS).

kusaal: Eastern Campus la anɛ zin' kanɛ k aba pa'an Communication and Cultural Studies (FCCS) nɛ Faculty of Sustainable Devvelopment Studies (FoSDS), Centre for Culture,Heritage and African Studies (CCHAS) nɛ Centre for Peace and Security Studies (CePSS)
english: Eastern Campus is a site for Faculty of Communication and Cultural Studies (FCCS) and Faculty of Sustainable Development Studies (FoSDS), Centre for Culture, Heritage and African Studies (CCHAS) and Centre for Peace and Security Studies (CePSS).

english: The University for Development Studies (UDS) is a public university located in Tamale, in the Northern Region of Ghana.

english: Tamale City Campus is a centre for the following: School of Business, Graduate School, Institute of Interdisciplinary Research (IIR), Institute of Distance and Continuing Education (IDCE), Colleges of Education Affiliation and Business Innovation and Incubation Centre (BIIC).

kusaal: Zamisʋg la yʋʋm pʋʋgin pʋdigir atan' ni la, Third Trimester Practical Programme (TTFPP) saŋa la wʋsa, ba ye ken nɛ ten-bibisinɛ tʋm linɛ k aba zamis sakurin la.
english: For the Third Trimester Practical Programme (TTFPP) the whole of the third trimester is devoted to practical field work in the local communities.

kusaal: Tʋʋm kaŋa da pin'il nɛ yʋʋ tusur yinne, kɔbɔs wai nɛ piswai nɛ atan' (1993) la ni li anɛ zamisʋg kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb kanɛ bɛ sakurin la ka ba ye gaŋi la'as k aba tʋmi li; Agriculture, Integrated Development Studies, Applied Science and the School of Medicine and Health Sciences.
english: It entails the combination of students from all the faculties: Agriculture, Integrated Development Studies; Applied Science, Engineering, Business, Economics, Medicine, Allied Health Sciences etc.

kusaal: campus la mɔr nɛ buʋŋfɔɔlig ka nɛ li mɛt bɛ kʋkɔg zug nɛ li kpa'ad Atlantic Ocean.
english: The campus has a rare seafront view and sits on a hill overlooking the Atlantic Ocean.

kusaal: Zin'ig kʋda ayi banɛ an yɛlkpanna bɛ Ghana nwa, Elmina nɛ Cape Coast Castle linɛ pʋ lal nɛ sakur laa.
english: Two of the most important historical sites in Ghana, Elmina and Cape Coast Castle, are a few kilometres away from its campus.

kusaal: Yʋʋma tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi(1972), college la da paam suor ka nɛ ba an university kanɛ sʋ'oe ba mɛŋ, nɛ paŋ kanɛ ka ba na nyaŋ tis ba mɛŋ degrees, diplomas nɛ certificates by an Act of Parliament.
english: In 1972, the college attained the status of a full and independent university, with the authority to confer its own degrees, diplomas and certificates by an Act of Parliament.

kusaal: UCC banɛ naae la sieba anɛ Ministers of State, High Commissioners, CEOs, wadmaanib, nɛ Ghana yiiga pʋ'a kanɛ an gɔmma nya'aŋ dɔl la.
english: UCC graduates include Ministers of State, High Commissioners, CEOs, Members of Parliament, and Ghana's first female vice president.

kusaal: University of Cape Coast da sɛŋnɛ October nwadig la yʋʋma tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ pisyɔbʋ nɛ ayi(1962) ka li an university college ka nɛ li kpinim si'ɛr nɛ University of Ghana, Legon.
english: The University of Cape Coast was established in October 1962 as a university college and placed in a special relationship with the University of Ghana, Legon.

kusaal: October nwadig la dabisir yinne, yʋʋma tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ piisyɔpɔi nɛ yinne ni (1971), ka college la paam ba mɛŋ ya'a ka sʋ'oe ba mɛŋ na nyaŋid tis ba mɛŋ degrees, diplomas nɛ and certificates dɔlisid Act of Parliament.
english: On 1 October 1971, the college attained the status of a full and independent University, with the authority to confer its own degrees, diplomas and certificates by an Act of Parliament.

kusaal: Di sɛŋir ni ba nɔkir sakurbiis kanl wʋʋ kɔbʋ-yinne nɛ piis-nu nɛ anu yʋʋma tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ pisyɔbʋ nɛ atan' la saŋa(1963), University of Cape Coast nanana mɔr sakurbiis kanl wʋʋ tusa kɔbis-nii(80,000)
english: From an initial student enrollment of 155 in 1963, the University of Cape Coast now has a total student population of about 80,000.

kusaal: Dinɛ na kɛ ka ba nyaŋid paam dinɛ ka ba bɔɔd, yʋʋma tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ pisyɔbʋ nɛ anaasi la ni (1964), university da pa'as Faculties nam ayi, linɛ an: Education nɛ Economics & Social Studies [nanana an Faculty of Social Sciences].
english: In order to achieve the set objectives, in 1964, the university created two more Faculties, namely: Education and Economics & Social Studies [now Faculty of Social Sciences].

kusaal: faculty kanɛ pa'as anu [School of Agriculture] da sɛŋ nɛ yʋʋma tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu la ni (1975).
english: The fifth faculty [School of Agriculture] was established in 1975.

kusaal: Ka Faculty of Science da pʋdig nɛ zin'is ayi Schools of Physical nɛ Biological Sciences linɛ da an yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayi/yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan' (2002/2003) gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yʋʋm ni, ka Business Studies wɛlʋg la mɛ tɔlis lɛbig School of Business sɛŋ tʋʋma din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ atan' / yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anaasi (2003)/(2004) gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yʋʋm la.
english: The Faculty of Science was split into the Schools of Physical and Biological Sciences during the 2002←/2003 academic year while the Department of Business Studies was also elevated to the School of Business with effect from the 2003/2004 academic year.

kusaal: Ka Medical School nɛ faculty of Law nɛ sieba banɛ bɛ mɛ nɔki pa'as.
english: The Medical School and faculty of Law among others have been added.

kusaal: Campus kʋdʋg la mɛ lɛm buon ye Ya-dagɔbʋg Campus la bɛnɛ kʋkɔng zug, lalli atɛʋk bien, li bɛnɛ Apewosika nɛ Kokoado teŋbibis bɛ Cape Coast metropolis.
english: The Old Site Campus also known as the Southern Campus is located on high grounds, above the sea level, within the Apewosika and Kokoado communities in the Cape Coast metropolis.

kusaal: Campus la da an gbɛɛnsid tis University's Old Central Administration, dina ma'aa da an gbɛɛnsid zin'ig tis bipʋmis, Adehye Hall, Atlantic Hall, Oguaa Hall, nɛ University laafi zin'ig, kanɛ da gɔsi sakurbiis la laafi yɛla sʋŋa nɛ yiiŋ dim la bɛnɛ ani.
english: The Campus houses the university's Old Central Administration, the only female hall of residence, the Adehye Hall, the Atlantic Hall, Oguaa Hall, and University Hospital, which provides quality health service to the student population and the general public is located in here.

kusaal: Vocational nɛ Technical Educational (VOTEC) wɛlʋg la bɛnɛ campus kʋdʋgin la.
english: The Department of Vocational and Technical Educational (VOTEC) is located at the old site campus.

kusaal: Campus paal bɛɛ Ya-datiʋŋ Campus, ka bɛdigʋ mi'i ye "Science" anɛ kilomɛta zaad bʋn kʋdʋg la lam nɛ Kwaprow nɛ Amamoma teŋbibis la.
english: New Site Campus or Northern Campus, popularly known as "Science" is within a kilometer distance from Old Site is located near the Kwaprow and Amamoma communities.

kusaal: Li bɛnɛ zin'ikanɛ ka Science Complex mɛɛb la ka bɛdigʋ mi'i li yʋ'ʋr ye "Science".
english: It is the location of the Science Complex Building therefore the popular name "Science".

kusaal: University lɔmbɔn'ɔg nɛ University Zoo la wʋsa bɛnɛ university la campus paal la bɛ zin'isi'ɛr la.
english: University Garden and the University Zoo are also located in the New Site Campus of the university.

kusaal: Li da pin'il nɔ'asid sakurbiis kɔbʋg yinne nɛ pis-nu nɛ anu (155) yʋʋma tusa pii nɛ awai nɛ pisyɔbʋ nɛ atan', (1963) University of Cape Coast nanana mɔr sakurbiis wʋsa ka li an kanl tusa kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ anaasi pa'as nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piisi (74,720).
english: From an initial student enrolment of 155 in 1963, the University of Cape Coast now has a total student population of 74,720.

kusaal: Iinɛ pʋr si'ɛm mɛ awa: tusa kɔbis pii nɛ anii nɛ kɔbis awai du'al pisnaasi nɛ awai (18,949) an regular undergraduate students, 1445 an sandwich undergraduate students, 1014 an regular postgraduate students, 2773 an sandwich postgraduate students, 48,989 an distance undergraduate students, ka 1540 an postgraduate distance students.
english: The breakdown is as follows: 18,949 regular undergraduate students, 1445 sandwich undergraduate students, 1014 regular postgraduate students, 2773 sandwich postgraduate students, 48,989 distance undergraduate students, and 1540 postgraduate distance students.

kusaal: university la nɔk kanl ka li wʋsa duoe 24,723 sakurbiis ba zamisʋg zin'is kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayɔbʋg /yʋʋma tusa pii nɛ ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi zamisʋg yʋʋm la ni.
english: The university admitted a total of 24,723 students into its various programs for the 2016/2017 academic year.

kusaal: Nanana nwa, sakur la mɔr biis kanl 78,485, ka 41,165 (52.40%) an dab, ka 37,320 (47.60%) mɛ an pʋ'ab kanl la pʋʋg, ka kanl la wʋsa duoe 2,765 bɛdigʋ gat banɛ da mɔr si'em yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayɔbʋg /yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yʋʋm la ni (2016/2017).
english: Currently, the school has a student population of 78,485 with 41,165 (52.40%) male and 37,320 (47.60%) female student population, which in total is exactly 2,765 more than what they had in the 2016/2017 academic year.

kusaal: Sakurbiis la kanl nɛ pʋr si'em nwa bɛ yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pis-yi nɛ ayi/yʋʋma tusa ayi nɛ pis-yi nɛ atan' (2022/2023) gbaʋŋ zamisʋg yʋʋm la dɔl si'em nwa: ba da mɔr nidib awai (9) ka ba an sandwich students, bam ma'aa da maan certificate bɛ ba programs kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb la ni, ka bani ayi (2)da an dab ka ayɔpɔi(7) la an pʋ'ab.
english: The breakdown of the student population in the 2022/2023 academic year is as follows: there have 9 sandwich students who are the only ones offering certificate in their various programs with 2 of them being males and 7 females.

kusaal: Ka tɔt nɛ Burkina Faso Gaana tuon, Togo Gaana dagɔbʋg, Wa sʋ'ʋlim li datiʋŋ ka Tamar sʋ'ʋlim bɛɛ li nya'aŋ.
