kusaal: Zin'ig da paami yi Upper Region sankan la, dinɛ yʋ'ʋn an Upper East Region nanna la.
english: The area was carved out of the former Upper Region, which is now the Upper East Region.

kusaal: Wɔɔ yʋma pistan' nɛ anu nwa, di anɛ region bil ti Ghana kpɛ' ti paae yʋʋm 2018 la ni dinɛ ka region nam ayuobʋ da paami pɛ'ɛs ka di yinɛ Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo yʋʋm lag ni; kɛt ka region nam la kanl yʋ'ʋn an piinɛ ayuobʋ.
english: For about thirty-five years, it remained the youngest region of Ghana until 2018 when six more regions were created by the Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo government; hence increasing the total number of administrative regions in the country to sixteen.

kusaal: Upper West Region anɛ region piiga nɛ ayuobu banɛ bɛ Ghana a yinne.
english: The Upper West Region is a region of Ghana located in the northwestern corner of the country.

kusaal: Ghana-Burkina Faso datiŋ nwa ya'ya'aŋ anɛ Upper East region nɛ Northern regions, ka li dagɔbʋg an Northern region, ka li Ya-tuona an western Ghana-Burkina Faso.
english: The northern Ghana-Burkina Faso is bordered on the east by the Upper East region and Northern regions, on the south by the Northern region, on the west by western Ghana-Burkina Faso, and the Upper West region on the north.

kusaal: Linɛ paas regions nam ayɔpɔi zu'oe gaadi ba taaba Ghana sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa, ka li mɔr districts piiga nɛ yinne.
english: It is the seventh largest region in Ghana in total area, and it is made up of 11 districts.

kusaal: Lin bɛi zin'ig sia la kɛ ka Upper West Region mɔr da' diib nɛ tɛŋ banɛ kpie ba ka ka' Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka mɔr nɔɔr naalig nɛ tɛŋ sieba, amaa nimbɛ'ɛdnam tʋʋma nɛ wina'am tʋʋm sieba linɛ nwɛnɛ mɔɔg bugum nyɔ'ɔb, wiim nam nɛ daamug sieba nam, mɔr zaba la'adi fan'ad nidib nɛ yɛla bɛdego banɛ bɛ tɛŋ banɛ kpie ba la anɛ daamʋgʋ tisi ba.
english: The Upper West Region is one of the 16 regions of Ghana.

kusaal: Upper West Region da'adiib nɛ ba tʋʋma anɛ kpaadib (agriculture).
english: The major economic activity of the Upper West Region is agriculture.

kusaal: Ba bʋnbʋtta sieba anɛ corn, millet, peanuts, okra, shea tree, nɛ rice.
english: Crops grown include corn, millet, peanuts, okra, shea tree, and rice.

kusaal: Region la tʋmmi li tʋʋma dɔl local government system.
english: The political administration of the region is through the local government system.

kusaal: Girimadaan Ursula Owusu-Ekuful (du'anɛ 20 October 1964) yinɛ Akim Oda bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Ghana la.
english: Ursula Owusu-Ekuful (born 20 October 1964) is a Ghanaian lawyer, women's rights activist, and a politician who has been actively involved in politics and public service.

kusaal: Ursula yinɛ Akim Oda bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim bɛ Ghana la.
english: Ursula hails from Akim Oda in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

kusaal: o da keŋ Labone Senior High School ka tɔlisi keŋ Mfantisman Girls Secondary School maali o sixth form education.
english: She attended Labone Senior High School and proceeded to Mfantsiman Girls Secondary School for sixth-form education.

kusaal: O da lɛn tɔlisi keŋ University of Ghana nɛ Ghana School Of Law, ani ka o da di'e LLB kasɛta gbaʋŋ.
english: She continued to the University of Ghana and the Ghana School of Law, where she obtained an LL.B..

kusaal: O da maal master's degree in Conflict, Peace and Security, Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre la ni.
english: She obtained a master's degree in Conflict, Peace, and Security from the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre.

kusaal: O da tʋm lɔya tʋʋma yʋʋm piiga tis Akufo-Addo, Prempeh & Co.
english: She worked for 10 years as a lawyer at the Akufo-Addo, Prempeh & Co. law firm before moving into the telecommunication industry to lead a telecom technology company.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ anu la ni, 2015, o da nyi'a Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, NPP Na'am la Ablekuma West Constituency ka di.
english: In 2015, she contested and won the NPP parliamentary primaries in the Ablekuma West Constituency.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayɔpɔi (2017), Pirɛsidɛn Akufo-Addo da gaŋ o ye o an minista tis lʋgʋr kanɛ gɔsid pian'ad nɛ Na'asaasɔɔng yɛla..
english: She was reported as saying that she was considering her future in politics but in 2017, she was appointed the Minister of Communications and digitalization by President Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisyi Nwadis piinɛ ayi vɔɔtʋgin (December 2020), o da nya' ya ye ba lɛn vɔɔt o ka o an Wadmaan yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi 2020 Ghana dim wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: In December 2020, she contested the re-election as a member of Parliament.

kusaal: Vɔɔt la da paae la, ba da lɛn vɔɔt o ya'as ye o an Wadmaani tisi Ablekuma West Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim, o da lɛn di o kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan nɛ ayɔpɔi, kɔbistan nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan (37,363) yi vɔɔt tusa pisyubʋ nɛ awai, kɔbistan nɛ pisnu nɛ atan (69,353).
english: Going into the election as the incumbent Member of Parliament of the Ablekuma West (Ghana Parliament) constituency, she retained her seat after polling 37,363 out of 69,353 votes.

kusaal: Onɛ da pʋ lal nɛ o, Kweku Addo onɛ an Ma'asim tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) nid la da paasi ayi nɛ vɔɔt tusa pistan, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pistan nɛ atan (30,733), ka Na'adɔbanɛ kpɛlim la, GUM, LPG nɛ PNC nidib paam kɔbistan nɛ pisnu nɛ awai (359), kɔbistan nɛ pistan (330) nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anu (65) nwɛnɛ ba yʋda la dɔl taaba si'em la.
english: Her closest competitor, Rev. Kweku Addo of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), was second with 30,733 votes, while the other candidates who contested from the other parties, GUM, LPG, and PNC, polled 359, 330, and 65, respectively.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii Nwadsaanaasi la ni (April 2018) Gaana dim bɛdigʋ da tʋ'ʋ o hali nɛ on da pʋdʋg pian'azug kanɛ pa'al ye Gaana mɔɔm anɛ tʋbpʋwʋnnim dim la.
english: In April 2018, she suffered a backlash from a section of the Ghanaian community when she made headlines for sharing a post on social media that suggested Ghanaian Muslims were intolerant.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne Nwadisa anu la ni, May 2021, o da sa'al banɛ tʋm tʋʋmkan LGBT+ bɛ Ghana la ye ba su'am tʋm ka Ghana dim kʋ siaki di'e daʋ dig nɛ daʋ ka pʋ'a mɛ dig nɛ pʋ'aa.
english: She also, in May 2021, advised LGBT+ individuals in Ghana to keep their activities private as Ghanaians were unable to accept same-sex relations.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai (2019) la nii, International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) da nyɛ on zabidi tisid pʋ'ab nɛ biis bɛlim yɛla si'em la da tisi o piini yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ awai la (2019) FIDA Africa Regional Congress la'askanɛ ka ba da maal Abuja, Nigeria la.
english: In February 2019 she was honoured by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) in recognition of her work in the protection of the rights of women and children at the 2019 FIDA Africa Regional Congress held in Abuja, Nigeria.

kusaal: O anɛ lɔya onɛ zabid tisid pʋ'ab, ka an Ghana Wadmaani tis Ablekuma West constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: Going into the election as the incumbent Member of Parliament of the Ablekuma West (Ghana Parliament) constituency, she retained her seat after polling 37,363 out of 69,353 votes.

kusaal: Nannanna, onɛ an Minista onɛ gɔsid pian'ad nɛ Na'asaasɔɔng yɛla (Communications and Digitalisation).
english: She is the former member of Parliament for Ablekuma West Constituency in the Greater Accra Region and former Minister of Communications and Digitalisation.

kusaal: · Pirɛsidɛn nya'adɔl kʋdʋgʋ tis Africa Regional FIDA International.
english: In February 2019 she was honoured by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) in recognition of her work in the protection of the rights of women and children at the 2019 FIDA Africa Regional Congress held in Abuja, Nigeria.

kusaal: · O da paas African Women Lawyers Association (AWLA)
english: In February 2019 she was honoured by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) in recognition of her work in the protection of the rights of women and children at the 2019 FIDA Africa Regional Congress held in Abuja, Nigeria.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ piinɛ ayi la ni, ba da vɔɔt gaŋ o ka o lieb Wadmaani tis, Ablekuma West Constituency sʋ'ʋlim dim.
english: In 2012, Ursula Owusu-Ekuful was elected as the first Member of Parliament for the newly created Ablekuma West Constituency.

kusaal: Ka o da yɛl ye on gɔsidnɛ o pɔlitks bɛʋg yɛla, ka yʋʋmkanɛ dɔl la ka o da lieb minista kanɛ gɔsid pian'ad yɛla (Communications).
english: She was reported as saying that she was considering her future in politics but in 2017, she was appointed the Minister of Communications and digitalization by President Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii, Nwadisa awai la dab pisi nɛ awai daari da an Sibit daar la, Akem Asuom bɛ Eastern Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la da diis o Na'am, Asuomhene Osabarima Ofosuhene Apenteng II yin ka pʋd o ye Nkosuohemaa (Temmaalʋg Pʋ'ana'ab).
english: The installment took place at the Palace of Asuomhene, Osabarima Ofosuhene Apenteng II.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne (2021), Ghana daʋ digin nɛ daʋ ka pʋ'a mɛ digin nɛ pʋ'a Ghanaian anti-LGBT bill wada gbaʋŋ la da yinɛ la, o da zɛrigi di zin'sieba ye di bɔɔd ye di kena ka nidib mɔr gbannya'am ka an ziri dim ka ba maligim gɔsi di yɛla.
english: In July 2023, during the second reading of the Promotion of Proper Human Sexual Rights and Ghanaian Family Values Bill 2021, also known as the Ghanaian anti-LGBT bill, in parliament, she had a rebuttal with Hon. Murtala Mohammed when he made claims of her being an LGBTQ+ individual.

kusaal: O ɛlnɛ Ghana ninkanɛ bɛ UK an nini Du'ata Duata Sam Ekufu.
english: Hon. Ursula Owusu-Ekuful, born by Christiana Akua Birago Diawo, is married with three children to the UK-based Ghanaian optometrist, Dr. Sam Ekuful.

kusaal: O da lieb gɔmena lɔya nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai (1990) la ni.
english: She was called to the bar in 1990.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ vɔɔtʋgin la,o da lɛn di kʋk la nɛ vɔɔt kal tusa pistan' nɛ anaassi nɛ kɔbistan nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (34,3760 yit vɔɔt la tusa pisyuobʋ nɛ kɔbisnu nɛ pisnu nɛ anii (60,558) dinɛ an pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ du'al piswai nɛ ayuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (56.96%).
english: She proceeded to retain her parliamentary seat during the 2016 Ghanaian general elections by winning with 34,376 votes out of the 60,558 valid votes cast, making 56.96%.

kusaal: Ba nya'ad nɛ Ebusua Dwarfs.
english: They have a local rivalry with Ebusua Dwarfs.

kusaal: Venomous Vipers paas clubs banɛ yʋʋg Ghana sʋ'ʋlim ka ba da kaanbi buoli ba ye ba kɛna gɔs ban da zʋŋid national league yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛe pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ ni la (1956).
english: The Venomous Vipers are one of the oldest clubs in Ghana and were invited to participate in the inaugural national league in 1956.

kusaal: Ba da paasi nwɛn'ɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nam saŋa di'ema (1960s) ka ba nwɛn'ɛd-nwɛn'ɛdib tuongatib yinnɛ da an Robert Takyi.
english: They participated at the national level on and off during the 1960s and were led by players such as Robert Takyi.

kusaal: Ba da tɔlis club la tuon ye ba paasi nya'a Ghana's Division One di'ema nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ yɔpɔi ni (2017).
english: The club was promoted to Ghana's Division One in 2017.

kusaal: Venomous Vipers da lɛb nya'aŋ yʋʋm tusair, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai ni (1990).
english: The Venomous Vipers were relegated from the top flight in 1990.

kusaal: Ba da maligim duoe kpɛɛmnam banɛ gɔsidi li yela la tʋʋma nɛ yʋʋm tusayi nɛ piinɛ anaasi ni (2014).
english: The club's management board was restructured in 2014.

kusaal: Victor Ekpuk (ka ba dʋ'a o yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiwasi nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi, 1964) anɛ onɛ ka ba dʋ'a o Nigeria ka o lɛɛ an di'em-di'em bɛ Washington, DC.
english: Victor Ekpuk (born 1964) is a Nigerian-born artist from Uyo in Akwa Ibom State.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ awai la ni, Victor da di'e o Bachelor of Fine Art degree (BFA), yi Obafemi Awolowo University, Ife, Nigeria, zin'ikanɛ ka o da zamis vɛnllim kanɛ bɛ Nsibidi gban'ar ni la.
english: In 1989 Victor received his Bachelor of Fine Art degree (BFA), Obafemi Awolowo University, Ife, Nigeria, where he first explored the aesthetic philosophies of Nsibidi.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi (2017) la ni ka daʋŋ kanɛ an Diaspora Quarterly, Visual Collaborative sɔbi bɛ Ekpuk's tʋʋmkanɛ ka o da maal zaŋi ken Africa la'ad yɛla la.
english: In a 2017 issue of Diaspora Quarterly, Visual Collaborative cited Ekpuk's work on the heritage of Africa art.

kusaal: Ekpuk da naal DTN an onɛ nɛɛsid si'elnami pa'an din yi yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne nwadisa ayuobʋ dabpiinɛ ayɔpɔi daar (June 17, 1991), nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ ayɔpɔi nwadis piiga la dabpisi nɛ awai daar (October 29, 1997), bɛ Daily Times dinɛ bɛ Nigeria la, ka tʋʋma da an ye o bɔɔnd la'adi pa'an babsieba bɛ Daily Times nɛ li tʋʋma kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ni.
english: Ekpuk joined DTN as an illustrator between June 17, 1991, and October 29, 1997, at the Daily Times of Nigeria, and was responsible for developing visual material for columns in the Daily Times and its related publications.

kusaal: La'abanɛ ka Ekpuk's maal ka di paae nidib bɛdigʋ ya'am nɛ DTN anɛ dinɛ ka o sig ye The New Agenda: Behind Abacha's Game-Plan, gbaʋŋ kanɛ ka o da sɔbi pa'an zabkanɛ ka soogianam da zabi kad Ibrahim Babangida yisi o kʋkin la.
english: A notable example of illustrations from Ekpuk's time with DTN are from The New Agenda: Behind Abacha's Game-Plan, an article covering the bloodless coup d'état that removed Ibrahim Babangida from his seat as military head of state.

kusaal: Ba sieba anɛ Smithsonian Institution National Museum of African Art, Newark Museum, The World Bank, University of Maryland University College, Hood Museum, United States Art in Embassies Art Collection nɛ Fidelity Investment Art Collection.
english: His artworks are in private and public collections, such as Smithsonian Institution National Museum of African Art, Newark Museum, The World Bank, University of Maryland University College, Hood Museum, United States Art in Embassies Art Collection and the Fidelity Investment Art Collection.

kusaal: Ekpuk pa'ali o tʋʋma la bɛ zin'is bɛdigʋ, ba sieba anɛ: Krannert Art Museum, Champaign, Illinois; The Fowler Museum, Los Angeles; Museum of Art and Design (MAD), New York City; Newark Museum, New Jersey; The World Bank, Washington DC; Smithsonian Institution, National Museum of African Art, Washington DC; New Museum of Contemporary Art, New York City; Johannesburg Biennial, South Africa.
english: Ekpuk's work have been featured at venues including: Krannert Art Museum, Champaign, Illinois; The Fowler Museum, Los Angeles; Museum of Art and Design (MAD), New York City; Newark Museum, New Jersey; The World Bank, Washington DC; Smithsonian Institution, National Museum of African Art, Washington DC; New Museum of Contemporary Art, New York City; Johannesburg Biennial, South Africa.

kusaal: Ekpuk yʋ'ʋr da lalig hali ka di yinɛ on bɔɔn ka gʋlʋsʋd ka di pa'an African gban'akanɛ an Nsibidi nɛ Uli ya'abʋg suor la.
english: He is currently based in Washington, D.C. Ekpuk came to prominence through his paintings and drawings, which reflect indigenous African philosophies of the Nsibidi and Uli art forms.

kusaal: Ekpuk's tʋʋma bɛdigʋ pa'annɛ ninaal bɛllim an si'em sʋ'ʋlim nam ni.
english: Born in southern Nigeria, Victor Ekpuk's contemporary artwork draws upon early visual influences from the male-oriented Ekpe secret society found within the South-South and South-Eastern region.

kusaal: Di da' dɔlisid si'em nɛ di gbinni an si'em la zug ka o da keŋ tuoni gɔs bʋʋsʋm ka di an sɔbʋg ka yʋ'ʋm maal Ekpuk's mɛŋ Glyphs.
english: Its economy of lines and encoded meanings led him to further explore drawing as writing, and to the invention of Ekpuk's own Glyphs.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991) la ni, Ekpuk da naal Daily Times Nigeria (DTN), gɔmina labaya tʋʋma zin'ig.
english: In 1991, Ekpuk joined the Daily Times Nigeria (DTN), a government-controlled media outlet.

kusaal: la'am nɛ pɔlitisi da dʋ paae li bɛn la, ka di yinɛ soogianami da zanl Nigeria la, Ekpuk da ya'ab bʋnvɛlla banɛ da pian'adi pa'an pɔlitisi an si'em teŋ la ni.
english: Ekpuk joined DTN as an illustrator between June 17, 1991, and October 29, 1997, at the Daily Times of Nigeria, and was responsible for developing visual material for columns in the Daily Times and its related publications.

kusaal: O tʋʋma bɛɛ di kɔn' la zug, o da mɔri o mɛŋ Nsibidi maan bʋʋnlim banɛ pa'an pɔlitis yɛla.
english: His unique style consisted of political cartooning and his own unique Nsibidi inspired illustration.

kusaal: 2009: Of Lines and Life, The Richard F. Brush Gallery, University of St.
english: 2015: Portraits: A solo exhibition by Victor Ekpuk, Sulger-Buel Lovell Gallery, Surrey Row, London (29 September – 24 October)

kusaal: Vincent Ekow Assafuah (dʋ'anɛ 27 September 1990) anɛ Gaana pɔlitiks nwɛ'ɛd ka an Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party (NPP) nid.
english: Vincent Ekow Assafuah (born 27 September 1990) is a Ghanaian lawyer and politician who is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O anɛ Wadmaani tis Old-Tafo Constituency bɛɛ Ashanti Region.
english: He is the member of Parliament for the Old-Tafo Constituency in the Ashanti Region.

kusaal: Vincent Ekow Assafuah du'adib anɛ Polykarp Assafuah nɛ Paulina Assafuah bɛ Kumasi.
english: Vincent Ekow Assafuah was born to Polykarp Assafuah and Paulina Assafuah in Kumasi.

kusaal: O da keŋnɛ Martyrs of Uganda Junior High School ka tɔlisi zamis General Arts St.
english: He attended Martyrs of Uganda Junior High School and proceeded to study General Arts at the St. Huberts' Seminary in Kumasi.

kusaal: Assafuah o mɔr Bachelor of Arts degree in political science dinɛ ka o di'e Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), nɛ Master of Arts degree in Economic Policy nɛ Master of Science in Development Finance o di'e ba wʋsa nɛ University of Ghana (UG), bɛ Legon la.
english: Assafuah holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), and Master of Arts degree in Economic Policy and a Master of Science in Development Finance both from University of Ghana (UG), Legon.

kusaal: O lɛn mɔr Bachelor of Law Degree (LLB) yi Central University.
english: He also holds a Bachelor of Law Degree (LLB) from Central University and a Professional Law Certificate from the Ghana School of Law.

kusaal: Din nya'aŋ o da tɔlisi keŋ Ghana Institute of Journalism anina o da di'e Master of Arts in Public Relations.
english: He later proceeded to the Ghana Institute of Journalism where he obtained a Master of Arts in Public Relations.

kusaal: Nannanna, o maanɛ Ph.D. degree in Public Administration and Public Policy.
english: He is currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Public Administration and Public Policy.

kusaal: Assafuah da nya'aya ka di National Service Personnel Association (NASPA) National president on da nan maani o National Service on da mɔ ye lieb USAG pirɛsidɛn vɔɔtʋg ka pʋ di la, o da tʋm tʋʋm kan yʋʋm yinne.
english: Assafuah contested and won the National Service Personnel Association (NASPA) National president whilst doing his National Service after his unsuccessful attempt in USAG presidential election, he served in that role for one year.

kusaal: O da anɛ onɛ sʋŋid Samira Bawumia yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2015) paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la ni (2017).
english: He was a special assistant to the Second lady Samira Bawumia from 2015 to 2017.

kusaal: yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi la nii (2017), o da anɛ onɛ piana'di tisid Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg la nya'adɔl, New Patriotic Party (NPP).
english: In 2017, he was the acting Deputy Communication Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party la da di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi yʋʋmpaal Nwadig, January 2017, ba da gaŋ o ye an head of public relations bɛ gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ anii la ni (2018).
english: After the New Patriotic Party came in power in January 2017, He was subsequently appointed as the head of public relations at the Ministry of Education in 2018.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ part-time lecturer tis Dominion University College.
english: He is also a part-time lecturer at the Dominion University College.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi Nwadisa ayuobʋ la, June 2020, o da nya' Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg,New Patriotic Party kʋk la Old Tafo Constituency sʋ'ʋlim, onɛ da zin'i kʋk la zug Anthony Akoto Osei da yɛl ye on kʋ lɛn zi'en ya'as yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi 2020 vɔɔtʋg la.
english: In June 2020, Assafuah stood for the New Patriotic Party seat for the Old Tafo Constituency after the incumbent Anthony Akoto Osei declared his intention not to contest the 2020 election.

kusaal: o da paam vɔɔt kɔbisyi nɛ piswai nɛ awai (299), Assafuah da nya' nɛ nidib anu (5) sieba, onɛ da kpi'e o hali, Dr.
english: With a total votes of 299, Assafuah won the primaries against the 5 other contenders.

kusaal: Louisa Serwaa Carole da paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ pistan nɛ atan (133) ka banɛ kpɛlim la Prince Odeneho Oppong paam piswai (90), Archibald Acquah pʋ paam si'ela, Emmanuel Obeng nɛ Lord Inusah Lansah da paam pisnaasi nɛ anaasi (44) nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (27).
english: His closest contender Dr. Louisa Serwaa Carole got 133 whilst the others which included Prince Odeneho Oppong got 90, Archibald Acquah had no votes, Emmanuel Obeng and Lord Inusah Lansah had 44 votes and 27 votes respectively.

english: It no longer has a representation in the Parliament of Ghana and does not elect a Member of Parliament (MP) as the new name is Weija-Gbawe.

kusaal: West Africa nidib kanl ane wʋʋ miliyɔn kɔbis naasi nɛ piiga nɛ awai yɛla(419) yʋma tusa ayi nɛ pisyi nɛ yinne la, ka yʋma tusa ayi nɛ piiga nɛ ayipɔi la, nidib la kanl da anɛ miliyɔn kɔbis atan'nɛ pisnii nɛ ayinne, tusa kɔbis awai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayinne(381,981,000) ka miliyɔn kɔbiga nɛ pisnii nɛ awai, tusa kɔbis yuobu nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayi(189,672,000) an puab, ka miliyɔn kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ ayi, tusa kɔbis atan' nɛ awai (192,309,000) mɛ da an dap.
english: As of 2021, the population of West Africa is estimated at 419 million, and approximately 382 million in 2017, of which 189.7 million were female and 192.3 million male.

kusaal: West Africa yiiga yɛlkuda anɛ ba paŋ dinɛ k aba da mɔri tʋ'e teens banɛ da bɛ kpinkpɛmis nɛ teŋsʋg teens dinɛ anɛ Mali nɛ Gao Empires la.
english: Historically, West Africa was home to several powerful states and empires that controlled regional trade routes, including the Mali and Gao Empires.

kusaal: West Africa dinɛ ka ba lɛm buoni li ye Western Africa la anɛ teŋ kanɛ an kuom teŋ bɛ Africa sʋ'ʋlim.
english: West Africa, also known as Western Africa, is the westernmost region of Africa. The United Nations defines Western Africa as the 16 countries of Benin, Burkina Faso, Cape Verde, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, and Togo, as well as Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha (a United Kingdom Overseas Territory).

kusaal: United Nations teŋndim pa'al yee Western Africa teŋkanɛ pɛɛs teens piiga nɛ ayuobu la ni (16) la, ani Benin, Burkina Faso, Cape Verde, Gambia la, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, nɛ Togo, pɛɛs nɛ Saint Helena, Ascension nɛ Tristan da Cunha (United Kingdom Overseas Territory).
english: West Africa, also known as Western Africa, is the westernmost region of Africa. The United Nations defines Western Africa as the 16 countries of Benin, Burkina Faso, Cape Verde, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, and Togo, as well as Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha (a United Kingdom Overseas Territory).

kusaal: West Africa da dit ti ba nɛ suokitakita dinɛ Arab nɛ North Africa hali nɛ teens banɛ lali la wʋsa, ka dinɛ ka ba da kuosid tita'am anɛ salima nɛ kuntzɛn'ʋg tʋʋma nɛ wabid iilla.
english: Due to Mauritania's increasingly close ties to the Arab World and its 1999 withdrawal from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), in modern times it is often considered, especially in Africa, as now part of western North Africa.

kusaal: Europe dim la nyɛ ka da' la ken sʋ'ʋm siem la nɛ teens bɛdigʋ laa, di da kene ka Atlantic slave trade la da yʋ'ʋm duo lɛn tʋm nwɛnɛ ban daa tʋm si'em la sʋ'ʋŋid ka America dim la nidib banɛ na tʋm tisiba.
english: During European exploration, local economies were incorporated into the Atlantic slave trade, which expanded existing systems of slavery.

kusaal: Sankpansim tʋʋma da naae saŋa 19th century nya'aŋ la, Europe kas-kas anɛ France nɛ Britain dim la da kpɛm ke tuoni la'asidi tʋm nɛ nidib la.Tituul anɛ ban da mɔr nwenɛɛ kpaadib tʋʋma la'adnam wʋʋ kooko, nɛɛ coffee, siarin la'adnmnam wʋʋ daadnam nɛ kug vɛɛnla banɛ bɛ teŋin k aba ligidi kpi'im hali wʋʋ salima ɛ.
english: Even after the end of the slave trade in the early 19th century, colonial powers — especially France and Britain — continued to exploit the region through colonial relationships.

kusaal: Din yii asʋ'ʋmɛŋ saŋa sa West African teens la bɛdigʋ dinɛ ane Ivory Coast, Ghana, Nigeria, nɛ Senegal la da tʋm yɛlkpan dinɛ anɛ sʋ'ʋlim la nɛ di lgidi yɛla.
english: In the United Nations scheme of African regions, the region of Western Africa includes 16 states and the United Kingdom Overseas Territory of Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha: Mali, Burkina Faso, Senegal and the Niger are mostly in the Sahel, a transition zone between the Sahara desert and the Sudanian Savanna; Benin, Ivory Coast, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Togo and Nigeria compose most of Guinea, the traditional name for the area near the Gulf of Guinea; Mauritania lies in the Maghreb, the northwestern region of Africa that has historically been inhabited by West African groups such as the Fulani, Soninke, Wolof, Serer and Toucouleur people, along with Arab-Berber Maghrebi people such as the Tuareg; Cape Verde is an island country in the Atlantic Ocean; and Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha consists of eight main islands located in four different parts of the Atlantic.

kusaal: West Africa da mɔr ekologi nɛ biyodivɛsiti paŋ pamm nɛ teens si'eba.
english: The major multi-sport event of West Africa is the ECOWAS Games which commenced at the 2012 ECOWAS Games.

kusaal: Pɛbis gɛnd bama tisit West Africa la kpan'am nɛ si'elnam bɛdigʋ yit biyɔmisnam(biomes) la ni yi biyɔdivɛsiti kpan'am(biodiversity-rich) trophical forest paae teŋkpi'imis (drylands) ka li daamid bunkɔbid bɛdigʋ dinɛ anɛ pangolins, rhinocerous nɛɛ wabidnam.
english: This climatic mix creates a range of biomes, from tropical forests to drylands, supporting species such as pangolin, rhinoceros, and elephant.

kusaal: Western North Region anɛ regions of Ghana nam ayuobʋ la yinne ka ba da pin'ili di yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ awai (2019).
english: The Western North region is one of the six new regions of Ghana created in 2019.

kusaal: Region la tɔdnɛ nɛ Ivory Coast (Comoé District) lɛb Ya-datiʋŋ, Central region lɛbid Ya-tuona, nɛ Ashanti, Ahafo, Bono East nɛ Bono region nam lɛb Ya-dagɔbʋg.
english: The region is bounded by the Ivory Coast (Comoé District) on the west, the Central region in the southeast, and the Ashanti, Ahafo, Bono East and Bono regions in the north.

kusaal: Buudbanɛ ka ba pian'ada ani Sefwi, Akan, French nɛ English.
english: The main languages spoken are Sefwi, Akan, French and English.

kusaal: Region paala la maalʋg dɔlisnɛ New Patriotic Party da zi'el nɔɔr si'em 2016 Ghana wʋsa vɔɔtʋgin la.
english: This creation of this new region was in fulfillment of a promise made by the New Patriotic Party prior to the 2016 Ghana general election.

kusaal: On da di vɔɔt la, Zugraan, Nana Akuffo Addo da maal Ministry of Regional Reorganization ye di gɔs yɛlsieba maalʋg.
english: Upon winning the elections, the president, Nana Akuffo Addo created the Ministry of Regional Reorganization to oversee policy formulation and implementation.

kusaal: Region paala la sieba anɛ Bono East, Ahafo, Savannah, North East, nɛ Oti Region.
english: The other new regions are Bono East, Ahafo, Savannah, North East, and Oti regions.

kusaal: Lʋgʋr paal Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development da gɔs ka si'el wʋsa maal ka Hon.
english: The execution of plans for the creation of the regions was ceded to the newly created Ministry of Regional Reorganization and Development which is under the leadership of Hon. Dan Botwe.

kusaal: Yʋʋmtusa ayi nɛ piinɛ ayɔpɔi nwadisa atan (March 2017) la ni, ministry da maal suoya ye ba pin'il region naming la la'as nɛ Council of State.
english: In March 2017, the ministry sent the blueprint for the creation of the region along with others to the Council of State.

kusaal: Region nam la maalʋg wʋsa naar da anɛ vɔɔtʋg kanɛ ka ba da kɛ ka nimbanɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlimin la vɔɔt ye ba maal region paal la 27 December 2018.
english: The final stage for the creation of the region was decided through a referendum by the people within the area of the new region on 27 December 2018.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ yinne nwadisa anii la (August 2021), H5N1 avian influenza da gban'e nidib region la ni.
english: In August 2021, the region recorded an outbreak of H5N1 avian influenza.

kusaal: Region la pʋnɛ MMDA's nama awai (0 Metropolitan, 3 Municipal nɛ 6 Ordinary Assemblies).
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into nine MMDA's (made up of 0 Metropolitan, 3 Municipal and 6 Ordinary Assemblies).

kusaal: Western North Region ka saa nidi gat zin'ig wʋsa Ghana, di mɔr zuoya, ka teŋ la mɛ mɔr kʋ'ʋlim.
english: The Western North region has the highest rainfall in Ghana, lush green hills, and fertile soils.

kusaal: Salima tuub zin'is (gold mines) bɛdegʋ bɛ region la ni.
english: There are numerous small and large-scale gold mines companies in the region.

kusaal: Buudi banɛ bɛ region la ni bɛdegʋ anɛ Sefwi nam.
english: The ethnic culture of the region is dominated by the Sefwi .

kusaal: Western North Region of Ghana anɛ region paal kanɛ ka ba da nwaae yi Western Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: The Western North region is a new region carved out of the existing Western region of Ghana.

kusaal: La'asʋg pʋʋgin, Region paala ayuobʋ ka ba da nyaŋi maal yi region nam piiga banɛ pʋn dɛŋim bɛ Ghana la.
english: This creation of this new region was in fulfillment of a promise made by the New Patriotic Party prior to the 2016 Ghana general election.

kusaal: Western North region mɔr post-secondary schools bɛdegʋ, teachers' nɛ nursing college nam.
english: The Western North region is a new region carved out of the existing Western region of Ghana.

kusaal: District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly wʋsa, mɔrnɛ Chief Executive, ka o zi'eni ti central government amaa di kpieʋŋ wʋsa anɛ presiding member onɛ ka Assembly member la vɔɔti gaŋ.
english: Each district, municipal or metropolitan assembly is administered by a chief executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Di pɛ'ɛs Ghana ya-dagɔbʋg paa zi'ig, Cape Three Points, zi'ikani ka ba baŋ ye kpaam bɛ teŋin la bɛdigʋ June 2007 yʋʋm la ni.
english: It includes Ghana's southernmost location, Cape Three Points, where crude oil was discovered in commercial quantities in June 2007.

kusaal: Region la mɔr paalʋ wʋʋ 13,842 km2, ka mɔr nidib 2,060,585 yʋʋm 2021 nidib kaanlʋg la ni.
english: The region covers an area of 13,842 km2, and had a population of 2,060,585 at the 2021 Census.

kusaal: Ba kʋdabɛda anɛ Ankobra River, Bia River, nɛ Pra River dinɛ bɛ ya- nya'aŋ, Tano River la kilimit western national border la.
english: The largest rivers are the Ankobra River, the Bia River, and the Pra River in the east, with the Tano River partly forming the western national border.

kusaal: Zi'ig la ka ba mi' di ye UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nzulezo teŋkpɛŋ dinɛ ka ba mɛ ku'om zut gilik pɛ'ɛsnɛ Ankasa Protected Area.
english: The area is known for the UNESCO World Heritage Site, the village of Nzulezo built entirely on stilts and platforms over water and the Ankasa Protected Area.

kusaal: Ninvɛnla wʋʋ Portuguese, Dutch, British, nɛ Brandenburgian bɛ ku'om la nɔɔrin, di da mɛnɛ bɛ yʋʋm 1512 ka nam bɛ.
english: There is a series of imposing Portuguese, Dutch, British, and Brandenburgian forts along the coast, built from 1512 on.

kusaal: Western region mɔr post-secondary schools bɛdigʋ, pɛ'ɛsnɛ pa'anib nɛ ti'ebidib kɔliginam, nɛ universities nam ayi -University of Mines and Technology (dinɛ bɛ Tarkwa) nɛ Takoradi Technical University (dinɛ ka ba da buon ye Takoradi Polythecnic).
english: The Western region has many post-secondary schools, including teachers' and nursing colleges, and two universities--University of Mines and Technology (in Tarkwa) and Takoradi Technical University (formerly known as Takoradi Polytechnic).

kusaal: Pɔi ka ba da mak ka zi'el region la December 2018 yʋʋm la ni, region la da mɔri 23 MMDA's (1 Metropolitan, 11 Municipal and 11 Ordinary Assemblies).
english: Before the regional demarcation in December 2018, the region had 23 MMDA's (made up of 1 Metropolitan, 11 Municipal and 11 Ordinary Assemblies).

kusaal: Dinzʋgɔ, dinɛ da pɛ'ɛs amaligim-maal la zugɔ, MMDA's nam awai ( 3 Municipal and 6 Ordinary Assemblies) ka ba da yisi yi Western Region ka nɔki zi'el dinɛ an paalʋg dinɛ ka di teŋpʋtita'ar an Wiawso.
english: Therefore, as part of this reorganisation, nine MMDA's (those in bold and asterisks below, which were 3 Municipal and 6 Ordinary Assemblies) were removed from the Western region and formed into a new Western North region with its new capital at Wiawso.

kusaal: Tʋʋma pʋʋgʋn kaŋa, region la pʋnɛ 14 MMDA's ( 1 Metropolitan, 8 Municipal and 5 Ordinary Assemblies).
english: Under this administration system, the region is divided into 14 MMDA's (made up of 1 Metropolitan, 8 Municipal and 5 Ordinary Assemblies).

kusaal: District yinne wʋsa, Municipal bɛɛ Metropolitan Assembly, tʋʋma wʋsa bɛnɛ Chief Executive la nu'usin, zie tis central government amaa o paŋ wʋsa yitnɛ Assembly man onɛ ka nidib la vɔɔt.
english: Each District, Municipal or Metropolitan Assembly, is administered by a Chief Executive, representing the central government but deriving authority from an Assembly headed by a presiding member elected from among the members themselves.

kusaal: Western Region dit malisim nɛ ku'okani bɛ di ni Ghana ya-dagɔbʋg nɛ Ivory Coast dinɛ ka Western region tɔnd nɛ Central Region ya-nya'aŋ la.
english: The Western region, located in south Ghana, spreads from the Ivory Coast (Comoé District) in the west to the Central region in the east, includes the capital and large twin city of Sekondi-Takoradi on the coast, coastal Axim, and a hilly inland area including Elubo.

kusaal: Western Region mɔr saku'om gat Ghana ni, kʋnkʋna nɛ kʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: The Western region, located in south Ghana, spreads from the Ivory Coast (Comoé District) in the west to the Central region in the east, includes the capital and large twin city of Sekondi-Takoradi on the coast, coastal Axim, and a hilly inland area including Elubo.

kusaal: Di anɛ Akans malima ma'aa bɛ anina; ba pian'adi Akan, French nɛ English ma'aa.
english: The region is an Akan region comprised Wassa, Ahanta, and Nzema.

kusaal: Pɔlitis tʋʋma dinɛ bɛ region la ni yitnɛ local government system ni.
english: The political administration of the region is through the local government system.

kusaal: White Volta la yinɛ Burkina Faso ya-datiʋŋ baba, ka pʋbidi dɔl Northern Ghana ka kpa'adi kpɛn'ɛd Lake Volta bɛ Ghana la ni.
english: The White Volta emerges in northern Burkina Faso, flows through Northern Ghana and empties into Lake Volta in Ghana.

kusaal: White Volta kuosuoya anɛ Black Volta nɛ Red Volta.
english: The Volta River Basin comprises the drainage basins of the Volta River and its various branches, including the White Volta, Black Volta, Red Volta, Oti, and Lower Volta sub basins.

kusaal: White Volta anɛ ku'onuudim tis tɛɛns banɛ bɛ di nɔɔrin nɛ banɛ kpi'e di wʋsa nɛ sieba.
english: Red Volta, or Nazinon, as well as Sissili, are two of the major tributaries of White Volta, and they also originate in Burkina Faso.

kusaal: Widi sieba bɛ dunia la ni bɛɛ yadig teŋgbaŋ wʋsa ka an' si'anrin bʋnam ka ba buon ye feral widi ka ba nan zi'i kpɛ'n yin nɛ.
english: The European wild horse, also known as the tarpan, that went extinct in the late 19th or early 20th century has previously been treated as the nominate subspecies of wild horse, Equus ferus ferus, but more recent studies have cast doubt on whether tarpans were truly wild or if they actually were feral horses or hybrids.

kusaal: widi banɛ ka ba ba'ad saŋa bɛdigʋ la na pin'il wɔɔ nʋ'ʋs wa'alim 15.2 (62 inches, 157 cm) ka ɛnti wa'am wɔɔ nʋ'ʋs wa'alim piinɛ ayɔpɔi (68 inches, 173 cm) ka tɛbisim an wɔɔ 500 kiŋ paaɛ 600 kilograms (1,100 to 1,320 Ib).
english: Some extinct wild horse populations are thought to have been considerably larger, with some Pleistocene European wild horses (including those assigned to Equus (ferus) mosbachensis and Equus (ferus) latipes) suggested to have body masses of around 500–607 kilograms (1,102–1,338 lb).ST2 Earlier Middle Pleistocene horses (such as those assigned to E. (ferus) mosbachensis) differ from later ones in some aspects of the anatomy of the limbs and teeth.

kusaal: Ya'a kai widi'i, genus Equus mɔr widi la kɔn'bkɔn'b zin'isa ayuobu.
english: The horse family Equidae evolved in North America, with the genus Equus appearing on the continent during the Pliocene (5.3-2.6 million years ago).

kusaal: Ba sieba anɛ bʋŋ, Equus asinus; zuɔrin tɛŋinbʋŋ, Equus zebra; tɛŋinbuŋ, Equus quagga; Grevy's zebra, Equus grevyi; kiang; nɛ onager, Equus hemionus.
english: However, other subspecies of Equus ferus may have existed.

kusaal: Laba'ar yiiga yitnɛ palaɛological nɛ archaeological dim vɛɛrsig; linɛ paasa ayi la anɛ DNA kpa'sib kanɛ ka ba gɔs nan'nan'na widi nɛ widi banɛ da dɛŋim bɛ ka kpi'la kɔba nɛ ba nyina.
english: Ancient DNA analysis suggests North American horses were largely genetically distinct from Eurasian horses, with limited and intermittent interbreeding between the two populations following the initial dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge.

kusaal: Amaa widi banɛ da bɛ ya'an Botai Kazakhstan la da anɛ Przewalski widi ka kai yʋʋmpʋkʋ'tin widi banɛ bɛ dʋn'na laa.
english: Today the only living wild horse subspecies, Przewalski's horse, which was formerly extinct in the wild, has been reintroduced to small areas spanning from its former distribution in northeast China, Mongolia and Kazakhstan, as well as areas outside of its historical distribution, including Spain.

kusaal: Yʋʋmpʋkʋ'tin widi kɛ ka ba kanl la zʋɔɛ yalig Eurasia, sin'iŋid yʋma tʋsa anaasi nɛ kɔbʋsyi banɛ gaad la.
english: Around 900–800,000 years ago, at the Early-Middle Pleistocene boundary, the ancestors of Eurasian wild horses crossed over the Bering Land Bridge from North America. Early horses in Eurasia are referred to species like Equus mosbachensis.

kusaal: Makir anɛ ye widi na an wan wʋʋ 9,500,000 United States tɛŋin ma'a.
english: The term "wild horse" is also used colloquially in reference to free-roaming herds of feral horses; for example, the mustang in the United States, and the brumby in Australia.

kusaal: William Folorunso Kumuyi (ka ba dʋ'a o yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnaasi nɛ yinne, nwadis ayuobu, dabisa ayuobʋ daar, 6 June 1941) o anɛ one gat pʋ'ʋs kanɛ paad dunia wʋsa ka ba buon Global Crusade with Kumuyi (GCK) la tuon, one an kpɛɛm kanɛ ka ba buon General Superintendent ka o pin'il Deeper Christian Life Ministry ka li bɛ Gbagada, Lagos, Nigeria.
english: William Folorunso Kumuyi () (born 6 June 1941) is the convener of Global Crusade with Kumuyi (GCK), and the founder and General Superintendent of the Deeper Christian Life Ministry situated at Gbagada, Lagos, Nigeria.

kusaal: Ba da dʋ'a Kumuyi kristo biis yir ka li bɛ Erin-Odo Ijesa, Osun State, Nigeria yatu'ona.
english: Kumuyi was born into a Christian family in Erin-Ijesa, Osun State, in the western part of Nigeria.

kusaal: O da naae o secondary school nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ yinne (1961) bɛnɛ Mayflower School linɛ Ikenne, Ogun State, anina ka o tɔlis tuoni kɛŋ University of Ibadan ka naae anina yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayɔpɔi (1967) ka mɔr first-class honours degree bɛnɛ kaanlig zamisig (mathematics) anina one da an one zamis gbaŋi gaad o taaba yʋʋm kan pʋʋgin.
english: He completed his secondary school education in 1961 at Mayflower School in Ikenne, Ogun State, from where he proceeded to the University of Ibadan and in 1967 graduated with a first-class honours degree in mathematics where he graduated as overall best graduating student in that year.

kusaal: o da paam dʋ'am paal kristo sa'an nɛ lasid daar, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi, nwadis anaasi, dabisa anu daar (Sunday, April 5, 1964) on da an yʋʋm pisi nɛ atan' la (23).
english: He became a born-again Christian on Sunday, 5 April 1964 at 23.

kusaal: Saŋa daa kɛna, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ atan' la (1963), yʋʋm yʋʋmidib nɛ wina'am labaar mɔɔnib da paam suori kɛn sakurin la na.
english: Eventually, in 1963, a group of singers and preachers from a Gospel church got permission to come to the school.

kusaal: o saam da anɛ Anglican Church pʋ'ʋsim nid.
english: His father was a member of the Anglican Church.

kusaal: Kumuyi da pin'ili zamisid mathematics yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayi (1962) bɛ Mayflower School, anina ka o da naae o da kɛŋ tuon la, yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi (1970) pin'ilig, ka o da an mathematics pa'an-pa'ani bɛ University of Lagos.
english: Kumuyi began teaching mathematics in 1962 at Mayflower School, his alma mater.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' (1973) la, on da an pa'an-pa'an mathematics ni bɛ University of Lagos la, Kumuyi da pin'il wina'am gbaŋ zamisig nɛ sakur biis piinɛnu (15 students) banɛ da kɛn wina'am gbaŋ zamisig la.
english: In 1973, while a Professor of mathematics at the University of Lagos, Kumuyi began a Bible study group with 15 students who had come to him for Bible training.

kusaal: yʋʋm tʋsir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu (1975), ba da kat Kumuyi yis Apostolic Faith Church on da pa'an wina'am siig kasi sʋʋb la yela.
english: In 1975, Kumuyi was expelled from the Apostolic Faith Church for preaching on the baptism of the Holy Spirit.

kusaal: O da pin'il o mɛŋ pʋʋsim, ka yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ ayi (1982) ka da kilim Deeper Life Bible Church.
english: He continued his independent ministry, which in 1982 became the Deeper Life Bible Church.

kusaal: pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg la da pin'il tʋʋma nɛ yʋʋm tusayi, piinɛ anii, nwadis anaasi, dabisa pisi nɛ anaasi (24 April 2018) daar; Vice President of Nigeria, Yemi Osinbajo, nɛ kpɛɛm nam si'eba da kɛŋ la'asig nwa'.
english: The auditorium was inaugurated on 24 April 2018; the Vice President of Nigeria Yemi Osinbajo, and other important dignitaries attended the inauguration.

kusaal: Pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔd la si'eba banɛ nyɛ yʋ'ʋri an: Deeper Life Conference Centre bɛ Ogun State, Kilometer 42, Lagos–Ibadan Expressway nɛ International Bible Training Centre (IBTC) ka din mɛ bɛ Ayobo, Lagos.
english: Other places of worship of his Christian ministry include: the Deeper Life Conference Centre in Ogun State at Kilometer 42, Lagos–Ibadan Expressway and the International Bible Training Centre (IBTC) at Ayobo, Lagos.

kusaal: Kumuyi da si'al Abiodun Olowu nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ anu, nwadis awai (September 1972).da o da paas o sakur biis banɛ ka o paani ba wina'am gbaŋ la ni.
english: Kumuyi met Abiodun Olowu in September 1972.

kusaal: O da dii o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii, nwadis awai, dabisa piinɛ atan' (13 September 1980) bɛ Lagos, ka ba dʋ'a biis ayi, Jeremiah nɛ John.
english: They married on 13 September 1980 in Lagos, and had two children, Jeremiah and John.

kusaal: Mrs Abiodun Kumuyi da kpi' nɛ y nɛ y nɛ yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ awai, nwadis anaasi, dabisa piinɛ yinne (11 April 2009) la.
english: Abiodun Kumuyi died on 11 April 2009.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piiga, nwadis piiga, dabisa piinɛ atan' (13 October 2010), nwadis piinɛ anii, o pʋ'a kpi la nya'aŋ, Kumuyi da di' Folashade Adenike Blaize bɛ London.
english: On 13 October 2010, Kumuyi married Folashade Adenike Blaize in London.

kusaal: Folashade da anɛ kpɛɛm kanɛ ka ba buon Administrator tis Deeper Life Bible Church, London.
english: Folashade was the administrator of the Deeper Life Bible Church, London.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛ atan' (2013) la, Foreign Policy magazine da kaanl Kumuyi paas "nidib kɔbisnu (500) banɛ mɔr paŋ tɛngbaŋ zug".
english: In 2013, Foreign Policy magazine listed Kumuyi among the "500 most powerful people on the planet".

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛ anii (2018) la, Kumuyi da paam girim kanɛ an PhD yi University of Abuja.
english: In 2018, Kumuyi received an honorary PhD from the University of Abuja.

kusaal: Di nwadis ayʋobʋ la'asig da bɛnɛ Abuja, ka nwadis ayɔpɔi la'asig da bɛ Calabar, ka nwadis anii la'asig da bɛ Enugu, yʋʋm tusayi, pisi nɛ yinne la ni (2021).
english: Subsequent editions were held in June, July, and August 2021 in Abuja, Calabar, and Enugu, respectively.

kusaal: Gbaŋ nwa' mɔr lakir kɔbistan' nɛ pisi nɛ anu (325 pages) ka di pian'zug an, Kumuyi: Defender of the Faith.
english: The biography of 325 pages is entitled, Kumuyi: Defender of the Faith.

kusaal: Nigeria gɔmɛna zugraan ya'andɔl kʋdʋg, Yemi Osibanjo nɛ Lagos state governor, Baba Jide Sanwo-olu da paas nidib banɛ da bɛ gbaŋ nwa zʋŋʋr ni.
english: Former Vice President of Nigeria Yemi Osibanjo and Lagos state governor BabaJide Sanwo-olu were at the launch of the book.

kusaal: O da tɔlis tuoni kɛŋ sakuri zamis zamisigi bɛnɛ gbaŋ zamisig lʋgir la pʋʋgin bɛ University of Lagos.
english: He subsequently took a post-graduate course in Education at the University of Lagos.

kusaal: Mam da kɛŋ secondary school la, mam da pʋ lɛn mɔr nya'asim nɛ pʋ'ʋsim, bɔzugɔ, ti sakur kpɛɛm la da pa'ali ti ye ti da dɔl wina'am.
english: When I went to secondary school I lost interest in the church because our principal taught us atheism.

kusaal: Mam da gban'ae labaar la gbin ka paam dʋ'am paal nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi, nwadis anaasi, dabisa anu daar (Sunday, April 5, 1964).
english: He became a born-again Christian on Sunday, 5 April 1964 at 23.

kusaal: Mam da karim John Wesley, Charles Finney, Spurgeon, nɛ gbana bɛdigʋ.
english: Kumuyi was influenced by John Wesley, Charles Finney and Charles Spurgeon.

kusaal: Mam da paas Scripture Union, ka nɔbigi kɛŋ tuon.
english: I got involved with the Scripture Union, and I grew.

kusaal: Kumuyi paam ya'am bɛdigʋ yi John Wesley, Charles Finney nɛ Charles Spurgeon ni.
english: Kumuyi was influenced by John Wesley, Charles Finney and Charles Spurgeon.

kusaal: Wina'am gbaŋ zamisig kan ni ka Deeper Christian Life Ministry da dɔlisi pin'il.
english: This training led to the foundation of the Deeper Christian Life Ministry.

kusaal: Deeper Christian Life Ministry ka Kumuyi an one pin'ili li la mɔr pʋ'ʋs dɔɔg tita'ar kanɛ bɛ Gbagada, Lagos.
english: The Deeper Christian Life Ministry founded by Kumuyi has headquarters in Gbagada, Lagos.

kusaal: W.F. Kumuyi pin'ili maan dunia wʋsa nwadig-nwadig wina'am gbaŋ zamisig nɛ yʋʋm tusayi, pisi nɛ yinne, nwadis anaasi (April 2021) la bɛ Abuja, Nigeria sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Kumuyi began conducting a series of Global Gospel Crusades in April 2021, starting in Abuja, Nigeria.

kusaal: Nidib da paas la'asig la pʋʋin, dɔlisid na'asaasɔɔng dinɛ an social media nɛ Zoom ni.
english: These events were broadcast globally, with participants joining via social media and dedicated Zoom connections.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, pisi nɛ yinne, nwadis anii (August 2021) la'asig la da pa'an Don Moen ka o yʋʋm yʋʋma.
english: The August 2021 edition featured gospel artist Don Moen, who ministered alongside Kumuyi.

kusaal: la'asig bama ba buoni ba ye Global Crusade with Kumuyi (GCK) nɛ yʋʋm tusayi, pisi nɛ ayi, nwadis ayɔpɔi (July 2022) la ka Nigeria gɔmɛna zugdaan kʋdʋg nɛ, Olusegun Obasanjo nɛ Zambia gɔmɛna ya'andɔl kʋdʋg Nevers Mumba da paas banɛ da kɛn la'as kaŋa nina.
english: The launch event was attended by former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo and former Zambian Vice President Nevers Mumba, among others.

kusaal: Gbaŋ kanɛ an yiiga pa'an Pastor Kumuyi vʋ'ʋm yela da yinɛ yʋʋm tusayi, pisi nɛ yinne (2021) ka one sɔb la an Banji Ojewale.
english: A book-length biography of Kumuyi was written and published in 2021 by Banji Ojewale.

kusaal: Banɛ da si'ak gbaŋ kaŋa yiib na anɛ Pastor Enoch Adeboye.
english: The foreword was written by Enoch Adeboye.

kusaal: pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg la nidib na nyaŋi kpɛn'ɛ anina paae tusa pistan' (30,000) pʋ'ʋs wina'am; bani mi' da ye di paan nɛ winpʋ'ʋs dɔɔd anaasi banɛ yalim dunia wʋsa.
english: The church auditorium at the headquarters could seat up to 30,000 worshippers; it was described by experts as the fourth largest in the world.

kusaal: William Kwasi Sabi (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ nwadisa anii la dabpisi nɛ atan daar- August 23, 1966) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ Mp tis Seventh Parliament bɛ Fourth Republic of Ghana tis Dormaa East Constituency dinɛ bɛ Brong-Ahafo Region bɛ New Patriotic Party (NPP) la ni.
english: William Kwasi Sabi (born 23 August 1966) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Dormaa East Constituency in the Bono Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O yinɛ Wamfie dinɛ bɛ Bono Region of Ghana.
english: He hails from Wamfie in the Bono Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr Bachelor of Science degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ Administration yit University of Ghana Legon nɛ Master's in Public Health yit University of Cape Town ni mɛn.
english: He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Administration from the University of Ghana Legon and a Master's in Public Health from the University of Cape Town.

kusaal: Sabi pin'ili tʋʋma la, o anɛ Sibiti administrator bɛ Catholic Health Service, Sunyani din yi yʋma 1997 ti paae yʋma 2003.
english: Sabi began his career as a hospital administrator at the Catholic Health Service, Sunyani from 1997 to 2003.

kusaal: O an lecturer bɛ Catholic University College of Ghana din yi yʋma 2005 ti paae yʋma 2009 ni.
english: He worked as a lecturer at the Catholic University College of Ghana from 2005 to 2009.

kusaal: Ka yʋma 2008 ni la, o da an operations manager tis National Health Insurance Authority.
english: In 2008, he became the operations manager for National Health Insurance Authority.

kusaal: O da yuolim an management consultant bɛ MDF West Africa Limited ni.
english: He later worked as a management consultant with MDF West Africa Limited.

kusaal: Sabi zi'eni tis Dormaa East constituency bɛ New Patriotic Party bɛ 2012 vɔɔtʋg la ni ka di.
english: Sabi contested for the seat of the Dormaa East constituency on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party in the 2012 Ghanaian general election and won.

kusaal: O da mɔri vɔɔtnam kal 13,712 ka mɔr 56.87% yit vɔɔtʋg bani wʋsa vɔɔt la, ka o di ka bas bani wʋsa vɔɔt la paas nɛ Ali Adjei Ibrahim, Felix Kumi Kwaku, Asante Oppong Alexander, nɛ Adoma Hayford.
english: He garnered 13,712 votes which represent 56.87% of the total votes cast and therefore defeated the other contestants including Ali Adjei Ibrahim, Felix Kumi Kwaku, Asante Oppong Alexander, and Adoma Hayford.

kusaal: O tʋm an Deputy Minista tis Ministry of Monitoring and Evaluation din yi yʋma 2016 ti paae yʋma 2020, ka nannana, o anɛ Technical Advisor bɛ Monitoring and Evaluation Secretariat, Ghana Zugdaan zɔŋ la ni.
english: He served as the Deputy Minister for the Ministry of Monitoring and Evaluation from 2016 to 2020, and currently, he is the Technical Advisor at the Monitoring and Evaluation Secretariat, Office of the President.

kusaal: Sabi anɛ Ayisa biig dinɛ ka na'asaalin an Christian la.
english: Sabi is a Christian.

kusaal: Sabi du'am yʋʋm anɛ August 23, 1966.
english: Sabi was born on 23 August 1966.

kusaal: O da yʋolim an Minister for Foreign Affairs bɛ Ghana's second republic dinɛ bɛ 1971 ti paae 1972 ni.
english: He later became a Minister for Foreign Affairs in Ghana's second republic between 1971 and 1972.

kusaal: Nana William Ofori Atta da anɛ Nana Sir Ofori Atta I biig onɛ da an Omanhene (Na'ab) tis Akyem Abuakwa dinɛ yi 1912 ti paae 1943.
english: Nana William Ofori Atta was born at Kyebi and was the son of Nana Sir Ofori Atta I who was the Omanhene (King) of Akyem Abuakwa between 1912 and 1943.

kusaal: Onɛ da an nobleman bɛ na'ayir tis Ofori-Atta dynasty, la'amnɛ Akan nidib la dit ti ba mayir faar la bigis ye onɛ da an na'abiig.
english: He was thus a nobleman of royal lineage of the Ofori-Atta dynasty, although the fact that the Akan people (to which he belonged) are traditionally matrilineal meant that he was not a dynastic prince.

kusaal: William Ofori Atta kɛŋnɛ Mfantsipim School ka ba yis o lɛbis Achimota School dinɛ ka o da pɛ'ɛs yiiga sakur biis banɛ zi'ini sɔb Cambridge School Certificate la.
english: William Ofori Atta attended Mfantsipim School, but was withdrawn by the school to Achimota School where he was among the first batch of students to sit for the Cambridge School Certificate.

kusaal: O sakur bitaaba anɛ Komla Agbeli Gbedemah nɛ Edward Akufo-Addo.
english: Some of his school mates included Komla Agbeli Gbedemah and Edward Akufo-Addo.

kusaal: O da lɛm anɛ yiiga School prefect.
english: He was also the first ever school prefect of the School.

kusaal: O da keŋ Queens' College, University of Cambridge dinɛ yi 1935 ti paae 1938 ni.
english: He attended Queens' College, University of Cambridge from 1935 to 1938.

kusaal: O da kilim lawyer bɛ 1956 ni.
english: He became a lawyer in 1956.

kusaal: O tɔn' anɛ Susan Ofori-Atta, yiiga pʋ'a kani kilim physician Ghana nwa ni.
english: His sister was Susan Ofori-Atta, the first Ghanaian woman to become a physician.

kusaal: William Ofori Atta da anɛ onɛ pɛ'ɛs banɛ pin'il United Gold Coast Convention la onɛ da pɛ'ɛsi bɛ 1947 ni la.
english: William Ofori Atta was a founding member of the United Gold Coast Convention after joining in 1947.

kusaal: O da di Akim Abuakwa kuk la yinne dinɛ bɛ 1951 Gold Coast vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: He won one of the Akim Abuakwa seats during the 1951 Gold Coast election.

kusaal: O da lɛm an tuongat tis United Party dinɛ bɛ di kɔn' nɛ Dr Kwame Nkrumah paati la.
english: He later became the leader of the United Party in opposition to Dr Kwame Nkrumah.

kusaal: Ofori Atta ka Nkrumah da vɛ'ɛd saŋkani da an yiiga republic bɛ Preventive Detention Act la ni.
english: Ofori Atta was detained by Nkrumah during the first republic under the Preventive Detention Act.

kusaal: Republic ayi' ni la, o da zi'en tis Akwatia nidib la an yiiga Mp tis Second Republic la, o da lɛm anɛ Minister for Education nɛ Minister for Foreign Affairs bɛ Progress Party government bɛ Dr.
english: During the second republic, he represented the people of Akwatia as a member of the 1st Parliament of the Second Republic, he was also the Minister for Education and then Minister for Foreign Affairs in the Progress Party government of Dr. Busia.

kusaal: O da anɛ ninkpiɛŋ tis People's Movement bɛ Freedom and Justice (PMFJ) dinɛ ka o da nwɛ' pɔlitiks tʋ'ʋs 'Union Government' dinɛ ka General I. K. Acheampong da mɔr, onɛ da an Head of state tis Ghana nɛ Chairman tis Supreme Military Council (SMC).
english: He was an active member of the People's Movement for Freedom and Justice (PMFJ) which campaigned against the 'Union Government' concept by General I. K. Acheampong, then Head of state of Ghana and Chairman of the Supreme Military Council (SMC).

kusaal: SMC liig la nya'aŋ, o da zi'eni bɔɔd zugdaan bɛ 1979 Ghana vɔɔtʋg la bɛ United National Convention ka bɛ atan' ka mɔr 17.41% yi vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: After the fall of the SMC, he stood for president in the 1979 Ghanaian presidential election on the ticket of the United National Convention coming third with 17.41 per cent of the popular vote.

kusaal: Onɛ da an chairman tis Council of State bɛ Third Republic.
english: Eventually, he became chairman of the Council of State for the Third Republic.

kusaal: William Ofori Atta da kenna an Christian ka tʋm bɛdigʋ tis Christian tʋʋma nam ni.
english: William Ofori Atta became a devout Christian and played various roles in Christian circles.

kusaal: O da pɛ'ɛs banɛ pin'il Accra Chapel Trust, (nanna yʋ'ʋn an Korle-Bu Community Chapel) di anɛ evangelical church bɛ Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Accra bɛ 1967 ni.
english: He was one of the founders of the Accra Chapel Trust, (now the Korle-Bu Community Chapel) an independent evangelical church at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra in 1967.

kusaal: Ofori Atta da tis J. B. Danquah Memorial Lectures tu'am dinɛ ka Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences da na'am la bɛ 1985.
english: Ofori Atta delivered the J. B. Danquah Memorial Lectures organised by the Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences in 1985.

kusaal: O da kpinɛ 1988 ka ba da tis o state burial.
english: He died in 1988 and was given a state burial.

kusaal: Onɛ o sakur taaba la pin'il intermediate degree programs la.
english: His batch of students also pioneered the intermediate degree programs.

kusaal: Nɛ' nam wʋsa da pɛ'ɛsi kɛ' ka University of Ghana zi'en.
english: This arrangements went on to form the nucleus of the University of Ghana.

kusaal: O pia'azug da anɛ – "Ghana, teŋkani mɔr yɛla".
english: His topic was – "Ghana, A Nation in Crisis".

kusaal: O da anɛ mp tis Akropong Constituency dinɛ bɛ Eastern region of Ghana bɛ 4th, 5th nɛ 6th Parliament tis 4th Republic of Ghana.
english: He was the Member of Parliament representing Akropong Constituency in the Eastern region of Ghana in the 4th, 5th and 6th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ University of Ghana sakur biig kʋdʋg.
english: He is a product of the University of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr Bachelor of Law degree yit university la ni.
english: He obtained a Bachelor of Law degree from the university.

kusaal: O lɛm anɛ Ghana School of Law sakur biig kʋdʋg dinɛ ka o kɛŋ tuoni zamisi paam Bachelor of Law degree bɛ 1970 ni.
english: He is also a product of the Ghana School of Law where he furthered his law education and had Bachelor of Law degree.

kusaal: Boafo anɛ lɔya ka pɛ'ɛsi bɛ Onimpa Akouku & Company ni.
english: He was a partner at Onimpa Akouku & Company.

kusaal: O da anɛ 4th, 5th nɛ 6th mp tis 7th Parliament bɛ Republic of Ghana ka da zi'en kuk la zug bɛ January 2005 ni.
english: He was a member of the 4th, 5th and 6th parliament and also a current member of the 7th Parliament of the Republic of Ghana assuming office in January 2005.

kusaal: Boafo ba da vɔɔt o Mp tis Akropong constituency dinɛ bɛ Eastern Region of Ghana an yiiga daan bɛ 2004 yʋʋm la ni bɛ Ghana sɔ' wʋsa vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: Boafo was elected as the member of parliament for the Akropong constituency of the Eastern Region of Ghana for the first time in the 2004 Ghanaian general elections.

kusaal: O constituency la da pɛ'ɛs mpnam 22 bani da di yi mpnam 28 bani da bɛ NPP ka di bɛ Eastern Region la ni.
english: His constituency was a part of the 22 parliamentary seats out of 28 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Eastern Region.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o nɛ vɔɔtnam 21,655 yit vɔɔtnam 34,199 ni pʋʋgʋn ka mɔr 63.3% yi vɔɔtʋg la ni wʋsa.
english: He was elected with 21,655 votes out of 34,199 total valid votes cast equivalent to 63.3% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O da paam ka bas Ohene Nyarkoh onɛ bɛ People's National Convention, Richie Agyemfra-Kumi onɛ bɛ National Democratic Congress, Kwabena Awuku-Lokko onɛ bɛ Convention People's Party nɛ Ronni Nanan Esi Botsio onɛ da zi'eni o kɔn' ka ba ye independent la.
english: He was elected over Ohene Nyarkoh of the People's National Convention, Richie Agyemfra-Kumi of the National Democratic Congress, Kwabena Awuku-Lokko of the Convention People's Party and Ronni Nanan Esi Botsio an independent candidate .

kusaal: 2008 nii, o di vɔɔtʋg la wʋsa bɛ New Patriotic Party la ni bɛ constituency kan la nɔɔ.
english: In 2008, he won the general elections on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party for the same constituency.

kusaal: O constituency la da pɛ'ɛs mp zi'is 19 yit mp nam 28 bɛ New Patriotic Party bɛ Eastern Region ni.
english: His constituency was part of the 19 parliamentary seats out of 28 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Eastern Region.

kusaal: Wabig paati la di majoriti nɛ mp nam 109 yit mp zi'is 230.
english: The New Patriotic Party won a minority total of 109 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔt o nɛ vɔɔtnam 20,245 yit vɔɔtnam 34,350 ka mɔr 58.94% bɛ vɔɔtʋg bani vɔɔt la ni.
english: He was elected with 20,245 votes out of 34,350 total valid votes cast equivalent to 58.94% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O da di ka bas Hawa Isaka onɛ bɛ People's National Convention, Anthony Gyampo onɛ bɛ National Democratic Congress, Augustus Osae-Akonnor onɛ bɛ Convention People's Party Samuel Apenteng onɛ zi'eni o kɔn'.
english: He was elected over Hawa Isaka of the People's National Convention, Anthony Gyampo of the National Democratic Congress, Augustus Osae-Akonnor of the Convention People's Party Samuel Apenteng an independent candidate.

kusaal: Boafo du'am yʋʋm anɛ December 30, 1946.
english: Boafo was born on December 30, 1946.

kusaal: O yitnɛ Akropong, teŋpʋbil yinne kani bɛ Eastern region, Ghana.
english: He hails from Akropong, a town in the Eastern region of Ghana.

kusaal: Boafo anɛ New Patriotic Party nid.
english: Boafo is a member of New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da lɛm zi'eni mp vɔɔtʋg la bɛ Akropong Constituency la ni.
english: He contested for re-election into the Akropong Constituency Parliamentary seat in all subsequent Ghanaian General Elections and won them.

kusaal: O nɔknɛ New Patriotic Party paati la di.
english: His constituency was a part of the 22 parliamentary seats out of 28 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in that election for the Eastern Region.

kusaal: Wabig paati la da di mp nam bɛdigʋ ka fu ya'a la'asi ba ka ba duoe mp nam 128 yi mp nam 230 la ni.
english: The New Patriotic Party won a majority total of 128 parliamentary seats out of 230 seats.

kusaal: Boafo mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biig yinne.
english: Boafo is married with one child.

kusaal: Nɛ' nwa da maali bɛ1969 ni.
english: This was in 1969.

kusaal: William Owuraku Aidoo (Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ anaasi, Yʋʋmpaal nwadig la dabpistan' daar, (30 January 1964) ka o an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka an wadmaani paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paas ayɔpɔi nɛ anii Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni tis Afigya Kwabre South Constituency bɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg, New Patriotic Party nɔba zug.
english: William Owuraku Aidoo (born 30 January 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana and the 8th Parliament of the Fourth republic of Ghana, representing the Afigya Kwabre South Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Hemang-Kwabre bɛɛ Ashanti Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: He hails from Hemang-Kwabre in the Ashanti Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O da maali o GCE O Level nɛ Tetrem Secondary School nɛ A Level certificate bɛnɛ St Augustine's College.
english: He got his GCE O Level from Tetrem Secondary School and A Level certificate from St Augustine's College.

kusaal: O da di'e o Bachelor of Arts degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ in Entrepreneurship yinɛ Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anu la ni (2005).
english: He received his Bachelor of Arts degree in Entrepreneurship from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) in 2005.

kusaal: On da nam pʋ kpɛn' pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛbin la, o da anɛ managing director tis Kucons Company Limited, a construction company kanɛ gaad ka maan mu'aa.
english: Prior to entering politics, he was the managing director of Kucons Company Limited, a construction company involved in the construction and rehabilitation of dams.

kusaal: O da anɛ Senior Superintendent gbaʋŋ zamisʋg lʋgʋr la ni din yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ yinne (1991) ti paae yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (1994) ka lɛn an Senior Manager tis Ghana Commercial Bank (GCB) din yi yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piswai nɛ anu (1995) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni (2012).
english: He was a Senior Superintendent at the Ghana Education Service (GES) between 1991 and 1994 and a Senior Manager at the Ghana Commercial Bank (GCB) from 1995 until 2012.

kusaal: On da tʋm bank ni la, o da lɛn anɛ pa'an-pa'an (lecturer) ya'as bɛ University of Education, Winneba ni din yi yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ awai (2009) ti paae yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayi' la ni (2012).
english: While working at the bank, he doubled as a lecturer at the University of Education, Winneba from 2009 to 2012.

kusaal: William Owuraku Aidoo da kpɛn' wadmaanib yin la yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ atan' Yʋʋm paal Nwadig la daba ayɔpɔi daar (7 January 2013) zi'eni tis Afigya Kwabre South constituency zi'en Wabʋg Na'adɔɔg nɔba zug, New Patriotic Party.
english: William Owuraku Aidoo entered parliament on 7 January 2013 as the representative of the Afigya Kwabre South constituency on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O da nyi'a yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ (2016) wadmaanib vɔɔdʋg la ka di.
english: He contested the seat again during the 2016 parliamentary elections and won.

kusaal: William da nyi'a yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pisi (2020) vɔɔdʋg la ka di keŋ wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi anii Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la ni.
english: William was reelected again in the 2020 General election for the 8th Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.
