english: The NBA and the NYSAC sometimes crowned different "world champions" in the same division, leading to confusion about who was the real champion.

kusaal: Di da nwɛnɛ American Association of Boxing Commissions an si'em nananna la, NBA da mɔr tʋbtɛɛgir tis title bouts, mɔɔn banɛ bɛ suor ye ba zab, nɛ si'elnam bɛdegʋ, amaa ka da pʋ mɔ' ye di gaanis di mɛŋ kpɛɛmbanɛ na gɔsidi title bout yɛla bɛɛba nɔki ban mɛŋ bɔɔdim kpɛn'ɛs championship zaba la nii.
english: Originally more comparable to the present American Association of Boxing Commissions than to its offspring and successor, the NBA sanctioned title bouts, published lists of outstanding challengers, withdrew titular recognition, but did not attempt to appoint its own title bout officials or otherwise impose its will on championship fights.

kusaal: NBA da tiaki lieb WBA nyain nɛ 23 August 1962.
english: The NBA officially became the WBA on 23 August 1962.

kusaal: Gilberto Mendoza da an WBA zuraan din yi 1982 kem paae o kum 2016, din nya'aŋ ka Gilberto Mendoza Jr.
english: Gilberto Mendoza was the President of the WBA from 1982 until his death in 2016, after which Gilberto Mendoza Jr. took over as president.

kusaal: 1990s ni, WBA da yisi ba ɔfisnam Panama City, Panama, keŋ Caracas, Venezuela.
english: In the 1990s, the WBA moved its central offices from Panama City, Panama, to Caracas, Venezuela.

kusaal: January 2007, ka ba lɛ mɔr ɔfisnam la lɛbis Panama.
english: In January 2007, it returned its offices to Panama.

kusaal: WBA pʋd nɛ'ɛŋa nɛ ye Man of Triumph belt, ba da sigi dinɛ daʋ kanɛ da di Mayweather vs.
english: The WBA called this the Man of Triumph belt, named after the trophy awarded to the winner of the Mayweather vs. Pacquiao fight.

kusaal: Banɛ di'e sanlima din la sieba anɛ Anthony Joshua, Vasyl Lomachenko, Manny Pacquiao, Oleksandr Usyk, Canelo Álvarez nɛ Callum Smith.
english: Other recipients of the custom gold-plated belt are Anthony Joshua, Vasyl Lomachenko, Manny Pacquiao, Oleksandr Usyk, Canelo Álvarez and Callum Smith.

kusaal: WBA da tikya ye ba na tʋm nɛ amateur governing body, International Boxing Association yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ pisi nɛ ayi (2022).
english: The WBA signed a cooperation agreement with the Russian-led amateur governing body International Boxing Association in 2022.

kusaal: · Federación Latinoamericana de Comisiones de Boxeo Profesional (WBA Fedelatin)
english: Federación Latinoamericana de Comisiones de Boxeo Profesional (WBA Fedelatin)

kusaal: · Federación Bolivariana de Boxeo (WBA Fedebol)
english: Federación Bolivariana de Boxeo (WBA Fedebol)

kusaal: · Federación Centroamericana de Boxeo (WBA Fedecentro)
english: Federación Centroamericana de Boxeo (WBA Fedecentro)

kusaal: · Federación del Caribe de Boxeo (WBA Fedecaribe)
english: Federación del Caribe de Boxeo (WBA Fedecaribe)

kusaal: · North American Boxing Association (NABA)
english: North American Boxing Association (NABA)

kusaal: WBA tisid dunia wʋsa championship title nɛ professional level.
english: The WBA awards its world championship title at the professional level.

kusaal: World Boxing Association yinɛ dinɛ da an National Boxing Association, ka ba da pin'ili di 1921 la.
english: The WBA can be traced back to the original National Boxing Association, organized in 1921.

kusaal: Din yi 2015, WBA piinɛ WBA Super champion belt tisid zabtita'akanɛ an WBA championship.
english: Since 2015, the WBA awards a customized version of their WBA Super champion belt to big fights involving a WBA championship.

kusaal: da di'e yiiga dinɛ ka di pilate la da an sanlim la ka Manny Pacquiao da di'e one-time rhodium plated.
english: Floyd Mayweather Jr. received the first gold-plated version of the belt while Manny Pacquiao was awarded a one-time rhodium-plated version.

kusaal: Belt la pilate mɔrnɛ zabzabidiba ayi banɛ zabid la footonam the.
english: The plate of the belt has the images of the two boxers fighting.

kusaal: International Boxing Hall of Fame (IBHOF) da bas suor ka di lieb dunia wʋsa championship la'asʋg nama anaasi la yinne, ban nɛ World Boxing Association (WBA), World Boxing Council (WBC), nɛ International Boxing Federation (IBF).
english: It is recognized by the International Boxing Hall of Fame (IBHOF) as one of the four major world championship groups, alongside the World Boxing Association (WBA), World Boxing Council (WBC), and International Boxing Federation (IBF).

kusaal: WBO ɔfis tita'ar bɛnɛ San Juan, Puerto Rico.
english: The WBO's headquarters are located in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

kusaal: WBO da pin'ili yinɛ Puerto Rican nɛ Dominican dap banɛ an kpikpikpinnibi da aaen yi WBA yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnii nɛ anii (1988) yʋʋm-yʋʋm la'asʋg dinɛ da bɛ Isla Margarita, Venezuela dɔlisid nɔŋgbannwa'ar wada banɛ ka ba na nɔki tʋm yɛla.
english: The WBO started after a group of Puerto Rican and Dominican businessmen broke out of the WBA's 1988 annual convention in Isla Margarita, Venezuela over disputes regarding what rules should be applied.

kusaal: WBO yiiga zuraan da anɛ Ramon Pina Acevedo onɛ yi Dominican Republic.
english: The WBO's first president was Ramon Pina Acevedo of the Dominican Republic.

kusaal: Di yiiga championship zaba da anɛ super middleweight title, ka Thomas Hearns nɛ James Kinchen da zab; Hearns da diya dɔlisid gban'ar.
english: Its first championship fight was for its vacant super middleweight title, between Thomas Hearns and James Kinchen; Hearns won by decision.

kusaal: Ban da bɔɔd na'asi la, WBO da vɔɔti gaŋ dunia wʋsa light heavyweight champion José Torres onɛ yi Ponce, Puerto Rico, ye o aan di zuraan.
english: In order to gain respectability, the WBO next elected former world light heavyweight champion José Torres of Ponce, Puerto Rico, as its president.

kusaal: Torres da yi 1996, ka bas suori tis Puerto Rican lɔya Francisco Valcarcel ye o an zuraan.
english: Torres left in 1996, giving way to Puerto Rican lawyer Francisco Valcarcel as president.

kusaal: 2022 Russian da faand Ukraine la, WBO da gu'oe championship zaba kanɛ ka Russi nid nɛ Belarusian zab zabid da ye ba zab.
english: In response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the WBO blocked championship fights involving Russian and Belarusian boxers.

kusaal: Zabzabidib banɛ di'e WBO Super Champion anɛ: Anthony Joshua, Wladimir Klitschko, Oleksandr Usyk, Joe Calzaghe, Oscar De La Hoya, Bernard Hopkins, Jermain Taylor, Kelly Pavlik, Saúl Álvarez, Juan Manuel Márquez, Juan Díaz, Manny Pacquiao, Timothy Bradley, Marco Antonio Barrera, Fernando Montiel, Jorge Arce, Omar Narváez, Donnie Nietes, Kosei Tanaka, Iván Calderón, Marco Huck, Sergey Kovalev, Vasyl Lomachenko, nɛ Terence Crawford.
english: Boxers who have been named WBO Super Champion include: Anthony Joshua, Wladimir Klitschko, Oleksandr Usyk (Cruiserweight & Heavyweight), Joe Calzaghe, Oscar De La Hoya, Bernard Hopkins, Jermain Taylor, Kelly Pavlik, Saúl Álvarez, Juan Manuel Márquez, Juan Díaz, Naoya Inoue, Manny Pacquiao, Timothy Bradley, Marco Antonio Barrera, Acelino Freitas, Jorge Arce, Omar Narváez, Donnie Nietes, Kosei Tanaka, Iván Calderón, Marco Huck, Sergey Kovalev, Vasyl Lomachenko, and Terence Crawford.

kusaal: Pʋ'aba ayi ma'aa an zabzabidib ka di'e "Super Champion" kpɛŋ: Amanda Serrano nɛ Claressa Shields.
english: There are currently only two female boxers who earned the distinction of "Super Champion": Amanda Serrano and Claressa Shields.

kusaal: Japanese manga series Bleach dinɛ an series naar (finale) la da giligidnɛ ka wʋrʋg la gɔsid zabkanɛ ka Yasutora Sado da paas, on da lieb professional boxer yʋʋm piiga nya'aŋ ka da nya' WBO world heavyweight championship la.
english: The series finale of Japanese manga series Bleach revolves around the main cast gathering to watch a fight in which a character named Yasutora Sado is involved, having become a professional boxer ten years after the storyline and challenging for the WBO world heavyweight championship.

kusaal: di ɛɛnti paas ninwisigiri lʋgsieba din ka ba da kɛ ka René Santiago da zabi tis North American Boxing Organization minimumweight title gɛɛs Fernando Tonos ka di paas professional wrestling ka da bɛ International Wrestling Association (IWA-PR).
english: The entity has, on occasion, been involved in other areas of sports entertainment, such as when it allowed René Santiago to defend the North American Boxing Organization minimumweight title in a staged match against Fernando Tonos as part of a professional wrestling card held by the International Wrestling Association (IWA-PR).

kusaal: WBO World Heavyweight Championship da lɛn nwɛnɛ minor storyline element nɛ Creed III.
english: The WBO World Heavyweight Championship also appears as a minor storyline element in Creed III, as one of the belts held by the titular character as undisputed titlist of his division.

kusaal: World Boxing Organization (WBO) anɛ la'askanɛ tɛɛgid professional boxing bouts tʋbir.
english: The World Boxing Organization (WBO) is an organization which sanctions professional boxing bouts.

kusaal: On da pin'il la nya'aŋ, WBO da maan dunia wʋsa championship bouts dunia wʋsa.
english: Soon after its beginning, the WBO was staging world championship bouts around the globe.

kusaal: WBO dap championship belts anɛ zinzauk, ka pʋ'ab championship belts an pink.
english: WBO men's championship belts are brown, whereas women's championship belts are pink.

kusaal: Din yi yʋʋm tusa ayi (2000) la ni, WBO piinl zabzabidib sieba "Super Champion" kpɛŋ tɛbisim kɔn'ɔb kɔn'ɔb ni.
english: By 2000, the WBA was giving the same recognition to WBO champions as it did to WBC and IBF champions.

kusaal: Banɛ paas WHA ni la la'asid taaba yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin nwadis anu ni (May) bɛ Geneva zin'ig kanɛ ka ba buon Palace of Nations, ka di bɛ WHO tʋʋma zin'ig tita'ar la ni.
english: The members of the WHA generally meet every year in May in Geneva, Switzerland, at the Palace of Nations, the location of WHO Headquarters.

kusaal: World Health Assembly (WHA) anɛ lʋgir kanɛ gɔsid World Health Organization (WHO) nɛ din paae tɛns kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (194) si'eba la.
english: The World Health Assembly (WHA) is the forum through which the World Health Organization (WHO) is governed by its 193 member states.

kusaal: Ba tʋʋma anɛ ye ba gban'ae gba'asa, ka mɛ bas suor ka WHO dim tʋmi ba tʋʋma ka gɔsi ba ligidi kʋʋb pʋʋgin ka mɛ lɛn gaŋi ba kpɛn'ɛm kanɛ ka ba buon Director-General (yʋʋma anu wʋsa pʋʋgin) ka yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin ka ba gan'asidi nidib piiga banɛ ka ba an ba kpɛɛmnam.
english: The main tasks of the WHA are to decide major policy questions, as well as to approve the WHO work programme and budget and elect its Director-General (every fifth year) and annually to elect ten members to renew part of its executive board.

kusaal: Dina an dunia wʋsa lʋgir kanɛ maan laafi yela wada ka ninbanɛ paasi li pʋʋgin anɛ tɛŋ banɛ paasi di pʋʋgin la minister banɛ gɔsid laafi yela ba tɛnsin.
english: It is the world's highest health policy setting body and is composed of health ministers from member states.

kusaal: Di mɔr la'ad bɛdigʋ, nɛ tʋmtʋmnib, nɛ tɛn'ɛs bɛdigʋ laafi la'asig kanɛ ka ba buon League of Nations' Health Organization nɛ Office International d'Hygiène Publique dinɛ bɛ Paris la, ka bani paas an International Classification of Diseases (ICD).
english: It incorporated the assets, personnel, and duties of the League of Nations' Health Organization and the Paris-based Office International d'Hygiène Publique, including the International Classification of Diseases (ICD).

kusaal: WHA anɛ banɛ gaŋid ka mɛ lɛn sa'an laafi yela kpɛɛmnam ban pistan' nɛ anaasi (34); ka gaŋid kpɛɛm banɛ an Chief administrator, Director-General (one an nananna anɛ Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, one yit Ethiopia la); banɛ gban'ad gban'asa; ka bas suor ka ba tʋm tʋʋmsi'eba bɛɛ da'a la'ad.
english: The WHA elects and advises an executive board made up of 34 health specialists; selects the WHO's chief administrator, the director-general (currently Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus of Ethiopia); sets goals and priorities; and approves the budget and activities.

kusaal: Di tʋʋma dɔtita'ar bɛnɛ Geneva, Switzerland sʋ'ʋlim, Di mɔr tʋʋma zin'is titada ayuobʋ nɛ tʋʋma zin'is bibis kɔbiga nɛ pisnu duni wʋsa ni.
english: It is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and has six regional offices and 150 field offices worldwide.

kusaal: Ba labaya gbaŋ kanɛ ka ba buon World Health Report la, mɔr labaya kati wa'ae dunia wʋsa laafi yela.
english: The WHO regularly publishes a World Health Report, its leading publication, including an expert assessment of a specific global health topic.

kusaal: Ba gaad tuoni tʋm tʋʋma hali laafi yela, ba tʋʋm sʋma la si'eba anɛ ba nyaŋi kad ban'a kanɛ buon smallpox la, ka polio mɛ kpɛlim bi'ela ka ba kad o, nɛ ban lɛn nyaŋi maal Ebola pin'im la.
english: The WHO has played a leading role in several public health achievements, most notably the eradication of smallpox, the near-eradication of polio, and the development of an Ebola vaccine.

kusaal: Ban yʋ'ʋn gɔsid ban'a si'eba nananna anɛ ban'as banɛ lɔmisid wʋʋ HIV/AIDS, Ebola, malaria nɛ tuberculosis; ban'as banɛ pʋ lɔmisida ka ba si'eba an sʋsʋnya ban's nɛ dindiig ban'a (cancer); laafi diib yela, di'sʋma yela, nutrition, nɛ diib sʋ'ab yela; tʋmtʋmnib laafi; nɛ banɛ la'asid tiima nʋʋd ka li pʋ dɔl suor la yela.
english: Its current priorities include communicable diseases, such as HIV/AIDS, Ebola, malaria and tuberculosis; non-communicable diseases such as heart disease and cancer; healthy diet, nutrition, and food security; occupational health; and substance abuse.

kusaal: Lʋgir kanɛ gɔsidi ba tʋʋma anɛ World Health Assembly (WHA), dinɛ ka tɛns kɔbiga nɛ piswai nɛ anaasi (194) paasi di pʋʋgin.
english: The World Health Assembly (WHA) is the legislative and supreme body of the WHO.

kusaal: Ba tʋʋma anɛ ye ba sʋŋ ka laafi yela kɛŋ tuon ka ba sʋŋ banɛ an tadimnam dunia wʋsa.
english: The agency advocates for universal health care coverage, engagement with the monitoring of public health risks, coordinating responses to health emergencies, and promoting health and well-being generally.

kusaal: Ba sʋŋid tɛns nɛ tʋʋma la'ad, ka tisidi ba laafi nyɛɛb wada, ka di'esid labaya laafi yela dunia wʋsa, ka anina ka la'asidi sɔnsid na'asaasɔn'ɔg nɛ wada banɛ bɛ laafi yela.
english: It provides technical assistance to countries, sets international health standards, collects data on global health issues, and serves as a forum for scientific or policy discussions related to health.

kusaal: Lʋgir nwa' mɔɔd ye laafi yela paae sɔ' wʋsa dunia ni, ka gɔsid dinɛ na nyaŋi mɔr ban'asi kɛna yela, ka sʋŋid ka ban'as gad tɔ'ɔtɔ', ka kpɛn gɔsid nɛ bʋn dinɛ an laafi yela wʋsa vuguri.
english: The agency advocates for universal health care coverage, engagement with the monitoring of public health risks, coordinating responses to health emergencies, and promoting health and well-being generally.

kusaal: Kordofan melons yitnɛ Sudan ka mɔr kpinnim nɛ banɛ kuod watamilo paalis bɛɛ saamis.
english: Kordofan melons from Sudan are the closest relatives and may be progenitors of modern, cultivated watermelons.

kusaal: Ba da nyɛ nɛ watamilo biili la nɛ mɔɔgʋnɛ kpi'e nɛ Uan Muhuggiag la.Banɛ gɔsid yɛl banɛ naam sa yɛlla bɛ Libya teŋin la daa vɛɛns nyɛ biili nwa yʋʋm 3500 BC.
english: Wild watermelon seeds were found in Uan Muhuggiag, a prehistoric site in Libya that dates to approximately 3500 BC.

kusaal: Citrullis lanatus, buudi caffer, nɔbigid mɔɔgin Kalahari Desert, anina ka ba buoni li ye tsamma.
english: Citrullis lanatus, variety caffer, grows wild in the Kalahari Desert, where it is known as tsamma.

kusaal: Wɔtamɛlɔn anɛ bʋnbʋta banɛ banɛ ka ba kuod zin'is banɛ ka tʋʋlig bɛ, ka lin bɔɔd tʋʋlig si'em bɛn nar ye li gaad 25 °C (77 °F) ka ba nyaŋi nɔbig.
english: Watermelons grow in tropical to temperate climates, needing temperatures higher than 25 °C (77 °F) to thrive.

kusaal: Wɔtamɛlɔn ka sieba buon ye watamilo la anɛ bʋmbʋtir kanɛ puud la buudi yinne kanɛ bɛ Cucurbitaceae ni, linɛ mɔri wɛlditir tita'ar.
english: The watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is a species of flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae, that has a large, edible fruit.

kusaal: yʋʋm 2022 la ni, ka ba lɛn vɛɛns ka ye, watamilo biili pʋn bɛ wʋʋ yʋma tusa yuobu, 6,000-year-old ka di bɛ Libya pipirisin wɛn wʋʋ Nigerian nyiiri biili nɛ bɛ west Africa sʋ'ʋlʋm la.
english: In 2022, a study was released that traced 6,000-year-old watermelon seeds found in the Libyan desert to the Egusi seeds of Nigeria, West Africa. Watermelons were domesticated in Sudan and cultivated in Egypt by 2000 BC; an image of an apparent one on a tray has been found in an Egyptian tomb dating at least to 4000 years ago.

kusaal: Watamilo da dɛŋin kuod nɛ north-east Africa sʋ'ʋlʋm nɛ Egypt wʋʋ yʋʋm 2000 BC la ni, amaa saŋa kan la ba da nam pʋ malisi wan wʋʋ nannanna bʋnam laa.
english: In 2022, a study was released that traced 6,000-year-old watermelon seeds found in the Libyan desert to the Egusi seeds of Nigeria, West Africa. Watermelons were domesticated in Sudan and cultivated in Egypt by 2000 BC; an image of an apparent one on a tray has been found in an Egyptian tomb dating at least to 4000 years ago.

kusaal: Li na tun'e tiɛn wa'am paae wʋʋ mitanam 3 (10 feet) ka li ya'am la bɛɛ bullin la mɔr gbɛɛnd zɛn'ɛʋg.
english: Stems are up to 3 metres (10 feet) long and new growth has yellow or brown hairs.

kusaal: Gɛndir yinnɛ wʋsa nyaŋid puud puum daag bɛɛ puum nya'aŋ ka li an piel bɛɛ dɔnbʋʋlʋm ka wa'am agɔl wʋʋ milimitanam 40 (1+1⁄2 in) ka mɔr gbɛɛnd bɛdigʋ ginnir la ni.
english: Plants have unisexual male or female flowers that are white or yellow and borne on 40-millimetre-long (1+1⁄2 in) hairy stalks.

kusaal: Mɔɔgin bʋnam la wɛla anɛ wʋʋ 20 cm (8 in) zu'or pʋʋgin ka dinɛ ka ba bʋt la wɛla zu'olum mɛ na tun'e gaad wʋʋ 60 cm (24 in).
english: Wild plants have fruits up to 20 cm (8 in) in diameter, while cultivated varieties may exceed 60 cm (24 in).

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbis yɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ atan' (1753) la ni, Carl Linnaeus da ba da an onɛ pa'alɛ di yɛla yiiga ka pʋdi yʋ'ʋr yee Cucurbita citrullus.
english: The sweet watermelon was first described by Carl Linnaeus in 1753 and given the name Cucurbita citrullus.

kusaal: Bʋnvʋya banɛ san'amid wɔtamɛlɔn anɛ aphids, fruit flies, nɛ root-knot nematodes.
english: Major pests of the watermelon include aphids, fruit flies, and root-knot nematodes.

kusaal: Zin'ig kanɛ ka kuom bɛ hali, wiim tɔ'ɔe li nɛ wan wʋʋ powdery mildew nɛ mosaic virus.
english: In conditions of high humidity, the plants are prone to plant diseases such as powdery mildew and mosaic virus.

kusaal: BA kuod si'eba bɛ Japan nɛ ya'nya'aŋ ka fusarium wilt wiim la da tɔ'ɔe ba.
english: Some varieties often grown in Japan and other parts of the Far East are susceptible to fusarium wilt.

kusaal: Wɔtamɛlɔn banɛ ka ba buon tsamma ka li bɛ Khoisan language nɛ makataan bɛ Tswana buudi pian'ad ni la, anɛ banɛ mɔr kuom hali bɛ South Africa, Kalahari Desert, nɛ East Africa tisid nidib nɛ bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa.
english: Watermelons are an important water source in South Africa, the Kalahari Desert, and East Africa for both humans and animals.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi ni (2020), dunia wʋsa wɔtamɛlɔn da anɛ 101.6 million tonnes, ka China (mainland) tɛŋin mɔr pisyuobʋ kɔbiga pʋʋgin (60%) dunia wʋsa din la (60.1 million tonnes).
english: In 2023, world production of watermelons was 105 million tonnes, led by China (mainland) accounting for 64% of the total (table).

kusaal: Banɛ da dɔl nya'aŋ ka li maali ba tɛŋin sʋ'ʋŋa anɛ Turkey, India, Iran, Algeria nɛ Brazil – ba wʋsa yʋʋm la pʋʋgin wɔtamɛlɔn da maal paae 2–3 million tonnes yʋʋm tusayi nɛ pisi ni (2020).
english: Secondary producers were India, Turkey, Algeria, and Brazil.

kusaal: Li anɛ tʋŋ kanɛ tɛɛnd ka vin ka ba bʋti li dʋnia nwa zin'is bɛdigʋ ni.
english: It is a scrambling and trailing vine-like plant, and is widely cultivated worldwide, with more than 1,000 varieties.

kusaal: watamilo gɛndir anɛ dinɛ aadimid wila bɛdigʋ.
english: Major pests of the watermelon include aphids, fruit flies, and root-knot nematodes.

kusaal: Li biili la mɔr nyʋʋg kanɛ malis ka ba dɛligid ka sɛn'ɛdi li bɛɛ ba nɛɛmi li ka li kilim zɔ'ɔm.
english: The fruit can be eaten raw or pickled, and the rind is edible after cooking.

kusaal: Si'el ya'a kae anina na zi puum di puum la gɛndig taaba, wala la tita'am ku mɔr biili li pʋʋginɛ, ala ka li nar ye siins dɔɔg la an wan wʋʋ atan' eka wʋsa pʋʋgin (1,300 m2 wʋsa ka siins bɛ).
english: Since the supply of viable pollen is reduced, and pollination is much more critical in producing the seedless variety, the recommended number of hives per acre increases to three hives per acre (1,300 m2 per hive).

kusaal: Xi'an guyue (Chinese: 西安鼓乐), bɛɛ Shaanxi guyue (陕西鼓乐), anɛ Chinese ritual music malima ka mɔr sisi'em li pʋʋgin ka li da yi nɛ Xi'an, linɛ Shaanxi sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Xi'an guyue (Chinese: 西安鼓乐), also Shaanxi guyue (陕西鼓乐), is the regional Chinese ritual music genre featuring a type of wind and percussion ensemble named for its place of origin, Xi'an, in Shaanxi Province.

kusaal: Maliŋ kaŋa da bɛ hali yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyuobu saŋa (1960), yʋʋm tusayi nɛ awai (2009) ka li kpɛn'ɛ UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List malima kanl pʋʋgin.
english: A folk genre, sustained by amateur groups before the 1960s, it was placed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List in 2009.

kusaal: Bunwɛ'ɛda nwa' pʋdig nɛ zin'is ayi, dɔlnɛ ban wa'adi li siem, zin'ig nɛ kɛn (zin'ig la mɔr yʋ'ʋma), nɛ zin'is atan' ka li kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb anɛ lin yi zin'ig siya na, Buddhist (Seng), Daoist (Dao), nɛ secular (Su).
english: The music is split into two categories based on performance, sitting and walking (the latter including chorus), and into three repertoires based on transmission, Buddhist (Seng), Daoist (Dao), and secular (Su).

kusaal: Yʋʋma dim banɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋr yi sieba an An Laixu (安来绪, 1895-1977), Daoist master onɛ yit Xi'an's Chenghuangmiao pʋ'ʋsum dɔɔg.
english: Famous musicians include An Laixu (安来绪, 1895-1977), Daoist master of Xi'an's Chenghuangmiao temple.

kusaal: Sieba buoni li ye Xi'an drum music ba zi'ilim zug.
english: It is also, somewhat misleadingly, called Xi'an drum music.

kusaal: Tang dynasty buudi la da maani li bɛdegu (na'asi nɛ pʋtɛn'ɛr kanɛ bɛɛ li pʋʋgin la yela), malima nwa mɛ da bɛ Ming nɛ Qing dɔɔdin.
english: Though associated with the Tang dynasty (due to its prestige and history), the genre shares more with the late Ming and Qing dynasties.

kusaal: Ba da paas bʋnwɛ'ɛda nwɛnni pipa nɛ daqin (bɛɛ zheng), wʋʋ lin bɛ gongche gbana pʋʋgin la.
english: The ensembles formerly included other instruments, such as the pipa and daqin (presumably the zheng), as witnessed in gongche manuscripts.

kusaal: Ba da vɔɔti tis o Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) vɔɔtʋg la ni, ka o da di vɔɔt la ka di kal an tʋsir, kɔbistan nɛ pistan (1, 330) gaad onɛ da nya'a paas la, ka da di vɔɔt la lieb wadmaani tis sʋ'ʋlim la.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and won a majority of 1,330 votes more than candidate closest in the race, to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: O da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug nɛ 4th Republic Parliament dɔlisid National Democratic Congress.
english: He had represented the constituency in the 4th Republican parliament on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Onɛ an wadmaani tis constituency la nananna anɛ Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim.
english: He succeeded Abdul-Rauf Tanko Ibrahim.

kusaal: Ba vɔɔtidnɛ gaŋid nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaann.
english: It elects one Member of Parliament (MP) by the first past the post system of election.

kusaal: Yapei-Kusawgu Constituency anɛ constituency kanɛ mɔr sɔ' ka o zi'e di nɔba zug bɛ Parliament of Ghana.
english: Yapei-Kusawgu is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Onɛ an wadmaan nananna tis constituency la anɛ Alhaji Seidu Amadu.
english: He succeeded Alhaji Seidu Amadu.

kusaal: O da zi'enɛ Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress (NDC) wadmaannib vɔɔtʋg la ni ka da paam vɔɔt kɔbiga nɛ pisnaasi nɛ anu gaad onɛ tia'al o nya'aŋ la, ka li da pa'al ye o di ya'an ka na nyaŋi nya' wadmaan vɔɔtʋg la ni.
english: He was elected on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and won a majority of votes to win the constituency election to become the MP.

kusaal: O da zi'en constituency la nɔba zug bɛnɛ 4th Republic parliament la ni, Ma'asim Tiig Na'adɔɔg, National Democratic Congress nɔba.
english: He had represented the constituency in the 4th Republican parliament on the ticket of the National Democratic Congress.

kusaal: Yaw Maama Aful(Ba da dʋ'a o nɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswsi nɛ pisnu nɛ awai nwadisa ayuobʋ la dabpiiga daar ka ob an Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaani paas Ghana wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: Yaw Maama Afful (born 10 June 1959) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the Fifth and Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Jaman South Constituency in the Brong-Ahafo Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O yinɛ Mpuasu tenpʋkanɛ bɛ Brong Ahafo Region sʋ'ʋlʋm Ghana nwa ni la.
english: He hails from Mpuasu, a town in the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O daa keŋnɛ Kennesaw State University, Atlanta, USA ka paam o Bachelor of Arts degree kasɛta gbaʋŋ bɛ International Affairs nɛ Political Science in 1997.
english: He entered Kennesaw State University, Atlanta, USA, and obtained his Bachelor of Arts degree in International Affairs and Political Science in 1997.

kusaal: Afful anɛ kpɛɛm bɛ EO, Kids Heaven Learning Centre bɛ Aworth, Atlanta n bɛ US.O anɛ kpikpiʋŋ sɔb.
english: Afful was the CEO of EO, Kids Heaven Learning Centre in Aworth, Atlanta, in the US.

kusaal: O daa zi'enɛ tis o constituency n bɛ Ghana Republic anu la nɛ ayuobʋ la.Ban daa gaŋ o la, o daa paamnɛ vɔɔt kal 16,878 yit 30,266 pʋʋgin, nidib la wʋsa n daa vɔɔt naae la.
english: Afful contested the Jaman South constituency parliamentary seat on the ticket of New Patriotic Party during the 2008 Ghanaian general election and won with 16,878 votes out of the 30,266 valid votes cast equivalent to 55.77% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: O daa di ka bas Ofori Aikins onɛ zi'en tis nɔraʋg paati la nɛ Peter Kwabena Ankomah onɛ mɛ nɛ zi'enɛ tis ma'asim tiig paati la nɛ Jacob Oteng-Ahyemang kanɛ zi'en tis nɔraʋg paati la nɛ Kwadwo Boakye onɛ mɛ nɛ zi'enɛ o nyari ka pʋ dɔl paati si'a.kɔbʋg pʋʋgin ban daa paam vɔɔtnam kal si'em nwa; 0.75%, 34.27%, 0.44% nɛ 8.77% yit vɔɔt la wʋsa kallin.
english: He won against Ofori Aikins of the People's National Convention, Peter Kwabena Ankomah of the National Democratic Congress, Jacob Oteng-Ahyemang of the Convention People's Party and Kwadwo Boakye Djan an independent candidate.

kusaal: Afful anɛ Kristo biig (Presbyterian).
english: Afful is a Christian (Presbyterian).

kusaal: Ba da du'a Afful nɛ yʋma tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ awai , li nwadisa ayuobʋ la, dabisim piiga daar (June 10, 1959).
english: Afful was born on 10 June 1959.

kusaal: Afful anɛ wadmaani tis wabʋg na'adɔɔg la (NPP).
english: Afful is a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ anii la ni ka ba da gaŋ o ye o an wadmaani tis Jaman South Constituency teŋ sʋ'ʋlʋm.
english: In 2008, he was elected on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party as the Member of Parliament for the Jaman South Constituency.

kusaal: Kɔbʋg pʋʋgin o daa mɔri 55.77% yit nidib banɛ daa vɔɔt la wʋsa la kallin.
english: Afful contested the Jaman South constituency parliamentary seat on the ticket of New Patriotic Party during the 2008 Ghanaian general election and won with 16,878 votes out of the 30,266 valid votes cast equivalent to 55.77% of total valid votes cast.

kusaal: Ghana republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la, ka di.
english: He thus represented the constituency in the 5th, 6th, and 7th parliament of the 4th republic of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɔr pʋ'a nɛ biisa atan'.
english: He is married (with three children).

kusaal: Lin daa yi yʋma 2003 ti paae yʋma 2005, Yaw Buaben Asamoa da anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ tʋʋm gɔmina lʋgir kanɛ ka ti boun ye program officer.
english: From 2003 to 2005, Yaw Buaben Asamoa worked for the Ghanaian government as a programme officer.

kusaal: Yaw Buaben Asamoa anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ wadmaan kʋdʋg paas wadmaanib yikanɛ paasi ayɔpɔi la Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: Yaw Buaben Asamoa (born 16 September 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and former member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Adenta Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaani tis Adentan Constituency n bɛ Greater Accra Region sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Yaw Buaben Asamoa (born 16 September 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and former member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana representing the Adenta Constituency in the Greater Accra Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Ka lin yi yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anu (2005) ti paae yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ ayuobʋ (2006) la ni, o da anɛ tʋʋmi sʋgin gɔmɛna zʋgran nya'aŋdɔl.
english: From 2005 to 2006, he served as the late Alhaji Aliu Mahama's senior special assistant.

kusaal: Yaw Osei Adutwum anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd ka mɛn paas wadmaanib yir linɛ paas ayɔpɔi la, ti Ghana Republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: Dr. Yaw Osei Adutwum (born 9 April 1964) is a Ghanaian politician and member of the ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Bosomtwe Constituency in the Ashanti Region on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party.

kusaal: Yaw Osei Adutwum keŋ o yiiga sakur tita'ar bɛ Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology n naae ka di'e o kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an bachelor's degree in Land Economy (Zamisυg linɛ an tɔlυŋ nɛ kpiisυg tυυma yɛla), o da yii anina n tɔlisi kɛŋ USA zamisi di'e o mastɛs kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an master's degree in Education Management linɛ an gbaυŋ lυgυr zamisυg yɛla n yi University of La Verne ka o yii anina lɛn tɔlisi zamisi di'e kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ an PhD in Educational Policy, Planning and Administration n yi University of Southern California.
english: He holds a master's degree in Education Management from the University of La Verne and a PhD in Educational Policy, Planning and Administration from the University of Southern California.

kusaal: Onɛ pin'il New Designs Charter Schools la'am nɛ din wυsa, o da anɛ tυmtυm n bɛ Manual Arts High Sakur la ni aan ba Gɛligir nɛ Information Technology pa'an-pa'an wυυ yʋma piiga ka saŋkana win la yim, ka o pin'ili mɔr International Studies Academy linɛ da an ye li sυŋ sakur bibis banɛ bɛ teŋkpɛmɛs la ka ba zamis gbaυŋ nɛ ba bɛllim yɛla sυ'ʋŋa.
english: Prior to that, he worked as a Mathematics and Information Technology teacher at the Manual Arts High School for ten years, and within this period, he founded the International Studies Academy, which served as a small learning community for students.

kusaal: O da lɛn anɛ Giligir pa'an bɛ the USC/ Manual Arts Neighborhood Academic Initiative (NAI).
english: He also served as the lead math teacher in the USC/Manual Arts Neighborhood Academic Initiative (NAI).

kusaal: Vɔɔt kanɛ da maal yʋma 2016 la, o da mɔri vɔɔt wυυ bam 46,238 n yi kanl la wυsa ni linɛ da an 54, 144, ka kɔbʋg pυυgin o da mɔri 85.82% ka onɛ an District Chief Executive (DCE) n tis Bosomtwe Sυ'υlυm Veronica Antwi-Adjei ka an Ma'asim Tiig na'adɔɔg nid ka on nɛ on da nya'ad la mɛn da nyɛnɛ vɔɔt kal 7,215 ka li zi'esim kɔbʋg pυυgin an 13.39%.
english: He contested the Bosomtwe Constituency in the Ashanti region of Ghana on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party during the 2016 Ghanaian general election, He obtained 46,238 votes out of the total 54,144 votes cast representing 85.82%, while his closest contender, the then District Chief Executive (DCE) of the Bosomtwe District, Veronica Antwi-Adjei of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), had 7,215 votes, representing 13.39%.

kusaal: O anɛ Pentecost karimbiig.
english: He is a Christian and worships at the Pentecost Church.

kusaal: O yinɛ Jachie ti Ghana Kumasi sυ'υlυm.
english: Yaw Osei Adutwum hails from Jachie in the Ashanti region of Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ anɛ Kumasi High Sakur linɛ bɛ Ghana Kumasi sυ'υlυm la, ani ka o paam o zamisυg kasɛta gbaυŋ linɛ zii o keŋ tuon.
english: He had his secondary education at Kumasi High School in the Ashanti Region of Ghana, where he received his Advanced level education certificate.

kusaal: O da lɛn paas banɛ ka ba gaansi ba ye ba gɔs sakur bibis bɛog tʋʋma yɛla linɛ ka National Research for Career and Technical dim da mɔri yina ye ba gɔs ka zamisυg linɛ an fυ bɛog tυυma yɛla nɔbig tituaa kɔliginam la ni.
english: He was also part of the task force established by the National Research Council for Career and Technical Education to develop a national model for career and technical education at the high school and College levels.

kusaal: Burnya nya'aŋ nwadisa atan' la yʋma tusa ayi' ne pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni ka ti Ghana gɔmina zudaan Nana Akufo-Addo da gaŋ Adutwun ye o an onɛ gɔsid gbaυŋ zamisυg lυgυr la nya'andɔl.
english: On 5 March 2021, Adutwum was appointed by President Nana Akufo-Addo as the Minister of Education in Ghana.

kusaal: Yʋma tusa ayi' nɛ pii nɛ awai la ni ka nimbanɛ vɛɛnsidi gɔsid minista banɛ tυυma an sum la (Alliance for Social Equity nɛ Public Accountability (ASEPA) nɛ FAKS Investigative Services) da gaŋ o ye o tυυma an sʋm hali.
english: In 2019, he was voted the Best Performing Deputy Minister by two research bodies: the Alliance for Social Equity and Public Accountability (ASEPA) and FAKS Investigative Services.

kusaal: Yeongsanjae (영산재, 靈山齋) anɛ Korean Buddhist malima linɛ ka Siddhartha Gautama da yisid waazu ka ba yʋ'ʋn buoni li Lotus Sutra.
english: Yeongsanjae (Korean: 영산재; Hanja: 靈山齋) is a Korean Buddhist ceremony which re-enacts Siddhartha Gautama delivering the sermon now known as the Lotus Sutra.

kusaal: Banɛ dɔlisid malima nwa anɛ Taego Order, ba maani li yʋʋm wʋsa nwadisa ayuobu, dabisa ayuobu daar (June 6), ba mɔr la'avɛnla anina, winsɔsʋg nam, tea maliŋ, ka maan piini maani tisid Buddha ka lɛn maan malima tisid banɛ kpi la.
english: Primarily preserved and conducted by the Taego Order, the ceremony, which takes place annually on June 6, includes tea ceremonies, decorations, prayers, rites of purification, offerings to Buddha, and rites for the dead.

kusaal: Ban bɔɔd ye ba tɔlis Yeongsanjae la, Korea dim maalnɛ lʋgir kanɛ gur maliŋ nwa' ka ba buoni ba Yeongsanjae Preservation Society.
english: In order to preserve Yeongsanjae, Korea has created the Yeongsanjae Preservation Society.

kusaal: "Beopgo" anɛ Buddhist yʋʋma la'ad yinne linɛ nwɛn wʋʋ ba nɔknɛ binnir ka ba nɔk daadi maal nɛ.
english: "Beopgo" refers to one of the Buddhist instruments that looks like a big drum made with wood.

kusaal: "Beompae (梵唄) bɛ Buddhist malima ni ka anɛ Beomseo (梵書) bʋʋdi din ka ba buoni li Eosan (魚山).
english: "Beompae (梵唄) used in Buddhist ceremonies is a tribute to Beomseo (梵書) and is called Eosan (魚山).

kusaal: Beompae da dɔlis zʋmaani paae Korean beompae dimi yinɛ Jingamseonsa (眞鑑禪師), one da tu' suori kɛŋ Tang Dynasty ye o zamis la.
english: This beompae was passed down to the Korean beompae by Jingamseonsa (眞鑑禪師), who went to the Tang Dynasty to study abroad."

kusaal: Barramu (바라무) bama anɛ Baramu yʋʋma: Gwanyoksi, Shinsinjokbeopsi, Jojeonjeomansi, Gwaebuliunsi.
english: Baramu (바라무) These were Baramu's ordeal poems: Gwanyoksi, Shinsinjokbeopsi, Jojeonjeomansi, Gwaebuliunsi.

kusaal: Beopgomu (법고무) "zamisig yʋʋma (beop rubber la bʋnib nya'aŋ yʋʋma), nɛ diib kʋosig zin'ig yʋʋma (beop rubber after the cultivation suor)."
english: Beopgomu (법고무) "Trial poem (beop rubber after the ear cultivation method), disclosure of the upper volume (beop rubber after a method of cultivation), and a restaurant method poem (beop rubber after the cultivation method)."

kusaal: Majesty anɛ la'a vɛnlif kan ka ba mɔri maan dɔɔd banɛ ka Buddha bada la bɛ, nɛ doryang ka bugum la'ad mɛ paas ani ka ba sɔb Bodhisattva nɛ Jihwa yʋda la.
english: Majesty is a decorative element which refers to the splendid decoration of the sanctuary where the Buddha is enshrined and the doryang with various fire bodhisattvas inscribed with the name of the Bodhisattva and Jihwa.

kusaal: Yʋ'ʋma nɛ wa'a bɛdegʋ bɛ malima la ni, nɛ di'ema bɛdegʋ banɛ an Martial arts.
english: There are also many different music that are used in the ceremonies, along with the use of certain Martial arts.

kusaal: Wa'a nwa da pin'il nɛ Goryeo Dynasty saŋa.
english: The dance originated during the Goryeo period.

kusaal: Yeongsanjae anɛ malima banɛ ka Buddhist maan la yinne, ba maani li ye ba sɔs suguru tis banɛ kpi la ka mɛ lɛn sɔsid ye ba yi namisʋg pʋʋgin.
english: Yeongsanjae is one form of Buddhist ritual, performed in hopes of wishing the deceased to rest in peace and be free from the sufferings.

kusaal: Yeongsanjae maliŋ la maan si'em anɛ onɛ bɛ Buddhism ka kpi, li dabisa pisnaasi nɛ awai daar, ban malima anɛ ye dabisa pisnaasi nɛ awai ka one kpi na paae arezana ni.
english: Yeongsanjae is practiced on the 49th day after a person's death because in Buddhism, it is believed that the soul of the deceased will reach the heaven on the 49th day.

kusaal: Kʋdʋmin la, ba da ɛɛnti maal Yeongsanjae nɛ dabisa atan', amaa nannanna, ba maani linɛ daar yinne.
english: Yeongsanjae is one form of Buddhist ritual, performed in hopes of wishing the deceased to rest in peace and be free from the sufferings.

kusaal: Malima bɛdegʋ maan dabisir pisnaasi nɛ awai la daar, amaa, Yeongsanjae an linɛ gati ba wʋsa.
english: In the past, Yeongsanjae was practiced for over 3 days, but now it has been reduced in size, which they only perform the ceremony for one day.

kusaal: Li paas maliŋ titada banɛ bɛ Korea tɛŋin la ni, li da anɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbʋs wai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan' (1973) ka ba da pin'ili siak nwa'.
english: It is one of the Important Intangible Cultural Properties of Korea, having been designated as such in 1973.

kusaal: Ba wa'ad wa'a bɛdegʋ Yeongsanjae malima saŋa ka ba sieba an Barachum, Beopgochum nɛ Nabichum.
english: Unlike Barachum and Nabichum, Beopgochum contains rapid, big movements and loud sounds.

kusaal: Barachum, ka ba lɛm buon ye cymbals wa'a, da nyɛ yʋ'ʋr kan bɔzugɔ, ban mɔr la'asi'a nwɛ'ɛd ka wa'ad wa'a la yʋ'ʋri an "bara".
english: Barachum, also known as the cymbals dance, was named this because they used the instrument called "bara".

kusaal: Beopgochum anɛ wa'a banɛ ka ba wa'ad Yeongsanjae ni la yinne.
english: Beopgochum is another dance that is performed during Yeongsanjae.

kusaal: Nabichum wa'a la da nyɛ li yʋ'ʋr la yinɛ li wa'a ya'a nɔbir ya'asigi wɛn nabi la zug, ka lin gbin anɛ pimpiŋ (butterfly) Korea dim pin'ad pʋʋgin.
english: Nabichum was named because the dance moves resemble the appearance of nabi, which means a butterfly in Korean.

kusaal: La'asieba banɛ ka ba nwɛ'ɛd Yeongsanjae diema zin'igin la sieba an jang-gu (Korean lʋŋ), haegeum (kon ), nɛ geomungo (kon kanɛ mɔr dʋndis ayuobʋ).
english: Some of the instruments played at the Yeongsanjae are jang-gu (Korean drum), haegeum (string instruments ), and geomungo (instrument with six strings).

kusaal: Li ya' an beompae pin'il zin'ig siya yela, bedego mi'ilim anɛ ye li yinɛ Yeongsanhoesang, myoeum bodhisattva's yʋʋma nina, Chinese dimi pa'al siem la.契), nɛ Kang Seung-hoe (康僧会) da kɛ ka Nihang Beompae (泥恒梵唄) yʋ'ʋr nɔbig Gangnam sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Regarding the origin of beompae, there are theories of the origin of Yeongsanhoesang, myoeum bodhisattva's music offering, and Chinese breakfast creation theory.契), and Kang Seung-hoe (康僧会) made the Nihang Beompae (泥恒梵唄) and spread the name of the Beompae (梵唄聲明) in Gangnam.

kusaal: Ba dɔlisidnɛ suoya piiga nɛ ayi ka nyaan maan Yeongsanjae malima la, ka maliŋ suor wʋsa mɔri li gbin.
english: There are a total of 12 steps to performing the Yeongsanjae and each step of the procedure has its own meaning.

kusaal: Nadimu (나비무) "Butterfly radish ordeal poetry (suor yinne kanɛ bɛ suoya anaasi pʋʋgin, suoya bedego, bʋnib suor), gaebuliunsi (suoya bedego), paalʋ ni yʋʋma (siis atan' suor, doryang suor, suoya bedego, hyanghwa crab suor, three male taesjak, spear) pʋ'adiir nya'aŋ, Hell Manipulation suor, Salvation Keonjang suor, yokgeoni/jeongbeop world mantra, nɛ Baron Om suor, Unshim crab suor, Diagonal Shakyat veneration suor), nɛ diib dɔɔgin suor yʋʋma (jagwi's illegitimate suor)."
english: Nabimu (나비무) "Butterfly radish ordeal poetry (single method of four directions, multiple methods, cultivating method), gaebuliunsi (multiple methods), upper-gwon public poetry (three spirits method, doryang method, multiple method, hyanghwa crab method, three male taesjak, spear) After marriage, the Hell Manipulation Method, the Salvation Keonjang method, the yokgeoni/jeongbeop world mantra, then the Baron Om method, the Unshim crab method, the Diagonal Shakyat veneration method), and the dining room method poem (jagwi's illegitimate method)."

kusaal: Tajumu (타주무) nwa' anɛ wa'a kanɛ ka ba wa'ad ba ya' maal dikʋosidim naae.
english: Tajumu (타주무) This is a dance performed between the ceremonial ceremonies in the restaurant recipe.

kusaal: Ming dynasty saŋa la, bani ʋgʋd la da dɔl suor kanɛ buon swivel weaving la ʋgʋg ka li kɛ ka ba fuud la vɛnl ka li sieba an satin.
english: During the Ming dynasty, the yunjin weavers developed a technique of swivel weaving that enabled them to weave colourful designs onto a base fabric in other weaves, such as satin.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi nɛ awai (2009), ba da gaŋ Nanjing brocade ye li paas oral and intangible heritage of humanity bɛ UNESCO la ni.
english: In 2009, Nanjing brocade was selected into the representative list of oral and intangible heritage of humanity at UNESCO.

kusaal: Brocade bɛ Nanjing la pin'il nɛ Three Kingdoms period (220-280).
english: The history of brocade in Nanjing can be traced back to the Three Kingdoms period (220-280).

kusaal: Zaba kanɛ da paae ba, Eastern Jin Dynasty (317-420), General Liu Yu da nyaŋ Xi'an-based Later Qin kingdom (384-417).
english: In a war, which broke out at the end of the Eastern Jin Dynasty (317-420), General Liu Yu defeated the Xi'an-based Later Qin kingdom (384-417).

kusaal: Eastern Jin government maal nɛ brocade dɔtita'ar ka li bɛ Nanjing ye ba gɔs brocade maalig yɛla, ka lin da pa'al ye Nanjing brocade yʋ'ʋn da kpɛn'ɛ gbana ni.
english: The Eastern Jin government had set up a special brocade office in Nanjing to manage the production of the brocade, which represented the formal establishment of Nanjing brocade.

kusaal: Qing Dynasty ni la, "Jiangning Weaving Department" da bɛnɛ Nanjing.

kusaal: Di anɛ Important Intangible Cultural Properties of Japan, ka paas UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity pʋʋgin.
english: It is designated as one of the Important Intangible Cultural Properties of Japan, and has also been inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Labakʋda banɛ bɛ zaŋi ken yūki-tsumugi nyɛɛ di pin'il Important Intangible Cultural Properties of g nɛ crafthouse dinɛ k aba buon ye Nagahatabeno Ashiginu Emperor Sujin Na'atita'ar na'am saŋa.
english: The traditional history of yūki-tsumugi traces its origin to a crafthouse known as Nagahatabeno Ashiginu during the reign of the legendary Emperor Sujin.

kusaal: Ba da ye feudal lord tis kpaadib buudi banɛ bɛ Hitachi Province la tʋm tsumugi fuugu tis gɔmena kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Kamakura Kanryo yʋʋm wʋsa ka di an piini.
english: It is said that the feudal lord of a farmer family in the Hitachi Province sent tsumugi fabric to a governor called Kamakura Kanryo every year as a gift.

kusaal: Din da nɔbʋgidi yit nwiis fuud ʋgʋbin la, "yūki-tsumugi" k aba da nɔk ka di an yʋ'ʋri tis fuug la yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ ayi la ni (1602).
english: Developing from earlier silk techniques, the name "yūki-tsumugi" was adopted in 1602.

kusaal: Ba da kaanbi buol banɛ ʋgʋd fuud la ba bɛ Ueda Castle la nɛ fuug la, pin'ilʋgin la, ba da nɔki linɛ ka di an piini tis shōgun.
english: Weavers were invited from Ueda Castle and the cloth, at first plain, was used as a gift for the shōgun.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan (1873) la ni, ba da yis yūki-tsumugi paalʋ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisnii nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ atan (1873) bɛ Vienna World's Fair, ka nidib yʋ'ʋm baŋi li yɛla dunia bɛn wʋsa ni.
english: In 1873, yūki-tsumugi was exhibited at the 1873 Vienna World's Fair, and became known worldwide.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisnu nɛ ayuobʋ (1956) la ni, ba da gaŋ yūki-tsumugi ye di an Important Intangible Cultural Properties yinne tis Japan dim.
english: In 1956, yūki-tsumugi was designated one of the Important Intangible Cultural Properties of Japan.

kusaal: Association for the Preservation of the Honba Yūki-tsumugi Weaving Technique (本場結城紬技術保持会) da pin'ilnɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayuobʋ (1976) la ni ka sʋŋi maal ka kɛ ka fuud ʋgʋb keŋ tuon.
english: The Association for the Preservation of the Honba Yūki-tsumugi Weaving Technique (本場結城紬技術保持会) was established in 1976 and helps promote and transmit the craft.

kusaal: Yūki Daiichi High School bɛ Yūki la mɔr yūki-tsumugi la'asʋg kilab.
english: Yūki Daiichi High School in Yūki has a yūki-tsumugi club.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ni, yūki-tsumugi da paas Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
english: In 2010, UNESCO inscribed yūki-tsumugi on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

kusaal: Labakʋda sieba mɛ da ye Muromachi period (14th-16th century) da an saŋkanɛ ka ba da pin'il yūki-tsumugi ka di nɔbʋg.
english: Another account identified the Muromachi period (14th–16th century) as the period when yūki-tsumugi was developed.

kusaal: Nananna, nwɛnɛ fu-ʋgʋdib kɔbiga nɛ pistan' ʋgʋd yūki-tsumugi bɛ Yūki nɛ Oyama.
english: Currently, approximately one hundred and thirty craftsmen practice the craft of yūki-tsumugi production in Yūki and Oyama.

kusaal: Fʋ ya'a bɔɔd ye fʋ maal fuug, ba ɛɛnti yisnɛ silk floss yi silkworm cocoons ni ka nɔk nu'usi nwɛdisi di ka di lie yarn.
english: To produce the fabric, silk floss is first extracted from silkworm cocoons and is spun by hand into yarn.

kusaal: Ba na maal ban bɔɔd ye fuug la an si'em nɛ kasuri ikat ka naan pin'ili ʋgʋdi li nɛ masin kanɛ yʋ'ʋri an jibata (地機).
english: Dyed patterns are added to the cloth with kasuri ikat before weaving with a loom known as a jibata (地機).

kusaal: O anɛ Jerry Rawlings onɛ da an Ghana Zugraan kʋdʋg 4th Republic Ghana dinɛ yi 1993 ti paae 2001) nɛ o pu'a Nana Konadu Agyeman 1993 paae 2001 bikpɛɛm.

english: She is National Democratic Congress' Member of Parliament for the Klottey-Korle Constituency in the 7th, 8th and the 9th parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana and a humanitarian.

kusaal: O yinɛ Dzelukope linɛ bɛ Volta Region Ghana sʋ'ʋlʋm.

english: She then graduated from the Wesley Girls High School in Cape Coast in 1996.

kusaal: Nasaa nwadig atan' yʋʋm 2014 la ni, Zanetor Rawlings da anɛ saan zummir onɛ da paas Gbansabʋlig Sʋ'ʋlim Pu'ab La'asʋg, Cranes-Montana Forum linɛ na kɛ ka Africa nɛ South-South Nɔɔryinne gban'ar in Dakhla', na keŋ tuonɛ sʋŋ ka saalib lam bɛnɛ taab dunia nwa ka barigaŋ kae.
english: In March 2014, Rawlings was a special guest of the exceptional Meeting of African Women in the framework of the crans-Montana Forum on Africa and the South-South Cooperation in Dakhla, which was aimed at promoting a more humane and impartial world.

english: In 2004, the club changed its name from Stay Cool F.C. to Zaytuna F.C. United and launched another campaign for the premiership.

english: The premiership home games were played at the El Wak Stadium.

english: In the year 2000, the football club initiated a campaign to secure a spot in the prestigious premiership.

kusaal: Ba da dii li bɛ 2003 saŋkanɛ ka ba da paas ayi bɛ Division one league la ni.
english: They achieved this 2003 when they reached second place in the Division One League and earned promotion.

kusaal: Ban da pin'ili mɔɔd nɛ suoya wʋsa la, ba da nyaŋ nyɛ ye ba na nwɛ' nwɛ'ɛb kanɛ ken 2006 ni na la.

kusaal: Dinɛ pɛɛsi ayi anɛ ye ba ya'a bɛ teŋ kanɛ ka waad bɛ ba puudnɛ yimmʋ yʋʋm wsa puugin, saŋa kanɛ ka saa niid nɛ saŋa kanɛ an ʋʋn bɛ (Northern Hemisphere Vaala Nwadig la nɛ Sigir Nwadig la teŋsʋk, Southern Hemisphere October nɛ Samampiid Nwadig la teŋsʋk).
