kusaal: French botanist François Alexandre Pierre de Garsault da pa'al ye tiig kaŋa anɛ Balanus myrepsica amaa yʋ'ʋbanɛ ka o da tis la ba da pʋsiaki li ye li an sʋm, ka li anɛ ye da pʋ pa'an ka li dɔl binomial yʋda tisib wadaa.
english: French botanist François Alexandre Pierre de Garsault described the species as Balanus myrepsica, but his names are not accepted as valid, as he did not always give his descriptions binomial names.

kusaal: French naturalist Jean-Baptiste Lamarck mɛ da pa'al tiig la yɛla bɛ yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnii n anu (1785) la ni.
english: French naturalist Jean-Baptiste Lamarck described the species in 1785.

kusaal: O da nɔknɛ morphology nɛ DNA pa'al ye M. oleifera wɛni M. concanensis, ka fʋ ya'a gɔs ti bama ayi la keŋ wɛn taaba siem la, di yitnɛ of M. peregrina tiis buudi la ni na.
english: A combined analysis of morphology and DNA shows that M. oleifera is most closely related to M. concanensis, and the common ancestor of these two diverged from the lineage of M. peregrina.

kusaal: Tiig la yʋ'ʋr Moringa la yini Tamil pian'adin na dinɛ an murungai la, di gbin anɛ "wɛla banɛ wɛɛnlim taaba", wɛl paala la.
english: The genus name Moringa derives from the Tamil word, murungai, meaning "twisted pod", alluding to the young fruit.

kusaal: Li yʋ'ʋr mɛŋir oleifera la yini Latin dim pian'adin oleum "kpaam" nɛferre "ban na wɛl".
english: The specific name oleifera is derived from the Latin words oleum "oil" and ferre "to bear".

kusaal: Zaŋgbeduan la mɔr Leveillula taurica, dinɛ an zɔ'ɔm mildew, ka li san'amid papaya tiis bɛ south India.
english: The moringa tree is a host to Leveillula taurica, a powdery mildew, which causes damage in papaya crops in south India.

kusaal: Oxalate tun'e naan 430 paae 1050 mg/100g, fʋ ya'a maki di nɛ oxalate dinɛ bɛ spinach ni la (750 mg/100g).
english: Oxalate levels may vary from 430 to 1050 mg/100g, compared to the oxalate in spinach (average 750 mg/100g).

kusaal: yʋda banɛ ka ba yiti mɔri buonɛ ba anɛ, moringa, drumstick tiig (din yi di wa'alimɛn la sig na paae di yadigirin la nɛ di wala ni.), horseradish tree (din yi di nya'a la ni, din nwɛnɛ horseradish la), bɛɛ malunggay (wʋʋ ban mi'i li ye maritime bɛɛ archipelagic zin'is banɛ bɛ Asia la).
english: Common names include moringa, drumstick tree (from the long, slender, triangular seed-pods), horseradish tree (from the taste of the roots, which resembles horseradish), ben tree (for its oil), or malunggay (as known in maritime or archipelagic areas in Asia).

kusaal: Ba bʋmbaanlʋg la ɛɛnti bʋsid vaand ka li sin'im an purplish bɛɛ greenish-white, hairy bark.
english: Young shoots have purplish or greenish-white, hairy bark.

kusaal: Di puum la anɛ fragrant nɛ hermaphroditic, gilig nɛ thinly veined, yellowish-white petals.
english: The flowers are fragrant and hermaphroditic, surrounded by five unequal, thinly veined, yellowish-white petals.

kusaal: Di biidnɛ tilkanɛ mɔr zuobid, o anɛ ti kanɛ sʋʋgidi o puum basid, o til la wa'alim anɛ 10–25 cm (4–10 in).
english: They grow on slender, hairy stalks in spreading or drooping flower clusters, which have a length of 10–25 cm (4–10 in).

kusaal: Tiig la mɔr yʋda kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb bɛdigʋ bɛ teens bɛdigʋ ni zin'is banɛ ka ba kuodi li, nɛ drumstick tiig, horseradish tiig bɛɛ giŋa anɛ moringa ka ba mɔri buon naasaalin la.
english: The plant has numerous common names across regions where it is cultivated, with drumstick tree, horseradish tree, or simply moringa used in English.

kusaal: Budworms yit Noctuidae mɔri wiim pamm kenna san'amid tiig la puum.
english: Budworms from the Noctuidae are known to cause serious defoliation.

kusaal: Dinɛ mɛ lɛm pɛɛs anɛ, zunzunya banɛ an snout moth Noorda blitealis la didnɛ ba vaand la ka tun'e san'am vaand la wʋsa.
english: Furthermore, the caterpillars of the snout moth Noorda blitealis feed primarily on the leaves and can cause complete leaf loss.

kusaal: zangbeduan tun'e daam ti nuudim kanɛka bas ti sibiti ni dinɛ an cytochrome P450 (la'am nɛ CYP3A4) ka na tun'e mɔr antihyperglycemic mɔe daaʋŋ tis sitagliptin.
english: M. oleifera may interfere with prescription drugs affecting cytochrome P450 (including CYP3A4) and may inhibit the antihyperglycemic effect of sitagliptin.

kusaal: Zaŋgbeduan vankanɛ an 100 g (about 5 cups) la bɛ teebul kanɛ digi teŋir la (USDA data).
english: Nutritional content of 100 g of fresh M. oleifera leaves (about 5 cups) is shown in the table (USDA data).

kusaal: Vaand la an luokanɛ malisi gaad tiig la luos wʋsa, din mɔr B vitamins, vitamin C, provitamin A as beta-carotene, vitamin K, manganese, nɛ protein la zug.
english: The leaves are the most nutritious part of the plant, being a significant source of B vitamins, vitamin C, provitamin A as beta-carotene, vitamin K, manganese, and protein.

kusaal: Calcium dinɛ bɛ moringa vaandin la sieba anɛ dinɛ ka ba buon ye crystals of calcium oxalate.
english: Some of the calcium in moringa leaves is bound as crystals of calcium oxalate.

kusaal: Department of Agriculture and Fisheries (Queensland) lʋgir la pa'al ye zaŋgbeduan la an sʋm ka mɔr tʋʋm paam bɛ siind maalʋg ni bɔzugo di ked k aba paamid siind bɛdigʋ yʋʋm wʋsa.
english: According to the Department of Agriculture and Fisheries (Queensland), the moringa tree is useful for honey production because it blooms for a long period of the year.

kusaal: Di tun'e nɔki ma bʋŋkɔbid yaama, diib kuomalisiŋ, wina'am maalʋg anthelmintic, nɛ adjuvant.
english: It may be used as forage for livestock, a micronutrient liquid, a natural anthelmintic, and possible adjuvant.

kusaal: Zaŋgbeduan(Moringa oleifera) vaanzɔ'ɔm la anɛ ki'ib kanɛ sʋm nɛ nu'us piesʋg di ya'a dɛŋim wʋ'ʋl di ke ka antiseptic nɛ detergent yi phytochemicals bɛ viand la ni.
english: Moringa oleifera leaf powder was as effective as soap for hand washing when wetted in advance to enable antiseptic and detergent properties from phytochemicals in the leaves.

kusaal: Zaŋgbeduan(Moringa oleifera) biili la nɛ press cake la ba maali di nɛ ka li an wasterwater ka li yisid kuom kanɛ bɛ binin la.
english: Moringa oleifera seeds and press cake have been implemented as wastewater conditioners for dewatering and drying fecal sludge.

kusaal: Zaŋgbeduan biili la mɔri dimeric cationic proteins, ka li sʋŋidi yisid ka pieɛd di'ad kanɛ wʋsa dinɛ bɛ turbid water la ni, ka ket ka sa'adnam la wʋsa la'as taaba, ka li sʋŋ ka sa'ad banɛ puki agɔla la nyaŋi yis sa'ad la bas fʋ tun'e siligi li bɛɛ yuuoe li.
english: Moringa seeds contain dimeric cationic proteins, which absorb and neutralize colloidal charges in turbid water, causing the colloidal particles to clump together, making the suspended particles easier to remove as sludge by either settling or filtration.

kusaal: Li kuob anɛ nwa', ba ɛɛnti kia ba nɛ yʋʋm wʋsa ka basi li wa'alim la ka li an 1–2 m (3.3–6.6 ft) ka bas ka li lɛm bus ya'as, wala ka li wɛla la na nɛ li biili la nu'us na nyaŋi paae.
english: In cultivation, it is often cut back annually to 1–2 m (3.3–6.6 ft) and allowed to regrow so the pods and leaves remain within arm's reach.

kusaal: Zebilla constituency bɛnɛ Bawku West districti bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: Zebilla is located in the Bawku West district of the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ba gaŋid nid yinne ka o aan ba wadmaani zi'eni tisi ba wadmaannib yin la dɔlisid Ghana vɔɔtʋg suor.
english: Zebilla is one of the constituencies represented in the Parliament of Ghana.

kusaal: Kʋk la bɛnɛ Bawku West Districti bɛ Upper East Region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana la.
english: The seat is located within the Bawku West District in the Upper East Region of Ghana.

kusaal: Ziblim Iddi anɛ Ghana nid kanɛ an pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd nɛ wadamaan paas wadmaanib yikanɛ passi ayɔpɔi la, Ghana Republic kanɛ paasi anaasi la.
english: Ziblim Iddi (born 15 September 1967) is a Ghanaian politician and was a member of the Seventh Parliament of the Fourth Republic of Ghana, representing the Gushegu Constituency on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

kusaal: O mɔr kasɛta gbaʋŋ kanɛ an doctor of philosophy bɛ political science (international relations nɛ comparative pɔlitis ) bɛ Clark University, Atlanta, wadmaani tis Gusheigu la bɛ Northern region sʋ'ʋlim.[2 Pa'an la mɛ lɛn mɔr kasɛta gbaʋŋ kanɛ buon ye Bachelor of Arts bɛ Political Science yi University of Ghana nɛ Masters bɛ International Affairs nɛ Development (MIAD) yi Clark University.
english: He also possesses a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science from the University of Ghana and a master's in International Affairs and Development (MIAD) from Clark University.

kusaal: O daa anɛ library assistant bɛ Fulton County Library din yi yʋma 1996 ti paae yʋma 2004.
english: Iddi worked as a library assistant at the Fulton County Library from 1996 to 2004.

kusaal: ka lin lɛn yi yʋma 2004 ti paae yʋma 2008 la ni la, O daa lɛn anɛ pa'an nya'andɔl bɛ Clark Atlanta University.
english: From 2004 to 2008, he worked as a teaching assistant at Clark Atlanta University.

kusaal: Yi 2008 to 2016, O daa lɛm an pa'an bɛ University of Ghana la ni.
english: From 2008 to 2016, he lectured at the University of Ghana.

kusaal: Babir kanɛ ka o mi' sʋ'ʋga anɛ political economy, comparative pɔlitis nɛ international relations.
english: His areas of expertise include political economy, comparative politics, and international relations.

kusaal: Plasma, an ziim kanɛ pʋ mɔr si'im la anɛ 55% zi-ku'om, ka li tita'am an water, ku'om (ka zɛm nɛ 92% volume).
english: Plasma, which constitutes 55% of blood fluid, is mostly water (92% by volume), and contains proteins, glucose, mineral ions, and hormones.

kusaal: ziim bʋnvʋr banɛ zu'oe anɛ ziim bʋnvʋr zɛn'ug la nɛ ziim bʋnvʋ pielig, Jawed vertebrates mɔri niŋgbinna bʋn gu'uda, adaptive immune system Ka white blood cells, ziim bʋnvʋ piela la la mɔri li.
english: Jawed vertebrates have an adaptive immune system, based largely on white blood cells.

kusaal: 200,000-500,000 thrombocytes: ka mɛ buon platelets la, ba mɛ paas ziim gbisib, (coagulation) tʋʋma la ni.
english: 200,000–500,000 thrombocytes: Also called platelets, they take part in blood clotting (coagulation).

kusaal: Fibrin nɛ yi ziim gbisibin la, ni maanɛ mesh ka li lus platelet plug la zugin.
english: Fibrin from the coagulation cascade creates a mesh over the platelet plug.

kusaal: Li anɛ aqueous kuod kanɛ mɔri kuom 92%, plasma proteins 8% nɛ la'asieba mɛn ya'as.
english: It is essentially an aqueous solution containing 92% water, 8% blood plasma proteins, and trace amounts of other materials.

kusaal: Erythrocytes nam banɛ mɔr laafi mɔr plasma vʋm linɛ wʋʋ dabisa 120 ka nyaan san'am, nɛ Kupffer zi-vʋya linɛ bɛ sɔɔnr la ni.
english: Healthy erythrocytes have a plasma life of about 120 days before they are degraded by the spleen, and the Kupffer cells in the liver.

kusaal: Ziim anɛ niŋgbiʋŋ ku'okanɛ bɛ circulatory system humans ni, nɛ vertebrates, ninsaalib bɛɛ bʋnvʋ sieba niŋgbiʋŋin pobidi giligid, ka tisid cells la, niŋgbina la nutrients nɛ oxegen, la'ad woo diib nɛ pɛbsim ka lɛn ziid la'abɛ'ɛd nami yisid cells la, niŋgbiʋŋ kan la ni.
english: Blood is a body fluid in the circulatory system of humans and other vertebrates that delivers necessary substances such as nutrients and oxygen to the cells of the body, and transports metabolic waste products away from those same cells.

kusaal: Ziim anɛ niŋgbina bɛ blood plasma, ziim kanɛ pʋ mɔr si'im la pʋʋgin.
english: Blood is composed of blood cells suspended in plasma.

kusaal: Ka mɔri protein, glucose, mineral ions nɛ hormones niŋgbiŋin la.
english: Plasma, which constitutes 55% of blood fluid, is mostly water (92% by volume), and contains proteins, glucose, mineral ions, and hormones.

kusaal: Niŋgbina la'ad la bɛ ziimin la si'im anɛ red blood cells, zi-zɛn'ɛug (erythrocytes), zi-pielig (leukocytes), ka bʋnvʋya banɛ (du'adi ba biis) ni an platelets (thrombocyte)
english: The formed elements are the two types of blood cell or corpuscle – the red blood cells, (erythrocytes) and white blood cells (leukocytes) – and the cell fragments called platelets that are involved in clotting.

kusaal: Bama mɔr nɛ hemoglobin li pʋʋgin.
english: 4.7 to 6.1 million (male), 4.2 to 5.4 million (female) erythrocytes: Red blood cells contain the blood's hemoglobin and distribute oxygen.

kusaal: Bʋnkɔnbid banɛ mɔri lungs, sɔnfulinfuud nii arterial ziim la ziid oxegen, pɛbisim kanɛ vʋ'ʋsi kpɛn'ɛs la mɔri paad niŋgbiŋin la ka venous ziim ziid carbon dioxide pɛbis bɛ'ɛd kanɛ naam nɛ niŋgbiŋ la metabolism tʋʋma ni, zaŋi tis sɔnfulinfuud la ka li vʋ'ʋsi yis.
english: In animals with lungs, arterial blood carries oxygen from inhaled air to the tissues of the body, and venous blood carries carbon dioxide, a waste product of metabolism produced by cells, from the tissues to the lungs to be exhaled.

kusaal: laafi pian zut banɛ dɔlisid nɛ ziim yɛla tita'am pin'ini nɛ hemo-, hemato-, haemo or haemoto- ka li yi nɛ Greek pian'ad kaŋa…(haima) ka lin an "ziim".
english: Medical terms related to blood often begin with hemo-, hemato-, haemo- or haemato- from the Greek word αἷμα (haima) for "blood".

kusaal: Tisid niŋgbiʋŋ la diib bɔ'ɔg woo glucose, amino acids and fatty acids (linɛ buoe ziimin bɛɛ plasma protein ni (blood lipids)).
english: Supply of nutrients such as glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids (dissolved in the blood or bound to plasma proteins (e.g., blood lipids))

kusaal: Li yisid la'abɛ'ɛd nam niŋgbiʋŋin la, woo carbon dioxide, nɛ lactic acid.
english: Plasma circulates dissolved nutrients, such as glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids (dissolved in the blood or bound to plasma proteins), and removes waste products, such as carbon dioxide, urea, and lactic acid.

kusaal: Coagulation, li tiebid ziim giinl, li ya' paam dɛŋ, li kɛt ka zi-kuod liebid gan'alʋg ka li sʋŋi guoe ziim kpa'ar niŋgbiʋŋin la.
english: Coagulation can form a thrombosis, which can obstruct vessels.

kusaal: Linɛ sʋ'oe ka body temperature, niŋgbiʋŋ la tʋʋlim zɛmis.
english: In contrast, when the external temperature is low, blood flow to the extremities and surface of the skin is reduced to prevent heat loss and is circulated to the important organs of the body, preferentially.

kusaal: Ziim la'ad banɛ naam la pa'an ziim gʋn-gʋn bɛɛ li buudi linɛ an zi-pielig (leukocytes), nɛ ziim giinla linɛ an fragments ka ba buon ye platelets la nɛ linɛ an ziim yiib sʋŋʋr.
english: The formed elements are the two types of blood cell or corpuscle – the red blood cells, (erythrocytes) and white blood cells (leukocytes) – and the cell fragments called platelets that are involved in clotting.

kusaal: 4.2 ti paae 5.4 million (pu'a) erythrocytes: Zi-zɛn'ɛug la mɔri ziim la hemoglobin ka pʋdigid oxegen.
english: 4.7 to 6.1 million (male), 4.2 to 5.4 million (female) erythrocytes: Red blood cells contain the blood's hemoglobin and distribute oxygen.

kusaal: Zi-zɛn'ɛug la (la'am nɛ endothelial giinla nɛ la'asieba mɛ pa'al ye glycoproteins bɛɛ li ni, kanɛ pa'an blood types, ziim buudi wʋsa.
english: The red blood cells (together with endothelial vessel cells and other cells) are also marked by glycoproteins that define the different blood types.

kusaal: Ziim la makir kanɛ ka zi-zɛn'ɛug bɛ la buonɛ hematocrit, ka zɛm nɛ 45%.
english: The proportion of blood occupied by red blood cells is referred to as the hematocrit, and is normally about 45%.

kusaal: Ninsaal niŋgbiʋŋ makir bɛn kanɛ ka zi-zɛn'ɛug bɛ la zɛmi nɛ woo mɔɔrim 2,000, li zu'oe zɛmi nɛ exterior surface, niŋgbiʋŋ la wʋsa.
english: The combined surface area of all red blood cells of the human body would be roughly 2,000 times as great as the body's exterior surface.

kusaal: .4000-11,000 leukocytes: zi-pielig paas nɛ niŋgbiʋŋ la immune system, laafi bɛllim yɛla.
english: 4,000–11,000 leukocytes: White blood cells are part of the body's immune system; they destroy and remove old or aberrant cells and cellular debris, as well as attack infectious agents (pathogens) and foreign substances.

kusaal: Leukocytes cancer la buonɛ leukemia.
english: The cancer of leukocytes is called leukemia.

kusaal: Woo 55% ziim anɛ blood plasma, ku'or kanɛ ni ka ziim la bɛ,kanɛ ka li mɛŋ si'im an dɔnbʋʋlʋm.
english: About 55% of blood is blood plasma, a fluid that is the blood's liquid medium, which by itself is straw-yellow in color.

kusaal: Blood plasma la zɛmisim wʋsa anɛ 2.7-3.0 liters (2.8-3.2 quarts) saal wʋsa ni.
english: The total blood plasma volume in an average human is 2.7–3.0 liters (2.8–3.2 quarts).

kusaal: Plasma ziid diibi giligid niŋgbiʋŋ la ni, diban anɛ glucose, amino acids nɛ fatty acids (kanɛ buoe ziimin bɛɛ n bɛ plasma protein ni), ka yisid la'abɛ'ɛdnamɛ woo carbon dioxide, urea, nɛ lactic acid.
english: Plasma circulates dissolved nutrients, such as glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids (dissolved in the blood or bound to plasma proteins), and removes waste products, such as carbon dioxide, urea, and lactic acid.

kusaal: electrolytes buudi bɛdigʋ ( ba tita'am anɛ sodium nɛ chloride)
english: Various electrolytes (mainly sodium and chloride)

kusaal: Protein kanɛ kplim la tita'am anɛ albumin nɛ immunoglobulins.
english: Most of the proteins remaining are albumin and immunoglobulins.

kusaal: Ziim, blood PH maalɛye li zi'e 7.35 ken paae 7.45 bɛn, kɛt ka li zɛmis nɛ basic (compensation).
english: Blood pH is regulated to stay within the narrow range of 7.35 to 7.45, making it slightly basic (compensation).

kusaal: Kuod sieba banɛ bɛ ziimin ka mɔri PH ka li pʋ paae 7.35 mɔrɛ mi'isim, acidic galis, ka ziim PH kanɛ 7.45 mɛ pʋ mɔri paŋa, basic.
english: Extra-cellular fluid in blood that has a pH below 7.35 is too acidic, whereas blood pH above 7.45 is too basic.

kusaal: PH kanɛ pʋ paae 6.9 bɛɛ gaad 7.8 mɔri lethal saŋa wʋsa.
english: A pH below 6.9 or above 7.8 is usually lethal.

kusaal: Ziim PH, partial pressure of oxegen (pO), partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO), nɛ bicarbonate (CHO) maalɛ sʋŋa nɛ homeostatic mechanisms nam, kɛt ka vʋ'ʋsim la'ad zin'igin nɛ dʋ'ʋnim la'ad zin'igin ka li zɛmisid mi'isim la nɛ vʋ'ʋʋsim la kanɛ buon compensation la.
english: Blood pH, partial pressure of oxygen (pO2), partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO2), and bicarbonate (HCO3−) are carefully regulated by a number of homeostatic mechanisms, which exert their influence principally through the respiratory system and the urinary system to control the acid–base balance and respiration, which is called compensation.

kusaal: Plasma ziid hormones giligid, kɛt ka ka di paad tissue wʋsa.
english: Plasma also circulates hormones transmitting their messages to various tissues.

kusaal: Ziim buudi wʋsa electrolytes reference ranges maanɛ niŋgbiʋŋ zin'ig wʋsa.
english: The list of normal reference ranges for various blood electrolytes is extensive.

kusaal: Bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa nii, platelets anɛ linɛ bɛ li kɔn'ɔ nɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ ka' bʋnkɔnbid la; nucleated bʋmbil, zi-vʋya suor linɛ buon ye thrombocytes linɛ tʋm n sʋŋidi gʋ'ʋd ziim kɔɔb.
english: Platelets are unique to mammals; in other vertebrates, small nucleated, spindle cells called thrombocytes are responsible for blood clotting instead.

kusaal: Ani ka li yu'un tabili kpɛn' datiʋŋ ventricle la ni ka ani ka li yu'un pɔmppii dɔl sɔnfulifuud la ni kpɛn' sɔnfulifuud la ni ka fɛndigi dɔl sɔnfulifuud giinla la ni n lɛb dagɔbʋg dɔɔg la ni.
english: Blood then enters the left ventricle to be circulated again.

kusaal: Li anɛ William Harvey Yʋʋma 1628 la ni ka o da pian'a bigis ziim kaarʋŋ la yɛla.
english: The blood circulation was described by William Harvey in 1628.

kusaal: Li ya'a anɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ ka' bʋnkɔnbid la nii, ziim vʋya la naamidnɛ n bɛ kɔnba biim la ni ka lin dɔl suo-si'a tʋm la buonnɛ ye hematopoiesis, linɛ paasi li ni anɛ erythropoiesis, linɛ naamid zi-vʋya wiid la; nɛ myelopoiesis, linɛ mɛ naamid zi-vʋya piela la nɛ platelets nam.
english: In vertebrates, the various cells of blood are made in the bone marrow in a process called hematopoiesis, which includes erythropoiesis, the production of red blood cells; and myelopoiesis, the production of white blood cells and platelets.

kusaal: as adults, red blood cell production is limited to the larger bones: the bodies of the vertebrae, the breastbone (sternum), sapidi kɔnba baba la, nyu'ur tɛŋir baba kɔnba, nɛ kɔnba banɛ bɛ kpɛkpama zug nɛ nɔba.
english: During childhood, almost every human bone produces red blood cells; as adults, red blood cell production is limited to the larger bones: the bodies of the vertebrae, the breastbone (sternum), the ribcage, the pelvic bones, and the bones of the upper arms and legs.

kusaal: Linɛ lɛn paas ya'as, biilimin win, thymus gland la, bɛnɛ tɛnsʋg, li anɛ nimua babir zi'ekanɛ ka ti paamid T lymphocytes.
english: In addition, during childhood, the thymus gland, found in the mediastinum, is an important source of T lymphocytes.

kusaal: Hemoglobin anɛ yɛlkpan , dina pa'an ziim la nwasim(hemochrome).
english: Hemoglobin is the principal determinant of the color of blood (hemochrome).

kusaal: Ninsaalib nii, ziim la ɛɛnti pɔmnɛ yi dagɔbʋg sunsunf la baba n dɔl niŋgbaʋŋ sieba ni yina ka dɔl giinl sieba ni n fɛndigi lɛb sunsunf la datiʋŋ baba.
english: Blood is circulated around the body through blood vessels by the pumping action of the heart.

kusaal: Zuarungu Senior High School (French: Lycée Zuarungu) anɛ sakur biis zamisʋg zin'ikanɛ bɛ Upper East region sʋ'ʋlim, Ghana.
english: Zuarungu Senior High School (French: Lycée Zuarungu) is a second cycle co-educational institution in the Upper East region of Ghana.

kusaal: Di bɛnɛ Bolgatanga East Districti bɛ Upper East region, Ghana.
english: It is located in Bolgatanga East District in the Upper East region of Ghana.

kusaal: Banɛ an sakur kanɛ an yiiga di ya'an National Science and Maths Quiz region la wʋsa ni.
english: It is the first school to win a contest at the regional level of the National Science and Maths Quiz.

kusaal: Sakur la mɔr zamisʋg dɔɔd, komputanam dɔɔg, nɛ gbana buorʋg.
english: The school has classrooms, a computer laboratory, a science laboratory and library.

kusaal: Kanl kaŋa da nɔbʋgʋ paae kɔbʋsnu nɛ pisnii nɛ anu, yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piinɛ yinne ka yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piimnɛ ayi la ka bii la kanl an tusir yinne nɛ pistan nɛ awai (1039).
english: This number increased to 585 in 2011 and to 1039 in 2012.

kusaal: Zuor yiti mɔri wʋʋ 300 metres (980ft) gat teŋ saaŋ la.
english: In addition, some definitions also include a topographical prominence requirement, such as that the mountain rises 300 metres (984 ft) above the surrounding terrain.

kusaal: Ba da du'a Ibrahimah nɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris ayɔpɔi la li dabisim piisi nɛ ayɔpɔi yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyɔpɔi la ni, o saam onɛ maal ka'alim la yυ'υr buon Kuntundawura, Alhaji Mohammed Zublilah Ibrahimah onɛ yi Kpembe la, da anɛ Tamale Polytechnic la linɛ ka ba yυ'υn buonɛ li nannanna Tamale Technical University and Adisah Nassamu Ibrahimah la zugdaan.
english: Zuwera Mohammed was born on 27 July 1970 to late Kuntundawura, Alhaji Mohammed Zublilah Ibrahimah of Kpembe, who was a former principal and rector of Tamale Polytechnic, now Tamale Technical University and Adisah Nassamu Ibrahimah.

kusaal: O keŋi o secondary sakuri n bɛ Tamale Senior High Scool la ni Ka lin nya'aŋ ka o keŋ Nigeria ani ka o saam da pa'an n bɛ Adu Bayero University linɛ bɛ Nigeria Kano sυ'υlυm la.
english: She had her secondary education at the Tamale Senior High School and later in Nigeria where her father was then serving as lecturer at the Adu Bayero University in Kano, Nigeria.

kusaal: O maal Bachelor of Arts digirɛɛ linɛ an Management Studies University of Cape Coast sakur la ni yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piiswai nɛ anii la ni ka maal o Diploma linɛ an Community Development la Trent University sakur linɛ bɛ Canada.
english: She holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in Management Studies from the University of Cape Coast from 1998 and a post Graduate Diploma in Community Development, from Trent University in Canada.

kusaal: O mɛ da maal o mastɛs digirɛɛ linɛ an Diplomacy and International Trade Business (Diplomacy) n yi University of East Anglia linɛ bɛ UK yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piina yi' la ni.
english: She obtained her master's degree in Diplomacy and International Trade Business (Diplomacy) from the University of East Anglia in the UK in 2012.

kusaal: Nannanna o bɛɛ ani n zamisid ye o maal o PhD zamisυg kpazɛɛri linɛ an Media and Communication n bɛ Goldsmiths College, sakur linɛ bɛ London United Kingdom la.
english: She is currently on her thesis project in pursuit of a PhD in Media and Communication from the Goldsmiths College, University of London in the United Kingdom.

kusaal: On da nam pυ kpɛn' pɔlitis la o da tυmnɛ an Information Services Department tυυma la director nya'andɔl.
english: Prior to entering politics, she was the deputy director of the Information Services Department.

kusaal: Onɛ da an project officer Northern Regions nam atan' (Upper East Region, Upper West Region nɛ Northern Region) la wυsa ni n gɔsid Small Town Water Supply Systems project la ka lɛn an project officer tis Catholic Relief Services ye o gɔs lin na niŋ si'em ka Primary sakur nam tυυma la nɔbig Northern Regions sυ'υlυm la.
english: She worked as a project officer in the three Northern Regions (Upper East Region, Upper West Region and Northern Region) on the Small Town Water Supply Systems project and also as a project officer with the Catholic Relief Services on the Quality Improvements in Primary school programme in the Northern Regions as well.

kusaal: Ibrahimah da an Joint Monitoring tυυma la saawada nwɛ'ɛd n tis Water Supply Sanitation nɛ Hygiene (JMP) linɛ an ye WHO/UNICEF n bɛ Ghana la.
english: Zuwera worked as a consultant on the Joint Monitoring Programme for Water Supply Sanitation and Hygiene (JMP) by WHO/UNICEF in Ghana.

kusaal: O mɛ da lɛn tυmnɛ an Manager tis ti Ghana Association of Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA) ka da lɛn an onɛ zi'e ti Gaan nɔba zug n bɛ Discovery Channel Global Education Partnership la ni.
english: She also worked respectively as the country Manager of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA) and the country Representative of the Discovery Channel Global Education Partnership.

kusaal: Zuwera Ibrahimah da paamnɛ vɔt bam 472 ka o tiraan Ibrahim Dey Abubakari onɛ da bɛ kυk la zug nɔɔr ayi' la, nɛ Ahmed Saaka Shaibu Dan nɛ Lukman Jawula mɛ da paam 260, 116 nɛ 1 vɔt wυυ ba yυda la pυd si'em kena la.
english: Zuwera Ibrahimah garnered 472 votes to win the election against Ibrahim Dey Abubakari, a former two-term member of parliament for the constituency, Ahmed Saaka Shaibu Dan and Lukman Jawula who had 260, 116 and 1 votes respectively.

kusaal: O da paamnɛ vɔt bam 20,525 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da paamnɛ 49.5% ka o tiraan Salifu Adam Braimah onɛ da an Wabυg nid onɛ da an da an Minista n tis Savannah Regional sυ'υlυm nɔɔr ayi la, da paamnɛ 19,086 kɔbiga pυυginɛ o da paamnɛ 45.90%.
english: She won after polling 20,525 votes representing 49.5% against the incumbent member of parliament Salifu Adam Braimah of the New Patriotic Party who also doubled as the Savannah Regional Minister, who had 19,086 votes representing 45.90%.

kusaal: Ibrahimah da kpɛn' wadmaanib yir la ye o zi'enɛ tis Salaga South sυ'υlυm la wadmaanib yir line paas anii la ti Gaana Republic linɛ paas anaasi Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la li dabisim ayɔpɔi yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ yinne la ni.
english: Ibrahimah was sworn in as Member of Parliament representing the Salaga South Constituency in the 8th Parliament of the 4th Republic of Ghana on 7 January 2021.

kusaal: O da paas kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid Foreign Affairs la ni ka ka lɛn an kpɛɛm banɛ gɔsid ka ba gaansid kpɛɛmnam wadmaanib yir la ni mɛn.
english: She serves as a member on the Foreign Affairs Committee and the Appointments Committee of Parliament.

kusaal: Zuwera Mohammed Ibrahimah anɛ Ghana pɔlitis nwɛ'ɛd, ba da du'anɛ Buniya nya'aŋ nwaris ayɔpɔi la li dabisim piisi nɛ ayɔpɔi yυυm tusir nɛ kɔbiswai nɛ piisyɔpɔi la ni.
english: Zuwera Mohammed Ibrahimah (born 27 July 1970) is a Ghanaian politician.

kusaal: O anɛ wadmaan n tis Salaga South constituency linɛ Ghana Savannah Region sυ'υlυm la.
english: She is the Member of Parliament for the Salaga South Constituency in the Savannah Region of Ghana.

kusaal: O anɛ da an yiiga pu'a onɛ zin'in kυk la zug Salaga sυ'υlυm la ba da vɔɔti gaŋi o ye o paas wadmaanib yir la ti Ghana republic linɛ paas anaasi la ni.
english: She was the first woman in the Salaga area to be elected as a member of parliament in the fourth republic.

kusaal: O biillimin bɛllim wυsa o zin'inɛ Winneba ani ka o si'iŋi o biilimin sakur ken.
english: She spent her childhood in Winneba where she started basic education.

kusaal: Ibrahimah tυm bɛ zi'is kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb li sieba anɛ development planning, administration and diplomacy la.
english: Zuwera has worked in different sectors especially in community development planning, administration and diplomacy.

kusaal: Buniya nya'aŋ nwarig yinne la li dabisim ayɔpɔi yυυma tusa yi' nɛ piisi nɛ yinne la ni da paas pu'ab bam piisnaasi banɛ kpɛn' wadmaanib yir la ni, o mɛ da anɛ pu'a onɛ paas ani n zi'enɛ tis Savannah Region sυ'ulum la wadmaanib yir linɛ paas anii la ni.
english: As of 7 January 2021, she is one of the 40 women and the only one from the Savannah Region who are representing their respective constituencies in the 8th Parliament.

kusaal: Rye zɔ'ɔm anɛ zɔ'ɔm kanɛ ka ba mɔri paasidi maan bodobodo bɛ Central Europe nɛ Northern Europe.
english: Other cereal flours include corn flour, which has been important in Mesoamerican cuisine since ancient times and remains a staple in the Americas, while rye flour is a constituent of bread in both Central Europe and Northern Europe.

kusaal: Na'asaalin ka ba buon zɔ'ɔm ye flour la da yina pʋʋm ka ba buon ye flower la ni na, ka yʋda ayi' la wʋsa yinɛ Old French fleur bɛɛ flour ni, ka di gbin da pa'al ye din na "vɛnlim", ka mɛ lɛn pa'al ye "bʋnbʋʋlʋg".
english: The English word flour is originally a variant of the word flower, and both words derive from the Old French fleur or flour, which had the literal meaning "blossom", and a figurative meaning "the finest".

kusaal: Rye zɔ'ɔm anɛ zɔ'ɔm kanɛ ka ba mɔri maan bodobodo bɛ central nɛ northern Europe.
english: Rye flour is a constituent of bread in central and northern Europe.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusayi, nɛ piinɛ nii (2018), banɛ zamisid kʋdʋmin yela da yɛl ye ba nyɛ zin'ig kanɛ ka ba da maan bodobodo ka di bɛ Shubayqa 1, lin bɛnɛ Natufian tɔn'ɔsnam la'asig zin'ig ka di na bɛɛ tʋʋg yʋʋma tusa piinɛ anaasi (14,000) ka di bɛ northwest Jordan tɛŋin.
english: In 2018, archaeologists reported finding evidence of bread making at Shubayqa 1, a Natufian hunter-gatherer site more than 14,000 years old in northwest Jordan.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnii nɛ ayuobʋ (1786) ni, sankan ka nifnɛɛlim da kɛna la, zɔ'ɔm banɛka kanɛ ka ba mɔr tʋʋlig paŋi nɛɛmid, ka ba buon Albion Mills, Southwark, da yina bɛ London tɛŋin.
english: In 1786, at the beginning of the Industrial Era, the first steam-powered flour mill, Albion Mills, Southwark, was completed in London.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusir, kɔbiswai nɛ pistan' la saŋa (1930s), ka ba pin'ili gɛndigid zɔ'ɔm nɛ la'asi'eba wan wʋʋ iron, niacin, thiamine nɛ riboflavin.
english: In the 1930s, some flour began to be enriched with iron, niacin, thiamine and riboflavin.

kusaal: Kawɛnna zɔ'ɔm an dinɛ yɛla pak hali tis Mesoamerican cuisine hali kʋdʋmin sa, ka nan kpɛn an dikpɛŋi tis banɛ bɛ America sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Maize or corn flour has been important in Mesoamerican cuisine since ancient times and remains a staple in the Americas.

kusaal: Kawɛnna zɔ'ɔm da anɛ nimmua bʋn Mesoamerican cuisine saŋa sa ka nan kpɛn an ba dikpɛŋi bɛ America sʋ'ʋlim.
english: Maize or corn flour has been important in Mesoamerican cuisine since ancient times and remains a staple in the Americas.

kusaal: Zanbina bɛ pa'al ye ba da nɛm zɔ'ɔm (wheat bi'elim ka ba nyɛ ka di bɛ zin'ig si'a ka ba nɛɛmi di nɛ kuga) ka ba gɔs ka di yʋʋgi tʋʋg yʋʋma 6000 BC.
english: Archaeological evidence for making wheat flour dates to at least 6000 BC.

kusaal: Bread, pasta, crackers, cakes, nɛ diib buudi bɛdigʋ ka ba mɔr zɔ'ɔm maan.
english: Bread, pasta, crackers, cakes, and several other foods are made using flour.

kusaal: Fu ya'a gɔs zina nwa', "kuga nɛɛr" pa'al ye bi'elim la nwa'as nɛ nɛɛm ka di anɛ kugur bɛɛ kʋnt zi'edigi gban'ae kugur bɛɛ kʋnt kanɛ giligid ka ba kpa'asid bi'elim la niŋid tɛnsʋk ka di nɛɛmid.
english: Today, "stone-ground" usually means that the grain has been ground in a mill in which a revolving stone wheel turns over a stationary stone wheel, vertically or horizontally with the grain in between.

kusaal: Škofja Loka Passion Play (Latin: Processio locopolitana, Slovene: Škofjeloški pasijon) Slovene di'emkanɛ yuugi gaadi ba wʋsa.
english: The Škofja Loka Passion Play (Latin: Processio locopolitana, Slovene: Škofjeloški pasijon) is the oldest play in Slovene.

kusaal: Din an si'em nananna la, di anɛ dinɛ mɔr Passion procession.
english: In its current form, it was a penitential Passion procession.

kusaal: Ba da sɔbi li dɔlisinɛ ba malimkʋda yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ piinɛ anu (1715) la ni,ka Father Romuald (Lovrenc Marusič; 1676–1748) da maal tia'as baanlʋg yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (1727) la ni, onɛ an Capuchin friar ka da bɛ saŋa bi'ela Škofja Loka Capuchin monastery ni Škofja Loka tɛɛnsin.
english: It was written on the basis of an older tradition in 1715, with minor corrections until 1727, by Father Romuald (Lovrenc Marusič; 1676–1748), a Capuchin friar who lived for a period in the Škofja Loka Capuchin monastery in the town of Škofja Loka.

kusaal: Ba pʋnɛ tableaux nam ban piinɛ atan (13).
english: They are divided into 13 tableaux.

kusaal: Di anɛ Baroque saŋa din ka zi'eni tis director's book in the world.
english: It belongs to the Baroque period and represents the oldest preserved director's book in the world.

kusaal: Di'ema la da bɛnɛ Good Friday daar yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin kem paae kem paae yʋʋm tusir, kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnu nɛ yinne (1751) la ni.
english: The play was originally staged on Good Friday each year until 1751.

kusaal: Bʋnnama ayi banɛ da gaad tuon la, Marjan Kokalj da gɔsi li yɛla, ka nananna la ka Borut Gartner da gɔsi li yɛla.
english: The first two reprisals were directed by Marjan Kokalj, and the latest by Borut Gartner.

kusaal: Tableaux nam la da pʋnɛ zin'is pisi (20).
english: The tableaux were divided into 20 scenes.

kusaal: National Youth Council of Slovenia da tis Municipality of Škofja Loka gɔs kanɛ bɛ li kɔn' ka tisi ba apɛsigim mɛŋ tʋʋma yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ piiga (2010) la ni, municipality da maal di'ema yʋʋm kanɛ da dɛŋ tuon la.
english: The National Youth Council of Slovenia bestowed the Municipality of Škofja Loka a special recognition for a volunteer project in 2010, after the municipality had organised the play in the previous year.

kusaal: Yʋʋm tusa ayi nɛ anii (2008) la ni, ba da zaŋ di'ema la kpɛn'ɛs Slovenian intangible cultural heritage gbaʋŋin.
english: In 2008, the performance has been entered in the Slovenian intangible cultural heritage register.

kusaal: Di buudi banɛ bɛ Škofja Loka la an dinɛ an open-air theatre production kanɛ zu'oe gaad banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa Slovenia.
english: Its reprisals in Škofja Loka are the largest open-air theatre productions in Slovenia.

kusaal: Di mɔrnɛ verse nam kɔbisnii nɛ piswai nɛ ayuobʋ (896), ka ba sɔbi li niŋ Škofja Loka kʋdʋg pian'ad ni.
english: It consists of 869 verses, written in the old Škofja Loka dialect.

kusaal: Škofja Loka monastery su'ad di'ema la manuscript la.
english: The play's manuscript is kept by the Škofja Loka monastery.

kusaal: Nidib nwɛnɛ di'em di'emnib kɔbisyuobʋ nɛ pisnaasi (640) dap nɛ pʋ'ab, ka pisnii (80) an cavalry men.
english: They were performed by around 640 amateur actors and actresses, among them 80 cavalrymen.
